english: Why is it important to space my cocoa trees 10 feet by 10 feet apart?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ abɔ he ni ji ninetalɔi 10 kɛ ninetalɔi 10 lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures each tree gets enough sunlight, soil nutrients, and airflow. Planting them 10 feet by 10 feet prevents overcrowding, reduces the spread of diseases, and gives cocoa plants room to yield healthy pods.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa ni hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Koo tsei ni akwɛ̃ɔ ni kɛlɛ ji ninetalɔi 10 kɛ ninetalɔi 10 lɛ baaye abua ni akafee nɔ ni fa fe nine. Ha helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ aba shi ni eha cacao tsei lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛwo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What is pegging, and why is it done on my farmland before planting?
ga: Mɛni ji fimɔ? Ni mɛni hewɔ afeɔ enɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ dani aduɔ nii?

english: Pegging involves placing wooden sticks in the ground to mark the exact spots where crops should be planted. It helps keep your farm rows straight and evenly spaced, making weeding, spraying, and harvesting much easier later on.
ga: Nɔ ni fata pinning he ji ni akɛ tsei awo shikpɔŋ koni akɛkadi he pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɛ. Ye obua ni oŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋtayaai lɛ afee ja ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ afee ekome. Enɛ haa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ, kɛ nikpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do we plant crops in straight lines instead of placing them randomly across the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni wɔkɛaawo ŋmɔ lɛ mli he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines ensures that every crop gets equal room and light, prevents overcrowding, and allows you to walk through the farm easily to carry out maintenance without damaging young plants.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ náa he ko kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Tsiɔ nibii ni eyi obɔ lɛ naa ni ehaa onyɛɔ otsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli oya kɛha saamɔ ni ofiteee dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why must I clear my land completely before planting new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ dani madu kookoo dumɔwui heei lɛ?

english: Clearing weeds, bushes, and heavy debris removes competition for soil nutrients and water, while also eliminating pests and diseases that could attack delicate young cocoa plants.
ga: Jwɛi, tsei bibii kɛ sũ ni tsii ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ akaŋshii ni akɛtaoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ kɛyaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baanyɛ atutua kookoo tsei bibii lɛ kɛyaa.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains next to my new cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantains yɛ kookoo tsei heei ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Should I plant my plantains before or at the same time as my cocoa seedlings?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui dani loo yɛ be kome too mli? Kɛ kookoo dumɔwui?

english: It is best to plant plantains slightly before or at the same time as cocoa so that the plantain leaves can grow fast enough to provide protective shade before hot weather damages the young cocoa.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu plantain fioo dani loo yɛ be kome mli kɛ kookoo lɛ bɔni afee ni plantain baai lɛ adara oya bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ hulutsoo be aba dani kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ akpata kookoo bibioo lɛ hiɛ.

english: Will planting plantains next to my cocoa steal nutrients away from the cocoa?
ga: dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Ani mi-kokoo lɛ baaju niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ mli?

english: No, when spaced correctly, plantains and cocoa share the soil well. The plantains protect the cocoa from harsh weather and provide early food and income for your family before the cocoa begins to produce.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ Plantains kɛ cocoa to amɛhe jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaja shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Plantains buɔ kookoo he kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai ahe, ni ehaa oweku lɛ niyenii kɛ shika dani kookoo feemɔ jeɔ shishi.

english: How do young cocoa leaves react if they get too much direct sunlight?
ga: Te kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ tsɔ lɛ fa babaoo?

english: Young cocoa leaves exposed to harsh sun turn yellow, dry out at the edges, and drop off early because the young roots cannot draw enough water to replace what the hot sun burns away.
ga: Kokoo baai bibii ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ Etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, egbiɔ yɛ eshishigbɛ, ni egbeeɔ shi oya ejaakɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbala nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛto nɔ ni hulu lɛ eshã lɛ najiaŋ.

english: What happens if I delay and leave cocoa seedlings in their nursery bags for too long?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ be shwie shi ni mishi mi-cacao tsei lɛ yɛ grow bag lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Leaving seedlings too long in nursery bags causes their roots to twist, coil, or dry out, which weakens the plant and makes it difficult for it to establish strong roots once planted in the farm.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi dumɔwui yɛ grow bags amli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ, atsɔ loo amɛgbi, ni no haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ewaa akɛ amɛaawo shishifãi ni mli wa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do young cocoa plants die so easily during the dry season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii gboiɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have short, shallow roots that cannot reach water deep underground. Without temporary shade crops like plantains to hold soil moisture, intense sun rapidly dehydrates and kills the plants.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi kukuji ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo baa be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains, ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi lɛ bɛ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa nu sɛɛ foɔ oya ni egbeɔ tsei.

english: How do I know if my young cocoa plants are getting enough water during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: If young cocoa plants do not get enough water, their leaves will droop, curl, and turn brown at the tips. You can check the soil by digging a few inches down near the plant; if it feels completely dry and crumbles easily, the roots need water.
ga: Kɛji akɛ cacao tsei bibii lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, amɛbaai lɛ baagbee shi, amɛbaabɔle amɛhe, ni amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ amɛyitseiaŋ. Obaanyɛ okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ inchi fioo ko ni oootsɔ shishi yɛ tso lɛ masɛi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji enu he akɛ egbi kwraa ni efoɔ oya Tsɔɔ akɛ nu he miihia shishifãi lɛ.

english: Is it helpful to manually water my young cocoa seedlings using simple containers like cups during dry months?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ akɛ niji baawo cacao tsei bibii amli nu kɛtsɔ tsɛnsi ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ kɔɔpoo nɔ yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli?

english: Yes, during severe dry spells, pouring a measured cup or small tin of water directly at the base of each seedling keeps the main roots alive without wasting water on surrounding weeds.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa mli Nu ni afɔseɔ awoɔ susumɔ kɔɔpoo loo kan bibioo mli Tɛ̃ɛ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishi. Enɛ baaha shishifãi titrii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfiteee nu yɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anɔ.

english: What is the best time of day to water my cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ kookoo tsei anɔ nu?

english: The best time to water cocoa seedlings is early in the morning or late in the afternoon. During these cooler times, water does not evaporate quickly in the sun, allowing the roots to absorb most of it.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ kookoo dumɔwui anɔ nu ji leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli. Yɛ fɛ̃i be nɛɛ mli Nu lɛ shwieee oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ enɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ nu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Can I attach simple hose pipes or drip nozzles to a water drum to irrigate my crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ hose loo drip nozzle ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ afata mi nu tsɛnsi lɛ he koni mikɛshwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu?

english: Yes, connecting basic hose pipes or drip attachments to a elevated water drum allows water to trickle slowly to the base of each plant, saving you labor while delivering steady moisture directly to the roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ okɛ shishijee hose paipi loo drip attachment tsa baagi ni awo nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ blɛoo. kɛyashi tso fɛɛ tso shishi Ehereɔ bo kɛjɛɔ nitsumɔ mli yɛ be mli ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How can I measure the right amount of liquid fertilizer or water to give each seedling without expensive tools?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masusu nu loo nu ni sa ni akɛbaahã dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko lɛ he ni mikɛ nibii ni jara wa tsuuu nii?

english: You can use standard plastic cups or small tins as measurement units to ensure every seedling receives the exact same amount of liquid, preventing plant damage from over-application.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ plastic kɔɔpoo loo tsinsii bibioo ko ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ atsu nii akɛ nɔ ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu nine shɛɔ nu ni tamɔ nakai pɛpɛɛpɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji koni akafite tsei kɛtsɔ nitsumɔ fe nine nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before they turn into full pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani amɛfee ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed flowers if they experience stress, such as a sudden lack of water, extreme heat, or insufficient nutrients in the soil.
ga: Cocoa tsei baafɔ fɔfɔi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛna haomɔi, tamɔ nu ni bɛ trukaa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: What causes my cocoa leaves to turn yellow and dry out at the edges?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-kokoo baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ amɛshishigbɛ?

english: Yellow leaves with dry edges usually indicate that the plant is getting too much harsh sunlight without enough moisture, or that the soil is lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ ni egbi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ eshɛ tso lɛ he ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Aloo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are some cocoa trees on my farm growing very fast while others remain small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu daraaa lolo lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees grow at different speeds depending on variations in soil quality across your farm, differing sunlight exposure, or competition for nutrients from nearby weed roots.
ga: Cocoa tsei daa oya yɛ srɔtoi amli. Enɛ damɔ tsakemɔi ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ nɔ. hulu la ni yɔɔ srɔtoi loo akaŋshii kɛha niyenii ni jɛɔ jwɛi shishifãi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: How does too much standing water around the base affect my cocoa trees?
ga: Te nu ni damɔ shi babaoo ni ebɔle shishitoo lɛ he lɛ saa mi cacao tsei lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When water sits around the base of a cocoa tree for too long, it prevents the roots from breathing, leading to root rot which causes leaves to turn yellow and fall off.
ga: Kɛ nu hi kookoo tso lɛ shishi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ, ni no haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants need shade trees planted around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ abɔle mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that sunburn easily under direct heat. Shade trees act like protective canopies, keeping the soil cool and reducing moisture loss from the ground.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, hulu lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning yellow and dropping off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop leaves during the dry Harmattan season to reduce water loss. However, severe leaf yellowing and drop often mean the trees lack adequate shade from larger trees or are stressed by a shortage of soil nutrients like nitrogen and potassium.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Shi kɛlɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni naa wa kɛ baai ni laajeɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ bɛ hulutsoo ni sa kɛjɛ tsei wuji lɛ adɛŋ. Aloo haomɔ ni jɛɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen kɛ potassium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa.

english: Why does my cassava plant grow very tall with thick green leaves, but the tubers underground remain very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing branches and leaves above the ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ niji kɛ baai ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant before producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences stress from very high temperatures, irregular watering, or a lack of pollination. Without steady moisture and proper heat management, the flower fails to set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa mli baa lɛ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo pollination ni bɛ Kɛji hulutsoo be fɛɛ be kɛ dɔlɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo kpakpa bɛ lɛ Fɔfɔi nyɛŋ awo yibii.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up, shrink, and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso, amɛmiigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ kpakpa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the sap, or by a virus transmitted by these insects that distorts plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni fiteɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ nɔ

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to grow green and strong. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure gives the plants the nutrients required to regain their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil repeatedly and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the field. Rotating with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nutrients naturally back into the soil.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ daa be lɛ baajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shii abɔ. ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni kɔɔ tsei pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe baa Kɛ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Will I harvest more food if I plant my crop seeds very close together in the field?
ga: Ani makpa niyenii babaoo kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: No, planting seeds too close causes the crops to fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin, weak plants with small yields. Giving crops proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough resources to produce a large harvest.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ awuu koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa kã ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ekpa nii babaoo.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei kakadaji ama shi lɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce the energy required to grow large tubers underground. Staking lifts the foliage off the damp soil into the sunlight, which also prevents fungal diseases from destroying wet leaves on the ground.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ akafite baai ni efɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground in the soil before I get to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when excessive rainwater sits in heavy soil and smothers the root system. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away easily so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ ni efiteɔ shishifãi lɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die during the hot harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ harmattan be ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry harmattan winds and intense sunlight draw water out of young cocoa plants faster than their small roots can drink it. Planting plantains alongside young cocoa provides shade and traps moisture, protecting the seedlings until they grow strong roots.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ kookoo tsei bibii amli oya fe shishifãi bibii. Abaanyɛ anu tso lɛ mli nibii lɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ baaha hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ dumɔwui ahe kɛyashiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe waa.

english: What is causing ragged holes in my maize leaves along with small brownish dirt inside the top of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ mi-abɛi lɛ amli ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ kɛ muji bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baa? Yɛ tso lɛ yiteŋ?

english: Ragged holes and brownish dirt are signs of Fall Armyworm caterpillars eating the center of your maize plants. Applying recommended treatments directly into the central funnel of the plant early in the morning destroys the caterpillars before they ruin the whole crop.
ga: Buji ni etse kɛ muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ o-corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ he okadii. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ wo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaakpata ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛbaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and twisting tightly like old paper?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ wolo momo lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is typically caused by tiny sucking pests like aphids or thrips that spread plant viruses while feeding on leaf sap. Controlling these pests early with neem oil or recommended sprays protects new leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ tsei ahe helai eshwaa be mli ni eyeɔ tsofa ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ Kudɔmɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ mra Neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu baai heei lɛ ahe koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from sudden heat stress or uneven watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the base of the plant during hot periods encourages the flowers to stay on and turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ hulutsoo ni baa trukaa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha ebɔle ehe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ Tso lɛ yitso lɛ yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛtsɔɔ tomatoi.

english: Why do weeds make my crops stay small and weak even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds act as aggressive competitors that drink up the water and steal the soil food meant for your crops. Removing weeds early gives your crops full access to the nutrients they need to grow tall and strong.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ akaŋshilɔi ni yɔɔ basabasa ni nuɔ nu ni amɛjuɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa otsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants turn brown and scorch in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight and intense heat. Planting shade crops like plantains next to young cocoa creates a canopy that shields them from heat stress and preserves soil moisture.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ Cocoa tso lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: How far apart should I plant my plantain suckers when setting up a new farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu plantain tsei lɛ kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ he tɛŋŋ beni miito ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers should be planted about 3 meters apart. Proper spacing prevents the leaves from shading each other out completely and stops roots from competing for water and nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ aaafee mitai 3 kɛjɛ amɛhe. He ni jɛkɛmɔ ni sa baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsi amɛhe kwraa. ni etsĩɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden stakes next to my yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko fɔ̃ɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need stakes to expose their leaves to sunlight. Lifted leaves make more food to grow big underground tubers and stay off the wet ground where leaf diseases spread.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ko ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni akɛwo tso nɔ koni ebaa lɛ aha hulu la lɛ. Baai ni awó nɔ lɛ haa niyenii babaoo kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni miida. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni ji foliary helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my maize leaves full of ragged holes with small worms inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa baa lɛ eyi kɛ buji ni etsilɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: This leaf damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that feed on the soft growing center of young maize. Early detection and applying recommended insecticides or botanical treatments like neem extract protect the yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ ana tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii tamɔ neem mli nu lɛ mra ni akɛtsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants twisting and curling up tight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking sap, or by a viral infection spread by whiteflies. Controlling these sap-sucking insects stops the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu nɛɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off without turning into small tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato bibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or extreme dry spells. Keeping soil moisture consistent prevents stress and allows flowers to set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ daa loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi waa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ tsiɔ haomɔ naa ni ehaa fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my maize stalks staying short and turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing maize leaves mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants use to grow tall and produce chlorophyll. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or compost restores healthy green growth.
ga: Abɛi baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛdara ni amɛfee klorofil. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help improve my soil for the next season?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ aha be ni baa lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas absorb nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the roots decompose after harvest, they release this extra nitrogen into the soil, feeding the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ shwieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Amɛjieɔ nitrogen ni fa fe nine nɛɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: How do I know when my cassava crop is ready to be dug up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni abaaku?

english: Cassava is generally ready for harvest between 9 to 12 months after planting, when lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil surrounding the stem begins to crack from expanding roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha nikpamɔ yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ shishifãi lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ hewɔ lɛ.

english: Why does my lowland rice crop perform better when there is standing water in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-lowland rice lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nu ni damɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Standing water drowns out weeds that compete with rice for nutrients and maintains a steady soil temperature, allowing the rice plants to focus energy on producing full grain heads.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni efuɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋshii mli lɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔlɛ yaa nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ maa dumɔwui ayitsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do many of the small flowers on my cocoa trees fall off without ever turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ji No hewɔ lɛ, mi-kookoo tso lɛ nɔ fã ni fa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi kɔkɔɔkɔ?

english: Cocoa flowers need to be pollinated—either by tiny insects like midges or by hand—to form pods. If a flower isn't pollinated within a day or two, it dies and drops off the tree naturally.
ga: Ehe miihia ni aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ awo kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ amli. Ekolɛ kɛtsɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo kɛtsɔ nine nɔ. koni akɛfee pod Kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ fɔfɔii lɛ amli pollin yɛ gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ mli lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagboi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛbaagbee shi kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: How does hand pollination actually work to increase the amount of cocoa I harvest?
ga: Te nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii ehaa tɛŋŋ koni eha kookoo ni mikpaa lɛ aya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Hand pollination means manually transferring pollen from one cocoa flower to another using small brushes or forceps. This ensures almost every flower receives pollen and develops into a healthy pod, rather than waiting for scarce insects to do it.
ga: Nɔ ni fata nine ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ he ji ni akɛ niji ajie fɔfɔi kɛjɛ kookoo fɔfɔi kome mli kɛya ekroko mli kɛtsɔ brɔsh bibioo loo pliers nɔ. Enɛ haa nɔ ni miihe ashɛ fɔfɔi fɛɛ fɔfɔi nine shɛɔ pollen nɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi ni mli wa baa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ ni kooloi bibii ni anaaa amɛ waa lɛ afee nakai lɛ

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants turn yellow and dry up when there are no shade trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade trees or plantains nearby to filter the light and protect their tender leaves until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ he miihia amɛ. koni ekɛjie la ni ebu ehe baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa

english: Why should I cut off extra stems and small shoots from my cocoa trees when they seem to be growing fine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei krokomɛi kɛ tsei bibii lɛ? Kɛjɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ nɔ beni etamɔ nɔ ni eedara jogbaŋŋ nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary stems so the tree doesn't waste energy on useless leaves. It allows sunlight and air to move freely through the tree, which prevents diseases and encourages big pod growth.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ akafite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ tsiɔ helai anaa ni ehaa ŋmeii wuji lɛ daraa.

english: What causes green cocoa pods to suddenly turn black and rot on the branch during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ feɔ diŋ trukaa ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, dark weather. Removing affected pods early and keeping the farm clear of weeds helps stop the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. This is a fungus that grows in humid and overcast conditions. Pods ni ena hela lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Ni jwɛi ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni oooha ehi shi lɛ baaye abua ni ekpa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why do insects attack my cocoa trees more when the farm is overgrown with weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa mi-kokoo tsei lɛ beni jwɛi eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli obɔ lɛ?

english: Tall weeds create a moist, hidden environment where pests and insects can breed safely. Keeping your land clear deprives insects of hiding spots and reduces attacks on your trees.
ga: Jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ feɔ shihilɛ ni mli efɔ, ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ. he ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ kooloi bibii baanyɛ afɔ yɛ shweshweeshwe Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee faŋŋ lɛ baaha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anijiaŋ aje wui kɛjɛ hei ni amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ mli lɛ, ni ebaaha tutuamɔ ni baa otsei lɛ anɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: What will happen if I plant my cocoa seedlings very close together so I can fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu kookoo dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ he ko babaoo?

english: When cocoa trees are planted too close, their roots and leaves fight for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. This results in weak trees, smaller pods, and a higher risk of disease spread.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu kookoo ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ŋmeii bibii kɛ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he oshara kpele.

english: How can I tell if my soil is weak and needs fertilizer for my cocoa farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ehe miihia ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛha mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: If your cocoa trees grow very slowly, have pale leaves, or produce small and empty-looking pods, it means the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, or potassium.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-cacao tsei lɛ daraa blɛoo waa, amɛyɛ baai ni tsuɔ, loo amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii ni tamɔ nɔ ni nɔ ko bɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus loo potassium.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my cocoa pods from the tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Ripe cocoa pods change color completely from green or dark red to bright yellow or orange. Harvesting them when they turn fully yellow ensures the beans inside are mature and ready for fermentation.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su kwraa kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo akutu ni mli tse nɔ. Kɛ́ akpa dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛfee klalo kɛha ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Is it good for me to plant cassava on the same piece of land as my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Cassava is a heavy feeder that aggressive pulls water and nutrients out of the soil, which can starve young cocoa trees. It is better to use plantains, which provide good shade without choking the cocoa.
ga: Cassava ji niyenii ni tsii ni jieɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa. Enɛ baanyɛ aha hɔmɔ aye kookoo tsei bibii. Esa akɛ akɛ plantains atsu nii, ni haa hulutsoo kpakpa ni ehaaa kookoo lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: How can I tell if the maize seeds I saved from last season are good enough to plant this year?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mijie kɛjɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu afi nɛɛ?

english: You can do a simple germination test before planting. Place ten seeds inside a wet paper or cloth towel, keep it moist for five days, and count how many sprout. If eight or more sprout, your seed batch is strong enough to plant.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee shweremɔ he kaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo dani odu: Okɛ dumɔwui 10 awo wolo ni mli ewo fɔ loo wolo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Shi ni edɔ gbii 5 ni okane dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ ayibɔ. Kɛji tsei kpaanyɔ loo nɔ ni fe nakai Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ odumɔwui akuu lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellowing on cassava is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Using certified disease-resistant stems and pulling out infected plants early stops the disease from spreading across your farm.
ga: Kasava lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela kɛbaa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Tsoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer when the ground is dry during a hot dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so roots can absorb it safely. Applying fertilizer on dry soil under intense heat can burn crop roots and waste your money, as the nutrients cannot be taken up without soil moisture.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛshwie shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ shweshweeshwe. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa shishi lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni efite shika. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ.

english: What happens to my maize crop if I plant seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in thin, weak stalks that fall over easily and produce very small or empty maize cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya. ni ekɛ ŋmãa bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I cut down all the large trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikookoo tsei bibii lɛ egbi ni amɛgboi beni mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct, intense sunlight and high heat. Leaving or planting shade trees like plantains or leguminous trees keeps the air cool and protects young cocoa leaves from burning while they establish roots.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo legumes ni ashiɔ loo aduɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa kookoo baai bibii lɛ ashã be mli ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my crops even after I put fertilizer on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔji lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli moŋ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that absorb water and fertilizer nutrients much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early in the season ensures your crops get to consume the fertilizer before weeds steal it.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛheɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuɔ nii dani jwɛi lɛ juɔ lɛ.

english: Why are insects eating up my harvested maize inside sealed storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiye mi-ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ yɛ kotokui ni akɛtoɔ nii amli ni atsĩ naa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Insects or their invisible eggs were likely already on the maize before bagging, or the grain had too much moisture inside. Drying your maize thoroughly in the sun until it crackles and using airtight PICS bags suffocates any remaining pests.
ga: Ekolɛ kooloi loo ŋmeii ni anaaa lɛ baanyɛ ahi ŋmãa lɛ mli dani akɛwo kotoku mli. aloo dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo Gbimɔ ŋmãa lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaagbala. Ni kɛ akɛ PICS vacuum bag tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Is it better for my tomato crops if I water them early in the morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha mi-tomato tsei lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu wo amɛmli leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil absorbs the moisture before the midday heat. Watering in the afternoon causes water to evaporate rapidly before reaching roots and can burn warm leaves.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baaŋɔ nu dani hulutsoo be lɛ aba. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli shwane mli lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya dani eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni ebaanyɛ eshã baai ni mli edɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant maize on the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients every season and allows specific soil pests to build up. Rotating maize with beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally and breaks pest life cycles.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ daa be mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa. Akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsakeɔ ŋmãa lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ, ni efiteɔ ŋmãa ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ wala shihilɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my groundnuts so they don't rot in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei? Koni ŋmeii lɛ akafite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Groundnuts are ready when the leaves turn yellow and begin to dry up. You can pull up one plant to check—if the insides of the shells have dark brown markings and the nuts fill out the shell completely, it is time to harvest.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbɔi ŋmɔlɔ. Obaanyɛ ogbala tso lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi koni okwɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ ni ŋshɔŋlooi lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ, no lɛ be eshɛɛ ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Why do some groundnut plants produce large seeds while others produce small seeds on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii komɛi woɔ dumɔwui wuji lɛ? yɛ be mli ni no hewɔ lɛ kooloi srɔtoi komɛi woɔ dumɔwui bibii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: Different groundnut varieties carry different traits. Plant breeders intentionally develop some varieties to produce larger seeds for snacking and direct eating, while smaller-seeded varieties are often developed for oil extraction.
ga: Esoro bɔ ni ŋmeii srɔtoi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko yɔɔ ha. Mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei anɔ lɛ eto amɛyiŋ akɛ amɛbaafee tsei srɔtoi komɛi koni amɛkɛwo dumɔwui wuji ni akɛyeɔ niyenii fioo kɛ niyenii ni ayeɔ tɛ̃ɛ. yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, afeɔ dumɔwui bibii srɔtoi koni akɛjie mu.

english: How do I choose the best groundnut variety if I want to sell to traders who make groundnut paste or oil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei srɔtoi ni hi fe fɛɛ? Koni ahɔ̃ɔ aha jarayelɔi ni feɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo fɔ

english: Different buyers look for different qualities. Varieties rich in oil are best for processors, while high-yield, sweet varieties are preferred for roasted snacks. Extension officers and plant breeders work with processors to recommend specific varieties that meet these exact market demands.
ga: Mɛi srɔtoi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ sui srɔtoi. Srɔtoi ni mu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni sa jogbaŋŋ kɛha mɛi ni feɔ nibii lɛ. yɛ be mli ni akɛ srɔtoi ni ŋɔɔ ni woɔ yibii babaoo tsuɔ nii yɛ niyenii ni ashãa mli. Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ kɛ mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei anɔ lɛ kɛ mɛi ni tsuɔ tsei ahe nii lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛjie tsei srɔtoi pɔtɛɛ ni kɛ jarayeli hiamɔ nii kpãa gbee diɛŋtsɛ lɛ akpo.

english: Why should I buy newly developed groundnut seeds instead of planting the seeds I saved from last year's harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe ŋmei dumɔwui ni afee ehee lɛ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds can lose their purity and vigor over time, leading to lower yields and disease susceptibility. Newly developed seeds are carefully selected by plant breeders to offer higher yields, better disease resistance, and improved market quality.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite amɛhetsemɔ kɛ hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi, ni helai hu baa mɔ nɔ oya. Mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei anɔ lɛ ehala dumɔwui heei ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ. bɔni afee ni ekɛ yibii babaoo aba Helai ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛbaatsu nii ni eha jarayeli lɛ aya hiɛ

english: Why do market traders offer lower prices for certain types of groundnuts even when they are fresh?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayelɔi kɛ jara ni baa shi haa ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi kɛji akɛ amɛji ŋmeii heei po lɛ?

english: Traders favor seed varieties that match consumer preferences, such as uniform size, easy shelling, or specific seed coat colors. Growing seed varieties developed in consultation with market sellers helps ensure your harvest meets market demands and gets a better price.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, jarayelɔi sumɔɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni kɛ jarayelɔi ahiamɔ nii kpãa gbee, tamɔ amɛdalɛ kome kɛ amɛhe ni ajieɔ lɛ mlɛo. loo dumɔwui pɔtɛɛ ko he su Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni afee yɛ jara nɔ jarayelɔi ahe sanegbaa mli lɛ haa onikpamɔ lɛ kɛ jara nɔ nibii ni ataoɔ lɛ kpãa gbee ni onine shɛɔ jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɔ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants have plenty of green leaves above ground but very few pods under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ hiɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi pods fioo ko pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Excessive leafy growth often happens when there is too much nitrogen in the soil or a lack of calcium. Groundnut plants need balanced nutrients so they can shift their energy from leaf growth to forming strong pegs that grow into the soil to yield healthy pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni daa fe nine lɛ baa kɛji nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo calcium bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Peanut tsei lɛ hia niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni sa bɔni afee ni amɛtsake hewalɛ kɛjɛ baai ni miida lɛ mli kɛya ŋmeii ni wa ni daa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afeemɔ mli koni amɛfee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do groundnut pods form underground instead of growing on the branches like beans or maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei ŋmɔji feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ̃ yɛ tsei niji tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei nɔ lɛ?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated above ground, the plant produces a growing stem called a peg. This peg grows downwards into the soil, where it develops into a pod underground to protect the seeds from heat, birds, and pests.
ga: Beni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ewo ŋmɔtɔ sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ woɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ pegs. Pin nɛɛ baakwɛ̃ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, etsɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni ebuɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ, okpoi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Why do some groundnut varieties survive when dry weather hits, while others dry up and die quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi hiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ amli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni henɔi komɛi gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya lɛ.

english: Different varieties possess different natural traits. Plant breeders select drought-tolerant varieties that develop deeper roots or conserve water better, allowing them to withstand dry spells far better than standard varieties.
ga: Srɔtoi srɔtoi yɛ adebɔɔ mli sui srɔtoi. Mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei anɔ lɛ halaa tsei srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ loo amɛhe esa jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu he. Enɛ haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa babaoo fe ŋmeii srɔtoi ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ.

english: Why do crop researchers come to our villages to ask farmers to test new seeds on our fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe niiamlitaolɔi miiba wɔ akrowa lɛ koni amɛbabi okwaafoi ni amɛka dumɔwui heei amɛkwɛ yɛ wɔŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Breeding successful crops requires creative variations, but only farmers know the practical conditions of their local soil and climate. Researchers collaborate with farmers to see which experimental seeds perform best under real field conditions before releasing them widely.
ga: Tsei afɔmɔ ni yeɔ omanye lɛ biɔ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ afee nibii. Shi okwaafoi pɛ le shihilɛi ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii yɛ amɛmaŋ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ mli. Nibii amlitaolɔi kɛ okwaafoi tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ dumɔwui ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ lɛ ateŋ nɔ ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ amli dani amɛjieɔ amɛ kpo babaoo.

english: Why do some groundnut varieties rot easily in storage while others stay good for months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi fiteɔ oya kɛ́ akɛto lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni abaanyɛ akɛ henɔi komɛi ato nyɔji babaoo lɛ?

english: Post-harvest durability depends on genetic traits such as shell thickness and natural resistance to mold. Breeders select varieties with tougher shells and lower moisture retention to reduce spoilage after harvest.
ga: Bɔ ni ebaahi shi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ damɔ fɔmɔ su tamɔ bɔ ni eshishifãi lɛ mli tse ha lɛ nɔ. kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ ŋmeii lɛ Mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ halaa ŋmeii srɔtoi ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni wa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhiɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ. Koni nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ

english: How can I tell if a groundnut variety matures quickly so I can harvest before the rains stop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-peanut henɔi lɛ miida oya bɔni afee ni manyɛ makpa amɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ akpa?

english: Varieties are developed with specific maturity periods, usually ranging from 90 days for early-maturing types to 120 days for late-maturing ones. Checking seed descriptions or asking an extension officer helps you match the variety to your area's rainy season length.
ga: Afeɔ henɔi srɔtoi ni dalɛ bei pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɔɔ mli. Enɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ gbii 90 kɛha ŋmeii ni shwereɔ mra lɛ kɛyashiɔ gbii 120 kɛha ŋmeii ni shwereɔ sɛɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe saji amli loo obi mɔ ko ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni okɛ dumɔwui lɛ afee ekome kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow while the top leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ shi ŋwɛi baa lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually means the crop is short on nitrogen, an important plant food. When nitrogen runs low in the soil, the plant moves what little it has left to the newer upper leaves to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen fioo pɛ eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ baajie nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ koni ehi shi.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge, bushy leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or is overly rich in animal manure, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems on top instead of sending food down to build fat roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo kooloi ashishifãi fa tsɔ. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsu niyenii kɛba shi koni ekɛfee shishifãi ni yɔɔ fɔ

english: Why do my groundnut plants push their flowers into the dirt after they bloom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ tsiɔ efɔfɔi lɛ awoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts naturally produce their pods underground. After the yellow flower on top is pollinated, the plant grows a small stem called a peg that burrows into the soil where the actual peanut grows.
ga: Peanuts feɔ pods yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. After the yellow flowers on top have been pollinated, The plant has a small trunk. Atsɛɔ enɛɛmɛi akɛ ŋtayaai ni afoɔ awoɔ sũ ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the heat becomes too intense or when the plant experiences sudden dry spells. The plant drops its flowers to save water and energy when stressed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ mli egbi trukaa. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛ́ amɛmiihao.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and looking crinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from under the leaf, or from a virus spread by those pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ helai ni nakai tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop most of their small leaves during the dry hamattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ miiho baai bibii lɛ? Titri lɛ, yɛ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during dry weather as a survival tactic to reduce the amount of water escaping from the tree when the soil has very little moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ aba shi beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees alongside my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide the necessary shade and keep the soil moist for young cocoa plants to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni cacao tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do I need to put wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso he hiaa mi koni mikɛ sweet potato wain tso awo mli bɔni afee ni makwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can capture maximum sunlight, which allows the plant to make enough food to send down to build larger tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaa shi koni efee bulbs wuji.

english: Why do my maize cobs stay small when I plant seeds close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii nɛkɛ beni adu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Planted too closely, maize roots fight each other for limited soil nutrients and water, which leaves every plant weak and results in small cobs.
ga: adu ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ Abɛi shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni fa fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why should I prune away some of the young suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi tsɔne titri lɛ eje kpo.

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow forces the mother plantain to share its food and water. Removing extra shoots ensures the main plant gets full energy to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ nyɛ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ niyenii kɛ nu aha. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing of lower maize leaves usually signals a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen helps plants make food; when it runs short, the plant moves what little it has to newer leaves at the top, leaving the old bottom leaves starving.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni efeɔ niyenii. Kɛ́ eyɛ kuku lɛ, tso lɛ tsiɔ ehe fioo kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Ha shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ aye hɔmɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves dry up and burn when I place fertilizer directly at the base of the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Placing concentrated fertilizer directly against the stem draws moisture out of the roots, causing chemical burn. Fertilizer should be placed in a small ring a few centimeters away from the stem so the roots absorb it safely.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli edɔ wo tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaagbala ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ekɛ tsofa ni shãa nii baa. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmeii bibii amli. Sɛntimitai fioo komɛi kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli. koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe

english: Why do people recommend planting groundnuts or beans on the same land where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which traps nitrogen gas from the air and stores it in the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil with nutrients for heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha niyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why should I cut away some of the young suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantain wulu lɛ he lɛ?

english: Too many suckers compete with the main plantain tree for soil nutrients, light, and water. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, which results in much larger plantain bunches.
ga: Tsobii babaoo ni fa tsɔ kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, la, kɛ nu mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baajɛ mli aba. Enɛ haa plantains lɛ feɔ agboi babaoo.

english: Why do I need to put tall sticks next to my yam mounds for the vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso nine kakadaŋŋ ama emasɛi lɛ? Pile sweet potatoes kɛha wain tsei lɛ koni amɛkwɔ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can spread out and catch direct sunlight. Good sunlight exposure helps the leaves manufacture the energy needed to grow large tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛha baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Hulu la ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and looking twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle ehe ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni efite lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites, or a virus spread by these insects. They feed on leaf sap, causing young leaves to deform and twist as they expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Amɛyeɔ baa mli nu. Enɛ haa baai bibii lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfiteɔ be mli ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa lɛ.

english: Why are my young cocoa leaves turning brown and drying up during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat, which scorch their tender leaves. Providing shade from shade trees or shade plants like plantains protects them until they mature.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Enɛ baaha baai bibii lɛ ashã. Shade ni jɛɔ tsei ni haa shade loo tsei ni haa shade tamɔ plantains lɛ baaye abua ni abu tsei nɛɛ ahe kɛyashi tsei lɛ baadara.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when temperatures get too high or when water availability changes suddenly. Heat stress disrupts pollination, causing the plant to shed unpollinated flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ tsake trukaa. Dɔlɛ mli haomɔ tsiɔ pollination naa. Ha tsei ajie fɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why is it risky for me to sow my maize seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the year is often followed by a long dry spell before the main rainy season settles. Sowing early causes seeds to germinate, only to dry up and die when the moisture quickly disappears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ baashɛ. Kɛ́ adu mra lɛ, ebaawo dumɔwui lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃. Shi egbiɔ ni egboɔ kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ laaje oya.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when heavy rains flood my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa eyi miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe and stay healthy. When water sits on the field without draining, roots suffocate and become vulnerable to fungal rots that destroy the crop.
ga: Cassava shishifãi hia kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni amɛmu ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baafo ni amɛbaafee oshara akɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How do I know which direction is the top when I am planting cassava stems in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male he ni adu ŋmeii lɛ yɛ?

english: Look at the small buds or nodes along the cassava stem where the old leaves used to grow. These buds should always point upwards toward the sky so the plant can sprout leaves easily out of the soil.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii lɛ. Yɛ ŋmei tso lɛ he yɛ he ni tsutsu lɛ baai momoi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ akwɛ baai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with very tiny food when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛ niyenii fioo ko pɛ? Akɛni midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ hewɔ lɛ

english: Crops need light, water, and food from the soil to grow strong. When planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, stretching tall and weak while starving for nutrients.
ga: Tsei taoɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ adu amɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Ekpã shi ni egbɔjɔ be mli ni hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ kɛha niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do farmers build high mounds of earth before planting yam tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi maa sũi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ dani amɛduɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need loose, soft soil to expand and grow big underneath the ground. Mounds keep the soil loose and prevent excess water from standing around the roots, which would cause the yam to rot.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛdara agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Gɔji yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ abua naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ baaha sweet potato lɛ agbo.

english: Why does my land produce less harvest if I plant maize on the exact same spot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmaa fioo kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on specific soil nutrients every season. Planting the same crop continuously drains those nutrients completely. Rotating maize with crops like beans or groundnuts helps put natural food back into the soil.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo daa be mli. Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni ayaa nɔ akwɛ̃ɔ lɛ baaha nakai niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ afite kwraa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni ekuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves burn and dry up when I put fertilizer directly touching the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer contains concentrated salts. Placing it directly against the stem burns the plant tissue and sucks water away from the roots, so it should always be buried a few inches away from the stem.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli ŋmei babaoo yɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaashã tso lɛ fãji lɛ ni ebaaŋɔ nu kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, be fɛɛ be lɛ, fuu amɛ aaafee 2-3 inch kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot during the heavy rain season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain creates high humidity that allows a fungus called Black Pod disease to grow and spread fast. Clearing farm weeds and pruning excess tree branches allows sunlight in to dry the pods and protect them.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo baa, ni no haa tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela lɛ daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Kɛ́ ajieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni afoɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa hulu la lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ebuɔ amɛhe.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects sucking the sap from under the leaves or spreading a plant virus. Spraying with organic neem oil or safe insecticides helps control these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi loo helai ni baa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ organic neem fɔ loo tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛtsɔko aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from extremely dry to very wet. Keeping soil moisture steady and providing slight shade helps the plant hold its flowers to produce tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be ni ahaa hulutsoo fioo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛwo tomato.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn light yellow when rainwater stays standing on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni nugbɔ nu hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe in the soil. When water stays logged on the field, the roots choke, stop working, and cannot pick up food, causing the leaves to turn yellow from starvation.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛkpaa nitsumɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hɔmɔ hewɔ.

english: Why do young plantain suckers wilt and dry out when I move them to a new farm in the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ tee ŋmɔ hee ko mli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Digging up a young sucker damages its root system, making it hard for the plant to draw water. Moving plants early in the morning or late evening gives the roots time to settle in cool, moist soil before facing harsh sunlight.
ga: Kɛ́ atsa tsei bibii lɛ, ebaafite amɛshishifãi lɛ. Ehaa ewaa ahaa tsei lɛ akɛ amɛaaŋɔ nu Tsei ni ajieɔ amɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛjɔɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ nɔ dani hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees are like human babies—they burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo be. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small even when the branches grow tall and leafy above ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ daraaa nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ niji lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛyɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When soil is too hard or contains too much nitrogen, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves instead of expanding its tuber roots. Loosening the soil well before planting gives the roots room to expand.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nitrogen babaoo yɛ mli lɛ. Cassava tso lɛ baafite ebe ni ekɛdu hewalɛ ŋmɔshi nibii muu fɛɛ moŋ fe ni eeedu tuber shishifãi. Kɛ́ okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwie shi jogbaŋŋ dani odu lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ ahe gbɛ lɛ mli alɛɛ.

english: Why is it necessary to put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the plant. Staking lifts the vines off the ground so leaves get maximum sunlight, which sends energy down to build big, healthy tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni efee niyenii eha tso lɛ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ tsuɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni he wa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow and curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Yellow and curling leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen nutrients or that pests like armyworms are feeding on the plant. Adding fertilizer or checking under the leaves for caterpillars can help fix the issue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔleɔ ehe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ tsei tamɔ cutworms lɛ eye tsei lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli loo okwɛ kɛji ŋmeii yɛ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni asaa naagba lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the plot where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu tsina loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmã yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally refills the nutrients that maize took out during the previous farming season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa niyenii ni ŋmãa lɛ ná yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛjɛ ŋmãa lɛ shweremɔ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms drop off without turning into fruits during very hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat dries up the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing them from fertilizing. When a flower cannot form a seed, the plant sheds it to conserve its water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ agbi. tsiɔ fɔmɔ naa Kɛ́ fɔfɔi nyɛɛɛ awo dumɔwui Tsei hoɔ yaafo koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why is it bad to save seeds from my hybrid maize harvest to plant again next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mikɛ mi-hybrid corn dumɔwui lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ afi ni baa lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred from two strong parent lines for high yield, but seeds saved from their harvest lose those special traits in the next generation, resulting in smaller yields and uneven growth.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔɔ dumɔwui enyɔ ni he wa lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Shi dumɔwui ni ahere amɛ kɛjɛ kpamɔ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi ni eyaaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves droop in the middle of the day even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In intense afternoon heat, pepper plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up from the soil. They wilt temporarily to protect themselves, usually bouncing back when the heat cools off in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaagbo yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe. Bei pii lɛ, amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do weeds harm my young crops much more during the first four weeks than later in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ awui waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ lɛ amli fe sɛɛ mli yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young crops have small roots and few leaves, so they easily lose the fight against fast-growing weeds for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Once the crop grows tall and broad, its own shade naturally prevents new weeds from growing.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii kɛ baai fioo. No hewɔ lɛ, hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni daa oya lɛ mli lɛ haaa amɛhe ajɔ amɛ oya. Beni tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛdaraa lɛ Susumɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baatsi jwɛi heei anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn into white powder and get tiny holes inside the storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ni eyɛ bu bibii lɛ? Nibii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli?

english: Tiny insects called grain weevils burrow into dry maize to lay eggs, and their young eat the grain from the inside out. Drying maize completely and storing it in sealed, airtight bags prevents these insects from destroying your harvest.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ seed moths lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa ni egbi mli koni amɛwo wɔji. ni amɛbii lɛ baaye dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛ mli kɛba kponɔgbɛ. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa kwraa ni okɛto kotokui ni akɛ vacuum tsiɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkafite onibii lɛ.

english: Why do people recommend planting plantains together with cocoa on a new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu plantains kɛ cocoa yɛ ŋmɔji heei amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under harsh sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and keeping the soil moist while the cocoa trees mature.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: How close should I plant my plantain trees to my cocoa seedlings?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi plantain dumɔwui lɛ kɛ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ abɛŋkɛ tɛŋŋ?

english: Plantains should generally be planted about 3 meters apart in between your cocoa rows. This gives the cocoa seedlings enough shade without completely blocking sunlight or competing too heavily for soil nutrients.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, esa akɛ adu plantains yɛ he ko ni jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 3 yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji ateŋ. Enɛ baaha kookoo dumɔwui lɛ aná hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛtsiŋ hulu lɛ naa loo amɛheŋ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii babaoo.

english: How long does it usually take for a plantain tree to give fruit after planting?
ga: Be enyiɛ dumɔwu ko fɔɔ yibiiwoo yɛ adumɔ sɛɛ?

english: A plantain tree generally takes about 9 to 12 months to flower, and another 3 to 4 months after flowering for the bunch to mature fully for harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantains heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi, ni nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 krokomɛi hu yɛ fɔfɔi ni ewo lɛ sɛɛ dani fɔfɔi lɛ adara kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ.

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over when the fruit bunch starts growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi beni aduawai akui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems. As the fruit bunch gets heavy, top-heavy weight or strong winds can easily pull the tree down, so propping the stem with a sturdy wooden pole helps support the weight.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsii lɛ Muji ni tsii loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala tsei kɛba shi mlɛo. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛfiɔ tsɔne lɛ muji lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How should I care for plantain suckers before I plant them in the soil?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ banana tsei lɛ anɔ dani madu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Keep the suckers in a cool, shaded area away from direct sunlight, trim off damaged roots, and plant them into moist soil as soon as possible so the roots do not dry out.
ga: Ha tsei lɛ ahi he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni hulu la shɛɛɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kpɔ̃ɔ shishifãi ni efite lɛ. Ni okɛdu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ oya bɔ ni ooonyɛ koni shishifãi lɛ akagbi.

english: How do I know when my cocoa pods are ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cocoa pods are ready when their outer shell changes color from green or deep red to a yellow or orange color, and they produce a hollow sound when gently tapped.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ tsake su kɛjɛ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛtee ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. Ni kɛ́ otswa shinaa lɛ fioo lɛ, Gbee ko ni mli ewo muji baaje kpo.

english: Why are the flowers dropping off my cocoa tree without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ cacao tsei anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off mainly due to dry weather, intense heat, lack of water, or low soil nutrients. The tree sheds its flowers to preserve energy and water during stressful conditions.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fɔfɔi shwiemɔ baa. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he yɛ shihilɛi ni haoɔ mɔ mli.

english: What should I do on my field right after completing a major cocoa harvest?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni agbe kookoo kpamɔ wulu lɛ naa lɛ?

english: After harvesting, clear away infected pods, prune dead branches, and break cocoa pods open away from tree roots to prevent fungal diseases like black pod from spreading in the soil.
ga: yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Jiemɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni egboi lɛ. ni amɛgbala kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ amli koni ŋmeii helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji akagbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What is the best time of day to plant new crop seedlings on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu tsei heei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: It is best to plant seedlings in the early morning or late afternoon when temperatures are cooler. This prevents the delicate roots from drying out and reduces transplant shock.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu dumɔwui leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ waa lɛ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbi, ni ehaa shoofeemɔ ni jɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: How do I keep government-distributed seedlings alive before transplanting them to the main field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha dumɔwui ni nɔyeli lɛ jaa lɛ ahi shi dani mikɛ amɛ aya shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ?

english: Store the seedlings together under a shady tree or thatched roof, water them every morning or late afternoon, and wait until regular seasonal rains start before planting them out in the open field.
ga: Ha dumɔwui lɛ afee ekome yɛ tso ko ni yɔɔ hulutsoo loo jwɛi tsũ ko shishi. Nu daa leebi loo shwane mli. Ni mɛ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ aje shishi dani odu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse mli.

english: Why should I cut off some branches from my healthy-looking cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tso ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ niji komɛi?

english: Even if cocoa trees look green and healthy, having too many dense leaves and branches traps shade and wastes energy. Pruning removes useless branches so the tree can put its full energy into growing fresh flowers and cocoa pods.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ cacao tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ, Shi kɛji akɛ eyɛ baai kɛ eniji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ, etsĩɔ hulutsoo naa ni efiteɔ hewalɛ.
