Niji ni afolɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ niji ni anyɛɛɛ akɛtsu nii. Enɛ ji koni tsei lɛ anyɛ amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ fɔfɔi heei kɛ kookoo ŋmɔji.

english: How often am I supposed to prune or trim my cocoa farm?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mafolɔ loo mafolɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You should prune your cocoa trees at least once every year. Regular yearly trimming opens up the trees to sunlight and fresh air, keeping them healthy and productive.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ ofolɔ o-cocoa tso lɛ shikome yɛ afi mli. Tso lɛ ni afoɔ daa afi lɛ haa tso lɛ naa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Ehaa tsei feɔ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How can I tell if the leaves on my cocoa farm have become too bushy?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji baai ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ?

english: If your farm is so dark during the daytime that sunlight cannot touch the ground, or if the leaves from nearby trees interlock into a thick roof, your trees are too bushy and need pruning.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ewo duŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli aahu akɛ hulu la nyɛŋ akpɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ahe baai lɛ ebɔ he ni efee ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli wa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ mli tse tsɔ ni ehe miihia ni afolɔ mli.

english: Why am I not seeing any improvement in my yield after applying fertilizer to my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaaa hiɛyaa ko yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo mi-kokoo tsei lɛ amli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer cannot work properly if the tree leaves are too dense and overgrown. Without sunlight reaching the tree properly, the cocoa plant cannot process the nutrients from the fertilizer to produce good fruit.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nyɛŋ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji tso lɛ baai lɛ ebɔle ehe tsɔ ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine. Kɛji hulu la shɛɛɛ tsei lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Cocoa tsei lɛ hu nyɛɛɛ atsu niyenii ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ he nii koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Should I prune my cocoa farm before or after applying fertilizer?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ dani mikɛwo mli loo beni mikɛwo mli sɛɛ?

english: You should always prune your farm before applying fertilizer. Trimming overgrown leaves and branches first ensures that the fertilizer feeds the productive parts of the tree instead of wasting nutrients on extra foliage.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli. Baai kɛ niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni aaafolɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ boteɔ tso lɛ fãi ni woɔ yibii lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni yɔɔ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: What happens if I put fertilizer on a cocoa farm that has very thick, unpruned leaves?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo kookoo ŋmɔ ko mli ni baai lɛ mli edɔ waa ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni afolɔ mli lɛ bɛ mli?

english: When you apply fertilizer under a very thick leaf canopy, you get poor results and waste money because the tree will put that energy into growing even more bushy leaves rather than pods.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo ŋmɔ lɛ shishi lɛ, baai lɛ shwieɔ shi waa. Obaaná yibii ni ehiii ni obaafite shika ejaakɛ tso lɛ kɛ nakai hewalɛ lɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛfee baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo yɛ ŋmɔtɔ najiaŋ.

english: Why does sunlight need to reach the main branches of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ hulu la lɛ ashɛ mikoo tso lɛ niji titrii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods grow directly on the main trunk and heavy branches. Sunlight reaching these parts triggers the tree to blossom and form healthy pods instead of remaining bare.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ kɛ niji ni tsii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Hulu la ni shɛɔ hei srɔtoi Enɛɛmɛi baaha tso lɛ afɔlɔ ni ewo ŋmeii ni mli wa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaashi amɛ yɛ sɛɛ

english: Will cutting off branches reduce the total amount of cocoa I harvest?
ga: Ani tsei ni akpaa lɛ baaha kookoo ni mikpaa lɛ fɛɛ aba shi?

english: No, cutting off overgrown or unproductive branches actually increases your harvest. It opens up the tree to light and air, helping the plant grow bigger and healthier cocoa pods.
ga: Dabi, niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine loo ni wooo yibii lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaha onibii lɛ aya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe amɛhaa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa, ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Can a cocoa tree grow so many leaves that it becomes a problem for the farm?
ga: Ani kookoo tsei baanyɛ akwɛ baai babaoo ni amɛkɛ naagbai aba ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, when cocoa leaves become too thick, they create too much shade and trap moisture. This turns the tree into a nuisance because it blocks sunlight and encourages diseases to spread.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ kookoo baai lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Ehaa hulutsoo be babaoo baa ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ nɔ ni haoɔ mɔ ejaakɛ etsĩɔ hulu la naa ni ewoɔ helai hewalɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do my cocoa pods rot quickly when the tree foliage is very thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikokoo ŋmɔji lɛ fiteɔ oya be mli ni tso lɛ baai lɛ egbɔjɔ waa lɛ?

english: Very thick foliage traps damp, heavy air inside the tree crown. This wet environment helps diseases like black pod rot thrive and spread across your pods quickly.
ga: Baai ni mli tse waa lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsii yɛ tso lɛ shishi. Nɛkɛ shihilɛ ni mli efɔ nɛɛ haa helai tamɔ black pod rot lɛ daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa pod lɛ mli fɛɛ oya.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when I clear all the big trees away from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect them from direct sunlight and high heat. Without shade trees or temporary food crops like plantains to cover them, intense sun scorches their delicate leaves and dries out the soil, killing the young seedlings.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo loo niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ bɛ Hulu la ni naa wa baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei bibii lɛ agbele.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants showing ragged holes and looking like they were chewed by small worms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn plants lɛ baai lɛ yɛ bu ni etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmeii bibii eye amɛ lɛ?

english: This leaf damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworms. They crawl into the center (whorl) of the maize plant during the day to feed on fresh leaves, leaving ragged holes and sawdust-like waste behind.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛfoɔ amɛhe kɛboteɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ (ring) lɛ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye baai heei lɛ. Eshiɔ buji ni ekpɔtɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ esɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when the heavy rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: When soil stays waterlogged or poorly drained during heavy rains, oxygen cannot reach the cassava roots. This suffocates the roots and creates room for harmful soil fungi and bacteria to cause root rot. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps water drain away safely.
ga: Beni nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa gbɛ kɛhaa sũ mli ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni kɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: How can I tell if my soil is weak and needs fertilizer before I plant my crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ehe miihia ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli dani madu?

english: Weak soil often shows signs from previous harvests: crops grow slowly, leaves turn pale green or yellow instead of deep green, and yields are small. Testing the soil or adding well-rotted animal manure before planting helps restore essential nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ jieɔ okadii ni jɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ kpo: tsei lɛ daa blɛoo, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. ni nibii fioo pɛ anáa Shikpɔŋ lɛ kaa loo kooloi aŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfataa he dani aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Can I plant cowpeas or beans together on the same piece of land with my maize?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ ŋmãa?

english: Yes, planting beans or cowpeas with maize is very beneficial. Legumes take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil to nourish the maize, while tall maize stalks provide natural support for climbing bean vines.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Legumes lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli yelikɛbuamɔ kɛha ŋmãa tsei ni akwɔɔ lɛ.

english: If I plant my crop seeds very close to each other, will I get a bigger harvest?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani maná yibii babaoo?

english: No, planting too close together causes plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks and very small fruits. Giving each plant proper spacing ensures it gets enough food to produce a healthy harvest.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai bibii waa baa. He ni sa ni akɛhaa tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ haa enáa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmaa kpakpa.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants without forming any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeee pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant is under stress, which can be caused by dry soil, high temperatures, pest attacks, or lack of soil nutrients. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing balanced nutrients stops flower drop.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ yɛ haomɔ mli. This can be caused by dry soil, high temperatures, and pest attacks. aloo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa ni niyenii ni sa haa lɛ, ebaaha fɔfɔi lɛ akpa shwiemɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow back much faster than my crops even after I clear and weed the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? Beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mijie jwɛi lɛ po sɛɛ.

english: Weed seeds are extremely tough and can sleep in the soil for years. When you clear the land, sunlight and water reach these hidden seeds, causing them to germinate instantly and grow faster than planted crops.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa waa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo. Kɛji otsi jɛmɛ lɛ Hulu la kɛ nu shɛɔ nɛkɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ ahe. Enɛ haa dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛdaraa oya fe tsei ni aduɔ.

english: How do I prevent insects from eating and destroying my harvested maize while it is stored in the barn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkaye ni amɛfite mi-ŋmãa lɛ be mli ni mikɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Insects like weevils thrive when maize is stored with moisture. You must dry your maize thoroughly in the sun until the grains are hard, treat them with safe grain protectant powder, and store them in airtight bags or clean, sealed containers.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa wo mli ni edɔ. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmãa lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ dumɔwui ahebuu powda ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ atsu he nii. ni okɛto kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo nɔ ko ni he tse ni atsĩ naa mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upwards and turning yellow during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is commonly caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies, which multiply quickly in warm, dry weather. Controlling whiteflies early with soapy water or approved sprays helps protect the tomato leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Amɛshwereɔ oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni jɛmɛ egbi lɛ amli. Whitefly Kudɔmɔ Mra Kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛ samla loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, obaanyɛ obu o-tomato baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I leave large trees on my farm instead of cutting them all down when clearing land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi tsei wuji yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mafo amɛ fɛɛ beni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ miitsu nii lɛ?

english: Large trees protect your crops from strong winds and harsh sunlight, keep the soil cool and moist, and drop leaves that decompose into natural fertilizer for your crops.
ga: Tsei ni eda lɛ buɔ onibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. ni ehaa baai ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha onibii.

english: Will planting shade trees on my farm steal water and plant food away from my food crops?
ga: Ani tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaju nu ni ebaadu niyenii kɛjɛ mi niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe?

english: Most big trees have deep roots that fetch water and nutrients from far underground, deeper than your crops' roots reach. They actually bring those nutrients up to the surface when their leaves drop and decay on the soil.
ga: Tsei wuji lɛ ateŋ babaoo yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔlɔ ni gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Enɛ mli kwɔ fe bɔ ni otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Amɛkɛ nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ baai gbee shi ni amɛfite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do trees on and around my farm help make sure my crops get enough rainfall?
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ mli kɛ ehewɔ lɛ Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ana nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: Trees release water vapor from their leaves into the air, which cools the local climate and helps clouds form rain. Having trees nearby creates a cooler environment that holds moisture in the air and soil longer.
ga: Tsei jieɔ nu lasu kɛjɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa jɛmɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa atatui ni amɛfeɔ nugbɔ Tsei ni yɔɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why does my soil dry out so fast a few days after rain, and how can I keep it moist longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nu be babaoo?

english: Bare soil loses water quickly to direct sunlight and heat. Leaving tree leaves, grass, or crop residues on the soil surface acts as a cover that shields the soil from the sun and slows down water evaporation.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya kɛji akɛ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ shɛ enɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Baai, jwɛi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛbu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulutsoo he ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo.

english: Why do heavy rains wash away the good topsoil on my sloping land, and how do I prevent it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ miiho sũ kpakpa ni yɔɔ mi gɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu he?

english: Heavy rain drops hit bare soil with force and carry away the rich top layer. The roots of trees and cover crops hold the soil in place like a net, while tree leaves break the fall of heavy rain drops.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tswaa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ lɛ nɔ kɛ hewalɛ ni efoɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ashishifãi kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi tamɔ ŋtayaa. yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fiteɔ tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ.

english: Why do leaves that fall from trees onto my farm floor make my soil richer over time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛbaa miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nii babaoo yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ?

english: Fallen leaves are full of nutrients that the tree drew from the ground. As earthworms and soil insects break down these leaves, they turn into dark humus, which is natural plant food for your crops.
ga: Niyenii nibii ni tsei gbalaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ eyi baai ni egbee shi lɛ amli obɔ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kpata nɛkɛ baai nɛɛ ahiɛ lɛ, Amɛtsɔɔ humus ni tsuɔ waa, ni ji adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Is it better for my soil to clear my bush by burning it or by clearing it manually with a group?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ baafolɔ jwɛi lɛ kɛtsɔ shãa nɔ loo mikɛ miniji baafolɔ amɛ babaoo?

english: Burning destroys the good organic matter and beneficial insects in the soil. Clearing manually keeps the grass and leaves on the ground to rot into rich compost, making your soil stronger for future seasons.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii kpakpai ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Ni akɛ niji shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha jwɛi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ agbo ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa. Enɛ haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛha wɔsɛɛ bei.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and yellow during the sunny dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive and get sunburned when exposed to direct heat. They need temporary shade from plantain plants or shade trees to stay cool until their leaves grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ he waa ni hulu lɛ shãa amɛ kɛ́ amɛshɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛjɛ dumɔwui loo hulutsoo tsei amli koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi baai lɛ amli baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhe hulu la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do aggressive weeds grow so much faster in open areas of my field than under tree shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ gbeyei waa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli hei ni yɔɔ faŋŋ lɛ fe tsei ashishi lɛ?

english: Most troublesome weeds need full direct sunlight to germinate and grow rapidly. Tree shade blocks that light, naturally slowing down weed growth and saving you labor on weeding.
ga: Jwɛi ni yɔɔ naagba lɛ ateŋ babaoo he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛdara oya. Tsei lɛ ahe hulutsoo lɛ tsi kane lɛ naa. Ehaa jwɛi lɛ adalɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni ekɛ be ni okɛjieɔ jwɛi lɛ baa shi

english: How do I know if the first rainfall of the season is enough for me to start planting my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ?

english: Do not plant after just one early rain because a dry spell might follow and scorch the seeds. Dig a small hole into the soil; if the ground is moist down to the depth of your hand, the soil is ready for planting.
ga: Kaadu yɛ nugbɔ kome pɛ ni nɛ mra lɛ sɛɛ. Hɔmɔ baanyɛ anyiɛ sɛɛ ni eshã dumɔwui lɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ bu bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛyashɛ onine mli. Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ eshɛ he kɛha dumɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil, which plants need to grow green and leafy, or that too much water around the roots is preventing the plant from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛfee baai. Aloo nu babaoo ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ haaa tso lɛ aná niyenii kpakpai.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my young tomato plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle mi tomato tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops water from evaporating quickly in the sun, keeps the roots cool, prevents weeds from growing, and stops heavy rain from washing away soil nutrients.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ la oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ enɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants twisting and curling upwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from young leaves, or by a virus spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ

english: Why do insects attack my cowpea flowers as soon as they open?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛfɔ̃ pɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers produce sweet nectar and soft petals that attract pests like thrips and pod borers. Protecting the crop early before flowering prevents these insects from damaging the flowers and reducing your yield.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ jieɔ nu kɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni gbalaa kooloi tamɔ thrips kɛ pod borers. Nibii ni abuɔ he mra dani fɔfɔii baa lɛ tsiɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkafite fɔfɔii ni ehaa onibii ni onáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do I need to cut away some of the small shoots growing around my plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Ajieɔ Mi plantain tsei lɛ.

english: Removing extra shoots leaves only one main stem and one small follower shoot, so the plant doesn't waste water and nutrients on too many stems, resulting in larger plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, tso lɛ shishifã titri kome kɛ afã kome pɛ shwɛɔ, no hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ efiteee nu kɛ niyenii babaoo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, plantains lɛ baaná jwɛi wuji.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Staking gets yam leaves up into the sunlight so they can produce more food for the tubers underground, while keeping the leaves off the damp wet ground where fungal diseases spread.
ga: Staking haa hulu la shɛɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni niyenii babaoo aba aha ŋmeii lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants falling off before producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when the soil dries out suddenly during flowering, or when the plant lacks sufficient plant food like calcium and nitrogen.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ trukaa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ tsei amli niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa tamɔ calcium kɛ nitrogen.

english: How can I tell that my cassava is mature and ready to harvest under the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, growth slows down, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack as the tubers expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. slow growth Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings struggle to survive when planted in direct, open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛhi shi kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to intense heat and wind; planting them under shade crops like plantains protects them from harsh sun and keeps humidity high around the young leaves.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ latsaa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he waa. Tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he, ni ebaaha hulutsoo ni fa babaoo ahi baai bibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my garden crops wither when I give them water during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibɔɔ mli tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Watering under strong sun causes water to evaporate rapidly before reaching the roots, and hot water drops on leaves can scorch the tender foliage. It is best to water early in the morning or late in the evening.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya dani eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ni nu ni mli edɔ ni shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha baai bibii lɛ ashã. Esa akɛ afɔ lɛ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ.

english: How long does a new cocoa tree take from the day I plant it until it starts bearing fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso hee ko kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ be mli ni adu lɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ebɔi yibiiwoo?

english: Hybrid cocoa varieties commonly planted in Ghana begin producing pods within 2 to 3 years after planting, whereas older traditional cocoa trees usually take 4 to 5 years.
ga: Kookoo henɔi ni akɛfee ekome ni afɔɔ dumɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli beni adu lɛ sɛɛ, yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, blema kookoo tsei ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need shade plants like plantains around them when they are small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he hiaa ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ, tamɔ plantains lɛ abɔle amɛhe beni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and delicate roots that easily dry out or burn under direct sunlight. Tall shade plants act like natural umbrellas, protecting the young trees from extreme heat and retaining soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ, egbiɔ loo eshãa oya. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Buu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why do my crop leaves dry up and shed off during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During Harmattan, dry air and low humidity cause plants to lose water rapidly. Many crops drop some of their leaves naturally to reduce water loss and survive until the rainy season returns.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan beaŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ hulutsoo be ni baa shi lɛ haa tsei lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Nibii babaoo ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ekomɛi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛhi shi kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my maize plants produce smaller cobs if I plant them late in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo kɛji midu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Maize needs steady moisture while flowering and forming cobs. Late planting means rains may stop mid-way through growth, leaving the plants without enough water to fully fill out the cobs.
ga: Abɛi he miihia ŋmɔtɔ daa be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ cob feemɔ. Dumɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nugbɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpa yɛ teŋgbɛ koni eha tsei lɛ adara. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛwoɔ ŋmei lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes crop leaves to turn pale green or yellow even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni haa tso baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po?

english: Yellow or pale leaves often mean the plant is lacking nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for leaves to grow green and healthy. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer usually solves this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hia yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: How do I know if my soil is rich enough to grow leafy vegetables and food crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ baai kɛ niyenii?

english: Good soil is typically dark in color, crumbles easily in your hands, holds moisture without staying waterlogged, and contains earthworms or decaying plant matter.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ mli ni nu shwieee mli. ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo tsei ni fiteɔ lɛ ahe nibii ni eshwɛ yɛ jɛmɛ

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, cool, and poorly ventilated environments when rainfall is heavy and tree canopies are overly dense.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ, fɛ̃i yɔɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ miinɛ waa ni tsei ashishifãi lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ lɛ.

english: Why do insects attack my pepper and vegetable plants more during the dry season than in the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi babaoo tutuaa mi-pepper tsei kɛ aduawai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: In dry weather, many insects look for plant sap as a source of water, while warmer temperatures also allow pest populations to multiply faster.
ga: yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli lɛ Kooloi bibii babaoo kwɛɔ tsei amli nu lɛ akɛ nu jɛɛhe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dɔlɛ ni mli edɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ babaoo oya.

english: Why is it important to leave proper space between my plants instead of putting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maná gbɛ ni sa yɛ mitsei lɛ ateŋ, moŋ fe ni makɛ amɛ ama amɛhe lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures each crop gets enough sunlight, soil nutrients, and airflow without competing with surrounding plants, leading to healthier growth and better yields.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa ni hoɔ ni ekɛ tsei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ yeee akaŋ Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do vegetable seeds like pepper grow better when I start them in a small nursery bed before moving them to the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma dumɔwui tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mije shishi yɛ dumɔwui bibii amli lɛ? dani amɛfã kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli

english: Seedlings are very delicate. Nursing them in a small, controlled area lets you easily shelter them from strong rain and pests so that only healthy, strong plants are transplanted into the main field.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ahe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Amɛtsɔsemɔ yɛ he bibioo ko He ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa onyɛɔ obuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe oya. Koni akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ awo ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to dry my corn after harvesting it from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni magbi mi-ŋmãa lɛ beni mikpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested corn contains a lot of natural water. Drying removes this excess water so the corn will not rot, grow mold, or attract destructive pests during storage.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli nu babaoo yɛ ŋmãa ni akpa ehee lɛ mli. Kɛ́ egbi lɛ, ejieɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ. koni ŋmãa lɛ akafite ni ekɛ ŋmeii aba loo egbala ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ kɛba be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know if my harvested corn still has too much water inside it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ yɛ nu babaoo yɛ mli lolo?

english: If corn grains feel soft when you press them with your thumbnail, dent easily, or feel heavy and damp, they still contain a high amount of water (around 25 percent or more) and require further drying.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo beni okɛ oshishifa lɛ nyɛɔ nɔ lɛ, efoɔ oya, loo enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ tsii ni edɔ. Nu babaoo yɛ ŋmãa mli lolo (aaafee oha mlijaa 25 loo nɔ ni fe nakai) ni esa akɛ eya nɔ egbi.

english: What happens if I store my corn in bags immediately without drying it properly?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa wo kotoku mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni migbiko lɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Storing wet corn traps heat and moisture inside the sacks, which quickly creates mold, rots the grains, and can ruin your entire harvest within a few days.
ga: Abɛi ni efɔ ni akɛtoɔ lɛ baamɔmɔ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i yɛ kotoku lɛ mli. ni haa ŋmeii feɔ ŋmãa ni egbo oya Ni ebaanyɛ efite oŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli.

english: What is the right moisture level I should aim for when drying my corn?
ga: Mɛni ji hulutsoo be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ makwɛ nɔ kɛ́ miigbi ŋmãa?

english: You should dry your corn until the water content drops from high levels (around 25 percent) down to about 18 percent or lower, which is the safe level for storage and selling.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmãa lɛ agbi kɛyashi nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baa shi kɛjɛ he ni nɔ kwɔ (aaafee oha mlijaa 25) kɛyashɛ aaafee oha mlijaa 18 loo nɔ ni shɛɛɛ nakai. Enɛ ji he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha nitoo kɛ mlijaa.

english: How does sun-drying actually help lower the water content inside corn grains?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ hulu ni tsoɔ lɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ baa shi?

english: The heat from the sun warms the outside of the corn grains, which draws out the trapped moisture inside the kernels and causes it to evaporate into the air.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ kponɔgbɛ dɔɔ. Enɛ gbalaa nu ni emɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ehaa efoɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Why does a bag of fresh corn weigh more than a bag of dry corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ kotoku kome tsiimɔ fe ŋmãa kotoku ni egbi lɛ?

english: Fresh corn carries a lot of water weight inside each kernel. As you dry the corn, that water leaves the grain, making the final dried crop lighter but much safer to store.
ga: Abɛi hee mli ŋmei lɛ eko fɛɛ eko yɛ nu babaoo ni tsiimɔ yɔɔ mli. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa lɛ Nu baajɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ naagbee gbimɔ lɛ feɔ mlɛo shi eyɛ shweshweeshwe kwraa akɛ akɛtoɔ.

english: What is the best way to spread my corn under the sun so the moisture leaves evenly?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbɛɔ ŋmãa ashwaa hulu lɛ shishi koni ajie ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: Spread your corn in a thin layer on a clean tarpaulin or drying floor in direct sunlight, and turn the grains regularly so every side gets equal heat to release its water.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibioo ko awo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ tarp loo shikpɔŋ ni he tse nɔ koni egbi yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Ni otsake ŋmãa lɛ daa bɔni afee ni fãi lɛ fɛɛ aná dɔlɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛho.

english: Will buyers at the market pay less for my corn if it still has high water content?
ga: Ani mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ baawo mi ŋmãa lɛ he nyɔmɔ fioo kɛji akɛ nu babaoo yɛ mli lolo?

english: Yes, traders and millers pay less for wet corn because it spoils quickly during transport and causes problems during grinding, whereas properly dried corn fetches a higher price.
ga: Hɛɛ, jarayelɔi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsulɔi baawo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efɔ lɛ nyɔmɔ fioo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmãa fiteɔ oya kɛ́ akɛmiiya, ni ekɛ naagbai baa kɛ́ ashɛreɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ biɔ ni awo lɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ.

english: Why is it difficult to grind corn into flour if the water content is still high?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ aaatsɔ ŋmãa nɔ afee ashikishaŋ kɛji nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fa lolo lɛ?

english: When corn has too much water inside, milling machines crush the wet kernels into a thick paste instead of grinding them into fine, dry flour.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ yɛ nu babaoo lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa ni efɔ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa efeɔ ŋmãa ni mli edɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsɔ mli ni etsɔ powda kpakpa ni egbi lɛ.

english: How many days does it usually take to bring the water content of corn down to a safe level?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, gbii enyiɛ eheɔ dani nu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ baa shi kɛyashɛɔ he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe?

english: Under strong, hot sunshine, it typically takes several days of continuous drying to lower the moisture from around 25 percent down to 18 percent or less, depending on how hot the weather is.
ga: Yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ gbii babaoo ni akɛgbiɔ be fɛɛ be koni hulutsoo be lɛ aba shi kɛjɛ aaafee oha mlijaa 25 kɛyashɛ oha mlijaa 18 loo nɔ ni shɛɛɛ nakai. Eda bɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli dɔɔ ha lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves when water is scarce to prevent moisture loss through the leaves, allowing the plant to survive in the ground until the rains return.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu faaa koni ŋmɔtɔ akatsɔ baai lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tsei hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop without fruiting when the weather becomes too hot or when the plant experiences sudden dry spells without regular watering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Aloo kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ egbi trukaa ni awooo amɛ nu daa.

english: How does planting plantains or banana trees next to my young cocoa help them grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ banana dumɔwui loo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ mi kokoo tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sunlight; the large leaves of plantains act as natural umbrellas, keeping the air cool and moist around the cocoa.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain baai agboi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ni ehaa kokoo lɛ mli jɔ ni edɔ

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a vital nutrient in the soil that plants need to grow strong and green, or that the soil is holding too much water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee eŋɔli. loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo tsɔ

english: Why do my bean crops make the soil better for other crops I plant afterward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tso lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha tsei krokomɛi ni miduɔ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Beans and other legumes naturally take nitrogen from the air and trap it in their roots, leaving free fertilizer in the dirt for the next crop you plant.
ga: Beans kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: How do I know if my farmland soil is rich enough for planting vegetables?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli tse bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu aduawai?

english: Good soil is usually dark in color, crumbles easily in your hands, holds moisture without staying flooded, and supports healthy, fast-growing weeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Ha ŋmɔtɔ akashɛ nu afua he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa jwɛi lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni amɛdaraa oya

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and stopping the plant from growing taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves, feeding on the plant's juices and passing along plant sicknesses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Enuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni egbɛɔ tso helai eshwaa.

english: What causes my yam tubers to rot under the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpaa?

english: Yam tubers rot when rain water sits in the soil without draining away properly, creating wet conditions where tiny fungal pests can easily attack the tuber.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ baa ni ŋmeii bibii ni baanyɛ atutua ŋmeii lɛ oya.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster on my farm than the crops I actually planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally stronger at grabbing water, light, and soil nutrients than domesticated farm crops, so they grow fast if not cleared early.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shia lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi lɛ daa oya kɛji akɛ ajieee amɛ oya.

english: Why do my maize plants fall over so easily when a strong rain or wind comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ loo kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa lɛ?

english: Maize falls over easily when its roots are too shallow, which happens if the seeds were planted too close to the surface or if the ground was too hard for the roots to push deep down.
ga: Abɛi gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ tsɔ. Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛhe kɛya shɔŋŋ.

english: Why is it better for me to plant my maize seeds in straight lines instead of scattering them randomly across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ trukaa lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines makes it much easier to walk through your field to clear weeds, apply fertilizer, and harvest. It also ensures each plant gets adequate air flow and sunlight to grow properly.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ aaatsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛha jwɛi shwiemɔ, ŋmɔ mli nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ. Ekwɛɔ koni tso fɛɛ tso aná kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I easily make sure my planting rows stay completely straight across my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana nɔmimaa akɛ midumɔ ŋtayaai lɛ ja yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: You can stretch a tight rope or string between two wooden pegs driven into the ground at opposite ends of your plot, then plant your seeds directly along the line of the rope.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ kpã loo kpãa atsɔ tsei enyɔ ni akɛwo shikpɔŋ yɛ saatso lɛ fãi ni kɛ amɛhe kpaa gbee lɛ ateŋ. Kɛkɛ lɛ, aduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ kpãa lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Does planting my crops in organized rows actually give me a bigger harvest?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ haa miwoɔ yibii babaoo diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, because straight rows allow you to fit the ideal number of plants on your land without overcrowding them. Each plant gets maximum sunlight and nutrients, resulting in larger, healthier cobs.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni ja lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ tsei ayibɔ ni sa woɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni okɛ ohe wooo mli fe nine. Tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la kɛ niyenii kpakpai babaoo. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ feɔ ŋmei ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What will happen to my corn plants if I place the seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown plants fight each other for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. This makes the stalks grow thin and weak, leading to very small corn cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ, ni no haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmãa lɛ ji bibioo kwraa.

english: Why is it important that the distance between every single corn plant is the same?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ŋmãa tsei fɛɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ afee ekome lɛ?

english: Equal spacing ensures every individual plant receives an equal share of water, nutrients, and sunlight. This allows all the plants across your farm to grow at the same speed and mature together.
ga: Gbɛ ni kã tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ haa tsei lɛ fɛɛ naa nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ ekome kɛdaraa.

english: Why do corn plants grow stronger stalks when they are given enough space around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ shwereɔ waa yɛ be mli ni he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: When given enough space, corn roots can spread wide into the soil to absorb nutrients, and sunlight can reach the lower leaves. This creates thick, strong stalks that resist falling over in wind or rain.
ga: Beni gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ Abɛi shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Ni hulu la baanyɛ ashɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe. Ehaa tso lɛ mli tseɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ shigbeemɔ.

english: How do I measure the right distance between seeds if I don't have a measuring tape on the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masusu gbɛ ni sa ni kã dumɔwui ateŋ lɛ he? Kɛji akɛ tɛp ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: You can cut a wooden stick to the recommended spacing length or tie knots at fixed intervals along your planting rope to quickly check the distance between each seed.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofo tsei lɛ amli kɛyashɛ he ni atsɔɔ akɛ amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ nɔ loo okɛ ŋmeii akpɛtɛ he yɛ be pɔtɛɛ ko mli yɛ dumɔwui kpãa lɛ he koni okwɛ bɔ ni dumɔwui aŋkroaŋkroi lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ oya.

english: How does keeping equal spaces between plants help me control weeds on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ gbɛ ni kã tsei ateŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaye abua mi ni makwɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Well-spaced plants leave clear, open pathways between rows, making it easy for you to spot weeds early and remove them with a hoe without accidentally damaging your crop roots.
ga: Tsei ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ tsɔɔ tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa bo akɛ obaana jwɛi mra. Ni okɛ ŋmei ajie jwɛi lɛ ni ofiteee tso lɛ shishifãi yɛ oshara mli.

english: Can proper spacing between my plants save me money when applying fertilizer?
ga: Ani Tsei Ahe Gbɛjianɔtoo ni Sa Baanyɛ Akɛ Shika Ahe Shika ni Akɛbaatsu Nii?

english: Yes, because when your crops are neatly spaced, you can place fertilizer precisely at the base of each plant rather than spreading it across empty ground or feeding unwanted weeds.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ be mli ni otsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe ebɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo tso fɛɛ tso shishi pɛpɛɛpɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooogbɛ eshwa he ko ni nɔ ko bɛ nɔ loo oooha jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ niyenii.

english: How does well-spaced row planting make harvesting easier for me?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ haa ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kɛhaa mi?

english: Clear pathways allow you to walk freely through the field with baskets or sacks, picking mature cobs easily without knocking down or stepping on neighboring crops.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni mli tse lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ tsɛnsi loo kotoku nyiɛɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli oya. Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmeii ni eda lɛ oya ni okɛ ohe akatswaaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anɔ loo okɛ onaji akatswaaa amɛnɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable crops need so much water every single day during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa mi-vegetables lɛ daa gbi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Vegetables are made mostly of water and lose moisture through their leaves to cool down in hot weather. During the dry season, intense heat causes fast evaporation, so regular watering keeps the plants from drying out and dying.
ga: Akɛ nu feɔ aduawai babaoo ni amɛshwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛhe ajɔɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa hulutsoo be lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni oooha tso lɛ daa lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ akagbi ni egbo.

english: How can I tell if my maize crop is getting too much water or not enough water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-abele lɛ miiná nu babaoo loo eshɛɛɛ he?

english: When maize gets too much water, the leaves turn yellow and look limp because the roots are drowning. When it does not get enough water, the leaves roll up tightly like straws to protect themselves from losing moisture.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa ná nu babaoo lɛ Baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaafee tamɔ mɛi ni egbɔjɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ miiho nu. Beni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Akɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi koni ŋmɔtɔ akaje mli.

english: Why do some of my pawpaw trees produce plenty of flowers but never grow any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mipapaya tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewooo yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Pawpaw trees can be male, female, or mixed. Male pawpaw trees only produce pollen and cannot grow fruit, while female and mixed trees grow the actual pawpaw fruit after receiving pollen.
ga: Pawpaw tsei baanyɛ afee nuu, yoo, loo tsei ni akɛfee ekome. Papaya tsei hii woɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei yei kɛ tsei ni afee amɛ ekome lɛ baawo papaya yibii diɛŋtsɛ beni amɛná pollen sɛɛ.

english: Do crops like watermelons have male and female flowers on the same vine?
ga: Ani tsei tamɔ watermelon yɛ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei yɛ wain tso kome nɔ?

english: Yes, watermelon vines produce separate male and female flowers on the same plant. Bees must carry pollen from the male flower to the female flower, which has a tiny fruit shape at its base, for fruit to grow.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, watermelon wain tsei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi yɛ tso kome nɔ. Esa akɛ wuobii awo pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi hii lɛ amli kɛya fɔfɔi yei lɛ anɔ, ni amɛhe yɔɔ tamɔ aduawai bibii yɛ amɛshishigbɛ, bɔni afee ni aduawai lɛ adara.

english: Why do my pepper leaves wilt in the afternoon sun but look fresh again in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli shi amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa kɛ hejɔɔmɔ leebi lɛ?

english: In the hot afternoon sun, pepper plants lose water faster through their leaves than the roots can drink from the soil. Wilting is the plant's way of resting to save water, and it recovers overnight when the air cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ Pepper tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Withering ji gbɛ ni tso tsɔɔ nɔ ejɔɔ ehe koni ekɛbu nu he. ni ebaahe ejɔ ehe nyɔɔŋ kome mli be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young tomato plants bend towards one direction instead of growing straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso bibioo lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants naturally bend toward the direction of sunlight because light helps them make food. If one side of the plant gets more sun, it will grow toward that light source.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛkoto amɛhe yɛ he ni hulu la lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ ejaakɛ la yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. Kɛji tso lɛ fã kome ná hulu la babaoo lɛ, Tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ kɛya nakai la jɛɛhe lɛ he.

english: How can I tell the difference between improved hybrid cassava stems and traditional local stems when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛ blema maŋbii tsei lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Improved cassava stems often have closer leaf nodes along the stem and grow thicker faster. Although they look similar as young plants, improved varieties mature earlier and give much higher root yields than local ones.
ga: Cassava tsei ni atsake lɛ fɔɔ baa ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe yɛ tso lɛ he ni ebaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ oya. Eyɛ mli akɛ amɛtamɔ tsei bibii moŋ, shi tsei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ lɛ shwereɔ oya ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi ni fa babaoo fe tsei srɔtoi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: Why do different varieties of maize take different amounts of time to mature in the same soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔi srɔtoi heɔ be srɔtoi dani amɛdaraa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Different maize varieties are bred with different internal clocks. Early-maturing varieties complete their growth quickly to beat short rains, while late-maturing varieties grow larger and take longer to produce grain.
ga: Abele henɔi srɔtoi Akɛ mligbɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai srɔtoi fɔ̃ɔ amɛ. Henɔi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ daa oya koni amɛye nugbɔshiimɔi kukuji anɔ kunim. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni shwereɔ sɛɛ mli lɛ daraa ni amɛheɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ dumɔwui.

english: Can I plant cassava and cowpea together on the same piece of land without them damaging each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mifiteee amɛhe?

english: Yes, mixing cassava and cowpea works well because cowpeas cover the soil to prevent weeds and trap nitrogen from the air to feed the soil, which helps the cassava grow stronger.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei ni akɛfutu mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmei lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni jwɛi akabote mli, ni emɔɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmei lɛ daa waa.

english: How do I know when groundnuts growing under the soil are fully ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni ŋmeii ni akwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ efee klalo kwraa kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Groundnuts are ready when the outer leaves turn yellow and start falling off. You can pull up one plant to test: if the inside of the pods has dark brown spots instead of white, the crop is ready.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii efee klalo kɛ́ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbɔi shwiemɔ. Obaanyɛ ogbala tso lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi koni oka lɛ okwɛ. Kɛji akɛ pod lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ najiaŋ. Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ.

english: Why are my crops producing smaller yields when I plant them very close together on my small plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ bibioo lɛ nɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which prevents individual plants from growing big and healthy.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa tsei aŋkroaŋkroi adara ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster and stronger than the crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants that are naturally better at quickly grabbing water, sunlight, and nutrients from the soil, which allows them to outgrow farm crops if they are not cleared early.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni jieɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa oya fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ ajieee amɛ mra.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and stay small even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efeɔ bibii eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen; water alone is not enough for crops to grow green and strong if the soil nutrients have been exhausted.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu pɛ faaa kɛha tsei ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ kɛji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa.

english: Why do some of my plants grow lots of big green leaves but produce very little fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ ekomɛi yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi aduawai fioo pɛ amɛwoɔ lɛ?

english: Having too much nitrogen in the soil makes plants focus all their energy on growing green leaves instead of developing flowers and fruit.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is healthy enough to support a good crop yield?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, crumbles easily in your hands, holds moisture well after rain, and contains living organisms like earthworms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yɛ

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and small even after staying in the ground for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ bibii yɛ be mli ni mikɛ amɛ ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots cannot expand if the ground is too hard and compact, or if the soil lacks proper nutrients and moisture needed for underground root swelling.
ga: Kasava shishifãi nyɛŋ alɛɛ mli kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa ni he hiaa kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: What causes my tomato plants to drop their flowers before any fruit develops?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwoɔ yibii?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extremely hot weather, lack of steady soil water, or damage from tiny insect pests.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni bɛ daa lɛ he. aloo kooloi bibii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ efite

english: Why is it bad for my crops if I plant the exact same crop on the same piece of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows specific crop pests and diseases to build up in the ground.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops dry up quickly during short dry spells while my neighbor's crops stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be kuku lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni okutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔshinii kã he efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Soil mixed with organic matter like compost or animal manure acts like a sponge, holding onto water much longer to keep crops hydrated during dry periods.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii efutu mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji Ehiɛɔ nu mli be babaoo koni eha tsei lɛ aná nu yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ.

english: How does cutting down all the big trees on my farm affect how my crops grow?
ga: Te tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Removing all trees exposes the soil directly to harsh sunlight and heavy rains, which dries out the soil quickly and washes away the rich topsoil your crops need.
ga: Tsei fɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya ni efoɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ ni jara wa ni he hiaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant regain its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my cassava stems very close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are set too close together, their underground roots fight each other for food and water, and their leaves block sunlight. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to build big, heavy tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. ni ebaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee bulbs agboi ni tsii.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or attacks from tiny insects. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the plant hold onto its flowers until fruit forms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be loo kooloi bibii ni tutuaa lɛ Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashi yibii lɛ baawo.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops when they are just growing next to them?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui kɛ́ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ amɛmasɛi tuuntu?

english: Weeds steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight that your crops need to thrive. They also serve as hidden homes for dangerous pests and diseases that easily spread to your main crops.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa koni onibii akwɛ̃ lɛ. Amɛtsuɔ nii hu akɛ shiai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ kɛha kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara kɛ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa onibii titrii lɛ anɔ oya lɛ.

english: Why should I not plant pepper on the exact same land where I just harvested tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa mi-tomato lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Pepper and tomatoes belong to the same plant family and share the same soil pests and sicknesses. Planting pepper in the same spot allows leftover diseases in the soil to attack your new crop immediately.
ga: Pepper kɛ tomato yɛ tso weku kome mli ni amɛ fɛɛ amɛyɔɔ sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai kome. Kɛ́ odu ŋmɔtɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha helai fɛɛ ni eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ atutua oŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do some farmers spread dry grass around the base of their crop stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi shwieɔ jwɛi ni egbi amɛshwãa tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, called mulching, acts like a blanket. It stops the hot sun from drying out the soil water, keeps the roots cool, and prevents unwanted weeds from sprouting.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ haaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why are my yam vines growing very long and thin under tall trees without making big yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ daa waa ni efeɔ mlɛo yɛ tsei kakadaji ashishi ni ekɛ sweet potato agbo baaa lɛ?

english: Yam plants rely on direct sunlight to make food for tuber growth. When shaded by tall trees, the vine wastes all its energy stretching high up to search for light instead of expanding the tuber underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ hulu la nɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha amɛ tuber lɛ dalɛ. Beni eyɔɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko shishi Wein tso lɛ fiteɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni eshɛɔ ŋwɛi koni etao la. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ ŋmeii lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: Why do I need to cut off the extra small shoots growing at the base of my plantain suckers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Nɔ krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantain tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ.

english: Extra shoots drain water and food away from the main plant. Removing them ensures all the nutrients go directly to the main plantain tree so it can produce a large bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ amɛ lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ yaa plantain wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. koni enyɛ efee kuu agbo ko.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable crops in the hot afternoon or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo aduawai anɔ nu yɛ shwane mli loo leebi?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the cool soil absorbs the water before the sun can dry it up. Afternoon watering causes water to evaporate quickly and can damage heat-stressed leaves.
ga: Nu ni ashwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ lɛ baaŋɔ nu dani hulu lɛ agbi. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli shwane mli lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya, ni ebaanyɛ efite tsei ahe tsei ni hulutsoo lɛ haa amɛnáa he sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do small insects always gather under the leaves of my crops instead of on top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, kooloi bibii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ashishi moŋ fe nɔ ni amɛbaabua amɛhe naa lɛ?

english: Insects hide underneath leaves to protect themselves from hot sunlight, heavy rainfall, and hungry birds. The underside of a leaf is also softer, making it easier for pests to bite and feed on plant juices.
ga: Kplukai kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai ashishi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ okpoi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ ahe. Baa lɛ shishi hu yɛ blɛoo. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akɛ amɛaakɔmɔ ni amɛnu tso mli nu.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or adding well-rotted animal manure will help the leaves turn green and produce bigger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea tsu nii loo akɛ kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: How do I know if my farm land needs animal manure or chemical fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia kooloi ashikpɔŋ loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: If your soil is sandy and dries out quickly, animal manure is best because it holds water and builds soil health long-term. If your crops need a quick food boost during active growth, chemical fertilizers provide fast-acting nutrients.
ga: Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ ji ŋã ni egbiɔ oya lɛ, Manure ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ ehiɛɔ nu mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ yaa hiɛ be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ otsei lɛ he miihia niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ oya yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni tsuɔ nii oya.

english: What are these small caterpillars eating the inside leaves of my maize, and how do I save my crop?
ga: Mɛni nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ yeɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ amli? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that destroys maize foliage. Spraying recommended insecticides early in the morning or late evening when the caterpillars come out to feed will stop them from damaging your crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni fiteɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni kooloi lɛ eje kpo amɛmiitao niyenii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the soil when heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers rot when standing water starves the roots of air. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu lɛ ŋmɛ shi, ni no haa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: What will happen if I plant my maize seeds very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ mihe lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients from each other. This results in weak, thin stalks and much smaller cobs compared to properly spaced crops.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo baa kɛ akɛto tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it better to clear weeds before planting my seeds instead of waiting for the crops to sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaajie jwɛi lɛ dani adu nii moŋ fe ni aaamɛ ni tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and will steal water and food from your seeds right from the start. Clearing weeds before planting gives your crop seeds a clean start to grow strong without competition.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii. Ni ebaaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ odumɔwui lɛ amli kɛjɛ shishijee tɔ̃ɔ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi dani odu lɛ, ehaa odumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ koni amɛdara waa ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without growing into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop mainly due to extreme afternoon heat or irregular watering, which stresses the plant. Covering the soil with dried grass (mulching) keeps the roots cool and moist, helping the blossoms stay on.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo jɛɔ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa lɛ hewɔ. ni kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli (mulching) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛya nɔ amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients every year and allows maize pests to build up in the soil. Switching to crops like cowpea or groundnut restores natural nitrogen to your soil.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa mli ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ cowpeas loo peanuts nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen aba oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and look droopy during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves in afternoon heat to slow down water loss from evaporation. Watering your plants deeply in the cool early morning helps them stay strong throughout the afternoon.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane mli koni nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ tsei anɔ nu yɛ leebi maŋkpa ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛnáa hewalɛ yɛ shwane muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: How can I prevent insects from eating my harvested maize and beans inside my storage room?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkaye ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni mikpaa yɛ mi-nitoohe lɛ?

english: Insects need moisture and air to survive inside stored grain. Thoroughly sun-drying your grains until they are completely hard and storing them in airtight bags (like PICS bags) suffocates pests and protects your harvest.
ga: Fɛ̃i kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia kooloi koni amɛhi shi yɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmaa kɛyashi ebaawa kwraa ni okɛto kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli (tamɔ PICS kotoku) mli lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebu onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my maize plants turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is essential for green growth. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost around the base will help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ afata tso lɛ he. Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant my seeds in straight lines instead of scattering them across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni magbɛ amɛ mashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines gives every crop equal space to get sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. It also makes it much easier to walk through the farm to weed, apply fertilizer, and harvest without damaging your plants.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ náa hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ehaa nyiɛmɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa jwɛi, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa. ni ofiteee otsei lɛ

english: Why do my cassava plants drop all their leaves when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves in dry weather to reduce water loss and protect its roots underground. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves and continue growing.
ga: Yucca shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be mli ni nu egbiɔ lɛ koni ekɛba nu ni fiteɔ lɛ shi ni ebu eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaya nɔ eda.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without turning into tomatoes when the weather is very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomatoi beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, causing them to fall off before fruit can form. Providing light shade or watering early in the morning helps cool the plants so fruit can set.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa pollen lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo loo nu wo tso lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔni afee ni eyibii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ shi.

english: What is causing the leaves on my pepper plants to curl up and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Curled or wrinkled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips sucking the plant's sap and spreading plant viruses. Spraying neem oil or insecticidal soap helps clear the pests so healthy leaves can grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni ebɔle loo ekpɔtɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe kooloi lɛ koni baai ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why are my yam tubers rotting in the ground before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot in the ground when the soil stays too wet due to poor drainage, or when seed yams already infected with fungi were used for planting. Planting on raised mounds helps excess water drain away.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛ́ sũ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Aloo kɛ́ oodu sweet potato dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmeii momo lɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ.

english: How does planting cowpeas together with my maize help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ cowpea ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes, meaning they pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This natural food feeds the nearby maize crops, helping them grow stronger while saving you money on artificial fertilizer.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii nɛɛ haa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii. Ye obua amɛ ni amɛdara waa yɛ be mli ni okɛ shika hu toɔ bo yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee lɛ he.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the fruit bunch gets heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akui lɛ tsii lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that can be weakened by microscopic soil worms called nematodes or stem borers. Supporting heavy stems with strong wooden poles prevents the trees from snapping or uprooting in high wind.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ, ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ shishi ni tsii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa tso lɛ akumɔ loo eshishifãi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why does my harvested maize get moldy inside my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli ewo muji yɛ mi-shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize gets moldy if it is placed in storage while it still contains moisture. Fungi thrive in damp conditions, so fully drying the grain in the sun before storing it will keep it safe and dry for months.
ga: Abele baanyɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lolo. Fungus daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ha dumɔwui lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani okɛto. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe ni amɛgbi nyɔji babaoo.

english: Why do my sweet potato plants produce big bushy green leaves but small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni ebɔle ehe shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil encourages sweet potatoes to spend all their energy growing leaves above ground instead of swelling the roots below. Using balanced fertilizers lower in nitrogen encourages bigger tuber growth.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaha sweet potato lɛ atsu ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ agbɔjɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni nitrogen faaa yɛ mli lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ baawo ŋmeii wuji lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and fall off during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves drop during the dry season because the trees lose water faster than their small roots can drink it. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or shade trees shields young cocoa from harsh sunlight and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli ejaakɛ tso lɛ nu fiteɔ oya fe shishifãi bibii lɛ. Abaanyɛ anu. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu cocoa tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are my plantain bunches getting smaller every year even though the plants are still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ bibii daa afi lɛ? Tso lɛ miida lolo?

english: Plantain bunches get smaller over time because too many sucker stems grow around one parent plant, competing for nutrients. Pruning the extra shoots so only two or three stems remain per stand keeps bunches large.
ga: Plantain ŋmeii lɛ baafee bibii yɛ be ni sa mli be mli ni suction ŋmeii babaoo shwereɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ. Tso ni ji nyɛ kome lɛ kɛ ehe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ mli.
