Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli bɔni afee ni tsei 2-3 pɛ ahi shi yɛ shidaamɔhe kome nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aná tsei akuu agbo ko.

english: Why are tiny holes suddenly showing up in the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii eba trukaa yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Holes in maize leaves are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the growing shoot. Spraying recommended bio-pesticides or neem water early into the leaf funnels kills the caterpillars before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmeii baai amli lɛ baa. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra. Yɛ baa funnel lɛ mli lɛ baagbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: When is the best time for me to put fertilizer on my maize farm so it grows tall and strong?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii koni tsei lɛ aya hiɛ ni amɛhe awa?

english: Applying NPK fertilizer within two weeks after the maize seeds sprout gives the roots early strength, followed by a second application of Urea fertilizer four weeks later when the plants start growing rapidly.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ otsii enyɔ mli beni ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ oya. Nɔ ni nyiɛɔ enɛ sɛɛ ji urea ni akɛwoɔ mli shii enyɔ nɔ yɛ otsii ejwɛ sɛɛ beni tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa oya lɛ.

english: Why do I need to keep water standing in my swamp rice field while it is growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akɛ nu ato ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli beni aduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Standing water in rice fields prevents weeds from growing and competing with the crop while keeping the soil constantly wet so the rice plants can form full grain heads.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akaŋ akaŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Koni ŋmãa tsei lɛ aná dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and showing green and yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves with yellow patches are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whitefly insects or infected stems. Using disease-resistant cassava stem varieties for planting prevents this problem.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ji ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii bibii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ahiɛ Kɛ akɛ ŋmei henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ baatsu nii kɛdu lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do some of my seed yams rot in the ground before they can sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Seed yams rot in the soil when the soil is too wet or when the seed piece was infected by fungus or tiny soil worms. Coating seed yam pieces with wood ash or fungicide before planting protects them from rotting.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛ́ sũ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ ŋmeii loo sũ mli ŋmeii bibii emɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso sũ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii wo sweet potato fãi lɛ ahe dani adu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkafite.

english: Why do my tomato stems and fruits turn dark brown and rot when heavy rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ kɛ amɛyibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This dark rot is caused by a fungal disease called late blight that spreads rapidly in wet weather. Spacing plants further apart for good airflow and spraying copper fungicide before heavy rains keeps the plants safe.
ga: Hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ leaf blight ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ diŋ nɛɛ baa. Gbɛ ni kã tsei ateŋ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ mli. Ni akɔɔble tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants dropping off without producing any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo pepper yibii ko lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, lack of water, or attacks by tiny insects like thrips. Mulching the soil to keep it cool and moist helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni tutuaa amɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ muji wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eha edɔ ni edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why does my stored maize turn into fine white powder after a few months in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikɛto lɛ etsɔ powda yɛŋ kpakpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni mikɛhi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Stored maize turns to powder because grain weevils bore inside the kernels to feed and lay eggs. Drying grains thoroughly until they are hard and storing them in sealed airtight bags stops weevils from surviving.
ga: Abɛi ni ato lɛ tsɔɔ powda ejaakɛ dumɔwui amli ŋmeii lɛ boteɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli koni amɛye ni amɛwo ŋmeii. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ebaawa ni okɛwo kotoku ko ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmei lɛ akajo foi.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantains yɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Why do my garden egg plants grow thin and weak when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ebɛ hewalɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, air, and food in the soil. Spacing them out allows each plant to get enough energy to grow strong stems and produce heavy fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ tsei ni wa ni ewo yibii ni tsii.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up like tubes during the dry afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves inward to protect themselves from losing water through evaporation. It is the plant's natural way of saving water until the hot afternoon sun cools down.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ yɛ la ni hoɔ lɛ hewɔ lɛ he. Eji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ nu he kɛyashiɔ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my tomato plants turning yellow during the sunny period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei ashishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is under stress from too much heat and direct sun without enough moisture, or that it has used up the nutrients like nitrogen in the soil to feed the top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ babaoo kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ mli. Aloo etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kɛ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ etsu nii ni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do pests like white tiny flies suddenly flood my vegetable bed during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ lɛ yiɔ mi-aduawai aŋmɔ lɛ mli obɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: In dry weather, insects multiply quickly because heavy rains are not there to wash them off the leaves. The heat also speeds up how fast their eggs hatch.
ga: yɛ be mli ni nu egbi lɛ, kooloi bibii lɛ faa oya ejaakɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni baafɔ baai lɛ ahe lɛ bɛ. Dɔlɛ hu haa ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ oya.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants before any peppers form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani pepper lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they feel stressed by sudden heat, irregular watering, or lack of soil food. The plant sheds flowers to save its strength for survival.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo ni baa trukaa lɛ hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛhiɛ hewalɛ mli koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my cucumber vines produce many yellow flowers but very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kukumba wain tsei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ babaoo shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Cucumbers produce two types of flowers: male flowers that only attract bees, and female flowers that actually grow into fruits. Early in the season, the plant naturally produces mostly male flowers first.
ga: Kukumba woɔ fɔfɔi henɔi enyɔ: Fɔfɔi hii lɛ gbalaa ŋmeii pɛ. kɛ fɔfɔi yei ni kwɛ̃ɔ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ. yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli Tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi hii babaoo klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are my cassava tubers small and skinny even though the leafy tops look huge and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa moŋ lɛ?

english: If the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or is too hard for roots to expand, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing green leaves on top instead of storing food in the underground tubers.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo shishifãi lɛ wa tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛgbɛ amɛshwã lɛ, Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai eŋɔli yɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii amli lɛ,.

english: How can I tell if my crops are hungry for food in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye miŋmɔshi nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants show hunger through their leaf colors. For example, when maize lacks nitrogen, the tips of the older leaves turn yellow in a V-shape, showing that the plant is pulling nutrients from old leaves to feed new growth.
ga: Tsei jieɔ amɛ hɔmɔ lɛ kpo kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ ahe su nɔ. Akɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa mli lɛ, Baai ni egbɔ lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miigbala niyenii kɛmiijɛ baai momoi lɛ amli koni ekɛha tso heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: How does growing tomatoes under a simple netted greenhouse structure protect them better than open land?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tomato ni akwɛɔ yɛ trellis greenhouse shishi lɛ buɔ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni agbele nɔ lɛ?

english: A greenhouse structure acts like a house for your crops. It blocks heavy beating rain from washing away soil nutrients, shelters delicate leaves from intense sun burn, and keeps destructive insects out without using heavy chemicals.
ga: Greenhouse lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ shia kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii. Ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ebuɔ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa he. ni ebuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahe ni akɛ tsofai ni tsii tsuuu nii.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow so tall and thin when I plant them under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo waa beni midu lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Pepper plants need direct sunlight to grow strong. When planted in the shade of big trees, they stretch upward searching for light, making them thin, weak, and less able to bear heavy fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ, ebaakpã kɛya ŋwɛi kɛya la lɛ he, ni ebaaha efee mlɛo, egbɔjɔ, ni ewoɔ yibii fioo komɛi ni tsii.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow mainly due to lack of water or nitrogen in the soil. When it is too dry, the plant cannot absorb nutrients properly, causing the leaves to lose their green color and vitality.
ga: Nu loo nitrogen ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ titri lɛ, ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. Kɛji edɔ tsɔ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ ahe su eŋɔli kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce small roots when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishifãi bibii yɔɔ kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded, their roots fight each other for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Giving each plant enough space allows the tubers room to swell and grow large.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ kɛhaa nu. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ amli shwereɔ ni amɛdaraa.

english: How do weeds cause my crop yield to drop so quickly?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiba shi oya nɛkɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal the sunlight, water, and soil food meant for your crops. When crops have to compete with weeds, they cannot develop full-sized stems or fruits.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaadu nii yɛ mli lɛ mli. Beni ehe baahia ni ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ jwɛi abɔ akaŋ lɛ Amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo ŋmeii loo aduawai ni dalɛ yeɔ emuu.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off before producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers usually drop off when the weather gets too hot, when water is irregular, or when there are no insects like bees around to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ mli ejɔɔɔ Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii bɛ ni baaha fɔfɔii lɛ afee ŋmeii.

english: Will trimming off some lower leaves on my tomato plants help them fruit better?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mifolɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ, ebaaha yibii lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Yes, pruning lower or diseased leaves directs more energy and plant food into developing fruits instead of wasting energy on excess leaf growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hewalɛ babaoo kɛ tsei aniyenii woɔ yibii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine ni miida lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Why are the leaves of my cowpea plants curling up and feeling sticky?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni minuɔ he akɛ amɛhe ejɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and stickiness are signs of tiny pests like aphids. They suck the nutrient juices out of the plant leaves and leave behind a sticky waste called honeydew.
ga: Baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi kɛ amɛhe ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ aphids lɛ he okadi. Amɛmuɔ niyenii mli nu ni yɔɔ tsei ahe baai amli lɛ ni amɛshiɔ nibii ni shwieɔ shi ni atsɛɔ lɛ honeydew lɛ amɛsɛɛ.

english: Why do my bean plants wither and die even when the soil is very wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa moŋ lɛ?

english: Excess water rots the roots of bean plants because they cannot breathe in flooded soil. Once roots rot, the plant can no longer drink water or take in nutrients, causing it to wither.
ga: Nu babaoo haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu kɛbote sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ egbo lɛ, tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ anu nu loo eŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ dɔŋŋ. ha egbi

english: How do I know if my land is fertile enough to plant yams?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Fertile soil for yams is usually dark, soft, rich in decayed leaves, holds moisture well without getting waterlogged, and breaks apart easily in your hands.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni baa nii kɛha sweet potato lɛ yɛ ediŋŋ, eyɛ bɔdɔɔ, ni baai ni fiteɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli. Ehiɛɔ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni nu shwieee nɔ. ni efoɔ oya kɛ́ eyɛ nine mli

english: Why is it good for my field to plant groundnuts after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ duɔ ŋmei beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of nitrogen food from the earth, but groundnuts put nitrogen back into the soil naturally, restoring soil fertility for the next season.
ga: Abɛi kɛ nitrogen ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Shi ŋmeii haa nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when the sun gets very bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ lɛ? Beni hulu la lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn and dry out easily in full sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or tree canopy above them to block the harsh heat and keep the soil moist while their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ koni amɛtsi dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ naa ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed to make leaves green and healthy. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shi waa.

english: What is making holes in my maize leaves and leaving brown sawdust-like dirt inside the plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni kɛ buji ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi lɛ amli lɛ baa ni eshiɔ muji ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: That damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the central leaves of the maize plant during the day and eat the soft growth from the inside, leaving small droppings that look like fine sawdust.
ga: The damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ baai lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Ni eyeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ kɛjɛɔ emli, ni ŋmeii bibii pɛ eshwɛɔ. ni tamɔ ŋmei kpakpa

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are fully grown and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ edara kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 and 12 months after planting. You can tell it is maturing when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baai lɛ edara kɛji baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do we build high dirt mounds to grow yams instead of just digging small holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔmaa sũi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ ni wɔkɛduɔ sweet potatoes yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni wɔbaafo bu bibii lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, deep, soft soil to expand into big tubers. High mounds keep the soil soft for easy root growth and stop excess rainwater from pooling around the roots and causing rot.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni etsɔ bulbs agboi. Gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ oya. ni etsĩ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ naa koni ekabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe ni eha amɛgboi.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with tiny fruits when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ, be mli ni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients from each other. Instead of growing thick stems and big fruits, they stretch upward competing for sunlight.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ tsei ni mli tse kɛ aduawai wuji. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔ a he kɛ ha hulu la ɔ he akaŋ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my vegetable crops with dried grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering soil with dried grass, called mulching, acts like a protective blanket. It keeps the ground cool, traps water in the soil so it stays wet longer, and stops weeds from getting light to sprout.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ. Ekɛ nu toɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃.

english: Why is it dangerous for me to plant my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara kɛha mi akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain often refreshes the surface, but the deep soil remains dry. If the rain stops for a few weeks afterward, your newly sprouted seeds will run out of water and dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ feɔ fɛo. Shi shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli egbi lolo. Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ baaná nu ni amɛbaagbi.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without turning into small tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato bibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant suffers from sudden heat stress, dry soil, or lack of insects like bees to pollinate them. The plant drops its flowers to save water and survival energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na piŋmɔ kɛjɛ latsaa ni baa trukaa lɛ mli, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii nyɛɛɛ amɛwo amɛmli. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why do weeds always grow back much faster than my planted crops after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya be fɛɛ be fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that have adapted strong root systems over time. They are built to absorb water and soil food much quicker than planted crops, allowing them to jump up right after rain.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni wa, ni yɔɔ koo mli ni shishifãi ni wa baa yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ. Abɔ amɛ koni amɛjie nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛjoɔ foi amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ.

english: How do I keep small insects from eating up my harvested maize while it is sitting in my storehouse?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkaye mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ be mli ni eta mi-nitoohe lɛ?

english: Insects like weevils multiply quickly in stored grain if the storehouse is warm and damp. You can protect your maize by drying it completely until it is hard, cleaning the storehouse thoroughly before storing, and using sealed airtight bags (PICS bags) or approved storage dusts to suffocate any pests.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii babaoo yaa hiɛ oya yɛ ŋmaa ni ato lɛ mli kɛji akɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ. Obaanyɛ obu o-corn lɛ he kɛtsɔ egbimɔ kwraa kɛyashi ebaawa lɛ nɔ. Tsumɔ shĩa lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ dani okɛto. Ni okɛ kotokui ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli (PICS kotokui) loo nibii ni akɛbuaa sũ naa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii ni okɛmu tsɛŋemɔ helai fɛɛ ni fiteɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why do my stored beans get small holes and powdery dust inside the sacks after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kɔfi ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni sũ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ.

english: Those small holes are caused by bean weevils (bruchids) that hatch from eggs laid on the seeds. The young insects eat the inside of the bean and leave dust behind. Storing fully dried beans in airtight containers prevents these insects from surviving and ruining your crop.
ga: Bean weevils (bruchids) ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii lɛ baa. Kplukai bibii lɛ yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛshiɔ sũ yɛ amɛsɛɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ wo tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkajo foi ni amɛfite onibii lɛ.

english: How often should I inspect my stored grains to make sure insects have not invaded them?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ makwɛ miŋmaa ni mikɛto lɛ mli koni mana nɔmimaa akɛ kooloi bibii eboteee mli?

english: You should check your stored grains at least once every two weeks. Look for fine dust at the bottom of the bags, feel if the bag feels unnaturally warm inside, or check for live bugs so you can re-dry or treat the grains before serious damage occurs.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ okwɛ ŋmaa ni okɛto lɛ shikome daa otsii enyɔ. Taomɔ sũ bibii ni yɔɔ kotoku lɛ shishi lɛ. Ani kotoku lɛ mli lɛ nuɔ he akɛ edɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ? Aloo kwɛmɔ kɛji kooloi ni hiɛ ka yɛ mli koni onyɛ okɛgbi loo otsa dumɔwui lɛ ekoŋŋ dani nɔ ko ni mli wa aba.

english: Why is it bad to put freshly harvested crops directly into storage sacks without drying them in the sun first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa ehee lɛ baawo kotokui amli tɛ̃ɛ ni agbiko yɛ hulutsoo be mli klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested crops contain high moisture. Putting them directly into bags creates a damp environment where mold and fungi grow rapidly, which generates heat and attracts destructive store insects that will destroy your entire harvest.
ga: Tsei ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ hulutsoo babaoo. Kɛ́ okɛwo kotoku lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha shihilɛ lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i. he ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwereɔ oya Enɛ haa hulutsoo baa ni egbalaa kooloi ni fiteɔ shwapoi ni baafite onibii fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Will cutting off big branches from my mature mango tree kill it, or is it actually good for the tree?
ga: Ani kɛ́ afo mango tso ni eda lɛ nine agbo ko lɛ, ebaagbe lɛ? Aloo eji nɔ kpakpa diɛŋtsɛ kɛha tso lɛ?

english: Cutting back heavy or overcrowded branches will not kill a healthy mango tree. Pruning actually helps by allowing sunlight and fresh air to reach the inner branches, which stops fungal diseases and encourages the tree to produce fresh, high-yielding shoots.
ga: Niji ni tsii tsɔ loo ni ebɔle tsɔ lɛ ni oookpa lɛ egbeŋ mango tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa diɛŋtsɛ kɛtsɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni ehaa eshɛɔ tsei niji amli lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii helai kpaa ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo ŋmeii heei ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my mango tree blossoms keep falling off before turning into real fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ aduawai diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Mango flowers often drop early due to insect pests like thrips, fungal diseases like anthracnose during rainy periods, or a sudden lack of water. Applying recommended safe sprays right before flowering helps protect the blooms so they can set fruit.
ga: Mango fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee oya yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ thrips kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ anthracnose hewɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli. aloo nu ni hoɔ trukaa Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni atsɔɔ akɛ ashwie nɔ dani fɔfɔi lɛ awo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛwo yibii.

english: If my old mango tree has stopped giving me good fruit, do I have to cut it down completely?
ga: Kɛji akɛ mango momo lɛ kpa yibii kpakpai hamɔ lɛ, ani ehe miihia ni afolɔ amɛ kwraa?

english: You do not need to remove the whole tree. You can perform heavy pruning to remove old branches, or graft scions from high-yielding mango varieties onto the existing trunk so it produces fresh, high-quality fruits much faster than planting a new seed.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa ni ojie tso muu lɛ fɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ofolɔ tsei lɛ ahe waa koni ojie niji momoi lɛ. Aloo okɛ mango henɔi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ awo tsei ni yɔɔ momo lɛ anɔ. Bɔni afee ni aná nibii heei ni hi jogbaŋŋ oya fe dumɔwui heei ni aduɔ lɛ.

english: What is the proper method for cutting branches off my fruit trees so I do not hurt them?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ afoɔ mi tso lɛ niji koni akaye lɛ awui?

english: Use a sharp, clean saw or cutlass to make smooth, angled cuts close to the main trunk without tearing the bark. Clean cuts heal fast, whereas ragged or torn cuts collect rainwater and attract boring insects that cause trunk rot.
ga: Kɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ tsei loo tsɔne ni mli wa atsu nii. Afolɔ ni he tse ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ koŋ ko ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ tso wulu lɛ he ni agbalaaa tso lɛ yibii lɛ amli. Pilamɔi ni he tse lɛ baatsa oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, pilamɔi ni ekumɔ loo etse lɛ buaa nugbɔ nu naa ni egbalaa kooloi bibii ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli ni haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to apply chemical sprays on my crops so they work best?
ga: Mɛɛ gbi mli be hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ makɛ tsofai afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ aba?

english: The best time to spray is early in the morning or late in the afternoon when temperatures are cool and the wind is calm. Spraying during hot afternoon sun causes the chemicals to evaporate too fast, and windy weather blows the liquid away from your plants.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔse tsofa lɛ ji leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli. Enɛ ji be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hu efee kpoo. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tsofai lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ. ni kɔɔyɔɔ shihilɛi shwieɔ nu lɛ kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know if my soil has enough moisture to start planting my seed crops after the first rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui akwɛmɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Squeeze a handful of topsoil tightly in your palm; if it forms a soft ball that easily breaks apart when touched, the moisture is just right for planting. If it oozes water or turns into sticky mud, it is too wet and your seeds might rot.
ga: Mimɔ shikpɔŋ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli fioo ko mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ onine mli. Kɛji akɛ bɔɔlu lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛji akɛ ashɛ he, ni efoɔ oya kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ, no lɛ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu. Kɛji eho kɛje kpo loo ebatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ, Eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ ni odumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ agbo.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crops are missing a vital plant food called nitrogen, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients away from the roots. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color so they can grow properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ bɛ tso niyenii ko ni he hiaa ni atsɛɔ lɛ nitrogen. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. Kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my pepper plants remaining short and refusing to grow taller after transplanting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ egbɔjɔ ni ekpooɔ akɛ ebaada babaoo yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper seedlings often stop growing if their root systems were disturbed during transplanting or if the soil is packed too tightly. Loosening the dirt around the base and adding compost encourages the roots to spread and feed the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper dumɔwui lɛ kpaɔ amɛkwɛ̃mɔ kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ gbala amɛhe yɛ be mli ni aduɔ amɛ lɛ loo kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Gbalamɔ muji ni ebɔle he lɛ Base lɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni eye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛha tsei lɛ niyenii.

english: How do I know if the land I want to farm in Accra is good for growing crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni misumɔɔ ni matsu nii yɛ nɔ yɛ Accra lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: Good agricultural land has dark, crumbly soil that lets water drain easily after heavy rain without forming long-lasting pools. If the ground dries out into hard, cracked blocks, it needs organic matter like compost mixed into it before planting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ okwaayeli he nii yɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni etse ni haa nu hoɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ ni ekɛ nugbɔshiimɔi efeee be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi aahu akɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɛ eshwa. Esa akɛ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii afutu mli dani adu.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds off my land before sowing seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Weeds grow very fast and steal valuable water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from young crops. Clearing the land completely gives your new seeds a clean space to establish strong root systems without competition.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛjuɔ nu ni jara wa, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni jɛɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kwraa lɛ, ebaaha odumɔwui heei lɛ aná he ko ni he tse ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛto shishifã ni mli wa ni akaŋshii bɛ mli lɛ shishi.

english: Why do some cassava plants produce large roots while others on the same farm stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei komɛi yɛ shishifãi wuji yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ ji bibii lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are planted too close together, their roots fight over the same soil food and moisture. Spacing them far enough apart ensures every plant gets enough room and nourishment to form large, heavy roots.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ baatswa niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Gbɛ ni kã tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ fa bɔ ni sa bɔni afee ni tso fɛɛ tso aná he ko kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi wuji ni tsii baa.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants often drop blossoms when they experience heat stress or irregular watering. Placing dry grass or mulch on the soil around the base keeps the root zone cool and moist, helping the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛna dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Akɛ jwɛi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ. Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni shishifã lɛ he afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How can I tell whether bugs or diseases are damaging my crop leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi bibii loo helai miifite miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ?

english: Bugs leave physical chew marks, holes, or missing leaf edges, whereas plant diseases usually cause spots, yellow rings, or powdery coatings without clean bites. Identifying which one it is helps you choose between pest traps or natural sprays like neem extract.
ga: Koolooi shĩɔ ŋmɔtɔ okadii, bu, loo baa lɛ naa ni elaaje. Yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, tsei ahelai kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. yellow ring loo powder coating ni etching ni he tse bɛ mli Nɔ ni tsɔɔ nɔ ni yeɔ ebua bo ni ohalaa tsɛŋemɔ hela loo adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ tamɔ neem mli nu.

english: How can I improve my farm so I get more 50-kilogram bags of crops at harvest time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔ lɛ aya hiɛ koni maná baagi 50kg babaoo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: Increasing your overall weight yield requires enriching your soil with manure before planting, planting at the right depth just as the rainy season starts, and protecting young plants early so each one reaches full mature weight.
ga: Bɔni afee ni sũ lɛ mli tsiimɔ fɛɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo awo sũ lɛ mli dani adu. Dumɔ yɛ he ni sa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. kɛ tsei bibii ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishijee mli bɔni afee ni tso fɛɛ tso aná etsitsinɔnii fɛɛ

english: What will happen to my soil if I plant the same crop on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating your primary crop with leguminous plants like beans or cowpeas feeds nutrient power back into the dirt.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii atsake oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ. Ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How does the dry Harmattan season affect how my crops consume water?
ga: Te Harmattan fɛ̃i be lɛ saa nu ni ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: The dry Harmattan wind sucks moisture out of both plant leaves and topsoil very quickly, causing crops to wilt fast. Covering the exposed ground with straw or leaves traps ground moisture so your crops stay hydrated longer.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei ahe baai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ lɛ fɛɛ mli oya. Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ oya Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai tsu nii ni okɛha hei ni agbele lɛ, ebaamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu koni onibii lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow instead of stay dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing maize leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, a vital nutrient for green growth. Adding organic manure, compost, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the plant regain its healthy green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ, ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot when the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water builds up around them and cannot drain away. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain off, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu ni ekã shi ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ. ni enyɛŋ ejie nu kɛya Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Why shouldn't I burn the cleared grass and bush on my farm before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishãa jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni ajie yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dani miduɔ nii?

english: Burning destroys rich organic material that could decompose and feed your soil. Leaving cut plants to decompose naturally or plowing them back into the dirt enriches the soil with nutrients and helps keep moisture in the ground.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii babaoo ni baanyɛ afite ni eha oshikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ fite yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe loo atsake amɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii lɛ aya hiɛ, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off before setting fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets extremely hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when insects damage the blossoms. Mulching the soil with dry grass helps keep the roots cool and moist, which protects the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii fiteɔ fɔfɔii lɛ Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni buɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe lɛ

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that feed on young shoots. Controlling these insects early prevents leaf damage and allows normal growth to continue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ tsei bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Etsiɔ baai lɛ afitemɔ naa ni ehaa amɛdalɛ yaa nɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing long and thin instead of big and round?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo moŋ fe ni amɛaafee agboi ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ?

english: Yam tubers stay thin if the soil is too hard and compact. Yams need deep, loose, soft soil in large mounds so the roots can expand easily without running into hard ground.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baafee bibioo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ yɛ gɔji wuji amli. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo ni amɛkaho kɛya shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees drop their leaves during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees drop leaves in dry weather to save water. Planting permanent shade trees alongside cocoa protects the young plants from harsh dry winds and keeps the soil shaded and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni nu egbi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ daa ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni haa egbiɔ lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over so easily when strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that struggle to support heavy fruit bunches during storms. Propping up fruiting plantain trees with strong wooden or bamboo poles stops them from tipping over.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye amɛbua aduawai ni tsii lɛ yɛ ahum be mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei loo ŋmeii ni wa ha dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkagbee shi.

english: How do I know the right time to start sowing seeds when the rainy season begins?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ aje dumɔwui adumɔ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ bashɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the soil gets two or three good, soaking rains rather than planting after the very first light rainfall, ensuring there is enough soil moisture to keep seeds germinating safely.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔshiimɔi fioo komɛi atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, moŋ fe ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ fioo lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crop after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants designed to swallow up moisture and fertilizer faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early gives your planted crops a fair chance to grow without competing for food and light.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni afee koni amɛŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha otso lɛ aná hegbɛ ni eda ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ niyenii kɛ la akaŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a vital nutrient for growth. It can also happen if heavy rains have washed the nutrients deep into the ground or if the soil is too waterlogged for roots to breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho niyenii mli nibii lɛ kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Aloo kɛji akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu.

english: Why do experienced farmers say planting groundnuts or beans makes the soil better for the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni adu lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have tiny natural factories on their roots that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. When the plants die, that nitrogen stays in the soil and acts as free food for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei bibii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni efeɔ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which spreads rapidly in wet, humid condition. Pruning excess branches lets sunlight and air into the farm to dry off the pods and keep the fungus away.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Black Pod, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ mli lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ekɛtsi ŋmeii anaa.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting underground before it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ dani akpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long in heavy soil. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ egbi ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and becoming small and twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ bibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Curled leaves are usually a sign that tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies are sucking the sap out of young leaves and passing diseases to the plant. Clearing weeds around your farm reduces where these insects hide.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii, tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies, miinu baai bibii amli nu lɛ ni amɛmiigbɛ hela amɛmiishwa tso lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ ni ajieɔ Oŋmɔ lɛ baaye abua ni hei ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mli lɛ aba shi.

english: How deep should I push maize seeds into the dirt when planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ matsi mi-ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashɛ he ni tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Maize seeds should be planted about 3 to 5 centimeters deep (about the depth of your thumb knuckle). If planted too deep, the seed runs out of energy before reaching the surface; if planted too shallow, dry air or birds will destroy it.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ mli aaafee sɛntimitai 3 kɛyashi 5 (aaafee bɔ ni otsitsi bibioo lɛ mli kwɔ ha). Hewalɛ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ dani amɛshɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo okpoi baafite lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant all my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a heatwave or a long dry spell. If you plant too early, the hot sun will scorch the young shoots before the main rains establish regular soil moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ be kakadaŋŋ loo hɔmɔ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ shãa tsei bibii lɛ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ po baa.

english: Why do I need to put tall sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsei kakadaji awo shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make the energy required to grow big tubers underground. Staking holds the vines up in the sun and prevents soil-borne diseases from attacking the leaves.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni bulbs wuji akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aba. Staking haa wain tso lɛ ŋmɛɔ hulutsoo be mli, ni ehaa helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ akatutua tso lɛ baai lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without turning into actual tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather becomes too hot or when the plants do not get a steady supply of water. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why should I cover the bare dirt around my crops with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Akɛ jwɛi loo baai ŋmɔɔ?

english: Covering soil with dry leaves or grass (called mulching) keeps the ground cool, traps water so you irrigate less, and prevents weeds from taking light and food away from your crops.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ Enɛ (ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching) yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i. Ehiɛɔ nu mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu awo mli fioo. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekajie la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and drying up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct sunlight and severe heat. Without taller shade plants like plantains or tree canopies to block the hot afternoon sun, the leaves lose moisture faster than the roots can drink it, causing them to scorch and turn yellow.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛji tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ahe tsɔi ni tsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ naa lɛ bɛ lɛ, Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ. Enɛ haa shãa ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants have ragged holes and small powder inside the middle cone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli etse kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli

english: This is a typical sign of the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central funnel of the plant where it is soft and moist, chewing on young leaves before they fully unroll.
ga: Enɛ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ahe okadi ni afɔɔ namɔ. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli he ni loo lɛ yɔɔ blɛoo ni edɔ lɛ. Kɛtsɔ baai bibii lɛ ni oooye dani ojie amɛ kpo kwraa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my corn plants turning light yellow starting from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛyitseiaŋ lɛ?

english: This happens when the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to make leaves green and healthy. When nitrogen is low, the plant moves what little it has left to the newest top leaves, leaving the bottom leaves to starve and turn yellow.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ nitrogen lɛ faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi baa hee fe fɛɛ lɛ nɔ. Ha baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground when there is heavy rain for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess rain fills all the spaces in the dirt without draining away, the roots drown, rot-causing germs multiply quickly, and the tubers turn watery.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo ni eyi sũ lɛ mli obɔ ni ekɛ nu shwieee nɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni helai ni fiteɔ lɛ faa oya. ni yitso lɛ tsɔ nu

english: Why do my yam vines need long wooden poles to climb on instead of just growing on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ shikpɔŋ kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Yam plants make tubers using food produced by leaves in full sunlight. By climbing tall stakes, the leaves spread out into the light without touching wet soil, which prevents disease and builds larger, healthier underground yams.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ baai ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli baa lɛ feɔ ŋmeii. Kɛtsɔ tso ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ kwɔɔ nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa la lɛ mli ni amɛtaaa shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ helai anaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my piece of land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil, but legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts actually feed the ground. They capture nitrogen from the air through their roots and leave it behind in the soil for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, shi ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii diɛŋtsɛ. Amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni amɛshiɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the blossoms on my pepper plants drop off instead of growing into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the air gets too hot, when the soil is too dry, or when there is too much chemical nitrogen in the soil. Under these stresses, the plant sheds flowers to protect itself rather than spending energy growing fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo be mli ni tsofa ni ji nitrogen lɛ fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Yɛ nɛkɛ haomɔi nɛɛ ashishi lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii kɛdu aduawai

english: Why does my plantain tree give smaller bunches when I let many suckers grow around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii beni mihaa ŋmeii babaoo shwereɔ yɛ plantain lɛ he lɛ?

english: Every new shoot or sucker acts like another mouth to feed. If you let too many suckers grow around one parent stem, they all fight for the same water, sunlight, and soil food, leaving less energy to form big plantain bunches.
ga: Tso loo tso hee fɛɛ tso tsuɔ nii tamɔ daaŋ kroko ni abaatsɔ nɔ aye nii. Kɛji oŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ he lɛ, tso kome lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛha nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ni no haa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ plantain tsei wuji lɛ faaa.

english: Why do dark spots and white powder appear on my tomato leaves during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ tomato baai anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: High moisture and humidity create the perfect home for microscopic fungi to grow on plant surfaces. When raindrops splash on infected soil or leaves, the fungus spreads to healthy parts of the tomato crop.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni mli edɔ lɛ feɔ shia ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii bibii ni anaaa lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ tsei anɔ. Kɛ nugbɔshiimɔi shwie shikpɔŋ loo baai ni hela lɛ emɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ baagbɛ eshwa tomato tso lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crop roots burn or wither if I place fertilizer directly against the plant stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso shishifãi lɛ shãa loo amɛgboɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers are concentrated salts. When placed right against the stem, they pull water straight out of the plant roots through osmosis, scorching the tissue just like hot water would.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ. Kɛ akɛwo tso lɛ shishi lɛ Amɛgbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔɔ osmosis nɔ. ni eshãa fãji lɛ tamɔ nu ni mli edɔ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains alongside my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantains yɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense direct sunlight and can easily burn or dry out. Plantains grow quickly and have broad leaves that create a soft shade umbrella, keeping the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa gets established during its first two years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. ni ebaanyɛ eshã loo egbi oya Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ baa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be mli ni kookoo bibioo lɛ jeɔ shishi ewaa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to grow properly when I plant them immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ beni midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The very first rain often heats up the dry ground and is quickly followed by a hot dry spell. It is better to wait until the rainy season settles in fully so the soil stays consistently moist, allowing the seeds to germinate without drying out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ. ni hɔmɔ ahum ni mli edɔ waa nyiɛɔ sɛɛ Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛkɛ lɛ dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Why are my cassava plants producing lots of green leaves above ground but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ miiwo baai eŋɔli babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or water, the cassava plant directs all its energy into growing tall stalks and bushy leaves instead of storing energy in its roots. Balancing your soil nutrients helps the plant focus on swelling its tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baato shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa bulb ni efuu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my corn plants turning yellow in a V-shape and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate that your crop lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants use to stay green and grow tall. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure can correct this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ amɛ ŋmɔji kɛ amɛ dalɛ nɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: What causes tiny holes in my young maize leaves with small dark droppings inside the center funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ anɔ ni ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ diŋ yɛ jɛmɛ. yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋgbɛ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing shoot of the maize plant to eat tender leaf tissue. Applying recommended treatments directly into the plant's central funnel early in the morning helps control them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Applying the recommended treatment directly into the center channel of the plant early in the morning will help control it.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants falling off instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress or sudden periods of drought. Keeping the soil consistently watered and mulched during hot dry weather helps the flowers set into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo hɔmɔ ni ba trukaa. Kɛ́ afɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ tomato he.

english: Why does clearing my land by burning the vegetation cause my soil to dry out faster during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsei ni ashãa lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the layer of dry leaves and organic matter on top of the earth that normally acts like a protective blanket. Without this cover, the sun bakes the bare ground directly, causing water to evaporate very quickly.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ baai ni egbi kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni bei pii lɛ etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ. Kɛji akɛ nɛkɛ nɔ ko bɛ lɛ Hulu la lɛ baashã he ni nɔ ko bɛ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa nu shwieɔ oya waa

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crops very close together so I can get more food from a small field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded together, they compete with one another for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to build strong roots and produce a full yield.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi ni wa baawo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the sunlight to make food for their underground tubers. Staking also lifts the foliage off the wet ground, protecting the leaves from soil-borne diseases and rotting.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli kɛ fitemɔ he.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up tightly and turning small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe shi ni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips, which spread plant viruses while feeding. Controlling these insects early prevents the leaf-curl virus from stunting your plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tsei amli be mli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ Mra be mli ni akudɔɔ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ Ebaaye abua ni leaf curl virus lɛ akaha tsei lɛ afee shoo.

english: Why are there different varieties of seeds for the exact same crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi yɔɔ kɛha tso kome lɛ?

english: Different seed varieties are bred to handle specific growing conditions, such as dry weather, short rainy seasons, or local pests. Having multiple options allows you to select the seed that matches your farm's soil and climate.
ga: Dumɔwui srɔtoi Atsɔse amɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛtsu shihilɛi pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni amɛdaraa yɛ mli, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi lɛ ahe nii. nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku loo maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui Kɛji oyɛ nibii babaoo ni obaanyɛ ohala lɛ, ehaa ohalaa dumɔwui ni kɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kpãa gbee.

english: How do I choose the best seed variety for my specific farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala dumɔwui srɔtoi ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha miŋmɔ pɔtɛɛ lɛ?

english: You choose based on how much rainfall your area receives, your soil type, and how quickly you want to harvest. Matching the seed's growing needs to your local conditions gives you the best chance of a good yield.
ga: Odamɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ henɔ, kɛ bɔ ni osumɔɔ ni okpa oya lɛ nɔ ohalaa. Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui ni miida lɛ ahe hiamɔ nii kpã shihilɛi ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha oná hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni okɛbaakpa nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do improved seeds yield more than the seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Improved seeds are specially selected and bred for strong growth, high yield, and disease resistance, whereas saved seeds gradually lose their strength and quality over generations.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ krɛdɛɛ ni akwɛɔ amɛ koni amɛdara waa, amɛwo yibii babaoo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye helai anɔ. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ baafite hewalɛ kɛ su fiofio yɛ yinɔi lɛ amli.

english: Can changing the seed variety I plant help protect my farm from crop diseases?
ga: Ani dumɔwui srɔtoi ni miduɔ lɛ ni mitsakeɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu miŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ tsei ahe helai ahe?

english: Yes, many modern crop varieties have natural resistance to specific diseases built into them, which helps your crops stay healthy without needing as many expensive chemicals.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsei babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ helai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ. Enɛ haa otsei lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni tsofai ni jara wa he ehiaaa.

english: Why do some crop varieties mature in just 85 days while others take four months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbii 85 pɛ mli, yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu yeɔ nyɔji ejwɛ lɛ?

english: Fast-maturing crops are bred to complete their life cycle quickly. This helps farmers produce food fast and harvest successfully even when rainy seasons are short.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei ni daa oya koni amɛgbe amɛshihilɛ be lɛ naa oya. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi ni amɛnáa niyenii oya ni amɛkpaa nii jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔnɛmɔ be lɛ faaa moŋ.

english: Does a fast-maturing crop require less rainfall to give a good yield?
ga: Ani tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ he ehiaaa nugbɔ fioo koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Yes, because the plant is in the field for a shorter period, it needs fewer total weeks of rainfall or irrigation to reach harvest compared to long-season crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ tsei yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kukuoo ko. No hewɔ lɛ, otsii fioo komɛi pɛ he hiaa ni nugbɔ nɛɔ loo nu shwieɔ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ koni anyɛ ana yibiiwoo kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ ahe.

english: Can I harvest crops twice in a single rainy season if I use quick-maturing seeds?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kome mli? Kɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tsu nii

english: Yes, using varieties that mature in under 90 days allows you to plant early, harvest quickly, and potentially grow a second crop before the rains completely stop.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tsei srɔtoi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbii 90 mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ oduɔ amɛ oya. Kpamɔ oya Ni abaanyɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ akpa kwraa.

english: How does visiting a demonstration farm help me improve my crop yield?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ŋmɔ ko ni miyasaraa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: A demonstration farm lets you see how different crop varieties grow side-by-side using proper techniques so you can learn what works best before spending money on your own field.
ga: Nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ŋmɔ lɛ haa onaa bɔ ni aduɔ tsei srɔtoi. Te abaafee tɛŋŋ adara yɛ he kome kɛtsɔ ŋaai ni ja nɔ? No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okase nɔ ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ dani ofite shika yɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ oshikpɔji lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do short or dwarf crop varieties produce big yields without falling over?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei kukuji loo bibii lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo ni amɛgbeeee shi lɛ?

english: Dwarf varieties focus their energy on growing strong stems and large fruits rather than tall leaves, which prevents them from falling over in strong winds or heavy rain.
ga: Dwarf henɔi lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa tsei ni wa kɛ aduawai wuji ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ nɔ. yɛ baai kakadaji najiaŋ Enɛ baatsi enaa koni ekagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli.

english: Why should I plant my seeds in measured rows instead of scattering them freely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni asusu he lɛ mli? yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshwa ehe

english: Row planting ensures every crop gets equal access to sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, while making weeding, fertilizing, and harvesting much easier.
ga: Row dumɔ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa jwɛi shwiemɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why do my crops keep getting sick when the bush around my farm gets tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hela mɔ amɛ waa yɛ be mli ni jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ miida lɛ? Miŋmɔ lɛ miiya hiɛ?

english: Tall weeds and thick bushes trap excess moisture and block sunlight around your crops, creating a damp environment where diseases can easily start and spread.
ga: Jwɛi ni kɛlɛ kɛ tsei bibii ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la ni bɔleɔ onibii lɛ ahe lɛ naa, ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ baa. Ebaanyɛ eje shishi ni egbɛ eshwa mlɛo

english: How does cutting down weeds help protect my crops from insect pests?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe?

english: Weeds and overgrown bushes serve as hiding places and breeding spots for destructive insects, so keeping your farm cleanly slashed removes their shelter and keeps them away from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ he ni kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ teeɔ amɛhe kɛ amɛfɔmɔhei. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ofo oŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaajie amɛhe nɔ ni amɛhaa lɛ, ni ebaaha amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: What is the simplest way to reduce general crop issues on my field without chemicals?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shi ni akɛ tsofai tsuuu nii?

english: Regularly clearing bushes and keeping your farm clean is the most effective way to prevent crop issues, as it naturally lowers both pest numbers and disease outbreaks.
ga: Tsoi bibii ni ooojie daa kɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni oooha ehe atse lɛ ji gbɛi ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe naagbai anaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa lɛ ayibɔ aba shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What actually happens to crop diseases when I clear the weeds around my farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni baa tsei ahe helai anɔ kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi shwie amɛhe? Okwaafoi daa?

english: Clearing weeds removes the damp, shaded micro-climate that fungi and bacteria need to grow, causing disease levels on your farm to drop significantly.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa ni fungi kɛ bacteria adara. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, helai ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi waa.

english: How does using a motorized slasher or cutter machine help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ nii loo tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ nii lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Slasher machines clear thick weeds quickly and evenly, ensuring weeds do not steal essential sunlight, water, and soil food away from your crops.
ga: Slasher lɛ jieɔ jwɛi ni mli tse lɛ oya ni ehaa efeɔ ekome. Enɛ haa jwɛi lɛ fiteɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops turn weak and discolored when weeds are left to grow around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛhe su tsakeɔ kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Overgrown weeds compete heavily with your crops for soil nutrients and block sunlight, leaving your crops malnourished and too weak to maintain healthy leaves.
ga: Jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la naa. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ náaa niyenii kpakpa ni egbɔjɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crop yields improve when the ground surrounding them is kept completely clean?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akwɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: A clean farm reduces pests and diseases while allowing your crops to absorb all available soil food, helping them direct all their energy into producing healthy harvests.
ga: Okwaafoi ni mli tse lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai baa shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛheɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to apply fertilizer to my crops if they are already growing in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛji amɛmiidara yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli momo?

english: Soil loses its natural nutrients over time, and fertilizer acts as extra food that feeds your crops so they can grow strong, stay healthy, and produce maximum yields.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni haa onibii lɛ hewalɛ. Bɔni afee ni amɛdara waa Hiɛ shi jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ nibii ni anáa kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ aha

english: How does applying fertilizer to my plants help them fight off pests and sickness?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mitsei lɛ amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwuɔ amɛshiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai?

english: Properly nourished crops develop stronger stems and leaves, making them tough enough to resist insect attacks and recover better from plant diseases.
ga: Tsei ni ayeɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ feɔ amɛshishifãi kɛ baai ni mli wa. Enɛ haa ehe waa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛteɔ shi ewoɔ kooloi ni baatutua lɛ lɛ, ni enáa hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe helai amli.

english: Why is it important that every single plant on my farm gets its share of fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni tso fɛɛ tso ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aná egbɛfaŋnɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: If some plants miss out on fertilizer, they become weak and vulnerable to diseases and pests, which can then easily spread to the rest of your healthy farm.
ga: Kɛji tsei komɛi bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii Ebaafee mɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ atswa lɛ. ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ fãi krokomɛi amli mlɛo.

english: Why are my plantain plants starting to look like they are dying from the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ miibɔi tamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiigboi kɛmiijɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Pests like nkakapɛ often gather at the base of the plantain plant beneath the soil line, attacking the main stem and roots, which causes the entire plant to weaken and look like it is dying.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ kapa buaa amɛhe naa yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashishi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Etutuaa tso wulu lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eegbo.

english: What are the pests that local farmers call nkakapɛ, and how do they affect plantains?
ga: Mɛni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi tsɛɔ lɛ nkakapɛ ni te amɛnáa plantains nɔ hewalɛ amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Nkakapɛ is a local Twi term for pests that cluster around the root base of plantains. They settle underneath the plant and slowly destroy its foundation if left unchecked.
ga: Nkakapɛ ji maŋ lɛ mli Twi wiemɔ ni tsɔɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni buaa ehe naa yɛ plantains shishi. Amɛhiɔ tsei lɛ ashishi ni amɛdaraa fiofio. Efiteɔ eshishitoo lɛ kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Where should I check on my plantain plant if I suspect insects are attacking it?
ga: Nɛgbɛ esa akɛ makwɛ mi plantains lɛ kɛji misusuɔ akɛ kooloi bibii miitutua amɛ?

english: You should inspect the very base of the plantain stem right near the ground level, as pests prefer to gather underground or beneath the weeds at the plant's foundation.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ plantain lɛ shishigbɛ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai sumɔɔ ni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi loo jwɛi ashishi yɛ tsei lɛ ashishi.

english: How does clearing weeds around the base of my plantain help keep pests away?
ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle mi lɛ ajiemɔ Te mi plantain shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote mli aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Clearing all weeds directly around the plant stem destroys the shady, moist environment where pests like to hide, effectively delaying them from invading the plantain.
ga: Jiemɔ jwɛi fɛɛ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ. Tsoi ni yɔɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fiteɔ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ. Biɛ ji he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai sumɔɔ ni amɛtee amɛhe yɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛsɛɛ tsɛɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkatutua plantains lɛ.

english: Why do weeds growing right next to my plantain stem attract pests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantain tsei lɛ ahe lɛ gbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai?

english: Weeds near the plant's base provide cover and shelter for pests, giving them a safe place to stay and multiply before moving onto the plantain itself.
ga: Jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ shishi lɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ he ko ni amɛhiɔ. Enɛ haa amɛnáa he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni amɛhiɔ ni amɛfɔɔ bii dani amɛfãa kɛyaa plantains lɛ anɔ.

english: What simple maintenance step can I take to delay pests from attacking my plantains?
ga: Mibaanyɛ makwɛ nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛsaa lɛ anɔ. Mɛni mafee koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akatutua mi plantains lɛ?

english: Regularly weeding the ground directly around the base of each plantain plant prevents pests from establishing themselves around the roots.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ plantain tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishi lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Will digging or turning the soil around my plantains bring pests to my crop?
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ ni akuɔ loo atsakeɔ Ani dumɔwui kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Turning the soil disturbs the ground and can eventually attract soil pests to the area, though keeping the base weed-free helps manage their impact.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oootsake lɛ baagbala shikpɔŋ lɛ naa, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, ebaagbala shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi kɛba jɛmɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ shishitoo lɛ ni jwɛi bɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni akwɛ nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ nɔ moŋ.

english: Why do my older plantain trees seem to get pests under them more than new ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mi plantain momo lɛ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo yɛ shishi fe nɔ hee lɛ?

english: When a plantain stays in the ground for a long time, pests have more time to naturally gather and build up colonies underneath the base of the plant.
ga: Kɛji akɛ plantains lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baaná be babaoo ni amɛkɛbua amɛhe naa ni amɛfee adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii yɛ tso lɛ shishi.

english: How can I prevent soil insects from settling under my plantain roots over time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi sũ mli ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkamɔ mi plantain shishifãi lɛ ashishi yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Ensure the soil surface around the stem is kept clean and free of overgrown weeds so pests cannot easily hide beneath the base of the plant.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ afee faŋŋ. Tso lɛ mli tse ni jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine bɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ewa aha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akɛ amɛaahi tso lɛ shishi.

english: What causes pests to gather underneath a plantain plant near the ground?
ga: Mɛni haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ dumɔwui ashishi ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Pests are drawn to the base of the plantain because of the shelter, moisture, and undisturbed cover provided by weeds and long-standing soil conditions.
