ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ heɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii ni abaanyɛ ahé lɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my yams so they store well without rotting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii? Koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ ni efiteee

english: Yams are mature and ready for harvest when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and dry up. Harvesting at this stage ensures the tubers have fully formed skin and will store for months.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ eda ni amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ hewolo ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he, ni ebaahi shi nyɔji babaoo.

english: How do I know if my crops need fertilizer, and what actually happens to them when I apply it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni mɛni baa nakai tsei lɛ anɔ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo amɛmli?

english: When crops lack food in the soil, their leaves often turn pale green or yellow, and their growth slows down. Fertilizer works like food for the crop, giving it essential nutrients that help it build strong roots, produce green leaves, and yield bigger fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei bɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. ni dalɛ baafee mlɛo Fertilizer nitsumɔi tamɔ tsei niyenii. Ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi ni wa lɛ maa shi. ha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni ekɛ yibii wuji aba

english: Why do my crops dry up or burn when I put too much fertilizer around their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ loo amɛshãa kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Putting too much fertilizer close to a crop draws water out of the roots, causing the plant to dry out and look burned. Fertilizer should always be applied a few inches away from the stem and in the right amounts so the roots can drink water normally.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ, ebaagbala nu kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbiɔ ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli inchii fioo komɛi kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi, ni akɛwo mli bɔ ni sa bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu nu lɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Can animal manure work as well as chemical fertilizer to feed my crops?
ga: Ani kooloi ashishifã baanyɛ atsu nii tamɔ bɔ ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni akɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ niyenii?

english: Yes, animal manure feeds crops while also improving the soil's ability to hold water for a long time. While chemical fertilizers feed the crop quickly, manure releases its nutrients slowly and keeps the soil healthy for future seasons.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii haa ŋmɔshi nibii niyenii yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ hu. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ nii oya moŋ, shi ŋmɔshi nibii jieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ blɛoo. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: How do chemical sprays protect my crops from insects and diseases?
ga: Te tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nibii anɔ lɛ baanyɛ abu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ kooloi kɛ helai ahe aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Chemical sprays coat the leaves to stop pests from eating them or treat plant sicknesses caused by fungi and bacteria. They act like medicine for crops to prevent harmful insects from destroying the harvest.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ koni kooloi akaye amɛ loo koni akɛtsa tsei ahe helai ni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛbaa lɛ. Amɛtsuɔ nii tamɔ tsofa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii koni kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why is it bad to spray my crops with pest chemicals right before it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ baashwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ dani nugbɔ anɛ lɛ?

english: Rain washes the chemical off the leaves before the plant can absorb it or before pests touch it. Spraying on clear, calm days ensures the chemical stays on the leaves long enough to do its job.
ga: Nugbɔ shwieɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ baai amli lɛ ahe dani tsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ gbi ni mli tse ni eyɛ kpoo lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsofai lɛ ahi baai lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛtsu amɛnitsumɔ lɛ.

english: Why do some insects destroy my crop leaves while others do not cause any damage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi komɛi fiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai ni ekrokomɛi hu fiteee lɛ?

english: Insects behave differently; pests eat leaves and stems for food, while beneficial insects like ladybugs eat those pests. Understanding which insects are pests helps you spray only when necessary to protect your crop.
ga: Esoro bɔ ni kooloi feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa. Kooloi yeɔ baai kɛ tsei lɛ anɔ. Yɛ be mli ni kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ladybugs yeɔ nakai kooloi lɛ. Kɛ́ onu tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fɔɔ baa lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni okɛ tsofa lɛ ashwie nɔ pɛ kɛji ehe miihia koni okɛbu onibii ahe.

english: What is the difference for my crops if I use organic methods instead of factory chemicals?
ga: Te miŋmɔshi nii lɛ baafee srɔto aha tɛŋŋ kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ nitsumɔhe lɛ tsu nii moŋ fe tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ nitsumɔhe lɛ?

english: Organic methods use natural materials like plant compost and manure to build long-term soil health and protect crops gently, whereas factory chemicals give fast results but do not improve the long-term quality of the soil.
ga: Organic gbɛi lɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛma shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni amɛbu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe blɛoo. Yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ haa nɔ ko baa oya lɛ, amɛhaaa sũ lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I plant beans alongside my maize instead of maize alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa masɛi moŋ fe ŋmãa pɛ?

english: Beans and legumes pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which naturally feeds neighboring crops like maize and helps prevent pests from spreading quickly across a single crop field.
ga: Beans kɛ legumes jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa tsɛŋemɔ helai akagbɛ ashwã ŋmɔshi nibii kome mli oya.

english: How does using a machine to plow my land help my crops grow better than clearing by hand?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔne ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe bɔ ni mikɛ niji tsuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii lɛ?

english: Plowing machines break up hard, compacted soil deep underground, making it easy for young crop roots to spread out, breathe, and reach deeper water during dry periods.
ga: Plɔmɔi gbálaa shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ashishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa, amɛmuɔ ni amɛshɛɔ nu mli shɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Why do my seeds sprout at different times when I plant them at different depths in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ srɔtoi lɛ?

english: Seeds buried too deep spend all their energy struggling to push through the soil, while seeds planted too shallow dry out in the sun. Planting all seeds at the same shallow depth helps them sprout evenly at the same time.
ga: Dumɔwui ni afu amɛ tsɔ lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni adu yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ baagbi yɛ hulu lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be kome mli.

english: Why is it better for me to harvest my tomatoes early in the morning instead of during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ makpa tomato leebi moŋ fe shwane lɛ?

english: Harvesting in the cool morning helps the crop retain water and stay firm. Harvesting under hot afternoon sun causes fruits to lose moisture quickly, leading to faster wilting and spoilage before they reach the market.
ga: Nikpamɔ yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli ni amɛkwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nikpamɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ haa aduawai lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya dani amɛshɛɔ jara nɔ.

english: How can I prevent my harvested cassava roots from going bad and turning dark within just a few days?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ni amɛkawo duŋ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ mli?

english: Cassava begins to deteriorate quickly once removed from the soil because air enters the cuts. Storing harvested cassava roots in cool shade or burying them in moist soil/sawdust temporarily slows down oxidation and keeps them fresh for market.
ga: Kasava jeɔ shishi efiteɔ oya kɛji ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ he ni afo lɛ mli. Okɛ ŋmei shishifãi ni akpa lɛ ato he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ loo ofu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ/sawdust mli. Ehaa oksideshin lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ be kukuoo ko, ni ehaa efeɔ ehee kɛha jarayeli.

english: Why do my garden eggs soften and turn yellow so quickly after I harvest them and prepare them for sale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ blɛoo oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ beni mikpa amɛ ni misaa amɛ koni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Garden eggs continue to ripen rapidly if they are exposed to sunlight or heat after picking. Keeping them in cool shade and covering them with wet jute sacks preserves their firmness and desirable bright color.
ga: Abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛshwereɔ oya kɛji akɛ hulu la loo dɔlɛ shɛ amɛnɔ yɛ be mli ni abua naa lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ okɛto he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ ni okɛ jute kotokui ni efɔ lɛ ha nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehi shi shiŋŋ ni ehiɛ sui ni kpɛɔ ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ amli.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains mold even after I leave them out in the sun to dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii beni mikɛ amɛ egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli po lɛ?

english: Drying grains directly on the bare ground allows soil moisture to seep back into them at night. Spreading grains on clean tarpaulins or elevated platforms ensures proper airflow and complete moisture removal, preventing mold growth.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ni agbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ eboteɔ mli gbɛkɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ ni agbɛɔ ashwãa tarp ni he tse loo kpoku ni awo nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kwraa. Etsiɔ fungal dalɛ naa

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up tight like pencils during the hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ pensil yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a defense mechanism. Maize leaves curl up in strong heat to reduce their surface area exposed to the sun, preventing excessive water loss until temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he. Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ dɔlɛ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Tsi nu ni hoɔ fe nine lɛ naa kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off instead of turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or heavy nitrogen fertilizing. Ensuring consistent watering and shade helps the plant hold its flowers and set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he. Nu kɛ hulutsoo ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi kɛ eyibii lɛ amli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my crop turning yellow and dying during periods of heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water in flooded soil fills all air spaces, effectively suffocating the roots. Without oxygen, roots cannot absorb nutrients from the soil, causing the lower leaves to turn yellow from nitrogen deficiency.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ he fɛɛ he. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛji oxygen bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nitrogen ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: What happens to my plantains if I plant them too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi plantains lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: Planting too close causes crops to shade each other and fight for soil nutrients. This competition leads to thin stems, longer growing times, and smaller bunch sizes.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ amɛhe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa anáa tsei bibii. Dalɛ be kakadaŋŋ kɛ kuu bibioo dalɛ

english: Why do my yam leaves get dark spots and wither before the yam tuber has fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Dark spots on yam leaves are typically caused by fungal diseases like leaf spot or anthracrosis, which thrive in humid conditions and stop the leaves from making food for the growing tuber.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ baa mli ŋmɔtɔ loo anthracrosis ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ shwereɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ, ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ niyenii kɛhaa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: How can I tell the exact right time to harvest my maize for fresh eating versus drying for grain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa koni aye ehee kɛ be ni esa akɛ agbi kɛha ŋmãa?

english: For fresh roasting or boiling, harvest when the silks turn dark brown and kernels release milky fluid when pressed. For dry grain, wait until the stalks turn completely yellow brown and the kernels become hard.
ga: Kɛha shãa hee loo shãa Kpamɔ be mli ni siliki lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ni dumɔwui lɛ jieɔ nu ni tamɔ mliki kɛji akɛ anyɛ amɛnɔ. kɛha dumɔwui ni egbi Mɛɛ kɛyashi tso lɛ shishifã lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ-ŋmɔŋ kwraa ni dumɔwui lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when the plants are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for leaf growth. It can also happen when heavy rains flood the soil, preventing the plant roots from breathing and taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop most of their leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Shedding leaves is cassava's natural way of protecting itself from drought. By dropping leaves, the plant reduces moisture loss through evaporation and conserves energy to keep the roots alive underground until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ ŋmei he kɛjɛɔ hɔmɔ he. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni eshwieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni elaajeɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. ni amɛto hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ pepper ko baaa lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers usually drop due to high heat stress, extreme dryness, or applying too much nitrogen fertilizer. When the weather is too hot or water is scarce, the plant discards its flowers to save energy for survival.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hulutsoo ni naa wa, loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ mli baa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo nu faaa Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl up during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes can be a self-defense mechanism against intense heat and sunlight to prevent water loss. However, if the leaves remain tightly curled and yellowed permanently, it is often caused by a virus transmitted by whitefly insects.
ga: Tomato baa lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la he koni nu akafite. Shi, kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tee nɔ amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ daa lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa.

english: Is it beneficial to plant cowpeas together with my maize on the same land?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ aaadu tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ he kome?

english: Yes, intercropping cowpeas with maize improves soil fertility. Cowpeas gather nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil to nourish the maize, while their broad leaves cover the ground to stop weed growth and keep soil moist.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ yaa hiɛ. Cowpeas buaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa lɛ aná hewalɛ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni jwɛi akakwɛ̃ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why is it harmful to plant my crops too close to one another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Planting crops too close creates competition for sunlight, soil nutrients, and ground moisture, leading to thin and weak stems. It also limits airflow between plants, creating a damp environment where fungal diseases spread rapidly.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ kɛ akaŋshii baa kɛha hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ sũ mli ŋmɔtɔ Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ tsei ateŋ lɛ hu baa shi. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take a very long time to produce fruit after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani mi dumɔwui lɛ woɔ yibii beni midu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers grow slowly if they are planted in poor soil, during dry weather, or if the parent sucker was weak. They require constant moisture, organic mulch, and rich nutrients to establish strong roots before flowering.
ga: Dumɔwui baakwɛ̃ fiofio kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ. Yɛ hulutsoo be mli Aloo kɛji tsɛ tso ni nuɔ nu lɛ bɛ hewalɛ Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be fɛɛ be. organic mulch kɛ niyenii babaoo ni haa shishifãi ni wa baa shi dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi

english: How can I easily check if my soil is good for growing vegetables?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana mlɛo akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha aduawai adumɔ?

english: Good agricultural soil is dark in color, crumbles easily in your hands, drains excess water well without drying out too fast, and contains decomposed leaves or manure which supply nutrients to young seedlings.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni akɛtsuɔ okwaayeli he nii lɛ su yɛ ediŋ, efiteɔ oya yɛ nine mli, ni ejieɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni egbiɛɛ oya tsɔ. ni baai loo ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ni haa tsei bibii lɛ niyenii yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing small and crooked instead of large and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee agbo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams become twisted when the soil is hard, stony, or heavily compacted, preventing the tuber from expanding freely underground. Microscopic soil worms called nematodes can also damage the tuber skin and restrict growth.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, tɛi yɔɔ nɔ, loo eyi obɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi amɛha amɛhe. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmeii lɛ ahewolo ni amɛha amɛdalɛ aba shi.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my crops with dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry organic material—known as mulching—keeps the soil cool under direct sunlight, slows water evaporation, suppresses weed growth, and eventually rots to enrich the soil naturally.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo. Tsi jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni yɛ naagbee lɛ amɛfite koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when I clear all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. Big shade trees act as living umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and protecting young cocoa from scorching until they grow strong.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe koni ekashã kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa waa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient that gives plants their green color and the strength to grow big leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni eyɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaa baa wuji.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans make my soil better for other crops later?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha tsei krokomɛi yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Groundnuts and beans pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, that nitrogen stays in the soil as natural food for your next crops.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when the rains become too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits around the roots without draining, it suffocates them and causes fungal rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ kpɛtɛ shishifãi ahe ni nu efooo Enɛ baaha mɔ agbɔjɔ ni eha ŋmɔtɔ agbo.

english: Why is it risky to plant my crop seeds right before a dry week even if I water them once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu dumɔwui dani otsi ni nu bɛ lɛ aba lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu wo mli shikome pɛ moŋ.

english: Once a seed starts sprouting underground, it needs continuous moisture to stay alive. If the soil dries out completely, the delicate young sprout dies before roots can reach deeper water.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ Esa akɛ ená ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be bɔni afee ni ehi shi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baagboi dani shishifãi lɛ ashɛ nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers without growing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi shi amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: When tomato plants experience severe heat or lack of water, they drop their flowers to conserve energy and survive, rather than spending resources on producing fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tomato tsei lɛ kɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu bɛ lɛ, Ebaafɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he ni ehi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baatsu nii koni ekɛwo yibii

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes next to my yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tso tso fɔ̃ɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Lifting yam leaves off the ground with stakes allows them to catch more sunlight and fresh air, helping the plant make more food to swell and grow large tubers underground.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tso wo sweet potato baai anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa hulu la babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni efeɔ niyenii babaoo ni ekɛfutuɔ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my crops grow smaller and weaker when I leave weeds in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ mishi jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive competitors that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer from the soil, leaving fewer resources for your main crops to grow well.
ga: Jwɛi ji akaŋshilɔi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nibii fioo pɛ ashiɔ koni onibii titrii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I avoid planting maize on the exact same piece of land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ he yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be mli lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously in one spot drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and soil diseases to multiply year after year.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ tsei pɔtɛɛ anɔ lɛ koni amɛfɔ afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why do my maize plants produce smaller cobs if I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded together, their roots and leaves compete with each other for space, light, and water, leaving less energy for each plant to develop full-sized cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná he ko, la, kɛ nu, ni no haa tso fɛɛ tso náaa hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛbaafee ŋmei ni dalɛ fɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing on lower leaves usually means your maize is starving for nitrogen, a key nutrient for green leaf growth. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen out of the soil, so applying fertilizer like NPK or urea at the right time supplies the foliage with the nutrients it needs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo urea wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni ená niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off before turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when soil moisture fluctuates wildly. Extreme heat prevents proper pollination, so watering consistently and providing partial shade during the dry season helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ waa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ tsiɔ pollination naa. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be fioo lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: How do I know when my cassava is ready to harvest so it does not rot?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa koni egboko?

english: Most local cassava varieties mature between 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop. Leaving tubers in waterlogged soil too long after maturity causes wet root rot, so harvesting on time keeps the tubers firm and healthy.
ga: Kuu lɛ mli ŋmeii srɔtoi lɛ ateŋ babaoo daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ. Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ ashi bulb lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ amɛdalɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akpa yɛ be naa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: What is eating small ragged holes into the young central leaves of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli lɛ yeli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central funnel of the maize plant to feed on fresh growth. Inspecting plants early and applying safe control measures directly into the plant funnel stops them before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye ŋmeii heei ni eda lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Akwɛ tsei lɛ amli mra ni akɛ gbɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛkwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ atsu nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli. Ehaa nakai tsei lɛ kpaa nitsumɔ dani amɛfiteɔ he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it better to grow my yams on high soil mounds rather than flat land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmeii yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, deep soil to expand into large, straight tubers. Mounding loosens the dirt, allows excess rainwater to drain away so the tubers do not rot, and makes harvesting much easier.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli ejɔ koni ekwɛ̃ ni etsɔ bulbs agboi ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ. Muji ni abua naa lɛ baajie muji. Ehaa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. koni ekafite Ni ehaa ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: What causes the leaves of my pepper plants to curl up and wrinkle?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites sucking plant juices from under the leaves, or by viral diseases spread by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early prevents leaf damage and keeps the plant growing normally.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa ji kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ tso mli nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebaatsi baai lɛ afitemɔ naa ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni eda bɔ ni sa.

english: Why is a weed with purple flowers making my maize stay short and stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni fɔɔ fɔfɔi purple lɛ miiha mi-ŋmã lɛ efee kuku ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: This weed is likely Striga, also known as witchweed, which attaches its roots directly to your maize roots to steal water and food. Rotating your field with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas helps reduce Striga seeds in the soil over time.
ga: Ekolɛ jwɛi nɛɛ ji Striga, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ witchweed. ni kɛ eshishifãi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ ŋmãa shishifãi ahe tɛ̃ɛ koni eju nu kɛ niyenii. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii atsake nibii ni odu lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni Striga dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Is it safe to plant my seeds right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Planting after the very first rain is risky because it is often followed by a long dry spell that bakes seeds in the soil. It is safer to wait until the rains become regular so the soil stays moist enough for seeds to germinate and grow.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ ni shãa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ bɔ ni sa koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛdara.

english: How does adding decomposed animal manure help my crops survive dry spells?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo ni akɛfataa he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi amli?

english: Decomposed manure acts like a sponge in the soil, holding onto rainwater and moisture longer so plant roots do not dry out quickly. It also slowly releases essential nutrients into the ground as crops grow.
ga: Muji ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Ehiɛɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ No hewɔ lɛ tso shishifãi lɛ akagbi oya. Ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa hu kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fiofio be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains or cassava next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui loo ŋmei yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under full sun. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains provides temporary shade to shield the cocoa from intense heat while keeping the surrounding soil cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko baa koni ebu kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape pattern?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually means the plant lacks nitrogen. When nitrogen in the soil is low, the maize plant moves whatever nitrogen it has from its old bottom leaves up to nourish the young top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Abele tsei lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni amɛyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with heavy leafy stems but yield small underground tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa lɛ, ni eyɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni mli tse, shi eyɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or stems are not pruned, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of sending food down to expand the tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo afolɔɔɔ tsei lɛ ahe. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ baatsu niyenii kɛya shi koni ekɛwo ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines with tall wooden poles instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ atswa mi-sweet potato tso lɛ he adafi lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves into the sunlight so they can catch direct light to make food for the tuber. It also keeps the leaves dry and off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ woɔ hulu la lɛ mli koni amɛnyɛ amɛmɔmɔ la tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkɛha bulb lɛ niyenii. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebaa lɛ haa egbiɔ ni ehiɛɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Tsi fungal helai anaa

english: Why should I cut off extra suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ plantain tsei titrii lɛ.

english: If too many suckers grow around one plant stem, they compete for water and nutrients from the soil. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, resulting in larger plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ, tso kome Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha ŋmeii wuji aba.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas in my farm make the soil richer for next season's maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa ni baaba yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that work with soil bacteria to capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do the blossoms on my pepper plants keep falling off without turning into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Flower drop happens when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of pollinators like bees. The plant drops its flowers to survive when conditions are unfavorable for bearing fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi yɛ be ni sa mli loo kooloi ni haa ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii baa lɛ ni bɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni esaaa akɛ amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and droop during hot afternoons even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu ha amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In intense midday heat, leaves lose moisture into the air faster than the roots can drink it up. Curling up is a defense mechanism to reduce leaf surface area exposed to the sun and save water.
ga: Yɛ shwane gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Curling ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ mɔ he koni akɛba baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi, ni akɛbuɔ nu he.

english: Why is it risky to sow my maize seeds right after the very first rain of the major season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be ni he hiaa lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long dry stretch before main rains start. If you sow immediately, seeds may germinate and then dry up and die from a lack of continuous rain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔi wuji lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛji odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ Dumɔwui baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbi ni amɛgboi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my young crop seedlings turn pale and stop growing so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha midumɔwui bibii lɛ miifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ oya nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients faster than young crop seedlings can. Clearing weeds early gives your crops exclusive access to food and light.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni dumɔwui bibii baanyɛ afee. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii kɛ la kroko.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they get full sunlight and prevents damp soil diseases from spreading to the plant.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la koni amɛná niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo aba, ni ehaaa helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ agbɛ ashwã tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Akɛni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ hewɔ lɛ

english: When maize seeds are planted too close, the plants compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of growing thick stems and big cobs, they spend all their energy stretching upward to reach the sun.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ tsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii wuji. Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛyashɛ hulu lɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop their leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baa shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves in dry weather as a survival strategy to conserve water. By shedding leaves, the plant stops losing moisture into the hot air and keeps its water and energy stored safely underground in the tubers until rain returns.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli akɛ shihilɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ nu he. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ akafite ŋmɔtɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. ni akɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe yɛ yitso lɛ mli kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow when my field gets flooded with rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nu eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air to breathe just as much as they need water. When water stays pooled in your field, it drowns the roots, preventing them from taking up essential nutrients like nitrogen from the soil, which turns the leaves yellow.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni tso shishifãi hu he hiaa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. kɛ nu he hiamɔ Kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, ni no haaa amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni no haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why are my pepper plant leaves curling upward during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl inward during extreme heat to reduce the leaf area exposed to the sun and slow down water loss. However, if they stay curled even in cool mornings, it usually means tiny pests like mites are sucking juice from the leaves.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ latsaa be mli koni ekɛba baa lɛ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi ni ekɛ nu ni hoɔ oya lɛ aba shi. Shi, kɛji amɛfo amɛhe yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ miitso po lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii miinu nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa adu tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to a family of plants that can capture nitrogen food from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them with maize naturally feeds the soil, helping your maize grow stronger without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas fata tsei ni baanyɛ aŋɔ nitrogen nibii ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ahe ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahe. Abɛi ni akɛ abele duɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua oŋmei lɛ ni ehiɛ wa ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa awo mli.

english: Why does my farmland soil turn hard and crusty after I harvest my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ beni mikpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil becomes hard when it lacks decayed leaves or manure and is left bare under the hot sun. Leaving crop remains on the ground or mixing in compost keeps the soil moist, soft, and easy for new roots to grow through.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ ebaa bɛ mli loo ŋmeii ni fiteɔ. ni ashi lɛ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ oshi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ loo okɛfutu ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni efee mlɛo ni shishifãi heei baatsɔ mli.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering. When the soil dries out completely and then gets flooded, or when daytime temperature is too high, the plant drops its flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ, nu eyi mli obɔ. aloo kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot on the tree during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that breeds in damp, cool, and shady conditions. During heavy rains, water splashes fungal spores onto the cocoa pods, causing them to rot quickly if the trees are not pruned to let air and light in.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni fɔɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni mli ejɔ, kɛ hulutsoo be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa. Nu lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii amli ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgboiɔ oya kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ tsei lɛ anɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la abote mli.

english: Why is it bad to harvest my cassava immediately after a heavy rain following a long drought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ abaakpa ŋmei amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa yɛ hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When rain falls after a long dry spell, the cassava plant rapidly absorbs water and uses its underground root reserves to grow new leaves. Harvesting right then results in watery tubers with low starch that spoil quickly after digging.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, Yucca tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni amɛkɛ amɛshishifãi ni amɛto yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai heei. Kɛ́ akpa amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nu, ni starch faaa yɛ mli lɛ baa, ni amɛfiteɔ oya kɛ́ atsa amɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to grow leaves and stay green. Applying fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure will supply nitrogen and restore their healthy color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaakwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen afata he ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does spread dry grass around my vegetable beds help my crops survive hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or dry leaves, called mulching, shields the soil from direct sunlight. This keeps the root area cool, traps moisture in the ground longer, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egboi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither when I clear away all the big trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to intense, direct sunlight. Shade trees or food crops like plantain act like umbrellas, protecting young seedlings from heat damage and helping the soil retain soil moisture.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo niyenii tsei tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Buu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fiteɔ amɛ lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot as soon as the heavy rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shɛ pɛ?

english: This rot is caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod. High humidity, heavy rain droplets splashing fungus onto the pods, and dense canopy shade without enough airflow create the ideal conditions for the disease to spread.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpod kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Fɛ̃i ni mli wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. kɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli ewo muji ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa baa kɛha helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground if I do not harvest them before heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ akpaaa amɛ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Too much water standing in the soil cuts off air to the roots. When cassava roots stay submerged in waterlogged soil for too long, they begin to suffocate and rot.
ga: Nu babaoo ni tsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ aŋɔ ŋmei shishifãi awo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔlɔ ni amɛbaagboi.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes for my yam plants to climb as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei awo mi sweet potato tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛkwɔ nɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to sunlight to create food for the growing tuber under the ground. Staking keeps the leaves off damp soil, prevents leaf diseases, and ensures maximum sunlight reaches the leaves.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsi baa helai anaa ni oha hulu la lɛ ashɛ baa lɛ he bɔ ni abaanyɛ

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into the inner leaves of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that burrows into the center whorl of young maize plants to feed on new leaves. They need to be identified early so appropriate pest control methods can be applied.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli koni amɛye baai heei. Ehe miihia ni ana enɛ mra. Bɔni afee ni anyɛ akɛ gbɛi ni sa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atsu nii.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like aphids, thrips, or whiteflies, which damage the leaves and can also spread crop viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Enɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ helai hu eshwa tso lɛ mli.

english: Why are the blossoms falling off my tomato plants without setting any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the plant experiences stress, such as very high daytime temperatures, irregular watering, or a lack of pollinators to fertilize the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ hulutsoo be mli latsaa ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ fɔmɔ nii baa lɛ ni bɛ

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when they start carrying heavy bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ebɔi ŋmeii wuji shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that do not anchor deeply in the soil. Soil pests like nematodes or root borers can also damage the roots, making the heavy tree collapse under wind or heavy fruit weight.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi tamɔ nematodes loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ Ebaanyɛ efite shishifãi lɛ hu. Ha tsei ni tsii lɛ agbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ loo aduawai ni tsii hewɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani akpa kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Leaves turn yellow mainly due to a lack of nitrogen in the soil or poor watering. Nitrogen feeds the plant to keep leaves green; when soil lacks nitrogen, the plant moves nutrients from older leaves to feed new growth, causing the lower leaves to yellow.
ga: Nitrogen ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ titri lɛ baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. Nitrogen haa tsei niyenii koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli. Beni nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ jieɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni amɛkɛha tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings keep dying when I plant them in an open field under full sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ hulutsoo be shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are like small children and cannot survive intense heat. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or cassava shields young cocoa from direct sunlight until their roots are deep enough to handle full heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii tamɔ gbekɛbii bibii ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains loo cassava lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ amli baawo mli bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: What causes small holes in my pepper leaves, and how can I fix it?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ pepper baai amli lɛ baa ni te abaafee tɛŋŋ asaa amɛ?

english: Holes in leaves are usually caused by insects like caterpillars or beetles chewing on them. Spraying a mixture of crushed neem leaves mixed with water is a safe way to drive pests away without damaging the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ baai amli lɛ baa. Neem baai ni atswa ni akɛ nu efutu mli lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ he ni efiteee tso lɛ.

english: How do I know if my tomato plants are getting too much water during the rainy season?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ o-tomato tsei lɛ miiná nu babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Too much water causes tomato leaves to droop, turn yellow, and drop off, while the roots rot under soggy soil. Wet conditions also cause fungal diseases that create dark spots on the leaves.
ga: Nu babaoo baaha tomato baai lɛ agbɔjɔ. Amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi, yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni efɔ lɛ mli. Shihilɛ ni mli efɔ lɛ hu kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why is my farm producing fewer crops now than it did five years ago, even though I use the same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ miiwo ŋmɔshi nibii fioo fe afii enumɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii moŋ.

english: Soil loses its richness over time when crops pull nutrients out season after season. Resting the land, rotating different crops, or adding organic manure helps rebuild the soil's strength so it can feed plants again.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei jieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛtsɔɔ bei lɛ amli, amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe, ni amɛtsakeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Aloo organic fertilizer ni akɛbaafata he lɛ baaye abua ni etswa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni enyɛ eye ebua tsei ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad to plant my maize seeds very close together in the same row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa kome mli lɛ ehiii lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Spacing them properly ensures every plant gets enough space to form large, healthy ears of corn.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmãa toi agboi ni wa baakwɛ̃.

english: Can I plant cowpeas together with my maize in the same farm, and will it help?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa afee ekome yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli? No hewɔ lɛ, ani ebaaye ebua loo eyeŋ ebuaaa?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize helps your soil. Cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which acts as a free natural fertilizer for your maize plants.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, cowpeas ni akɛ ŋmãa baadu lɛ baanyɛ aye abua oshikpɔŋ lɛ. Cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa o-corn tsei lɛ.

english: Why do buyers in the market offer me low prices for my cassava tubers even when they look big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayelɔi ni heɔ nii lɛ kɛ jara ni baa shi haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara moŋ?

english: Buyers look at internal starch quality and freshness, not just size. If cassava stays in the ground too long, it becomes woody, watery, or develops dark lines inside, making it poor for making gari or flour.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kwɛɔ bɔ ni ashikiŋsha lɛ hi ha kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ehee ha. Jeee bɔ ni edara ha lɛ pɛ he ewieɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmei hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaatsɔ tso, nu, loo ebaana ŋmeii ni tsuɔ yɛ emli. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ akɛbaatsu nii yɛ ashikishaŋ loo ashikishaŋ mli.

english: How can I tell the exact right time to harvest my yam tubers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yams are ready for harvesting when the above-ground leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and begin to dry up. This signal shows that the tuber has finished growing and storing food.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Okadi nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ egbe naa ni niyenii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ egbe naa.

english: Why are my harvested maize grains spoiling and rotting quickly inside storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya ni egboɔ yɛ kotokui ni akɛtoɔ nii amli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Grains spoil quickly if they are bagged while still carrying moisture, which creates heat and attracts mold and insects. Sun-drying grains until they are hard and crack cleanly between your teeth prevents spoilage during storage.
ga: Ŋmaa fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ awo kotoku mli ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lolo. Enɛ haa dɔlɛ baa ni egbalaa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii. Gbimɔ ŋmaa lɛ aahu kɛyashi ebaawa ni egbɛ eshwa ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ koni ekafite yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: How long will it take for my newly planted cocoa trees to start bearing fruits?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani mi-cacao tso ni midu ehee lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties in Ghana usually start producing pods within 2 to 3 years after planting, whereas older traditional cocoa trees take about 4 to 5 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo tsei ni akɛfutuɔ nii yɛ Ghana lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ, yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo tsei ni etsɛ fe tsutsu lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 4 kɛyashi 5.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants dry up and turn brown during the sunny months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nyɔji ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and cannot survive under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them provides shade and moisture to keep young leaves from burning.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛ nyɛɛɛ ahi shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ Emasɛi lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba koni baa bibii lɛ akashã.

english: Why do many tiny white flowers appear on my cocoa tree trunk but end up dropping off without making pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii yɛŋ lɛ babaoo jeɔ kpo yɛ kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Shi yɛ naagbee lɛ, egbeeɔ shi ni efeee pod?

english: Cocoa trees produce thousands of flowers, but only tiny midges (insects) can pollinate them. Unpollinated flowers drop off naturally, and trees also shed excess flowers if they do not have enough water or nutrients.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi kooloi bibii pɛ yɔɔ jɛmɛ. Amɛ pɛ ji mɛi ni baanyɛ afee pollin. Fɔfɔi ni pollin bɛ mli lɛ baagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Ni tsei hu jieɔ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine kɛji nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli.

english: Why do some of my very small cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ Mɛni hewɔ minɔ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbo dani eda lɛ?

english: This is often caused by 'cherelle wilt,' a natural process where the tree sheds excess young pods it cannot afford to feed, though damp conditions can also cause fungal infections that dry out tiny pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ‘cherelle wilt’, ni ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni tsei shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aha amɛ niyenii lɛ. Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ po baanyɛ aha tsɛŋemɔ hela ko aba ni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ agbiɔ.

english: What causes my green cocoa pods to suddenly develop large dark brown spots during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔi wuji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a water-loving fungus. Rain splashes spread the fungus onto pods, especially when farms are too shady or overgrown with weeds.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji ŋmeii ni sumɔɔ nu Nugbɔ gbɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ eshwaa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ewo ŋmɔlɔ tsɔ loo jwɛi eyi mli obɔ.

english: Why are the young branches on my cocoa trees drying out and turning black at the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ egbi ni amɛmiitsɔ ediŋŋ yɛ amɛnaa lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by capsids (mirid insects) that suck sap from soft shoots, leaving open wounds that cause the ends of branches to die back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, capsids (myrid kooloi) ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Shi pilamɔi ni agbele ni haa tso lɛ nine lɛ naa gboɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off extra sucker branches growing from the base of my cocoa tree trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: These sucker branches (chupons) steal nutrients, water, and sunlight from the main food-producing branches, lowering overall pod yields if left unchecked.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ tsei niji titri ni feɔ niyenii lɛ amli. Enɛ haa pod yibiiwoo lɛ fɛɛ baa shi kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad to chop cocoa pods directly off the bark with a sharp cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ akɛ tsɔne ni mli wa baafolɔ kookoo ŋmeii kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chopping pods directly off damages the flower cushion on the tree trunk. Once a cushion is injured, flowers and future pods cannot grow from that spot again.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaafite fɔfɔi lɛ akushin ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Kɛji akɛ kushɛŋ lɛ ye awui lɛ Wɔsɛɛ be fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii nyɛŋ adara kɛjɛ nakai he lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I pick cocoa pods while they are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mifoɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ?

english: Unripe green pods have flat, under-developed beans with low sugar content, which prevents proper fermentation and results in poor-quality, bitter cocoa beans.
ga: Pods eŋɔli ni edako lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni edako ni sugar fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli. ni tsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa naa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ ni ehiii kwraa baa.

english: Why do I need to cover my fresh cocoa beans with plantain leaves for several days after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ plantain baai haa kookoo yibii heei anɔ gbii babaoo yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Covering wet beans with plantain leaves allows heat to build up, starting the fermentation process that develops the dark brown chocolate flavor and aroma.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ plantain baai ha ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo baa. Gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ afeɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi ehaa tsokolate ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ehe ŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my young maize leaves turn light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build green leaves, or that heavy rain has washed the plant food out of the topsoil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo tsei amli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do farmers say planting cowpeas makes the soil richer for the next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛɔ akɛ, kɛ́ adu tsina ŋmei lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants have tiny nodules on their roots filled with beneficial bacteria that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for whatever you plant next.
ga: Cowpea tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. Muawai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ eyi shishifãi lɛ amli obɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do experienced farmers cover the dry ground around their crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛ jwɛi haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni ebɔle amɛnibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (called mulching) blocks the hot sun from drying out the soil, keeps the roots cool, and stops weeds from growing and taking the water.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi baaha Enɛ (ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching) lɛ baaye abua ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkaŋɔ nu.

english: Yam plants are vines that need to lift their leaves up toward the sunlight to make food; without stakes to climb, the leaves stay shaded on the ground and produce very small tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ni esa akɛ ewo ebaa lɛ nɔ koni eha hulu lɛ aje kpo koni efee niyenii. ni ehe ehiaaa ni akwɔ No sɛɛ lɛ, baai lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: Why should I cut off some of the small shoot suckers growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ

english: If too many young suckers grow around the mother plantain, they steal water and nutrients from it, resulting in small, weak bunches. Keeping only two or three shoots gives you big plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwu nyɛ lɛ he lɛ, amɛbaaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, tsei niji lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe waaa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ to lɛ, ebaaha oná plantain tso agbo.

english: Why is it bad practice to plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ ji nifeemɔ gbonyo lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the soil of the specific nutrients maize relies on and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the dirt.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni abɛi damɔ nɔ lɛ ni eha abɛi mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai pɔtɛɛi abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because water fills all the air spaces in the ground, causing the roots to drown and creating a perfect environment for fungal rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu eyi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why is it better for me to water my tomato garden early in the morning rather than at hot midday?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ nu woɔ mi-tomato abɔɔ lɛ mli babaoo leebi fe shwane mli latsaa be mli ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ?

english: Watering at midday causes much of the water to evaporate instantly in the heat before reaching the roots, and droplets left on leaves under intense sunlight can encourage fungal diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ nu lɛ yɛ shwane mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ latsaa be mli dani eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ni nu ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tsei ahe yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ baanyɛ awo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young green cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up on the tree trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji ni mli tse lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fast-spreading fungus that thrives when cocoa trees are planted too close together or kept under too much damp, heavy shade during the rainy season.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛ́ adu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo akɛwo hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ ni mli wa tsɔ shishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why can swamp rice survive submerged in water while my maize plants die if water stays on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋshɔŋ ŋmãa lɛ yɔɔ nu shishi yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ gboi kɛji nu lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ?

english: Swamp rice has special internal passages in its stems and roots that send air down from the surface underwater, whereas maize roots lack these tubes and drown without dry soil air.
ga: Swamp rice yɛ mligbɛ gbɛi krɛdɛɛi yɛ eshishifãi kɛ eshishifãi amli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baa shi kɛjɛɔ nu shishi. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ bɛ nɛkɛ tsɔnei nɛɛ ni amɛshwieɔ nu mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting maize seeds too close together forces the plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. When they compete, they grow thin and weak, producing very small cobs or no grain at all.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Kɛ amɛmiitswa akaŋ lɛ Amɛfeɔ shwilafoi ni amɛhe waaa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii waa baa loo dumɔwui ko kwraa bɛ mli.

english: Why do my yam vines need long wooden poles to climb on to give me big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ tsei kakadaŋŋ agboi lɛ? Ni kɛ́ okwɔ koni onine ashɛ yitso agbo nɔ lɛ hu?

english: Yam plants make food in their leaves using sunlight. Climbing up wooden stakes allows the vine leaves to spread out and catch maximum sunlight, which sends more energy down into the ground to build large tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Tso tsei ni akwɔɔ lɛ haa wein tso lɛ baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. ni tsuɔ hewalɛ babaoo kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛfee yitso ni da fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants blossom flowers above the ground but form the nuts under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts lɛ fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ shi ebafeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: After a groundnut flower is pollinated, it grows a special stem called a peg that bends downward and burrows itself into the dirt. The groundnut pod then develops and expands underground where it is protected from heat and pests.
ga: Beni afee ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ sɛɛ lɛ Eyɛ tso krɛdɛɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ peg ni shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shi ni efoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Peanut pods lɛ daa ni amɛgbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ shishi he ni abuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when I plant them in an open field without tall trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. They require shade from fast-growing plants like plantains or shade trees to keep them cool and maintain soil moisture while their roots establish.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Enɛ ji koni tso lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop almost all their leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves on purpose when water is scarce to prevent moisture from evaporating into the air. This resting state allows the plant to survive harsh dry weather while keeping the roots alive underground.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ baatsɔ yiŋtoo nɔ amɛshwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ beni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ni baatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ naa koni ekaho kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ hejɔɔmɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wa ni mli egbi lɛ amli, yɛ be mli ni eshishifãi lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does spreading dry grass around the base of my pepper plants help them survive heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the dirt with dry grass creates a protective layer called mulch. This layer shades the soil from direct sunlight, keeping the soil cool and stopping water from evaporating quickly.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ fã nɛɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning light yellow even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is starving for soil nutrients, especially nitrogen, which helps leaves stay green. Rain provides moisture, but it can also wash away soil nutrients if fertilizer or manure is not added.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli. Nugbɔ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Shi ebaanyɛ ejie niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he.

english: Why do weeds growing around my vegetable crops make my harvest smaller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mihe lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ mi-aduawai lɛ haa mi-ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi.

english: Weeds are fast-growing plants that steal soil nutrients, water, and root space away from your crops. When weeds take over, your vegetables cannot get enough food and remain small or stunted.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni daa oya ni juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, nu, kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Beni jwɛi lɛ baye nɔ lɛ O-aduawai lɛ nyɛŋ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Amɛji bibii loo amɛhe ejɔ hu.

english: Why do I find tiny caterpillars hiding right inside the rolled center leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mikɛ mihe ewo mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli

english: These are pests like the Fall Armyworm, which prefer hiding inside the soft center leaves (the whorl) because it protects them from scorching sun and predators while providing tender plant leaves to eat.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ baai bibii lɛ ateŋ (ring) mli, ejaakɛ enɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ahe, yɛ be mli ni ehaa tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ nɔ ko ni amɛyeɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without turning into fruit when the heat is too strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛtsɔɔɔ aduawai beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the sticky pollen inside tomato blossoms, preventing them from forming seeds. When a flower fails to pollinate properly due to heat, the plant drops it to save energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ. Enɛ haaa amɛfee dumɔwui. Beni fɔfɔi nyɛɛɛ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ yɛ latsaa hewɔ lɛ, ajieɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni akɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants wither and dry up when exposed to direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have fragile leaves and weak root systems that cannot pull up water fast enough to withstand high heat. They need temporary shade crops like plantain or cassava to shade them and keep the soil moist while they establish deeper roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛɛɛ agbala nu oya bɔ ni sa ni ekɛdamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo yucca. koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eha edɔ be mli ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ.

english: Why do new leaves on my cocoa trees turn reddish-pink before becoming green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: The red pigment in new cocoa leaves acts as a natural sunscreen, protecting the soft, young leaf tissues from harsh sunlight. As the leaf matures and hardens, it produces green chlorophyll to catch sunlight and make food for the tree.
ga: Nibii tsuru ni yɔɔ kookoo baai heei amli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni tsiɔ hulu naa. Ebuɔ baa bibii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Kɛji baai lɛ dara ni amɛhe wa Ejieɔ klorofil eŋɔli ni ekɛmɔɔ hulu la ni ekɛhaa tsei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the tree during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet, dark, and humid conditions. When rain stays trapped under heavy tree canopy, the fungus spreads quickly from pod to pod.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ, duŋ, kɛ hulutsoo be. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, ekpɛtɛɔ tsei ni etse amɛhe banee lɛ ashishi. Fuji lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ pod mli kɛyaa pod mli.

english: Why is a strange green plant growing on the branches of my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei eŋɔlii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ miida yɛ mi-kookoo tso ni eda lɛ niji anɔ lɛ?

english: That plant is mistletoe, a parasitic pest. It sticks its roots into your cocoa branches and steals water and nutrients directly from the tree, which weakens the tree and reduces the number of cocoa pods it can produce.
