ga: Nakai tso lɛ ji mistletoe. ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ mɔ awui Ewoɔ shishifãi yɛ kookoo niji amli ni ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni ehaa kookoo ŋmeii ni ebaanyɛ ewo lɛ ayibɔ baa shi.

english: Why are the flowers on my cocoa trees dropping off instead of forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are under stress from water shortages, lack of nutrients like potassium, or damage from tiny insects like mirids. Healthy soil and pest control help the flowers stay on and grow into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji nu ni faaa, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ potassium ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ mirids lɛ fiteɔ amɛ. Shikpɔŋ kpakpa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do some small cocoa pods turn brown and shrivel up when they are only the size of my finger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ Eyɛ mli akɛ etsɔ blɔfo ni egboɔ akɛ eshɛɔ mi nineshi dalɛ he?

english: This natural process is called cherelle wilt. The tree intentionally destroys some of its young pods when it realizes it does not have enough food or water to support all of them to maturity.
ga: Atsɛɔ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ cherry wilt. Tso lɛ tsɔɔ eyiŋ akɛ efiteɔ eshishifãi bibii lɛ ekomɛi ahiɛ beni enaa akɛ niyenii loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha eshishifãi lɛ fɛɛ aye abua kɛyashi amɛdara lɛ bɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow from the tips downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛnajiaŋ kɛmiiba shi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that the plant is starving for nitrogen, which is essential for healthy green foliage. Feeding the soil with poultry manure or nitrogen fertilizer will restore the dark green color.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha eŋɔli ni mli edɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why does spreading dry plant leaves around the base of my crops help them stay alive during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso baai ni egbi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mitsei lɛ ashishitoo lɛ haa tsei lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: This practice is called mulching. The dry leaves act as a blanket over the dirt, stopping the sun from baking the soil and evaporating the water trapped underground.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Baai ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashã shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa nu ni emɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do I need to cut off healthy branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifoɔ cacao tsei ni eda lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the canopy so air and sunlight can flow through the tree, reducing diseases. It also prevents the tree from wasting energy on extra leaves, forcing it to send nutrients to produce pods.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli lɛ, egbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ tso lɛ mli, ni no haa helai baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu koni tso lɛ akafite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tso lɛ atsu niyenii mli hewalɛ nii koni ekɛwo ŋmeii.

english: Why do weeds around my young cocoa seedlings make the cocoa trees grow so slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle Mi cacao tsei lɛ ahe lɛ ji gbekɛbii, no hewɔ lɛ amɛdaraa blɛoo waa lɛ.

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that quickly drink up all the water and eat the nutrients in the topsoil before your cocoa tree roots can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni nuɔ nu lɛ fɛɛ oya ni eyeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ dani kookoo shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ he.

english: Why do my crops still turn yellow even after I put fertilizer on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Crops need specific nutrients to stay green and healthy. If you apply the wrong type of fertilizer, or if the soil is too dry, the crop cannot absorb what it needs, causing the leaves to stay yellow.
ga: Niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi he miihia tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa wo mli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ. Ha baai lɛ ahi shi ŋmɔŋ.

english: How do I know which exact fertilizer my crops need to grow well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa mi tsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Different crops require different plant foods. Knowing your soil type and checking with an agricultural extension officer helps you pick the right blend of nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, or potassium for your specific crop.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi biɔ tsei niyenii srɔtoi. Kɛ́ ole shikpɔŋ ni oyɔɔ nɔ lɛ, ni okɛ mɔ ni kwɛɔ okwaayeli nɔ lɛ kwɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ohala niyenii mli hewalɛ ni sa, tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus, loo potassium, kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ.

english: Why does the soil in some patches of my farm look strange and make my crops stunt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ hei komɛi lɛ feɔ naakpɛɛ ni ehaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ foɔ lɛ?

english: Soil quality can change even within the same field due to past chemical use, soil washing away, or poor drainage. These patches lack balanced nutrients, which prevents crop roots from growing deep and healthy.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su baanyɛ atsake yɛ he kome po. Yɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ loo nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ Nɛkɛ hei nɛɛ bɛ niyenii ni sa. Enɛ haaa tso shishifãi lɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Can putting too much fertilizer damage my soil and kill my crops?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baanyɛ afite mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni efite miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, excessive fertilizer can burn plant roots and make the soil too salty or acidic. Over-application harms the crop rather than helping it produce more yield.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛtsu nii babaoo lɛ, ebaaye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui moŋ fe ni eeeye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ.

english: Why are my crops producing plenty of green leaves but very small fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ yɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi aduawai lɛ faaa kwraa lɛ?

english: Using a fertilizer with too much nitrogen makes crops focus all their energy on growing leaves instead of developing flowers, grains, or tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ tsei ahe tsei ni miida lɛ ahe nii. Mohu ɔ, a peeɔ fɔfɔi, duwuhi, aloo bulb.

english: Why do my crops dry up fast during a short dry spell while my neighbor's crops stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ? yɛ be mli ni akutsoŋnyo lɛ tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmɔji lolo lɛ.

english: Soil rich in organic matter and properly fed with the right nutrients acts like a sponge, holding moisture around the roots so crops can survive longer without rain.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli ni enine shɛɔ niyenii ni sa nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe koni tsei lɛ anyɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops produce a good harvest in the first year but perform poorly the next year on the same soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ ŋmaa kpakpa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli, shi ekpaaa ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops pull specific nutrients out of the earth as they grow. If you plant on the same land without replacing those nutrients, the soil becomes tired and crops in the next season suffer.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛji odu yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni okɛ nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ tsakeee lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaná he sɛɛ.

english: Should I just scatter fertilizer on top of the ground or bury it near my crop's roots?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashwã ŋmɔshi nibii ashwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo mafu yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ?

english: Burying or lightly covering fertilizer near the base of the crop protects it from evaporating in the hot sun or washing away in heavy rains, allowing roots to feed efficiently.
ga: Ni aaafu loo aha nɔ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔ fioo Yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ, ehaaa etsɔ la yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli loo ekaho yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛyeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad for me to apply fertilizer right before a heavy downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ ehiii kɛha mi lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes the fertilizer off the farm before the plant roots can soak it in, wasting your effort and money.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔji amli ŋmɔshi nibii dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Eji omɔdɛŋbɔɔ kɛ oshika fitemɔ.

english: How will attending a field demonstration help me improve my crop yield?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔ mli nɔkwɛmɔnɔ mli ni mikɛ mihe aaawo lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi koni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Demonstrations allow you to see firsthand how crop behavior changes when correct planting spacing, land preparation, and right fertilizer choices are used compared to traditional methods.
ga: Nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ haa onyɛɔ onaa bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ajeŋba tsakeɔ kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ateŋ gbɛ ni ja, shikpɔŋ he saamɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ halamɔ tsu nii kɛto blema gbɛi ahe.

english: Why should I clear heavy weeds from my farm instead of just letting them grow alongside my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi ni tsii kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mahã amɛkwɛ̃ kɛfata miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ?

english: Weeds act like extra mouths at the dinner table; they steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your crops. When weeds grow too dense, your crops get choked, stay small, and produce a very poor harvest.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ daaŋ krokomɛi yɛ gbɛkɛ niyeli okpɔlɔ lɛ nɔ. Amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Kɛ jwɛi lɛ dara tsɔ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ, bibii ni amɛbaawo yibii ni ehiii kwraa.

english: Why do weeds always seem to grow much faster than my planted maize or cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that are naturally adapted to grab nutrients and water from the soil faster than farm crops. Because they are so aggressive, they will easily overpower your crops if you do not clear them early.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo mli koni amɛjie niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Ejaakɛ amɛfeɔ basabasa waa. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛbaanyɛ amɛye oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ oya kɛji okɛjieee amɛ mra.

english: Why are my crop leaves turning yellow when the field is full of thick weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni jwɛi eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli obɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that your crop is starving for food, especially nitrogen. The dense weeds surrounding your crops are sucking up all the nutrients from the soil before your crop's roots can reach them.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye onibii. titri lɛ nitrogen Jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔle Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ miimu niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe.

english: Why is it important for me to remove weeds before they start showing flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi lɛ dani amɛbɔi fɔfɔi kpojiemɔ lɛ?

english: When weeds flower, they produce thousands of tiny seeds that drop into your soil. If you let them flower, those seeds will stay hidden in the dirt and create an even bigger weed problem for you during the next planting season.
ga: Kɛ́ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ lɛ Ebaawo dumɔwui bibii. Dumɔwui akpei abɔ ni miigbee oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛji oha ekwɛ Nakai dumɔwui lɛ baate shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛ jwɛi naagba wulu ko baaha bo yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: How often do I need to clear the weeds on my farm during the growing season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ mikɛ jwɛi shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ?

english: You should aim to weed at least two to three times during the season. The most critical time is during the first month after planting, when young crops are weak and need a clean field to establish strong roots.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ohiɛ afɔ nɔ akɛ kɛ hoo lɛ, obaajie jwɛi lɛ shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ yɛ be lɛ mli. Be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ ji klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ dumɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji be mli ni tsei bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ehe hiaa he ko ni he tse koni amɛshishifãi ni wa akwɛ̃.

english: Is it better for my farm if I pull weeds out by the roots or just cut the tops off with a cutlass?
ga: Ani ebaahi kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji mikɛ shishifãi lɛ shwie jwɛi lɛ anɔ loo mikɛ ŋmei shwie amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ?

english: Pulling weeds out by the roots or digging them out with a hoe is much better. If you only cut the tops off with a cutlass, the roots remain alive underground and the weeds will grow back within a few days.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ ogbala jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ mli loo okɛ ŋmei atsa amɛ. Kɛji okɛ ŋmei kuku fo ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baaya nɔ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi. Ni jwɛi lɛ baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ.

english: Will clearing all the weeds and bushes completely bare leave my soil damaged?
ga: Ani jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni mijie lɛ baafite mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaving the soil completely bare exposes it to the harsh sun and heavy rains, which can dry it out and wash away good topsoil. After clearing, it is good to leave the dead weeds on top of the soil as mulch to protect it.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kwraa lɛ, ebaaha hulu la ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa aba enɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni ekɛ ŋwɛi sũ lɛ afɔ. Beni ajie jwɛi lɛ sɛɛ Eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ oooshi jwɛi ni egboi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baabu amɛhe.

english: Can leaving dense weeds on my land attract animals that will destroy my crops?
ga: Jwɛi ni mli tse ni ashiɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbala kooloi. Ani no baafite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Yes, overgrown weeds create thick hiding places for farm pests like rodents and grasscutters. Dense bush can also attract stray cattle looking for food, which leads to your crops getting eaten and causes conflicts with animal herders.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ feɔ hei ni ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ jwɛi ŋmɔji lɛ nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ. Jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ hu baanyɛ agbala tsinai ni egbɛ eshwa ni miitao niyenii lɛ. Enɛ haa ayeɔ onibii ni oduɔ lɛ, ni ekɛ béi baa okɛ tookwɛlɔi ateŋ.

english: What can I do to stop livestock from invading my cleared farm land?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni kooloi akabote miŋmɔ shikpɔŋ ni ajie lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: You can build local fences using bamboo or living hedge plants like jatropha, plant border crops like hot peppers that animals avoid, and coordinate with local community leaders to set clear grazing pathways for livestock owners.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmei loo tsei ni yɔɔ wala mli tamɔ jatropha ama akutso lɛ mli gbogboi, odu husu tsei tamɔ chili ni kooloi tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ he, ni okɛ akutso lɛ mli hiɛnyiɛlɔi lɛ afee ekome koni amɛto gbɛi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni kooloi yeɔ kooloi lɛ anɔ lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ.

english: Does clearing the thick bushes around my farm boundary help reduce crop diseases?
ga: Ani miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii amli helai aba shi?

english: Yes, clearing bush boundaries removes the hiding and breeding spots for insects, rodents, and fungal diseases that spread from wild bushes into your clean crop fields.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baaye abua ni ajie hei ni ŋmeii, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii helai ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛjɛ koo mli ŋmeii amli kɛya oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni he tse lɛ nɔ lɛ ahi kɛ hei ni amɛfɔɔ yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong, direct sunlight. They need shade from nurse crops like plantains or taller shade trees to keep their delicate leaves cool and protect the soil moisture while their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛɔ helatsɛmɛi tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei kakadaji adɛŋ koni amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛbu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes in the middle leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworms, which prefer to hide and feed inside the soft inner leaves (the whorl) of young maize. Treating them early with recommended sprays or neem liquid stops them from ruining the plant's growing point.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛye nii yɛ ŋmeii bibii (rings) ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ amli. Amɛtsamɔ mra Kɛ akɛ neem tsofa loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekafite hei ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and turning yellowish-green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ-ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by tiny whiteflies. The virus weakens the leaves so they cannot make enough food, which stops the roots under the ground from growing into big, heavy tubers.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii mosaic hela. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Virus lɛ haa baai lɛ gbɔjɔɔ aahu akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plant turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves mean the soil is low in nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. The maize plant automatically moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to support the growth of the new green leaves at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Abɛi tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni eye ebua baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ adalɛ.

english: Covering the ground with organic material, called mulching, protects the soil from direct sunlight. It keeps the ground moist for longer, prevents soil erosion, and stops weeds from taking over your garden bed.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Tsi shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye obɔɔ mli saatsoi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants without forming any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo pepper yibii ko lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress caused by extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients. Keeping the soil evenly moist and well-fed helps the flowers stay attached and form healthy peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ mli baa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be ni eyeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut away the extra shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi plantain tsei titri lɛ etee.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, compete with the main stem for water, sunlight, and plant food. Removing all but one or two strong suckers allows the main plant to produce larger bunches of plantain.
ga: Tsoi ashishifãi krokomɛi loo tsei ashishifãi kɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha nu, hulu la, kɛ tso niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ mli tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo plantains babaoo.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines to climb up tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsɔse sweet potato wain tso ko koni enyɛ ekwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need plenty of sunlight to manufacture food for the growing tuber underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot soil where they could rot and allows them to capture more sunlight to make larger yams.
ga: Hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akabote shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi yɛ lɛ. ni ehaa hulu la babaoo baa koni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji aba.

english: Why does planting groundnuts before maize help my maize yield improve?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ adu ŋmei dani aŋɔ ŋmei lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmei lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their root nodules. When the groundnuts are harvested, that extra nitrogen stays in the soil to feed the next maize crop naturally.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ anɔ. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and collapse suddenly even when the soil has plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛkuɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is usually caused by bacterial wilt or fungal root rot present in the soil. These germs block the tiny water pipes inside the stem, preventing water from reaching the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ji bacteria wilt loo fungal root rot ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ tsiɔ nu paipii bibii anaa. yɛ tso lɛ mli Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekashɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: How do I choose the best crop variety to plant on my land this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Selecting the right variety depends on your soil type, rainfall pattern, and local weather. High-yield, certified seeds are specifically bred to survive local heat, resist pests, and give you a much higher market yield than uncertified seeds.
ga: Shikpɔŋ henɔ ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ ni abaahala tso ni sa lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ maŋ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi Dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo, ni awo he odaseyeli ni akwɛɔ amɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ maŋ lɛ mli dɔlɛ mli. Enyɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe Ni yibii ni anáa yɛ jara nɔ lɛ fa kwraa fe dumɔwui ni bɛ he odaseyeli.

english: Why is it better to buy certified seeds instead of saving seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ ooohe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mahere dumɔwui ni jɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Seeds saved from previous harvests lose their strength over time, resulting in smaller yields and weaker plants. Certified seeds are bred for strong growth, disease resistance, and reliable, uniform production.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ hu baa shi. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ana he odaseyeli koni amɛdara waa, helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ, kɛ yibiiwoo ni yaa nɔ daa, ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize crops rolling up into tubes during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ shwieɔ shi efeɔ tsɔnei yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves to protect themselves from intense sun and save water inside the plant. However, if they stay yellow and curled, it means the plant lacks water or essential soil nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Abele tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he ni amɛbu nu ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ he. Shi, kɛji amɛtee nɔ amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and cannot survive harsh, direct sunlight without protection. They need fast-growing shade crops like plantain or shade trees to shelter them and retain soil moisture during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ kɛji abuuu amɛhe. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei. Koni ekɛ wɔɔhe aha ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they face heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients. When the plant feels stressed, it drops flowers to preserve energy rather than growing fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa Kɛ tso lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with thick stems, but have very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: If cassava plants are planted too close together or receive too much nitrogen, the plant focuses all its energy on growing leaves and stems instead of storing energy in the roots to form fat tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo enine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe nii. Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, akɛ hewalɛ toɔ shishifãi lɛ amli koni amɛfee yitsei ni yɔɔ fɔ.

english: Why do my yam setts rot in the ground before they can even sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yam setts rot when planted in overly wet or waterlogged soil, or when infected by fungi and tiny worms in the soil. Treating setts with protective ash or fungicide before planting helps them sprout safely.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ tsɔ loo nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ. Aloo, kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ sũ ni tsiɔ hela loo tsofa ni gbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ tsu shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii dani adu lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans together with my maize make the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ du tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ, ehaa edaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds nearby nitrogen-hungry crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa tsei ni nitrogen he hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii.

english: What causes my pepper leaves to curl up and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaves and spreading viruses, which distorts leaf growth and stops the plant from producing well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa baai lɛ adalɛ ni ejaaa baa ni ehaa tsei lɛ adalɛ kpaɔ.

english: How can government agricultural programs help me get good planting materials for my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nɔyeli lɛ okwaayeli he gbɛjianɔtoi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná dumɔ nibii kpakpai kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Government agricultural initiatives work through district extension offices and farmer groups to supply certified seeds, improved seedlings, and subsidized fertilizers directly to farmers to boost farm productivity.
ga: Nɔyeli lɛ okwaayeli he nitsumɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ kpokpaa nɔ nitsumɔhei ni shwereɔ kɛ okwaafoi akui anɔ koni amɛná dumɔwui ni awo he hewalɛ. Ha dumɔwui lɛ aya hiɛ ni aha okwaafoi lɛ yelikɛbuamɔ ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii tɛ̃ɛ koni ŋmɔ mli nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my corn so it does not spoil in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa? Koni ŋmãa lɛ akafite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Corn is ready to harvest when the outer husks turn dry and brown and the kernels become hard. Leaving corn in the field for too long after it matures exposes the cobs to rain, birds, and insects, which causes rot and losses.
ga: Abɛi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ egbi ni efee ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ mli wa. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni ŋmãa lɛ egbɔ lɛ, no haa ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ. Nugbɔ nɛɔ, okpoi, kɛ kooloi nyɛɔ abele tsei lɛ ahe, ni no baanyɛ aha abele lɛ agbo ni elaaje.

english: Is it okay if I harvest my maize in small batches over several days instead of all at once?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba mli kɛji mikpa ŋmãa yɛ kui bibii amli? yɛ gbii babaoo mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaakpa fɛɛ shikome

english: Yes, harvesting in batches is fine if you are consuming or selling it fresh. However, for dry grain storage, harvesting everything at once during a dry period ensures all the grain dries evenly and prevents field pests from attacking remaining cobs.
ga: Hɛɛ, batch harvesting lɛ hi kɛji oye loo ohɔ̃ɔ ehee. Shi, kɛha dumɔwui ni egbi ni akɛtoɔ lɛ Kɛ́ akpa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ shikome yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmaa lɛ fɛɛ agbi pɛpɛɛpɛ. ni etsĩ kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anaa koni amɛkatutua ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: What signs should I look out for when inspecting my corn farm to make sure the plants are developing well?
ga: Mɛɛ okadii esa akɛ makwɛ jogbaŋŋ beni mikwɛɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mana nɔmimaa akɛ tsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ?

english: Healthy corn should have dark green leaves, sturdy stalks, and no large holes or discolored spots. You should inspect the central whorl of young plants for leaf-eating worms and check the undersides of leaves for signs of fungal disease.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ aná baai ni tsuɔ waa. stem ni wa Ni buji wuji loo ŋmeii ni etsake su bɛ jɛmɛ. Esa akɛ okwɛ tso bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli kɛji ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ yɛ mli. Ni okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi kɛji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko yɛ he.

english: What kind of sacks should I use to store my harvested corn so insects do not destroy it?
ga: Mɛɛ kotokui esa akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ato? koni kooloi bibii akafite lɛ

english: It is best to use hermetic (airtight) storage bags, such as PICS bags, rather than woven jute sacks. Airtight bags block oxygen, which naturally smothers any insects inside and prevents new pests from entering without using chemical powders.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛ kotokui ni akɛtoɔ nibii ahe ni akɛ vacuum tsiɔ naa tamɔ PICS kotokui baatsu nii moŋ fe jute kotokui ni akpɛ́. Vacuum kotokui lɛ baatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ naa. ni shwieɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni etsĩɔ kooloi heei ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkabote mli ni akɛ tsofa powda tsuuu nii.

english: Why do my harvested corn cobs need to be dried on a raised platform or tarp instead of directly on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ gĩɔ yɛ kpokui ni awó nɔ loo tarp nɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Drying corn directly on the soil allows moisture and soil fungus to get into the cobs, leading to mold growth and dangerous poisons called aflatoxins. Tarps or raised wooden platforms keep the grain dry, clean, and safe.
ga: Abele ni agbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ boteɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii daa kɛ tsofai fɔji ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni atsɛɔ amɛ aflatoxins lɛ. Tarp loo tso ni awo nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni dumɔwui lɛ agbiɔ, amɛhe tseɔ, ni amɛhiɔ shi shweshweeshwe.

english: How often should I inspect my stored bags of grain after harvesting?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ makwɛ ŋmaa kotokui ni ato lɛ amli yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should check your stored bags at least once every two weeks. Look for signs of moisture, warm spots inside the sacks, small holes, or tiny beetles (weevils), so you can dry or treat the grain before heavy damage occurs.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ okwɛ obaagi ni okɛto lɛ mli shikome daa otsii enyɔ. Taomɔ okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ, hei ni mli edɔ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli, buji bibii loo ŋmeii bibii (ŋmei) koni onyɛ ogbi loo otsa ŋmaa lɛ dani nɔ ko ni mli wa aba.

english: Why are the leaves of my young corn plants turning yellow even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, which corn needs in large amounts to grow healthy green leaves. Applying organic compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer will restore their strength and green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ŋmãa babaoo koni ebaakwɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ akwɛ jogbaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔshi nii.

english: Why do many farmers plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field with their corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo duɔ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni amɛduɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that feeds the corn crop while helping to cover and protect the soil from heat.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa tsei niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ teɔ shi ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he.

english: What is eating the leaves inside the tops of my corn plants, and how can I protect them?
ga: Mɛni miiye baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ amli lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛnaa?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Checking your field early and applying neem seed extract or recommended control products directly into the central funnel of the plant helps suppress them before they destroy the growing tip.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ nibii ni odu lɛ amli mra. Ni kɛ akɛ neem dumɔwui amli nu loo nɔ ko ni akɛkudɔɔ nibii ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ amɛnaa dani amɛfite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Can I save seeds from my harvested corn this year to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ afi nɛɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: If you planted traditional local seeds, you can save them for planting. However, if you planted commercial hybrid seeds, saving and re-planting them will result in weak plants and a very poor harvest; fresh hybrid seeds should be bought each season.
ga: Kɛji odu maŋ lɛ mli kusum dumɔwui Obaanyɛ okɛto kɛha dumɔwui, shi kɛlɛ, kɛji odu jarayeli dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome. Kɛ́ abu he ni adu ekoŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ, ni ŋmaa lɛ hu akafee nɔ ni ehiii kwraa. Esa akɛ ahe dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee hybrid lɛ daa afi.

english: Why does my corn struggle to grow big when weeds are growing close to it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni edara be mli ni jwɛi bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are fast-growing plants that steal water, sunlight, and vital nutrients directly from the soil surrounding your corn. Removing them early ensures all the food in the ground goes straight to helping your corn stalks grow tall and produce large ears.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle o-ŋmã lɛ he lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Ojie lɛ mra Enɛ baaha niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ afee tɛ̃ɛ koni eye ebua ni o-abele tsei lɛ aya hiɛ ni amɛtoi agbo.

english: How can using modern tools or chemicals help my crops better than using only a cutlass?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ nibii loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ fe dade kɛkɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii?

english: While cutlasses clear weeds on the surface, they require intense labor and can miss root systems. Modern tools and selective spraying cover large areas quickly, clearing weeds thoroughly without disturbing fragile crop roots or tiring you out.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ jwɛi lɛ jieɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ moŋ, shi eheɔ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ babaoo ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni sɛɛ efo. Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ nibii kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni ahalaa lɛ haa hei wuji ahe oya. Ejieɔ jwɛi lɛ kwraa ni egbaaa tso shishifãi ni waaa lɛ naa loo etɔɔɔ bo.

english: Why is it important to clear and loosen the soil properly before I plant my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ajie lɛ kpo jogbaŋŋ dani adu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Loosening the soil breaks up hard dirt so young crop roots can spread easily to absorb water and food. Proper preparation also buries old weeds, giving your new seeds a clean space to germinate.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ gbalaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo koni amɛhe nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Hesaamɔ ni sa hu yeɔ ebuaa ni afuɔ jwɛi momoi. Enɛ haa dumɔwui heei naa he ko ni he tse ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: What does spraying my crops actually do to help them grow safely?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nibii ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe?

english: Spraying applies protective treatments that stop insects from eating crop leaves and kill plant diseases before they ruin your harvest, keeping the plants healthy so they can produce well.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ji tsofa ko ni tsiɔ hela naa ni haaa kooloi bibii aye tsei ahe baai, ni egbeɔ tsei ahe helai dani amɛfiteɔ onibii. Koni tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni amɛwo nibii kpakpai.

english: How do I know the right time to spray chemicals on my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ afɔ tsofai yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: The best time to spray is early in the morning or late in the evening when pests are active, wind is low, and the sun won't quickly dry up the chemical before it works on the plants.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ ji leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ miitsu nii, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ faaa, ni hulu lɛ haaa tsofa lɛ agbi oya dani etsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some farmers in my area plant crops while others are already harvesting theirs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ miidu nii yɛ be mli ni mɛi krokomɛi hu miikpa momo lɛ?

english: Farmers plant at different times based on crop varieties, rainfall patterns, and land availability. Fast-maturing crops can be harvested early, while late-planted crops are timed to mature during drier periods.
ga: Okwaafoi duɔ nii yɛ bei srɔtoi amli yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Abaanyɛ akpa tsei ni daa oya lɛ mra. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni adu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ yɛ be ni mli egbi ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃.

english: How do I know when my maize is completely ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ ni abaakpa?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the leaves and outer husks turn dry and brown, and the kernels inside become hard and firm to the touch rather than soft or milky.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ egbi ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli wa ni amɛhe wa kɛji akɛ ata he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee blɛoo loo mliki

english: Why should I avoid planting my crop seeds too close together in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahe?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots block each other from getting water and nutrients, and their leaves block sunlight, leading to thin stalks and small yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Atsiɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná nu kɛ niyenii. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow early in the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually signal that your crops are starving for key nutrients like nitrogen, getting too much or too little water, or suffering from root damage caused by pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye onibii ni he hiaa waa tamɔ nitrogen, ni amɛmiiná nu babaoo loo fioo tsɔ. aloo efite shishifãi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛba lɛ

english: Why do different crops take different amounts of time before they are ready to eat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi yɛ bei srɔtoi amli dani efeɔ klalo akɛ ayeɔ lɛ?

english: Each crop species has its own internal biological clock. Leafy vegetables grow quickly because they only produce leaves, while grain crops like corn need more time to build deep roots, stalks, and heavy seeds.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ eko fɛɛ eko yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ emli wala yibii ahe ŋmɛlɛtswaa. Aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ daa oya ejaakɛ baai pɛ ji nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmaa nibii tamɔ ŋmãa biɔ be babaoo dani shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, ŋmeii, kɛ dumɔwui ni tsii aba.

english: How do I know if a farm medicine or chemical I buy in the market is safe to spray on my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai loo tsofai ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Always look for official government approval marks on the container. Approved farm medicines in Ghana have been tested by agricultural authorities to ensure they kill targeted pests effectively without ruining your crop or harming the people who eat the food.
ga: Taomɔ nɔyeli lɛ kpɛlɛmɔ he okadi ni yɔɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. Okwaayeli nitsumɔhei lɛ kaa ŋmɔ mli tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ amɛkwɛɔ koni amɛkwɛ akɛ amɛtsuɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ahe nii jogbaŋŋ. ni ofiteee onibii loo gbɔmɛi ni yeɔ lɛ awui.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to avoid buying cheap, unlabelled farm medicines from roadside sellers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔtsi wɔhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai ni jara waaa ni aŋmalako nɔ ko nɔ lɛ hemɔ kɛjɛ gbɛjegbɛ nɔ jarayelɔi adɛŋ lɛ?

english: Unlabelled or unapproved farm medicines are often fake, diluted, or dangerous chemicals. They can burn plant leaves, ruin soil health, or leave toxic chemical residues on your harvested produce that can make people sick.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni aŋmalako nɔ ko loo akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ ji amalei, tsofai ni akɛwo mli, loo tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛshã tsei ahe baai. efiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ Aloo eshiɔ tsofai fɔji ni eshwɛɔ yɛ okpamɔ lɛ nɔ ni baanyɛ aha gbɔmɛi aná hela.

english: Why does the government need to test and approve farm medicines before we use them on our Ghanaian farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni nɔyeli lɛ aka tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ akwɛ ni ekpɛlɛ nɔ dani wɔkɛtsu nii yɛ wɔ Ghana ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Testing ensures that the chemical actually works against local pests in Ghana, is safe for farmers to handle when sprayed properly, and will not leave harmful chemicals in the food crops sold in our markets.
ga: Kaai lɛ ha ana akɛ tsofai lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ Ghana lɛ ahe. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha okwaafoi ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsu he nii kɛji akɛ afɔ amɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni eshiŋ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ niyenii ni aduɔ ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ wɔ jarayeli hei lɛ amli.

english: Can I add household spirit or extra liquids to my crop spray to make it kill insects faster?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ shia mli mumɔi loo nu krokomɛi afata mi-plant spray lɛ he koni egbe kooloi bibii oya?

english: No, adding unapproved liquids like household spirits can burn crop leaves and destroy the active ingredients in the medicine. You should only mix crop medicines with clean water according to the instructions on approved containers.
ga: Dabi, nu ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ tamɔ shia mli mumɔi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai lɛ ni efite nibii ni tsuɔ nii ni yɔɔ tsofa lɛ mli lɛ. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afutu nu ni mli tse pɛ taakɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni yɔɔ tsɛnsi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops still get eaten by pests even after I spray them with farm medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa shwieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Pests may survive if you use the wrong medicine for that specific pest, spray at the wrong time of day, or dilute the mixture incorrectly. Using the correct government-approved medicine for your specific crop ensures the pest is targeted properly.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofa ni ejaaa tsu nii yɛ amɛhe. Tsofa ni ja ni nɔyeli lɛ kpɛlɛɔ nɔ kɛha onibii pɔtɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ ni okɛbaatsu nii yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni ejaaa mli loo ni okɛ tsofa ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ awo mli yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ yeɔ ebuaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes my crop leaves to turn yellow or burn right after I spray them for pests?
ga: Mɛni haa mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo amɛshãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Leaves usually burn if the medicine concentration was too strong, sprayed in hot afternoon sun, or if the chemical was not approved for that specific plant type. Always follow recommended mixing rates and application times.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ shãa kɛji tsofa lɛ mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. aloo kɛji akɛ akpɛlɛɛɛ tsofa lɛ nɔ kɛha nakai tso lɛ. Nyiɛmɔ bɔ ni akɛfutuɔ nii ahaa kɛ be ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ sɛɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why does a spray medicine that works well for cocoa trees destroy tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ kookoo tsei anɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ gbeɔ tomato tsei lɛ?

english: Different crops have different leaf structures and sensitivities. Medicines are formulated for specific crop types, which is why official product labels clearly state which crops the medicine is safe to use on.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi yɛ baai ahe gbɛjianɔtoo kɛ henumɔi srɔtoi. Afee tsofai kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi. Enɛ hewɔ ni nibii ni akɛwoɔ tsofafeemɔ mli lɛ ahe woji lɛ tsɔɔ tsei ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha tsofafeemɔ mli faŋŋ lɛ.

english: How does spraying medicine actually protect my crop from insects?
ga: Te tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ abu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Approved crop medicines contain active ingredients that either kill insects on contact or get absorbed by the plant leaves so insects die when they try to eat the plant, stopping pest damage before the crop dies.
ga: Tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ tsofai tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ yɛ nibii ni tsuɔ nii ni gbeɔ kooloi kɛji tsei ahe baai kɛ amɛ kpe loo amɛŋɔ amɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kooloi baagboi kɛ́ amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛye tsei. Koni akpa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbo.

english: Is it safe for me to harvest and eat my vegetables immediately after spraying them with pest medicine?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makpa mi-vegetables lɛ ni maye amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ eshwie nɔ lɛ?

english: No, every farm medicine has a required waiting period after spraying before harvest. This gives the chemical time to break down naturally so the crop becomes completely safe for human consumption.
ga: Dabi, tsofai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ biɔ ni amɛ be ni akɛshwie nɔ dani akpa. Enɛ haa tsofai lɛ naa be ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kwraa kɛha adesa niyenii.

english: How can I stop insects on my farm from getting used to the spray medicine I use every season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha ŋmɔ mli kooloi lɛ akatsɔ tsofa ni mikɛshwieɔ shi daa afi lɛ nɔ?

english: Insects build resistance if you use the exact same medicine repeatedly. Rotating between different government-approved medicines with different active ingredients prevents pests from becoming immune to your spray.
ga: Kplukai baanyɛ aná hewalɛ ni tsiɔ hela naa kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii shii abɔ. Tsofai srɔtoi ni akɛtsakeɔ Tsofai ni Nɔyeli lɛ ekpɛlɛ nɔ ni nibii srɔtoi ni tsuɔ nii yɔɔ mli lɛ baatsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee nɔ ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ otsofa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an important food that plants need to grow green and strong leaves. It can also happen when too much rain washes nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛná baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni mli wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: How does planting beans or cowpeas in my field help my soil for the next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas have special roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil. When the leaves and roots decay, they leave behind free natural food for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ fite Ebaashi adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers need water to dissolve so the crop's roots can drink them up. Applying fertilizer to dry soil leaves concentrated salts around the roots, which can burn the roots and kill the plant.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ biɔ nu ni etsɔ mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu amɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa ŋoo feɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no baanyɛ ashã shishifãi lɛ ni egbe tso lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in a clear field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to heat and direct sunlight. Planting them under fast-growing shade crops like plantains protects their delicate leaves from burning and keeps the soil moist until their roots grow deeper.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ yaa shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize crops produce smaller cobs when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops end up fighting each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of making big cobs, the plants waste energy growing tall and thin just to reach the light.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee cob blɔkii wuji Moŋ lɛ, tsei fiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo koni amɛná la kɛkɛ.

english: Why do caterpillars eat the inside leaves of my young maize plants mostly at night?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ babaoo gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm hide deep inside the central leaf funnel of the maize plant during the hot day to avoid drying out, coming out in the evening and night when it is cooler to feed on the fresh leaves.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Bɔni afee ni akagbi Amɛjeɔ kpo gbɛkɛ kɛ gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ koni amɛbaye baai heei.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the daytime temperatures become too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Extreme weather stresses the plant, forcing it to drop flowers to save water.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa lɛ haa tsei haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ ashɛrɛ fɔfɔi ashwie koni nu akafite.

english: Why do my mature cassava roots start rotting underground if left in the soil after heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni eda lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain fills all the small air spaces in the soil with water. Without air in the soil, the mature cassava roots suffocate and drown, allowing fungi and bacteria to quickly rot the tubers.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii baa. Nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Cassava shishifãi ni eda lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi baanyɛ afite ŋmeii lɛ oya.

english: Why won't my harvested seed yams sprout right away when I put them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ ekwɛɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ mikɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers go through a natural sleep period called dormancy immediately after harvest. During this time, the tuber rests internally and will not shoot fresh buds until a few months have passed.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli wɔɔhe be ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ Bulbs lɛ baajɔɔ amɛhe yɛ mli ni amɛbaafee ŋmeii heei kɛyashi nyɔji fioo komɛi baaho.

english: Why does cutting off unnecessary branches on my cashew trees give me a better yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji ni he ehiaaa ni afolɔ yɛ mi-cashew tso lɛ nɔ lɛ haa yibii kpakpai baa lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the middle of the tree so air and sunlight can reach every leaf, which prevents fungal diseases and encourages the tree to spend energy producing fresh flowers and nuts instead of useless stems.
ga: Tso lɛ mlifomɔ biɔ ni agbele tso lɛ teŋgbɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ashɛ tso lɛ baa fɛɛ baa he. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela mli baa lɛ anaa, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii heei yɛ ŋmeii ni he ehiaaa lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my crop roots rot whenever I plant them in parts of my farm where rainwater collects?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fiteɔ be fɛɛ be ni madu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ hei komɛi ni nugbɔ nu buaa ehe naa yɛ lɛ?

english: When water sits in one place for too long, it starves the plant roots of air. This extra wetness allows fungi and bacteria to grow easily, causing the roots and underground tubers to rot.
ga: Kɛ nu hi he kome be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa hiɛ nɛɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃. Enɛ haa shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: How can I tell if a low section of my farmland holds too much water for crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji okwaayeli shikpɔji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ miito nu babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If rainwater stays on the surface for several days after a heavy storm or if the soil feels extremely sticky and smells marshy, that part of your field holds too much water for most standard crops.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nu lɛ tee nɔ ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo yɛ ahum ni naa wa ko sɛɛ, Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ waa ni eŋmɔɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli he ko miihiɛ nu babaoo tsɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo.

english: What can I do to prevent standing water from damaging my crops during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni nu ni damɔ shi lɛ akafite miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: You can dig shallow drainage channels to lead extra water away from your field, or create raised earth mounds and ridges to plant your crops high above where water collects.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ he eko. Koni ojie nu ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ oŋmɔji lɛ amli Aloo ofee gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ kɛ ŋshɔkei ni okɛwó onibii anɔ kɛya ŋwɛi he ni nu buaa ehe naa yɛ lɛ.

english: Are there specific crops that will rot in wet ground and others that actually like excess water?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ ni baafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ kɛ tsei krokomɛi ni sumɔɔ nu babaoo?

english: Crops like cassava, pepper, and maize have soft roots or tubers that rot quickly in standing water, while crops like rice and cocoa yams thrive in wet, swampy soils.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi bibii loo ŋmeii ni fiteɔ oya yɛ nu ni damɔ shi mli. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ omɔ kɛ kookoo yams shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ, ni jwɛi yɔɔ nɔ.

english: If I plant cassava in an area that gets flooded, how will the crop behave underground?
ga: Kɛji odu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ. Te tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baafee tɛŋŋ?

english: The excess moisture prevents the cassava roots from developing firm tubers, turning them soft, watery, and foul-smelling as they rot beneath the soil.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine lɛ tsiɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmeii ni wa, ni ehaa amɛfeɔ bɔdɔɔ, amɛfeɔ nu, ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do farmers clear their land right after Christmas in January before the new year rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi shwieɔ shikpɔji anɔ yɛ Blonya sɛɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ January mli, dani Afi Hee nugbɔ lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Clearing farm land during the dry period between December and February gives slashed brush and weeds enough sunshine to dry properly, making it easy to clear or burn before planting season starts.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie dumɔwui ni adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni yɔɔ December kɛ February teŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha brɔshi ni afolɔ mli kɛ jwɛi lɛ aná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛgbi jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaajie loo ashã dani ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ aje shishi.

english: How does the dry season from January to March affect crop growth in the field?
ga: Te nugbɔshiimɔ be ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ January kɛyashi March lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: The extreme heat and lack of groundwater cause soil to dry out and harden, which slows down growth and makes established plants drop leaves to save water.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni bɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ ni ewaa. ni haa shweremɔ baa shi ni ekɛshwieɔ tsei ni damɔ shi lɛ anɔ koni ekɛbu nu he.

english: How do I know the right month to put my seeds in the ground so they do not dry up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male nyɔŋ ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ? koni dumɔwui lɛ akagbi

english: Planting should begin after the first continuous heavy rains arrive—usually around March or April—when the soil has enough deep moisture to keep seeds alive.
ga: Esa akɛ aje dumɔ shishi beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ eba lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baa mli (bei pii lɛ, yɛ March loo April mli) beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa bɔ ni sa ni dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi lɛ.

english: Why do some crops need to stay in the soil until the end of the year before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni tsei komɛi ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi afi lɛ naagbee dani amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa amɛ?

english: Certain long-term crops like yam and cassava need a full cycle of both rainy and dry periods across 9 to 12 months to store enough strength and swell their roots properly.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ be kakadaŋŋ komɛi, tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ hɔmɔ be ni ji nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 he miihia koni hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ahi shi ni shishifãi lɛ alɛɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens to mature crops if I leave them in the ground too long after their harvest time has passed?
ga: Mɛni baa ŋmɔshi nibii ni edara lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni kpamɔɔ be lɛ eho lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Leaving crops in the farm past maturity exposes them to soil insects and underground fungi, causing them to lose nutritional quality, become tough, or rot completely.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni ashiɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ haa amɛnaa kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Enɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baa shi, ewaa, loo efiteɔ kwraa.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with big leaves, but the tubers underground are small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassavas lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai wuji shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems instead of feeding and swelling its underground roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo ni potassium faaa lɛ Tsei kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ baai kɛ tsei lɛ tsuɔ nii. Mohu ɔ, e yeɔ ní, nɛ e haa nɛ zugba a sisi sisi ɔ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why does planting maize on the exact same plot every year make my yields smaller each time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Repeatedly planting the same crop depletes specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground season after season.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up into tight tubes during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a survival reaction; the maize plant reduces its leaf surface area to prevent moisture from escaping when the sun is hottest.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji wala yiwalaheremɔ he nifeemɔ. Abɛi tsei haa amɛbaai lɛ anɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ baa shi koni ŋmɔtɔ akaje mli beni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable plants wilt in the afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: In intense midday heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can absorb it from the soil, causing temporary wilting until temperatures cool down.
ga: Yɛ shwane gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers instead of producing peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when stressed by irregular watering, extreme heat, or a lack of balance in soil nutrients during the blooming stage.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ miihao amɛ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees die so quickly when planted in an open field without shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli tse ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ mli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves and short roots that burn easily under direct sunlight; fast-growing shade plants like plantains shield them until they are strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains lɛ baabu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛbaafee mɛi ni he wa.

english: What crop can I grow to supply poultry farmers who are producing eggs in my area?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu koni mikɛha kooloi akwɛlɔi ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Maize and soybeans are in high demand by poultry farmers because they are the main ingredients needed to process feed for egg-laying chickens.
ga: Abɛi kɛ soybeans ji nɔ ni kooloi akwɛlɔi taoɔ waa ejaakɛ amɛji nibii titri ni he hiaa koni akɛfee niyenii ni akɛhaa kooloi ni woɔ bii lɛ.

english: Why does leaving weeds around my crops cost me money at harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ashi jwɛi yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifite mi shika yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: Weeds aggressively steal fertilizers, sunlight, and water directly from your crops, leaving the main plants weak and reducing the total amount of crop you sell.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, hulu la, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ baa shi ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni ohɔ̃ɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my crop turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves often signal a nitrogen shortage; the plant takes nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to keep new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Tsei kɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni eha baai heei akwɛ̃ yɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomato fruits turning black and rotting before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition, known as blossom-end rot, happens when plants lack calcium or experience inconsistent watering that stops calcium from reaching the developing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ calcium loo amɛnáa nu be fɛɛ be. Enɛ haaa calcium lɛ ayashɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it important to use a straight string line when I am planting my maize seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akɛ kpãa ni ja atsu nii kɛ́ oodu ŋmãa dumɔwui?

english: Using a string line ensures you plant in straight rows with consistent spacing. This makes it much easier to walk through the farm to weed, ensures every crop gets equal sunlight and nutrients, and allows tools or machinery to move smoothly between rows.
ga: Kɛ okɛ kpãa tsu nii lɛ, ehaa oduɔ nii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja kɛ gbɛ ni kã amɛteŋ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enɛ haa nyiɛmɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ajie jwɛi lɛ feɔ mlɛo kwraa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ naa hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa. ni ehaa nitsumɔ dadei loo tsɔnei nyiɛɔ mlɛo yɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ teŋ.

english: How does using a hand-held corn planter help me compared to dropping seeds by hand?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmãa ni akɛ nine tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni akɛ niji duɔ lɛ he?

english: A hand-held planter automatically punches a hole at the correct depth, drops the right number of corn seeds, and covers them up in one motion. It prevents back pain from bending and makes sure seeds are planted deep enough to escape birds and germinate properly.
ga: Nibii ni akɛduɔ nii ni akɛ nine tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shwieɔ bu yɛ he ni sa. No sɛɛ lɛ, shwie ŋmãa dumɔwui abɔ ni otaoɔ lɛ nɔ. ni ekɛha ŋmãa lɛ nɔ shikome Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa sɛɛ piŋmɔ akafee arching. ni eyeɔ ebuaa koni adu dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛjo okpoi anaa foi ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Which direction should I position cassava cuttings when I push them into the ground?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ mikɛ mi yucca niji lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: You should plant cassava cuttings at a slight angle with the small buds (nodes) pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting them upside down causes the new shoots to grow weak and struggle to reach the surface.
ga: Esa akɛ odu o-yucca niji lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ fioo ni ŋmeii bibii (tsoji) lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu ŋwɛi ŋwɛi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii heei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛshɛ ŋwɛi.

english: What is the benefit of pulling a plow behind a tractor to clear my field before planting?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛgbalaɔ trakta sɛɛ koni akɛjie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu nii lɛ he?

english: A tractor plow turns over hard, packed soil, buries old weeds, and loosens the earth deep below the surface. Soft, loose soil allows young plant roots to spread quickly and absorb water more easily.
ga: Trakta lɛ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Fuu jwɛi momo ni ehaa sũ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shishigbɛ tɔ̃ɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni etse ehe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei bibii ashishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa oya ni amɛmɔɔ nu oya.

english: Why should I make high soil mounds or ridges before planting my yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafee gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ dani madu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow large deep underground. Creating loose soil mounds gives the tubers room to expand without hitting hard ground, and it keeps water from settling around the tubers and causing them to rot.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ daa, ni amɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji ni afee lɛ haa yitso he lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni enaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ. ni etsĩ nu naa koni ekabɔle yitso he ni efite

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your corn plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for leaf growth. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen out of the soil, so applying urea or NPK fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, urea loo NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves curl and droop during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves curl and droop to reduce their exposure to the strong sun during hot, dry periods like the Harmattan. It is the plant's natural way of saving water, though adding mulch around the base will help keep moisture in the ground.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi koni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ aba shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa, ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi tamɔ harmattan lɛ. Eji tso lɛ adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ shishi lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi moŋ.

english: Why do some of my harvested corn cobs only have grains on one side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ ekomɛi yɛ ŋmeii yɛ efã kome pɛ lɛ?

english: Corn cobs lack full grains when the plant suffers from water stress or a lack of nutrients while producing pollen. It can also happen if plants are planted too close together, blocking wind from spreading pollen evenly to all the silks.
ga: Abɛi ŋmeii lɛ bɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ kɛji tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ nu he haomɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ he yɛ be mli ni ejieɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Enɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ agbɛ pollen lɛ ashwã siliki mama lɛ fɛɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why do weeds harm my young corn crop more in the first four weeks than later in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ awui waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ lɛ amli fe sɛɛ mli yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young corn plants have small, weak roots that cannot fight well against weeds. In the first few weeks, fast-growing weeds steal the soil's water, fertilizer, and sunlight, which can permanently stunt the corn before it grows tall enough to shade out weeds.
ga: Abɛi tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni kɛ jwɛi wuuu jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmãa lɛ afee shoo kɛya naanɔ dani ekwɛ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ jwɛi lɛ baaha jwɛi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the funnel leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which prefer to hide in the tender, growing center of young corn plants. Removing them early by hand or using appropriate treatments stops them from destroying the main shoot where the corn cob will form.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni miida blɛoo lɛ ateŋ. Ni akɛ niji ajieɔ lɛ mra loo akɛ tsofa ni sa baatsu nii Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmeii titrii ni ŋmeii lɛ baafee yɛ mli lɛ.

english: Where exactly around my young plant stem should I place fertilizer so it works quickly without damaging the plant?
ga: Ani esa akɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi tsei bibii lɛ ahe koni etsu nii oya ni efiteee tsei lɛ?

english: Fertilizer works best when placed in a ring a few inches away from the stem, near where the roots spread out. Placing it directly against the stem can burn the plant tissue, while placing it near the feeder roots allows the plant to safely drink up the nutrients fast.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo ŋwɛi ŋta ni kɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo komɛi. ni bɛŋkɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Kɛ́ akɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ fãji lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛwo niyenii ni akɛhaa lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ anu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ oya ni ekɛtsu nii shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does putting strong crop medicine directly on top of fresh leaves sometimes burn them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, tsei ahe tsofai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akɛwoɔ baai heei anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa baai lɛ shãa lɛ?

english: Young leaves are tender and soft. Concentrated chemicals can strip moisture out of leaf cells very quickly, causing leaf burn; diluting the medicine properly with water protects the leaves while still killing pests.
ga: Baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ. Tsofai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ baa lɛ mli wala yibii lɛ amli oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji baai lɛ ashãa Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa lɛ wo nu mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaabu baai lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni egbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ lolo.

english: How does crop medicine applied near the roots travel all the way up to protect the top shoots and leaves?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tso tsofa ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ yaa ŋwɛi koni ebu tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ahe?

english: Plants have tiny internal tubes that act like drinking straws. When roots take in water from the soil, they suck systemic medicine upward through these tubes, distributing protection to the very top leaves and branches.
ga: Tsei yɛ mligbɛ tsɔnei bibii. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ jwɛi ni anuɔ Beni shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Ekɛ tsofa lɛ shwieɔ ŋwɛi yɛ gbɛjianɔtoo naa kɛtsɔɔ nɛkɛ tsɔnei nɛɛ amli. Jaa hebuu kɛha baai kɛ niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Can spraying liquid fertilizer directly onto leaves feed my crops faster than putting fertilizer in the soil?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yes, leaves have tiny openings on their surfaces that can absorb dissolved nutrients immediately for a quick boost, whereas soil fertilizer must wait for moisture to dissolve it before roots can drink it in.
ga: Hɛɛ, baai lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. Yɛ hiɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ejie niyenii ni mli ewo muji lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni ekɛha ebɔi aya hiɛ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, esa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amɛ ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ atsɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ anu.

english: Why do some pest medicines kill insects instantly while others take a few days to show results?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai komɛi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ gbeɔ kooloi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ? yɛ be mli ni mɛi krokomɛi heɔ gbii fioo komɛi dani amɛnaa nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa.

english: Contact medicines kill insects as soon as the spray touches them, giving immediate results. Systemic medicines must first be absorbed into the plant's sap and eaten by the insects, which takes a bit longer but gives longer-lasting protection.
ga: Kpeemɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ahe kɛji tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ kɛ kooloi lɛ kpe pɛ. Ehaa nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa amrɔ nɔŋŋ Esa akɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli lɛ awo tso lɛ mli nu lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ ni kooloi bibii lɛ aye. Enɛ heɔ be fioo shi ehaa hebuu ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ haa.

english: If I apply pest medicine to the stem of my cocoa tree, how long will it take to protect the pods higher up?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsu nii yɛ kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ, Be enyiɛ ebaahe ni mikɛbu ŋmeii ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ ahe?

english: It takes time for the tree to suck the chemical up through its sap channels. Depending on the size of the tree and weather conditions, trunk-applied treatment can take anywhere from a few days to a few weeks to reach full strength in the upper pods.
ga: Eheɔ be fioo dani tso lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ emli nu lɛ nɔ eŋɔ tsofai lɛ. Edamɔ tso lɛ dalɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi anɔ. Stem tsamɔi baanyɛ ahé gbii fioo kɛyashi otsii fioo komɛi dani ŋwɛi ŋmeii lɛ ashɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ he.

english: Why do the soft young leaves at the very top head of my plant wilt first when the plant is stressed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ gboɔ klɛŋklɛŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao lɛ?

english: The growing tip at the top of a plant requires the most water pressure to stay upright. When a plant lacks water or gets diseased, it loses water pressure at the highest points first before older, tougher lower leaves show damage.
ga: Nu ni tsiɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ biɔ nu ni tsii fe fɛɛ koni ehi shi shiŋŋ. Kɛji tsei bɛ nu loo hela mɔ amɛ Ebaaje nu mli hewalɛ yɛ he ni eyɔɔ ŋwɛi fe fɛɛ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Dani baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baadara ni amɛhe awa lɛ, nɔ ni efite lɛ baatsɔɔ.

english: Why does spraying crop medicine in the hot afternoon sun cause leaves to dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni akɛ tsofa shwieɔ nɔ yɛ shwane hulutsoo be mli lɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ lɛ?

english: Hot sunlight makes spray droplets on leaves act like tiny magnifying glasses that concentrate heat, while also causing the chemicals to evaporate too quickly or scorch the open leaf pores.
ga: Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ haa nu ni shwieɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ tamɔ glase bibii ni buaa dɔlɛ naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsofai lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ loo eshãa ŋmeii ni agbele lɛ.

english: Does spraying pest medicine under the plant leaves work better than spraying only on top?
ga: Ani tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ ashishi lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe nɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ pɛ?

english: Yes, most insects hide on the undersides of leaves to avoid rain and heat, and the bottom of a leaf has more tiny pores that absorb systemic medicine faster than the smooth top side.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooloi bibii babaoo kɛ amɛhe teeɔ baai ashishi koni nugbɔ kɛ latsaa akanɛ. Ni baa lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni baanyɛ aŋɔ tsofa ni yɔɔ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli lɛ oya fe ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ.
