english: Why do my crops grow faster when I pour liquid manure near the base instead of scattering dry manure far away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya kɛ́ mikɛ nu ni mli ewo muji shwie shi yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shishitoo lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni magbɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi ashwã he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Liquid manure is already dissolved, so the small feeder roots near the base of the stem can absorb it instantly, while dry manure scattered far away must wait for rain to decompose and carry nutrients to the plant.
ga: Nu ni mli ewo muji lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi bibii lɛ Ebɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ hewɔ lɛ ebaanyɛ eŋɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. be mli ni ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shɔŋŋ Esa akɛ omɛ nugbɔ lɛ ni egbɛ eshwa ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aya tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when I clear all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ egbo beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. Shade trees or food crops like plantains protect young cocoa plants from intense heat and keep moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei ni akɛyeɔ niyenii tamɔ plantains lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ shishifãi ni wa baa.

english: Why are the pods on my cocoa trees turning black and rotting when the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in damp, shaded, and wet conditions. Pruning overcrowded branches lets sunlight and air flow through the farm to dry off the pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, kɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ amli babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow from the middle instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a sign that the soil is low on nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to grow leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni baai lɛ akwɛ̃ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa loo nitrogen ŋmãa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa lɛ afee ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do experienced farmers say planting groundnuts on my plot will make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to a crop family that pulls nitrogen from the air and leaves it in the soil through their roots. When you harvest them, that trapped nitrogen stays in the earth to feed your next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji tsei aweku ko ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛshiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji okpa amɛ Nakai nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are ready for harvesting without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifã ko efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil right around the base of the main stem begins to crack upward from the expanding tubers below.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ bulb ni miigbɛ eshwa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why does my plantain plant produce smaller bunches when I allow many young shoots to grow around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii beni miha ŋmeii bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Nakai plantain tso lɛ

english: When too many shoots grow around one plantain stem, they all compete for the same soil water and nutrients. Removing extra suckers leaves only the strongest ones to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ ebɔle ehe lɛ tso kome ŋmeii fɛɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ feɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop to the ground without growing into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers fall off when the plant suffers from stress like extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. Keeping the soil moist and adding organic food helps the plant hold onto its flowers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ kɛ haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ kpe. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni okɛ niyenii ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why does spreading dry leaves around the base of my crop plants help them stay alive through the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni agbɛ baai ni egbi ashwã he fɛɛ he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mitsei lɛ ashishitoo lɛ haa amɛhiɔ shi yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves or straw acts like a blanket over the soil. It blocks the harsh sun from drying out the ground, keeping water around the roots for a much longer time.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaafee tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Etsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ehaa nu hiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe be babaoo.

english: Why do small caterpillars hide deep inside the center funnel of my maize stalks during the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe teeɔ mi-ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: These pests, like the fall armyworm, hide inside the tight leaves of the maize center to protect themselves from hot sunshine and birds while feeding on the tender young leaves inside.
ga: Nɔ ni fata nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ahe ji fall armyworms. Ekɛ ehe ewo ŋmãa tsui lɛ mli tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ amli. Bɔni afee ni obu ohe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ kɛ okpoi ahe be mli ni oyeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops right after the first rain of the season falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are extremely tough and can sleep in dry soil for months. When the rain comes, they wake up immediately and grow fast because wild weeds are naturally stronger at taking up early soil moisture than farm seeds.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa waa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ nyɔji babaoo. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, amɛteɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛdaraa oya ejaakɛ koo mli jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmɔ mli dumɔwui.

english: Why do many of us clear our farmland by burning the bush before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔteŋ mɛi babaoo shwieɔ wɔdumɔ nii lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni wɔshãa dani wɔduɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Burning bush is a fast and low-cost way to clear thick vegetation. The ash left behind provides a quick boost of nutrients like potassium to the soil, though repeated burning can damage soil structure over time.
ga: Hedgerows ni ashãa lɛ ji gbɛ ni yɔɔ oya ni jara waaa ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. Lalu ni ashiɔ yɛ sɛɛ lɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ potassium baa sũ lɛ mli oya. Eyɛ mli akɛ shãa ni afɔɔ feemɔ moŋ Ebaanyɛ efite shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Is burning my farm land before planting good or bad for my soil in the long run?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ ni mishãa dani miduɔ nii lɛ hi loo ehiii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli?

english: While burning gives a quick nutrient boost from ash, doing it repeatedly damages the soil. It kills beneficial soil organisms, destroys natural organic matter, and makes the land dry out faster during hot periods.
ga: Beni shãa lɛ haa niyenii ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ oya lɛ. Shi kɛ́ ofee enɛ shii abɔ lɛ, ebaafite shikpɔŋ lɛ. Egbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. efiteɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do some farmers plant their crops little by little instead of planting the whole field at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii bibii moŋ fe ni amɛduɔ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ shikome lɛ?

english: Staggering your planting helps spread out labor and financial risk. If unexpected bad weather hits, you only lose a portion of your crops rather than everything, and it allows for a steady continuous harvest.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ gbɛɔ nitsumɔ kɛ shika he osharai eshwaa. Kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ gbonyo ni akpaaa gbɛ ba Obaafite onibii lɛ fã ko pɛ yɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ najiaŋ. ni eŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni akpaa ŋmaa lɛ daa, ni eyaa nɔ

english: How does the changing climate in Ghana affect when I should plant my crops?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yaa nɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ saa be ni esa akɛ madu nii lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Changing climate patterns make rainfall unpredictable, shifting the traditional start of the rainy season. Relying solely on old calendar dates can lead to planting too early before rains are steady, so monitoring current weather patterns is now essential.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi haa anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nugbɔ ni baa lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, bɔ ni afeɔ ajeɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishi yɛ kusum naa lɛ etsake. Kusum kalanda gbii pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha adu nii mra tsɔ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ aba. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni okwɛ bɔ ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi yɔɔ amrɔ nɛɛ.

english: Why are traditional farming habits no longer giving me the high crop yields I used to get?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ blema okwaayeli nifeemɔi haaa miná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tamɔ tsutsu lɛ dɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Rising temperatures, irregular rains, and worn-out soil from continuous clearing mean traditional reliance on natural rainfall is less dependable. Modern adjustments like soil conservation and improved crop varieties are now needed.
ga: hulutsoo ni nɔ kwɔ Nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be. ni shikpɔŋ lɛ efite kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ lɛ daa lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kusum nifeemɔ ni akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔshiimɔ nɔ lɛ miifee nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛ he afɔ̃ nɔ. Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsakemɔi ahe miihia, tamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ tsei ahenɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is irrigation, and how does it help crops grow?
ga: Mɛni ji nu shwiemɔ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa?

english: Irrigation is the artificial application of water to land or soil to help crops grow. It supplies crops with steady water from rivers, wells, or ponds when natural rainfall is insufficient or absent.
ga: Nu shwiemɔ ji nu ni akɛfee ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ loo sũ mli koni eye ebua tsei ni amɛdara. Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ faai, nubui loo ŋshɔi amli nu daa be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ faaa loo ebɛ.

english: Has irrigation actually been tested and used by farmers in Ghana before?
ga: Ani okwaafoi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ eka nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ amɛkwɛ ni amɛkɛtsu nii pɛŋ?

english: Yes, Ghana has used irrigation for decades. Government irrigation schemes started in places like Dawhenya and Kpong in the 1960s, and today many vegetable farmers successfully use small water pumps along rivers.
ga: Hɛɛ, Ghana kɛ nu shwiemɔ gbɛjianɔtoi etsu nii afii nyɔŋmai abɔ nɛ. Nɔyeli lɛ nu shwiemɔ gbɛjianɔtoi je shishi yɛ hei tamɔ Dawhenya kɛ Kpong yɛ 1960 afii lɛ amli ni ŋmɛnɛ Aduawai okwaafoi babaoo eye omanye kɛtsɔ nu pɔmpii bibii ni yɔɔ faai ahe lɛ ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Can a smallholder farmer like me use irrigation, or is it only for large commercial farms?
ga: Ani okwaafoi bibii tamɔ mi baanyɛ amɛkɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ atsu nii? Aloo jarayeli ŋmɔji wuji pɛ?

english: Irrigation is not just for big farms. Small farmers can use affordable methods like watering cans, simple treadle pumps, or small motorized pumps connected to stream points or shallow wells.
ga: Jeee ŋmɔji wuji pɛ ji nɔ ni akɛ nu shwieɔ nɔ. Okwaafoi bibii baanyɛ amɛkɛ gbɛi ni jara waaa tamɔ nu tsɛnsii kɛ pedal pɔmpii ni yɔɔ mlɛo atsu nii. aloo pɔmp bibioo ko ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii ni akɛtsaa faa ko he loo nubu ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ he eko.

english: How does hot and dry weather affect the behavior and growth of my crops?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nu ni mli egbi lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛ amɛdalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Extreme heat causes crops to lose water rapidly through their leaves. Without adequate soil moisture, plants protect themselves by wilting, dropping blossoms, stopping growth, or producing smaller yields.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa ŋmɔshi nibii amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baabu amɛhe kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ, fɔfɔi ni baa shi, kɛ dalɛ ni amɛbaakpa lɛ nɔ. loo amɛwoɔ fioo

english: What simple steps can I take to keep water in my soil during long dry spells?
ga: Ma nyɛ ma nyɛɛ blɔ nya tomi komɛ a nɔ. Mɛni ji nibii komɛi ni akɛtoɔ nu he yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli?

english: You can cover the soil around your crops with dried leaves or straw (mulching) to stop water from evaporating quickly, and avoid bare soil clearing to help the ground stay cool and moist longer.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Okɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi (mulch) aha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ koni nu lɛ akaho oya. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ ni oootsi lɛ he koni eye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehi shi ni efee fɛ̃i ni edɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops refuse to grow well when I plant them on land where sand has been dug up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋã shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Digging sand removes the rich topsoil where crops get their food and water. Without this layer, crop roots cannot find nutrients, causing plants to stay small, turn yellow, and produce very little yield.
ga: Ŋã ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ jieɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni ŋmɔshi nibii náa niyenii kɛ nu yɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ nɛkɛ fã nɛɛ bɛ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ana niyenii mli hewalɛ. ha tsei bibii lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛwo yibii fioo ko pɛ

english: Why do my maize plants wilt so quickly in the sun even when it rained a few days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: When soil is poor or stripped of organic matter, it loses its ability to hold water like a sponge. The sun dries out the dirt quickly, forcing maize leaves to curl up to save whatever moisture they have left.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ efo mli lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ahiɛ nu mli tamɔ sponji. Hulu la haa muji gĩɔ oya. Enɛ haa ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops need healthy dark soil instead of just rain to grow strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ he hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ moŋ fe nugbɔ kɛkɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ waa lɛ?

english: Rain provides water, but dark topsoil provides the food plants need to build strong stems and produce fruits. Without good soil, crops drink water but stay weak and hungry.
ga: Nugbɔ haa nu, shi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni tsuɔ waa lɛ haa tsei lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛwo yibii. Kɛji shikpɔŋ kpakpa bɛ lɛ Nibii ni adu lɛ baanu nu lɛ shi amɛbaakã he amɛgbɔjɔ ni hɔmɔ baaye amɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop their leaves during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shwieɔ baai yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves on purpose when it is dry to save water. It is the plant's way of protecting itself so it does not dry out completely and die before the rains return.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi kɛji amɛgbi koni amɛbu nu he. Eji gbɛ ni tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe koni ekagbi kwraa ni egbo dani nugbɔ lɛ aku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my tomato roots rot and die when rain leaves standing water on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ haa nu hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When rainwater sits on the soil surface without draining, it cuts off air to the roots, causing them to drown, rot, and die.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nu lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efooo kɛyaa lɛ Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli, ni ehaa amɛshwieɔ nu mli, amɛgboiɔ, ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do heavy rains wash away my young crops instead of helping them grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara lɛ?

english: When farm soil is left completely bare without trees or grass roots to anchor it, heavy rain sweeps away both the dirt and small plant roots. Keeping ground cover slows down water and protects the plants.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tsei loo jwɛi shishifãi bɛ ni baaha etswa shi. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ tsei bibii ashishifãi fɛɛ kɛyaa. Mulching baaha nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni ebaabu tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I leave dry leaves or mulch on top of the dirt around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mishi baai ni egboi loo ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle mihe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Dry leaves act like a blanket over the soil, keeping it cool and trapping moisture so the hot sun does not bake the crop roots or dry out the ground.
ga: Baai ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Enɛ ji koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akashã tsei ashishifãi loo ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi.

english: Why does burning the bush on my land make crops grow well at first, but poorly in the years after?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni ashãa lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishijee mli, shi yɛ sɛɛ mli afii lɛ amli lɛ, ehiii kwraa lɛ?

english: Burning gives a fast burst of ash nutrients for the first season, but it kills beneficial soil bugs and burns away the organic food in the ground, leaving the soil weak for future crops.
ga: Shãa haa ashwishwɛ mli niyenii lɛ tswaa oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ mli. Mohu ɔ, e gbeɔ zugba a mi koolohi nɛ a he hia lɛ, nɛ e shãa niye ní nɛ a ngɛ zugba a mi ɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my plants turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: When soil runs low on plant food like nitrogen, the crop pulls nutrients from its old bottom leaves to feed the new growing leaves at the top, causing the lower leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsei amli niyenii tamɔ nitrogen lɛ faaa. Tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans help my soil produce better maize next season?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ewo ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Beans and cowpeas take food from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants die, that stored food remains in the dirt, serving as free natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, niyenii ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow and dying even when I give them water from the local river?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛɔ maŋ lɛ mli faa lɛ mli haa amɛ lɛ?

english: Rivers near mining or 'galamsey' sites often carry dangerous chemicals like mercury or heavy mud. This polluted water damages plant roots, preventing them from taking up nutrients and causing the leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara tamɔ mercury loo sũ ni tsii yɔɔ faai ni bɛŋkɛ hei ni atsaa shika tsuru yɛ loo ‘galamseys’ lɛ amli. Nu ni mli ewo muji nɛɛ baafite tsei shishifãi. Ehaa tso lɛ náa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why is the soil on my farm becoming so hard that my crop roots cannot grow deep into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa waa akɛ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: When heavy machinery or land clearing removes the dark top layer of earth, the rich, soft soil is lost. The hard subsoil left behind lacks air pockets, making it feel like concrete and stopping roots from spreading.
ga: Kɛ tsɔnei ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ jie shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ duŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ baaje mli. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni edɔ lɛ eshwɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kotoku ko bɛ mli. Enɛ haa enuɔ he tamɔ kɔnkrit ni ehaaa shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Can crops grown on land near gold digging areas absorb harmful chemicals into the food we eat?
ga: Ani tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ hei ni atsaa shika tsuru yɛ lɛ baanyɛ agbala tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui awo niyenii ni wɔyeɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, plants draw up liquids and minerals from the ground through their roots. If the soil or groundwater contains toxic chemicals like mercury or cyanide, the crop can absorb those toxins into its roots, leaves, or fruits.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei gbalaa nu kɛ shika tsuru kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji tsofai fɔji tamɔ mercury loo cyanide yɛ shikpɔŋ loo shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ mli lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ ajie nakai tsofai fɔji lɛ awo amɛshishifãi, amɛbaai, loo amɛyibii amli.

english: Why do my vegetable crops dry out and die so quickly during short dry spells compared to past years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be kuku lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛ akɛto afi ni eho lɛ he

english: Healthy soil acts like a sponge to hold moisture for dry days. When soil loses its natural cover and organic material from land disturbance, it loses its ability to hold water, causing crops to dry out rapidly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji koni ekɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ anɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ laajeɔ ebɔɔ su kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ haomɔ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ nu dɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya.

english: Why are my cassava tubers growing very small and twisted this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ bibii ni efite yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Root crops like cassava need loose, fertile topsoil to expand freely. If the fertile soil has been washed away or mixed with barren clay from deep digging, the roots struggle to expand into big, healthy tubers.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi, tamɔ ŋmei, he miihia shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse, ni woɔ yibii koni amɛshwere yɛ heyeli mli. Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ ni jara wa lɛ ho loo akɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛ yibii ni jɛ shikpɔŋ ni akumɔ mli kwɔ mli lɛ futu mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ bulbs agboi ni he wa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die shortly after muddy flood water from nearby diggings overflows onto my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni nu afua ko ni jɛ shika tsuru ŋmɔ ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ ho kɛba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Muddy water from land clearing carries heavy silt that settles on the ground, sealing the surface. This suffocates the tree roots by cutting off the oxygen they need to survive.
ga: Nu ni mli ewo muji ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli sũ ni tsii ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsiɔ ehe lɛ yɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yaa nɔ lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my maize plants wilting under the hot sun even when the ground looks wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miiho yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni edɔ moŋ?

english: If the underground water has become acidic or polluted by dangerous chemicals, it burns the fine root hairs of the plant. Without those root hairs, the crop cannot drink water even if the ground is wet.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara. Eshãa tso lɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ kɛji shishifãi bɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nyɛŋ anu nu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Why are tough wild weeds the only plants growing on land that was previously cleared for mining?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɛkɛ koo mli jwɛi ni wa nɛɛ pɛ ji tso ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ ajie koni akɛtsa shika tsuru lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Wild weeds are extremely tough and can survive in poor, damaged soil. Cultivated crops are delicate and require balanced nutrients, good topsoil, and clean water that damaged land cannot provide.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi lɛ wa waa ni ebaanyɛ ehi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii ni efite nɔ. Tsei lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛbiɔ niyenii ni sa. Shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ kpakpa kɛ nu ni mli tse ni sũ ni efite lɛ nyɛŋ aha.

english: Why won't chemical fertilizer help my crops grow on land where the top dirt was scraped off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ eyeee ebuaaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ajie lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer acts like food, but topsoil acts like the plate that holds it. Without organic topsoil to hold onto the fertilizer, rain easily washes the chemicals away before crop roots can feed on them.
ga: Fertilizer tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii. Shi sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ plɛte ni fiɔ lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ ni baanyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nugbɔ lɛ hoɔ tsofai kɛyaa oya dani tsei shishifãi baanyɛ aye amɛ.

english: If farm soil has been damaged by land digging, how long will it take before crops can grow well on it again?
ga: Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fite kɛtsɔ ŋmɔ mli ni atsa lɛ nɔ Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ?

english: Without help, nature can take decades to rebuild rich topsoil. However, farmers can speed up recovery over a few years by planting soil-rebuilding cover crops, adding animal manure, and avoiding harmful chemicals.
ga: Kɛji yelikɛbuamɔ ko bɛ Ebaanyɛ ehe adebɔɔ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni ekɛma shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ ekoŋŋ. Shi kɛlɛ, okwaafoi baanyɛ aha amɛhe aya hiɛ oya yɛ afii fioo komɛi pɛ mli kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa amɛhe feɔ shoo lɛ ni amɛduɔ lɛ nɔ. kɛ kooloi ashishifã afata he ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide the necessary shade and moisture for cocoa seedlings during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: How do I know it is the right time to plant my maize after the first rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eji be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Do not plant after the very first rain because the soil may still be too dry underneath. Wait until you get two or three good rains so the soil is wet enough to keep the seeds growing without drying out.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ ejaakɛ ekolɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi tsɔ lolo. Mɛɛ kɛyashi obaaná nugbɔ kpakpa ko. shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests when I plant cassava in the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same spot continuously exhausts specific nutrients from the soil. Rotating your crops gives the soil time to recover and stops crop-specific pests from building up.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ otsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛbaatsu nii jogbaŋŋ, ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shi.

english: How does adding dried animal manure help my soil better than using only chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kooloo ŋmei ni egbi ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ fe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei mli pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii?

english: Chemical fertilizer feeds the plant quickly, but animal manure improves the soil itself by helping it hold water longer and keeping the land soft and rich for future seasons.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei niyenii oya. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii haa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛo kɛtsɔ yelikɛbuamɔ ni ekɛhaa nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha bei ni baaba lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and twisting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking sap from the leaves or spreading a virus. Spraying with neem water or safe insecticides helps control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ loo helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ neem nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot in the ground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Yam rot happens when water collects in the soil without draining, creating a wet environment where fungal diseases thrive and decay the tubers before maturity.
ga: Sweet potato rot lɛ baa kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. creating a wet environment Nɛkɛ ŋmeii hela nɛɛ daa ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛdaraa.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛtsɔko aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the plant doesn't get enough water. Extremely high temperatures stop the flowers from producing seeds, causing them to drop.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Dɔlɛ ni mli wa waa lɛ baatsi fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkawo dumɔwui. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ ni shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and fall off during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ harmatta be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is the cassava plant's natural way of saving water during dry periods. By losing its leaves, the plant reduces water loss and stays alive until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji ŋmei tso lɛ adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Baai ni laajeɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ nu ni laajeɔ lɛ baa shi ni ehiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants roll up into tight tubes on very hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tsɔnei ni mli wa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves to protect themselves from the heat. It reduces the leaf surface exposed to the sun, helping the plant retain moisture during the hottest part of the day.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulu la ni baa baa lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when heavy winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that do not go deep into the ground. As the heavy bunch of fruit grows on top, the tree becomes top-heavy and needs wooden poles for support.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji aduawai lɛ dara yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ tsei akwɛ nɔ.

english: Can I plant fresh green maize seeds directly from a soft cob into my field?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mli tse ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: No, fresh green seeds are not fully mature or dried, so they will rot in the soil. Maize seeds must be fully mature, properly dried, and treated to germinate successfully into healthy plants.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni kpɛɔ lɛ ekwɛko kwraa loo amɛgbiko. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ baagboi yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Esa akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Egbi jogbaŋŋ ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛyashi ekwɛ̃ ni etsɔ tso ni he wa.

english: Why should I buy certified seed varieties instead of planting seeds I saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred to give higher yields, resist local pests and diseases, and tolerate weather changes better than saved seeds, which lose their strength and quality over time.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ maŋ lɛ mli helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni enyɛɔ eshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi hu fe dumɔwui ni ato Enɛ baaha ehewalɛ kɛ ekpakpafeemɔ afite yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How can I check if the maize seeds I bought are still good before planting my whole field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ hi dani madu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: You can do a simple germination test by placing 10 seeds in wet cloth or soil; if 8 or 9 sprout within a few days, your seeds are healthy and good for planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee shweremɔ he kaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Obaanyɛ ofee enɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni okɛaawo mama loo shikpɔŋ ni efɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji dumɔwui 8 loo 9 kwɛ̃ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli lɛ, Odumɔwui lɛ baaná hewalɛ ni amɛhi kɛha dumɔ.

english: What requirements do I need to meet to get subsidized seeds under government farming programs like 'Planting for Food and Jobs'?
ga: Mɛɛ taomɔ nii esa akɛ mashɛ he koni maná dumɔwui ni akɛ shika yeɔ ebuaa yɛ nɔyeli okwaayeli gbɛjianɔtoi tamɔ ‘Okwaayeli kɛha Niyenii kɛ Nitsumɔi’ shishi?

english: You usually need a valid national ID card, basic details about your farm location and size, and registration with your local district agriculture office or recognized farmer group.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ID kaadi ni sa he baahia bo. Shishijee saji ni kɔɔ he ni oŋmɔ lɛ yɔɔ kɛ bɔ ni edara ha lɛ he. kɛ gbɛi ni oooŋmala yɛ okpokpaa nɔ okwaayeli nitsumɔhe loo okwaafoi akuu ko ni akpɛlɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: How many kilograms of maize seed do I actually need to plant one acre of land?
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui kilogram enyiɛ he hiaa mi koni manyɛ madu acre kome?

english: To plant one acre of farmland properly, you need about 8 to 10 kilograms of certified maize seed, depending on the recommended planting distance.
ga: Bɔni afee ni odu ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre 1 jogbaŋŋ lɛ Obaasumɔ aaafee kilogram 8 kɛyashi 10 ni ji ŋmãa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli, ni enɛ damɔ he ni atsɔɔ akɛ adu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin without producing cobs when I plant them under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeee ŋmeii beni midu amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ashishi lɛ?

english: Maize needs direct sunlight to make food and form cobs. When shaded by big trees, the plant stretches upward toward the light, using up all its energy on stem growth instead of cob formation.
ga: Abɛi he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ehoo ni efee ŋmei. Beni yɔɔ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ Tsei lɛ baagbala amɛhe kɛya ŋwɛi kɛya la lɛ he. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ etso lɛ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee cob

english: What happens to my maize crop if I plant two or three seeds too close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui enyɔ loo etɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ bu kome mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the young plants compete with each other for space, soil nutrients, and water, leading to weak stems and small or missing cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei bibii lɛ baatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná hegbɛ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe waaa ni dumɔwui lɛ bibii loo amɛlaaje.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize crops turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen or that heavy rains have washed nutrients away. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or Urea helps restore their dark green color and strong growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo urea lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ dalɛ ni mli wa aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Does it mean my maize is ready to harvest as soon as the hair on top of the cob turns brown?
ga: Ani enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ mi-ŋmã lɛ efee klalo akɛ ebaakpa kɛji yitsɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛ?

english: Not immediately. Brown silks mean pollination is complete and kernels are forming, but you need to wait a few more weeks until the cobs dry out and feel hard before harvesting.
ga: Jeee amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Siliki ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ pollination egbe naa ni dumɔwui miifee. Shi esa akɛ omɛ otsii fioo komɛi kɛyashi ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛnu he akɛ amɛhe wa dani okpa.

english: When is the right time to put fertilizer on my maize so the plants feed properly during growth?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ awo ŋmãa mli koni tso lɛ aná niyenii kpakpa yɛ be mli ni edaa lɛ?

english: Apply your first batch of NPK fertilizer about 2 weeks after the seeds sprout to help roots grow, followed by a top-dressing of Urea at 4 to 5 weeks when the plant grows fast before producing cobs.
ga: Okɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ awo mli aaafee otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ koni eye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdara. Nyiɛmɔ sɛɛ kɛ urea ni akɛwoɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ otsii 4 kɛyashi 5 be mli ni tsei lɛ miida oya dani amɛwo cob.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants looking like someone shot tiny holes all through them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni mɔ ko efo bu bibii kɛtsɔ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide in the center whorl of young maize plants and eat the leaves from the inside out. Spraying targeted controls early in the morning or late afternoon when caterpillars are active helps protect the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli ni amɛyeɔ baai kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kpo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni kudɔɔ nii lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo shwane mli be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or mites that transmit viruses. Controlling these insects early with neem oil or recommended sprays prevents the virus from spreading through your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo mites ni hiɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ neem fɔ loo spray ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ lɛ ebaaye ebua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why did my plantain tree snap and fall over right when the fruits were growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ fãa trukaa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantain stems often collapse under the heavy weight of growing bunches, especially if underground pests like nematodes or stem borers have weakened the root system. Supporting heavy stems with wooden props prevents them from snapping in strong winds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantain tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ jwɛi ni miida lɛ ni tsii waa lɛ shishi. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ nematodes loo stem borers yɛ. Ehaa shishifã lɛ he waaa Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni akɛfiɔ tso ni tsii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekakumɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning yellow and burning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiitso lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because intense direct sunlight burns their soft leaves. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains nearby creates a natural umbrella that shields cocoa seedlings until they are strong enough for full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Ehaa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop during the hot afternoon sun but look fresh again early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, shi amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa kɛ hejɔɔmɔ leebi lɛ?

english: Plants droop in the afternoon heat to slow down water loss when sunlight makes them lose moisture faster than roots can drink. As long as they bounce back by morning, it is a normal protective behavior, but persistent drooping means the soil is too dry.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli koni nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aba shi fioo ejaakɛ hulu la haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Shii abɔ ni amɛbaaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba leebi lɛ Abuɔ lɛ akɛ eji hebuu subaŋ ni sa. Shi shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi be fɛɛ be lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting underground before I am ready to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ dani akpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds water for too long after heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting green shoots in the storage barn before planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ miije shishi amɛmiikwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani amɛkwɛ̃mɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yams naturally break dormancy and begin to sprout after a few months of storage when temperature and humidity rise. Storing yams in a cool, well-ventilated barn on raised racks delays sprouting and preserves root quality.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ shihilɛ ni eyɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ebɔi shweremɔ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni akɛto lɛ sɛɛ beni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ. Too atomo yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli yɛ adekai ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ kɛ amɛkwɛmɔ lɛ asɛɛ afo.

english: Why is my rice crop turning light green and growing slowly even though the field is flooded?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiida blɛoo lɛ? Ani nu eyi ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli?

english: Yellowing rice often indicates a lack of nitrogen in the soil, as heavy water flow can wash away plant nutrients. Applying the right amount of nitrogen fertilizer at key growth stages restores the deep green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu ni hoɔ lɛ mli tsiimɔ baanyɛ ajie tsei amli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii yɛ bei ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli kwɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing plenty of yellow flowers, but the flowers drop off without setting fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when high daytime temperatures prevent pollination, or when the soil alternates between being too dry and too wet. Giving the plants consistent moisture and avoiding excessive nitrogen fertilizer helps flowers develop into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa lɛ tsiɔ pollination naa. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ ehe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ tsɔ teŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná nu daa, ni ajie nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛjɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize together on the same plot of land at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ be kome mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, maize and cassava grow well together because maize matures quickly and is harvested in a few months, leaving plenty of room and sunlight for the slower-growing cassava to expand afterwards.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he kome. Ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Enɛ haa gbɛ kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ agbɛ ashwã sɛɛ mli.

english: Which month of the year is best for me to plant my new cocoa seedlings into the ground?
ga: Mɛɛ nyɔŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha mi akɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: The best time to plant cocoa seedlings is at the beginning of the major rainy season, usually around May or June in Ghana. Planting in wet soil gives the young roots enough water to establish themselves strongly before the harsh dry season arrives.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu kookoo dumɔwui ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ May loo June mli yɛ Ghana. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ ni aduɔ lɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ náa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛmaa hewalɛ dani hɔmɔ ni naa wa lɛ baa.

english: How far apart should I plant my cocoa trees so they grow well without crowding each other?
ga: Te esa akɛ adu kookoo tsei kɛjɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkafee ekome?

english: You should space your cocoa trees about 3 meters by 3 meters apart. This spacing ensures the roots do not struggle against each other for nutrients and water, and it leaves room for air to flow, which prevents fungal diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ o-cacao tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ afee aaafee mitai 3 x mitai 3. Nɛkɛ jɛkɛmɔ nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛkaye niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. ni oha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need shade plants like plantains planted around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ ehe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that shade young cocoa, keeping the ground cool and moist during their first few critical years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa kookoo bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants turn brown and crisp during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the dry season or harmattan, intense heat and dry winds cause young cocoa leaves to lose water faster than their small roots can absorb it. Providing shade trees and placing dried leaves around the base as mulch helps protect them.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli loo Harmattan Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa kookoo baai bibii lɛ amli nu fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ahe shade kɛ baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shishi lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tso lɛ he.

english: Can I plant food crops like cassava or plantain on the same farm while waiting for my cocoa trees to grow?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli be mli ni mimɛɔ ni cacao tsei lɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Yes, intercropping with plantain, cassava, or cocoyam in the first two years gives you food and income while cocoa matures. However, you must keep cassava slightly away from the cocoa stem so it does not block light or steal water.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni akɛ plantains, cassava loo cocoa du yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha oná niyenii kɛ shika be mli ni cocoa lɛ daa lɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ okɛ ŋmei lɛ akabɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ahe fioo. Bɔni afee ni akatsi kane lɛ naa loo akaju nu

english: How many years will I have to wait after planting cocoa before I can start harvesting pods?
ga: Kɛ́ mɔ ko du kookoo sɛɛ lɛ, afii enyiɛ esa akɛ emɛ dani enyɛ ekpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties usually start producing fruit within 2 to 3 years after planting, whereas older traditional varieties take 4 to 5 years. Proper weeding, shading, and soil care help trees produce faster.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli beni adu lɛ sɛɛ, yɛ be mli ni kusum kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ, hulutsoo, kɛ sũ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii oya.

english: Why do so many small flowers on my cocoa tree fall off without turning into full cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Kokoo ŋmeii enyiɛ ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ?

english: A cocoa tree produces thousands of flowers, but only a few turn into pods because they rely on tiny insects for pollination. Extreme weather, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients also cause the tree to drop extra flowers it cannot support.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔii akpei abɔ. Shi fɔfɔi fioo ko pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ejaakɛ amɛkɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ kooloi bibii anɔ koni amɛná ŋmeii. Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii, nu ni bɛ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ hu baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ ajie fɔfɔi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut off extra shoots and small side branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii kɛ tsei aniji lɛ? kɛjɛ kookoo tso lɛ mli

english: Cutting off unwanted shoots, called suckers, prevents them from stealing food and energy from the main tree. Trimming branches also opens up the tree canopy, letting in light and fresh air to prevent black pod disease.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni ataooo, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, no haaa amɛju niyenii kɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni egbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi. Na kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli tse kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa koni okɛtsi black pod hela lɛ naa.

english: How often do I need to clear weeds around my young cocoa trees during their first year?
ga: Ehe miihia ni mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ. Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ madu mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli?

english: You should clear weeds around young seedlings every 4 to 6 weeks during the rainy season. Fast-growing weeds will quickly steal sunlight, water, and soil food from your young trees if left uncontrolled.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ jwɛi awo tsei bibii lɛ ahe daa otsii 4 kɛyashi 6 yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya nɛɛ baaju hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ otsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ oya kɛji akɛ okwɛɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my soil is good enough for growing cocoa before I invest in planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ dani mikɛ mishika awo mli?

english: Good cocoa soil is usually deep, dark, and well-drained topsoil that holds moisture without staying waterlogged. If the land previously supported healthy food crops or dense forest trees, it is generally suitable for cocoa.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ fɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni nu bɛ mli Kɛji akɛ tsutsu lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fiɔ niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni aduɔ loo tsei ni yɔɔ kooi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ amli lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which acts as plant food. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves turn green so the plant can make food and produce good yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji niyenii kɛha tso lɛ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli koni tsei lɛ afee niyenii ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas in my farm help make the soil better for my other crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in tiny nodules on their roots. When the plant dies and rots, this natural nitrogen stays in the soil, acting as free fertilizer for the next crop you plant.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi bibii amli kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo ni egbo. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tightly and causing the plant to stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe waa ni ehaa tso lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the leaf juices, or by a virus spread by these insects. Controlling these pests early with neem oil or approved sprays stops the curling and restores growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni shwieɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ anɔ Kudɔɔ kooloi nɛɛ mra Kɛtsɔ neem fɔ loo tsofa ko ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni awo he odaseyeli nɔ lɛ, ekpaa ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shweremɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is my plantain stem falling over easily even when there is no strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko bɛ po lɛ?

english: Plantain stems fall over when tiny microscopic worms called nematodes or banana root weevils eat away the roots underground. Planting clean, treated suckers and keeping the base mulched helps build strong roots that keep the plant upright.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo banana shishifãi lɛ ye shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni he tse ni atsa amɛ, ni aha amɛshishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi ni wa ni haa tso lɛ damɔɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ baa.

english: Why are all the flowers dropping off my cocoa trees without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ cacao tsei anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when the tree suffers from drought stress, too much shade, or attack by insects like mirids (capsids). Pruning excess shade trees and protecting the farm from insects during flowering helps the flowers set into healthy pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na hɔmɔ he haomɔ. Shade babaoo loo kooloi bibii tamɔ mirids (capsids) tutuaa amɛ. Tsei ni afolɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo be babaoo ni amɛbu ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei kakadaji ahe hiaa mi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes so their leaves can spread out and catch direct sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to make energy, which flows down to grow big, heavy yam tubers under the ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai ni amɛfeɔ hewalɛ. ni hoɔ kɛyaa shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni yam ŋmeii wuji ni tsii feɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi

english: Why do my small mango fruits drop off the tree when they are only the size of marbles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango bibii lɛ miigbee shi kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ be mli ni amɛji marble kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Mango trees naturally drop extra fruit they cannot feed, but heavy fruit drop is usually caused by lack of water during flowering or a fungal disease called anthracnose. Regular watering during dry spells and spraying against fungal infection saves the young fruit.
ga: Mango tsei lɛ jieɔ aduawai ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aye lɛ kpo yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Shi bei pii lɛ, nu ni bɛ yɛ fɔfɔi be mli loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ aduawai ni fiteɔ waa lɛ baa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote tso lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni tso yibii bibii lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when heavy water collects in the soil and prevents air from reaching the roots. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ muji bua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaaa kɔɔyɔɔ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why are my ripe tomatoes cracking open on the sides right before I pick them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ afãi dani mifoɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when watering is irregular—such as a heavy rainstorm following a dry period—causing the inside of the fruit to expand faster than the skin. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and mulching prevents cracking.
ga: Tomatoi tswaa kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ nu lɛ be fɛɛ be, tamɔ yɛ ahum ni naa wa ko ni naa wa mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso yibii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe ehewolo lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii akagbala.

english: Why does my rice farm produce very small yields if I do not clear weeds during the first month?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛji mikɛ jwɛi shwieee nɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young rice plants and steal essential sunlight, water, and soil nutrients during the early critical growth stage. Removing weeds within the first 3 to 4 weeks lets the rice produce strong stems and full grain heads.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmãa tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la ni he hiaa, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii yɛ mra be mli dalɛ bei ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 3 kɛyashi 4 lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ aná ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Can I save the corn seeds from my harvest to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mahere ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛjɛ kpamɔ be mli koni madu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: While you can save seeds, using seeds from a previous harvest often results in smaller cobs and weaker plants in the next season, especially if it was a hybrid variety. Buying certified seeds ensures strong growth and better yields, but if you must re-use seeds, select the healthiest cobs from the middle of your farm.
ga: Kɛji obaanyɛ ohere dumɔwui lɛ po. Shi bei pii lɛ, kɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui bibii kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ baa yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Titri lɛ kɛji akɛ eji nɔ ko ni akɛfee nɔ ko. Dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ahemɔ baaha amɛdara waa ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai. Shi kɛ ehe bahia ni okɛ dumɔwui lɛ atsu nii ekoŋŋ Halamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: How should I store my harvested dry corn seeds so that insects do not destroy them?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ ato koni kooloi akafite amɛ?

english: Dry your corn until the kernels are very hard, clean them well to remove dust, and store them in airtight sacks or sealed containers in a dry place elevated off the floor to prevent moisture, weevils, and mold.
ga: Gbimɔ ŋmãa lɛ kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa. Tsumɔ he jogbaŋŋ koni ojie sũ kɛjɛ mli. Ni okɛto kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo tsɛnsi ko ni atsĩ naa mli yɛ he ko ni egbi ni awó nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ebu he kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmeii, kɛ ŋmeii ahe.

english: Is it good to leave dry corn stalks and husks on my farm after harvesting?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashi ŋmãa ni egbi kɛ ŋmãa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, leaving crop residues like corn husks and dry stalks on the field acts as a living blanket for the soil. It holds soil moisture, keeps the ground cool, and slowly rots down to feed the soil with rich natural nutrients for your next crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ tamɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii akɛ ŋmãa ni hiɛ ka aha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni efiteɔ fiofio koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii babaoo aha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How can I improve my soil for planting corn if I cannot afford chemical fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni akɛduɔ ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ kɛji minyɛɛɛ mahe tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ?

english: You can improve your soil naturally by tilling crop leftovers like old corn husks back into the soil, adding animal manure, or planting beans and peanuts, which naturally put good food back into the earth.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔtɔi ni egbɔ lɛ ni oooku sɛɛ okɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. kɛ kooloo ŋmei afata he loo dumɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ni kɛ niyenii kpakpa baaba Ku sɛɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Why do some farmers harvest their corn while it is fresh instead of waiting for it to dry on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kpaɔ ŋmãa be mli ni eyɔɔ ehee moŋ fe ni amɛaamɛ ni egbi yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Harvesting fresh corn (green maize) allows farmers to get quick money from market women selling roasted or boiled corn. It also clears the land earlier so the farmer can prepare for a second crop before the rains stop.
ga: ŋmãa hee ni akpaa (Green Corn) yeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi ni amɛnáa shika oya kɛjɛɔ jarayeli yei ni hɔ̃ɔ ŋmãa ni ji popcorn loo ŋmãa ni ahoo lɛ adɛŋ. Ejieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hu kɛtsɔ hiɛ bɔni afee ni okwaafoi lɛ asaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ akpa.

english: How do I know when my corn is ready to be harvested fresh for eating?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-abele lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa ehee? Koni aye nii?

english: Corn is ready for fresh harvest when the silk hairs at the top of the cob turn dark brown, the outer husk is still bright green, and squeezing a kernel releases a milky liquid.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ hee beni siliki yitsɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ yiteŋ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ. Kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ eŋɔli ni mli tse. Ni kɛ́ amɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ, nu ko ni tamɔ mliki jeɔ kpo.

english: Can I plant corn twice in the same year on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa shii enyɔ yɛ afi kome mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, if your area gets two distinct rainy seasons, you can plant an early major season crop and a late minor season crop, provided you use fast-maturing seed varieties.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei srɔtoi enyɔ. Obaanyɛ odu shishijee be mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tsu nii

english: Why are my neighbor's corn plants ripening faster than mine when we planted around the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwereɔ oya fe mi nɔ lɛ kɛ́ wɔdu amɛ yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Corn matures at different speeds depending on the exact seed variety used, how much water and sunlight the soil gets, and whether the land had enough natural food to power plant growth.
ga: Abɛi shwereɔ yɛ oyaiyeli srɔtoi amli yɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi pɔtɛɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ naa. Nu kɛ hulu la ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ falɛ Ni ani shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tsei akwɛ̃?

english: What causes my corn to produce small cobs with missing kernels?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-abele lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii? Ni dumɔwui ni elaaje yɛ?

english: Small cobs with empty spots usually happen when the corn plant did not get enough water or plant food when flowering, or because extreme heat prevented proper pollination between plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa kɛji akɛ ŋmeii tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ loo amɛduɔ niyenii beni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Aloo akɛni latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ hewɔ lɛ, pollination ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ aba mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my corn leaves turn yellow when the crop is still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young corn usually mean the plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is their main plant food, or that heavy rains flooded the soil and drowned the plant's roots.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji tso lɛ niyenii titri. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tsei ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu.

english: How long does it usually take for a young coconut tree to start producing fruits on my farm?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: It depends on the variety you plant. Dwarf coconut varieties usually start fruiting within 3 to 4 years, while the traditional tall varieties take about 6 to 10 years to produce their first harvest.
ga: Edamɔ tso srɔtoi ni oduɔ lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni ji dwarf lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii srɔtoi ni yɔɔ blema lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 6 kɛyashi 10 dani amɛwoɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are the first coconuts appearing on my young trees so small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ Ejeɔ kpo yɛ mi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ no hewɔ lɛ eyɛ bibioo waa?

english: Young trees are still growing and developing their transport systems. The first fruits often start small and will naturally expand as the tree matures, provided it receives enough water, sunlight, and soil nutrients.
ga: Tsei bibii yaa nɔ amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ gbɛfaa gbɛjianɔtoi. Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ yibii lɛ jeɔ shishi bibii ni ebaagbɛ eshwa yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni tso lɛ daa lɛ, kɛji akɛ enine shɛ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why does my young coconut seedling seem to grow so slowly in its first year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei tso bibioo lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the first year, coconut seedlings focus most of their energy on developing strong root systems deep underground to absorb water and nutrients, which prepares the tree for faster leaf and stem growth later.
ga: Yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmei tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ shishifãi ni mli wa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni esaa tso lɛ he kɛha baai kɛ shishifãi ni baa oya yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Can I use the water from my fish pond to irrigate my coconut trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛɔ loo nubu mli lɛ afɔ ŋmei tso nɔ nu?

english: Yes, fish pond water is excellent for crops. It contains fish waste and dissolved organic matter rich in nitrogen, which acts as a natural fertilizer to help your coconut trees grow faster and healthier.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, loo ŋshɔ mli nu lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Nɔ ni yɔɔ mli ji loo mli jwɛi kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni mli edɔ ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa o-coconut tso lɛ ni edara oya ni enáa hewalɛ.

english: Is it safe to plant crops like cassava or maize between my young coconut trees?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mi ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, intercropping cassava, vegetables, or legumes between young coconut trees is a great practice. It maximizes land use and provides extra food and income while the coconut trees grow big enough to shade the ground.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei, aduawai loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii ateŋ lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yaa hiɛ kɛyashɛɔ sɛɛnamɔ babaoo he. Ha niyenii kɛ shika kroko yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii tsei daraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are small, young coconuts falling off my tree before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akokoobii bibii shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Premature nut drop is usually caused by water stress during dry weather, sudden changes in weather, lack of key soil nutrients like potassium, or insect pest attacks on the young flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu mli haomɔ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nut ni shwieɔ oya lɛ baa. Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi trukaa Niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, tamɔ potassium, loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni tutuaa fɔfɔi bibii.

english: What causes the bottom leaves of my coconut tree to turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the tree lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen or potassium in the soil, or it is not getting enough water during long dry periods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. aloo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni enine shɛɛɛ nɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli

english: How much water do my young coconut trees need during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Nu enyiɛ he hiaa mi ŋmei tso bibioo lɛ yɛ harmattan be ni nu lɛ mli egbi lɛ mli?

english: Young coconut trees need regular watering to survive dry weather. Pouring about 20 to 30 liters of water around the base of each tree twice a week helps keep the root zone moist.
ga: Ehe miihia ni afɔse ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ nu daa koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli. Akɛ nu aaafee litai 20 kɛyashi 30 shwieɔ tso fɛɛ tso shishi shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni shishifã lɛ he afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Do coconut trees need full sunlight, or can I plant them under shade?
ga: Kokoo tsei biɔ hulutsoo be fɛɛ loo abaanyɛ adu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Coconut trees require full, direct sunlight for at least 6 to 8 hours a day. Shading them under larger trees slows their growth and reduces the amount of fruit they can produce.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, hulu la shɛɔ ŋmei tsei anɔ tɛ̃ɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 6 kɛyashi 8 daa gbi. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo tsei wuji ashishi lɛ, ebaaha amɛdara fioo, ni ebaaha yibii ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo lɛ aba shi.

english: What kind of soil is best if I want to plant coconut trees on my land?
ga: Kɛji miitao madu ŋmei tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ, mɛɛ shikpɔŋ esa akɛ mikɛtsu nii?

english: Coconuts grow best in well-drained sandy loam soil that retains moisture but allows excess water to drain away, preventing the roots from rotting in stagnant water.
ga: Kokooi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa hulutsoo be lɛ hiɔ shi ehaa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ agbo yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to grow green and strong. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure can help the plants recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa abifao koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to rotate my crops every season instead of planting the same crop on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake ŋmɔshi nibii daa be mli moŋ fe ni makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Planting different crops each season prevents pests and diseases from building up in the soil and stops the soil from losing all of one specific nutrient.
ga: Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni aduɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ haaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii kome pɛ fiteɔ.

english: What causes my pepper plant leaves to curl up and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the plant juices, or by a virus they carry. Controlling these insects early prevents the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛhiɛ lɛ kɛbaa Kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai akagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Black cocoa pods are caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which spreads rapidly in high humidity and heavy shade. Pruning overhead branches to let in sunlight and air helps reduce the disease.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpod kɛ kookoo diji baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ kɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. Niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni helai aba shi.

english: What is making my yam tubers rot in the ground before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mikpa amɛ po?

english: Yam rot in the ground is usually caused by waterlogged soil, fungi, or tiny worms called nematodes. Planting on high mounds with good water drainage helps keep the tubers healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ, ŋmei, loo ŋmeii bibii ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ nematodes Kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni bulb lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly when the plants experience severe heat stress, dry soil, or a lack of balanced nutrients. Keeping the soil moist and mulching around the roots helps fruits to set.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni sa lɛ bɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ ni amɛwaa.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my crops while they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Miŋmɔshi nibii be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and plant food from the soil. Clearing them early ensures your crops get all the resources they need to grow fast and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Amɛjiemɔ mra Ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: How does planting my maize with proper spacing help me get bigger cobs?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ŋmãa wuji aba?

english: When maize plants are given enough space, their roots and leaves do not fight each other for food and sunlight, allowing each plant to build larger cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ aha ŋmãa tsei lɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe etswaaa niyenii kɛ hulu la he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso woɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually mature between 9 and 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves yellow and fall off, and the main stem thickens. You can also dig up one root carefully to test its size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ. Baai lɛ ashishigbɛ fã lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebaagbee shi. ni tso lɛ tso titri lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsu shishifã kome hu he nii ni oka bɔ ni elɛɛmɔ ji lɛ okwɛ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to produce fruit in poor soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains require rich soil and plenty of moisture to grow well. In poor soil, root development slows down, delaying flowering. Adding organic compost around the plant speeds up fruit production.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni baa nii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia plantains koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ anɔyaa baa shi, fɔfɔii lɛ asɛɛ tsɛɔ. Organic compost ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni ewo yibii oya.

english: I keep hearing about new improved seed varieties in Ghana, but where can a farmer like me actually get them to buy?
ga: Minu dumɔwui srɔtoi heei ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe. Be fɛɛ be yɛ Ghana Shi nɛgbɛ okwaafoi tamɔ mi baanyɛ ahé dumɔwui nɛɛ yɛ?

english: You can get certified seed varieties through registered agro-input dealers, your local district agricultural extension office, or recognized seed producer associations across Ghana that distribute government-approved seeds.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona dumɔwui srɔtoi ni yɔɔ odaseyeli kɛtsɔ okwaayeli nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ajalɔi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ anɔ. Kpokpaa nɔ Okwaafoi Ahe Nitsumɔhe ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ loo dumɔwui ahe nitsulɔi akui ni akpɛlɛɔ amɛnɔ yɛ Ghana fɛɛ ni hɔ̃ɔ dumɔwui ni nɔyeli lɛ ekpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the seeds I save from my own maize harvest produce less yield when I plant them the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their strength and genetic purity after the first harvest. Certified seeds are specially bred in controlled research fields to ensure every plant grows strong and gives a maximum yield each time you plant fresh ones.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ laajeɔ amɛhewalɛ kɛ amɛfɔmɔ su mli hetsemɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ anɔ yɛ niiamlitaomɔ ŋmɔji ni akudɔɔ mli lɛ amli krɛdɛɛ koni tso fɛɛ tso ada waa ni ewo yibii babaoo be fɛɛ be ni obaadu ŋmɔshi nibii heei.

english: Why do some of these new crop varieties survive better when the rains stop early in my district?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei heei nɛɛ ekomɛi hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?
