english: Agricultural scientists breed these improved crops to mature faster or develop deeper roots, allowing the plant to make the best use of short rainy seasons and resist drought before the dry spell sets in.
ga: Okwaayeli he nilelɔi fɔɔ tsei ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ nɛɛ koni amɛdara oya loo amɛná shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. ni ote shi owo hɔmɔ dani hɔmɔ be lɛ aba.

english: How do improved crop seeds protect my plants from diseases without me spending too much money on chemicals?
ga: Dumɔwui ni atsake lɛ baabu mitsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ helai srɔtoi ahe. Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafee enɛ ni mifiteee shika babaoo yɛ tsofai ahe?

english: Crop researchers combine the natural strength of different plant parents into one seed, giving the plant built-in immunity to fight off common local crop diseases on its own.
ga: Nibii amlitaolɔi kɛ tsei afɔlɔi srɔtoi lɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛi feɔ ekome. yɛ dumɔwu kome mli Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwuɔ amɛshiɔ tsei ahe helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and grow slowly even when I use seeds from the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdaraa blɛoo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ jara nɔ tsuɔ nii moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing often means the plant lacks nitrogen or is suffering from root disease. Uncertified market seeds may carry hidden seed-borne diseases or lack the vigor to draw nutrients effectively from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen loo eyɛ shishifã hela. Ekolɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ jara nɔ ni bɛ he odaseyeli lɛ yɛ helai ni jɛɔ dumɔwui amli baa lɛ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ loo amɛbɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛjieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to plant improved seeds in straight rows with specific spacing instead of broadcasting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu dumɔwui ni asaa amɛhe lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni gbɛ pɔtɛɛ ko yɔɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ dumɔwui adumɔ najiaŋ?

english: Proper spacing ensures each plant gets its own fair share of sunlight, air, water, and soil nutrients without choking its neighbor, which leads to bigger fruits and higher yields.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa enáa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa ni enaaa ekutsoŋbii lɛ anɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ feɔ wuji ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: What does crop improvement research at centers like Legon actually do to help a smallholder farmer?
ga: Mɛni ŋmɔshi nibii ahe niiamlitaomɔ ni afeɔ yɛ hei tamɔ Legon lɛ baanyɛ aye abua okwaafoi bibii?

english: Researchers study local crops and use scientific breeding to fix common farm problems—like low yield, pest attack, and slow growth—so farmers get seeds that produce more food with less effort.
ga: Nibii amlitaolɔi kaseɔ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nii ni amɛkɛ jeŋ nilee mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ naagbai ni afɔɔ namɔ tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa shi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe nii. kɛ shweremɔ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo Koni aha okwaafoi lɛ aná dumɔwui ni woɔ niyenii babaoo kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ fioo

english: How do I know if a new seed variety developed by Ghanaian researchers will actually grow well in my region's soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui heei ni Ghana niiamlitaolɔi lɛ fee lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mikpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Before any new variety is released to farmers, researchers test it in different ecological zones across Ghana—such as the savanna, forest, and coastal areas—to ensure it matches your specific environment.
ga: dani ajie ŋmeii heei kpo amɛtsɔɔ okwaafoi Niiamlitaolɔi lɛ baaka ŋmeii lɛ amɛkwɛ yɛ hei srɔtoi ni bɔɔ nii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yɔɔ lɛ. Yɛ Ghana fɛɛ, tamɔ savannahs, kooi kɛ ŋshɔnaa hei. koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ ekɛ he pɔtɛɛ ni oyɔɔ lɛ kpãa gbee.

english: Why do some new crop varieties stay good in the barn for a long time while others get destroyed quickly by weevils?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii heei No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni henɔi krokomɛi Oya ni ŋmei ko kpataa amɛhiɛ?

english: Researchers deliberately breed certain crops with harder grain coats and natural protective qualities that make it difficult for pests like weevils to bite into and damage the harvest during storage.
ga: Nibii amlitaolɔi etsɔ hiɛ amɛfɔ tsei komɛi ni dumɔwui ni wa fe tsutsu lɛ yɔɔ mli, ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ adebɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do new improved crop varieties require me to apply fertilizer for them to perform well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ tsofa awo tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli bɔni afee ni amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Improved seeds are high-performing crops designed to produce much heavier yields than traditional seeds, and just like a hard worker needs good food, they need adequate soil nutrients to reach their full potential.
ga: Dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji tsei ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni afee koni amɛwo yibii ni tsii fe dumɔwui ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ lɛ. Ni nakai pɛpɛɛpɛ, niyenii kpakpa he miihia mɛi ni tsuɔ nii waa lɛ. Niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli he miihia amɛ koni amɛshɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ he.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow and staying short even after I gave them some fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ be mli ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo mli po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crops need the right type and correct quantity of nutrients at specific times. If you do not give them enough food or apply the wrong fertilizer, the plants cannot develop properly or yield well.
ga: Tsei lɛ hia niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni sa kɛ bɔ ni sa yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛji okɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa haaa lɛ loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa fataaa he lɛ, Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ adara jogbaŋŋ loo amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: What will happen to my cassava harvest if I choose not to apply any fertilizer at all?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava ni mikpaa lɛ nɔ kɛji mihala akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli kwraa?

english: Without sufficient nutrients in the soil, crops cannot build up energy, resulting in stunted growth and small tubers that produce very little yield at harvest time.
ga: Kɛji niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Dumɔwui nyɛŋ afee hewalɛ. Enɛ haa amɛdalɛ sɛɛ foɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce plenty of green leaves but very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ewoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: When crops receive the wrong balance of nutrients, they spend all their energy growing leaves instead of focusing their strength on producing fruits or seeds.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ejaaa lɛ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai. Mohu ɔ, nɔ́ nɛ a kɛ a juɛmi maa nɔ ji yiblii loo dumɔwuhi a peemi.

english: How does giving my crops water irregularly affect their ability to produce a good harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ saa nyɛmɔ ni miyɔɔ akɛ makpa ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai lɛ he?

english: Crops require steady water to carry food from the soil to their leaves and fruits. Irregular watering stresses the plant, causing it to stop growing and drop its flowers before fruit can form.
ga: Tsei hia nu ni yaa nɔ daa koni amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya baai kɛ aduawai lɛ anɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ baaha tso lɛ aná haomɔ. Enɛ haa amɛkpaa dalɛ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔii dani amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why should I treat my crop field for diseases before I even notice any sick plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsa ŋmɔji dani mana tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ po lɛ?

english: Preventive treatments act like vaccines for your crops. Protecting plants before diseases strike prevents infections from taking root and destroying your potential harvest.
ga: Tsofai ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsofai ni akɛbuɔ onibii ahe. Kɛ́ obu tsei ahe dani helai ba lɛ, ebaatsi helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkatswa shishifãi ni amɛfite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What happens if I use the wrong chemical spray to treat spots on my tomato leaves?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni ejaaa ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii kɛtsa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Using the wrong medicine or incorrect doses on crops will not cure the disease and can burn the leaves, causing the plant to stop growing entirely.
ga: Tsofa ni ejaaa loo tsofa ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ tsaaa hela lɛ ni ehaa baa lɛ shãa. Ehaa tsei kpaɔ dalɛ kwraa.

english: Why do sick leaves left on my farm cause healthy plants nearby to also stop growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ ni ashi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ hu kpaɔ amɛkwɛ̃mɔ lɛ?

english: Diseases spread quickly through rain and air from sick crop parts to healthy ones. Leaving infected plants in the field allows sickness to multiply and damage the entire crop yield.
ga: Hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ fãi ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa fãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ehaa hela lɛ yaa hiɛ ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds in my cocoa farm reduce the amount of cocoa pods I get at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni minine shɛɔ nɔ yɛ kpamɔ be mli lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds steal the food, water, and sunlight meant for your crops. When weeds consume these resources, your crops do not get enough nutrients to grow strong and produce good yields.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Beni jwɛi kɛ nibii nɛɛ tsuɔ nii Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ enaaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛdara waa ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my vegetable flowers fall off without producing any vegetables during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When crops face extreme heat without enough water or proper care, they lose the energy required to support fruits, causing flowers to drop off as a survival reaction.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsei lɛ wo la ni mli edɔ waa mli ni nu ni fa loo akwɛɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ewo yibii lɛ baaje edɛŋ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ nɔ ko ni haa mɔ hiɔ shi.

english: How does planting my crops too close together prevent them from yielding big fruits?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ amɛnaa koni amɛkawo yibii wuji?

english: When crops are crowded, they compete against each other for the limited food and light available, leaving no single plant with enough energy to produce a large, healthy harvest.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛkɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ la ni faaa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: I am thinking of growing oil palm trees; do I need to worry much about plant diseases destroying them?
ga: Misusuɔ mu tsei adumɔ he. Ani ehe miihia ni mahao waa yɛ tsei ahelai ni miifite amɛ lɛ ahe?

english: Oil palm trees in Ghana are naturally very tough against most plant diseases, so disease is rarely a major problem for them compared to other crops.
ga: Mu tsei ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ tsei ahelai babaoo anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, hela jeee naagba wulu kɛha ŋmei tsei kɛ akɛto tsei krokomɛi ahe.

english: Do all crops in Ghana suffer equally from diseases, or are palm trees different?
ga: Ani helai naa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ loo esoro ŋmei tsei?

english: Different crops handle threats differently. While crops like cocoa or vegetables easily catch diseases, oil palm trees rarely get sick from diseases, though they do face threats from insects.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi kɛ gbeyeishemɔi srɔtoi kpeɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ kookoo loo aduawai po baanyɛ aná hela oya. Shi bei pii lɛ, helai baaa oil palm tsei anɔ. Yɛ hegbeyeiwoo ni jɛɔ kooloi amli lɛ po mli.

english: What is the main threat to my oil palm trees if diseases aren't a big problem?
ga: Mɛni ji gbeyeishemɔi titrii ni baa mi-oil palm tso lɛ nɔ kɛji hela jeee naagba wulu?

english: The main threat to oil palm trees in Ghana comes from insect pests rather than diseases, specifically insects that attack and damage the leaves.
ga: Nɔ titri ni woɔ mu tsei ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ ahe gbeyei lɛ jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli moŋ fe helai. Titri lɛ, kooloi bibii ni tutuaa ni amɛfiteɔ baai lɛ.

english: What are leaf miners, and what do they do to my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji tsofa-kɛ-ŋma? Ni mɛni amɛfeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Leaf miners are tiny insect pests whose young crawl inside the leaves of plants like oil palms, eating the tissue from the inside and damaging the plant's ability to grow.
ga: Mɛi ni shwieɔ baai lɛ ji kooloi bibii. Amɛkpãa tsei tamɔ mu tsei ahe baai lɛ amli, ni amɛyeɔ fãji ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. ni efite nyɛmɔ ni tsei yɔɔ ni amɛkɛbaadara lɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my palm trees looking damaged even though there is no disease on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-palm tso lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni efite eyɛ mli akɛ efite moŋ lɛ? Ani helai komɛi bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Even without disease, insect pests like leaf miners can burrow into your palm leaves and damage them, making the foliage look dry, brown, or eaten.
ga: Kɛji hela ko bɛ po lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ mɛi ni shwieɔ baai lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ ŋmeii amli ni amɛfite amɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbi, asarasu, loo aye.

english: How often should I walk through my palm plantation to check on the trees?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ amli koni mayakwɛ tsei lɛ?

english: You should walk through your oil palm farm to inspect the trees at least once every two weeks so you can spot insect problems early.
ga: Esa akɛ otsɔ mu ŋmɔ ko mli ni okwɛ tsei lɛ amli kɛ hoo lɛ daa otsii enyɔ bɔni afee ni ona kooloi amli naagbai mra.

english: Why is it important to check my palm leaves every two weeks instead of just once a month?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ mi-palm baai lɛ amli daa otsii enyɔ moŋ fe shikome pɛ yɛ nyɔŋ mli lɛ?

english: Checking every two weeks helps you catch pests like leaf miners when they first arrive, preventing them from spreading across the entire leaf and multiplying across your farm.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni akwɛɔ mli Otsii enyɔ baaye abua bo ni omɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ tso ni atsɛɔ lɛ leaf miners lɛ beni amɛba klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ. Enɛ ji koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã tsei lɛ ahe ni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Should I spend more money buying disease sprays or spending time checking for insects on my palm trees?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafite shika babaoo yɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ helai anɔ lɛ he loo mafite be babaoo kɛkwɛ ŋmei tsei amli koni mana kɛji kooloi bibii yɛ mli?

english: You should focus more time on checking for insects. Because palm trees in Ghana rarely get sick from diseases, buying disease sprays is often unnecessary, but monitoring for insect pests is essential.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ be babaoo ama kooloi bibii akwɛmɔ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, bei pii lɛ, helai baaa ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ bei pii lɛ ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofa ni akɛtsiɔ hela naa lɛ. Shi hiŋmɛi ni aaakwɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ lɛ he miihia.

english: Are there specific insect pests I should look out for if my palm farm is in northern Ghana?
ga: Ani tsɛŋemɔ helai pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ ni esa akɛ male kɛji akɛ mi-palm ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ?

english: In northern Ghana, leaf miners are a common and specific pest problem for oil palms, so farmers in that area must pay extra attention to their leaves.
ga: yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ Leaf miners ji naagba ni afɔɔ namɔ ni ji naagba pɔtɛɛ ko kɛha mu tso. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ nakai kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ agbala amɛjwɛŋmɔ krɛdɛɛ kɛba amɛbaai lɛ anɔ.

english: What parts of the palm tree should I look at closely when inspecting for pests in the north?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmei tso lɛ fãi esa akɛ makwɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikwɛ kɛji kooyigbɛ ŋmeii yɛ mli?

english: You should look closely at the leaves of the palm trees, as pests like leaf miners in northern Ghana target the leaf tissue directly.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ ŋmei tso lɛ baai lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ ji akɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ tutuaa baa lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are my young cocoa pods dropping off the tree before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo bibii lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce more flowers and small pods than they can support. When the tree carries too many pods or faces water stress, it sheds the extra ones so it can direct enough nutrients to make the remaining pods grow big and healthy.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔi bibii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. nɔ ni fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ eye ebua Kɛji tsei lɛ eyi kɛ ŋmeii fe nine loo amɛna nu he haomɔ Ejieɔ ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ koni enyɛ ehiɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ adara ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why should I pull out some healthy maize seedlings after they sprout when I worked hard to plant all the seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmãa dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛjɛ mli beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ beni mitsu nii waa koni mikɛdu dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: When maize seedlings grow too close together, they fight for soil nutrients and sunlight, leaving all of them weak. Removing the excess plants gives the remaining ones enough space and food to produce large, heavy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ náa he ko kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why does cutting off green leaves from my tomato plants help them produce bigger fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe baai eŋɔli lɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-tomato lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii wuji lɛ?

english: Extra leaves consume food that the plant could use for fruiting. When you trim unnecessary lower leaves, the plant sends all its nutrients straight into growing larger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Baai ni fa fe nine lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni tso lɛ baanyɛ ekɛwo yibii. Kɛji ofolɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni he ehiaaa lɛ Tsei lɛ baatsu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛkwɛ tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Is it useful to plow crop leaves and stalks back into my farm soil after harvest instead of burning them?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ abaaku sɛɛ akɛ tsei ahe baai kɛ ŋmeii awo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshã lɛ?

english: Burying crop leftovers returns valuable nutrients back into the soil as they break down. It improves the soil's ability to hold water and feeds your next crop naturally, saving you money on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Nibii ni eshwɛ ni afuɔ lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni amɛfiteɔ lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli ni ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okɛ shika toɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe.

english: Why is my maize crop growing very tall with thick green leaves, but the corn cobs are tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi ŋmãa lɛ ji bibioo.

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer makes the plant focus all its energy on growing leaves and stems instead of fruit. A balanced fertilizer gives the plant what it needs to develop strong, full cobs.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai kɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe aduawai. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop most of their leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is a defense mechanism. Leaves lose water quickly in dry air, so the tree sheds them to save moisture in its trunk and roots until the rainy season returns.
ga: Baai ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he. Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi mli. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my pepper plants lose their flowers without producing any peppers during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ fite ni ekɛ pepper wooo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When weather conditions are too hot or dry, pepper plants drop flowers to protect themselves from overworking. Once temperatures drop and moisture increases, the plant will keep its flowers and set fruit.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nitsumɔ ni fe nine lɛ he. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi ni hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baaya nɔ awo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii.

english: What will happen if I plant my cassava cuttings very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu yucca tsei aniji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ mihe lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: Planting cassava too close causes the roots to overcrowd underground with no space to expand. You will harvest many thin, woody roots instead of large, heavy tubers.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi aahu akɛ amɛbɛ he ko ni amɛbaagbɛ amɛshwã. Obaakpa shishifãi komɛi. yɛ yibɔi babaoo mli moŋ fe ni akɛ yitsei wuji ni tsii baatsu nii

english: If I plant a whole, very large yam tuber, will it give me a bigger harvest than planting a small piece?
ga: Kɛ midu tso muu ni ji sweet potatoes wuji waa Ani ebaawo yibii babaoo fe bulbs bibii ni mikwɛɔ lɛ?

english: Not necessarily. A seed yam that is too large spends its energy feeding the old tuber body rather than building a strong root system. Cutting large tubers into proper seed sizes encourages healthy, new tuber growth.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Sweet potato dumɔwui ni dara tsɔ lɛ baafite hewalɛ ni ekɛha ŋmeii momo lɛ niyenii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaama shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii wuji kɛyashɛ dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaawo ŋmeii heei ni he wa lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil if I do not harvest them during a heavy rainy period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji mikpaaa amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Mature cassava tubers stop growing and begin absorbing excess water from soaked soil. If left in waterlogged ground too long, the tuber tissues suffocate and decay underground.
ga: Cassava tsei ni eda lɛ kpaɔ amɛdalɛ ni amɛjeɔ nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ shishi. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Tuber fãji lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do I have to cut down my cocoa tree if only a few leaves look sick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ afo cacao tsei lɛ amli kɛji akɛ baai fioo pɛ hela mɔ amɛ?

english: Diseases like Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus spread quickly through the tree's roots and through tiny insects to nearby healthy trees. Cutting down infected trees immediately is the only proven way to protect the rest of your farm from catching the sickness.
ga: Helai tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ tsei shishifãi kɛ kooloi bibii amli. kɛya tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ nɔ Tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooofolɔ oya lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni ana he odaseyeli akɛ oootsɔ nɔ obu oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he kɛjɛ hela he.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are getting sick before they stop bearing fruit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cacao tsei lɛ hela mɔ amɛ dani amɛkpa yibiiwoo?

english: Look closely at the young leaves for red or yellow veins, check if the branches look swollen, or notice if young pods turn black quickly. Catching these early signs helps you act before the whole farm gets infected.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai bibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni ona fãji tsuru loo ŋmɔŋ. Kwɛmɔ kɛji tsei lɛ aniji lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛfuu. Aloo kadimɔ kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ oya? Kɛ́ omɔ okadii nɛɛ mra lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ofee nɔ ko dani ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ aná hela.

english: Can disease spread to my cocoa farm from a neighboring farm?
ga: Ani hela baanyɛ ajɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli agbɛ ashwã mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, pests like mealybugs, wind, rain, and even dirty cutlasses can carry diseases from a neighbor's sick trees directly to your healthy ones.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ mealybugs, kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ, kɛ ŋmeii ni he tseee po. Helai ni jɛɔ akutsoŋnyo tso ni hela mɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ otso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess moisture and low sunlight create fungi that cause Black Pod disease. Clearing thick branches to let in sunlight and harvesting ripe pods quickly helps prevent this rot.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine kɛ hulu la fioo pɛ kɛ ŋmei ni kɛ blackpod hela baa lɛ baa. Niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ amlijaa koni hulu la ashɛ nɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ ni akpaa oya lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: What should I do to the soil before planting new cocoa trees where diseased trees were cut down?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee shikpɔŋ lɛ dani madu cacao tsei heei ni afo kɛjɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: You must completely remove all old infected roots from the ground, leave the land to rest for a few months, and plant barrier crops like plantains before putting in new hybrid cocoa seedlings.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie shishifãi momoi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe nyɔji fioo komɛi. kɛ tsei ni tsiɔ mɔ gbɛ, tamɔ plantains lɛ adumɔ dani akɛ hybrid cocoa dumɔwui heei afata he.

english: If I abandon my sick cocoa farm for a few years, will the crop disease disappear on its own?
ga: Kɛji mishi mi-kookoo ŋmɔ ni hela mɔ lɛ afii fioo komɛi. Ani tso hela lɛ baaho lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: No, many diseases and pests can survive in the soil or on wild plants around the farm. You must actively clear the infected trees and treat the land properly before planting again.
ga: Dabi, helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui babaoo baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo yɛ koo mli tsei ni bɔle oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ anɔ. Esa akɛ ojie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ dani odu ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know when a cocoa tree is too old and needs to be cut down and replaced?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ cacao tso ko egbɔ tsɔ ni ehe miihia ni afo lɛ ni akɛtsake?

english: If a tree is over 25 to 30 years old, produces very few pods despite good care, or has a hollow and decaying trunk, it has reached the end of its productive life and should be replaced.
ga: Kɛ́ tso lɛ eye fe afii 25 kɛyashi 30 lɛ, kɛ́ akwɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ po lɛ, ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ. aloo eyɛ tso lɛ shishi ni mli ewo muji ni egbo Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ eshɛ esɛɛnamɔ shihilɛ naagbee ni esa akɛ atsake lɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees giving me fewer pods every year even though I weed regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo daa afi lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ daa?

english: As trees age or suffer from hidden diseases and poor soil nutrients, their energy goes into surviving rather than producing pods. Weeding helps, but trees also need pruning and fertilizer to yield well.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ daraa loo helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ, Amɛ hewalɛ baahi shi moŋ fe ni amɛaafee ŋmeii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua. Shi ehe miihia hu ni akumɔ tsei ni awo amɛ nu koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Does too much direct sunlight hurt my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ tsɔ lɛ yeɔ mi kokoo tsei lɛ awui?

english: Yes, direct sunlight scorches cocoa leaves and dries out the tree, especially when young. Cocoa trees need temporary shade from plantains or permanent shade trees to stay healthy and retain moisture.
ga: Hɛɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa kookoo baai lɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ gĩɔ. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ oji oblanyo fioo. Cocoa tsei lɛ he miihia amɛ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ni baa daa lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: What food crops can I grow to earn money while waiting for my newly planted cocoa trees to produce?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu koni maná shika be mli ni mimɛɔ ni mi-kokoo tsei heei ni midu lɛ ajie amɛhe kpo lɛ?

english: You can plant food crops like plantain, cassava, maize, and cocoyam. These grow fast, bring quick food and money, and provide necessary shade for your young cocoa plants.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu niyenii tamɔ plantains, cassava, ŋmãa, kɛ kookoo. Enɛɛmɛi daa oya. Okɛ niyenii kɛ shika aba oya. ni okɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa aha o-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ.

english: Leaves turn yellow mainly when the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or when roots are sitting in waterlogged ground. Nitrogen helps plants build green food, so adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps bring back the dark green color.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ titri lɛ kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ ta hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛsu ni ji eŋɔli ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do crops planted under big, bushy shade trees grow tall and skinny with very little fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ashishi lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Most crops need direct sunlight to produce energy for flowers and fruit. When growing under dense shade, the plant spends all its energy stretching upward to reach the light, leaving no energy to grow strong stems or yield fruit.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo biɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ amɛha amɛfɔfɔi kɛ amɛyibii lɛ. Kɛji amɛmiida yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛgbala amɛhe kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛná la. Hewalɛ ko bɛ ni eshwɛ ni baaha tsei ni wa akwɛ̃ loo amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so poorly even when rain falls heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal water, fertilizer nutrients, and root space directly from your crops. Even with plenty of rain, the weeds consume the soil food before your crops can absorb it.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu. ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shishifãi ahe tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛ otsei lɛ amli. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ, shi jwɛi hu yeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Why do the tiny flowers on my cocoa tree keep falling off before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from water stress, sudden hot weather, or insect attacks from pests like mirids. Maintaining reasonable shade, mulching to hold soil moisture, and managing pests keeps flowers on the branches.
ga: Cocoa tsei baawo fɔfɔi kɛji nu he haomɔ miipiŋ amɛ. kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ trukaa loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ pollen, hulutsoo ni sa ni akwɛɔ nɔ Mulching koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akwɛmɔ Ye obua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their blossoms instead of forming peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the soil dries out completely or when midday temperatures become too hot. Mulching around the roots and watering regularly keeps the soil cool and encourages fruit to set.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛ nu ni oooha amɛ daa lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni eye ebua aduawai lɛ ni amɛma shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall down when strong winds blow or when bunches get heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa loo kɛ́ jwɛi lɛ mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants do not have a deep taproot to anchor them securely in the soil. Their shallow root system struggles to support heavy fruit during high winds, so propping the stalk with a strong wooden pole is needed for support.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifã ni mli kwɔ ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ amɛ shiŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛshishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi aduawai ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni akɛ tso ni wa afi tso lɛ sɛɛ koni akɛfi tso lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling tightly upward and looking stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso kɛmiiya ŋwɛi ni etamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is commonly caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that transmit plant viruses, or by severe dry heat. Controlling whiteflies early and keeping soil moisture steady stops the curling disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni hiɛ helai ni baa tsei amli lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli Early Whitefly Control Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ baaye abua ni yitsɔi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ akagbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft, watery, and rotten inside the soil when heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ, nu yɔɔ mli ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When rain saturates waterlogged ground, the roots drown and soil fungi cause them to rot. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds allows excess water to drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, jɛmɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee nu mli ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaha amɛgboi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why do my stored yam tubers start sprouting white shoots in the barn long before planting season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii yɛŋ kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be saŋŋ dani amɛkwɛ̃mɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Yams naturally wake up from their resting period after a few months, triggered by warmth and humidity in storage. Keeping your yam barn well-ventilated, elevated, and shaded slows down early sprouting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ wɔɔ mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ nitoohe lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ oha o-sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa, ni ewo nɔ, ni eyɛ hulutsoo lɛ, ebaaha ekwɛ̃mɔ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why do my mature maize stalks break and snap near the base right before I am ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei ni eda lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfoɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he dani mifeɔ klalo akɛ makpãa lɛ?

english: Maize stalks break mainly due to stem borer insects eating the inside of the stem or from weak stalk growth caused by overcrowding. Planting with proper spacing and applying appropriate pest control keeps the stalks strong until harvest.
ga: Koolooi ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ abele tsei ni ekumɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa. aloo kɛjɛ tsei bibii ni shwereɔ fe nine lɛ kɛbaa lɛ adalɛ mli. Dumɔ ni akɛ gbɛ ni sa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ ni sa baaha ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi kpamɔ be mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither and die when I plant them in an open field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct sunlight and heat. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa protects them from harsh sun, keeps the soil moist, and prevents the seedlings from drying out.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he waa diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa tamɔ plantains kɛ cocoa bibii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaaa dumɔwui lɛ agbi

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over easily during strong winds before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can be weakened by tiny pests called nematodes or banana weevils that eat the underground bulb. Earthing up soil around the base and supporting the plants with wooden props prevents them from tipping over.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ nematodes loo banana ŋmeii ni yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni bɔleɔ shishitoo lɛ he lɛ ni akɛaabɔle tso lɛ he kɛ tso nibii ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ Ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is an essential nutrient for leaf growth, or that heavy rains have washed nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my maize leaves and dark powdery dirt inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai kɛ muji ni tamɔ powder ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mfonirifeemɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a pest that burrows into the center of maize plants to feed on fresh growing leaves.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmei tsei amli koni amɛye baai heei.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same plot of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously on the same land exhausts specific soil nutrients and allows maize-specific pests and weeds to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the soil.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ daa yɛ he kome lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ afite. ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ jwɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to erect tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mato tso kakadaŋŋ ko koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch sunlight efficiently for tuber growth, and keeping leaves off damp soil prevents fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ. Ni kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi baa helai ni jɛɔ ŋmeii amli baa lɛ anaa.

english: How do I know when my cassava crop is ready for harvesting, and why do tubers turn soft if left too long?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa? Ni mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ feɔ blɛoo kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava is typically ready when lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, usually between 9 to 12 months after planting. Leaving tubers in wet soil past maturity causes soil fungi to enter and rot the tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ dumɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ kɛyashi amɛbaadara tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ abote mli ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my tomato plants with dry grass or straw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, traps soil moisture, keeps the roots cool during hot afternoons, and prevents weeds from taking nutrients away from your tomatoes.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ tomato mli

english: Why do the blossoms on my pepper plants drop off to the ground without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛtsakeee pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper blossoms drop when the plant experiences severe heat stress, irregular watering, or a shortage of essential soil nutrients needed to support fruit development.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni ashwieɔ shi daa loo niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha aduawai adalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: What is the correct way to apply chemical fertilizer so it doesn't burn my crops?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ awo mli jogbaŋŋ koni akashã tsei lɛ?

english: Fertilizer should be applied a few inches away from the plant stem in moist soil rather than directly touching the stalk, allowing roots to safely draw in nutrients without leaf or root burn.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ inchii fioo komɛi. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeshɛ tso lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni amɛshãaa baai loo shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I burn my maize stalks after harvest like my father used to do?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ oshãaa ŋmãa lɛ beni okpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ tamɔ bɔ ni Ataa feɔ tsutsu lɛ?

english: Burning crop stalks destroys valuable nutrients and leaves your soil bare under the hot sun. Leaving the stalks on the land lets them decay naturally, turning into free fertilizer that makes your soil richer for the next planting season.
ga: Tso shishifãi ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ashi tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha amɛgboi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Ebafeɔ nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli, ni baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: What should I do with all the dried plant leaves and stems left on my land after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee tso lɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni egbi ni eshwɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: Instead of clearing or throwing them away, spread those dried plant remains across your field. They act as a natural protective cover that shields your soil from harsh heat and heavy rain.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsi loo oshɛrɛ lɛ ashwie lɛ, Gbalamɔ nakai tsei ni egbi ni eshwɛ lɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Amɛtsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni buɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he.

english: How does leaving dried plant materials on my farm help my crops survive long dry spells?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni egbi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli?

english: Dried plant remains act like a blanket over your field, trapping moisture in the dirt and stopping the sun from drying out the soil too quickly so your crops have water longer.
ga: Tsei ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii lolo akɛ tsɔne ni akɛhaa oŋmɔji lɛ anɔ. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ni ehaa hulu la lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Koni onibii lɛ ahi nu mli be kakadaŋŋ

english: Why does the bare ground on my farm get so hot that it hurts my young crop roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ he ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔ waa aahu akɛ eefite mishishifãi bibii lɛ?

english: Bare soil absorbs direct sunlight like a dark stone, heating up root zones to harmful levels. Covering the ground with old crop remains keeps the soil cool and safe for tender young roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ ŋmɛɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ tamɔ tɛ ni tsuɔ. Enɛ haa shishifã lɛ mli dɔɔ kɛyashɛɔ he ko ni yɔɔ oshara. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii momoi shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shishifãi bibii lɛ feɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Can leaving old plant waste on my soil really save me money on chemical fertilizers?
ga: Ani tsei momo ni etse amɛhe lɛ ni oooshi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha okɛ shika akafite yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, as the plant remains break down and rot into the earth, they feed beneficial organisms like earthworms and slowly release natural nutrients back into the soil, reducing your need for bought fertilizers.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ tsei yaa nɔ amɛgboɔ ni amɛboteɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛkɛ lɛ amɛhaa niyenii nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii mli hewalɛ fiofio kɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ahemɔ baa shi.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away my topsoil, and how can plant waste on the ground stop it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Ni te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni jwɛi ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aaatsi enaa?

english: Heavy raindrops hit bare soil like small hammers, breaking it apart and washing it away. Plant waste left on the ground breaks the impact of the rain, holding your good topsoil in place.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tswa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ tamɔ hama bibii. Ha efo mli bibii bibii ni ofɔ he. Tsei amli jwɛi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ haa nɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ baa shi. ni ehaa osũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Will leaving dead plant stems on my farm attract dangerous pests to my new crops?
ga: Ani tsei ni egboi ni ajieɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baagbala tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ kɛba miŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ anɔ?

english: Not if managed correctly; while some pests prefer dead plants, leaving crop remains also creates a home for beneficial insects and spiders that eat harmful farm pests, helping balance your field naturally.
ga: Dabi kɛji akɛ atsu he nii jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni kooloi komɛi sumɔɔ tsei ni egboi lɛ, Shi ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ hu feɔ shia kɛha kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ. Enɛ haa oŋmɔ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How can leaving old crop remains on the soil help me control weeds without buying expensive chemicals?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbɔ ni mashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni makwɛ jwɛi anɔ ni miheee tsofai ni jara wa?

english: A thick layer of crop remains blocks sunlight from reaching the ground, which prevents weed seeds from getting the light they need to sprout and grow.
ga: Nibii ni ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ mli ni etse ehe lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa lolo koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ aná la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛdara.

english: Why do extension officers say that leaving plant remains on the land helps us fight changing weather patterns?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ akɛ nitsumɔhei ni wɔshiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa wɔ ni wɔwuɔ wɔshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ?

english: As temperatures rise and rain becomes unpredictable, keeping plant remains on the field protects the soil from drying out fast, helping crops withstand unexpected heatwaves and droughts.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ bafee nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ Tsei ni ashi yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni abu shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdamɔɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ naa.

english: Can I plant my new seeds directly into a field that still has old crop remains covering it?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwui heei yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni ŋmɔshi nibii momo ehà nɔ lolo lɛ mli?

english: Yes, you can simply clear small spaces in the plant remains where you want to drop your seeds, leaving the rest of the soil covered and protected while your new crops grow.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ ojie he bibioo ko. yɛ tso humus lɛ mli he ni osumɔɔ ni odu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ lɛ. Afeɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni eshwɛ lɛ ni oooshi ni okɛha nɔ ni obu he yɛ be mli ni otso hee lɛ miida lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees take several years before they start producing any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ebɔi ŋmeii feemɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees require time to build strong root systems and thick branches to support heavy pods. Expecting fruits early is like expecting a child to do adult work; the plant must focus its energy on growing strong first.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ he miihia be koni amɛná shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ niji ni mli tse ni baaye abua ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ. Kɛ́ wɔkpa nɔ ko ni baajɛ mli aba oya gbɛ lɛ, etamɔ nɔ ni wɔkpaa gbɛ akɛ gbekɛbii baatsu onukpai anitsumɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ jwɛŋmɔ ama tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛdara waa klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither when I cut down all the big shade trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi beni mifoɔ tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or canopy trees to shelter them and keep the surrounding soil moist while they mature.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo canopy tsei koni amɛná he ko ni amɛhi ni amɛha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cut off healthy-looking branches from my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mifolɔ tso lɛ niji ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary branches that suck energy away from pod production. It also lets sunlight and air flow through the tree, which stops mold and diseases from growing.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa ni shwieɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ pod feemɔ mli lɛ. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hu tsɔɔ tsei lɛ amli. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai srɔtoi adalɛ naa

english: Why do I need to keep weeding my farm even after I cleared everything thoroughly last month?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maya nɔ mafolɔ jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mijie nɔ fɛɛ nɔ kɛjɛ mli nyɔŋ kome ni eho nɛ moŋ?

english: Weeds grow back continuously and steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crops. Crop care is an ongoing effort throughout the season, not a one-time job.
ga: Jwɛi baaya nɔ akwɛ̃ ni amɛbaajɔɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ ji mɔdɛŋbɔɔ ni yaa nɔ yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ. Jeee shikome nitsumɔ ni.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow even though I applied fertilizer once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli shikome pɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: A single application of fertilizer may not be enough, or heavy rains might have washed it away before the plant could absorb it. Crops need continuous nutrient care and proper soil moisture to stay green and healthy.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli shikome pɛ lɛ faaa. Aloo, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ahoo tsei lɛ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ amɛ. Tsei lɛ he miihia ni akwɛ amɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ahi shi jogbaŋŋ koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do pests come back to my farm even after I sprayed insecticide a few weeks ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ miiku amɛsɛɛ amɛmiiba miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie shi otsii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ moŋ.

english: Chemicals only kill the insects present at the time of spraying, but new eggs hatch and pests fly in from neighboring fields. Protecting crops requires regular farm visits and continuous pest monitoring.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ be mli ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ pɛ. Shi ŋmeii heei kɛ ŋmeii baajɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli aba. Dumɔwui ahebuu biɔ ŋmɔ saramɔi daa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai akwɛmɔ daa.

english: Why can't I plant my maize at any time of the year I choose in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ afi lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni mihala yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Crops rely heavily on natural rainfall cycles and specific temperature conditions to germinate and grow. Planting outside the proper rainy season causes seeds to dry up in the soil.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ damɔ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔshiimɔi kɛ dɔlɛ shihilɛi pɔtɛɛ anɔ waa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests now than it did when I first started farming it years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo tamɔ beni mije okwaayeli shishi afii babaoo ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Soil loses its nutrients every time crops are harvested. Without giving the land rest, adding manure, or practicing crop rotation, the soil gets exhausted and yields will drop over time.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ laajeɔ be fɛɛ be ni abaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli ni ahaaa he ko ni akɛjɔɔ ehe, akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he, loo akaseee ŋmɔshi nibii ni akwɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep falling off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress, such as extreme heat or uneven watering. Consistent care and watering help the plant retain its flowers so they can form fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he. Kɛ́ akwɛ tso lɛ nɔ daa ni awo lɛ nu lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni ewo yibii.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous harvest not grow as well as certified seeds from the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛ mikpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛɛɛ tamɔ jarayeli dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Farm-saved seeds lose their strength and disease resistance over time. Certified seeds are specially produced to resist local diseases and yield higher harvests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ hewalɛ kɛ helai ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Afeɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni ekɛte shi ewo maŋ lɛ mli helai ni ekɛ yibiiwoo babaoo baa.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and drop off when exposed to full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle intense direct sunlight because their root systems are not strong enough to replace lost moisture. Providing shade crops like plantains protects the leaves from burning and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ ahe waaa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ atsake ŋmɔtɔ ni elaaje lɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my crop plants stop growing and look weak during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry Harmattan winds rapidly pull moisture out of plant leaves and dry up the soil. Crops naturally slow down their growth to conserve energy and water until the rains return.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli egbiɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ haa amɛdalɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in cool, humid conditions when air cannot flow freely. Clearing excess branches and picking ripe pods early helps prevent moisture buildup and stops the rot from spreading.
ga: Fɛ̃i ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni mli edɔ waa lɛ kɛ black pod hela baa. he ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ atsɔ mli oya Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ mligbalamɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ akpamɔ mra Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi lɛ naa ni ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ naa.

english: Why are small insects creating dark spots on my young cocoa stems and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ mi-kookoo bibii lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Dark spots on stems are usually caused by sap-sucking pests like mirids or capsids. These insects damage the plant's tissues while feeding, which can stunt the tree's growth if left unmanaged.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mirids loo capsids lɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ mli fãji beni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tso lɛ dalɛ naa kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many flowers, but very few of them grow into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔi fioo komɛi pɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Flowers fail to form pods mainly due to a lack of tiny pollinating insects, prolonged dry weather, or poor soil nutrients. Maintaining adequate moisture and shade helps pollinators thrive and supports pod development.
ga: Fɔfɔi nyɛɛɛ afee pods, titri lɛ yɛ pollinators ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ni aaakwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa pollinators lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa pod lɛ shweremɔ.

english: Will cutting off branches from my crop trees reduce the total amount of harvest I get?
ga: Ani niji ni mifoɔ kɛjɛɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha mikpamɔ fɛɛ aba shi?

english: Pruning unwanted or diseased branches actually increases your yield. It allows sunlight and fresh air to reach the productive parts of the plant, helping healthy flowers grow while reducing disease risk.
ga: Niji ni ataooo loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni aaafo lɛ baanyɛ aha yibiiwoo aya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ fãi ni woɔ yibii lɛ ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ be mli ni ehaa helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why is it important to wait until cocoa pods turn fully yellow before picking them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni amɛ kɛyashi kookoo lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ajie lɛ?

english: Fully ripe pods have fully developed sugars and oils inside the beans. Harvesting green or partially ripe pods leads to flat, bitter beans that fail quality checks and fetch lower market prices.
ga: Pods ni ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ yɛ sugar kɛ fɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli kwraa. Pods ni ji eŋɔli loo ni ekwɛ̃ fioo lɛ ni akpaa lɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ akwɛ bɔ ni amɛhi ha lɛ mli ni amɛhaa jara ni baa shi lɛ baa.

english: Why does clearing weeds around my crops help them produce better yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ ni mijieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Weeds aggressively steal water, light, and soil nutrients from your crop plants. Removing them ensures all available food in the ground goes directly into feeding your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ nu, la, kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli lɛ waa. Kɛ́ ojie lɛ, ehaa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ yaa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farmland needs extra fertilizer or manure to grow crops well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi koni ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Signs like slow plant growth, pale or yellowing leaves, and small fruit yields usually indicate that the soil is running low on essential nutrients needed for healthy crop development.
ga: Okadii tamɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔŋ kɛ aduawai bibii ni baa lɛ Bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava directly next to my young cocoa trees on the same land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ kookoo tso ko masɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Cassava is not ideal right next to young cocoa because cassava roots compete heavily for moisture and soil food, while its tall leaves can choke out the young cocoa trees.
ga: Cassava esaaa kɛha cocoa bibii ejaakɛ cassava shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni baai ni kɛlɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha cacao tsei bibii lɛ agbo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when there is too much sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that dry out quickly under direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantain or shade trees to provide cover, maintain moisture, and cool the surrounding air until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo, koni amɛha amɛhe nɔ ni amɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi amɛhe. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli jɔɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why is it recommended to plant plantains alongside my new cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ madu plantains yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ hee lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Plantains grow quickly and produce large, wide leaves that create an natural canopy. This canopy shields young cocoa plants from harsh heat while providing the farmer with food and quick income while waiting for the cocoa to produce.
ga: Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta. Nɛkɛ ŋwɛitsu nɛɛ buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa okwaafoi lɛ niyenii ni ehaa amɛnáa shika oya be mli ni amɛmɛɔ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: When is the best time for me to plant maize during the rainy season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ be hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli yɛ Ghana?

english: Maize should be planted right after the first stable major rains arrive (usually between March and April in Southern Ghana). Planting early ensures the seeds get enough moisture to germinate and establish strong roots before dry spells occur.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. (Be pii lɛ, afeɔ yɛ March kɛ April teŋ yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ.) Dumɔ mra. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ náa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa dani hɔmɔ shihilɛi baa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow and dropping early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso lɛ shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually signal that the soil is running out of vital nutrients like nitrogen, or that the ground is too dry. Adding compost or well-rotted manure helps enrich the soil so the cassava can stay green and yield bigger tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔshi nii babaoo. Bɔni afee ni ŋmei lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni ekɛ ŋmei wuji aba.

english: What causes black spots on my cocoa pods, and how do I prevent them from spreading?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ baa? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi enaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa?

english: Black spots are caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that thrives in dark, wet, and humid conditions. Clearing weeds around the farm and pruning thick cocoa branches lets sunlight in and air circulate, which stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Jwɛi ni yɔɔ Cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛ tsei ni afoɔ ni mli wa lɛ haa hulu la boteɔ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ baaha helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: How can I tell if fall armyworms are attacking my maize, and what should I do?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji fall cutworms lɛ miitutua mi ŋmãa lɛ? Ni mɛni esa akɛ mafee?

english: If you see ragged holes on the maize leaves and small brownish droppings inside the growing shoots, armyworms are feeding on your crop. Catching them early and spraying recommended biopesticides or neem extract protects your harvest.
ga: Kɛji ona buji ni etse yɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ amli kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. mli ŋmeii ni miida Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii miiye oŋmɔshi nibii. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ewo pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil fertility. Regular watering during hot periods and feeding the plant balanced nutrients encourages flowers to stay on and turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛkɛ haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ kpe. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ, ni aha tso lɛ niyenii ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees fall over so easily during heavy rain and wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni eda lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and heavy fruit bunches, making them top-heavy. Support them by propping strong, sturdy wooden stakes against the main stem under the heavy bunch to keep the plant stable.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii. kɛ muji babaoo baa Fi amɛ sɛɛ kɛtsɔ tso ni wa ni shishifã titri lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ ni oookɛwo tso ni tsii lɛ shishi koni tso lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I dry my cocoa beans on raised wooden platforms instead of on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbi mi-kookoo lɛ yɛ tso ni awo nɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Drying cocoa beans on raised bamboo or wooden mats keeps them off the cold ground, protecting them from dirt, livestock, and ground humidity. This allows air to flow underneath for faster, cleaner drying and higher cocoa quality.
ga: Kɛ́ agbi kookoo ŋmeii lɛ yɛ ŋmeii loo tsei ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkashɛ he ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ lɛ. Ebuɔ kookoo yibii ahe kɛjɛɔ muji, kooloi kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ shishigbɛ koni egbi oya. he tse ni ehi jogbaŋŋ yɛ kookoo mli

english: How can I protect my stored maize grains from weevils without using harsh chemicals?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu ŋmãa ni ato lɛ he kɛjɛ ŋmeii ahe ni mikɛ tsofai ni mli wa tsuuu nii?

english: You must dry the maize completely until the grains are very hard, then store them in airtight hermetic bags (PICS bags). These bags cut off oxygen, suffocating any weevils and preventing them from destroying your harvest.
ga: Osumɔɔ ni oha ŋmãa lɛ agbi kwraa kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa. No sɛɛ lɛ, akɛwoɔ vacuum kotokui (PICS kotokui) amli. Nɛkɛ kotokui nɛɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ. ni haa ŋmei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa ekpata oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why should I give fertilizer to my crop seedlings when they are still tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mitso lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ? Ni eji bibioo lolo?

english: Just like young children need good food early in life to grow strong, young seedlings need early soil nutrients to build a strong root foundation. This deep foundation helps the crop survive dry conditions and produce a heavy harvest later.
ga: Tamɔ gbekɛbii pɛpɛɛpɛ Niyenii kpakpa he miihia amɛ mra. Bɔni afee ni dumɔwui bibii lɛ adara ni amɛhe wa lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná niyenii kpakpa yɛ sũ lɛ mli mra. koni akɛma shishitoo ni wa Shishitoo ni mli kwɔ nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli, ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains alongside my new cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantains yɛ kookoo tsei heei ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that shield young cocoa plants from harsh sun rays, preserving moisture in the soil until the cocoa becomes strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ mli waaa bɔ ni sa.

english: What will happen to my maize if I plant the seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition causes the plants to grow thin and weak, resulting in small or empty maize cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Enɛ haa ŋmãa bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes next to my yam vines as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso ko ama sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahe beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high into the sunlight to make food for the plant. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, preventing leaf rot and ensuring the plant directs maximum energy into growing large tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ. yɛ hulu la mli koni ekɛ niyenii aha sweet potato tsei lɛ Staking baaye abua ni ewó baai anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ tsiɔ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ naa ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo woɔ bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why should I avoid planting maize on the exact same plot of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ he yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same land repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and encourages pests that attack maize to build up in the ground. Rotating crops restores soil food naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shii abɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my young vegetables with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle aduawai bibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, shields the soil from hot sun rays so water does not dry up quickly, while keeping weeds down and slowly decomposing into rich organic plant food.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. koni nu lɛ akagbi oya Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ mli ni fiofio lɛ, ejara mli ewo tsei amli niyenii ni jara wa.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and falling off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a cry for food from your crop, showing that the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen or is severely dry. Feeding the soil helps the plant regain its healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji foomɔ ni akɛtaoɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo edɔ waa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akɛ niyenii haa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enáa ebaai eŋɔli ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops even if my soil is rich?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baa nii moŋ?

english: Weeds act like aggressive guests at a meal—they quickly steal water and nutrients out of the soil before your crop roots can drink them, effectively starving your crops of food.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ gbɔi ni yɔɔ basabasa yɛ niyeli shishi. Amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ oniyenii ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cut off extra branches from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ bo akɛ ofolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Removing small side branches forces the plant to stop wasting food on unnecessary leaves and direct all its energy into growing bigger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Niji bibii ni akɛbaa Fãi lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite niyenii kɛjɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ amli. Ni okɛ nakai hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ awo tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetables in the early morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha aduawai anɔ nu leebi maŋkpa loo shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Watering in the early morning allows plants to drink deeply before the afternoon heat sets in. Watering under the hot sun causes most water to evaporate instantly and can shock hot plant leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu leebi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nuɔ nu ni mli kwɔ dani shwane mli latsaa lɛ baaje shishi.Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu yɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi lɛ, ehaa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ, ni ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ baai ni mli edɔ lɛ akpokpo.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small shoots around them, and can I plant those shoots to grow new plantains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ, ni ani manyɛ madu nakai ŋmeii lɛ koni tsei heei akwɛ̃?

english: Those small shoots are called suckers or offspring. You can carefully dig them up and replant them in fresh soil to grow new plantain trees without buying new planting material every time.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmeii bibii lɛ akɛ ŋmeii loo suckers. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsu nii ni okɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ hee nɔ koni okwɛ plantain hee ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé dumɔ nibii heei be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do my hybrid maize seeds produce a poor yield when I save them from my harvest and plant them again the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-hybrid corn dumɔwui lɛ woɔ yibii fioo beni mihereɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ mli ni miduɔ amɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for high yield in their first generation only. If you save and replant those seeds, the second generation loses its strength, resulting in lower yields and unequal plant growth.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Kɛji obua nakai dumɔwui lɛ anaa ni odu lɛ Yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahewalɛ baaje amɛdɛŋ. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ hu daaa ni ekɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee.

english: How many times can I harvest cassava from the same stem before I need to plant a new batch?
ga: Shii enyiɛ manyɛ makpa ŋmei kɛjɛ tso kome nɔ dani ehe baahia ni madu ŋmei hee?

english: Cassava yields only one main harvest per planting cycle, which usually happens 9 to 12 months after planting. After digging up the mature tubers, you must cut new stem pieces from the stalk to plant for the next harvest.
ga: Cassava woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii titri kome pɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ, beni atsa bulbs ni eda lɛ sɛɛ. Esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei heei kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli koni okɛdu kɛha kpamɔɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and turn brown during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ mli egbi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot withstand direct sunlight and intense heat. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or bananas nearby protects the young cocoa leaves from burning and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains loo banana yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaabu kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What is eating the center leaves of my young maize plants and leaving small droppings inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ni eshiɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ baai lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the leaf whorl. Applying approved pest treatments or organic remedies like neem extract early in the morning helps protect your crop from destruction.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai amli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo tsofa ko ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli tamɔ morning neem extract tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe kɛjɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden stakes next to my yam vines as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama emasɛi lɛ? Sweet potato wain tsei beni amɛdaraa lɛ

english: Yam vines are climbing plants that need exposure to sunlight to generate energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot ground, preventing rot and encouraging better tuber growth.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la koni ekɛfee hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ fitemɔ naa ni ehaa tuber lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil consistently moist and using balanced fertilizer helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛfataa he Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops each year even when I plant at the same time every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ yɔɔ daa afi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ amɛ yɛ be kome mli daa afi moŋ.

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up. Rotating your crops—like planting cowpeas or groundnuts after maize—restores natural nutrients like nitrogen to the soil.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Oŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaatsake, tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni ooodu yɛ ŋmãa sɛɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow, twisted, and curly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Etsɔ kɛ wavy?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny insects called whiteflies and infected planting stems. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava varieties helps prevent this condition from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Amɛji mɛi ni hiɛɔ kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Kasava henɔi ni ana he odaseyeli akɛ helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ hela nɛɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why shouldn't I pour fertilizer directly against the stem of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?
