english: Placing chemical fertilizer directly against the stem can burn the plant's skin and roots. Applying fertilizer in a small ring a few inches away from the stem allows the roots to safely absorb the nutrients without damaging the plant.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli tɛ̃ɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ hewolo kɛ shishifãi. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ kooyigbɛ bibii amli Inchi fioo komɛi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni efiteee tso lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and dropping off during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil. Planting shade crops like plantains around them protects them until they grow strong enough to withstand the sun.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso lɛ he kɛyashi ebaada ni enyɛ eŋmɛ hulu lɛ naa.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp soil, preventing fungal diseases and allowing the leaves to catch light easily.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni ehaa baai lɛ shɛɔ la he oya.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with big leaves, but the tubers underground stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When cassava receives too much nitrogen from soil or heavy fertilizer, it spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the roots underground.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii mli. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkwɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baato eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why should I cut off some of the young shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Too many young shoots compete directly with the main plant for water and soil nutrients, leading to small plantain bunches. Leaving only two or three healthy shoots ensures larger fruit.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. cause plantains bibii Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ yɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaawo yibii wuji.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants often drop their flowers during extremely hot weather or when they lack water. Extreme heat stresses the plant, causing it to drop flowers to conserve its energy to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli waa loo nu bɛ lɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ gbeeɔ shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why are there tiny holes in my young maize leaves and small green caterpillars hidden inside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibi lɛ ji ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Mi nɔ lɛ yɛ bu bibioo ko. Akɛtee mli?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest that feeds on young maize leaves from the center out. Spraying recommended biopesticides early in the morning or late evening helps control them effectively.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛjɛɔ teŋgbɛ kɛyaa kpo lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in cool, wet weather and heavy shade. Pruning overhead branches to let in sunlight and clearing infected pods prevents the disease from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, fɔ́ kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Niji ni yɔɔ yiteŋ lɛ ni aaafolɔ koni hulu la aba mli ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt during the hottest part of the day even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji mikɛ nu wo nɔ leebi po.

english: In intense afternoon heat, tomato plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can draw it from the soil. Adding organic mulch around the stem keeps the soil cool and helps retain root moisture.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Organic mulch ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas or groundnuts makes the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni adu lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have beneficial bacteria in their roots that take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Muawai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa mli yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my lowland rice need standing water in the field during its early growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mi-shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmãa lɛ aná nu ni damɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni edaa mra lɛ?

english: Lowland rice thrives in shallow standing water, which smothers competing weeds that cannot survive underwater while keeping the soil temperature steady for proper nutrient intake.
ga: Omɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ mli. Enɛ jieɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ ni nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ nu shishi lɛ kɛyaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔlɛ yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be koni ekɛ niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ aha.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, which acts as the main food for leaf growth. Applying fertilizer like NPK or adding well-rotted animal manure gives the soil the nutrients the plant needs to regain its green color and produce large ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baai lɛ daa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK tsu nii loo akɛ kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni ekɛ eŋɔli kɛ etoi ni dara lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in a plain open field with no larger trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides living shelter and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulutsoo be lɛ naa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when we get heavy rainfall for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy, but excess standing water suffocates them and encourages fungal disease. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges allows heavy rainwater to drain off safely, keeping the roots firm and healthy.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Shi nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela he hewalɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛhe waaa

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper and tomato plants falling off before any fruits can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper kɛ tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani aduawai lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Vegetable flowers often fall off when the plant experiences heat stress or uneven watering. Mulching the soil around the plant's base with dry grass keeps the roots cool and holds moisture, which helps the flowers stay on the plant and develop into fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofa-kɛ-ŋma fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Mulching around Akɛ jwɛi ni egbi ehà tso lɛ shishi koni eye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Enɛ haa fɔfɔii lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall down easily when heavy wind blows during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswa waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots near the soil surface, making them top-heavy when they carry heavy bunches. Burying suckers deep during planting, building up mound soil around the base, and supporting fruiting stems with sturdy wooden poles prevents wind from pushing them over.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa tsɔne lɛ tsiimɔ babaoo baa kɛ́ etere tsɔne agbo ko. Ni aaafu tsei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ ni afee yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he Ni akɛ tsei ni wa fiɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ baatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa kɛtsɔɔ mli lɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my garden eggs curling up and twisting together into tight bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni etsɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies hiding underneath the leaves. Spraying the leaves with a gentle mixture of soapy water or neem leaf extract removes the bugs and allows smooth, healthy new leaves to unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo neem tso lɛ mli nu shwie baai lɛ anɔ blɛoo lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi bibii lɛ, ni ebaaye ebua ni baai heei lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛ ahi amɛhe nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: If I plant my seeds very close to each other, won't I harvest more crops from my small farm?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ makpa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli. Ani minɔ lɛ nyɛŋ aya hiɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close together causes plants to fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stalks and tiny yields. Following proper distance guidelines ensures every single plant gets enough food and space to bear a full harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Ŋaawoi ni kɔɔ gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ sɛɛnyiɛmɔ haa anáa niyenii kɛ he ni fa bɔ ni sa ni tsei fɛɛ baanyɛ ashɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni yeɔ emuu lɛ he.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the air to catch as much sunlight as possible, which feeds the underground tuber. Staking keeps the leaves away from wet soil pests and ensures the plant converts sunshine into big, heavy yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. ni ji shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ aniyenii Staking baaha baai lɛ akaje ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ ahe. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtsakeɔ hulu la lɛ amɛfeɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in my farm after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension agent lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have natural roots that fix nitrogen gas from the air back into the earth. Planting them after heavy feeders like maize naturally restores lost soil nutrients, so your land stays fertile without relying entirely on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ adebɔɔ mli shishifãi ni haa nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Niyenii mli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii mli nibii ni elaaje yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, oshikpɔŋ lɛ baakã he ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he ehiaaa kwraa.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable garden in the hot afternoon or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu yɛ shwane mli loo leebi?

english: Watering early in the morning allows plant roots to soak up moisture before the day's heat begins. Watering under hot afternoon sun causes most of the water to evaporate quickly in the heat and can shock hot leaves, causing stress to the plant.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ni amɛheɔ nu dani gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ jeɔ shishi. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ eha baai ni mli edɔ lɛ akpokpo Enɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when I clear all the big trees away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni edara lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight because their leaves burn easily. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a living shelter that shields the young cocoa from harsh heat and keeps moisture in the soil until the trees are mature enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa shihilɛhe ko ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he lɛ baa. ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: When soil runs out of nitrogen—the main nutrient crops use to make leaves green and healthy—the maize plant steals nitrogen from its oldest lower leaves to feed the young growing leaves at the top, causing the lower leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Abele juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and droop during the hot afternoon even when the soil is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Under intense heat, tomato leaves lose water into the air faster than their roots can draw it up from the ground. The plant temporarily curls its leaves to reduce its surface area exposed to the sun and save water until the air cools down in the evening.
ga: yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa shishi lɛ Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli koni hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi, ni amɛbu nu lɛ he kɛyashi gbɛkɛ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground when we get heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air pockets in the soil to breathe. When heavy rains flood land that lacks good water drainage, water fills those air pockets and suffocates the roots, allowing harmful soil fungi to infect and rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyiɔ hei ni nu kpakpa bɛ lɛ. Nu eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ amli ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni amɛgboɔ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping all their flowers instead of growing peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shi moŋ ni eeekwɛ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms as a natural defense mechanism when they suffer from stress such as severe dry heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients, choosing to conserve energy rather than support new fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ kɛji amɛmiipiŋ kɛjɛ haomɔ tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa waa mli. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Amɛhala akɛ amɛbaakwɛ hewalɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ aduawai heei.

english: How can I store my harvested maize seeds without buying chemical powders so insects do not destroy them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ ato ni miheee tsofa powda koni kooloi akafite amɛ?

english: Drying maize seeds completely until they are hard and mixing them with clean, dry wood ash or neem leaf powder coats the seeds and blocks small insects like weevils from moving, breathing, or laying eggs in the grain.
ga: Abɛi ŋmeii ni agbiɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni no sɛɛ lɛ akɛ tso sũ ni egbi ni he tse loo neem baa powder futuɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ ahe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni ji ŋmeii lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe, amɛkamuɔ loo amɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my yam mounds with dry leaves and grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry plant material acts like a protective blanket that keeps the sun from drying out the earth, stops rain from washing away topsoil, and gradually rots to feed the soil naturally.
ga: Tsei ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa hulu lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ehaa nugbɔ nɛɔ koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ fiofio koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are tiny insects gathering under my garden egg leaves and making the leaves roll inward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ eggplant baai lɛ ashishi yɛ mibɔɔ lɛ mli ni amɛhaa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli lɛ?

english: Insects like aphids hide on the undersides of leaves to protect themselves from hot sun and rain while sucking the sweet sap out of the plant, which causes the leaf tissues to distort and curl up.
ga: Kooloi bibii, tamɔ aphids, kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ he. kɛ agbɛnɛ hu, tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni ejieɔ lɛ Enɛ haa tso lɛ baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my field make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni adu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have friendly microbes living in small nodules on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, naturally enriching the land with free plant food for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ naanyobɔɔ nibii bibii ni hiɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ lɛ amɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli. Ekɛ tsei aniyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How does adding decomposed cow dung or poultry manure help my crops grow bigger tubers?
ga: Te tsina loo kooloi ashishifã ni egbo ni akɛfataa he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Decomposed manure loosens hard soil so crop roots can spread out easily, while slowly releasing essential plant nutrients and helping the ground hold onto water longer during dry spells.
ga: Nibii ni efite lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, fiofio lɛ, ejieɔ tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ kpo fiofio. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I cut down all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct sunlight burns their sensitive leaves and dries out the topsoil. Keeping tall shade trees or intercropping with plantains creates a cool environment and holds moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli lɛ gĩɔ. Kɛ́ aha tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ yaa shɔŋŋ loo akɛ plantains du amɛ lɛ, ehaa shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why does adding just a small pinch of fertilizer to my maize crop make it grow so fast?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko fata mi-ŋmãa lɛ he lɛ, ehaa edaa oya lɛ?

english: Fertilizer contains concentrated plant nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus. Even though the physical amount you apply looks small, it gives the crop a dense supply of food that speeds up leaf and stem growth.
ga: Tso mli niyenii ni fa babaoo tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni gbɔmɔtsoŋ nɔ ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ faaa moŋ, Shi ehaa tso lɛ niyenii babaoo hu, ni no haa tso lɛ baai kɛ eshishifãi lɛ daraa oya.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and fall off after heavy rain floods my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa eha ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When heavy rain floods the soil, water displaces the air that root systems need to breathe, and essential nutrients get washed away. This suffocates the roots and causes the leaves to turn yellow from stress.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu yeɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni he hiaa ni shishifãi lɛ amu lɛ najiaŋ. ni niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ hoɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔnyɛɛ hewɔ.

english: Why does my sorghum crop stay green during dry spells while my maize wilts and dies?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli yɛ fɛ̃i be mli yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ lɛ?

english: Sorghum has deep root systems that reach far down for underground water, and its leaves naturally roll up to trap moisture. Maize has shallower roots and loses water quickly through its broad leaves when rain stops.
ga: Sorghum yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yaa shɔŋŋ koni eyatao shikpɔŋ shishi nu. Ni ebaai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Abɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛtsɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow thin and fail to produce big cobs when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ amli tsei ni amɛwooo ŋmeii wuji beni midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the crops to fight one another for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough food and light to grow thick stems and large cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and stopping new peppers from forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiikpa pepper heei ni baa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the sap and spreading plant viruses. Removing affected leaves or using safe pesticides stops the insects from stunting crop growth.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ. Ajieɔ baai ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Ehaa kooloi bibii tsiɔ tsei adalɛ naa.

english: Why do seeds saved from my last hybrid maize harvest produce smaller cobs when I replant them this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛ minaagbee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni mikɛwo mli lɛ mli lɛ wo ŋmãa bibii beni midu ekoŋŋ yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to produce a high yield for one season only. Replanting saved hybrid seeds loses that special genetic strength, resulting in weaker plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ be kome pɛ mli. Hybrid dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baafite amɛ fɔmɔ nii ahe hewalɛ krɛdɛɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger than my yam plants after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe mi sweet potato tsei lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants adapted to steal water and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your yam plants get full access to the nourishment they need to grow large tubers.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ baaha o-sweet potato tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ ŋmeii wuji lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my harvested oil palm fruits start spoiling quickly if I do not boil or process them right away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm ni mikpaa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya kɛji mikɛwooo mli loo mikɛtsuuu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Once harvested, natural enzymes inside oil palm fruits rapidly break down the oil into bad acids. Boiling the fruits early stops these enzymes and preserves both the quality and yield of the palm oil.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akpa Adebɔɔ mli enzymes ni yɔɔ mu tso lɛ yibii lɛ amli lɛ gbálaa mu lɛ mli oya ni etsɔɔ acid gbonyo. Yibii ni ashãa mra Ehaa nɛkɛ enzymes nɛɛ kpaa ni ehaa ŋmei fɔ lɛ hilɛ kɛ yibiiwoo fɛɛ hiɔ shi.

english: How do I know if my soil is tired, and how does planting groundnuts help refresh it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etse? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Tired soil produces slow-growing crops with pale leaves and poor yields. Groundnuts refresh soil because their roots capture nitrogen gas from the air and deposit it into the ground, fertilizing the soil for future crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ haa tsei lɛ daa blɛoo, amɛbaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Peanuts haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: This usually happens when the plant lacks nitrogen, a key soil nutrient. The crop naturally moves available nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the young growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei bɛ nitrogen, ni ji shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why does my rice field need so much standing water compared to my maize or cassava crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo he hiaa mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ kɛ akɛto mi ŋmãa loo ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Rice plants are naturally adapted to aquatic conditions, and maintaining water in the field helps suppress weeds that would otherwise compete with the rice for sunlight and nutrients.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ nu mli shihilɛi amli. Ni nu ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ baaye abua ni ajie jwɛi ni baanyɛ ekɛ ŋmãa lɛ abɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii kpakpai lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farmland soil is healthy enough for planting without taking it to a laboratory?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha okwaayeli ni mikɛyaaa laboratori?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, feels crumbly in your hands, holds moisture well after rain, and contains living earthworms or decaying leaf matter.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Enuɔ he akɛ egbɔjɔ yɛ enine mli Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka loo baai bibii ni miifite yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with bushy leaves but give me very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai bibii shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: This happens when the soil has too much nitrogen, which pushes the plant to spend all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground rather than storing food in the root tubers.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my crops regularly even when the crops are taller than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ji daa. Kɛji tso lɛ kwɔ fe jwɛi lɛ po.

english: Weeds have deep and aggressive root systems that steal water and essential soil nutrients away from your crop's roots, even if the crop looks bigger on top.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni amɛhe wa. Enɛ juɔ nu kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛji akɛ tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eda kɛjɛ ŋwɛi po.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too high, when watering is inconsistent, or when there are no insects around to help pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli loo be mli ni kooloi bɛ jɛmɛ Koni eye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb up on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves up into full sunlight so the plant can make more food to expand its underground tuber, while also keeping leaves off wet soil to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ afee niyenii babaoo ni ekɛgbala ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akamɔ bo.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the tree before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly during rainy and humid weather, especially when cocoa branches are not pruned to let in sunlight and airflow.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ afolɔko kookoo niji koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during heavy rains even when there is no strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa bɛ moŋ?

english: Tiny pests called nematodes or root borers often attack and destroy the roots underground, leaving the heavy plantain tree without a firm anchor in soft, wet soil.
ga: ŋmeii bibii Atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo shishifãi ni shwieɔ ŋmeii. Bei pii lɛ, etutuaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ni efiteɔ amɛ. Ha plantains lɛ afee nɔ ni tsii Nɔ ko bɛ ni ma shi shiŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni efɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are there small ragged holes in my young maize leaves with sawdust-like powder inside the center fold?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni yɔɔ powda ni tamɔ ŋmei yɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the center of the growing maize crop and feeds on the tender young leaves from the inside out.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni boteɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kpo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Can letting birds stay on my farm for a few weeks completely ruin my harvest?
ga: Ani okpoi ni mashi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli otsii fioo komɛi lɛ baanyɛ afite nibii ni mifeɔ lɛ kwraa?

english: Yes. If birds remain undisturbed in your field for a long time, they can destroy your entire harvest. Even if they do not eat every grain or fruit, their continuous presence causes massive yield loss through pecking, trampling, and knocking mature crops to the ground.
ga: Hɛɛ. Kɛji okpoi lɛ tee nɔ amɛhi oŋmɔji amli be kakadaŋŋ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko gbaaa amɛnaa. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite onibii fɛɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ amɛyeee dumɔwui loo aduawai srɔtoi komɛi moŋ, shi E-hiɛ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ fiteɔ babaoo kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eda lɛ ni ekɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ekɛshwieɔ shi, ni ekɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops rot so quickly after birds peck at them, even if the bird only ate a small piece?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ beni okpoi egbe amɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Kɛji akɛ okpo lɛ yeɔ fã bibioo ko pɛ po?

english: When a bird pecks at a fruit or grain cob, it breaks the plant's outer protective skin. This open wound allows rainwater, bacteria, and fungal spores to enter, causing the rest of the crop to decay and spoil rapidly.
ga: Kɛ okpoi ŋmɔ aduawai loo dumɔwui akui lɛ Ebaafite tso lɛ kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ. Nɛkɛ pilamɔ ni agbele nɛɛ haa nugbɔ nu, helatsɛmɛi, kɛ ŋmeii amli tsɛŋemɔ helai boteɔ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfiteɔ oya.

english: Why do birds stop being afraid of the scarecrows I place in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okpoi lɛ kpa ŋmɔlɔ ni mikɛwo miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbeyeishemɔ lɛ?

english: Birds are intelligent and quickly realize that a stationary scarecrow poses no actual danger. To keep them scared, you must move the scarecrow to different locations every few days or use dynamic scarers like shiny reflective ribbons and noisemakers that move unpredictable with the wind.
ga: Okpoi lɛ le nii jogbaŋŋ ni amɛyɔseɔ oya akɛ ŋmeii ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ bɛ awui ko bɔni afee ni amɛwo amɛ gbeyei. Ebaabi ni okɛ gbeyeishemɔ lɛ aya he kroko daa gbii fioo komɛi loo okɛ tsɔne ko ni haa gbee ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ tsɔne ko ni kpɛɔ ni haa hulu kpɛɔ lɛ atsu nii. kɛ gbee ni akɛtswaa gbee ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ.

english: What time of day do I need to be most active in chasing birds away from my field?
ga: Mɛɛ gbi mli be esa akɛ matsu nii waa koni okpoi akabote miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Birds feed most aggressively during two main periods: early in the morning right after sunrise, and late in the afternoon before sunset. Concentrating your bird-scaring efforts during these peak hours provides the greatest protection for your crops.
ga: Okpoi yeɔ nii waa fe fɛɛ yɛ bei titrii enyɔ mli: leebi beni hulu lɛ ete shi sɛɛ. kɛ shwane mli dani hulu lɛ nyɔ shi Kɛ́ okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ma okpoi akwɛmɔ nɔ yɛ nɛkɛ bei ni mɛi fa babaoo nɛɛ amli lɛ, ebaabu onibii ahe jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does chasing birds off my farm feel useless when my neighboring farmers do not chase theirs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okpoi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ yakayaka nii yɛ be mli ni okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ shwieee amɛokpoi lɛ?

english: Birds simply move back and forth between adjacent fields. If neighboring farmers do not scare them away, the birds remain in the area and return to your crops the moment you leave. Working together with neighbors to chase birds simultaneously is much more effective.
ga: Okpoi nyiɛɔ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ ateŋ kɛkɛ. Kɛji okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ wooo amɛ gbeyei. Okpoi baahi jɛmɛ ni amɛbaaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛji oshi jɛmɛ pɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ akutsoŋbii tsu nii koni amɛshwie okpoi yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ebaatsu nii jogbaŋŋ babaoo.

english: Why do birds always attack my grain crops right when they are almost ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okpoi tutuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ be fɛɛ be kɛji ebɛŋkɛ nikpamɔ be lɛ pɛ?

english: Birds target crops during the soft grain and ripening stages because the seeds are soft, sweet, and rich in nutrients. This critical window right before full harvest requires high vigilance because it is when grains are most attractive to wild birds.
ga: Okpoi lɛ kwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Enɛ ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛmli ŋɔɔ ni niyenii babaoo yɛ mli. Yɛ nɛkɛ be ni he hiaa waa nɛɛ mli, dani abaakpa nikpamɔ lɛ kwraa lɛ, ehe miihia ni akwɛ jogbaŋŋ waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ ji nɔ ni ŋa mli okpoi sumɔɔ waa.

english: Should I harvest my grains early if I notice birds starting to attack my farm?
ga: Kulɛ esa akɛ makpa dumɔwui lɛ mra. Kɛji miyɔse akɛ okpoi miibɔi miŋmɔ lɛ tutuamɔ?

english: If your crop has reached full maturity, harvesting promptly prevents heavy losses to birds. However, harvesting too early when grains still contain high moisture will lead to drying problems and storage mold, so active bird-scaring until full maturity is recommended.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ Amrɔ nɔŋŋ nikpamɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni okpoi ni fiteɔ nii babaoo lɛ tsiɔ naa. Shi kɛlɛ, kɛ́ akpa dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ beni edɔ lolo lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ naagbai aba yɛ amɛgbimɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, atsɔɔ akɛ ahoo okpo ŋmeii kɛyashi amɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the crops planted near big trees on my farm damaged by birds more than the rest of the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe lɛ okpoi fiteɔ amɛ fe ŋmɔ lɛ mli hei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Large trees near field borders provide birds with safe roosting spots, shade, and lookout positions where they can scan for danger before swooping down to feed. Trimming overhanging branches near farm borders helps reduce bird visits.
ga: Tsei wuji ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ haa okpoi lɛ naa he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni amɛhiɔ shi, amɛnáa hulutsoo, ni amɛkwɛɔ nii yɛ. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ oshara ko mli dani amɛfo kɛba shi koni amɛyaye nii. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni etse amɛhe banee yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ husui lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha okpoi ni baasara lɛ ayibɔ aba shi.

english: Is crop produce that has been pecked by birds safe for my family to eat or sell at the market?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni okpoi shwieɔ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha miweku lɛ ni amɛye loo amɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ?

english: Produce pecked by birds carries a risk of microbial contamination from the bird's beak and drops significantly in market value. Severely pecked crops should be discarded, while lightly damaged ones should have the damaged parts cut away completely and consumed immediately rather than stored.
ga: Nibii ni okpoi ŋmɔɔ lɛ yɛ oshara mli akɛ helai bibii ni jɛɔ okpoi lɛ anaabu mli lɛ baafite amɛ. ni eha jara ni akɛheɔ nii lɛ ba shi waa. Esa akɛ ashɛrɛ tsei ni shwieɔ shi waa lɛ ashwie. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, esa akɛ afolɔ tsei ni efite fioo lɛ kwraa ni aye amrɔ nɔŋŋ moŋ fe ni akɛtoɔ he ko.

english: What happens to grain heads that birds knock down onto the soil?
ga: Mɛni baa ŋmaa yitsei ni okpoi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Grains knocked to the ground absorb dampness from the soil, leading to rapid rotting, mold growth, and insect attack. Preventing birds from landing on crop heads keeps the stalks standing strong and keeps the grain clean and dry.
ga: Nibii ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa fitemɔ baa oya. Fungal dalɛ kɛ kooloi tutuamɔ. Kɛ́ atsĩ okpoi anaa koni amɛkagbee ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ ahe wa, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ ahe tseɔ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: How does putting neem into the soil help protect my crops from insects?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ neem ni mikɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ buɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ahe?

english: When neem cake or oil is applied to the soil, the roots absorb its natural compounds. This makes the leaves and stems bitter and toxic to pests feeding on the crop, protecting the plant from the inside out.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ neem keeki loo fɔ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shwieɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa baai kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ awui kɛhaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Buu tsei ahe kɛjɛ mli kɛya kponɔgbɛ

english: Why do insects still attack my crops even after I spray the surface of the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ moŋ?

english: Surface sprays often miss pests hiding under leaves or inside stems. Treatments that get absorbed through the roots move throughout the whole plant so pests are affected wherever they bite.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ baai ashishi loo tsei lɛ amli lɛ anaaa. Tsofai ni tsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli fɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, he fɛɛ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baa lɛ, amɛnáa he sɛɛ.

english: Why are my crop leaves turning yellow and covered in tiny crawling bugs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni kooloi bibii ni shwereɔ lɛ ehà nɔ lɛ?

english: Sap-sucking insects like aphids drain vital nutrients from your leaves, causing them to turn yellow and weaken. Using natural treatments like neem can clear these bugs away safely.
ga: Kplukai ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai tamɔ neem tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ ejie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Can my crops absorb pest medicine directly through their roots from the dirt?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ aŋɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yes, plants can draw up certain liquid or organic soil treatments through their root system just as they draw up water and fertilizers.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei baanyɛ ajie nu loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛtsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ tamɔ bɔ ni amɛjieɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: What is neem cake and how does it help my farm soil?
ga: Mɛni ji neem keeki ni te eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Neem cake is the organic material left after extracting oil from neem seeds. Adding it to soil enriches it with organic nutrients and kills underground pests like nematodes that damage roots.
ga: Neem keeki ji nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni eshwɛɔ kɛjɛɔ mu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ neem dumɔwui amli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛfata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ehaa niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ nematodes, ni haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ.

english: How long does it take for natural remedies added to the soil to start protecting my crops?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni akɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ aje shishi ebu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: It typically takes a few days to a week for crop roots to absorb the natural compounds and distribute them into the stems and leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ gbii fioo kɛyashi otsi kome dani tso shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛja amɛha tso lɛ shishi kɛ baai lɛ.

english: How can I protect my crops from pests if farm chemicals in the market are too expensive?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe? Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ jara wa tsɔ?

english: You can make affordable organic remedies by crushing local neem leaves or seeds and mixing them with water and soap to spray on crops and soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona tsofa ko ni jara waaa, ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli kɛtsɔ neem baai loo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni oootsɔ mli ni okɛ nu kɛ samla afutu mli ni okɛshwie ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: What cheap materials can I add to my soil to keep it healthy without buying costly fertilizers?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii ni jara waaa manyɛ mikɛfata shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ ni miheee ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa?

english: Adding farm waste, animal manure, or compost mixed with neem residue feeds the soil naturally, improves moisture retention, and saves money.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔ mli jwɛi, kooloi aŋmei loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ neem ŋmɔtɔ efutu mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ha ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ mli lɛ aya hiɛ ni okɛ shika ato

english: Why should I use plant-based pest treatments instead of chemical sprays on my food crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni jɛ tsei amli lɛ atsu nii yɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mi niyenii tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Plant-based treatments like neem break down safely in the soil, do not leave harmful chemical residues on your harvested food, and improve overall soil health.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛ tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ neem lɛ fiteɔ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eshiii tsofai ni eshwɛ yɛ niyenii ni akpa lɛ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ lɛ fɛɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Can applying natural oils or cakes to my soil harm my crops if I use too much?
ga: Ani adebɔɔ mli fɔ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ keeki ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui kɛji mikɛtsu nii babaoo?

english: While natural treatments are safer than chemicals, using extremely heavy amounts of crude oil on roots can cause burning or smothering, so proper mixture rates are important.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofafeemɔi yɛ shweshweeshwe fe tsofai moŋ, shi kɛ akɛ mu ni mli edɔ babaoo tsu nii yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ shãa loo ŋmɔlɔ aba, no hewɔ lɛ, bɔ ni sa ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ he miihia.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and drying up during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have shallow roots and tender leaves that easily lose water under harsh sun and dry winds. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a canopy that protects young cocoa from scorched leaves and moisture loss.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ baai ni shãa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi lɛ he.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Those extra shoots, called suckers, compete with the main plant for food, water, and sunlight. Pruning them down to leave just one or two strong suckers helps the parent plant put all its energy into growing a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ plantain tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Why does my maize crop grow very tall with big leaves but only produce small, empty cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli pɛ lɛ?

english: Maize needs specific nutrients at different stages. High nitrogen makes the plant grow tall and leaf-rich, but without enough phosphorus and potassium—or if the plant lacks water during flowering—the cobs cannot fill out properly with grains.
ga: Abele biɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ fãi srɔtoi amli. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo lɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛheɔ baai babaoo. Shi fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. aloo kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ Cob lɛ hu nyɛŋ ekɛ ŋmaa awo mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my rice yield drop so much if I delay clearing weeds during the first few weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ baa shi waa kɛji mikɛ jwɛi lɛ shwiemɔ sɛɛ fo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni mikɛdu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young rice seedlings grow slowly at first and get easily overcrowded by fast-growing weeds. Clearing weeds early ensures your rice gets all the fertilizer, light, and water it needs to develop strong stems before it begins to head.
ga: Omɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ daraa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni bei pii lɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ eyiɔ mli obɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ baaha ŋmãa lɛ aná ŋmɔshi nibii, la, kɛ nu ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmãa ni mli wa dani ebɔi kwɛ̃mɔ.

english: What will happen if I plant my cassava stem cuttings into the soil upside down by mistake?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ oshara du ŋmei nine ni mikɛwo shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava buds point upward toward the sky. If planted upside down, the shoots must bend completely around to reach light, which wastes the plant's stored energy, delays sprouting, and results in poor root formation.
ga: Cassava fɔfɔi tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Esa akɛ abɔle Tso lɛ he fɛɛ koni ená la. Enɛ baaha hewalɛ ni tso lɛ eto lɛ afite. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ. ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shishifãi ni ehiii kwraa

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes exposes more leaves to sunlight, which the plant uses to make food. Vines left on the hot ground are also more likely to suffer from leaf diseases and rot, leading to smaller tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu la babaoo naa tsei lɛ ahe, ni tso lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii kɛyeɔ niyenii. Wein tsei ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ foliar helai kɛ fitemɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso bibioo.

english: Why do my tomato fruits get dark, sunken rotten patches at the bottom before they even turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ mli edɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? yɛ tɔ lɛ shishi dani etsɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ po.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by uneven watering where the soil gets very dry and then suddenly very wet.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. He ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi waa ni trukaa lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and wrinkling, making the whole plant look stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ? Ha tso muu lɛ fɛɛ afee tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips, aphids, or mites, or a virus transmitted by whiteflies. These pests feed on the underside of leaves and damage the leaf tissues as they expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, aphids loo mites, loo helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛfiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ be mli ni amɛmli shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it good practice to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my land before I plant maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have natural bacteria in their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. When the legumes are harvested, that extra nitrogen stays in the ground to feed the next maize crop naturally.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ adebɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings suddenly collapse at the soil line and die right after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal disease called damping-off, which attacks tender stems at soil level. It thrives when the soil stays too wet, seeds are planted too close together, or there is poor airflow around the seedbed.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ damping off, ni tutuaa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Ebaashwere jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ Bad seed plot lɛ he

english: Why do the tiny flowers on my cocoa trees keep falling off before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Ani mi-kookoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa flowers fall off easily when the trees are stressed by dry spells, lack proper nutrients in the soil, or get too much harsh, direct sunlight before the rainy season arrives.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa. Niyenii ni sa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baashɛ

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are getting enough water during the rainy season?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji okokoo tsei lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: When cocoa trees get enough rain, they produce bright green, healthy leaves and start swelling fresh green pods, whereas thirsty trees drop leaves and show stunted pod growth.
ga: Kɛji kookoo tsei lɛ ná nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa Ebaawo baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebaabɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ ni amɛjie pod lɛ dalɛ ni egbɔjɔ kpo.

english: Is heavy rain always good for my cocoa crops, or can it cause problems?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hi kɛha mi-kokoo tsei lɛ be fɛɛ be loo ebaanyɛ ekɛ naagbai aba?

english: While rain helps pods grow, continuous heavy rain with little sunlight creates damp conditions that encourage black pod disease, a fungal infection that ruins the crop.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa moŋ, shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ ni hulu la fioo pɛ baa lɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni woɔ ŋmeii diji hela lɛ he hewalɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii

english: What happens to my crops when rain falls after a long season of harsh sun and drought?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ hulutsoo kɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ?

english: Rain after drought gives crops a strong burst of energy, causing them to take up soil nutrients quickly and sprout new leaves and flowers within days.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ hɔmɔ sɛɛ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii náa hewalɛ babaoo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei naa niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii kɛ fɔfɔi heei yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli.

english: Why do farmers build raised wooden structures or kiosks to dry their cocoa beans instead of putting them on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi maa tsei ni akɛfee tsũi loo tsũi ni awó nɔ koni amɛha amɛkookoo ŋmɔji lɛ agbi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛbaafɔ̃ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Drying cocoa beans on raised wooden platforms keeps them off the damp soil, allows warm air to circulate beneath them, and prevents mold from growing on the beans.
ga: Kɛ́ agbi kookoo ŋmeii lɛ yɛ tso ni awo nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkahi shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ tsɔɔ kookoo yibii lɛ ashishi. ni otsi ŋmɔtɔ ni shwereɔ yɛ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ naa

english: How does rain hurt my cocoa beans after I have already harvested them?
ga: Te nugbɔ lɛ saa mi-kokoo yibii lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ beni mikpa amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Rain striking harvested beans traps unwanted moisture inside them, causing rot, bad smell, and mold, which spoils the high quality that cocoa buyers look for.
ga: Kɔfi yibii ni akpaa ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ataooo awo mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa, ni efiteɔ su ni mɛi ni heɔ kookoo lɛ taoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings struggle to grow even when the soil looks moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eda eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni edɔ moŋ?

english: Moist soil is not enough if the soil lacks nutrients or if young cocoa plants are exposed to scorching sun without protective shade trees to cover them.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ faaa kɛji akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛji akɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ kookoo tsei bibii anɔ ni tsei haaa amɛ hulutsoo.

english: How can I know if my farmland has lost its strength after years of heavy planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ midumɔ lɛ miihe hewalɛ miiho yɛ afii babaoo ni mikɛdu nii waa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When your farmland loses strength, crops grow slowly, leaves look pale yellow instead of dark green, and trees yield far fewer pods even when it rains well.
ga: Beni oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ fiteɔ lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ daa fiofio. Baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. Ni tsei lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kwraa, kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ jogbaŋŋ po.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting shade trees alongside my cocoa plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mi kokoo tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Shade trees act as natural umbrellas that protect delicate young cocoa plants from intense sun heat, block heavy winds, and help keep moisture in the soil.
ga: Shade tsei tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shade ni buɔ kokoo tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo be ni naa wa lɛ he, etsĩɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why do black spots start spreading across my cocoa pods during the cool wet months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ fɛɛ anɔ yɛ nyɔji ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Black spots come from excess moisture hanging on the pods during heavy rains; trimming extra branches helps sunlight and air pass through to dry the pods faster.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni buaa ehe naa yɛ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei krokomɛi amli lɛ, ebaaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli koni eha tsei lɛ agbi oya.

english: How do I know if the early rains are enough for me to start planting my maize seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔwui?

english: The first few rains of the season can be tricking because the soil underneath is still dry and hot. You should wait until the rain falls continuously for two or three days and soaks deep into the soil (at least hand-depth) so your seeds get enough steady moisture to germinate without drying up in the sun.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ fioo ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ alaka mɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi ni edɔ lolo. Esa akɛ omɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ be fɛɛ be gbii enyɔ loo etɛ ni ekɛ ehe awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. (kɛ hoo lɛ, eshɛɔ nine mli) koni dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa be fɛɛ be koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when the bright sun comes out after the rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand strong, direct sunlight because their roots are shallow and their leaves dry out quickly. Planting nurse crops like plantains or cassava next to them creates shade, which protects the cocoa from sunburn and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni baai lɛ hu gbɛ́ɔ oya. Nurse tsei tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ baaha hulutsoo aba Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo he kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with large leaves, but the tubers in the ground are very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛ baa wuji shi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji bibii lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or if plants are shaded too much, the cassava focuses all its energy on growing stem and leaves above the ground instead of storing food in its roots. Cutting back excessive shade and avoiding high-nitrogen fertilizers helps the plant redirect energy to grow bigger tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo kɛji tso lɛ yɛ hulutsoo babaoo. Yucca kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ tsei kɛ baai ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, hulutsoo ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ nitrogen ni fa babaoo mli lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ aku sɛɛ ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ aya bulbs wuji ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together to fit more on my land, why do the plants become weak and produce tiny cobs?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ mihe lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ hu? Mɛni hewɔ tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients just like people sharing a small plate of food. When planted too close, no single plant gets enough sunshine or nutrients, leading to thin, weak stalks and small cobs.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋshii mli tamɔ bɔ ni gbɔmɛi jaa niyenii tsɛnsii bibii. Beni adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ eko kwraa enine shɛɛɛ hulu la loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: Why does planting beans in the same farm with my yam help the yam grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans have special roots that take air from the atmosphere and convert it into natural plant food (nitrogen) in the soil. As the beans grow and drop leaves, they feed the soil, making extra nutrients available for the yam to grow strong.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii (nitrogen) yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ, Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa niyenii krokomɛi fataa he koni ŋmeii lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants during the hot dry days without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ ni nu bɛ lɛ amli ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Extreme heat during the day prevents tomato pollen from working properly, so the flowers cannot get fertilized. When this happens, the plant drops the useless flowers to save energy until the weather cools down or moisture increases.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ haa tomato pollen lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ. Anyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ fɔmɔ nii. Kɛ enɛ ba lɛ Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ loo hulutsoo be lɛ baaya hiɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall down when heavy rain and strong wind come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantains do not have deep taproots like hardwood trees; their roots spread out shallowly near the surface. When heavy rains soften the soil, shallow roots lose their grip, making the top-heavy plant fall easily under strong winds.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ tsei ni wa. Eshishifãi lɛ gbɛ eshwa he ko ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ fee blɛoo lɛ, shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ. Enɛ haa tsei ni amɛhe tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa shishi.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and stop growing after a period of warm weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ yɛ hulutsoo be ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often a defense response by the plant when tiny sucking insects (like thrips or aphids) attack it during warm weather, or when the leaves lose water faster than the roots can drink. The curling protects the leaf underside from drying out further.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ baa lɛ ji bɔ ni ebuɔ ehe ehaa. Beni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu (tamɔ thrips loo aphids) tutuaa tsei yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ. Aloo be mli ni baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ. Yitsɔi lɛ ni aaakpɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shishigbɛ baai lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi babaoo.

english: How can I tell that my groundnuts are fully mature and ready to harvest under the ground without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni mikɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Look at the main leaves above ground—when they start turning yellow and shedding, dig up just two or three test plants. Crack open the pods; if the inside lining of the shell has turned dark brown or black and the nuts are plump, the crop is ready for harvest.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai titrii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi lɛ Tsɔmɔmɔ kaa tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ, ni ofomɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛji mligbɛ ŋmeii lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ediŋŋ. ni ŋmeii lɛ yɛ loo ni mli edɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ he kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slowly even after I apply fertilizer to my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with very aggressive roots that absorb water and fertilizer much faster than farm crops. If weeds are not cleared before applying fertilizer, they eat up all the plant food, leaving your crops hungry and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei waa ni shwieɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Kɛji ajieee jwɛi lɛ dani awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Jwɛi lɛ baaye tso lɛ niyenii lɛ fɛɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye oŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to build green leaves. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea or adding well-rotted manure will help the plants turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo tsei lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the soil before I get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani minine shɛɔ hegbɛ nɔ ni mikpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when too much water stays trapped in the soil around them during heavy rains. Planting cassava on high mounds or raised ridges helps excess water drain away so the roots can breathe.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo tsɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo saatso ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures get extremely hot or when the soil dries out completely. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and mulching helps the plant hold onto its flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli koni ewo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and wrinkling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the juice from under the leaves, or by a virus carried by insects. Spraying the leaves early with neem seed extract or appropriate crop protection help clear these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni kooloi kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Okɛbaa lɛ afɔsemɔ mra Kɛtsɔ neem dumɔwu mli nu loo ŋmɔshi nibii ahebuu ni sa nɔ lɛ obaanyɛ ojie kooloi nɛɛ.

english: How do I know if the worm eating my maize crop is the fall armyworm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmeii ni yeɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ ji fall cutworms?

english: Fall armyworm leaves ragged holes in the maize leaves and creates sawdust-like dirt inside the center funnel of the plant. If you look closely at the caterpillar's head, you will see a clear inverted 'Y' pattern.
ga: Fall cutworms lɛ shĩɔ bu ni mli edɔ yɛ ŋmãa baai amli ni amɛfeɔ muji ni tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ nubu lɛ mli. Kɛ okwɛ ŋmei lɛ yitso jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Obaana ‘Y’ ni atsake lɛ he mfoniri ni yɔɔ faŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up early when I do not stake them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ miiho oya nɛkɛ? Ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli?

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes to spread their leaves and catch direct sunlight. When left crawling on the hot ground, the leaves get scorched, exposed to soil diseases, and cannot produce enough food to grow big tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tso ko nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã ni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni efo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaashã baai lɛ. Shikpɔŋ hela ji lɛ. ni enyɛɛɛ efee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ bulbs wuji

english: Why is my young oil palm tree producing flowers but no fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi shi ebɛ yibii lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees produce separate male and female flowers. Young trees often produce only male flowers at first, or stress from dry weather prevents pollination, but as the tree matures and receives good nutrients, female flowers will form fruit bunches.
ga: Mu tsei woɔ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi. Bei pii lɛ, tsei bibii woɔ fɔfɔi hii yɛ shishijee mli. Aloo, nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli baa lɛ tsiɔ pollination naa. Shi kɛ́ tso lɛ eda jogbaŋŋ ni ená niyenii kpakpa lɛ, fɔfɔi yei lɛ woɔ yibii akui.

english: Why shouldn't I save and replant seeds from the hybrid maize I harvested last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ hybrid corn ni mikpa yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni mikɛduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to give high yield only in their first planting. If you save seeds from that harvest to replant, the new crop loses its strength, resulting in uneven growth, smaller cobs, and a lower harvest.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ pɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ to koni okɛdu ekoŋŋ. Nibii heei ni aduɔ lɛ ahewalɛ baaje mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee. Cob lɛ ji bibioo fe no. kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ fioo

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn into powder after a few months in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ batsɔ powda yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni mikɛto lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize turns to powder because tiny insects called grain weevils hatch inside the stored grain and eat it from the inside out. Drying the maize thoroughly until it is bone-dry and storing it in airtight hermetic bags suffocates pests and protects the grain.
ga: Abɛi tsɔɔ sũ yɛ kooloi bibii ahewɔ. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ dumɔwui ŋmei lɛ fɔɔ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ amli ni eyeɔ nii kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa kɛyashi egbɔ ni akɛwo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebu ŋmãa lɛ he.

english: Do my crops grow during the night or only during the day when the sun is out?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ gbɛkɛ loo shwane mli pɛ ni hulu la bɛ?

english: Crops make their food from sunlight during the day, but they actually do most of their physical growth at night while using the energy stored during the daytime.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ feɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ hulu la mli yɛ gbi mli, shi yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ, amɛdaraa yɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ babaoo gbɛkɛ mli yɛ be mli ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ gbi mli lɛ tsuɔ nii.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetables late in the evening or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafɔ aduawai anɔ nu gbɛkɛ loo leebi?

english: Watering late in the evening gives the soil plenty of time to soak up water in the cool night air without the hot sun evaporating it immediately.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛnuɔ nu ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni yɔɔ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ni ekɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shwieee shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop leaves look chewed up in the morning when I don't see any insects during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ashɛreɔ leebi lɛ? Akɛni minaaa kooloi bibii yɛ gbi lɛ mli hewɔ lɛ?

english: Many farm pests like armyworms and beetles stay hidden in the soil during the hot day to avoid heat and come out to feed heavily on your crops at night.
ga: Okwaafoi amli kooloi babaoo, tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii, kɛ amɛhe woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli koni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be lɛ he, ni amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye onibii babaoo gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop during the hot afternoon sun but look completely fresh by morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, shi amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛfee ehee leebi lɛ?

english: During hot daylight hours, plants lose water faster than their roots can pull it from the ground, but overnight they recover and refill their leaves with water.
ga: Yɛ gbi mli be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi nyɔɔŋ kome mli lɛ, tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ ni ekɛ nu awo ebaai lɛ amli ekoŋŋ.

english: Do crop roots keep absorbing fertilizer from the soil while it is dark outside?
ga: Ani tsei shishifãi lɛ baaŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ duŋ ewo kpo lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, plant roots continue to drink water and take in essential plant nutrients from the soil all through the night.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei shishifãi yaa nɔ amɛnuɔ nu ni amɛheɔ tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gbɛkɛ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my young seedlings need much more frequent watering than my mature crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ anɔ nu shii abɔ fe tsei ni eda lɛ?

english: Young crops have small, shallow roots that dry out very quickly and cannot reach the deep moisture stored far below the soil surface like older plants can.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni gbɛ́ɔ oya waa, ni amɛnáaa gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛyaa nu ni mli kwɔ ni buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ mli tamɔ tsei ni edara lɛ.

english: Should I feed my young crop plants the same amount of fertilizer as my fully grown crops?
ga: Ani esa akɛ maha tsei bibii lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha tsei ni eda lɛ?

english: No, young plants have tender roots that can burn easily from heavy fertilizer, so they need lighter, gentler feedings while they are small.
ga: Dabi, tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii baanyɛ ashã amɛ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, niyenii ni waaa ni yɔɔ mlɛo he miihia amɛ beni amɛji gbekɛbii lɛ.

english: Why do my young transplanted crops need temporary shade for their first few days in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ he hiaa ni amɛná hulutsoo be kukuoo ko yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbii fioo ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young transplants are weak and stressed; shade protects them from scorching sunlight while their roots settle into the ground.
ga: Oblahii kɛ oblayei ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhaoɔ amɛhe. Shade lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are young crop shoots more easily destroyed by pests overnight than older crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ fiteɔ mlɛo yɛ nyɔɔŋ kome mli fe tsei ni edara lɛ?

english: Young shoots are soft, sweet, and rich in moisture, making them an easy and preferred night food for farm pests compared to tough, mature leaves.
ga: Tsobii bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe ŋɔɔ ni amɛmli ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. Ehaa ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ gbɛkɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ehe gbɛi. Kɛ akɛto baai bibii ni eda kwraa lɛ ahe

english: Why is it important to clear weeds around young crops more often than around adult plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi awo tsei bibii ahe shii abɔ fe tsei ni eda lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young plants grow slowly at first, so fast-growing weeds will quickly steal their water, sunlight, and soil nutrients if not removed early.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya kɛji ajieee amɛ oya.

english: Why do wild animals like squirrels and grasscutters target my best crops right before I am ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ jwɛi ŋmɔlɔi lɛ kwɛɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ anɔ dani mifeɔ klalo akɛ makpãa amɛ lɛ?

english: Animals have a strong sense of smell and are naturally drawn to crops when they reach peak ripeness because that is when the fruits are sweetest and highest in nutrients. Clearing the weed perimeter around your farm and setting simple deterrents like scarecrows or fencing can help keep them away.
ga: Koolooi yɛ henumɔ ni mli wa ni amɛnuɔ nii ahe waa ni bei pii lɛ amɛsumɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji amɛshɛ amɛshweremɔ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, aduawai lɛ ji nɔ ni ŋɔɔ fe fɛɛ, ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɛ mli. Nɔ ni fata enɛ he ji jwɛi ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ ni ooojie ni okɛ hebuu ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ ŋmeii loo gbogboi awo mli. baanyɛ aye abua ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ he.
