english: Why do insects attack the fruits that look the healthiest on my farm instead of the weak ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa aduawai ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ moŋ fe nɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Insects prefer healthy, juicy, and nutrient-rich fruits because they provide the most energy for them and their young. Inspecting your farm early and using proper pest control helps protect your highest-value harvest.
ga: Kplukai sumɔɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni mli ewo nu, ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɔɔ mli. Ejaakɛ amɛhaa amɛ kɛ amɛbii lɛ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni sa ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu onibii ni jara wa fe fɛɛ lɛ ahe.

english: If a fruit looks good but has a tiny mark where an animal touched it, why won't market buyers pay full price for it?
ga: Kɛji akɛ aduawai lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ shi eyɛ okadii bibii ni kooloi baanyɛ ata he lɛ Mɛni hewɔ jarayelɔi ni heɔ nii lɛ ewooo jara lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Buyers reject produce with small scratches or bite marks because any break in the outer skin allows bacteria and fungi to enter quickly. This causes the crop to rot long before it reaches the final consumer.
ga: Mɔ ni heɔ lɛ kpooɔ nibii ni ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ bibii loo ŋmɔlɔ he okadii yɔɔ nɔ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewolo lɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ haa helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii boteɔ mli oya. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ fiteɔ be kakadaŋŋ dani eshɛɔ naagbee niyelɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ.

english: How do market traders decide which of my crops are top quality and which ones are low quality?
ga: Te jarayelɔi feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛkpɛɔ amɛyiŋ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛ nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ he?

english: Traders inspect produce based on skin cleanliness, size, firmness, and freedom from insect holes or bruises. Produce without blemishes stays fresh longer during transport and sale, so buyers pay a higher price for it.
ga: Jarayelɔi damɔɔ bɔ ni amɛhewolo lɛ he tse ha, bɔ ni eda ha, bɔ ni eyɛ shiŋŋ ha, kɛ bɔ ni kooloi bibii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ bɛ mli lɛ nɔ amɛkwɛɔ nibii ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ. Nibii ni tɔmɔ ko bɛ he lɛ hiɔ shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ yɛ majemɔ kɛ jarayeli be mli. No hewɔ lɛ, mɔ ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ jara ni nɔ kwɔ fe no.

english: When is the best time of day for me to pick my crops so they stay fresh for buyers?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mahala miŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛhi shi ehee kɛha mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ?

english: The best time to harvest is early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the weather is cool. Picking crops during hot afternoon sun causes heat stress, which makes them wilt and spoil much faster.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛkpaa nii ji leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gboɔ ni egboɔ oya kwraa.

english: Why is it necessary to separate bruised or damaged crops from healthy ones immediately after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite loo efite lɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Damaged crops release rot spores and gases that spread quickly to nearby healthy produce. Sorting them right after harvest prevents a few damaged items from ruining your whole basket.
ga: Tsei ni efite lɛ jieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛyaa nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ ohala nibii amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi nibii komɛi ni efite lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite o-basket muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my harvested vegetables spoil so quickly when I pack them tightly into heavy sacks to carry to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔi lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛwo kotokui ni tsii amli koni mikɛya jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Tightly packing produce in sealed sacks builds up heat and crushes the soft skin of crops. Using well-ventilated crates or baskets allows air to flow, keeping crops cool and preventing bruising during transport.
ga: Nibii ni adu lɛ ni akɛwoɔ kotokui ni atsĩ mli lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa dɔlɛ baa ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahewolo ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ. Krɛti loo tsɛnsi ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli. ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli ejɔ ni otsi ŋmɔshi nibii anaa yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ

english: Where should I store my harvested produce at home while waiting for the buyer to arrive?
ga: Nɛgbɛ esa akɛ mikɛ mikpamɔ lɛ ato yɛ shia beni mimɛɔ ni mɛi ni baahe nii lɛ aba lɛ?

english: Store your harvest in a cool, dry, well-ventilated shed off the bare ground and away from direct sunlight. High heat and ground moisture encourage rot and attract pests.
ga: Kɛ onibii lɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni egbi, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli. yɛ he ko ni gbɛ yɔɔ kpo nɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ bɛ jɛmɛ Dɔlɛ ni fa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ ni egbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ.

english: What can I do with produce that has slight cosmetic damage so I do not waste my hard work?
ga: Mɛni mifeɔ kɛ nibii ni efite fioo yɛ tsɔne ni akɛsaa mɔ he lɛ he? Bɔni afee ni ehe akahia ni ofite be kɛtsu nii waa?

english: Crops with minor surface damage can be processed right away into dried goods, local pastes, juices, or animal feed. Processing lets you earn income or feed your family from crops that market buyers will reject.
ga: Abaanyɛ afee tsei ni efite fioo yɛ amɛhiɛ lɛ afee nibii ni egbi. maŋ lɛ mli chili paste, aduawai amli nu loo kooloi aniyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ Nitsumɔ haa onáa shika loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jarayelɔi baakpoo lɛ haa oweku lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do cassava and yam roots spoil so fast after they get cut or cracked during harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei kɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ beni afolɔ amɛ loo akumɔ amɛ yɛ kpamɔ be mli lɛ?

english: When root crops are cut or cracked, their inner tissue is exposed to air and moisture, causing rapid oxidation and micro-organism attacks. Drying or processing damaged roots immediately helps preserve their value.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afo tso shishifãi lɛ loo akumɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa mli fãji lɛ amli. Enɛ haa oksideshin kɛ helai bibii ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa oya. Shishifãi ni efite lɛ ni agbiɔ loo atsuɔ he nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni amɛsɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn brown whenever the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Plantains require a lot of water to remain healthy. During the dry season, soil moisture drops quickly, causing the leaves to dry out and turn brown as the plant tries to conserve water for its main stem.
ga: Nu babaoo he miihia plantains koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ baa shi oya. Enɛ haa baai ni egbi, ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa be mli ni tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekɛ nu ato kɛha tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ.

english: Why do my pineapple plants turn yellow and brown when the rains stop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pineapple tso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ?

english: When rainfall stops and soil moisture disappears, pineapple plants suffer heat stress. Without water in the root zone, the plant cannot feed its leaves, causing them to turn brown.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ kpa ni nugbɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ laaje lɛ, Pineapple tsei lɛ baaná dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Kɛji nu bɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ atsɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ amɛye nii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ tsɔɔ asarasu.

english: If my plantain trees turn brown during a dry spell, will they die completely?
ga: Kɛji midumɔwui lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Ani tso lɛ baagbo kwraa?

english: Not necessarily. If the root system stays alive underground, the plantain tree can bounce back and produce fresh green leaves once rainfall or water returns to the soil.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lolo. Dumɔwui baanyɛ aku amɛsɛɛ ni amɛwo baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ loo nu ku esɛɛ eba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I protect my crops from drying up when there is no rainfall?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni amɛkagbi be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: You can protect your crops by adding organic material to the soil to trap moisture and covering the ground around the crops with dried grass or leaves to protect the soil from direct sun heat.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛtsɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni okɛbaafata shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekɛmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekɛha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ŋmɔɔ nibii koni akɛbu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: How can organic fertilizer help my farm stay green even when it doesn't rain?
ga: Te organic fertilizer baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ ni ehi shi eŋɔli yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ po lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Organic fertilizer acts like a sponge in the soil. It improves the soil's ability to trap and hold onto moisture, allowing crop roots to access water long after the rain stops.
ga: Organic fertilizer tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekɛtoɔ. Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ náa nu be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ.

english: Will putting fertilizer on my farm ruin my land in the long run?
ga: Ani miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye mishikpɔŋ lɛ awui yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli?

english: Overusing harsh chemical fertilizers can degrade soil quality over time, but natural organic fertilizers actually build up healthy soil and make your land richer over time.
ga: Tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ afite shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Shi adebɔɔ mli nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ maa shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ehaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nii babaoo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: What is the difference between organic fertilizer and regular chemical fertilizer?
ga: Organic ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ Te amɛsoro amɛhe amɛha tɛŋŋ?

english: Organic fertilizer comes from natural plant and animal materials that feed both the crop and the soil, whereas chemical fertilizer gives plants a fast nutrient boost but does not improve the soil's ability to hold water.
ga: Organic fertilizers lɛ jɛɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei kɛ kooloi anibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ niyenii lɛ amli. Yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa niyenii mli hewalɛ oya lɛ, amɛhaaa sũ lɛ anyɛ ahi nu mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Are organic fertilizers made here in Ghana effective for growing crops?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee yɛ Ghana lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ?

english: Yes, locally produced Ghanaian organic fertilizers are made from rich organic waste and compost, making them well-suited for restoring local soils and improving crop yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, Ghana ŋmɔshi nibii ni afeɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha maŋ lɛ mli shikpɔji lɛ ahe hewalɛwoo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why does my soil become dry and hard so quickly after the rainy season ends?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ ni ewaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil dries out quickly when it lacks organic matter. Without compost or decaying leaves to hold water, heat from the sun evaporates the soil moisture very fast.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo baai ni egboi ni baaha nu ahi mli lɛ bɛ. Dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli lɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Should I apply organic fertilizer when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa?

english: It is best to apply organic fertilizer when there is some moisture in the ground or just before expected rains, as water helps crop roots absorb the nutrients from the fertilizer.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli afata he kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo dani nugbɔ anɛ. Enɛ ji akɛ, nu yeɔ ebuaa tsei shishifãi ni amɛheɔ niyenii ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ.

english: Can I get a good harvest of vegetables like carrots if I only have a small plot of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ maná aduawai kpakpai tamɔ karɔt kɛji miyɛ shikpɔŋ fioo ko pɛ?

english: Yes, crops like carrots and beetroot do not require large acreage. Because they can be planted close together in raised beds, you can produce a high yield and earn good income even from a small piece of land.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ karɔt kɛ beetroot biɔ he ko ni da. Ejaakɛ abaanyɛ adu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ saatsoi ni awo nɔ lɛ anɔ. Obaanyɛ onine ashɛ yibii babaoo kɛ shika kpakpa nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko po nɔ.

english: Which crops can I grow if I want to harvest and sell in a very short time?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei srɔtoi manyɛ makwɛ kɛji miisumɔ ni makpa ni mahɔ̃ɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli?

english: Vegetables such as carrots, beetroot, and leafy greens are short-cycle crops. Most of them mature within two to three months, allowing you to harvest, sell, and replant multiple times in a single year.
ga: Aduawai tamɔ karɔt, beets kɛ baai eŋɔli ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ kuku. Mɛi babaoo baakwɛ̃ yɛ nyɔji enyɔ loo etɛ mli. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa, ohɔ̃ɔ, ni oduɔ ekoŋŋ shii abɔ yɛ afi kome mli.

english: Is beetroot a difficult crop for a new farmer in Ghana to start with?
ga: Ani beetroot ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa kɛha okwaafoi heei ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ?

english: Beetroot is quite beginner-friendly. It grows quickly, requires minimal land, and needs only basic care like regular watering, well-drained soil, and simple weeding to produce a great crop.
ga: Beetroot ji shishijee-naanyobɔɔ kwraa. Edaa oya Eheɔ he fioo pɛ ni ehe hiaa shishijee kwɛmɔ tamɔ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa pɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ mlɛo koni aná yibii kpakpai

english: Do I need expensive heavy machinery to prepare my farm for root vegetables?
ga: Ani tsɔnei ni tsii ni jara wa he miihia mi koni mikɛsaa miŋmɔ lɛ kɛha shishifãi ni aduɔ lɛ?

english: No, heavy machines are not always necessary, especially for small plots. You can prepare loose soil beds manually using simple hand tools like hoes and rakes, which work perfectly fine for root crops.
ga: Dabi, jeee be fɛɛ be tsɔnei ni tsii he hiaa. Titri lɛ kɛha shikpɔji bibii Obaanyɛ okɛ nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei, ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ jogbaŋŋ kɛha shishifãi lɛ asaa shikpɔŋ ni etse ehe lɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear rocks and break up hard soil before planting carrots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo tɛi amli ni mafo shikpɔŋ ni wa mli dani madu karɔt lɛ?

english: Carrots grow directly down into the earth. If the soil is hard, compact, or full of stones, the roots split or become twisted, resulting in misshapen crops that are difficult to sell.
ga: Karɔt kwɛ̃ɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ. Afolɔ shishifãi lɛ amli loo etsake. Enɛ haa tsei ni efite ni ewa akɛ ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why is it better to make raised soil beds when planting root crops like carrots and beetroot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaafee saatsoi ni awó nɔ beni aduɔ shishifãi tamɔ karɔt kɛ beets lɛ?

english: Raised beds keep the soil loose and fluffy, allowing the roots to expand easily underground. They also improve water drainage so excess rain doesn't rot the roots.
ga: Saji ni awo nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi mlɛo. Ehaa nu lɛ hu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ akaha shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: How long does it take from planting beetroot seeds to harvesting the mature roots?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ kɛjɛɔ beetroot dumɔwui lɛ adumɔ mli kɛyashiɔ shishifãi ni eda lɛ akpamɔ nɔ?

english: Beetroot usually takes between 60 to 70 days (about two months) from planting to reach harvest size, provided the crop gets adequate water and sunlight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, beetroot heɔ aaafee gbii 60 kɛyashi 70 (aaafee nyɔji 2) kɛjɛɔ edalɛ mli dani eshɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ dalɛ he. Kɛji akɛ tsei lɛ ná nu kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my crops perform better when I plant them in organized lines instead of scattering the seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ gbɛi ni yɔɔ fɛo nɔ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Planting in neat rows ensures each plant gets enough sunlight, air, and nutrients without competing with its neighbors. It also makes weeding, watering, and harvesting much easier.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ yeee akaŋ. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ, kɛ nikpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: How do crops like carrots behave if they do not get enough water while growing?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ karɔt feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ kɛji amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: When carrots suffer from uneven watering or drought, their roots become tough and woody, and sudden heavy watering afterwards can cause the roots to crack open.
ga: Kɛji karɔt na nu loo ŋmɔlɔ ni bɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ wa ni amɛfeɔ tsei. Ni nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi trukaa yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ akumɔ.

english: Why do carrot and beetroot leaves stay above ground while the edible part grows under the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ karɔt kɛ beetroot baai lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni fãi ni ayeɔ lɛ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: The leafy top acts as a food factory that catches sunlight to create energy. The plant then sends that energy down into the soil to feed and expand the taproot, which becomes the vegetable you harvest.
ga: Tsei ayitsei tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii afeemɔ hei ni heɔ hulu la koni ekɛfee hewalɛ. Kɛkɛ ni tso lɛ tsuɔ nakai hewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eye niyenii ni ekɛ eshishifã lɛ akwɛ̃, ni no bafeɔ aduawai ni okpaa lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and dry up when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ hulu la fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because intense direct sunlight scorches their delicate leaves and dries out the soil moisture before their shallow roots can absorb enough water.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gĩɔ dani shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my mature cocoa pods turn black and rot during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni edara lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in high humidity and wet weather. Heavy rain splashes the fungus from the soil and infected leaves onto the pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ baai ni hela emɔ lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the tip towards the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ eshishigbɛ kɛyaa teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing maize leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has to the newest growth at the top, causing the older bottom leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baajie nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛya tso hee ni eda fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas in my field improve the soil for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni midu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the plants decay, this nitrogen stays in the soil as fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ be mli ni tso lɛ fiteɔ lɛ. Nitrogen nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when the farm stays flooded with water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni nu eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because excess water cuts off the oxygen supply to the tubers, allowing soil fungal diseases to invade and rot the underground crop.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu ni fa fe nine lɛ kpaɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa tu lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ boteɔ mli ni ehaa tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Yam vines need to climb stakes so their leaves can spread out to catch direct sunlight, which gives the plant the energy it needs to grow large, healthy underground tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tso ko nɔ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why are my pepper plant leaves curling upward and twisting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites feeding on the undersides of the leaves, or by a viral infection spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli.

english: What causes tiny holes in my maize leaves and small brown powder inside the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ powda bibioo ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ Mɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the leaf funnels of young maize plants during the night.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ naagbai lɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ baai amli gbɛkɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences heat stress or irregular watering. Extreme heat or sudden dry spells prevent the flowers from pollinating successfully.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo ŋmɔlɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small stems growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Removing excess suckers prevents them from stealing water, nutrients, and sunlight from the main mother plant, ensuring the main plant produces a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaaa amɛju nu, niyenii mli hewalɛ, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ awo dumɔwui wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when there are no big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni tsei wuji komɛi bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and small roots that cannot handle direct, intense heat. Plantains or shade trees act like umbrellas to keep the young cocoa cool and keep moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii. ni nyɛŋ adamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ naa Dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai koni amɛha kookoo bibii lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛha sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my growing maize turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele ni miida lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the key food plants use to build green leaves and grow tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why does adding dried poultry manure make my garden vegetables grow much bigger than using basic soil alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ kooloi ashishifãi ni egbi fata he lɛ, ehaa aduawai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa fe sũ ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ pɛ?

english: Poultry manure improves the soil structure and slowly releases essential plant foods like nitrogen and phosphorus that feed the plant roots over a long period.
ga: Kooloi ashishifãi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ni fiofio lɛ Ejieɔ tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. ni haa niyenii ni akɛduɔ shishifãi fiofio yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ

english: Why do my maize plants grow very thin and produce small ears when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛtoi bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ, kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, their roots fight each other for water and soil nutrients, and their leaves block sunlight from one another, leaving all the plants weak.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso muu lɛ fɛɛ bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I wait until the major rains fully settle before planting my main crop seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔshiimɔi wuji lɛ aba shi dani madu midumɔwui titrii lɛ?

english: Seeds need continuous soil moisture to sprout properly; if you plant during early unpredictable rains, a dry stretch can heat the ground and ruin the seeds before they grow.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji odu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ mli mra lɛ, Dry stretching baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli adɔ ni efite dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off before any peppers start to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they suffer from stress caused by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of insects to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni bɛ ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground if I leave them in the farm during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil prevents air from reaching the roots, which causes fungi and bacteria to multiply and break down the cassava tubers into mush.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ faa babaoo ni amɛgbalaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli amɛfeɔ ŋmei.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the young inner leaves inside the whorl of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ miiye baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ a-rings lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These pests are Fall Armyworms, which attack the softest, newest part of the maize plant where growth happens because it is easy for them to chew and digest.
ga: Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni tutuaa ŋmãa tso lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo, ni ji ehee fe fɛɛ yɛ he ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ ejaakɛ eyɛ mlɛo akɛ eeeye ni eshɛreɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes on the same plot of land where I harvested garden eggs last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tomato yɛ he ni mibua ŋmeii anaa yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Tomatoes and garden eggs belong to the same plant family and share the same soil diseases; planting them in the same spot allows hidden soil pests to attack the new crop immediately.
ga: Tomato kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii jɛ tso weku kome mli ni amɛyeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai kome. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he kome lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do wild weeds make my crops grow much slower than a well-cleared farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo fe ŋmɔ ni ajie mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and have stronger roots than farm crops, so they steal the available fertilizer, water, and sunlight before your crops can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. No hewɔ lɛ amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ lɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ.

english: Is it better to plant my crops close together so I can fit more on my land?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi akɛ madu tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe bɔni afee ni maná he ko babaoo?

english: Planting crops too close together forces them to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to weak plants and smaller yields. Proper spacing ensures each crop gets enough air and food to produce well.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛwuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: How do I know if my soil is healthy enough to start growing maize this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Healthy soil is dark, crumbly, and holds moisture without staying waterlogged. You can test it by squeezing moist soil in your hand—if it forms a soft ball that crumbles easily when touched, it has a good balance for root growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli edɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni nu bɛ mli. Obaanyɛ oka enɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni oookɛwo onine mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji efee bɔɔlu ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni fãa oya kɛji akɛ ata he lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells as a natural survival mechanism to conserve water. As long as the stem remains green and firm, the plant is alive and will sprout fresh leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ nu he. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ yitso lɛ baafee eŋɔli ni ehi shi shiŋŋ lɛ Tso lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni ebaakwɛ ŋmeii heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing very tall with lush leaves but no fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? Ani oyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi obɛ yibii?

english: Excessive foliage with no flowers or fruit usually means there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen encourages leaf and stem growth rather than flowering, so switching to a phosphorus-rich fertilizer helps crop fruiting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai babaoo ni fɔfɔi loo aduawai bɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen haa baa kɛ tso lɛ dalɛ yaa hiɛ fe fɔfɔi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii ni fɔsfɔs babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl inward when the afternoon sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl during extreme heat to reduce water loss from evaporation. Placing grass mulch around the base of the plant keeps the roots cool and retains soil moisture.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Can I grow beans together with my maize on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping beans with maize is very beneficial. Beans fix nitrogen from the air into the soil, providing natural fertilizer that helps the maize grow stronger.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Beans saa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, eji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃ɔ waa.

english: How do I know if my young cocoa trees are getting too much sunlight?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiná hulu la babaoo tsɔ?

english: Young cocoa leaves will look burnt, yellowish, or dry around the edges if exposed to full sun. Planting fast-growing temporary shade crops like plantains nearby provides the canopy shade young cocoa trees need to survive.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ baafee tamɔ nɔ ni ashã. Ehe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo egbiɔ yɛ eshishigbɛ kɛji hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛ enɔ. Be kukuoo mli shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni kookoo tso lɛ he miihia hulutsoo lolo.

english: Why does water sit on top of my field for days after a heavy rain instead of sinking in?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ moŋ fe ni eeebote nu shishi lɛ?

english: Standing water means the soil has heavy clay or a compacted layer underneath that blocks drainage. Digging simple drainage channels allows excess water to escape so plant roots do not rot from lack of air.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo nɔ ko ni ebɔle ehe ni tsiɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ naa. Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni aaafo lɛ Haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjeɔ kpo. No hewɔ lɛ tsei shishifãi lɛ fiteee yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ hewɔ.

english: How can I tell when my yam tubers are fully mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ edara jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yams are ready for harvest when the leaves and vines turn yellow and begin to dry up naturally. This signals that the plant has completed its growth cycle and stored all its energy into the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe edalɛ be lɛ naa ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ eto ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take much longer to produce fruit than those on other farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii fe ŋmɔji krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Plantains require deep, organic-rich soil and consistent moisture. If suckers are planted in poor soil, lack organic manure, or compete with weeds, their growth and fruiting cycle will be significantly delayed.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli yɔɔ mli babaoo ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ he miihia plantains. Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ Organic fertilizer ni bɛ loo jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ lɛ Dalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ waa.

english: How do I properly prepare fresh bush land before putting my seeds into the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa mi-sod shrub he lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani mikɛ dumɔwui awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Preparing fresh land requires clearing thick weeds, removing stubborn stumps, and loosening the topsoil so young plant roots can easily spread and find water and nutrients.
ga: He ni jwɛi lɛ yɔɔ lɛ he saamɔ biɔ ni ajie jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Jiemɔ tsei akui ni wa lɛ kɛjɛ ohe. ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ afee mlɛo koni tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya ni amɛtao nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Should I cut down all the old wild trees on my land before I start planting my farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo koo mli tsei momoi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani mabɔi ŋmɔshi nitsumɔ?

english: You do not need to remove every tree. Leaving a few mature shade trees helps protect delicate young crops from intense sun heat, preserves soil moisture, and reduces wind damage.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa ni ojie tso fɛɛ tso. Kɛ́ ashi tsei fioo komɛi ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni oha kɔɔyɔɔ ni fiteɔ nii lɛ aba shi

english: What is the best time of the year for me to clear my land for a new farming season?
ga: Mɛɛ afi lɛ mli be hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ kɛha okwaayeli be hee lɛ?

english: It is best to clear land towards the end of the dry season. This allows cleared brush to dry easily for removal, ensuring your field is ready right when the main rains begin.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi jɛmɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ naagbee. Eyeɔ ebuaa brɔshii ni atsuu he lɛ ni egbiɔ ni ehaa ejiemɔ feɔ mlɛo. Enɛ baaha oŋmɔ lɛ afee klalo beni nugbɔ titri lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ.

english: Can old tree roots left buried in the ground harm my new crops?
ga: Ani tsei shishifãi momo ni ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ awui?

english: Yes, old decaying roots and stumps can attract termites or harbor root-rot fungi, which can spread and attack the fresh root systems of your new crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, shishifãi kɛ tsei akutsei ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbala ŋmeii loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ ŋmeii. Enɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni etutua shishifãi heei ni yɔɔ onibii heei lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do long, snake-like wild vines keep creeping back into my farm after I clear the bush?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli wain tsei kakadaji ni tamɔ onufu lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mijie jwɛi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Many wild vines have deep underground root systems or thick stems that store nutrients. Even when you cut the top off, the roots remain alive underground and quickly send up fresh shoots toward sunlight.
ga: Koo mli wain tsei babaoo yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi loo tsei ni mli tse ni amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛi toɔ. Kɛji akɛ ofo ŋwɛi fã lɛ po. Shishifãi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛkɛ ŋmeii heei tsuɔ nii oya kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli.

english: Why do strange new weeds suddenly pop up right after I finish clearing my planting area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ jeɔ kpo trukaa beni ajie he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Clearing the land exposes long-buried weed seeds to direct sunlight and rainwater, which triggers them to germinate and grow rapidly in the open space.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa jwɛi dumɔwui ni afu be kakadaŋŋ lɛ naa hulu la kɛ nugbɔ nu tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baaha jwɛi dumɔwui akwɛ̃ ni amɛdara oya yɛ hei ni gbɛ yɔɔ.

english: How can I tell if a wild plant on my land will harm my crops or help them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui loo ebaaye ebua amɛ?

english: Harmful wild plants usually grow very aggressively, wrap tightly around your crops, or choke their roots. Helpful plants grow moderately, provide light shade, or add nitrogen to enrich the soil.
ga: Koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ fɔɔ daa oya. Okɛwo oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ. loo efite eshishifãi lɛ. Tsei ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ daa yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ, amɛhaa hulutsoo, loo amɛkɛ nitrogen fataa he koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do crops grow well on my neighbor's land in Adanse South but struggle on my own plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mikutsoŋnyo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ Adanse South lɛ nɔ shi amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ yɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Soil depth, water retention, shade cover, and nutrient levels can vary widely even between neighboring farms. Your land might have harder soil or lower organic matter that needs extra care.
ga: shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ Nu ni ahiɔ mli, nɔ ni akɛhaa nɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baanyɛ asoro lɛ waa yɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ ateŋ po. Ekolɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni biɔ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko bɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my young crops turning yellow even after I removed all the surrounding weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mijie jwɛi fɛɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves often indicate that young crops are getting scorched by strong sunlight, suffering from poor drainage, or lacking key nutrients like nitrogen in the newly cleared soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shã tsei bibii lɛ. Naagbai ni kɔɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen ni bɛ shikpɔŋ hee ni ajie lɛ mli lɛ he

english: What should I do if I find strange insect nests or burrows while tilling my raw land?
ga: Kɛ́ ona kooloi ashihilɛhe loo bu ko ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ beni otsuɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lɛ, mɛni esa akɛ ofee?

english: It is best to identify and treat insect nests, like termite mounds or root-eating grubs, before planting. If left untreated, these pests will attack young seeds and seedlings as soon as they sprout.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooona kooloi ashihilɛhei, tamɔ termite mounds loo root beetles lɛ, ni otsa amɛ dani adu. Kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ, Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ tutuaa dumɔwui bibii kɛ dumɔwui bibii kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I cut down all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikookoo tsei bibii lɛ egbi ni amɛgboi beni mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to intense heat and need partial shade to survive. Leaving shade trees or planting plantains around them keeps the soil moist and protects the young cocoa leaves from burning in the hot sun.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa ni amɛbiɔ hulutsoo fioo koni amɛhi shi. Tsei ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or Urea helps the crop turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ NPK loo urea tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Should I put chemical fertilizer in the planting hole right at the same time I sow my maize seeds?
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ awo dumɔ bui lɛ amli yɛ be kome too mli. Kɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni aduɔ loo daabi?

english: No, you should wait about two weeks after sprouting before applying fertilizer. Seeds use their own internal energy to sprout, and putting chemical fertilizer too close to new seeds can burn the young roots.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ omɛ aaafee otsii enyɔ beni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ dani okɛ fɔmɔ nii awo mli. Dumɔwui kɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmli hewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Ni tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛfataa dumɔwui heei ahe tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi bibii lɛ ashã.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava cuttings very close together to fit more plants on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei niji ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni tsei babaoo akwɛ̃ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are packed too closely, their roots compete heavily for sunlight, water, and soil food. Proper spacing of about one meter apart gives each plant enough space to develop large tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Kɛji akɛ amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mita kome lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ bulbs agboi baa.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning soft and black before the fruits are even ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ediŋŋ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium and irregular watering while the fruit is growing. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant absorb calcium and prevents the rotting.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa calcium ni haaa amɛfite.

english: Why are all the flowers falling off my pepper plants without producing any actual peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni pepper diɛŋtsɛ ko kwraa bɛ ni miida lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat, dry soil, or a lack of soil nutrients. Regular watering and keeping the soil cool helps the flowers stay on the plant and turn into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa ni ahaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why is it good for my land if I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my plot after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize takes away a lot of nitrogen from the soil. Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground, naturally restoring soil fertility for your next crops.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds while my crops are still very small instead of waiting until they grow bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa kwraa lolo lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ kɛyashi jwɛi lɛ aakwɛ̃?

english: Young crops have small roots and easily lose the fight against fast-growing weeds for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early protects your crops during their most critical growing stage.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwu amɛshi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ mlɛo koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe yɛ amɛdalɛ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do some farmers cover the ground around their vegetable plants with dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai haa he ni amɛŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves is called mulching. It holds moisture in the ground during hot days, keeps the soil cool, and prevents weeds from sprouting.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: Why do certified seeds from the agric store give better harvests than the seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni jɛ okwaayeli shwapo ko mli lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred to resist common local diseases and produce higher yields. Saved seeds lose their strength over time and are more likely to carry seed-borne diseases into your new crop.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli helai ni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ he hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai ni jɛɔ dumɔwui amli baa lɛ aba onibii heei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and dropping off during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle full, direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantain alongside young cocoa protects them from direct heat and keeps moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fɛɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, kɛ kookoo bibii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ mli waa

english: Why do I need to make big earth mounds before planting my seed yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa shikpɔŋ ŋmɔ agbo dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow deep under the ground and need loose, soft soil to expand properly. Making high mounds provides soft soil for big tubers to develop and protects them from rot caused by standing water.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi shɔŋŋ. Ni ehe miihia ni ená shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni enyɛ egbɛ eshwa jogbaŋŋ. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo koni bulb lɛ anyɛ akwɛ, ni ehaaa amɛfite kɛjɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow even though there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? He ni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the food plants need to stay green and grow tall. Adding NPK fertilizer or well-rotted manure restores this vital nutrient.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii ni he hia tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ niyenii ni he hiaa nɛɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why is it good for my soil if I plant groundnuts or beans on the land where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil, but groundnuts and beans are special crops that naturally grab nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, restoring fertility for your next crop.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Ku sɛɛ okɛ fɔmɔ aba oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: What is eating the soft center leaves of my young maize plants and leaving tiny holes?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ ni eshiɔ bu bibii?

english: This is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the growing center of maize plants. Spraying recommended insecticides or applying neem extract early in the morning kills them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ hei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ shwie nɔ loo okɛ neem mli nu lɛ tsu nii leebi lɛ, ebaagbe amɛ dani amɛbaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and rot before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant or irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist and adding lime to acidic soil prevents the fruit from rotting.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ tsei amli loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa ni okɛ lime fata shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ he lɛ, ebaatsi aduawai anaa koni amɛkafite.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my farm?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too close makes crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants and tiny yields. Proper spacing gives each plant enough food and room to grow big fruit or grain.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha tso fɛɛ tso aná niyenii kɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ aduawai loo dumɔwui wuji.

english: Why do my crops slow down in growth when I allow weeds to stay in the farm for just two weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo lɛ? Beni miha jwɛi lɛ hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli otsii enyɔ pɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight away from your plants. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I plant cassava stems in the dry season so they start growing early?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cassava tsei yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛje shishi amɛda oya?

english: Cassava stem cuttings need moist soil to sprout roots and initial leaves. Planting them in dry soil causes the stems to dry out and die before roots can form.
ga: Kasava tsei lɛ afolɔ biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ koni shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ aje shishi amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi dani shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do seeds I buy from certified agro-dealers perform better than seeds I save from my previous maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miheɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli he nihɔɔlɔ ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ dɛŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni mikpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified hybrid seeds are specially bred to resist diseases, survive dry spells, and yield large uniform cobs, whereas saved seeds lose these special qualities after the first harvest.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee hybrid ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai. amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji be fɛɛ be Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ sui krɛdɛɛi nɛɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize farm turning pale yellow before the corn is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is an important plant food. Adding a small amount of NPK fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will help the leaves turn dark green again so the cobs can grow big.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii fioo loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ waa ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ agbo.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground during the heavy rain season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water sits around them for too long. Planting your cassava cuttings on raised mounds or ridges lets extra rainwater drain away quickly, keeping the underground roots dry enough to stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ta amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. ni oha shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ agbi bɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why must I stake my yam plants with tall sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji atswa mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ ama shi moŋ fe ni mahã amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the sunlight to make the energy needed for growing big tubers underground. Staking also lifts the leaves off the wet soil, which protects the plant from fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu woɔ tsei ahe baai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant gets too stressed by dry soil or extreme afternoon heat. Watering your plants early in the morning keeps the soil moist so the flowers stay attached and form fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ loo shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa ha tsei lɛ miihao. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Is it good for my land if I plant cowpeas and maize together on the same field?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji mikɛ tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa fee ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize is very beneficial. Cowpeas naturally pull nitrogen food out of the air and feed it into the soil, which helps the maize grow strong while giving you two different crops to harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ daa waa kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ni ehaa bo ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi enyɔ ni obaakpa.

english: What is making small holes in the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Mi ŋmãa tso bibioo lɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: Those holes are caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar eating the tender leaves. Checking your farm early and spraying approved organic mixtures or recommended chemical treatments directly into the leaf center will stop them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tsei ahe baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra. Ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ ateŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa amɛkpaa.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up and look tiny and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ bibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap out of the leaves. Spraying the plants with a mild neem leaf oil extract or soapy water helps clear these insects away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper leaf curl baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem baa mli fɔ ni mli ejɔ loo nu ni mli edɔ shwie tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ he.

english: Why do some of my seeds fail to grow out of the soil after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds usually fail to sprout if they are buried too deep where air cannot reach them, or if the soil is too dry. Planting seeds at a shallow depth—about twice their size—in moist soil gives them the best chance to sprout.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ kwɛŋ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ yɛ he ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛhe. Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. (aaafee dumɔwu lɛ dalɛ toi enyɔ) lɛ baaha dumɔwu lɛ aná hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni ekɛkwɛ̃.

english: How can I tell if my soil is rich enough to feed my crops well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ nibii ni miduɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Good, fertile soil is usually dark in color, feels soft and crumbly in your hands, holds moisture well, and contains earthworms. If your soil is pale or hard like dry clay, adding composted leaves and manure will rebuild its richness.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi ni baa nii lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. E nuɔ he kaa e ngɛ bɔdɔ nɛ e ngɛ tsɔe ngɛ nine mi. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii hu yɛ. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli tse loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ Baai kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaafata he lɛ baaye abua ni etswa ebɔi babaoo lɛ ema shi ekoŋŋ.

english: What happens to my maize crop if heavy rains cause water to sit on my field for many days?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu hi mi ŋmɔji amli gbii babaoo?

english: When water sits on your field for too long, it chokes the roots of your maize by cutting off air. This turns the leaves yellow, stunts growth, and causes root rot, which can eventually kill the plants.
ga: Kɛ nu hi oŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ Nu lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. ni baaha baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ aha dalɛ akpa Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaanyɛ egbe tso lɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to use river water that has trash or dirty waste dumped in it to water my vegetables?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛ faa ko ni jwɛi loo jwɛi ni mli ewo muji yɔɔ mli lɛ baatsu nii kɛha mi-aduawai lɛ nu?

english: No, using polluted river water can introduce harmful chemicals or germs to your farm. This can stunt crop growth, make your vegetables unsafe for consumption, and damage your soil over time.
ga: Dabi, faa mli nu ni mli ewo muji ni okɛaatsu nii lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofai loo helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui aba oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tsei adalɛ naa. Enɛ haaa o-vegetables lɛ afee nɔ ni esaaa akɛ ayeɔ. ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fitemɔ baa yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants turn black and drop off during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Excess rain and high humidity create a humid environment where fungal diseases thrive. The constant moisture stays on the leaves and roots, encouraging fungus to attack and weaken the plant.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ baa. Fɛ̃i hiɔ baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ be fɛɛ be. Enɛ woɔ ŋmei lɛ hewalɛ koni etutua tso lɛ ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and dry up when I plant them in an open field without big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. Without temporary shade from plants like plantain or shade trees, the intense sun burns their young leaves and dries out the moisture in the soil.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii nuɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛji akɛ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo ni jɛ tsei tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli lɛ bɛ lɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ agbi.

english: Why do people spread dried leaves or palm fronds on top of the soil around their crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi shwieɔ baai ni egbi loo tsei ahe tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This practice is called mulching. It acts like a protective cover over the soil, keeping it cool, preventing soil water from evaporating under the hot sun, and stopping weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ gãimlibii ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he, ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with big leaves, but the tubers under the ground remain very tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: This usually happens when the soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium or phosphorus. The plant uses all its energy to grow big green leaves above ground instead of feeding the tubers below.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium loo phosphorus ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeeha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my soil turn into sticky mud when it rains and then form deep cracks when the sun dries it out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ muji kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ? Ni ŋmeii ni mli kwɔlɔ jeɔ kpo kɛ́ hulu lɛ shã lɛ?

english: This means your soil has a high clay content. Clay soil holds water for a long time, making it sticky, and shrinks into hard clumps when dry. Adding organic manure or compost helps loosen clay soil and improves drainage.
ga: Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fa babaoo. Shikpɔŋ ni sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ hiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. ha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni wa kɛji egbi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ sũ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi ni ehaa nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know when it is the right time to plant my rain-fed maize after the first rain falls?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should not plant immediately after the very first rain because the soil underneath may still be dry. Wait until you get a few days of steady rain so the ground is soaked deep enough to keep the seeds moist until they sprout.
ga: Kaadu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ejaakɛ ekolɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi lolo. Mɛɛ ni oná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa gbii fioo komɛi koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi amɛbaakwɛ̃.

english: If I plant my cassava cuttings very close together, will I harvest more cassava from my land?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ mihe lɛ Ani makpã ŋmei babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, planting too close causes the cassava plants to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving them proper space allows each plant to spread its roots and produce larger, healthier tubers.
ga: Dabi, dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmei tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso shwereɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli ni efeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant maize on the exact same patch of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously in the same spot drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up. Rotating maize with crops like beans or groundnuts helps restore nitrogen to the soil and clears pest problems.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kɔɔ ŋmãa he pɔtɛɛ aba. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni ejieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe naagbai kɛyaa.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow instead of healthy green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or when roots sit in waterlogged soil. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or improving drainage helps the leaves get green and strong again.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ ta sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the bottom ends of my tomatoes turn black and rot before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomatoi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes, known as blossom-end rot, happen when the soil doesn't deliver enough calcium to the fruit, often caused by irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture consistent and adding compost or lime helps prevent this.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ aha aduawai lɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I plant beans alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ahe lɛ?

english: Beans are legumes that fix nitrogen gas from the air into the soil. Planting them with maize naturally enriches the soil, giving the maize the extra food it needs to grow taller and yield more.
ga: Beans ji ŋmeii ni saa nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Abɛi ni akɛ abele duɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ naa niyenii kroko ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes in the middle leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-babi corn baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the central leaves during the day. Inspecting fields early and applying approved pest treatments directly into the plant funnel stops them from destroying your crop.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ateŋ yɛ gbi mli. He ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra kɛ gbɛi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛgbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli. Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkafite onibii.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting in the soil before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when planted in heavy soil that holds too much water or when stem cuttings infected with fungus are used. Planting on raised mounds and selecting clean, healthy stems protects the roots from rotting.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Aloo okɛ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii emɔ amɛ lɛ atsu nii. Kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ, ni ahala tsei ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shishifãi lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite.

english: Why is my harvest getting smaller when I plant tomatoes on the exact same patch of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa kɛ́ midu tomato yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in one spot year after year lets pests and soil diseases specific to that crop build up in the ground. Rotating crops breaks this disease cycle and restores balance to your soil.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, ebaabua tso pɔtɛɛ ko he tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai anaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa hela nɛɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ kpaa ni ehaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ekome ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to support my yam vines with tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji afi mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb toward the sun so their leaves can trap sunlight and make plant food. Staking keeps the leaves off the ground and exposed to light, which encourages the plant to grow large tubers under the soil.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ he koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ hulu la lɛ ni amɛtsɔmɔ niyenii aha tso lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehaa la baa amɛnɔ. Enɛ baawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekwɛ̃ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees lose their flowers before they turn into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi dani amɛmiitsɔ cacao ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they experience stress from intense sunshine, heat, drought, or pest attacks. Providing shade trees around cocoa and managing pests keeps the air humid and helps flowers set into full pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulu la, dɔlɛ, hɔmɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hao amɛ. Ni akɛ hulutsoo haa yɛ Cocoa he kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe nitsumɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops stay small and produce fewer fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ bibii ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, water, and soil nutrients away from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nourishment they need to grow large and produce a full yield.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛwo yibii yɛ amɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why should I apply fertilizer after rain instead of when the ground is dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ moŋ fe be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi lɛ?

english: Fertilizer requires water to dissolve so plant roots can absorb it. Applying it to dry soil can burn plant roots or leave the nutrients useless until rain washes them away.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ biɔ nu koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi loo eha niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ afee nɔ ni he ehiaaa kɛyashi nugbɔ baaho tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I cut down all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and cannot survive direct, scorching sunlight. Keeping shade trees on your farm creates a cool environment, retains soil moisture, and protects the young plants until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ haa shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni obu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛná hulu la ni fa.

english: Why should I leave space between my cassava stems when planting instead of putting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ midu? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ amɛ ama amɛhe lɛ

english: Cassava roots need space underground to expand and form thick tubers. Planting them too close causes the roots to compete for space, water, and plant food, resulting in long, thin, unusable tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ shishi he ko koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛfee ŋmeii ni mli tse. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ abɔ he akaŋ koni amɛná he ko, nu, kɛ tsei aniyenii. Enɛ haa yitsei kakadaji, ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni anyɛɛɛ akɛtsu nii.

english: Why shouldn't I just plant the maize seeds I saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds, especially from high-yielding varieties, lose their strength and yield potential over generations. Using certified seeds from accredited dealers ensures strong plants that can resist local diseases and yield much higher harvests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛ Titri lɛ kɛjɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ amli. Ehewalɛ baaje edɛŋ ni ebaawo yibii yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni jɛ jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ adɛŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning light green and yellow from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Applying the right fertilizer, like NPK or urea, at the right growth stage gives the plant energy to stay green and produce full cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tamɔ NPK loo urea wo tso lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ehi shi ŋmɔŋ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo aba.

english: Why does my farmland produce big harvests during the first year after clearing bush, but gives very small harvests after three years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli beni ajie ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ? Shi ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ yɛ afii etɛ sɛɛ?

english: Clearing bush leaves rich organic matter that feeds crops during the first year. Repeated farming removes nutrients every harvest, so without adding animal manure, compost, or fertilizer, the soil becomes tired and worn out.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ tsei bibii lɛ, ehaa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ baa. okwaayeli ni afɔɔ feemɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. harvest No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite ni ebaafite.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slow and produce weak fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo ni amɛwo yibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and steal water, sunlight, and soil food away from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before growing into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani eda ni etsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or insect attacks. Regular watering during hot spells and controlling pests helps the flowers stay on the plant and turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo koolooi tutuamɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why is it important to prune the lowest leaves of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ofolɔ o-tomato tsei lɛ ahe baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ?

english: The lowest leaves touch the wet soil where fungal diseases live. Pruning them prevents dirt from splashing onto the leaves when it rains, keeping the plant healthy and focusing its energy on fruit growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai hiɔ mli lɛ kpeɔ. Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ amli lɛ, ebaatsi muji ni shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ naa kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ. Ehaa tso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa aduawai lɛ adalɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves fold or droop during hot afternoons even when the soil is damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: When the sun is hot, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the ground. Folding or wilting temporarily is the plant's natural shield to save moisture until the day cools down.
ga: Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Be kukuoo mli ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ni tsiɔ nu lɛ naa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edɔ.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot so quickly when stored in an enclosed room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto tsu ko ni atsĩ naa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams are alive and release heat and moisture after harvest. If kept in an enclosed room without cool, circulating air, heat builds up and encourages fungi to rot the tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni amɛjieɔ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kpo yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ akɛto tsu ko ni aŋã mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli Dɔlɛ buaa ehe naa ni ewoɔ ŋmɔtɔ hewalɛ ni efite.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the tall trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei kakadaji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. Keeping taller shade trees or planting fast-growing plantains alongside them provides essential shade and keeps the soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
