ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ to he loo dumɔwui ni daa oya yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ aba, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden stakes in the ground for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei kakadaji ama shi lɛ? Shi yɛ shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi.

english: Yam plants rely on their leaves receiving sunlight to produce food for the growing tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground, maximizing sunlight exposure and airflow, which leads to larger and healthier yam roots.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ baai ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ agbo. Na hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ babaoo. Enɛ baaha sweet potato shishifãi lɛ adara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why should I cut away some of the shoots growing around the base of my plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ekomɛi.

english: Leaving too many suckers around one plantain stem creates competition for water and soil nutrients. Pruning extra suckers ensures the main plant gets maximum nourishment to produce large, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Nibii ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ Ashishifãi babaoo tsɔ kɛ akaŋshii baa kɛha niyenii ni jɛɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli. Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi babaoo lɛ haa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii babaoo ni haa ewoɔ yibii ni tsii ni dara.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on young maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is essential for leafy green growth, and adding compost, manure, or nitrogen-based fertilizer can help the plant recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he hiaa waa kɛha aduawai ni yɔɔ baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ. Ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ nitrogen fee lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it good practice to plant groundnuts or beans in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This enriches the soil with free nutrients, making it healthier for heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ niyenii kpakpai ni aheee nɔ ko. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ kooloi babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my vegetable stems with dry grass during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-vegetable tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, prevents soil moisture from evaporating in the sun. It keeps the roots cool, conserves water, and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ hulu la lɛ mli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ, ehaa nu hiɔ shi, ni ehaaa jwɛi lɛ aŋɔ he.

english: What causes tiny ragged holes and dark dirt inside the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ muji ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the growing center of maize. Catching them early and using natural remedies like neem oil or approved insecticides helps protect your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni boteɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai tamɔ neem fɔ loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and stopping the plant from growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekadara lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like mites, aphids, or thrips sucking leaf sap, or spreading a plant virus. Controlling these small pests early keeps the leaves healthy and flat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii, ŋmeii, loo thrips ni nuɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei amli Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa lɛ mli waa ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do the yellow flowers on my tomato plants fall off without producing any small tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo tomato bibii ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants experience heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of insect pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist and allowing good airflow helps flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni ashwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ faaa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when I leave them in the soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the ground becomes completely waterlogged because the roots cannot breathe in water-soaked soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baagboi kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwraa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu kɛbote shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why are the green leaves on my maize farm turning yellow from the tips down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛnajiaŋ kɛmiiba shi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops use to build green leaves and grow strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni wa.

english: When is the best time for me to put fertilizer around my crops after planting?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mawo fɔmɔ nii yɛ he fɛɛ he? Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ?

english: Apply fertilizer about two to three weeks after sprouting when roots are ready to eat, and make sure the soil is moist so the plants can easily drink up the nutrients.
ga: Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli aaafee otsii enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ beni shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaaye lɛ. Ni kwɛmɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ anu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ mlɛo.

english: Why do people advise me to plant plantains on the same land with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants get burned easily by the strong sun, so plantains grow fast and act like living umbrellas to provide shade and trap moisture in the soil.
ga: Hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shãa cacao tsei bibii lɛ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛtsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔi ni hiɛ ka koni amɛha hulutsoo ni amɛha nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How do I choose the right cassava stem to cut and plant on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tso ni sa ni mafolɔ ni madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Choose hard, woody stems from the middle of a healthy mature plant, because soft green tips rot in the dirt while older stems sprout quickly and strong.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni wa ni jɛ tsei ni eda lɛ amli ejaakɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni tsei momo lɛ baadara oya ni amɛhe wa lɛ.

english: Will planting my seeds very close together give me a bigger harvest from my field?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni madu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, planting seeds too close makes crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in thin plants with very small yields.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ yibiiwoo fioo pɛ baa.

english: Why are small green and brown caterpillars eating the inside leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ?

english: Those caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, which like to hide inside the central leaf funnel of young maize plants where the tissue is soft and easy to chew.
ga: Kplukai lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛtee amɛhe amɛwo ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli, he ni fãji lɛ yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛyeɔ oya lɛ.

english: What is making the leaves of my pepper plants curl up into tight cups?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi ni mli wa?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the juice from under the leaves, which damages the leaf surface as it grows.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni baafite baai lɛ ahiɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Tomato blossoms fall off when the weather gets too hot or the plants don't get enough water, causing heat stress that stops fruit from setting.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni tsiɔ aduawai lɛ anaa lɛ baa.

english: Why does letting weeds grow near my crops slow down their growth so much?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ haa amɛdalɛ baa shi waa lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that steal water and soil nutrients faster than your crops can, leaving your crops hungry and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni boteɔ mli ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe onibii ni oduɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye oŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ.

english: How do I know the rain has soaked the ground enough for me to start planting my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nugbɔ lɛ efɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔ ni sa ni mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ?

english: Dig down into your soil after the rain; if the soil is wet down to the depth of your hand, it has enough moisture to keep your seeds alive through germination.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni aaakumɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛyashɛ onine mli Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi kɛtsɔ amɛkwɛ̃mɔ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my crops curling and drying up during the hot season in my region?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ mikpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When the sun becomes very intense and water is scarce, plants curl their leaves to reduce water loss through evaporation. Browning leaves mean the heat is drying the plant out faster than its roots can pull water from the dry soil.
ga: Beni hulu la lɛ mli wa waa ni nu hu faaa lɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni nu ni amɛlaaje kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ la ni tsoɔ lɛ miigbi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ.

english: What can I cover the soil with to stop the harsh sun from drying out my crops' roots?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ makɛwo mli koni hulu ni naa wa lɛ akagbi mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ?

english: Covering the ground around your plants with dry grass, leaves, or crop residues—known as mulching—acts like a protective blanket. It blocks direct sunlight, keeps the soil cooler, and traps water in the ground longer.
ga: Kɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni etsĩɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni nu hiɔ sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ

english: How do I choose the best time of year to plant my plantain suckers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛdu dumɔwui?

english: Planting plantains at the start of the main rainy season gives the young suckers continuous soil moisture so they can build strong root systems before any fierce heat or dry spell arrives.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli lɛ haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ naa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛbaanyɛ amɛto shishifãi ni mli wa amɛma shi dani hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ shihilɛi aba.

english: Why should I remove some of the extra shoots growing at the base of my plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ ekomɛi?

english: When too many shoots (suckers) grow around one stem, they compete for water, light, and soil nutrients. Leaving only 2 to 3 strong suckers allows the main plant to grow tall and bear large, healthy bunches.
ga: Beni ŋmeii (ŋmei) babaoo miida yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Tsobii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ashi tsei bibii 2 kɛyashi 3 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso titri lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ni efee jwɛi agbo ni mli wa.

english: Why do the lower leaves on my plantain trees turn yellow and hang down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves often indicate that the plant is short on soil nutrients like nitrogen or is struggling with dry conditions. The plant naturally drops older leaves to save water and food for its growing center.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen, loo ekɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi miikpe. Tsei shwieɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛto nu kɛ niyenii he kɛha he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: How does adding manure or compost help my crops survive long dry spells?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Organic materials like manure act like sponges in the soil. They improve the soil's structure so it can absorb and hold onto water during rains, giving roots a water supply even when the weather turns very hot.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmeii tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛhaa bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ feɔ fɛo bɔni afee ni enyɛ eŋɔ nu ni ehiɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa nu kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa po.

english: Is it bad to burn all the cleared bush on my land before I start planting?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ gbonyo akɛ mashã tsei bibii fɛɛ ni ajie yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani mabɔi dumɔwui?

english: Yes, burning destroys beneficial organic matter and leaves the bare soil exposed to scorching heat. Clearing without burning allows plant material to rot into rich topsoil that holds moisture better.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, shãa fiteɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ shɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ashãaa lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ mli nibii lɛ fiteɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ mli, ni no haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees suddenly fall over after a moderate breeze?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains ni eda lɛ gbeeɔ shi trukaa beni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli wa tswa lɛ?

english: When seemingly healthy plantain trees fall easily, pests like plantain weevils or microscopic root worms (nematodes) have likely eaten away the underground stem and root system, destroying the plant's anchor.
ga: Kɛji akɛ plantains ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ gbee shi mlɛo lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ plantain weevils loo shishifãi bibii ni anaaa lɛ baanyɛ aba. (Nematodes) lɛ yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei kɛ shishifãi. efiteɔ tsei ahe ŋtayaai

english: Why do pests and diseases seem to attack my crops more when the sun is very intense?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Harsh weather stresses plants and weakens their natural defenses, making it easier for pests and diseases to invade and multiply quickly.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa lɛ haa tsei haoɔ ni ehaa amɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu hewalɛ lɛ baa shi. Ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai baa Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ ebaatutua ni eshwere oya

english: Why is it helpful to plant fast-growing plantains alongside my young tree crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ yɛ mi tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young tree crops burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly and produce broad leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity needed for young trees to thrive.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa koni tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and burning in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiishã yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight all day because their leaves are tender. They need shade trees or plantain crops grown around them to shield them from high heat and preserve soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ yɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ ahewɔ. Tsei loo tsei bibii ni adu yɛ amɛhe lɛ he miihia amɛ. Bɔni afee ni akafee dɔlɛ ni fe nine ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: What is causing small holes in the leaves of my young maize crop early in the season?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Mi ŋmãa gbekɛ lɛ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by pests like fall armyworms that hide in the growing tip of the plant. Spraying approved organic or chemical treatments early in the morning when the insects are active helps stop the damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ fall worms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ naagbee ni miida lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa bibii amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ wo nɔ leebi be mli ni kooloi lɛ miitsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekpa nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge stems and leaves above ground, but the tubers underground stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: Cassava puts its energy into leaf growth instead of root development when the soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are spaced improperly. Reducing nitrogen-heavy fertilizers encourages the crop to store energy in its tubers.
ga: Yucca haa ehe baai lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛdaraa. Mohu ɔ, sisifãhi daa ke nitrogen fuu ngɛ zugba a nɔ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe ebɔko he ni sa Nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔtsemɔ baawo tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato bulb lɛ mli.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my maize seeds very close together in the same row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces crops to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition results in thin, weak stems and small corn cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: How can I tell if my crops are lacking nutrients in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Crops show nutrient lack through leaf signs: yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen, while stunted growth or purplish leaves signal a need for phosphorus.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ kpo kɛtsɔ okadii ni yɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni ana fɔsfɔs.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up into tight tubes during the dry afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tsɔnei ni mli wa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in high heat is a natural defense mechanism plants use to reduce the leaf surface exposed to the sun, preventing moisture loss during the hot afternoon hours.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛba baa lɛ nɔ hulu la ni baa lɛ shi. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Why do weeds harm my crop yields even after my plants grow bigger than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ mitsei lɛ eda fe jwɛi lɛ moŋ?

english: Even small weeds have roots that steal moisture, fertilizer, and valuable soil nutrients underneath the ground that your main crop needs to produce full seeds or fruit.
ga: Jwɛi bibii po Ojogbaŋŋ, shishifãi komɛi yɛ ni juɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni jara wa, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni tsei ni oyɔɔ mli lɛ he hiaa koni amɛwo dumɔwui loo aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the ground, they naturally replenish soil fertility for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Amɛbaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do dark spots appear on my tomato leaves and cause them to drop off during rainy weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ tomato baai anɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Rain and high humidity create ideal conditions for fungal diseases (blights) to spread. Spacing plants well and keeping water off the foliage helps keep leaves dry and healthy.
ga: Nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ hela (leaf blight) ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei lɛ to amɛhe jogbaŋŋ ni ajie nu kɛjɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I save seeds from my hybrid maize harvest to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ ato koni madu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops lose their strength in the second generation, leading to uneven crop growth, lower yields, and weaker resistance to diseases compared to fresh hybrid seed.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ, amɛwoɔ yibii fioo, ni helai nyɛŋ amɛye amɛhe kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves of my crops turning yellow even though the soil around them is completely soaked with water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nu ebɔle shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air just like they need water to survive. When the soil is completely soaked, water fills up all the space in the soil and pushes out the air, causing the roots to choke and the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi tamɔ bɔ ni nu he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kwraa Nu lɛ eyiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli obɔ ni ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: What will happen to my cocoa trees if rainwater sits on the farm without draining away for many days?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu lɛ hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni efooo gbii babaoo?

english: Standing water rots the underground roots of your cocoa trees because they cannot breathe. Rotting roots prevent the plant from absorbing food, making it weak and exposed to fungal diseases like black pod disease.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa kookoo tso lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ fiteɔ ejaakɛ amɛmuɔ. Shishifãi ni egboi lɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekaŋɔ niyenii. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod hela lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my crops look like they are dying of drought even when the ground around them is wet and muddy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni hɔmɔ miigbo eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ edɔ ni eyɛ muji moŋ?

english: Too much standing water rots the root system of the crop. Once the roots rot and die, the plant can no longer take up any water into its stems and leaves, causing it to wilt as if it were dry.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ baaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ agbo. Kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ fite ni amɛgboi lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ nu awo eshishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli dɔŋŋ. ni haa egbiɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbi

english: How can I prevent rainwater from soaking my farm land completely after heavy rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nugbɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekafɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kwraa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ?

english: You can dig simple drainage gutters around your farm and plant your crops on raised soil mounds or ridges so that extra water flows away instead of standing around the crop roots.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ nu mli lɛ he nubu ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni obɔle he. Okwaa ni okwɛ onibii yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ koni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli, moŋ fe ni ooodamɔ tsei shishifãi ahe.

english: Why is my cassava plant growing plenty of big green leaves but giving me very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When a plant gets too much water or nitrogen, it uses all its energy to grow big leaves and branches above ground instead of storing energy in the food roots below.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nu loo nitrogen babaoo Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo baai agboi kɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ he wami ɔ ngɛ sisijehi nɛ a ngɛ sisi ɔ a mi.

english: Why do some plants stay green and healthy-looking on my farm without producing any flowers or fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ji eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni mikwɛɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni fɔfɔi loo aduawai ko bɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops receive excessive water and nutrients, they sit comfortably in a continuous leaf-growing state and delay flowering because they do not feel any natural trigger to produce seeds or fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nu kɛ niyenii babaoo lɛ Tso lɛ baata shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni baai lɛ yaa nɔ amɛdaraa lɛ amli. ni amɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ Enɛ ji akɛ amɛnuuu adebɔɔ mli henumɔ ni haa amɛwoɔ dumɔwui loo aduawai lɛ he.

english: Why do some of my crops drink much more water than the other crops planted right next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi nuɔ nu babaoo fe ekrokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Different crops have different root sizes and leaf surfaces. Crops with large leaves or fast growth rates drink far more water to cool themselves down and transport nutrients compared to smaller or slower-growing crops.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi yɛ shishifãi kɛ baai srɔtoi. Tsei ni baai lɛ dara loo amɛdaraa oya lɛ nuɔ nu babaoo koni amɛhe ajɔɔ amɛ ni amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo aya. Kɛ akɛto tsei ni daraaa fioo loo amɛdaraa blɛoo lɛ ahe.

english: Should I continue watering my crops if the soil is still damp and wet from yesterday?
ga: Ani esa akɛ maya nɔ mawo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ nu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo ni edɔ kɛjɛ nyɛ?

english: No, you should wait until the top layer of the soil dries out slightly before adding more water. Adding water to already wet soil starves the roots of oxygen and causes root rot.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ agbi fioo dani okɛ nu babaoo afata he. Kɛ́ akɛ nu fata shikpɔŋ ni edɔ momo lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baa lɛ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ, ni ebaaha amɛgboi.

english: How can I tell if I am giving my crops too much water during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ nu babaoo miiha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Signs of overwatering include soft or mushy stems, lower leaves turning yellow and dropping off, and soil that smells sour or damp even after a couple of days.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ nu fa babaoo lɛ he ji tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ loo ni mli edɔ. Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni shãa loo edɔ yɛ gbii 2-3 po sɛɛ.

english: Why are my crops still weak even after I gave them fertilizer on a soaked field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔji ni efɔ lɛ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: When the field is soaked, crop roots cannot breathe or absorb nutrients properly. Fertilizer added to flooded soil simply gets washed away or sits in the water without being used by the plant.
ga: Beni ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu loo amɛhe niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ. Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ loo ekɛwoɔ nu lɛ mli ni tsei kɛtsuuu nii.

english: Why do my crop plants die after only six months while my neighbor's crops keep fruiting for up to two years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ gbo yɛ nyɔji enumɔ pɛ sɛɛ yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii afii enyɔ lɛ?

english: Crops fail early when they do not receive steady nutrients, sufficient water, and early disease control. When a plant gets complete care, its immunity stays high, allowing it to survive and produce yields for its full natural lifespan.
ga: Tsei lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ amɛnáaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ daa. Na nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni oye hela lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Beni akwɛ tsei anɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Ehewalɛ ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ baakã he ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ bii yɛ amɛ adebɔɔ mli wala be fɛɛ mli.

english: How long can I expect to keep harvesting from the same crops before I need to clear the field and replant?
ga: Be enyiɛ manyɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ makpa nii kɛjɛ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli dani ehe baahia ni ajie jɛmɛ ni adu ekoŋŋ?

english: The lifespan depends on the crop, but with proper watering, feeding, and weed management, many semi-perennial crops can remain strong and productive for two years or even longer.
ga: Wala shihilɛ damɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ. Shi kɛ nu ni akɛhaa, niyenii kɛ jwɛi akwɛmɔ ni sa. Tsei babaoo ni yeɔ afii fã lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi ni amɛhe wa ni amɛwo yibii afii enyɔ loo nɔ ni fe nakai po.

english: Why is it necessary to feed fertilizer and water to my crops continuously instead of just at planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo miŋmɔshi nibii amli ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwo amɛmli lɛ nu daa lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha kɛkɛ beni oduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Plants need a steady supply of food and water throughout their growth to stay healthy. Interrupting their food or water supply weakens them, causing them to dry up and die long before their normal lifecycle ends.
ga: Niyenii kɛ nu he miihia tsei be fɛɛ be yɛ amɛdalɛ be fɛɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ niyenii loo nu gba amɛnaa lɛ, ebaaha amɛgbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ be kakadaŋŋ dani amɛshihilɛ be ni amɛyɔɔ daa lɛ baa naagbee.

english: What happens to my crops if I miss watering them during long dry spells in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ nu shwieee nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni yaa nɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ mli?

english: Dry stress starves the crop of essential moisture, which severely stunts growth and makes the plant vulnerable to pests, often leading to total crop failure within a few months.
ga: Dry stress haa tsei lɛ bɛ nu ni he hiaa. Enɛ baatsi dalɛ naa waa. ni ehaa tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai Bei pii lɛ Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli.

english: How does keeping my farm clean and free of weeds help my crops live and produce longer?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ miha miŋmɔ lɛ mli tse ni jwɛi bɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Good farm hygiene removes wild weeds that steal food and water from your crops. It also destroys breeding spots for pests and diseases that otherwise kill crops early.
ga: Okwaafoi amli hetsemɔ kpakpa yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ koo mli jwɛi ni juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ onibii amli lɛ kɛyaa. Efiteɔ hei ni kooloi kɛ helai ni gbeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii oya lɛ fɔɔ yɛ lɛ hu.

english: Why do agricultural officers stress keeping the ground around my crop stems clear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ esa akɛ he ni mi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ lɛ afee faŋŋ lɛ?

english: Clearing around the base of plants allows air to circulate and sunlight to dry excess moisture, preventing fungal rot and soil diseases from killing the stem and roots.
ga: clearing around Tso lɛ shishi haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. ni hulu la lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ mli egbiɔ. Etsiɔ fungal rot kɛ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbe tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Is there any treatment I can give my crops to protect them from diseases before they get sick?
ga: Ani tsofa ko yɛ ni manyɛ maha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni hela akamɔ amɛ dani hela mɔ amɛ?

english: Yes, using certified disease-resistant seeds and applying preventive sprays acts like a protective shield for crops, stopping infections before they can destroy your plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baatsu nii akɛ gãimlibii ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Ekpaa helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ dani amɛfiteɔ otsei lɛ.

english: Why do my plants still dry up and fail even when I give them plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ gĩɔ lolo ni amɛfiteɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Water alone is not enough; if insects or fungi attack the plant's roots and stems, the crop cannot absorb water. Plants require disease protection and proper nutrients alongside water to stay alive.
ga: Nu pɛ kɛkɛ faaa. Kɛji kooloi bibii loo ŋmeii tutua tsei ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ nu. Tsei he miihia ni atsĩ helai anaa kɛ niyenii ni sa kɛfata nu he koni amɛhi shi.

english: What signs should I look out for to know if my crops are failing due to poor care?
ga: Mɛɛ okadii esa akɛ makwɛ jogbaŋŋ koni male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifite yɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni ehiii hewɔ?

english: Yellowing leaves, stunted growth, premature dropping of flowers or fruit, and weak stems are clear warning signs that your crops are suffering from poor nutrition, water shortage, or disease.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ, dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ Fɔfɔi loo aduawai gbeeɔ shi oya. Ni tsei ahe tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ji kɔkɔbɔɔ okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ niyenii ni esaaa ni oduɔ lɛ miipiŋ. nu ni faaa loo hela

english: If I follow all the recommended farming practices properly, can my crops survive and yield beyond two years?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ okwaayeli nifeemɔi fɛɛ ni ajieɔ yi lɛ tsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baahi shi ni amɛwo yibii fe afii enyɔ?

english: Yes, when you consistently satisfy all requirements—providing balanced fertilizer, regular water, clean field hygiene, and pest protection—many crops can thrive and continue yielding well past two years.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ onyiɛ taomɔ nii lɛ fɛɛ tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja, nu ni akɛhaa daa, ŋmɔ mli hetsemɔ ni he tse lɛ sɛɛ be fɛɛ be. kɛ hebuu kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe Nibii babaoo enyɛ ekwɛ̃ ni ewo yibii be fɛɛ be yɛ afii enyɔ ni eho lɛ mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the crop is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani abele tsei lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Yellowing of lower leaves in a V-shape usually means your soil is low in nitrogen. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and grow strong ears, so adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or compost can help correct this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ, ni tamɔ V lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni eha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni etoi lɛ hu ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why does my crop yield keep dropping every year even though I farm on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ baa shi daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikwɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ?

english: Crops pull nutrients out of the soil every season. If you plant the same crop on the same land repeatedly without adding manure, fertilizer, or alternating with legumes like beans or groundnuts, the soil nutrients become exhausted.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛji akɛ odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeee. Niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baafite.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die during the sunny afternoon even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: This is often caused by bacterial wilt, a disease in the soil that blocks water from moving up the plant stem. Using disease-resistant tomato seeds and rotating your crops with maize or cassava helps prevent it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji shikpɔŋ hela ko ni haaa nu aya tso lɛ shishi. Tomato dumɔwui ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: What is eating small ragged holes in my young maize leaves and leaving brown dirt inside the plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli lɛ ni ayeɔ ni ashiɔ muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central shoot of the maize plant. Applying recommended treatments early in the morning or using neem leaf extracts can protect your crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ tsu nii leebi loo okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close to each other to get more crops on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná yibii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting maize too close causes the plants to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in thin, weak stems that produce very small ears or no grain at all.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa amɛtoi bibii waa loo dumɔwui ko kwraa bɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the tall trees from my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei kakadaji fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive direct harsh sunlight because their roots and leaves dry out quickly. Leaving taller trees or planting plantains provides shade, keeping the air cool and moist so the cocoa can establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. tsei kakadaji ni ajieɔ Aloo dumɔwui ni aduɔ koni eye ebua ni eha hulutsoo. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo lɛ afee.

english: Why should I remove some of the young shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie plantain tso lɛ tso lɛ

english: Too many shoots (suckers) steal food, light, and water from the main mother plant, leading to small plantain bunches. Keeping only one or two strong suckers ensures big, heavy bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ (tso lɛ) babaoo juɔ niyenii, la, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Ekɛ mɔ yaa plantain tso bibioo ko mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha efee ŋmeii agbo ni tsii.

english: Is it better for my pepper plants if I water them in the middle of the hot day or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha mi-pepper tso lɛ kɛji miwo lɛ nu yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli loo leebi?

english: It is best to water early in the morning or late afternoon because hot mid-day sun causes water to evaporate quickly before roots can drink it, and wet leaves in hot sun can easily get scorched.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔ lɛ nu leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli. Ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnuɔ. Ni baai ni efɔ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shãa oya.

english: How do I know the exact time my cassava roots are ready to harvest under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, depending on the variety. You can tell it is maturing when the lower leaves start turning yellow and falling off, and the soil around the base starts cracking.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Edamɔ henɔi lɛ anɔ Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baai lɛ miikwɛ̃ kɛ́ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my crops flower well but fail to produce seeds when heavy rain falls during flowering time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ shi enyɛɛɛ ewo dumɔwui beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔi be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain during flowering can wash away pollen or prevent wind and bees from pollinating the flowers. Without successful pollination, the flowers simply drop off without turning into seeds or fruits.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ baanyɛ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ ahe loo etsĩ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛ́ pollination bɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛbatsɔmɔɔ dumɔwui loo aduawai.

english: Why do pests seem to multiply so quickly on my cocoa farm if I leave the surrounding bushes untouched?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayi fa oya yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji miha jwɛi lɛ bɔle Ni Mɔ ko mɔ ko etaaa he?

english: When weeds and surrounding bushes are left unmanaged, they provide a safe breeding ground and shelter for pests, allowing their numbers to grow rapidly before invading your cocoa trees.
ga: Beni akwɛɛɛ jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anɔ lɛ Amɛbaahã tsɛŋemɔ helai aná he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfɔ kɛ amɛhi. Enɛ haa amɛyibɔ ​​yaa hiɛ oya dani amɛtutuaa o-cacao tsei lɛ.

english: What kind of chemical sprays can I use to stop insect pests from damaging my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ manyɛ mikɛkpa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Insecticides such as Akate Master or Confido are effective chemical sprays that target and stop sap-sucking insects like capsids from destroying your cocoa pods and young shoots.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi tamɔ Akate Master loo Confido ji tsofai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ capsids lɛ anɔ ni ekpaa amɛ koni amɛkafite o-cocoa ŋmɔji kɛ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: How do fungicides help protect my cocoa pods from decaying or rotting?
ga: Te tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ abu mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite loo amɛkafite?

english: Fungicides are specialized sprays that prevent fungal spores from growing on your cocoa pods, effectively stopping diseases like Black Pod disease from damaging your crop.
ga: Fungicides ji tsofai krɛdɛɛi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni tsiɔ ŋmeii ahe nibii ni baa o-cocoa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ anaa. Enɛ tsiɔ helai tamɔ black pod hela lɛ naa jogbaŋŋ koni ekafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why is it important to spray chemical treatments regularly rather than waiting until pests appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ tsofai afɔse nɔ daa moŋ fe ni aaamɛ kɛyashi tsɛŋemɔ helai baaje kpo lɛ?

english: Preventative spraying keeps pest numbers low so they cannot establish big populations, whereas waiting allows pests to build up in high numbers and cause severe damage before you can stop them.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni akɛtsiɔ hela naa lɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ayibɔ akafee nɔ ni baa shi. no hewɔ lɛ enyɛɛɛ efee gbɔmɛi babaoo Mɛmɔ, yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ aya hiɛ ni amɛfite nii waa dani obaanyɛ okpa amɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees get more diseases during years when there is heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ náa helai babaoo yɛ afii ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall creates high humidity and damp conditions, which make it much easier for fungal diseases to multiply and spread across your cocoa trees.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi baa. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ ŋmeii helai baagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kookoo tso lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why does having too much shade on my cocoa farm attract more pests and diseases?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hulutsoo babaoo ni mikɛhaa yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbalaa kooloi kɛ helai babaoo kɛbaa lɛ?

english: Deep shade traps moisture and blocks sunlight from drying out the farm, creating a cool, humid environment where pests and fungi thrive and easily infest cocoa trees.
ga: Shade ni mli kwɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni etsĩɔ hulu la naa, ni ehaaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli agbi. Feemɔ shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli. Ewaaa akɛ kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii shwereɔ ni amɛyeɔ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Can pests from neighbouring unkept farms move over to infest my healthy cocoa trees?
ga: Ani tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛ ŋmɔ ko ni bɛŋkɛ ni atsako nɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aba ni amɛbafite mi-cacao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, pests multiply on overgrown or neglected lands and will travel into nearby clean farms looking for fresh cocoa stems, leaves, and pods to feed on.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɔɔ yɛ hei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine loo hei ni aku hiɛ ashwie nɔ lɛ. ni ebaafã gbɛ kɛya ŋmɔji ni mli tse ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli koni eyatao kookoo tsei, baai, kɛ ŋmeii heei ni amɛye.

english: How does trimming excess shade tree branches help reduce pest infestations on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei lɛ ni afolɔ ashwie shi fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi?

english: Trimming shade trees lets in sun and air flow, which dries out excess moisture on cocoa trees and creates unfavorable conditions for pests and fungi to settle.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ agbi. ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni esaaa aba koni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ ŋmeii ahi shi.

english: What causes small dark spots and dying shoots on my young cocoa branches?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii baa? Ni tsei ni miigboi lɛ shwieɔ mi-kookoo niji bibii lɛ anɔ

english: This damage is typically caused by capsids (commonly called Akate), which feed on young cocoa shoots and pods, causing dieback unless controlled with suitable insecticides.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji kapsid lɛ. (ni afɔɔ tsɛmɔ akɛ akaate) ni yeɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ kookoo ŋmeii. kɛ gbele baa ja akɛ tsofai ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ akudɔ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend applying both insecticides and fungicides to cocoa crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nitsumɔhe lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi kɛ ŋmeii fɛɛ atsu nii yɛ kookoo tsei anɔ lɛ?

english: Insecticides eliminate insect pests like capsids, while fungicides protect against fungal infections like Black Pod, giving your cocoa complete protection against both primary threats.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi bibii lɛ gbeɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ capsids, yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi bibii lɛ tsiɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ black pods naa, ni ehaa o-cocoa lɛ buɔ ehe kwraa kɛjɛɔ gbeyeishemɔi titrii enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ahe.

english: Why should I avoid burning the dry grass and clearings on my farm field before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ jwɛi ni ashãa kɛ miŋmɔji amli ŋmɔji ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ ahe dani madu nii lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the rich organic matter and beneficial micro-organisms in the soil that plants need for food. It leaves the soil exposed to hot sun and heavy rains, which wash away nutrients and cause topsoil erosion.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo kɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni tsei taoɔ kɛha niyenii lɛ ahiɛ. Okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ awo hulu ni tsoɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe ni ehaa sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans on my field help my maize crop grow better afterward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni mi-ŋmei lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop dies, that nitrogen stays in the soil as free, natural fertilizer for your next crop of maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii gboi lɛ Nakai nitrogen lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko, ni ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains alongside my newly planted cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantains yɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to strong sunlight and will burn easily. Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that shade the young cocoa plants and keep the surrounding soil cool and moist.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa ni amɛbaashã oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa

english: Why do my vegetable crops droop and wilt in the afternoon heat even when the soil is damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: On very hot days, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can absorb it from the ground. The plant temporary wilts to reduce its surface area and save water, usually standing back up once the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni mli edɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ, baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei baagbi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu nu he. Bei pii lɛ, amɛteɔ shi beni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi sɛɛ.

english: Why should I cut off extra suckers growing at the base of my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: When too many suckers grow around one stem, they fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Leaving only one main stem and one small replacement sucker ensures the plant has enough energy to grow big, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso kome he lɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ shishifã titri kome pɛ kɛ tso lɛ shishifã bibioo kome ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni etsɔ kuu agbo ni tsii.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow instead of healthy green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the primary nutrient needed for green leaf growth. It can also happen when too much water stays around the roots, preventing them from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nu babaoo bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛkaye nii.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they suffer from high temperature stress, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. When stressed, the plant drops flowers to save its remaining energy to stay alive.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛhere hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ koni amɛhi wala mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids, mites, or whiteflies feeding on the underside of leaves, or by a virus transmitted into the plant by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, mites, loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my yam tubers rot in the soil before I get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛnáa hegbɛ ni amɛkpaa nii lɛ?

english: Yam rot underground is caused by excess water sitting in heavy soil, or by tiny soil worms and fungi entering small cuts made by farm tools or soil insects during weeding.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi sweet potato fitemɔ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ sũ mli ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii anɔ. ni yaa ŋmeii bibii ni ŋmɔ mli nibii loo kooloi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa yɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: How do I know when my cassava crop is mature enough to be dug up from the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is typically ready for harvest when the bottom leaves turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare stem, and the ground around the main stem starts to crack due to the swelling tubers underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ashi tso lɛ ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Tso titri lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni yitso lɛ fũuɔ yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and burning during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains or shade trees above them creates a canopy that protects young cocoa leaves from scorching and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he lɛ baa, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the top leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing on the bottom leaves is a sign that the maize plant is starving for nitrogen. The plant steals nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new top leaves, showing that your soil needs more nutrients or fertilizer.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo he miihia oshikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When fields stay flooded with excess water, air gets trapped out of the soil, causing the roots to suffocate and rot from fungal infections.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni ŋmɔji lɛ ná nu babaoo lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ mli.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants without turning into any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too high or when the plant experiences water stress. Without cool conditions or adequate moisture, the flower cannot pollinate itself to form a tomato.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ loo hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Fɔfɔi nyɛŋ afee amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe pollination ni amɛtsɔmɔ tomato.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during strong winds right when the bunch gets big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli beni ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees do not have deep taproots like hardwood trees; their roots spread shallowly near the surface. When a heavy fruit bunch grows, the plant becomes top-heavy and needs a bamboo or wooden stake prop to keep it upright.
ga: Dumɔwui bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ tsei ni wa. Eshishifãi lɛ gbɛ eshwa kɛbɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ mli shwereɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baafee tsiimɔ ni ehe baahia ni akɛ ŋmei loo tsei awo mli koni ekɛha ehi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same spot on my farm every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously in the same place drains the specific food nutrients maize needs from the soil and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the ground season after season.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni abele taoɔ lɛ jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller yields when I plant many seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak plants that produce smaller fruits or grains.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii bibii loo dumɔwui baa.

english: Why does cutting off healthy-looking branches from my fruit tree make it yield bigger fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi tso lɛ niji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ yibii lɛ feɔ agbo lɛ?

english: Pruning removes excess branches that steal water and energy from the tree, allowing sunlight and air to reach the inner canopy and forcing the plant to focus its energy on making larger, healthier fruit.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni juɔ nu kɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tsũ lɛ mligbɛ. ni enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baakwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ.

english: How does planting cowpea or groundnut help improve my soil for the next season?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ aha be ni baa lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts have friendly bacteria living in tiny knots on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and put it directly into the soil, acting like natural, free fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo ni hiɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsofai bɛ mli kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do caterpillars hide deep inside the funnel leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai ni tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The central funnel of a young maize plant is soft, moist, and protected from hot sun and predators, making it the ideal shelter for pests like Fall Armyworm to safely feed on the plant.
ga: Abɛi tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ tsu lɛ mli yɛ bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa efeɔ abobaahe ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ tsei tamɔ Fall Armyworm koni amɛye tsei shweshweeshwe.

english: What does pruning actually mean, and why should I cut healthy-looking branches off my cocoa trees?
ga: Pruning diɛŋtsɛ No hewɔ lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning means cutting away dead, overcrowded, or unwanted branches from your cocoa trees. Removing extra branches lets sunlight and air reach the inside of the tree, which stops diseases like black pod from spreading and encourages the tree to produce more pods.
ga: Tso niji ni egboi lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ tsɔɔ. Niji lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ. loo niji ni ataooo ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ Niji ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa helai tamɔ black pods lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. ni ekanyaa tsei lɛ koni amɛwo ŋmeii babaoo

english: When is the best time of the year for me to trim or prune my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mafolɔ loo mafolɔ cacao tsei?

english: The best time to prune cocoa trees in Ghana is usually right before the main rainy season starts, around February or March. Pruning at this time prepares the tree to send its food and water to new pods once the rains begin.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afolɔ kookoo tsei yɛ Ghana ji dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi. Aaafee February loo March mli lɛ, tso lɛ ni afoɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ baasaa tso lɛ he koni ekɛ niyenii kɛ nu aya ŋmeii heei lɛ amli kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ.

english: How do I know which specific branches I should cut off when pruning my cocoa tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male niji pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ mafo beni mifoɔ mi-kokoo tso lɛ?

english: You should remove dead or dry branches, shoots that grow straight up from the lower trunk (chupons), branches growing inward toward the center, and low branches touching the ground. Leave the healthy main branches that point outward to form an open shape.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie tsei niji ni egboi loo ni egbi lɛ fɛɛ. Tso lɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ (chupons). Niji ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛyaa mli, kɛyaa teŋgbɛ. kɛ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni taa shikpɔŋ lɛ Ha niji titrii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni tsɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ afee mfoniri ni agbele naa.

english: Will cutting branches off my cocoa tree hurt the plant or reduce my harvest?
ga: Ani mi-cocoa tsei lɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ baafite tso lɛ loo ebaaha mi-cocoa tsei lɛ anɔ aba shi?

english: No, it will not hurt the tree if done correctly. In fact, removing weak or extra branches forces the tree to direct all its nutrients toward growing bigger, healthier cocoa pods, which increases your overall harvest.
ga: Dabi, eyeŋ tso lɛ awui kɛji akɛ afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ, niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni fa babaoo lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha tso lɛ akudɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ kɛya kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. Enɛ baaha onitsumɔ lɛ fɛɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What happens to my farm if I never prune my cocoa trees at all?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji mifolɔɔɔ mikoo tsei lɛ kɔkɔɔkɔ?

english: If you do not prune, your cocoa trees will become thick and bushy, blocking out sunlight and trapping humidity. Dark, damp farms attract pests and fungal diseases like black pod, which reduces the number of cocoa pods you can harvest.
ga: Kɛji ofooo Cacao tsei lɛ amli lɛ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsiɔ hulu lɛ naa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Okwaafoi ni mli ewo duŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji, ni no haa ŋmeii ni obaanyɛ okpa lɛ ayibɔ baa shi.

english: Why are some cocoa trees on my farm producing very small pods while others grow big ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi woɔ ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Trees produce small pods when they have too many unnecessary branches competing for food, water, and sunlight. Trimming away useless branches helps the tree supply enough energy to turn flower buds into large, full pods.
ga: Tso lɛ baawo ŋmeii bibii. Kɛ́ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa babaoo ni miitswa akaŋ kɛha niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la lɛ, tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛtsakeɔ ŋmeii lɛ ewoɔ dumɔwui wuji ni eyi obɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees turn yellow and drop off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi oya lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the tree is getting too little sunlight because the upper branches are too dense, or it is infected by diseases. Clearing crowded branches helps air circulate better and allows light to keep the remaining leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miiná hulu la fioo tsɔ ejaakɛ niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ebɔle ehe tsɔ loo hela emɔ tso lɛ. Niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa la lɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa baai ni eshwɛ lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Can I prune my cocoa trees by myself, or do I need specialist officers to do it for me?
ga: Ani bo diɛŋtsɛ obaanyɛ ofolɔ kookoo tsei lɛ, aloo esa akɛ oha mɛi ni he esa waa lɛ afɔ̃ amɛ amɛha bo?

english: You can prune your farm by yourself once you understand the basic steps. Starting with simple steps like removing dead wood and low shoots helps you gain confidence to handle your whole farm independently.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofo ŋmɔ ko mli bo diɛŋtsɛ kɛji onu shishijee gbɛi lɛ ashishi pɛ. Kɛ oje shishi kɛ gbɛi ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ tsei ni egboi kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ajiemɔ lɛ, ebaaha oná hekɛnɔfɔɔ ni okɛ ohe awo oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: What tools should I use to trim my cocoa trees without damaging the trunk?
ga: Mɛɛ dɛŋdade esa akɛ mikɛfo mi-kookoo tso lɛ mli ni mifiteee tso lɛ shishi?

english: It is best to use sharp pruning shears, cutlasses, or pruning saws. Clean, sharp tools cut smoothly without tearing the bark, which prevents wood rot and helps the tree heal quickly.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ tsei, tsɔne kuku, loo tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ atsu nii. Dɛŋdade ni he tse ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ baafolɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbaŋ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni etsa oya.

english: How high off the ground should I trim the lower branches of my cocoa trees?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ kɛyashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: You should trim lower branches so that the lowest hanging pods and leaves are well clear of the ground, ideally around chest height. This stops soil-borne diseases from splashing onto the tree during heavy rains.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni ŋmeii kɛ baai lɛ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔ ni abaanyɛ. Esa akɛ efee nɔ ni miihe ashɛ tsitsi nɔ. Enɛ ji koni helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ akashwie tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: If I plant cocoa trees on my land, how many years can I expect them to keep producing pods for me?
ga: Kɛji midu kookoo tsei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Afii enyiɛ manyɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ kookoo tso lɛ baawo ŋmɔtɔ eha mi?

english: Cocoa trees start producing fruit after 3 to 5 years and can continue yielding healthy pods for 20 to 30 years or more if they are properly pruned, weeded, and protected from diseases like black pod.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 sɛɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛya nɔ amɛwo yibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ afii 20 kɛyashi 30 loo nɔ ni fe nakai kɛji akɛ afolɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ, ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ amɛmli ni atsĩ helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji anaa.

english: Why do people advise me to plant plantains next to my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ emasɛi lɛ? Mi kookoo tso bibioo lɛ

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that shade the young cocoa, keeping the soil moist while giving you food to harvest while waiting for the cocoa to mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa kookoo bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa onáa niyenii be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a primary nutrient plants need to grow. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or organic compost helps the leaves regain their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛná amɛ su ni mli kwɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my tomato plant flowers falling off without turning into tomato fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off mainly due to extreme heat, irregular watering, or poor pollination. Regular watering during dry spells and avoiding excessive nitrogen fertilizer help flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa loo pollination ni ehiii Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa kɛ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Should I sow my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is safer to wait until the rainfall becomes steady. The first rain is often followed by a dry spell that can heat the soil and kill newly germinated seeds before the main rain returns.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ ni baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli adɔ ni egbe dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ titri lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds very close together to fit more crops on my farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the crops compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in tall, thin, weak stalks and smaller corn cobs, reducing your total yield.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa, ni abele ŋmeii lɛ hu daraaa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nɔ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are ready to harvest under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Most cassava varieties mature between 9 to 12 months after planting. You will know it is ready when the ground base around the stem starts to crack and the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo hiɔ shi aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaale akɛ efee klalo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ ebɔle ehe lɛ. Tso lɛ mli tsɔne lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa. ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why does my farm produce less harvest when I plant maize on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmaa lɛ baa shi fioo yɛ be mli ni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil. Rotating crops by planting legumes like beans or cowpeas after maize puts nitrogen back into the soil and keeps it productive.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ ekɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ ewoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa kɛ yibiiwoo.

english: Why do I see small ragged holes in my maize leaves and sticky waste inside the central whorl?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ gunk ni shwieɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ? yɛ fã ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds on the young growing tip of the maize plant. Spraying approved biopesticides or applying neem extract early in the morning or late evening helps control them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei ni yeɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ loo okɛ neem mli nu tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crop seedlings grow slowly and look weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔwui lɛ daraa blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants that steal soil nutrients, water, and sunlight faster than your crops can. Clearing weeds during the first 3 to 4 weeks after planting allows your seedlings to grow strong without competition.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli oya fe otsei lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 3 kɛyashi 4 lɛ mli yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa odumɔwui lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains rot or turn moldy so quickly when I store them in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ loo ehiɛɔ oya kɛji mikɛwo kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Maize grains rot because they still contain high moisture when bagged too soon. Freshly harvested maize continues to 'breathe' and generate heat, creating a damp environment where mold grows. Thoroughly sun-drying the grains until they are hard and dry before bagging prevents this spoilage.
ga: Abɛi mli ŋmeii fiteɔ ejaakɛ amɛhiɛɔ nu babaoo mli kɛ́ akɛwo kotoku mli oya tsɔ. Abele ni akpa ehee lɛ yaa nɔ ‘emuɔ’ ni ekɛ dɔlɛ baa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ daa yɛ mli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmaa lɛ aahu kɛyashi ebaawa ni egbi dani akɛwo kotoku mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting shoots while sitting in my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ be mli ni mita mi shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that naturally break dormancy after a few months in storage. When they feel air and warmth, they start growing new shoots, which draws energy from the yam itself. Storing yams in a cool, well-ventilated barn and gently rubbing off early sprouts helps maintain their weight and quality.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni baafo shihilɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji akɛ akɛto nyɔji fioo komɛi. Beni amɛnuɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ latsaa he lɛ Amɛbɔi ŋmeii heei hu ŋmɔmɔ. ni jieɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mli Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmei lɛ ato ŋmei ŋtayaa ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli ni okɛ ŋmei lɛ afɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ blɛoo. Ebaaye ebua ni eha shwiili lɛ mli tsiimɔ kɛ kpakpafeemɔ ahi shi.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes turn soft and decay so fast before I can get them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya dani mikɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes continue to ripen and release gas after being picked. If they are harvested when overly ripe or piled too high in rough wooden crates, the pressure bruises the fruit, allowing heat and rot-causing bacteria to spread rapidly.
ga: Tomato yaa nɔ ekwɛ̃ɔ ni ejieɔ gas kpo beni ajie lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ akpa beni ekwɛ̃ tsɔ loo ato he ko ni nɔ kwɔ tsɔ yɛ adekai ni mli ewo muji amli. Nɔnyɛɛ lɛ baafite aduawai lɛ. Enɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and dropping off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during dry spells as a survival mechanism to save water. When water is scarce, the plant reduces the number of leaves it has to feed, but it will grow fresh green leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehiɔ shi koni ekɛbu nu he. Beni nu faaa Tso lɛ baaha baai ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ aba shi. Shi baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni kpɛɔ lɛ baahi shi kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field without direct shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-koko tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. They need living shade—like plantain or banana trees—to shield them from heat and hold moisture around their young roots until they are mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka, tamɔ plantains loo banana tsei. Enɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ latsaa he, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ hiɔ shi. Eshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ aahu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why are my pepper plants staying very short and refusing to grow taller even when I give them water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɔɔ kuku nɛkɛ ni ekpooɔ akɛ ebaatsɔ ŋwɛi beni mikɛ nu wo enɔ po lɛ?

english: Stunted pepper plants usually mean the soil is too hard for the roots to spread, or the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen. Loosening the soil around the plant base and adding well-rotted animal manure gives roots room and nourishment to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tsei ni afee amɛ bibii lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. aloo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ, ni akɛ kooloo ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aná hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my tomato plants shed their flowers without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when temperatures get too high or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Extreme heat stress prevents proper pollination, so the plant drops the unpollinated flower to save energy.
