ga: Tomatoi shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baaha pollination ni esaaa aba. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shiiɔ fɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my sweet orange fruits fall off the tree before they are fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet oranges lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛmiikwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ?

english: Premature fruit drop in oranges is often caused by fruit fly attacks or uneven water supply. Fruit flies lay eggs inside the skin, causing the tissue inside to decay, which forces the tree to drop the damaged fruit early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ citrus aduawai ni fiteɔ oya lɛ baa ji aduawai amli ŋmeii ni tutuaa amɛ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa. Yibii amli ŋmeii woɔ amɛwui yɛ hewolo lɛ mli. Ehaa fãji ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ yibii ni efite lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why did my groundnut seeds fail to sprout after I buried them deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ beni mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Groundnut seeds need air, warmth, and light moisture near the surface to germinate. Burial too deep smothers the seed because it runs out of stored energy before the shoot can reach the sunlight.
ga: Peanut dumɔwui hia kɔɔyɔɔ, dɔlɛ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo ni bɛŋkɛ ŋwɛi koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ afu dumɔwui lɛ amli tsɔ lɛ, ebaafite dumɔwui lɛ ejaakɛ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ sɛɛ foɔ dani ŋmeii lɛ shɛɔ hulu la lɛ he.

english: Why are caterpillars eating the foliage of my young maize crop so fast right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yeɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ oya nɛkɛ beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ lɛ?

english: Warm, rainy conditions cause insect eggs (like Fall Armyworm) hidden in the soil or weeds to hatch rapidly. The hungry young caterpillars target tender maize leaves because they are soft and full of water and nutrients.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ haa kooloi bibii (tamɔ Fall Armyworm) ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ loo jwɛi amli lɛ afɔ̃ɔ oya. Hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ kɛ amɛhiɛ fɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ anɔ ejaakɛ amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai eyi mli obɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize turn yellow and die so quickly after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: This rapid sickness is often caused by tiny plant germs called pathogens, like fungi or bacteria. They multiply very fast in warm, wet weather and attack the plant's food supply, causing leaf tissues to dry up quickly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei amli helai bibii ni gbeɔ helai oya nɛɛ kɛbaa. Atsɛɔ enɛɛmɛi akɛ muawai, tamɔ ŋmei loo muawai. Amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa oya waa yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. ni amɛtutuaa tsei aniyenii jɛɛhei Ehaa baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya

english: What causes black spots to appear on my pepper leaves so suddenly?
ga: Mɛni miiha ŋmeii diji miije kpo trukaa yɛ mi-pepper baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Black spots are usually caused by microscopic fungal pathogens that land on the plant tissue. When the air is humid, these germs multiply and damage the plant's leaf tissue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni kpɛtɛɔ tso fãji ahe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji baa. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ Nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ faa babaoo ni amɛfiteɔ tso lɛ baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ.

english: Why do some insects make my crop plants look sick even if they do not chew the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi komɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni hela mɔ amɛ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛyeee baai lɛ moŋ?

english: Insects often act as carriers for plant pathogens. When they bite the plant to drink sap, they transfer tiny disease germs directly into the plant's tissue, making the whole crop sick.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tsuɔ nii akɛ mɛi ni kɛ tsei amli helai baa. Kɛ amɛye tsei koni amɛnu nu lɛ Amɛkɛ helai bibii woɔ tsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, hela mɔɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my crop stems rot right where they touch the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ fiteɔ kɛji amɛta shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Soil contains natural microscopic pathogens. When the ground stays very wet, these soil germs attack the delicate stem tissue at ground level and block water from reaching the rest of the plant.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii bibii ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa Nɛkɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nɛɛ tutuaa tso lɛ mli fãji ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni etsĩɔ nu naa koni ekashɛ tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do healthy, well-fed crops survive plant sickness better than weak crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni ayeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yeɔ tsei ahe helai jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni baanyɛ atswa amɛ oya lɛ?

english: Just like healthy human bodies fight off illness easily, crops with good soil nutrients build natural strength that helps their tissues resist and slow down the spread of disease pathogens.
ga: Taakɛ adesa gbɔmɔtso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛ helai wuɔ oya lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni sũ mli nibii kpakpai yɔɔ mli lɛ maa adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni yeɔ ebuaa fãji lɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ni amɛhaa amɛgbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: How can I stop a sickness from spreading from one sick plant to the rest of my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa hela ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome ni hela mɔ lɛ kɛyaa miŋmɔ lɛ fã kroko lɛ mli?

english: You should carefully cut off damaged plant parts or remove the sick plant entirely and burn or bury it. This destroys the pathogens in the diseased tissue before wind or water carries them to healthy plants.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ fãi srɔtoi. ni ajie tsei ni efite lɛ jogbaŋŋ Aloo ajie tsei fɛɛ ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni ashã loo afu amɛ. Enɛ kpataa helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ahiɛ dani kɔɔyɔɔ loo nu baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Can plant sickness stay in my soil even after I harvest all my crops?
ga: Ani tsei ahe helai baakã he ahi mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ po sɛɛ?

english: Yes, many plant pathogens can live in the soil or inside leftover plant tissue during the dry season, waiting to infect new crops when you plant again.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei amli helai babaoo baanyɛ ahi sũ lɛ mli loo tsei amli fãji ni eshwɛ lɛ amli yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. koni omɛ ni hela aba tsei heei anɔ beni oduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ

english: Is it true that watering my crops late in the evening can cause them to get sick?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ kɛ́ afɔ tsei anɔ nu gbɛkɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha amɛná hela?

english: Yes, leaving water on leaves overnight creates ideal wet conditions for fungal pathogens to grow quickly and invade the plant tissue before the morning sun dries them.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni ashiɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni mli edɔ baa koni ŋmeii lɛ adara oya. ni etutuaa tsei ahe fãji dani leebi hulu lɛ haa amɛgbiɔ.

english: If my cassava roots show signs of rotting tissue, is it safe for my family to eat them?
ga: Kɛji mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ yɛ fãji ni fiteɔ lɛ Ani miweku lɛ baanyɛ aye?

english: It is not safe. Some plant rots produce dangerous toxins in the tissue that can make humans sick, so rotten or moldy crop parts should never be eaten.
ga: Ebɛ shweshweeshwe. Tsei komɛi ni egboi lɛ jieɔ tsofai fɔji ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ amɛfãji amli ni baanyɛ aha adesai aná hela. No hewɔ lɛ, esaaa akɛ ayeɔ tso lɛ fãi ni egbo loo etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How do I know if my crop is wilting from heat or if it is sick from a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigbo yɛ latsaa lɛ hewɔ loo hela miipiŋ amɛ?

english: Heat wilting usually recovers in the cool evening when the plant regains strength. If the wilting is caused by a pathogen destroying the inner tissue, the plant will remain dry and wilted even at night.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo lɛ baa shi yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli beni tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ helai ni fiteɔ fãji ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa Gbi gbɛkɛ po lɛ, tsei lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagbi.

english: Why do different rice seeds have specific names like Agra or Savanna instead of just being called rice?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ŋmãa henɔ fɛɛ henɔ yɛ gbɛi krɛdɛɛ ko tamɔ Agra loo Savannah lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsɛ lɛ ŋmãa kɛkɛ

english: Different named varieties are bred with distinct traits—such as tolerance to drought, resistance to local pests, or specific cooking qualities—so knowing the name helps you select the exact seed suited to your farm's conditions.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi ni yɔɔ gbɛi srɔtoi lɛ kɛ sui srɔtoi, tamɔ hɔmɔ ni amɛŋmɛɔ amɛtsui shi. shitee-kɛ-woo ni akɛteɔ shi awoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ; loo nibii pɔtɛɛ ni akɛhooɔ nii No hewɔ lɛ, gbɛi lɛ ni ooole lɛ baaye abua bo ni ohala dumɔwui ni sa kɛha shihilɛ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Can I just buy grain from the local food market and plant it on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mahe ŋmaa kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ mli niyenii jarayelihe lɛ ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Grain sold for eating is often not treated or certified for planting, which leads to low germination rates, uneven growth, and high susceptibility to diseases compared to certified planting seeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, atsuuu dumɔwui ni ahɔ̃ɔ koni aye lɛ ahe nii loo ahaaa amɛ odaseyeli akɛ abaanyɛ adu. ni haa shweremɔ ni baa shi lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ekɛ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know which crop variety is best suited for my land before I buy seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei srɔtoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ dani mahe dumɔwui?

english: You should consider your soil type, water availability, and local climate, then check seed labels or ask extension officers to match those conditions with the right variety's characteristics.
ga: Esa akɛ osusu shikpɔŋ henɔ ni yɔɔ lɛ he. Nu ni yɔɔ kɛ maŋ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi No sɛɛ lɛ kwɛmɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe wolo lɛ loo bi sɛɛgbɛtsɔɔmɔ he nitsulɔ ko ni ekɛ nakai shihilɛi lɛ kɛ sui srɔtoi ni sa lɛ ato he.

english: Why does one crop variety grow well in dry northern regions while another fails completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome shwereɔ yɛ kooyigbɛ hei ni nu bɛ lɛ, yɛ be mli ni ekroko hu shwereɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: Certain varieties are naturally developed to tolerate dry spells and mature quickly with minimal water, whereas other varieties require constant moisture and longer rainy seasons to produce yield.
ga: Afee tsei srɔtoi komɛi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ hɔmɔ naa ni amɛdara oya kɛ nu fioo pɛ. yɛ be mli ni henɔi krokomɛi Ehe miihia ni hulutsoo be aba daa kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ koni ewo yibii.

english: Why do some types of crops mature faster than others planted at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi daa oya fe ekrokomɛi ni daa yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Varieties have different genetic lifecycles; early-maturing types are designed to produce harvest quickly to escape dry seasons, while late-maturing types use extra time to build up higher yield if water is abundant.
ga: Henɔi lɛ yɛ wala yibii sɔrɔtoi. Afee tsei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ koni akpa oya koni hulutsoo be lɛ akashɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ sɛɛ mli lɛ baahe be kroko koni amɛwo yibii babaoo kɛji amɛyɛ nu babaoo.

english: Why did my crop produce low yield even though I used the same fertilizer as my neighbor?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii kpakpai eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ?

english: Different varieties respond differently to nutrients; if your seed variety is not suited to your soil type or environment, adding fertilizer alone cannot make it perform beyond its genetic potential.
ga: Henɔi srɔtoi lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he. Kɛji odumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ esaaa oshikpɔŋ henɔ loo he ni oyɔɔ lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ fɔmɔ kotoku mli lɛ pɛ nyɛŋ aha etsu nii fe bɔ ni eyɔɔ yɛ fɔmɔ nii amli lɛ.

english: Will mixing two different crop varieties together in the same field give me a bigger harvest?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ futu mli yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ, ebaaha maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: Mixing varieties leads to uneven growth, staggered flowering, and unequal maturity times, making field maintenance, pest control, and harvesting very difficult and reducing overall grain quality.
ga: Fɔmɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ kɛ dalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee baa. fɔfɔi ni shwereɔ kɛ dalɛ be lɛ jeee ekome Ha ŋmɔ mli saamɔ afee tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ afee nɔ ni wa ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ ahilɛ-kɛhamɔ baa shi.

english: Why are certified seeds from agricultural stores more expensive than seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni jɛ okwaayeli shwapoi amli lɛ jara wa fe dumɔwui ni mibua naa kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds undergo strict breeding and quality controls to guarantee high purity, disease resistance, and strong germination, whereas saved seeds lose their yield strength and purity over seasons.
ga: Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ tsɔɔ fɔmɔ mli waa kɛ bɔ ni amɛhi ha lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ mli koni amɛná hetsemɔ ni nɔ kwɔ, helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe kɛ shweremɔ ni mli wa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato lɛ fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ kɛ amɛhetsemɔ yɛ be lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if a crop variety will survive common field pests and diseases in my area?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso henɔ ko baahi shi yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ amli?

english: Certified seed varieties are tested in field trials before release, and their resistance traits to specific diseases or pests are documented on their official packaging and recommended by agricultural officers.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni ana he odaseyeli lɛ akwɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli kaa mli dani ajieɔ lɛ kpo. kɛ helai loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe sui pɔtɛɛ komɛi aŋmalaa awoɔ nibii ni amralo lɛ woɔ mli lɛ anɔ, ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ jieɔ he ŋaa.

english: Does the specific variety of crop I plant affect how easily I can sell it after harvest?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni miduɔ lɛ saa bɔ ni efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ahɔ̃ɔ amɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ he?

english: Yes, market buyers and consumers prefer specific grain sizes, aromas, and cooking qualities, so planting popular, high-demand varieties ensures faster sales and better market prices.
ga: Hɛɛ, jara nɔ jarayelɔi kɛ jarayelɔi sumɔɔ ŋmaa dalɛ pɔtɛɛ, naa ŋɔɔ, kɛ nihoomɔ sui. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu tsei srɔtoi ni ehe gbɛi ni mɛi biɔ amɛ waa lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ oya ni amɛná jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is my farm soil drying up, cracking, and turning as hard as stone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli egbi, egbɛ eshwa, ni ewa tamɔ tɛ lɛ?

english: Soil becomes very hard and cracked when it loses organic matter and natural moisture. This often happens when excessive agrochemicals destroy the soil's natural structure over time, leaving it tightly packed.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ adebɔɔ mli nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fite. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ okwaayeli mli lɛ fite bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why does fertilizer just sit on top of my soil when I apply it instead of sinking in?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii hiɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛfata he moŋ fe ni eeebote mli lɛ?

english: When farm soil becomes damaged and hardens into a tight crust, water and liquid nutrients cannot pass through it. The fertilizer remains trapped on the surface and gets washed away by rain instead of reaching the crop roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ efite ni efee ŋmɔtɔ ni wa Nu kɛ niyenii ni mli ewo muji nyɛŋ atsɔ mli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nugbɔ shwieɔ lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeshɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe.

english: Can using too many chemical fertilizers actually harm my land?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baaye mishikpɔŋ lɛ awui diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, putting excessive chemical fertilizers into the ground damages beneficial soil life and organic matter. Over time, this causes the soil to harden, crack, and lose its ability to absorb plant nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ sũ mli wala ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa, egbɛɔ ni enyɛŋ eŋɔ niyenii ni jɛɔ tsei amli lɛ dɔŋŋ.

english: Why are my crops failing to grow well even though I keep adding fertilizer to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: If past chemical overuse has hardened your soil, the ground acts like a barrier. Adding more fertilizer will not help because the nutrients cannot penetrate the hard surface to reach the roots.
ga: Kɛji tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ha oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ gbɛtsii nii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata he lɛ, eyeee ebuaaa ejaakɛ niyenii mli nibii lɛ nyɛŋ abote shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ ni eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: What makes farm soil become so tough that a cutlass cannot easily dig into it?
ga: Mɛni ha sũ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ batsɔ sũ aahu akɛ dade nyɛɛɛ atsɔ mli mlɛo?

english: Soil loses its soft texture when continuous heavy chemical use strips away organic content. Without organic material to keep the earth loose, the soil compacts heavily and bakes hard under the sun.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛji akɛ tsofai ni tsii ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ jieɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kɛji akɛ nɔ ko bɛ ni baaye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaafee shiŋŋ yɛ hulu lɛ shishi.

english: How do chemical sprays affect the way rainwater moves through my farm ground?
ga: Te tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ saa nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Overusing agricultural chemicals breaks down soil particles into a dense layer. This stops rainwater from soaking deep into the ground, causing water runoff on top and deep cracks as the surface dries out.
ga: Okwaayeli mli tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa sũ mli nibii bibii lɛ fãa kɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli ewo wu. Enɛ baatsi nugbɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ŋmeii ni mli kwɔlɔ baa beni ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ lɛ.

english: Why does rainwater pool on top of my field instead of soaking down to my crop roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ buaa ehe naa yɛ ŋmɔji lɛ amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Excessive chemical inputs create a hard top crust on your land. This crust blocks both rainwater and added plant food from penetrating down into the root zone where your crops need them.
ga: Tsofai babaoo baaha shikpɔŋ ni wa aba oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ ŋshɔŋloo nɛɛ tsiɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ tsei aniyenii fɛɛ naa koni amɛkabote shishifãi lɛ amli he ni otsei lɛ he hiaa yɛ lɛ.

english: Is it possible that using too much weedicide or crop medicine is worsening my soil?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi loo tsei ahe tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ miiha mishikpɔŋ lɛ miifite?

english: Yes, applying more chemicals than recommended hurts the living earth. It breaks down the natural bonds in the soil, leading to severe soil hardening, cracking, and poor plant feeding.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe bɔ ni ajieɔ yi lɛ yeɔ shibɔlemɔ ŋulami ni hiɛ ka lɛ awui. Efoɔ adebɔɔ mli tsakpaai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa, egbɛɔ ni ehaaa tsei lɛ niyenii kpakpa.

english: Why does my soil crack into big pieces during dry weather more than it used to?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli fãa kɛfeɔ fãi wuji yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: Land that has been heavily treated with chemicals loses its capacity to retain organic moisture. When dry weather arrives, this depleted soil shrinks rapidly, hardens, and forms deep cracks.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛ tsofai etsu he nii waa lɛ nyɛɛɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ mli dɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ ba Shikpɔŋ ni efite nɛɛ shwieɔ shi oya, ewaa, ni ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ baa.

english: How can I help fertilizer soak deeper into my hard, cracked ground to feed my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua ni ŋmɔshi nibii abote mihei ni wa ni egbɛ eshwa lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ niyenii?

english: To get nutrients down to the roots, you must soften the soil by reducing heavy chemical use and adding organic matter like animal manure or compost, which restores the soil's ability to absorb food and water.
ga: Bɔni afee ni niyenii mli hewalɛ aya shishifãi lɛ ahe Ehe miihia ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee mlɛo kɛtsɔ tsofai ni tsii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ eŋɔɔ niyenii kɛ nu ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does rainwater sit on top of my farmland for days instead of sinking into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Heavy clay soil has very tiny, tightly packed particles that block water from draining quickly. While this helps hold moisture for a long time during dry spells, standing water can choke plant roots if it cannot escape.
ga: Shikpɔji ni akɛ shikpɔŋ sũ fee ni tsii lɛ yɛ nibii bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe ni tsiɔ nu naa koni ekaho oya. Eyɛ mli akɛ enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli moŋ. Shi nu ni damɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ kɛji amɛnyɛŋ amɛjo foi.

english: Why is the ground on my farm so tough and hard to dig during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa ni ewa akɛ aaafo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Soil with high clay content bakes hard like a brick when exposed to strong sun and drought. Mixing organic matter like livestock manure or dead leaves into the soil helps loosen it up and keeps it workable.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni shikpɔŋ sũ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ baashã waa tamɔ brikii kɛji akɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ shɛ enɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ kooloi aŋmei loo baai ni egboi futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua ni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava leaves are turning yellow from too much water or dry weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ nu babaoo loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli?

english: When crops get too much standing water, their leaves turn yellow and feel soft or soggy. When crops lack water, the leaves turn yellow, become dry and crisp, and curl inward to protect themselves from the heat.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ Baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛnu he akɛ amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ loo amɛhe ejɔ. Kɛ nu bɛ tsei lɛ Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛgbiɔ ni amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa mli koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he.

english: Why do my traditional local maize seeds take much longer to mature than the improved seeds from the agricultural office?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ fe dumɔwui ni atsake ni jɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ?

english: Local seeds are naturally slow-growing varieties adapted to survive tough conditions over a long period, while improved hybrid seeds are bred specifically to grow fast and mature early before dry weather sets in.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ ji dumɔwui srɔtoi ni daa blɛoo ni amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli be kakadaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛshwere oya dani kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ aba.

english: Are my local seed varieties tougher against harsh weather than the high-yielding seeds?
ga: Ani dumɔwui srɔtoi ni yɔɔ mimaŋ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ amɛtsui shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli fe dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Local varieties are often very tough against local pests and sudden droughts because they have adapted over many years, but they usually yield less harvest compared to improved varieties that require good soil care.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akutsoŋbii srɔtoi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ akutseiaŋ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ. Yɛ tsakemɔi ni afee afii babaoo lɛ hewɔ lɛ Shi amɛfɔɔ yibiiwoo fioo kɛ akɛtoɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ ni biɔ shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my local crop varieties require continuous weeding and physical labor all through the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni miyɔɔ mli lɛ biɔ ni ajie jwɛi kɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ nitsumɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Because traditional varieties grow slowly, they take longer to form a full canopy of leaves, leaving the surrounding ground exposed to sunlight which allows weeds to keep sprouting for months.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishijee tso lɛ daa fiofio. No hewɔ lɛ, eheɔ be babaoo dani anyɛɔ afee ŋmeii ni akɛ baai fee. Okɛ he ni ebɔle ohe lɛ awo hulu la mli, ni no haa jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ nyɔji babaoo.

english: Why do some of my crops survive a dry spell while others wilt and die right away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi hiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Crops with long taproots can reach deep underground to pull up hidden water when the top layer dries out, while surface-rooted crops rely entirely on topsoil moisture and dry up fast.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi kakadaŋŋ abaanyɛ aya shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ koni amɛyajie nu ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ kɛji ŋwɛi fã lɛ egbi. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni shishifãi yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ kwraa, ni amɛgbiɔ oya.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their small flowers when the rains stop unexpectedly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Beni nugbɔ lɛ kpaɔ trukaa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers as a survival defense when water is scarce. By discarding young flowers, the tree saves its remaining energy and moisture to keep its main stem and roots alive.
ga: Cacao tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi kɛ́ nu faaa. Fɔfɔi bibii ni ashɛrɛɔ ashwieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu ni eshwɛ lɛ toɔ koni ekɛkwɛ tso lɛ shishifãi titri lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my improved crop varieties require more manure and fertilizer than my local crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei srɔtoi ni mifee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ biɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fe mimaŋ tsei lɛ?

english: Improved varieties are heavy feeders because they grow rapidly and produce much larger fruits or grains, meaning they draw nutrients out of the soil far faster than slow-growing local varieties.
ga: Henɔi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji niyenii ni tsii ejaakɛ amɛdaraa oya ni amɛwoɔ aduawai loo dumɔwui wuji babaoo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛjieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni daraa blɛoo lɛ.

english: Why is it so much harder to clear and prepare land that has been left fallow for years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewaa kwraa akɛ abaajie shikpɔŋ ni ashi afii babaoo lɛ nɔ ni asaa he lɛ?

english: Land left wild for years develops a dense, tough network of wild roots and hard-packed soil. Although it takes heavy physical labor to clear, this land is usually rich in buried organic nutrients for your crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ashi lɛ akɛ adebɔɔ nɔ afii babaoo lɛ ebɔi shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋa nɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ehe nitsumɔ ni wa dani anyɛ ajie jɛmɛ moŋ, shi bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ eyi kɛ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni afu kɛha onibii.

english: Why does water stay pooled on my farmland for days after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu hiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Water pools when the soil has poor drainage, heavy clay content, or low spots on the field. Standing water suffocates crop roots by blocking oxygen, which leads to root rot and poor plant growth.
ga: Pond be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nu kpakpa Shikpɔŋ ni tsii yɛ. aloo he ko ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ tsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni tsei lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: What should I do if my farm land holds too much water and damages my crops?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji nu babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni efite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: You can dig simple drainage channels around your field or plant your crops on raised mounds and ridges. This helps excess water flow away from crop roots during heavy rains.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ gbɛ yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ. ŋmɔji ahe loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ kɛ ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why is it important to level my farm field before sowing my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Leveling your field prevents water from collecting in deep spots and causing waterlogging, ensuring rainfall spreads evenly to all your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ afee ŋmɔji lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaha nu akabua ehe naa yɛ hei ni mli kwɔ ni ekɛ nu afua aba. Enɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ jaa onibii fɛɛ amli pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: How does removing old tree stumps and roots from my field help my new crops?
ga: Te ŋmeii kɛ shishifãi momoi ni mijieɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Removing stumps clears the ground so roots can spread freely, makes field preparation easier, and eliminates breeding grounds for underground pests like termites and fungus.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Ehaa jɛmɛ he saamɔ feɔ mlɛo. kɛ hei ni shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ termites kɛ fungi fɔɔ yɛ lɛ ajiemɔ.

english: How does clearing all weeds completely before planting help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni mijieɔ dani miduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Clearing weeds completely removes competition for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, allowing young crops to establish strong roots without being choked.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ jieɔ akaŋshii ni akɛtaoɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kwraa. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei bibii ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa, ni nɔ ko tsiii amɛ gbɛ.

english: Why do stubborn bush weeds keep coming back even after I cut them down with a cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yitsoŋ wa lɛ yaa nɔ amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa beni mikɛ tsɔne shwieɔ amɛ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Many wild weeds have deep root systems or underground tubers that sprout back if only the tops are cut. Removing the entire root system from the soil prevents them from growing back.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi babaoo yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ kɛji akɛ afo amɛyiteŋ pɛ. Kɛ́ ajie shishifãi lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi heei baakwɛ̃.

english: What happens to my food crops if I plant them on uncleared or partially cleared land?
ga: Mɛni baa miniyenii tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ajieee nɔ ko nɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni ajie nɔ ko nɔ ko yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting on uncleared land forces your crops to fight wild bushes for sunlight and soil nutrients, resulting in weak stems, yellow leaves, and very low yield.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni ooodu lɛ baaha onibii lɛ kɛ koo mli tsei lɛ awuu koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi waa.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow when there is standing water on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni nu ni damɔ shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that crop roots are drowning from excess water and cannot absorb essential nitrogen and nutrients from the soil.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ebote nu shishi tsɔ. ni enyɛɛɛ ejie nitrogen kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Why is making mounds or ridges better for crops like cassava and yams during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni afeɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Mounds and ridges raise the tubers above flooded soil, keeping the root area loose and well-aerated so the tubers can expand without rotting in standing water.
ga: Gɔji kɛ ŋshɔkei wo amɛyitsei anɔ kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ. Ha shishifã lɛ he lɛ afee mlɛo ni kɔɔyɔɔ hu abote mli jogbaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ alɛɛ mli ni amɛkafite yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if my soil is properly prepared and ready for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ asaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ adu nii?

english: Properly prepared soil is free of major weeds and stumps, loose enough for roots to penetrate easily, and graded so rain water drains gently without washing away topsoil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni asaa he jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ jwɛi wuji kɛ ŋmeii. Ehe ejɔ bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi lɛ abote mli mlɛo. ni okɛfee lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ bɔni afee ni nugbɔ nu lɛ atsɔ mli blɛoo ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ efɔɔɔ.

english: If I spray chemical medicine on my crops today, why do the pests come back after a few weeks?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ tsofai shwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ ŋmɛnɛ Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Most chemical sprays only kill the adult insects present during spraying. They do not destroy insect eggs hidden under leaves or in the soil, which hatch later and require proper timing to control.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo baagbe kooloi bibii ni eda ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ pɛ. Efiteee kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ baai ashishi loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ awui. Amɛfɔɔ sɛɛ mli ni ebiɔ be dani anyɛ akudɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it safe for me to mix two different plant medicines together to save time when spraying my crops?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsei ahe tsofai enyɔ baafutu koni mikɛ be ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ akafite?

english: No, mixing different chemicals without proper guidance can cause a chemical reaction that damages your crops, destroys the effectiveness of the medicine, or creates harmful fumes.
ga: Dabi, tsofai srɔtoi ni okɛfutuɔ ni gbɛtsɔɔmɔ ni sa bɛ he lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofai ni fiteɔ onibii lɛ aba. fiteɔ bɔ ni tsofa lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ehaa lɛ loo ehaa lasu ni yɔɔ oshara baa.

english: Why do my cocoa pod husks turn black and dry up on the trees before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, heavily shaded farms. Pruning excess tree branches to let in sunlight and air helps prevent it.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ebu amɛhe.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing very tall with thick green leaves, but producing very few flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ daraa babaoo ni amɛyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi ani ehaa fɔfɔi fioo ko pɛ?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, they focus all their energy on growing stems and leaves instead of flowering and producing fruit.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ fɔɔ amɛshishifãi kɛ baai ni miida lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii lɛ

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up into tight cups during the sunny afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ kɔɔpoi ni mli wa yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips sucking sap from the leaves, or by the plant trying to protect itself from extreme heat and water loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during rainstorms even when the soil is soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ bɔdɔɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can be destroyed by microscopic soil pests called nematodes or root rot, leaving the heavy plant without a strong anchor in wet weather.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei ni tsii lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn pale yellow when the plant lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or when drought prevents the roots from drawing up food from the soil.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, loo kɛji hɔmɔ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbala niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I avoid applying fertilizer when the farm soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Crop roots cannot drink dry fertilizer. Fertilizer needs water to dissolve into the soil, and applying it dry can burn and damage the roots of your crops.
ga: Tso shishifãi nyɛŋ anu ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi. Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii koni egbi lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ shãa aba ni efite tsei lɛ ashishifãi.

english: How can I tell if my soil is tired and needs extra food or rest before planting again?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ etɔ ni ehe miihia ni aha lɛ niyenii loo hejɔɔmɔ kroko dani madu ekoŋŋ?

english: Tired soil produces slow-growing crops with thin stems, yellowing leaves, and small yields, even when you get good rainfall.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa blɛoo ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yɛ mlɛo, amɛbaai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ, ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Kɛji akɛ oyɛ nugbɔ kpakpa po

english: Why is it better to plant my crops in straight rows instead of scattering seeds everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni aaagbɛ dumɔwui ashwã he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Planting in rows gives each crop equal space, sunlight, and soil nutrients, while making weeding, fertilizing, and harvesting much easier for you.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I clear all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense heat. They need shade trees or plantains grown next to them to act as living umbrellas, protecting the leaves from scorching and keeping the soil moist while their roots develop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiisumɔ ni adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo plantains yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni etsu nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Ebuɔ baai ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants full of holes with tiny caterpillars hiding inside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai eyi kɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni akɛtee mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that eats the growing leaves of young maize. Detecting them early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract helps protect the crop before the heart of the plant is destroyed.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni yeɔ ŋmei bibii ni miida lɛ ahe baai lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ayɔse amɛ mra Ni akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe dani tso lɛ tsui lɛ afite.

english: Why do my cassava leaves look crumpled with yellow spots, and why are the roots underneath so small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekpɔtɔ lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ daraaa kwraa lɛ?

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by small whiteflies or by planting stems from infected plants. Using disease-resistant cassava cuttings recommended by extension officers prevents this disease and produces large tubers.
ga: Enɛ ji cassava mosaic hela, ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ amli ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava shishifãi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ hela nɛɛ naa ni ebaaha ŋmeii wuji aba.

english: When is the right time for me to put fertilizer on my maize farm so that I do not waste my money?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ awo ŋmãa ŋmɔ mli ŋmãa koni akafite shika?

english: The best practice is to apply NPK fertilizer 2 to 3 weeks after planting when the seedlings have strong roots, followed by Urea or SOA 5 to 6 weeks after planting when the stalks grow rapidly toward flowering.
ga: Nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni akɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ otsii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ sɛɛ beni adu dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi ni wa. Nyiɛmɔ urea loo SOA sɛɛ otsii 5 kɛyashi 6 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ beni ŋmeii lɛ daraa oya kɛyashiɔ fɔfɔi.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too high, when water is irregular, or when the plant lacks calcium and nitrogen. Regular watering and using balanced compost or fertilizers help the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ calcium kɛ nitrogen Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines with tall sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu sweet potato wain tsei ni tsei kakadaji yɔɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Staking lifts yam leaves into the sunlight so they can make more food for the plant, which makes the tubers beneath the ground grow much larger while protecting the leaves from soil diseases.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli koni amɛfee niyenii babaoo amɛha tso lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ daraa babaoo, ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ hu ahe.

english: How can I tell if my crops are getting too much water during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Excess water chokes the plant roots by removing air from the soil, causing the lower leaves to turn pale yellow, drop off, or soft-rot near the soil surface.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ tsiɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi anaa kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛgbeeɔ shi, loo amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and remaining small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the sap from young leaves, or a virus spread by aphids. Controlling these insects early prevents the leaves from twisting and stunting the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ baa. loo helai ni aphids gbɛɔ eshwaa Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ tso lɛ ni amɛkafee shwilafo.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to produce bunches when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ be babaoo dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii kɛji midu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Planting plantains too close causes them to fight for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, leading to slender stems and tiny bunches. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to absorb what it needs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha amɛye hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaaŋɔ nɔ ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ.

english: Is it helpful for my farm if I plant cowpeas or groundnuts between my rows of maize?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ baaba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, leguminous crops like cowpeas and groundnuts naturally trap nitrogen from the air and enrich the soil, which feeds the maize crop and helps maintain soil health without relying solely on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni ŋɔɔ. ni ji niyenii kɛha ŋmãa tsei ni eyeɔ ebuaa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli pɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Can crops grow normally on land that was previously used for galamsey mining?
ga: Ani tsei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ akɛ galamsey tsuɔ nii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Mining strips away the fertile topsoil and packs the earth tight. To grow crops there again, you must break up the hard ground, add plenty of organic manure, and plant cover crops to rebuild the soil's nutrients over time.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ ni oootsi kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ooofee lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Koni okwɛ tsei yɛ jɛmɛ ekoŋŋ Esa akɛ ogbala shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo afata he. ni amɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow when heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Excess water washes key nutrients like nitrogen deeper into the dirt where roots cannot reach, or waterlogs the roots so they cannot breathe. The yellow leaves show that the plant is starving for food.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ, kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Aloo ha shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ aahu akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas make my soil better for the next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family. Their roots work with good soil bacteria to pull nitrogen directly from the air and store it in the ground, providing natural fertilizer for whatever you plant next.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans fata legume weku lɛ he. Eshishifãi lɛ kɛ sũ mli helai kpakpai tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkɛto sũ lɛ mli. akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ

english: Why do my cassava plants produce tiny tubers when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he?

english: When crops are crowded, their roots fight each other for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Giving plants enough space allows their roots to expand fully and absorb what they need to make large roots.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ kɛhaa nu. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ kwraa ni amɛheɔ nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná shishifãi wuji lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and show light green patches during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. The virus prevents the leaves from trapping sunlight properly, slowing down crop growth.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Virus lɛ tsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkamɔ hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa tsei daa blɛoo.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too hot or when the plant does not get steady water. High heat weakens the pollen, preventing fruit formation, so the plant sheds the flower.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ nu daa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa pollen lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Tsi aduawai ni baa lɛ naa No sɛɛ lɛ tso lɛ shwie efɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Why is it bad for me to water my vegetables in the middle of a hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ oooha aduawai anɔ nu yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: In the hot afternoon sun, water evaporates quickly before reaching the roots, and water droplets left on leaves can act like magnifying glass lenses, scorching the soft leaf surface.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Nu lɛ shwieɔ oya dani eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ni nu ni shwieɔ shi yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ glase ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo. Eshãa baa lɛ hiɛ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why does chemical fertilizer burn my crops if I put it right against the plant stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shãa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛji mikɛwo mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizers contain concentrated salts. When placed right against a stem, the fertilizer draws moisture out of the plant's skin, drying it out and burning the plant tissues.
ga: Fertilizer lɛ yɛ ŋoo babaoo. Kɛ akɛwo tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ, Fertilizer lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ hewolo lɛ mli. Egbiɔ ni eshãa tso lɛ mli fãji.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my crops after clearing the bush?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni ajie ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are tough and can lie hidden in the soil for years. Clearing the land exposes these seeds to sunlight and moisture, triggering them to sprout faster than cultivated crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afii babaoo. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui nɛɛ naa hulu la kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ.

english: How long does it usually take after planting cassava before I can harvest big tubers?
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei sɛɛ lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani anyɛɔ akpaa ŋmeii wuji?

english: Most cassava varieties in Ghana take between 9 to 12 months to mature fully. Harvesting too early yields thin, watery roots, while allowing them a full year gives the plant time to store maximum starch and expand the size of the tubers.
ga: Kasava ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ ateŋ babaoo heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani eshɛɔ shweremɔ he. Kɛ́ akpa mra tsɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ afee nu ni amɛbaafee mlɛo. Yɛ be mli ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni edaa afi muu fɛɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ be ni ekɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo mli bɔ ni eeenyɛ ni ekɛhaa e-bulbs lɛ dalɛ mli waa lɛ.

english: How do I know when my yam tubers are fully mature and ready to be dug up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ o-sweet potato tubers lɛ edara jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: Yams are ready for harvest when the leaves and vines begin to turn yellow and dry up naturally, usually 6 to 8 months after planting. This drying shows that the plant has stopped growing leaves and transferred all its energy into the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 6 kɛyashi 8 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kpaɔ baai lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ yaa ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why are my maize stalks growing very tall, but the corn cobs remain small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miiya hiɛ waa nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi ani ŋmãa lɛ ji bibioo lolo?

english: Tall stalks with small cobs usually happen when maize plants are planted too close together or get too much nitrogen without enough phosphorus and water. The plants spend all their energy fighting for sunlight to grow tall instead of filling out the cobs.
ga: Tso lɛ kwɔ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Aloo nitrogen babaoo yɛ ni fɔsfɔs kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ wuɔ koni amɛtsɔ hulu la nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo amɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before any fruits actually grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani aduawai lɛ eda diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off without setting fruit mainly because of extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of bees to pollinate them. When temperatures get too high, the plant drops flowers to conserve energy and survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii, titri lɛ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa hewɔ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa Aloo ŋmeii ni baawo ŋmeii lɛ bɛ. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why does a young cocoa tree take a few years before it starts bearing any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ afii fioo komɛi dani amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need 3 to 5 years to build a deep root system and strong canopy capable of supporting heavy pods. Modern hybrid cocoa varieties can start fruiting earlier, around 2 to 3 years, if given sufficient shade and care when young.
ga: Akɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 tsuɔ nii dani cacao tso ko náa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli wa ni baanyɛ akwɛ ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ anɔ. Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii mra kɛjɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akɛ aha amɛ hulutsoo ni sa ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ beni amɛdarako lɛ.

english: How does giving space between my plantain suckers help them produce bigger bunches?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ miha mi plantain tsei lɛ ahe gbɛ lɛ eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji?

english: Proper spacing ensures each plantain tree gets its own share of sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. When planted too close, their large leaves block sunlight from each other, resulting in thin stems and smaller fruit bunches.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ nu lɛ ji lɛ diɛŋtsɛ enɔ Kɛji adu ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ Baai wuji lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ aduawai bibii feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Can planting groundnuts together with my maize help my maize grow better?
ga: Ani ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots. This natural nitrogen feeds the nearby maize plants, helping them grow stronger and greener without extra fertilizer.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen nɛɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ niyenii. Ye obua amɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi fataaa he.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛkpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips, aphids, or mites feeding on leaf sap, or by a plant virus spread by whiteflies. These pests damage leaf tissue, causing them to twist and stunt crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji. Enɛ haa amɛtsiɔ amɛhe ni amɛtsiɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Heavy rainfall can wash essential nutrients like nitrogen deep into the soil below root level. Too much water can also drown the roots, preventing them from breathing and taking up nutrients properly.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ he kɛya sũ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ashishi. Nu babaoo baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ shishi. Ehaa ewaa akɛ aaamu ni aná niyenii mli hewalɛ

english: How does placing dry leaves around my crop stems help them during hot weather?
ga: Baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te mi tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tɛŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Placing dry leaves or grass around crops—known as mulching—acts like a blanket over the soil. It traps moisture in the ground, keeps root temperatures cool under the hot sun, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Ale baai gbohii loo jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaafee enii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli fɛ̃i hiɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Why does the extension officer tell me to cut down my cocoa trees when they are sick instead of just spraying them with medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mɛi akɛ amɛfo cocoa tsei kɛji hela mɔ amɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo amɛ tsofa kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Some serious cocoa diseases, like Swollen Shoot virus, live inside the tree's sap system where chemical sprays cannot reach. Cutting down and removing infected trees is the only reliable way to destroy the disease and stop it from spreading to healthy trees.
ga: Kookoo helai komɛi ni naa wa waa, tamɔ bud swollen virus lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ mli he ni tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akpataa hela lɛ hiɛ ni atsĩɔ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: If a plant disease keeps coming back on my farm, is it better to abandon the land or clear it completely?
ga: Kɛji tsei ahe hela ku esɛɛ eba miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Ani ehi akɛ mashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo majie mli kwraa?

english: Leaving a diseased farm untouched allows pests and viruses to multiply and spread to neighboring lands. Clearing infected plants completely removes the source of the disease so you can safely prepare the soil to plant healthy crops again.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔ ko ni hela emɔ lɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko etaaa he lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ faa babaoo ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaajie nɔ ni hela lɛ jɛ lɛ kwraa. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ osaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shweshweeshwe koni tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does plant disease stay on my farm even after I have harvested all the fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikpa aduawai lɛ fɛɛ moŋ?

english: Many crop diseases live in the stems, leaves, roots, or soil, not just in the fruit. If infected branches or trunks remain standing after harvest, the disease stays alive and attacks any new leaves or pods that try to grow.
ga: Tsei ahe helai babaoo hiɔ tsei ashishifãi, baai, shishifãi, loo shikpɔŋ mli, shi jeee aduawai pɛ amli. Kɛji tsei niji loo tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ damɔ shi lolo yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ Hela lɛ baahi shi ni ebaatutua baai loo tsei heei. ni miitao ni eda

english: Can disease spread to my cocoa farm if my neighbor abandons their sick trees?
ga: Ani hela baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji mikutsoŋbii lɛ shi amɛkookoo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, insects like mealybugs, as well as wind and rain, can carry diseases from a nearby neglected farm directly to your healthy trees. Managing sick farms across a area helps protect everyone's crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooloi bibii sumɔɔ mealybugs, kɛ agbɛnɛ hu kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ. Abaanyɛ akɛ helai ni jɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ ni aku hiɛ ashwie nɔ lɛ amli lɛ aya otsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Gbɛjegbɛi ni helatsɛmɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ yɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees are too old or sick to produce good harvests anymore?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cacao tsei lɛ egbɔ tsɔ loo hela mɔ amɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai dɔŋŋ?

english: If your trees show declining yield every year, swollen branches, yellowish leaves, or dried-up pods despite good rainfall and fertilizer, they are severely affected by age or disease and need to be replaced.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ yibiiwoo miiba shi daa afi lɛ, no lɛ tsei lɛ aniji efuu, baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ, loo ŋmeii lɛ egbi yɛ nugbɔ kpakpa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Afii loo hela baanyɛ aná tsei nɛɛ anɔ hewalɛ waa. ni ehe miihia ni atsake

english: If I agree to cut down my old cocoa trees and replant, how long will I wait before I can harvest again?
ga: Kɛji mikpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ mafo kokoo tso momo lɛ ni madu ehee. Be enyiɛ mamɛ ni makpa nii ekoŋŋ?

english: Modern high-yield cocoa varieties can start bearing fruit within 2 to 3 years with proper care, which is much faster than traditional older varieties that took up to 5 years.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo henɔi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ yaa oya kwraa fe blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ ni heɔ afii 5 lɛ.

english: Why are government-supplied seedlings better than planting seeds from my own harvested cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni nɔyeli lɛ kɛhaa lɛ hi fe dumɔwui ni jɛɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpaa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Seedlings provided by official extension services are specially bred in research centers to resist common diseases, mature faster, and produce significantly higher pod yields than seeds saved from older farm trees.
ga: Akwɛɔ official extension service dumɔwui lɛ anɔ yɛ niiamlitaomɔ hei koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ, amɛdara oya ni amɛwo pod yibii ni fa babaoo fe dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli tsei momo amli lɛ.

english: What happens to the soil when old crops are cut down and replaced with new ones?
ga: Mɛni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ afo tsei momoi ni akɛ tsei heei wo najiaŋ?

english: Clearing old trees removes shade overload and allows nutrients and sunlight to reach the land. Replanting with healthy, fresh crops helps the soil support rapid plant growth and higher future yields.
ga: Tsei momoi ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ hulutsoo ni fa fe nine lɛ, ni ehaa niyenii kɛ hulu la shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Sod tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ adalɛ oya ni ehaa wɔsɛɛ be mli yibii babaoo baa.

english: What can I plant to feed my family and earn money while waiting for newly planted cocoa trees to grow?
ga: Mɛni makwɛ koni makwɛ miweku lɛ ni maná shika yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni kookoo tsei heei ni adu lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: You can plant food crops like plantain, cassava, or cocoyam alongside young cocoa. These crops provide immediate food and income while giving essential shade to protect the young cocoa plants from harsh sunlight.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantain, cassava loo kookoo afata kookoo bibii ahe. Tsei nɛɛ haa niyenii kɛ shika amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni akɛbu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he.

english: How can I get assistance if I do not have enough money or labor to cut down and replant my diseased cocoa farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná yelikɛbuamɔ? Ni kɛji akɛ mibɛ shika loo nitsumɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni mikɛbaafolɔ kookoo ŋmɔji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni mikɛbaadu ekoŋŋ hu?

english: You can contact your local agricultural extension office. Government cocoa rehabilitation schemes often provide free seedlings, technical support, and financial incentives or labor assistance to help farmers clear diseased trees and replant.
ga: Obaanyɛ oya okwaayeli he nitsumɔhe ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔyeli gbɛjianɔtoi ni akɛbaatsu kookoo he nii lɛ haa dumɔwui ni aheee nɔ ko. Teknik yelikɛbuamɔ kɛ shika he kanyamɔi loo nitsumɔ he yelikɛbuamɔ. Koni eye ebua okwaafoi ni amɛjie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni amɛdu eheei.

english: How many years does it take for a cocoa tree to start producing a heavy harvest?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo tso ko jeɔ yibii babaoo woɔ shishi?

english: While cocoa trees may start showing a few pods around 3 to 5 years after planting, they typically reach their peak fruit-bearing stage around 7 years when their trunk, branches, and root systems are fully developed.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ cacao tso baanyɛ aje shishi ewo yibii fioo komɛi aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 5 sɛɛ moŋ, shi bei pii lɛ, eshɛɔ yibiiwoo be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ he aaafee afii 7 beni tso lɛ shishi, eniji, kɛ shishifãi lɛ edara kwraa lɛ.

english: Why do my younger cocoa trees yield far less fruit than my older trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kwraa fe mi-cacao tsei ni eda lɛ?

english: Young trees spend most of their early years putting energy into growing strong roots and branches. As the tree grows older, it shifts its energy from growing wood to producing more flowers and pods.
ga: Tsei bibii yeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli be babaoo ni amɛdaraa. Koni akɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni akɛwo shishifãi kɛ tsei niji ni mli wa. Kɛ tso lɛ da Etsakeɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ tsei ni miida lɛ mli lɛ mli kɛfeɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why do some trees take many years to yield fruit while crops like maize take only a few months?
ga: Mɛni he je nɛ tso komɛ heɔ jehahi babauu loko e woɔ yiblii ɔ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa heɔ nyɔji fioo pɛ?

english: Tree crops like cocoa are perennial, meaning they live for decades. They invest several years building a strong permanent structure and deep roots before they can support heavy harvests year after year.
ga: Tsei tamɔ kookoo ji tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛhiɔ shi afii nyɔŋmai abɔ. Amɛkɛ afii babaoo maa tsũ ko ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ yɔɔ mli ni baahi shi daa dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua ŋmaakpamɔ agbo ko afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Is it normal for my cocoa harvest to increase suddenly after several years of small yields?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni ja akɛ mi-cocoa ni miwoɔ lɛ baaya hiɛ trukaa yɛ afii babaoo ni mikɛwoɔ nii fioo lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, as trees reach full maturity—usually around 7 years—their internal capacity to absorb nutrients increases, leading to a natural jump in pod production compared to their earlier years.
ga: Hɛɛ, beni tsei lɛ daraa—bei pii lɛ amɛyeɔ aaafee afii 7 lɛ—nyɛmɔ ni amɛyɔɔ yɛ amɛmli ni amɛkɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ lɛ yaa hiɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, pod ni afeɔ lɛ etee hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ akɛto afii ni eho lɛ ahe.

english: Why would I need to install water pipes on my farm if rain already falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ nu paipii awo miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ miinɛ momo lɛ?

english: Rainfall can be unpredictable during dry seasons. Using irrigation pipes ensures your crops get a steady supply of water year-round, preventing stress and keeping mature trees productive.
ga: Anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ he paipii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa onibii lɛ náa nu be fɛɛ be yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. Tsi haomɔ naa ni oha tsei wuji awo yibii babaoo.

english: What happens to mature crop trees if they do not get enough water during the fruiting stage?
ga: Mɛni baa tsei ni eda lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: When trees lack water while forming fruit, they protect themselves by shedding young pods or flowers, which severely reduces the size and quality of your final harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu be mli ni ewoɔ yibii lɛ Tsei buɔ amɛhe he kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii loo fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha naagbee nibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ dalɛ kɛ ehilɛ aba shi waa.

english: Can proper watering help my crops reach their full production stage faster?
ga: Ani nu ni sa ni akɛhaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaye abua ni amɛshɛ yibiiwoo ni fa oya he?

english: Yes, consistent water prevents growth interruptions caused by dry spells, allowing trees to grow continuously and reach their full fruit-bearing potential without unnecessary delays.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ tsiɔ dalɛ mligbalamɔ ni hɔmɔ kɛbaa lɛ naa. Ehaa tso lɛ daa daa ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo ni sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ ni ehe ehiaaa.

english: How does managing a large farm of over 100 acres affect crop yield compared to a small farm?
ga: Te ŋmɔji wuji ni fe acre 100 lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛ akɛto ŋmɔji bibii ahe?

english: A larger farm produces much more total crop, but it requires reliable infrastructure like water access and organized labor to ensure every section receives equal care.
ga: Okwaafoi wuji woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ fɛɛ mli. Shi esa akɛ nibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ tamɔ nu ni anáa kɛ nitsumɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahi shi koni anyɛ akwɛ mɛi fɛɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some parts of my farm produce better yields than other parts planted at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fãi komɛi woɔ yibii fe ekrokomɛi lɛ? Ani adu yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yield differences across a farm are usually caused by variations in soil nutrients, shade levels, or uneven water distribution across different sections of land.
ga: Srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ yibiiwoo mli yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii srɔtoi, hulutsoo, loo nu mlijaa ni ejaaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hei srɔtoi lɛ amli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do cocoa trees drop their flowers before they develop into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Trees drop flowers when they are under stress from drought, lack essential soil nutrients, or when the tree is still too young to carry the weight of developing fruit.
ga: Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛyɔɔ hɔmɔ he haomɔ shishi. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo be mli ni tso lɛ ji gbekɛ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ amli tsiimɔ nɔ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves and grow strong. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will help restore their dark green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai eŋɔli kɛ dalɛ ni mli wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Does it matter which direction I insert cassava stem cuttings into the ground when planting?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ akɛ ŋmei niji lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, you should plant the stick with the small buds pointing upward toward the sky. If you plant it upside down, the shoots will struggle to grow, resulting in weak plants and very small cassava tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ odu tsei niji ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji odu ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ Tsoi lɛ baawa akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ hu faaa kwraa.

english: Why shouldn't I sow my maize seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell before the main rainy season truly starts. Seeds planted too early will sprout and then dry up and die due to heat and lack of steady rainfall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi diɛŋtsɛ. Dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛbaagbi ni amɛbaagboi yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plants without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off mainly due to extreme heat or irregular watering. When the plant experiences drought stress or too much heat, it drops its flowers to save energy and water just to stay alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni fe nine loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Kɛ tsei na haomɔ kɛjɛ hɔmɔ loo dɔlɛ ni fe nine mli Ebaashwie efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he koni ehi wala mli kɛkɛ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts on my farm next season instead of planting maize again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli moŋ fe ni madu ŋmei ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously drains the soil of its nutrients. Groundnuts and beans natural trap nitrogen gas from the air and put it back into the earth, restoring fertility for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Peanuts kɛ nuts lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni ekɛ fɔmɔ aku sɛɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: What is causing tiny caterpillars to eat the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Ye mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ.

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which hatch from eggs laid by moths on young leaves. They hide inside the funnel of the maize plant to feed on fresh foliage, but catching them early allows you to control them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ baai bibii anɔ lɛ amli. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli koni amɛye baai heei. Shi amɛmɔmɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ oyeɔ amɛnɔ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tso ko koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to manufacture food that feeds the tubers growing under the ground. Staking lifts the vines off the soil so they catch more light and stay safe from ground fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii ni amɛkɛbaaha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking woɔ wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni la babaoo ashɛ amɛhe ni eha amɛhe akafee shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my stored grains develop small holes and turn to powder after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni etsɔɔ powda yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ.

english: This damage is caused by insects called grain weevils that lay eggs inside seeds. Thoroughly sun-drying your grain to remove moisture and storing it in sealed, airtight bags prevents these insects from multiplying.
ga: Kooloo ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ seed moth ni fɔɔ wuji yɛ dumɔwu lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ajie ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni akɛto kotoku ko ni mli ewo muji mli lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkafa babaoo.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to cover the dirt around my pepper plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, shields the ground from hot sun, stops moisture from evaporating quickly so you water less, and prevents weeds from taking over your crop.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Etsiɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekaho oya bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akashwie nɔ fioo ni eha jwɛi akaye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. Planting shade crops like plantain or shade trees protects them from heat stress, retains soil moisture, and helps them establish strong roots.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua tsei ni amɛná shishifãi ni wa

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is essential for green growth. Adding compost or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore leaf color and boost plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ ahe afee fɛo ekoŋŋ ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why should I avoid planting cassava on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmei dumɔ he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Cassava takes a heavy amount of nutrients out of the ground. Planting it continuously in the same spot exhausts the soil and encourages pests; rotating with legumes like beans or groundnuts helps the soil recover.
ga: Cassava jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Dumɔ ni yaa nɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa sũ lɛ fiteɔ ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ehe feɔ fɛo.

english: Can I plant groundnuts between my cassava plants, or will they compete for food?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ateŋ? Aloo amɛbaashi akaŋ yɛ niyenii he?

english: You can safely plant them together. Groundnuts actually pull nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, which helps feed the cassava and improves overall soil fertility without competing heavily.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ amɛ afee ekome shweshweeshwe. Yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni adu ŋmei ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ afee fɛo ni akaŋshii ni mli wa bɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops yield less food when I plant seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naaa niyenii babaoo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded together, their leaves shade each other from sunlight and their roots compete for soil nutrients and water, resulting in weaker stems and smaller harvests.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛbaai lɛ haa hulu lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baa shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why do experienced farmers build high mounds to plant yam instead of planting on flat soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ maa gɔji ni kwɔlɔ koni amɛdu sweet potatoes yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, deep soil to expand smoothly. High mounds provide loose soil for tuber growth, prevent waterlogging around the roots, and make harvesting much easier.
