ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ. Gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha tuber dalɛ. Etsiɔ nu ni shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ naa. Ni ehaa nikpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Is it better for me to water my tomato plants early in the morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: It is best to water early in the morning so the roots absorb moisture before the day gets hot. Afternoon watering leads to rapid evaporation and can stress the plants or promote fungal diseases.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu leebi koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu dani hulu lɛ adɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli shwane mli lɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi oya, ni ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ aná haomɔ loo ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela aba.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly when I delay clearing weeds from my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa blɛoo nɛkɛ beni mikɛ be shwieɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal vital sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients away from your crops. Removing weeds early allows your crops to consume all available resources and grow faster.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni jɛɔ onibii amli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ye obua onibii ni okɛ nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ atsu nii ni amɛdara oya.

english: What is causing tiny holes in the leaves and middle shoots of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ baai kɛ amɛteŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ.

english: Holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Detecting them early allows you to use recommended pest management methods before they destroy the plant's growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ amɔmɔ amɛ mra lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua. Enɛ baaha okɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ lɛ atsu nii dani amɛfite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why is it important to cut off the extra shoots growing near the base of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, often called suckers, waste the tree's food and energy. Removing them directs vital nutrients to the main trunk, helping the tree produce more healthy flowers and cocoa pods.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ suckers lɛ, haa tso lɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ baa shi. Amɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa baa tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ kookoo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant cassava and maize together on the same field instead of growing them separately?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu amɛ srɔtoi lɛ

english: Planting cassava and maize together keeps your field protected like a family. Maize grows quickly to give you early food and income, while cassava stays in the soil longer and creates ground cover that retains moisture and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Kasava kɛ ŋmãa ni ooofee ekome kɛdu lɛ buɔ oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ he tamɔ weku. Abele daa oya bɔni afee ni oná niyenii kɛ shika oya. Shi Yucca lɛ, ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be babaoo ni efeɔ nɔ ko ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I plant cowpeas around my maize stalks, and how does that help my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ehe? Ani manyɛ maná ŋmãa tsei? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ enɛ baaye abua miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize is very beneficial. The cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air to feed the maize soil, while the tall maize stalks give the vines support, allowing both crops to share space and support each other's growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Cowpeas lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa tsei ni kɛlɛ fiɔ wain tsei lɛ asɛɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ jaa he ko ni amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa amɛhe dalɛ.

english: How do cover crops like mucuna protect my land when heavy rains start falling?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ abu shikpɔŋ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ abu mishikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛ́ nugbɔ ni naa wa bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: Cover crops spread thick roots and heavy leaves that hold the soil tightly together. Even during torrential rains, these roots keep your fertile topsoil in place so your nutrients are not washed away.
ga: Tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ gbɛɔ shishifãi ni mli tse kɛ baai ni tsii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ eshwaa. Yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa po mli Nɛkɛ shishifãi nɛɛ buɔ oshikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ akaho.

english: Why do legume crop roots leave small bumps on them, and should I clean them off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ legume shishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ni ani esa akɛ matsumɔ he?

english: Do not clean those small bumps off; they are root nodules that store friendly bacteria. These bacteria stay put in the soil and feed nitrogen to your crops, enriching the land for whatever you plant next.
ga: Kaatsumɔ nakai ŋmeii bibii lɛ, amɛji shishifãi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji naanyobɔɔ helai lɛ yɔɔ mli. Nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛkɛ nitrogen haa oŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baahã nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ aba.

english: Why do I see ladybugs and small wasps coming to my field as soon as insects start eating my cowpea leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miyaa nɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni baa miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji ŋmeii lɛ bɔi mi-cowpea baai lɛ yeli pɛ?

english: When pest insects start damage on your crops, the plants release natural signals into the air. Useful insects pick up these signals and rush in immediately to eat the pests, acting as natural guards for your field.
ga: Beni tsɛŋemɔ helai jeɔ shishi amɛfiteɔ onibii lɛ Tsei jieɔ adebɔɔ mli okadii kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Kplukai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ holeɔ okadii nɛɛ ni amɛhoɔ oya koni amɛyaye kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli bulɔ kɛha oyale lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to plant Napier grass around the borders of our maize farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔdu Napier jwɛi yɛ wɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Napier grass acts as a protective barrier plant. When stemborers attack, they are attracted to the Napier grass first and rush to it, trapping the pests on the border so your main maize crop stays safe inside.
ga: Napier jwɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ tso ni buɔ mɔ he. Beni trunk borer lɛ tutuaa Napier jwɛi lɛ gbalaa amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛjoɔ foi kɛyaa jɛmɛ. Koni okɛmɔmɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ husu lɛ he lɛ Koni okɛ o-corn ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ahi mli shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up tightly when the dry sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ hulu ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants cannot move to find shade, so they curl their leaves to shrink their surface area. This reduces water loss and signals that the crop is under heat stress and needs mulching or watering.
ga: Pepper tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ afã kɛyatao hulutsoo. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛfoɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛha ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ afee bibioo. Enɛ haa nu ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi, ni eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ shishi ni ehe miihia ni atsɔ nɔ awo amɛmli loo awo amɛ nu.

english: Why do my yam vines wither and dry up in the dry season while the yam underground stays healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lolo lɛ?

english: The yam plant protects itself by letting its surface leaves dry out during heat while keeping all its energy safely stored in the tuber underground, waiting for the rains to return.
ga: Sweet potato tsei buɔ amɛhe he kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ ni amɛhaa egbiɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, akɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ toɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli shweshweeshwe, ni amɛmiimɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why is it important to keep large shade trees inside my cocoa farm instead of cutting all of them down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ ahi mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mafolɔ tsei lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Permanent shade trees stay in place year after year to shield young and mature cocoa trees from strong sun exposure and wind damage, keeping the soil cool so the whole farm survives tough dry seasons.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ daa lɛ hiɔ shi daa afi koni amɛkɛbu kookoo tsei bibii kɛ mɛi ni eda lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahe. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni wa lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds and wild sunflowers sprout up so fast immediately after the first rains arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kɛ koo mli hulutsoo tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya nɛkɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie quietly in dry soil for months waiting for moisture. As soon as rain touches them, they react instantly and germinate without delay to cover bare ground.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui kã shi dioo Amɛtaraa shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ nyɔji babaoo ni amɛmiimɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ pɛ kɛkɛ ni amɛtsuɔ he nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛhaa he ni agbele lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when the sun is too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil moisture around their roots. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains protects them until they grow strong enough to handle direct sun.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa sũ mli nu ni bɔleɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ gĩɔ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu tsei nɛɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before they produce corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani amɛwoɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow mainly due to a lack of nitrogen in the soil or heavy rains washing nutrients away. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizers or animal manure helps restore their green color and boosts corn production.
ga: Nitrogen ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni haa niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ laajeɔ lɛ hewɔ titri lɛ, ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How do I know which direction to plant my cassava stem cuttings in the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole he ni esa akɛ okɛ o-cassava ŋmɔtɔi lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: You should plant cassava stems with the small growth buds pointing upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down makes it hard for the shoots to emerge, resulting in weak plants and very small cassava roots.
ga: Esa akɛ odu cassava tsei ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛ́ adu kɛya ŋwɛi lɛ, ebaaha ewa aha ŋmeii lɛ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmei shishifãi bibii waa baa.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously on the same land drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows specialized pests and diseases to build up. Rotating maize with beans or cowpeas restores vital nitrogen back into the ground naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai pɔtɛɛ aba. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my crops stay small and weak when weeds grow close to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa ni amɛhe waaa be mli ni jwɛi bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and food from the soil that your crops need to thrive. Clearing weeds early allows your crop roots to absorb all available nutrients, leading to larger leaves and healthier yields.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni amɛŋɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ daraa ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hu baa.

english: Why do I need to heap the soil into high mounds before planting yam?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ wɔbua shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ naa dani wɔdu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose, and deep soil to expand easily under the ground. Mounds create soft soil space for large tubers to grow and ensure proper water drainage so the seed yams do not rot.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi oya. Gɔji feɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni bulbs wuji baanyɛ akwɛ̃. ni akwɛ koni nu lɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Koni sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ akafite

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the central leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Those caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a destructive pest that feeds on the growing shoots of maize. Checking your field early and applying safe bio-pesticides or recommended treatments keeps them from destroying your harvest.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii ni yeɔ ŋmãa ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ. Kwɛmɔ nibii ni odu lɛ amli mra ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ atsu nii. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How does planting beans alongside my main crops help my soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Beans and other legumes take nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. This naturally fertilizes the soil and feeds neighboring plants without requiring extra money spent on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Beans kɛ legumes krokomɛi Ejieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eha tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii ni afiteee shika babaoo yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my stored grains turn into powder and get full of holes after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ bafeɔ powder kɛ ŋmeii yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Small insects called weevils eat through stored grains if the seeds are not fully dried before bagging. Thoroughly sun-drying grains until they are hard and storing them in sealed, airtight bags stops weevils from damaging your crop.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ baaye dumɔwui ni ato lɛ kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛwo kotoku mli. Gbimɔ dumɔwui lɛ aahu kɛyashi ebaawa ni okɛwo kotoku ko ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli lɛ mli. Tsi ŋmeii ni fiteɔ onibii lɛ anaa.

english: Why should I wait for rain or wet soil before putting chemical fertilizer on my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni efɔ dani mikɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer requires water to dissolve so that plant roots can absorb the nutrients. Applying chemical fertilizer to dry soil can burn and destroy plant roots or simply blow away in dry wind without helping the crop.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ biɔ nu koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite tsei lɛ ashishifãi loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ baanyɛ atswa amɛ kɛya ni ehaaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How do I plant plantain when I cannot find any seeds for it at the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ plantain? Be mli ni onyɛɛɛ ona dumɔwui yɛ jara nɔ?

english: Plantains do not grow from seeds like maize or vegetables. Instead, they are grown using shoots called suckers that emerge from the base of a mature plant.
ga: Plantains jɛɛɛ dumɔwui tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai amli. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ tsohi nɛ a tsɛɛ ke suckers nɛ jeɔ tsehi nɛ a wa a sisi ɔ tsuɔ ní kɛ duɔ mɛ.

english: Why can't I buy a bag of plantain seeds to nurse before the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ mahe plantain dumɔwui kotoku kome kɛkɛ ni madu dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba lɛ?

english: Cultivated plantains are seedless crops. Because they do not produce viable seeds, farmers propagate them vegetatively using suckers taken from existing plants.
ga: Aduɔ dumɔwui akɛ tsei ni dumɔwui bɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛwooo dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okwaafoi kɛ ŋmeii ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ momo lɛ amli lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why is it recommended that I do not plant too many plantain suckers all at once in my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔɔ akɛ madu plantains babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli shikome lɛ?

english: Plantains mature stem by stem over an extended period. Planting too many at the same time can overcrowd your farm and lead to an unmanageable harvest where bunches mature faster than you can sell or eat them.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Kɛ́ odu nii babaoo yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha oŋmɔ lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni anyɛɛɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kuu lɛ baadara oya fe bɔ ni obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ loo oye.

english: How does planting corn differ from planting plantain on my land?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esoro ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he?

english: Corn is sown directly into the soil using dry seeds that germinate together, whereas plantain requires digging holes to plant individual living suckers that produce shoots one by one.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni egbi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ ŋmãa awoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni plantains lɛ atsa bu koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka, ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ ekomekomei.

english: Why do plantain plants sprout new shoots one by one near the stem instead of all at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɔ ŋmeii heei komekomei yɛ tso lɛ shishi moŋ fe ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ shikome lɛ?

english: Plantain grows from an underground stem called an corm, which naturally sends up individual suckers sequentially as the plant matures.
ga: Plantains lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni atsɛɔ amɛ tubers lɛ amli. Nɔ ni jɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ tsuɔ ŋmeii kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ gbɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ nɔ be mli ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: How does the fruiting behavior of plantain differ from grain crops like maize?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esoro plantains yibiiwoo su lɛ yɛ ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ he?

english: Maize plants mature and produce grain across the field at roughly the same time, while plantains grow continuously and produce single bunches from individual stems over a longer timeframe.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ daa ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ yɛ be kome mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, plantains yaa nɔ edaa ni ejieɔ panicles komekomei kɛjɛɔ tsei aŋkroaŋkroi amli yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: What is 'apemto' plantain, and why do many local farmers grow it?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘apemto’ plantain ni mɛni hewɔ maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi babaoo duɔ lɛ?

english: Apemto' is a local plantain variety that is highly valued because it is versatile and widely used to prepare popular Ghanaian staples like fufu.
ga: Apemto’ ji maŋ lɛ mli plantain henɔ ko ni abuɔ waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eyɛ srɔtoi babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii babaoo yɛ Ghana niyenii ni ehe gbɛi tamɔ fufu lɛ saamɔ mli.

english: Which crop should I focus on if I want something versatile for local food preparation?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei esa akɛ mikɛ mijwɛŋmɔ ama nɔ kɛji miitao nɔ ko ni yɔɔ srɔtoi kɛha maŋ lɛ mli niyenii ahe saamɔ?

english: Plantain varieties like 'apemto' are excellent choices because they can be processed into multiple traditional meals, making them very popular in local food markets.
ga: Plantain henɔi tamɔ ‘apemto’ ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ abaanyɛ afee amɛ kusum niyenii babaoo. Enɛ haa ehe gbɛi waa yɛ maŋ lɛ niyenii jarayelihe lɛ.

english: When extension officers talk about 'crops', are they mainly referring to food plants?
ga: Kɛji akɛ sɛɛgbɛtsɔɔmɔ nitsulɔi lɛ wie ‘ŋmɔshi nibii’ ahe lɛ, ani amɛtsɔɔ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii titri?

english: Yes, in general farming discussions, crops usually refer to cultivated food plants like plantain, corn, and root vegetables grown for consumption and sale.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ okwaayeli he sanegbaai amli. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tsɔɔ niyenii ni aduɔ tamɔ plantains, ŋmãa, kɛ shishifãi ni aduɔ koni aye ni ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: Is plantain prepared and cooked the same way as other root crops like cassava or yam?
ga: Ani ahoɔ plantains ni ahoɔ lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni tamɔ nɔ ni ahoɔ shishifãi krokomɛi tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: No, plantains have a different texture and starch structure than root crops, meaning they are processed differently—often pounded into fufu or cooked in specialized dishes rather than simply boiled like yam.
ga: Dabi, plantains yɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ starch lɛ yɛ srɔto fe tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, esoro bɔ ni atsuɔ he nii ahaa. Bei pii lɛ, atswaa lɛ ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ahoɔ yɛ niyenii krɛdɛɛi amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetswa tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ

english: How do I know if my soil has enough water for planting maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ nɔ?

english: You can test your soil moisture by squeezing a handful of earth from a few inches deep; if it holds together in a ball without dripping water, the land has enough moisture for planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu ni mli edɔ lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni oootsi kɛjɛ inchi fioo komɛi amli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji ebɔle ehe ni nu shwieee shi lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔwui.

english: Why do my crops dry up quickly even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu daa moŋ lɛ?

english: If your soil lacks organic matter like compost or mulch, water drains away or evaporates too fast instead of staying in the root zone where the plant can drink it.
ga: Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii. Nu lɛ baaho loo ebaatsɔ la oya tsɔ. Mohu ɔ, e ngɛ tso ɔ sisi he nɛ tso ɔ ma nyɛ maa nu nu ngɛ ɔ.

english: Which crops are best to plant on low land that easily floods during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei esa akɛ adu yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni nu shwieɔ nɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Crops like rice and cocoyam thrive in very wet or flooded soils, whereas root crops like cassava will rot if their roots remain submerged in water for too long.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ kookoo kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ loo nu eyi nɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi, tamɔ ŋmei lɛ baagboi kɛji akɛ akɛ shishifãi lɛ wo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants turn yellow and drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is a cassava plant's natural self-defense strategy to save water and keep its underground roots alive until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ kɛha ŋmei tso lɛ. Koni akɛbu nu he ni akɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: How do long-term tree crops like cocoa behave differently from seasonal crops like maize?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ kookoo lɛ feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Seasonal crops like maize finish growing and producing within a few months, whereas tree crops like cocoa take years to mature but continue giving harvests on the same land for decades.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be mli, tamɔ ŋmãa, kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei tamɔ kookoo heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛshɛɔ shweremɔ he. Shi etee nɔ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nɔŋŋ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetables early in the morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because it gives roots time to absorb moisture before the hot sun causes the water to evaporate from the soil.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛjieɔ nu dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa ejɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I burn all the grass and vegetation on my land before clearing it for farming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishãa jwɛi kɛ tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani mijie nɔ koni mikɛdu nii?

english: Burning kills good soil organisms and burns away organic material that helps the soil absorb rain and feed your crops naturally.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii kpakpai ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ ni eshãa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ ni ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing plenty of dark green leaves but no flowers or fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo lɛ? Shi fɔfɔii loo aduawai bɛ jɛmɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes plants focus all their energy on leaf growth rather than flowering and producing fruit.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai ni amɛbaawo lɛ.

english: How does planting my crops in straight rows help them yield better than broadcasting seeds randomly?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa yibii kpakpai baa fe dumɔwui ni aduɔ trukaa lɛ?

english: Row planting ensures every crop gets its fair share of sunlight, ground space, and soil nutrients without choking its neighbors.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ naa hulu la, shikpɔŋ nɔ he ko, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ bɔ ni sa ni egbaaa amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings die when heavy rain leaves standing water on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like humans do, and standing water starves the roots of oxygen, causing them to drown and rot.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni adesai feɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Ni nu ni ekã shi lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ. ni haa efoɔ nu mli ni egboɔ.

english: Why do my okra plants keep producing new flowers every time I pick the mature pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi heei be fɛɛ be ni mafolɔ tso ni eda lɛ?

english: Okra plants naturally try to reproduce. When you harvest mature pods regularly, it stops the plant from making seeds, encouraging it to continuously produce fresh flowers and new pods.
ga: Okra tsei lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛfɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Kɛji okpa ŋmeii ni eda lɛ daa lɛ Tso lɛ baakpa dumɔwui feemɔ. Tswaa tsei lɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi heei kɛ ŋmeii heei be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do my okra pods become hard and woody if I leave them on the plant for just a few extra days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsei kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ gbii fioo komɛi krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Okra pods mature very rapidly. As they age, the plant deposits tough fiber into the pods to protect the seeds inside, making them hard and unmarketable if not picked early while still young and tender.
ga: Okra ŋmeii lɛ daa oya waa. Beni amɛdaraa lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ tsɔji ni wa toɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli koni amɛkɛbu dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa amɛwaa ni anyɛɛɛ ahɔ̃ɔ kɛji akɛ ajieee amɛ mra. Beni eji oblanyo fioo lolo ni eyɛ blɛoo lɛ

english: Can I harvest okra bit by bit every few days without damaging the plant?
ga: Mibaanyɛ makpa okra fioo fioo yɛ be kome mli. Ani ebaanyɛ ehi shi gbii fioo komɛi ni efiteee tso lɛ?

english: Yes, picking okra bit by bit is actually beneficial. Frequent picking prevents the plant from spending energy on old pods and forces it to keep growing new pods over a longer season.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔi diɛŋtsɛ yɛ okra ni ajieɔ yɛ fãi bibii amli lɛ he. Nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ shii abɔ lɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekɛ hewalɛ akatsu nii yɛ ŋmeii momo lɛ anɔ, ni enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni eya nɔ ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: How long can an okra plant continue giving me pods before it completely slows down?
ga: Be enyiɛ mi gumbo lɛ baanyɛ aha mi pods dani egbɔjɔ kwraa?

english: With proper watering and regular harvesting, an okra plant typically yields fresh pods continuously for two to three months before the plant becomes exhausted and needs to be replaced.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ahã Gumbo tsei lɛ nu jogbaŋŋ ni akpa amɛ daa lɛ, bei pii lɛ amɛwoɔ ŋmeii heei be fɛɛ be nyɔji enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ dani tsei lɛ amli shwieɔ shi ni ehe bahiaa ni atsake amɛ.

english: Why do my okra plants look weak and exhausted after I harvest from them repeatedly for a couple of months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra tsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛhe ejɔ amɛ beni mikpa amɛ shii abɔ sɛɛ lɛ? ekomefeemɔ nyɔji enyɔ loo etɛ?

english: Continuous fruiting draws a lot of energy and nutrients out of the plant and soil. Applying compost, manure, or fertilizer after peak harvests helps rebuild the plant's strength so it can keep producing.
ga: Yibiiwoo ni yaa nɔ lɛ jieɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ tsu nii babaoo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ewaje tsei lɛ koni amɛya nɔ amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my okra plants grow tall and thin with very few pods when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-okra lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni ebɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko pɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, they compete fiercely for sunlight and soil nutrients. The plants stretch upward to catch sun instead of spreading out to grow strong stems and fruit buds.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Tsei lɛ baafee tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛmɔ hulu la lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã koni amɛha amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why are my okra plants growing huge green leaves but producing very few flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra lɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi fɔfɔi fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: This usually happens when the soil has too much nitrogen. Nitrogen promotes thick leaf growth, but plants need nutrients like phosphorus to trigger flowering and pod production.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shi tsei lɛ he miihia niyenii tamɔ fɔsfɔs koni eha amɛwo fɔfɔii kɛ podi.

english: Why do extension officers encourage us to plant fast-growing crops like okra alongside our long-term crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ hewalɛ koni wɔdu ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ okra yɛ wɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Fast-growing vegetables like okra mature quickly and produce small, frequent yields. This gives you steady daily or weekly cash flow to cover minor household expenses while waiting for main seasonal crops to mature.
ga: Aduawai ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ okra lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni fɔɔ baa. Enɛ haa onáa shika ni yaa nɔ daa gbi loo otsi fɛɛ otsi ni okɛbaatsu shia mli shika bibii ahe nii yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ be mli nibii titrii ni aduɔ lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why do my okra leaves droop in the hot afternoon sun even when the soil is not completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra baai lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbiko kwraa moŋ?

english: In intense afternoon heat, okra leaves lose moisture faster than the roots can suck it up from the ground. The leaves wilt temporarily to protect the plant from sun damage and usually bounce back by evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ, Roselle baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni ebu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu lɛ he. ni bei pii lɛ, ekuɔ esɛɛ ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ

english: Why are the leaves of my okra plants turning yellow and curling upward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellowing are often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies, which transmit plant viruses. Controlling these insects early prevents the disease from spreading across your plot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ whiteflies, ni gbɛɔ muawai amɛshwãa tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ye ebua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã okpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with lots of leaves but give me very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: This usually happens when the soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are crowded together. The cassava puts all its energy into growing leaves towards the sun instead of storing food in the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ tsei ebɔle amɛhe. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛhaa ebaa ni miida lɛ kwɛɔ hulu lɛ hiɛ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato eshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow starting from the middle of the leaf?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing along the main vein of a leaf usually means the soil is short on nitrogen, which plants need to make green leaves. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ahe fãji titrii lɛ ahe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni ehe hiaa ni tsei lɛ afee amɛbaai lɛ eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my farmland is healthy enough to plant without buying expensive commercial fertilizers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midumɔ nii lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaakwɛ̃ ni miheee jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa?

english: Healthy soil is dark, crumbles easily in your hand when moist, and is full of earthworms. You can also plant nitrogen-fixing crops like cowpeas or groundnuts to naturally enrich the soil before main planting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa yɛ su ni tsuɔ. Efoɔ oya yɛ nine mli kɛ́ edɔ. ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii eyi mli obɔ Obaanyɛ odu nibii ni haa nitrogen hiɔ shi tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii hu. Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa dani adu tso titri lɛ

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the plant juices, or by a virus they spread. Spraying with neem water or insecticidal soap helps control these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ amli Kɛ́ akɛ neem nu loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits get a dark, rotten spot at the bottom before they can even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔi ni yɔɔ diŋ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot and is caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often brought on by irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly damp helps the roots absorb calcium properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and wilt during the hot afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In intense heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the ground. They temporarily droop to conserve water and usually recover once the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaakoto shi be kukuoo ko koni amɛbu nu he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: How does covering the soil with dry grass or leaves help my crops survive dry periods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ bei amli?

english: Covering the ground with dry organic material, called mulching, acts like a blanket that stops the sun from evaporating water from the soil, keeping the root area cool and moist for longer.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni egbi ni akɛhaa lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ko ni tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekajie nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam leaves and vines start drying up and turning brown when harvest time is near?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni kpamɔ be lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ lɛ?

english: When yam plants complete their growth cycle, they naturally stop sending food to the leaves and redirect all remaining energy into the underground tuber. Yellowing leaves mean the tuber is fully mature.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potato tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Ebaakpa niyenii ni ekɛmajeɔ baai lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ baatsake kɛya ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ edara kwraa.

english: Why are the blossoms falling off my cowpea plants without forming any beans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii ko lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers drop when the weather is too hot, during heavy rainfall, or when tiny pests called thrips feed on the flowers. Keeping plants protected from pests during early flowering prevents this blossom loss.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli loo be mli ni kooloi bibii Atsɛɔ amɛ thrips ni yeɔ fɔfɔi. Kɛ́ abu tsei ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ nɛɛ akafite.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning pale yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen in the soil or getting choked by waterlogged soil. Nitrogen is the plant food that keeps leaves green so the crop can feed itself and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu eyi mli obɔ. Nitrogen ji tso niyenii ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli koni tsei lɛ anyɛ aye amɛhe niyenii ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds in my field make my crops grow so slowly even when rain is falling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔji amli lɛ haa midumɔ nii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo nɛkɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that drink up the water and eat the natural plant food in the soil faster than your crop can, while also blocking sunlight from reaching your plants' leaves.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ basabasa ni nuɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya fe onibii ni oduɔ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ otso lɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: What causes my maize plants to produce flowers at the top before I see any cobs forming?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miifɔlɔ yɛ ŋwɛi dani ŋmãa lɛ je kpo?

english: The flowers at the top are called tassels, and they appear first to release pollen. That pollen dust drifts down on the wind to catch the silks lower down on the stem, which is what creates the grains on your maize cobs.
ga: Atsɛɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ akɛ tassel. ni ebaaje kpo klɛŋklɛŋ koni ejie pollen. Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa pollen sũ lɛ koni emɔ siliki ni yɔɔ shishi yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni feɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ o-corn cob lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and drop off without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot and dry or when the plant suffers from sudden water shortages, which prevents the flower from successfully setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ naa nu ni faaa trukaa lɛ. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Planting too close forces your crops to fight each other for limited sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in thin, weak plants with very small yields instead of big, healthy harvests.
ga: Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awuu kɛha hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni faaa Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo pɛ baa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooona ŋmɔshi nibii agbo ni mli wa

english: Does local rice always need to stand in flooded water to grow well in Ghana?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ afee nɔ ni nu afua nyɛɔ eshɛɔ he be fɛɛ be koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana?

english: No, while lowland paddy rice loves standing water to control weeds, upland rice varieties are designed to grow in regular moist soil just like maize, relying directly on steady rainfall.
ga: Dabi, eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa sumɔɔ nu ni damɔ shi koni ekɛye jwɛi anɔ moŋ. Shi afee ŋmãa henɔi ni yɔɔ gɔŋ nɔ lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ tamɔ ŋmãa nɔ. Kɛtsɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ nɔ ni akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with lots of leaves but give me small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛlɛ waa shi amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or excessive early rain, it puts all its energy into growing tall branches and leaves above ground instead of storing starch down in the roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei ná nitrogen ŋmei babaoo loo nugbɔ babaoo mra Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ niji kɛ baai ni kwɔlɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ

english: Staking spreads out the yam leaves so they can catch maximum sunlight to make plant food, which directly feeds the tuber underground and makes it grow much larger.
ga: Staking gbɛɔ sweet potato baai lɛ eshwaa koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ ni amɛkɛtsu nii akɛ tsei aniyenii. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ niyenii tɛ̃ɛ ni ehaa amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa tree flowers drop off without forming cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee cacao ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees shed flowers when they are stressed by hot sun, dry spells, or tiny sap-sucking insects; providing shade trees protects them until they are strong enough to carry pods.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. be mli ni nu lɛ mli egbi loo kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ Shade haa hebuu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ehe wa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why does planting beans or cowpeas in my farm make my next crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans have special roots that grab nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the earth, leaving behind free soil food that helps your next crop grow stronger.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eshiɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eye ebua oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and curling up in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves turn yellow and curl when they get too much direct sunlight or heat stress. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains or bananas next to young cocoa creates a canopy that protects them from harsh sun until they mature.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ tsakeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ hulu la loo dɔlɛ ni fe nine shɛ amɛnɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantain loo banana, yɛ kookoo tso masɛi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes small ragged holes in my young maize leaves with tiny dark droppings inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ amli lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ diŋ yɛ jɛmɛ. Yɛ baa lɛ mli?

english: These holes and droppings are caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on the soft central shoot of the maize plant. Spraying recommended biopesticides or applying neem leaf extracts into the whorls early in the morning helps clear them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ shi loo okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu lɛ wo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie ŋmeii nɛɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before any fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers fall off when plants experience heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients like potassium. Regular watering during hot spells and adding well-rotted manure helps the flowers stay attached and form peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ potassium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ, ni akɛ ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo ŋmeii.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning pale yellow starting from the leaf tips down the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛyitseiaŋ kɛyaa amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing along the center of maize leaves is a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Applying NPK fertilizer or well-decomposed animal manure around the root zone early in the growth stage will restore leaf color and boost growth.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ lɛ abɔle ehe. Shishifã he yɛ shishijee dalɛ mli Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ baai lɛ ahe su aku sɛɛ aba ni eha dalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why should I put dried animal dung or decayed crop waste into my soil before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he dani madu?

english: Dried manure and plant waste act as organic fertilizer, improving the soil's ability to hold water and slowly feeding essential nutrients to your crop's roots throughout the growing season.
ga: Nibii ni egbi kɛ tsei amli nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛmɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu mli lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni fiofio lɛ, ehaa otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa fiofio yɛ nugbɔ babaoo ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than main crops and steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from your crops' roots. Removing weeds early gives your crops full access to the nutrients they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa otsei lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Will planting my maize seeds closer together give me a bigger harvest on my plot?
ga: Ani ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛduɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ baaha maná ŋmaa babaoo?

english: No, planting too close forces crops to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stalks and smaller cobs. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to produce a large, healthy yield.
ga: Dabi, dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ abɔ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to put wooden sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam is a climbing plant that needs wooden stakes to lift its leaves off the ground into sunlight. Lifting the leaves helps the plant gather solar energy to develop large, heavy tubers under the soil.
ga: Sweet potato ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ ni akɛ tsei awo amɛnɔ koni amɛwo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ. Baai lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ebuaa hulu hewalɛ naa koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni tsii aba.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground in wet soil before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water suffocates them in heavy or flat soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli, ni no haa amɛmuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: How do I know when it is safe to plant my crops after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ehi akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eba naagbee lɛ?

english: It is safest to plant after the main rains have fallen consistently for at least two weeks so the soil stays moist deep down. Planting during early single rains can cause seeds to sprout and then wither if dry conditions return.
ga: Gbɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ ji kɛ hoo lɛ, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ otsii enyɔ sɛɛ. koni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashɛ shishigbɛ Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ Baanyɛ aha dumɔwui akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ ku amɛsɛɛ amɛba.

english: Why does a new improved seed variety give a better harvest than the seeds I save from my own farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni atsake lɛ haa ŋmaa kpakpa fe dumɔwui ni mibuaa naa kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their strength over generations and can carry hidden diseases. New improved seeds are specially bred by scientists to resist common pests, withstand weather changes, and focus their energy on producing bigger grains or tubers.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ aba. Jeŋ nilelɔi ekwɛ dumɔwui heei ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo kooloi ni fɔɔ baa lɛ. Ekɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kpeɔ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa dumɔwui wuji loo bulbs ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my neighbor's crops mature much faster than mine even though we planted at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ tsei lɛ daa oya fe mi nɔ lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ wɔfee ekome kɛdu amɛ moŋ?

english: Different plant varieties have different internal clocks. Early-maturing crop varieties are designed to grow and produce harvest quickly before the dry season starts, while traditional varieties take a longer time to complete their growth cycle.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi yɛ mligbɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai srɔtoi. Afee tsei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii oya dani hulutsoo be lɛ aje shishi. yɛ be mli ni blema henɔi lɛ heɔ be babaoo yɛ amɛdalɛ mli.

english: Why do my rice leaves turn yellow when water sits in the field for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Crop roots need to breathe air just like human beings. When heavy water stays trapped in the soil without draining, the roots drown and cannot suck up nutrients from the ground, causing the leaves to starve and turn yellow.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, ehe miihia ni tsei shishifãi amu kɔɔyɔɔ. Beni shwiili lɛ tsiimɔ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa baai lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots are storage organs that need well-drained soil. In soggy, heavy soil, water fills all the air spaces, allowing soil bacteria and fungi to attack and rot the roots while they are still hidden underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ji gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli nibii ni biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni tsii nɔ Nu baayi kɔɔyɔɔ mli he lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ be mli ni amɛhiɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lolo lɛ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yields every time I plant maize on the same field year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Every crop feeds on specific nutrients in the soil. Planting maize continuously drains the exact same plant food every season without giving the soil time to rebuild, making the land tired and weak.
ga: Tsei fɛɛ yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ be fɛɛ be. be mli ni ekɛ be haaa ni ekɛma shikpɔŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ gbɔjɔmɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and thin with tiny fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ aduawai bibii waa lɛ, kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other like crowd members for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. They stretch upward to reach the light, spending all their energy growing tall instead of building big fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei wuɔ tamɔ adesai koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Amɛkpã amɛhe koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Okɛ ohewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni okɛkwɛ shɔŋŋ moŋ fe ni ooofee aduawai agbo.

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn pale and weak even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli po lɛ?

english: Weeds are fast-growing wild plants with strong roots. When you apply fertilizer, the weeds steal the nutrients and water faster than your main crops can drink them, leaving your crops hungry.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni daa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa. Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, jwɛi lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu oya fe bɔ ni tsei ni yɔɔ ohe lɛ baanyɛ anu. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers drop off my pepper plants before they turn into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowering is a stressful task for plants. When the plant suffers from extreme heat, lack of water, or sudden weather changes, it drops its flowers to save energy and protect itself from drying out.
ga: Fɔfɔii afeemɔ ji nitsumɔ ko ni haoɔ mɔ waa kɛha tsei. Kɛ́ tsei miipiŋ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ba trukaa lɛ hewɔ lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why do young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I cut down all the large shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mifolɔ tsei wuji ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and small roots that cannot handle direct, burning sunlight. Tall shade trees act as living umbrellas that keep the air cool and retain soil moisture until the cocoa plants grow strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii. ni nyɛŋ aná hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ tɛ̃ɛ Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ni hiɛ ka ni yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ shishifãi ni wa baa.

english: Why do my rice plants stop growing for a few days after I move them from the nursery to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã tsei lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ gbii fioo komɛi beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is called transplant shock. When you move seedlings, their tiny root hairs get torn, so the plant has to rest and repair its roots before it can start drinking water and growing leaves in the new soil again.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Kɛji okɛ dumɔwu ko wo he kroko lɛ, eshishifãi ahe yitsɔi bibii lɛ fãa, no hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ ajɔɔ ehe ni esaa eshishifãi lɛ dani enyɛ enu nu ni ekwɛ baai heei yɛ sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people tell me to plant plantain trees next to my young cocoa crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ midu dumɔwui yɛ emasɛi lɛ? Mi kookoo tso bibioo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade from direct sunlight so their leaves don't burn. Plantain trees grow very fast and provide natural shade and extra moisture for the young cocoa trees until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ koni amɛkashã baai lɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛhaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe waaa bɔ ni sa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves in the sunlight to make energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves toward the sun and keeps them off the hot, wet soil where diseases easily spread.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulu lɛ mli koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba kɛha bulbs wuji ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akwɛ hulu lɛ hiɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ akadɔ ni edɔ, he ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning pale yellow from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key plant nutrient. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer to the soil helps the leaves turn healthy green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji tso lɛ mli niyenii titri lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata sũ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I mix dried leaves and animal droppings into my farmland before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egbi kɛ ŋmeii afutu midumɔi lɛ amli dani madu?

english: This practice makes natural compost, which acts like rich food for the soil. It helps the soil hold water longer during dry days and gives your crops steady nutrients to grow strong roots.
ga: Nifeemɔ nɛɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni jara wa kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii kpakpai daa koni amɛshishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans together with my maize help my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are special plants that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. This naturally feeds the soil and helps surrounding crops grow bigger without buying extra fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Edaraa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: How do I choose the right cassava stem to cut and plant for a good yield?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ahala ni adu ŋmei tsei koni aná yibii kpakpai?

english: Choose thick, mature stems from healthy plants that are 8 to 12 months old with no insect spots. Strong, woody stems sprout much faster and produce more roots than thin or soft stem tops.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 ni ŋmeii bɛ amɛhe lɛ amli tsei ni mli tse ni eda. Tso tsei ni he wa lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya kwraa ni amɛbaawo shishifãi babaoo fe tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo loo ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain often warms up dry soil, but it is usually followed by a hot dry spell. It is safer to wait until the rainfall becomes steady so your sprouting seeds do not dry up and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ. Shi bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni naa wa waa nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ be fɛɛ be koni dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ akagbi ni amɛgboi.

english: What is making small ragged holes in my young corn leaves with tiny worms inside the central leaves?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-baby corn baai lɛ miifee bu bibii? ni ŋmeii bibii yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: That is likely the Fall Armyworm, a common caterpillar pest that eats corn leaves. You can protect your corn by checking the plants early and applying recommended remedies directly into the central leaf funnel.
ga: No baafee Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai. Obaanyɛ obu o-corn lɛ he kɛtsɔ otsei lɛ ni oookwɛ mli mra lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ awo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Does leaving weeds in my vegetable farm really reduce my harvest?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni mashi yɛ mi-aduawai ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, weeds act like thief plants that steal water, sunlight, and plant food directly from your crops, which makes your vegetables small and weak.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, jwɛi lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ tsei ni juɔ, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa o-vegetables lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Why are flowers dropping off my tomato plants without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant does not get enough water. Keeping the soil moist and adding light shade during extreme heat helps the plant hold its flowers and form fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ anine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni akɛ hulutsoo bei ni mli edɔ waa lɛ fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why does it take so many years for a mango tree to start giving fruit compared to maize or cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii babaoo dani mango tso woɔ yibii kɛ akɛtoɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Tree crops spend their first few years building deep root systems and strong trunks so they can support heavy fruit harvests for decades, unlike seasonal crops like maize that complete their whole lifecycle in a few months.
ga: Tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ heɔ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ dani amɛtoɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ shishifãi ni wa. Koni enyɛ ekpa aduawai babaoo afii nyɔŋmai abɔ. Enɛ tamɔɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni gbeɔ amɛwala be fɛɛ naa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli lɛ.

english: Why do some of my mango trees drop their flowers before the fruits even start to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tsei lɛ ekomɛi shwieɔ shi dani aduawai po jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ lɛ?

english: Mango trees drop flowers when they suffer from dry spells during flowering, or when fungal diseases like anthracnose and small insect pests attack the blossom stems. Proper watering and spraying before flowering help flowers set fruit.
ga: Mango tsei baawo fɔfɔi kɛji amɛna piŋmɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. aloo kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ anthracnose kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tutua fɔfɔii ahe tsei. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ dani fɔfɔi lɛ woɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why does the agricultural office advise us to plant mango trees in straight lines with wide spacing between them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu mango yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ ni sɛɛ jɛkɛmɔ ahi tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Wide, straight spacing ensures every tree receives enough sunlight, airflow, and soil nutrients, while making it much easier to walk through the farm to spray, prune, and harvest without crowded branches.
ga: Gbɛ ni mli kwɔ, ni ja lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la. kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ aaatsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ayafɔ̃, afolɔ ni akpa ni tsei niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ bɛ mli.

english: Is it good for me to plant cassava or vegetables in between my young mango trees?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmei loo aduawai yɛ mango tsei ateŋ?

english: Yes, intercropping young trees with short-term crops like beans or vegetables gives you food and income while the trees are growing, keeps weeds down, and makes good use of the open land before the tree canopy closes.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei bibii ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kukuoo tamɔ ŋmeii loo aduawai baadu lɛ baaha oná niyenii kɛ shika yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ miida lɛ, ebaagbe jwɛi, ni okɛ he ni yɔɔ faŋŋ lɛ atsu nii dani tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ aŋmɛ.

english: Why are many farmers in my community switching from growing tomatoes to planting cashew and mango trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo ni yɔɔ mikutso lɛ mli lɛ miitsake kɛmiijɛ tomato dumɔ mli kɛmiiya cashew kɛ mango tsei dumɔ mli lɛ?

english: Tree crops like mango and cashew require less daily labor and watering once established, resist drought better than vegetables, and provide a reliable long-term harvest every year for decades.
ga: Tsoi ni yɔɔ jwɛi mli tamɔ mango kɛ cashews biɔ daa gbi nitsumɔ kɛ nu fioo kɛji amɛto amɛhe shi. Eteɔ shi ewoɔ hɔmɔ jogbaŋŋ fe aduawai. ni ekɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni heɔ be kakadaŋŋ haa daa afi kɛyashiɔ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ.

english: Why does my mango tree give me a massive harvest one year, but very few fruits the following year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei woɔ yibii babaoo nɛkɛ yɛ afi kome mli lɛ? Shi afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ewo yibii fioo ko pɛ?

english: Mangoes naturally experience 'alternate bearing,' where a heavy harvest drains the tree's stored energy, requiring the following year to rest and rebuild nutrient reserves unless it receives regular fertilizer and pruning.
ga: Mango naa adebɔɔ mli ‘tsakemɔ’ ko ni ŋmaakpamɔ ni tsii fiteɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ. Ehe miihia ni amɛkɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ajɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛsaa amɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ. Ja amɛná ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa.

english: How do I know if my land is suitable for growing fruit trees like mangoes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha tsei ni woɔ yibii tamɔ mango?

english: Fruit trees need deep, well-drained soil where water does not stand in pools after heavy rain, allowing their deep taproots to search for underground water without rotting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ he miihia tsei ni woɔ yibii. He ni nu nyɛŋ ahi nubu lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ. Enɛ haa shishifã ni mli kwɔ lɛ taoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni egbooo.

english: Why do the leaves on my young fruit trees turn yellow and fall off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing and leaf loss during dry periods are a tree's natural defense mechanism to conserve water, as dropping leaves reduces moisture loss through transpiration until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛlaajeɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛbuɔ nu he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: What is the difference between planting local mango seeds directly in the ground and buying grafted seedlings from government nurseries?
ga: Mango ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni akɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahemɔ kɛjɛ nɔyeli dumɔwui akwɛmɔhei. Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ amɛsoro amɛhe?

english: Grafted seedlings combine the best fruit varieties with strong rootstocks, producing fruit in just 3 to 4 years with uniform size and taste, whereas trees grown from local seeds can take up to 7 years to fruit and produce unpredictable yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ kɛ aduawai srɔtoi ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ kɛ shishifã ni yɔɔ hewalɛ feɔ ekome. Amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 pɛ mli ni amɛdalɛ kɛ amɛmli ŋɔɔmɔ yaa nɔ daa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni akɛ dumɔwui duɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii kpawo dani amɛwo yibii ni amɛwo yibii ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba.

english: Why do fruit flies attack my mangoes just when they start getting sweet and ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii tutuaa mi mangoi lɛ be mli ni amɛmli ŋɔɔ ni amɛshwere lɛ?

english: Fruit flies are attracted to the sweet smell and soft skin of ripening fruit to lay their eggs inside; hanging pheromone traps early in the season and picking fruits just as they begin to turn yellow prevents them from getting spoiled.
ga: Aduawai amli ŋmeii lɛ sumɔɔ aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ahewolo ni ŋɔɔ kɛ amɛhewolo ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ koni amɛwo amɛwui yɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ pheromone tsɔnei fĩ shi yɛ be lɛ mli mra, ni oootsi aduawai beni ebɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekafite.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up into tight tubes during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, maize plants roll their leaves inward to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun. This is a natural defense mechanism to stop water from evaporating out of the plant too fast during peak heat.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Abɛi tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he koni nu akajɛ tsei amli oya tsɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep falling off without forming fruits when the weather is very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses pepper plants and makes their pollen dry out and become infertile. When flowers fail to get pollinated due to high temperatures, the plant drops them to conserve its energy and water.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa chili tsei anɔ. ni ehaa pollen lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe. Beni fɔfɔii nyɛɛɛ afee pollin yɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa hewɔ lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛ fɔfɔii lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he.

english: Why are dry white patches developing on the sides of my tomatoes that face direct midday sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni egbi yɛ mi-tomato lɛ afãi ni hulu ni tsoɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called sunscald. Just like human skin burns under intense heat, raw fruits left unprotected under strong, direct sunlight get scorched, causing the fruit skin to dry out and turn papery white.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ hulutsoo. Taakɛ gbɔmɔ hewolo shãa yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shishi lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Yibii ni ahoko ni ashi ni abuuu he yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi lɛ baashã. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso yibii lɛ ahewolo lɛ gbiɔ ni efeɔ futafuta tamɔ wolo.

english: Why are my leafy green vegetables producing small leaves and jumping straight to flowering when the sun gets hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-green lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi trukaa kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he lɛ?

english: High temperatures signal to the plant that conditions are becoming harsh. In response, the crop panics and rushes to produce flowers and seeds to ensure its survival before it dies, a process known as bolting.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli wa lɛ haa tso lɛ leɔ akɛ shihilɛi miitsake. Emiifee hiɛdɔɔ sane waa. Yɛ hetoohamɔ mli lɛ, Dumɔwui sheɔ gbeyei ni amɛyaa oya koni amɛwo fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui koni amɛkwɛ akɛ amɛhi shi dani amɛgboi. Enɛ ji gbɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ bolting.

english: How does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass help them handle hot weather?
ga: Mulching around Te miŋmɔshi nibii ni jwɛi yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ kpeɔ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Spreading dry grass or crop leaves—known as mulching—acts like an insulating blanket. It shields the ground from direct sun rays, keeping the soil cool and stopping soil moisture from evaporating quickly into the air.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ahe baai ni agbɛɔ ashwãa, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni haa hulutsoo baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Is it better for me to water my crop field early in the morning or during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mitsei lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: It is best to water early in the morning while the soil and air are still cool. Watering in the heat of the day causes most of the water to evaporate instantly into the air before the roots can soak it up.
ga: Esa akɛ afee nu lɛ leebi be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ lolo lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋɔ nu lɛ.

english: Which food crops can survive better naturally in very hot and dry regions compared to delicate vegetables?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii tsei baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa ni jɛmɛ egbi lɛ? Kɛ akɛto aduawai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe

english: Crops like sorghum, millet, cowpea, and cassava have deep root systems and tough outer leaf layers that allow them to handle hot temperatures and dry soils much better than soft vegetables like lettuce or cucumber.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, tsina ŋmãa, kɛ ŋmãa Eyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ kponɔgbɛ baa ni mli wa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei nɛɛ ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛkpeɔ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ naa jogbaŋŋ fe aduawai ni yɔɔ blɛoo tamɔ lettuce loo kukumba.

english: Why do my tomato and vegetable seeds fail to sprout when I sow them directly into hot ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato kɛ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Extremely hot soil can cook seeds or force them into a heat-induced deep sleep where they refuse to germinate. Starting seeds in shaded seedling trays where the temperature is cooler gives them the conditions they need to sprout.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ loo enyɛ amɛnɔ ni amɛwɔ wɔɔ ni mli kwɔ ni dɔlɛ kɛbaa lɛ. kɛ dumɔwui lɛ kpooɔ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ Dumɔwui ni ajeɔ shishi yɛ dumɔwui atoohe ko ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná shihilɛi ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Can growing taller crops like maize next to lower crops like beans help protect the smaller crops from heat?
ga: Ani tsei ni kɛlɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ ahe lɛ baabu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he?

english: Yes, planting tall crops alongside low crops creates beneficial shade and acts as a windbreak. The taller plants lower the surrounding temperature for smaller plants beneath them, protecting them from heat stress.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei kakadaji ni aduɔ yɛ tsei kukuji ahe lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ baa ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsimɔ. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baa shi kɛha tsei bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ. Koni abu tsei ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he

english: Why do crops grown inside a shaded nursery structure grow better than those outside in direct heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo mli lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni yɔɔ kpo nɔ yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Shade structures block extreme solar radiation and lower the surrounding air temperature by several degrees. This keeps crops inside an ideal temperature range, allowing them to focus energy on growing leaves and roots instead of fighting heat stress.
ga: Shade gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. ni ebaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli latsaa lɛ shi digrii babaoo Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii ahiɔ latsaa ni sa mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baa kɛ shishifãi adalɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooowu oshi dɔlɛ he haomɔ

english: Why does the extension service recommend cutting down my sick cocoa trees instead of just spraying them with medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsumɔhei ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ afolɔ kookoo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ moŋ fe ni akɛ tsofa baashwie nɔ lɛ?

english: Some serious crop diseases, like Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, have no chemical cure. Cutting down the infected trees removes the source of the virus so it cannot spread through sap, roots, or insects to the healthy trees on your farm and neighboring farms.
ga: Anyɛɛɛ akɛ tsofai atsa tsei ahe helai komɛi ni naa wa waa, tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus lɛ. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni abaakpa lɛ baajie he ni hela lɛ jɛ lɛ kɛya. Enɛ ji koni ekatsɔ nu mli nu, shishifãi loo kooloi bibii anɔ egbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ amli.

english: If one tree on my farm gets sick, can the disease move to the healthy trees next to it?
ga: Kɛji hela mɔ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ ekome Ani hela lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, many crop diseases spread easily to neighboring healthy trees through insect vectors like mealybugs, direct branch-to-branch contact, shared farm tools, or root connections underground.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai babaoo gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli mlɛo kɛtsɔɔ kooloi bibii ni kɛ hela lɛ baa tamɔ mealybugs, ni jɛɔ tso nine kome mli kɛyaa tso nine kroko nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Okwaafoi anitsumɔ nibii loo shikpɔŋ shishi shishifã tsakpaa

english: Why is my farm dying bit by bit over time instead of all at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ gboɔ fiofio yɛ be ni sa mli moŋ fe fɛɛ shikome lɛ?

english: Diseases usually start in a small patch and spread gradually from one tree to adjacent trees. As insects move from tree to tree or roots touch underground, the infection expands slowly across the field year after year.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai jeɔ shishi bibii ni fiofio lɛ, amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ kooloi bibii jɛ tso kome nɔ kɛtee tso kroko nɔ loo shishifãi lɛ ta shikpɔŋ shishi. Hela lɛ baaya hiɛ fiofio. Egbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ daa afi

english: Why should I agree to cut down a sick tree if it is still producing a few cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ mafo tso ni hela mɔ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ tsei woɔ kookoo ŋmeii lolo yɛ?
