english: Even if a diseased tree still yields a few pods, it acts as a dangerous breeding ground for the disease. Keeping it alive allows the infection to spread, which will eventually destroy your entire farm and cause much bigger losses later.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tso ni hela emɔ lɛ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo komɛi pɛ lolo po lɛ, Shi etsuɔ ​​nii hu akɛ he ni helai ni yɔɔ oshara fɔɔ yɛ. Kɛ́ okɛto he ko lɛ, ebaaha hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã. ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaafite oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ. ni ekɛ fitemɔi wuji baa sɛɛ mli.

english: Does my cocoa farm become more likely to catch diseases as the trees get very old?
ga: Ani helai baa mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ babaoo be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Yes, older cocoa trees—especially those around 30 to 50 years old—lose their vigor and immune strength over time, making them much more vulnerable to infections, pests, and harsh environmental conditions.
ga: Hɛɛ, cacao tsei ni edara Titri lɛ tsei ni eye aaafee afii 30 kɛyashi 50 lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli hewalɛ ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa helai, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, kɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai baa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: How many years can a cocoa tree continue to produce good pods before it gets too old?
ga: Afii enyiɛ cacao tso baanyɛ awo ŋmeii kpakpai dani egbɔ tsɔ?

english: A cocoa tree typically produces its highest yields between 10 and 25 years of age. After 30 to 50 years, productivity drops significantly, and the old trees become more susceptible to diseases and decay.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei lɛ shɛɔ amɛyibii babaoo he beni amɛye kɛjɛ afii 10 kɛyashi 25 lɛ. Yɛ afii 30 kɛyashi 50 sɛɛ lɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi waa. Ni tsei ni edara lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ helai kɛ fitemɔ oya.

english: How can I tell if my old cocoa farm is suffering from a disease or just dying of old age?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kookoo ŋmɔ momo lɛ miipiŋ loo miigbo kɛkɛ yɛ onukpayeli hewɔ?

english: Old age causes a slow, even decline in yield across the tree, while diseases cause specific symptoms like swollen stems, red leaf veins, yellowing patterns, dieback of branches, or sudden wilting in patches.
ga: Kɛ́ mɔ ko eda lɛ, ehaa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feemɔ yaa hiɛ fioo po. Yɛ be mli ni helai srɔtoi Ekɛ okadii pɔtɛɛ komɛi tamɔ tsei ni efuu, baai tsuru, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, tsei niji ni egboi, loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi trukaa yɛ hei komɛi baa.

english: If my diseased cocoa trees are cut down to stop an outbreak, will I get any help or compensation to start over?
ga: Kɛji akɛ afolɔ kookoo tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ koni akɛkpa hela lɛ, Ani maná yelikɛbuamɔ loo nyɔmɔwoo koni mabɔi shishijee ekoŋŋ?

english: Yes, government extension programs often provide financial compensation per hectare, free high-yielding hybrid seedlings, and technical support to help farmers clear, treat, and replant affected cocoa farms.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ maŋ nɔyeli hiɛyaa gbɛjianɔtoi haa shika nyɔmɔwoo yɛ hectare fɛɛ hectare mli. Hybrid dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni aheee nɔ ko kɛ ŋaa gbɛ nɔ yelikɛbuamɔ ni baaye abua okwaafoi ni amɛjie, amɛtsa, ni amɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji ni ena naagbai lɛ amli.

english: What should I do immediately if I suspect a serious disease has entered my farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji misusu akɛ hela ko ni naa wa ebote miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You should contact an extension officer right away to inspect your farm, correctly diagnose the issue, and guide you on whether to isolate, treat, or safely remove the infected trees before the problem gets worse.
ga: Esa akɛ oyana extension nitsulɔ ko amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni ekwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kwɛmɔ naagbai lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni owo bo ŋaa yɛ bɔ ni ooofee otsi tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ahe, otsa amɛ, loo oshɛrɛ amɛ ashwie shweshweeshwe dani naagba lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What steps do I need to take to replant my farm after cutting down diseased trees?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii esa akɛ mafee koni manyɛ madu miŋmɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ beni mifo tsei ni helai emɔ amɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: After removing infected trees and clearing the land, you need to plant fast-growing shade crops like plantains first. Once good shade is established, you can plant new, disease-resistant cocoa hybrid seedlings provided by extension services.
ga: Beni ojie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ojie he ni oyɔɔ lɛ, Obaasumɔ ni odu tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya, tamɔ plantains, klɛŋklɛŋ, kɛji amɛná hulutsoo jogbaŋŋ. Obaanyɛ odu kookoo dumɔwui heei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni sɔɔmɔ lɛ woɔ he hewalɛ lɛ.

english: Officer, why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the top leaves are still green?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ shi ŋwɛi baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your plants are hungry for nitrogen. The plant moves nitrogen from old lower leaves up to feed the new growth at the top, showing you it needs fertilizer or compost.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye otso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha nɔ hee ni eda yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Etsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and look limp during the hot afternoon sun, but go back to normal at night?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Shi gbɛkɛ mli lɛ, ekuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Plants lose water quickly through their leaves in intense heat. By curling up and drooping, the plant reduces its leaf surface area exposed to the sun to hold onto moisture until cool night air arrives.
ga: Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Kɛtsɔ amɛhe ni amɛfoɔ kɛ amɛgbee shi lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baa amɛbaai lɛ anɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ gbɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ lɛ baashɛ.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together in large numbers, won't I get a bigger harvest from my farm?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe Ani mana yibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close, crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition leaves you with thin, weak plants that produce tiny harvests compared to properly spaced plants.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa onáa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛ akɛto tsei ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the stem before any fruit starts to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat, severe drought, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. When stressed, the plant drops its blossoms to save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. hɔmɔ ni naa wa loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he koni amɛhi wala mli.

english: Why is it harmful to let tall weeds grow around my young yam mounds for just a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi kakadaji akwɛ̃ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mi-sweet potato bibii ni mikɛtoɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ mli lɛ yɛ oshara.

english: Weeds grow faster than crop seedlings and quietly steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight your yams need. Clearing weeds early ensures young yam roots build big tubers without underground competition.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei amli dumɔwui ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa o-sweet potato lɛ dioo. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ baaha sweet potato shishifãi bibii lɛ afee bulbs wuji ni shikpɔŋ shishi akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cut off healthy-looking leafy branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mifolɔ tso lɛ niji fɛfɛji ni yɔɔ baai lɛ?

english: Removing excess upper branches opens the tree to sunlight and lets fresh air circulate. Good airflow dries out extra moisture that causes fungal diseases like black pod, allowing energy to go directly into cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la shɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni baanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni feɔ diŋ lɛ aba lɛ, ni ehaa hewalɛ hoɔ kɛboteɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How do fall armyworms destroy my maize leaves so quickly without me noticing when they first arrive?
ga: Fall cutworms miigbe mi-corn foliage lɛ oya aahu akɛ mileee bɔ ni fee ni amɛshɛ jɛmɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Fall armyworms lay hundreds of tiny hidden eggs on the undersides of leaves that hatch rapidly. The young caterpillars crawl inside the tight central funnel of the plant to feed, staying hidden until major leaf damage shows.
ga: Autumn flukes woɔ ŋmeii bibii. Akɛ ŋmeii ohai abɔ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni shwereɔ oya lɛ ehiɛ. Kplukai bibii shwieɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi ni mli wa lɛ amli koni amɛyatao niyenii. Akɛ amɛ teeɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni baai lɛ fiteɔ waa.

english: Why shouldn't I put all my fertilizer into the soil on the very same day I plant my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbi kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ duɔ lɛ?

english: Young seeds only need a tiny amount of nutrients to start. Applying all your fertilizer at planting can burn tender new roots and allows heavy rains to wash away expensive nutrients before the plant grows big enough to drink them.
ga: Niyenii fioo ko pɛ he hiaa dumɔwui bibii koni amɛje shishi. Nibii fɛɛ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli yɛ dumɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã shishifãi heei blɛoo. Ni ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni jara wa lɛ nɔ dani tsei lɛ daraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛnuɔ.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant maize on the exact same plot every single farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same soil nutrients and gives crop-specific pests and diseases a permanent home to multiply. Rotating with cowpeas or groundnuts rebuilds soil fertility naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite. ni ehaa tsei amli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ naa shia ni amɛfɔɔ daa. Kɛ́ okɛ cowpeas loo peanuts tsake lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I save seeds from my high-yielding hybrid maize harvest to plant again next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred for peak strength in their first generation only. If you save and replant those seeds, the second generation loses that strength, resulting in uneven growth and a much smaller yield.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Kɛji obua nakai dumɔwui lɛ anaa ni odu ekoŋŋ lɛ Yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahewalɛ baaje amɛdɛŋ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa baa, ni yibiiwoo hu baa shi kwraa.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to direct sunlight and can easily burn. Fast-growing plantain leaves act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and keeping the soil cool and moist while the cocoa establishes roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshã oya. Plantain baai ni daa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ. Ha hulutsoo ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for green growth. The plant starves and pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to support new top growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Hɔmɔ baaye lɛ ni ebaagbala nitrogen kɛjɛ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei anɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the dry soil around my tomato plants with dried grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni bɔle mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket. It traps moisture in the ground, reduces weed growth, and keeps plant roots cool during hot days.
ga: Mulching ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fũuɔ Ehaa jwɛi lɛ adalɛ baa shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants need clear access to sunlight to make energy in their leaves. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they catch maximum sunlight, which directs energy into growing large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ hia hulu la ni mli tse koni amɛná hewalɛ amɛha amɛbaai lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akaje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ baaha aná hewalɛ ni akɛbaakwɛ bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the inner leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a destructive pest that hides inside the central funnel of maize to feed on tender leaves, which can stunt crop growth if left untreated.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii, ni baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ adalɛ aba shi kɛji akɛ atsaaa amɛ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot quickly depletes specific soil nutrients and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil season after season.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛi baa shi oya. ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do my pepper plants give small fruits when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, their roots fight each other for water and soil nutrients, while their leaves shade each other. This competition leaves less energy for developing large peppers.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛfee chili ŋmeii wuji lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground when heavy rains flood my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa eyi miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. Standing water smothers the root system, causing tissues to break down and allowing fungal rot to spread quickly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ baaŋɔ shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa fãji lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa ŋmei ni fiteɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Why are the flowers on my garden egg plants falling off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Flower drop happens when plants experience stress from high heat, dry soil, or a lack of bees and insects to pollinate them. Without pollination or enough water, the plant sheds flowers to save energy.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ pollination loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why should I place fertilizer near the plant stems instead of scattering it all over the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo tso lɛ tso lɛ he moŋ fe ni magbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Burying or placing fertilizer near the base of the crop ensures the plant's roots absorb the nutrients directly, preventing rains from washing it away or feeding surrounding weeds.
ga: Kɛ́ afu loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Etsiɔ nugbɔ naa koni ekafɔ tsei loo jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ niyenii.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my rice so it doesn't spoil in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male nikpamɔ be ni sa? Koni ŋmãa lɛ akafite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You should cut your rice when about 80 to 85 percent of the grains turn a golden-yellow color. Waiting too long causes grains to fall off the stalk onto the ground, while harvesting too early leaves you with small, underdeveloped grains.
ga: Esa akɛ ofo ŋmãa beni ŋmãa lɛ mli aaafee oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 etsɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ. Be kakadaŋŋ ni akɛmɛɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ okpa mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha oná dumɔwui bibii ni ekwɛko.

english: How can I test if my harvested rice is dry enough for storage without using expensive equipment?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji mikpamɔ lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛto ni nibii ni jara wa bɛ mli?

english: You can perform a simple bite test: take a dry grain and press it between your teeth. If it snaps cleanly with a sharp sound, it is dry enough. If it crushes softly, it still contains water and will rot if stored.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee ŋmɔlɔ he kaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛtsɔ dumɔwu ni egbi ni ooonyɛ onyanyɔji ateŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji efo mli jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ Egbi bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ atswa lɛ fioo lɛ, nu baahi mli lolo, ni kɛ́ akɛto lɛ, ebaagbo.

english: Why is keeping my drying area clean so important for my harvested crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ he ni migbiɔ nii yɛ lɛ ni maha ehe atse lɛ he hiaa mikpamɔ lɛ?

english: Drying crops directly on dirty ground introduces sand, small stones, and harmful molds. Drying your harvest on clean tarpaulins or concrete floors keeps the grain safe to eat and significantly increases its market value.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni agbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa ŋã, tɛi bibii, kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui baa. Oŋmɔshi nibii ni ooogbi yɛ tarp loo kɔnkrit ni he tse nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ayeɔ. ni ehaa jara nɔ jara yaa hiɛ waa

english: Why do buyers in the market complain about the quality of locally grown Ghana rice?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayelɔi ni heɔ nii lɛ miiwie huhuuhu yɛ Ghana ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ he lɛ?

english: Buyers often complain because local rice can contain dirt, small stones, or broken grains due to rough harvesting and drying practices. Maintaining high hygiene and careful processing helps local rice match the high quality of imported brands.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ wieɔ amɛshiɔ akɛ ekolɛ muji, tɛi bibii loo ŋmeii ni ekumɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa mli yɛ ŋmãa ni akpaa kɛ egbimɔ ni wa lɛ hewɔ. Hetsemɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ nitsumɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛ ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ baa lɛ yeɔ egbɔ.

english: What steps do I need to take so my rice can meet the standards to be sold in modern supermarkets?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni mi-ŋmãa lɛ ashɛ shishitoo mlai ni esa akɛ ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ jarayeli hei wuji lɛ ahe?

english: Supermarkets require stone-free, clean rice of a single variety packed in neatly sealed bags. You achieve this by planting certified pure seeds, keeping your harvest clean, and using proper destoning and milling machines.
ga: Shwapoi wuji biɔ ŋmãa ni he tse ni tɛ bɛ mli ni akɛwo kotokui ni atsĩ naa mli jogbaŋŋ. Obaanyɛ onine ashɛ enɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui krɔŋŋ ni awo he odase lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Kwɛmɔ hetsemɔ nɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli ni okɛ shredder kɛ penti ni sa atsu nii.

english: What causes my rice grains to break into small pieces during threshing or milling?
ga: Mɛni haa mi ŋmãa lɛ mli fãa bibii bibii? Yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔmɔ loo ŋmãa ŋmɔmɔ be mli?

english: Rice grains crack and break easily if the crop was harvested when it was too dry, or if it was dried too fast under harsh midday heat. Drying your cut rice gradually in mild sunlight prevents the grains from cracking inside.
ga: Omɔ ŋmeii lɛ fãa oya ni amɛkuɔ kɛji akɛ akpa amɛ be mli ni amɛgbi tsɔ. Aloo egbiɔ oya tsɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa ni yɔɔ gbi lɛ mli lɛ shishi. Ni aaagbi ŋmãa ni afo lɛ fiofio yɛ hulu la ni mli jɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baatsi ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafo mli.

english: What is the best way to package my harvested rice so it stays fresh for a long time?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ mawo mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli koni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Pack your fully dried rice in clean, moisture-proof bags and store them off the floor on wooden pallets in a cool, well-ventilated room to protect the crop from dampness and pest damage.
ga: Okɛ o-rice ni egbi lɛ awo kotokui ni he tse ni ŋmɔtɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli. ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ yɛ tsei anɔ yɛ tsu ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ mli. Koni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ fitemɔ ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ he.

english: How can I protect my stored grains from insect attacks without using dangerous chemicals?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmaa ni mikɛto lɛ he koni kooloi akatutua amɛ ni mikɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara tsuuu nii?

english: You can store well-dried grains in special airtight (hermetic) storage bags. These bags seal out oxygen, naturally suffocating any insects and preventing mold growth without needing chemical powders.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmaa ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ awo vacuum (vacuum) kotokui krɛdɛɛi amli. Nɛkɛ kotokui nɛɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa lɛ naa. Enɛ haa kooloi bibii lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. ni atsĩ ŋmeii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ anaa ni akɛ tsofa powda tsuuu nii

english: Why should I weigh my crop on a scale instead of selling it by traditional bag sizes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe yɛ sɛkɛl nɔ moŋ fe ni mahɔ̃ɔ amɛ yɛ blema kotoku lɛ dalɛ naa?

english: Using a weighing scale ensures you are paid fairly for the actual weight of your harvest. Traditional bag measurements often favor the buyer because bags can be overfilled, causing you to lose money on your hard work.
ga: Sɛkɛn ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe lɛ ni okɛaatsu nii lɛ haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ abaawo bo nyɔmɔ ni sa yɛ onikpamɔ lɛ mli tsiimɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ he. Kusum kotokui lɛ adalɛi asusumɔ Bei pii lɛ, ehe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ kɛhaa mɔ ni heɔ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, abaanyɛ awo kotoku lɛ mli kɛyashɛ he ni eyiɔ obɔ. Ehaa ofiteɔ shika kɛjɛɔ nitsumɔ ni wa mli.

english: How does keeping simple written records of my harvest help me make more profit?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmaakpamɔ he saji ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni aŋmala ashwie shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi koni maná sɛɛnamɔ babaoo?

english: Simple record keeping allows you to track your exact production costs, see which farming practices gave you the best yield, and prove your harvest history to major buyers or banks.
ga: Niŋmaa ni yɔɔ mlɛo yeɔ ebua bo ni okwɛɔ nibii ni afee lɛ ahe nyɔmɔwoo pɔtɛɛ. Taomɔ okwaayeli nifeemɔi ni haa yibii kpakpai baa lɛ. ni okɛ okpamɔ he yinɔsane lɛ ama nɔ mi otsɔɔ mɛi wuji loo shikatoohei.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and dry during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants get scorched easily by harsh direct sunlight and lack of water. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa keeps the soil cool and moist, protecting the young plants until they grow strong enough to withstand the sun.
ga: Hulu la ni naa wa kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ shãa cacao tsei bibii lɛ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la lɛ gbɛ.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: When too many shoots grow around a single plantain tree, they steal water, light, and soil nutrients from the main plant. Keeping only one or two healthy shoots allows the main tree to grow bigger and produce heavier bunches of plantain.
ga: Beni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ ebɔleɔ he lɛ Dumɔwu kome baaju nu, la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hi shi lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ adara ni ewo ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow from the middle instead of staying bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is a vital food for growth. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer gives the plant the nutrient boost it needs to stay green and produce full ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ.

english: What is causing tiny holes in my maize leaves and making the young stalks break easily?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ fãa oya?

english: This damage is typically caused by stem borer caterpillars that eat into the stalk. Planting early at the start of the rainy season and clearing old crop stalks after harvest helps break their breeding cycle.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, stem borers ni yeɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli kɛ tsei momo ni abua naa yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ni akumɔ fɔmɔ be lɛ mli.

english: What causes my cassava roots to turn soft and rot in the ground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpaa?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil retains too much water, preventing air from reaching the roots. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds allows extra rainwater to drain away so the roots stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo. Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ egbi ni amɛhe wa.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food that grows the tuber under the ground. Staking holds the vines up to catch sunshine and keeps the leaves off the hot ground where diseases easily spread.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ́ akwɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Okɛ wain tso lɛ awo tso lɛ nɔ koni hulu la ashɛ nɔ ni oha tso lɛ yibii lɛ akashɛ hei ni mli edɔ yɛ ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ he.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers, but the flowers keep falling off without making tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomatoi?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air is too hot or when the plant experiences sudden dry spells. Watering the roots regularly early in the morning helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they can turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na hɔmɔ trukaa. Kɛ́ afɔseɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ nu daa leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔii ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and twisting together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny pests like thrips or mites sucking juices from the underside of the leaves. Sprinkling wood ash or using safe organic sprays early helps keep these pests away and keeps leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Tso sũ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo ni akɛ tsofa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ajie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ. ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How do groundnuts form their pods under the dirt when the flowers grow above the ground?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii feɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ fɔfɔii kwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated, they form long stems called pegs that grow downwards and push into the soil. Once inside the earth, the tips of these pegs expand to grow the groundnut pods.
ga: Beni afee ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ pollen sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs lɛ baafee, ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛya shi ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni eboteɔ je lɛ mli lɛ Pins nɛɛ anaagbee lɛ mli lɛɛɔ koni eha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans make my soil better for my next crop of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans have special root nodules that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop finishes growing, that leftover nitrogen fertilizes the soil naturally for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tso lɛ egbe naa lɛ Nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees alongside my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under full sunlight. Plantain trees grow fast and have large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil cool, helping cocoa seedlings survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hɔɔŋ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb up off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso koni enyɛ ekwɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to reach high sunlight to make energy for growing large tubers. Keeping vines off the damp soil also prevents leaves from rotting and protects the crop from fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs wuji ni baakwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ wain tso lɛ tee shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ hu, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ, ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why should I wait until the rains are steady before sowing my maize seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ akpa dani madu ŋmãa?

english: Maize seeds need continuous moisture to germinate and build roots. If you plant in dry or lightly wet soil, the seeds may dry out, rot, or get eaten by insects before they can sprout.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui he hiaa nu daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi. Kɛji odu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo efɔ fioo nɔ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ agbi, amɛgboi, loo koolooi baaye amɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. When nitrogen is low, the plant steals food from older bottom leaves to feed the young growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa Tso lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni eda ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep falling off without forming peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛfeee pepper lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress from high heat, dry soil, or poor pollination. Keeping soil evenly moist helps flowers stay on the stem and turn into fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo pollination ni ehiii lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants twisting and curling up tight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies spreading viral diseases, or by excessive heat and uneven watering. Catching insects early stops the spread.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa mli. Kɛ́ amɔmɔ kooloi bibii mra lɛ, ebaaha hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã

english: Why do weeds slow down the growth of my crops so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ oya nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are fast-growing thieves that compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, taking away essential food your crops need to mature.
ga: Jwɛi ji julɔi ni daa oya ni kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eheɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa otso lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Growing maize repeatedly on the same spot depletes specific nutrients and allows pests to build up in the soil. Rotating with cowpeas or groundnuts restores nitrogen to the land.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi baa shi ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsina loo ŋmei tsake lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are ready to dig up without harvesting the whole field?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Cassava is usually ready around 9 to 12 months when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack from expanding roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli, be mli ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ beni shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it bad to spray liquid fertilizer or water on my crops in the middle of a hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mafɔ nu loo nu mli ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hot midday sun causes water to evaporate rapidly before plants can drink it. Sunlight reflecting through water droplets on hot leaves can also scorch the plant surfaces.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya dani tsei nyɛɔ amɛnuɔ. Hulu la ni jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ nu mli nu ni hoɔ yɛ baai ni mli edɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does my cassava crop yield well in sandy soil, but my maize struggles to grow on that same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋã shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ? Shi mi-abele lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ.

english: Cassava has deep, tough roots that can search far for water and store food in poor, sandy soil. Maize has shallow roots and needs rich soil that holds plenty of water and nutrients near the surface to produce good ears.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa ni baanyɛ atao nu kɛya shɔŋŋ ni ekɛ niyenii ato shikpɔŋ ni ehiii ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni ehe miihia shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni nu kɛ niyenii babaoo yɔɔ mli ni bɛŋkɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ koni ekɛfee toi kpakpai.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans on my farm make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants die, that nitrogen stays in the soil as natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my green maize plants turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of the plant usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential food in the soil that gives plants their green color and healthy leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni haa tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli kɛ baai ni wa

english: Why is my pepper plant growing plenty of big green leaves but no flowers or peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi fɔfɔii loo ŋmeii bɛ?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen or shade, they spend all their energy making leaves and stems instead of producing flowers and fruits. Reducing shade and balancing crop nutrients encourages flowering.
ga: Kɛ tsei ná nitrogen loo shade babaoo Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ feɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yiblii. Shade ni abaaba shi kɛ tsei amli niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɛ fɔfɔi.

english: Why do the leaves of my cowpea plants curl up and dry out when small insects gather underneath them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ kooloi bibii bua amɛhe naa yɛ amɛshishi lɛ?

english: Tiny insects like aphids sit under leaves to suck out the plant's water and juices. This damages the leaves, causing them to curl up and lose their ability to make food for the crop.
ga: Kplukai bibii, tamɔ aphids, taraa baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛnu nu kɛ nu kɛjɛ tsei amli. Enɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ. Enɛ haa ebɔleɔ ehe ni enyɛɛɛ efee niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii dɔŋŋ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant plantains next to my newly planted cocoa shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu plantains yɛ kookoo tsei ni adu ehee lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under strong, open sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have wide leaves that act like living umbrellas, giving young cocoa trees the shade and cool moisture they need to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni mli tse lɛ shishi. Plantain ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my vegetable seeds very close together instead of giving them space?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ midu aduawai dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ he ni maha amɛ gbɛ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crowded plants fight each other for limited sunlight, soil food, and water. This leaves all of them small, weak, and produce lower yields.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ hulu la ni faaa, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋ. Enɛ haa amɛ fɛɛ amɛfeɔ bibii, amɛgbɔjɔ, ni ehaa nibii ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and stronger than my main crops even when they sprout at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe mitso titri lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ be kome mli moŋ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops. Clearing them early stops them from starving your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baatsi oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni hɔmɔ akaye amɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their blossoms without making tomatoes during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɛɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni mifeee tomato yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive rain and cold temperatures shock tomato flowers and wash away pollen before insects can spread it. Without successful pollination, the flower dies and falls off the stem.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni mli edɔ lɛ haa tomato fɔfɔii lɛ ahe feɔ shoo ni ejieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Kɛji akɛ pollination lɛ yeee omanye lɛ Fɔfɔ lɛ baagbo ni ebaagbee shi kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting so fast when I leave them under direct sunshine after digging them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mishi amɛ yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ beni mifo amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are alive after harvest and contain water. Direct hot sun bakes and damages their outer skin, causing them to lose water quickly and allowing rot fungus to enter through the heat-damaged skin.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ, ni nu yɛ mli. Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ shãa amɛhewolo ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ ni efiteɔ lɛ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. ni oha ŋmeii lɛ atsɔ hewolo ni dɔlɛ efite lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize start turning yellow when floodwater sits on my farm for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air in the soil to breathe just like people do. When water sits on the field for too long, it pushes all the air out of the soil, causing the roots to choke so they cannot absorb food, which turns the leaves yellow.
ga: Taakɛ gbɔmɛi ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyashɛɔ he ko ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji kaadi ŋmɔŋ

english: Why do my cassava plants shed most of their leaves during the dry season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baa lɛ babaoo shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is the cassava plant's clever way of surviving drought. Leaves lose water to the dry air, so the plant drops them to store its remaining moisture safely in the roots until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni ashwieɔ shi lɛ ji ŋaa gbɛ ni ŋmei tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli. Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi mli. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ shiɔ lɛ koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ ato eshishifãi lɛ amli shweshweeshwe kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Extension officers keep telling me to buy hybrid seeds, but what is a hybrid seed and why is it better?
ga: Extension nitsulɔi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛkɛɛɔ mi akɛ mihe dumɔwui ni akɛ tsofa ewo mli lɛ. Shi mɛni ji dumɔwui ni akɛfutuɔ nii? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehi fe no lɛ?

english: A hybrid seed is created by deliberately crossing two different strong plant parents to combine their best traits, resulting in crops that produce higher yields, grow faster, and handle local diseases better than traditional seeds.
ga: Akɛ tsei enyɔ ni wa ni akɛ amɛsui ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ feɔ ekome lɛ feɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee hybrid lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo. shwereɔ oya ni etsuɔ ​​maŋ lɛ mli helai ahe nii jogbaŋŋ fe blema dumɔwui.

english: Why do some tomato varieties produce all their fruits at once while others keep fruiting for months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato henɔi komɛi woɔ yibii shikome lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni henɔi komɛi tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ nyɔji babaoo lɛ?

english: Tomato varieties have different natural growth behaviors: 'determinate' varieties grow to a fixed size and stop to produce all fruit at once, while 'indeterminate' varieties keep growing tall and producing new flowers and fruits continuously as long as they stay healthy.
ga: Tomato henɔi lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ sui srɔtoi: ‘Determined’ henɔi lɛ daraa kɛyashɛɔ he ko ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni amɛkpaa yibiiwoo shikome. Yɛ be mli ni ‘indeterminate’ henɔi lɛ baaya nɔ adara ni amɛwo fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai heei be fɛɛ be ni amɛyɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my corn leaves curl up into tight rolls during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a plant's natural defense against heat stress. By curling its leaves inward, the plant hides part of its surface from direct sunlight to save water and keep from drying out.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Tso lɛ kɛ ehiɛ fã ko teeɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔ ebaai ni ekɛwoɔ emli lɛ nɔ. Koni ekɛ nu akafite ni eha baai lɛ akagbi.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants fall off without turning into pepper fruits when the sun is too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper aduawai beni hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, the pepper plant gets stressed and drops its flowers to save energy, knowing it does not have enough moisture to support growing heavy fruits.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Nilee akɛ pepper tsei lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua aduawai ni tsii ni amɛdaraa lɛ

english: Why do my vegetable crops grow tall and skinny with tiny leaves if I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ baai bibii lɛ? Kɛji midu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ

english: When crops are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight and air. The plants use all their strength growing upward as fast as possible to reach the light instead of growing thick stems and healthy leaves.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he akaŋ yɛ amɛteŋ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara oya bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Mohu ɔ, mo ha tsohi nɛ a mi mi wa kɛ tsohi nɛ a he wa.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stay greener than my crops when there is little rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya kwraa ni amɛhiɔ shi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be mli ni nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: Wild weeds are naturally adapted to hard conditions and have strong, deep roots that extract hidden soil water and nutrients much faster than cultivated farm crops can.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni mli kwɔ ni gbalaa sũ mli nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ oya fe bɔ ni ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee.

english: Why does planting cowpea or groundnuts on my farm make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have friendly bacteria in their roots that catch nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, providing free natural fertilizer for crops planted afterward.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ naanyobɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji nitrogen lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, eji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on in order to give big tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ lɛ? Kwɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni yitso agbo lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to manufacture food for the plant. Staking lifts the vine up into the sun and air, keeping it away from ground diseases so it can send plenty of stored energy down to build big tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii amɛha tso lɛ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛyaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Etsiɔ hela naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ atsu hewalɛ babaoo ni ato lɛ kɛba shi koni efee yitso agbo.

english: Why are wild animals suddenly eating my ripe cocoa pods when they usually stay deep in the bush?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋa nɔ lɛ miiye mi-kookoo ŋmɔtɔi ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ trukaa lɛ? Akɛni bei pii lɛ amɛhiɔ jwɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ hewɔ lɛ?

english: When natural food sources in the forest dry up or get destroyed, animals like squirrels and monkeys look for alternatives. Ripe cocoa pods are sweet, juicy, and easy for them to access, making your farm an easy target when forest wild fruits are scarce.
ga: Kɛ́ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ kooi amli lɛ mli egbi loo efite lɛ, kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii taoɔ gbɛi krokomɛi ni amɛaatsɔ nɔ amɛye niyenii. Kookoo tsei ni egbɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ, eyɛ nu, ni anyɛɔ ashɛɔ he oya. Ha oŋmɔ lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni okɛbaatsu nii beni koo mli aduawai faaa yɛ koo lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my damaged cocoa pods were eaten by animals or destroyed by black pod disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi ye mi-kookoo ŋmɔji ni efite lɛ loo black pod hela emɔ amɛ?

english: Animal damage usually leaves clear bite marks, scattered husk pieces on the ground, or hollowed-out pods with the beans missing. Black pod disease, on the other hand, makes the pod turn brown or black, soft, and covered in a white powdery fungus without open bite marks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi ni fiteɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔlɔ he okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ baa. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni egbɛ eshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ŋmeii ni etse amɛhe ni kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ bɛ mli lɛ. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, hela ni ji black pod lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ, amɛfeɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ha amɛhe ni ŋmɔtɔ ko bɛ he.

english: What simple methods can I use to stop squirrels and small animals from destroying my cocoa?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo atsu nii. Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafite mi-kookoo lɛ?

english: You can keep small animals away by clearing the bush around your farm boundaries to remove their hiding paths, setting traditional non-lethal traps, or hanging shiny objects and bells in the trees to scare them away with noise and light reflection.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha kooloi bibii akabote he kroko kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ ni oootsi koni ojie amɛgbɛi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Too kusum mli tsɔnei ni gbeɔ mɔ. Aloo okɛ nibii ni kpɛɔ kɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai awo tsei anɔ koni okɛ gbee kɛ hulutsoo awo amɛ gbeyei.

english: Why do forest animals seem to prefer eating cocoa pods over other green plants in my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni koo mli kooloi sumɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii fe tsei krokomɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: Cocoa pods contain a sweet mucilage pulp around the beans that provides quick energy and water for animals. Most other leaves and wild plants do not offer the same high sugar and moisture content as ripe cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ ni tamɔ mucilaginous ni ebɔle kɔfe ŋmeii lɛ ahe ni haa kooloo lɛ hewalɛ oya kɛ nu. Baai kɛ koo mli tsei krokomɛi Mɛi babaoo bɛ sugar kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to harvest and sell cocoa beans from pods that animals have partially chewed?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makpa kookoo ŋmeii ni jɛ ŋmeii ni kooloi eye fã ko lɛ amli lɛ ni mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: It is best to discard beans from pods bitten by wild animals. Animals carry germs and diseases in their saliva that can contaminate the cocoa beans, lower the quality during fermentation, and pose health risks.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshɛrɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni koo mli kooloi emɔ amɛ lɛ ashwie. Koolooi hiɛɔ muawai kɛ helai yɛ amɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli, ni baanyɛ afite kookoo yibii. Nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni ekɛ hewalɛnamɔ he osharai baa

english: Why do animals attack cocoa farms more during certain months of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi tutuaa kookoo ŋmɔji babaoo yɛ afi lɛ mli nyɔji komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Animal attacks usually spike during dry seasons or periods when wild forest fruits are out of season. During these times, crops like cocoa become the main source of food and water for survival in the area.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi tutuamɔ yaa hiɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo be mli ni koo mli aduawai lɛ bɛ be mli. Yɛ nɛkɛ bei nɛɛ amli lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ kookoo ebatsɔ niyenii kɛ nu jɛɛhe titri kɛha wala yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Will clearing the weeds and undergrowth in my cocoa farm stop bush animals from coming in?
ga: Ani jwɛi kɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni mijieɔ lɛ baatsi koo mli kooloi anaa koni amɛkabote mli?

english: Yes, keeping your farm clean removes the cover that rodents and small mammals use to travel safely. Animals dislike open spaces where predators can easily spot them, so a well-weeded farm discourages them from visiting.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ, ejieɔ nɔ ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ fɔmɔ kotoku mli lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfã gbɛ shweshweeshwe lɛ. Koolooi sumɔɔɔ hei ni agbele ni kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ baanyɛ ana amɛ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, atsɔɔɔ amɛ akɛ amɛyasara ŋmɔji ni jwɛi kpakpai yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Can I spray ordinary insecticides to stop rodents and monkeys from eating my cocoa pods?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafɔse tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi daa koni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii akaye mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: No, chemical insecticides are made to kill insects, not mammals like rodents or monkeys. Spraying heavy chemicals on pods to scare animals can poison your crop, harm beneficial insects, and make the cocoa unsafe for human consumption.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi yɛ koni akɛgbe kooloi. Amɛjeee kooloi ni yɔɔ fɔmɔ kotoku mli tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii. Tsofai ni tsii ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ koni akɛwo kooloi ahe gbeyei lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni gbeɔ onibii lɛ. Eyeɔ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ awui ni ehaa kookoo feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha adesa niyenii.

english: What time of the day do most animals usually come to feed on cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbi mli be kooloi fɔɔ baa koni amɛbaye kookoo ŋmeii?

english: Most crop-damaging animals like rodents, bats, and civet cats feed during the late night or early morning when human activity is low. Monkeys, however, usually visit during early morning or late afternoon.
ga: Nibii ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo, tamɔ ŋmeii, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni ji civet cats lɛ tsuɔ nii waa gbɛkɛ loo leebi maŋkpa, be mli ni adesai anifeemɔi tsuuu nii tsɔ lɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, ŋmeii baasara amɛ leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli.

english: Are there barrier crops I can plant around my farm edge to protect my cocoa from wild animals?
ga: Tsei ni tsiɔ nii anaa lɛ yɛ ni manyɛ madu yɛ he fɛɛ he. Ani ŋmɔ mli husui baanyɛ abu kookoo he kɛjɛ koo mli kooloi ahe?

english: Planting thorny crops or strong-smelling barrier plants like citrus, chillies, or thick grass hedges along your farm borders can create a physical barrier that deters animals from easily walking into your main cocoa farm.
ga: Kɛ́ odu tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmeii loo ni shãa mɔ tamɔ ŋmeii, chili, loo jwɛi ni mli edɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ, ebaanyɛ efee gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛtsii nii ko ni tsiɔ kooloi anaa koni amɛkanyiɛ kɛya oŋmɔ titri lɛ mli.

english: What does liquid potassium actually do for my crops?
ga: Te potassium ni ji nu lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Liquid potassium helps plants build strong stems, fight off diseases, and produce larger, sweeter fruits or heavier tubers. Because it is in liquid form, the plant roots absorb it much faster than solid fertilizers.
ga: Potassium ni ji nu lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛmaa shifãi ni wa, amɛwuɔ amɛshiɔ helai, ni amɛwoɔ aduawai wuji, ni ŋɔɔ loo bulbs ni tsii. Akɛni eyɛ nu mli hewɔ lɛ, tso shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ lɛ oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa.

english: Why should I consider using liquid fertilizer instead of the normal granules on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu nu mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ najiaŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: Liquid fertilizer works much faster because plants can drink it immediately through their roots or leaves, making it very helpful when your crops show sudden signs of weakness or nutrient hunger.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii oya kwraa ejaakɛ tsei baanyɛ anu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛtsɔ shishifãi loo baai lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa ehe baa sɛɛnamɔ waa kɛ́ otsei lɛ jie bɔjɔmɔ loo niyenii he hɔmɔ he okadii trukaa.

english: Can I spray liquid fertilizer directly onto the leaves of my crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yes, spraying liquid nutrients directly onto leaves is called foliar feeding. Leaves absorb nutrients quickly through their tiny pores, which gives plants a quick boost, especially when the soil is dry.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɛɔ nu mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ akɛ foliar feeding. Baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli kɛmɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ oya. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi.

english: At what stage of growth do my crops need potassium the most?
ga: Mɛɛ dalɛ mli mi tso lɛ he hiaa potassium fe fɛɛ?

english: Crops need the most potassium when they start flowering and setting fruits or forming tubers, because potassium gives the plant energy to fill out heavy, healthy produce.
ga: Potassium he miihia tsei fe fɛɛ beni amɛjeɔ fɔfɔii afeemɔ shishi ni amɛwoɔ aduawai loo bulbs lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, potassium haa tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ nibii ni tsii ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ amli.

english: What is the best time of day for me to water my crops in hot weather?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mafɔ midumɔ nii lɛ anɔ nu yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Early morning is the best time to water because the soil stays cool longer and absorbs the water deeply before the harsh midday heat causes it to evaporate.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ nu. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baahi shi be kakadaŋŋ ni ebaaŋɔ nu kɛya shɔŋŋ dani gbi lɛ mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baaha etsɔ la.

english: How can I tell if I am giving my crops too much water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ nu babaoo miiha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: If leaves turn yellow, look soft, or start dropping while the soil is constantly muddy, you are giving them too much water, which starves the roots of air.
ga: Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ, etamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ, loo amɛje shishi amɛgbee shi yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo muji be fɛɛ be lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ooha nu babaoo tsɔ. Enɛ baaha nu akafee shishifãi ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Should I water my crops lightly every day or heavily a few times a week?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ nu fioo daa gbi loo mawo amɛ nu babaoo shii fioo komɛi yɛ otsi mli?

english: It is better to water deeply 2 to 3 times a week. Deep watering encourages roots to grow deep into the soil where ground moisture lasts longer during dry days.
ga: Esa akɛ awo mli nu waa shii 2 kɛyashi 3 yɛ otsi mli. Nu ni mli kwɔ haa shishifãi lɛ daa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu ni mli edɔ lɛ baahi shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Is well water or stream water just as good for my crops as rain?
ga: Nubu mli nu loo faa mli nu lɛ hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ nugbɔ loo daabi?

english: Clean well or stream water is good for keeping crops alive, but rainwater is best because it carries natural nitrogen from the air that helps plants turn deep green.
ga: Nubui loo faa mli nu ni mli tse lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Shi nugbɔ nu lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ mli, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli kwɔ.

english: Why are my crop leaves turning yellow around the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ eshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaf edges usually mean the crop is short of potassium or water. When a plant lacks potassium, it cannot move water and food smoothly to the outer tips of its leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ potassium loo nu. Beni tsei bɛ potassium Amɛnyɛŋ amɛjie nu kɛ niyenii kɛya baai lɛ asɛɛgbɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: My crops have big green leaves, but why are they not producing many fruits?
ga: Miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Shi mɛni hewɔ ewooo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Too many leaves with little fruit usually means the plant received too much nitrogen and not enough potassium or phosphorus, which are needed to push the plant to flower and fruit.
ga: Baai babaoo shi aduawai fioo pɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ miiná nitrogen babaoo ni potassium loo phosphorus ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ. ni he hiaa koni akɛtsi tsei anaa koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii

english: Why should I buy new maize seed varieties instead of planting the seeds I saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe ŋmãa dumɔwui heei yɛ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ?

english: New maize varieties are bred by researchers to resist local pests, tolerate drought, and produce bigger yields. Seeds saved from previous harvests lose their strength over generations, leading to weaker plants and smaller cobs.
ga: Nibii amlitaolɔi efɔ ŋmãa henɔ hee ko koni ekɛte shi ewo ŋmãa ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ hɔmɔ ni ewoɔ babaoo Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛhewalɛ kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ hu feɔ bibii.

english: Why does my maize crop sometimes produce small, half-empty cobs even when the leaves look green and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ mi-abele lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? fã efolo Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa po

english: Half-empty cobs usually happen when hot weather or lack of rain disrupts pollination when the tassels and silks appear, or when the soil lacks essential nutrients. Planting newer improved varieties helps the crop pollinate successfully even under mild weather stress.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni fã ko bɛ mli lɛ baa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ tsiɔ pollination naa beni ŋmeii kɛ siliki jeɔ kpo lɛ. aloo be mli ni niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ adumɔ haa tsei lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ehiii po amli.

english: I hear there are several different types of rice seeds available; how do I know which one will grow best on my land?
ga: Mi nu akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui srɔtoi yɛ. Te mafee tɛŋŋ male nɔ ni baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Different rice varieties are developed for specific field conditions—some thrive in low swampy areas that hold water, while upland varieties grow well on dry land with normal rainfall. Choosing the variety designed for your specific soil and water level ensures a good harvest.
ga: Afee ŋmãa henɔi srɔtoi babaoo kɛha shikpɔŋ nɔ shihilɛi pɔtɛɛ komɛi. Tsofai komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni ŋmeii yɔɔ ni nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi yɛ lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni gɔŋ nɔ tsei lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa lɛ. Kɛ́ ohala tsofai srɔtoi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oshikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ kɛ nu lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni onáa ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Do all rice varieties need to grow in flooded water to survive?
ga: Ani esa akɛ adu ŋmãa srɔtoi fɛɛ yɛ nu afua mli koni amɛhi shi?

english: No, not all rice needs standing water. While lowland rice requires flooded fields, upland rice varieties are bred to grow on dry farmland just like maize, depending entirely on normal rainfall.
ga: Dabi, ŋmãa henɔi fɛɛ biɔ nu ni yɔɔ kpoo. Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa he miihia hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ moŋ. Shi atsɔse shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmãa henɔi hu koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ okwaayeli shikpɔji ni egbi tamɔ ŋmãa nɔ. Enɛ damɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does one type of rice take four months to harvest while another variety is ready in just three months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ nyɔji ejwɛ dani anyɛɔ akpaa ŋmãa henɔ ko lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni srɔtofeemɔ kroko baafee klalo yɛ nyɔji etɛ pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Researchers create short-duration rice varieties so farmers can plant and harvest quickly during short rainy seasons, while longer-duration varieties take more time to build up larger yields in areas with reliable, long rains.
ga: Nibii amlitaolɔi fee ŋmãa henɔi ni heɔ be kuku koni okwaafoi lɛ anyɛ adu ni amɛkpa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why are agricultural extension officers always encouraging us farmers to try newly released seed varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ okwaafoi hewalɛ be fɛɛ be koni amɛka dumɔwui heei ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ amɛkwɛ lɛ?

english: Researchers develop new seed varieties to solve emerging challenges that farmers face, such as new crop diseases, unpredictable rainfall patterns, and changing market preferences for grain quality.
ga: Nibii amlitaolɔi feɔ tsei ahe dumɔwui heei Koni amɛkɛtsu naagbai heei ni esa akɛ okwaafoi kɛkpe lɛ ahe nii, tamɔ tsei ahe helai heei Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba kɛ tsakemɔi ni baa jarayeli nibii ni ataoɔ yɛ ŋmaa kpakpa he lɛ mli.

english: How can two different varieties of the same crop planted on the same day behave so differently on my farm?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsei enyɔ ni ji tso kome ni adu yɛ gbi kome nɔ lɛ afee amɛnii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Every variety carries different genetic traits. One variety might focus energy on growing deep roots to withstand dry spells, while another variety focuses on growing thick stems to resist heavy winds.
ga: Henɔi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko yɛ fɔmɔ nii sɔrɔtoi. Ekolɛ henɔ kome kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yaa hiɛ koni enyɛ edamɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ nɔ. yɛ be mli ni henɔ kroko hu kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa tsei ni mli tse ni yaa hiɛ lɛ nɔ koni enyɛ edamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa.

english: Why are my neighbor's maize plants staying green while mine are turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ ji eŋɔli yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbi lɛ?

english: Your neighbor might be growing a modern variety bred for disease resistance or nutrient efficiency, or their soil may have better drainage and organic matter that retains moisture longer.
ga: Ekolɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ miidu ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ. Aloo ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: If the rains start late this season, is there a specific maize variety I should plant to avoid losing my crop?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ bɔi nɛmɔ yɛ be nɛɛ naagbee gbɛ Ani ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ ko yɛ ni esa akɛ madu koni ŋmɔshi nibii akafite?

english: Yes, during short or delayed rainy seasons, you should plant early-maturing maize varieties. These varieties flower and form cobs quickly before the dry harmattan period starts.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo loo esɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ mli Esa akɛ odu ŋmãa henɔi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya. Nɛkɛ tsei srɔtoi nɛɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii oya dani harmatta be ni egbi lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Why do seeds from official seed dealers germinate better than seeds bought from the open food market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni jɛ dumɔwui ajalɔi ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ adɛŋ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni aheɔ yɛ niyenii ajarayelihe ni agbele naa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Certified seeds from official dealers are properly processed, treated against fungi and insects, and tested for high germination rates, whereas grain from the market is meant for eating and often germinates poorly or unevenly.
ga: Atsuɔ dumɔwui ni ana he odaseyeli kɛjɛ jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahe nii jogbaŋŋ. Jiemɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii kɛjɛ mli ni eye kaa ni ji shweremɔ ni yaa hiɛ waa lɛ nɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni jɛ jara nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ koni aye ni bei pii lɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ loo amɛkwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is a nutrient that helps plants stay green and grow strong. When the soil lacks nitrogen, the plant moves what little it has to the newest top leaves, causing the older bottom leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa hewalɛ. Kɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ tsiɔ ehe fioo kɛyaa ŋwɛi baa hee fe fɛɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why does my farm produce smaller cassava tubers when I plant cassava on the exact same field every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmei shishifãi bibii beni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Crops pull specific nutrients from the ground to grow. When you plant cassava in the same spot continuously, it drains all those specific nutrients without giving the soil time to recover, which weakens the soil and results in smaller yields.
ga: Tsei gbalaa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛdara. Beni oduɔ ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa lɛ. Ebaajie nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yibiiwoo fioo.

english: Why shouldn't I dump fertilizer right at the base of my crop stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ mitso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer is full of strong salts that can burn the stems and roots if applied directly against them. It is best to place fertilizer in a small ring or groove a few inches away from the stem so the roots can safely reach out and feed on it.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ eyi kɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa ni baanyɛ ashã tsei lɛ ashishi kɛ shishifãi kɛji akɛ akɛwo mli tɛ̃ɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he yɛ ŋmeii bibii amli. Aloo ŋshɔ lɛ mli ŋshɔ lɛ kɛ ŋshɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ ajie amɛhe kpo ni aye amɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: If I plant my corn seeds very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my small piece of land?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani minine shɛɛɛ yibii babaoo nɔ kɛjɛŋ mihe bibioo lɛ mli?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they end up fighting each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition makes all the plants grow tall and skinny with tiny or empty corn cob yield.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ ha tsei lɛ fɛɛ dara ni amɛfee shwiili kɛ ŋmãa bibioo loo nɔ ko ni bɛ mli ni ji ŋmãa.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain suckers near my young cocoa trees when starting a new cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe beni mijeɔ kookoo ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and can easily burn or dry out under full sunlight. Plantain trees grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshã loo amɛgbi yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ haa.

english: Why do my crops wilt during the afternoon heat even though I watered them two days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ gbii enyɔ ni eho nɛ moŋ?

english: In hot weather, plant leaves lose moisture quickly through tiny pores as they breathe. If the soil around the roots has dried out, the roots cannot suck up water fast enough to replace what is lost to the hot sun, causing the leaves to droop.
ga: yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Tsei ahe baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli beni amɛmuɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli egbi. Shishifãi nyɛŋ aŋɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛto nɔ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ elaaje lɛ najiaŋ. ha baai lɛ agbo

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow short and weak if they are both growing in the same dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ kuku ni egbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ fɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that grow much faster than regular crops, stealing the water, fertilizer, and sunlight your crops need. If weeds are not removed, your crops stay starved of essentials.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni daa oya fe tsei ni daa lɛ, ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ. Kɛji ajieee jwɛi lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa.

english: What is causing tiny ragged holes in my corn leaves and powdery waste in the center of the plants?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli

english: This is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, a pest common in Ghana that hides inside the center whorl of maize plants and eats the tender leaves before they fully unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm caterpillar, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋtayaai amli ni eyeɔ baai bibii dani amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe kwraa lɛ.

english: My cassava plant has grown very tall with plenty of leaves, so why are the tubers under the ground still very small?
ga: Mi-cassava tso lɛ daa waa ni eyɛ baai babaoo. Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: If soil has too much nitrogen or if plants are shaded, the cassava focuses all its energy on growing tall stems and leafy foliage instead of storing food down in the root tubers.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo tsei lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when the bunches start to mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ tsei lɛ aniji je shishi amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots grow shallowly in the soil, and as the fruit bunch grows large and heavy, the top becomes too heavy for the shallow roots to anchor, especially during strong winds or heavy rains unless supported with a prop stick.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ nɔ. Ni kɛ́ aduawai akuu lɛ da ni egbɔjɔ lɛ Yibii lɛ yiteŋ tsii tsɔ ni shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ nyɛŋ aye abua. Titri lɛ, yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. ja akɛ tso ni akɛtsuɔ nii

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and turn brown when the sun gets very bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ egbi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides a protective umbrella that shields the seedlings and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu dumɔwui lɛ ahe, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize turning yellow starting from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the maize plant is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for healthy leaf growth. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the plant regain its deep green color and produce healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ aya hiɛ waa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛbafee ŋmɔji ni mli kwɔ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know which direction to put cassava stem cuttings into the soil when planting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole he ni esa akɛ okɛ o-cassava niji lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava stems must be planted with the tiny buds on the stem nodes pointing upward toward the sky. If you plant the stem upside down, the shoots struggle to grow, leading to weak plants and small tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ adu cassava tsei kɛ fɔfɔi bibii. Tso lɛ yiteŋ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaawa akɛ tso lɛ baakwɛ̃. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ bulb bibii baa.

english: How do the dry Harmattan winds affect my crops, and how can I protect them?
ga: Te Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: Harmattan winds carry dry air and dust that quickly pull moisture out of plant leaves and topsoil. Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass or leaves (mulching) helps lock moisture in the ground and prevents plants from wilting.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ sũ baa. ni gbalaa nu oya kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Mulching around Mulching around Kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi baaha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe (mulching) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa tsei lɛ agbo.

english: Why do flowers keep dropping off my pepper plants before any peppers grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani pepper lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress from irregular watering or extreme heat. Maintaining consistent soil moisture at the roots helps the plant retain its blossoms so they can develop into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛna haomɔ kɛjɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo latsaa ni naa wa mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli koni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: What causes small ragged holes in the central whorl of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Nakai ŋmei ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: These holes are caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that crawl inside the leafy center of maize plants to feed. Early inspection and applying recommended biological or chemical controls prevent them from eating the growing tip.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwereɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ koni amɛyatao niyenii lɛ ji mɛi ni feɔ buji nɛɛ. Kwɛmɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that naturally pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the crop is harvested and its roots decay, this nitrogen stays in the ground to feed future crops.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛgbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni shishifãi lɛ fite lɛ, Nɛkɛ nitrogen nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha tsei ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow thin and weak even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for plant food, sunlight, and root space in the soil. Clearing weeds early ensures all available soil nutrients go strictly into your main crops.
