ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha tsei niyenii, hulu la kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ekwɛɔ koni shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ aya oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ anɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines to climb on wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔse mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ koni ekwɔ tso tso nɔ?

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves high into the air to absorb maximum sunlight for food production. Staking keeps the leaves dry and off the wet ground, which prevents leaf diseases and results in larger tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛŋɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ agbi ni amɛkafee ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ baa helai anaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout if I plant them in dry soil before the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds require moisture to soften their outer shells and signal the dormant plant inside to begin root growth. Without moisture, the seeds either sit inactive in the dirt or rot from soil heat before they can sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui he hiaa nu koni eha kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ afee blɛoo ni etsɔɔ tso ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akɛ ebɔi dalɛ. Kɛji hulutsoo be bɛ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsuuu nii yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo amɛgboiɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli dɔlɛ hewɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and curl up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops face extreme heat and a lack of water, they curl their leaves to reduce water loss through evaporation. Yellowing happens because the plant slows down food production to save energy to survive the dry weather.
ga: Kɛji tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe wo latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni nu ni amɛlaaje kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Su ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa ejaakɛ tsei haa niyenii ni amɛfeɔ lɛ baa shi koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my rice plants need continuous water on the field while my maize dies in stagnant water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ he hiaa nu ni yaa nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa gboɔ yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special air channels inside their roots that allow them to breathe under flooded conditions. Maize roots lack these channels, so sitting in water starves the roots of air and causes them to rot.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui krɛdɛɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni haa amɛmuɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni nu afua yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Abɛi shishifãi bɛ gbɛi nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ mɔ ko wo nu mli lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ, ni ebaaha amɛgboi.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers during very hot weather even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo enɔ po lɛ?

english: When air temperatures get too high, pepper plants suffer heat stress, which prevents flowers from pollinating properly. To protect itself from wasting energy, the plant drops its flowers until cooler conditions return.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ baaná dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni obu ohe kɛjɛ hewalɛ ni baafite lɛ he Tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ akpo kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes turn soft and rot so quickly while waiting for transport to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ miifee blɛoo ni miifite oya be mli ni mimɛɔ ni akɛya jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes continue to breathe and produce heat after being picked. When trapped in tight sacks under the hot sun, heat builds up rapidly, speeding up decay and allowing mold to spoil the fruit.
ga: Tomato yaa nɔ emuɔ ni ekɛ dɔlɛ baa beni ajie lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ akɛwo kotoku ni mli wa mli Yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Dɔlɛ buaa ehe naa oya. Ehaa nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ yaa oya ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting in the storage barn before I can take them to buyers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpa lɛ bɔi shweremɔ yɛ shĩa lɛ mli dani mikɛtee mɔ ni heɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that naturally wake up from dormancy when exposed to warm, humid air. Sprouting is the yam's attempt to grow a new plant, which uses up its internal food reserves and causes the tuber to shrink.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji tsei ni hiɛ ka ni teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ wɔɔhe kɛji akɛ amɛbote kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ mli. Sprouting ji sweet potato lɛ mɔdɛŋ ni ebɔɔ koni ekwɛ tso hee. Enɛ yeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ ni ehaa yitso lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my groundnuts turn moldy when stored immediately after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛji akɛ akɛto beni akpa kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested groundnuts contain high moisture. If they are packed into bags without being thoroughly dried in the sun, trapped moisture encourages dangerous molds like aflatoxin to grow.
ga: Peanuts ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. Kɛji akɛ awo kotoku mli ni hulu lɛ mli egbiko lɛ, nu ni mli edɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ aflatoxin lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my young maize plants turn purple?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ purple lɛ?

english: Purple leaves on young maize are a sign of phosphorus deficiency in the soil. Phosphorus helps plants build strong roots, so without enough of it, growth stalls and leaves turn purple.
ga: Baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Fosforo yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtswaa shishifãi ni wa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ fɔsfɔs ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ baai lɛ baatsɔ purple.

english: Why does adding too much fertilizer burn my crops instead of helping them grow faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ shãa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ moŋ fe ni eeeye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara oya lɛ?

english: Fertilizer contains concentrated mineral salts. Too much fertilizer creates a high salt level in the soil, which pulls water out of the plant's roots, causing the leaves to dry out and look burned.
ga: Mineral salts ni mli wa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmei babaoo aya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ashã.

english: Why do high-yield seeds from government programs perform better than seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni jɛɔ nɔyeli gbɛjianɔtoi amli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mikpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Program seeds are specially bred hybrids developed for strong vigor and disease resistance. Seeds saved from a harvested hybrid crop lose those combined strengths in the second generation, producing smaller yields.
ga: Program dumɔwui ji dumɔwui krɛdɛɛi ni afee kɛha hewalɛ kɛ helai ahe hewalɛ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ nakai hewalɛ ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni afee lɛ fioo

english: Why do early-maturing cowpea varieties produce pods much faster than local varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii ni shwereɔ mra lɛ woɔ ŋmeii oya fe maŋ lɛ mli ŋmeii srɔtoi lɛ?

english: Early-maturing cowpeas are genetically programmed to flower after fewer days of sunlight, allowing them to complete their life cycle rapidly before dry conditions destroy the crop.
ga: Ato tsina ŋmeii ni shwereɔ mra lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi beni hulu la fioo pɛ amɛná lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni egbeɔ wala shihilɛ lɛ naa oya dani shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: I planted plantains about five months ago, so what main farm work should I be doing for them right now?
ga: Midu plantains lɛ aaafee nyɔji enumɔ ni eho nɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, mɛɛ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ titri esa akɛ matsu maha amɛ bianɛ?

english: At around five months, plantains enter a fast growth phase. You need to keep weeds down around the base, trim old leaves, and ensure the plants receive adequate fertilizer so they can grow strong enough to bear heavy fruit.
ga: Beni aaafee nyɔji enumɔ eho lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ baabote be ko ni amɛdaraa oya lɛ mli. Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ, ofolɔ baai momoi lɛ, ni okwɛ koni tsei lɛ aná ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii ni tsii.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young plantain trees turning brown and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: As plantain plants grow new leaves from the top, the older leaves naturally dry up and die. You should trim these dead leaves off so the plant does not waste resources on them and to keep pests away.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ baai heei kɛjɛ ŋwɛi Baai momo lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgboiɔ. Esa akɛ ofolɔ baai ni egboi lɛ koni tso lɛ akafite nibii ni eyɔɔ lɛ ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: How do I stop my plantain trees from falling over when they start carrying heavy bunches?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-plantain lɛ akagbee shi beni mibɔi ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ awomɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots, so heavy bunches can pull the entire plant down. You need to prop them up using strong bamboo or wooden poles placed securely against the stem under the bunch.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei niji ni tsii baanyɛ agbala tso muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛba shi. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni wa ni akɛma tso lɛ shishi jogbaŋŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ shishi lɛ afi esɛɛ.

english: Why do you advise putting chemical fertilizer right at the base of my crop instead of scattering it everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okɛɔ akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ awo mi tsei lɛ ashishi moŋ fe ni ooogbɛ amɛ ashwã he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer in a ring around the base puts the nutrients directly where the feeder roots are, ensuring the crop eats the food before weeds steal it or rain washes it away.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni bɔle Shishitoo lɛ he lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ ahi he ni shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii dani jwɛi lɛ juɔ amɛ loo nugbɔ shwieɔ amɛ.

english: How close to the main stem of my plant should I place chemical fertilizers?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mitso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he kɛbɛŋkɛ tɛŋŋ?

english: You should apply fertilizer in a circle about a hand's length away from the main stem. Putting chemicals directly against the stem can cause chemical burns and damage the plant.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo mli yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ kokroo nɔ, ni okɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee tamɔ tso lɛ dalɛ. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofai ashã tso lɛ ni efite tso lɛ.

english: How do I know when my growing crops are hungry for chemical fertilizers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni hɔmɔ miiye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛha tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Slow growth, thin stems, or leaves turning pale yellow are clear signs that your crops lack food. Applying fertilizer early during their growth boost gives them the energy needed for high yields.
ga: Dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo, tsei lɛ ahe tsei bibii, loo baai ni miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ji okadii ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ niyenii ni oduɔ lɛ eshɛɛɛ he. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli mra Yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ ehaa amɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do so many small shoots grow around the base of my main plantain stem, and should I cut them off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ babaoo miida yɛ ehe lɛ. Mi plantain shishitoo titri lɛ Ni ani esa akɛ mafo mli?

english: Those extra shoots are called suckers. Leaving too many creates competition for food and water, so you should cut most of them off, leaving only one or two healthy ones to produce your next harvest.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmeii ni fata he lɛ akɛ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ ashi babaoo lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ akaŋshii aba niyenii kɛ nu he. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ofo amɛteŋ babaoo. ni ashiɔ eko loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds specifically around the base of my crop rather than just cutting the high grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ, titri lɛ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishigbɛ he lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofo jwɛi kakadaji kɛkɛ

english: Clearing a clean circle around the base prevents weeds from stealing water and fertilizer from the main feeder roots, and it stops soil insects from hiding near the trunk.
ga: Afee kooloo ni he tse ni bɔle Shishitoo lɛ he lɛ baatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaju nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ niyenii hamɔ titri lɛ shishifãi amli. ni etsĩɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ anaa koni amɛkatee amɛhe amɛwo tso lɛ shishi.

english: What kind of chemicals should I put around the root area to protect my plantains from soil insects?
ga: Mɛɛ tsofai esa akɛ mikɛtsu nii yɛ he fɛɛ he? shishifãi lɛ ahe koni ebu plantains lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahe

english: Soil pests like root nematicides or insecticides are applied around the base to destroy microscopic worms and beetles that attack roots, preventing the plant from rotting or blowing over in high winds.
ga: Abaakɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ahe lɛ baatsu nii yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he koni akɛkpãtã ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni tutuaa shishifãi lɛ ahiɛ. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkafite loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa akatswa amɛ.

english: Why does covering the soil around the base of my crop with dry leaves help it grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ baai ni egboi wo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Covering the base with organic mulch keeps the soil cool and holds moisture in the ground longer, which helps the roots absorb fertilizer better during hot or dry weather.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni wala yɔɔ mli shwie shishi lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛŋɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be loo hulutsoo be mli lɛ.

english: How can I get water to reach all my crops if I cannot afford a water pump?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nu koni eshɛ miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ahe? Kɛji minyɛɛɛ maná nu pɔmp

english: You can use the natural slope of your land to create small earth channels. By guiding water downhill along the land's natural curves, gravity moves the water across your field automatically without needing a powered pump.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ afee muji kotokui bibii. Kɛtsɔ nu lɛ ni akudɔɔ kɛyaa gɔŋ lɛ shishi ni nyiɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsiɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ oyale mli lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ pɔmp ni yɔɔ hewalɛ atsu nii.

english: Does directing rainwater through simple ditches in my field count as real irrigation?
ga: Nugbɔ nu ni akɛhaa kɛtsɔɔ nubu bibioo ko mli Yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ani abuɔ enɛ akɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, irrigation simply means supplying water to your crops systematically. Using simple dug channels to guide rainwater or stream water across your farm is an effective form of natural gravity irrigation.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ tsɔɔ nu ni okɛbaahã oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ gbɛjianɔtoo naa. Ni akɛ shika tsuru shwiemɔ gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛtsuɔ nii Koni akudɔ nugbɔ nu loo nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ nu nɔ.

english: Can I keep my vegetable farm watered during the dry season without buying expensive equipment?
ga: Ani manyɛ mawo mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni miheee nibii ni jara wa?

english: Yes, if your farm has a slight slope near a streamside or water source, you can dig shallow pathways to let gravity carry the water straight to your crop beds without fuel or machines.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli etse fioo ni bɛŋkɛ faa loo nu jɛɛhe ko naa. Obaanyɛ otsa gbɛ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ nu yaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ fuɛl loo tsɔne atsu nii.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away the top layer of soil on my sloping farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ miŋmɔ shikpɔŋ ni etse ehe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When rain hits slanted ground, it rushes straight downhill quickly and carries away fertile soil. Planting along the natural curves of the land slows the water down so it sinks into the ground instead of washing your soil away.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ tswa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ Nugbɔ lɛ hoɔ oya kɛbaa shi ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ afee mlɛo ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni eeefo lɛ.

english: What is contour farming, and how does it help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni ji kontu okwaayeli? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Contour farming means plowing and planting across a slope following the natural shape of the land rather than up and down. This traps rainwater, holds soil moisture longer, and keeps crop nutrients in the field.
ga: Kontu okwaayeli tsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋji lɛ anɔ koni akɛnyiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ su lɛ sɛɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsu nii kɛya ŋwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ Gbɛ nɛɛ baamɔmɔ nugbɔ nu. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei amli niyenii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ hiɔ shi

english: How does building small ridges of soil across a hill save water for my crops?
ga: Gbɛjegbɛ bibioo ko ni afeɔ Te Over the Hill baafee tɛŋŋ ekɛ nu ato kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Soil ridges built along the natural curves of a hill act like small walls. They hold back running rainwater, giving it time to soak deep into the soil where your crop roots can reach it.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni abɔ yɛ gɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ gbogbo bibioo ko. Amɛhiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli bɔni afee ni ená be ni ekɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: What can I do to stop rainwater from cutting deep trenches through my farm?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni nugbɔ nu lɛ akafo bu ni mli kwɔ kɛbote miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Deep channels form when water flows downhill too fast. By planting grass barriers or building soil banks along the natural contours of your land, you slow down the water so it waters your soil gently instead of damaging it.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni mli kwɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu lɛ ho oya tsɔ kɛmiijɛ gɔŋ lɛ shishi. Jwɛi ni aduɔ akɛ gbɛtsii nii loo shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋshɔnaa ni afee yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli hei lɛ ahe. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ agbɔjɔ bɔni afee ni sũ lɛ anyɛ ama shi fiofio. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeefite

english: Why do some parts of my farmland stay wet while other areas dry out quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ fã ko nɔ edɔ yɛ be mli ni hei krokomɛi hu gbɛ́ɔ oya lɛ?

english: Land naturally has high spots and low dips that gather water differently. Spotting these natural shapes helps you know where to dig water channels or plant crops that need extra water.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hei srɔtoi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ kɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishi ni nu buaa ehe naa yɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii nɛɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ole he ni esa akɛ otsa nubu loo odu tsei ni he hiaa nu kroko yɛ.

english: How can I figure out which direction water will naturally flow across my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni nu baatsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Walk through your field during or right after a heavy rain to see where water collects and flows. High spots push water away, while natural low paths show you where you can clear channels to guide water to your crops.
ga: Nyiɛmɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo yɛ no sɛɛ koni ona he ni nu buaa ehe naa ni ehoɔ yɛ. Hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ baatsi nu kɛya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, adebɔɔ mli gbɛi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baatsɔɔ bo he ni obaanyɛ ojie gbɛi ni okɛ nu aya onibii amli lɛ.

english: Why are my crops on the top part of the hill drying out faster than those at the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya fe nɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Gravity pulls water downhill, leaving hilltops dry while moisture collects at the bottom. By digging shallow contour ditches across the hill, you catch water higher up so crops on the slope stay hydrated.
ga: Nibii ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ gbalaa nu kɛyaa gɔŋ lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa gɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ buaa ehe naa yɛ shishigbɛ. Kɛ́ atsa bu ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ yɛ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu lɛ aya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋji lɛ anɔ lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and burning during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains nearby to block the harsh heat, their leaves get scorched and turn yellow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa hulutsoo lɛ bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ ni baatsi dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ naa lɛ Amɛbaai lɛ baashã ni amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning pale green and yellow starting from the tips, even when it rains well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli kɛjɛɔ amɛyiteŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ moŋ?

english: Yellowing leaves often mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to make green leaves and food. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or animal manure supplies this missing nutrient so the leaves stay dark green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehe hiaa ni tsei lɛ afee baai kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaha niyenii ni elaaje lɛ aba. Baai lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot under the ground when heavy rain stays on the farm for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits in the field without draining away, it drowns the roots and allows soil rot to destroy the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eshwɛ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli ni ajieee kɛjɛɛɛ mli lɛ Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ shishi ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbo, ni ebaafite bulb lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miifɔlɔ ni ewooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato plants often drop flowers when they experience stress, such as sudden hot weather or moving from dry soil to very wet soil. The plant drops flowers to save its strength during stressful conditions.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ ko, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ trukaa lɛ he. loo ni ejɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni efɔ waa nɔ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛhiɛ hewalɛ mli yɛ haomɔ shihilɛi amli.

english: Why do I need to clear the bush and put wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi lɛ amli ni mikɛ tsei awo mli koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct light to make food for the tubers underneath. Staking lifts the vine leaves up into the sun so they can grow bigger, healthier yams underground.
ga: La tɛ̃ɛ he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la mli koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce very small bunches when I leave all the young shoots growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ kui bibii waa beni mishiɔ ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he lɛ?

english: Too many young shoots compete directly with the main plant for water, light, and soil food. Cutting away extra shoots leaves only the strongest ones, ensuring bigger plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashi. Bɔni afee ni ana akɛ plantains lɛ baafee wuji.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and causing the plant to stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle ehe ni eha tso lɛ miikpa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juice from under the leaves. This damages the plant and stops it from growing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ ni ehaaa eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or cowpeas makes the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni adu lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have natural root bacteria that pull nitrogen from the air into the soil. When the crop is harvested, that nitrogen stays in the soil as free plant food for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ adebɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Beni akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ tsei niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha sɛɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do weeds reduce my crop harvest so much more when my crops are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ baa shi babaoo yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops have small roots and leaves, so fast-growing weeds easily steal their water, sunshine, and soil nutrients. Once crops grow big and leafy, they block sunlight from weeds.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi kɛ baai bibii. Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Kɛ tso lɛ da ni eyɛ baai Amɛbaaha hulu lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ jwɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my garden egg leaves look soft and droopy in the hot afternoon but stand up straight again in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Shi shidaamɔ tɛ̃ɛ ekoŋŋ leebi?

english: During hot afternoons, leaves lose water to the air faster than the roots can pull it from the dry soil. At night, the plant stops losing water and recovers, allowing the leaves to firm up by morning.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Gbi gbɛkɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ kpaa nu ni amɛshwieɔ lɛ ni amɛhe baajɔ amɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ mli waa leebi

english: Why do insects keep coming back to my crops even after I spray them with strong chemical medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa miŋmɔshi nibii amli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni mli wa shwieɔ nɔ moŋ?

english: Spraying only kills the visible insects on top of the plant, but it does not stop the problem if you do not target where they hide and lay eggs. To stop them completely, you must find where they settle, such as underneath the leaves or inside the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi bibii ni anaa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ pɛ. Shi no ekpaaa naagba lɛ kɛji akɛ okɛ ohiɛ emaaa he ni amɛteeɔ amɛhe ni amɛfɔɔ bii lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni okpa amɛ kwraa Ehe miihia ni otao he ni eyɔɔ, tamɔ tso lɛ baa shishi loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Is it better to spray my entire farm with pest medicine or only the spots where I see insects?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ loo he ni minaa kooloi lɛ pɛ?

english: Spraying the entire field blindly wastes money and can harm helpful insects. It is better to target the specific parts of the plant or field where the pests actually live and gather.
ga: Shika ni akɛshwieɔ shia lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ ji shika fitemɔ, ni ebaanyɛ eye kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ awui. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookwɛ tso lɛ fãi pɔtɛɛ komɛi loo hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai hiɔ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛbuaa amɛhe naa lɛ.

english: Why do pests on my farm prefer to stay underneath the leaves instead of on top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛhi baai shishi moŋ fe nɔ ni amɛaahi nɔ lɛ?

english: Insects hide on the underside of leaves to shield themselves from direct sunlight, heavy rain, and chemical sprays. When applying treatments, you must direct the spray upward to reach where they settle.
ga: Kplukai kɛ amɛhe teeɔ baai ashishi koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ amɛnɔ lɛ ahe. Kɛ okɛ tsofa lɛ miitsu nii Esa akɛ okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ ŋwɛi koni oyashɛ he ni tsofa lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: How do I know if the pest medicine I am applying is truly protecting my crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ miibu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Effective treatment does more than just kill a few bugs on contact; it prevents pests from returning to their nesting spots. If you notice new crop damage a few days after spraying, the pests have likely moved to an untreated part of the plant.
ga: Jeee akɛ tsofafeemɔ ni mɔɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ gbeɔ kooloi komɛi kɛji amɛkpe kɛkɛ. Etsiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkaku amɛsɛɛ amɛya he ni amɛfeɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛji ona ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni efite yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ efã kɛtee he ni atsako lɛ.

english: Why do insects attack only specific parts of my crop, like the young shoots or roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fãi komɛi pɛ, tamɔ ŋmeii bibii loo shishifãi lɛ?

english: Pests choose specific plant parts because they offer soft food and safe shelter. Identifying these favorite settling spots allows you to apply protection directly where the plant is most vulnerable.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ halaa tso lɛ fãi pɔtɛɛ komɛi ejaakɛ amɛhaa niyenii ni mli jɔ kɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe. Kɛ́ oyɔse nɛkɛ hei ni osumɔɔ waa ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nɛɛ haa onyɛɔ obuɔ hei ni tsei yɔɔ oshara fe fɛɛ lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why should I clear weeds and dead leaves from my farm before applying pest medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛ baai ni egboi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ atsu nii?

english: Weeds and crop waste serve as hiding places and breeding grounds for insects. Clearing them removes the shelter where pests settle, making your farm treatments much more effective.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashwieɔ lɛ ji hei ni kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli kɛ hei ni amɛfɔɔ yɛ. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ejieɔ nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ehi nɔ lɛ. Ha tsofafeemɔ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Will spraying pest medicine on the soil around my crops help stop insects from attacking?
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle mihe lɛ nɔ Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baatsi kooloi ni baatutua mi lɛ anaa?

english: Yes, many crop pests hide or lay eggs in the topsoil around the plant base. Treating the soil directly around these settling areas stops insects before they can climb up to damage the crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooloi bibii babaoo kɛ amɛhe teeɔ loo amɛwoɔ amɛwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ he nitsumɔ tɛ̃ɛ Hei ni mɛi ehi shi nɛɛ tsiɔ kooloi bibii lɛ anaa dani amɛkwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How do I protect my maize leaves from caterpillars that hide deep inside the plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu ŋmãa baai ahe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tso lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ ahe?

english: Caterpillars like Fall Armyworms settle deep inside the central funnel of the maize plant. You must direct the treatment right into the funnel where they live, rather than just spraying the outer leaves.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ Fall Armyworms lɛ hiɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ. Esa akɛ okɛ tsofa lɛ awo ŋmei ni amɛyɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshwie kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ pɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Why does pest medicine fail to work when I spray my crops during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsuuu nii kɛ́ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Rain washes away chemical medicine before it can penetrate the places where insects hide. Applying treatments during dry hours ensures the medicine stays long enough on the spots where pests settle.
ga: Nugbɔ hoɔ tsofai lɛ kɛyaa dani eboteɔ hei ni kooloi bibii lɛ ehiɛ amɛhe yɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa lɛ tsu nii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa tsofa lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa yɛ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ yɔɔ lɛ.

english: What happens to farm pests after I harvest my crops, and where do they go?
ga: Mɛni baa ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ beni mikpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ sɛɛ? Ni nɛgbɛ amɛbaaya?

english: After harvest, insects settle in remaining crop stalks, moist soil, or nearby wild bushes to survive the dry season. Clearing and properly disposing of harvest waste destroys their resting places before the next planting season.
ga: kpamɔ sɛɛ Kplukai lɛ shwieɔ tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ ashishifãi, shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ, loo koo mli tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Nikpamɔ mli jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ashɛrɛɔ ashwieɔ lɛ fiteɔ amɛshihilɛhe lɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baashɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I clear all the tall trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ lɛ? Beni mijie tsei kakadaji ni ebɔle mihe lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight. Leaving tall trees or planting fast-growing food crops like plantains provides living shade and holds moisture in the air, protecting the cocoa until it matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni ashiɔ loo niyenii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ hu haa hulutsoo baa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Buu kookoo he kɛyashi ebaatsɔ shweremɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt in the afternoon heat even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the ground. If the soil is still moist, the plants are just conserving water and will bounce back as the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ Tsei lɛ miihiɛ nu kɛkɛ ni amɛbaaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba kɛji hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Why do my cassava plants shed most of their leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baa lɛ babaoo shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves in dry weather to reduce water loss and protect itself from drought. Once the rains start again, the plant will sprout new leaves and continue feeding its underground roots.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hɔmɔ he. Kɛ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ ekoŋŋ Tso lɛ baawo baai heei ni ebaaya nɔ eye shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ niyenii.

english: How do I know when my dry maize is ready to be harvested from the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Dry maize is ready when the outer husks turn completely brown and papery, the stalks dry out, and the individual grains become hard enough that you cannot dent them with your fingernail.
ga: Abɛi ni egbi lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ batsɔ blɔfo ni efee tamɔ wolo, ni ŋmeii lɛ egbi, ni ŋmeii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko mli wa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ nineshi ŋmeii lɛ eko eko efoŋ.

english: What will happen if I plant my yam mounds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmeii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: If yam mounds are placed too close, the plant roots will compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in smaller yam tubers at harvest time.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni ato lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, sweet potato lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds early while my maize plants are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ ani ehe miihia yɛ be mli ni mi-abele tsei lɛ darako kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young maize and steal the soil's water and nutrients. Clearing them early gives your maize crops unhindered access to sunlight and soil food so they can establish strong stems.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmãa bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii mra Enɛ haa o-corn lɛ naa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko etsĩii enaa. koni amɛná tsei ni wa

english: Why is planting cowpeas or beans good for my land before I plant maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ hi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ dani aduɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. When you plant maize in that same soil afterward, the maize uses that natural food to grow faster and yield bigger ears.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni oduɔ ŋmãa yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa kɛ nakai adebɔɔ mli niyenii lɛ tsuɔ nii koni eda oya ni ekɛ toi wuji aba lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow in a V-shape down the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni V su yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves that start from the leaf tip and move downward usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to build strong green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni eyaa shi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji.

english: How do I select the right cassava stems to cut and plant for my new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tsei ni sa ni mafolɔ ni madu kɛha miŋmɔ hee lɛ?

english: Choose stem cuttings from fully grown, healthy plants that are 8 to 12 months old. Make sure the stems are firm, have visible growth buds, and show no signs of insect damage or disease holes.
ga: Halamɔ niji ni jɛ tsei ni eda ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 lɛ amli. Kwɛmɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ. yɛ hiŋmɛii wuji ni anaa ni okadi ko bɛ ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi efite loo hela buji.

english: Why are small worms eating holes inside the center funnel of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the tender center leaves of young maize. Finding them early allows you to treat the plant center directly before the pest destroys the growing point.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ anɔ. Amɛtaomɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ otsaa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ dani tsɛŋemɔ helai fiteɔ he ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen helps plants stay green and make food; when there isn't enough, the plant moves what little it has to its new top leaves, leaving the bottom ones to turn yellow and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛhaa niyenii. Beni eshɛɛɛ Tso lɛ baajie nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ. Ha baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi.

english: Why are the bottoms of my growing green tomatoes turning black and soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli ni miida lɛ shishi lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni eyɛ blɛoo lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot, and it usually happens when the plant gets irregular amounts of water. Inconsistent watering makes it hard for the tomato plant to absorb calcium from the soil, causing the bottom of the fruit to rot.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ni bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Nu ni afɔɔɔ amɛ daa lɛ haa ewaa ahaa tomato tsei lɛ akɛ amɛaaŋɔ calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ ashishi shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in a clear, open field with direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to high heat and harsh sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains grown next to them early on to shield their delicate leaves from burning until they grow older and stronger.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. ekome kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ buɔ ebaai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe waɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear the excess suckers growing around my plantain stand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantains lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: If too many suckers grow around the main plantain tree, they steal water and food from it. Leaving only two or three strong suckers allows the main plant to put its full energy into producing a large bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo miida yɛ ehe lɛ, dumɔwui titri Amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui titrii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ashi tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo plantains babaoo.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines with tall wooden sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu sweet potato wain tsei ni tsei kakadaji yɔɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need maximum sunlight on their leaves to produce large tubers under the soil. Lifting the vines off the ground also keeps the leaves dry and prevents fungal diseases from spreading.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la ni fa babaoo yɛ tsei lɛ ahe koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji aba. Wein tso lɛ ni ooowo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ gĩɔ, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and stopping the plant from growing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekawo yibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips feeding on the leaves and spreading plant viruses. Controlling these small pests early stops the disease from spreading across your field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ tso lɛ helai lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli. Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: Why are small worms leaving white winding tracks all over my tomato leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ shiɔ okadii yɛŋ ni tamɔ onufu yɛ mi-tomato baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Those white winding lines are caused by insect larvae called leaf miners that burrow inside the leaves to eat. This damage reduces the leaf's ability to catch sunlight and feed the plant, making it weak.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ leafworms ni shwieɔ baai amli koni amɛye nii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nakai ŋmeii yɛŋ ni etse amɛhe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni baai lɛ yɔɔ ni amɛkɛ hulu la ni amɛhaa tso lɛ niyenii lɛ baa shi. ha egbɔjɔ

english: Why do my maize plants produce very small cobs if I plant seeds too close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for limited soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Spacing plants properly gives each stalk enough resource to grow full, big cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni fa fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli. Kɛ́ ajie tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ shishifã lɛ eko fɛɛ eko aná nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do weeds make my vegetable crops grow so slow and look weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi-vegetables lɛ daa blɛoo ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most vegetable crops and aggressively drink up the soil's water and fertilizers. They block sunlight and effectively starve your crop of the nutrients it needs to grow big and produce healthy vegetables.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe aduawai babaoo. ni anuɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ waa Amɛtsiɔ hulu la naa ni amɛjieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛwo aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting in the soil before I get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani minine shɛɔ hegbɛ nɔ ni mikpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil for too long without draining away. Excess water suffocates the roots and encourages fungal rot, so planting on ridges or in well-drained soil prevents this loss.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Nu babaoo haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii anɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ nɛkɛ laajemɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees burning and turning yellow during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside young cocoa creates natural shade that cools the soil and protects the seedlings until they grow strong enough to withstand the sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ebuɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu lɛ naa.

english: Why do my maize plants stay short and turn pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves and stunted growth usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to build green leaves and grow tall. Adding well-composted manure or nitrogen fertilizer gives the maize the food it needs to turn healthy green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my cassava stem cuttings fail to grow big tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmɔji lɛ ekomɛi nyɛɛɛ akwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava needs healthy, mature stems planted in loose, well-aerated soil to form large roots. If you plant weak cuttings or plant them upside down, the plant wastes energy struggling to grow leaves instead of storing food in the root tubers.
ga: Cassava biɔ tsei ni wa, ni eda ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ koni efee shishifãi wuji. Kɛji odu tso nine bibioo loo ni etsɔ ehe lɛ Tsei lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛkwɛ baai lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaato niyenii yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miifɔlɔ ni ewooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the air gets extremely hot or when the plant goes through sudden dry spells. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and mulching helps the flowers stay attached and turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tso lɛ tsɔ hulutsoo be mli trukaa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛfee tomatoi.

english: Why is it necessary for me to put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to make food that feeds the tuber growing deep underground. Staking keeps the vines off the damp ground, exposing leaves to full light while preventing fungal diseases that spread on wet ground.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni haa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ niyenii. Staking baaha wain tsei lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni oooha amɛná la ni fa babaoo lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why is it helpful to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my land before planting maize the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. Planting them first leaves free natural fertilizer in the soil that helps the next maize crop grow bigger grains.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔ lɛ shĩɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmãa wuji.

english: Why are there ragged holes and soft brown dust inside the center leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ sũ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Holes and sawdust-like material are signs that caterpillars, such as Fall Armyworms, are eating inside the plant's growing center. Catching them early by inspecting the leaves allows you to remove or treat them before they destroy the main stem.
ga: Bu kɛ nibii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ji okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworms, miiye he ni tso lɛ daa yɛ lɛ. Amɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ lɛ obaanyɛ ojie loo otsa amɛ dani amɛfite tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ.

english: Why does spreading dry grass around the base of my crops keep them fresh during dry days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ No hewɔ lɛ, ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ haa jwɛi lɛ feɔ ehee yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or straw creates mulch, which acts like a blanket over the dirt. It stops the sun from evaporating soil water, keeping the roots cool and wet even when it does not rain for a few days.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo jwɛi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ehaa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Ha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji nugbɔ enɛko gbii fioo komɛi po.

english: Why do my crops yield smaller fruits when I plant many seeds close together in one spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii beni midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crowded plants compete with each other for water, sunlight, and soil food. Giving each seed proper spacing allows roots to spread out and gather enough nutrients to grow large, healthy produce.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Dumɔwui aŋkroaŋkroi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa ni amɛbuaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout when I bury them deep in the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: A seed carries only a tiny amount of stored energy to push its first sprout up into the light. If buried too deep, the sprout runs out of energy before reaching the surface and dies underground, so seeds must be planted at a shallow depth.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ni ato ni amɛkɛtsiɔ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwu ni kwɛ̃ lɛ kɛyaa la mli. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ Hewalɛ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ dani eshɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ.

english: Why are my crops not growing well near old tree stumps on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsei momo ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Old tree stumps and their hidden roots compete with young crops for water and nutrients. Their deep root networks also physically block your new crops' roots from spreading wide to get food from the soil.
ga: Tsoi akui ni egbɔ kɛ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei bibii yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. Amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ hu tsiɔ otso hee lɛ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã koni amɛná niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it really necessary to uproot all tree stumps before I plant new crops on fresh land?
ga: Ani ehe miihia diɛŋtsɛ ni ajie tsei akutsei lɛ fɛɛ dani adu tsei heei yɛ sũ nɔ?

english: Yes, removing tree stumps allows crop roots to spread easily, makes tilling the soil much faster, prevents wood-rotting diseases from spreading to your new crops, and maximizes your usable farm area.
ga: Hɛɛ, shishifãi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitsumɔ yaa oya kwraa. Tsi tso ni fiteɔ lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa oŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ amli. ni okɛ oŋmɔ mli he ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ atsu nii babaoo

english: What happens to my maize or cassava roots if the soil underground is full of old tree roots?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi ŋmãa loo ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ tso shishifãi momo eyi shikpɔŋ shishi sũ lɛ mli obɔ?

english: When crop roots hit hard tree roots or compacted soil, they stop growing deep. This causes the plant to stay small, dry out quickly in the sun, and produce very little yield.
ga: Beni tso shishifãi tswa tso shishifãi ni wa loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ. Tse shishifãi lɛ baakpa shweremɔ ni mli kwɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ bibioo. Egbiɔ oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ enɔ. ni amɛwoɔ nɔ ko fioo pɛ

english: How does clearing tree stumps help me plant more crops on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni akpaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi koni makwɛ tsei babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Clearing underground stumps opens up hidden spaces in the field, allowing you to plant crops at the correct spacing without roots fighting each other, which increases your overall farm acreage.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi tsei akui ni ajieɔ lɛ baagbele hei ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ oduɔ tsei yɛ he ni sa ni shishifãi kɛ amɛhe etswaaa akaŋ. Enɛ baaha oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn out small and bent when I plant them in uncleared soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni he tseee nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers need loose, clear soil to expand smoothly. If they hit underground stumps or hard roots while growing, they bend, remain tiny, and become difficult to harvest.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni mli tse he miihia cassava tsei lɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji amɛtswa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei loo shishifãi ni wa beni amɛdaraa lɛ, amɛbaakoto, amɛbaaya nɔ amɛhi shi bibii, ni ebaawa akɛ abaakpa.

english: Why do wild shoots keep sprouting back from tree stumps even after I cut them down to farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ekoŋŋ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi beni mifo amɛ kɛha okwaayeli po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tree stumps have deep living root systems that store food. They will keep pushing up new leaves that shade your crops and steal water until the whole stump and root system is completely removed.
ga: Tsoi akutsei lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni hiɛ ka ni mli kwɔ ni kɛ niyenii toɔ. Amɛbaatsi baai heei kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛju nu kɛyashi abaajie tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fɛɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Can leaving dead tree roots in the soil bring pests that will damage my crops?
ga: Ani tso shishifãi ni egboi ni mashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsɛŋemɔ helai aba ni amɛbafite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Yes, rotting tree stumps and buried roots attract termites, white grubs, and root-rot fungi, which can easily move from the dead stump to attack the roots of your healthy crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei akutsei ni fiteɔ kɛ shishifãi ni afu lɛ gbalaa ŋmeii, ŋmeii yɛŋ, kɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ ŋmeii. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛshi tsei ni egboi lɛ amli oya koni amɛyatutua onibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ashishifãi lɛ.

english: How deep do I need to clear root obstacles before planting cocoa or fruit trees?
ga: Te ehe hiaa ni majie shishifãi ni tsiɔ nii anaa lɛ kɛyashɛ he ni mli kwɔ ha tɛŋŋ dani madu kookoo loo aduawai tsei?

english: You need to clear roots and rocks down to at least two feet deep so the main taproot of the tree can go deep into the ground to anchor itself and reach water during dry seasons.
ga: Obaasumɔ ni otsi shishifãi kɛ tɛi lɛ amli kɛyashɛ he ko ni kɛ hoo lɛ, eshɛɔ ninetalɔi enyɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ aya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni ekɛ ehe awo mli ni ená nu yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: What should I put in the deep holes left behind after pulling out big tree stumps?
ga: Beni ejie tso agbo ko ni efu lɛ yɛ bu ni mli kwɔ ni eshi lɛ mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fill the holes with topsoil mixed with organic manure or compost so the ground settles level and provides rich food for the new crop roots that grow into that space.
ga: Okɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli efutu mli lɛ awo bu lɛ mli koni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni eha niyenii babaoo aha tsei shishifãi heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: Does using a machine to remove tree stumps damage the soil for planting?
ga: Ani nɔ ni akɛjieɔ ŋmeii lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ?

english: If done properly when the soil is not overly wet, machine stump removal actually helps by loosening hard underground soil, making it easier for crop roots to penetrate and grow strong.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔɔɔ tsɔ. Tsɔne ni akɛjieɔ ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa diɛŋtsɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ shishi sũ ni wa lɛ ni ejieɔ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ tso shishifãi lɛ baabote mli ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with many leaves, but only produce tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi eyɛ yitso bibioo ko pɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when cassava is planted too close together, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems to fight for sunlight instead of storing energy underground in the roots. Cutting back on nitrogen fertilizer and spacing plants properly encourages bigger tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Tsei kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ amɛbaai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwu amɛshi hulu la moŋ fe ni amɛkɛaato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa shi kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baawo bulbs wuji lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without forming fruit when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: High heat causes heat stress in tomatoes, which damages the pollen inside the flowers so they cannot fertilize properly. Without fertilization, the plant sheds the flowers to conserve energy and water until cooler temperatures return.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa tomato mli. Enɛ baafite pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo fɔmɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb tall wooden stakes instead of just spreading on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooogbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on as many leaves as possible to make food for the tuber underground. Lifting the vines off the damp ground also prevents leaf diseases and rotting caused by high humidity and soil-borne fungi.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Wein tsei ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsei ahe helai kɛ fitemɔ ni hulutsoo babaoo kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants filled with small ragged holes and fine powder?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni powda kpakpa lɛ hu?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides deep inside the growing shoot of the maize plant during the day and feeds on the soft leaves, leaving behind leaf damage and frass (waste) that looks like sawdust.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa, ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii, ni amɛshiɔ baai ni efite kɛ ŋmeii (sũi) ni tamɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and turning wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips, mites, or aphids feeding on the underside of young leaves, or by a virus carried by whiteflies. As the insects suck the sap, the leaves distort and stunt plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, mites, loo aphids ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ anɔ. be mli ni kooloi bibii nuɔ nu lɛ Baai lɛ hu tsɔɔ sɛɛ ni amɛtsiɔ tso lɛ dalɛ naa.

english: Why should I cut away some of the young shoots growing at the bottom of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ ekomɛi?

english: If you leave all the shoots (suckers) growing together, they will compete with the mother plant for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Keeping only one main plant, one medium shoot, and one small shoot ensures the main plant produces large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji oshi ŋmeii (ŋmeii) lɛ fɛɛ yɛ he kome Amɛkɛ tso nyɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Tso titri kome pɛ, tso bibioo kome, kɛ tso bibioo kome pɛ ni akwɛɔ lɛ baaha tso titri lɛ awo dumɔwui wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when I clear all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sunlight and heat. They need shade from larger trees or temporary shade crops like plantains to keep their leaves cool and preserve moisture in the soil while their root systems develop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛbaai lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ mli be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas in the same farm as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni miduɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the soil. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to grow, so planting them together naturally fertilizes the soil for the maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ helai krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do weeds on my farm grow so much faster than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni midu jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive hard conditions with deep roots and fast germination systems. Domesticated crops have been bred to produce food rather than to compete aggressively, making them slower to start than wild weeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli, kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ kwɛ̃mɔ gbɛjianɔtoo oya. Akwɛ tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ shia lɛ koni amɛná niyenii moŋ fe akaŋshii ni naa wa. Enɛ haa shishijee lɛ yaa hiɛ blɛoo fe koo mli jwɛi.

english: Why do my seeds rot in the ground when I plant immediately after the very first rainy day of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbi lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The very first rain often heats up the dry soil without providing enough long-term moisture, creating a hot, damp environment that rots seeds. It is better to wait until the rains become consistent so the soil stays cool and wet enough for seed germination.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ haaa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ fɛ̃i baa ni haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Can I actually grow a new yam plant by cutting pieces from the stem instead of planting a full tuber?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ sweet potato tsei heei kɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi ni afoɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni makwɛ bulbs ni eyi obɔ?

english: Yes, you can grow new yam plants using stem cuttings. Cutting a healthy vine into small stem pieces allows you to produce many new yam plants without using up valuable food tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ atsu nii ni okɛdu sweet potato tsei heei. Wein tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ooofo mli bibii lɛ Eyeɔ ebua bo ni ofeɔ sweet potato tsei heei. Na babaoo ni okɛ niyenii ni jara wa lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii.

english: How many new planting pieces can I get from a single yam stem?
ga: Tsei heei enyiɛ manyɛ makwɛ kɛjɛ sweet potato tso kome mli?

english: A healthy, well-developed yam stem can yield anywhere from 300 to 500 small stem pieces for planting, making it a very efficient way to multiply your crop.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ awo niji bibii. Ebaanyɛ eda yɛ he fɛɛ he kɛjɛ tsei 300 kɛyashi 500, ni no haa efeɔ gbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbɛɔ otsei lɛ ashwãa.

english: How long does a yam plant need to grow before its stems are ready to be cut for planting?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ sweet potato tso ko ada dani efee klalo akɛ aaafo lɛ koni adu?

english: It usually takes about three months of growth for a yam vine to reach the direct stem stage where the stems are mature enough to be cut into viable planting pieces.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ aaafee nyɔji etɛ dani sweet potato wain tsei lɛ daraa dani amɛshɛɔ stem stage lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Tso lɛ baafee agbo bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ afo mli bibii bibii koni akɛdu.

english: What does an extension officer mean by the 'direct stem stage' of yam?
ga: Mɛni mɛi ni woɔ hiɛyaa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ yɛ ‘Straight stem length’ ni ji sweet potato lɛ he?

english: The direct stem stage is the period in the yam's growth cycle—around three months in—when the vine stems are thick and mature enough to be cut directly into pieces for growing new plants.
ga: Be ni sweet potato lɛ dalɛ mli (aaafee nyɔji 3 ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ) ji be ni wain tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli edɔ ni edara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ afo mli tɛ̃ɛ ni akɛwo tsei heei amli.

english: Why should I plant my cut yam stems in a special nursery medium instead of straight into the farm soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ sweet potato tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ ŋmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli

english: A special planting medium holds moisture and nutrients better than plain soil, giving delicate young stem cuttings a protected environment to grow strong roots before facing harsher field conditions.
ga: Nibii krɛdɛɛi ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ fe shikpɔŋ folo. Ehaa tsei bibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ naa he ko ni abuɔ he koni ewaje shishifãi lɛ dani amɛkɛ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi ni mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ akpee.

english: Do I plant just one stem piece per spot when doing stem propagation?
ga: Ani miduɔ tso kome pɛ yɛ he fɛɛ he kɛ́ migbɛ tsei lɛ ashwã?

english: Yes, you plant one stem cut per space or container so that each piece has enough room, light, and nutrients to develop its own root system and mini-tuber.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu tso 1 ni afoɔ yɛ he loo tsɛnsi mli. Enɛ ji koni eha tso fɛɛ tso aná he ko, la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eshishifãi kɛ eshishifãi.

english: How does a small piece of a cut yam stem turn into a real yam plant?
ga: Sweet potato tsei, ni afolɔ mli bibii Te aaafee tɛŋŋ afee sweet potato tso diɛŋtsɛ?

english: The cut stem piece contains active growth points called nodes. When buried in moist soil medium, these nodes sprout roots below and shoot leaves above, forming a complete new plant.
ga: Tso lɛ mli fãi ni afo lɛ yɛ hei ni amɛdaraa yɛ ni atsɛɔ amɛ nodes. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ Nɛkɛ nodes nɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ shishifãi yɛ shishigbɛ ni baai hu kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. ebatsɔ tso hee kwraa

english: Should I plant my yam stem pieces immediately after cutting them?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu sweet potato tsei lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji mifo amɛ?

english: Yes, cut stem pieces should be planted into your prepared moist medium as soon as possible so they do not dry out or lose the vitality needed to root.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ adu tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ awo he ko ni mli edɔ ni asaa he oya bɔ ni aaanyɛ koni amɛkagbi loo amɛkafite hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo shishifãi lɛ.

english: How do I choose which yam stem is good enough to cut for new plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala sweet potato tsei ni sa kɛha ŋmeii ni afolɔ kɛha ŋmeii heei ni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Look for strong, green, disease-free stems that have been growing for about three months, as weak or diseased stems will not produce healthy new plants.
ga: Taomɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji, ni helai bɛ mli ni baanyɛ akwɛ̃ aaafee nyɔji etɛ, ejaakɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ loo hela yɔɔ mli lɛ nyɛŋ afee tsei heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Will taking stem cuttings from my yam vine hurt the original plant?
ga: Ani mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ mli tsei ni afolɔ lɛ baafite shishijee tso lɛ?

english: If done at the proper stage (around three months) from mature vines, taking stem cuttings allows you to multiply your crop while the established plant continues its normal growth cycle.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afee yɛ he ni sa (aaafee nyɔji etɛ) kɛjɛ wain tsei ni eda kwraa lɛ ahe lɛ, ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baaha onyɛ ogbɛ tso lɛ oshwã yɛ be mli ni tso ni ato ama shi lɛ yaa nɔ edaa bɔ ni sa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibioo lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize turning yellow starting from the bottom of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves and grow strong cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with thick branches, but only gives me tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ niji ni mli tse lɛ? shi eha yitso bibioo Shikpɔŋ shishi pɛ

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen or grows in heavy shade, it spends all its energy building big leafy stems above ground instead of sending food down to grow fat roots.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo edaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛmaa tsei agboi ni yɔɔ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu niyenii kɛba shi koni shishifãi ni yɔɔ fɔ lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers, but the flowers fall off without growing into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi?

english: Tomato flowers fall off if weather gets extremely hot, or if the soil has too much fertilizer causing the plant to prioritize leaves over fruits, or if insects fail to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ anɔ fe aduawai lɛ. aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔii amli ŋmɔtɔ

english: Why do young mangoes keep dropping off my tree before they get big enough to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango yaa nɔ egbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani edara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Trees drop young fruit when they don't have enough water to feed them all, or when fruit flies lay eggs inside the small mangoes, causing them to spoil early.
ga: Tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ aduawai bibii kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua amɛ fɛɛ lɛ bɛ. Aloo beni aduawai amli ŋmeii woɔ ŋmeii yɛ mango bibii amli lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛgboɔ oya.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches and side shoots from my tomato plants when they seem to be growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ niji kɛ esɛɛ tsei lɛ amli be mli ni etamɔ nɔ ni eekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Removing side shoots prevents the plant from wasting energy on extra leaves, directing all its strength into producing larger, healthier fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ, no tsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekafite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ehewalɛ fɛɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves curl up during the hot afternoon and look like they are dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ahe baai shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli tamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in the heat is a defense mechanism to prevent water from evaporating too quickly from the plant. If they revive in the cool evening, the plant is simply protecting itself.
ga: Baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa mli lɛ ji gbɛ ni buɔ mɔ he koni nu akajɛ tso lɛ mli oya tsɔ. Kɛji amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba wala mli ekoŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ ko ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli. Tso lɛ miibu ehe kɛkɛ.

english: Why do cashew trees flower during the dry season when there is barely any rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cashew tsei fɔɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli ni nugbɔ baaa kwraa lɛ?

english: Cashews trigger their flowering in dry weather because dry air prevents fungal diseases from rotting the delicate flowers and helps insects easily transfer pollen.
ga: Cashew ŋmeii woɔ fɔfɔii ahe hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ mli ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ anaa koni ekafite fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni amɛjieɔ pollen lɛ mlɛo

english: Why do some of my maize seeds sprout in four days, while others in the same farm take over a week or do not come up at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ ekomɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbii ejwɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui komɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ heɔ nɔ ni fe otsi kome loo amɛkwɛɛɛ kwraa lɛ?

english: Seeds sprout at different speeds depending on how deeply they were buried and how moist the soil around them stays. Seeds buried too deep struggle to push through the dirt.
ga: Dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oyaiyeli srɔtoi amli. Edamɔ bɔ ni afu lɛ mli kwɔ ha lɛ nɔ. kɛ bɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle dumɔwu lɛ he lɛ Dumɔwui ni afu amɛ ni mli kwɔ tsɔ lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How do weeds actually weaken my pepper plants if they are just growing next to them without touching?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aha mi-pepper tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ tɛŋŋ? Kɛji amɛdara yɛ amɛhe masɛi amɛ ni amɛtaaa amɛhe?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and nutrients directly out of the soil around your pepper plants, leaving less food for your peppers to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli. pepper tree directly Enɛ haa niyenii fioo pɛ baahã pepper lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can spraying weed killer on the ground near my cocoa trees hurt their roots?
ga: Ani tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ mi-kokoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite eshishifãi lɛ?

english: Yes, it can. Crop roots spread out under the soil surface to collect water, and if chemical weed killers are on the ground, the roots will absorb those chemicals along with the soil moisture, which can harm or weaken the tree.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ afee. Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi koni nu lɛ ahi mli. ni kɛji akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nakai tsofai lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aye tso lɛ awui loo egbɔjɔ.

english: What is 2,4-D weedicide and how does it affect crops if they absorb it?
ga: Mɛni ji 2,4-D tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ, ni te ebaaná tsei anɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ kɛji eŋɔ lɛ?

english: 2,4-D is a strong chemical weed killer designed to destroy broad-leaf weeds. If crops like cocoa accidentally absorb it through their roots, it can cause twisted leaves, abnormal growth, or even severe damage to the tree.
ga: 2,4-D ji tsofa ko ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni afee koni ekɛkpãtã jwɛi ni yɔɔ baai babaoo lɛ ahiɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo tsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛŋɔ lɛ yɛ oshara mli lɛ, Ebaanyɛ eha baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. dalɛ ni ejaaa loo tso lɛ ni efite waa po.

english: Is it safer to clear weeds under my cocoa trees by hand or with chemical sprays?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛ nine loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei ashishi lɛ?

english: Clearing by hand or using cutlasses is safer for the roots because chemical sprays can leave residues in the soil that cocoa roots take up during rains, potentially damaging the trees from the inside.
