ga: Nine ni akɛjieɔ nii loo akɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ nii lɛ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha shishifãi lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashi nibii ni eshwɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Enɛ baanyɛ afite tso lɛ kɛjɛ emli.

english: How far from the trunk of my cocoa tree should I keep chemical weed sprays?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ ashɛ kookoo tso lɛ shishi kɛjɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: You should keep weedicides at a safe distance from the base of the trunk because cocoa trees have shallow feeder roots close to the surface around the tree that quickly absorb chemicals dissolved in the soil.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ ato he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ tso lɛ he lɛ, ni amɛmɔɔ tsofai ni egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya.

english: What happens to farm chemicals on the ground when rain falls on my farm?
ga: Mɛni baa ŋmɔ mli tsofai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Rain dissolves the chemicals sitting on top of the soil and carries them down into the ground. Once dissolved, these chemicals mix with soil water and become easily accessible for plant roots to drink up.
ga: Nugbɔ lɛ shwieɔ tsofai ni ekpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni ehoɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ Tsofai nɛɛ kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ futuɔ ni ehaa tso shishifãi lɛ nuɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do my cocoa tree roots suck up weed killer if it is harmful to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa shishifãi lɛ miinu tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ kɛji akɛ eyeɔ amɛ awui lɛ?

english: Roots do not have eyes or taste buds to distinguish between good food and dangerous chemicals. They act like sponges that automatically absorb whatever liquids are dissolved in the soil water around them.
ga: Shishifãi lɛ bɛ hiŋmɛii loo tsɔne ni haa anaa srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ niyenii kpakpa kɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ ateŋ. Amɛtsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji, ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛheɔ nu fɛɛ nu ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ nu ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Can chemical weed killers move through the soil and reach nearby trees that I didn't spray?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eyashɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ ni mifɔko nɔ lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, water flowing through the soil after a rainstorm can wash dissolved chemicals across the farm, allowing nearby tree roots to absorb weed killers even if you didn't spray right underneath them.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ baanyɛ ajie tsofai ni egbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmuɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ. Kɛji akɛ okɛshwieee shishi po.

english: Can chemical weed killers stay in my farm soil and affect my crops over time?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ baanyɛ ahi sũ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli ni ená miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Some chemicals stay active in the soil longer than others. If used repeatedly, chemical residues can build up in the ground, causing long-term damage to the fine root systems of your crops every time it rains.
ga: Tsofai komɛi hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ fe ekrokomɛi. Kɛ akɛtsu nii shii abɔ lɛ, tsofai ni eshwɛ lɛ baanyɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifã bibioo lɛ fiteɔ be kakadaŋŋ. nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ

english: How can I tell if my cocoa tree has absorbed weed killer through its roots?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kokoo tso lɛ etsɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ eŋɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ?

english: Signs of root damage from chemical intake include curling or deformed leaves, yellowing foliage, stunted new growth, or sudden leaf dropping, even if the leaves themselves were never directly sprayed.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ efite shishifãi lɛ ahe ji baai ni ebɔle loo efite, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ, kɛ dalɛ hee ni egbɔjɔ. loo egbee shi trukaa Kɛji akɛ ashwieee baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ po.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees look twisted even though I only sprayed the weeds on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni efite eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ jwɛi lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Twisted or distorted leaves are a classic sign that the roots absorbed weedicide—like 2,4-D—from the soil, which then traveled up through the trunk into the leaves and disturbed their normal growth pattern.
ga: Baai ni etsake loo etsɔ ehe lɛ ji okadi ni ale jogbaŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi eŋɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi tamɔ 2,4-D kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛtsɔ tsei lɛ amli kɛtee baa lɛ mli. ni efiteɔ bɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛhaa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow green leaves. Adding animal manure or the right fertilizer will help them turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my land is good enough to plant cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmei?

english: Cassava grows best in loose soil that allows water to drain away easily. If your soil holds too much water like sticky clay, the cassava roots will rot underground before you can harvest them.
ga: Cassava kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni haa nu hoɔ oya lɛ nɔ. Kɛji nu babaoo yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ baagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani obaanyɛ okpa amɛ.

english: Why do my newly planted cocoa seedlings dry up and die when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have soft leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. They need shade crops like plantain or cassava planted next to them to block the intense sun while their roots grow deep.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiisumɔ ni adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ amɛmasɛi. koni amɛtsi hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi shi amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when the weather is too hot or when they do not get steady water. When the plant feels heat stress, it sheds flowers to save energy to survive.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ amɛnáaa nu daa. Kɛ tsei nu dɔlɛ he haomɔ he lɛ Efɔ̃ɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato koni ehi shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and turning pale light green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Curling and pale leaves are signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. Using disease-resistant stem cuttings for planting stops this disease from spreading.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmei bibioo lɛ ji nɔ ni hiɛɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ hela lɛ tsu nii kɛ́ adu lɛ, ebaaha hela nɛɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ akpa.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow small and bent instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers become small and twisted when the soil is packed too hard for the tuber to expand smoothly, or when tiny worms in the soil attack the growing root.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛfiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã jogbaŋŋ. Aloo kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutua shishifãi ni miida lɛ.

english: How can I tell the exact time my cocoa pods are ready to be picked?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ ajie kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods are ready for harvest when their color changes completely from green or dark red to bright yellow or orange. Harvesting only fully yellow pods ensures high-quality beans inside.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ kɛji amɛhe su tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli kwɔ mli kɛtee ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse waa. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kwraa lɛ pɛ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa mli.

english: Why do my harvested fresh peppers spoil so quickly after picking them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peppers ni mikpa ehee lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akpa lɛ?

english: Fresh peppers rot quickly if they are harvested while wet from rain, bruised during picking, or stored in tightly sealed plastic bags under hot weather without air flowing through.
ga: Chili hee lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akpa lɛ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ edɔ lɛ. Epila yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ Aloo akɛto plastic kotoku ko ni atsĩ naa mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi ni kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔɔ mli.

english: What makes my stored maize turn into powder with tiny holes in the grains?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ tsɔɔ powda ni ehaa bu bibii yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: Tiny insects called weevils eat into the stored maize grains from the inside out. Properly drying your maize until it is very hard before putting it in airtight bags keeps weevils out.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ yeɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Kɛji akɛ agbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ebaawa waa dani akɛwo vacuum mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa lɛ akabote mli.

english: Why do tiny bugs appear inside my stored cowpeas even when I keep them in a closed room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii No hewɔ lɛ ejie ehe kpo yɛ mi stash ni ji cowpeas lɛ mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛtoɔ tsu ko ni aŋã mli moŋ.

english: Weevil insects often lay invisible eggs on the cowpea pods while they are still growing in the field. Drying the beans thoroughly and storing them in sealed, airless containers prevents the eggs from hatching.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ woɔ tsina ŋmeii ni anaaa lɛ amli be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmeii lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafɔ̃.

english: Why do some of my maize seeds die in the soil right after I plant them instead of sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu amɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Seeds often fail to grow because the soil is too dry, seeds were planted too deep, or tiny soil insects ate them before they could break through the surface.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Adu dumɔwui lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. loo kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ Ye amɛ dani amɛbote sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my neighbor's maize plants growing tall and green while mine remain short and yellowish?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ miida ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa tso lɛ ji kuku ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Maize plants stay short and turn yellow when the soil lacks proper plant food (nutrients like nitrogen) or when the roots are not getting enough water to feed the plant.
ga: Abɛi hiɔ shi be kukuoo ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ tsei niyenii ni sa. (Nibii ni haa mɔ he waa tamɔ nitrogen) loo be mli ni shishifãi lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso lɛ aye nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some types of maize grow well without extra feeding, while other types require added inputs to yield anything?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ akɛ niyenii kroko fataaa he lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa henɔi komɛi biɔ nibii krokomɛi koni amɛná yibiiwoo lɛ.

english: Traditional local seeds are adapted to survive in poor soil with little care, whereas improved hybrid seeds are bred to produce very high yields but require extra food and water to grow well.
ga: Atsake maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii, ni asaaa nɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ be mli ni afɔɔ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo waa lɛ. Shi ebiɔ niyenii kɛ nu krokomɛi ni fata he dani ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I choose the right maize seed to plant if I do not have money for expensive crop treatments?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmãa dumɔwui ni sa ni mikɛbaadu? Kɛji obɛ shika ni okɛbaawo ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa lɛ ahe nyɔmɔ?

english: Look for local open-pollinated or drought-tolerant maize varieties that are known to produce reliable yields in your local soil without needing costly inputs.
ga: Taomɔ ŋmãa henɔi ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli ni agbeleɔ naa loo ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa ni ale akɛ amɛwoɔ yibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ nibii ni jara wa awo mli.

english: How does a shortage of rain or water affect my young maize crops right after planting?
ga: Te nugbɔ loo nu ni bɛ lɛ saa mibi lɛ ŋmãa lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ?

english: Without water, young seeds cannot soften to sprout, and seedling roots cannot pull up nutrients from the dirt, causing the plants to dry out and die early.
ga: Kɛ nu bɛ lɛ, dumɔwui bibii nyɛŋ akwɛ̃. Ni dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Ehaa tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya.

english: Why should I put fertilizer down near the base of my maize plants instead of just scattering it anywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmei tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ moŋ fe ni magbɛ amɛshwã he fɛɛ he?

english: Placing plant food close to the root area ensures the maize roots can quickly drink it up before rain washes it away or nearby weeds steal it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei aniyenii to he ni bɛŋkɛ shishifã lɛ he lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ nuɔ oya dani nugbɔ shwieɔ nɔ loo jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ juɔ lɛ.

english: What can I do to prepare my farm soil before planting so my crops do not fail?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni mikɛsaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dani madu nii koni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ akafite?

english: Clearing weeds, loosening hard dirt, and mixing in animal manure or compost helps the soil hold moisture and gives young roots an easy place to spread.
ga: weeding hard soil removal Ni kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ futu mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni eha shishifãi bibii lɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo.

english: What is the difference between food for the crop and medicine for crop diseases?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ niyenii ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsofa ni akɛtsaa tsei ahe helai ateŋ?

english: Fertilizer is like food that helps the crop grow strong, while plant medicine (pesticides or fungicides) protects or cures the crop when insects or diseases attack it.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tamɔ niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛdaraa waa. yɛ be mli ni tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ tsei (Insecticide loo fungicide) yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe loo ekwɛɔ nɔ kɛji kooloi loo helai tutua amɛ.

english: Is there a specific medicine I can pour under my maize when the plants start dying unexpectedly?
ga: Ani tsofa ko yɛ ni manyɛ mafɔse yɛ ŋmãa lɛ shishi kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɔi gbele trukaa?

english: Yes, if insects or soil fungi are killing your crops, specific pesticides or fungicides can be applied to the soil or leaves to stop the damage.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ miigbe onibii. Obaanyɛ okɛ tsofai komɛi ni gbeɔ kooloi loo ŋmeii awo shikpɔŋ loo baai lɛ anɔ koni ekpa nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: How can I tell whether my maize is dying because of insect pests or because it lacks food and water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmã lɛ miigbo yɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo niyenii kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ?

english: Pest damage usually leaves visible holes, spots, or chewed edges on leaves, whereas a lack of water or food causes whole leaves to roll up, turn yellow uniformly, or dry out from the tips.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shiɔ bu ni anaa, he ko, loo baa lɛ naa. yɛ be mli ni nu loo niyenii ni bɛ lɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Tsakemɔi kɛyaa su ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni tamɔ ekome loo ŋmɔlɔ ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to grow. Without enough nitrogen in the soil or from fertilizer, the leaves cannot make energy, leading to poor plant growth and small cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ni tsei akwɛ̃ Kɛji nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli Baai nyɛŋ afee hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why do my maize plants roll up their leaves tightly during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ shiŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves is the plant's natural defense against heat and dry weather. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun, helping it hold onto moisture and survive until the heat passes.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi ahe. Kɛ́ tso lɛ baai lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ehaa he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ehiɔ jɛmɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni latsaa lɛ hoɔ.

english: Why do I get smaller cobs when I replant seeds saved from my previous corn harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmei bibioo nɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds from hybrid maize varieties lose their vigor and yield strength in the next generation. Using fresh, certified seeds bought from official dealers ensures plants grow uniform, healthy, and produce maximum yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmãa srɔtoi ni akɛfee ŋmãa mli lɛ baafite hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Kɛ akɛ dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli ni ahe kɛjɛ mɛi ni jaa lɛ adɛŋ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ daa, ni amɛnáa hewalɛ, ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: How can I get more corn cobs from the small piece of land I farm?
ga: Mibaanyɛ maná ŋmãa ŋmeii babaoo kɛjɛ he bibioo ko. Nɛgbɛ mifeɔ okwaa yɛ?

english: You can maximize yield by planting seeds with proper spacing rather than scattering them, applying fertilizer at the right growth stages, and keeping weeds away early so the corn does not have to fight for nutrients.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha onibii babaoo aba kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni ooodu yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ. yɛ dumɔwui ni ooodu lɛ najiaŋ Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ be ni sa mli. ni ojie jwɛi lɛ mra. Bɔni afee ni ehe akahia ni ŋmãa lɛ atswa akaŋ kɛha niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: What causes holes in my young corn leaves and small caterpillars hidden inside the main leaf funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa? Minɔ lɛ yɛ teemɔ baa lɛ gbɛjegbɛ wulu lɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central leaf funnel to feed on young growth, but applying recommended insecticides or natural treatments early protects the growing tip of the plant.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛha tso bibioo lɛ dalɛ niyenii. Shi atsɔɔ akɛ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo adebɔɔ mli tsofafeemɔi atsu nii mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni abu tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe.

english: Why are some of my corn stems breaking and falling over before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miikumɔ ni amɛmiigbee shi dani kpamɔ baa lɛ?

english: Stems break when plant stalks are weakened by fungal diseases, stemborer insects, or a lack of potassium in the soil. Stalks need potassium to stay strong enough to carry heavy cobs through wind and rain.
ga: Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fãa kɛji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ha tso lɛ shishifã lɛ gbɔjɔ. He ni kooloi jɛ loo potassium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Potassium he miihia tsei lɛ koni amɛhe awa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo ŋmeii ni tsii kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ nɔ.

english: Why did my maize leaves turn brown and burn after I applied chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ ewo mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer burns plants if placed directly against the stem or applied when the soil is completely dry. Always place fertilizer a few centimeters away from the plant stem and apply it when the soil is moist from rain.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baashã tso lɛ kɛji akɛ akɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji sɛntimitai 2-3. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛjɛ nugbɔ mli.

english: Can I plant cowpeas or beans in the same field with my corn to improve my harvest?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmãa koni ŋmaa lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Yes, planting legumes like cowpeas alongside maize improves soil fertility because legumes trap nitrogen from the air and feed the soil, giving you a better maize harvest and an extra crop from the same field.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni onáa ŋmãa krokomɛi kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: Why does my harvested corn turn into white powder and get full of small insects in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpa lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ni ŋmeii bibii ebɔle he fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Grain weevils attack maize if the cobs are stored before they are completely dry or without protective grain treatment. Drying the grain until it is hard and using clean, hermetic storage bags keeps insects out.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ baatutua ŋmãa kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ to dani egbi kwraa loo kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsiɔ hela naa. Kɛ́ oogbi dumɔwui lɛ aahu kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni okɛ kotokui ni he tse ni atsĩ naa lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkabote mli.

english: Why do my corn plants stop growing and stay stunted if rain stops for two weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji nugbɔ kpa nɛmɔ otsii enyɔ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young maize roots need continuous soil moisture to absorb nutrients and expand. A dry spell right after germination forces the plant into survival mode, stopping its growth until moisture returns.
ga: Abɛi bibii shishifãi taoɔ shikpɔŋ nu ni mli edɔ daa koni eŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni egbɛ eshwa. Be ni tso lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ehi wala mli. ni okpa shweremɔ kɛyashi ŋmɔtɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my crops stop producing for a short while and then suddenly start flowering again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpa yibiiwoo be fioo, ni no sɛɛ lɛ ebɔi fɔfɔii shwiemɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Crops naturally go through cycles where flowering slows down while fruits mature. Once the mature fruit is harvested, good water and nutrients trigger the plant to re-flower and enter a new production cycle.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsɔɔ shihilɛ ko mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni fɔfɔi lɛ baa shi yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ. Kɛji akpa aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ Nu kpakpa kɛ niyenii kpakpai baaha tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ ni amɛbote nibii afeemɔ gbɛjianɔtoo hee mli.

english: How do I know if my crops are still active and capable of yielding another harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ lolo, ni kɛji manyɛ mawo ŋmaa kroko hu?

english: If your crop plants show green leaves, fresh shoots, or new blossom buds forming, they are still active and will produce more yield with proper care.
ga: Kɛji onibii lɛ miitsɔɔ baai eŋɔli, ŋmeii heei, loo ŋmeii heei. Amɛtsuɔ nii lolo ni amɛbaawo babaoo kɛji akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my harvest yield drop temporarily before increasing again during the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi be kukuoo ko dani eyaa hiɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yield drops temporarily because the crop diverts its energy from feeding mature fruit to growing new shoots and buds. Regular watering and fertilizer help speed up this recovery.
ga: Yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi yɛ be kukuoo mli beni tsei lɛ tsakeɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ni amɛhaa amɛ kɛyaa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii heei ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ helatsamɔ nɛɛ aya hiɛ oya.

english: Why do my cocoa trees flower again while there are still mature pods on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ekoŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii ni eda lolo lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees can flower continuously when there is sufficient rainfall and soil nutrients, allowing new pods to develop even while older pods are ready for harvest.
ga: Cacao tsei baanyɛ aya nɔ awo fɔfɔi kɛji nugbɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii heei jeɔ kpo yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii momoi lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ po.

english: What simple practices will help keep my crops producing continuously throughout the season?
ga: Gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo Mɛni baaye abua ni miŋmɔshi nibii aya nɔ awo yibii yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Ensuring regular irrigation, pruning dead branches, applying fertilizer at key growing stages, and controlling weeds will keep crop plants active and flowering longer.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi daa lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ Niji ni egboi lɛ akwɛmɔ Ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ dalɛ bei ni he hiaa lɛ amli Kɛ jwɛi ni akudɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important to start my seeds in a nursery before moving them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni aje dumɔwui ashishi yɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe lɛ dani ajie amɛ kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: A nursery protects tender young seedlings from strong sunlight, heavy rain, and pests, giving them a safe environment to build strong root systems before field planting.
ga: He ni akwɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ lɛ buɔ dumɔwui bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe, ni ehaa amɛnáa shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛma shishifãi ni mli wa dani amɛdu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: What steps should I take on my farm before receiving new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii esa akɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani maná kookoo dumɔwui heei?

english: Clear the land, dig planting holes of the correct size, and establish shade crops like plantains so the delicate cocoa seedlings are protected when transplanted.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ Tsɔɔmɔ dumɔ bu ni dalɛ sa. ni amɛfee tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛkɛbu kookoo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛ́ adu amɛ.

english: How do I know if the seeds or planting materials I buy are healthy and ready to plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui loo dumɔ nibii ni miheɔ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni esa akɛ adu?

english: Good planting materials should be uniform in size, free of visible mold or insect damage, and sourced from certified agricultural suppliers or extension offices.
ga: Esa akɛ nibii ni hi ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ dalɛ afee ekome. Ebɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo kooloi bibii ni anaa. ni anáa kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli nibii ahe nitsulɔi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ loo nitsumɔhei ni yaa hiɛ lɛ adɛŋ.

english: How long should my seedlings stay in the nursery before I plant them in the ground?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mi dumɔwui lɛ ahi ŋmɔ mli dani mikɛ amɛ awo shikpɔŋ?

english: Seedlings should remain in the nursery until they are strong enough, usually when they have developed several true leaves and a firm root mass, which takes a few weeks depending on the crop.
ga: Esa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahi ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli beni anɔkwa baai babaoo kɛ shishifãi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ heɔ otsii fioo komɛi yɛ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ naa.

english: Is it better for me to buy ready seedlings from a nursery or plant seeds directly on my land?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni asaa he kɛjɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe loo madu dumɔwui yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Buying prepared nursery seedlings increases plant survival rates because the seedlings have already passed their most vulnerable growth stage under protected conditions.
ga: Dumɔwui ni asaa he lɛ ahemɔ haa tso lɛ wala yaa hiɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dumɔwui eho amɛdalɛ be ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ lɛ mli momo yɛ shihilɛi ni abuɔ he lɛ amli.

english: Why are my mango trees dropping all their flowers before any fruit begins to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tsei lɛ fɛɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ?

english: Mango trees often shed flowers due to sudden dry spells, strong winds, or pests like thrips. Ensuring the trees get enough water during flowering and controlling pests early helps the flowers stay on and turn into fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mango tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ thrips hewɔ. Ehe miihia ni akwɛ koni tso lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ fɔfɔi be mli kɛ mra be mli ni agbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai. Enɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil or the ground is waterlogged. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted compost helps restore the soil nutrients and greens up the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu eyi sũ lɛ mli obɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi ŋmɔji.

english: How do I know the right distance to leave between my crops when planting on large acreage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni sa ni kã ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ kɛ́ mikwɛ̃ yɛ he ko ni da?

english: Different crops need specific spacing so their roots and leaves do not fight for food and sunlight. For example, large fruit trees need several meters between them, while grain crops like maize are planted closer together in straight rows.
ga: Esa akɛ aŋmɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi lɛ ahe gbɛ pɔtɛɛ ko bɔni afee ni shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ akatswa niyenii kɛ hulu la he akaŋ. Ákɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni tsei wuji ni woɔ yibii lɛ kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ahi mitai babaoo. yɛ be mli ni aduɔ ŋmaa nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa ni ja mli.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are ready to harvest under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell it is maturing when the bottom leaves yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to crack as the tubers swell.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ edara kwraa kɛ́ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ amli shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Is it safe for my soil if I plant cassava and maize together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa fee ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, this is called intercropping. Maize grows fast and is harvested in a few months, while cassava grows slower and takes over the field after the maize is harvested, helping you get two crops from one field.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ intercropping. Abɛi daa oya ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Shi ŋmãa lɛ, daa blɛoo ni eŋɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ. Ehaa onine shɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and getting dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛgbi lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a virus, or by severe heat stress. Removing affected plants early and keeping whiteflies away helps prevent the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli ni ajieɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ mra Ni ajieɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my crops wilt in the afternoon heat even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: In hot afternoon sun, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can drink it from the soil. Covering the soil around the plant roots with dry grass or leaves keeps the soil cool and holds moisture longer.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds always grow faster and taller than my planted crops after the rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛkwɔ fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to grow aggressively in poor soils and steal water, sunlight, and nutrients. Clearing weeds early in the season ensures your main crops get the food they need to outgrow the weeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ ni amɛju nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni onibii titri lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ oya fe jwɛi lɛ.

english: Should I start planting my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui akwɛmɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is better to wait until the rains become regular. The first rain is often followed by a long dry stretch, which can dry out and kill newly germinated seeds in the hot soil.
ga: Ehi akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot while they are still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads in wet, shady conditions. Trimming excess branches to let in sunshine and removing damaged pods keeps the rest of the tree healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la aba ni ojie tsei ni efite lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen or is waterlogged. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or well-decomposed animal manure will help the plants regain their green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant groundnuts or beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ akwɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts naturally pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. Planting them alongside maize improves soil fertility for free and gives you two different food crops from the same piece of land.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ yaa hiɛ yaka. Ni ehaa onine shɛɔ niyenii srɔtoi enyɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my young crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, called mulching, acts like an umbrella against the hot sun. It keeps moisture in the ground for much longer, keeps the roots cool, and stops weeds from growing easily.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ mlɛo

english: What happens if I plant my crops too close to each other on the farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ mihe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, soil water, and food. This makes the plants grow thin and weak, resulting in very small fruits or grains compared to crops given proper space.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ Ekɛ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii yeɔ akaŋ, ni no haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai loo dumɔwui lɛ faaa kwraa kɛ akɛto tsei ni aha amɛ he ko ni sa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do I need to cut away some of the young shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwu titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Too many shoots around the mother plantain tree force it to share its food with all of them, which makes the plantain bunch very small. Leaving only one or two strong shoots ensures your main tree yields big, heavy bunches.
ga: Dumɔwui aniji babaoo ni ebɔle fɔlɔ tso lɛ he lɛ nyɛɔ enɔ ni ekɛ dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ yeɔ niyenii. ni haa plantains akuu lɛ feɔ bibioo waa Kɛ́ oshi niji kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha otso titri lɛ awo niji wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops after the rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that naturally absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than farm crops. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing food and water from your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni jɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Okɛ ohe awo mli mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting in the ground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long, especially during heavy rains in poorly drained land. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ hei ni nu hoɔ yɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers without forming cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miijie fɔfɔi ni amɛjieee cacao ŋmɔtɔi lɛ kpo lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by prolonged heat, poor soil nutrients, or insect pests like mirids. Providing shade trees, feeding the soil, and managing pests help the flowers turn into healthy pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛbote hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ pollen, ni haa hulutsoo, kɛ niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ Ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and stopping the plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiikpa tso lɛ dalɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is often caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies, or by extreme heat. Using insect nets, spraying recommended insecticides, and watering regularly protects the plants from curl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly loo kɛjɛɔ latsaa ni naa wa mli Kɛtsɔ kooloi a-netting ni akɛtsuɔ nii Tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni ajieɔ yi akɛ ashwie nɔ Ni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa lɛ baaye abua ni ebu tso lɛ he koni ekafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How do I know if caterpillars are destroying my maize leaves inside the stalk?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmeii miifite ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: If caterpillars like Fall Armyworm are present, you will see ragged holes in the leaves and small powdery droppings inside the central funnel of the maize plant. Identifying this early allows you to apply control measures before the central shoot is destroyed.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm yɛ lɛ, obaana ŋmeii ni ekpɔtɔ yɛ baai lɛ amli kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tamɔ powda. Eyɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Enɛ ni oooyɔse mra Enɛ baaha onyɛ okɛ gbɛjianɔtoi akudɔ dani akpata la ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ hiɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow instead of bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer will help them regain their strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes my cocoa flowers to dry up and fall off without making pods?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they suffer from extreme heat, water shortage, or pest attacks. Maintaining good shade trees in your farm helps keep the soil moist and protects the delicate flowers from hot sun.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ amɛyashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ he. nu ni faaa loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni ebu fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize together on the same plot of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting cassava and maize together works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested within a few months, leaving plenty of room and sunlight for the cassava to grow heavy tubers later.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ he kome lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Enɛ haa gbɛ kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ŋmei lɛ akwɛ ŋmeii ni tsii yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why are my tomato plants staying short and bushy instead of growing tall and strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ feɔ kukuji ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaadara ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Tomato plants remain stunted when the soil is packed too tight for roots to spread, when water is lacking, or when early pest infections weaken the plant root system.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbɛ ashwã, kɛ́ nu bɛ, loo kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ mra lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: What makes my yam tubers start rotting underground before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni ha mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ bɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mikpa amɛ po?

english: Yam rot in the soil happens when rain sits in waterlogged ground without proper drainage, or when small soil pests bite into the yam and let fungal rot enter the tuber.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ baa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ. Aloo beni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii ŋmɔɔ sweet potatoes ni amɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants start producing many flowers right after the major rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Rainwater provides a sudden rush of moisture and nutrients, signaling to the plant that conditions are ideal to produce flowers and feed growing fruits.
ga: Nugbɔ haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yaa hiɛ trukaa. Etsɔɔ tso lɛ akɛ shihilɛi ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha fɔfɔii afeemɔ kɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do weeds in my farm cause my crops to produce smaller harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal essential water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. When crops have to fight weeds for food, they do not have enough energy left to yield large grains or fruits.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Beni esa akɛ tsei kɛ jwɛi awuu koni amɛná niyenii Amɛbɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaawo dumɔwui loo aduawai wuji.

english: Why should I cut off some of the healthy branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ niji ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Removing excess branches allows fresh air and sunlight to pass deep into the tree crown. This reduces humidity that causes black pod disease and forces the tree to direct energy into pod growth.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la boteɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ shɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ baa shi, ni enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ tsuɔ black pods ni miida lɛ ahe nii.

english: Why do maize seeds saved from my last harvest yield less than new certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from harvested hybrid crops lose their strength in the next generation. Certified seeds are specially produced under strict conditions to ensure high yields and disease resistance every planting season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Afeɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wa amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni ekwɛ akɛ ewo yibii babaoo ni helai nyɛɔ eshiɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my plantain trees turn brown and dry during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees naturally drop their older bottom leaves to save water and keep the green top leaves alive when moisture in the ground drops low.
ga: Plantains lɛ shwieɔ amɛshishi baai ni egbɔ lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ nɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ faaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when there is too much sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate roots and soft leaves that dry out quickly under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains nearby creates a protective canopy that reduces heat stress and retains moisture around the cocoa until it grows stronger.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo he haomɔ baa shi ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni ebɔle he lɛ hiɔ shi. kookoo kɛyashi ebaawa

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow instead of green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ eŋɔli najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to build food and stay green. Adding compost, manure, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the maize regain its natural green color and grow stronger.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua o-ŋmei lɛ ni ehi shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes my cassava roots to rot underground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔ be baashɛ?

english: Cassava root rot happens when soil stays soaked with too much water for too long, preventing air from reaching the roots. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji akɛ akɛ nu babaoo wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, they fight each other for limited space, sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Spacing them properly gives each plant room to stretch its roots and leaves for maximum yield.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná he ko, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. kɛ nu fioo Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa hegbɛ ni ekɛ eshishifãi kɛ ebaai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do improved seed varieties yield more than the seeds I save from last year's harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi nikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Improved seeds are bred to fight off local diseases, withstand drought, and produce larger crops, while seeds saved over many seasons gradually lose their strength and become more vulnerable to pests.
ga: Abaawo dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ koni akɛwu ashi maŋ lɛ mli helai. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ hɔmɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ yɛ bei babaoo mli lɛ baafite hewalɛ fiofio ni ebaafee nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ aye amɛnɔ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants without producing any pepper fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo pepper yibii ko lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by intense heat, uneven watering, or a lack of bees and insects to pollinate them. Maintaining steady moisture in the soil helps the plant hold onto its flowers until fruit forms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ be fɛɛ be loo ŋmeii kɛ kooloi krokomɛi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ baa lɛ ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Is it better to water my garden vegetables early in the morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha obɔɔ mli aduawai lɛ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: Watering early in the morning allows the soil to absorb water deeply before heat causes it to evaporate, giving plants the moisture they need to survive the hottest parts of the day.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ dani la ni tsoɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ naa nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: Why does planting groundnuts make my soil better for growing maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei dumɔ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmei dumɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the groundnut plant dies, that stored nitrogen breaks down in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for future crops like maize.
ga: Akpɔlɔi jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji ŋmei tso lɛ gbo Nitrogen ni ato lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my harvested grains turn to powder and get small holes after a few months in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ ji powder ni amɛyɛ bu bibii lɛ? Beni akɛto nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ

english: Small holes and powder are signs of weevils, which lay eggs inside stored grain. Drying grain thoroughly in the sun and keeping it sealed tightly in airtight bags stops these insects from breeding.
ga: Buji bibii kɛ sũ ji ŋmeii ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ amli lɛ ahe okadi. Dumɔwui lɛ ni agbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni akɛwoɔ vacuum kotokui amli jogbaŋŋ lɛ haaa nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ afɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my main crops after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to steal water and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops a fair chance to take up fertilizer and grow unhindered.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛná ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛdara ni nɔ ko nɔ ko akatsi amɛ gbɛ.

english: What is a greenhouse, and how does farming inside it help my vegetables grow better than in an open field?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋwɛitsu? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ okwaayeli ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi aduawai lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: A greenhouse is a plastic or mesh structure that covers crops to shield tender vegetables like tomatoes and peppers from heavy rains, scorching sun, and harmful insects, allowing them to produce high yields all year round.
ga: Greenhouses ji plastic loo ŋshɔŋlooi ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni ebu aduawai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, tamɔ tomato kɛ shitoi ahe, kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa, kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara Enɛ haa tsei nɛɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants roll up tightly into tubes during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during extreme heat as a natural self-defense mechanism to reduce water evaporation and conserve soil moisture until temperatures cool down.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni haa nu ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yaa hiɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni latsaa lɛ baashɛ shi.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Blossoms drop off when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of essential soil nutrients like calcium, which prevents successful pollination.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ calcium, ni haaa pollination lɛ aye omanye.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when planted in direct sunlight without any surrounding shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni hulutsoo bɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive, soft leaves that easily burn under full sun; they require temporary shade from fast-growing plants like plantains to maintain soil moisture and establish healthy roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni amɛma shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings look weak and droop for a few days immediately after I move them from the nursery to my main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables dumɔwui lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi gbii fioo komɛi beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: This is called transplant shock, caused by root disturbance during movement; planting during cooler late afternoons and watering heavily helps seedlings recover quickly.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji shishifãi lɛ ni agbalaa amɛhe yɛ be mli ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe lɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shwane ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ babaoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhe waaa oya.

english: How does a cassava crop manage to survive and grow roots even during long dry spells when rain does not fall?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei tsei ahi shi ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ po mli?

english: Cassava has deep, tough root systems that store water and starch, allowing the plant to shut down excess leaf growth and draw stored energy from underground during dry weather.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, ni wa ni kɛ nu kɛ starch toɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtsiɔ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anaa ni amɛgbalaa hewalɛ ni ato kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be mli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my tomato plants turning yellow while the top leaves remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil or overwatering, forcing the plant to move nutrients upward to protect new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ ajie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi koni ebu shweremɔ hee ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ he.

english: When is the right time for me to apply fertilizer to my maize crop so the stalk grows thick and strong?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi ni amɛhe awa?

english: Fertilizer should be applied early—first around two weeks after germination and again when the plant is knee-high—so the crop has nutrients when it builds its stem before flowering.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii mra. Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ ji aaafee otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni ekwɛ̃ lɛ. kɛ agbɛnɛ hu beni tso lɛ shɛɔ etsitsi nɔ Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ beni amɛmaa ŋmeii dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to pinch off the small side shoots growing in the stem joints of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tomato tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Removing side shoots, also called suckers, directs food and water away from unnecessary foliage and focuses the plant's strength into growing bigger and healthier fruit.
ga: Ajieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ afã, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ ŋmeii. Ejieɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni he ehiaaa kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli. ni ema hewalɛ ni akɛaaha tsei koni amɛwo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ mi.

english: Why do weeds make my crop plants look stunted even when I apply enough water to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miikpa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔji amli moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that aggressively steal hidden soil nutrients, fertilizer, and light directly from your main crops before the crops can absorb them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ tsei ni oyɔɔ mli lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ amɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my young maize farm turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the food plants use to build strong green leaves. It can also happen if heavy rain has washed nutrients deep into the soil where roots cannot reach them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: What is causing small leaves in the center of my maize plants to look like they were chewed by insects?
ga: Mɛni haa baai lɛ feɔ bibii? Mi-abɛi tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni kooloi bibii eye.

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central leaves of young maize plants to eat the tender growth, and early control with proper treatment is needed to save the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli koni amɛye ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ. Ni ehe miihia ni akudɔ tsofafeemɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ mra. koni akɛbu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe

english: Why do the leaves on my newly transplanted cocoa seedlings wither and dry up in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui ni midu ehee lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive to intense heat and need shade to survive. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains around them keeps the air cool and protects their tender leaves from burning.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa ni amɛ taoɔ shade koni amɛ hi shi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, yɛ amɛhe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaaa baai bibii lɛ ashã.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when the rain becomes too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess rainwater sits around the roots for too long without draining, fungal rot develops, so planting on mounds or ridges helps water flow away easily.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ taraa shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Mushroom fitemɔ baa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu lɛ ajɛ mli oya.

english: Why do I need to tie long wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafi tsei kakadaji koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines produce bigger tubers when their leaves catch maximum sunlight. Lifting the leaves off the ground with stakes keeps them exposed to light and prevents soil diseases from infecting the foliage.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ bulbs wuji kɛji amɛbaai lɛ shɛ hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei wo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa baa lɛ naa la, ni ehaaa helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ akabote baai lɛ amli.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant groundnuts or beans inside my maize field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ mi-corn ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans have special roots that take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. Planting them alongside maize naturally improves the soil quality for your maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ odu lɛ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo kɛha oŋmãa lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crop stems with dry grass and leave it there?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ ni mashi jɛmɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops sunlight from drying out the earth too fast, suppresses weeds from growing, and slowly decays into rich organic plant food.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu la akagbi shikpɔŋ lɛ oya tsɔ. Ehaa jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa fiofio ni etsɔɔ tsei aniyenii ni jara wa, ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli.

english: When is the best time for me to put fertilizer on my crops so it works effectively?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli koni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist, ideally right after light rain or early in the morning. Applying it during heavy rain washes it away, while applying it to dry soil can burn plant roots.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ fioo sɛɛ. loo leebi maŋkpa Kɛ́ okɛtsu nii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha etsɔ. Yɛ be mli ni kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ shishifãi ashã.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers before any peppers form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani pepper lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they suffer from sudden temperature changes, poor soil moisture, or a lack of key nutrients. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the plant keep its flowers and produce fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tsake trukaa. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehiii loo niyenii mli nibii titrii ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔii amli ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How do I choose the best plantain shoots from my old farm to start a new field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantains ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli koni mikɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Look for young shoots called 'maiden suckers' that have thick stems at the bottom and narrow, spear-like leaves. These shoots grow faster and establish stronger roots than shoots with wide, fully open leaves.
ga: Taomɔ tsei bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘tsei,’ ni amɛshishigbɛ tsei lɛ amli tsei kɛ baai ni mli tseee ni tamɔ akpɔlɔi. Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ baakwɛ̃ oya ni amɛbaawo shishifãi ni mli wa fe tsei ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ, ni amɛgbele amɛhe kwraa lɛ.

english: Is it safe to plant seed tubers or stem cuttings if they feel soft on the inside?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu dumɔwui ayitsei loo ŋmeii kɛji akɛ emli nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ bɔdɔɔ?

english: Soft planting material is often rotting or damaged by pests. Planting soft materials makes them sprout very slowly or fail completely because they lack the healthy strength needed to push out new shoots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ fiteɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai fiteɔ. Nibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni aduɔ lɛ baaha amɛkwɛ̃ blɛoo waa loo amɛfite kwraa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbɛ hewalɛ ni sa ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei.

english: How can I tell if my planting materials are healthy enough to put in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midumɔ nii lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Healthy planting materials should feel firm and solid to the touch, have no bad smell, and show no signs of mold or rot on the inside or outside.
ga: Esa akɛ dumɔ nii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ anu he akɛ eyɛ shiŋŋ ni ehi shi shiŋŋ kɛji akɛ ata he. ŋmɔlɔ gbonyo ko bɛ Ni ŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔ ko bɛ mli loo kponɔgbɛ.

english: Why do my seeds sometimes decay in the ground before they can sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds rot underground when the soil is overly wet, or if the seeds were already damaged and soft before planting, making them vulnerable to soil diseases.
ga: Dumɔwui fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ. aloo kɛji dumɔwui lɛ efite ni amɛfee bɔdɔɔ dani adu Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ oshara kɛha helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli baa lɛ.

english: How many weeks should I expect to wait before my planted crops sprout out of the ground?
ga: Otsii enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani miŋmɔshi nibii ni midu lɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Depending on the crop type and soil conditions, sprouting usually takes anywhere from a few days to two or three weeks for new shoots to appear above the soil.
ga: Edamɔ tso henɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwereɔ lɛ heɔ gbii fioo komɛi kɛyashi otsii enyɔ loo etɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii heei jeɔ kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my crops taking longer than three weeks to show shoots after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ heɔ be fe otsii etɛ dani ejieɔ ŋmeii kpo beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Delayed sprouting happens if the soil is too dry, if seeds are planted too deep, or if the planting material was weak or soft before it went into the ground.
ga: Nibii ni shwereɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ mli kwɔ tsɔ loo kɛji akɛ nɔ ni akɛduɔ lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ loo eyɛ bɔdɔɔ dani adu yɛ shikpɔŋ.

english: Why do some crops come out of the soil quickly while others take weeks to appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi jeɔ kpo oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu heɔ otsii babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Different crops have different growth speeds; simple seeds sprout quickly, while thick cuttings, root setts, or crops planted in tough soil take two to three weeks to push shoots to the surface.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi yɛ bɔ ni amɛdaraa oya amɛhaa lɛ srɔtoi. Dumɔwui folo kwɛ̃ɔ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi ni shishifãi yɔɔ mli loo tsei ni akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ sũ mli lɛ baahe otsii enyɔ loo etɛ ni ekɛtsi ŋmeii lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Does clearing weeds early really help my crops sprout faster?
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ani eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛdaraa oya?

english: Yes, clearing weeds gives your planted seeds full access to sunlight, soil nutrients, and moisture, which helps shoots break through the soil much faster.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui ni odu lɛ naa hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulutsoo kwraa Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya kwraa.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops before the plants even break through the surface?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui dani amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amɛha tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal water and plant food from the soil around your buried seeds, making the ground dry and starved, which slows down shoot emergence.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ. dumɔwui ni afu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ adara blɛoo.

english: What simple field care should I provide right after planting to ensure good sprouting?
ga: Esa akɛ makwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ mlɛo. Mɛni esa akɛ afee yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Keep the soil weed-free, ensure the soil stays moderately moist, and avoid compacting the dirt so shoots can easily push upwards.
ga: Ha jwɛi akafee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kwɛmɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ooofee lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ he koni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ ashɛre kɛya ŋwɛi oya.

english: Why is it important to work and loosen the soil well before putting my crops in?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni atsu nii ni ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani adu nii lɛ?

english: Loosening the ground makes it easy for water to soak in and gives young shoots a soft path to emerge without spending too much energy.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa nu lɛ boteɔ mli mlɛo. ni ehaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni amɛaatsɔ nɔ amɛdara ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuuu nii.

english: How can I tell if a piece of land will be good for planting maize before I buy or clear it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male shikpɔŋ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔ dani mahe loo mafo mli?

english: Good maize land has deep, dark soil that does not hold standing water after heavy rain. If you see tall green grasses and thick vegetation naturally growing on the land, it is a strong sign that the soil has rich nutrients suitable for crops.
ga: Abɛi shikpɔŋ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli edɔ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ mli. Kɛji ona jwɛi kakadaŋŋ aŋɔli kɛ tsei ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. No ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ niyenii ni sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees turn yellow and dry up when there are no big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle strong direct sunlight because their leaves burn easily. Big shade trees or temporary crops like plantains act like umbrellas, keeping the cocoa cool and helping the soil retain moisture so the young plants can survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo loo be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ koni tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with thin stems but yield tiny tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? Tso lɛ mli tse shi ehaa yitso bibioo.

english: When cassava plants are planted too close together, they compete for sunlight and soil nutrients. The plant spends all its energy growing tall to reach the sun instead of sending food down into the roots to build large tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ Ebaatswa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛ́ amɛmiida yɛ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛshɛ hulu lɛ he. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye ní kɛ yaa sisi ɔ mi konɛ e pee bulb nguahi.

english: Why do my plantain suckers fail to grow if I plant them right at the start of the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers need a constant supply of water to sprout fresh roots. Planting them just before the dry season leaves them in hot, dry soil where they dry out and die before they can establish strong roots.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ ahe miihia nu ni yaa nɔ koni shishifãi heei akwɛ̃. Kɛ́ adu amɛ dani hulutsoo be lɛ shɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛhi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ. Amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why does my farm yield less maize every year when I plant it in the exact same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa kome lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on nitrogen in the soil. Planting maize in the same spot year after year drains the soil of those nutrients, causing weak plants and smaller harvests unless you rotate with crops like cowpea or add nutrients back to the soil.
ga: Abele haa nitrogen babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa nakai niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Ja okɛ tsei tamɔ tsina ŋmei tsakeɔ loo okɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ku sɛɛ ewoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and stopping the fruits from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiikpa aduawai lɛ adalɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites that hide under the leaves and suck out the juice. This damages the plant tissue, stunting new leaf growth and preventing flowers from turning into pepper pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii, tamɔ thrips loo mites, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni amɛmuɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Enɛ fiteɔ tsei amli fãji. ha baai heei akpa ni etsĩ fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ pepper ŋmɔtɔi

english: Can I plant cassava and maize on the same piece of land without them killing each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni migbeee mihe?

english: Yes, planting cassava and maize together works well because maize grows fast and is harvested in about three to four months, while cassava grows slowly at first and takes over the field after the maize is harvested.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya ni akpaa yɛ aaafee nyɔji 3-4 mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni eŋɔ he lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot underground before I am ready to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mifee klalo akɛ makpa lɛ?

english: Yams rot underground when the soil holds too much water or when tiny worms in the soil bite the skin of the tuber. Excessive water prevents air from reaching the roots, allowing rot-causing fungi to multiply quickly in the wet earth.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo loo kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ŋmɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahewolo. Nu babaoo baatsi kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ feɔ babaoo oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ.

english: Why should I buy fresh certified seeds instead of saving seeds from my last maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe ni makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ naagbee ŋmãa kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato?

english: Seeds saved from harvested maize often lose their vigor and carry diseases from the previous season. Certified seeds are specially bred and treated to resist pests, germinate uniformly, and produce much higher yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ baa shi ni ekɛ helai ni jɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baa. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni atsuɔ he nii koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai, amɛkwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster than my crop seedlings after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe midumɔwui lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Wild weeds are naturally adapted to local soil conditions and have deep root systems or dormant seeds waiting in the dirt. When the rains arrive, weeds absorb water and fertilizer much faster than young crops, which is why clearing them early is essential.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛyaa he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo dumɔwui ni egboi yɛ ni miimɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie lɛ mra lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the corn is fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient for growth. The plant steals nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the younger growing leaves on top when the soil does not have enough fertilizer or manure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why does applying fertilizer to my crops during heavy rain wash away its benefits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ejieɔ sɛɛnamɔi ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes the fertilizer off the soil surface before the roots have a chance to drink it. This leads to wasted input costs and leaves the crop without the nutrients it needs to grow strong.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani shishifãi lɛ naa hegbɛ amɛnuɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahe nyɔmɔwoo fiteɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ bɛ.

english: Why do my crops yield smaller fruits when I plant the seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?
