english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight for the same water and soil nutrients, and their leaves block sunlight from each other. This competition leaves the plant with less energy to produce large fruits or grains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. ni baai lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haaa tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ babaoo ni amɛkɛwo aduawai loo ŋmaa wuji.

english: Why do some of the maize seeds I buy fail to sprout after I plant them in wet soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mihe lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are too old, were stored in hot or humid conditions, or were damaged by insects. Bad storage destroys the living embryo inside the seed, preventing it from growing into a healthy shoot.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji amɛgbɔ tsɔ. ni akɛtoɔ he ko ni mli edɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ loo kooloi bibii efite lɛ Kɛ́ akɛtoɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaakpata fɔmɔ kotokui ni hiɛ ka ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ ahiɛ. Etsiɔ enaa koni ekatsɔ ŋmeii ni he wa.

english: Why do insects keep returning to damage my crops even after I spray chemical pesticides?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi akuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbafiteɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ eshwie nɔ po lɛ?

english: Pests return if the chemical mixture is diluted too much, sprayed at the wrong time of day when insects are hiding, or if the same pesticide is used continuously, which makes the insects resistant to the chemical over time.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛfutu mli lɛ wo nu mli tsɔ. Okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni esaaa mli beni kooloi kɛ amɛhe ewo mli lɛ. aloo kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii be fɛɛ be Enɛ haa kooloi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ tsofai lɛ anɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and turning pale green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is commonly caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading viral diseases to the plant, or by the plant reacting to severe heat and drought stress to prevent water loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni tsɛŋeɔ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei ni feɔ amɛnii yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ mli koni nu akafite lɛ nɔ.

english: How do weeds growing near my young crops slow down their overall growth?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ aha amɛdalɛ fɛɛ aba shi?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal vital soil nutrients, fertilizers, water, and sunlight away from your crops, effectively starving the young crop during its most critical growth stage.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, ŋmɔshi nibii, nu kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii yɛ amɛdalɛ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers fall off the tree branches without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they suffer from heat stress, lack of soil moisture, or when tiny insects called midges are missing to pollinate the blossoms and form pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ laajeɔ koni ekɛ fɔfɔi lɛ awo ŋmɔtɔ mli ni efee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: What causes my cassava roots to rot underground before I am ready to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays waterlogged for too long during heavy rains. Excess water cuts off oxygen to the roots, allowing harmful soil fungi to attack and decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa amɛ ni amɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the heavy fruit bunch starts to ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛji aduawai akui lɛ bɔi shweremɔ pɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that stay near the top of the soil. As the heavy bunch grows at the top, the plant becomes top-heavy and can easily tip over in strong winds unless supported with a wooden stake.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛji akɛ kuu lɛ da yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Tsei lɛ tsii ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbee shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. ja akɛ tso ko efi sɛɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow at the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient for growth. Rain can wash nitrogen away, so applying fertilizer like NPK or urea at the right time helps bring back the green color and boost yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Nugbɔ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo urea tsu nii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What is eating small holes in the center of my young corn leaves?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that hides inside the young maize leaves. Catching them early and applying approved crop protection sprays will protect your plants before they are destroyed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni ebu otsei lɛ ahe dani amɛfite.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open sunny field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni midu yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu la kpɛɔ yɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive harsh direct sunlight and heat. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects them from burning and keeps the soil moist while they grow strong roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ gbɛ. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shãa shãaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small plantain shoots growing around my main plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ plantain tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Mi tso titri lɛ he Ajie.

english: If too many shoots grow around one plantain tree, they fight for nutrients and produce small fruit. Leaving only two or three strong shoots ensures the main plant gets enough food to grow large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ dumɔwu kome Ebaatswa niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ ni ebaawo yibii bibii. Kɛ́ ashi tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: How do I know when my cassava is ready to be harvested from under the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmãa lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves start turning yellow and dropping off. You can also carefully dig around one plant to check if the roots are thick and firm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ ohe awo mli hu. Kwɛmɔ tso kome mli jogbaŋŋ koni ona kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli tse ni amɛma shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to put tall sticks in the ground for my yam plants to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ awo shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves off the wet soil so they can catch maximum sunlight to make food for the plant. It also prevents leaf rot, helping the yam tubers grow much bigger underground.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Etsiɔ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ hu naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet. Giving your tomatoes steady water and shading them during intense heat helps the flowers turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Kɛ́ aha tomato nu kɛ hulutsoo yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfee yɛ tomato lɛ nɔ.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves healthy so the plant can produce good peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ekpɔtɔ yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Ehe hia ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ mra. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ awo ŋmeii kpakpai.

english: Why does clearing weeds early make my crops grow so much bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ ni miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ babaoo?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from your crops. Clearing them during the first few weeks gives your crops full access to the soil's food so they can grow strong without competition.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: How does adding dried animal manure to my farm help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni egbi ni mikɛfataa miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Animal manure acts as a natural soil builder, slowly feeding nutrients to your crops. It also helps the soil hold onto moisture longer during dry spells, protecting your plants from drying out.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii, ni fiofio lɛ ekɛ niyenii haa onibii lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hu ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Can I use salty well water to irrigate my tomato crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmei nu ŋshɔ lɛ mli nu awo tomato tsei anɔ?

english: Salty underground water damages crop roots and prevents plants from taking up essential nutrients, which wilts tomatoes and reduces fruit yields.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli edɔ lɛ fiteɔ tsei shishifãi ni ehaaa tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ. Enɛ baaha tomatoi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha aduawai ni anáa lɛ aba shi.

english: Why should I test my borehole water before using it to water my vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maka nu ni yɔɔ mi-borehole lɛ mli lɛ makwɛ dani mikɛtsu nii kɛwo aduawai amli nu lɛ?

english: Underground water can carry hidden salts or harmful minerals that cause crop diseases, burn plant roots, or slow down crop growth without you realizing it.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi nu baanyɛ ahiɛ ŋmeii loo sũ mli nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni baanyɛ aha tsei aná helai, efite tsei shishifãi, loo eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni oleee.

english: Can using bad quality water from a shallow well make my crops sick?
ga: Ani nu ni ehiii ni jɛɔ nu bu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ mli lɛ ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ baaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hela?

english: Yes, water containing harmful bacteria or excessive minerals can cause root rot, fungal spots on leaves, and general crop sickness.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni muawai ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo minerals ni fa fe nine yɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbo, baai amli ŋmeii, kɛ tsei ahe helai fɛɛ aba.

english: Why are my crop leaves turning yellow even though I give them borehole water every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ borehole nu daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: If your underground water contains high levels of salt or chemicals, it damages the root system, preventing the plant from absorbing nutrients, which turns the leaves yellow.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei loo tsofai babaoo yɛ oshikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ mli. Ebaakpata shishifãi lɛ ahiɛ. Ehaa tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ

english: Why are the leaf edges of my pepper plants turning brown after watering them from my new well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni mikɛ nu jɛ mi-po hee lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is often a sign of salt burn caused by underground water that has high salt content, which accumulates in the leaves and dries them out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji ŋoo shãa ni shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni ŋoo babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛbaa lɛ he okadi, ni buaa ehe naa yɛ baai lɛ amli ni ehaa amɛgbiɔ.

english: Is underground water from a borehole as good for my crops as normal rainwater?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni jɛɔ nubu mli lɛ hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ nugbɔ nu ni baa daa lɛ?

english: Rainwater is pure and naturally best for crops, whereas underground water may contain salts or heavy minerals depending on the soil layers in your area.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ he tse ni ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni ŋmeii loo minerals ni tsii yɔɔ mli. Edamɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Will salty underground water completely stop my maize from growing?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli edɔ lɛ baaha mi-abele lɛ akpa shweremɔ kwraa?

english: High salt levels in water create toxic conditions for maize roots, causing stunted growth, poor cob development, or even complete crop failure.
ga: Nu ni fa babaoo yɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ haa shihilɛi ni yeɔ awui kɛhaa ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ baa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ Cob lɛ dalɛ ni ehiii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite kwraa po.

english: How can I tell if the water pump machine in my community produces safe water for my cabbage field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu pɔmpii ni yɔɔ mi akutso lɛ mli lɛ miifee nu ni hi kɛha mi-cabbage ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: You can request an extension officer or technician to test a sample of the pumped water for salt levels and toxicity before applying it to sensitive leafy greens.
ga: Obaanyɛ obi extension nitsulɔ loo ŋaalɔ ko ni eka nu ni akɛ pɔmpi ewo mli lɛ eko mli ekwɛ kɛji ŋmei kɛ tsofa fɔŋ yɛ mli dani ekɛtsu nii yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ anɔ.

english: Why do my vegetables still wilt during the day even when I pump plenty of well water to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi lolo yɛ gbi lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ ajieɔ nu babaoo kɛjɛɔ nubu lɛ mli moŋ?

english: If the pumped well water is too salty, it pulls moisture out of the plant roots instead of feeding them, making the crops wilt despite being watered.
ga: Kɛji nu bu ni ajieɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ Ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboɔ yɛ be mli ni awo amɛ nu po sɛɛ.

english: Can water tested and cleared for human drinking also be safe for all my farm crops?
ga: Ani nu ni aka lɛ akwɛ ni ajie lɛ kpo koni adesai anu lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi okwaayeli nibii fɛɛ ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Generally yes, but some crops are much more sensitive to minor salts than humans are, so checking for irrigation suitability helps protect delicate plants.
ga: Yɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ, hɛɛ. Shi tsei komɛi nuɔ ŋoo fioo he waa fe adesai. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni abu tsei ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahe.

english: I hear people talking about Moringa all the time, but why should I grow it on my farm?
ga: Mi nuɔ ni mɛi wieɔ moringa he be fɛɛ be. Shi mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Moringa grows very fast in Ghanaian soil and its leaves are packed with vitamins and minerals. Eating it helps boost your family's health, and you can also dry and process the leaves to sell for extra income.
ga: Moringa kwɛ̃ɔ oya waa yɛ Ghana shikpɔŋ nɔ. Ni Moringa tso lɛ baai lɛ eyi kɛ vitamini kɛ mineral. Kɛ́ oye amɛ lɛ, ebaaha oweku lɛ aná hewalɛ kpakpa. Obaanyɛ okɛ baai lɛ hu agbi ni otsu he nii ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ koni onine ashɛ shika kroko nɔ.

english: Can I cut down the top of my Moringa tree when it gets too tall, or will that kill it?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafolɔ horseradish lɛ yiteŋ kɛji amɛkwɔ tsɔ? Aloo ebaagbo?

english: Cutting the main top branch (pruning) will not kill Moringa; it actually forces the tree to grow many new side branches lower down, giving you far more green leaves to harvest easily.
ga: Nine titri ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni aaafo (Pruning) lɛ egbeŋ ŋmei lɛ. Enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ niji heei kɛyaa shishigbɛ, ni ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa baai eŋɔli babaoo.

english: Why are my pawpaw trees flowering heavily, but no fruits are forming on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi papaya tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi waa lɛ? Shi ani nɔ ko bɛ ni jɛɔ mli baa?

english: Pawpaw trees can be male, female, or hermaphrodite. Male trees produce lots of flowers on long stems but cannot bear fruit. You need female or hermaphrodite trees in your farm to get fruits.
ga: Pawpaw tsei baanyɛ afee nuu, yoo, loo nɔ ni kɛ hii feɔ yakayaka nii. Tsei ni ji hii lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ tsei kakadaji anɔ shi amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii. Esa akɛ oná tsei ni ji yei loo tsei ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ yakayaka nii yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛwo yibii.

english: How many years can a pawpaw tree keep producing good fruit before I need to clear and replant?
ga: Afii enyiɛ papaya tso baanyɛ awo yibii kpakpai dani esa akɛ ajie lɛ ni adu ekoŋŋ?

english: Pawpaw trees produce their best and largest fruit yields for about 3 to 4 years. After that, they grow too tall to harvest safely and yield smaller fruits, so it is best to replant fresh seedlings.
ga: Pawpaw tsei lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛdara fe fɛɛ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 4, ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛfeɔ shɔŋŋ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkpa ni amɛwo yibii bibii shweshweeshwe. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi akɛ ooodu dumɔwui heei moŋ.

english: Why do my sweet orange trees drop their green fruits long before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso ni ŋɔɔ lɛ shĩɔ aduawai eŋɔli be kakadaŋŋ dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: Young oranges often drop early because of irregular rain or dry spells, lack of nutrients in the soil, or attacks from sap-sucking insects. Putting mulch around the trunk and feeding the soil helps the tree hold its fruit.
ga: Akutu bibii lɛ fɔɔ gbee oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee loo hulutsoo be lɛ hewɔ. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ tutuamɔi Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akɛyeɔ niyenii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my sweet orange tree turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tso ni ŋɔɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your tree lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or the soil around the roots is waterlogged and cannot breathe. Adding rich compost or manure around the root area usually fixes this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli, loo akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli eyi kɛ nu ni enyɛɛɛ emu. Kompost loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ Bei pii lɛ, shishifã lɛ he lɛ tsuɔ naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: When I open my ripe guavas, I often find small white worms inside. How can I stop this?
ga: Kɛ́ agbele guava ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ naa lɛ, bei pii lɛ, anaa ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ yɛ mli. Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa enɛ?

english: Those worms come from fruit flies that lay eggs under the skin while the guava is still small and green. Covering young fruits with small paper or cloth bags stops the flies from reaching them.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii lɛ jɛɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ hewolo lɛ shishi lɛ amli. Yɛ be mli ni guava lɛ ji bibioo ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ. Woji loo mama kotokui bibii ni akɛhaa aduawai bibii ahe Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii akashɛ he.

english: Is it better to plant guava seeds directly from a fruit or buy grafted seedlings from a nursery?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooodu guava dumɔwui kɛjɛ aduawai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ loo ooohe dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: Grafted seedlings are better because they grow into trees that yield sweet, high-quality fruit in about 2 years, whereas fruit seeds take longer to grow and may produce small or sour guavas.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ tsei ni woɔ aduawai ni ŋɔɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ aaafee afii enyɔ mli, yɛ be mli ni aduawai dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛdaraa, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo guava bibii loo ni mli edɔ.

english: How long after planting my oil palm seedlings should I expect them to give me fruit clusters?
ga: Kɛ́ odu oil palm dumɔwui lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, mɛɛ be esa akɛ okpa gbɛ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ baawo yibii babaoo?

english: Improved varieties like the Tenera oil palm start producing fruit clusters within 3 to 4 years after planting, provided they receive adequate rain and proper weeding.
ga: Henɔi ni atsake amɛhe tamɔ Tenera oil palm Yibii akui jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ kɛji amɛná nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to space fruit trees far apart instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkɛ tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ ato he ko moŋ fe ni wɔɔdu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When fruit trees are planted too close, their leaves block sunlight from each other and their roots fight for nutrients and water, resulting in smaller harvests and weak trees.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu aduawai tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Ni tsei shishifãi kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi fioo ni tsei lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the leaves inside the center roll of my young maize plants, and how do I stop them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye baai ni yɔɔ mibii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛ naa?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana. They hide in the central growing tip (the whorl) of maize plants. Applying recommended insecticides or clean wood ash directly into the whorls early in the morning or late evening will help kill them before they destroy the growing plant.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmãa (ring) ni miida lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tso mli sũ ni he tse lɛ wo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe amɛ dani amɛfite tsei ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves get dark spots and curl up when the weather becomes damp and rain falls continuously?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni nugbɔ miinɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: This is usually fungal blight or a leaf virus spread by tiny insects that thrive in high humidity. Spacing your plants further apart for good airflow, picking off infected lower leaves, and planting disease-resistant seed varieties help prevent this spread.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji baa mli hela loo hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa. ni daa yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ Shi gbɛ yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ mli. Jiemɔ shishigbɛ baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ni dumɔwui ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ nɛkɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant plantains on my field before transplanting my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension official lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛ kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and produce broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa plants need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I plant my maize in straight rows with specific spacing instead of scattering the seeds randomly across the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa mli ni gbɛ pɔtɛɛ ko yɔɔ mli? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaadu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ trukaa lɛ

english: When seeds are scattered, plants grow too close together and fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stalks and tiny cobs. Planting in measured rows gives every plant enough space and food to produce large cobs, while making weeding much easier.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ eshwa Tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa. Kɛ́ adu yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa jwɛi nɔyeli feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why do I need to cut off some of the side branches and extra leaves from my pepper and tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji ni yɔɔ afã kɛ baai krokomɛi ni fata he kɛjɛ mi-pepper kɛ tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Removing lower leaves and side shoots (pruning) redirects the plant's food and energy away from growing useless foliage and puts it directly into growing larger, healthier fruits.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishi kɛ sɛɛ ŋmeii lɛ ajiemɔ Pruning (pruning) tsɔɔ tso niyenii kɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni he ehiaaa ni miida lɛ ahe. Ni etsɔɔ tso yibii ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning light yellow even during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves during wet weather usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen or is holding too much water (waterlogging). Poor drainage causes roots to rot, stopping the plant from taking up food. Digging drainage channels and adding organic manure will help restore the leaves' green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ehiɛɔ nu babaoo (nu ni hoɔ). Nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Ehaa tsei nyɛɛɛ aye niyenii Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ mli ni aaakumɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does spreading dry grass or palm fronds around the roots of my vegetables help them grow better in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni agbɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmei tsei ashwã he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ mishishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: This practice is called mulching. Placing dried plant material over the soil protects it from direct sun, traps soil moisture, keeps the root area cool, stops weeds from growing, and decomposes into rich manure over time.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ahe nibii ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛfiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl tightly inward into small tubes when the sun gets very hot in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural mechanism plants use to protect themselves from severe heat. By rolling its leaves, the pepper plant reduces the surface area exposed to direct sunlight to prevent losing moisture too quickly. If they stay curled in the evening, it means the plant needs urgent watering.
ga: Baai ni abɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Pepper tsei haa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ akafite oya tsɔ Kɛji amɛfolɔ amɛhe gbɛkɛ mli Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni awo tso lɛ nu oya.

english: Why do my groundnut plants produce flowers above ground and then push green pegs down into the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ, ni no sɛɛ lɛ eduɔ ŋmeii eŋɔli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is the natural way groundnut plants reproduce. Once the flowers are pollinated above ground, the plant grows pegs that push deep into the dirt so that the actual groundnut pods can grow safely underground in cool soil.
ga: Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni ŋmei tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛfɔɔ bii. Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔii lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ baadu tso yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Enɛ ji koni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ nɔ.

english: Why do tiny insects destroy my harvested maize inside the barn even when the cobs looked healthy in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miifite mi ŋmãa ni mikpa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ cob lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli moŋ.

english: Weevils enter stored maize if the grain contains leftover moisture or if storage bags are not sealed. Drying your maize thoroughly under the sun until the kernels are completely hard and using airtight hermetic bags (like PICS bags) prevents insects from surviving and eating your harvest.
ga: Weevils baabote ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ko eshwɛ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. aloo kɛji akɛ atsĩko kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ naa Abele ni agbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ŋmeii lɛ amli baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kwraa. Ni okɛ vacuum bags (tamɔ PICS bags) atsu nii koni ŋmeii akajo foi ni amɛye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing from the bottom leaf tips upward usually means your crop lacks nitrogen. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer like Urea when the soil is moist will help the leaves regain their deep green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jɛ baa lɛ shishigbɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ onibii amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, loo nitrogen ni yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea fata he beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛsu ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ni amɛdara waa.

english: How does growing groundnuts or cowpeas on my land help my next season's maize farm?
ga: Te ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. When the crop is harvested, that trapped nitrogen stays in the dirt and acts as free fertilizer for the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Beni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nakai nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Which direction should the buds point when I push cassava stems into the ground?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ kɛji akɛ ashɛre ŋmei tso lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: The small buds on the cassava stem must always point upward toward the sky. If you plant the stem upside down, the plant spends too much energy trying to turn its shoots around, which results in weak growth and smaller tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be. Kɛji odu tso lɛ yitso lɛ shishi lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo baatsu nii ni ekɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni etsɔ eyiteŋ. Enɛ haa amɛdalɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Does putting tall wooden sticks next to my yam plants actually help grow bigger yam tubers?
ga: Ani tso kakadaŋŋ ni akɛma mi sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Yes, staking yam vines lifts their leaves up to catch as much sunlight as possible. Leaves use sunlight to make food for the plant, and that extra energy gets stored underground, producing larger and heavier yams.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, staking sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Baai kɛ hulu la feɔ niyenii kɛhaa tso lɛ. Ni akɛ nakai hewalɛ ni fa lɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ feɔ agbo ni etsiiɔ.

english: Why should I plant plantains next to my newly transplanted cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ ahe?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full, harsh sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad leaves that act like living umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and cool soil moisture it needs during its first few years.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha kookoo bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ.

english: What is causing small holes and saw-dust looking dirt in the center leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Kɛ ŋmeii ni tamɔ muji ni bɔle mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: This is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the growing tip of the corn plant. Applying approved pesticides or dropping fine neem leaf powder mixed with dry sand into the center whorl early in the morning can control them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ashishifãi amli lɛ. Abaanyɛ akudɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo neem baa fɛfɛo ni akɛ ŋã ni egbi efutu mli lɛ mli nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ni akɛwoɔ teŋgbɛ kooyigbɛ lɛ mli leebi maŋkpa.

english: Why do my pepper fruits get dark, soft rotten spots on the bottom while still on the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peppers lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni eyɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lolo lɛ?

english: Soft spots on the tips of pepper fruits are usually caused by uneven watering or a lack of calcium in the soil, known as blossom-end rot. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and adding wood ash or lime helps stop it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo calcium ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ hei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ pepper aduawai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baa. Ale lɛ hu akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ muji ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni okɛ tso sũ loo lime fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekpa.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off without producing any tomato fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or doesn't get enough water. Shading young plants slightly during severe hot dry spells and watering them regularly around the base helps the flowers stay on and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Ha dumɔwui lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ kɛ nu ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. Konui ni afeɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai ahiɔ shi.

english: Why is it better to leave cut weeds on top of my soil instead of burning them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaashi jwɛi ni afo lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ moŋ fe ni aaashã lɛ?

english: Burning destroys healthy soil organisms and burns away beneficial nutrients. Leaving dead weeds on top of the soil creates a blanket called mulch, which keeps the ground cool, retains rainwater, and rots down into rich natural manure.
ga: Shãa kpataa shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahiɛ ni eshãa niyenii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi jwɛi ni egboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch baa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi, ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo.

english: When is the best time for me to put chemical fertilizer on my crops so it doesn't wash away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni amɛkaho?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already damp after a light rain, but avoid applying it right before a heavy downpour. Covering the fertilizer lightly with a bit of soil keeps heavy rain from washing it off into ditches.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Shi tsi ohe kɛjɛ he ni ooowo dani nugbɔ anɛ waa lɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ sũ fioo ko ha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe fioo lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ lɛ kɛyaa nubu lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field without any shade trees nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni midu lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade from crops like plantain or shade trees to protect their soft leaves from direct intense sunlight, which scorches them and dries out the soil moisture needed for early root development.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli koni ebu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni he hiaa koni shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ mra lɛ mli agbi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava sticks too close together on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛɔ he tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting cassava too close forces the plants to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in tall thin stems and small tubers instead of large, healthy roots.
ga: Cassava ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ yitsei bibii. Yɛ shishifãi wuji ni mli wa najiaŋ

english: Why should I buy certified seeds from registered agro-dealers instead of planting grains saved from my last maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko ni aŋma egbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ dɛŋ? Mohu ɔ, i du duwuhi nɛ a yi wami kɛ je ye nyagbe ngma kpami ɔ mi ɔ.

english: Certified seeds are specially bred to resist local pests, tolerate weather stresses, and give high yields, whereas saved grains lose their vigor and produce much smaller yields in subsequent seasons.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmaa ni ato lɛ he waaa ni ewooo yibii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ mli bei lɛ amli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in the middle of the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is an essential nutrient plants need to produce chlorophyll and build strong green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee klorofil ni amɛfee baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I apply fertilizer near my crops when the soil is moist rather than when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ fe be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Plants can only take up nutrients that are dissolved in water. Applying fertilizer to dry soil prevents root absorption and can cause fertilizer burn or waste as the chemicals sit unused.
ga: Tsei baanyɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ ni akɛwo nu mli pɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa, ni ebaanyɛ eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashã loo eyafite ejaakɛ akɛ tsofa ko tsuuu nii.

english: Why are caterpillars eating the middle leaves of my young maize plants, and why doesn't spraying water flush them out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ amɛnɔ lɛ efɔɔɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms that hide deep inside the central leaf funnel of the maize plant where water cannot easily reach them, requiring targeted pest management solutions applied directly into the leaf funnel.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni akɛtee ŋmãa tsei ahe baai lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni nu nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛhe mlɛo lɛ. Enɛ biɔ ni akwɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ yɛ baa lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my pepper flowers keep falling off the plant without turning into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat or drought stress to protect themselves and save energy, preventing the flowers from successfully developing into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji amɛkɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ he haomɔ kpe. Koni obu ohe he ni okɛ hewalɛ ato Eyeɔ omanye ni ekɛtsiɔ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkatsɔ aduawai.

english: Why is it bad practice to plant tomatoes on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ ji nifeemɔ gbonyo lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously allows soil-borne diseases and pests that target tomatoes to build up in the soil, while also depleting the specific nutrients tomatoes rely on most.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aaaya nɔ akwɛ lɛ baaha helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ tomato nɔ lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, efiteɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tomato damɔ nɔ babaoo lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my young tomato plants stay small even after I have added fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mitato tsei bibii lɛ feɔ bibii eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii amli moŋ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal water, light, and fertilizer nutrients away from young crops, effectively starving the main crop before it can establish itself.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii amli. ni hɔmɔ aye tso ni hereɔ lɛ lɛ dani enyɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot in the ground if I delay harvesting them long after the leaves have dried off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpamɔ be sɛɛ beni baai lɛ egbi lɛ?

english: Leaving mature yams in dry, hot soil leaves them vulnerable to soil pests, termites, and high heat stress, which break down the tuber tissue and lead to rotting before harvest.
ga: Ni aaashi sweet potatoes ni eda lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, ŋmeii, kɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa aba amɛnɔ. Enɛ haa tuber tissue lɛ mli fãa ni egboɔ dani akpaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings burning and turning brown in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or bananas alongside young cocoa trees creates a protective umbrella that keeps the soil moist and shields the young leaves until the cocoa canopy matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains loo banana yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning pale green and yellow from the tips down to the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛyitseiaŋ kɛyashi amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the tip in a V-shape indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Applying a nitrogen-based fertilizer early in the crop's growth helps the plant build green foliage and produce large, full corn cobs.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ V yɛ amɛnaa, ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ shishijee mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ baai eŋɔli ni amɛwoɔ ŋmãa wuji.

english: What will happen if I plant my cassava cuttings too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ?

english: When cassava cuttings are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight for limited soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. This causes the plants to grow tall and leafy stems while producing very thin and poor cassava tubers underground.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, nu kɛ hulu la ni faaa lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi kakadaji kɛ baai kakadaji yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ ŋmei shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni ehiii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating ragged holes into the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni ekpɔtɔ yɛ mi-babi corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a destructive pest that hides in the growing center (whorl) of young maize plants. Catching them early and applying an approved treatment directly into the whorl prevents the caterpillar from killing the main growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni fiteɔ nii ni ekɛ ehe ewoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ adalɛ hei (rings) lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɔmɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ awo ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ koni ŋmeii lɛ akagbe he titri ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know if the soil is wet enough to plant my seeds after the first rain falls?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is safest to wait until the soil is moist down to a depth of about 10 to 15 centimeters across several rain days. Planting immediately after a single early rain shower can cause seeds to sprout and then wither quickly if a dry spell follows.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ akɛ ooomɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛyashɛ aaafee sɛntimita 10 kɛyashi 15 yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ gbii babaoo lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome sɛɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi oya kɛji akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ba.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off before any peppers start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience environmental stress such as extreme heat, dry soil, or excessive fertilizer. Maintaining steady moisture around the roots helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they can turn into pepper fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔi, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo amɛmli. Nibii ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ebɔleɔ he lɛ Shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso lɛ kpɛtɛɔ fɔfɔi ahe ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why is it good for my land to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same plot where I harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpaa ŋmãa yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them after cereal crops like maize restores natural soil fertility and reduces the need for costly chemical fertilizers in the next season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii nɛɛ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ. ni ekɛ tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ atsu nii yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do I need to put tall sticks in the ground for my yam vines to grow on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ŋmei wain tso lɛ aya nɔ eda lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need plenty of direct sunlight to make the energy required to swell big tubers under the ground. Staking lifts the vines off the damp soil, exposing the leaves to maximum sunlight while reducing fungal rot on the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛkwɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aba. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Ha baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ baai lɛ ahe okadii lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce a very small harvest even when rain falls regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital nutrients, water, and sunlight directly from your main crops before the crops can use them. Clearing weeds within the first 3 to 6 weeks after planting keeps the root zone free so your crops get all the food they need to grow well.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ tsei ni oyɔɔ mli lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 3 kɛyashi 6 mli yɛ dumɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha shishifã lɛ he afee faŋŋ. Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut off extra small shoots that grow around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ Ajieɔ midumɔwu titri lɛ shishi.

english: Extra small shoots (suckers) act like extra mouths to feed, draining water and nutrients away from the main fruiting tree. Pruning away excess suckers and keeping only one or two healthy ones ensures the parent tree has maximum energy to form heavy bunches of plantains.
ga: Tsobii bibii krokomɛi (tsoji) tsuɔ nii tamɔ daaŋ krɛdɛɛ ko ni akɛhaa niyenii. Tsɔɔmɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri ni woɔ yibii lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ amli ni ahiɛ tsei kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso nyɛ lɛ náa hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛwoɔ dumɔwui babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow instead of green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps bring back their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper flowers drop off without turning into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or lack of water. Giving them consistent water at the roots and mulching the soil to keep it cool helps the flowers stay on and turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo shishifãi lɛ anɔ daa ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo mli koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize in the exact same spot every season drains the soil of specific nutrients and allows pests to build up in the dirt. Rotating maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores natural plant food back into the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ bua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow small and crooked instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose soil to push downward freely as they expand. When planted in hard, unplowed soil, the root gets squished and cannot grow properly, resulting in small or twisted yams.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛya shi be mli ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa lɛ. Kɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni atsuko nɔ lɛ nɔ Shishifãi lɛ baafo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni ekpɔtɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the soil when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long because the roots drown without air. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tight during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl up in the afternoon heat to reduce water loss and protect themselves from harsh sunlight. While this is a normal self-defense reaction, regular morning watering helps reduce severe leaf curling.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni ebu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Eyɛ mli akɛ enɛ ji nɔ ko ni afɔɔ feemɔ ni akɛbuɔ mɔ he moŋ, shi nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa leebi lɛ baaye abua ni eha baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi waa lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do caterpillars eat through my young maize leaves so fast during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yeɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm reproduce faster in warm, dry weather, and dry spells make young maize weaker and easier to attack. Inspecting the center leaves of young maize early allows you to catch and control them before they destroy the field.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm fɔɔ oya yɛ hei ni edɔɔ, ni egbi. Ni hulutsoo be lɛ haa ŋmãa bibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛtutuaa amɛ oya. Abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ omɔɔ amɛ ni okudɔɔ amɛ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my plantain trees turning yellow and dying off one by one?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi komekomei lɛ?

english: Lower plantain leaves naturally age and dry up, but rapid yellowing can mean the plant lacks water or has a fungal infection in the soil. Cutting off dead leaves and applying compost around the plant base keeps the plant clean and nourished.
ga: Plantain ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baai lɛ daa ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi ŋmɔŋ ni baa oya lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ nu efo tso lɛ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko yɛ tso lɛ mli. Kpɔ̃ɔ baai ni egboi lɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii abɔle amɛhe. Tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ he atse ni ená niyenii kpakpa.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my young cocoa trees so often?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ ehe bahiaa ni mafolɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ amli jwɛi lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young cocoa trees and steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients your cocoa needs to survive. Keeping the base of young cocoa trees clean gives them full access to essential food and water.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe kookoo tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he hiaa okookoo lɛ koni ehi shi. Kɛ́ cacao tso lɛ shishi he tse lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enáa niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and carry heavy bunches of fruit, making them top-heavy. Supporting fruiting plantain trees with sturdy bamboo or wooden poles prevents strong winds from knocking them over.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛwoɔ aduawai babaoo, ni no haa amɛfeɔ tsiimɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo tsei ni wa fi dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa koni ekatswa amɛ shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani akpa kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for green growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: If I plant maize on the same piece of land every year, why do my harvests keep getting smaller?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi Mɛni hewɔ mi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ miiba shi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas naturally puts nitrogen back into the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Enɛ baaha nitrogen lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni efo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe sɛɛkuu lɛ mli

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer so the rain does not wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni nugbɔ akashwie nɔ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist, but not during heavy downpours. Burying the fertilizer a few inches into the soil near the base of the plant right after light rain ensures the roots absorb it before heavy rains carry it off.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo lɛ. Shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Ni aaafu ŋmɔshi nibii fioo komɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko pɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ lɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: What causes my cassava tubers to rot in the ground when heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Too much standing water trapped in heavy soil cuts off air to the roots, encouraging fungal rot. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away and keeps the tubers dry and healthy.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo ni ekpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii he lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei lɛ baanyɛ afite. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni ehaa yitso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miijie fɔfɔi ni ewooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: High heat, irregular watering, or tiny insect pests can stress the plant, causing it to shed flowers to survive. Regular watering during dry spells and checking under the leaves for pests can prevent flower drop.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be Loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii po baanyɛ aha tso lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ baanyɛ agbee shi. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ, kɛ ŋmeii ni baa yɛ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ fɔfɔi lɛ ni fiteɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open, sunny clearing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight and get scorched easily. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain beside them acts like a living canopy, protecting the young cocoa until they grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ni amɛshãa oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi cacao lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I wait for the major rains to fully settle before planting my seeds instead of planting after the first early shower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akpa dani madu dumɔwui yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu yɛ mi klɛŋklɛŋ leebi nu ni mikɛwoɔ mihe lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rainfall often heats up dry soil without soaking deep down. Planting too early can cause seeds to sprout and then wither if a dry spell follows, whereas waiting for steady rains guarantees enough soil moisture for seeds to establish.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ekɛwooo mli. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ba. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are overcrowded, their roots compete over water and soil nutrients, and their leaves block sunlight from each other. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough food and light to yield big produce.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni amɛbaai lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: How do weeds growing around my crops actually slow down my harvest growth?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Te miŋmɔshi nii lɛ miiha midalɛ miiba shi eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to the soil's nourishment so they can produce a full yield.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ. bɔni afee ni afee nibii ni fa babaoo

english: Why do my stored yam tubers start sprouting shoots even when I keep them inside a cool barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛtoɔ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Yams naturally break their dormancy after a few months as part of their natural growth cycle. Storing them in a well-ventilated, dark area and carefully breaking off early sprouts helps keep the tubers fresh for longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ wɔɔhe yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ akɛ amɛ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ fã. Ha ehi he ko ni duŋ ewo ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli ni okɛ hiɛdɔɔ afo tsei bibii lɛ amli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii heei lɛ ahi shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important for me to plant food crops like cassava alongside my long-term tree crops like cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ kookoo masɛi?

english: Planting food crops gives you immediate food and income to eat and sell while your long-term tree crops grow and prepare to produce steady future wealth.
ga: Niyenii ni okwɛɔ lɛ haa onáa niyenii kɛ shika ni oyeɔ ni ohɔ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Be mli ni otsei ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ daraa ni amɛsaa amɛhe koni amɛfee wɔsɛɛ ninamɔ ni mli wa.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds instead of just planting seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specifically bred to resist local pests and diseases, tolerate dry spells, and produce much higher yields compared to saved seeds that lose their strength over time.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli kooloi bibii kɛ helai. Enyɛɔ shiɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my young cashew trees take several years before they start producing fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ebɔi yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: Tree crops spend their early years building deep roots and strong branches to support heavy harvests later, requiring time and care before they can produce good fruit.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ jwɛi mli lɛ yeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ ni amɛdaraa. Koni afee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ niji ni mli wa ni baaye abua ŋmaakpamɔ agbo ko sɛɛ mli. Enɛ heɔ be kɛ hiɛdɔɔ dani ewoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cut off some of the healthy-looking branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mafo kookoo niji ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ekomɛi lɛ?

english: Pruning excess branches allows sunlight and fresh air to reach inside the tree canopy, which prevents fungal diseases like black pod rot and encourages the tree to flower more.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod rot naa ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo fɔfɔi babaoo.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow even after I put fertilizer on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves can mean the soil lacks specific nutrients like nitrogen, that the fertilizer was applied at the wrong time, or that heavy rain washed the fertilizer away from the roots.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, tamɔ nitrogen, ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be ni esaaa mli. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why should I not plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ? Dumɔ be

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and builds up crop-specific pests; rotating with legumes like beans or groundnuts naturally restores soil fertility.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni efee tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui Ekɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni akɛtsakeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crops very close to each other so I can fit more on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná gbɛ babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting crops too close together forces them to fight over sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants and a smaller overall harvest.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni ŋmaa lɛ hu baa shi fioo.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains next to my newly transplanted cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei ni adu ehee lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily in direct sunlight, so fast-growing plantains act as living umbrellas, providing the vital shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, plantains ni daa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ haa.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce much less food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo kwraa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal vital water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crops, leaving your crops hungry and weak.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu ni he hiaa waa, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Shimɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ hɔmɔ kɛ gbɔjɔmɔ.

english: Why do my yam leaves curl up and drop during the heat of the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a plant's natural defense mechanism to conserve water and prevent drying out when moisture in the soil is low.
ga: Baai ni akpɛ́ɔ lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni ekɛbuɔ nu he ni ekɛtsiɔ gbimɔ naa kɛji sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ faaa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient they need to grow strong. Adding manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea helps bring back the healthy green color so the plant can make food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii mli hewalɛ ko ni he hiaa ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba koni tsei lɛ anyɛ awo niyenii.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with big leaves, but the root tubers underneath stay tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji lɛ? Shi shishifã ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ji bibioo lolo?

english: This happens when the soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium. Excess nitrogen makes the plant put all its energy into growing tall stem and leaves above ground instead of feeding and swelling the roots underground.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai ni miida ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, e yeɔ ní, nɛ e haa nɛ sisifã ɔmɛ puɛɔ ngɛ zugba a sisi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in a clear open field with full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very delicate and burn easily under strong sunlight and heat. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees planted next to them to shield them from direct heat and keep the soil moist while they are young.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa, ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni eyɔɔ gbekɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei awo mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ koni makwɔ nɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally search for height to spread their leaves toward sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground away from diseases and pests, allowing the leaves to trap sunlight efficiently to build larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ taoɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛkɛ hulu lɛ akpee. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni ekɛ helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ teɔ shi. Enɛ haa baai lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛfee bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences heat stress or uneven watering. When weather becomes too hot or water is low, the plant drops its flowers to conserve water and survive rather than spending energy growing fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii kɛdu aduawai

english: Why should I cut off extra baby shoots growing around my main plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: When too many suckers grow around one mother plantain, they fight over the same nutrients and water in the soil. Pruning away weaker shoots leaves only one or two strong ones, ensuring the main plant produces a heavy, healthy bunch.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ dumɔwu kome Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaashi tsei kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii ni tsii ni mli wa.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas or beans makes my land better for maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans can take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it inside their root nodes. When the plant leaves and roots decay in the soil, that stored plant food remains behind to feed the maize crop that follows.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans baanyɛ aŋɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛmɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni tsei ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Ashiɔ tsei aniyenii ni ato lɛ koni akɛye ŋmãa tsei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are holes appearing in the center leaves of my maize, and why is the top part dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-ŋma lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ ŋwɛi fã lɛ gbo lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by caterpillars called fall armyworms or stem borers feeding inside the leaf whorl. Catching them early and applying proper controls stops them from destroying the plant's growing point.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ cutworms loo stem borers ni yeɔ baai ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ omɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkafite hei ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings fall over and rot at the soil line shortly after coming up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ miiho ni amɛmiifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni amɛje kpo etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: This condition is called 'damping-off,' caused by soil fungi that thrive when nursery beds are kept too wet and lack drainage. Allowing the topsoil to dry slightly between waterings prevents the seedling stems from rotting.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ ‘Damping’, ni tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni kwɛ̃ɔ beni ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔhei lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni nu bɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli lɛ agbi fioo yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ teŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains get soft, moldy, and smelly inside storage bags after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ yɛ nitoohe kotoku lɛ mli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Grains rot when they are put into bags while still carrying moisture inside them. Properly drying maize in the sun until the grains are hard prevents mold and insects from destroying the harvest in storage.
ga: Ŋmãa baafite kɛ akɛwo kotoku mli ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lolo. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii akafite nibii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: I keep hearing officers talk about 'improved seeds' for beans, but what does that actually mean for my farm?
ga: Mi nu ni onukpai lɛ miiwie akɛ Be fɛɛ be lɛ, ‘dumɔwui ni atsake’ yɛ kɛha ŋmeii, shi mɛni ji nɔ ni no tsɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Improved seeds are bred or scientifically developed to carry special traits—like growing faster, resisting harmful insects, or surviving dry spells—so you can harvest more food compared to traditional seeds.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ loo atsɔɔ jeŋ nilee nɔ afee amɛ koni amɛná sui krɛdɛɛi, tamɔ amɛdalɛ oya. Te shi owo kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui Aloo ohi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okpa niyenii babaoo kɛ akɛto blema dumɔwui ahe.

english: Can scientists really take good traits from tiny organisms like bacteria and put them into crop seeds?
ga: Ani jeŋ nilelɔi baanyɛ ajie sui kpakpai kɛjɛ nibii bibii tamɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni amɛkɛwo tsei amli dumɔwui amli diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, plant scientists can identify a beneficial trait in a natural organism—such as protection against a specific caterpillar—and transfer that trait into seeds so the growing crop can defend itself naturally.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei ahe nilelɔi enyɛ amɛna sui ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii amli, tamɔ hebuu kɛjɛ ŋmeii komɛi ahe. ni amɛkɛ sui nɛɛ awo dumɔwui amli koni ŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ anyɛ abu amɛhe yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do some new cowpea varieties suffer less from insect attacks than the seeds I saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii enaaa cowpea henɔi heei lɛ ekomɛi anɔ hewalɛ tsɔ fe dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: New seed varieties often contain built-in protective traits that stop specific pests from eating the plant, which keeps the crop healthy without relying heavily on expensive chemical sprays.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui heei yɛ nibii ni buɔ amɛhe ni tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi anaa koni amɛkaye tsei lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ amɛhe afɔ̃ tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: What causes my bean leaves to develop strange spots and wither even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-bean baai lɛ náa he ko ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po?

english: Diseases caused by microscopic organisms like fungi or bacteria can attack plant leaves and roots, blocking the crop from taking up food and water properly.
ga: Helai ni nibii bibii tamɔ ŋmei loo muawai kɛbaa lɛ baanyɛ atutua tsei baai kɛ shishifãi. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii kɛ nu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Are all tiny bacteria in my soil bad for my crops, or do some of them actually help?
ga: Ani helai fioo komɛi ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ehiii kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii? Aloo ani henɔi komɛi baanyɛ aye abua diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Not all bacteria are harmful. Many soil bacteria are friendly organisms that capture nitrogen from the air and feed it directly to crops like beans, helping them grow naturally strong.
ga: Jeee helatsɛmɛi fɛɛ yeɔ mɔ awui. Shikpɔŋ nɔ helai babaoo ji naanyobɔɔ nibii ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmeii tɛ̃ɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my bean crops grow well even when I do not apply a lot of chemical fertilizer compared to my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ nɛkɛ? Ni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ babaoo tsuuu nii kɛ akɛtoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ?

english: Beans are legumes that work together with good bacteria in the soil to produce their own plant food, whereas maize relies entirely on nutrients already in the ground or added through fertilizer.
