ga: Beans ji ŋmeii ni kɛ bacteria kpakpa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfee amɛ niyenii. Shi ŋmãa lɛ, ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo ni akɛfataa he kɛtsɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ nɔ kwraa.

english: Is it safe for my family and community to eat food crops that were developed using laboratory science?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ miweku lɛ kɛ mi akutso lɛ baaye niyenii tsei ni akɛ laboratori jeŋ nilee fee lɛ?

english: Yes, before any new engineered or improved crop seed is released to farmers, it undergoes strict testing by agricultural authorities to ensure it is completely safe for human consumption and the environment.
ga: Hɛɛ, dani abaajie dumɔwui ni afee lɛ tsɔne loo ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ aha okwaafoi. Esa akɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ aka dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ waa koni amɛkwɛ akɛ amɛhe yɛ shweshweeshwe kwraa kɛha adesai aniyeli kɛ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: If I plant seeds that have special insect-resistant traits, will those seeds harm my soil for next year?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui ni yɔɔ sui krɛdɛɛi ni haa kooloi nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ, Ani nakai dumɔwui lɛ baaye mishikpɔŋ lɛ awui yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli?

english: No, the protective traits inside the plant act only against specific destructive pests that eat the crop; they do not contaminate or harm the fertility of your farm soil.
ga: Dabi, nibii ni buɔ mɔ he ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii eshiɔ kooloi pɔtɛɛ ni fiteɔ nii ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ pɛ. Amɛfiteee shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ loo amɛyeee lɛ awui.

english: Why do my neighbor's crops mature and produce pods much faster than mine when we planted on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ tso lɛ kwɛ̃ ni ewo ŋmeii mra kwraa fe mi nɔ lɛ beni wɔdu lɛ yɛ gbi kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Different crop varieties inherit different growth traits. Early-maturing varieties are specifically selected to complete their life cycle quickly, which is very helpful when the rainy season is short.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi yɛ bɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛhaa lɛ srɔtoi. Ahalaa tsei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛgbe amɛshihilɛ be lɛ naa oya. Enɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli.

english: If I harvest beans from an improved seed variety, can I save those same seeds to plant next season?
ga: Kɛji mikpa ŋmeii kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli Ani manyɛ makɛ nakai dumɔwui lɛ nɔŋŋ ato koni madu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: You can plant saved seeds, but they often lose their special protective traits and strength in the second generation, so buying fresh certified seeds gives you the highest yield every time.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu dumɔwui ni ato. Shi amɛfɔɔ amɛhebuu nibii krɛdɛɛi kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ baaha oná yibii babaoo be fɛɛ be.

english: How do I know when the rains have truly started so I can plant my maize without losing seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nugbɔ miibɔi nɛmɔ diɛŋtsɛ? No hewɔ lɛ ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmãa ni afiteee dumɔwui?

english: Do not plant after the very first light shower; wait until you receive two or three heavy rains that soak the ground deeply, ensuring the soil stays moist so seeds can germinate and survive.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ahum lɛ sɛɛ. Mɛɛ kɛyashi obaaná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi. Kwɛmɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why does my crop farm in the southern forest zone require different land care than farms in drier northern areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ kooyigbɛ ni kooi yɔɔ mli lɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto fe miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ kooyigbɛ kpokpaa ni nɔ egbi lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Southern forest soils carry more organic matter but erode easily under heavy rain, while drier northern soils lose moisture quickly and need organic cover like mulch to stay damp.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ kooi ni yɔɔ anaigbɛ lɛ amli lɛ yɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, efiteɔ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kooyigbɛ shikpɔji ni egbi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya ni ehe hiaa ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ aha nɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and drop off during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves on purpose during dry periods to save water and protect the valuable tubers growing underground until rain returns.
ga: Cassava tsei tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu ŋmeii ni jara wa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep falling off without forming any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of soil nutrients needed to support fruit growth.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa he, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni he hiaa koni aduawai lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak and stay small even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni ebɛ bibioo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that steal water, fertilizer, and soil nutrients faster than your main crops can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni tsei ni yɔɔ ohe lɛ baanyɛ aná.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees next to my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Mi kookoo tso bibioo lɛ

english: Young cocoa trees easily burn under full sunshine; plantain leaves act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and cooler air during the cocoa's early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain baai tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ. Ha hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ yɛ kookoo lɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: If I put many maize seeds into the same hole, will I harvest more corn?
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii babaoo wo bu kome mli. Ani abaakpa ŋmãa babaoo?

english: No, planting too many seeds in one spot forces the plants to fight over sunlight and food, resulting in thin stalks with tiny or empty cobs.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui babaoo ni adu yɛ he kome lɛ baaha tso lɛ abɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii he mɔdɛŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa. loo dumɔwui ni nɔ ko bɛ mli

english: Why do I need to make raised mounds of earth before I plant my yam setts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow straight down into the soil; raised mounds keep the soil loose and soft so the yam tubers can expand easily into large sizes.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Gɔŋ ni awo nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ bɔdɔɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛyashɛ ŋmeii wuji amli oya.

english: Will removing small extra branches from my tomato plants help me get bigger tomatoes?
ga: niji bibii amlijaa Ani ejie kɛjɛ tomato tso lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua mi ni maná tomatoi wuji?

english: Yes, trimming off non-essential side branches directs the plant's energy straight into feeding the growing fruits instead of unnecessary leaf stems.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛ niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ kudɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛyaa yibii ni miida lɛ niyenii nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ baai ni he ehiaaa baatsu nii lɛ

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil and rot if I put it straight into bags after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ ni egboɔ kɛji mikɛwo kotoku lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grain contains moisture that trapped heat attracts mold and insects; maize must be sun-dried properly before bagging to keep it safe.
ga: Nibii ni akpa etsɛko lɛ yɛ nu ni mli edɔ ni gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ koolooi. Esa akɛ agbi ŋmãa yɛ hulu mli dani akɛwo kotokui amli koni ehi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: When lower leaves turn yellow from the leaf tips inward, it usually means the plant lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main plant food needed to make leaves dark green and healthy.
ga: Kɛji akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ baa lɛ mligbɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ Bei pii lɛ enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni eha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni eyɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani wɔdu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts put free plant food (nitrogen) back into the soil through their roots. Planting maize after them helps the maize grow stronger without needing as much expensive commercial fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts kɛ tsei aniyenii (nitrogen) ni aheee nɔ ko lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Abele ni aduɔ yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni abele lɛ daa waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa awo mli.

english: Why do my maize plants produce very small ears when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ woɔ toi bibii waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, soil water, and plant food. Giving each plant enough space allows it to get everything it needs to grow full, large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu, kɛ tsei aniyenii ahe akaŋshii mli. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ náa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛkwɛ̃ ŋmei agbo.

english: Why do I need to put tall sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei kakadaji ama shi koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the yam tuber under the ground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground into the sun, which increases yield and protects the plant from diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ, ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ahe.

english: Why should I cut off extra small branches and leaves from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei aniji bibii kɛ baai lɛ? kɛjɛ kookoo tso lɛ mli

english: Pruning cocoa lets sunlight and fresh air pass through the tree canopy. This dries up excess moisture that causes black pod disease and ensures the tree sends its strength into growing cocoa pods.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ agbi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtsuɔ hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ kookoo ŋmeii

english: How do I know which cassava stems are best to cut and plant for a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmei tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ afolɔ ni adu koni maná ŋmaa kpakpa?

english: Select mature, healthy stems from the middle section of a strong plant that had no disease symptoms. Avoid the soft green tips at the top and the overly hard, dry wood at the very bottom.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni eda ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni hela he okadi ko bɛ he lɛ teŋgbɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ tso ni wa tsɔ ni egbi yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he.

english: Tomato flowers fall off mainly due to extreme heat or lack of water in the soil. When the plant gets stressed by drought or hot weather, it drops flowers to save its own energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Kɛji hɔmɔ loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ hao tsei lɛ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehewalɛ.

english: What causes holes in the leaves of my maize with small dirt-like powder inside the center leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa mi ŋmãa baa lɛ mli nibii bibii ni tamɔ muji yɔɔ? Ani bu ko yɛ baa lɛ teŋ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides in the center fold of the plant (the whorl), eats the soft leaves, and leaves behind its waste product, which looks like saw dust.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii (whorls) lɛ amli, amɛyeɔ baai bibii, ni amɛshiɔ jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why does removing weeds early in the season help my crops grow much faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya lɛ?

english: Young crops are delicate and weak. Weeds grow very fast and steal water, fertilizer, and light from young seedlings, so clearing weeds early gives crops a head start.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛhe waaa. Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii amli. No hewɔ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my pepper plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass (mulching) keeps the soil shaded and cool, prevents water from evaporating quickly under the hot sun, and stops weeds from sprouting around your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekatsɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ naa.

english: How do I know when my young cashew trees are old enough to produce nuts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cashew tso lɛ eda bɔ ni sa ni ebaawo ŋmeii?

english: Cashew trees usually begin flowering and producing their first small harvest about two to three years after planting, provided they receive adequate water and sunlight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cashew tsei jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi ni amɛwoɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii aaafee afii enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ beni adu amɛ. Kɛji onine shɛ nu kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cashew trees turning yellow and falling off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the tree is stressed from too little water during dry periods, or the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to keep their leaves healthy and green.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ nu fioo ni ekɛtsuɔ nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ hewɔ. loo shikpɔŋ ni nitrogen bɛ nɔ Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni tsei lɛ aha amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee eŋɔli.

english: How does putting shade over my young tree seedlings help them survive?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shading ni mikɛwoɔ midumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi?

english: Shade protects tender young seedlings from harsh afternoon heat, preventing the leaves from burning and keeping moisture in the soil around their roots.
ga: Shade lɛ buɔ dumɔwui bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shwane latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he. Etsiɔ baa lɛ shãa naa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ebatsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they get too hot, when water is inconsistent, or when there are not enough insects around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji edɔ tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ mli ejɔɔɔ loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔii lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ bɛ

english: How can I tell if my maize crop is getting enough water during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abele lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Maize leaves curl up during hot afternoons to save water, but if they remain rolled up early in the morning, the crop is suffering from severe drought stress and needs water.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛbu nu he. Shi kɛji akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lolo yɛ leebi maŋkpa lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ naa hɔmɔ he haomɔ ni naa wa ni ehe hiaa nu.

english: What causes the edges of my crop leaves to look burnt and brown?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ anaa lɛ miifee tamɔ nɔ ni eshã ni efee ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Burnt leaf edges often happen when the plant lacks potassium, when the soil is too dry, or when fertilizer was applied too close to the plant's stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shãa lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ potassium. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo be mli ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli ni ebɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi tsɔ

english: Why should I clear weeds away from around the base of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and nutrients in the soil, which stunts crop growth and reduces your yield.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ akpa shweremɔ ni ebaaha onibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ aba shi.

english: Why is it better for me to plant my seeds right at the start of the main rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Planting early allows seeds to germinate in steady moisture, giving young roots time to grow deep before unpredictable dry spells happen later.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ gbekɛbiiashi Eyeɔ ebuaa ni dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ naa be ni amɛdaraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ dani hɔmɔ shihilɛi ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ baa sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to dry my raw cashew nuts in the sun before storing them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-cashew ŋmeii ni afeee lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yɛ hulu mli dani mikɛto?

english: Sun-drying removes moisture from inside the nut shell, which stops harmful mold from growing and keeps the nut kernel inside good to sell for months.
ga: Kɛ́ egbi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akakwɛ̃. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ahɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ nyɔji babaoo.

english: How can I stop my harvested cassava roots from going bad so fast?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite oya?

english: Cassava roots spoil within two to three days after harvest; processing them quickly into cassava flour or gari removes moisture and preserves them for months.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ afee lɛ cassava ashikiŋsha loo gari oya lɛ, ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa ehiɔ shi nyɔji babaoo.

english: Why do my crops get smaller and produce less harvest if I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Crops need their own personal space to drink water, breathe, and gather nutrients from the soil. When planted too close, their roots and leaves fight each other for survival, causing the plants to stay small and weak.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ he ni amɛnu nu, amɛmu, ni amɛbua niyenii mli hewalɛ naa kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji adu lɛ ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ baawu koni amɛhi shi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why does rot attack my pepper fruits more during the rainy season when the plants are bushy and crowded?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper rot tutuaa mi pepper aduawai lɛ babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli beni tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛmli eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, rainwater and damp air get trapped between the leaves with no breeze to dry them out. This continuous wetness creates the perfect home for rot and fungal diseases to grow and ruin your harvest.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Nugbɔ nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ hiɔ baai lɛ anɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ ni haa amɛgbiɔ. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa nɛɛ feɔ he ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni efite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: If one of my cassava plants gets sick with yellow leaves, why does the sickness quickly spread to the nearby plants?
ga: Kɛji mi-cassava tsei lɛ eko hela mɔ lɛ ni baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Mɛni hewɔ hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Plant diseases spread through wind, insects, or direct contact between leaves. When healthy plants stand right next to a sick plant, insects easily jump across and carry the sickness to destroy the rest of your farm.
ga: Tse helai gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, kooloi bibii, loo baai ni kɛ amɛhe kpaa gbee tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ damɔ tso ni hela mɔ lɛ masɛi lɛ, ewaaa akɛ ŋmeii baatsɔ nɔ ni amɛkɛ hela baafite oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off and destroy sick leaves instead of leaving them on the crop to recover?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ baai ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni makpãtã amɛhiɛ moŋ fe ni mashi amɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ koni amɛhiɛ ahi amɛhe nɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Unlike human skin, diseased plant leaves rarely heal. Leaving infected leaves on your crop allows the disease to keep breeding spores, which will spread and eventually kill the whole plant.
ga: Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ gbɔmɔ hewolo lɛ, anyɛɛɛ atsa tso baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa hela lɛ shwereɔ. ni baagbɛ eshwa ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaakpata tso muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I cut down all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ shã ni egbo beni mifo tsei ni eda ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are like human babies—they burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Taller trees provide essential shade and keep the soil moist so the tender young cocoa plants can survive their early years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ baaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up into little rolls during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle ehe bibii lɛ? Yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Leaf curling is a plant's natural defense against heat. By rolling its leaves inward, the plant hides from the hot sun to conserve water and prevent itself from drying out.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Tsei kɛ amɛhe teeɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he kɛtsɔ amɛbaai ni amɛfoɔ mli kɛyaa mli koni nu ahi mli ni amɛtsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my young maize crops turn pale yellow and stop growing fast?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi-baby corn lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni ekpa dalɛ oya lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive thieves that steal fertilizer and groundwater away from your crop. When weeds surround your maize, the maize starves and loses the vital green nutrients it needs to grow tall.
ga: Jwɛi ji julɔi ni yɔɔ basabasa ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Beni jwɛi ebɔle o-ŋmã lɛ he lɛ Hɔmɔ baaye lɛ ni ŋmã lɛ baaye niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why do insects destroy my farm faster when I plant only maize compared to when I mix maize with cowpea?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ miŋmɔ lɛ oya kɛ́ midu ŋmãa pɛ fe kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmãa futu tsina ŋmãa mli lɛ?

english: A single continuous crop makes it easy for pests to move effortlessly from one plant to the next. Mixing different crops creates natural barriers and smells that confuse insects and stop them from invading the entire field.
ga: Nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ kome ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli oya. Nibii srɔtoi ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii kɛ ŋmeii ni futuɔ kooloi bibii lɛ baa ni ehaaa amɛtutua ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers stay short and crooked when the soil is packed very hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ feɔ kukuji ni ebɔle amɛhe be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa waa lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow by pushing down into the earth. If the soil is too hard and unplowed, the roots exhaust their energy fighting the tough soil instead of expanding into long, smooth tubers.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa kɛtsɔ amɛshwiemɔ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ ni atsuuu he nii lɛ Shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ sũ lɛ wuɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛfee bulbs kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does my land produce much smaller yields when I grow cassava in the exact same spot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo tsɔ beni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Every crop pulls specific nutrients out of the earth. Planted continuously in the same place, cassava drains the soil of those exact food reserves, leaving the land tired and unable to support new growth without a rest or crop rotation.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fɛɛ gbalaa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu Cassava yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ ajɛ niyenii jɛɛhe ko ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɔ̃ɔ ni enyɛɛɛ eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni edaaa lɛ ni ekɛ hejɔɔmɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsakeee.

english: Why do produce buyers refuse to buy my grains right after I harvest them from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpooɔ akɛ amɛbaahɔɔ miŋmaa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested crops contain too much water inside them. Buyers require crops to be dried to a low moisture content so the grains do not spoil, mold, or decay before reaching the market.
ga: Nibii ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ nu babaoo tsɔ yɛ mli. Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ miisumɔ ni amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbi kɛyashɛ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli. Enɛ ji koni dumɔwui lɛ akafite, akafee ŋmɔtɔ, loo akafite dani amɛyashɛ jara nɔ.

english: What happens to my crop if I leave it in the field too long after it is ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni amɛshɛ he kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Leaving mature crops on the field exposes them to excessive rain, pests, and soil wetness, which causes seeds to rot, crack, or get eaten before you can collect them.
ga: Nibii ni eda ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa amɛnaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine, kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ, amɛkuɔ, loo ayeɔ amɛ dani obaanyɛ okpa amɛ.

english: Why should I separate bad or broken grains from the good ones before drying my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbala dumɔwui ni ehiii loo ni ekumɔ lɛ kɛjɛ dumɔwui kpakpai amli dani magbi miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Damaged grains hold extra moisture and rot much faster. Removing them stops mold and pests from spreading to the healthy grains while they dry.
ga: Dumɔwui ni efite lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo mli ni amɛgboiɔ oya. Kɛ́ ojie lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli be mli ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my harvested grains are dry enough for buyers or long-term storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa kɛha mɛi ni heɔ loo akɛtoɔ be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Dry grains feel hard and crisp. A common simple check for maize is to bite a kernel; if it cracks sharply without feeling soft or chewy, it has lost enough water content for safe storage.
ga: Nibii ni egbi lɛ nuɔ he akɛ ewa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ yɛ ŋmãa mli kwɛmɔ ji kɛtsɔ ŋmãa lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji egbɛ eshwa oya ni enuuu he akɛ eyɛ bɔdɔɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa elaaje koni akɛto he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does my harvested crop shrink and become lighter after I dry it in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efoɔ kɛji egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Crops lose weight because the water trapped inside them evaporates into the air during drying. Even though the crop gets lighter, the actual solid food content remains healthy and preserved.
ga: Tsei lɛ ahe waaa beni nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ be mli ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho yɛ amɛhe moŋ Shi niyenii ni wa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ falɛ yɛ hewalɛ lolo ni ato he gbɛjianɔ.

english: Why does sun-drying my harvested crops take much longer in wet or cloudy weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani mikɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛgbiɔ mikpamɔ lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo loo atatu yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Drying relies on warm, dry air to draw water out of the crop. When the air is already filled with humidity or rainwater, the water inside the crop evaporates very slowly.
ga: Egbimɔ biɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi koni ejie nu kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli eyi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo nugbɔ Nu Nu ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi blɛoo waa.

english: What causes my harvested grains to smell bad and grow mold inside my storehouse?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmaa ni mikpaa lɛ shãa ni ŋmɔtɔ shwereɔ yɛ mi nitoohe lɛ?

english: Mold grows when wet or partially dried crops are kept in enclosed spaces. Trapped dampness creates heat and moisture, which causes fungi and rot to spread quickly.
ga: Fung lɛ daa kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efɔ loo fã ko ni egbi lɛ to hei ni afo he. Fɛ̃i ni amɔmɔ lɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i baa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Why do tiny insects appear in my stored grains even when I cleaned them before storing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Eje kpo yɛ dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ amli. Eyɛ mli akɛ mitsu he dani mikɛto moŋ.

english: Insects often lay invisible tiny eggs inside crops while they are still growing in the field. If crops are not dried properly, the warmth and dampness in storage cause those eggs to hatch.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi fɔɔ wɔji bibii. ni anyɛɛɛ ana yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni amɛmiida lolo yɛ ŋmɔji amli Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbiko jogbaŋŋ He ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ mli latsaa kɛ latsaa lɛ baaha nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afɔ.

english: Can I dry my damaged or lower-quality crops and use them as feed for farm animals?
ga: Ani manyɛ magbi ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite loo ni ehiii lɛ ni mikɛtsu nii akɛ niyenii maha ŋmɔ mli kooloi?

english: Yes, crops that are slightly damaged or small can be thoroughly dried and ground up into good animal feed, as long as they are free from poisonous mold.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ agbi tsei ni efite fioo loo bibii lɛ ni agbɛ amɛ ni amɛfee kooloi aniyenii kpakpa. Shii abɔ ni tsei lɛ bɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ gbeyei.

english: What should I do immediately if my drying crops get caught in a sudden rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ mɔ mitsei ni egbi lɛ?

english: Spread the wet crops out on a clean, raised surface as soon as the rain stops to let air pass through them. Turn them frequently under bright sunlight until all surface dampness disappears.
ga: Gbalamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efɔ lɛ amli yɛ he ko ni he tse ni owó nɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa pɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Tsɔɔmɔ shii abɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli kɛyashi ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ baaje mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and getting burnt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiitswa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains planted beside them to act as living umbrellas until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to endure full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni enyɛ edamɔ hulu muu lɛ fɛɛ naa.

english: Why should I avoid planting my plantain suckers too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ adumɔ he?

english: Planting suckers too close causes them to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which results in weak plants and very small bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ kui bibii waa baa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in the shape of a V?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting at the tip of the lower leaves usually means your soil is running low on nitrogen, which maize needs in large amounts to grow healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele babaoo he miihia koni ekwɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli wa.

english: How do I know when my cassava is fully ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the ground around the root base begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. kɛ hei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgbalaa.

english: Yam leaves need to catch plenty of sunlight to make food for the tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing diseases and maximizing sun exposure.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Tsi helai anaa ni oha hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, usually caused by extreme sun heat, dry soil, or a lack of balanced nutrients during the flowering stage.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ he. Bei pii lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ babaoo, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni sa ni bɛ yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and looking twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni efite lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that feed on the leaves and spread leaf-curl viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and allows pests and soil diseases that feed on that crop to build up and ruin future harvests.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa sũ mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ.

english: How does spreading dry grass or leaves around my plants help them grow better?
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa kɛbɔleɔ Te mitso lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil around your crops, known as mulching, traps soil moisture during dry days, keeps the roots cool, reduces weed growth, and rots into natural fertilizer.
ga: Mulching ni akɛbɔleɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ hu ji mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i Ehaa jwɛi lɛ adalɛ baa shi ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What is the best time of day for me to apply fertilizer to my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the sun is cool, because intense mid-day heat combined with fertilizer can burn the roots of your crops.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli leebi loo shwane be mli ni hulu lɛ edɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni baa yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ ashishifãi ashã.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my maize crops as soon as the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ pɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants that are fully adapted to Ghanaian soils and local weather. They germinate rapidly and consume soil nutrients and water much faster than cultivated crops like maize, which need extra care to grow well.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji tso ko ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni atsake lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛha Ghana shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ. Amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛheɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa. ni biɔ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko bɔni afee ni eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ

english: What will happen to my cassava farm if I leave it unweeded for just a few months?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ nyɔji fioo pɛ ni jwɛi bɛ nɔ?

english: If you leave your cassava unweeded, wild bushes and aggressive weeds will quickly block sunlight and drain nutrients from the soil. This starves the cassava plants, leaving you with tiny, unusable tubers while the bush takes over your land.
ga: Kɛji oshi o-cassava lɛ ni jwɛi bɛ nɔ lɛ, Koo mli tsei bibii kɛ jwɛi ni baa shi lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa oya ni amɛjieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye ŋmei tso lɛ. Enɛ haa ohiɛɔ oyitso bibioo. No tsuuu nii yɛ be mli ni jwɛi lɛ yeɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my corn plants turning yellow and looking weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your corn plants are starving for essential nutrients like nitrogen. This happens when the soil becomes worn out from continuous farming or when nearby weeds are stealing the plant's food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ yɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen he. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ efite kɛjɛ okwaayeli ni afeɔ daa lɛ mli loo kɛ́ jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ju tsei aniyenii.

english: Why does my farm soil become hard and dried out after I clear all the natural trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa ni egbi beni mijie adebɔɔ mli tsei fɛɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tree canopy and leaf cover shield the earth from the intense sun. When all shade is removed, the heat bakes the exposed soil, burning away organic matter and turning rich earth into hard, infertile ground.
ga: Tsei ahe tsũi kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ he. Kɛji ajie hulutsoo be fɛɛ lɛ Dɔlɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shã nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. ni ehaa sũ ni baa nii lɛ feɔ sũ ni wa ni baaa nii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees stop producing pods when the bush around them grows too thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ ekpa ŋmɔtɔ feemɔ be mli ni jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ miida lɛ? Kakao lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ.

english: Overgrown bush creates excessive shade and traps damp air around cocoa trees. This environment prevents trees from receiving the light needed to flower and encourages fungal diseases like black pod rot to spread.
ga: Tsoi bibii ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo baa ni amɛmɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni bɔleɔ kookoo tso lɛ he. Shihilɛ nɛɛ haaa tso lɛ aná la ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod rot lɛ baa.

english: Why do I need to pick off diseased pods and clear dead branches from my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni majie tsei niji ni egboi kɛjɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dead branches and infected pods harbor pests and diseases like black pod rot. Leaving them on the tree or ground allows infections to multiply and spread to healthy trees across your whole farm.
ga: Niji ni egboi kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ hiɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai tamɔ ŋmeii ni egbo ni etsɔ diŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ oshi amɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my plantain plants grow tall and thin with small fruit bunches when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni ewoɔ yibii bibii lɛ? Be ni mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plantain suckers are planted too close, they compete fiercely with each other for sunlight and ground nutrients. Instead of developing thick stems and large fruit bunches, they stretch upward searching for light.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, e ngɛ tsohi nɛ a mi wa kɛ tso yiblii nguahi. Mohu ɔ, e ngmɛɛ e he kɛ ya hla la ɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable crops dry up quickly during the Harmattan season even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ Harmattan be lɛ mli, eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ amɛmli moŋ?

english: The dry Harmattan winds and strong sun cause water to evaporate from exposed soil very quickly. Covering the ground around crops with dried grass or leaves helps trap moisture in the root zone.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ha he ni oŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do wild bushes return so quickly on my land even after I burn the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi miiku amɛsɛɛ amɛmiiba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya nɛkɛ? Kɛji mishã ŋmɔ lɛ po?

english: Burning only destroys the surface parts of weeds. The deep roots, tubers, and buried seeds remain alive underneath the soil and will shoot back up immediately after the first rain.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ jwɛi lɛ hiɛ pɛ. Shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, ŋmeii, kɛ dumɔwui ni afu lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. ni ebaakwɛ̃ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their leaves and flowers after heavy flooding in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miiho baai kɛ fɔfɔi yɛ nu afua ni naa wa ni ba ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Flooded soil leaves no air space for roots to breathe, causing them to drown and rot. When roots fail, the plant cannot absorb water or food, forcing it to drop leaves and flowers to survive.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa gbɛ ko kwraa aha shishifãi lɛ ni amɛmu. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboɔ. Kɛ shishifãi lɛ egbo lɛ Tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu loo niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ amɛshwie amɛbaai kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwie shi bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and fall off during the dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants naturally drop leaves during dry seasons to conserve water and protect the tuber underground. Once the rains return, fresh green leaves will sprout back, so as long as the stems remain firm, your harvest is safe.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ahe. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Baai eŋɔli heei baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ. Be fɛɛ be ni tso lɛ tso lɛ mli wa lɛ Okpamɔ lɛ baafee shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding under the leaves. Applying neem oil water mixture or safe pesticides gets rid of them so the foliage can expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ ni akɛ nu efutu mli loo tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe tsu nii lɛ, ebaajie lɛ koni eha baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my crops sometimes look droopy in the middle of the day even when the soil is damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ gbi lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Under intense hot sun, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the soil. They temporarily wilt to save moisture and will perk up again when the midday heat drops.
ga: Yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaagboi be kukuoo ko koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Ni ebaakpɛ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ la ni tsoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ba shi.

english: Why do I need to put stakes or wooden poles next to my young yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei loo tsei ama sweet potato tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to expose maximum leaf area to sunlight, which powers root growth. Staking keeps leaves off the damp ground, preventing rot and disease while boosting yield size.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛha hulu la lɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe babaoo. ni haa shishifãi lɛ daraa Staking baaye abua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai anaa yɛ be mli ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my seeds very close to each other in the row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close forces crops to fight each other for soil nutrients, moisture, and sunshine. Proper spacing gives every single root room to swell and yield bigger produce.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tsei lɛ atswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ hulu la. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa shishifã tsu fɛɛ shishifã mlilɛɛmɔ ni ewoɔ babaoo.

english: How do I select the best stem cuttings when preparing to plant cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tsei niji ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ kɛ́ miisaa mihe koni madu ŋmei?

english: Choose mature, healthy stem sections from the middle of the plant that show no signs of rot or insect pest damage. Ensure each cutting has at least four to five strong leaf buds before planting.
ga: Halamɔ tso lɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni eda kɛjɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni ejieee okadi ko ni tsɔɔ akɛ egbo loo tsɛŋemɔ helai efite lɛ kpo. Kwɛmɔ ni kɛ hoo lɛ, tso nine lɛ eko fɛɛ eko aná ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ejwɛ kɛyashi enumɔ dani okɛdu.

english: Can I grow cassava and maize together on the same plot of land?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping maize and cassava works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested early, leaving the land open for the slower-growing cassava to mature later without competition.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya ni akpaa lɛ mra. Shi he ko koni yucca ni daa blɛoo lɛ adara sɛɛ mli ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has lost its nutrients and needs rest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ efo mli ni ehe miihia ni majɔɔ mihe?

english: When soil nutrients run low, crops grow slowly, display pale or yellowish leaves, and produce much smaller yields than in previous harvests. Planting leguminous crops or leaving the land fallow helps restore soil fertility.
ga: Beni niyenii mli nibii fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio. Baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kwraa fe tsutsu kpamɔ lɛ Legumes ni aduɔ loo ashiɔ hei ni ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants with aggressive roots adapted to quickly absorb rainwater and fertilizer. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing vital resources away from your main crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji koo mli tso ko ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei tsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛŋɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nibii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: How can I know that my cassava tubers are ready for harvesting underground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting when lower leaves naturally turn yellow and shed, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to swell and crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso wulu lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi shwiemɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why are my mango trees producing plenty of flowers, but no actual fruits are coming out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi amɛwooo yibii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Mango trees often drop flowers or fail to set fruit if they don't get enough water during flowering, if pests like thrips attack the blossoms, or if strong winds and lack of bees prevent proper pollination.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mango tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi loo amɛwooo yibii kɛji amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ fɔfɔi be mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ba koni amɛbaye fɔfɔi lɛ, loo kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ ŋmeii haa enyɛɛɛ ekɛ fɔfɔi lɛ awo fɔfɔi lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: I planted cashew trees a few years ago, so why am I still not seeing any cashews to harvest?
ga: Midu cashew tso ko afii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ. Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ mana cashew ŋmeii komɛi ni mikɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Cashew trees typically take 3 to 5 years to start bearing significant fruit. If they are older than that and still not producing, it could be due to poor soil nutrients, heavy shade from nearby trees, or dieback disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani cashew tso ko jeɔ yibii babaoo shishi. Kɛji amɛdara ni amɛwooo yibii lolo. Enɛ baanyɛ ajɛ niyenii kpakpai ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Shade ni jɛɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli loo gbele ni jɛɔ hela mli baa

english: Why are all the tiny young cashews falling off my tree before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cashew ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ mitso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Young cashew fruits drop early mainly due to insect attacks like the tea mosquito bug, or because the tree is stressed from sudden dry dry spells and lacks enough moisture.
ga: Cashew yibii bibii lɛ baagbee shi oya. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji kooloi bibii, tamɔ Aedes ŋmeii, loo akɛni tso lɛ egbi trukaa kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni bɛ lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ hewɔ.

english: How much land space do I need to leave between my mango trees when planting them?
ga: Gbɛ enyiɛ esa akɛ mashi yɛ mango tsei ateŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Mango trees grow large roots and wide branches, so they need about 10 meters by 10 meters of space between each tree to prevent overcrowding and ensure every tree gets enough sunlight.
ga: Mango tsei yɛ shishifãi wuji kɛ niji ni mli kwɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni mango tsei lɛ aná he ko ni miihe ashɛ mitai 10 x 10 yɛ tso fɛɛ tso teŋ koni akafee nɔ ni fa fe nine ni ekwɛ koni tso fɛɛ tso aná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: How can I tell if my piece of land is big enough to grow cashews profitably?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ da bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu cashews ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he?

english: Cashews need spacious land because mature trees spread out widely. A standard acre can comfortably fit about 40 to 50 cashew trees, which is enough to start a viable small-scale farm.
ga: He ko he miihia cashew ŋmeii ejaakɛ tsei lɛ egbɛ eshwã he fɛɛ he. Acre kome ni sa lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ cashew tsei aaafee 40 kɛyashi 50 yɛ hejɔlɛ mli. Enɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛjeɔ ŋmɔ bibioo ko ni baanyɛ aba mli lɛ shishi.

english: Can I plant other crops on the leftover land between my young cashew trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ tsei krokomɛi yɛ he ni eshwɛ yɛ mi-cashew tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, while cashew trees are young and small, you can intercrop short-term crops like maize, groundnuts, or cassava in the open spaces between them to maximize your land use.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ cashew tso lɛ ji gbekɛ ni eyɛ bibioo po. Obaanyɛ odu nibii ni heɔ be kukuoo tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo ŋmãa yɛ he ni yɔɔ amɛteŋ lɛ mli koni akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii babaoo.

english: How much produce yield should I expect from one acre of mature mango trees?
ga: Yibii enyiɛ esa akɛ makpa gbɛ kɛjɛ mango tsei ni ekwɛ̃ ni ji acre kome mli?

english: A well-managed acre of mature mango trees in Ghana can yield between 4 to 8 tons of fruit per year, depending on the tree variety, proper pruning, and good pest control.
ga: Mango tso ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii ni shɛɔ tɔn 4 kɛyashi 8 daa afi, ni enɛ damɔ tso lɛ henɔ nɔ. ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do my harvested mangoes spoil or rot so quickly before I can even sell them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ loo egboɔ oya dani manyɛ mahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Mangoes often rot quickly after harvest due to fungal infections like anthracnose that start while the fruit is still on the tree, or from rough handling that bruises the fruit skin during picking.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mango lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ anthracnose ni jeɔ shishi be mli ni aduawai lɛ yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ hewɔ. aloo kɛjɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni akɛtaa he Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ ahewolo lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: What kind of soil is best if I want to start growing cashews in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ hi fe fɛɛ kɛji miisumɔ ni mabɔi cashew ŋmeii adumɔ yɛ Ghana?

english: Cashews grow best in well-drained sandy or loamy soil. They do not do well in clay or waterlogged soils where water stands for long periods, as this rots their root system.
ga: Cashews kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã loo ŋã yɔɔ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Ekwɛ̃ɔɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni sũ yɔɔ nɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ ni haa nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Ejaakɛ ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Should I cut back the big branches of my old mango tree if it stops producing fruit?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo mango tso momo ko nine agbo ko kɛji ekpa yibiiwoo?

english: Yes, heavy pruning of old or overgrown mango trees allows sunlight to reach the inner branches and encourages new shoots to grow, which will bring fresh flowers and fruit in the next season.
ga: Hɛɛ, mango tsei ni egbɔ loo ni eda fe nine lɛ ni aaafo lɛ haa hulu la shɛɔ tsei lɛ aniji amli ni ewoɔ tsei heei ahe hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Enɛ baaha fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai heei aba yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if my farmland needs organic fertilizer like manure or chemical fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Organic fertilizer like animal manure feeds the soil over a long period and helps it hold water during dry spells, while chemical fertilizer provides quick food directly to the crops. Using manure regularly improves the health of your land for future seasons.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ kooloi ashishifãi, haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii be kakadaŋŋ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. Yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii niyenii oya tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when the plants are still very young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tsei lɛ darako kwraa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant food. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer early in the plant's life turns the leaves green and helps the maize grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ tso lɛ wala shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni eye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops right after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with deep, established root systems that drink up rain instantly. Your young crop seedlings are still building roots, so clearing weeds early gives your crops a fair chance to drink the water and nutrients first.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni baanyɛ aŋɔ nugbɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Odumɔwui bibii lɛ miifee shishifãi lolo. No hewɔ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Enɛ baaha otsei lɛ aná hegbɛ amɛnu nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Pepper plants often drop flowers when they experience stress from extreme sun heat or irregular watering. Giving them consistent water and light shade during very hot afternoons helps the flowers stay on and turn into peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hao amɛ. Nu kɛ hulutsoo ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees drying up when I clear all the big trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ mijie tsei ni edara lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive direct, harsh sunlight because their leaves burn easily. Planting tall crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides temporary shade umbrellas that protect the young cocoa until it is strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ, ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa be kukuoo mli hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe waɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and fall off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry periods on purpose to save water and protect itself from hot weather. Once the rains return, the stem will sprout fresh green leaves and continue growing tubers underground.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ he. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii.

english: Why do some of my tomato seeds fail to sprout even when I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato dumɔwui komɛi kwɛɛɛ kɛji akɛ awo amɛ nu daa gbi po lɛ?

english: Giving seeds too much water can rot them under the ground before they wake up, or planting them too deep prevents shoots from reaching the sunlight. Seeds only need moist, loose soil and moderate warmth to sprout.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nu wo dumɔwui lɛ anɔ fe nine lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛte shi. Aloo kɛ́ adu mli tsɔ lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná hulu la. Dumɔwui taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni efɔ kɛ dɔlɛ fioo pɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away the rich dark soil on my sloped farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Bare soil on a slope has nothing to hold it in place when heavy rain falls. Planting grass barriers across the slope or spreading dry leaves as mulch slows down rainwater and keeps your fertile topsoil on the farm.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ nɔ ko ni ekɛbaamɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋji lɛ ahe loo ni akɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ agbɛɔ baai ni egboi lɛ ashwãa lɛ baaha nugbɔ nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why does my harvested maize get eaten by insects so quickly inside my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ miiye mi ŋmãa lɛ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Insects thrive in damp grains. If maize is stored before it is completely dry, small bugs will multiply fast; drying your maize thoroughly under the sun until the grains are hard keeps insects from destroying your harvest.
ga: Kplukai shwereɔ yɛ dumɔwui ni mli efɔ mli. Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa to dani egbi kwraa lɛ, ŋmãa bibii lɛ baafa oya. Okɛ ŋmãa lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tsi kooloi bibii ni fiteɔ onibii lɛ anaa.

english: How does planting crops in the minor rainy season differ from planting in the major rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli lɛ yɔɔ srɔto yɛ amɛdumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu mli lɛ he?

english: The major rainy season brings long, heavy rains suitable for crops that take months to mature, while the minor season is short with less water. In the minor season, it is best to plant quick-yielding crops that need less rain to produce.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa be kakadaŋŋ baa. Ehi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ nyɔji babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ. Be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ, nu baafee fioo. Yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ yibii mra ni biɔ nugbɔ fioo dani ewo yibii.

english: How do I know what a chemical bottle will actually do to the pests on my farm when I am buying it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male nɔ ni tsofa-kɛ-ŋma tsɛnsi ko baafee tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ diɛŋtsɛ kɛ́ mihe lɛ?

english: Every plant medicine contains specific active ingredients listed on the label that explain its main job—whether it kills chewing insects, controls leaf diseases, or stops weeds from growing.
ga: Tsofa fɛɛ tsofa yɛ tsofa pɔtɛɛ ko ni tsuɔ nii ni aŋmala awo nɔ ni tsɔɔ tsofa lɛ nitsumɔ titri lɛ nɔ. Kɛji abaagbe kooloi bibii ni yeɔ nii lɛ Kudɔ baa helai loo akpa jwɛi lɛ adalɛ

english: Why does the plant medicine I use on my farm stop working even when I buy the exact same brand as last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso tsofa ni mikɛtsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekpa nitsumɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mihe tsofa nɛɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pests can get used to the active ingredient in a medicine if you use it repeatedly. Switching to a product with a different active ingredient prevents the pests from building resistance.
ga: Nibii ni tsuɔ nii ni yɔɔ tsofa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ atsɔse amɛhe kɛji akɛ okɛtsu nii shii abɔ. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee tsofa ko ni yɔɔ mli ni tsuɔ nii kroko lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni amɛkafee nɔ ni teɔ shi woɔ hela lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves get burnt after I spray them with chemical medicine on a very hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa beni mikɛ tsofai eshwie nɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Strong heat makes active ingredients in chemicals evaporate quickly or react too aggressively on fresh leaf surfaces, scorching the crop; it is best to spray early in the morning or late in the evening.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa nibii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ tsofa lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya loo amɛfeɔ amɛnii waa tsɔ yɛ baai heei anɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii shãa. Esa akɛ afɔse nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under strong sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad canopy shade and keep moisture in the soil, helping the cocoa survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop turning yellow starting from the middle down to the stalk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ kɛmiiya shishi kɛmiiya shishi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient in the soil that gives plants their deep green color and healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa su eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts alongside my maize make my maize grow stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ haa mi ŋmãa lɛ mli waa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that naturally pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, feeding the neighboring maize crop without needing extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ niyenii ni tsofa kroko fataaa he.

english: Does my cassava plant growing very tall with lots of big green leaves mean I will get huge tubers underground?
ga: Mi yucca tso lɛ ekwɛ̃ waa ni eyɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli. Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ maná tuber agbo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Not always. When a cassava plant puts too much energy into leaf and stem growth—often caused by high nitrogen—it may produce small tubers because the strength did not go underground.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ yucca tso ko kɛ hewalɛ babaoo wo baai kɛ eshishifãi ni miida lɛ amli—bei pii lɛ, nitrogen ni fa babaoo hewɔ lɛ—ebaanyɛ efee ŋmeii bibii ejaakɛ ehewalɛ lɛ eyaaa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do I need to spend time tying my yam vines up on tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ be ni mikɛfi sweet potato wain tsei ahe yɛ tsei kakadaji ahe lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves into direct sunlight so they can make food efficiently and send that nourishment down into the soil to build bigger tubers.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ bɔni afee ni amɛhoo nii jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛfee bulbs wuji.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my green tomatoes turning black and rotting before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ fãi lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛba po lɛ?

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes are caused by a shortage of calcium or irregular watering, which prevents the crop from moving essential nutrients into the growing fruit.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ jɛɔ calcium ni faaa loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛya aduawai ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping all their flowers without forming any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shi ni ekɛ pepper ko kwraa wooo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when stressed by intense heat, lack of water, or poor pollination, as a defense mechanism to preserve energy and save the main plant.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo pollination ni ehiii lɛ hao amɛ. akɛ gbɛ ni buɔ mɔ he koni akɛbu hewalɛ he ni akɛbu tso titri lɛ he

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow before the corn even forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen or that heavy rains have soaked the soil so much that the roots cannot breathe and pull food from the earth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ kɛyashɛ he ko ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛgbala niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt in the hot afternoon sun even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ lɛ nu leebi moŋ?

english: In intense heat, pepper leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can drink it up, causing temporary wilting that usually fixes itself once the sun cools down in the evening.
ga: yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli lɛ Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa be kukuoo ko mli ni bei pii lɛ, efoɔ kɛji hulu lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the tree before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, dark conditions when there is too much shade or weeds trapping water around your cocoa trees.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni duŋ yɔɔ mli kɛ́ hulutsoo be babaoo yɛ. Aloo jwɛi komɛi yɛ ni miimɔ nu yɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Can I use natural sprays made from local neem leaves to protect my vegetables from insects?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ko ni akɛ neem tso ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ fee lɛ atsu nii kɛbu mi-aduawai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe?

english: Yes, neem leaves contain natural compounds that bitter the crop leaves and stop insects from feeding, though you need to spray more frequently than synthetic chemicals because rain washes it away easily.
ga: Hɛɛ, adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni haaa kooloi bibii aye amɛ lɛ yɛ neem baai lɛ amli. Eyɛ mli akɛ ehe baahia ni okɛ tsofai afɔ shi shii abɔ fe tsofai ni akɛfee tsofai moŋ ejaakɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ ni ekɛshwieɔ shi oya.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with big leaves but have tiny, thin roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ, ni eyɛ baai wuji shi shishifãi bibii yɔɔ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or is planted too close together, it spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the roots below.
ga: Beni ŋmei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ loo adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ehe tsɔ. Ekɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ ŋmei ni akwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli baa lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off without growing into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the weather gets extremely hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when the plant does not get enough phosphorus to support fruit formation.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ fɔsfɔs ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo yibii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers turn out bent and misshapen instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers twist and bend when they hit hard, rocky, or unplowed soil underground, as the soft growing tip cannot easily force its way through compacted earth.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ amɛtswa shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ, loo shikpɔŋ ni atsuuu nii yɛ nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei ni miida blɛoo lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ mlɛo.

english: Why should I plant plantain suckers alongside my newly planted cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ adu dumɔwui?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily in direct sunlight; fast-growing plantains provide wide leaf canopy shade to protect young cocoa trees and keep the soil moist during dry spells.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei bibii ni daraa oya lɛ haa hulutsoo baai ni mli kwɔ ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cowpea bean crops produce plenty of green leaves but very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi dumɔwui bibii fioo pɛ?

english: Cowpeas naturally create their own nitrogen in the soil, so adding chemical nitrogen fertilizer causes them to produce heavy green foliage instead of flowering and setting seed pods.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni ji nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ wo mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui ashishifãi najiaŋ.

english: How can I tell if a plant medicine or fertilizer I applied is actually helping my crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso tsofa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Within one to two weeks of application, a healthy crop response shows through vibrant green new growth, firmer stems, and a halt in the spread of leaf spots or pest damage.
ga: yɛ otsi kome kɛyashi otsii enyɔ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii Tso hetoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baatsɔɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni yaa hiɛ ni mli tse nɔ. Tso lɛ mli wa ni ekpa baa he muji loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why does hybrid maize perform better than the seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred for higher vigor, uniform growth, and resistance to local diseases. Saved seeds from previous harvests lose these specialized traits over generations, resulting in lower yields and unequal plant growth.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee Hybrid lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwa. shweremɔ ni yɔɔ ekomefeemɔ kɛ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahewalɛ Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ baafite sui krɛdɛɛi nɛɛ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ hu daaa ni ekɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee.

english: Why does a cocoa variety that yields heavily in the Western Region produce poorly on my farm in the Volta Region?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo henɔi ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni yɔɔ anaigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ wooo yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ Volta Kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crop varieties react directly to local climate, rainfall levels, and soil composition. A variety bred for high-rainfall forest zones will experience stress and low production in drier or different soil environments.
ga: Tsei henɔi kɛ akutsoŋ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi, nugbɔshiimɔi, kɛ sũ mli nibii yeɔ tsakpaa tɛ̃ɛ. Henɔi srɔtoi Kooi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ mli lɛ baaná haomɔ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi yɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa loo yɛ shikpɔji srɔtoi anɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and drying up in full sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and underdeveloped root systems that burn easily under direct sunlight. They require temporary shade plants like plantains to shelter them and retain soil moisture during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni edako jogbaŋŋ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛná he ko ni amɛhi ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl upward during the heat of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural stress response where the plant reduces its leaf surface area exposed to the sun to conserve moisture and prevent excess water loss through transpiration.
ga: Leaf curling ji adebɔɔ mli hetoo kɛha nɔnyɛɛ. Tso lɛ baaha ebaa ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi. Koni afee ni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi ni akatsi nu ni fa fe nine ni fiteɔ lɛ naa kɛtsɔ nu ni faaa yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain bunches take much longer to mature during the dry season compared to the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains heɔ be babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani ekwɛ̃ɔ fe nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plantains rely heavily on water to transport nutrients from the soil up into the fruit. Without sufficient water, the plant's internal processes slow down, delaying fruit growth and ripening.
ga: Plantains kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ nu nɔ waa koni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya aduawai lɛ amli. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ mli nibii ni yaa nɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ daaa blɛoo ni amɛshwereɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants have huge green leaves but produce very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil contains too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, the plant spends all its energy developing leaves and stems above ground rather than storing starches in the roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ

english: Why do my pepper flowers drop off the plant before forming any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ebatsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when subjected to extreme heat, insufficient watering, or nutrient imbalances (like low calcium or excess nitrogen), which prevents the flowers from successfully setting fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafite amɛ fɔfɔii kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli. nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa (tamɔ calcium ni faaa loo nitrogen ni fa fe nine) ni tsiɔ fɔfɔii anaa koni amɛkawo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my maize leaves are curling because of drought or because of fall armyworm attack?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abɛi lɛ miiho yɛ hɔmɔ hewɔ loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ hewɔ?

english: Drought causes uniform leaf rolling across the whole field without physical damage, whereas fall armyworms leave ragged holes in the leaves and visible sawdust-like waste inside the central shoot.
ga: Hɔmɔ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni gbɔmɔtsoŋ nɔ ko nɔ ko efiteee. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, asraafoi a-armyworms ni egbee shi lɛ shĩɔ bu ni ekpɔtɔ yɛ baai lɛ amli kɛ jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni anaa yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why does spear grass keep growing back on my land even after I clear the leaves above ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akpɔlɔ jwɛi yaa nɔ ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mijie baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Spear grass has strong underground stem networks (rhizomes) that store food energy. Cutting or burning only removes the top portion, allowing the underground stems to quickly shoot up new growth.
ga: Spear jwɛi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei (rhizomes) ni kɛ niyenii hewalɛ toɔ lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔtoo ni mli wa. Kɛ́ afo loo ashã lɛ, ejieɔ ŋwɛigbɛ pɛ. Enɛ baaha tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ oya.

english: Why does planting beans together with my maize help both crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ du ŋmei lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans capture nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into soil food that benefits neighboring crops like maize, while the taller maize stalks provide natural shade and support.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ tamɔ ŋmei, yɛ be mli ni ŋmei tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo kɛ yelikɛbuamɔ.

english: Why are the fruits on my young oil palm tree turning black and falling off before they get big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ yibii ni yɔɔ mi-oil palm tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Young oil palm trees often drop their early fruits because the tree is still using most of its energy to grow strong roots and leaves rather than support heavy fruit. It can also happen if the flowers were not properly pollinated by insects or if the soil lacks essential nutrients like potassium.
