ga: Mu tsei bibii lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛwo yibii mra ejaakɛ tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ babaoo miitsu nii lolo ni ekɛmiikwɛ shishifãi kɛ baai ni mli wa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeye ebua nibii ni tsii ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ ŋmeii efɔɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ. Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my oil palm trees turning yellowish-orange while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on an oil palm tree are usually a warning sign that the soil is running out of nutrients like potassium or magnesium. The tree naturally takes nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the new top growth and developing fruit bunches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ mu tsei anɔ lɛ ji kɔkɔbɔɔ okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii tamɔ potassium loo magnesium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ heɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee kɛ aduawai akui.

english: How can I tell when my oil palm fruit bunches are mature enough to yield the maximum amount of palm oil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-oil palm yibii lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aha oil oil babaoo aba?

english: An oil palm bunch is ready for harvest when a few loose, bright reddish-orange fruits start naturally dropping from the bunch onto the ground. Harvesting too early means the fruits will produce very little oil, while harvesting too late reduces the quality of the oil.
ga: Mu tsei akui lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni ŋmeii tsuru fioo komɛi ni kpɛɔ lɛ gbee shikpɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Kɛ́ akpa mra tsɔ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ fɔ fioo pɛ baajɛ yibii lɛ amli aba. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ akpaa fɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha fɔ lɛ mli afee fɛo.

english: How do my groundnut plants manage to grow their nuts under the soil after flowering above ground?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni mi-peanut tso lɛ akwɛ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni ewo fɔfɔi yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Groundnuts have a unique way of reproducing. Once the yellow flowers above ground are fertilized, the flower stems turn downward and grow long stalks called 'pegs' that push themselves deep into the soil. The actual groundnut pods then form and ripen completely underground.
ga: Peanuts yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko ni etsɔɔ nɔ egbɛɔ eshwaa. Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ wo ŋmɔ mli lɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘pegs’ ni tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Bean pods lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baafee ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my maize crops grow much better when I plant them in the same field where I harvested groundnuts last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ midu yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa mi-ŋmãa lɛ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts have friendly bacteria in their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest the groundnuts, that trapped nitrogen stays in the earth, acting as free natural fertilizer for the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ naanyobɔɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okpa ŋmei Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: My soybean crop has very thick, green leaves, so why are the pods inside remaining flat and empty?
ga: Mi soybeans lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli tse waa. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ pod ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lolo ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Applying too much nitrogen fertilizer or planting in overly rich soil makes soybeans spend all their energy growing tall stems and bushy leaves instead of seed. To fill out the pods with seeds, the crop needs balanced sunlight and nutrients like phosphorus during flowering.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine loo dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɔshi nii yɔɔ nɔ tsɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa soybeans kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei kakadaji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ dumɔwui najiaŋ. Tsei hia hulu la kɛ niyenii tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni sa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛdumɔwui lɛ ayi obɔ.

english: Why do my coconut trees keep dropping small, green coconuts long before they are ready to drink?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei tso lɛ yaa nɔ ekɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaanu nu lɛ?

english: Early coconut drop usually happens when the tree experiences water stress during dry spells, lacks key soil nutrients, or suffers from sap-sucking insect pests. Ensuring the trees get adequate water and organic compost helps them hold onto their fruit until full maturity.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi mra lɛ baa beni tso lɛ naa nu he haomɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu lɛ yeɔ he amanehulu Kwɛmɔ ni tso lɛ aná nu kɛ ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ haa tso lɛ hiɛɔ eyibii lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni eshɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why do the flowers on my cashew trees dry up and turn brown without producing any cashew nuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ nɔ lɛ egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni cashew ŋmɔtɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cashew flowers dry up mainly due to attacks by insect pests like thrips or fungal diseases triggered by heavy morning dew and humid air. If the delicate flowers are damaged before bees can pollinate them, they wither and fall off without setting fruit.
ga: Cashew fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ titri yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ thrips loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni hulutsoo be ni naa wa kɛbaa leebi kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ tutuamɔ hewɔ. Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ fite dani ŋmeii lɛ nyɛ amɛwo amɛmli lɛ, Nakai fɔfɔi lɛ baagbo ni amɛbaagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii.

english: Why do the flower heads on my young sunflower crop turn to follow the sun from morning to evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ayitsei ni yɔɔ mi hulutsoo tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ hulu lɛ sɛɛ kɛjɛɔ leebi kɛyashiɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Young sunflowers track the sun due to a natural growth response called heliotropism. The stems grow faster on the shaded side, constantly pushing the flower face toward the sunlight so the plant can make food efficiently and build up oil in its seeds.
ga: Hulutsoo fɔfɔi bibii nyiɛɔ hulu lɛ sɛɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ hetoo ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ heliotropism lɛ hewɔ. Tso lɛ daa oya yɛ hei ni shade yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi lɛ hiɛ ni etsiɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji koni tsei lɛ anyɛ afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ ni amɛha fɔ aba amɛdumɔwui lɛ amli.

english: Why do the seed pods on my sesame crops burst open and scatter seeds on the ground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mi-sesame tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ fãa ni amɛgbɛɔ dumɔwui amɛshwãa shikpɔŋ dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Sesame pods naturally split open when they dry out completely so the plant can spread its seeds for future growth. To prevent losing your seeds on the soil, you should harvest the stalks as soon as the lower pods turn yellowish-brown, then dry them upright on a clean tarp.
ga: Sesame pods lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji egbi kwraa bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ agbala dumɔwui lɛ amli kɛha wɔsɛɛ dalɛ. Bɔni afee ni dumɔwui akafite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Esa akɛ okpa ŋmeii lɛ kɛji shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ-ŋmɔŋ pɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, gĩ yɛ kanvas ni he tse nɔ.

english: Why is it worrying for my cocoa trees if the rains stop early around November or December?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ haoɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra yɛ November loo December aaafee lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need adequate moisture late in the year to finish maturing their late-season pods; an early end to the rains can cause young pods to wilt, shrivel, or stop growing before harvest.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ he hiaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ afi lɛ naagbee gbɛ koni amɛwo ŋmeii lɛ adara yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ. Kɛ́ agbe nugbɔ lɛ naa mra lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmeii bibii lɛ agbɔjɔ, amɛgboi, loo amɛkpa amɛdalɛ dani akpa.

english: What happens to my crops if the rainy season is delayed past its usual starting time?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ fo fe be ni esa akɛ eje shishi lɛ?

english: When rain is delayed, newly planted seeds or young sprouts in the dry soil may dry out and die before establishing roots, which requires waiting for steady rains before planting.
ga: Beni nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ Dumɔwui heei loo dumɔwui bibii ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbi ni amɛgboi dani amɛfee shishifãi. Esa akɛ omɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa dani odu.

english: If my farm is located in an area that gets rain throughout all twelve months, can I plant cocoa at any time of the year?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ he ko ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ nyɔji nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ mli. Ani manyɛ madu kookoo yɛ afi lɛ mli be fɛɛ be?

english: Even in areas with year-round rainfall, it is best to plant during the months of heaviest rain so young cocoa plants can build deep, strong roots before lighter rain periods.
ga: Yɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ po Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu yɛ nyɔji ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ amli. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ afee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa dani nugbɔ fioo anɛ.

english: How do changing rain patterns affect how my cocoa trees produce flowers and pods?
ga: Te nugbɔshiimɔ ni tsakeɔ lɛ saa bɔ ni mi-cacao tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Cocoa trees rely on a change from dry weather to rain to trigger flowering; unpredictable rainfall can confuse the tree's natural cycle, leading to uneven flowering and reduced pod production.
ga: Cacao tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ tsakemɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi kɛyaa nugbɔshiimɔ mli lɛ nɔ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ahe hewalɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ baanyɛ afite tso adebɔɔ mli shihilɛ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ ekome ni ehaa pod ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: What key preparations should my family and I make on the farm before the main cocoa season starts?
ga: Mɛɛ hesaamɔi ni he hiaa esa akɛ mi kɛ miweku lɛ afee yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani kookoo be titri lɛ aje shishi?

english: Before the season begins, you should clear weeds, prune overgrown branches to let in light, clear pathways, and prepare your pod-breaking tools and drying mats.
ga: Dani be lɛ baaje shishi Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ ohe. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni edara fe nine lɛ koni la aba. Tsɔɔmɔ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ nɔ ni osaa nibii ni akɛfoɔ pods kɛ mat ni egbi lɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to start clearing land for planting new cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛduɔ kokoo tsei heei lɛ?

english: Land clearing is best done towards the end of the dry season so that the brush dries easily for clearing and the field is ready immediately when the first rains arrive.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaajie jwɛi lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ naagbee bɔni afee ni jwɛi lɛ ajiemɔ afee mlɛo. Ni ŋmɔ lɛ fee klalo beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ pɛ kɛkɛ.

english: Why should I keep my cocoa seedlings under shade in a nursery before moving them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahã kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahi hulutsoo shishi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛ amɛ awo shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Nursery shade protects delicate seedlings from scorching sun and strong winds, allowing them to grow strong stems and leaves before facing harsh open-field conditions.
ga: He ni akwɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ lɛ hulutsoo buɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ tsei kɛ baai ni mli wa dani amɛyajeɔ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers when a dry spell lasts longer than expected?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ fe bɔ ni akpaa gbɛ lɛ?

english: Dropping flowers is a defense mechanism; when water is scarce, the cocoa tree sheds flowers to conserve water and keep its trunk and branches alive until rain returns.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he. Beni nu faaa lɛ Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛ nu ato. ni okwɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛ eniji lɛ anɔ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: What can I do on my farm to help keep the soil moist when the rains are delayed?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ?

english: You can spread dry leaves, weeds, or straw around the base of your crops—a practice called mulching—to trap soil moisture and shade the roots from hot sunlight.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ baai ni egbi, jwɛi, loo jwɛi afɔ otsei lɛ ashishi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ he. Koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ebu shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Do young cocoa seedlings suffer more from a lack of rain than older, mature cocoa trees?
ga: Ani cacao tsei bibii lɛ naa piŋmɔ babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ hewɔ fe cacao tsei ni eda lɛ?

english: Yes, young cocoa seedlings have shallow roots that cannot reach deep underground water sources, making them far more vulnerable to dry spells than old trees with deep roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo tsei lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu jɛɛhei ni mli kwɔ lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɔ amɛshɛɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ ahe oya fe tsei ni edara ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ.

english: Why are tiny green and brown worms eating the leaves of my young maize plants, and how can I stop them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛ naa?

english: Young maize leaves are soft and juicy, attracting pests like fall armyworms. Spraying safe, recommended pesticides or neem extract early in the morning when the worms are active kills them before they eat the growing tip of the plant.
ga: Abɛi bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛ nu. Egbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ cutworms yɛ fɛ̃i be mli. Tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe, ni atsɔɔ akɛ ashwie nɔ leebi be mli ni kooloi lɛ miitsu nii lɛ baagbe amɛ dani amɛye tso lɛ shishigbɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and die suddenly even when the soil around them is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is usually caused by soil-borne bacterial or fungal diseases. The disease blocks the water pipes inside the plant stem, preventing water from reaching the leaves even if the soil has plenty of moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni jɛɔ bacteria loo fungal mli ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli efɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Hela nɛɛ tsiɔ nu paipii ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli lɛ anaa. Tsĩ nu naa koni ekashɛ baai lɛ ahe kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ po.

english: Why do my stored maize and cowpea grains develop tiny holes and turn into powder after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa kɛ tsina ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni etsɔɔ powda yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ.

english: Insects called weevils lay eggs on the grains. When the eggs hatch, the tiny insects eat the grain from the inside out. Drying your grains completely under the sun and storing them in airtight bags or containers smothers the insects.
ga: Kplukai ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ dumɔwui anɔ. Kɛ́ wɔji lɛ fɔ lɛ, kooloi bibii lɛ yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hulu shishi ni akɛto kotoku loo tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaashwie kooloi bibii.

english: Is it safe for me to plant my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is safer to wait until the rains become regular, usually after two or three good downpours. The first rain often tricks seeds into sprouting, but if dry heat returns for a few weeks, the young seedlings will scorch and die.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ lakaa dumɔwui koni amɛkwɛ̃. Shi kɛji akɛ latsaa ni egbi lɛ ku esɛɛ eba otsii fioo komɛi hu? Tso bibioo lɛ baashã ni egbo.

english: How can I tell if my crop is suffering from too much water or not enough rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu babaoo loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ faaa?

english: When crops lack water, their leaves curl up and feel crisp or limp during midday heat. When crops get too much water, their leaves turn pale yellow and the roots start rotting in soggy soil due to lack of air.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ bɛ nu lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛnuɔ he akɛ amɛhe ejɔ loo amɛhe ejɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa be mli. Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nu babaoo lɛ Baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Ni shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow and dropping off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso lɛ shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi oya lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its lower leaves when it lacks vital soil nutrients like nitrogen or when experiencing drought stress. Adding well-rotted animal manure or compost around the base gives the soil the food the plant needs to stay green.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ eshishi baai lɛ kɛji akɛ ebɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, loo kɛji akɛ ekɛ hɔmɔ haomɔ kpe. Koolooi ashishifã loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he Shishitoo lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and thin with weak stems when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ waa lɛ, kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they compete for sunlight. Each plant stretches upwards as fast as it can to reach the light, using all its energy to grow tall rather than building a thick, strong stem.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛbaatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná hulu la. Tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko tsɔɔ ehe oya bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni eshɛ la lɛ he. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛkwɛ̃ moŋ fe ni eeefee tsei ni mli tse ni mli wa.

english: Why do weeds always grow so much faster than the crops I planted carefully?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya be fɛɛ be fe tsei ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally adapted to survive harsh conditions. They absorb water and nutrients from the soil much faster than cultivated crops, which is why clearing them early is essential.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni afɔ amɛhe mra lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep falling off without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ pepper ko baaa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when temperatures get extremely hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps hold the flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ akɛ mulch ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi amɛhe.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my yam tubers from the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa sweet potato ŋmeii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yams are mature when the leaves and vines on top of the soil start turning yellow and naturally dry up. This signals that the plant has stopped growing leaves and stored all its food inside the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ shɛɔ shweremɔ he beni baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa baai lɛ akwɛmɔ ni ekɛ eniyenii fɛɛ eto ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: I bought high-yielding maize seeds from Accra, but why are they growing poorly on my farm in Tamale?
ga: Mihe ŋmãa dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo kɛjɛ Accra. Shi mɛni hewɔ amɛkwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ Tamale lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds perform differently based on local rainfall, heat, and soil types. Seeds bred for southern forest zones often struggle with the higher heat and drier conditions in northern regions, which is why new varieties should always be tested locally first.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ahewalɛ srɔtoi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ, dɔlɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ henɔ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, ehe bahiaa ni dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ yɛ kooi ni yɔɔ kooyigbɛ lɛ amli lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni mli wa kɛ hulutsoo be ni yɔɔ kooyigbɛ hei lɛ akpee. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni aka ŋmeii heei akwɛ lɛ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, yɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ

english: Why should I test a small batch of new crop seeds on a tiny plot before planting my whole farm with them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maka dumɔwui heei akuu bibioo ko makwɛ? yɛ he bibioo ko nɔ dani ekɛ nakai dumɔwui lɛ adu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ

english: Testing a new variety on a small patch allows you to see how it copes with your local pests, rainfall, and soil without risking your entire seasonal income if the variety fails to adapt to your land.
ga: Kaa henɔi heei yɛ he bibioo ko Ehaa onaa bɔ ni henɔi lɛ tsuɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he nii amɛhaa. ni okɛ shika fɛɛ ni onáa yɛ be mli lɛ wooo oshara mli. Kɛji akɛ srɔtoi lɛ kɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ kpaaa gbee

english: I imported tomato seeds from abroad, but why are the plants dropping flowers without producing any fruit?
ga: Mikɛ tomato dumɔwui baa kɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ. Shi mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi shi amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Foreign crop varieties are often adapted to cooler climates. The high heat and humidity in local Ghanaian environments can cause flower abortion, where the plant drops its blooms because the heat prevents proper pollination.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, maŋsɛɛ tsei srɔtoi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli ejɔ mli. Dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa ni yɔɔ Ghana shihilɛhe lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ afɔ shi. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi ejaakɛ latsaa lɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa.

english: If a seed package claims it produces 30 bags per acre, why am I only getting 10 bags on my farm?
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ kɛɛ ebaawo kotokui 30 yɛ acre kome mli. Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛ baagi 10 pɛ nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Package estimates come from ideal trial farm conditions. Your local yield depends on your specific soil fertility, rain patterns, and pest presence, which varies from one district or farm to another.
ga: Paketi akɔntaabuu damɔ ŋmɔ shikpamɔ shihilɛi ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɔ. Omaŋ lɛ mli yibiiwoo lɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ kpokpaa fɛɛ kpokpaa loo ŋmɔ mli.

english: My relative in Kumasi gets huge yields using a specific fertilizer, so why is it not working for my crops in Volta?
ga: Miwekumɛi ni yɔɔ Kumasi lɛ naa yibii babaoo kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛhaaa miŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ Volta lɛ?

english: Soil composition changes completely from one region to another. Land in Volta may lack different nutrients than land in Kumasi, meaning the fertilizer your relative uses might not supply what your specific soil needs.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii tsakeɔ kwraa kɛjɛɔ kpokpaa kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ. Ekolɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ Volta lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai srɔtoi fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ Kumasi lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni owekunyo lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haŋ nɔ pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why does cabbage grow very well on my neighbor's land, but stays tiny on my plot right across the road?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kaabii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ akutsoŋnyo ko shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ? Shi eji bibioo lolo yɛ mishikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ naa lɛ nɔ.

english: Soil health can vary across very short distances. Your neighbor's soil might hold more water, have better drainage, or contain less acid than your land, requiring you to treat your soil differently.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ baanyɛ atsake yɛ he ko ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ kuku waa. Ekolɛ nu babaoo yɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ loo acid ni faaa fe shikpɔŋ Ehaa okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper roots rot when I water them as often as my neighbor in the valley waters theirs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ shii abɔ tamɔ bɔ ni mikutsoŋbii ni yɔɔ jɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa amɛ nu lɛ?

english: Valley soil holds onto water much longer than soil on higher ground or sandy soil. If your land drains differently, watering at the same schedule as someone nearby will drown your roots and cause fungal disease.
ga: Jɔɔ mli shikpɔji lɛ hiɛɔ nu be kakadaŋŋ fe gɔŋ loo ŋã shikpɔji. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu homɔ srɔtoi. Nu ni oooha yɛ be kome mli kɛ okutsoŋbii lɛ baaha oshishifãi lɛ atsɔ shishi ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela aba.

english: Why do crops planted in April do very well in Sunyani but fail when I plant them in Bolgatanga at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ April mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ Sunyani lɛ? Shi ehiii beni midu yɛ Bolgatanga yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Ghana has distinct climate zones with different rainy season schedules. April marks the main rains in the middle forest belt, but the dry season continues longer in the north, causing crops planted too early to dry up.
ga: Ghana yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ hei srɔtoi kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be he gbɛjianɔtooi srɔtoi. Abuɔ April akɛ eji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri yɛ koo lɛ teŋgbɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ. Shi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baatsɛ fe nakai yɛ kooyigbɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa saplings wither quickly when planted in open land, but thrive when planted in the forest zone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ? Shi ani ebaanyɛ eda kɛ́ adu yɛ koo ko mli?

english: Cocoa trees need humidity and partial canopy cover when young. In open areas with full sun exposure, the heat evaporates moisture from the leaves faster than the roots can drink, causing the plant to dry out.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ko kɛji amɛdara. Yɛ hei ni hulu la babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. Dɔlɛ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni egbi

english: Why does a farm two miles away have no armyworms, while my maize farm is full of them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔ ni kɛ jɛmɛ jɛkɛmɔ ji kilomitai enyɔ lɛ bɛ asraafoi akuu mli ŋmeii lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ eyi kɛ amɛ?

english: Pest infestations depend on micro-climates, wind trends, and exact planting dates. A small difference in location or planting timing can cause your field to match the breeding cycle of pests while nearby farms miss it.
ga: Bɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ damɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi bibii, kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa, kɛ gbii pɔtɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ. He ni aduɔ nii yɛ loo bei ni yɔɔ srɔtoi fioo lɛ baanyɛ aha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kɛ be ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ fɔɔ lɛ akpã gbee. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ nyɛɛɛ aya.

english: Is it better to water my crops early in the morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooofɔ tsei anɔ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: Early morning is best because the soil absorbs water before the hot afternoon sun evaporates it. Watering in the hot sun can also shock the roots and waste expensive water.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ nɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ akpokpo ni efite nu ni jara wa.

english: Why are my maize leaves curling up like tubes during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe tamɔ paipii yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up to protect themselves and reduce water loss when the weather is too hot or the soil is dry. It is a natural sign that your crop is stressed and needs moisture.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe ni amɛha nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ. Eji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miihao ni ehe miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with big leaves, but the tubers underneath are tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ baai wuji shi bulbs bibii lɛ?

english: This happens when the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or rich animal manure. Nitrogen makes the plant focus all its energy on growing leafy tops instead of sending nutrients down to build large tubers.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsɔ. Nitrogen haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni miida lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ níhi nɛ haa nɔ he wami ɔ kɛ yaa si konɛ e pee bulb nguahi.

english: Why do my bean plants grow so well when I plant them in the same farm with maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Beans are natural soil improvers that trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the dirt, which helps the hungry maize grow stronger without needing extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peas ji adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ waa ni tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: How do I know if my farm soil needs fertilizer or just extra animal manure?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi kɛkɛ?

english: If your crops grow slowly and leaves turn light green or yellow, they lack nutrients. Animal manure improves soil moisture retention over time, while quick fertilizer gives an immediate boost of specific plant food.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ miida blɛoo ni baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. Etsɔɔ akɛ nakai tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Koolooi ashishifã haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli oya lɛ baaha tsei aniyenii komɛi aya hiɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ,.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants dropping off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers fall off when the plant experiences heat stress or uneven watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist prevents the plant from dropping its flowers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ekɛhaaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbee shi.

english: What causes tiny round holes in my vegetable leaves and how do I stop them?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ baa? yɛ mi-vegetables baai lɛ anɔ Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: Tiny holes are usually caused by small beetles or caterpillars feeding on the leaves. Spraying a mixture made from crushed neem tree leaves and water can naturally protect the plant from being eaten.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ kɛ bu bibii baa. Kɛ́ akɛ nu shwie nɔ ni akɛ neem baai ni atswa lɛ efutu nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ebu tso lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni akaye lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to plant plantain trees next to young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔdu dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Kookoo tso bibioo?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have wide leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving the cocoa seedlings shade and moisture during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Ehaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I harvest my yam tubers immediately after a heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikpaa sweet potato ŋmeii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa?

english: Harvesting yams when the soil is soaked causes the tubers to absorb too much water, making them soft and prone to rotting very quickly in storage.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa sweet potatoes be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ aŋɔ nu babaoo. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ blɛoo ni amɛfɔɔ fitemɔ oya waa kɛ́ akɛto he.

english: Why do seeds saved from last year's hybrid maize produce a smaller harvest than newly bought seed packages?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni ahe ehee lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically cross-bred to produce a high yield for only one season. The seeds you collect from that crop lose their vigor and yield much less if planted a second time.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ woɔ mli pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ be kome pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni obua naa kɛjɛɔ nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ baaje mli, ni ebaawo yibii fioo kwraa kɛji akɛ adu shii enyɔ nɔ.

english: Why do I get a mix of very big ones and very small ones when I harvest crops from the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii wuji kɛ bibii fɛɛ nɔ beni mikpaa nii kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Crops grow to different sizes because of uneven access to water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Planting with proper spacing and distributing fertilizer evenly across your farm helps all your crops grow to a uniform, large size.
ga: Tsei daa yɛ dalɛi srɔtoi amli yɛ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni amɛnáaa lɛ hewɔ. Tsei ni ooodu yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii agbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ baaye abua onibii fɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ ni amɛdara kɛyashɛ he ko ni amɛfee ekome ni amɛdara.

english: Should I sort my harvested crops into big ones and small ones before taking them to the market?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majara mikpamɔ lɛ mli awo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji kɛ bibii amli dani mikɛwo jara nɔ?

english: Yes, separating your produce by size and condition—known as grading—allows you to sell the larger, premium produce at a higher price to buyers who want top quality, rather than selling everything mixed together at a lower average price.
ga: Hɛɛ, nibii ni adu lɛ mligbalamɔ yɛ bɔ ni amɛda ha kɛ bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ ha lɛ naa Ale lɛ hu akɛ srɔtofeemɔ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ nibii ni da ni jara wa waa lɛ yɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ ohaa mɛi ni heɔ nii ni biɔ nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooohɔ̃ɔ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni akɛfutu mli lɛ yɛ jara ni baa shi nɔ.

english: How can I stop my produce from getting damaged when transporting it from rural farms to major city markets like Accra?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ anaa koni ekafite kɛji akɛ ajie kɛjɛ akrowai amli ŋmɔji amli kɛtee jarayeli hei ni yɔɔ maji wuji tamɔ Accra lɛ amli lɛ?

english: To prevent damage during long journeys, harvest early in the morning when temperatures are cool, pack your produce in sturdy, ventilated crates instead of heavy sacks, and keep the crops shaded from direct heat during travel.
ga: Koni akafite yɛ gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ mli. Kpaa nii lɛ leebi yɛ he ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. Okɛ onibii awo adekai ni wa ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ amli moŋ fe kotokui ni tsii. ni oha ŋmɔshi nibii ahi hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gbɛfaa mli.

english: Why do my harvested vegetables spoil so quickly when packed tightly in bags for transport?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔi lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ akɛwo kotokui amli jogbaŋŋ koni akɛmaje lɛ?

english: Tightly packed bags crush delicate produce and trap heat and moisture, which creates the perfect environment for rot and fungi. Using breathable baskets or plastic crates protects crops from pressure and allows air to flow.
ga: Baagi ni awo mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ shwieɔ aduawai kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni emɔɔ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha fitemɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsɛnsii loo plastic adekai ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli tsu nii lɛ, ebaabu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ nɔnyɛɛ he, ni ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli.

english: How do I know the right stage to harvest my crops so they survive long-distance market trips without spoiling?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛi kpakpai ni esa akɛ matsɔ nɔ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ? Enɛ ji koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi yɛ gbɛ kakadaŋŋ ni akɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ mli ni amɛfiteee.

english: Harvest crops when they reach full maturity but are still firm, just before they are fully ripe. This gives them enough shelf life to endure handling and long journeys to distant city buyers without becoming soft or rotten.
ga: Kpaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni tso lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ shi eyɛ shiŋŋ lolo dani ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ehiɔ shi be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaatsu nii kɛ gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ kɛmiiya mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ maji ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ aŋɔɔ ni efeee blɛoo loo efiteee.

english: Why do crop prices at the market change so heavily from month to month?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nibii ni aduɔ yɛ jarayelihe lɛ jara srɔtoɔ waa yɛ nyɔŋ fɛɛ nyɔŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Market prices are controlled by supply and demand. When everyone harvests and brings their produce to market at the same time, high supply pushes prices down; during off-seasons when crops are scarce, prices rise.
ga: Nibii ni akɛhaa kɛ nibii ni ataoɔ lɛ kudɔɔ jarayeli jara. Beni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ kpaɔ ni ekɛ nibii ni ewo lɛ baa jara nɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ. Nibii ni akɛhaa babaoo lɛ baaha nibii ajara aba shi. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lɛ, be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii faaa lɛ, jara baaya hiɛ.

english: How can I reduce my high transport expenses when sending goods to urban markets so I don't lose my profit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafo nibii ni akɛmajeɔ lɛ ahe nyɔmɔwoo ni fa babaoo lɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ nibii miiya maŋtiasei lɛ amli jarayeli hei? Koni sɛɛnamɔi ni anáa lɛ akalaaje?

english: You can cut transport costs by joining a local farmers' cooperative to share truck loads with other growers, or by selling directly to farmgate traders who collect the crops directly from your farm.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ shika ni akɛmajeɔ lɛ aba shi kɛtsɔ maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi akuu ko ni okɛ okwaafoi krokomɛi baaja lɔlei lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ ŋmɔ shinaa naa jarayelɔi ni buaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ni ooohɔ̃ɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I plan my planting so my crops are ready when market prices are highest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mato miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee klalo be mli ni jara nɔ jara wa fe fɛɛ lɛ?

english: You can adjust your planting calendar to harvest early in the season before the market gets flooded, or use dry-season irrigation to produce crops when supply is low and buyers are willing to pay higher prices.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsake odumɔ kalanda lɛ mli bɔni afee ni okpa mra yɛ be lɛ mli dani jara lɛ nɔ nu afua. aloo okɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hɔmɔ baa lɛ atsu nii ni okɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii amli beni nibii ni yɔɔ lɛ faaa ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛwo nyɔmɔ ni nɔ kwɔ.

english: Why do some crops like cassava rot within days after harvest while tubers like yam stay fresh for months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi, tamɔ ŋmei lɛ fiteɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni akpaa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ lɛ hiɔ shi nyɔji babaoo.

english: Cassava roots react rapidly with oxygen once removed from the soil, causing internal breakdown, whereas yams have thick outer skins and enter a natural resting state that protects them if stored in a cool, dry place.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ feɔ amɛnii oya kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baa lɛ kɛji ajie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. cause internal decay Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, sweet potatoes yɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni mli tse ni eboteɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmei ni buɔ ehe kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi.

english: Why do my crops produce small fruits and low yields when there is a short dry spell during flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kuku ko yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Flowering is the most sensitive stage for crops; lack of water during this time prevents proper pollination and fruit development, leading to stunted or small produce.
ga: Fɔfɔi fɔmɔ ji be ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Nu ni bɛ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ pollination kɛ aduawai ni sa lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi loo ebaa shi fioo.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abele tso baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed to make leaves green and healthy, or that heavy rains have washed the nutrients too deep into the soil for the roots to reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tsei lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni baaha baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa Aloo, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why does my soil dry out so quickly even after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa po lɛ?

english: Soil dries out quickly when it lacks organic matter like decomposed plant material or manure, which acts like a sponge to hold water in the root zone so crops can drink over time.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji akɛ ebɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ tsei ahe nibii loo ŋmeii ni egbo. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu yɛ shishifã lɛ mli bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ anu yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How do I know the right distance to leave between my cassava stems when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni sa ni kã ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ?

english: Spacing cassava about one meter apart gives each plant enough space under the ground to grow large tubers without competing with neighboring plants for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight.
ga: Kasava tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji aaafee mita kome, ni ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji baa. Ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ abɔi niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli lɛ akaŋ.

english: Should I plant my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the farming season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ okwaayeli be lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is often safer to wait until the rains become steady, because the very first rain is often followed by a dry spell that can scorch and kill newly germinated seedlings.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ ba shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be ni baanyɛ ashã ni egbe dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the stems without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or dry, which causes stress to the plant and prevents successful pollination necessary for the fruit to form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ waa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ehaaa egbe pollination, ni he hiaa koni ewo yibii lɛ naa.

english: Why are my cowpea plants growing plenty of green leaves but very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi dumɔwui fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or manure, cowpea plants put all their energy into growing stems and foliage instead of producing flowers and seed pods.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ Cowpea tsei lɛ kudɔɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai ni miida lɛ amli. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwuhi.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and turning hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from underneath the leaves, or by a virus carried by these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni ji nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ anɔ

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting plantains alongside new cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nitsumɔhe lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei heei ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under full sunlight; plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide the necessary shade and moisture protection during the cocoa plant's first two years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ hebuu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ ni cacao tso lɛ yeɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it important for me to weed my field while my crops are still very young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ majie jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔji amli be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako kwraa lɛ?

english: Young crops have small root systems and cannot compete with aggressive weeds, which quickly steal light, water, and nutrients needed for early development.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni mli wa lɛ abɔ he akaŋ. Enɛ juɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha mra be mli dalɛ.

english: How can I tell if my maize is dry enough and fully ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the surrounding husk leaves turn completely brown and paper-dry, and the kernels become hard enough that you cannot press an indentation into them with your fingernail.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni ŋmei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kwraa ni egbi tamɔ wolo lɛ. ni dumɔwui lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ okɛ onineshi tsɔne lɛ atswa he ni ebote mli lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green and grow strong. It can also happen when the ground stays flooded for too long, preventing roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when I clear away all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa saplings cannot survive intense sunlight directly on them. They need shade from larger plants like plantains or forest trees to keep the air cool and protect their tender leaves from burning while they establish roots.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji tamɔ plantains loo koo mli tsei adɛŋ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ajɔ ni ebu baai bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã be mli ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: How do I know when my cassava is ready to dig up without unearthing the whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ eshɛɛɛ he ni abaakumɔ?

english: Cassava is usually ready around 8 to 12 months after planting. Look for the bottom leaves naturally turning yellow and falling off, and check for small cracks in the soil right around the base of the main stem where tubers are expanding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha dumɔ aaafee nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Taomɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. ni okwɛ kɛji ŋmeii bibii komɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi he ni bulb lɛ miigbɛ eshwa lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs its leaves spread out high in the air to capture sunlight. Direct sunlight helps the leaves produce energy, which travels down to make the underground tubers grow big and heavy.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ ni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ mli shɔŋŋ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛjieɔ hewalɛ ni yaa shi ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do small green caterpillars eat the inner center leaves of my maize, and how can I stop them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele lɛ teŋ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a pest that feeds on the soft funnel leaves of maize. You can control them by spraying neem leaf extract or recommended extension officer pesticides directly into the center whorl of the plant early in the morning.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa ni ji cone lɛ baai bibii lɛ. Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ kɛtsɔ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofa ko ni mɛi ni kwɛɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ ni oooshwie tso lɛ teŋ tɛ̃ɛ leebi maŋkpa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot on the tree during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, dark environments. Pruning excess tree branches and clearing weeds allows sunlight and wind to dry the farm, which stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni duŋ yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli ni ajie jwɛi lɛ, ebaaha hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aha ŋmɔ lɛ mli agbi. Enɛ baakpa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn dark and squishy before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni eyɛ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, usually triggered by irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist and mixing compost into the soil helps the plant take up calcium.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná calcium.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily whenever a light wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko baa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that cannot support heavy fruit bunches alone, especially if too many sucker shoots are growing from the base. Cutting away extra suckers and propping up heavy trees with bamboo poles prevents them from falling.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛŋ akwɛ aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ anɔ. alone Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo miida kɛjɛ shishigbɛ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ ni okɛ ŋmeii afi tsei ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ koni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Why is my soil getting hard like concrete after using chemical fertilizer for many years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔshikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tamɔ kɔnkrit yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli afii babaoo ni wɔkɛtsu nii lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Using only chemical fertilizers without adding natural organic materials kills beneficial earthworms and microbes that keep soil soft. Mixing animal manure or compost into the soil keeps it loose, spongy, and healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli pɛ tsu nii ni akɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he lɛ, egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii futu mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ehiɛɔ ŋmeii, ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad to plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously in the same soil drains all the specific nutrients maize needs and allows pests to settle permanently in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts puts natural nitrogen back into the earth.
ga: Abɛi ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ haa abɛi lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ hoɔ. ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it important to have a technical officer come check my farm in Techiman before I plant my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ŋaalɔi akwɛ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ Techiman lɛ mli dani amɛdu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: A technical officer can test your soil and check the field conditions to tell you exactly which nutrients your land is missing, helping you choose the right fertilizers and avoid wasting money.
ga: Wɔ ŋaalɔi lɛ baanyɛ aka oshikpɔŋ lɛ amɛkwɛ ni amɛkwɛ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛ lɛ nɔ koni amɛtsɔɔ bo niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ ni bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni ohalaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni otsiɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ shika ni ofiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main plant food they need to grow strong and leafy. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps them turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara ni amɛná baai. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I alternate planting maize and soybeans on the same field every season instead of planting maize every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake ŋmãa kɛ soybeans dumɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaadu ŋmãa daa afi lɛ

english: Planting maize continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil and allows corn pests to build up in the ground. Rotating with soybeans restores natural plant food to the soil and breaks the cycle of pests.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa mli ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ soybeans tsake lɛ, ehaa tso niyenii ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: People say soybeans feed the ground, but how does a plant put food back into the soil?
ga: Mɛi komɛi kɛɔ akɛ soya haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii. Shi te tsei feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛkuɔ niyenii kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ?

english: Soybeans have tiny nodules on their roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it. When the soybean roots and leaves rot in the field after harvest, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil as free fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Soybean lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ Beni soybean shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Nitrogen ni emɔ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my soybean plants drop off during dry spells without producing pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi soybean tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Soybeans drop their flowers when they experience heat and drought stress as a defense mechanism to survive. Giving them enough water during the flowering stage helps them hold their flowers and form full pods.
ga: Soybeans shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ he akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛha wala. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa amɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together to get more plants on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná tsei babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When maize plants are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stems and tiny or empty cobs. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to produce big cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ dumɔwui bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Can I plant maize and soybeans together on the same plot at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ soybean yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kome mli? Ani wɔbaanyɛ wɔkɛ wɔhe abɔ?

english: Yes, this is called intercropping. Planting them together helps cover the ground to prevent weeds, makes efficient use of space, and allows the soybeans to share natural root food with the maize plants.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ intercropping. Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ebu he kɛjɛ jwɛi ahe. Kɛ he ko atsu nii jogbaŋŋ Ni ehaa soybeans lɛ jaa amɛ adebɔɔ mli shishifã niyenii lɛ kɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ.

english: Why are small worms eating holes inside the leaves at the center of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Those are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that loves hiding in the funnel of growing maize. Inspecting your farm early allows you to spray recommended treatments before the worms destroy the plant's growing point.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni sumɔɔ ni ekɛ ehe awo ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Okwaafoi lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ tsofa ni akɛhaa akɛ akɛbaatsu nii lɛ tsuɔ nii dani ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do certified seeds from seed companies yield better than the grain I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ he odaseyeli ni jɛ dumɔwui anitsumɔhei amli lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are carefully bred and treated by seed specialists to resist common diseases and withstand harsh weather, whereas saved grain loses its vigor and strength over time.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ ji mɛi ni dumɔwui ahe nilelɔi kwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛnyɛ amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai anaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How can I tell if my maize field is healthy or if it is suffering from a disease I cannot see?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abele ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ loo eyɛ hela ko ni minyɛɛɛ mana?

english: A healthy maize field grows evenly with thick stems and broad green leaves. If you notice uneven growth, pale patches, curled leaves, or strange spots, it is a sign that an extension officer needs to inspect the crop for underlying pests or diseases.
ga: Abɛi ŋmɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ daa pɛpɛɛpɛ ni eshishifãi lɛ mli tse kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ. Kɛji ona dalɛ ni ejaaa, hei ni su tsake, baai ni ebɔle ehe, loo hei ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛji amɛna tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ loo daabi.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning light yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil runs out of nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to make green leaves and grow strong. This often happens after heavy rains wash nutrients away or when the soil has been farmed for a long time without adding manure or fertilizer.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛha baai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa lɛ efo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo beni atsu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii be kakadaŋŋ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii efataaa he lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them out in the open sun without any shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kooko tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse ni hulutsoo bɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct heat and strong sunlight, which cause them to lose water faster than their small roots can pull it from the ground. Planting quick-growing shade crops like plantains beside them shields the tender cocoa leaves until they grow strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. ni haa nu fiteɔ oya fe shishifãi bibii ni abaanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ebuɔ kookoo baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ shishifãi lɛ baa.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops even when there is very little rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛɔ moŋ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that have adapted over thousands of years to survive in harsh conditions. They have deeper, more aggressive root systems that can steal small bits of moisture and nutrients from the soil much faster than domesticated farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe yɛ afii akpei abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ gbeyei waa ni baanyɛ aju ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shia lɛ.

english: Why do the tiny flowers fall off my cocoa trees before they can turn into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Koni migbee shi kɛjɛ mi-kokoo tso lɛ nɔ dani etsɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa flowers must be pollinated by tiny harmless insects called midges to turn into pods. If the weather is too dry, or if harsh chemicals have killed off these insects, the unpollinated flowers naturally drop off the tree.
ga: Esa akɛ kooloi bibii awo kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ amli. No sɛɛ lɛ, tso ko ni bɛ awui ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ tsakeɔ efeɔ pod. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ Aloo tsofai ni mli wa egbe kooloi bibii nɛɛ? Fɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow plenty of big green leaves but produce very few peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔlii wuji waa shi ewoɔ pepper fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: When pepper plants get too much nitrogen fertilizer or rich manure, they focus all their energy on growing tall stems and large leaves instead of setting flowers and fruiting.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai wuji ni amɛdaraa lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii lɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up tightly and stopping the plant from growing fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe waa ni etsĩɔ tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often spread by tiny whitefly insects that pass a virus to the plant, or it happens as a defense mechanism when the plant is stressed by severe sun heat and dry soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ ji nɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa. ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tsei amli Aloo ebaa akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he kɛji hulu la ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ miigba tsei anaa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot inside the soil during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air inside the soil to breathe. When water sits stagnant in the field without proper drainage, the roots drown and microscopic fungi in the wet soil attack and rot them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu ekã shi yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni nu tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ bɛ mli lɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee nu mli ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baatutua ni amɛbaagboi.

english: Why do my yam tubers crack and split open inside the mound before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miigba ni amɛmiijara amɛmiifee gɔji dani akpa lɛ?

english: Yam tubers crack when a long dry spell is followed by sudden, heavy rainfall. The inside of the yam expands rapidly with water faster than the outer skin can grow, causing the tuber skin to burst.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ tswaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Sweet potato lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya kɛ nu oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ada. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso hewolo lɛ fãmɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when a light wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that can easily be damaged by tiny microscopic worms called nematodes. Once the roots are damaged, they can no longer hold the tree firmly in the ground when the heavy bunch of plantains weighs it down.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ baanyɛ afite amɛ oya. Beni shishifãi lɛ efite lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ atswa shikpɔŋ dɔŋŋ beni plantains babaoo lɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea crops flower very quickly in some months but take a long time to flower in other months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ fɔɔ oya waa yɛ nyɔji komɛi amli shi ekɛ be babaoo fɔɔ yɛ nyɔji krokomɛi amli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas respond to changes in the length of daylight throughout the year. When the days get shorter in certain months, the plant gets a natural signal to stop growing leaves and immediately start producing flowers and seed pods.
ga: Cowpea tsuɔ tsakemɔi ni baa yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ he nii. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ bafee kuku yɛ nyɔji komɛi amli lɛ Tso lɛ baaná adebɔɔ mli okadi ko ni baaha ekpa baai lɛ akwɛlɛ. ni amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ ebɔi fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwui ashishifãi feemɔ

english: Why do some pest medicines fail to kill the worms on my crops even after I spray them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai komɛi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbe kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ beni mikɛ tsofai lɛ eshwie nɔ po lɛ?

english: Pest medicines only work if they match the specific pest affecting your farm. Using unapproved chemicals or spraying at the wrong dose can make pests resistant, meaning the medicine no longer stops them from damaging your crops.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ amɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai pɔtɛɛ ni saa oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ kpãa gbee pɛ. Tsofai ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni esaaa lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ akafee nɔ ko. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsofa lɛ haŋ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akpãtãmɔ dɔŋŋ.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot before they are ready to pick?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly during rainy weather and high humidity. Excess shade and water droplets trap dampness on the pods, allowing the rot to grow and destroy the yield.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Shade ni fa fe nine kɛ nu ni hoɔ lɛ baamɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ anɔ. Ha ŋmeii akwɛ̃ ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall with big leaves, but producing very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛ baa wuji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil encourages the cassava plant to put all its energy into growing leaves and stems above ground instead of sending nutrients down to grow plump root tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ yucca tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ awo baai kɛ tsei ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye níhi kɛ yaa si konɛ e sa nɛ a hwɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear away all the plantain trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie dumɔwui fɛɛ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaf skin that scorches easily in direct sunlight. Plantain trees act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and trapping soil moisture that the young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Dumɔwui tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shade. Ehaa hulutsoo ni ehaa sũ mli nu ni he hiaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do armyworms keep coming back to eat my maize even after I treated the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yaa nɔ amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa koni amɛbaye mi-ŋma lɛ? Kɛji mihere ŋmɔji lɛ po?

english: Armyworms hide deep inside the funnel leaves of the maize plant during the day. If the spray does not reach inside the leaf funnel or if the chemical is too weak, the surviving pests multiply quickly and return.
ga: Asraafoi aŋmeii lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei ahe baai ni tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ eyashɛɛɛ baa lɛ mli loo tsofa lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ lɛ, Kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli lolo lɛ baafa oya ni amɛbaaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the seeds I save from my last maize harvest grow weaker plants than the new seed packets from the store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee ŋmãa kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbɔjɔ fe dumɔwui akuu hee ni jɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Store-bought hybrid seeds are specially bred for high yields and disease protection in their first generation. Seeds saved from harvested crops lose those protective traits, leading to uneven growth and lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nibii krokomɛi ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ helai ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛhebuu nibii. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee kɛ nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do the flowers drop off my pepper plants without forming any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeee pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when stressed by intense heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. Without steady water and shade during peak heat, the plant drops flowers to keep itself alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafite amɛ fɔfɔii kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛji nu kɛ hulutsoo be ni yaa nɔ daa bɛ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, Tso lɛ baajie fɔfɔii koni ekɛha ehe ahi wala mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomatoes burn after I apply crop medicine in the middle of a hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shãa beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo tsofa mli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Liquid spray droplets sit on leaves like tiny magnifying glasses. Applying chemicals under strong, hot sunlight intensifies the sun's heat through the droplets, burning the soft leaf tissues before the plant absorbs the medicine.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ taraa baai lɛ anɔ tamɔ glase bibii ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo. Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ baaha hulu lɛ mli dɔlɛ aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ baai bibii lɛ ashãa dani tso lɛ nyɛɔ eŋɔ tsofa lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants curl tightly into tubes during the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up as a survival instinct when the soil is dry and the air is hot. By curling up, the plant shrinks its exposed surface area to stop water from escaping into the dry air.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ nɔ ko ni haa mɔ hiɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ haa he ni eyɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu akaje kpo kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ mli.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops if there is plenty of space between the plants on my farm?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji akɛ gbɛ babaoo yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ?

english: Even if plants look separated above ground, weed roots spread fast underground. Weeds steal water, soil fertilizers, and sunlight away from your crop roots, starving your crop even if the field looks spacious.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbala moŋ Shi jwɛi lɛ shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Jwɛi juɔ nu, shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi amli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ oŋmɔshi nibii eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmɔji lɛ mli lɛɛ moŋ.

english: Why should I plant coconut trees on my land instead of only growing seasonal crops like maize or cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei tsei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu be mli nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa pɛ lɛ,.

english: Coconut trees provide continuous long-term income for decades once mature, require less frequent land clearing, and yield harvests throughout the year, serving as a reliable financial cushion for your farm family.
ga: Kokoo tsei haa shika ni yaa nɔ, ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Ebiɔ ni ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shii abɔ ni afee nibii yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ Sɔmɔ akɛ shika he gbɛjianɔtoo ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛha oŋmɔ mli weku lɛ.

english: How many years will it take for a newly planted coconut tree to start bearing fruit?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei tso ni adu ehee lɛ woɔ yibii?

english: Improved dwarf coconut varieties usually start bearing fruit in 3 to 4 years, while traditional tall varieties typically take 6 to 8 years to produce their first full harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii srɔtoi ni yɔɔ blema ni kɛlɛ lɛ heɔ afii 6 kɛyashi 8 dani amɛwoɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yibii ni eyi obɔ.

english: How do large trees like coconuts survive long dry seasons when smaller crops wither and die?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tso agbo ko ni tamɔ ŋmei ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli beni ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ egbi ni amɛgboi lɛ?

english: Large trees develop deep and wide root systems that pull moisture from far beneath the soil surface, allowing them to remain green and store water even during extended dry spells.
ga: Tsei wuji lɛ feɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli kwɔ ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ po.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops wilt and droop during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops lose moisture rapidly through their leaves in high heat. Drooping is a natural mechanism to reduce surface area exposed to the sun and conserve water until the temperature cools down.
ga: Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa hewɔ. Drooping ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ hulu la ni shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shi, ni akɛbuɔ nu he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baashɛ shi.

english: How do tree crops help keep my farm soil from washing away during heavy rains?
ga: Te tsei baanyɛ afee tɛŋŋ atsĩ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekaho yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Tree roots act like strong anchors that bind soil particles together, while their high canopies break the impact of falling raindrops, preventing topsoil erosion and keeping the soil fertile.
ga: Tso shishifãi tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋshɔkei ni wa ni fiɔ sũ mli nibii bibii lɛ anaa. yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi ŋta ni kɛlɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ he hewalɛ baa shi. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii

english: Can I plant short-season food crops between my coconut seedlings while I wait for them to grow?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii ni heɔ be kukuoo yɛ ŋmeii tsei ateŋ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Yes, intercropping crops like beans, groundnuts, or vegetables between young trees allows you to harvest food and earn income from the same land while the tree canopy is still open.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii, ŋmeii loo aduawai ni akɛwoɔ dumɔwui ateŋ lɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa niyenii kɛ shika kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ kã he egbele.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell us not to plant our crops too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkadu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots fight over water and soil nutrients, and their leaves block sunlight from each other, resulting in thin plants and very low yields.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni baai lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi waa baa.

english: Why do young coconut flowers fall off the tree before turning into real fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei fɔfɔi bibii shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛbatsɔmɔɔ anɔkwa yibii lɛ?

english: Flower drop occurs mainly when the tree lacks sufficient water or critical nutrients like potassium in the soil. Adding proper compost or fertilizer helps the tree retain its blossoms and produce full nuts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ nu ni fa loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii ni ewoɔ lɛ amli.

english: What causes the lower leaves of my coconut palm to turn yellow and brown prematurely?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ mra yɛ shishigbɛ?

english: Premature leaf yellowing can be caused by nutrient deficiency, drought stress, or pest attacks like palm beetles. Clearing weeds around the base and applying suitable fertilizers usually corrects this.
ga: Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ oya. hɔmɔ he haomɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii ni ji palm beetles lɛ atuatsemɔ, jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɔɔ naagba lɛ naa tsabaa.

english: How can I tell if a seedling in a nursery is strong enough to be planted on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: A healthy seedling has deep green leaves, a thick stem, a well-formed root system without rot, and shows no signs of pest damage or leaf spot diseases.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli diŋŋ, tsei ni mli wa, kɛ shishifãi ni efee jogbaŋŋ, ni fiteee. ni okadi ko bɛ ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo baai amli hela efite.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants turn yellow when they are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ beni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen or are not getting enough water to absorb nutrients from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ loo amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛjie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if my farm soil has enough nutrients before planting cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa dani madu ŋmei?

english: If previous crops on that land grew slowly, had pale green leaves, or gave very small harvests, your soil is likely low in nutrients and needs organic manure or compost.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsutsu ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ dara blɛoo Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. loo ewoɔ nibii fioo ko pɛ Ekolɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ hu mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli awo mli.
