english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and turning pale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curling leaves on cassava are typically caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, a disease spread by tiny whiteflies that feed on the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Cassava Mosaic Virus, ni ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ yucca nɔ lɛ baa.

english: Is it good for my soil to plant cowpeas together with my maize?
ga: Ani mishikpɔŋ lɛ baafee nɔ ni sa kɛha tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa woɔ mli lɛ dumɔ?

english: Yes, cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, which helps feed the maize plants and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ejieɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off before any peppers start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they get stressed by sudden heat waves, very dry soil, or too much standing water around their roots.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji hulutsoo ni baa trukaa lɛ hao amɛ. shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa Aloo nu ni damɔ shi babaoo yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves compete fiercely with each other for water, sunlight, and nutrients in the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I keep seeds from my hybrid maize harvest to plant for the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ hybrid corn dumɔwui lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds lose their strong growth traits and high yields after the first generation, so planting saved hybrid seeds leads to smaller, uneven crops.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ laajeɔ amɛdalɛ ni mli wa kɛ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ sɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛfee hybrid ni ahere lɛ ni adu lɛ baaha tsei bibii ni bɛ ekomefeemɔ aba.

english: Why do my stored yams rot quickly after I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni ato lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Yams give off moisture after harvest, and if stored in hot, unventilated places, the trapped heat and moisture encourage fungi and rot.
ga: Sweet potatoes baahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Ni kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ Dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɔmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he hewalɛ.

english: How do weeds affect the size of my tomato harvest?
ga: Te jwɛi lɛ saa bɔ ni mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ da ha lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal essential water, sunlight, and fertilizer from your tomato plants, while also harboring insects and diseases that harm your crop.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu ni he hiaa, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ otomato tsei lɛ amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui lɛ yɔɔ jɛmɛ.

english: Why does heavy rain during flowering time cause issues for my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ kɛ naagbai baa mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Continuous rain washes away pollen needed for cocoa pods to form and creates wet conditions that encourage fungal infections like black pod disease.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ hoɔ ŋmeii ni he hiaa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ahe koni ekɛ shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ ni woɔ ŋmeii ahe helai tamɔ black pod hela lɛ he hewalɛ aba.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil or the ground is waterlogged from heavy rain, which stops roots from breathing and taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ kpaɔ mumɔ ni amɛkpaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and dry up while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly during rainy and humid weather, especially when cocoa trees are untrimmed and have too much shade.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ afolɔɔɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains next to my newly planted young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei ni adu ehee lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it better for me to plant my cassava on soil ridges rather than on flat land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ ŋmeii anɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Ridges loosen the soil so cassava roots can grow deep and swell into big tubers easily, while also preventing heavy rain from pooling and rotting the roots.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ anyɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ oya ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Kɛfata he lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ni ebaatsi enaa koni ekabua ehe naa ni eha shishifãi lɛ akagbo.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating holes in the middle leaves of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that hides in the whorl of maize plants; catching them early with recommended treatments protects the growing point from being destroyed.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmãa tsei amli lɛ. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofafeemɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebuɔ he ni edaa lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hiɛkpatamɔ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Tomato leaf curl is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny whiteflies, or by severe heat stress when the plant cannot take up enough water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli beni tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop during the hot afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In intense afternoon sun, crops lose moisture through leaves faster than roots can draw it from the soil, so they wilt temporarily to save water until the day cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, no hewɔ lɛ amɛgboiɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛbu nu he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edɔɔ.

english: How does heavy rainfall immediately after I apply fertilizer affect my crops?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa beni awo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ baaná ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ hewalɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy rain washes fertilizer away from the root zone into gutters or deep soil, meaning the crop cannot absorb the nutrients and the fertilizer is wasted.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛyaa nubui loo shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni pepper ko kwraa bɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when heat is extreme, soil moisture fluctuates too much, or there is too much nitrogen fertilizer which encourages leaf growth instead of fruit growth.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji latsaa lɛ mli wa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsakeɔ tsɔ. Aloo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fa tsɔ, ni haa baai lɛ daa yɛ aduawai lɛ adalɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start rotting quickly when I store them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛto lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they were bruised or cut during harvest, or if they are stored in damp, warm rooms without good airflow where fungi can easily grow.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ loo afo amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ akɛwo tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ mli. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmɔtɔ baanyɛ ada yɛ mlɛo.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my maize seeds too close together in the same row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmãa kome mli lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the young plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition leads to thin, weak stalks and very small or empty corn cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. kɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ bibioo waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow very quickly and provide broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, giving the cocoa trees essential shade and moisture during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Ha kookoo tso lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and turning light yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellow patches on cassava are usually signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease. This is spread by tiny whiteflies that suck the plant's juices, which weakens the plant and reduces the size of the cassava tubers underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ lɛ ji ŋmɔtɔ mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Agbɛnɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ gbɛɔ amɛshwãa. ni shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei amli Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei shishifãi lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my cocoa tree leaves turn yellow and drop off during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their leaves during dry periods to save water and prevent the tree from dying of thirst. Giving the trees proper shade and mulching around the base helps them hold moisture longer.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛtsi tso lɛ naa koni kumai akagbe lɛ. Tso lɛ he hulutsoo kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt in the afternoon sun even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: During the hottest part of the day, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the soil. This temporary wilting is the plant's way of protecting itself until the air cools down in the evening.
ga: yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ tso lɛ ni egboɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli nɛɛ ji gbɛ ni tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe kɛyashiɔ gbɛkɛ mli fɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I leave dead leaves on top of the soil instead of burning them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mishi baai ni egboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mashã amɛ lɛ?

english: Leaving dead leaves on the soil creates a blanket called mulch. This blanket keeps the ground cool, traps water in the soil during hot days, and gradually rots to feed your crops with rich, natural food.
ga: Baai ni egboi ni ajieɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ blanket ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch. Kuntu nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ. Ekɛ nu toɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli, ni efiteɔ fiofio koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii babaoo aha onibii.

english: Why do weeds slow down the growth of my pepper plants so quickly if I don't clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi-pepper tsei lɛ daraa oya kɛji mijieee amɛ oya lɛ?

english: Weeds have strong roots that greedily drink up water and fertilizer before your pepper plants can reach them. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need to grow big and produce healthy peppers.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni kɛ hiɛjoomɔ nuɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii dani ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing any tomatoes when the weather becomes too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When temperatures get extremely high, the heat damages the pollen inside tomato blossoms. Because the flowers cannot be pollinated, the plant drops them to save its energy for new growth.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, hulutsoo be lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, anyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔii amli ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛkɛ lɛ tso lɛ shĩɔ fɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha dalɛ hee.

english: Why does my yam plant spend so much time growing long vines before any yams grow underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ wain tsei kakadaji dani sweet potato lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: The yam plant uses its leafy vines above ground like solar panels to make energy from sunlight. Once the vine is big enough, the plant sends all that captured energy down into the roots to build heavy tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ wain tsei ni baai yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ hulutsoo be mli tsɔnei tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛná hewalɛ kɛjɛ hulu la mli. Kɛ wain tso lɛ da bɔ ni sa Tso lɛ tsuɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni emɔ lɛ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli koni ekɛfee bulbs ni tsii.

english: Why shouldn't I save and plant seeds from last year's hybrid maize harvest for this new season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni maduɔ kɛha be hee nɛɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to produce a high yield only in their first generation. If you plant seeds saved from a hybrid harvest, the new plants will lose their strength, resulting in lower yields and weaker crops.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ hybrid ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ Tsei heei baafite hewalɛ. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni ŋmɔshi nibii hu baa shi.

english: Why is it better for me to apply water directly at the base of my crops instead of pouring it over the whole plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafɔ nu yɛ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe tso lɛ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: Crops drink water through their roots in the soil, not through their leaves. Wetting the leaves wastes water through evaporation and can attract leaves diseases, while watering the base sends moisture straight to where the plant drinks.
ga: Tsei nuɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ, shi jeee kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, nu lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ebaanyɛ egbala baai lɛ ahe helai. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ yaa tso lɛ he ni enuɔ nu yɛ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my vegetables grow better when they receive small drops of water slowly over time rather than a heavy bucket of water all at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ amɛná nu bibioo ko lɛ? Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooona nu baagi ni tsii shikome

english: Pouring heavy water all at once can wash away soil nutrients and block air from reaching roots. Slow dripping lets the soil soak up moisture like a sponge so roots can drink continuously without choking.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔse fɛɛ shikome lɛ, ebaanyɛ efɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ahe, ni etsĩ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ shwieɔ shi fiofio lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shi tamɔ sponji. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anu nu be fɛɛ be ni amɛtsiii amɛhe.

english: Is it better for my crops if I water them early in the morning or in the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu wo mli leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil is cool, allowing roots to drink before the sun gets strong and evaporates the water before the plant can use it.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mli ejɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu dani hulu lɛ mli waa tsɔ. ni ehaa nu lɛ feɔ lasu dani tsei baanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants roll up and droop during the middle of the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the sun is extremely hot, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can collect it. Rolling up leaves is the crop's natural way of reducing water loss until the air cools down.
ga: Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ abua amɛhe naa. Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehaa nu ni efiteɔ lɛ baa shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my crops turning yellow while the top leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow bottom leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nutrients like nitrogen or is struggling with root water. The plant moves whatever strength it has left to its newest top leaves to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia niyenii, tamɔ nitrogen, loo ekɛ shishifãi amli nu miiwuu. Tso lɛ baajie ehewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛya baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi fe fɛɛ lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni ehi shi.

english: Why does my cassava crop lose most of its leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves in dry weather to save water and keep its underground tubers alive, going into a resting stage until the rains return.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ koni akɛbu nu he ni eha ŋmeii lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi. Ebabote hejɔɔmɔ be mli kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: How can I check if the soil around my crops has enough water without waiting for the leaves to wither?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana kɛji shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle mihe lɛ mli edɔ? Ani ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛmɛɛɛ ni baai lɛ agbi?

english: Push your finger about two inches into the dirt near the crop. If the soil feels dry and warm at your fingertip, the roots need water, even if the leaves look fine on top.
ga: Nyɛɛ oniji anɔ aaafee inchi enyɔ kɛya shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ egbi ni edɔ kɛ onineshi nibii ni okɛtaa he kɛkɛ lɛ. Nu he miihia shishifãi hu. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ po

english: Why does placing dry grass around the roots of my crops help them stay green during hot dry weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ shi lɛ ebɔle he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mitsei lɛ ashishifãi yeɔ ebuaa ni jwɛi lɛ feɔ eŋɔli yɛ otsii ni hulu tsoɔ ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: Dry grass acts like a protective blanket over the soil, shade-blocking the hot sun so water stays in the ground longer and keeps crop roots cool.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with very few fruits when planted close to large trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni ewoɔ yibii fioo kɛji akɛ adu yɛ tsei wuji ahe lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to make food for growth. Under large trees, they stretch upwards seeking sunlight, spending energy on tall stems instead of producing food and fruit.
ga: Tsei hia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha amɛdalɛ. tso agbo lɛ shishi Amɛkpã amɛhe kɛtee ŋwɛi, ni amɛmiitao hulu la. Ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ nɔ yɛ niyenii kɛ aduawai ni ekɛbaa lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my crops yield smaller harvests when I plant the seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, their roots fight each other for the limited water and food in the soil, leaving all plants underfed instead of strong and full of fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ fɛɛ náaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Mohu ɔ, yiblii ɔ mi wa nɛ e hyi tɔ.

english: When is the best time for me to spray weedicide on my crop field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ afɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: The best time to spray weedicide is early in the crop's lifecycle when weeds are young and small. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing nutrients, light, and water from your young crops.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔse tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ ji yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wala be lɛ jeɔ shishi mra. Beni jwɛi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛji bibii Jwɛi lɛ ni ooojie mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii, la, kɛ nu kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: Will spraying weedicide on my farm harm my young crops along with the weeds?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ kɛ jwɛi lɛ awui?

english: Non-selective weedicides will damage any plant they touch, including crops. To protect your young crops, use a selective weedicide meant for your specific crop or use a spray shield to keep the chemical on the weeds only.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni halaaa lɛ fiteɔ tsei fɛɛ ni amɛkɛkpeɔ lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ fata he. Bɔni afee ni obu oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ahe Kɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni halaa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ lɛ atsu nii. Aloo okɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ tsofai lɛ anɔ lɛ atsu nii ni okɛha tsofai lɛ ahi jwɛi lɛ pɛ anɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my planted crops during the first few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ dara oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive harsh conditions, so they sprout quickly and greedily take up water and soil nutrients faster than domestic crops can.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛheɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ oya fe shia tsei.

english: Why is it important for me to apply fertilizer right at the beginning of planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ dumɔ mli?

english: Applying fertilizer early gives young seedlings the essential nutrients they need to build strong roots and healthy stems, helping them withstand diseases and early dry spells.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli mra Enɛ baaha dumɔwui bibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa kɛ ŋmeii ni wa. Eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui ni amɛdamɔɔ helai kɛ hɔmɔ ni baa mra lɛ naa.

english: Can I apply all my crop fertilizer at once, or should I space it out over time?
ga: Ani manyɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ fɛɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii shikome? Aloo esa akɛ ajie lɛ kpo yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: It is better to split fertilizer application into two or more stages. Plants cannot absorb all nutrients at once, and heavy rains can wash away extra fertilizer before the crop can use it.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooojara ŋmɔshi nibii amli awo gbɛi enyɔ loo nɔ ni fe nakai mli. Tsei nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ shikome. Ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ dani tsei lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: Why should I harvest my crop gradually little by little instead of all on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bibii bibii moŋ fe fɛɛ yɛ gbi kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Harvesting gradually allows crops to mature fully at their own pace, reduces crop damage and losses from handling too much produce at once, and helps spread out your labor.
ga: Kpamɔ fiofio Ye obua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ oyaiyeli naa. Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ kɛ nibii ni laajeɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be kome mli lɛ nɔ. ni oye obua ni okɛ onitsumɔhe lɛ afee srɔtoi

english: How does harvesting my produce over a couple of weeks benefit me at the local market?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mikpamɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli lɛ baaye abua mi yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ?

english: Selling your harvest bit by bit over several weeks keeps your produce fresh for buyers, prevents market flooding, and helps you maintain a steady cash flow.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ onibii lɛ hɔ̃ɔ fiofio yɛ otsii babaoo mli lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ ahi shi ehee kɛha mɛi ni heɔ lɛ. Tsi jarayeli nu afua lɛ naa ni oye obua bo ni oná shika ni yaa nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know when a three-month crop is ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni tsei ni eye nyɔji etɛ lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa?

english: Crops usually show clear physical signs when mature, such as leaves turning yellow and drying up, stalks dropping, or fruit pods turning brown and dry around the 90-day mark.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei jieɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo beni amɛdaraa lɛ, tamɔ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ, amɛshishifãi ni shwieɔ shi, loo aduawai amli ŋmeii ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni amɛye gbii 90 lɛ.

english: What main activities do I need to focus on during the first two weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛɛ nitsumɔi titri esa akɛ mikɛ mijwɛŋmɔ ama nɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii enyɔ ni mikɛdu nii lɛ sɛɛ?

english: During the first two weeks, focus on checking for successful seed germination, replacing seeds that failed to sprout, applying basal fertilizer, and keeping early weeds under control.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii enyɔ lɛ mli Moŋ lɛ, okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ ni yeɔ omanye lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ najiaŋdamɔlɔ Shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ jwɛi nɔyeli yɛ shishijee bei amli

english: Why does a short-season crop that lasts three months require continuous work throughout its life?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ atsu ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ be kukuoo, ni heɔ nyɔji etɛ lɛ ahe nii be fɛɛ be yɛ ewala be fɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fast-growing crops move through their growth stages quickly—from germination to flowering to fruiting—requiring timely weeding, feeding, and moisture monitoring at every phase to yield well.
ga: Tsei ni daa oya lɛ tsɔɔ amɛdalɛ be lɛ mli oya. Kɛjɛ shweremɔ, fɔfɔi, kɛ aduawai ni baa lɛ nɔ, ni biɔ ni ajie jwɛi lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli, aha lɛ niyenii, ni akwɛ bɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ ha lɛ nɔ yɛ fã fɛɛ fã mli bɔni afee ni ená yibii kpakpai.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape while the plant is still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ miida lolo lɛ?

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow starting from the tip, it usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow strong. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or compost early in the season fixes this issue.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ ŋmãa lɛ naa lɛ Bei pii lɛ enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up tightly into small cups and stop the plant from growing new shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee kɔɔpoi bibii ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekawo ŋmeii heei lɛ?

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding on the underside of young leaves. Spraying an organic neem oil solution or an approved insecticide gets rid of these pests so healthy leaves can grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ organic neem oil solution loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi nɛɛ koni baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground whenever there is heavy rainfall for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because standing water blocks air from reaching the roots, allowing harmful rot-causing fungi to grow. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away and keeps the roots safe.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ daa. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops right after the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie dormant in the soil and are naturally adapted to sprout immediately at the first rain to capture water and sunlight. Weeding your farm within the first three weeks gives your crops a head start so they are not choked out.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ pɛ koni amɛhiɛ nu kɛ hulu la mli. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi shwie oŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aje shishi jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni nɔ ko akatsi amɛnaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the large trees off my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft, delicate leaves that easily burn under intense, direct sunlight. Leaving larger shade trees on the land creates a protective umbrella that keeps the air humid and prevents young cocoa seedlings from scorching.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi. Kɛ́ ashi tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ baa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. ni ehaaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ashã.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of yellow flowers, but the flowers fall off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔi ko gbeeɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or uneven watering, such as going from very dry soil to suddenly flooded soil. Mulching around the plants and watering regularly keeps the soil moist and helps flowers turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be, tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa nɔ ni amɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ trukaa lɛ nɔ. Mulching around Tsei lɛ kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ tomatoi.

english: Why do my cabbage plants grow large loose leaves but fail to form a tight, hard head in the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage tso lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni etse amɛhe shi enyɛɛɛ efee yitso ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni wa lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to form tight heads when exposed to extreme heat or given too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to grow only outer leaves. Applying balanced fertilizer and planting in cooler periods encourages solid head formation.
ga: Kaabage nyɛŋ afee yitsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo la ni mli edɔ waa loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli. Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekwɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ pɛ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja tsu nii kɛ dumɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli ejɔ lɛ, ebaaha bulb ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants look green and healthy above ground, but produce empty pods with no seeds inside when harvested?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi kɛ́ akpa amɛ lɛ, amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli ni dumɔwui bɛ mli.

english: Empty groundnut pods occur when the soil lacks calcium during the period when the pods are expanding underground. Spreading wood ash or agricultural lime into the soil around the plants provides the calcium needed for full kernels to form.
ga: Peanut ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ miigbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Tso mli sũ loo okwaayeli mli sũ ni akɛshwãa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa calcium ni he hiaa koni dumɔwui lɛ afee nɔ ni yeɔ emuu lɛ baa.

english: Why do my yams grow small, twisted, and bumpy instead of long, smooth tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ ji bibii, etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɛkɛ lɛ? Yɛ yitso kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ?

english: Yams become twisted when the soil underground is too hard and compact, or when tiny pests called nematodes attack the growing root tip. Clearing stones, loosening the soil deeply, and making high mounds allows the yam tuber to expand smoothly.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Aloo kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ tutua shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi ni miida lɛ. tɛi ni ajieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mli kwɔ Ni afeɔ gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees break or fall over easily during strong winds when the bunch starts getting heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ fãa loo amɛgbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli beni ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛhe feɔ shwiili lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have soft stems and shallow root systems that struggle to hold up heavy fruit bunches against wind. Supporting the fruiting stem with sturdy bamboo or wooden props acts as a crutch, holding the plant upright until harvest.
ga: Plantains yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛwo aduawai akui ni tsii yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo tso ni wa fiɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsu nii akɛ nɔ ni fiɔ amɛsɛɛ. Amɛhiɛɔ tsei lɛ amli jaŋŋ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni akpaa amɛ.

english: How far apart should I plant my coconut trees on my farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu ŋmei tsei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Coconut trees need plenty of room for their wide leaves and long roots to spread out. If you plant them too close together, they will fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in smaller trees that produce fewer nuts.
ga: He ko babaoo he miihia ŋmei tsei koni amɛbaai ni mli kwɔlɔ kɛ amɛshishifãi kakadaji lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ kɛje kpo. Kɛji odu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ daraaa, ni no hewɔ lɛ amɛwoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ.

english: Why are my green coconuts dropping from the tree before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Premature nut fall usually happens when the tree experiences stress from lack of water, missing nutrients like potassium in the soil, or attacks from insect pests that damage the stem holding the nut.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi oya lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ he haomɔ ni niyenii tamɔ potassium ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ laaje. loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ ŋmeii ni hiɛ ŋmeii lɛ atutuamɔ.

english: How can I tell when my coconuts are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-koko lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Mature coconuts usually change color from green to brown, sound hollow with sloshing water when you shake them, and have a dry, fibrous outer husk.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni eda lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli nɔ kɛyaa asarasu nɔ. Egbɛɛmɔ tamɔ muji kɛ nu kɛji okpokpo lɛ. ni eyɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni egbi ni eyɛ ŋmei

english: Why do my harvested coconuts start rotting when I heap them in a big pile?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛ́ ato amɛhe agbo lɛ?

english: Heaping coconuts tightly in a big pile traps heat and moisture inside the stack. This warm, damp environment creates ideal conditions for mold and fungi to grow and ruin your crop.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ to ŋmeii agboi amli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i baa ŋmeii lɛ amli. Nɛkɛ shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baakwɛ̃ ni efite onibii.

english: Why shouldn't I spread my harvested produce too thickly on a drying table?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ mikpamɔ lɛ shwieɔ okpɔlɔ ni akɛgbiɔ nii lɛ nɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are laid too thick, sunlight and airflow cannot reach the bottom layers. Spreading them evenly in thin layers ensures everything dries uniformly without trapping moisture underneath.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei lɛ, Hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishigbɛ fã lɛ he. ni aja mli pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta bibioo mli Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nɔ fɛɛ nɔ mli egbiɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ŋmɔtɔ emɔɔɔ shishi.

english: What simple adjustments can I make to protect my stored coconuts during wet weather?
ga: Mibaanyɛ matsake nibii mlɛo. Ani abaanyɛ abu ŋmeii ni ato lɛ ahe yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: You should raise the coconuts off the bare ground using wooden pallets, keep them in a well-ventilated shelter, and cover them loosely so air can still circulate to remove dampness.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ tso ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ awo ŋmei lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Okɛto he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ. ni okɛha he mlɛo Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ebɔleɔ ehe koni ejie ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why is it important to leave enough space around my workspace when arranging coconuts for sorting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ashiɔ he ko ni ebɔleɔ he lɛ Ehe miihia ni maná nitsumɔ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa beni mihalaa ŋmeii kɛha srɔtofeemɔ.

english: Leaving clear space allows workers to easily reach, inspect, and remove damaged or diseased nuts without overcrowding, which prevents accidental damage to good produce and speeds up work.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi he ko ni yɔɔ lɛ, ehaa nitsulɔi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyaa, amɛkwɛɔ, ni amɛjieɔ ŋmeii ni efite loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya. ni afeee lɛ tight tsɔ Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ nibii kpakpai ni aduɔ lɛ ahe fitemɔ naa yɛ oshara mli. ni oha nitsumɔ aya oya

english: How does the speed at which I move or process my harvested crops affect their quality?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ bɔ ni mikɛ oyaiyeli tsiɔ mikpamɔ lɛ he loo mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ saa bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ he?

english: Moving crops too fast can cause rough handling and severe bruising, while moving too slowly can delay drying or packing, causing produce to over-ripen or spoil before reaching buyers.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmɔshi nii lɛ oya tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha mɔ lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ ni eha egbɔjɔ waa. yɛ be mli ni enyiɛɔ blɛoo tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha egbi loo ekɛwo tsɔne mli lɛ asɛɛ afo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nibii ni aduɔ lɛ egbɔ fe nine loo egbo dani eshɛɔ mɔ ni heɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ.

english: Why do I need to adjust my working space when I harvest a much larger batch of crops than usual?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsake he ni mitsuɔ nii yɛ lɛ mli beni mikpaa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fe bɔ ni mikpaa daa lɛ?

english: A larger harvest requires more room for sorting and handling to prevent bottlenecks. Adjusting your workspace prevents overcrowding, reduces physical strain on workers, and keeps quality control effective.
ga: Nikpamɔi wuji biɔ he babaoo kɛha srɔtofeemɔ kɛ nitsumɔ koni akatsi tsɔnei ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ anaa. Kɛ́ otsake onitsumɔhe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni mɛi eyimɔ obɔbɔ. Ha gbɔmɔtsoŋ nɔnyɛɛ ni baa nitsulɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ aba shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekwɛɔ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ

english: Why should I sort my coconuts by size before selling or processing them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majara ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ bɔ ni amɛda ha lɛ naa dani mahɔ̃ɔ loo matsu he nii lɛ?

english: Sorting by size ensures uniform processing quality—such as when extracting oil or shelling—and helps you get fair market prices, as buyers prefer consistently sized produce.
ga: Nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ yɛ dalɛ naa lɛ haa nitsumɔ lɛ yaa nɔ jogbaŋŋ, nɔkwɛmɔnɔ kɛji ajieɔ fɔ loo ajieɔ mu. ni eye ebua bo ni oná jara ni sa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ miitao nibii ni dalɛ yaa nɔ daa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die when I clear all the big trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni edara lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive direct, harsh sunlight. Leaving high shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains provides shade and retains soil moisture, protecting the young plants until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha hulutsoo aba ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Buu tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in the middle of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, a key food crop plants need. Applying organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer early in the plant's growth helps keep the leaves green and improves yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei lɛ Kɛ akɛ organic fertilizer loo nitrogen fertilizer tsu nii yɛ shishijee be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my field after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil. Planting leguminous crops like groundnuts or cowpeas puts vital nitrogen back into the earth naturally, restoring soil fertility for your next planting season without buying expensive inputs.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii amli lɛ haa nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eheee nibii ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on cassava are usually a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems is the best way to prevent this and ensure a good harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle yucca he lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Cassava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ ŋmaa kpakpa naa ni akwɛɔ koni abakpa nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating holes in the leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on maize. Checking your field early and applying neem seed extract or approved control measures directly into the center leaf whorls will protect your crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Ni neem dumɔwui amli nu loo nɔ ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛbaatsu nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomatoes turning black and rotting before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Black rot at the bottom of tomatoes is caused by a lack of calcium, usually brought on by irregular watering. Water your tomato plants consistently so the roots can continuously take up nutrients from the soil.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa ji calcium ni faaa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Ha o-tomato tsei lɛ nu daa bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Watering evenly and providing light cover during very hot periods helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ha tso lɛ hao. Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ.

english: How does covering the soil with dry grass or leaves help my crops during hot periods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material, known as mulching, traps moisture in the ground, keeps the soil cool, and stops weeds from growing, allowing crops to survive longer during dry spells.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fũuɔ, ehaa edɔɔɔ, ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Why do I need to support my yam vines with tall sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji afi mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Staking yam vines lifts the leaves toward sunlight, allowing the plant to capture energy better and produce larger tubers under the ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ baaha baai lɛ kɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni emɔɔ hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ bulbs wuji baa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my rice plants turn yellow when water sits on the field without flowing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni nu ko bɛ ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: While rice needs water, stagnant and deep water prevents the roots from getting oxygen. Creating proper drainage allows fresh water to circulate and keeps the roots healthy enough to absorb soil nutrients.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ nu he miihia ŋmãa moŋ Shi kɛlɛ, nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni afee lɛ haa nu kpakpa hoɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are weeds still growing heavily under my cocoa trees even though I have been growing them for three years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miikwɛ̃ waa lolo yɛ mikoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ afii etɛ etsu nii bianɛ moŋ.

english: By three years, healthy cocoa trees should develop a full canopy of branches and leaves that shade the ground and naturally stop weeds from growing. If weeds are still growing underneath, your trees may be planted too far apart, pruned incorrectly, or lacking the nutrients needed to build a dense leaf canopy.
ga: Yɛ afii etɛ mli lɛ, esa akɛ kookoo tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ aná niji kɛ baai babaoo. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Kɛji jwɛi miidara lolo yɛ Otsei lɛ ashishi lɛ, ekolɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ tsɔ. afolɔɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni he hiaa ni akɛbaafee baai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ bɛ mli

english: Will leaving weeds at the base of my mature cocoa trees affect how many pods I harvest?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni mashi yɛ cacao tso ni eda lɛ shishi lɛ baaná ŋmeii ayibɔ ni mikpaa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, weeds growing near the base steal water, soil nutrients, and sunlight from your cocoa trees. This weakens the tree, reduces pod yield, and creates a damp environment where pests and diseases like black pod disease can thrive.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ juɔ nu. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ kookoo tsei lɛ amli lɛ Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ehaa pod ni ajieɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa. Biɛ ji he ni kooloi bibii kɛ helai tamɔ black pod hela lɛ baanyɛ ada yɛ.

english: How long should it take for my cocoa farm canopy to close and block out weeds on its own?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ aŋa ni ekɛ jwɛi lɛ atsu nii?

english: With proper spacing, regular weed clearing, and good soil care, a cocoa farm canopy should close within three to four years. Once the branches touch and shade the ground, weed growth drops significantly.
ga: kɛ sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni sa Esa akɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa Esa akɛ Cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ yiteŋ agbe yɛ afii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Kɛ́ tsei niji lɛ ta shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni amɛha amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ, jwɛi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Why do weeds keep returning quickly on my cocoa farm even after I cut them down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa oya yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mifo amɛ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds quickly return if sunlight can still reach the soil through gaps in your tree canopy, or if they are cleared without addressing underlying causes like wide tree spacing or missing shade management.
ga: Jwɛi baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba oya kɛji hulu la baanyɛ atsɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ otso lɛ mli lɛ anɔ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo. Aloo kɛji akɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ ni atsuuu nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa lɛ he nii, tamɔ tsei ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni mli kwɔ loo hulutsoo ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How far apart should I plant my cocoa trees so that they grow properly and shade out weeds?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-kokoo tsei lɛ kɛjɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛha jwɛi lɛ aná hulutsoo?

english: Cocoa trees should typically be planted about 3 meters by 3 meters (10 feet by 10 feet) apart. This spacing gives each tree enough room to grow strong roots while allowing their branches to overlap and shade out weeds within three to four years.
ga: Esa akɛ adu cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 3 x mitai 3 (naji 10 x naji 10). Nɛkɛ jɛkɛmɔ nɛɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni shishifãi ni wa baanyɛ akwɛ̃. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ha niji lɛ abɔle amɛhe ni amɛha jwɛi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ afii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli.

english: What happens to my cocoa trees if I cut away too many branches when pruning?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cocoa tso lɛ nɔ kɛji mifolɔ niji babaoo beni mifoɔ tso lɛ?

english: Pruning too heavily opens up the leaf canopy, allowing direct sunlight to reach the soil. This encourages heavy weed growth, dries out soil moisture, and exposes delicate cocoa branches to heat stress.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli babaoo lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ agbele. Ehaa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa jwɛi ni tsii lɛ daa. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli egbiɔ. ni no hewɔ lɛ, kookoo niji ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ naa dɔlɛ he haomɔ.

english: What is the best way to clean weeds around the base of my cocoa trees without damaging them?
ga: Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuuɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ ahe Mɛni ji kookoo tso shishitoo ni efiteee jwɛi lɛ?

english: Carefully removing weeds by hand or using a cutlass to slash weeds flat near the base is best. Cocoa trees have shallow feeder roots near the surface that can easily be damaged by deep hoeing or aggressive digging.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ okɛ onine loo ŋmei baajie jwɛi lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ shishi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Cocoa tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. ni baanyɛ afite oya kɛtsɔ ŋtayaa ni mli kwɔ loo ŋtayaa ni naa wa nɔ

english: Why must I remove all weeds from around my cocoa trees before applying fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Cocoa tsei dani awo amɛ ŋmɔshi nii?

english: Weeds grow faster than cocoa trees and will quickly absorb the fertilizer from the soil before your cocoa roots can reach it, wasting your effort and money.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe kookoo tsei ni amɛbaaŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii oya kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani kookoo shishifãi lɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Ekɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ kɛ shika ni afiteɔ baa.

english: How can I tell if my three-year-old cocoa farm is developing healthily?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ ni eye afii etɛ lɛ miiya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: A healthy three-year-old cocoa farm will have thick, bushy trees with dark green leaves, branches beginning to interlock with neighboring trees, and early signs of flowering or small pods forming on the trunk.
ga: Kookoo ŋmɔji ni eye afii 3 ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ tsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Niji jeɔ shishi amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ kpaa gbee. kɛ klɛŋklɛŋ okadii ni tsɔɔ fɔfɔi loo ŋmeii bibii. Afee yɛ tso lɛ nɔ

english: Should I remove all shade trees from my farm once my cocoa trees reach three years old?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ kookoo tsei lɛ eye afii etɛ pɛ?

english: No, mature cocoa trees still require moderate shade from permanent shade trees. Shade trees protect cocoa from harsh sunlight, keep the soil cool and moist, and help prevent the canopy from drying out.
ga: Dabi, kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ biɔ hulutsoo ni sa kɛjɛ hulutsoo tsei ni yɔɔ daa lɛ adɛŋ lolo. Tsei ni haa hulu kpɛɔ lɛ buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa koni ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ akagbi

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy growth. Applying a top-dressing fertilizer like urea early in the growing stage will give the plants the nitrogen they need to stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni haa tso lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ tamɔ urea wo mli yɛ tso lɛ shishijee bei amli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize on the same plot every season empties specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up in the dirt. Rotating your maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ Enɛ baaha nitrogen lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my corn plants grow tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for light, water, and soil food. Giving each plant proper spacing allows the leaves to catch enough sunlight and the roots to gather enough water to build big, heavy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko to he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yibii lɛ aná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Ni shishifãi lɛ buaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛfeɔ tso agbo ko ni tsii.

english: Why do my cocoa plants need shade from plantain trees when they are young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ he hiaa ni ená hulutsoo kɛjɛ dumɔwui lɛ adɛŋ beni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that easily dry out and burn in direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing plantains next to young cocoa creates temporary shade that cools the seedlings and keeps soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni gbɛ́ɔ oya ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni daa oya ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko baa ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden poles for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa bo koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines produce tubers underground by capturing sunlight through their leaves. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground so they get full sunlight and don't rot, helping the vine feed and enlarge the tubers beneath the soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛmɔɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Staking baaye abua ni ewó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo ni amɛkafite. Eyeɔ ebuaa wain tso lɛ ni enaa niyenii ni ekwɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my vegetable crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni bɔle aduawai ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket that stops heat from drying out the soil water. It also keeps weeds from sprouting and turns into natural fertilizer as it rots into the earth.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni tsiɔ dɔlɛ naa ni ehaaa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ agbi. Ehaa jwɛi hu kwɛ̃ɔ ni ebafeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji egbo yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat ragged holes in the middle of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ buji ni etse amɛhe yɛ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are fall armyworms, which hatch from eggs laid by moths inside the plant leaves. Spraying recommended treatments early in the morning or late evening when the worms come out to feed will protect your crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji fall armyworms ni fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii woɔ yɛ tsei ahe baai amli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ okɛtsu nii lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ miitao niyenii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up with yellow and green patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This leaf damage is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by tiny whiteflies and infected stem cuttings. You can prevent it by planting clean, disease-resistant cassava varieties provided by agricultural offices.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii kɛ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ashishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa. Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmei henɔi ni he tse ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ kɛhaa lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops wilt and shed flowers when the dry harmattan winds start blowing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi beni Harmatta kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ jeɔ shishi etswaa lɛ?

english: Dry harmattan air sucks moisture out of leaves faster than roots can pull water from dry soil. Plants shed flowers to save energy and water so they can survive until the next moisture arrives.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he koni amɛhi shi kɛyashi hulutsoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baashɛ.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are mature and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, usually 9 to 12 months after planting. You can test harvest one stand by carefully digging around the base to check if the tubers are thick enough.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ oka okpamɔ lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ shishigbɛ ni ooofo jogbaŋŋ koni ona kɛji ŋmeii lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibioo lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and yield very little when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, they fight each other for water, sunlight, and food in the soil. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and food to grow strong and produce big yields.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, a key food in the soil. Rain often washes nitrogen away, or the soil has run out of it, which stops the plant from staying healthy and green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii titri ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ Bei pii lɛ nugbɔ shwieɔ nitrogen lɛ loo ehaa sũ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haaa tsei aná hewalɛ kpakpa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmei masɛi?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas take good air from above and trap it in the soil as plant food. This natural fertilizer helps feed nearby maize crops while protecting the soil from weed growth.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsuɔ nii. kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛi ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ niyenii kɛha tsei. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ niyenii yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why is burning my farm land before planting bad for my soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni ashãa dani aduɔ nii lɛ ehiii kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Burning kills tiny beneficial living organisms in the ground and destroys decayed leaves that hold moisture. Over time, burning bakes the soil hard and makes it infertile.
ga: Shãa gbeɔ bɔɔ nii bibii. ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ baai ni egboi ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, Shãa haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa ni ehaa mɔ nyɛɛɛ afɔ.

english: Leaf curling in cassava is usually caused by a virus carried by tiny white flies. The virus stops the leaves from making food, which prevents the roots underneath from growing into big cassava tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ woɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Virus lɛ tsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee niyenii. Enɛ haaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ adara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my tomato plants rot and turn black when the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain creates high humidity and wet soil, which lets tiny soil fungi grow quickly and attack tomato stems and roots. Excessive water cuts off air to the roots, making them rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ hulutsoo babaoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ baa. ni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya ni amɛtutuaa tomato shishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ. Nu babaoo ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. ha egbo

english: Why should I cover the ground around my crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo he ni ebɔle he lɛ mli lɛ? Nibii ni aduɔ kɛ jwɛi?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, called mulching, keeps the hot sun from drying out the dirt. It traps moisture in the ground so crops don't suffer during dry days and keeps weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ ji koni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off before turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they get stressed by extreme hot weather or sudden dry spells. The plant drops flowers to save its strength and water to survive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛ nu koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant yams on the exact same patch of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting yams in the same spot repeatedly drains all the specific nutrients yams need to grow big. It also lets pests and diseases that love yams build up in that soil year after year.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ he kome shii abɔ lɛ, ebaajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu akɛ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize farm turning yellow from the bottom leaves upward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to stay green and grow strong. Adding manure or the right nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or Urea will help restore the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo urea wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant maize on the exact same piece of land three years in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ ji nɔ fɔŋ kɛha mi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally puts nitrogen back into the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Enɛ baaha nitrogen lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni efo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe sɛɛkuu lɛ mli

english: What causes tiny holes in my young maize leaves and leaves that look like they have dirt or sawdust inside them?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi gbekɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa baai kɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ muji loo ŋmei ŋmei yɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by a caterpillar called the Fall Armyworm that hides inside the young maize leaves to eat them. Spraying with recommended insecticides early in the morning or late evening when they come out to feed will protect your crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli koni amɛye amɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ shwie amɛnɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni amɛje kpo kɛmiiya niyenii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cut off healthy-looking extra branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mifolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Removing excess branches, called pruning, allows sunlight and air to pass freely through the cocoa trees. This prevents dark, damp conditions where diseases like black pod disease thrive and helps the tree put its energy into producing bigger pods.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ niji ni afolɔ, ni haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ kookoo tso lɛ mli oya. Enɛ haaa duŋ kɛ hulutsoo aba, he ni helai tamɔ black pod hela lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Is it better for me to water my pepper crops during the afternoon sun or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ nu shwane loo leebi?

english: It is best to water early in the morning or late in the afternoon because hot afternoon sun causes the water to evaporate quickly into the air before the plant roots can drink it, and hot water on warm leaves can stress the crop.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔ lɛ nu leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Ni nu ni mli edɔ yɛ baai ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ.

english: Why do some farmers spread dry grass and leaves on the ground around their tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi shwieɔ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai amɛshwãa amɛ tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: This practice is called mulching, and it works like a blanket for the soil. It traps water in the dirt so you don't have to water as often, keeps the soil cool during dry hot days, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ gbɛ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. ni etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nɔ Emɔɔ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ nu afɔ nɔ shii abɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ amli. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together so I can get more plants on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná tsei babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow thin and weak, resulting in tiny or empty maize cobs instead of big, healthy ones.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain suckers alongside my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are like babies and cannot survive direct, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that provide living shade umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and moist for the young cocoa to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ abifabii ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: How do I know that my cassava tubers are ready under the ground without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifã ko efee klalo akɛ ebaaya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni okɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ efooo?

english: Cassava shows signs above ground when it is mature, usually when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to swell and crack as the tubers grow big beneath.
ga: Yucca baajie okadii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akpo beni edara lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi shwiemɔ ni egbɛ eshwa beni ŋmeii lɛ daraa yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and stronger than my crops right after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild local plants that have deep, aggressive root systems adapted to capture water and fertilizer much faster than farm crops. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing food away from your growing plants.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji tso ko ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei waa lɛ nyɛɔ emɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛjɛ otsei ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and delicate root systems that burn easily under full sunlight. Keeping larger shade trees or planting plantains nearby provides a natural canopy that shields the young cocoa from direct sun and holds moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. english: Why do I need to put long sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsei kakadaji lɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines produce leaves that need direct sunlight to make food for the plant. Staking the vines holds them off the ground so all leaves catch maximum light, which directly feeds the growing yam tubers underground and makes them much larger.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ baai ni biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni eha tso lɛ niyenii. Wein tsei lɛ ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ amɛ fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni baa fɛɛ baa aná la babaoo. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii tɛ̃ɛ ni ehaa amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily once they start carrying heavy bunches of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ebɔi aduawai babaoo womɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that do not anchor deep into the soil. When heavy fruit bunches develop, the top becomes too heavy for the shallow roots to hold up, especially in high winds, so farmers use strong wooden props to support the main stem.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baafee tsiimɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ nyɛŋ awo. Titri lɛ, yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli. No hewɔ lɛ okwaafoi kɛ tsei ni mli wa tsuɔ nii kɛfiɔ tso titri lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on maize are usually a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, a major food component crops need to build strong leaves. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer restores the nutrients needed for dark green, healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji tso ko ni ji niyenii titri ni akɛfeɔ baai ni mli wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or beans in the same farm with my maize makes the soil richer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ, kɛ́ midu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which has special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. This natural food stays in the ground and feeds hungry crops like maize planted alongside or after them.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ tamɔ ŋmãa ni adu yɛ emasɛi lɛ niyenii. loo no sɛɛ

english: Why does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass help them survive during dry hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mulching around No hewɔ lɛ mikɛ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket over the dirt. It stops hot sunlight from evaporating soil water quickly and keeps plant roots cool so crops stay hydrated longer.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ mli jɔɔ Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ ahi ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers, but the flowers keep falling off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsɔɔɔ tomato?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by sudden changes, such as dry soil, excessive heat, or pests feeding on the blooms. Keeping the water supply steady and protecting plants from extreme heat helps the flowers stay attached and form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsakemɔi ni baa trukaa tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo la ni mli edɔ fe nine lɛ hao tso lɛ. Aloo kooloi bibii ni yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa daa kɛ tsei ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot inside the soil during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil for too long without draining away, choking the roots of air and inviting fungal diseases. Planting cassava on raised soil ridges or mounds helps rainfall drain off quickly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejeee kpo. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo gɔji anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like mites or aphids feeding on the undersides of young leaves, or by a plant virus spread by insects. Controlling these tiny pests early prevents leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ mli nibii bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akwɛmɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe.

english: How do weeds actually reduce my crop harvest even if I give my crops plenty of water?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ nu babaoo moŋ?
