english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively consume food and fertilizer from the soil before your crop roots can reach it. Even with enough water, your crops suffer because weeds steal the essential plant food needed to produce heavy yield.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ yeɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa po Oŋmɔshi nibii hu naa amanehulu be mli ni jwɛi juɔ tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo lɛ.

english: How do I know if my land is good enough to plant maize this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Good land for maize has dark, rich soil that drains water easily and does not form big, standing muddy pools for days after a heavy rain.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa kɛha ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsuɔ ni baa nii. Nu ni hoɔ oya Ni sũ ŋmeii wuji efeee gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes on the exact same patch of ground every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tomato yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same spot repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ. Ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily under full sun, so they need shade from larger plants like plantains to survive their early months.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni cacao tsei lɛ aná hulutsoo kɛjɛ cacao tsei wuji tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli.

english: What causes my cassava plants to produce very small roots even when the leaves look big and healthy?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava tso lɛ shishifãi bibii waa eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa moŋ?

english: Cassava roots need soft, loose soil to expand properly, and if the soil is too hard or compacted, the plant puts its energy into growing top leaves instead of large tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli edɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ. Ni kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ baai yɛ nɔ moŋ fe bulbs wuji.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before any peppers grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔii dani pepper lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience extreme heat, lack of water, or a lack of beneficial insects like bees to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa he, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollin lɛ bɛ.

english: What will happen if I plant my crops very close together to fit more on my field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ mihe lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in thin, weak stems and small yields.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my crops with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass, called mulching, keeps the ground cool, traps moisture so you water less, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi haa lɛ akɛ mulching. baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli fioo ni otsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkaye nɔ.

english: Why do heavy winds keep breaking my maize stalks, and how can I prevent it?
ga: Mɛni he je nɛ behi fuu ɔ, kɔɔhiɔ nɛ nya wa haa nɛ abele nɛ ɔmɛ puɛɔ ɔ, nɛ mɛni wa ma nyɛ maa pee kɛ tsi enɛ ɔ nya?

english: Maize stalks break when strong winds hit fields with shallow root systems; planting sturdy trees around the edges of your farm creates a natural shield to block the wind.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ fãa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa ŋmɔji lɛ kɛ amɛshishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ. Tsei ni wa ni ooodu yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ he.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning pale yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, a key plant food that can be washed away from the soil by heavy rains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa ni baanyɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa.

english: How do I know it is the right time to sow my seeds after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eji be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eho lɛ?

english: You should wait until the major rains have fully established with several steady rainfalls so that the soil stays consistently moist enough for seeds to germinate.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ wulu lɛ aba shi kwraa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa shii abɔ. Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i be fɛɛ be bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the nutrient responsible for healthy green leaves and strong growth. It can also happen when heavy rainfall floods the soil, preventing the roots from absorbing nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni haa baai eŋɔli lɛ mli waa ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni eha shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii.

english: How does growing cowpeas or groundnuts help make my farmland richer for future crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha miŋmɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food in the soil through their roots. When the crop is harvested and the roots decay, they leave this free fertilizer behind for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni shishifãi lɛ egbo lɛ Amɛbaashi nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko nɛɛ amɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: What causes the leaves on my cassava plants to curl up and show pale green patches?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: This leaf twisting is caused by Cassava Mosaic Virus, a disease spread by tiny whiteflies that feed on the sap of the leaves. Using disease-resistant cassava stems during planting is the best way to prevent this issue.
ga: Cassava Mosaic Virus, ni ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ tsɔmɔ nɛɛ baa. ni yeɔ baa mli nu lɛ Kasava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ dumɔ be mli lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why is it harmful to plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific soil nutrients and allows pests, like the fall armyworm, to build up in the field. Rotating with legumes or root crops breaks pest cycles and restores soil nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ cutworms yɛ fɛ̃i be mli. buaa ehe naa yɛ ŋmɔji amli Kɛ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni akɛtsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off before growing into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop when temperatures become too hot or when irrigation is inconsistent. When the plant experiences severe heat or drought stress, it drops its flowers to preserve energy and water.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ejaaa. Kɛ tsei na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ he haomɔ Eshiɔ fɔfɔi yɛ esɛɛ koni ekɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he.

english: Why do my sweet potato vines produce heavy leafy stems but almost no thick tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse shi eshwɛ fioo ni ŋmeii ni mli tse bɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen fertilizer or excess water causes sweet potatoes to put all their energy into leafy top growth above ground instead of storing food in the roots to form large tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen loo nu babaoo fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ niye ní ngɛ tso ɔ sisije ɔmɛ a mi konɛ e pee bulb nguahi.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, won't I get a larger harvest from my farm?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe Ani maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too close forces crops to compete for sunlight, water, and nutrients, resulting in weak, thin stalks with small or missing cobs. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to produce large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ tsɔ lɛ, ejieɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli, ni no haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni egbɔjɔ, ni dumɔwui bibii loo elaaje. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow twisted and split instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɛ eshwa moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers twist when they encounter hard, stony, or compacted soil underground. Clearing deep, loose soil mounds or ridges allows the tuber to expand smoothly downwards without obstruction.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baatsɔ amɛhe kɛji amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa kpe. tɛi loo shikpɔŋ shishi ni eyi obɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni etse ehe lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ mli shwereɔ mlɛo kɛyaa shishigbɛ ni nɔ ko tsiii enaa.

english: Why do my pepper leaves wilt during the hot afternoon sun even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: In intense midday sun, pepper leaves lose moisture into the dry air faster than the roots can drink water from the soil. The leaves temporarily droop to conserve moisture, usually recovering by evening.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ shishi lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛha kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain suckers alongside my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain suckers provide temporary shade and cooler humidity under their broad leaves until the young cocoa trees are strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya haa hɔɔŋ be kukuoo kɛ nu ni mli ejɔ yɛ baai lɛ ashishi. Kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso bibioo lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food. The plant moves the available nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the fresh, growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too high or when the plant experiences water stress. Without steady watering, the plant drops flowers to conserve its energy to survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ. Kɛji akɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa bɛ Tsei lɛ hu baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why do the bottoms of my growing tomatoes turn black and soft before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikwɛɔ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efee blɛoo dani eshɛ po lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit. It typically happens when soil moisture goes up and down rapidly, making it difficult for roots to draw up nutrients.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake oya. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaajie niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and showing bright yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kpɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. The virus stops the plant from making food properly, leading to poor root yields unless disease-free planting materials are used.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Virus tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkafee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni baa shi lɛ baa shi. ja akɛ dumɔ nii ni hela bɛ mli tsu nii

english: Why are the green pods on my cocoa trees turning black and rotting right on the branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, heavy shade. Pruning overhead tree branches allows sunlight and air to dry out the pods and reduce fungus growth.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo, shade ni mli wa mli kɛbaa. Niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my healthy plantain trees suddenly fall over after a light rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are often attacked below the ground by microscopic worms called nematodes or stem borer insects. Once the roots rot away, the plant loses its anchor in the soil and falls under its own weight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ tutuaa plantain shishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Beni shishifãi lɛ miifite lɛ Tso lɛ laajeɔ eshishitoo mla lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni egbeeɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɔjɔmɔ shishi.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field without tall trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are tender and burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains creates a shelter that keeps the soil cool and humid for the cocoa to grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa koni kookoo akwɛ̃.

english: Why are my maize stalks growing very tall and thin with very small cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close to one another, the plants compete for sunlight and soil food. They stretch upward to beat their neighbors for light instead of putting energy into growing strong stems and big cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkpã amɛhe koni amɛtswa amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ koni amɛna la lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ he wami kɛ haa a tso nɛ he wa kɛ a tso nguahi nɛ a ngɛ wae ɔ.

english: Why does my soil dry out completely just two days after a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil dries out quickly when it lacks organic matter such as compost or decomposed manure. Adding organic material acts like a sponge beneath the surface, holding water near the roots for much longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo bɛ mli. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛfataa he lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu bɛŋkɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe be babaoo.

english: Why do weeds grow back much faster than my cassava sprouts after I clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi yucca lɛ beni mijie jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds can rest hidden in the soil for years waiting for light. Clearing the field opens up full sunlight to the ground, triggering millions of dormant weed seeds to germinate long before your planted crop canopy covers the soil.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afii babaoo, ni amɛmɛ la. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha hulu la ni fa babaoo lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ewoɔ jwɛi dumɔwui akpekpei abɔ hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ be kakadaŋŋ dani otso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build strong leaves. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help them turn dark green and grow fast.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛdara oya.

english: Is it good for me to plant groundnuts or beans together with my maize on the same field?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei kɛfata ŋmei he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting beans or groundnuts with maize is very beneficial because leguminous crops take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, which feeds the maize and keeps your soil rich.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei loo ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ lɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii kɛha ŋmãa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii

english: Why do extension officers tell us to cover the soil around our crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkɛ jwɛi ni egbi afee ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbɔleɔ wɔŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a shade cover that keeps the soil cool, stops water from evaporating in the hot sun, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ shade ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛji akɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shɛ enɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Why do many flowers fall off my cocoa trees without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can support, so dropping some flowers is normal. However, if too many fall, it usually means the tree lacks water or nutrients, or tiny beneficial insects called midges are not available to pollinate them.
ga: Kookoo tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ fɔfɔi baagbee shi. Shi, kɛji amɛgbee shi babaoo lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii. Aloo, kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges lɛ nyɛŋ afee amɛ pollination.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground when there is heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain creates standing water in the soil, the roots drown and rot, which is why planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ ehaa nu ni ŋmɛɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛbaagboi. Enɛ hewɔ ni kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa lɛ.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi lɛ? Ha sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food and expand the tubers underground. Staking the vines lifts the leaves off the ground so they get full sunlight and stay safe from rot.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ wain tso lɛ wo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ akaje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni enine ashɛ hulu la ni fa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ nɔ, ni ehi shi shweshweeshwe koni ekafite.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seeds very close together so that I can harvest more?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ midumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná ŋmaa babaoo?

english: Planting seeds too close causes the crops to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients in the soil. This competition leaves you with thin, weak plants that produce very small yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa onáa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why does leaving weeds on my farm make my main crops look weak and stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm because they steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops, leaving your plants hungry and unable to grow properly.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ejaakɛ ejuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei lɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is causing the leaves of my young maize to look like someone shot small holes through them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ mɔ ko ni efo bu bibii kɛtsɔ mli?

english: Those holes are caused by a pest called the Fall Armyworm, which eats the growing center of young maize leaves. Checking your fields early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem treatments helps control them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ buji lɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii ni miida lɛ ateŋgbɛ. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli mra Ni tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die even when the soil has plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is usually caused by tiny fungal or bacterial germs in the ground that block the water channels inside the stem, stopping water from reaching the top of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsiɔ nu gbɛ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa nu lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ayiteŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when there are no plantains or bigger trees planted around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikookoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui loo tsei wuji komɛi bɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have soft, tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Shade crops like plantains act as living covers that shield the young cocoa from hot sun and keep the soil moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my maize plants turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure gives the maize the food it needs to stay green and build large ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ehaa ŋmei lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ewo toi wuji.

english: If I plant my cassava stems very close together, will I get a larger harvest?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he waa Ani mawo yibii babaoo?

english: No, planting cassava stems too close together makes them fight for food, water, and sunlight, resulting in many tiny roots. Spacing them about one meter apart gives each plant enough space to produce large, heavy tubers.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛye niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la he akaŋ, ni no baaha amɛná shishifãi bibii babaoo. Aaafee mita kome ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ bulbs agboi ni tsii baa.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up and turning pale during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is often caused by a virus carried by tiny whitefly insects that thrive in dry weather. Clearing surrounding weeds and using insect nets or safe sprays helps stop these insects from infecting your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli Jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ ni ooojie Ni okɛ ŋmeii loo tsofa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii nɛɛ akafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before setting any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ewoɔ pepper yibii lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too hot or the soil dries out completely, pepper plants drop their blossoms to preserve their own water and energy. Mulching the soil and watering early in the morning helps the plant hold onto its flowers.
ga: Beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ sũ wo tso lɛ nɔ ni awo lɛ nu leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell that my yam tubers under the ground are mature without digging up the whole mound?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni mikɛ jɛmɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Yam tubers are ready for harvest when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and dry up. This signals that the plant has finished sending energy down to the tuber and is ready for storage.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni ekɛmajeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ naa, ni efee klalo akɛ akɛtoɔ.

english: Why do I need to cut off the extra small shoots growing around my plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Plantain tso lɛ he

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water and nutrients away from the main mother plant, causing smaller fruit bunches. Keeping only two or three healthy suckers ensures your main plant yields a large plantain bunch while preparing the next plant for harvest.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei krokomɛi loo tsei lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai lɛ feɔ bibii. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ wo mli lɛ, ebaaha otso titri lɛ awo plantains wuji yɛ be mli ni osaa tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ he kɛha kpamɔɔ lɛ.

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which pulls natural nitrogen out of the air and traps it in the soil. This naturally fertilizes the soil and feeds your maize without costing extra money.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eha ŋmãa lɛ niyenii ni shika kroko fataaa he.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to turn weak and thin so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively drink up the water and soil nutrients meant for your plants. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food in the ground.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛyeɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha otsei lɛ mli lɛ waa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do some of the maize seeds I stored in my barn fail to sprout when I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ekomɛi kwɛɛɛ kɛji adu lɛ?

english: Stored seeds can lose their ability to grow if they were stored with moisture inside them or damaged by insects like weevils. Drying seeds thoroughly and storing them in airtight containers protects their viability until planting season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baanyɛ afite amɛhe kɛji akɛ akɛto ŋmɔtɔ mli loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii fite amɛ. Dumɔwui ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtoɔ tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ baaye abua ni abu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛdalɛ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them in an open field under direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have soft leaves and delicate root systems that cannot withstand intense sunlight and direct heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides a protective canopy, keeping the leaves cool and retaining soil moisture until the trees mature.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ he. Ha baai lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni okwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from my cocoa tree when it is already growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi kɛjɛ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ kɛji etswa shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Pruning removes dead, diseased, or crowded branches to allow sunlight and fresh air to pass through the tree canopy. Good airflow and sunlight prevent moisture buildup that causes black pod disease, while allowing the tree to direct its food energy into producing bigger pods.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi, ni hela emɔ amɛ, loo niji ni egbɔjɔ lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote tso lɛ yiteŋ. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ kɛ hulu la yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ni eyɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellowing of lower maize leaves is usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen is a key nutrient that plants need for leaf growth; when it runs low, the plant moves what little nitrogen it has to the upper leaves to keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni baai lɛ adara. Kɛji akɛ nɔ ko fioo pɛ eshwɛ Tsei lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fioo ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Why do I get a smaller harvest when I plant my maize seeds very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ yibii fioo nɔ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition makes all the stalks weak and thin, resulting in small ears of corn and an overall reduced harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa. Enɛ haa ŋmãa toi bibii kɛ ŋmaa fɛɛ ni akpaa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very tall with lots of leaves but only produces small root tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii. Shikpɔŋ shishi pɛ

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or receives excessive water, cassava plants direct all their energy into growing leaves and stems instead of storing starch in the roots. Soft or loose soil with balanced nutrients is needed for the tubers to expand properly.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo enine shɛɔ nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa ebaa kɛ eshishifãi ni miida lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ loo sũ ni mli edɔ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ he miihia koni bulb lɛ agbɛ ashwã jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to make raised mounds or ridges in the soil before planting my seed yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ dani madu ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Yams require loose, deep soil so their roots can grow downwards easily and expand into large tubers. Mounding the soil also keeps the root system elevated above excess standing water during heavy rainfall, preventing seed yams from rotting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse he miihia sweet potatoes bɔni afee ni amɛshishifãi lɛ anyɛ adara kɛya shi oya ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Shikpɔŋ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ yaa ŋwɛi fe nu ni damɔ shi fe nine lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ ji koni sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ akafite.

english: Why do the blossoms on my tomato plants fall off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or poor pollination. Maintaining steady moisture in the soil and preventing heat buildup helps the flowers stay healthy and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo pollination ni ehiii Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ dɔlɛ ni baa lɛ naatsii haa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plant roots rot and turn black after heavy rainy days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper shishifãi lɛ miifite ni amɛmiifee ediŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper roots need oxygen from the air pockets in the soil to survive. When fields become waterlogged for long periods, water fills those air pockets, suffocating the roots and inviting fungal pathogens that rot the plant from the base.
ga: Pepper shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi. Beni nu eyi ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli be kakadaŋŋ Nu baayi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. ni efɔ̃ɔ helai ni haa tsei fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishi lɛ nine.

english: Why do the leaves of my vegetable crops curl upward during the hottest afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism plants use to survive intense heat. By rolling their leaves inward, plants reduce the surface area exposed to direct sunshine, which cuts down on water evaporation through the leaves.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ awo mli lɛ, ehaa hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi. ni haa nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi

english: Why do bees and small insects visit my farm flowers, and will they harm my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii krokomɛi yasaraa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Ni ani amɛbaaye midumɔ nii lɛ awui?

english: Bees and insects are beneficial pollinators rather than pests. As they move from flower to flower drinking nectar, they transfer pollen, which enables crops like cucumbers, peppers, and squashes to successfully develop into healthy fruits.
ga: Wuobii kɛ wuobii ji ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ moŋ fe ŋmeii. be mli ni amɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli koni amɛnu nu mli nu lɛ Amɛjieɔ pollen kɛyaa fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kukumba, shito, kɛ squash yeɔ omanye ni amɛfeɔ aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know which way to stick cassava stem cuttings into the soil when planting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni esa akɛ odu ŋmei ni afo lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Look closely at the small buds or nodes on the cassava stem cutting—they must point upwards toward the sky. Planting them upside down makes it difficult for shoots to sprout and reduces your yield.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii lɛ jogbaŋŋ. yɛ ŋmei nine lɛ nɔ Esa akɛ etsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ akwɛmɔ ni ehaa yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks and very small cobs.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa baa.

english: Why do people advise me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas in the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ duɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. This naturally enriches the soil, giving your maize plants extra nourishment without needing extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa o-corn tsei lɛ naa niyenii krokomɛi ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ tsofai krokomɛi awo mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when exposed to full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and short roots that dry out easily under strong sun. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects the young cocoa from direct heat and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden stakes in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tsei kakadaji ama shi lɛ? Yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves up to catch direct sunlight, which gives the plant energy to develop tubers underground. Staking also keeps leaves off the damp ground, protecting them from rot and fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Buu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ahe helai ahe.

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves is called mulching. It traps moisture in the ground during hot weather so you water less often, keeps the soil cool, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ. koni okɛ nu akashwie nɔ fioo Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: Is it better for me to water my crops in the hot afternoon or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafɔ midumɔ nii lɛ anɔ nu yɛ shwane mli loo leebi?

english: It is best to water early in the morning or late in the evening. Watering during the hot afternoon causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before the plant roots can absorb it.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔ lɛ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize are usually a sign that the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Applying a nitrogen-based fertilizer like Urea or well-decayed animal manure will turn the leaves green and restore healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni ebaaha amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes tiny caterpillars to eat holes in the middle leaves of my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-abele baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on the central growing leaves of young maize. They can be managed by applying safe insecticides or spraying diluted neem leaf extract early in the morning.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ateŋ lɛ. Abaanyɛ atsu enɛ he nii kɛtsɔ tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo kɛtsɔ neem tso lɛ mli nu ni ajie mli nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up and turning yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl to protect themselves from intense heat and drought, but curling mixed with yellowing often means tiny insects called whiteflies have spread a virus to the plant. Watering regularly and managing whiteflies helps keep the plants healthy.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ he. Shi bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔlɔ efutu mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ egbɛ hela lɛ eshwã tso lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa kɛ whitefly nɔkwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do buyers offer higher prices for beans that are clean and unmixed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ haa kɛha ŋmeii ni he tse ni akɛfutuuu mli lɛ?

english: International and local buyers pay a premium price for uniform, high-quality beans because they meet strict quality standards. When beans are clean and pure, buyers trust the product, whereas mixed or poor-quality batches lower overall market value and lose trust.
ga: Majimaji ateŋ kɛ maŋbii ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ nyɔmɔ ni nɔ kwɔ waa kɛha kɔfi yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ daa. Yɛ shishitoo mlai ni mli wa ni kɔɔ nibii ahe lɛ ahewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ ahe tse ni amɛhe tse lɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ baahe nɔ ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ amɛye. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nibii ni afee ni akɛfutuɔ nii loo nɔ ni ehiii lɛ baaha jarayeli mli jara fɛɛ aba shi, ni ekɛ hekɛnɔfɔɔ ni baa shi lɛ aba shi.

english: What happens to the price of my harvest if bad quality crops are mixed with good ones in the local market?
ga: Mɛni baaba minibii lɛ ajara nɔ kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehiii futu ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ?

english: When low-quality or adulterated crops are mixed into the supply, buyers lower their offer price across the entire area to protect themselves from loss, causing even good farmers to earn less for their produce.
ga: Beni akɛ tsei ni ehiii loo ni akɛ tsofa ewo mli lɛ futu nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ mli. Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ baashɛ amɛ jara ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ shi yɛ hei srɔtoi koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nibii ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ ahe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, okwaafoi kpakpai po anine shɛɛɛ nɔ ni amɛduɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it bad to mix different varieties of harvested beans together in the same bag?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaafutu ŋmeii srɔtoi ni akpa yɛ kotoku kome mli lɛ?

english: Different bean varieties dry at different rates and have distinct sizes and flavors. Mixing them creates an uneven product that is difficult to process, which reduces buyer interest and lowers the selling price.
ga: Beans henɔi srɔtoi gbɛ́ɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. Ni amɛdalɛ kɛ amɛhe ŋɔɔ yɛ srɔtoi. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ futu mli lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee ni ewa akɛ aaatsu he nii lɛ baa. Enɛ haa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ amiishɛɛ baa shi, ni ehaa jara ni akɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my stored beans lose their quality and color over time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-coffee ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛto lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛ amɛhe su baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ?

english: Beans lose quality during storage if they absorb dampness from the air or are exposed to heat. Proper drying and storing in airtight bags prevent moisture damage, mold, and discoloration.
ga: Nuts lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kɛji amɛjie ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli loo amɛwo la mli. Kɛji akɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛto kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ akafite, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ akafite.

english: Why is it risky to sell my beans when they are still slightly damp inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ ahɔ̃ɔmɔ ji oshara lɛ? Ani eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo lolo yɛ emli?

english: Damp beans trap moisture inside the sack, causing them to rot, heat up, and develop mold quickly. Exporters and buyers reject damp crops because they spoil entire shipments during transport.
ga: Beans ni mli efɔ lɛ baamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ, amɛdɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii baa oya. Mɛi ni kɛ nibii majeɔ maŋsɛɛ kɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kpooɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli efɔ ejaakɛ efiteɔ nibii fɛɛ ni akɛmajeɔ lɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa lɛ.

english: Why do insects like weevils destroy my harvested beans so fast if I don't treat them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii fiteɔ mi ŋmeii ni mikpaa lɛ oya kɛji mitsaaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Weevil insects lay tiny, invisible eggs on bean pods while they are still in the field. After harvest, these eggs hatch inside stored sacks, and the larvae eat the inside of the seeds unless the beans are thoroughly sun-dried or safely treated.
ga: Kpɔŋɔ lɛ woɔ wɔji bibii. Anaaa lɛ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. kpamɔ sɛɛ Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ fɔɔ yɛ kotokui ni akɛtoɔ mli lɛ amli. ni ŋmeii lɛ baaye dumɔwu lɛ mligbɛ. Ja agbi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ hulu mli loo atsu he nii yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ ni ehi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can experts tell where my crop was grown just by looking at the harvest?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋaalɔ ko ale he ni adu miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ yɛ yibiiwoo lɛ nɔ?

english: Crops develop specific characteristics based on local soil, rainfall, and climate. Expert buyers can identify a crop's origin by inspecting its bean size, shell texture, color, and moisture content.
ga: Tsei feɔ sui pɔtɛɛ ni damɔ shikpɔŋ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ maŋ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi anɔ. Mɛi ni heɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ ale he ni tso lɛ jɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ, ehewolo, su kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mlipɛimɔ nɔ.

english: How do I know when my bean pods are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-pea pods lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Bean pods show maturity when they turn dry and brittle, changing color from green to brown. If you shake a mature pod, you will hear the seeds rattling freely inside.
ga: Bean pods lɛ daa kɛji egbi ni egbɔjɔ. Kɛtsɔ su ni etsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli kɛyaa blɔfo mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji otsi pod ni eda kwraa lɛ Obaanyɛ onu dumɔwui lɛ ni miihoso yɛ mli lɛ he.

english: Why do my bean plants turn yellow during heavy rains instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli moŋ fe ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Excess water in the soil drowns the roots and starves them of air, making it hard for the plant to take up nitrogen. This lack of nutrients causes the leaves to turn yellow and slows growth.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ shishi ni ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ aba. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei akɛ amɛaaŋɔ nitrogen. Niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ ni bɛ lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdaraa blɛoo.

english: Why do my leguminous crops like beans help make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-legumes tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi-ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Bean plants have special tiny nodules on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. This naturally fertilizes the earth, leaving rich soil for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Bean tsei yɛ ŋmeii bibii krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ babaoo shwɛɔ kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Pale yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to grow green and strong. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn dark green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei, ŋmei, loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas makes the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants have small bumps on their roots that pull nitrogen out of the air and trap it in the dirt. When the cowpea plant dies, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil as free food for the next crop.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tsina tso lɛ gbo Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my small young cocoa shoots dry up and burn when there are no big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ daraaa lɛ? Mi nɔ lɛ gĩɔ ni eshãa kɛ́ tsei wuji komɛi bɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive and cannot handle direct afternoon sunlight. They need shade trees or plantain plants around them to block the intense heat and keep the surrounding air moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shwane mli lɛ gbɛ. Tsei loo plantains ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ he miihia amɛ. Bɔni afee ni akafee dɔlɛ ni fe nine ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle lɛ lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and twisting into tight balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni etsɔ bɔɔlu ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny invisible insects like mites or thrips hiding underneath the leaves and sucking out the juices. Spraying the leaves with neem oil or soap solution helps stop them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii kɛ baai lɛ shwiemɔ baa. ni anyɛɛɛ ana, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni teɔ shi yɛ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ nu lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo samla shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi amɛnaa.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge green leaves but very small, thin roots under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi shishifãi bibii waa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: If the soil has too much nitrogen or water, the cassava plant puts all its energy into making bushy leaves above ground instead of storing food in the tubers below ground.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen loo nu babaoo Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai akui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to keep clear space around my young yam mounds so often?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee he ko ni mabɔle he lɛ? Bei pii lɛ, okɛ sweet potato ato he.

english: Yam vines grow slowly at first and need full sunlight and space. If weeds grow over the mound, they steal the water and soil nutrients before the yam tuber can start growing big.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ daaa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni amɛbiɔ hulu kɛ he ko ni fa babaoo. Kɛji jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my plantain stalks keep falling over during windstorms even when they have fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ ahum ni tswaa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛwoɔ yibii momo moŋ?

english: Plantain roots do not grow deep into the soil. Tiny worms called nematodes often eat the roots underground, making the stem loose so heavy fruit and wind easily tip the plant over.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi waa aahu akɛ yibii lɛ feɔ tsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi mlɛo.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off without turning into tomato fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when there are no bees around to shake the pollen inside the flowers to make fruit set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii bɛ ni baajie ŋmeii ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are the fruit bunches on my oil palm trees dropping early before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-mu tsei lɛ anɔ yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: Oil palms drop early fruit when they do not get enough water during dry spells or when the soil lacks potassium, which is the nutrient responsible for filling out heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ baawo yibii oya kɛ́ amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli loo kɛ́ potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa aduawai ni tsii lɛ woɔ mli ekoŋŋ

english: Why does my swamp rice grow so much better when shallow water stays on the land continuously?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-marsh ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ be mli ni nu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Standing water smothers grass weeds that try to choke the rice, keeps the soil cool, and keeps nutrients dissolved so the rice roots can drink them up constantly.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ gbeɔ jwɛi jwɛi ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛfo ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu amɛ daa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is lacking key nutrients like nitrogen, often because heavy rains have washed the goodness deeper into the ground. Adding manure or the right fertilizer restores the plant's health and turns the leaves green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ onibii amli, bei pii lɛ ejaakɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ kpakpa lɛ kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my soil turn as hard as a brick during the dry season, and how can I fix it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tamɔ brikii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa?

english: Soil hardens when it lacks organic matter such as decayed leaves or compost. Adding organic material keeps the soil loose and spongy, helping crop roots penetrate deeply to reach moisture during dry spells.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ bɛ mli. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli tseɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmeii. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso shishifãi ni amɛboteɔ mli jogbaŋŋ koni amɛna nu yɛ hɔmɔ bei amli.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my seeds when the rainy season keeps changing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni tsakeɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli?

english: Avoid planting immediately after the very first rain, as the ground underneath is still dry and hot. Wait for two or three heavy, steady rains so the ground stays moist enough for seeds to germinate and survive.
ga: Tsi ohe kɛjɛ dumɔwui ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli egbi ni edɔ lolo. Mɛɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my cocoa tree leaves burn and drop off when the dry Harmattan wind starts blowing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-koko tsei lɛ shãa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ jeɔ shishi etswaa lɛ?

english: The dry Harmattan wind sucks moisture out of leaves faster than roots can drink from the dry ground. Planting shade trees around cocoa protects the crop by blocking harsh winds and keeping moisture in the air.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni aduɔ koni ekɛ hulutsoo aha yɛ Cocoa he lɛ buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni tsiɔ naa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli tseɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: What is eating small holes inside the middle leaves of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Mi ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli?

english: This damage is typically caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm that hide in the center of the plant. Catching them early and spraying recommended natural extracts like neem oil can protect your crop before severe damage occurs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ omɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni ajieɔ yi akɛ ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli, tamɔ neem fɔ lɛ afɔɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ebu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani nɔ ko ni yɔɔ hiɛdɔɔ aba.

english: Why are my tomato fruits getting black rotten spots at the bottom before they turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ dani etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: This is known as blossom-end rot, caused when plants cannot get enough calcium due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist and applying wood ash or lime helps the fruit grow healthy and clean.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa beni tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa ni okɛ tso sũ loo lime wo nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua aduawai lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhe atse.

english: If I plant my cassava closer together, will I harvest more tubers from my land?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe Ani manyɛ makpa ŋmei babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting too closely forces crops to fight for sunlight, water, and plant food, resulting in thin plants with very tiny tubers. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to produce large, healthy yields.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ atswa hulu la, nu, kɛ tso niyenii he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ bulb bibii waa baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Can I plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize on the same farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsina loo ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, planting legumes like beans alongside maize is beneficial because beans take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, which feeds the maize naturally and keeps your soil rich.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmãa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Why does removing grass and weeds make my crops grow so much faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya waa lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures all the food in the ground goes directly to helping your crops grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ekwɛɔ koni niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aya nɔ eye ebua onibii ni okwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are some of my cassava roots big and soft while others stay small and woody?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ekomɛi dara ni amɛhe yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni shishifãi komɛi ji bibii ni amɛji tsei lolo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need loose, well-drained soil to expand properly. Hard soil or cuttings taken from weak parent plants prevent tubers from growing large and fleshy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ŋmeii ni ajie kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso ni egbɔjɔ lɛ mli lɛ baatsi bulb lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ agbo ni efee loo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plant is lacking food, especially nitrogen, or is getting too much water around its roots. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn green and photosynthesize properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii bɛ o-corn tsei lɛ ahe. titri lɛ nitrogen loo nu babaoo yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛfeɔ fotosintɛsis jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the flowers dropping off my tomato plants without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ tomato tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the plants do not get a steady supply of water. High heat disrupts pollination, causing the plant to drop flowers to protect itself from stress.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ tsiɔ pollination naa. Ha tsei agbee shi koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ haomɔ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up like little cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from underneath the leaves, or by extreme heat and lack of water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni faaa yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli lɛ mli

english: Cassava roots rot in soggy ground because excessive standing water prevents the roots from getting air, causing them to drown and decay. Planting on raised ridges or mounds helps excess rainwater drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ. ni haa efoɔ nu mli ni egboɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why shouldn't I spread fertilizer on dry soil under the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ afɔseɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve so plant roots can drink it in. When put on dry soil in high heat, chemical fertilizers can burn the crop roots or evaporate into the air before the plant can use them.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tso shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu lɛ. Kɛji akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ miiwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni mli edɔ waa nɔ Enɛ baaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ashã loo amɛho kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tso lɛ anyɛ ekɛtsu nii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when there are no shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo be bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under full sun. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantain nearby creates a cool canopy that protects young cocoa from heat stress until they mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa ŋmɔlɔ ni buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa.

english: Why do crops grow better when I plant cassava and maize together in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei fee ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize grows fast and uses space near the surface while taking only a few months to harvest. Cassava grows slower and deeper, taking over the space after the maize is harvested, which lets you maximize land and rainfall.
ga: Abɛi daa oya ni eŋɔ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ, ni eheɔ nyɔji fioo pɛ dani akpaa. Cassava daa blɛoo ni eyaa shɔŋŋ. Ebaaye jɛmɛ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than my main crops after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mitso titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants that naturally absorb water and plant nutrients much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing food and sunlight from your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei amli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Ni oootsi ohe mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when their fruit bunches grow large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya beni eyibii lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems and thick stems that carry heavy weight at the top. When rain softens the ground and wind blows, top-heavy plants easily fall unless supported with strong wooden props.
ga: Dumɔwu lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ tso ni mli wa, ni tsii yɛ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa. Tsei ni amɛyitsei tsii lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya. ja tso ni wa fiɔ sɛɛ

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting shoots while stored in the yam barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ bɔi shweremɔ beni akɛtoɔ sweet potatoes ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that break their natural sleep cycle when exposed to warmth and high humidity. Keeping your yam barn well-ventilated, shaded, and cool helps slow down sprouting so tubers stay fresh longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji bulbs ni hiɛ ka ni gbalaa adebɔɔ mli wɔɔhe gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli kɛji akɛ akɛwo hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa mli. Kɛ́ oha o-sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa, eyɛ hulutsoo, ni eyɛ fɛ̃i lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow crooked and small instead of deep into the earth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers push deep into the ground searching for loose soil and moisture. If the soil is hard or compacted, the tuber cannot force its way down and will bend sideways, which is why building tall, soft mounds is essential for long, smooth yams.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛtao shikpɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa loo ebɔle ehe lɛ Yitso lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ shi ni ebaakoto kɛya afã. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni gɔŋ kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni aaafee lɛ he hiaa waa kɛha sweet potatoes kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ.

english: Are the small earthworms and insects living in my crop soil harmful to my cassava plants?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ mi-pot sũ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ awui?

english: No, most earthworms and soil insects are helpful. They break down dead leaves into rich organic nutrients and create tiny tunnels in the earth that help plant roots breathe and absorb water easily.
ga: Dabi, shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi babaoo he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ. Amɛgbalaa baai ni egboi lɛ amli amɛfeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa. ni amɛma gbɛ bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni haa tsei shishifãi nyɛɔ amɛmuɔ ni amɛmɔɔ nu mlɛo.

english: How can I get my sandy farmland to hold enough water for crops to survive dry days?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ ahi nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli?

english: Sandy soil lets water drain away too quickly. Mixing organic compost, dried leaves, or well-rotted animal manure into sandy soil helps it act like a sponge, holding onto water and nutrients so crop roots do not dry out.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ oya tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, baai ni egbi, loo kooloi ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo sũ ni mli edɔ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa sũ lɛ ni etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ spunji, ni ehiɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii. Tse shishifãi lɛ egbiɛɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ?

english: Maize is a heavy feeder that requires a lot of soil nutrients to grow strong green leaves. When leaves turn yellow, it means the plant has used up all the nitrogen in the soil and needs extra feeding through manure or fertilizer.
ga: Abɛi ji niyenii ni tsii ni biɔ niyenii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ebaa ni eŋɔli lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ efite nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ. ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he

english: Why do wild grasses grow so much faster on my farm field than the maize I actually planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe ŋmãa ni miduɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Wild grasses have aggressive root systems adapted to quickly drink up available water and soil food before crop roots can reach them, which is why clearing weeds early gives your planted crops a fair chance to grow.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni tsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛnu nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ. Enɛ baaha onibii ni odu lɛ aná hegbɛ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young oil palm trees drying up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young oil palms use a lot of water to build new fronds. During dry periods, the plant sacrifices its lower leaves to save moisture for its core, so covering the ground around the stem with mulch helps keep the roots damp.
ga: Palm tsei kɛ nu babaoo feɔ baai heei. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Tso lɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ shaa afɔle koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he yɛ shishijee he lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ wo tso lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do the roots of my pepper plants rot when water sits on my farm after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nu shwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Roots need air inside the soil to survive. When water sits trapped in muddy land for too long, air cannot enter, causing the roots to drown and making it easy for rot fungi in the water to attack the plant.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa shishifãi yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ nu hi muji lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ abote mli.ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli Nu mli fitemɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ tutuaa tsei oya.

english: Is it better to mix animal manure into the soil before planting or just drop it on top of the land later?
ga: Ani esa akɛ akɛ kooloi ashishifã afutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani adu loo esa akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni agbe naa lɛ?

english: Mixing rotted manure directly into the soil before planting allows crop roots to easily reach nutrients right as they sprout, whereas manure left on top of dry land loses its nutrient strength under the hot sun.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ dani adu lɛ, ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ náa niyenii kpakpai mlɛo beni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Nuŋtsɔ ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ baafite niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Why do I need to soak fresh cassava roots in water for a few days before processing them into flour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmei shishifãi heei awo nu mli gbii fioo komɛi dani mafee amɛ ashikishaŋ lɛ?

english: Fresh cassava naturally contains mild bitter toxins that are unsafe to consume in large amounts. Soaking and fermenting the roots breaks down these natural chemicals, making the food safe and soft for cooking.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, tsofai fɔji ni mli wa fioo ni bɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ayeɔ babaoo yɛ cassava hee mli. Kɛ́ akɛ shishifãi lɛ wo nu mli ni afee amɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, efiteɔ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai nɛɛ. Ehaa niyenii feɔ shweshweeshwe ni efeɔ blɛoo kɛha nihoomɔ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting quickly when stored in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya kɛ́ akɛto ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Harvested yams rot when they get wounded during digging or stay under direct hot sun. Allowing tubers to rest in cool, shaded air right after harvest hardens their skins and protects them from air rot while in storage.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ epila yɛ be mli ni akuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo akɛwo hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ ni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛhewolo lɛ mli awa ni ebaabu amɛhe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fiteɔ amɛhe lɛ he beni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: How do I properly separate plantain suckers from the main mother plant to plant them in a new field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ magbala plantain tsei lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli koni madu yɛ saatso hee nɔ?

english: You carefully dig around the young sucker attached to the mother plant, cut it cleanly at the base without damaging the main roots, and move it to its new spot so it can grow independently.
ga: Okɛ hiɛdɔɔ shwieɔ tso bibioo ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Kpãa shishigbɛ lɛ he ni okɛ shishifãi titrii lɛ akafiteee. ni okɛya he ko hee koni eha eda yɛ heyeli mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need to stay under shade in a nursery before I move them into the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ awo hulutsoo be mli yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani ajie amɛ kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young seedlings are delicate when growing near their nursery environment; keeping them under shade helps them build strength before facing the harsh sun and winds of the open field.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ waaa kɛji akwɛ amɛ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ he ni akwɛɔ tsei lɛ yɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ tee hulutsoo be shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ dani hulu ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ aba amɛnɔ.

english: How can I tell if a young shoot growing near my crop is a useful offshoot or a weed?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ ji ŋmeii loo jwɛi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ?

english: You can identify whether a shoot belongs to your crop by carefully looking at its leaf shape and stem structure, comparing its features directly to the mother plant.
ga: Obaanyɛ ole ŋmeii ni ji onibii lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ baa lɛ su kɛ tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ kwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ tso ni ji nyɛ lɛ sui ni akɛtoɔ he tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know if a cassava plant growing on my land is a high-yielding variety or a wild type?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ji tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo loo tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli?

english: Different cassava varieties show clear physical signs like leaf stem color, branching height, and root bark texture, which tell you if the plant belongs to a productive farm variety or a wild one.
ga: Cassava henɔi srɔtoi Tsɔɔmɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ tamɔ baa lɛ shishigbɛ su kɛ eniji lɛ ashishifãi. kɛ shishifã ŋmɔtɔ Enɛ baatsɔɔ bo kɛji tso lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni woɔ yibii loo eji koo mli tso henɔ.

english: How should I transport young crop seedlings to a distant farm so they do not die on the way?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ dumɔwui bibii aya ŋmɔ ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ mli? Koni amɛkagboi yɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Keep the seedling roots covered with moist soil or damp leaves during travel, shield them from hot sun and wind, and plant them immediately when you arrive at the farm.
ga: Ha dumɔwu lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ loo baai ni mli efɔ nɔ yɛ gbɛfaa lɛ mli. Abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he ni aduɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji ebashɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: Why do my young seedlings wilt right after I transport and plant them in new soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ gboɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ tee ni mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ hee nɔ lɛ?

english: Transporting plants causes shock because their roots get disturbed and temporarily lose the ability to take up water until they settle into the new ground.
ga: Tsei ni tsiɔ amɛhe lɛ kɛ shoofeemɔ baa ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ haoɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ nu yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛyashi amɛbaagbee shikpɔŋ hee nɔ.

english: What should I do if my cocoa pods develop dark spreading spots that threaten the whole harvest?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli egbɛ eshwã ŋmɔji diji ni woɔ ŋmaakpamɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ he gbeyei lɛ?

english: This is a serious fungal disease like black pod; you must quickly remove the infected pods and apply the recommended crop treatment to protect the remaining healthy pods.
