ga: Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni naa wa tamɔ black pods. Esa akɛ ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya. ni okɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii lɛ atsu nii ni okɛbu ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow even though there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, which requires applying fertilizer or organic manure to restore health.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ biɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli atsu nii koni akɛha hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Can planting different types of crops next to each other stop diseases from spreading?
ga: Tsei srɔtoi ni aduɔ Ani shihilɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ baanyɛ akpa helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa?

english: Yes, mixing different crops creates natural barriers that prevent plant-specific diseases from moving easily from one crop to another across your farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii baa koni ekɛtsi tsei pɔtɛɛ ahe helai anaa koni amɛkajɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome mli kɛya ekroko mli oya yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How do I safely apply medicine to sick crops without harming nearby healthy plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ tsofa awo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ shweshweeshwe ni miyeee tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ awui?

english: Apply the treatment directly to the affected plants during calm weather in the early morning or late afternoon so spray drift does not blow onto healthy crops.
ga: Okɛ tsofa lɛ awo tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli. Enɛ ji koni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that scorch easily in intense sunlight and harsh harmattan winds. Planting shade trees or plantains alongside them creates a cooler microclimate that retains soil moisture and protects the delicate leaves.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo plantains ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ Ehaa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo ko ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning pale yellow starting from the tips of the bottom leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the bottom of the plant usually mean your soil is low on nitrogen. Maize needs nitrogen to grow green and strong, so adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help the leaves regain their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava roots are ready to harvest without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: When cassava is mature, the leaves lower on the stem naturally turn yellow and drop off, leaving mostly bare stems. You can also gently clear away soil around the base of one stem to check if the roots have swollen into thick tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Baai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Tso lɛ pɛ ji nɔ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ mli babaoo. Obaanyɛ ojie sũ ni bɔle tso kome shishi lɛ hu blɛoo koni okwɛ kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli edɔ ni efuu.

english: Why are small holes appearing on my tomatoes and causing them to rot before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ mli bu bibii lɛ? Ni ni oooha tomatoi lɛ agbo dani amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Insects like caterpillars or fruit borers lay eggs on the flowers or young fruits, and the larvae bore inside to feed. Removing damaged fruits immediately and spraying natural neem leaf extracts can help keep these pests away.
ga: Akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo aduawai ahe ŋmeii woɔ fɔfɔi loo aduawai bibii anɔ. ni ŋmeii lɛ baabote mli koni amɛyatao niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie aduawai ni efite lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni akɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni abu he kɛjɛ nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ ahe.

english: Why should I cut off the extra shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ plantain tsei titrii lɛ.

english: Multiple extra shoots compete with the main plantain stem for water, light, and soil nutrients. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main stem gets enough energy to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei babaoo ni fata he Tso lɛ kɛ plantain tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee tso agbo ni tsii.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves toward sunlight to generate energy for root growth. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground to prevent leaf diseases and encourages larger tubers to grow underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbala amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛya hulu la lɛ he koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha shishifãi lɛ adalɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛtsi foliar hela naa ni ewo bulbs wuji hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants dropping off without making any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni mifeee pepper ko lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the soil gets too dry between waterings. Maintaining consistent moisture in the soil around the roots during flowering helps the blossoms stay on and turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ teŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ Shishifãi ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa yɛ fɔfɔii ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔi.

english: When maize plants are crowded, their roots fight for nutrients and water while their leaves block sun from each other. This causes the stems to grow thin and weak, resulting in very small cobs or no cobs at all.
ga: Beni ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe Ehaa tso lɛ shishi feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii waa loo eko kwraa baaa.

english: Why do my garden vegetable leaves wilt in the afternoon heat even when the soil is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibɔɔ mli aduawai lɛ miiho yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, vegetable leaves lose water to the air faster than the roots can pull it up from the ground. This temporary wilting is a natural defense to conserve moisture, and the leaves usually stand back up by morning.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwieɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli nɛɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Ni bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ teɔ shi ekoŋŋ leebi.

english: Why do my groundnut plants produce flowers above the ground if the nuts grow under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants bloom above ground so insects can pollinate the flowers. Once pollinated, the flower stems turn into long 'pegs' that grow downward, push into the soil, and develop into groundnut pods beneath the ground.
ga: Peanut tsei fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni kooloi anyɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi. Kɛji akɛ ashɛre pollination lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifã lɛ bafeɔ ‘peg’ kakadaŋŋ ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛyaa shi, ni ekɛ ehe woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni etsɔɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying before the corn matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani abele lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow green and strong. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer around the base of the crop helps feed the plant and restore its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ haa niyenii ni ehaa tso lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ewaa ekoŋŋ.

english: How does adding my chicken or goat manure to the soil help my crop field grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ tsina loo too ŋmei fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua miŋmɔ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Animal manure acts as a natural food for the soil. It adds vital nutrients, improves the soil's ability to hold water during hot dry spells, and feeds beneficial living organisms in the earth so your crops grow stronger.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa afata he Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli. ni oha bɔɔ nii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ je lɛŋ lɛ niyenii koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ waa.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or beans together with my maize helps the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋma lɛ du ŋmei loo ŋmei lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa mi-ŋmei lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans have special roots that trap natural plant food from the air and put it into the soil. When planted near maize, they share this free food, helping the maize stay green without needing as much bought fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei aniyenii amli kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmãa Amɛjaraa niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko nɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe ŋmãa babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into tight shapes and refusing to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ekpoo akɛ ebaada lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insect pests like whiteflies or thrips sucking the juice out of the leaves, or transmitting viruses. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves open so the plant can catch sunlight and make fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu loo helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baaha baai lɛ agbele koni tso lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la ni ewo yibii.

english: Why are there small holes appearing in the tender center leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ani ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai bibii lɛ anɔ?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by caterpillars, such as the Fall Armyworm, eating the new shoots. Checking your fields early and using appropriate neem oil sprays or targeted insecticides can stop them before they destroy the yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ ŋmeii heei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni baa ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli mra. Ni kɛ akɛ neem fɔ ni sa loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekpa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my vegetable crops stay small and weak if I do not clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi-aduawai lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa kɛji mijieee amɛ mra lɛ?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors—they steal water, sunlight, and plant food from the soil that your vegetables need. Clearing them early ensures all the goodness in your land goes straight to your crops.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ. Amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni he hiaa o-vegetables lɛ nɔ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kpakpai fɛɛ aya oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when heavy rains fall for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water collects and stands on the farm without draining away, it drowns the roots and brings fungal diseases that turn the tubers soft and rotten. Planting on raised ridges or mounds helps excess water flow away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu bua ehe naa ni edamɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Nu baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ shishi ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ afee blɛoo ni amɛgboi aba. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ loo gɔŋ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the stems without turning into tomato fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants often drop their blossoms when daytime heat gets too extreme or when the soil gets too dry. When the plant feels stressed by weather, it drops flowers to save its strength until conditions improve.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Kɛ tsei nu he akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ miigba amɛnaa lɛ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ehiɛ ehewalɛ mli kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do young plantain suckers need to be planted right beside my new cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui bibii yɛ mi-kookoo tso hee lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Fast-growing plantains produce big leaves that create a soft canopy of shade, protecting the delicate cocoa trees from direct sun and keeping the ground cool while they are young.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo baa blɛoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ

english: Why do my crops yield less food when I plant too many seeds close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naaa niyenii babaoo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown plants end up fighting each other for soil food, water, and space to spread their roots. Giving each plant proper space allows it to grow big leaves and produce maximum fruit.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Kɛji amɛto amɛhe shi pɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ he ko ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amɛshwã he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni ekwɛ baai wuji ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do small shoots grow around the base of my plantain tree, and should I leave all of them there?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ daraaa lɛ? Koni eda yɛ mi plantain shishitoo lɛ he Ni ani esa akɛ mashi ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ yɛ jɛmɛ?

english: Those small shoots around the main stem are called suckers (often locally referred to as 'children'). Leaving all of them causes them to compete with the main plant for nutrients and water, resulting in small plantain bunches. You should prune most of them and leave only one or two strong ones to replace the main plant after harvest.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei bibii ni bɔle tso titri lɛ he lɛ akɛ suckers. (Bei pii lɛ, atsɛɔ amɛ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli akɛ ‘gbekɛbii’.) Kɛ́ ashi amɛ ni amɛhiɛɛɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu ni jɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Enɛ haa plantains bibii shwieɔ shi. Esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ ateŋ babaoo ni oshi tso kome loo enyɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛye tso titri lɛ najiaŋ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How do I know if my pineapple plant is producing 'slips' or 'suckers', and which one is better to plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-pineapple tso lɛ yɛ ‘ŋmeii’ loo ‘ŋmeii’ ni nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu?

english: Suckers grow from the base of the plant near the ground, while slips grow right at the base of the fruit stem. Both can be used for planting, but suckers usually grow faster and produce pineapples earlier than slips.
ga: Tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ. yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ aduawai lɛ shishigbɛ. Abaanyɛ akɛtsu nii ni akɛkwɛ enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ. Shi ŋmeii lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear away all the big trees in my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot withstand direct, harsh sun because their leaves burn easily and the soil dries out quickly. Planting nurse crops like plantains or leaving some large trees provides essential shade and moisture while the cocoa plants are young.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hu gbɛ́ɔ oya. Tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ tamɔ plantains loo tsei wuji ni ashiɔ amɛma shi lɛ baaha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ dara lolo lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants roll up into tight tubes during hot dry afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tsɔnei ni mli wa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso ni nu egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up as a self-defense mechanism to reduce surface area exposed to the sun, which prevents excessive water loss through evaporation during the heat of the day.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ gbɛ ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni mli edɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why are my cassava roots remaining small even though the leaves and stem look very big and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ ji bibii lolo lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ baai kɛ tsei lɛ agbo ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ?

english: When soil contains too much nitrogen (such as from excess fresh manure), cassava puts most of its energy into growing lush leaves and stems above ground instead of expanding its underground tubers. Loose, well-drained soil with balanced nutrients encourages good tuber growth.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ (akɛ nɔkwɛmɔ nɔ lɛ, kɛjɛ ŋmeii heei ni fa fe nine mli lɛ), ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi Loose, shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni niyenii ni ja yɔɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same farm with our maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni wɔduɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special nodules on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. This naturally enriches the soil, supplying free nutrients to neighboring crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Amɛhaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets extremely hot, when there is irregular watering, or when the soil lacks key nutrients like phosphorus. Consistent watering and proper nutrient management help the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Kɛji nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ daa loo kɛji akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa daa kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their leaves and turn yellow after heavy rains cover the farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwie shi ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nugbɔ ni nɛ waa ha ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants hate standing water. Waterlogged soil suffocates the roots by cutting off oxygen, leading to root rot. Without healthy roots, the plant cannot take up nutrients, causing leaves to turn yellow and fall.
ga: Pepper tsei nyɛɔ nu ni damɔ shi. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Kɛji shishifãi ni wa bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ aná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: What are yam minisetts, and why do we cut seed yams into small pieces before planting?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmɔtɔ bibioo? Ni mɛni hewɔ wɔfoɔ sweet potato bibii bibii dani wɔduɔ lɛ?

english: Yam minisetts are small, healthy cut pieces of a seed yam containing skin and sprouting 'eyes'. Cutting yams into minisetts allows farmers to multiply their planting material so they can plant a larger field using fewer whole yams.
ga: Mini sweet potatoes ji sweet potato dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ hewolo kɛ 'buds' ni miida. Sweet potatoes ni afoɔ awoɔ mini sets mli lɛ haa okwaafoi nyɛɔ amɛgbɛɔ nibii ni amɛduɔ lɛ amɛshwãa. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ aduɔ ŋmɔji wuji ni akɛ sweet potatoes muu fioo pɛ tsuɔ nii.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my oil palm trees dry up and hang down as the tree gets taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi beni tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: As oil palms grow, the older lower leaves naturally age, turn brown, and stop contributing energy to the tree. Regularly pruning these dead fronds keeps the tree healthy and makes harvesting fruit bunches easier.
ga: Kɛji oil palm lɛ da lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. ni ekpa hewalɛ ni ekɛhaa tsei Nɛkɛ baai ni egboi nɛɛ ni afoɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa aduawai akui lɛ akpamɔ feɔ mlɛo.

english: Why are there so many ants crawling on my crop trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii babaoo ni shwieɔ mi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Ants are usually drawn to sweet sap or smaller sap-sucking insects like aphids living on your trees. While some ants are harmless, others can shelter destructive pests or weaken your trees by building large nests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ wuo loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ aphids, ni hiɔ otsei lɛ anɔ lɛ gbalaa amɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmeii komɛi yeee mɔ awui moŋ, shi ŋmeii komɛi baanyɛ abu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni miifite loo miigbɔjɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni amɛmaa lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know if ants on my farm are actually destroying my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miifite miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: If you notice ants burrowing into stems, stripping leaves, or protecting smaller bugs that turn leaves yellow, they are actively harming your crops and need to be controlled.
ga: Kɛji ona akɛ ŋmeii miifolɔ tsei lɛ amli, amɛmiikpa baai, loo amɛmiibu kooloi bibii ahe. ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiiye onibii awui ni ehe miihia ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: What causes heavy branches on my trees to break and fall on their own?
ga: Mɛni ha tsei niji ni tsii ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ kumɔ ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛgbee shi lɛ?

english: Branches often break because of strong winds, excessive weight from leaves and rain, rot from high humidity, or internal damage caused by boring insects weakening the wood structure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa hewɔ ni tsei niji fãa lɛ. Baai lɛ kɛ nugbɔ lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Rot ni jɛɔ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo mli loo mligbɛ fitemɔ ni kooloi bibii ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli kɛbaa lɛ haa tso lɛ mli tsɔne lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: What should I do with a big branch that breaks and falls in the middle of my farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji tso nine agbo ko gbá yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: You should clear the fallen branch away from your growing area immediately. Rotting branches attract termites, fungal diseases, and destructive pests that can easily spread to healthy crops nearby.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie tsei niji ni egbee shi yɛ he ni okwɛɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Niji ni egboi lɛ gbalaa ŋmeii, ŋmeii helai, kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni fiteɔ nii. ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli oya.

english: When is the right time to cut off a damaged or infested branch from a tree?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ afolɔ tso niji ni efite loo niji ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ewo mli lɛ?

english: Cut off a damaged branch as soon as you see it splitting or showing signs of heavy insect infestation. Cutting it cleanly prevents disease and rot from spreading into the main trunk of the tree.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni efite lɛ pɛ kɛji ona niji ni ekumɔ loo okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii ebɔle amɛhe waa. Tso lɛ ni afoɔ ni he tse lɛ haaa hela kɛ ŋmɔtɔ akagbɛ ashwã tso lɛ shishigbɛ titri lɛ mli.

english: How can I stop tree branches from snapping off easily during bad weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi tsei niji anaa koni amɛkakumɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be mli?

english: Regularly trim weak, overcrowded, or top-heavy branches. Proper pruning reduces wind resistance against the tree and keeps its structure balanced and strong.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji bibii kɛ tsei niji ni egbɔjɔ tsɔ lɛ. loo tsei niji ni tsii yɛ nɔ daa lɛ Tso lɛ niji ni afolɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ tso lɛ naa lɛ baa shi. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa bɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ koni ehi jogbaŋŋ ni ewa.

english: Should I cut down a rubber tree if pests start attacking it?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo mi rɔba tso lɛ mli kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ bɔi tutuamɔ?

english: You only need to cut it down if the infestation is severe and threatens to spread to your neighboring healthy trees. If caught early, you can prune the affected parts or treat the tree instead.
ga: Ehe baahia ni ofo lɛ kɛji akɛ hela lɛ mli wa waa ni ewoɔ ehe gbeyei akɛ ebaagbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ amɔ lɛ oya Obaanyɛ ofolɔ hei ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ loo otsa tso lɛ moŋ.

english: Why do pests seem to gather and multiply right in the middle of my crop field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa ni amɛfɔɔ yɛ miŋmɔji lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: The middle of a farm often has more shade, higher moisture, and abundant food. This protected environment creates ideal conditions for insect colonies to settle and grow quickly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be babaoo. Fɛ̃i babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. ni niyenii babaoo yɛ Shihilɛ ni abuɔ he nɛɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa baa koni kooloi akui lɛ ahi shi ni amɛdara oya.

english: What signs show that pests on one tree are starting to spread to the rest of my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ tso kome nɔ lɛ miije shishi egbɛ eshwa miŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ mli?

english: Look out for insects crawling onto neighboring branches, widespread leaf yellowing, or pests migrating directly toward your main food crops in search of new feed.
ga: Taomɔ kooloi bibii ni miiho yɛ tsei niji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ahe. Baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni ji ŋmɔŋ loo kooloi ni fãa kɛyaa oniyenii ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛyatao niyenii hee.

english: Why is it important to clear dead wood and debris from around my healthy crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie tsei ni egboi kɛ sũ ni efite kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Clearing dead wood removes potential breeding sites for dangerous pests like ants and wood-borers, keeping your soil healthy and protecting nearby crops from disease.
ga: Tsoi ni egboi ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ hei ni kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsei ni shwieɔ tsei lɛ fɔɔ yɛ lɛ. Ehaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ, ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ahe.

english: How many stages of planting does a seed yam go through before it reaches us farmers?
ga: Nibii enyiɛ mli esa akɛ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ atsɔ mli dani amɛshɛ okwaafoi lɛ ahe?

english: Seed yams are usually multiplied through three distinct stages at the seed center. This multi-step process makes sure the small starter materials grow into strong, disease-free seed yams ready for field planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afeɔ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ babaoo yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi etɛ nɔ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ. Nɛkɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii babaoo nɛɛ haa shishijee nibii bibii lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni hela bɛ mli ni asaa he kɛha dumɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: Why can't I plant the tiny yams from the initial nursery stage directly on my commercial farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ makwɛ ŋmeii bibii? Kɛjɛ gbekɛbii askul lɛ mli kɛjɛ mi jarayeli ŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: The tubers produced in the very first stage are small starter seeds meant only for further multiplication. They need to go through additional growing stages to reach the proper size and strength for farm production.
ga: Bulbs ni ajieɔ lɛ shishijee lɛ ji dumɔwui bibii ni jeɔ shishi kɛha shweremɔ kroko pɛ. Ehe miihia ni amɛtsɔ dalɛ mli nibii krokomɛi amli koni amɛshɛ dalɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni sa kɛha nibii ni afeɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ he.

english: What happens during the first stage of seed yam multiplication?
ga: Mɛni baaba yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ fã ni ji ŋmeii ayibɔ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ mli?

english: The first stage acts as the starting point where clean plant material is grown to produce the initial generation of small, healthy seed tubers.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ fã lɛ ji shishijee he kɛha tsei ni he tse ni akwɛɔ koni amɛwo dumɔwui ayitsei bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ shishijee mli.

english: How long does it take for seed yams to complete all their production stages?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ gbeɔ nifeemɔ lɛ fɛɛ naa?

english: Because seed yams move through three progressive stages of growth and harvest, the entire multiplication process typically takes about two to three seasons before final seeds are given to farmers.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ tsɔɔ dalɛ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ mli fãi etɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbɛɔ ashwãa lɛ fɛɛ heɔ aaafee bei enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ dani akɛ naagbee dumɔwui lɛ haa okwaafoi.

english: Why does the original mother yam tuber rot away after a new yam starts growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato ŋmeii momoi lɛ fiteɔ beni eheei je shishi amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: The mother tuber acts like a lunchbox for the young plant, transferring all its stored energy into the growing stem until it is empty and naturally replaced by the new tuber.
ga: Tuber nyɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ shwane niyenii adeka kɛhaa tso bibioo lɛ. Kɛtsɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ato lɛ ni akɛyaa tso ni miida lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛyashi ebaatsɔ efolo ni akɛ yitso hee baaye najiaŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What happens to the old seed piece once the new generation of yam tubers form?
ga: Mɛni baa dumɔwui momo lɛ anɔ beni sweet potato tubers yinɔ hee ko ba lɛ?

english: The old seed piece finishes its job once its nutrients are fully used up by the new plant, making way for the new tuber to take over and grow.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ amli fãi momo lɛ gbeɔ amɛnitsumɔ lɛ naa beni tso hee lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ. Koni agbele gbɛ aha yitsei heei ni amɛye nɔ ni amɛdara.

english: Why do seed producers cycle seed tubers through different generations before giving them out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ahe nitsulɔi lɛ tsakeɔ dumɔwui ayitsei lɛ kɛtsɔɔ yinɔi srɔtoi anɔ lɛ? dani aja lɛ

english: Replacing tubers from one stage to the next allows seed producers to multiply a small amount of clean material into thousands of healthy seed yams for distribution.
ga: Tubers ni atsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ fã kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli lɛ haa mɛi ni feɔ dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɔ amɛfeɔ nibii bibii ni he tse lɛ babaoo ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akpei abɔ ni akɛhɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why should I wait to get final-stage seed yams instead of planting whatever yams I buy from the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ koni maná naagbee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni madu ŋmɔtɔ ni mihe yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Market yams may carry hidden rot or diseases, while final-stage seed yams from specialized producers have been carefully multiplied through clean stages to ensure high yields.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, atsɔɔ gbɛ ni he tse nɔ atsɔɔ sweet potatoes ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni jɛɔ sweet potatoes ni yɔɔ sɛɛ mli lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ koni anyɛ ana yibii babaoo.

english: How do I know if the seed yams given to me are ready for planting in my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ sweet potato dumɔwui ni akɛha mi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The seed yams handed out to farmers come from the final stage of multiplication, meaning they are healthy, medium-sized tubers that have broken dormancy and are ready to sprout.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui ni ajaa ahaa okwaafoi lɛ jɛɔ naagbee fã ni ji shweremɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni dalɛ ji teŋgbɛ. Be ni akɛwɔɔ lɛ efo mli ni efee klalo akɛ ebaakwɛ̃.

english: Will the seed yams I get from the extension office yield better than my old saved seed?
ga: Ani sweet potato dumɔwui ni minine shɛɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ extension office lɛ baawo yibii kpakpai fe dumɔwui momo ni ato lɛ?

english: Yes, because the extension seed yams have gone through clean, controlled multiplication stages that clear out diseases that accumulate in old, reused farm seed.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ agbɛɔ sweet potatoes ni woɔ dumɔwui lɛ ashwaa kɛtsɔɔ gbɛ ni he tse ni akudɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ helai ni buaa amɛhe naa yɛ dumɔwui momoi ni akɛtsuɔ nii ekoŋŋ lɛ amli lɛ kɛyaa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Fast-growing crops like plantains provide big leaves that act as natural shade umbrellas, protecting cocoa seedlings while keeping the soil moist during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains lɛ woɔ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ebuɔ kookoo dumɔwui ahe yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant is missing essential nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or the roots are sitting in waterlogged ground. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps leaves regain their green color and produce good yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. loo shishifãi ni ta shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Is it helpful to plant groundnuts and cassava together on the same field?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ aaadu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting groundnuts alongside cassava is very beneficial. Groundnuts fix natural nitrogen from the air into the soil, which feeds the soil and helps the surrounding cassava plants grow bigger tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmei fataa ŋmei he lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ŋmeii saa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmei tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni amɛnáa yitso ni da

english: What causes small caterpillars to chew holes in the center leaves of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ bu yɛ mi-ŋmei tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, an invasive pest that hides in the whorl of corn plants. Spraying early with recommended botanical remedies like neem leaf extract or approved insecticides keeps them from destroying your entire harvest.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni baa mɔ nɔ ni ekɛ ehe ewoɔ ŋmãa tsei amli. Tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra tamɔ neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ. Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite onibii fɛɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds as soon as the very first rain falls in April?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ yɛ April mli pɛ?

english: The very first rain is often followed by a dry spell that can scorch seeds planted in hot soil. Waiting until the rainy season fully settles ensures constant soil moisture for seeds to germinate safely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baaho lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ aya hiɛ bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why should I cut off healthy-looking branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ cacao tso ni eda lɛ niji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning thick branches opens up the tree canopy to let in sunlight and airflow. Sunlight helps cocoa trees flower better, while good airflow prevents damp conditions that cause black pod disease.
ga: Niji ni mli tse ni afolɔ Enɛ baagbele tso lɛ shishigbɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ naa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes on the exact same spot where I just harvested peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-tomato lɛ yɛ he ni mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwie shi kɛkɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Tomatoes and peppers belong to the same plant family and attract identical diseases and soil pests. Rotating to a different crop family like beans or corn breaks the disease cycle and leaves the soil healthier.
ga: Tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tsei akuu kome mli ni amɛgbalaa helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ. Ni aaatsake kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii aweku kroko nɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Efoɔ helai ni baa lɛ amli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Staking lifts yam vines off the ground so their leaves can catch direct sunlight. Leaves exposed to sunshine generate more energy, which translates into larger and heavier yam tubers underground.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni eshishifãi lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Baai ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ haa hewalɛ babaoo baa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ shishi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ dara ni amɛtsii.

english: How do I know when my cassava crop is fully ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the main stem begins to crack as the tubers swell.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni ŋmei lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Should I put fertilizer on my crops right before a heavy rain comes?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli dani nugbɔ anɛ waa?

english: No, applying fertilizer right before a heavy rain will cause the water to wash the nutrients off the farm into streams. Apply fertilizer when the soil is damp but not during continuous downpours.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛyaa faai amli. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi kaaŋmɛ gbɛ ni nugbɔ nɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field without any shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need protection from harsh, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside them provides necessary shade and keeps the soil moist so the young cocoa can establish strong roots.
ga: Esa akɛ abu kookoo dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ he. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ Emasɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná ŋmɔlɔ ni he hiaa, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Bɔni afee ni kookoo bibioo lɛ anyɛ afee shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: How do I choose the best plantain suckers from my farm to start a new field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Look for maiden suckers or sword suckers, which have narrow, blade-like leaves and thick bases. These grow faster, produce bigger bunches, and are healthier than broad-leafed water suckers.
ga: Taomɔ ŋmeii loo klante ŋmeii. Eyɛ baai bibii ni tamɔ ŋmei kɛ shishi ni mli tse. Nibii nɛɛ daa oya. Baje kpo yɛ tso ni da fe no mli. ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ fe tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni nuɔ nu lɛ

english: How far apart should I plant my plantain suckers to get a good yield?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-banana ŋmɔji lɛ kɛjɛ he ko ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ tɛŋŋ koni maná yibiiwoo kpakpa?

english: Plantain suckers should usually be spaced about 3 meters (10 feet) apart. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough sunlight, water, and nutrients without competing with neighboring plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, esa akɛ plantain tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ afee mitai 3 (naji 10). Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeee akaŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my plantain trees turning yellow and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi plantain lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves often indicate a lack of nutrients like nitrogen or potassium in the soil, or inadequate water during dry spells. Adding well-rotted animal manure or compost around the base helps restore essential nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium bɛ sũ lɛ mli. aloo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Koolooi ashishifã loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite lɛ ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni aku sɛɛ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do some farmers cover the soil around plantain stems with dry leaves and grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛ plantain tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves is called mulching. It holds moisture in the ground during dry weather, keeps weeds from growing, and slowly decays into rich organic fertilizer for the plant.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo kɛha tsei.

english: How do I know if my land is suitable for planting plantains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha plantains ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Plantains thrive in deep, dark soil that holds moisture well but drains excess water easily. Land that stays flooded or waterlogged for days after rain is not suitable because it rots the plant's roots.
ga: Amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli edɔ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi ewaaa akɛ abaajie nu ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛjɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ loo nu ehi shi gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ esaaa ejaakɛ ebaaha tsei ashishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: Can I plant cassava together with plantain on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmei kɛ plantains yɛ he kome?

english: Yes, intercropping cassava and plantain works well, but you must space them carefully. Cassava grows quickly and can shade out young plantain suckers if they are planted too close together.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmei kɛ plantain yɛ he kome lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ. Shi esa akɛ okɛ ohe akabɔ he jogbaŋŋ. Yucca daa oya ni ebaanyɛ eha ŋmeii bibii ahe kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my crops, and how does clearing them help?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that quickly steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. Removing weeds regularly leaves all those vital resources for your crops, allowing them to grow faster and yield more.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ baaha nakai nibii ni he hiaa lɛ aye ohe kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: What causes small holes near the base of my plantain stem that make the plant fall over easily?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Ebɛŋkɛ plantains ni haa tso lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya lɛ ashishi.

english: Small holes near the ground are usually caused by plantain stem borers or root nematodes. These pests eat through the stem and roots, weakening the plant so strong winds can easily knock it down.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, buji bibii ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni plantain tso lɛ shishifãi loo shishifãi ni ji nematodes lɛ kɛbaa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni egbɔjɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ akumɔ lɛ shi mlɛo.

english: How can I tell when my plantain bunch is ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni plantains lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: A plantain bunch is mature and ready for harvest when the individual fruits look full and rounded, and the sharp ridges along their sides begin to smooth out, even while the skin is still green.
ga: Plantain tsei akui lɛ edara kwraa ni amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko tamɔ nɔ ni eyi obɔ ni eyɛ kokroo lɛ. ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ afãi lɛ amli lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛji akɛ hewolo lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo po.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, shielding the cocoa seedlings from direct sun and keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Buu kookoo dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually indicate a nitrogen deficiency. The plant moves nitrogen from older lower leaves to feed newer top leaves, showing it needs fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛyaha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii. ni tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni awo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like aphids, thrips, or mites, which damage the leaves and can also spread leaf-curl viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, thrips, loo mites, ni fiteɔ baai lɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant suffers heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients, which prevents the flowers from pollinating and setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛkawo yibii.

english: Why do my green cocoa pods turn black and rot while still on the branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives during wet, humid weather and spreads easily through rainwater splashes and unpruned shade.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni akpɛko nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava root rot happens when soil stays waterlogged for too long or when fungal pathogens in wet, poorly drained soil attack the storage roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fitemɔ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ehi shi yɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. aloo kɛ́ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa shishifãi ni ato lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up completely before the tubers are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ miiho kwraa dani bulb lɛ miida kwraa lɛ?

english: Early vine drying can be caused by yam anthracnose disease or root damage from nematodes, which stop the plant from moving water and nutrients from the soil to the leaves.
ga: Nɔ ni baanyɛ aha wain tso lɛ agbi mra ji sweet potato anthracnose loo shishifãi ni nematodes fiteɔ lɛ. Enɛ tsĩɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekajie nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛya baai lɛ amli.

english: Why should I wait until after it rains before putting fertilizer on my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ omɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ dani okɛ ŋmãa awo ŋmãa mli?

english: Fertilizer requires soil moisture to dissolve properly so roots can absorb it. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can scorch and burn crop roots.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei shishifãi lɛ ashã ni amɛshã.

english: Why do my crops yield less when I plant the seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Planting too closely forces crops to compete with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak plants with smaller yields.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: How does covering the soil with dry grass help my vegetable crops grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mulching yeɔ ebuaa mi aduawai lɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Mulching with dry grass prevents soil moisture from evaporating in the heat, keeps the ground cool, and suppresses weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekaho yɛ latsaa be mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under the strong sun. Plantain trees grow very fast and produce large leaves that provide essential shade and retain soil moisture for the cocoa trees during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛhaa kookoo tso lɛ yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves at the base of your maize usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen. Nitrogen helps plants stay green and grow strong leaves; without enough of it, the plant moves nutrients to its newest leaves, causing the older lower leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛbaa lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ eshɛɛɛ Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛyaa baai heei lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, which you can tell when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and the ground around the base of the stem begins to crack as the tubers expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ole be mli ni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. kɛ hei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni eyitso lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants before any tomatoes grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ tomato tsei anɔ dani tomato lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers usually drop off when temperatures get too high, when the soil receives irregular amounts of water, or when the plant lacks sufficient nutrients like phosphorus to support fruit growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nine shɛɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa, tamɔ fɔsfɔs, ni baaye abua aduawai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds early when my crops are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ? Be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crop seedlings and steal critical water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, which can permanently stunt your crops before they get the chance to establish strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei amli dumɔwui ni amɛjuɔ nu ni he hiaa, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Enɛ baanyɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee shoo kɛya naanɔ dani ená hegbɛ ni ekɛ shishifãi ni wa aba.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that capture nitrogen gas from the air and release it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that feeds your maize crop naturally.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Covering the ground with dry organic material, called mulching, blocks the sun from drying out the dirt, keeps the plant roots cool, and prevents weeds from sprouting.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsĩ hulu lɛ naa ni ebaatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni etsĩ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃

english: Why do I need to use wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso tso he hiaa mi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch maximum sunlight for leaf food production, which prevents soil-borne fungal diseases and allows the tubers underground to swell much larger.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo kɛha foliar niyenii feemɔ. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ anaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ shishi tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: What is causing the leaves on my pepper plants to curl up and shrink?
ga: Mɛni miiha baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites that feed on plant sap, or by a virus carried from plant to plant by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛyaa tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crops too close together during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ aduɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli lɛ?

english: Planting too closely prevents air from circulating between crops, creating a wet environment that encourages fungal leaf diseases to spread rapidly throughout your entire farm.
ga: Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ewo fɔ ni woɔ fungal leaf helai lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How does covering my vegetables with a fine net keep insects away from my farm?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni kɛ́ mikɛ ŋshɔŋlooi kpakpai ha mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkabote miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: A protective net creates a physical wall that stops harmful insects from flying onto your crops to lay eggs or feed on leaves, keeping your plants healthy without relying heavily on chemical sprays.
ga: Nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ feɔ gbɛtsii nii ko ni tsiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafo kɛba oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni amɛbawo ŋmeii loo amɛye baai lɛ. Ha otsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ ohe akafɔ̃ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ tsɔ.

english: Why do my cabbage leaves get full of tiny holes after the rainy season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kaabe baa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The rain creates warm, moist conditions that encourage insect eggs to hatch into caterpillars. These young pests feed aggressively on tender green leaves, leaving visible holes as they grow.
ga: Nugbɔ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. ni haa kooloi bibii akui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ waa. Shi buji ni anaa beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do insects prefer to attack young crop shoots rather than older stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii sumɔɔ ni amɛtutua tsei bibii fe tsei ni eda lɛ?

english: Young shoots are soft, tender, and rich in water and fresh nutrients, making them easy for pests to bite and digest compared to tough, older plant stems.
ga: Tsobii bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe yɛ mlɛo ni nu kpakpa kɛ niyenii kpakpai babaoo yɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baaye ni amɛyeɔ nii kɛ akɛto tsei ni wa ni egbɔ lɛ ahe.

english: How can I tell if my tomato plants are being damaged by insects or by a plant disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi loo helai efite mitato tsei lɛ?

english: Insect damage usually leaves clear physical signs like chewed leaf edges, holes, or visible bugs, while diseases often cause dark spots, mold, or sudden wilting without any insects present.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ shĩɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ, tamɔ baa lɛ naa, bu, loo koolooi ni anaa. Yɛ be mli ni helai srɔtoi Bei pii lɛ, ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji, ŋmɔtɔ, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni baa trukaa ni kooloi bibii bɛ mli baa.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt during the hottest part of the afternoon even if I watered them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ nɔ moŋ?

english: Harsh afternoon heat causes leaves to lose water faster than roots can draw it from the soil. The plant droops temporarily to reduce water loss and usually recovers when temperatures drop.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa baai lɛ sɛɛ foɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi.

english: Why do crops grown under shade nets stay green longer during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Nets break the force of dry winds and reduce intense sunlight, which slows down water evaporation from the soil and leaves, helping crops hold onto moisture much longer.
ga: Ŋshɔ lɛ fiteɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ hewalɛ ni ehaa hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baa shi. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ blɛoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ baai lɛ amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young crop leaves turn yellow when they receive full afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibaai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ amɛná shwane hulu ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Excessive sunlight and heat can burn tender young leaves and damage their chlorophyll, which is the green material plants use to absorb sunlight and make food.
ga: Hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine baanyɛ ashã baai bibii ni efite klorofil, ni ji nibii ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛgbala hulu la ni amɛfee niyenii lɛ.

english: Will covering my crops with a protective net house block the sunlight they need to grow?
ga: Ani mi-trellised greenhouse lɛ baatsi hulu la ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ naa?

english: No, agricultural nets are woven to let essential light and air pass through while filtering out excessive heat and keeping destructive insects out.
ga: Dabi, akpɛɔ okwaayeli he ŋshɔŋlooi koni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni he hiaa lɛ atsɔ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli, ni ehaaa kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ akabote mli.

english: Will the temperature inside a net house become too hot for my crops to survive?
ga: Ani ŋshɔŋ hulutsoo be ni yɔɔ shia lɛ mli lɛ baafee hulutsoo tsɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛŋ ahi shi?

english: Net houses are built with breathable mesh that allows fresh breeze to circulate freely, keeping the inside cool while protecting plants from strong sun and pests.
ga: Akɛ ŋtayaa ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ mli lɛ ma ŋtayaa shia lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa mligbɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli, yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Can building a net structure help stop viral diseases from spreading among my vegetables?
ga: Ani trellis ni afee lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ekpa helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela mli baa lɛ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa mi-vegetables lɛ amli?

english: Yes, many serious crop viruses are carried from field to field by flying insects like whiteflies and aphids. Keeping these insects out prevents them from spreading diseases to your healthy plants.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei ahe helai babaoo ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ, kooloi bibii ni foɔ tamɔ whiteflies kɛ aphids lɛ kɛ amɛ yaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔ mli. Kɛ́ otsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa lɛ, ehaaa amɛgbɛ hela amɛshwã otsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or keeping shade trees nearby shields the young cocoa leaves and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ dumɔwui loo shade tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baaye abua ni abu kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Why do my plantain bunches get smaller every year on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ bibii daa afi yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: When too many suckers grow around a mother plantain, they compete for water and nutrients. Cutting away extra suckers so only two or three main shoots remain ensures the plant gets enough nutrients to produce large bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwu ko he lɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ koni ashi ŋmeii titrii 2-3 pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do farmers cover the soil around their vegetable plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛ jwɛi haa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, stops water from evaporating under the hot sun, keeps the root area cool, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ la yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: How can I tell if the first rain of the season is enough for me to start planting my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ?

english: A single early rain often dries out quickly and can cause germinating seeds to die. It is best to wait until rainfall becomes regular and moistens the topsoil down to at least the depth of your hand before planting.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ tso kome nɔ lɛ haa egbiɔ oya, ni ebaanyɛ egbe dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be ni okɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ awo mli kɛyashɛ kɛ hoo lɛ nine mli dani odu.

english: Why do I see small holes in my young maize leaves and tiny green worms hiding inside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni akɛtee mli lɛ amli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest that eats the growing heart of maize plants. Inspecting fields early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts early in the morning or late evening helps protect the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei atsui ni miida lɛ. He ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ ni atsɔɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting underground before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when planted in soil that collects too much water during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows water to drain properly so the roots stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu babaoo hiɛɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Shishifãi lɛ egbi ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why are my tomato plants wilting and dying suddenly even though I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting in green tomato plants is often caused by bacterial wilt, a soil-borne disease that blocks water flow inside the stem. Rotating tomatoes with non-susceptible crops like maize helps clear the disease from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato tsei ni eŋɔli lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa lɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni tsiɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni nyɛɛɛ hela, tamɔ ŋmãa tsake tomato lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ hela lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the lower leaves on my maize crop start turning yellow from the tip towards the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛmiijɛ amɛyitseiaŋ kɛmiiya amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts at the tip of older maize leaves usually means the soil lacks nitrogen. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer early in the crop's growth restores leaf color and boosts yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa baai momoi lɛ anaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he mra yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai lɛ ahe afee fɛo ekoŋŋ ni eha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes to expose their leaves to maximum sunlight, which helps the plant manufacture food. Without stakes, low light limits tuber growth beneath the soil.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ koni amɛbai lɛ ajie amɛhe kpo yɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii. Kɛji akɛ tsei bɛ lɛ, la ni baa shi lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off before forming any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant is stressed by extreme heat or prolonged dry soil. Watering regularly and providing light organic mulch keeps the plant cool enough to retain its flowers and set fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli be kakadaŋŋ. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔ ni sa koni fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ahi shi.

english: Why should I leave tall trees on my farm instead of clearing everything before planting my cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi tsei kakadaji yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mafo nɔ fɛɛ nɔ dani madu kookoo?

english: Tall trees provide natural shade that cools your farm, keeps moisture in the soil, and protects young cocoa from harsh sunlight. Dropped leaves from these trees also rot and act as free fertilizer for your crops.
ga: Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he Baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tsei nɛɛ anɔ lɛ hu fiteɔ ni amɛtsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Will planting timber trees alongside my cocoa crops reduce how much cocoa I harvest?
ga: Ani tsei ni mikɛduɔ yɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ahe lɛ baaha kookoo ni mikpaa lɛ nɔ aba shi?

english: Not if you space them properly. While too much shade reduces pods, the right amount of shade keeps cocoa trees healthier for many more years and protects them from dying during severe heat.
ga: Jeee nakai kɛji akɛ okɛ ohe teŋ jɛkɛ jogbaŋŋ. Shi kɛlɛ, hulutsoo babaoo baaha ŋmeii lɛ akumɔ. Shi kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo be ni sa ha lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni o-cocoa tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ afii babaoo. ni ehaaa kookoo tsei lɛ agboi yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa mli.

english: Which kinds of trees are good to plant as shade for my cocoa crops?
ga: Mɛɛ tso hi fe fɛɛ kɛha mi-kookoo tso lɛ?

english: Trees like Gliricidia and local forest trees like Emesa (Terminalia) are great because they spread their branches high up to let filtered sunlight through while adding beneficial nitrogen to the soil.
ga: Tsei tamɔ glicidia kɛ maŋ lɛ mli koo mli tsei tamɔ emesa. (Terminalia) lɛ hi waa ejaakɛ amɛgbɛɔ amɛniji lɛ amɛshwãa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni hulu la ni atsɔ mli lɛ atsɔ mli yɛ be mli ni amɛkɛ nitrogen ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to trim or prune the big shade trees on our cocoa farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔfo loo wɔfo tsei wuji ni haa shade yɔɔ wɔ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Pruning regulates the light coming through so your cocoa gets enough sun to flower and bear pods, while also preventing dark, damp conditions where black pod disease thrives.
ga: Nibii ni afoɔ lɛ kudɔɔ la ni boteɔ mli lɛ bɔni afee ni o-cocoa lɛ aná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfɔ̃ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ shihilɛi ni mli ewo duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli ni black pod hela baanyɛ ada yɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: How does keeping shade trees on my farm help my crops survive long dry spells?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli?

english: Shade trees act as a shield against the hot sun and strong winds, reducing water evaporation from the ground so the soil stays moist long into the dry season.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ he tsɔne ni akɛbuɔ mɔ he. Ha nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do crops grow much faster and greener on freshly cleared forest land than on my old farmlands?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii daa oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji yɛ koo shikpɔŋ hee ni ajie lɛ nɔ fe miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ momo lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Forest soil has spent years accumulating rich, natural food from fallen leaves and rotten wood, whereas old farm soils have lost most of their nutrients from repeated planting.
ga: Koo mli shikpɔŋ heɔ afii babaoo dani ebuaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii babaoo ni jɛɔ baai ni egbee shi kɛ tsei ni egboi amli lɛ anaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ momo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ateŋ babaoo laaje kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni adu ekoŋŋ lɛ mli.

english: Is it possible to plant cocoa directly under an existing thick forest without cutting down any trees?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu kookoo yɛ koo ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ ni afooo tso ko kwraa?

english: If the forest is too dense, no light will reach the cocoa plants, causing them to grow weak and fail to produce pods. You must thin out some trees to let light through.
ga: Kɛji koo lɛ mli eyi obɔ lɛ La lɛ shɛɛɛ kookoo tso lɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, kookoo tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni enyɛɛɛ ewo ŋmeii. Esa akɛ okɛ tsei komɛi afee bibioo koni la atsɔ mli.

english: What will happen to my cocoa trees if I expose them to full direct sunlight all day?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛ wo hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: In full sun, young cocoa leaves burn, the trees become stressed, and pest insects like capsids attack them much more easily, causing the farm to die off early.
ga: Beni hulu lɛ tsoɔ lɛ, kookoo baai bibii lɛ baashã. Tso lɛ miihao. Ni ewaaa kwraa akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids lɛ baatutua amɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmɔ lɛ gboɔ oya.

english: How can I tell if the big trees on my farm are giving my cocoa too much shade?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha kookoo ŋmɔlɔ babaoo?

english: If your cocoa trees look tall, thin, and leggy as if reaching for the sky, and they have very few flowers or pods, the shade above them is too heavy.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-cocoa tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni kɛlɛ, eyɛ mlɛo, ni eyɛ naji kakadaji ni shɛɔ ŋwɛi. ni eyɛ fɔfɔi loo ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ Susumɔ ni yɔɔ cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ mli tsii tsɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa roots are very short and cannot reach deep underground water. Without shade trees or plantain plants to cover them, the dry Harmattan wind sucks out all their moisture.
ga: Kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ yɛ kuku waa, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he. Kɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo plantain nɔ ko bɛ lɛ, Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ kɛyaa.

english: Can I use leftover banana peels to help my crops grow better in the farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ banana ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, banana peels are full of potassium and other natural nutrients that break down to feed the soil, helping your crops grow stronger stalks and produce better yields.
ga: No ji anɔkwale akɛ, potassium kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii krokomɛi eyi banana ŋmɔtɔ mli obɔ. ni fiteɔ koni ebatsɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ehaa onibii lɛ ashishifãi ni wa ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Is it good to mix fresh pineapple waste directly into my farm soil before planting?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ makɛ ŋmei heei ni eshwɛ lɛ aaafutu shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ dani adu?

english: Pineapple waste adds good organic matter to the soil, but it is best to let it rot or mix it with compost first so it does not make the soil too acidic for young crop roots.
ga: Pineapple ŋmɔtɔ lɛ kɛ nibii kpakpai ni wala yɔɔ mli baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha egbo loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afutu mli klɛŋklɛŋ. Bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ akafee acid tsɔ kɛha tsei bibii ashishifãi.

english: How does using oil palm fruit waste help my land during the dry season?
ga: Te oil palm tso yibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Oil palm waste acts like a sponge in the ground. It holds moisture in the soil for a long time, protecting your crops from drying out quickly when rains stop.
ga: Mu tso mli jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Buu onibii ahe koni amɛkagbi oya kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa.

english: Does spreading dry leaves and fruit peels around the base of my crops keep the soil cool?
ga: Baai ni egbi kɛ aduawai ahe tsɔi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa Ani mitsei lɛ ashishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ?

english: Yes, covering the soil around your crops with plant waste creates mulch. Mulch shields the ground from direct sun heat and keeps moisture in the soil longer.
ga: Hɛɛ, mulching ni okɛ tsei ni afolɔ ashwie Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ baaha mulch aba. Mulching buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pineapple plants take much longer to produce fruit compared to crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pineapple tso lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii kɛ akɛto tsei tamɔ ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Pineapples are slow-growing crops that take between 12 to 18 months to mature because they store water and food gradually in their thick leaves before forming fruit.
ga: Anana ji tso ko ni daa blɛoo ni heɔ aaafee nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 18 dani ekwɛ̃ɔ. Ejaakɛ fiofio lɛ amɛbaato nu kɛ niyenii yɛ baai ni mli tse mli. dani ebaabɔi nitsumɔ

english: Does pineapple crop need a lot of watering during the dry weather?
ga: Ani nu babaoo he hiaa pineapple tsei yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: No, pineapples are naturally tough crops. Their thick, waxy leaves trap moisture inside, allowing them to survive long periods without heavy rain.
ga: Dabi, pineapple ji tso ko ni wa kɛjɛ adebɔɔ mli. Baai ni mli tse ni tamɔ wax lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mli. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ ahiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ waa.

english: Why are the leaf tips of my pineapple plants turning yellow and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pineapple tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaf tips usually mean the plant is short of vital soil nutrients like potassium or nitrogen, or the roots are struggling in overly dry or poorly drained soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium loo nitrogen. Aloo shishifãi miibɔ mɔdɛŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ loo nu shwieee nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my banana plants fall down easily when strong wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi banana tso lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Banana plants have shallow roots and top-heavy stems filled with water. Adding compost and heaping soil tightly around the base helps anchor their roots deeper.
ga: Banana tsei lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛshishifãi ni tsii ni nu eyi mli obɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he ni okɛ sũ to shishigbɛ lɛ he shiŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are so many small shoots coming up around my main banana plant, and should I remove them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ lɛ? Nibii babaoo ni yaa nɔ yɛ mi banana tso titri lɛ he. Ni ani esa akɛ majie kɛjɛ mihe?

english: Those small shoots are called suckers. Leaving too many makes them fight with the main plant for soil food, so you should cut away all but one or two strong ones.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmeii bibii lɛ akɛ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ ashi babaoo ni eshwɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ tsei ni hereɔ lɛ lɛ awuu koni ená niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Ja tso kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ.

english: Why do banana leaves turn brown and curl up during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ banana baai lɛ feɔ blɔfo ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Banana leaves curl up in hot weather to reduce the amount of surface exposed to the sun, which stops the plant from losing water too quickly.
ga: Banana baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛba hulu la ni shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ akafite nu oya tsɔ.

english: Why do farmers in southern Ghana plant crops twice a year, while in the north we usually plant only once?
