ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ Ghana wuoyigbɛ lɛ duɔ nii shii enyɔ yɛ afi mli lɛ? yɛ be mli ni yɛ kooyigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ wɔduɔ shikome pɛ.

english: Southern Ghana experiences two distinct rainy seasons each year (the major and minor rains), allowing for two growing periods. Northern Ghana has a single, longer rainy season followed by a long dry period, so crops can only be planted once a year without artificial irrigation.
ga: Ghana wuoyigbɛ yɛ nugbɔnɛmɔ bei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ daa afi. (nugbɔ wulu kɛ nugbɔ fioo) ni kɛ bei krokomɛi enyɔ baa. Ghana Kooyigbɛ yɛ nugbɔnɛmɔ be kome, ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ fe no. Nɔ ni nyiɛ enɛ sɛɛ ji nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ adu tso lɛ shikome pɛ yɛ afi mli. ni nu ni akɛfee lɛ bɛ mli

english: How do I know if it is the right time to sow my maize seeds after the very first rain falls?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eji be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Planting immediately after the first rain is risky because it might just be a false start to the season. It is best to wait until the rain has soaked the soil deep enough—about the depth of your hand—and consistent rain is forecasted so your seeds do not dry out after sprouting.
ga: Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyɛ oshara ejaakɛ ekolɛ eji be lɛ shishijee ni ejaaa kɛkɛ. Nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ ofee ji ni omɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔ ni sa—aaafee bɔ ni onine lɛ mli kwɔ ha lɛ—ni okpa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ gbɛ. Enɛ baaha odumɔwui lɛ akagbi beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ.

english: What happens to my young crops if the rain suddenly stops for two weeks right after they sprout?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa yɛ otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have very short roots that only reach the top layer of soil, which dries out quickly. Without rain, the young plants will wilt, stop growing, and may die because they cannot reach water deeper underground yet.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi kukuji waa ni shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ, ni egbiɔ oya. Kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ, tso bibioo lɛ baagbi, ebaakpa dalɛ, ni ekolɛ ebaagbo ejaakɛ enyɛŋ eshɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ he.

english: Which crops are safest for me to plant if my area receives very unpredictable rainfall?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ akɛ makwɛ? Kɛji akɛ mimaŋ lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ

english: Crops like millet, sorghum, cowpeas, and cassava are drought-tolerant because they have deep root systems or naturally retain water, making them survive better during dry spells compared to water-sensitive crops like maize or rice.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, tsina ŋmãa, kɛ ŋmãa. Enyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa ejaakɛ eyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo ekɛ nu toɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Kɛ akɛto tsei ni nu tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa he lɛ he.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants curl up and fall off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry periods as a self-defense mechanism to reduce water loss through transpiration. Once the rains return, the plant will drink water and quickly grow fresh green leaves again.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ aba shi. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baanu nu lɛ ni ebaakwɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ oya ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and rot when there is too much continuous rain for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Too much continuous rain fills all the small air spaces in the soil with water, drowning the root system. Without air, roots cannot breathe or absorb nutrients, which causes the leaves to turn yellow and the plant to rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo ni yaa nɔ lɛ ha kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ba. Nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu loo amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tso lɛ agbo.

english: Why does heavy rain destroy my crops if it falls while the plants are flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii kɛji egbee be mli ni tsei lɛ miikwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Heavy rain during the flowering stage can physically wash away pollen or damage flowers before insects can pollinate them. Without successful pollination, the plant cannot produce grains, pods, or fruits.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ beaŋ lɛ baanyɛ afɔ fɔfɔii lɛ amli fɔfɔii lɛ ahe loo egbe fɔfɔii lɛ dani kooloi bibii baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Kɛji akɛ pollination ni yeɔ omanye bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ awo dumɔwui, ŋmeii, loo aduawai.

english: How can I check if my field soil has enough moisture for planting without using expensive equipment?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli eyi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔ nii ni mikɛ nibii ni jara wa tsuuu nii?

english: Dig down about a hand's depth into your field, scoop up a handful of soil, and squeeze it into a ball. If the soil holds together in a soft clump without dripping water or crumbling apart, it has the ideal moisture level for seed germination.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli aaafee nine kome. Kpɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ ni eyi obɔ kɛ nine. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛmimɔ mli ni efee bɔɔlu. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bua ehe naa ni efee ŋmɔtɔ ni nu shwieee shi loo egbɛ eshwaaa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa jogbaŋŋ kɛha dumɔwui akwɛ̃mɔ.

english: Why does my neighbor's farm hold water longer after it rains while my field dries up very quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ hiɛɔ nu be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Soils rich in organic matter (like compost or decomposed plant material) act like sponges and trap water longer. Sandy or degraded soil lets rainwater drain away quickly or evaporate before crops can absorb it.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli (tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsei ni egbo) tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya loo etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow much faster during steady light rains than during short heavy downpours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ fioo be fɛɛ be lɛ fe be kukuoo mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Short, heavy downpours often wash off the surface of the land as runoff without sinking deep into the soil. Steady, gentle rains soak deep into the root zone, allowing plants to continuously drink water and absorb nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ nu ni hoɔ ni ekɛ ehe wooo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ blɛoo ni nɛɔ daa lɛ boteɔ shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ nuɔ nu be fɛɛ be ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and turn brown during the bright sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ mli egbi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees planted around them to protect their soft leaves from burning and to keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ tsei bibii loo hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ amɛhe lɛ. Koni akɛbu baai bibii ahe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and moldy during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Black pods are caused by a fungal disease that spreads rapidly in cool, damp conditions. Pruning excess tree branches lets sunlight and air in, which dries out the farm and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli Enɛ baaha ŋmɔ lɛ mli agbi ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up and become tiny and crinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ bibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Curled leaves are usually a sign of tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the juices from under the leaves. Spraying the plants with neem oil solution can clear the insects and help new leaves grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids miinu nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ egbe kooloi bibii ni eye ebua baai heei ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the corn is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which maize needs to grow green and strong. Adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer early in the growing season keeps the leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden stakes next to my growing yam shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama ŋmei ni miida lɛ yiteŋ lɛ?

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need plenty of sun to make food for the tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground toward the sunlight, preventing diseases and increasing tuber size.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he. Tsi helai anaa ni oha yitso lɛ aya hiɛ

english: How does planting beans or cowpeas help make my soil better for maize next season?
ga: Te ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehi aha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Beans and cowpeas pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through small nodules on their roots. When the plants decay, they release this free plant food into the soil for your next crop.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ anɔ beni tsei lɛ fiteɔ lɛ. Amɛjieɔ tso niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko nɛɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tso lɛ shishi lɛ he

english: If too many shoots grow together, they steal water, soil nutrients, and sunlight from the main stem. Leaving only one main plant and one or two young shoots ensures bigger, heavier bunches of plantain.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo bua amɛhe naa lɛ, amɛbaaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ mli Kɛ́ ashi tso titri kome pɛ kɛ tso lɛ yibii bibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha plantains akui wuji ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ aba.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot under the ground when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need soil that lets water drain quickly. When water sits around the roots without draining, it starves them of air and causes rot. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets excess rain flow away easily.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya lɛ he miihia cassava shishifãi. Kɛ nu bɔle shishifãi ahe ni nu shwieee lɛ Ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ ni ekɛ fitemɔ aba. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Why do my young maize plants have small ragged holes in the leaves and missing centers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Yɛ baa lɛ nɔ ni teŋgbɛ ko bɛ?

english: Ragged holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworms hiding inside the central funnel. Inspecting your farm early and applying organic or recommended sprays directly into the funnel kills the pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ awo cone lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni okɛgbe kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Why do flowers fall off my tomato plants without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when temperatures get too high, when water is inconsistent, or when pests disturb the flowers. Water your tomatoes regularly at the base and avoid letting the soil dry out completely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛji nu lɛ ejaaa loo kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ye fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ Ha tomato ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nu daa ni okwɛ jogbaŋŋ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ akagbi kwraa.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees alongside my young cocoa crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under the strong Ghanaian sun. Plantain trees grow quickly and have broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ Ghana hulu ni naa wa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, an essential plant nutrient. Adding animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizers like urea helps the leaves turn dark green so the plants can grow large ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei loo ŋmei ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni tsuɔ nii koni eha tso lɛ aná toi wuji.

english: Why do other farmers plant beans or cowpeas in the same field with their maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi duɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔji ni amɛduɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for the maize. They also cover the ground surface, which keeps the soil moist and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hu nɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: Why should I avoid planting maize on the exact same plot of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ŋmãa dumɔ he afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains all the specific nutrients maize needs and allows soil pests to multiply. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or cassava restores the soil and starves out crop-specific pests.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ abɛi lɛ mli lɛ baafite. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ayi fa babaoo. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni ejie tsei pɔtɛɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Does it matter which direction I point cassava stem cuttings when planting them in the ground?
ga: Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ani abaatsɔɔ tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ yɛ he ko?

english: Yes, cassava cuttings must be planted with the tiny leaf buds pointing upward toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the shoots struggle to reach the surface, leading to weak plants and very small tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji okɛ tsei shwie shi lɛ Tsobii lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛshɛ nu lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa baa.

english: Why do I need to build heaps of earth before planting my yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa gɔŋ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose soil so they can swell and grow long underground. Raising the soil into mounds also improves water drainage, preventing the roots from sitting in soggy dirt and rotting.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse bɔni afee ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi be kakadaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni awoɔ nɔ kɛfeɔ gɔŋ lɛ hu haa nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkabote shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ mli ni amɛkafite.

english: What happens if I plant my seeds very close to each other in the row?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves them tall, skinny, and too weak to produce good yields.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛkwɔ tsɔ, amɛgbɔjɔ, ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why should I cut off the thin stems growing out from the bottom trunk of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ kɛjɛ mikoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ

english: Those extra shoots—often called water shoots or chupons—steal water and nutrients away from the main tree without producing cocoa pods. Removing them directs all the tree's energy into producing large, healthy pods.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii krokomɛi - ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ amɛ nu ŋmeii loo chupon lɛ - juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso wulu lɛ mli ni amɛjieee kookoo ŋmeii. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ lɛ, etsɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ gbɛ koni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa aba.

english: Why should I cover the bare ground around my young plants with dried grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi aha he ni bɛ nɔ ko ni bɔle tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dried plant materials acts like a protective blanket. It keeps the soil cool under the sun, prevents moisture from evaporating during dry spells, and stops weeds from popping up.
ga: Tsei ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu la shishi. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ naa. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa.

english: What is making ragged holes in the leaves at the center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa baai lɛ feɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ?

english: Ragged leaves in young maize are usually caused by fall armyworms, small caterpillars that hide inside the central leaves of the plant. They must be treated early using recommended sprays or traditional control methods like putting clean sand or ash in the funnels.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni egbee shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ekumɔ yɛ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmeii bibii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ. Ehe miihia ni atsa amɛ mra. kɛtsɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii loo blema gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ nii tamɔ ŋã loo sũ ni he tse ni akɛwoɔ hoppers amli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains next to my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Mi kookoo tso bibioo lɛ

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that provide temporary shade and keep the soil moist while the young cocoa trees develop strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai wuji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni wa yɔɔ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the plant. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground toward the light, which keeps the plant healthy and leads to larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha tso lɛ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa la lɛ he. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil runs out of nitrogen, which is the key food plants use to stay green. Adding fertilizer or animal manure restores this nutrient so the plant can grow properly.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ba shi. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ niyenii nɛɛ aku sɛɛ aba koni tsei lɛ anyɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cowpea and groundnut plants make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have tiny bumps on their roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acting as natural fertilizer for whatever you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why should I not plant maize on the exact same farm patch every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil and allows specific pests to build up; changing crops helps the soil recover and starves crop-specific pests.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔi yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛi yeɔ hɔmɔ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants before any peppers grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei anɔ dani ŋmɔtɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat, lack of water, or insect damage, as a defense mechanism to save energy rather than produce fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo koolooi fitemɔ. Taakɛ eji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he koni akɛ hewalɛ ato moŋ fe ni aaawo yibii.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and rotten?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efite lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium or irregular watering, which prevents the fruit from developing strong skins at the base as it grows.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni ji nɔ ni kɛ calcium ni faaa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ baa. Enɛ haaa aduawai lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa yɛ shishigbɛ beni edaa lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its older leaves during dry periods to conserve water in its stems and tubers, allowing the plant to survive until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa ni egbɔ lɛ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛ nu ato eshishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why should I cut away some of the extra suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: When too many suckers grow together, they fight for the same soil food and water, which results in small, weak plantain bunches instead of one large, healthy bunch.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ he kome lɛ Amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Enɛ haa plantains bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ feɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why does covering the base of my crops with dried grass keep them alive longer during hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi ha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Dried grass acts as a blanket (mulch) over the dirt, which keeps the soil cool and stops the morning water from evaporating quickly under the afternoon heat.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulch), ni no haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ, ni ehaaa leebi nu lɛ atsɔ oya yɛ shwane latsaa be mli.

english: Why do crop diseases suddenly appear on my farm just when my plants start growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai baa trukaa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji mitsei lɛ bɔi dalɛ jogbaŋŋ pɛ?

english: Disease germs often live silently in the soil, weeds, or arrive through wind and insects. When weather conditions change or plants reach a certain growth stage, the disease becomes active and spreads quickly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ hiɔ shi dioo yɛ shikpɔŋ, jwɛi amli, loo amɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ kooloi amli amɛboteɔ mli. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsake loo tso lɛ shɛ shweremɔ he lɛ. Hela lɛ bafeɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Can my crop be sick even if the leaves still look green and healthy?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aná hela kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ eŋɔli lolo ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ po?

english: Yes, many plant diseases start inside the roots or stem before any signs show on the leaves. Early symptoms might just be subtle slow growth or brief wilting during the hottest part of the afternoon.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai babaoo jeɔ shishi yɛ amɛshishifãi loo amɛshishifãi lɛ amli dani amɛjieɔ okadi ko kpo yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Mra be mli okadii lɛ baanyɛ afee akɛ edaa blɛoo fioo loo egbɔjɔɔ be kukuoo ko. Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli

english: Why is it much harder to save my crops when I notice a disease late?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewaa kwraa akɛ matsa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni miyɔseɔ hela yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: By the time symptoms spread across the whole plant, the disease has already damaged the internal tubes that carry water and food. Catching it early allows you to cut off infected leaves before the whole plant is ruined.
ga: Beni hela lɛ he okadii lɛ gbɛ eshwa tso lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ Hela lɛ efite mligbɛ tsɔnei ni kɛ nu kɛ niyenii yaa lɛ. Ni ooomɔ lɛ mra Enɛ baaha onyɛ ofolɔ baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ dani tso muu lɛ fɛɛ akpata.

english: Why are my young seedlings drying up and withering even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ po lɛ?

english: Young plants wither if their delicate roots are burnt by hot soil or intense direct sunlight. Giving young plants shade and putting dry grass mulching around the base keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Tsei bibii baagbi kɛji shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo hulu la ni naa wa shã amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Tsei bibii ni akɛwoɔ amɛhe lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni akɛ sũ ni egbi aha amɛshishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How can I plant my young trees so they survive the hot dry season without dying?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ tsei bibii koni manyɛ mahi shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli ni migbooo?

english: Plant early during the rainy season so roots grow deep before the drought starts, and leave nurse crops like plantains nearby to provide shade and trap moisture around the young trees.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli koni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ akwɛ̃ dani hɔmɔ lɛ aje shishi. Ni shi tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ koni eha hulutsoo aba ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi tsei bibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do some plants in my field stay small and weak while the ones next to them grow tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe waaa yɛ be mli ni mɛi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Uneven growth is often caused by hidden root problems, such as underground pests or localized soil disease attacking the roots of the weaker plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ, tamɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsɛŋemɔ helai loo shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ni tutuaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ dalɛ ni ejaaa baa.

english: What should I do first if I spot a strange plant sickness on my farm that I don't recognize?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee klɛŋklɛŋ kɛji mikɛ tso hela ko ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ kpe? Yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mileee mli

english: Isolate or carefully destroy the infected plant parts, wash your hands and tools before touching healthy plants, and report the issue to an extension officer for proper identification.
ga: Okɛ hiɛdɔɔ agbala tso lɛ fãi ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ amli loo ofite amɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ oniji kɛ nitsumɔ dadei ahe dani ota tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe. ni amɛbɔ naagbai ahe amaniɛ amɛtsɔɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ koni amɛyoo amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: If a sickness ruins my crops this season, can I ever plant on that same land again?
ga: Kɛji hela kpata miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahiɛ yɛ be nɛɛ mli Ani manyɛ madu tsei yɛ nakai he lɛ nɔŋŋ ekoŋŋ?

english: Yes, you can farm there again, but you must practice crop rotation by planting a completely different type of crop that the disease cannot attack, allowing the soil time to recover.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ oya okwaa yɛ jɛmɛ ekoŋŋ. Shi ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atsakemɔ atsu nii kɛtsɔ tsei srɔtoi kwraa ni hela lɛ nyɛŋ atutua amɛ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛ ehe awo mli ekoŋŋ

english: Can diseases travel from my neighbor's field onto my farm?
ga: Ani hela baanyɛ ajɛ akutsoŋnyo ko ŋmɔ mli kɛba miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, plant diseases spread easily through wind, rain splashes, insects, infected seeds, and even on dirty boots or farm cutlasses shared between fields.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, kooloi bibii, dumɔwui ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ. kɛ bɔɔtui ni he tseee loo ŋmɔ mli dadei ni ajaa yɛ ŋmɔji ateŋ lɛ po nɔ.

english: How often do I need to walk through my farm to check on the health of my crops?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni makwɛ bɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ ha?

english: It is best to inspect your farm at least twice a week. Looking closely at the stems, under the leaves, and near the soil helps you catch problems before they spread to the rest of the field.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ kɛ hoo lɛ, obaakwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli, ni okwɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi, baai ashishi kɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaye abua bo ni oyoo naagbai dani amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli hei krokomɛi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape and dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: Yellowing along the middle of lower maize leaves means the plant is hungry for nitrogen. Nitrogen acts as main food for leaf growth, and when soil lacks it, the plant steals nitrogen from older leaves to feed newer ones at the top.
ga: Yellow ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ daa. ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli etse Tso lɛ baaju nitrogen kɛjɛ baai momo lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with bushy green leaves but produce very small tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ jwɛi ni baai eŋɔli yɔɔ mli shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or too much shade, cassava puts all its strength into growing stems and leaves above ground instead of storing food in roots. Balanced soil nutrients and clear sunlight encourage the plant to swell its tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo hulutsoo babaoo lɛ, ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo ŋmeii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja kɛ hulu la ni mli tse yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do my maize cobs stay small and weak when I plant three or four seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo ni amɛhe waaa beni mikɛ dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ feɔ ekome yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting multiple seeds in one spot forces the crops to fight each other for limited groundwater, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Giving each seed its own space allows roots to spread out and feed properly, leading to bigger cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná shikpɔŋ shishi nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni fa fioo. Kɛ́ aha dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa ni amɛyeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa anáa cob ni da fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants twisting, curling upwards, and staying small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ebɔle ehe, ni efee bibii lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually a reaction to tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the undersides of young leaves, or passing a virus to the plant. Protecting plants early stops leaf distortion and keeps fruit growing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ baa ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ feɔ amɛnii. loo ekɛ hela lɛ aha tso lɛ Ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ amɛgbekɛbiiashi Ehaa baa lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die during hot afternoons even when the soil is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is often caused by bacterial wilt or root rot damaging underground water tubes. When the hot sun speeds up leaf drying, damaged roots cannot pump water fast enough, causing the whole plant to collapse.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ mli shwiemɔ baa trukaa ji helai ni gbeɔ mɔ loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ ni fiteɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu paipii lɛ. Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ lɛ ehaa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Shishifãi ni efite lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛre nu oya bɔ ni sa. ni eha tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbee shi

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and lose their leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛbaai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry Harmattan winds suck moisture out of cocoa leaves faster than roots can draw water from dry soil. Providing shade trees like plantains and keeping mulch over the roots shields young plants from harsh wind and conserves soil water.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ kookoo baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ha kɛ shishifãi ni akɛwoɔ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he, ni ebaaye ebua ni nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ akafite.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants dry up and fall off without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or water supply drops suddenly. Extreme heat or drought causes extreme stress, so the plant drops its blossoms to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ba shi trukaa. Dɔlɛ loo hɔmɔ ni naa wa waa kɛ nɔnyɛɛ kpele baa. No hewɔ lɛ tsei baa amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛshihilɛ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans in the same field make my next maize crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ baaha mi-ŋmei srɔtoi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans have beneficial root bacteria that capture nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil. When leaf litter and roots decay, they leave behind free natural fertilizer for crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ shishifãi amli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ fite Amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start sprouting buds and shrinking in weight inside my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ ni miigbɔjɔ yɛ mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that naturally wake up from dormancy after a few months. As they prepare to grow new shoots, they use up their stored food and water reserves, causing the tubers to soften and lose weight.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ wɔɔhe yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ. be mli ni amɛsaa amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ ŋmeii heei Amɛkɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni ato lɛ baatsu nii. ehaa yitso lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehaa shwiili lɛ mli tsiimɔ baa shi

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster and greener after a rain than my planted crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants with aggressive root systems adapted to grab rainwater and soil nutrients instantly. Removing weeds early prevents them from stealing vital nutrients away from your planted crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji koo mli tso ko ni yɔɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni atsake koni ejie nugbɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Jwɛi ni ooojie mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ tsei ni oduɔ lɛ amli.

english: Is oil palm really a profitable crop for me to plant compared to cocoa?
ga: Ani oil palm ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he diɛŋtsɛ ni mikɛbaakwɛ kɛ akɛto kookoo he?

english: Oil palm is very profitable because once mature, it produces fresh fruit bunches continuously throughout the year, providing a steady income stream, whereas cocoa harvests are seasonal.
ga: Sɛɛnamɔi babaoo yɛ mu tsei ahe ejaakɛ kɛ́ amɛdara kwraa lɛ amɛyaa nɔ amɛwoɔ aduawai heei babaoo yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. Ehaa enáa shika jɛɛhe ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni kookoo kpamɔ lɛ ji be mli lɛ,.

english: Can I plant oil palm trees on the exact same land together with my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu oil palm tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni aduɔ cocoa tsei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: It is generally not recommended to mix them fully on the same land because mature oil palms create heavy shade and have wide root systems that steal water and nutrients from cocoa trees.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, atsɔɔɔ akɛ akɛ amɛ fɛɛ afutu yɛ he kome. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, mu tsei ni eda lɛ feɔ hulutsoo ni mli wa, ni eyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt when I plant them in direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and shallow roots that dry out quickly under harsh sunlight; they need temporary shade crops like plantains to protect them during their early growth stage.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee be mli.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees drop off before forming small cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ cacao ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when exposed to dry spells, nutrient stress, or a lack of small pollinating insects (midges), as the tree conserves energy for its own survival.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli. nutritional stress Loo pollinators bibii (teŋgbɛ nibii) lɛ faaa ejaakɛ tsei toɔ hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Why do agricultural officers insist on precise spacing between cocoa trees instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ esa akɛ aná gbɛ pɔtɛɛ ni kã kookoo tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ

english: Proper spacing gives roots enough space to suck nutrients and allows air flow between trees, which stops fungal diseases like black pod from spreading easily.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ akagbɛ ashwã mlɛo.

english: How long will I have to wait after planting oil palm before it starts yielding fruit?
ga: Kɛ́ odu mu tsei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani amɛje yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Improved varieties of oil palm usually start bearing harvestable fruit bunches within 3 to 4 years after field planting if properly weeded and fertilized.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mu tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ aduawai akui ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli beni adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shishi. Kɛji ajie jwɛi lɛ ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: What type of soil behavior or land condition makes oil palm grow best?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ subaŋ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ shihilɛ haa oil palm lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Oil palm thrives in deep, well-drained loamy soil that retains moisture during dry periods but does not stay flooded or waterlogged for long times.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ mli hulutsoo be lɛ mli shi nu shwieee nɔ loo nu shwieee nɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How can the district agricultural extension office assist me in setting up a new farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ Kpokpaa nɔ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni mato ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Extension officers help by testing your soil, measuring proper tree spacing, advising on high-yielding crop varieties, and guiding land clearing methods to maximize future harvests.
ga: Extension nitsulɔi yeɔ amɛbuaa kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kaa nɔ. Susumɔ gbɛ ni sa ni ka tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ he. Ha ŋaawoo yɛ tsei srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ ahe. ni amɛtsɔɔ gbɛi ni aaatsɔ nɔ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ koni nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ wɔsɛɛ.

english: What kind of help can young farmers get when visiting the local district agric office?
ga: Mɛɛ yelikɛbuamɔ okwaafoi oblahii kɛ oblayei baanyɛ ana kɛji amɛtee amɛkpokpaa nɔ okwaayeli nitsumɔhe lɛ?

english: District agric offices offer young farmers technical training, access to subsidized seed inputs, disease management advice, and connection to youth farming initiatives.
ga: Kpokpaa nɔ okwaayeli nitsumɔhei lɛ haa okwaafoi oblahii kɛ oblayei lɛ ŋaa nitsumɔ he tsɔsemɔ. He ni anáa kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ mli ni akɛ shika yeɔ ebuaa lɛ mli Yiŋtoi kɛha helai akwɛmɔ kɛ tsakpaa ni yɔɔ oblahii kɛ oblayei okwaayeli nitsumɔi amli.

english: Will cattle destroy my young cocoa and oil palm crops if they walk through my farm?
ga: Ani tsinai baafite mi-kookoo kɛ mi-palm oil tsei lɛ kɛji amɛtsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, cattle will eat tender young leaves and trample saplings, destroying early growth. Fencing off your crop field prevents livestock from damaging young trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsinai baaye tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛbaanaa tsei bibii lɛ anɔ. ni fiteɔ mra be mli dalɛ He Fɛ̃i ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔji lɛ asɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ni kooloi akafite tsei bibii.

english: Why are my coconut trees along the coast dying and turning brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ naa lɛ gboi ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Coastal areas in Ghana are heavily affected by a severe coconut disease that attacks traditional trees. Planting disease-resistant varieties developed through agricultural research is the best way to keep your trees healthy in these areas.
ga: Ŋshɔnaa hei ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ emɔ ŋshɔnaa hela ko ni naa wa ni tutuaa blema tsei lɛ waa. Tsoi srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni afee kɛtsɔ okwaayeli mli niiamlitaomɔ nɔ lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ oha otsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei nɛɛ.

english: How can I protect my coconut farm from being completely destroyed by disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ he koni helai akafite lɛ?

english: The most effective way to protect your farm is to replace old or vulnerable trees with modern coconut varieties that have been specifically bred to withstand local diseases.
ga: Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ obu oŋmɔ lɛ he ji ni okɛ tsei ni egbɔ loo ni egbɔjɔ lɛ atsake tsei heei ni akwɛɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Is it safe to plant new coconut trees on land where previous trees died of disease?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu ŋmei tso hee yɛ shikpɔŋ ni hela gbe tso ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, but you must use specialized, disease-resistant varieties provided by agricultural programs, as traditional varieties will likely catch the same disease and die.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi esa akɛ okɛ tsofai srɔtoi ni yɔɔ pɔtɛɛ ni nyɛɔ helai ni okwaayeli he gbɛjianɔtoi feɔ lɛ ahe lɛ atsu nii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishijee tsofa lɛ baanyɛ aná hela kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni egbo.

english: What does it mean when an extension officer says a coconut seedling is 'disease-resistant'?
ga: Kɛ́ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɛ akɛ ŋmei tsei nyɛŋ hela amɔ amɛ lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ?

english: A disease-resistant seedling is a crop variety that has been scientifically tested to stay healthy and survive even when exposed to diseases that normally kill ordinary trees.
ga: Dumɔwui ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ji tsei srɔtoi ni aka amɛ akwɛ yɛ jeŋ nilee mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhi shi kɛji akɛ helai ni baagbe tsei foloi lɛ po kpe amɛ.

english: Can I just collect coconut seeds from any healthy-looking tree to plant on my coastal farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mabua ŋmei dumɔwui anaa kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli koni mikɛdu yɛ miŋshɔnaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: It is risky because even healthy-looking traditional trees might produce seeds that cannot survive coastal coconut diseases. It is safer to get tested, disease-resistant varieties.
ga: Oshara ko yɛ ejaakɛ shishijee tsei ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ po baanyɛ awo dumɔwui ni nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ Coastal Coconut Disease lɛ mli. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ oooka tsofai srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ okwɛ.

english: Do disease-resistant coconut trees produce the same good coconuts as the old traditional ones?
ga: Ani ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ baawo ŋmei kpakpai tamɔ blema tsei srɔtoi lɛ?

english: Yes, disease-resistant varieties produce good quality coconuts just like traditional trees, with the main difference being that they survive in areas where disease usually kills other trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ tamɔ tsei krokomɛi pɛpɛɛpɛ. Shi srɔtofeemɔ titri ni yɔɔ mli ji akɛ, ŋmeii baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ hei ni bei pii lɛ helai gbeɔ tsei krokomɛi lɛ.

english: Why do coconut trees grow fine in some parts of Ghana but die quickly near the coast?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana hei komɛi shi amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa lɛ?

english: The disease affecting coconuts is particularly severe in coastal zones. Varieties that grow well inland may not survive the intense disease pressure present in coastal environments.
ga: Helai ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ mli wa waa yɛ ŋshɔnaa hei titri. Ekolɛ tsei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ helai ni naa wa ni yɔɔ ŋshɔnaa hei lɛ amli.

english: Where are these new disease-resistant coconut seedlings coming from?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ŋmei tsei srɔtoi heei ni helai nɛɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ jɛɔ?

english: These improved seedlings come from research collaborations between the Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA), international partners like the French government, and local agricultural NGOs.
ga: Nɛkɛ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ nɛɛ jɛ niiamlitaomɔ nitsumɔ ko ni Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA), majimaji ateŋ hefatalɔi tamɔ French nɔyeli lɛ fee lɛ mli. kɛ maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli he NGOs

english: Why are government officers and NGOs distributing new coconut varieties in our community?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɔyeli mli onukpai kɛ NGOs miihɔ ŋmei henɔi heei yɛ wɔ akutsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: They are helping coastal farmers rebuild their farms by providing new crop varieties that won't die from the severe coconut diseases affecting the region.
ga: Amɛmiiye amɛmiibua ŋshɔnaa okwaafoi lɛ koni amɛsaa amɛŋmɔji lɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni amɛkɛhaa amɛ lɛ nɔ. koni akagbo yɛ ŋmei hela ni naa wa ni miigba kpokpaa lɛ naa lɛ hewɔ.

english: How can smallholder farmers in coastal villages get access to these improved coconut varieties?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni okwaafoi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋshɔnaa akrowai lɛ amli lɛ aná nɛkɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ nɛɛ?

english: Farmers can get access through local Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA) offices and partner NGOs that are distributing disease-resistant seedlings directly to affected coastal communities.
ga: Okwaafoi lɛ náa gbɛ kɛtsɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA) nitsumɔhei lɛ kɛ NGOs ni fata he ni hɔ̃ɔ dumɔwui ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ amɛhaa ŋshɔnaa akutsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why should I plant plantain trees in the same field where I am growing new cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ kookoo hee yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under strong sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad leaves that shade the young cocoa seedlings and keep the soil cool and moist during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil, which is an essential nutrient for leaf growth. Heavy rains can also wash away these soil nutrients before the crop can use them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ ajie niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔji nɛɛ amli lɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsu nii.

english: How can I tell that my cassava crop underground is mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil surrounding the base of the plant begins to crack as the roots swell underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ yɛ eshishi lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves in direct sunlight to produce energy. Lifting the vines off the damp ground prevents leaf diseases and helps the underground tubers grow larger.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ aha amɛbaai lɛ aya hulu la nɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ owó wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ tso lɛ he helai anaa, ni ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ amli tsei lɛ adara.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into the center leaves of my young corn stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on the soft central leaves of corn. They hide inside the funnel of the plant, preventing new leaves from developing properly.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni fɔɔ baa ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ ŋmeii amli koni baai heei akakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off the plant without turning into actual peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ pepper diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers often fall off when the weather becomes extremely hot or dry. Heat stress causes the plant to shed its flowers to conserve water and energy.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo edɔ waa. Dɔlɛ haa tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why shouldn't I put chemical fertilizer right against the main stem of my plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mitso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the stem can burn the plant's skin and roots by pulling water out of them. Fertilizer should be placed a short distance away from the stem where feeder roots can safely reach it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ hewolo kɛ shishifãi kɛtsɔ nu ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ fioo. ni shishifãi ni haa niyenii lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he shweshweeshwe lɛ.

english: Why is it better to start tomato seeds in a small nursery bed before moving them to the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ odu tomato dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli lɛ? dani amɛfã kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli

english: Tomato seeds are tiny and fragile. Raising them in a protected nursery makes it easier to shelter young seedlings from heavy rain, bright heat, and pests until they grow strong enough to survive on the main farm.
ga: Tomato dumɔwui lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe waaa. Kɛ́ atsɔse dumɔwui bibii yɛ he ko ni abuɔ he lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaabu dumɔwui bibii ahe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, latsaa ni naa wa, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe. Kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds slow down the growth of my crops even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraaa oya eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for nutrients and sunlight. Even with enough water, weeds often grow faster and steal the plant food out of the soil before your crops can take it in.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii kɛ hulu la. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa po yɛ lɛ Jwɛi lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛdara oya ni amɛju tsei aniyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ abote mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my cowpea plants curl up during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ miihoso yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpea leaves curl or fold during the hottest part of the day to reduce the leaf area exposed to the sun, which helps the plant reduce water loss and protect itself from drying out.
ga: Cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛfoɔ amɛhe yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Koni akɛba he ni baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la lɛ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni nu ni efiteɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ebuɔ ehe koni ekagbi.

english: Why are my young cocoa leaves turning yellow and dry when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji hulu la fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need partial shade because direct sunlight scorches their leaves and dries out the moisture needed for their roots to establish properly.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo be fioo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha nu ni he hiaa koni shishifãi lɛ afee jogbaŋŋ lɛ agbi.

english: Why should I plant plantain trees close to my young cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ bibioo lɛ masɛi?

english: Plantain trees grow quickly and have broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing necessary shade and preserving soil moisture for young cocoa trees.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋtayaai. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hia ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fũuɔ kɛhaa kookoo tsei bibii.

english: What will happen if I plant my cassava stems too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting cassava too closely causes plants to compete for light, water, and soil nutrients, leading to tall leafy stems but small tuber yields underground.
ga: Cassava ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛɔ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ yitso lɛ yɛ baai kakadaji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii ni woɔ nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do I need to clear young suckers from the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mi-plantains titrii lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Leaving too many suckers allows them to steal food from the main plant, resulting in smaller plantain bunches and delayed harvest times.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo ni amɛgbele lɛ, ebaaha amɛju niyenii kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Enɛ haa plantains lɛ feɔ bibii ni ehaa ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why are small holes appearing in my young maize leaves with chewed center shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ejeɔ kpo ni eyɛ teŋgbɛ bud ni ashɛreɔ?

english: Small holes and chewed shoot centers in maize are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which attack early crop growth and require prompt control.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni tutuaa tsei lɛ adalɛ mra ni ehe hiaa ni akudɔ amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni ashɛreɔ yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and collapse even when the ground is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛkuɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting in moist soil is often caused by bacterial wilt disease, which clogs the water-conducting tissues inside the stem and starves the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. ni tsiɔ fãji ni tsɔɔ nu mli yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ anaa ni ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ tso lɛ.

english: Why are my crops growing plenty of bushy green leaves but producing very little fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔlii akui shi ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer encourages lush leaf growth at the expense of flowering and fruit development, which require balanced phosphorus and potassium.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa baai lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni no biɔ ni phosphorus kɛ potassium ni sa aba mli.

english: How does spreading dried grass around my pepper plants help them grow better?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te mi-pepper tsei lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering soil with dried grass, or mulching, holds moisture in the ground, reduces soil temperature during hot weather, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa lɛ aba shi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ lɛ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: How can I tell that the ground has enough rain for me to plant my maize seed?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmãa dumɔwui akwɛ̃?

english: Maize seed should be planted after two or three good, continuous rains when the top layer of soil remains wet enough to support seed germination.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi kpakpai enyɔ loo etɛ ni yaa nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off without forming any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers due to extreme heat, irregular watering, or poor pollination, preventing the plant from setting fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo pollin ni ehiii lɛ haaa tso lɛ awo yibii

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is essential plant food. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer restores their green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ ni ebaaha edalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits get dark, sunken spots on the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ hiɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni eshishigbɛ shwieɔ shi dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by inconsistent watering or a lack of calcium in the soil. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the plant move calcium into the growing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛjieɔ calcium kɛyaa aduawai ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants lose all their leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava sheds its leaves to protect itself from losing water in hot, dry weather. The plant is still alive underground and will grow fresh leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ koni nu akafite yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nu ni mli egbi lɛ mli. Tso lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lolo ni ebaakwɛ baai heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why should I wait until the rains are fully steady before sowing my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi kwraa dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Seeds need continuous moisture to germinate and build roots. Early erratic rains can trick seeds into sprouting, only for dry heat to kill the young shoots before full rains begin.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ nu daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra ni bɛ faŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ alaka dumɔwui ni amɛkwɛ̃. Bɔni afee ni la ni mli egbi lɛ agbe tsei bibii pɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ anɛ kwraa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither when I plant them in an open field without big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are easily burned by direct sunlight. They need shade from larger trees or fast-growing plantains to stay cool and retain moisture in their early years.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa cacao tsei bibii lɛ oya. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why is it better to leave space between my crops instead of planting them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Crops planted too close together fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing lets each plant gather enough resources to yield a bigger harvest.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso buaa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa naa koni ekɛ yibii babaoo aba.

english: Why does adding animal manure help my farm soil stay wet during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Animal manure acts like a natural sponge in the soil. It improves the soil structure so it absorbs rainwater and holds on to it longer for your crops.
ga: Manure tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli sponji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ feɔ jogbaŋŋ koni enyɛ eŋɔ nugbɔ nu ni ekɛ nu ahi onibii amli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant maize on the same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every season and builds up pests. Rotating with legumes like cowpeas restores nutrients like nitrogen back into the soil.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be mli ni ebuaa tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsake amɛhe lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow small and produce very little harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ bibioo ni mikpamɔ lɛ feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive competitors that steal water, sunlight, and soil food directly from your crops, leaving your plants starved and weak.
ga: Jwɛi ji akaŋshilɔi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye otsei lɛ ni amɛgbɔjɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the tender leaves. Treating the plants with safe insect sprays stops the damage so leaves can grow properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ tsu tsei ahe nii lɛ, ehaa nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ kpaa koni baai lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I grow the exact same crops in Northern Ghana as someone farming in the forest regions of the South?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ tamɔ mɛi ni tsuɔ okwaayeli yɛ kooi lɛ anaigbɛ hei lɛ?

english: No, Ghana has different ecological zones. The North is hotter and drier with savannah conditions, while the South has dense forest, higher humidity, and more rainfall. Crops like cocoa prefer the rainy South, whereas crops like sorghum and millet thrive in the dry North.
ga: Dabi, Ghana yɛ shihilɛhei srɔtoi. Kooyigbɛ lɛ mli edɔɔ ni egbiɔ yɛ savannah shihilɛi amli. yɛ be mli ni kooi ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii yɛ anaigbɛ. eyɛ hulutsoo ni nɔ kwɔ Ni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ kookoo sumɔɔ anaigbɛ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kooyigbɛ kpokpaa ni nɔ egbi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some crops grow very well in forest zones but fail when planted in savannah areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kooi amli shi amɛkwɛɛɛ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Forest zones provide rich organic soil, natural shade, and frequent rain. Savannah areas have intense sunshine, low humidity, and sandy or rocky soils, which dry out moisture-loving crops quickly unless they are naturally drought-resistant or receive irrigation.
ga: Koo lɛ mli kpokpaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, savannah lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be babaoo, hulutsoo be babaoo, kɛ ŋã loo tɛi shikpɔŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni sumɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Ja tso lɛ nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ adebɔɔ mli hɔmɔ naa loo awo lɛ nu.

english: How do I know if my land in the Middle Belt is suitable for growing forest crops like cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ Central Belt lɛ sa kɛha koo mli tsei tamɔ kookoo?

english: The Middle Belt is a transition zone between forest and savannah. Your land is suitable if it receives consistent two-peak rainy seasons, has deep, dark topsoil, and retains enough trees to shade young crops during dry spells.
ga: Middle Belt ji he ko ni kooi kɛ ŋmɔji ateŋ tsakeɔ. Oshikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛji akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ daa. Shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni edɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Ni tsei babaoo yɛ lolo ni baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why does cassava seem to grow successfully in almost every region across Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmei yeɔ omanye yɛ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ kpokpai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava is a very resilient root crop. It can store water in its roots and survive in poor soils, allowing it to withstand both the long dry season of the Northern savannah and the damp conditions of Southern forest regions.
ga: Cassava ji tso ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa. Amɛ baanyɛ ato nu yɛ amɛ shishifãi lɛ amli ni amɛ hi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛdamɔɔ kooyigbɛ kooyigbɛ kooi lɛ amli nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ kɛ kooyigbɛ kooi lɛ amli nugbɔshiimɔ shihilɛi lɛ fɛɛ anaa.

english: How does the weather in Northern Ghana affect my crop's growth compared to the weather in the South?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛ akɛto kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ anaigbɛ lɛ he?

english: Northern Ghana has a single rainy season followed by a long, intense dry period, requiring crops that mature quickly or tolerate heat. Southern Ghana has two rainy seasons, allowing farmers to plant and harvest twice a year for many water-dependent crops.
ga: Ghana Kooyigbɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kome pɛ. Nɔ ni nyiɛ enɛ sɛɛ ji nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni naa wa waa. Enɛ haa ehe hiaa ni adu tsei ni daa oya loo ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ dɔlɛ naa. Ghana wuoyigbɛ yɛ nugbɔnɛmɔ bei enyɔ, ni haa okwaafoi duɔ ni amɛkpaa nibii ni heɔ nu shii enyɔ yɛ afi mli.

english: Why are crops like yam grown mostly in the Middle Belt and North rather than in heavy forest areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduɔ tsei tamɔ sweet potatoes titri yɛ maŋ lɛ teŋgbɛ kɛ kooyigbɛ kpokpai anɔ moŋ fe kooi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Yams need deep, loose, well-drained soil to grow large tubers, as well as full sunlight. The open ground of the Middle Belt and North offers easier soil mounding and clear sunlight compared to dense forest shade.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni mli tse, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ he miihia sweet potato koni enyɛ ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji kɛ hulu ni eyi obɔ. He ni agbele yɛ teŋgbɛ kɛ kooyigbɛ lɛ haa anyɛɔ ashɛɔ ŋshɔkei kɛ hulu la ni mli tse he mlɛo. Kɛ akɛto koo ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔ he lɛ

english: If I am starting a farm in a dry savannah area, what types of crops should I choose?
ga: Kɛji mije ŋmɔ shishi yɛ savannah ni egbi lɛ mli Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii esa akɛ mahala?

english: You should choose heat-tolerant crops that need minimal rainfall and short growing cycles, such as millet, sorghum, groundnuts, cowpeas, and sesame, or fast-growing varieties of maize.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyɛɔ hulutsoo be mli ni nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛɔ ni amɛdalɛ be kukuoo, tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, ŋmãa, tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa, loo ŋmãa henɔi ni daa oya.

english: Can I successfully grow high-water crops in dry regions if I set up an irrigation system?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ tsei ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛji mikɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ wo mli?

english: Yes, irrigation supplies the water that rain does not provide, making it possible to grow water-loving vegetables and rice in dry regions, provided you also protect delicate leaves from extreme heat.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ haa nu ni nugbɔ lɛ haaa. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ aduɔ aduawai kɛ ŋmãa ni sumɔɔ nu yɛ hei ni nu bɛ. Ebaabi ni obu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ hu he.

english: Is it possible for me to grow vegetables like tomatoes anywhere in Ghana?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ makwɛ aduawai tamɔ tomato yɛ Ghana he fɛɛ he?

english: While tomatoes can grow in most parts of Ghana, high humidity and continuous rain in heavy forest zones cause severe fungal diseases. They perform better in areas with moderate rainfall, plenty of sun, and controlled water.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ tomatoi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Ghana hei babaoo moŋ, shi hulutsoo be ni mli wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ kooi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ amli lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni naa wa baa. Etsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ fioo yɛ lɛ. Hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ jɛmɛ. kɛ nu ni akudɔɔ lɛ mli

english: How does the difference between forest soil and savannah soil affect how my plants feed?
ga: Te srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ koo mli shikpɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ teŋ lɛ saa tsei aniyenii he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Forest soil is rich in decayed leaves that hold moisture and nutrients naturally. Savannah soil is often sandier or gravelly, meaning water drains fast and nutrients wash away quickly, so plants need extra compost or manure to thrive.
ga: Koo mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ baai ni fiteɔ ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Savannah shikpɔji lɛ fɔɔ ŋã loo ŋã bibii babaoo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu lɛ hoɔ oya ni niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii lɛ hoɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni tsei lɛ aná ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why are my oil palm seedlings growing so slowly compared to my neighbor's farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ oil palm dumɔwui lɛ daraa blɛoo nɛkɛ kɛ akɛto ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Oil palm seedlings need regular watering, weed control, and rich soil nutrients early on. If weeds compete for sunlight and food, or if the soil lacks key nutrients like potassium, seedling growth will stall.
ga: Ehe miihia ni afɔ oil palm dumɔwui lɛ anɔ nu daa. jwɛi nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii mra Kɛji jwɛi kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la kɛ niyenii he akaŋ Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii tamɔ potassium lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ baakpa.

english: How can I tell if my bearing oil palm trees need fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-palm tso ni woɔ fɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Look at the lower fronds and leaves. If older leaves turn yellow or bright orange, or if frond production slows down significantly, the tree is lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen and potassium needed to produce heavy fresh fruit bunches.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Kɛji akɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni kpɛɔ loo kɛji akɛ baai lɛ afeemɔ ba shi waa Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen kɛ potassium, ni he hiaa koni ekɛ aduawai heei babaoo aba.

english: This is usually caused by a fungal infection known as Black Pod Disease, which thrives in high humidity and deep shade. Pruning dense branches and removing infected pods helps air circulate and stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela kɛ enɛ baa. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli kwɔ. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi waa ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ baaye abua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli ni ekpa helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young plantain suckers turn yellow and fall over during heavy winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that are easily attacked by tiny soil worms called nematodes. When roots are damaged, the plant cannot drink enough water or anchor itself firmly in the soil, causing leaves to yellow and the plant to fall.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni sũ mli ŋmeii bibii jɛɔ mli baa. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ nematodes lɛ tutuaa mɔ oya. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ efite lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ anu nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo ekɛ ehe akpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants roll up tightly during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a crop's natural defense mechanism to conserve water. By curling inward, the plant reduces the leaf surface area exposed to hot sun and wind, slowing down moisture loss until temperatures cool down.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ nu he. Kɛtsɔ mligbɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ baaha amɛbaai lɛ anɔ ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ baashɛ amɛhe lɛ nɔ aba shi. Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi lɛ kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why is my maize growing tall thin stems with very small cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ yɛ tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: Maize plants grow tall and weak when planted too close together or when they lack sufficient sunlight and nitrogen. Overcrowding forces the plants to compete for light rather than putting energy into developing big cobs.
ga: Abɛi daa ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ loo kɛ́ hulu la kɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ la he moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii koni amɛkɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or poor soil moisture. Without a steady water supply and moderate soil conditions, the flowers fail to set fruit and drop off.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛbote la ni naa wa mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehiii Kɛji nu bɛ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ ni sa Fɔfɔi nyɛŋ awo yibii ni amɛgbee shi.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge green leaves above ground but very small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: This happens when there is too much nitrogen in the soil relative to potassium. High nitrogen encourages lush leaves, while potassium is what pushes energy downward to swell the roots into thick starch tubers.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ akɛto potassium he. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, potassium ji nɔ ni tsiɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shi koni eha shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛfee yitsei ni mli tse ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans make my soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas have beneficial bacteria in their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the roots decompose, they release this natural fertilizer, feeding the next crop you plant.
ga: Muawai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii amli yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ebuaa naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ shishifãi lɛ fite Ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is it better to leave cleared weeds to decay in my field instead of burning them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mashi jwɛi ni ajie lɛ koni egbo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mashã lɛ?

english: When cleared weeds decompose naturally, they feed the soil with organic matter. This organic material helps the soil retain water during dry spells and slowly releases nutrients that crops can absorb later.
ga: Kɛji ajie jwɛi lɛ pɛ lɛ, egboɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Nɛkɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ, ni ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni tsei baanyɛ aŋɔ sɛɛ mli lɛ kpo fiofio.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and curling up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?
