english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees to shelter them from severe heat and keep soil moisture from evaporating too fast.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo. koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he ni ekɛtsi sũ mli nu ni hoɔ oya lɛ naa.

english: Can I plant cassava alongside my young cocoa trees to harvest food while waiting for the cocoa to grow?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ahe koni makpa niyenii yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ŋmei lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: While intercropping is common, cassava grows heavy roots that aggressively compete with young cocoa trees for nutrients and water. Plantains or legumes are better companions because they provide gentle shade without strangling cocoa roots.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ afɔɔ dumɔ ni atsakeɔ lɛ moŋ, shi Shi ŋmei yɛ shishifãi ni tsii ni ekɛ cacao tsei bibii yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Plantains loo legumes ji nanemɛi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛhaa hulutsoo blɛoo ni amɛtsiii kookoo shishifãi lɛ.

english: If I plant timber trees on my cocoa farm, will they steal all the water and nutrients from my crop?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ mli Ani amɛbaaju nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Certain recommended shade trees grow deep roots that pull nutrients from lower soil layers without competing with cocoa roots. They also drop leaves that act as organic mulch, actually feeding the soil.
ga: Tsei komɛi ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli ni amɛkɛ kookoo shishifãi lɛ yeee akaŋ. Amɛshiɔ baai ni tsuɔ nii akɛ organic mulch hu, ni diɛŋtsɛ No sɛɛ lɛ eji niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why does my cocoa tree produce plenty of green leaves and big branches but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ baai eŋɔli kɛ niji wuji waa shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When a tree is overcrowded with excess branches or shaded too heavily, it spends all its energy on vegetative growth instead of flowering. Pruning excess stems opens up the canopy, letting light trigger flower and pod development.
ga: Beni tso ko yɛ niji babaoo loo hulutsoo be babaoo lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baagbele ŋwɛitsu lɛ naa. Ha la lɛ awo fɔfɔi kɛ pod lɛ shweremɔ he hewalɛ.

english: Why are my green cocoa pods turning black and rotting right on the stem during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in high humidity and cool shade. Removing damaged pods quickly and pruning tree branches improves air flow, helping pods dry faster after rains and reducing disease spread.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ kɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ. Pods ni efite lɛ ni ajieɔ oya kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa pods lɛ ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. ni eha helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ aba shi

english: Why do tiny insects cause young cocoa shoots to twist, turn brown, and dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii haa kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ? Etsɔ blɔfo ni egbi?

english: These are likely mirid bugs (capsids) that suck sap from tender leaves and stems, injecting toxins that kill the tissues. Treating affected areas with approved protection sprays during their peak season stops them from destroying new growth.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi bibii babaoo (capsids) ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli lɛ. kɛ tsofai fɔji ni fiteɔ fãji lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli Kɛ akɛ tsofa ni buɔ mɔ he ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsa hei ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ yɛ be mli ni fãji lɛ fa babaoo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ dalɛ hee ni fiteɔ nii lɛ naa.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa field soil is getting weak and running out of food for the crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni niyenii bɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Soil exhaustion shows when mature tree leaves turn pale yellow instead of dark green, flowering decreases, and yields drop every season. Replenishing soil with organic compost or suitable fertilizers restores key nutrients like potassium and phosphorus.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nijiaŋwujee tsɔɔ be mli ni tsei ni eda lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. fɔfɔii lɛ baa shi ni nibii ni anáa lɛ hu baa shi daa be mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium kɛ phosphorus lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do many tiny cocoa flowers form on the trunk but then dry up and fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kookoo fɔfɔi bibii lɛ feɔ henɔi babaoo yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, shi no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛtsɔɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when trees experience water stress, lack pollinating insects (like tiny midges), or suffer from poor soil nutrition. Keeping soil moist with mulch and avoiding harsh chemical sprays during blooming encourages insect pollination.
ga: Fɔfɔi baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ kɛ nu he haomɔ kpe. Kplukai ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa (tamɔ midges) loo shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii bɛ jɛmɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ he lɛ, ebaawo ŋmɔtɔi ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ hewalɛ.

english: What happens to the quality of my cocoa crop if I leave ripe pods hanging on the tree for too long?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe kɛji mishi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Leaving ripe pods on the tree attracts pests like squirrels and pod borers, and seeds inside may start sprouting. Germinated seeds ruin bean texture and flavor, resulting in lower sales value.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaagbala ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ abɔi kwɛ̃mɔ. Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ fiteɔ bɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ yɔɔ ha kɛ amɛhe ŋɔɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji jarayeli jara ni baa shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when strong winds and heavy rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and heavy stems. When soil becomes soft from rain and the fruit bunch grows heavy, strong winds easily uproot them. Supporting fruiting plantain stems with wooden props prevents them from falling.
ga: Plantains shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ tsii. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efee blɛoo kɛjɛ nugbɔ lɛ mli ni aduawai akui lɛ amli tsii Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ ajie shishifãi lɛ oya. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei fiɔ plantain tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Why do my crops get sick when stray goats and sheep keep walking through my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ yeɔ hela kɛ́ tooi kɛ tooi ni elaaje lɛ nyiɛ miŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Stray animals carry fungal spores, bacteria, and pest eggs on their feet and mouths from other infected farms, which transfer onto your crops when the animals touch, brush against, or bite your plants.
ga: Koolooi ni elaaje lɛ hiɛɔ fungal spores, bacteria kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ amɛnaji kɛ amɛdaaŋ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji krokomɛi ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli. Akɛ enɛ yaa oŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛji kooloi ta otsei lɛ ahe, amɛshwie sũ loo amɛye amɛ.

english: How does one diseased plant in my vegetable garden end up spreading sickness to my entire farm?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ yɛ mi-aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ agbɛ hela ashwã miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Crop diseases travel quickly through wind, splashing rainwater, insects moving from plant to plant, or even on dirty farm tools that carry germs from infected leaves to healthy ones.
ga: Tsei ahe helai tsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya. nugbɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi Kooloi bibii ni fãa kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ loo ŋmɔ mli nibii ni he tseee po ni hiɛɔ helatsɛmɛi kɛjɛɔ baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen in the soil, or that too much water around their roots is preventing them from absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ yɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. aloo nu yɛ he fɛɛ he Shishifãi babaoo tsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slow and weak even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ yɛ be mli ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo amɛmli po lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight intended for your crops before the crops have a chance to feed.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni boteɔ mli ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ dani amɛnáa hegbɛ amɛyeɔ nii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die if I clear away all the big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie cacao tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight; they require shade trees or plantain plants to protect them from intense heat and keep the surrounding soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Tsei loo plantains ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ he miihia amɛ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni eha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very small tubers when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava bulbs lɛ hiɛ bulbs bibii waa beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded, their roots fight each other underground for space, water, and plant food, leaving them without enough resources to form large tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná he ko, nu, kɛ tsei niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛbɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ yitsei wuji.

english: Why do the roots of my pepper plants rot when rainwater sits on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Roots need air in the soil to breathe, so standing water drowns the roots and creates the wet conditions that destructive soil fungi need to attack and decay the plant.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. No hewɔ lɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ ni ehaa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ baa ni ehe hiaa ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ atutua ni amɛha tso lɛ agbo.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔlɔ ni amɛwooo tomato ko lɛ?

english: Tomatoes shed their blossoms when exposed to extreme heat, irregular watering, or when pests feed on the delicate flowers before pollination occurs.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo la ni mli edɔ waa mli. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be Aloo be mli ni kooloi ni yeɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ yeɔ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo amɛmli.

english: Why am I supposed to cut off the extra suckers growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Extra suckers act like extra mouths to feed, taking water and nutrients away from the main mother plant and causing it to produce smaller bunches of plantains.
ga: Tsoi krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ daaŋ krokomɛi ni akɛhaa niyenii. Kɛtsɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. ni eha efee plantains bibii bibii

english: Why shouldn't I save seeds from my hybrid maize harvest to plant again next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid corn harvest lɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds from hybrid crops lose their strength in the second generation, leading to uneven crop growth, weaker resistance to pests, and much smaller harvests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ daraaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Nɔ ni tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa lɛ baa shi Ni ŋmaa lɛ hu faaa kwraa.

english: My new piece of land stays very wet and damp most of the year. What kind of crops can I plant there?
ga: Mishikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ edɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli bei babaoo mli. Mɛɛ tsei srɔtoi manyɛ makwɛ?

english: Wet or swampy land in valley bottoms is best suited for crops like rice, sugarcane, and cocoyam. These plants naturally thrive in heavy moisture, whereas crops like maize or cassava would suffer root rot in such soil.
ga: He ni ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ yɛ jɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ kookoo. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ shwereɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji hulutsoo be babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. Yɛ be mli ni tsei tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa baaha amɛshishifãi lɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tamɔ nɛkɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my land is too damp for planting tomatoes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ akɛ manyɛ madu tomato?

english: Squeeze a handful of wet soil from your field into a tight ball. If water freely drips out or if it turns into sticky mud that stays completely soaked for days after rain, it is too damp for tomatoes, which prefer well-drained soil.
ga: Mimɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ fioo ko ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli ni ofee bɔɔlu ni mli wa. Kɛji nu hoɔ oya loo etsɔ muji ni shwieɔ shi ni hiɔ shi gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ Enɛ mli edɔ tsɔ kɛha tomatoi ni sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize turn yellow and die whenever rainwater collects on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nu baabua ehe naa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize roots need air to breathe. When water sits on the soil for too long, it chokes the roots and stops them from taking up essential plant nutrients like nitrogen, which turns the leaves yellow.
ga: Abele shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Enɛ baatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa ni ebaatsi tso lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, ni baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Can I plant cocoa trees on low land that stays soggy after heavy rains?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi ni efɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ?

english: No, cocoa trees do not like standing water. Continuous soggy soil causes black pod disease and root rot, which will stunt the tree's growth and eventually kill it.
ga: Dabi, cacao tsei sumɔɔɔ nu ni damɔ shi. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ kɛ black pod hela kɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ baa. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ dalɛ akã shi ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaagbo.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and smell bad when planted in damp places?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ adu yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ shishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cassava is a root crop that needs loose, well-aerated soil to expand. In damp, airless ground, water gets trapped around the tubers, causing soil bacteria to rot them before they mature.
ga: Cassava ji tso ko ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa koni enyɛ egbɛ eshwa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ jɛmɛ. Nu baakã bulb lɛ he, ni ebaaha helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ afite dani ebaanyɛ eda kwraa.

english: If my farmland is very swampy, how can I prepare the ground so my vegetables don't spoil?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmeii babaoo Te mafee tɛŋŋ asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ koni aduawai akafite?

english: You can construct high mounds or raised soil beds and dig small drainage gutters around the field. Raising the soil keeps plant roots above standing water while still allowing them to access moist soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ loo shikpɔŋ saatso ni awo nɔ. Obaanyɛ okɛ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ jɛmɛ lɛ atsu bibioo ko hu obɔle shia lɛ he. Shikpɔŋ ni awoɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ hiɔ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ehaa amɛnáa shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lolo.

english: Will plantain trees fall over if I plant them in soil that holds a lot of water?
ga: Ani dumɔwui lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu babaoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes. While plantains love moisture, constant standing water rots the main root base (corm). This weakens the anchor of the plant, causing heavy wind to easily push the tree over.
ga: Hɛɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ plantains sumɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ moŋ, shi nu ni damɔ shi lɛ baaha shishifã titri lɛ (rhizome) lɛ agbo, ni no baaha tso lɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ agbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa waa lɛ tswaa tsei amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ.

english: Can I use damp valley land to farm during the dry season when there is no rain?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ akɛ jɔɔ lɛ mli he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ atsu okwaayeli he nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, valley land holds underground water long after the rains stop. This makes it perfect for growing dry-season vegetables like cabbage, okra, and peppers when market prices are high.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ hiɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni sa kɛha hulutsoo be mli aduawai tamɔ kaabe, okra, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ adumɔ beni jara nɔ jara wa lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster on wet land compared to dry land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya yɛ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ fe hei ni nu bɛ lɛ?

english: Damp soil provides a constant supply of water and dissolved nutrients, creating an ideal environment for aggressive water-loving weeds and sedges to sprout and spread rapidly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ haa nu kɛ niyenii ni mli ewo muji lɛ baa daa. Ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha jwɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ basabasa ni sumɔɔ nu lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya.

english: Why does lowland rice grow much better in damp valleys than on high ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ jɔɔ lɛ mli fe hei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ?

english: Lowland rice varieties are naturally adapted to grow with their lower stems submerged in water. The standing water in low fields nourishes the rice while helping to suppress competing weeds.
ga: Omɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji nɔ ko ni tsakeɔ ehe koni eda ni shishigbɛ tso lɛ awo nu mli. Nu ni damɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ hewalɛ, ni ehaa jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ hu tsiɔ naa.

english: Should I clear a fresh piece of land or use my old plot to plant my maize this season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ hee nɔ loo mikɛ shikpɔŋ momo adu ŋmãa yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Planting on the same plot repeatedly drains the soil of nutrients and increases crop pests. Using a fresh plot or rotating your crops restores soil fertility and gives your maize a better yield.
ga: Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shii abɔ lɛ, ehaa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo yaa hiɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ sũ ŋmɔji loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba.

english: Can I reuse the old soil from my previous nursery bags to raise new tomato seedlings?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ sũ momo ni jɛ tsutsu ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ kotokui amli lɛ atsu nii ekoŋŋ koni mikɛdu tomato dumɔwui heei?

english: Reusing old nursery soil is risky because it often contains hidden diseases, pests, and lacks nutrients. Using fresh, clean soil mixed with compost ensures healthy seedling growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ momo ni akɛkwɛɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii ekoŋŋ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ helai yɛ mli. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ kɛ niyenii ni esaaa Shikpɔŋ hee ni he tse ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii efutu mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I prepare a new piece of land so my pepper plants do not die early?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ asaa shikpɔŋ hee koni ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ akagboi oya?

english: Clear the weeds, break up the hard soil so roots can spread easily, and mix organic manure into the planting beds to nourish the soil before transplanting your peppers.
ga: Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ, gbála shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli koni shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo. Ni okɛ organic fertilizer afutu shikpɔŋ ni aduɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ mli koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ dani okɛ ŋmeii lɛ awo he kroko.

english: Does regular stream water have enough food in it to help my crops grow well?
ga: Ani bei pii lɛ, niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ faa mli nu mli?

english: Regular stream water provides moisture to keep plants alive, but it lacks key nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus. Adding compost or fertilizer to the soil gives plants the actual food they need.
ga: Nu ni jɛɔ faa mli daa lɛ haa fɛ̃i baa koni tsei ahi shi. Shi niyenii mli nibii titrii tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves turning yellow even though I water the farm every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Namɔ haa tsei lɛ nu daa gbi?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks essential nutrients. Giving plants only water without feeding the soil causes nutrient starvation, which turns leaves yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu pɛ ni akɛhaa tsei ni ahaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii lɛ kɛ niyenii ni esaaa baa. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: What is the difference between giving water to my crops and feeding my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ nu ni mikɛhaa miŋmɔshi nibii kɛ niyenii ni mikɛhaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ?

english: Water prevents crops from drying out and helps them transport food internally, while fertilizers and manure act as the actual food that builds strong roots, stems, and fruits.
ga: Nu tsiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anaa koni amɛkagbi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni akɛ niyenii yaa mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii diɛŋtsɛ ni maa shishifãi, ŋmeii, kɛ aduawai ni wa.

english: Can I mix dried chicken manure into my watering can to feed my vegetables directly?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmei ni egbi afutu nu tsɛnsi mli tɛ̃ɛ koni mikɛha aduawai niyenii?

english: Yes, soaking animal manure in water creates liquid manure. When applied near the plant roots, it delivers quick nutrients that boost crop growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei ni akɛwoɔ nu mli lɛ feɔ ŋmei ni ji nu. Kɛ akɛwo he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tso shishifãi lɛ Ehaa niyenii ni haa tso lɛ daa oya oya.

english: What should I put inside the planting hole before I drop my cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mikɛwo dumɔ bu lɛ mli dani madu kookoo dumɔwui?

english: Adding rich organic compost or well-rotted manure into the planting hole gives young cocoa roots immediate plant food and helps the soil hold moisture.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo dumɔ bu lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ náa niyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Is it safe to put chemical fertilizer directly into the hole together with my maize seed?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ baafata bu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against a seed can burn and destroy it. Fertilizer should always be placed a few centimeters away from the seed or mixed well with soil.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo dumɔwui lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã amɛ ni egbe amɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ko ni kɛ dumɔwui lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji sɛntimitai 2-3 loo akɛfutu shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow weaker every time I plant the same crop in the exact same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi be fɛɛ be ni madu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ?

english: The same crop continuously sucks out the exact same soil nutrients every season. Changing the crop type allows the soil to recover its nutrient balance.
ga: Tsei nɛɛ nɔŋŋ yaa nɔ amɛyeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ daa be fɛɛ be. Tso lɛ henɔ ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants are lacking nitrogen, which is a main food crops need to grow green and strong. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea will help the leaves turn green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do people tell me to plant plantain trees on the same farm with my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ midu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni mikɛ mi-kookoo dumɔwui heei lɛ duɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and can easily dry up or burn under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow very quickly and provide broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa with shade and keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbi loo amɛshã yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Buu kookoo tsei ahe kɛ hulutsoo ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Planting maize continuously in the same place drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets maize pests build up in the dirt. Switching to crops like groundnuts or cowpeas puts food back into the soil and breaks the cycle of pests.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ daa yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. kɛ ŋmɛlɛtswaa ni akɛhaa ŋmãa mli tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ni aaatsake kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmãa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ asɛɛkuu lɛ.

english: Is it better for my tomato plants if I water them early in the morning or in the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha mi-tomato tsei lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu wo amɛmli leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because it gives the roots time to drink before the heat sets in. Watering during the hot afternoon causes most of the water to evaporate into the air and can stress or damage the leaves.
ga: Nu ni oooha amɛ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛnuɔ nu dani hulutsoo be lɛ baa.Nu ni ooowo amɛnɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa babaoo atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ haomɔ aba loo efite baai lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the juices from the leaves and spreading plant diseases. Spraying the leaves early with neem water or an approved treatment helps get rid of these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahe helai amɛshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Neem baai lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Aloo, tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ajie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their tiny green pods before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? dani eda

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop small pods—a process called cherelle wilt—when they don't have enough water or nutrients to feed all the pods at once. It can also happen during dry spells when the tree tries to save itself.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ jieɔ ŋmeii bibii, ni ji nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ cherry wilt. Enɛ ji be mli ni amɛbɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaahã pod muu lɛ fɛɛ shikome. Ebaanyɛ eba yɛ hɔmɔ be mli hu beni tso lɛ miitao ehere ehe yiwala lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my yam seeds very close together so I can fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni manyɛ madu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When yam seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight each other underground for water, food, and space. This results in many small, thin tubers instead of large, healthy yams.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu sweet potato dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu, niyenii kɛ he ko, ni no haa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ.

english: Can I dry and plant the maize seeds I harvested last season, or do I need to buy fresh seeds?
ga: Ani manyɛ magbi ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikpa yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ ni madu? Aloo esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei?

english: If you planted hybrid maize seeds, saving those harvested seeds for the next season will result in weak plants and a low harvest. Buying fresh certified seeds each year guarantees strong plants and maximum yields.
ga: Kɛji odu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akɛfee ŋmãa Dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ ni oookɛto kɛha be ni baa lɛ baaha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ŋmãa lɛ akakpa jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli ni aheɔ daa afi lɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ ni woɔ yibii fe fɛɛ lɛ naa nɔmimaa.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops as soon as the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshinii lɛ kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ pɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally tough and built to survive in hard conditions, so they absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than farm crops. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing food from your main crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ni ama amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛjɛ onibii titrii lɛ amli.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers are mature enough to dig up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifã ko da bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa?

english: Cassava is usually ready to harvest between 9 to 12 months after planting, depending on the variety. You will notice the lower leaves turning yellow and dropping off, and the base of the stem becoming thick and woody.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Edamɔ henɔi lɛ anɔ Obaayɔse akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. ni tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ tso

english: Why should I leave space between my seeds when planting instead of putting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ moŋ fe ni mikɛ amɛ baabɔ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When seeds are planted too close, their roots fight each other under the soil for water and food, and their leaves block sunlight from one another. Spacing them properly ensures each plant gets enough light, water, and nutrients to yield a good harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ekpa nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to put wooden sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves out to catch sunlight, which gives the plant energy to build big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot, wet ground where they could rot or get shaded out.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã koni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛfeɔ bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaha baai lɛ akabote hei ni mli edɔ ni edɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi loo amɛfee hulutsoo.

english: Why does covering the soil around my vegetables with dry grass help them grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket. It stops the hot sun from drying out the soil water too fast, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ehaaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: Why is it bad to water my crops in the middle of the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaafɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu yɛ shwane hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Watering under the hot afternoon sun wastes water because most of it evaporates into the air before the roots can drink it. Cool morning or evening watering allows the soil to absorb the water deeply.
ga: Nu ni oooha yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ baafite nu. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, emli babaoo baaho kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ anu. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot inside the soil when the rain is too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When heavy rain leaves standing water on the field for too long, it drowns the roots and allows soil fungi to cause root rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu lɛ ta ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and turn brown when there are no plantain trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ egbi ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni dumɔwui bɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and provide broad leaves that shade the young cocoa plants while their roots grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli wa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow at the bottom while the top stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ kã he eji ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left to its newest top leaves to survive, leaving the old lower leaves to yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni ehi shi. Kɛtsɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ ni oooha amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into tomatoes when the weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperature stress or dry air prevents the pollen inside the flower from working. When the flower cannot produce seeds, the plant drops it to save energy.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi tsi pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ naa koni ekatsu nii. Kɛ fɔfɔii nyɛɛɛ awo dumɔwui lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛdumɔwui lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up tightly and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛkpa shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is often caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids hiding under the leaves and sucking out the sap, or by a virus carried by whiteflies that stops normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ kpaa.

english: Why are caterpillars eating the center leaves of my young maize plants during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm moth, which lays eggs inside the funnel of young maize plants. The caterpillars hatch and eat the soft growing leaf tissue in the middle where it is moist.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmei ni kɛ ewuobii woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ fɔɔ ni amɛyeɔ baa bibii ni miida lɛ. Teŋgbɛ lɛ mli edɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to make green leaves and grow strong. Applying a nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or NPK at the right time will help your crops turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo NPK wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans on the same land where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmei yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Crops like groundnuts and beans are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them after maize restores the soil's natural fertility so your next crop grows better without needing as much bought fertilizer.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ji ŋmei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele ni aduɔ yɛ abele ni adu sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: What is making my green cocoa pods turn black and rot before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly during heavy rains and high humidity. Clearing weeds and pruning excess tree branches to allow sunlight and wind through will help keep the pods dry and reduce the rot.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi lɛ ni ajie niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do the leaves of my corn look like small holes were shot through them with chewed-up bits inside the center top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ tamɔ buji bibii lɛ? No mli lɛ, akɛ ŋmei ni atsɔ mli lɛ etsɔ mli yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides and feeds inside the central growing tip of the maize plant. Checking your farm early after planting and spraying recommended treatments during early morning or late evening will control them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe teeɔ ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli yɛ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Beni adu ni afɔ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ nɔ yɛ leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ mli lɛ, abaanyɛ akudɔ ŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my small tomato seedlings falling over and dying at the stem right after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui bibii lɛ gbeeɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ beni amɛkwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: This is called 'damping-off,' a problem caused by soil fungi when the soil stays too wet and shaded. You can prevent this by not overwatering seedbeds and placing nurseries where they get good morning sunlight.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ ‘Damping’, ni ji naagba ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛbaa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni eyɛ hulutsoo Obaanyɛ otsi enɛ naa kɛtsɔ nu ni okɛwoɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli fe nine lɛ nɔ. Ni okɛ tsɔne ni akɛkwɛɔ gbekɛbii lɛ awo he ko ni hulu la ni tsoɔ leebi lɛ shɛɔ nɔ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my crops very close together so I can fit more on my plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa bɔni afee ni manyɛ mikɛ amɛ awo mihe lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow strong stems and produce bigger harvests.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ shi ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do I need to cut tall wooden poles to lift and support my yam vines off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei kakadaji koni mawo sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mikɛfi amɛsɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need to spread their leaves toward the sun to make food for the tubers under the ground. Staking keeps the leaves high in the light and stops damp soil from causing leaf rot.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulu lɛ mli koni amɛkɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ niyenii. Staking haa baai lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni no haaa baai lɛ afite.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off without turning into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowers usually drop off when the weather gets too hot and dry, or when the plant doesn't get steady water. Giving your plants regular water during dry spells helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi fɔɔ shigbeemɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ náaa nu daa Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni ekwɛ efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii.

english: Why do farmers spread dry grass and leaves around the stems of vegetables during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi shwieɔ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai amɛshwieɔ aduawai ashishi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This practice is called mulching. The dry leaves act like a blanket that shades the soil from the hot sun, keeps moisture in the ground for longer, and prevents weeds from popping up.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Baai ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu, ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are fully grown under the ground and ready to dig up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni sũ eyi ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli obɔ ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, depending on the variety. You will notice the bottom leaves turning yellow and dropping off, and the soil around the base of the main stem will begin to crack as the tubers expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Edamɔ henɔi lɛ anɔ Obaana akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ baabɔi fãmɔ be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why are you only harvesting a small portion of my farm today instead of the whole field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɛnɛ lɛ, fã bibioo ko pɛ nyɛkpaa lɛ? ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni makpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: We harvest a small sample area—often called a yield plot—to accurately measure how well the crop performed. This small sample gives us an exact estimate of your total farm yield before you harvest the entire field.
ga: Wɔkpa nɔkwɛmɔnɔ kpokpaa bibioo ko. Bei pii lɛ, atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ yibiiwoo shikpɔŋ. Koni akɛsusu bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii amɛhaa lɛ he pɛpɛɛpɛ Nɔkwɛmɔnɔ bibioo ko Enɛ haa wɔbuɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni baa lɛ he akɔntaa pɛpɛɛpɛ dani okpaa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: How can I tell when my cassava is fully mature and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava shows it is ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the stem thickens. You can also carefully dig up one test plant to check if the tubers are large and firm before harvesting the rest.
ga: Akɛɛ Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsa kaa tso kome hu koni okwɛ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ dara ni amɛhe wa dani okpa nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to plant a new crop variety on my entire farm all at once?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ matsake miŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ shikome?

english: It is safer to plant a new variety on a small portion of your farm first. This allows you to observe how it grows in your soil and weather before risking your full investment.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooodu tso hee yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli he bibioo ko klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ haa okwɛɔ bɔ ni ebaada yɛ oshikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ mli dani okɛ oshika fɛɛ ni okɛwo mli lɛ awo oshara mli.

english: Why are my maize plants giving smaller yields on land I have farmed for many years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ wooo yibii babaoo fe shikpɔŋ ni midu nɔ afii babaoo lɛ?

english: Crops remove nutrients from the ground every season. Continuously farming the same old plot without adding compost, manure, or resting the soil leaves it exhausted, causing lower crop yields.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. kusum mli okwaayeli Ni afeɔ daa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo sũ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ fataaa he lɛ baaha sũ lɛ mli agbɔjɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔtsemɔ

english: How can I restore the strength of my old farm soil before the new planting season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ momo lɛ aya hiɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be hee lɛ aba?

english: You can mix animal manure or compost into the soil, leave crop residues to decay instead of burning them, or plant cover crops like cowpeas which naturally add nitrogen back into the dirt.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛgboi moŋ fe ni oooshã amɛ. Aloo dumɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, tamɔ tsina ŋmei, ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do new improved seeds mature faster than the traditional seeds I usually use?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ lɛ shwereɔ oya fe dumɔwui ni mikɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ?

english: New seed varieties are specially developed to complete their growth cycle quicker. This helps them produce food before extended dry spells or seasonal rains can damage the crop.
ga: Afee dumɔwui heei lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛgbe dalɛ be lɛ naa oya. Enɛ haa amɛnáa niyenii dani nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my crops look weak and wilted during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During intense heat, crop leaves lose water faster than roots can draw it from the dry soil. The leaves droop to reduce water loss, but they usually recover in the cooler evening.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Tso baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Shi bei pii lɛ, ehaa ehe jɔɔ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plant flowers drop off before turning into actual fruits or pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai loo ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off when plants face stress from sudden extreme dry heat, heavy rains washing away pollen, or lack of water right when the flowers begin to set fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni ji trukaa ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ kpe. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni hoɔ pollen kɛyaa loo nu ni bɛ kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ bɔi yibiiwoo pɛ.

english: Why do plants yield better when they are planted in straight rows with clear gaps?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei woɔ yibii kpakpai kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli ka shi faŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Proper row spacing ensures every single plant gets enough sunlight, air, and soil nutrients. When crops are crowded together, they compete for food and stay thin and weak.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bafee ekome babaoo Amɛbaatswa niyenii he akaŋ ni amɛbaakã he amɛfee shwilafoi ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Why do my harvested grains develop mold and insects so quickly in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ mli ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii baa oya yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: If grains still hold moisture inside when you store them, mold and insects thrive in that dampness. Sun-drying your grains until they are completely hard prevents rotting during storage.
ga: Kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ lolo yɛ amɛmli beni okɛtoɔ lɛ, Mold kɛ kooloi bibii shwereɔ yɛ nakai ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui lɛ aahu kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kwraa lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes in the exact same spot where I harvested garden eggs last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-tomato lɛ yɛ he ni mifolɔ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Tomatoes and garden eggs belong to the same plant family and share the same soil diseases and pests. Planting them in the same spot season after season allows these pests and diseases to multiply in the soil, which weakens your crops.
ga: Tomato kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii yɛ tsei aweku kome mli ni amɛ fɛɛ amɛyeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai. Tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ he kome yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi kɛ helai nɛɛ aya hiɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do people recommend planting cowpea or beans alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas belong to the legume family, which has the natural ability to fix nitrogen into the soil. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to grow, so planting them together feeds the soil naturally and helps your maize grow better.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛyɛ adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛsaa nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa fee ekome lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua oŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize together on the same piece of land at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, maize and cassava make good field companions because maize matures quickly and is harvested within three to four months, leaving the field clear for the slower-growing cassava to expand and produce tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ji nanemɛi kpakpai yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmãa daa oya, ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Ha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ afee faŋŋ bɔni afee ni ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni ekɛ ŋmei aba.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow tall and weak with few leaves when I plant them under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔ ni ebɛ baai fioo pɛ kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Tomato plants need full direct sunlight to build energy and produce flowers. When shaded by big trees, the plant stretches upward trying to reach the light, spending all its energy on height instead of producing strong branches and fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi. Beni yɔɔ tso agbo ko shishi Tsei lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã kɛya ŋwɛi yɛ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbɔɔ koni amɛha la. ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ hei ni kwɔ waa Moŋ lɛ ebɔɔ niji kɛ aduawai ni mli wa.

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need sunlight on their leaves to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking holds the leaves up towards the light and keeps them off the wet ground, preventing leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking lɛ haa baai lɛ kwɛɔ la lɛ hiɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi. Koni akɛtsi baa helai anaa

english: Why do plantain trees produce smaller bunches when I leave many shoots growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains lɛ feɔ kui bibii beni mishiɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: All shoots attached to a main plantain stem share the same root system and food supply. When too many shoots grow together, they steal nutrients from each other, resulting in smaller bunches and slower growth.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii fɛɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛɔ plantain tso lɛ he lɛ fɛɛ yɛ shishifãi kɛ niyenii jɛɛhe kome. Kɛji ŋmeii lɛ fee ekome kɛdara tsɔ Amɛbaatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛdaraa blɛoo.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize turning yellow early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil or the soil is too wet for the roots to breathe and draw up nutrients. Adding balanced manure or nitrogen fertilizer usually restores green leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo akɛ sũ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛjie niyenii mli hewalɛ. Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai eŋɔli lɛ daa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress, such as severe heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen in the soil. When stressed, the plant drops flowers to save its water and energy for survival.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiihao, tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay very small even though the leaves look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Ani baai lɛ yɛ hewalɛ lolo?

english: When cassava stems are planted too close together or given too much nitrogen fertilizer, the plant focuses energy on producing big green leaves above ground instead of storing food in the underground roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo akɛ nitrogen babaoo wo mli. Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛbaa baai agboi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli lɛ

english: Why do weeds grow faster and choke my young crops right after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni efiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii kɛji nugbɔ enɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds in the soil are very tough and adapt faster to rain than young crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops a head start to capture sunlight, water, and soil food without competition.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa waa ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ nugbɔ mli oya fe tsei bibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛfeɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than my crops, and when is the best time to clear them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? Ni mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to quickly steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from your crops. Clearing them early—before they flower and produce seeds—keeps them from choking your young crops and stealing the plant food they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛju nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni jɛɔ onibii amli oya. Amɛjiemɔ mra Dani ewo fɔfɔi ni ewo dumɔwui Enɛ baatsi otsei bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkaju tsei niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: When the lower leaves of maize turn yellow in a V-shape starting from the tip, the crop is usually hungry for nitrogen. Nitrogen acts like food for green leaf growth, and when soil lacks it, the plant pulls nutrients from old leaves to feed new ones.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ shishi baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni efeɔ V su ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ eshishigbɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nitrogen he hiaa ŋmãa. Nitrogen tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ. ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli etse Tso lɛ baajie niyenii kɛjɛ baai momo lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cowpea plants have plenty of green leaves but fail to produce seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ewooo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: When legumes get too much nitrogen or water, they focus all their energy on growing leafy branches instead of flowers. Giving the soil balanced nutrients and letting the plant go through slight drying triggers it to bloom and form pods.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii lɛ ná nitrogen loo nu babaoo lɛ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ baai ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii. Kɛ́ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni sa ha tso lɛ ni eha egbi fioo lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo fɔfɔi ni efee ŋmeii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear away all the big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Shade trees act like living umbrellas that shield delicate cocoa seedlings, keeping the air humid and the soil moist until the cocoa bushes grow tough enough to handle direct sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Shade tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hu afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo jwɛi lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni hulu la lɛ baashɛ enɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when they start carrying big fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛji ebɔi yibii wuji womɔ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and stay near the surface of the soil rather than anchoring deep underground. As fruit bunches grow heavy, the weight pulls the stem down, which is why farmers prop them up with sturdy wooden Y-sticks for support.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaahi shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Kɛ aduawai akuu lɛ bafee tsiimɔ lɛ Muji lɛ baagbala tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ hewɔ ni esa akɛ okwaafoi kɛ tsei ni wa ni tamɔ Y fiɔ esɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground when the soil gets very wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess rain pools in the ground without draining away, it drowns the root system and creates ideal conditions for rot fungi to break down the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Shishifãi lɛ baafo nu mli ni eha shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba koni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ akpãtã ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Yam vines naturally spread out to catch sunlight. Staking lifts the vines off the damp ground where diseases live, allowing the leaves to absorb maximum sunlight and produce food that travels down to make bigger yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛɔ amɛshwãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛná hulu la. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tsei anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai kɛ helai yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii ni fãa kɛyaa shi ni amɛfeɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant without ever growing into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ tomato kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme hot dry weather, irregular watering, or a lack of insects to shake the pollen inside the flower. Keeping soil consistently moist helps flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ miigba tsei lɛ anaa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni bɛ ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants twisting and curling upwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips hiding under the leaves to suck out sap, or by viruses spread by these insects. Checking under leaves early helps you catch insects before they distort plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛnu nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛjɛ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Baai lɛ ashishi kwɛmɔ mra Ebaaye ebua bo ni omɔ kooloi dani amɛfite tsei lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests when I plant maize on the exact same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize eats the same specific nutrients from the soil season after season until the dirt is completely exhausted. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or beans restores nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni sũ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Enɛ baaha nitrogen lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow before the corn is ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani abele lɛ afee klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a sign that your soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to stay green and grow strong. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee eŋɔli.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small even when the leaves on top grow very big and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ daraaa waa nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ dara waa ni amɛhe wa moŋ?

english: When cassava plants get too much nitrogen or water, they spend all their energy growing tall leaves above ground instead of sending food down to the roots to develop thick tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ná nitrogen loo nu babaoo Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo ebaa lɛ nɔ kɛyashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye ní kɛ yaa sisi ɔ mi konɛ e pee bulb nɛ mi wa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the big shade trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni edara lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive direct, hot sunlight. They need temporary shade trees or plantains nearby to protect them from heat and keep the soil moist while their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ ni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kukuoo ko koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa he. ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: Why am I finding small holes in my maize leaves and tiny dirt piles inside the plant tops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu bibioo ko lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ muji bibii ni ato yɛ tsei ashishifãi amli lɛ amli

english: This damage is caused by pest caterpillars, like the Fall Armyworm, which hide inside the growing center of the plant and eat the soft young leaves before they unfold.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ teŋgbɛ ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii dani amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slow and yield very small harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for soil food, water, and sunlight. Because weeds grow very fast, they steal these vital resources before your crops can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ daa oya. No hewɔ lɛ amɛjuɔ nibii ni he hiaa nɛɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ.

english: Why should I cut off some of the small stems growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishi.

english: If too many shoots grow from one plantain stem, they fight each other for water and nutrients. Removing extra suckers leaves just two or three strong stems that produce much larger plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo miikwɛ̃ kɛjɛ tso kome mli lɛ, Plantains baatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baaha plantain tso ni da kwraa aba lɛ aba.

english: Why is it important to tie my yam vines onto tall wood stakes as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akpɛtɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko he beni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch sunshine, which gives the plant energy to build big yams underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off the wet soil so they do not rot.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ koni ekahi shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ koni amɛkafite.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant without ever turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the plant gets stressed by extreme hot weather or when the soil goes from very dry to soaked. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ ha tso lɛ hao loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seeds once the rainy season begins?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui beni nugbɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the soil gets a few steady, heavy rains so that moisture goes deep into the ground. Planting too early after just one light rain can cause seeds to sprout and then dry up.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔshiimɔi fioo komɛi ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be koni nugbɔ lɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Shikome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi.

english: How does planting cowpeas on my farm help make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and store it naturally in their roots. When the plants finish growing and rot into the soil, they leave that free food behind for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Kɛ tsei dara ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Amɛshiɔ nakai niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko lɛ amɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How do insects manage to get inside my maize ears when the husks look tightly closed?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni kooloi bibii abote mi ŋmãa toi lɛ amli be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Pests like corn earworms and stalk borers lay tiny eggs on the maize silks or leaves while the plant is young. Once the eggs hatch, the tiny worms crawl inside through the tip of the husk or chew directly through the green leaves to feed on the developing kernels.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmãa toi kɛ stem borers fɔɔ wɔji bibii. Yɛ siliki kpãai loo ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ. Kɛ́ wɔji lɛ fɔ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishi loo amɛtsɔɔ baai eŋɔli lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛye dumɔwui ni miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I see insect damage inside my maize cobs even before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ manyɛ mana bɔ ni kooloi bibii fiteɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii dani akpaa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Insects attack maize during the milky stage when the kernels are soft, sweet, and full of water. If you do not control field pests early, they feed and multiply inside the cob underneath the husk well before harvest time.
ga: Kplukai tutuaa ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ mli edɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ. Kɛji okwɛɛɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ mra lɛ, Amɛyeɔ nii ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ ŋmei lɛ mli yɛ ŋmei lɛ shishi jogbaŋŋ dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ baashɛ.

english: Can field insects follow my harvested maize into my storage barn?
ga: Ani ŋmɔ mli kooloi baanyɛ anyiɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ kɛbote mi ŋmãa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, insects like grain weevils often lay eggs in the ripening maize while it is still standing on your field. If you harvest and store the crop without proper drying or treatment, these hidden insects will hatch and destroy your stored grain.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃ mli be mli ni edamɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛji okpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛto ni ogbiɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ loo otsuuu he nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ baafɔ ni amɛbaafite dumɔwui ni okɛto lɛ.

english: If I plant my maize during the April rains, when should I expect to harvest it?
ga: Kɛji odu ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli yɛ April mli Mɛɛ be esa akɛ makpa?

english: Most common maize varieties in Ghana take between 90 and 120 days (around 3 to 4 months) to mature fully. Planting in April means your crop will typically be ready for harvest between July and August.
ga: Abele henɔ ni afɔɔ naa waa yɛ Ghana lɛ heɔ aaafee gbii 90 kɛyashi 120 (aaafee nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4) dani eshɛɔ shweremɔ he. Dumɔ yɛ April mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, onibii lɛ baafee klalo kɛha kpamɔ yɛ July kɛ August teŋ.

english: What is the danger of delaying my maize harvest after the crop has already ripened?
ga: Mɛni ji osharai ni yɔɔ mi-abele nikpamɔ lɛ ni mikɛbaakpa be mli beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Leaving ripe maize on the field for too long exposes it to wild animals, birds, fungal rot from sudden rainfall, and severe attacks by field weevils, leading to heavy yield losses.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha koo mli kooloi, okpoi, kɛ ŋmeii agbo kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ mli. kɛ yiwalɛ tutuamɔi ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ amli Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nibii ni afeɔ lɛ eba shi waa.

english: How can I tell that my maize is completely ripe and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Maize is ripe when the entire plant and husk turn dry and straw-colored, the silk turns dark brown, and the kernels become hard enough that you cannot dent them easily with your fingernail.
ga: Abɛi lɛ egbɔ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ kɛ ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ egbi ni amɛfee tamɔ jwɛi. Siliki lɛ etsɔ asarasu ni tsuɔ waa. Ni dumɔwui lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ atsɔ otsitsii lɛ anɔ atsɔ mlɛo.

english: What happens to my maize crop if I leave my farm unattended for a month during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ kɛji mishi miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ nyɔŋ kome yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ shweremɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Leaving your farm unattended allows weeds to choke the crop, diseases to spread, and pests to multiply unchecked, which drastically reduces your harvest quality and overall yield.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi oŋmɔ lɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha jwɛi lɛ atsĩ ŋmɔshi nibii anaa, helai baagbɛ ashwã ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baafa babaoo ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha okpamɔ lɛ mlihilɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaaná lɛ aba shi waa.

english: How can I protect my field from pests if I have to travel away from my farm for a few weeks?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔji lɛ ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe? Kɛ ehe bahia ni mafã gbɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli otsii fioo komɛi.

english: Before traveling, clear weeds around your field, apply appropriate pest controls, and ask a neighboring farmer or relative to inspect your farm regularly to catch any early signs of pest invasion.
ga: Dani obaafã gbɛ Jiemɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ oŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ kɛjɛ mli, kɛ tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atsu nii. Ni bi okwaafoi loo owekumɛi ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ ni amɛkwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa koni amɛna okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ ebatutua bo mra.

english: Why do pests attack my maize crop more aggressively right when it starts to ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa mi-ŋmãa lɛ waa beni ebɔi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: As maize ripens, it produces strong natural scents and builds up sugars and starch in the grain, which attracts insects and animals searching for rich food sources.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ shwere lɛ Adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa ni naa wa baaba. ni ekɛ sugar kɛ starch woɔ ŋmãa mli ni gbalaa kooloi kɛ kooloi ni miitao niyenii babaoo jɛɛhe lɛ.

english: Why does my maize take longer to dry on the stem during the August harvest period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani egbiɔ yɛ August ŋmaakpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: August often comes with high humidity, fog, and occasional light rains in many parts of Ghana. This moisture in the air prevents the maize kernels from drying quickly on the standing stalk.
ga: Bei pii lɛ fɛ̃i babaoo, afua kɛ nugbɔ fioo kadiɔ August. Bei komɛi lɛ, yɛ Ghana hei babaoo. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nɛɛ haaa ŋmãa lɛ agbi oya yɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my harvested vegetables turn soft and watery after just a few days in the kitchen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai ni mikpa lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ nu yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ ni mikɛhi shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops grow outside under harsh sun and irregular rain, their cell walls become weak. Once picked, these cells break down quickly, releasing internal water and causing the vegetable to get soft and rot faster.
ga: Beni tsei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kpo nɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ shishi. Amɛ wala yibii lɛ ahe gbogboi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ abua naa Nɛkɛ wala yibii nɛɛ fiteɔ oya. Ejieɔ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ kpo ni ehaa aduawai lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ oya.

english: Is it possible to keep my harvested vegetables fresh for up to three weeks without buying an expensive refrigerator?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ aha aduawai ni akpa lɛ ahi shi ehee kɛyashi otsii etɛ ni aheee friji ni jara wa?

english: Yes, crops grown in protected environments like greenhouses build stronger skins and balanced water content, allowing them to remain firm and fresh at standard room temperature for weeks without refrigeration.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ he ko ni abuɔ he tamɔ ŋmɔ mli tsei lɛ náa hewolo ni mli wa kɛ nu ni sa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ehee yɛ tsu mli latsaa ni sa mli otsii babaoo ni friji bɛ mli.

english: Why do my peppers and tomatoes spoil so quickly even when I harvest them looking healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper kɛ mi-tomato lɛ miifite oya nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ kɛ́ mikpa amɛ lɛ, amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Crops grown in open fields face constant weather stress from extreme heat and heavy rainfall. Even if they look good on the vine, this background stress shortens their natural lifespan once they are detached from the plant.
ga: Tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli baa lɛ kpeɔ be fɛɛ be. Eyɛ mli akɛ ehi jogbaŋŋ yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ moŋ. Shi nɛkɛ sɛɛgbɛ haomɔ nɛɛ haa amɛ adebɔɔ mli wala be lɛ feɔ kuku kɛji amɛtse amɛhe kɛjɛ tso lɛ he pɛ.

english: How does keeping my crops out of the fridge affect their quality after harvest?
ga: Te miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtoɔ friji lɛ kponɔ lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa sɛɛ lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: If a crop is grown under strong, controlled conditions, its natural defenses keep it fresh on a shelf. However, open-field crops usually require immediate cold storage to delay the rapid rotting caused by heat and rain damage during growth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akwɛ tsei yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wa ni akudɔɔ mli. Adebɔɔ mli hebuu baaha tsei lɛ ahi shi ehee yɛ shwapoi lɛ amli. Shi kɛlɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni agbele naa lɛ biɔ ni akɛto he ko ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni ekɛha hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ fiteɔ oya lɛ aba shi.

english: What is the main difference in crop quality between growing in an open field and growing inside a greenhouse?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ tsei ni akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛ tsei ni akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ateŋ?

english: Open-field crops are exposed to unpredictable sun, wind, and heavy rain, which lowers their overall quality and shelf life. Greenhouse crops are shielded from harsh weather, resulting in cleaner, firmer, and longer-lasting produce.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ naa hulu, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ. Enɛ haa nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ kɛ shihilɛ ni akɛtoɔ lɛ baa shi. Abuɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai ahe. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ he tseɔ, ewaa, ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How does excessive sunshine in my open field ruin the lifespan of my harvested tomatoes?
ga: Te hulu la ni fa babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ baafite mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ wala be lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Direct hot sun bakes the fruits while they are growing, causing them to ripen too fast and lose internal moisture balance. This makes them collapse and turn watery shortly after you pick them.
ga: Hulu la ni mli edɔ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã aduawai lɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛshwereɔ oya tsɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Enɛ baaha amɛshwie shi ni amɛtsɔ nu kɛji oŋɔ amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why are crops grown inside covered structures able to stay firm longer than my normal farm crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni aha nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ fe miŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ daa lɛ?
