english: Covered structures regulate light, moisture, and temperature around the plant. This stable environment allows the plant to put steady energy into building thick, durable fruit tissue that resists rotting.
ga: Tso lɛ yiteŋ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ kudɔɔ la, fɛ̃i, kɛ dɔlɛ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ he lɛ. Nɛkɛ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ nɛɛ haa tso lɛ kudɔɔ hewalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ koni ekɛfee aduawai ni mli tse, ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni teɔ shi ewoɔ fitemɔ.

english: Why do market traders offer lower prices for my outdoor vegetables compared to green-tent vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayelɔi kɛ mi kponɔgbɛ aduawai lɛ jara baa shi kɛ akɛto mi aduawai ni yɔɔ buu mli ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ he lɛ?

english: Traders know that outdoor vegetables spoil much faster on the market table. They pay more for protected-crop vegetables because those stay fresh long enough to sell without turning soft or going to waste.
ga: Jarayelɔi le akɛ kponɔgbɛ aduawai fiteɔ oya kwraa yɛ jarayeli okpɔlɔi anɔ. Amɛwoɔ nyɔmɔ babaoo kɛha aduawai ni abuɔ he lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ aduawai nɛɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ ni afeee lɛ blɛoo loo ashɛrɛɛɛ ashwie.

english: What causes harvested crops to release water and lose their skin firmess so rapidly?
ga: Mɛni haa tsei ni akpaa lɛ jieɔ nu ni amɛhewolo lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Rapid water loss and softness happen when the crop's outer skin is weak and internal tissues break down from stress experienced during the growing stage, especially heat and inconsistent watering.
ga: Nu ni fiteɔ oya kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ blɛoo lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. ni mligbɛ fãji lɛ fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ haomɔ ni baa yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ mli. Titri lɛ, hulutsoo kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee.

english: Can changing the way I grow my crops eliminate the need for cold storage before selling to buyers?
ga: Ani bɔ ni aduɔ tsei ahaa lɛ tsakemɔ baanyɛ aha friji mli nibii ni he hiaa dani ahɔ̃ɔ aha mɛi ni heɔ lɛ aba shi?

english: Yes, switching to protected farming methods like greenhouses produces high-quality vegetables that naturally resist spoiling, allowing you to store and transport them at room temperature without losing quality.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ atsake kɛtee okwaayeli gbɛi ni abuɔ he tamɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ, ebaaha aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni nyɛɛɛ afite lɛ aba. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ nakai aduawai lɛ toɔ shi ni okɛyaa he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli, ni nɔ ko nɔ ko fiteee.

english: How do I know if my farmland soil is healthy enough to give me a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Healthy soil is typically dark in color, holds moisture without becoming waterlogged, breaks apart easily in your hands, and contains living organisms like earthworms. Hard, pale, or dusty soil lacks organic matter and needs compost or animal manure to feed your crops properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni nu ehiɛɛɛ mli Efoɔ yɛ nine mli oya Ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni mli tse loo sũ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni ehe hiaa ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi ashishifãi aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: What will happen to my crop seeds if I sow them right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Planting after only one rainfall is risky because the soil underneath is still dry and hot. If the rains stop for a few days after that first shower, your seeds will dry out or rot, so it is safer to wait until the rainfall becomes regular before sowing.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi ni edɔ lolo. Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛmɔ gbii fioo komɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ baagbi loo amɛbaagboi. No hewɔ lɛ, eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ baanɛ dani odu dumɔwui.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient responsible for green leaf growth. It can also happen when heavy rain washes away nutrients or when weeds steal the food intended for your maize.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni haa baai eŋɔli lɛ daa lɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ kɛtee loo kɛ́ jwɛi ju niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha o-ŋmã lɛ.

english: Will I harvest more food if I plant my crops very close together to fit more seeds on my land?
ga: Ani makpa niyenii babaoo kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe bɔni afee ni dumɔwui babaoo ahi mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting crops too closely makes them fight with one another for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in weak, thin stems and tiny yields, whereas giving crops proper spacing allows each plant to grow strong and produce larger fruits or tubers.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ awu yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa, ni yibiiwoo hu baa shi. Yɛ be mli ni akɛ gbɛ ni sa haa tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni ewoɔ yibii loo bulbs wuji lɛ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees grow so slowly and suffer when there are no shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛnaa amanehulu be mli ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Fast-growing shade plants like plantains act as living umbrellas, keeping the air cool and moist around the cocoa while its root system establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. Cocoa akɛ eshishifã gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ toɔ ehe shi

english: Why do I see small holes in my crop leaves in the morning even when I do not see insects during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ mi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ leebi eyɛ mli akɛ minaaa kooloi bibii komɛi yɛ gbi lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Many crop pests, like armyworms and beetles, hide in the soil or under debris during the hot daytime and come out to feed at night or early morning. Inspecting your field at dawn helps you spot these pests early before they destroy your foliage.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui srɔtoi babaoo tamɔ cutworms kɛ beetles Hiɔ shikpɔŋ loo sũ shishi yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni oje kpo oyatao niyenii gbɛkɛ loo leebi maŋkpa Kɛ́ okwɛ nibii ni odu lɛ amli leebi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ mra. Dani ebaakpãtã obaai lɛ ahiɛ

english: Why are the blossoms falling off my pepper plants without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as sudden hot dry spells, lack of water, or receiving too much nitrogen fertilizer. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna haomɔi, tamɔ latsaa trukaa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Kɛji haomɔ ba lɛ Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become hard and woody if I leave them in the ground for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots store soft starch during their first year, but after 12 to 18 months, the plant converts that starch into tough wooden fibers. Harvesting cassava at the right maturity time prevents the roots from becoming dry and uncookable.
ga: Cassava shishifãi kɛ starch ni yɔɔ blɛoo toɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli. Shi yɛ nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 18 sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ tsakeɔ nakai ŋmei lɛ efeɔ tso mli tsɔi ni wa. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmei yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi ni amɛkafee nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ ahoo.

english: How can I tell that my yam tubers are fully mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yam tubers are ready for harvest when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and begin to dry up. This change shows that the plant has stopped growing leaves and has stored all its energy inside the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Tsakemɔ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kpaɔ ebaa lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ toɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Certified seeds are specifically selected and treated to resist common diseases, survive difficult weather, and yield more food. Seeds saved from past harvests often lose their vigor over time and carry hidden diseases that reduce your harvest.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ pɔtɛɛ ni atsaa amɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ. Hiɛ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli ni owo yibii babaoo Bei pii lɛ Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli ni ekɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni haa okpamɔ lɛ baa shi lɛ baa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-decomposed animal manure helps the leaves turn dark green and produce food properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni mli kwɔ ni eha niyenii ni sa aba.

english: Why does my land produce a smaller corn harvest every year when I plant corn on the exact same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season. Rotating your corn with leguminous crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nitrogen and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ yaa nɔ ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Okɛ ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nitrogen aba ekoŋŋ, ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and tall with small cobs when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ amli tsei ni amɛkwɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crowded plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and nourishment to build strong stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ tsei ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on to produce big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ koni ekɛ bulbs agboi aba lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy for the plant. Lifting the vines on wooden stakes spreads the leaves out to catch sunlight, which directs food down to grow large underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha tso lɛ. Kɛ́ owó wain tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe. ni baaha niyenii aba shi koni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under strong, direct sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides vital shade and retains soil moisture until the cocoa grows strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe. Ebaaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when heavy rain falls continuously?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni nugbɔ ni naa wa miinɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water starves the roots of air and encourages fungal growth. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away and protects the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu lɛ ŋmɛ shi, ni no haa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shishifãi lɛ amli ni ewoɔ ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa, ni ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants dropping off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop due to heat stress or irregular watering. Providing consistent water at the roots and mulching the soil helps keep the soil moist and encourages flowers to set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ daa kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are tiny worms eating holes inside the funnels of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that feed on the soft, growing parts of the maize plant. Checking fields early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or chemical sprays controls them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe nibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni miida lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. He ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baakudɔ hei nɛɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids that transmit plant viruses. Spraying the plants with neem oil extract or recommended insecticides prevents insect damage and leaf curl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni ji mɛi ni hiɛɔ helai ni baa tsei amli lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei amli loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ afɔ tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi akafite nibii ni baa lɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce tiny yields even when I apply fertilizer to the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa yibii babaoo aba miŋmɔshi nibii amli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your plants. Clearing weeds early in the crop cycle ensures your plants get all the nutrients they need.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha otsei lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Yɛ tsei lɛ ashihilɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: How can I tell if my oil palm fruits are mature enough to harvest for oil processing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-oil palm yibii lɛ edara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa koni akɛfee mu?

english: You know oil palm fruits are ready for harvest when a few loose fruits fall naturally to the ground around the tree, and the outer fruits change from dark purple or black to a bright reddish-orange color.
ga: O le kaa mu yiblii ɔ pee klaalo kɛ ha kpami benɛ yiblii fioo komɛ nɛ a ngɛ blɔ nya tomi ɔ ngɔ si ngɛ zugba nɛ e bɔle lɛ ɔ nɔ ɔ. adebɔɔ mli tso kɛ kponɔgbɛ aduawai lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ-tsuru ni mli tse nɔ.

english: Why do buyers insist that I bring my harvested palm fruits for oil processing on the same day I cut them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ mikɛ mi-palm aduawai ni akpa lɛ atsu nii koni maná fɔ yɛ gbi nɔŋŋ ni mifo lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Once palm fruit bunches are cut from the tree, the oil inside starts to spoil and ferment quickly. Processing them fresh ensures high-quality oil and prevents loss of fruit weight.
ga: Kɛ́ afo ŋmei yibii lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ Mu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baaje shishi oya ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Nibii heei ni afeɔ lɛ haa fɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa ni ehaa tso yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why are the lower branches and leaves of my palm trees turning yellow and brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-palm tso lɛ niji kɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually show that the soil lacks essential plant foods like nitrogen or potassium. Adding organic manure or the right fertilizer helps the tree stay healthy and produce better fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo tso lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enáa hewalɛ ni ewoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Why are small, young palm fruits falling off my tree before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Young fruits drop when the tree is stressed by long dry spells, poor soil nutrition, or lack of pollination. Ensuring the trees have enough water and nutrients helps them hold onto their fruit.
ga: Yibii bibii shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ hao tso lɛ. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo pollination ni bɛ Nɔmimaa akɛ tso lɛ ná nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ aduawai amli.

english: Why do my palm trees produce plenty of fruit bunches in some months and almost nothing during other months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-palm tso lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ nyɔji komɛi amli, ni nyɔji krokomɛi amli lɛ ewooo yibii kwraa lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees naturally follow rainfall patterns. They produce heavy yields a few months after the main rainy season finishes and rest during dry, hot periods when water is scarce.
ga: Mu tsei nyiɛɔ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔshiimɔi asɛɛ. Ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ eba naagbee lɛ sɛɛ. kɛ hejɔɔmɔ yɛ be mli ni hɔmɔ kɛ latsaa be mli ni nu faaa lɛ.

english: Why do some of my oil palm bunches have small, hard fruits with no palm oil inside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm ŋmɔji lɛ ekomɛi yɛ aduawai bibii ni wa ni palm fɔ bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Empty or undeveloped fruits happen when flowers on the palm tree do not get pollinated properly by tiny beneficial insects or wind during the blooming stage.
ga: Yibii ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko loo ni edako jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ etswaaa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei anɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli

english: Why shouldn't I plant my palm trees very close together so I can fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná he ko babaoo lɛ?

english: When trees are planted too close, their wide fronds block sunlight from reaching each other, and their roots fight for the same soil nutrients, leading to fewer and smaller fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Ni tsei shishifãi kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa aduawai akui fioo pɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Can I plant cassava or maize in between my palm trees while the trees are still small?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmei tsei ateŋ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Yes, planting short-term food crops between young palm trees is safe for the first two years, provided you leave enough open space around the stem of each palm tree so they do not compete for light.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii ateŋ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli. Kwɛmɔ ni oshi he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ŋmei tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishi koni ekɛ la lɛ akatswa akaŋ.

english: Why do I need to cut off old, dead fronds from my palm trees regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifoɔ mi-ŋmei tsei lɛ ahe baai ni egbɔ ni egboi lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Pruning dead fronds opens up space around the trunk, allowing sunlight to reach the growing fruit bunches, making harvesting easier, and keeping pests from hiding in dead plant material.
ga: Fern tsei ni egboi lɛ ni afolɔ mli lɛ gbeleɔ gbɛ ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ he lɛ naa koni hulu la ashɛ tso yibii lɛ aniji ni miida lɛ ahe. Ehaa ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo ni ehaaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akatee tsei ni egboi lɛ amli.

english: How do heavy weeds under my palm trees affect the amount of fruit the trees produce?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni mli tse ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei ashishi lɛ baanyɛ aná yibii babaoo ni tsei lɛ woɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Weeds act like thief plants that steal water, fertilizer, and soil food meant for your trees, which reduces the tree's strength and lowers its overall fruit yield.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsei ni juɔ, amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛhaa otsei lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ baa shi, ni ehaa yibiiwoo fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the plant is still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tso lɛ miida lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, a major nutrient needed for growth. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen deep into the soil where roots cannot reach, or the soil may simply need compost or nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Aloo ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he baahia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen awo mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their young pods and flowers during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii kɛ amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop extra flowers and tiny pods naturally when they do not have enough water or soil nutrients to support all of them during dry spells, saving energy to keep the tree alive.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Amɛjeɔ kpo yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe titri lɛ, kɛ́ amɛbɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni baaye abua amɛ fɛɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Enɛ haa hewalɛ baa shi koni tso lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do fall armyworms suddenly appear and eat my maize leaves so quickly after the early rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall worms jieɔ amɛhe kpo ni amɛyeɔ mi-corn baai lɛ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Armyworm moths lay hundreds of eggs on leaves at once. When the eggs hatch after the rain, thousands of caterpillars feed aggressively at the same time and spread across the field.
ga: Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii ohai abɔ yɛ baai anɔ shikome. Beni ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii akpei abɔ baaye nii yɛ koo mli yɛ be kome mli ni amɛbaagbɛ amɛshwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips, which feed on the sap and transfer the sickness from plant to plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. ni yeɔ nu mli nu lɛ ni ekɛ hela jɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli

english: Why does my soil turn hard and dry out quickly when I burn the weeds I cleared from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni egbiɔ oya kɛ́ mishã jwɛi ni mijie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Burning destroys organic matter and beneficial soil organisms that hold moisture. Leaving cleared weeds to rot into mulching material keeps the soil soft and helps it retain water.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ sũ mli nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ jwɛi ni ajie lɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo ni eye ebua ni nu lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground during heavy rainy periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water pools in heavy soil without draining away. The excess water starves the roots of air and allows harmful water mold and fungi to infect the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu tsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ mli. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ hɔmɔ aba shishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni oha ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ atswa ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why is it recommended that I plant plantain suckers next to my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛɔ akɛ midu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing necessary shade and moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Provides necessary shade and humidity.

english: Maize uses up a lot of soil nitrogen, but legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and return it to the soil, renewing soil fertility naturally.
ga: Corn uses a lot of nitrogen in the soil. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Restoring natural soil fertility

english: Why do seeds saved from my harvested hybrid maize produce poor crops if I plant them next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mi-hybrid corn harvest lɛ mli lɛ wooo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehiii kɛji midu yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred from two distinct parent plants to produce high yields for one generation. Seeds saved from that harvest lose those special traits, resulting in uneven growth and smaller cobs.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔ̃ɔ fɔlɔi tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ yinɔ kome mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa ni ekɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt during the hot afternoon sun even when the soil around them is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ mli edɔ po

english: In extreme afternoon heat, tomato leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can absorb it from the soil. The plant wilts temporarily to conserve water until temperatures drop.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei baagbo yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize turning yellow, and what kind of crop medicine can fix it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Ni mɛɛ tso tsofa baanyɛ asaa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen food or isn't getting enough water. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure feeds the soil so the leaves can turn dark green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-corn lɛ bɛ nitrogen niyenii loo enáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ aya hiɛ bɔni afee ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii waa ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How does weedicide work, and will it hurt my main crops if I use it on my farm?
ga: Te tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ? Ni ani ebaaye miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ awui kɛji mikɛtsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Weedicide is a chemical medicine that kills unwanted plants. Non-selective weedicides kill any green plant they touch, so you must shield your main crops or apply it carefully before planting to avoid damaging your food crops.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ji tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ tsei ni ataooo. Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni halaaa lɛ gbeɔ tsei eŋɔli ni amɛkɛkpeɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ obu otsei titrii lɛ ahe loo okɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ dani odu koni okafite niyenii tsei lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and look wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ekpɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the juice out of young leaves. Spraying an appropriate insect medicine kills these pests and allows new, healthy leaves to sprout.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi nɛɛ ni eye ebua ni baai heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that spreads in damp, shady conditions. You need to spray a recommended protective medicine and prune excess tree branches so sunlight and air can dry out the pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Esa akɛ okɛ tsofa ni akɛtsiɔ hela naa ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ afɔ nɔ ni ofolɔ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aha ŋmeii lɛ agbi.

english: Should I cut down all the big shade trees with my machete before planting new cocoa trees?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ machete afo tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ fɛɛ dani madu kookoo tsei heei?

english: No, you should keep some shade trees. Young cocoa trees burn easily in direct sunlight, so keeping large shade trees protects them from harsh heat and retains moisture in the soil.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ oná tsei komɛi ni haa hulutsoo. Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo ha tsei wuji lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves but yield small tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ kɛlɛ waa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyitso ji bibioo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or plants are placed too close together, cassava puts its energy into growing top leaves instead of expanding its roots underground. Giving plants enough space helps them produce larger tubers.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo akɛ tsei bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeegbɛ eshishifãi lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekwɛɔ bulbs wuji.

english: Why do my plantain suckers dry up and die shortly after I transplant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni adu amɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Transplanted suckers often die if the root base was damaged by pests like stem borers before planting, or if planted during a dry spell without enough soil moisture to establish new roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, suckers ni adu lɛ gboiɔ kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ stem borers lɛ fite amɛshishitoo lɛ dani adu loo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛfee shishifãi heei lɛ bɛ mli.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off without producing tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather is too hot, when the soil becomes too dry, or if insects aren't pollinating them. Regular watering at the root level helps keep flowers attached so fruit can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli lɛ Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifã lɛ he daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: What causes small holes in the leaves of my cabbage plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cabbage tso lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: Small holes are eaten by caterpillars or beetles feeding on the crop. Applying recommended insect control medicine early stops these pests before they destroy the cabbage head.
ga: Kplukai loo ŋmeii yeɔ bu bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ. Akɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi bibii lɛ atsu nii mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni ajie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa dani amɛfite kaabe yitsei lɛ.

english: How can I keep insects from destroying my harvested maize while it is stored in the barn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafite mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ be mli ni mikɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Insects like weevils attack stored grain if it isn't completely dry. You must dry maize thoroughly until hard, then treat it with safe grain-preservative powder or store it in sealed hermetic storage bags.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii baatutua dumɔwui ni ato lɛ kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa. Osumɔɔ ni ogbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ebaawa. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ powda ni buɔ dumɔwui ahe ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ atsa. Aloo okɛto kotoku ko ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli lɛ mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow and dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom up when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the primary food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizers like Urea or well-rotted animal manure near the roots will fix this issue.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua yɛ naagba nɛɛ he.

english: Is it better for me to apply fertilizer to my field right before a heavy rain or after the rain falls?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii dani nugbɔ nɛ waa loo yɛ no sɛɛ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer on moist soil shortly after a light rain. If you apply it right before a heavy rainstorm, the rushing water will wash the expensive nutrients away from your crops before their roots can soak them in.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Kɛ okɛtsu nii dani nugbɔ ni naa wa ba Nu ni hoɔ oya lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni jara wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ he dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: Why do experienced farmers tell me to plant plantain suckers alongside my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very fragile and will burn under the hot sun. Plantain trees grow very fast and produce large broad leaves that provide vital natural shade to protect the young cocoa until it is strong enough to survive on its own.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa, ni amɛbaashã yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni buɔ kookoo bibioo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhiɔ shi.

english: If I plant my maize seeds closer together than recommended, won't I harvest more food from my land?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe fe bɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ hu? Ani manyɛ makpa niyenii babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, planting seeds too close together forces the plants to fight with each other for water, sunlight, and soil food. This results in thin, weak plants that produce small or empty ears of corn, reducing your total harvest.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ yɛ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmãa toi bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nɔ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to suddenly eat holes in the leaves of my young corn field?
ga: Mɛni ha ŋmeii bibii lɛ ye bu ni yɔɔ mi-babi corn baai lɛ amli lɛ trukaa?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which hatch from eggs laid by flying moths directly onto crop leaves. Inspecting your farm early and using recommended biopesticides or neem leaf extracts while the caterpillars are still small will protect your field.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni foɔ kɛyaa tsei ahe baai anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ amli. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem tso lɛ mli nu ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ darako lolo lɛ baaye abua ni ebu he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he.

english: Why are my cocoa tree leaves developing red veins while the branches grow swollen like bumps?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ hiɛ ŋmeii tsuji yɛ be mli ni eniji lɛ daraa ni amɛfuu tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Red leaf veins and swollen stems are signs of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called mealybugs. Infected trees cannot be cured and must be carefully cut down so the virus does not spread to your healthy cocoa trees.
ga: Baai lɛ ahe fãji tsuji kɛ tsei lɛ ahe ni efuu lɛ ji Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, ni kooloi bibii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Anyɛɛɛ atsa tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ni esa akɛ afolɔ mli jogbaŋŋ koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã o-cacao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures are too high or when the soil goes from extremely dry to overly wet. Giving your plants consistent moisture and mulching the soil around them keeps the plants cool and helps the flowers form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ nɔ. Ni aaaha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni aaawo mli. Ehaa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground if I leave them in the soil for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when left in saturated, waterlogged soil during heavy rains after they have reached maturity. Harvesting cassava at its full maturity, usually between 9 and 12 months after planting, prevents the tubers from spoiling.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa be mli beni amɛdara sɛɛ. Cassava ni akpaa beni edara kwraa lɛ Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ akafite.

english: How do weeds growing around my crops reduce the final amount of grain I harvest?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Te feɔ tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ baa naagbee ŋmaa ni mikpaa lɛ shi?

english: Weeds act like theft in your field by rapidly stealing water, light, and nutrients meant for your crops. Removing weeds during the first four weeks of crop growth gives your plants the food and space they need to give you a maximum yield.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔji amli kɛtsɔ nu, kane, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛjuɔ oya lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ ni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ niyenii kɛ he ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛha bo yibii babaoo.

english: Why shouldn't I just save and replant seeds from the high-yielding maize I harvested last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni mikpa yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni mikɛduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds harvested from hybrid crop varieties lose their vigor and yield capacity in the next generation. Buying certified fresh seeds every season guarantees strong plants, disease resistance, and a consistently high yield.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ nyɛmɔ ni amɛyɔɔ ni amɛkɛwoɔ yibii lɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli ni aheɔ daa be lɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe, ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo be fɛɛ be.

english: How do I know when my crops are mature enough to harvest for long-distance transport to Accra?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa koni akɛya Accra gbɛ kakadaŋŋ?

english: Crops show clear physical signals when mature, such as color shifts, firm skin, or drying outer leaves. Harvesting at the right stage ensures produce stays firm during transport and reaches distant buyers before spoiling.
ga: Tsei jieɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo beni amɛdaraa lɛ, tamɔ su tsakemɔ kɛ hewolo ni mli wa. aloo kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ egbi Nikpamɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ haa nibii ni akwɛɔ lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ, ni eshɛɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ shɔŋŋ lɛ ahe dani efiteɔ.

english: Why do my freshly harvested vegetables spoil so fast before I can get them to buyers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai ni mikpa ehee lɛ fiteɔ oya dani eshɛɔ mɔ ni heɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ?

english: Crops continue to breathe and lose water after harvest. Harvesting during hot afternoon hours speeds up spoilage, while harvesting in the cool morning and keeping produce shaded preserves freshness.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ ni amɛnuɔ nu yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Nikpamɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baaha efite oya. Nikpamɔ yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be mli kɛ nibii ni akwɛɔ lɛ ni akɛtoɔ shia lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: What causes supermarket buyers to reject crops even when the produce looks big to me?
ga: Mɛni haa mɛi ni hɔɔ nii yɛ shwapoi wuji amli lɛ kpooɔ ŋmɔshi nibii eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara moŋ?

english: Supermarket buyers require uniformity in size, shape, and color, along with complete freedom from insect marks or chemical residue. Consistent watering and pest control help produce uniform crops.
ga: Mɛi ni hɔɔ nii yɛ shwapoi wuji amli lɛ miisumɔ ni amɛdalɛ, amɛhe su kɛ amɛhe su afee ekome, kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ni kooloi akadii loo tsofai ni eshwɛ akafee nɔ ko. Nu ni akɛhaa daa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii yaa nɔ daa.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow at the bottom while the top is still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni ŋwɛigbɛi lɛ miida lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean the plant is short on nitrogen. Maize moves nutrients from older bottom leaves up to the newer top leaves when soil nutrients run low.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Abele tsiɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi baa heei amli kɛji shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ faaa.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt during the hot afternoon heat even if I watered them earlier?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu ha lɛ mra moŋ?

english: In extreme sun, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it from the soil. They temporarily droop to conserve moisture and usually recover as the evening cools.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaagbee shi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehaa ehe feɔ fɛo kɛji akɛ edɔ

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, sudden moisture changes, or lack of insect activity for pollination cause tomato plants to drop flowers to protect themselves from stress.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hulutsoo tsakemɔi trukaa loo kooloi ni bɛ kɛha pollination Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ haomɔ he.

english: If I plant my seeds closer together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my plot?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe Ani mana yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too close forces crops to compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, leading to thin, weak plants that yield much smaller fruits or grains overall.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ aduawai loo dumɔwui bibii kwraa yɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do my crops yield less produce every year when I keep planting on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi be mli ni miyaa nɔ miduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and lets soil-borne pests build up. Rotating with different crops, like beans or groundnuts, restores soil health.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ hoɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Nibii ni aduɔ ni tsakeɔ amɛhe, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ

english: Why are my cabbage leaves full of small holes, and how does that slow down their growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eha dalɛ aba shi?

english: Insects like caterpillars eat holes in the leaves, which reduces the plant's ability to catch sunlight and make the food it needs to form a tight, solid cabbage head.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii yeɔ bu yɛ baai amli. Enɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛnaa hulu la lɛ baa shi. ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ haa koni ekɛfee kaabe yitsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are my young cassava stem cuttings growing so slowly compared to my neighbor's field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ kɛ akɛto mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Early cassava growth depends heavily on using healthy, mature stem cuttings, controlling weed competition early, and ensuring good root contact with moist soil during planting.
ga: Kasava dalɛ mra damɔ hewalɛ, tsei ni eda ni afolɔ nɔ. Kudɔmɔ jwɛi akaŋshii mra kɛ nɔmimaa akɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ abɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ dumɔ be mli.

english: Why should I plant plantains next to my newly planted young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ ahe?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, shielding young cocoa from the hot sun and keeping the soil moist until the cocoa matures.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Buu kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why is it important to dry my harvested maize completely in the sun before putting it into sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ agbi ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ yɛ hulu mli dani akɛwo kotokui amli lɛ?

english: If maize is bagged while still holding moisture, fungal mold and insects thrive inside the sack, which destroys the grain and makes it unsafe to eat or sell.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ wo kotoku mli ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lolo lɛ, Mold kɛ kooloi bibii daa yɛ kotoku lɛ mli. Enɛ fiteɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni ehaaa efee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe akɛ aye loo ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why do insects attack my stored cowpea seeds even when I tie the bags very tightly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miitutua mi-cowpea dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ kotokui lɛ efi shi waa moŋ?

english: Weevil eggs often attach to the pods in the farm before harvest. Sun-drying seeds thoroughly and treating them with safe storage dust before bagging kills these hidden eggs before they hatch inside.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akɛ ŋmeii akui fĩɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ahe dani akpaa. Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛ sũ ni ato he shweshweeshwe lɛ tsu he nii dani awo amɛ kotoku mli lɛ, ebaagbe nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ dani amɛwo mli.

english: Yellow leaves indicate a lack of nitrogen, which is the essential food plants use to grow green and strong. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do you recommend that I plant groundnuts on the same plot where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okɛɔ akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmei yɛ mli yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen from the ground, but groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and deposit it back into the soil, refreshing your land naturally.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Ha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛo yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Why shouldn't I drop four or five maize seeds into the exact same planting hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ejwɛ loo enumɔ woɔ dumɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When too many seeds grow in one spot, their roots compete fiercely for water, light, and nutrients, resulting in weak plants with tiny or empty cobs.
ga: Beni dumɔwui babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he kome lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa kɛha nu, la kɛ niyenii, ni no haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni dumɔwui bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa. loo nɔ ko bɛ mli

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my pepper plants with dry palm leaves or grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmei loo jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground, or mulching, traps moisture in the soil during dry days, stops weeds from growing, and keeps the soil cool so roots can expand.
ga: Mulching, loo mulching haa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ alɛɛ mli.

english: Yam vines need to reach up high so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight. The sunlight helps leaves produce the energy needed to swell the big yam tubers under the ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɛ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkɛwo sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Extreme heat and irregular watering stress the tomato plant, causing it to drop its flowers to conserve water and energy rather than growing tomatoes.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ ashɛrɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ashwie koni akɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni aaadu tomato.

english: How can I tell when my cassava roots are fully mature and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready around 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stem with leaves concentrated at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Shi tso ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni baai ebua amɛhe naa yɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wither during the main dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have shallow roots and cannot hold much water. During dry periods, hot winds pull moisture out of the leaves faster than the young roots can pull water from the soil, causing the plant to shed leaves to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛto nu babaoo. Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni no haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do tiny cocoa pods on my trees turn black and dry up before growing into full pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ Ani mi tsei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ?

english: This is often cherelle wilt or black pod disease. Cherelle wilt happens naturally when the tree produces more pods than it has nutrients to feed, but high humidity and damp shade can also cause black pod fungus to destroy young pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji wilt loo black pod hela. Cherelle wilt baa yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji tso lɛ wo ŋmeii babaoo fe niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Shi hulutsoo ni fa kɛ hulutsoo be hu baanyɛ aha black pod fungus lɛ akpata pod bibii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why do my older cocoa trees produce plenty of flowers but fail to form any cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tso ni egbɔ lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewooo kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects called midges for pollination. If the ground under your trees is swept completely bare or sprayed heavily with harsh chemicals, these insects cannot survive, leaving flowers unpollinated so they fall off.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ nakai midge kɛha ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji akɛ he ni tso lɛ yɔɔ lɛ eje kpo kwraa loo akɛ tsofai ni mli wa efɔ nɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ nyɛŋ ahi shi. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: Why is it important for me to trim away extra branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ cacao tso ni eda lɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unproductive and overgrown branches, allowing sunlight and air to pass through the canopy. This dries out excessive dampness that causes black pod disease and ensures nutrients go into pod production.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni wooo yibii ni eda fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ atsɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli. Enɛ baajie ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni kɛ black pod drying hela baa lɛ. ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ boteɔ pod lɛ feemɔ mli

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant plantains on the same land as my new cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni aduɔ kookoo tsei heei lɛ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that create essential shade. This living cover shields sensitive young cocoa seedlings from harsh direct sunlight while keeping the surrounding soil cool and moist.
ga: Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa baa. Nɛkɛ nɔ ni wala yɔɔ mli nɛɛ buɔ cacao tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ.

english: Can I plant cassava directly next to my young cocoa trees while waiting for them to grow?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cassava yɛ cacao tso ko masɛi be mli ni mimɛɔ ni ekwɛ̃?

english: It is best to keep cassava away from young cocoa because cassava roots spread aggressively and suck out nutrients and water, while its dense leaves block the gentle light young cocoa needs.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ tapioca ato he ko ni kɛ kookoo ni mli jɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ. Enɛ ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni amɛmɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu. yɛ be mli ni ebaai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni kookoo ni mli ejɔ biɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning pale green and staying small even when rain falls heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni eyɛ bibii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain alone is not enough if the soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen. In fact, intense rain can wash existing plant food deeper down into the earth where young maize roots cannot reach it.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ pɛ faaa kɛji akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ tsei amli niyenii ni yɔɔ momo lɛ mli kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni ŋmãa shishifãi bibii nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during heavy wind and rainstorms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow, fibrous roots rather than deep taproots. When the ground becomes soaked and soft, strong winds can pull the weak root network right out of the soil.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni yɔɔ fiber moŋ fe shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni eyɛ blɛoo Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that feed on the leaves and spread plant viruses, depriving the leaves of strength and color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amɛshwãa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ehaa baai lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ su.

english: Why do weeds slow down the growth of my crops even if I give my farm plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ fioo lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa nu babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ.

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for soil nutrients and sunlight. Even with enough water, your main crops will grow slowly because the weeds are consuming the plant food in the soil.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la. Kɛji nu fa bɔ ni sa po Oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ hu baafee mlɛo ejaakɛ jwɛi miiye tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the big trees from my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct, intense sunlight and high heat. Leaving mature shade trees or planting plantains provides temporary shade, preserving soil humidity and protecting delicate young leaves from scorching until the plants establish deep roots.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Tsei ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo plantains ni aduɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo be kukuoo ko Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã kɛyashi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and dying before the corn is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani abele lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Maize requires nitrogen to stay green and healthy, so when soil nutrients run low, the plant moves available nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to nourish new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe koni ekɛha tsei heei ni yaa hiɛ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when the rainy season lasts too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need well-drained soil and cannot survive in waterlogged ground. Excess water blocks oxygen from reaching the roots, causing root cells to die and allowing soil fungus and bacteria to rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni enyɛŋ ehi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa lɛ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli wala yibii lɛ gboiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and sunken before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efoɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a calcium deficiency in the developing fruit, often triggered by irregular watering. When soil moisture fluctuates sharply, the plant cannot properly transport calcium to the growing tips of the fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake oya Tso lɛ nyɛŋ ekɛ calcium aya aduawai lɛ ashishigbɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and getting crinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids, thrips, or mites sucking sap from the undersides of the leaves, or by viral diseases spread by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early protects leaf growth and fruit yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebuɔ baai lɛ adalɛ kɛ aduawai ni baa lɛ he.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during strong winds when the fruit bunch grows big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli beni aduawai akui lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots rather than a deep taproot, making them top-heavy when bearing heavy fruit. Soft wet soil or root damage from pests like nematodes weakens the plant's hold in the ground, causing wind to push it over.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ moŋ fe shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ muji kɛ́ amɛwo yibii ni tsii. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ loo shishifãi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ nematodes fiteɔ lɛ baaha tso lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa kɛtsɔɔ mli.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines instead of letting them spread flat on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ tso nɔ moŋ fe ni mahã amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves into direct sunlight, maximizing their ability to make food through photosynthesis while keeping foliage off moist soil, which reduces fungal infections and leads to larger tubers.
ga: Staking haa hulu la shɛɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa nyɛmɔ ni akɛfeɔ niyenii kɛtsɔ fotosintɛsis nɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anaa koni ekahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji baa.

english: How does planting cowpeas alongside my maize help improve my soil quality?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with natural soil bacteria to capture nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil. As the cowpea roots and leaves decompose, they release this trapped nitrogen, feeding the surrounding maize crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ adebɔɔ mli sũ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛsaa lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji cowpea shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ fite lɛ Amɛjieɔ nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ kpo akɛ niyenii kɛha ŋmãa ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why do my newly sprouted tomato seedlings collapse at the stem and die suddenly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ gbeeɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: This is known as damping-off, a fungal disease common in wet, overcrowded nursery beds with poor airflow. Fungi attack the tender stem right at the soil level, causing it to rot and snap.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ damping. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ gbekɛbii ashihilɛhei ni efɔ ni eyi obɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli. Fungi lɛ tutuaa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. ha egbo ni ekumɔ

english: Why shouldn't I place fertilizer right against the stem of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ he ni bɛŋkɛɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the stem causes fertilizer burn because concentrated chemical salts draw moisture out of the plant's living tissue. Fertilizer should be placed a few inches away from the stem where root tips can safely absorb it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashã ejaakɛ tsofai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ fãji ni hiɛ ka lɛ amli. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ. ni shishifã lɛ naa baanyɛ aŋɔ shweshweeshwe

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crops are hungry for nitrogen, which is a vital nutrient for growth. It can also happen when heavy rains wash nutrients deep into the soil where roots cannot reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye onibii lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho niyenii mli nibii lɛ kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the branch before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by black pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, wet conditions. Clearing weeds and pruning shade trees to let in sunlight and airflow helps keep the pods healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei ni haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up tightly like tiny cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the juices from the leaves, or by a virus carried by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ hiɛɔ lɛ anɔ

english: What causes my cassava roots to rot in the soil before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kpamɔ be baashɛ?

english: Root rot happens when soil holds too much standing water during heavy rains or when fungal diseases in the soil attack the tubers. Planting on raised mounds helps water drain away safely.
ga: Shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli loo kɛji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ tutua ŋmeii lɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain suckers next to my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? kookoo dumɔwui heei

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly and provide huge leaves that act as natural umbrellas, shading the cocoa and keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha kookoo lɛ nɔ ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Is it better for me to plant my yam and cassava on raised mounds rather than flat land?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ?

english: Raised mounds loosen the soil so root crops can expand easily. Mounds also prevent water from collecting around the roots and causing them to rot during rainstorms.
ga: Gɔŋ ni awo nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo. Gɔŋ lɛ hu tsiɔ nu naa koni ekabua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is rich enough to feed my crops well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli tse bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Rich soil is usually dark brown or black, crumbles easily in your hand, holds moisture without staying swampy, and contains earthworms or decaying organic matter.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ mli ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli. ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fiteɔ yɛ jɛmɛ

english: Why should I clear small weeds early when they do not seem to be harming my crops yet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi bibii lɛ mra be mli ni etamɔ nɔ ni amɛyeee miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer from the soil. Removing them early stops them from starving your crops while they are young and weak.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni hɔmɔ akaye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be mli ni amɛdarako ni amɛbɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo tomato ko lɛ?

english: Tomato plants often drop flowers during periods of extreme heat, prolonged drought, or when heavy rains prevent bees from pollinating the flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ laajeɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ Aloo be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tsiɔ ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow plenty of big green leaves but produce very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes bean plants focus all their energy on leaf growth instead of making flowers and pods. High temperatures during flowering can also stop pod formation.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii. Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ baanyɛ akpa pod feemɔ.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to space our maize seeds instead of planting them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ato he ko moŋ fe ni wɔbaadu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures each maize plant has enough room to spread its roots and capture sunshine. When planted too close together, crops fight each other for soil nutrients and light, resulting in thin stalks and smaller cobs.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ eshishifãi lɛ agbɛɔ eshwaa ni enáa hulu la. Kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ la. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my cassava plants when they are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Kasava tso lɛ beni eji gbekɛ fioo lɛ?

english: Young cassava plants have weak, small root systems that cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for sunlight, water, and soil food. Clearing weeds early allows the crop to establish strong roots that will later yield large tubers.
ga: Cassava tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni baawo ŋmeii wuji sɛɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for leaf growth. It can also happen when heavy rain saturates the soil, preventing roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi sũ lɛ mli obɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛkaye nii.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt during the hot afternoon even when the ground is not completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbiko kwraa moŋ?

english: During intense afternoon heat, pepper leaves lose water through evaporation faster than their roots can pull it up from the ground. As long as the soil has moisture, the plant usually recovers in the cooler evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, tsei lɛ he baajɔ amɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their leaves and develop black spots on the fruit during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ baai ni amɛhe feɔ diji yɛ amɛyibii lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: High humidity and continuous moisture during the rainy season create perfect conditions for fungal diseases like late blight. The fungus attacks the leaves and spreads to the fruit, causing dark rot patches.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni yaa nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ late blight. Fuŋ lɛ tutuaa baai lɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa aduawai lɛ anɔ. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ diŋ baa.

english: How do I tell if my yam leaf damage is caused by insects or by a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmeii loo helai ji nɔ ni kɛ mi sweet potato baa lɛ fitemɔ ba?

english: Insects usually leave physical signs such as holes, chewed edges, or visible bugs on the leaf. Plant diseases typically cause color changes, spots, powdery coatings, or whole-leaf wilting without any tissue missing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii shĩɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii, tamɔ bu, ŋmeii ni ŋmɔɔ, loo kooloi bibii ni anaa ni ŋmɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Bei pii lɛ, tsei ahe helai haa amɛhe su tsakeɔ, amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔtɔ, amɛfeɔ powda, loo amɛbaa lɛ shwieɔ shi kwraa ni fã ko bɛ ni elaaje.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers dry up and fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they experience water stress, lack sufficient nutrients, or when there are not enough tiny insects like midges around to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji amɛkɛ nu he haomɔ kpe. Niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni bɛ Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii, tamɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ bɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans in my field help the next maize crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When the legume plants decay, they leave behind natural nitrogen fertilizer that nourishes heavy feeders like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji ŋmeii lɛ fite lɛ Amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ŋmeii ni haa kooloi ni yeɔ niyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily before the bunches are ripe for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya dani ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that can be weakened by tiny soil pests like nematodes or weevils. When heavy fruit bunches grow, strong winds can easily topple trees with compromised roots.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ nematodes loo weevils baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ. Beni aduawai babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ aku tsei ni shishifãi efite lɛ ashwie shi mlɛo.

english: What causes my watermelon fruits to split open on the farm right before they are ready to pick?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-watermelons lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa amɛ?

english: Watermelons split when there is a sudden burst of heavy rain after a dry period. The plant absorbs a large amount of water quickly, making the inside of the fruit expand faster than the skin can stretch.
ga: Watermelons tswaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ. Tsei shwieɔ nu babaoo oya. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ amli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do tiny insects suddenly appear in huge numbers on my crops during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo baa trukaa yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Many crop pests, like aphids and whiteflies, reproduce extremely fast in warm weather because heat speeds up their life cycle. A few insects can multiply into thousands within days, sucking sap and weakening your crops.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui babaoo tamɔ aphids kɛ whiteflies Amɛfɔɔ oya waa yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dɔlɛ haa amɛshihilɛ yaa oya. Kplukai fioo komɛi pɛ baanyɛ ashwere ni amɛfee akpei abɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli. Ekɛ nu lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to walk through my field and inspect under the leaves regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔji amli daa ni makwɛ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Pests and fungal diseases usually start on the underside of crop leaves or inside young shoots. Checking your farm twice a week allows you to spot small outbreaks early before they spread to the whole field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai jeɔ shishi yɛ tsei ahe baai ashishi loo yɛ tsei bibii amli. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii. Na kɛjɛ shishijee dani egbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ

english: Why do fall armyworms cause so much damage to young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ fiteɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms hide inside the central funnel of young maize plants and eat the growing point. Because they feed hidden inside, they destroy the plant's ability to grow leaves and produce ears if not stopped early.
ga: Fall worms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ hei ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛyeɔ niyenii ni akɛtee mli. No hewɔ lɛ amɛfiteɔ nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛbaakwɛ baai ni ekɛbaawo toi lɛ kɛji akpaaa oya.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants roll up into tight tubes during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tsɔnei ni mli wa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?
