english: Maize leaves roll up to protect themselves from losing moisture when the heat is extreme. It acts like a defense mechanism to conserve water inside the plant until the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ shi koni ŋmɔtɔ akaje mli yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni haa nu hiɔ tso lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo baa.

english: How does water help my crops take up plant food from the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛjieɔ tsei amli niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Crops cannot absorb solid nutrients from the dirt. Water dissolves the fertilizers and soil minerals so the plant's roots can suck them up and transport food to the stems, leaves, and fruit.
ga: Tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni mli wa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nu shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shika tsuru ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei ashishifãi gbalaa niyenii kɛyaa amɛshishifãi lɛ, baai lɛ, kɛ aduawai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my crops die when rain water stands around their stems for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Crop roots need oxygen from the air gaps in the soil to stay alive. When standing water covers the roots for too long, the roots drown, stop taking up nutrients, and begin to rot.
ga: Tsei shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ nu ni ekã shi lɛ ha shishifãi lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, amɛkpaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ.

english: How can using a water pump or irrigation system help my vegetables during the dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu pɔmp loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: An irrigation system provides a steady water supply when there is no rain, allowing crops to grow continuously so you can harvest and sell when market prices are highest.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ haa nu lɛ yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii daa. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okpa ni ohɔ̃ɔ be mli ni jara lɛ nɔ jara wa fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know the right amount of space to leave between my crops when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male he ni sa ni esa akɛ mashi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ kɛ́ midu nii?

english: Proper spacing ensures each crop gets enough sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. If you plant crops too close together, they struggle and compete with each other, resulting in thin stems and small yields.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Kɛji odu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Ebaawuu ni ekɛ ehe awo akaŋshii mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before growing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed flowers when they suffer from stress caused by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. The plant drops its flowers to preserve energy to survive.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do weeds make my young crops grow so slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔwui lɛ daraa blɛoo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and aggressively steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer from the soil. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to food so they can grow strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii kwraa. bɔni afee ni amɛná shishifãi ni wa

english: What does grafting a tree seedling actually mean, and why should I do it instead of planting seeds?
ga: Mɛni dumɔwu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ tsɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafee yɛ dumɔwui adumɔ najiaŋ?

english: Grafting joins a branch from a strong, high-yielding adult tree onto the root system of a sturdy young plant. This allows your new tree to grow faster and produce high-quality fruit much sooner than starting from a plain seed.
ga: Nɔ ni fata tso ni akɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ he ji ni akɛ tso ni eda ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ niji kɛ tso bibioo ko ni yɔɔ hewalɛ shishifãi lɛ afee ekome. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa otso hee lɛ ni edaa oya ni ewoɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ oya fe bɔ ni ooobɔi dumɔwui ni aduɔ daa lɛ.

english: Why do grafted tree seedlings bear fruit much earlier than trees grown directly from seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ woɔ yibii oya fe tsei ni jɛ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: A grafted seedling uses a branch taken from a mature tree that is already genetically ready to produce fruit. Because the branch retains its maturity, the plant flowers and fruits years faster than a seedling starting from scratch.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ kɛ tsei niji ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni eda ni amɛfɔmɔ nii efee klalo akɛ amɛbaawo yibii lɛ tsuɔ nii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei niji lɛ miida kwraa lolo. Tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii afii komɛi mra fe dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛ shishijee.

english: Can I just cut a branch from a healthy fruit tree and push it into the soil to grow a new tree?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafo tso ni woɔ yibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ nine ni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ koni tso hee akwɛ̃?

english: Most tree branches will rot or die if stuck directly into the soil because they lack roots to draw water. Joining that branch onto a healthy rootstock through grafting provides the roots it needs to survive.
ga: Tsoi aniji babaoo baagboi loo amɛbaagboi kɛji akɛ amɛkpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ ejaakɛ amɛbɛ shishifãi ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛjie nu kɛjɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nakai tso nine lɛ fata shishifã ni yɔɔ hewalɛ he kɛtsɔ tso ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ená shishifãi ni he hiaa lɛ koni ehi shi.

english: Do I need to buy expensive chemical fertilizers before planting my new young trees?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mahe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni jara wa dani madu dumɔwui heei?

english: No, young tree seedlings usually do not need heavy chemical fertilizers right at planting. Mixing rich topsoil and natural organic matter into the planting hole gives roots enough natural food to establish safely without chemical burns.
ga: Dabi, bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui bibii lɛ he ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai babaoo awo mli koni amɛkwɛ̃. Shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni jara wa kɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛfutuɔ dumɔ bu lɛ mli lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aná adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛma shi shweshweeshwe ni tsofai ni akɛshãa amɛhe ehiaaa.

english: How do I care for a young grafted tree seedling during its first few months in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ dumɔwui bibii ni akɛwo amɛmli lɛ anɔ yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli?

english: Young tree seedlings need regular watering, protection from harsh sunlight, clear soil around their bases free of competing weeds, and gentle handling to keep the graft joint from snapping.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ he miihia ni afɔ amɛ nu daa. Buu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he. Shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ mli tse ni jwɛi bɛ mli. kɛ kwɛmɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo koni fã ni akɛwo mli lɛ akakumɔ.

english: How can I tell if my soil is healthy enough to support young tree crops without chemical additives?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ tsei bibii ni mikɛ tsofai tsuuu nii?

english: Healthy farm soil is dark in color, crumbles easily in your hand, holds moisture well, and contains earthworms or decaying plant matter, which naturally feeds new roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kpakpa mli lɛ yɛ diŋŋ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii, loo tsei amli nibii ni fiteɔ, ni jɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ naa niyenii kɛhaa shishifãi heei lɛ yɛ.

english: Why are insect pests damaging my young tree leaves even when the trees are very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai miifite mi tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ tsei lɛ daraaa kwraa moŋ?

english: Pests love young trees because tender new leaves and green shoots are soft and easy to eat. Insects are naturally attracted to fresh growth, especially during warm, rainy weather.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ sumɔɔ tsei bibii ejaakɛ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi heei lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyeli waaa. Bei pii lɛ, koolooi sumɔɔ dalɛ hee, titri lɛ yɛ be mli ni edɔ, ni nugbɔ nɛɔ.

english: Is it possible to protect my crops from harmful insects without spending money on chemical sprays?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ abu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe ni afiteee shika yɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, keeping your field clear of tall weeds, picking off infected leaves early, and keeping the farm clean helps prevent pest outbreaks naturally without immediate chemical sprays.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔji ni jwɛi kakadaji bɛ mli lɛ ni abaakwɛ nɔ. Ni oooŋɔ baai ni hela emɔ amɛ mra Ni oooha ŋmɔ lɛ mli atse lɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akaje kpo yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai afɔse nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do pests attack my crops more heavily during certain seasons of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ afi lɛ mli bei komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Pest numbers increase sharply during humid rainy seasons because warm, moist weather helps insect eggs hatch quickly, and young plant growth provides abundant food.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ yaa hiɛ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Enɛ ji akɛ, shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yeɔ ebuaa kooloi awɔlɔi ni amɛfɔ̃ɔ oya. Ni tsei bibii ni daraa lɛ hu ji niyenii babaoo jɛɛhe.

english: Why should I change my planting techniques if my family has farmed the traditional way for years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake bɔ ni miduɔ nii mihaa lɛ kɛji akɛ miweku lɛ hu miitsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ? Afii babaoo nɛ?

english: Changing weather patterns, worn-out soil, and tougher pests mean old methods may no longer yield as much. Modern techniques like grafting and improved land setup help protect your yields under current conditions.
ga: kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yaa nɔ shikpɔŋ ni efite kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni naa wa waa Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ gbɛi momo lɛ wooo yibii tamɔ nɛkɛ dɔŋŋ. Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋaai tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ahe saamɔ baaye abua ni abu onibii ahe yɛ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ amrɔ nɛɛ amli.

english: How long can I leave my planting materials stored in a bag before putting them in the ground?
ga: Be enyiɛ manyɛ mashi tso lɛ mli nibii lɛ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli dani mikɛwo shikpɔŋ?

english: You can store certain seeds or planting materials in bags for several weeks, such as 6 weeks, but keeping them too long without proper timing can cause them to spoil before you plant.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui loo nibii ni aduɔ lɛ awo kotoku lɛ mli otsii babaoo, tamɔ otsii 6, shi kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui to be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni be ni sa bɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha efite dani adu.

english: Why do my seeds start sprouting when I pour water on them while they are still in a bag?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo mli be mli ni amɛyɔɔ kotoku lɛ mli lolo lɛ?

english: Seeds stay dormant until moisture wakes them up. Adding water gives the seed the signal and hydration it needs to break its outer shell and start germinating.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ wɔɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ teɔ amɛ shi. Nu ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa okadi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛgbala kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli ni amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Is it helpful to let my crop seeds start sprouting in a bag before I take them to the farm?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ maha mi aduawai dumɔwui lɛ aje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli dani mikɛ amɛ aya ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, pre-germinating seeds in a controlled place allows you to see which ones are alive and healthy so you only spend time planting seeds that will actually grow.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni akudɔɔ lɛ haa onaa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ wala mli lolo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni baakwɛ̃ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ pɛ he miihia bo.

english: How can I tell that my seeds in the bag are ready to be planted in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Once you apply water and see small white roots or tiny sprouts popping out of the seed, it means germination has started and it is time to move them into the earth.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo nɔ lɛ onaa shishifãi bibii yɛŋ. loo ŋmeii bibii ni jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii eje shishi. Ni be eshɛ ni esa akɛ ajie amɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Will my seeds spoil if I keep them inside a closed bag for many weeks?
ga: Ani midumɔwui lɛ baagbo kɛji mikɛwo kotoku ko ni aŋã mli otsii babaoo?

english: If seeds are kept completely dry and stored properly, they can rest for about 6 weeks safely, but if moisture enters too early, mold and rot will destroy them.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akwɛ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ ni amɛgbi kwraa ni akɛto jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔwui baanyɛ ajɔɔ amɛhe shweshweeshwe aaafee otsii 6, shi kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ba oya tsɔ pɛ. Muji kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baafite dumɔwui lɛ.

english: At what point during seed storage should I add water to make them start growing?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ nu afata he yɛ dumɔwui lɛ anaabuamɔ be mli koni dumɔwui lɛ aje shishi amɛkwɛ̃?

english: You should keep seeds dry during their resting weeks and only add water about a week before you intend to plant so they germinate right on schedule.
ga: Esa akɛ oha dumɔwui lɛ agbi yɛ otsi ni akɛjɔɔ he lɛ mli. Ni okɛ nu afata he aaafee otsi kome pɛ dani oto gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaadu koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: What is the difference between planting dry seeds straight into my field versus sprouting them first?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni egbi ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dani akwɛ̃ɔ lɛ teŋ?

english: Direct planting relies entirely on soil rain, whereas sprouting seeds first gives the young plants a head start so they establish faster once placed in the field.
ga: Dumɔ tɛ̃ɛ damɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ kwraa. Yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ ehaa dumɔwui lɛ yitso shishijee. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛwo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, amɛbaakwɛ̃ oya.

english: Can I still get a good harvest if I plant weak or poor-quality seeds on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ maná ŋmaa kpakpa lolo kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni ehiii kwraa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, what you sow is what you reap. A healthy, high-yielding crop depends directly on starting with strong, good-quality seed material.
ga: Dabi, nɔ ni oduɔ lɛ, no nɔŋŋ okpaa. Nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ damɔ dumɔwui ni mli wa, ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛjeɔ shishi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it important to choose the right planting material before going to the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ahala nibii ni sa ni akɛbaadu nii dani abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Your final yield depends entirely on the initial quality of the crop material you sow, so selecting bad material guarantees a poor harvest regardless of your effort.
ga: Onaagbee yibiiwoo lɛ damɔ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ hi ha shishijee lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, nibii ni ahalaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa ŋmaakpamɔ ni ehiii baa, bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni ooofee obɔ mɔdɛŋ oha.

english: Why do my newly sprouted seeds need moisture in the soil as soon as I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ he hiaa shikpɔŋ nɔ nu kɛji midu amɛ pɛ?

english: Freshly sprouted seed roots are very delicate; without soil moisture, the new shoots will quickly dry up and die before establishing roots.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ ashishifãi lɛ waaa kwraa. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tsei heei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni amɛgboiɔ dani shishifãi baa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when the sun gets very bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and weak root systems that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Covering or shading them with temporary plants like plantains protects them until their roots grow deep enough to absorb water and withstand the heat.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei tamɔ plantains ha tso lɛ he loo okɛwo mli be kukuoo ko lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso lɛ he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ nu ni amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my maize crops are getting enough food from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ miiná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛmiijɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Healthy maize plants have thick stems and bright, dark green leaves. If the leaves begin to turn pale yellow starting from the tips down the center, it usually means the plant lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen and needs feeding.
ga: Abele tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ tsei ni mli wa kɛ baai ni kpɛɔ, eŋɔli ni tsuɔ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛyitseiaŋ kɛyaa amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, ni niyenii he miihia lɛ.

english: Why should I leave space between my crops instead of planting them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with one another for soil nutrients, groundwater, and sunlight. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough air, light, and food to grow strong and produce a good yield.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ mli, kɛ hulu la lɛ mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa kɔɔyɔɔ, la, kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do I need to nurse tomato seeds in a small seedbed before moving them to the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu tomato dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli lɛ? dani amɛfã kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli

english: Tomato seeds are very small and fragile, making them easy targets for heavy rains and pests. Nursing them allows you to protect and care for the tender sprouts until they are strong enough to survive transfer to the main field.
ga: Tomato dumɔwui lɛ daraaa kwraa ni amɛhe waaa. Enɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he oya. Nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ haa onyɛɔ obuɔ dumɔwui bibii ahe ni okwɛɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛwo saatso wulu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds from around my young crops regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Ehe miihia ni madu tsei bibii daa.

english: Weeds grow fast and steal food, water, and sunlight away from your main crops. Keeping the base of your young plants clean ensures all available soil nutrients go directly into growing your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ aha tsei bibii lɛ ashishi he tse lɛ, ehaa sũ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ baashɛ tso lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why is it bad to plant cassava on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmei yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the soil of the specific nutrients that crop needs and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating crops keeps the soil healthy and prevents pest infestation.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my maize seeds after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eho lɛ?

english: You should wait until the main rains have settled and the soil stays damp for several days. Planting immediately after the very first light rainfall can cause seeds to dry up and fail if a brief drought follows.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔi wuji lɛ aba shi ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbii babaoo. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛkafee nɔ ko kɛji hɔmɔ kuku ko ba.

english: Why do extension officers advise cutting off some branches from mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ afo kookoo niji ni eda lɛ ekomɛi amli lɛ?

english: Pruning removes old, shaded, or diseased branches, allowing air and sunlight to reach inside the tree canopy. Good airflow reduces humidity, which helps prevent fungal diseases like black pod from spreading.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egbɔ, ni yɔɔ shade, loo ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ashɛ tso lɛ mligbɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi, ni no yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pods lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids hidden under the leaves, or by a virus carried by insects. Early inspection helps you spot these pests before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni kooloi kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Kwɛmɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ haa onyɛɔ onaa nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfiteɔ onibii.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and collapse before the bunch matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi dani panicles lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Yellowing and collapsing leaves can be a sign of root damage caused by pests like nematodes or fungal diseases like wilt. Damaged roots cannot supply water to the heavy top leaves, causing them to wither early.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ afee okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ efite ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ nematodes loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛbaa. Shishifãi ni efite lɛ nyɛɛɛ aha ŋwɛi baai ni tsii lɛ nu. ha amɛgbi oya

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because their tender leaves burn easily under full sun. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains next to them creates a natural umbrella that provides shade and keeps the soil moist while the cocoa establishes.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta ni haa hulutsoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ baa.

english: How do I know when my cassava crops are fully mature and ready for harvesting underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready to harvest between 9 to 12 months after planting. You will see the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem will swell and crack as the tubers grow large.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaana akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ baafu ni egbɛ eshwa kɛ́ tso lɛ mli ŋmei lɛ da.

english: Where do I get new plants from after I harvest a full pineapple fruit?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ maná tso hee yɛ beni mikpa mi-pineapple lɛ sɛɛ?

english: After harvesting the main fruit, the pineapple plant naturally produces small shoots called suckers or slips along its stem. Once these shoots grow to about 30 centimeters tall, you can break them off and plant them in the ground to grow new pineapple plants.
ga: Beni akpa aduawai titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Pineapple tsei lɛ baawo ŋmeii bibii. Atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bibii. naturally along the trunk Kɛ́ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ dara kɛyashɛ aaafee sɛntimita 30 lɛ, obaanyɛ ogbala amɛmli ni okɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ŋmeii tso hee aba.

english: Why should I avoid planting maize on the exact same land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ŋmãa dumɔ he afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot drains essential nutrients like nitrogen from the soil and allows maize pests to multiply in the ground. Rotating maize with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa abɛi mli tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ lɛ mli.

english: How do groundnuts and beans help improve poor soil for my other crops?
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii haa shikpɔŋ ni ehiii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi. Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná minɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which can trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant roots decay in the ground after harvest, they release natural nitrogen fertilizer that nourishes future crops.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni tso shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Amɛjieɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How can I protect my crops from drying out quickly when the rains stop for a few weeks?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni amɛkagbi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii fioo komɛi?

english: You can cover the bare soil around your crops with dry grass, straw, or leaves, a method called mulching. This organic cover prevents sunlight from drying out the ground, keeps root temperatures low, and retains moisture in the soil much longer.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ sũ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko awo ehe. Akɛ jwɛi, jwɛi loo baai duɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Nɛkɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli nɛɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ha shishifãi lɛ amli dɔlɛ aba shi. ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ

english: Should I apply chemical fertilizer to my seeds right on the day I plant them?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ midumɔwui lɛ amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ dumɔ gbi lɛ nɔ?

english: It is best to wait about two weeks after seeds sprout before applying fertilizer like NPK. Seeds contain their own starting energy, and applying strong chemical fertilizer too early can burn the young, delicate roots before they are ready to absorb nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ aaafee otsi enyɔ beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK awo mli. Dumɔwui yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ shishijee hewalɛ. Ni kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni mli edɔ fata he oya tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants showing small holes and light yellow streaks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni linei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ?

english: Holes and yellowing on young maize leaves are common signs of Fall Armyworm feeding or a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Checking the central shoots for tiny caterpillars early in the morning helps you catch the pest early before it destroys the crop.
ga: Bu kɛ ŋmãa bibii ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadii ni afɔɔ naa yɛ Fall Armyworm niyenii loo nitrogen ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he. Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli kɛji ŋmeii bibii yɛ mli. Yɛ leebi lɛ ebaaye ebua bo ni omɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ mra. dani ekpata ŋmɔshi nibii ahiɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and causing the plants to stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle ehe ni eha tso lɛ miikpa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is typically caused by microscopic insects like whiteflies or mites that suck plant sap and spread viral diseases. Spraying the plants early with neem leaf extract helps control these insects and protects the remaining healthy leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii waa tamɔ whiteflies loo mites ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ helai amli baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Ni akɛ neem baa mli nu lɛ baashwie tsei anɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ ni ebu baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it unsafe for me to plant my seeds right after the very first rainy day of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ebɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ gbi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The very first rainfall of the season is often followed by a long sunny spell that can dry out newly sprouted seeds in the ground. Waiting until two or three steady rains have fallen ensures the soil has enough deep moisture to support continuous seedling growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni eye ebua dumɔwui ni yaa nɔ amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do my maize crops turn yellow and stop growing when water stays on my field for too long after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa kwɛ̃mɔ beni nu hiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crop roots need to breathe air just like human beings do. When excess water sits on the field, it pushes out air from the soil, suffocating the roots so they cannot absorb nutrients, which makes the leaves turn yellow.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, ehe miihia ni tsei shishifãi amu kɔɔyɔɔ. Kɛ nu babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ Ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyashɛɔ he ko ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhe niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Why do my vegetable crops grow much better in loose soil compared to hard, packed-down ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ he lɛ?

english: Loose soil leaves tiny spaces for air and water to move freely, allowing the roots to spread easily and take in oxygen. Hard, packed soil blocks root growth and starves the plant of air.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii bibii baa. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu aya he fɛɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa mlɛo ni amɛnáa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ adalɛ naa ni ehaa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Is it better to pour water forcefully on my young pepper plants or let it flow gently around them?
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha ŋmɔtɔ tsei bibii lɛ nu waa. aloo ha eho kɛbɔle dumɔwui lɛ ahe

english: Watering too forcefully can break delicate stems, wash away topsoil, and expose roots to direct sun. A gentle flow lets the soil absorb water deeply down to where the roots need it.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli waa lɛ baanyɛ akumɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Nu ni hoɔ blɛoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ nu lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyashɛɔ he ni shishifãi lɛ he hiaa yɛ lɛ.

english: Does the quality of water I draw from a local stream or well really affect how my crops grow?
ga: Ani bɔ ni nu ni mijieɔ kɛjɛɔ maŋ lɛ mli faa ko mli lɛ hi ha lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ he?

english: Yes, water can carry unseen salts, chemicals, or poor balance that damages crop roots and stops them from feeding, causing stunted growth even if you water them every day.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu baanyɛ atere ŋmeii ni anaaa, tsofai, loo nibii ni esaaa. Enɛ fiteɔ tsei ashishifãi ni ehaaa amɛye nii. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛji okɛ nu wo enɔ daa gbi po.

english: I hear people talk about soil being 'sour' or 'sweet'—how does that affect my tomatoes?
ga: Minuɔ mɛi ni wieɔ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni ‘mli edɔ’ loo ‘mli ŋɔɔ’ lɛ saa mi tomatoi lɛ ahe lɛ he.

english: Soil 'sourness' or 'sweetness' refers to its pH balance. If the soil is too sour or too alkaline, crop roots cannot swallow the food and nutrients in the dirt, causing poor growth even if you add fertilizer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ‘ŋmɔlɔ’ loo ‘ŋmɔlɔ’ lɛ tsɔɔ bɔ ni pH lɛ yɔɔ ha. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo eyɛ alkaline tsɔ lɛ, Tso shishifãi nyɛŋ ami niyenii kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haaa eda jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ okɛ fɔ wo mli po.

english: Why should I send my soil or water to a lab for testing before planting a new crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mishikpɔŋ loo mi nu lɛ amaje laboratori ko koni aka lɛ akwɛ dani madu tsei heei?

english: A lab test acts like a doctor's check-up for your farm; it reveals hidden problems like incorrect soil balance or missing nutrients so you do not waste money buying the wrong fertilizers.
ga: Lab kaai tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsofafeemɔ mli kwɛmɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ejieɔ naagbai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ, tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni ejaaa loo niyenii mli nibii ni bɛ mli lɛ kpo. No hewɔ lɛ ehe ehiaaa ni ofite shika kɛhe ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa.

english: How can I tell if my cassava crop is healthy while it is still growing underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ yɛ hewalɛ be mli ni amɛmiida lolo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Healthy cassava plants show bright green leaves, firm stems, and steady growth without dark spots or sudden leaf dropping, which tells you the roots underneath are developing well.
ga: Cassava tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ, amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ, kɛ dalɛ ni yaa nɔ ni ŋmeii diji loo baai ni laajeɔ trukaa bɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can putting too much fresh chicken manure on my crops harm them?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmɔtɔ hee ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aye amɛ awui?

english: Yes, fresh manure contains very strong raw gases like ammonia that can burn crop roots and leaves. It is best to let manure dry out and break down completely before applying it to your fields.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ewo muji tamɔ ammonia, ni baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ fa babaoo yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei amli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni efite dani okɛwo oŋmɔji amli.

english: Why does compost need time to rot before I mix it into my crop beds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii aheɔ be dani efiteɔ dani akɛfutuɔ midumɔ saatsoi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: As compost rots, natural organisms break down harsh chemical compounds into safe, gentle nutrients that plant roots can easily absorb without getting burned.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fite lɛ, nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ gbálaa tsofai ni mli wa lɛ amli kɛfeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni yɔɔ blɛoo. ni tso shishifãi baanyɛ aŋɔ oya ni ashãaa lɛ

english: Why do the leaves on my garden crops change colour even when I give them enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ mli lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsake amɛhe eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Colour changes often mean the crop is starving for specific nutrients or cannot absorb them due to poor soil conditions, showing that water alone is not enough for plant health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ su ni tsakeɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ko bɛ tso lɛ mli loo enyɛɛɛ eŋɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu pɛ faaa kɛha tsei ahewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and falling off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the Harmattan or dry season, high heat and low humidity cause young cocoa trees to lose moisture quickly. Without adequate shade trees to protect them, the cocoa leaves burn, turn yellow, and drop off so the tree can conserve remaining water.
ga: Yɛ harmattan loo hulutsoo be mli lɛ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulutsoo be ni baa shi lɛ haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ amli hulutsoo lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Kɛji tsei bɛ ni baaha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baabu amɛhe lɛ, Cocoa baai lɛ baashã. tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbee shi koni ekɛbu nu ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do cocoa flowers grow directly on the main trunk and thick branches instead of the branch tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ kɛ niji ni mli tse lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ niji lɛ anaagbee lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally flower on their main trunk and thick branches (a trait called cauliflory) because cocoa pods become very heavy as they mature. The strong wood of the trunk provides the support needed to hold the heavy fruit load until harvest.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ amɛtso wulu lɛ nɔ kɛ tsei niji ni mli tse lɛ anɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. (Atsɛɔ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ akɛ cauliflower) ejaakɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ tsii kɛji amɛdara kwraa. Tso ni mli wa ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ fiɔ aduawai ni tsii lɛ ashishi kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning purple?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ purple lɛ?

english: Purple leaves on young maize plants usually mean the soil is lacking phosphorus. Phosphorus is a critical nutrient for early root development, and when plants cannot access enough of it, they show stress by turning purple.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Fosforo ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha shishifãi lɛ akwɛmɔ mra. ni be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ fɔsfɔs ni fa bɔ ni sa Ebaajie haomɔ kpo kɛtsɔ purple ni eeetsɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are there small holes in my maize leaves and visible worms hiding in the center funnel of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ani ŋmeii ni anaa yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the soft, young center leaves of the maize plant to feed, which can stunt the growth of the crop if they are not controlled early.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei ahe baai bibii lɛ amli koni amɛye niyenii. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tsei adalɛ naa kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ amɛ mra.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of green leaves but yield tiny cassava tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ miiya hiɛ waa nɛkɛ? Baai eŋɔlii babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. Shi ŋmeii bibii komɛi yɛ jɛmɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, the cassava plant directs all its energy into growing top foliage (leaves and stems) instead of storing food in the underground root tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ baato niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa etso lɛ nɔ (baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ).

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds and stake my yam vines with wooden poles after they sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ kɛjɛ mihe lɛ? ni okɛ tsei awo sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahe beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ.

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need height to spread their leaves toward sunlight. Staking allows the leaves to trap solar energy to make food, which is then sent down into the ground to build big, heavy yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛkwɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaa lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛkɛ hulu lɛ akpee. Staking haa baai lɛ mɔ̃ɔ hulu hewalɛ kɛha nihoomɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, akɛyaa shikpɔŋ koni efee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do the blossom flowers on my tomato plants dry up and drop off without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛfeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and erratic watering cause stress to tomato plants, preventing successful pollination. When temperature spikes occur, the flower cannot set fruit and simply drops off off the vine.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haaa anyɛ afee pollination yɛ omanyeyeli mli. Kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ waa lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛŋ awo yibii ni amɛbaajɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ amɛgbee shi.

english: Upward curling in pepper leaves is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips. As these insects feed on the sap, they weaken the leaves and can spread plant viruses that distort growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ nu nu Amɛhaa baai lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ tsei amli helai ni fiteɔ amɛdalɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoot suckers growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishitoo lɛ

english: Multiple suckers growing from one plantain stem fight each other for water and soil nutrients. Pruning extra suckers to leave only one strong successor ensures the main plant gets enough energy to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni jɛɔ dumɔwu kome mli baa lɛ baawu koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ nu lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ koni sɛɛyelɔ kome pɛ ni he wa ahi shi lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do officers advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm before planting my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their root nodules. When the crop season finishes, this leaves free, natural fertility in the soil for heavy feeding crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji dumɔ be lɛ ba naagbee Ebaajie shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ niyenii babaoo tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why should I leave clear walking paths between my crop rows instead of planting seeds in every open space?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛjegbɛi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni mikɛnyiɛɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, mo du dumi ngɛ he fɛɛ he nɛ a ngɛ hɛ mi nyami ɔ.

english: Leaving clear pathways ensures that sunlight and air can reach all sides of your plants, preventing diseases from building up and making it easy for you to inspect, tend to, and harvest your farm without stepping on crops.
ga: Gbɛ ni mli ka shi faŋŋ ni oyɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ ashɛ otsei lɛ afãi fɛɛ. Tsĩ helai anaa ni ehaa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ, okwɛɔ nɔ, ni okpaa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ oya ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ onaji afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɔkɔɔkɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear away all the big trees from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have weak root systems and delicate leaves that easily burn under direct hot sun; they rely on shade trees to keep the air humid and the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛkɛ amɛhe fɔɔ tsei ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on to give me big tubers under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei he hiaa tsei ni amɛkwɔ koni amɛ bulbs wuji lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Yam leaves make food using sunlight, and lifting the leaves off the ground on stakes allows them to catch maximum sunlight and stay dry, directing more energy into growing large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛhooɔ nii. Ni kɛ́ awó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa hulu la ni fe fɛɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ. Enɛ haa akɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with lush green leaves, but the tubers underground are thin and small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛji bibii?

english: When crops get too much shade or too much leaf-growing nutrients in the soil, the plant uses all its energy to expand its leaves above ground rather than storing food in the roots below.
ga: Kɛ́ tso ko ná hulutsoo babaoo loo niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɛ mli lɛ, baai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying off before the corn cobs are ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves show that the plant has used up the nitrogen in the soil and is forced to steal food from its lower leaves to keep growing the corn cob at the top.
ga: Baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kɛ nitrogen fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ etsu nii. ni anyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛju niyenii kɛjɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ŋmãa lɛ aya nɔ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and look limp during the hot afternoon even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo moŋ?

english: Tomato plants curl their leaves in extreme heat as a natural defense to stop water from evaporating too fast from their skin, and they usually recover once the sun cools down in the evening.
ga: Tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ amɛhe nɔ koni nu akajɛ amɛhewolo lɛ nɔ oya tsɔ. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow and spread much faster than my crop plants right after the rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Wild weeds have naturally deep and tough root systems that are built to soak up water and soil food immediately, allowing them to overpower your young crops if they are not cleared early.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni wa ni ama koni ekɛjie nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa amɛyeɔ onibii bibii lɛ anɔ kunim kɛji akɛ ajieee amɛ mra.

english: Why should I cut my pepper pods with a sharp tool instead of twisting and pulling them off with my hands?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ afo pepper pods lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ onine atsɔ mli ni okɛjie lɛ.

english: Pulling peppers off by hand snaps off healthy branches and tears the stem tissue, leaving open wounds where plant diseases enter and stopping new flowers from forming.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ onine gbala ŋmeii lɛ, ebaakumɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli ni ebaagbala tso lɛ shishi fãji lɛ. Eshiɔ pilamɔi ni agbele yɛ he ni tso helai boteɔ mli lɛ, ni ehaaa fɔfɔi heei afee.

english: How can I tell that my green plantains are ready to harvest before they turn yellow and get eaten by birds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-plantains eŋɔli lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa dani amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni okpoi aye amɛ?

english: Plantain bunches are ready for harvest when the sharp corners or edges on the individual fruits become smooth and rounded, showing that the inside has filled up completely with starch.
ga: Plantains kuu ko efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko mli ŋwɛigbɛ loo ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ eko fɛɛ eko ji ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsɔɔ akɛ mligbɛ eyi kɛ ashikishaŋ.

english: Why do my harvested maize cobs get mouldy when I put them straight into tied plastic sacks after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ mikɛwo plastic kotokui ni akɛwo mli lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grains contain trapped moisture, and sealing them immediately in bags creates damp heat inside that causes mould to grow rapidly and spoil the harvest.
ga: Nibii ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔ amɛmli. Ni kɛ́ atswa kotoku lɛ naa amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo ni mli edɔ aba mli. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ daa oya ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize turn yellow after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away nitrogen—the main nutrient plants use to stay green—deeper into the soil where young roots cannot reach it. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer after heavy rains helps the maize regain its green color and strength.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen—ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli lɛ—kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ wo mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops every year even though I clear and farm it the same way?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mifo mli ni mifee okwaa yɛ gbɛ ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ nɔ moŋ.

english: Growing the same crop on the same piece of land continuously drains the soil of specific nutrients without giving the earth time to recover. Rotating your crops or planting leguminous plants like beans helps replenish nutrients naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa niyenii pɔtɛɛi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ yaa nɔ ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ loo aduɔ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii aba ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my yam tubers come out small and twisted instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need loose, soft soil to expand downwards easily. When the soil is hard, compacted, or stony, the growing tuber struggles to push through, resulting in small and misshapen yams.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ hia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shi oya. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo eyɛ tɛi lɛ, ŋmeii ni miida lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsi shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛya. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii ni efite.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up into small cups and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi etsɔɔ kɔɔpoo bibioo ko ni ekpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding on the sap beneath young leaves or transferring plant viruses. Inspecting the undersides of leaves early and applying appropriate neem-based or recommended sprays stops the damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ loo helai ni baa tsei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishi mra. Ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛ neem fee loo bɔ ni atsɔɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ atsu nii ni okɛkpa nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become excessively hot or when soil moisture swings rapidly from too dry to too wet, preventing successful pollination. Regular watering and using shade crops can keep the flower stems healthy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa anyɛɛɛ afee pollination yɛ omanyeyeli mli. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ daa kɛ nitsumɔ baanyɛ aye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when I leave them in the soil during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Soil that stays soaked in water deprives cassava roots of oxygen, creating ideal conditions for fungal rots to attack the tubers. Harvesting mature cassava before prolonged rains or planting on raised beds helps prevent root rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛ nu ewo mli lɛ baaha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa baa koni rot fungi lɛ atutua ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmei ni egbɔ dani nugbɔ nɛ be kakadaŋŋ loo adu yɛ saatsoi ni awo nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during strong wind storms right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ gbee shi yɛ ahum ni naa wa ko mli dani kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that sit near the surface, while heavy fruit bunches make the plant top-heavy. Supporting the stems with sturdy wooden Y-props and mounding soil around the base prevents wind damage.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, aduawai akutsei ni tsii baaha tso lɛ afee mlɛo. Akɛ nɔ ko ni tamɔ Y ni akɛ tsei kɛ muji ni abua naa ebɔle ehe lɛ fiɔ tsɔne lɛ sɛɛ. Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni kɔɔyɔɔ akafite nii.

english: Why do cocoa trees planted under large forest trees seem to live longer than cocoa trees in open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni kookoo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ ashishi lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ fe nɔ ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa naturally thrives under partial shade, which protects the leaves from burning heat, lowers water stress, and slows down aging. Open-sun cocoa grows fast initially but breaks down faster under heat and pest pressure.
ga: Cocoa daa yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Enɛ buɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Tsɔɔmɔ nu he haomɔ shi ni okɛ dalɛ asɛɛ afo Kookoo ni yɔɔ kpo nɔ lɛ daa oya yɛ shishijee mli. Shi efiteɔ oya yɛ latsaa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔnyɛɛ shishi.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my crops after I apply fertilizer to my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive, widespread root systems that absorb nutrients faster than crop seedlings. Clearing weeds thoroughly before applying fertilizer ensures your main crops get the food instead of the weeds.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni egbɛ eshwa he fɛɛ he ni ŋmɛɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe tsei amli dumɔwui. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani awo mli lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii yɛ jwɛi lɛ najiaŋ.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seeds when the rainy season keeps changing?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui? Beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ tsakeɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Instead of planting after the very first early rain, wait until the soil stays continuously moist at a depth of a few inches for several days. This ensures your seeds have enough reliable moisture to germinate without drying out during sudden heat spells.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ Mɛɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta fioo komɛi amli gbii babaoo. Enɛ haa odumɔwui lɛ náa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need for strong, green leaf growth. Heavy rains can also wash nitrogen deep into the soil where roots cannot reach it, so adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps bring back the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei kɛha hewalɛ, baa eŋɔli dalɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air is too hot or when the plant doesn't get a steady supply of water. When the crop gets stressed by extreme heat or dry soil, it sheds its flowers to save energy to survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa. Kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ ha tsei lɛ hao lɛ Eshwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛto hewalɛ ni ekɛhi shi lɛ he gbɛjianɔ.

english: Why do my crops under large shade trees grow tall and thin but give very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ hulutsoo be agbo shishi lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to make energy for flowering and fruiting. When heavy shade blocks the sun, the plant spends all its energy stretching upward to reach light, leaving no energy to build fruit.
ga: Tsei hia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tsi hulu lɛ naa lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛgbala ehe koni eha la lɛ abote mli. Hewalɛ ko bɛ ni eshwɛ ni akɛbaafee aduawai.

english: Why do my cassava stems need to be planted at an angle in the soil instead of straight or flat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei yɛ koŋ nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu amɛ tɛ̃ɛ loo amɛfee tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a slight angle helps the roots spread outward and downward evenly. This gives the tubers enough space to swell big while keeping the plant anchored firmly against strong wind.
ga: Yucca niji ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ fioo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara yɛ be mli ni ehaa tso lɛ hu hiɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains next to my newly planted cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide big leafy shade that protects cocoa seedlings from heat and keeps the soil moist during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni shwereɔ oya lɛ haa hulutsoo baai agboi ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ latsaa he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do tiny ragged holes appear in my maize leaf funnels just a few weeks after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-corn baa lɛ mli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Ragged holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by early attacks from Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the central leaf funnel. Applying treatments like neem extract early prevents them from destroying the growing tip of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, bu ni ekumɔ yɛ ŋmãa bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni jɛɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmei ni kɛ ehe woɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mli lɛ tutuamɔ mra lɛ mli baa. Neem mli nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra lɛ Ebaatsi tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni miida lɛ fitemɔ naa.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling inward and twisting up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso kɛmiiya mli ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny pests like aphids or thrips sucking sap from underneath the young leaves. Controlling these insects early allows fresh, healthy leaves to expand normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ebaaha baai lɛ afee ehee ni amɛhe awa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ amɛshwã bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my crops wilt during the hot afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: Under strong midday sun, crops lose water through their leaves faster than roots can draw it from the ground. Temporary wilting is the plant's defense mechanism to reduce leaf area exposed to heat, and plants usually recover by evening as air cools down.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Be kukuoo mli ŋmɔlɔ ji tso ko hebuu gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebaa baa lɛ he ni dɔlɛ baa lɛ shi. Ni tsei lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛhe ajɔ amɛ gbɛkɛ mli kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot in the soil when the heavy rain season comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain sitting in flat soil suffocates crop roots and allows fungal rot to spread quickly. Planting yams on raised mounds or ridges drains excess water away so roots stay dry and healthy.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Kɛ́ adu ŋmɔtɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ egbi ni amɛhe wa.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has lost its fertility after planting maize for three years straight?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ehiɛ edɔ waa yɛ be mli ni midu ŋmãa afii etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When soil gets exhausted, crops grow much slower, look pale or stunted, and produce tiny cobs or low yields despite good rain. Rotating your farm with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores vital nutrients to the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii daa blɛoo kwraa. Etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo egbɔjɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ babaoo nɛ moŋ Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii atsake oŋmɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up into tight pencil shapes during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ pensil henɔi ni mli wa lɛ? Yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Maize leaves curl up to protect the crop from losing too much water in extreme heat. By reducing the leaf surface area exposed to the sun, the plant slows down evaporation so it can survive dry spells.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni amɛkafite nu babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ ajie baai ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ shwieɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ fioo bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before any peppers start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed blossoms when they experience heat stress, poor soil moisture, or nutrient imbalance. Dropping flowers is the plant's natural self-defense mechanism to save energy and water when growing conditions are unfavorable.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛbote dɔlɛ he haomɔ mli. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehiii loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ejaaa Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe koni ekɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he kɛji shihilɛi ni haa edara lɛ ehiii.

english: How do my cassava plants manage to survive in dry weather when other crops wither?
ga: Te mi yucca tso lɛ baafee tɛŋŋ ahi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli be mli ni tsei krokomɛi miigbo lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its outer leaves during drought to reduce water loss while holding reserves in its thick stem and underground roots. This allows the plant to stay dormant until rainfall returns.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ esɛɛ baai lɛ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi yɛ be mli ni ekɛ nibii ni eto lɛ toɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni mli tse lɛ kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ akafee nɔ ko. Kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly and provide wide leaf canopy shade, creating a cool microclimate that keeps young cocoa roots moist and shaded until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ehaa baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo baa. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo ko ni haa kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my yam vines yield bigger tubers when I give them tall wooden stakes to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ naa bulbs wuji beni mikɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ ha amɛ lɛ? Ha amɛkwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to catch direct sunlight, which helps the leaves produce energy for tuber growth. Staking keeps the leaves off damp soil, preventing fungal rot and giving leaves maximum sun exposure.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ kɛha tuber lɛ dalɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ fungal rot naa ni ehaa baa lɛ naa hulu la babaoo.

english: Is it bad for my vegetable crops if I water them in the middle of a hot sunny day?
ga: Ani ebaaye mitsei lɛ awui kɛji mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Watering under mid-day sun causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before roots can drink it. Watering early in the morning or late afternoon ensures the water settles deep into the root zone where plants need it.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu la shishi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ anu. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi loo shwane mli Enɛ baaha nu lɛ abote shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsei lɛ he hiaa lɛ yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cabbage heads split open right before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ mli gbalaa dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Cabbage heads split when heavy watering or sudden rainfall follows a dry spell. The inner leaves absorb water quickly and expand faster than the outer leaves can stretch, bursting the outer shell.
ga: Kaabaji yitsei lɛ baatswa kɛji nu babaoo ba loo nugbɔ nɛ trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Baai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa oya fe bɔ ni baa ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Enɛ haa kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ mli fãa.

english: Why does putting fresh, wet poultry manure directly on my seedlings scorch them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ kooloi afɔfɔi heei ni efɔ lɛ wo dumɔwui lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ehaa amɛshãa lɛ?

english: Fresh, wet manure contains high levels of active nitrogen and ammonia that generate heat and pull moisture out of delicate roots. Letting manure dry and decompose breaks down these harsh chemicals into safe nutrients.
ga: Nitrogen kɛ ammonia babaoo yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee ehee ni efɔ lɛ amli ni haa hulutsoo baa ni egbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ waa lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni efite lɛ, efiteɔ tsofai ni mli wa nɛɛ ni etsɔɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my cowpea crops grow lots of green leaves but produce very few bean pods when I fertilize them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko pɛ?

english: Cowpeas naturally convert nitrogen from the air into soil nutrients. Adding excess fertilizer tricks the crop into spending its energy building leaves and vines instead of producing flowers and bean pods.
ga: Cowpeas tsakeɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ewoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine fataa he lɛ lakaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni ekɛ ehewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛdu baai kɛ wain tsei. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my tomato plants turn yellow during heavy rainy periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei ashishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil smothers tomato roots so they cannot breathe or draw up nutrients, while excessive rainwater washes nitrogen out of root depth. Excess water on leaves also encourages fungal diseases that turn leaves yellow.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baaha tomato shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haaa amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu loo amɛjie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ hoɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ hu woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Why are some of the crops on my farm growing big while others planted on the same day stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni adu yɛ gbi kome nɔ lɛ faaa kwraa lɛ?

english: Uneven growth happens when soil fertility varies across your land, water collects in some areas more than others, or underground pests damage the roots of weaker plants. Applying fertilizer evenly and ensuring good drainage helps all plants grow at the same pace.
ga: Dalɛ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ srɔtoi yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ naa. Nu buaa ehe naa yɛ hei komɛi fe hei krokomɛi. Aloo kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ fiteɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ashishifãi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli daa ni akwɛ koni nu atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛdara oyaiyeli kome mli.

english: How does leaving proper space between my crop plants help them produce bigger harvests?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ gbɛ ni sa ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mitsei lɛ ni amɛkpa nii babaoo?

english: Proper spacing ensures that each plant gets enough sunlight, air, water, and soil nutrients without fighting its neighbors. Overcrowded crops get weak and produce small yields because they compete for survival.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ awuu. Nibii ni aduɔ ni eyi obɔ lɛ baagbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ beni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛhi shi lɛ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant plantains alongside my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu plantains yɛ mi-cocoa dumɔwui heei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that create living shade, keeping the soil moist and protecting young cocoa seedlings from heat during their early years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient needed for leaf greenness and growth. It can also happen when heavy rains log the soil with water, preventing roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ baai adalɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni eha shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛmu.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with plenty of leaves but end up with tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo, shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to spend all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of tubers below. Plants need potassium to develop large, heavy roots.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Tsei he miihia potassium koni amɛná shishifãi wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my oil palm trees drop their flowers without forming any fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi ni ewooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Oil palms fail to set fruit when there are not enough pollinating insects around or when the trees suffer severe water stress during dry spells. Poor soil nutrition can also cause early flower drop.
ga: Mu tsei nyɛŋ awo yibii kɛ́ ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ faaa lɛ faaa loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ naa nu he haomɔ ni naa wa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ agbo oya.

english: Why should I prune or cut off some of the branches from my fruit trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ loo majie niji komɛi kɛjɛ mitso ni woɔ yibii lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or excess branches so the tree does not waste energy maintaining them. It also opens up the canopy for sunlight and air flow, directing the plant's energy into growing larger, healthier fruit.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ niji ni egboi loo ni fa fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ akafite hewalɛ yɛ amɛkwɛmɔ mli. Egbeleɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ hu naa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei naa hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my young crops with dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi kɛ baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei bibii ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground, known as mulching, stops heat from drying out the soil, keeps moisture in for plant roots during hot days, prevents weed growth, and turns into rich soil manure as it rots.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Ehaa la ni tsoɔ lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ tso shishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni ebafeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ beni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my seeds right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell before the main rains actually start. If you plant too early, seeds may sprout and then dry up and die from the heat due to lack of follow-up water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔi wuji lɛ jeɔ shishi diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbi ni amɛgboi kɛjɛ latsaa mli yɛ nu ni bɛ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds when my crops are already much taller than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi lɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ fe jwɛi lɛ momo lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that steal water and fertilizers from under the ground long before your crops can use them. Clearing weeds ensures all nutrients go directly to feeding your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ yaa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily under direct, hot sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantain or cassava alongside cocoa creates a canopy that shields young trees, keeping the soil cool and moist until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ cocoa masɛi lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe lɛ baa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmã tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛmiijɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the tip indicate that your maize lacks nitrogen, a vital nutrient for plant growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure early in the season helps the plant regain its deep green color and build large cobs.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛsu ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: How should I position cassava stem cuttings in the soil so they sprout properly?
ga: Te esa akɛ akɛ ŋmei ni afo lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli aha tɛŋŋ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cassava stems must be planted with the leaf buds pointing upward toward the sky, either planted at an angle or buried horizontally. Planting stems upside down forces the new shoots to grow downward into the dirt, weakening the plant and reducing your yield.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei ni baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Abaadu yɛ koŋ nɔ loo abaafu yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ shishi kɛtee shishi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii heei akwɛ̃ kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: Why do I need to use tall wooden stakes to lift my yam vines off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi koni mikɛwo mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb tall stakes so their leaves can catch direct sunlight to produce food for the underground tubers. Keeping vines off the wet ground also stops soil-borne fungi from spreading and rotting the leaves.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ koni amɛha amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he koni amɛná niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ wain tso lɛ tee hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ.

english: What is causing the leaves on my tomato plants to curl up tightly and stop setting fruit?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa yibiiwoo?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is commonly caused by a virus spread by tiny whitefly insects. Controlling whiteflies using neem oil sprays or sticky traps prevents the insects from passing the damaging virus to healthy plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo tsɔnei ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmeii anɔ lɛ tsu nii kɛkudɔ ŋmeii lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ helai ni fiteɔ mɔ nɔ amɛyashɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do the blossoms on my cowpea plants fall off before producing any bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Cowpea blossoms drop early when tiny pests called thrips feed on the flowers and damage them. Applying recommended organic or chemical sprays right at the start of flowering protects the blossoms so full pods can form.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛji kooloi bibii ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ba amɛnɔ. Atsɛɔ amɛ thrips, amɛyeɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ. Kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔii amli loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔii amli lɛ tsu nii yɛ fɔfɔii lɛ ashishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔii lɛ ahe koni eha amɛfee podi fɛɛ.

english: Why should I pile loose soil around the base of my groundnut plants after they bloom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabu sũ ni mli ewo muji mabɔle he lɛ? Peanut cones beni fɔfɔi lɛ efo sɛɛ?

english: After groundnuts flower, the plant sends down sharp pegs into the earth where the nuts form underground. Mounding loose soil around the base makes it easy for these pegs to penetrate the ground and form healthy pods.
