ga: Beni ŋmeii lɛ efɔ lɛ sɛɛ Tso lɛ tsuɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni ŋmeii feɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Pile loose soil around Shishitoo lɛ haa ewaa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛfee ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why should I cut away extra suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ plantain tsei titrii lɛ.

english: When too many suckers grow around one mother plantain tree, they fight for the same soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Removing excess suckers leaves the main plant strong enough to yield a heavy, full bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ dumɔwu kome Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ mli awa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni tsii ni eyi obɔ aba.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans together with my maize help the maize grow stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni mikɛ mi ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ewaa lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their root nodules. As those roots break down, they release natural nitrogen into the soil, feeding nearby maize plants for free.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ nakai shishifãi lɛ gbee shi lɛ Amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni oha ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ niyenii yaka

english: Why does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass keep them green during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mulching around lɛ mikɛ jwɛi duɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni eha amɛfee ŋmɔji yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves (mulching) acts like a shield that blocks direct sunlight from evaporating water out of the earth. This keeps the soil soft, cool, and moist so plant roots can drink even when rain is scarce.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni tsiɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa koni ekajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ bɔdɔɔ, efeɔ fɛ̃i, ni edɔɔ bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu nu kɛji nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛ po.

english: Why does rice need so much water to grow compared to crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ kɛ akɛto tsei tamɔ ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Rice naturally thrives in wet soil because its roots are specially adapted to handle standing water, which helps transport nutrients to the plant and suppresses weeds naturally.
ga: Omɔ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ ejaakɛ eshishifãi lɛ etsɔ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ koni amɛnyɛ amɛtsu nu ni damɔ shi lɛ he nii. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yaa tsei lɛ amli ni ekɛ jwɛi lɛ tsiɔ naa yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Can I successfully plant rice in the Ashanti or Central region, or does it only grow in specific parts of Ghana?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ ŋmãa yɛ Ashanti loo Central Kpokpaa lɛ nɔ yɛ omanyeyeli mli? Aloo abaanyɛ adu yɛ Ghana hei komɛi pɛ.

english: You can successfully grow rice in Ashanti, Central, and most parts of Ghana because these regions have abundant natural water sources and rich lowlands suitable for rice cultivation.
ga: Obaanyɛ oye omanye yɛ Ashanti, Central Kpokpaa lɛ nɔ kɛ Ghana hei babaoo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kpokpai nɛɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli nu jɛɛhei babaoo kɛ shikpɔji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni baa nii ni sa kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Does rice always require heavy rainfall, or can I grow it near natural streams and rivers on my land?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa he miihia ŋmãa be fɛɛ be aloo manyɛ madu yɛ adebɔɔ mli faai kɛ faai ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe?

english: You can grow rice near natural streams and rivers because the crop relies on consistent soil moisture, making naturally wet valley bottoms ideal even when rainfall is low.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ mli faai kɛ faai ahe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei damɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa jɔɔ lɛ shishi ni efɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛ po.

english: Why don't rice plants rot and die when their roots stay covered in water for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ fiteee ni amɛgbooo kɛ́ nu ehà amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have unique internal air tubes in their stems and roots that allow oxygen to flow down from the leaves, keeping the roots alive even under water.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi ni yɔɔ srɔto yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli kɛbaa shi. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ nu shishi po.

english: How do I know if the soil on my farm is good enough to hold water for growing rice?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aŋɔ nu kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔ?

english: Soil with high clay content or land located in low-lying swampy areas that naturally collects and retains surface water is best suited for rice growing.
ga: Shikpɔji ni shikpɔŋ sũ babaoo yɔɔ nɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋshɔkpɔi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni buaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa ni ekɛtoɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What simple management steps can I take to ensure my rice crop produces heavy grains?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mafee nɔkwɛmɔ gbɛi ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ awo dumɔwui ni tsii?

english: Ensuring steady water levels during flowering, using certified seed varieties, and applying fertilizer at key growth stages will help the rice plant fill out full, heavy grains.
ga: Nu lɛ mlihilɛ ni ahiɔ shi daa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni akɛtsuɔ nii Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ dalɛ be ni he hiaa lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmãa tso lɛ aná dumɔwui ni tsii.

english: What will happen to my rice crop if the water on the field dries up completely while the plant is flowering?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji nu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gĩ kwraa yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: If the soil dries out completely during flowering, the plant becomes stressed, which causes empty seed husks and drastically reduces your final harvest.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ Tso lɛ baaná haomɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ feɔ efolo ni ehaa naagbee kpamɔ lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Is the warm weather across Ghana suitable for rice crops to develop quickly?
ga: Ani kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ yɛ Ghana fɛɛ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii oya?

english: Yes, Ghana's warm tropical climate provides the ideal temperature range needed for rice seeds to germinate quickly and grow vigorously throughout the season.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo be ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛdara waa yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How do I choose between lowland rice and upland rice for my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: If your land stays naturally flooded or sits near water bodies, choose lowland rice. If your farm is on higher ground relying strictly on rain, plant upland rice varieties.
ga: Kɛji akɛ nu eyi oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa loo ebɛŋkɛ nu jɛɛhe ko. Halamɔ ŋshɔkpɔ nɔ ŋmãa Kɛji oŋmɔ lɛ yɛ gɔŋkpɔ ko ni damɔ nugbɔshiimɔ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ nɔ. Ha adu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ.

english: Can I rely on natural water streams in my community to start a small rice farm without expensive machinery?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ mihe afɔ̃ adebɔɔ mli nu jɛɛhei ni yɔɔ mi akutso lɛ mli lɛ anɔ koni maje ŋmãa ŋmɔ bibioo ko shishi ni tsɔnei ni jara wa bɛ mli?

english: Yes, many farmers in Ghana successfully farm rice by channeling natural streams into low-lying plots without needing expensive irrigation equipment.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, okwaafoi babaoo ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ eye omanye yɛ ŋmãa dumɔ mli kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli faai ni amɛtsuɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ kplanaa lɛ nɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ nu shwiemɔ nibii ni jara wa atsu nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow from the middle instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaakã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing maize leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is essential food for plant growth. Applying NPK fertilizer or well-decomposed animal manure will help the leaves return to a healthy dark green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tso lɛ dalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting on the tree during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in damp, shaded conditions. Pruning excess branches and weeding regularly allows sunlight and airflow into the farm to dry out moisture and stop the fungus.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ shade yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ daa kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔtɔ agbi ni ekɛtsi ŋmɔtɔ naa.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and stopping the fruits from growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi aduawai lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies transmitting plant viruses. Using neem seed oil spray or recommended pesticides helps control these insects and protects new leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Neem dumɔwui amli fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ ni ebu tsei ahe tsei heei ahe.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground before I get to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water settles around them in heavy, poorly drained soils. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the tubers stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni nu nyɛɛɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why should I cover the ground around my garden vegetables with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mibɔɔ mli aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass is called mulching. It acts like a blanket to prevent the sun from drying out the soil, keeps weeds down, and slowly breaks down into nutrients for your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli koni hulu lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi, ni egbeɔ jwɛi ni efiteɔ lɛ fiofio ni etsɔɔ niyenii ni haa onibii lɛ yeɔ hewalɛ.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my crops during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist, but not right before a heavy downpour. Heavy rain will wash the fertilizer away before the plant roots can soak it in, wasting your investment.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ, shi jeee dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. ni kɛ shika ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fitemɔ baa

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ haa.

english: Why do I need to tie my yam vines onto tall wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ fĩɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko he lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch enough sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off the wet ground, protecting them from fungal diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ niyenii. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: How do I choose the right plantain suckers from my field to start a new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni sa kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Choose 'sword suckers' that have narrow, spear-like leaves and a broad stem base. They grow much faster and produce larger, stronger bunches than 'water suckers' that have wide leaves early on.
ga: Halamɔ ‘Sword Bud’ ni baai lɛ mli tse, tamɔ akpɔlɔ kɛ shishigbɛ ni mli kwɔ. Amɛdaraa oya kwraa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni dara ni wa fe ‘nu mli ŋmeii’ ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ mra.

english: How can I stop insects from eating holes into my harvested maize while it is stored in the barn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi ni yeɔ mi-ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ naa be mli ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Dry your maize until the grains are very hard, then store them in sealed, airtight storage bags (like PICS bags). Cutting off the air supply stops weevils from surviving and multiplying inside your stored grain.
ga: Gbimɔ o-corn lɛ mli kɛyashi ŋmeii lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛwo kotoku ko ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli (tamɔ PICS kotoku mli). Kɔɔyɔɔ ni akɛhaa lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi ni amɛshwere yɛ ŋmaa ni ato lɛ mli.

english: Can I spread diseases to my healthy crops just by touching them with my bare hands after handling sick plants?
ga: Ani manyɛ magbɛ hela ashwã miŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli kɛtsɔ miniji ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni mikɛtaa amɛhe lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ beni mikɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ etsu nii sɛɛ?

english: Yes. Germs, fungi, and viruses can easily travel on your hands, clothing, or farm tools. If you touch a diseased crop and then handle a healthy one, you can transfer those germs and cause the disease to spread across your farm.
ga: Hɛɛ. Muawai, tsɛŋemɔ helai, kɛ muawai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oniji, otadei, loo ŋmɔ mli nibii amli oya. Kɛji ota tso ko ni hela emɔ lɛ he lɛ, no lɛ okɛ ohe awo tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli. Obaanyɛ okɛ nakai helai lɛ aya he kroko ni oha hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants develop rots near the stem when I water them using water dipped from stagnant ponds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fiteɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he beni mikɛ nu ni akɛwo nubu ko ni mli ejɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Stagnant pond water often hosts harmful bacteria and fungi. When you dip into this dirty water and splash it onto your crops, those germs attack the plant's outer skin, leading to rot and fungal infections.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nubu ni ekã shi lɛ hiɛɔ helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui. Beni okɛwoɔ nu ni mli ewo muji mli ni okɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ. Nakai helatsɛmɛi lɛ tutuaa tso lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ. Enɛ haa fitemɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa.

english: Can washing my dirty hands or tools in the bucket I use to water my crops make my vegetables sick?
ga: Ani niji loo nibii ni he tseee ni afɔɔ yɛ baagi ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli nu lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha aduawai aná hela?

english: Yes. Washing dirty hands or contaminated farm tools in your irrigation container introduces harmful germs directly into the water. When you pour that water on your crops, the germs transfer directly to the soil and plants.
ga: Hɛɛ. Niji ni mli ewo muji loo okwaayeli nibii ni mli ewo muji ni akɛwoɔ nu shwiemɔ tsinsii amli lɛ kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui baa nu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nakai nu lɛ wo onibii anɔ lɛ, helatsɛ lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How do crop diseases move from an infected farm to my clean field during the rainy season?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsei ahe helai jɛɔ ŋmɔji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa miŋmɔji ni mli tse lɛ amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Heavy rain splashes soil particles and germs from infected plants onto nearby healthy crops. Additionally, rainwater flowing across the ground carries pathogens from neighboring fields directly into your soil.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ sũ mli nibii bibii kɛ helai ni jɛ tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ. Nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ baa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: What is a simple way for me to check if my soil has enough moisture without buying expensive equipment?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni matsɔ nɔ makwɛ akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni miheee nibii ni jara wa?

english: You can push your bare finger about two inches into the soil. If your finger comes out dry and clean, the crops need water; if moist soil sticks to your finger, there is still enough water for the plants.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ onine ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli aaafee inchi enyɔ. Kɛji oniji je kpo ni egbi ni ehe tse Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ hu he miihia nu. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ yɛ onine nɔ lɛ, nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ lolo ni baaha tso lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why is it bad for me to pour water directly over the top of my tomato leaves instead of pouring it on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ ooofɔse nu tɛ̃ɛ yɛ tomato baai anɔ moŋ fe ni oooshwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Wet leaves create a warm, moist environment where crop germs and mold thrive. Pouring water directly at the base of the plant keeps the foliage dry while allowing the roots to drink safely.
ga: Baai ni efɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔɔ, ni mli edɔ baa. he ni tso mli helai kɛ ŋmeii baanyɛ ada yɛ Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ agbi yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni abaanyɛ anu.

english: Is it safe for me to collect rainwater in open barrels to water my young vegetable nursery later?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mabua nugbɔ nu naa yɛ baagi ni agbele mli koni mikɛwo mi aduawai abɔɔ bibioo lɛ mli nu sɛɛ mli?

english: Collecting rainwater is helpful, but leaving barrels open allows dirt, fallen leaves, and insects to breed germs in the water. Keeping your water containers covered ensures the water stays clean for your delicate crops.
ga: Nugbɔ nu ni ajieɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ. Shi kɛ́ oshi tanki lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha muji aba. baai ni egbee shi Ni kooloi baanyɛ afɔ́ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ nu lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni oooŋa lɛ baaha nu ni mli tse aba kɛha onibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into tubes during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ shwane mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a natural defense mechanism. By curling its leaves, the maize plant reduces the amount of leaf surface exposed to the hot sun, which stops moisture from evaporating too quickly from its body.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ baa baa lɛ nɔ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ baa shi. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ akafo oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my okro plants stop growing and turn yellow when the soil stays completely soaked in water for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra tso lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ nu mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When the soil is completely flooded for long periods, water pushes out all the air, drowning the roots and preventing them from taking up nutrients.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Nu lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my bean leaves droop and look lifeless when the soil gets very dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni wala bɛ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi waa lɛ?

english: Plants rely on internal water pressure to keep their leaves standing firm. When the soil dries out, the plant loses water and wilts, which is its way of conserving energy until moisture returns.
ga: Tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nu ni yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ nɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ gbi lɛ, tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu ni amɛgbiɔ. Enɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ hewalɛ toɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my crops need fertilizer to grow well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Just like people need good food to grow strong, crops need essential nutrients from fertilizer to develop green leaves, strong stems, and big fruits. Without enough nutrients in the soil, plants stay small and yield very little harvest.
ga: Taakɛ niyenii kpakpa he hiaa gbɔmɛi koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ hu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛná baai eŋɔli. tso ni mli wa kɛ aduawai wuji Kɛji niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ baafee bibii ni amɛbaawo yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: What happens to my crops if I buy bad or fake fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mihe ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehiii loo amale?

english: Poor-quality or fake fertilizer does not give your plants the proper nutrients they need. Using it can leave your crops weak, yellow, and stunted, which leads to a failed harvest despite all your hard work.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni ehiii loo ni akɛfee lɛ haaa tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni sa ni he hiaa amɛ. Kɛ́ okɛtsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ, efee ŋmɔŋ, ni efee ŋmɔŋ, ni no baaha ŋmɔshi nii lɛ akakpa yɛ nitsumɔ ni otsuɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops wither and yield nothing if I do not put fertilizer in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Over time, soil loses its natural food because crops take up nutrients every season. If you do not replenish the soil with fertilizer, the ground runs out of plant food, leaving your crops starving and unable to produce fruits or grains.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa akɛni tsei lɛ naa niyenii daa be mli lɛ hewɔ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ tsei ahe niyenii. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye oŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii loo ŋmaa.

english: What will happen to my farm if my fertilizer arrives late in the planting season?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bashɛ sɛɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ amli?

english: Crops need nutrients most when they are young and actively growing. If fertilizer arrives late after that critical stage has passed, the crops cannot make full use of it, resulting in poor growth and a low yield.
ga: Niyenii mli hewalɛ he hiaa tsei fe fɛɛ beni amɛji gbekɛbii ni amɛmiida jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bashɛ sɛɛ mli beni be ni he hiaa waa lɛ eho lɛ, anyɛɛɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii kɛyashɛ he ni ebaanyɛ eshɛ. Enɛ haaa ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ, ni yibiiwoo hu faaa.

english: Can I still get a good harvest if I plant my crops without buying chemical fertilizer?
ga: Ani manyɛ maná ŋmaa kpakpa lolo kɛji midu tsei ni miheee tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yes, but only if your soil is already very rich or if you feed it using organic options like compost, animal manure, or crop rotation, which naturally put missing nutrients back into the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo pɛ. Aloo kɛji akɛ okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛhaa niyenii. Enɛ baaha niyenii ni elaaje lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are my crops looking small and pale even though I am giving them enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe tseee eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: Water helps plants drink, but nutrients are the actual food. Even with plenty of rain or water, your crops will stay small, pale, and weak if the soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Nu yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnuɔ nu. Shi niyenii kpakpa ji niyenii diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ loo nu babaoo po Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakã he afee bibii, amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii tamɔ nitrogen.

english: How can I tell if my crops are struggling because the soil lacks food?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miihe afee shoo ejaakɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Plants show clear warning signs when hungry, such as leaves turning yellow or purple, slow stems growth, thin stalks, or leaves dropping off early before the crop produces fruit.
ga: Tsei jieɔ kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo kɛji hɔmɔ miiye amɛ, tamɔ baai ni tsakeɔ ŋmɔŋ loo pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kpãa lɛ daa fiofio, etso lɛ bafeɔ tsei, loo baai lɛ shwieɔ shi oya dani tso lɛ woɔ yibii.

english: Why do my crops produce flowers but fail to make any actual fruits or seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi shi jeee aduawai loo dumɔwui diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Crops need extra energy and specific nutrients like phosphorus and potassium to turn flowers into fruit. If the plants are malnourished, the flowers will fall off before fruit can form.
ga: Tsei biɔ hewalɛ kroko kɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛi, tamɔ fɔsfɔs kɛ potasiam. Koni atsake fɔfɔi afee aduawai Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi dani ewo yibii.

english: Does using good fertilizer mean I am guaranteed to get a big harvest?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ miyɛ nɔmimaa akɛ maná yibii babaoo?

english: Fertilizer gives your plants the energy to grow, but a big harvest also depends on using good seeds, getting enough rain, keeping pests away, and caring for your soil properly.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛdara. Shi nikpamɔ babaoo hu damɔ dumɔwui kpakpai ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni anáa Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ajiemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do my crops grow fast in the first few weeks but suddenly stop growing later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli, ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛfite trukaa lɛ? Ani ekpaa dalɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Young plants start by using stored food inside the seed. As they grow bigger, they demand much more nutrients from the soil; if the ground lacks food, their growth will suddenly stop.
ga: Tsei bibii jeɔ shishi kɛtsɔ niyenii ni ato yɛ amɛdumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Kɛ amɛdara lɛ Akɛ niyenii babaoo hu he miihia amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji niyenii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ Edalɛ baakpa trukaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my newly planted cocoa seedlings turning red and dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mikoo tso ni midu ehee lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: Leaves turning red at the base of a young seedling often signal that soil pests like termites are chewing into the main stem near the ground, cutting off water and nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei bibii ni baai lɛ feɔ tsuru lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ ŋmeii, miiye tso titri ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii laajeɔ.

english: How can I tell if insects are destroying my cocoa plants at ground level?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi bibii miifite mi-cacao tsei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: You can inspect the stem base right where it meets the soil; if termites are damaging the plant, you will see them actively eating into the stem tissue.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ he ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kpeɔ yɛ lɛ. Kɛji ŋmeii kpata tsei ahiɛ Obaana amɛ ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ shishi fãji lɛ.

english: Are young cocoa seedlings more vulnerable to soil pests than older trees?
ga: Ani kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai fe tsei ni edara lɛ?

english: Yes, freshly planted seedlings are small and tender, making them an easy target for soil insects like termites before the plant gets strong enough to survive.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛha kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ dani tso lɛ he wa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ehi shi.

english: Does the time of year I plant my cocoa affect whether insects will attack the seedlings?
ga: Ani afi lɛ mli be ni miduɔ kookoo lɛ saa bɔ ni kooloi bibii tutuaa dumɔwui lɛ amɛhaa lɛ he?

english: Yes, timing matters because termites in the soil become active under specific ground conditions, so planting at the right time helps seedlings survive the initial planting stage.
ga: Hɛɛ, be he miihia ejaakɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ shihilɛi pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ shishijee dumɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do termites attack my cocoa plants even when they are just placed in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii miitutua mi cacao tsei lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ akɛ amɛ fɔ shikpɔŋ kɛkɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Termites live naturally in the soil and will target small cocoa seedlings if the soil timing and conditions make the soft plant stems easy food sources.
ga: Termites hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛbaatutua kookoo dumɔwui bibii. Kɛji akɛ be kɛ shikpɔŋ shihilɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ niyenii jɛɛhe ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ,.

english: Can I put chemical treatments inside the planting hole before putting in my cocoa seedling?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofai awo dumɔ bu lɛ mli dani madu kookoo dumɔwui?

english: Yes, placing recommended chemical treatments directly into the planting hole creates a protective shield in the soil that stops termites from attacking the new roots and stem.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛwoɔ dumɔ bu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bulɛ ko baa koni ŋmeii akatutua shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii heei.

english: How can I create a protective barrier around my young cocoa trees to stop crawling pests?
ga: Matswa hebuu he ko mabɔle he. Bɔ ni aduɔ kookoo tsei bibii koni akɛkpa tsɛŋemɔ helai

english: You can apply protective soil treatments or barriers around the base of the stem to prevent ground-crawling pests like termites from reaching the tender cocoa plant.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ shikpɔŋ he loo gbɛtsii nii ko ni ebɔle ehe lɛ atsu nii. Tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ tsiɔ kooloi ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ, tamɔ ŋmeii, anaa koni amɛkashɛ kookoo tso ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ he.

english: Will putting chicken manure around my cocoa plants help protect them from insects?
ga: Kooloi ashishifã ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Ani cacao tsei baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ kooloi bibii ahe?

english: Adding chicken manure enriches the soil and strengthens the seedling, which can help the plant grow stronger and potentially deter pests when properly applied.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛo ni ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ aná hewalɛ. Amɛ baanyɛ aye abua tsei ni amɛ dara waa ni amɛ baanyɛ amɛ tsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa kɛ akɛ tsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: What should I look for around the base of my cocoa seedling if the plant looks weak?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ makwɛ he fɛɛ he? Cocoa tso shishi kɛji cocoa tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ

english: Check the soil directly around the stem base for signs of insect boring, soil disturbance, or termites eating into the seedling stem.
ga: Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle dumɔwui lɛ ashishigbɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli koni ona okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii, sũ mli ŋmeii, loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yeɔ nii.

english: What basic steps can I take before planting to prevent soil insects from eating my crop?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii titrii manyɛ mafee dani madu nii koni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi akaye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: You can prepare by treating planting holes with protective chemicals, applying organic options like chicken manure, and carefully timing your planting to avoid peak insect activity.
ga: Obaanyɛ osaa ohe kɛtsɔ tsofa ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni okɛbaatsu nii yɛ dumɔ bu lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ tsina ŋmei kɛ be ni okɛduɔ nii lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ koni kooloi akafee nɔ ni fe fɛɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and dying off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to stay green and build strong stalks. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps keep the leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛɛmɛi ji tsei ni niyenii ni he hiaa koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛfee ŋmeii ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans alongside my maize make the maize grow stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ midu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mi ŋmei lɛ masɛi lɛ, ehaa ŋmei lɛ mli waa lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans gather nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When they grow near maize, they feed natural fertilizer back into the soil, helping the maize grow bigger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Buaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmãa Amɛhaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I plant them in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains planted around them to block direct heat and keep moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛhe. Bɔni afee ni atsĩ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why does my cassava plant drop almost all its leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fite yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during hot, dry weather to conserve water and protect itself from drying out. Once the rains return, the plant naturally grows fresh leaves again.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba Tso lɛ baaná baai heei ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before growing any fruit during very hot weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ otsii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and prevents proper pollination. To protect itself from wasting energy, the plant sheds its blossoms until temperatures cool down.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaaa amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni obu ohe kɛjɛ hewalɛ ni fiteɔ lɛ he Tso lɛ efɔɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck the sap from the leaves or spread viruses that stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu loo helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ni haa tsei lɛ adalɛ sɛɛ foɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa.

english: Why do insects attack my cowpea crop mostly when the flowers begin to open?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-cowpea tsei lɛ babaoo kɛ́ amɛbɔi fɔmɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers produce sweet nectar and bright petals that attract pests like flower thrips. These insects feed on the buds and blossoms, which can prevent seed pods from forming.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ jieɔ nu kɛ fɔfɔi ni kpɛɔ ni gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fɔfɔi thrips lɛ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ ŋmeii kɛ fɔfɔi. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ dumɔwui ashishi koni ekafee.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily once the bunch of plantains grows big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and fibrous stems that struggle to hold heavy weight. Propping the main stem up with a sturdy bamboo pole helps support the plant until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi muji ni tsii lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ shishi tso titri lɛ to tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eye ebua tso lɛ kɛyashi be mli ni abaakpa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the soil when we get too much continuous rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ wɔná nugbɔ babaoo ni yaa nɔ lɛ?

english: When soil stays soaked for too long, air cannot reach the roots. This lack of oxygen causes cassava tubers to suffocate and decay under the ground.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Oxygen ni bɛ nɛɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do I need to put tall sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ awo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb toward sunlight to make food through their leaves. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to light so the tubers underground can grow large.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛtsɔ baai lɛ anɔ amɛfee niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Okɛwo kane mli bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ shishi tsɔnei lɛ adara.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow before they produce any corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani amɛwoɔ abele lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the food plants need to stay green and grow strong. It can also happen if the roots are sitting in too much water after heavy rain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii kɛha tsei ni ehe hiaa ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu babaoo mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers are ready to be harvested under the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually mature when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, typically around 9 to 12 months after planting, or when you see the soil cracking open around the base of the stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ eda kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Bei pii lɛ, aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Aloo kɛ́ ona shikpɔŋ ni egbɛ eshwa tso lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my cabbage plants grow very big leaves but fail to form a hard head in the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ baai lɛ dara waa shi enyɛɛɛ efee yitso ni wa yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to form heads when they experience extreme heat or when they are given too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus only on growing leaves instead of a tight head.
ga: Kaabage nyɛɛɛ afee yitsei kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo la ni mli edɔ waa mli loo kɛji akɛ aha lɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama baai ni miida lɛ pɛ nɔ. Yɛ yitso ni mli wa najiaŋ

english: Why does my land dry out so quickly just two days after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbiɔ oya yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Soil dries out quickly when it lacks organic matter like manure or dry leaves. Adding organic material acts like a sponge, helping the soil hold onto water longer during dry weather.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo baai ni egboi bɛ mli. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛfataa he lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Will planting shade trees help my young cocoa plants survive the hot dry season?
ga: Ani tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ duɔ lɛ baaye abua mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be ni nugbɔjɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, young cocoa plants burn easily in full sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains protects the young cocoa trees from intense sun and keeps the soil moist during the harmattan season.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants dropping off without making any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high, when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly, or when tiny pests damage the blossoms before they can turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ lɛ. Aloo kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii Fite fɔfɔi lɛ dani amɛtsɔ tomatoi.

english: What causes my pepper leaves to curl up and turn small and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck the juice from the leaves and spread plant sicknesses, stopping the leaf from growing flat and broad.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies kɛ chili baa baa. ni shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai amli ni egbɛɔ tsei ahelai eshwaa Ehaa baa lɛ efeee tɛ̃ɛ ni elɛɛɔ

english: Why are my plantain trees falling over on their own before the fruits are ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall over when microscopic worms called nematodes or stem borer insects destroy the underground roots, making the plant weak so heavy winds easily blow it down.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ kpata shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ ahiɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ aahu akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswaa lɛ kɛyaa shi oya.

english: Why do people tell me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko baakɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu tsina loo ŋmãa?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. This naturally fertilizes the soil and helps the maize crop grow better without buying as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛsaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing short, crooked, and twisted instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji kukuji, ni ebɔle ehe ni egbɛ eshwa moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams grow crooked when the soil mound is too hard, shallow, or full of stones. Yams need loose, deep, and well-dug soil so the tuber can expand downwards easily without hitches.
ga: Sweet potatoes baabɔle kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ, ekɔɔɔ he eko tsɔ, loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ, ni atsa jogbaŋŋ lɛ he miihia sweet potato koni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛya shi oya ni amɛkatsi amɛhe.

english: Are all the insects I see on my cocoa farm harmful to my crop?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii fɛɛ ni minaa yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui?

english: No, not all insects are bad. Some are beneficial insects that actually help your farm by eating harmful pests or pollinating cocoa flowers so they can turn into pods.
ga: Jeee kooloi bibii fɛɛ ehiii. Kplukai komɛi ji kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ diɛŋtsɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ ye obua oŋmɔ lɛ kɛtsɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ ni oooye loo kookoo fɔfɔi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ nɔ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How do insects help my cocoa trees make pods?
ga: Te kooloi bibii yeɔ ebuaa mi cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Very tiny insects, like midges, carry pollen from flower to flower. Without these beneficial insects doing this work, cocoa flowers cannot develop into healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Kplukai bibii waa, tamɔ midges lɛ, woɔ fɔfɔi amli fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko mli. Kɛji akɛ nɛkɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ tsuuu nitsumɔ nɛɛ, Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ cocoa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I avoid killing all insects on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ kooloi bibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ agbemɔ he?

english: If you kill all insects, you also destroy the helpful ones that pollinate your cocoa flowers and eat destructive pests, which can lead to lower harvests.
ga: Kɛ ogbe kooloi bibii lɛ fɛɛ Obaakpãtã kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ahiɛ ni oye kooloi bibii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha kpamɔ bibioo aba.

english: Will spraying insecticides on my farm destroy the good insects that help my cocoa?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baafite kooloi kpakpai ni yeɔ ebuaa mikoo lɛ?

english: Not necessarily. Certain approved chemicals are specifically tested to make sure they target harmful pests without destroying the beneficial insects on your farm.
ga: Jeee nakai kwraa. Akwɛɔ tsofai komɛi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ akwɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ana akɛ amɛtutua kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni amɛyeee kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ awui.

english: How can I be sure that a pesticide is safe to use on my cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha mi-cacao tsei lɛ?

english: You should use pesticides that have been tested and approved by research bodies like the Cocoa Research Institute, as they verify chemical safety for both cocoa trees and helpful creatures.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni niiamlitaomɔ gbɛjianɔtoo ko tamɔ Cocoa Research Institute lɛ eka amɛkwɛ ni amɛkpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛkwɛɔ bɔ ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ cacao tso lɛ mli lɛ kɛ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ fɛɛ yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ha.

english: Can I spray chemical pesticides on my cocoa farm at any time of the day?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be?

english: It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the afternoon when beneficial insects are less active, reducing the risk of harming them.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ leebi loo shwane be mli ni kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuuu nii tsɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa oshara ni yɔɔ akɛ ebaaye amɛ awui lɛ baa shi.

english: How does the research done at the Tafo cocoa center help a practical farmer like me?
ga: Te niiamlitaomɔ ni afeɔ yɛ Tafo Cocoa Center lɛ baanyɛ aye abua okwaafoi ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ tamɔ mi lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Researchers in Tafo test farm chemicals, crop varieties, and soil practices for years to make sure the advice and products given to farmers actually increase yield safely.
ga: Nibii amlitaolɔi ni yɔɔ Tafo lɛ eka ŋmɔ mli tsofai, ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nifeemɔi amɛkwɛ afii babaoo koni amɛkwɛ akɛ ŋaawoo kɛ nibii ni akɛhaa okwaafoi lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does it take researchers many years to test a farm chemical before telling us to use it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe bahia ni niiamlitaolɔi kɛ afii babaoo aka tsofai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ amɛkwɛ dani amɛkɛɛ wɔ akɛ wɔkɛtsu nii lɛ?

english: Long testing periods ensure that a chemical consistently kills pests over many seasons without harming cocoa trees, useful insects, or the soil over time.
ga: Kaa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ haa tsofai lɛ yaa nɔ egbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yɛ be babaoo mli. ni eyeee kookoo tso lɛ he sɛɛ kooloi loo shikpɔŋ lɛ awui yɛ be ni sa mli

english: What is meant by 'mixed cocoa' on a farm?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘koo ni akɛfutu’ shishi yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Mixed cocoa usually refers to planting different recommended varieties of cocoa together on the same farm, which can help improve pollination rates and protect against widespread disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, blended cocoa lɛ tsɔɔ kookoo henɔi srɔtoi ni aduɔ. Akɛ ŋaawoo ha akɛ afee ekome yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli Enɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ ni ekɛtsi helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ anaa.

english: What are the main pests I should be protecting my cocoa trees against?
ga: Mɛni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai titrii ni esa akɛ mabu mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ he?

english: The main harmful pests in cocoa are mirids (capsids) and mealybugs, which suck sap from stems and pods, causing dieback and reducing crop yield.
ga: Nibii titrii ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ kookoo mli ji mirids (capsids) kɛ mealybugs. ni shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ Ekɛ gbele baa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly after I manually clear my land for planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya nɛkɛ beni mikɛ miniji shwieɔ he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have deep roots and seeds buried in the soil that sprout immediately when exposed to sunlight and rain. Clearing only the surface leaves these roots alive, which is why agricultural chemicals or proper land preparation are needed to kill the weeds completely from the roots before planting.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ dumɔwui ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni kɛ́ hulu la kɛ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, amɛkwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋwɛigbɛ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi nɛɛ ahi shi. Enɛ hewɔ ni esa akɛ akɛ okwaayeli tsofai loo shikpɔŋ ni asaa jogbaŋŋ atsu nii koni akɛjie jwɛi kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli dani adu lɛ.

english: Will using chemical weed killers damage the soil where I want to plant my crops?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baafite shikpɔŋ ni misumɔɔ ni madu tsei yɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When used correctly according to instructions, recommended weed-killing chemicals target only the unwanted weeds and break down safely in the soil, allowing your crop seedlings to grow without competing for nutrients.
ga: Kɛ akɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi anaa Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yi lɛ tsɔɔ jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ pɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe. Ye obua otso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛdara ni okɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ akaŋ.

english: How exactly do weeds prevent my crops from growing well and yielding a good harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ atsĩ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai hu?

english: Weeds act like thief plants that steal essential groundwater, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your main crop, leaving your crops weak, stunted, and unproductive.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsei ni juɔ, amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii amli. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, egbɔjɔɔ ni etsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is the best time for me to kill and remove weeds from my field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ magbe ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: It is best to kill and clear weeds before planting your seeds so your young crops have a clean field to establish strong roots without any competition from day one.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooogbe jwɛi ni ojie dani odu koni oha onibii bibii lɛ aná ŋmɔ ni mli tse koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa ni akaŋshii bɛ mli kɛjɛ gbi klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my crops actually need fertilizer or if the soil is already rich enough?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia mi diɛŋtsɛ? Aloo ani shikpɔŋ lɛ baa nii bɔ ni sa?

english: If your crop leaves start turning pale green or yellow, or if the plants stay small and grow very slowly despite receiving enough rain, it means the soil lacks nutrients and requires fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ loo kɛji tsei lɛ ji bibii ni amɛdaraa blɛoo waa eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Does it matter when and how I apply fertilizer to my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be kɛ mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, timing is very important. Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist and the plants are actively growing so their roots can easily absorb the food without the fertilizer washing away or burning the crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, be he miihia waa. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ mlɛo ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akashwie shi loo eshãaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: What will happen to my crops if I put too much fertilizer on my farm?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Applying too much fertilizer can burn the crop roots and leaves, turning them brown or black, and can end up damaging or killing the plants instead of helping them grow.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai. Ha efee blɔfo loo ediŋŋ. ni ebaanyɛ efite loo efite tsei yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Why is it important to completely clear old plant remains before starting a new farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie tsei momo lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mli dani okwaayeli be hee lɛ aje shishi lɛ?

english: Old plant remains and dried weeds often hide dangerous insect pests and diseases from the previous season that will quickly jump onto your new crops if you do not clear the land properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei momo ni eshwɛ kɛ jwɛi ni egbi lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni jɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ teeɔ. Enɛ baaho oya kɛya oŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ anɔ kɛji ojieee he ni oyɔɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall with plenty of leaves but fail to yield big fruits or tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ebɛ yibii loo bulbs wuji lɛ?

english: Crops often grow excessive leaves without producing food when they get too much nitrogen but lack other vital soil nutrients like phosphorus and potassium that power flowering and fruiting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei kwɛ̃ɔ baai babaoo ni amɛwooo niyenii kɛ́ amɛná nitrogen babaoo. Shi ebɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii krokomɛi ni he hiaa tamɔ phosphorus kɛ potassium ni yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo.

english: Why do my young crop leaves turn yellow and wither when the weather becomes too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibaai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Hot weather causes plants to lose water faster than their young roots can take it up from the dry soil, leading to stress, leaf yellowing, and temporary growth stoppage.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ nu fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Ekɛ nɔnyɛɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ kɛ be kukuoo mli dalɛ ni kpaɔ baa.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when the plants are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tsei lɛ darako kwraa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or is too waterlogged, which prevents the roots from absorbing the food needed for healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow tall and thin with very few fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients, causing them to stretch upward for light instead of putting energy into making fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ ehe koni ekɛ la awo mli moŋ fe ni ekɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather temperatures become too hot, when the soil is too dry, or when insects are absent to help pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni baaye abua ni fɔfɔii lɛ afee pollination lɛ bɛ

english: Cocoa pods turn black due to Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads during wet and humid weather, damaging the pod before it can fully mature.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ black pod hela lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kpatamɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛdara.

english: Why do my yam vines grow lots of leaves but produce very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Yam vines produce small tubers if the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to spend its energy growing leaf branches on top rather than building food storage underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ baajie bulbs bibii kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛwo tsei niji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaama niyenii atoohe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are mature and ready for harvest?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually mature when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, the stem becomes thick and woody, and the ground right around the base of the stem starts to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ eda kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ tsei. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up during the hot afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves curl up during hot hours to protect themselves from sunlight and cut down on water loss, helping the plant stay alive until the heat drops.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni ebu he kɛjɛ hulu la he ni ekɛha nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni latsaa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do some of my planted maize seeds fail to sprout out of the dirt entirely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to come up if they are buried too deep in the soil, if there is not enough rainfall to start germination, or if ants and soil insects eat the seeds before they sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ bɔ ni sa ni baaje dumɔwui lɛ ashishi Aloo kɛji ŋmeii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my vegetable crops look pale and weak even when it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi-aduawai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe waaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal water, sunlight, and manure nutrients directly away from your crops, leaving the crops starved and weak.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do white powdery spots appear on my okra leaves during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ okra baai anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: White spots on okra leaves are caused by a fungal disease called powdery mildew, which grows easily in damp, humid conditions and slows down the plant's leaf growth.
ga: Hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ okra baa lɛ nɔ lɛ baa. Ekwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ. ni ehaa tsei ahe baai lɛ sɛɛ foɔ

english: Why do my harvested vegetables rot so fast when I tie them tightly inside plastic rubber bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ fĩ rɔbɔt plastic kotokui amli jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Harvested crops are still living and breathing. Tying them in airtight plastic bags traps heat and moisture inside, creating a warm, damp environment for mold and rot to quickly destroy your produce.
ga: Nibii ni akpa lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni amɛmiimu. Kɛ́ okɛwo plastic kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaamɔ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛha ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baafite onibii oya.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots turn dark and soft just a few days after transport?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni eyɛ blɛoo yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni akɛmaje lɛ?

english: Rough handling and stacking heavy bags cause internal bruising. When damaged plant tissues react with air, dark spots form and soft rot sets in, lowering the quality before you reach the market.
ga: Baagi ni tsii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ kɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ kɛ mligbɛ fãji baa. Kɛ tso mli fãji ni efite lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ fee ekome lɛ, hei ni yɔɔ duŋ kɛ fitemɔ baaba. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa shi dani eshɛɔ jara nɔ.

english: How do I know when my plantain is mature enough to cut and harvest for the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-plantains lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mafolɔ ni makpa kɛha jara?

english: As plantains mature, their sharp angular edges become smooth and rounded, and the top leaves begin to turn yellow naturally. Harvesting at this stage ensures good fruit quality and proper ripening.
ga: Kɛji akɛ plantains lɛ eda kwraa lɛ, eshishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nɛkɛ ŋmaakpamɔ fã nɛɛ haa aduawai lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛshwereɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop in the hot afternoon but look fresh again by morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii gboɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli, shi amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa kɛ hejɔɔmɔ leebi lɛ?

english: Drooping is the plant's natural defense against heat. Leaves curl and droop to reduce their exposure to the sun and save water, then recover overnight as the air cools and roots soak up soil moisture.
ga: Drooping ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Ha ebɔle ehe ni egbee shi koni hulu la lɛ aba shi ni ekɛ nu akafite. Kɛkɛ lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi nyɔɔŋ kome mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ lɛ. ni shishifãi lɛ baaŋɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow while the top stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: When soil nutrients like nitrogen run low, the crop starves its oldest lower leaves to feed the growing top leaves. Yellowing lower leaves mean your soil needs additional nutrients.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ faaa lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ hɔmɔ koni amɛha ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ niyenii. Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia niyenii krokomɛi.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off instead of turning into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when plants face stress from extreme heat, long dry spells, or poor soil food. To survive, the plant sheds its flowers because it lacks the water and nutrients to turn them into fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa kpe. hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ loo niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehiii ni akɛhiɔ shi Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ aduawai ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in full sunlight without shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and small roots that burn easily under full sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains provides shelter and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii. ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi lɛ Tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa mɔ náa he ko ni eyɔɔ fɛo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: If I cut off excess branches or leaves from my crops, will it help or hurt fruit growth?
ga: Kɛ mifo niji loo baai ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ, Ani ebaaye ebua loo ebaaye aduawai lɛ adalɛ awui?

english: Pruning unnecessary or dying leaves helps the crop. It prevents the plant from wasting food on useless leaves, directing extra energy into growing bigger, healthier fruits and tubers.
ga: Baai ni he ehiaaa loo ni egboi lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaye abua ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei akafite niyenii yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa akɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni akɛkwɛ aduawai kɛ bulbs ni dara, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crop plants stay short and weak even when I use good seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ kuku ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui kpakpai tsuɔ nii moŋ?

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that steal water, space, sunlight, and soil nutrients before your crop roots can reach them, essentially starving your crop.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, ŋwɛi, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye onibii lɛ.

english: Why does liquid leak out when I cut crop stems, and does it hurt the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu hoɔ kɛji mifo tso shishifãi lɛ? Ni ani efiteɔ tso lɛ?

english: The liquid is sap, which carries food and water through the plant. Clean cuts during harvest or pruning don't harm the plant because the cut heals over, but rough tears bleed out nutrients and welcome disease.
ga: Nu lɛ ji nu ni kɛ niyenii kɛ nu tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. Nibii ni afolɔ ni he tse yɛ be mli ni akpaa tso lɛ loo afoɔ lɛ lɛ yeee tso lɛ awui ejaakɛ pilamɔ lɛ baatsa. Shi yaafo ni mli wa haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ helai ni akɛhereɔ mɔ hiɛmɛɛ lɛ joɔ foi.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my maize plants turn yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. When the soil runs low on nitrogen, the plant moves what little it has from its old lower leaves to feed the growing top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Beni nitrogen fioo pɛ eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do farmers say planting cowpeas or beans makes the soil richer for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, kɛ́ midu tsina loo ŋmeii lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans have special bacteria on their roots that pull nitrogen from the air and put it into the ground. When the crop is harvested, that trapped nitrogen remains in the soil to help feed the next crop you plant, like maize.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ helai krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ baajie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni oduɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with lots of big leaves but produce tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji waa shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or rich chicken manure, it uses all its energy to grow big stems and leaves above ground instead of storing starch in its root tubers below ground.
ga: Beni ŋmei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei babaoo nɔ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo tsei agboi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ starch kɛ woɔ shishifãhi nɛ a ngɛ zugba a sisi ɔ a mi.

english: Why do groundnut stems bend down and push themselves into the soil after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts produce flowers above ground, but once fertilized, the plant sends out stems called 'pegs' that grow downward into the dirt. The groundnut pods actually form and mature safely underground inside those pegs.
ga: Peanuts woɔ fɔfɔi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛji akɛ awo mli fɔ lɛ Tso lɛ tsuɔ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘pegs’ ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bean pods feɔ ni amɛdaraa shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nakai ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes in the ground for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines off the dirt lets leaves spread out to catch maximum sunlight for leaf food production. It also keeps the leaves dry and away from soil-borne fungi that cause leaf diseases and reduce tuber growth.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa koni ená hulu la ni fa babaoo kɛha foliar niyenii feemɔ. Ehaa baa lɛ hu mli egbiɔ ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni kɛ baa helai baa lɛ he jɛkɛɔ, ni ehaa tuber lɛ dalɛ baa shi.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and thin roots that cannot handle direct harsh sunlight and hot winds. Planting plantains nearby creates shade umbrellas and traps moisture to help young cocoa survive its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo. ni nyɛŋ aná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ haa hulutsoo baa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi koni eye ebua kookoo bibii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do tiny green cocoa pods shrivel up and turn black before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ Koni egbo ni etsɔ ediŋŋ dani eda lɛ?

english: This is known as 'cherelle wilt.' It happens when the cocoa tree naturally discards extra pods it cannot feed due to water stress, lack of shade, or nutrient shortages, though fungal diseases can also cause it.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ ‘Cherelle wilt’ ni baa beni cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni nyɛŋ aye niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ nu mli haomɔ, hulutsoo ni bɛ, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ hewɔ lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai hu baanyɛ ekɛba moŋ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes develop dark rotten spots before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔlɔi diji yɔɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This spot is called blossom end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit or irregular soil moisture. Keeping soil consistently watered helps the plant draw calcium up from the soil to form healthy fruits.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ he nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ amli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ejaaa. Kɛ́ akɛ nu wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛgbalaa calcium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young maize leaves have ragged holes and small caterpillars hiding inside the center leaf funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ani okɛ ohe ewo baa ŋmei ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli?

english: This damage comes from the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the soft center funnel of maize plants to eat young leaves. Catching them early and applying approved controls prevents them from destroying the stalk.
ga: Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ jɛɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ amli. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ nibii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable crops wilt so fast during the Harmattan season even if I water them every morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ daa leebi moŋ.

english: The dry, dusty Harmattan wind pulls moisture out of plant leaves much faster than roots can suck up water from the soil. Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves (mulching) helps hold water in the ground longer.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under strong sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad leaves that shade the young cocoa plants, keeping the soil cool and moist until the cocoa is strong enough to handle direct sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ mli baawa bɔ ni sa ni hulu la lɛ baashɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do I need to support my yam vines with tall sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tsei kakadaji fiɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ asɛɛ moŋ fe ni mahã amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves up towards the sun and prevents fungal diseases that spread easily on damp ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ kwɛɔ hulu la lɛ hiɛ, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ oya lɛ naa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow instead of staying bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of a maize plant usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to grow green leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa loo nitrogen ŋmãa fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ su lɛ aku esɛɛ aba waa.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants dropping off before any fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani aduawai jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot, when the soil is too dry, or when insects fail to pollinate them. Consistent watering and protecting the plants from extreme heat helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo be mli ni kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites hiding underneath the leaves. Spraying the plants with mild soapy water or recommended neem oil helps get rid of these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli ejɔ loo neem fɔ ni ajieɔ yi lɛ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants produce very small cobs when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, their roots compete for soil nutrients and water, while their leaves block each other from sunlight. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to form full cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ he akaŋ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmei ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why should I cover the dirt around my vegetable crops with dry grass during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass (mulching) blocks direct sunlight from drying out the ground. It keeps moisture in the soil longer and prevents weeds from taking over your garden bed.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa, ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ, ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye obɔɔ mli saatsoi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts make the soil better for the next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans have special microbes in their roots that pull nitrogen out of the air and fix it into the soil naturally. When you harvest them, that extra nitrogen stays in the ground for your next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans yɛ nibii bibii krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Beni okpaa amɛ Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it bad for my field if I plant maize in the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating crops keeps the soil balanced and pest levels low.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots become hard and woody if I leave them in the ground too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: As cassava plants mature past their ideal harvest time, the smooth starch inside the roots turns into tough fiber and wood as the plant prepares to store energy long-term. Harvesting on time keeps the tubers soft and good to eat.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ dara fe ŋmaakpamɔ be ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ Starch ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ bafeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa be mli ni tso lɛ saa ehe koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato be kakadaŋŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ akpa yɛ be naa lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋɔɔ.
