english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow maize leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow strong green leaves. Adding well-rotted animal manure or the right fertilizer to the soil will help the leaves turn green and yield bigger ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmei ni sa fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛwo ŋmei babaoo.

english: Why is it bad to sow my crop seeds right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ yɛ be lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rainfall of the season often cools the hot soil, but it is usually followed by a dry sun spell that can dry out and kill young seeds. It is safer to wait until the rains become regular so your seeds get steady water to grow strong roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Shi bei pii lɛ, hulu la ni mli egbi lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui bibii lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ sɛɛ koni aha dumɔwui lɛ nu daa koni amɛshishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my farmland is suitable for planting cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmei ŋmɔ?

english: Cassava grows best in loose, well-draining soil where its storage roots can expand easily without holding excess water. If your land stays waterlogged and muddy for days after rainfall, cassava roots will rot, so you should plant on raised soil ridges to keep them dry.
ga: Cassava kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi ni ato lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo ni nu babaoo emɔɔɔ mli. Kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ muji gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ, Cassava shishifãi lɛ baagboi. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ odu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ koni ekagbi.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl inward to reduce water loss and protect themselves when the air is too hot and dry. Watering your plants early in the morning and putting dry grass around the base as mulch will keep the soil cool and moist, stopping the leaves from curling.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. Okɛ nu awo tso lɛ mli leebi ni okɛ jwɛi ni egbi abɔle shishigbɛ lɛ he ejaakɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi

english: Why do my tomato plants grow plenty of leafy branches but very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ yɛ niji kɛ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Tomato plants spend all their energy growing leaves if they get too much nitrogen or if you let extra branches spread out. Snipping off the tiny sucker branches that sprout in the branch joints forces the plant to send its food energy into producing flowers and fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛji amɛná nitrogen babaoo loo kɛji oha tsei lɛ aniji lɛ dara. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ amli lɛ, enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ niyenii ni eyɔɔ lɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing out small and twisted under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii ni etsɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Yam tubers become twisted when the ground is too hard, stony, or not dug deep enough for the tuber to push downward easily. Planting yams on high, soft mounds of loose soil free from stones gives the roots room to expand long, thick, and straight.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ, tɛi yɔɔ mli, loo atsako lɛ jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ shi mlɛo. Kɛ́ adu sweet potato yɛ shikpɔŋ ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni tɛi bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ kakadaŋŋ, ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni amɛfee tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes through the center of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-babi corn baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on young maize shoots. Spraying the crop early in the morning when the worms are active, or putting a small pinch of clean sand or neem leaf extract in the center leaf funnel, will help clear them.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ naa yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmeii bibii. Ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ leebi be mli ni ŋmeii miitsu nii Aloo akɛ ŋã ni he tse fioo loo neem baa mli nu awo funnel ni yɔɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli. Ebaaye ebua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Black pod rot is caused by a fungal disease that spreads easily in wet, overly shaded farms. Pruning overgrown tree branches lets sunlight and fresh air enter the farm, drying out dampness on the pods and stopping the fungus from spreading.
ga: Hela ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli efɔ ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pod rot baa. Tsei ni edara fe nine lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Yes, cassava and maize grow well together because maize matures quickly in three to four months, while cassava grows slowly at first. After you harvest the maize, the cassava takes over the space, allowing you to get two different food harvests from the same farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he kome. Ejaakɛ ŋmãa baakwɛ̃ oya yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei baakwɛ̃ fiofio yɛ shishijee mli lɛ. Kɛji okpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Cassava baaye he ni oyɔɔ lɛ najiaŋ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa niyenii enyɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains get destroyed by tiny bugs when I store them in my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛto mitsu lɛ mli?

english: Weevils attack stored grains if the maize was not dried completely before storage, leaving moisture inside for the bugs to multiply. Drying your maize kernels in the sun until they are hard and crack cleanly when bitten prevents weevils from surviving in the store.
ga: Weevils baatutua ŋmaa ni ato lɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmaa lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛto. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ashiɔ yɛ mli koni kooloi afɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ aahu kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ mɔ ko ŋmɔ lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmei lɛ naa koni ekajo foi kɛya shwapo lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa farm is suffering from a disease or just drying up from bad weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela miimɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli loo egbi kɛkɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii hewɔ?

english: Crop diseases usually show specific signs such as swollen stems, dark spots on leaves, or hardened pods, whereas weather stress usually causes the leaves across the whole tree to droop evenly. Checking the pods and stems closely helps you tell if a disease is attacking your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ahe helai jieɔ okadii pɔtɛɛ komɛi akpo, tamɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni efuu, ŋmɔtɔi ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ, loo ŋmɔtɔi ni wa, yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ tso lɛ mli fɛɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ ŋmeii kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona kɛji hela yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: What should I do if a crop disease keeps spreading on my farm even after I clean the field?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji tsei ahe helai gbɛ eshwa miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mijie ŋmɔji lɛ amli po sɛɛ?

english: When a disease keeps spreading, it usually means diseased roots or infected plant parts are still left in the soil or on neighboring trees. You need to completely cut out infected branches, clear diseased debris off the land, and plant disease-tolerant seedlings.
ga: Beni hela lɛ yaa nɔ egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Bei pii lɛ enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ loo tso lɛ fãi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lolo loo yɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ. Esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei niji fɛɛ ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ. Jiemɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. kɛ tsei ahe dumɔwui ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ

english: Can diseases travel from my neighbor's cocoa farm to my new seedlings?
ga: Ani helai baanyɛ aya kɛjɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛya midumɔwui heei lɛ amli?

english: Yes, plant diseases can easily spread across farm boundaries through wind, insects, shared farm tools, or rainwater runoff. It is important to monitor your farm borders and encourage neighboring farmers to manage infected trees on their farms as well.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmɔ mli husui lɛ amli oya kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, kooloi bibii, kɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ nɔ. loo nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ Ehe miihia ni okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ husui lɛ ni owo okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtsa tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ yɛ amɛŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hu.

english: How do I know if new seedlings from the nursery will survive better than my old plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui heei ni jɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baahi shi jogbaŋŋ fe mitsutsu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Improved or hybrid seedlings are specially bred by agricultural scientists to resist common local diseases and produce more pods. Buying certified seedlings from approved agricultural outfits ensures you get strong, disease-resistant plants.
ga: Okwaayeli he nilelɔi fɔɔ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ loo akwɛɔ amɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛwo ŋmeii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ kɛjɛ okwaayeli atade ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ haa onaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ.

english: Can I plant a small test patch of new seedlings before changing my whole field?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwui fioo komɛi ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ dani matsake jɛmɛ fɛɛ?

english: Yes, planting a small test plot is a smart way to observe how a new crop variety grows in your specific soil and rainfall conditions without risking your entire farm's income.
ga: Hɛɛ, kaa shikpɔŋ bibioo ko ni ooodu lɛ ji gbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋaa ni oootsɔ nɔ okwɛ bɔ ni tsei heei daa yɛ oshikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ shihilɛi amli. ni okɛ shika fɛɛ ni onáa kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ wooo oshara mli.

english: How long does it take to see if new seedlings are growing healthy and free from disease?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani ana kɛji dumɔwui heei lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni hela ko bɛ amɛhe?

english: Within the first 3 to 6 months, healthy seedlings should produce bright fresh shoots, strong leaves, and sturdy stems. If you notice yellowing leaves or stunted growth early on, it may indicate soil issues or early disease.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 6 lɛ mli lɛ, esa akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ awo ŋmeii heei, baai ni wa, kɛ tsei ni wa. Kɛji ona baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo amɛdalɛ ni egbɔjɔ mra lɛ, Ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ naagba loo hela ko yɛ shishijee bei lɛ amli.

english: If I cut down my cocoa trees, what other crops can I plant on my land to make money quickly?
ga: Kɛji mifo kookoo tso Mɛni kroko manyɛ madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni maná shika oya?

english: You can plant food crops like plantain, cassava, maize, or vegetables. These crops mature quickly, provide immediate food and cash income, and plantains can also supply useful shade if you decide to replant cocoa later.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu niyenii tamɔ plantains, cassava, ŋmãa loo aduawai. Tsei nɛɛ daa oya. Ha niyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni oná shika Ni plantains hu haa hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛji okpɛ oyiŋ akɛ obaadu cocoa sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees stop producing good yield as they get older?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ kpaɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age, their trunks and roots become weaker, making it harder for them to draw nutrients from the soil and fight off diseases. Over time, this natural aging reduces flowering and pod production.
ga: Kɛji kookoo tso lɛ da lɛ Tso lɛ shishi kɛ shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa cacao tsei lɛ akɛ amɛaajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛkɛ helai awuu. Beni be hoɔ lɛ Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ nɛɛ haa fɔfɔii kɛ podi ni ajieɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Is it safe to plant new seedlings right where I dug out diseased cocoa trees?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu dumɔwui heei yɛ he ni mifo kookoo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: It is risky to plant immediately in the exact same spot because disease germs and fungi can live in the remaining soil and old roots. You should clear and burn the diseased roots, let the soil rest, or treat the ground before planting new seedlings.
ga: Kɛ́ adu yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyɛ oshara ejaakɛ helai kɛ ŋmeii baanyɛ ahi sũ lɛ kɛ shishifãi momo ni eshwɛ lɛ amli. Esa akɛ ojie shishifãi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni oshã amɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe. loo okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii dani odu dumɔwui heei

english: What happens to my soil if I completely clear my old cocoa farm to start fresh?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mijie mi-kookoo ŋmɔ momo lɛ kwraa koni mije shishi ekoŋŋ?

english: Clearing the land removes diseased plant materials and gives your farm a fresh start, but it exposes the soil to heavy sun and rain. Planting shade crops like plantains right away helps protect the soil's moisture and nutrients for your new seedlings.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oootsi lɛ jieɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ehaa oŋmɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi ekoŋŋ. Shi ebaaha hulu la kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ odu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ he kɛha odumɔwui heei lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily in direct Ghanaian sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the vital shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ Ghana hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kookoo bibioo koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Can I put fresh cow dung directly onto my growing vegetables to help them grow?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmei hee awo mi-aduawai ni mikwɛɔ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara?

english: Fresh cow dung produces intense heat and high levels of ammonia as it breaks down, which can burn and kill young roots. It is best to dry or compost cow manure for a few weeks first so it becomes a safe, nutrient-rich fertilizer for your crops.
ga: Tsina ŋmei hee haa dɔlɛ babaoo kɛ ammonia babaoo baa kɛji efite. ni baanyɛ ashã ni efite shishifãi bibii Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooogbi loo ooofee ŋmɔshi nibii otsii fioo komɛi dani ebatsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow smaller every year if I plant maize in the exact same field every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibioo daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize heavily consumes nutrients like nitrogen from the soil. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot exhausts the soil; rotating maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores natural nitrogen back into the earth.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli babaoo aahu akɛ kɛ́ adu lɛ shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee shoo. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Enɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I protect my young cassava crop from stray goats that keep eating the green leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-cassava tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ tooi ni elaaje ni yeɔ baai eŋɔli lɛ kɛkɛ lɛ ahe?

english: Goats target tender green shoots, so planting a dense living fence of fast-growing, thorny hedges or closely spaced gliricidia trees around your plot creates a natural physical barrier that keeps goats out without costly fencing.
ga: Too lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ odu gbogbo ni yɔɔ wala mli ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya loo gliricidia tsei ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha adebɔɔ mli, adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni yeɔ ebuaa ni tooi akabote mli ni gbogbo ni jara wa bɛ mli.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that weaken the plant and spread viruses. Clearing weeds around your plot and spraying a mild homemade neem leaf solution helps drive these insects away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ ni okɛ neem baa tsofa ni mli ejɔ afɔ nɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni ashwie nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together so I can get more crops on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops compete aggressively for light, water, and soil nutrients. This causes all the plants to grow tall, thin, and weak, resulting in small or empty cobs; proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough resources to form large, healthy ears.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, egbɔjɔɔ ni egbɔjɔ, ni no haa tso lɛ feɔ bibioo loo nɔ ko bɛ mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ toi wuji ni mli wa.

english: Is it safe for my soil if I plant cassava and groundnuts together in the same field?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji mikɛ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei fee ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting them together is very beneficial. Groundnuts grow low to the ground and add valuable nitrogen to the soil, while cassava grows taller later in the season, allowing both crops to share space and sunlight without harming each other.
ga: Hɛɛ, amɛ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Peanuts kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi ni ekɛ nitrogen ni jara wa fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei baakwɛ̃ babaoo yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ. Enɛ haa tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ jaa he ko kɛ hulu la ni amɛyeee amɛhe awui.

english: Why should I cover the dirt around my yam mounds with dry leaves and grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves, called mulching, shields the soil from the harsh sun. It traps moisture in the ground so yam tubers stay hydrated, prevents weed seeds from sprouting, and decays into helpful soil food over time.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli koni eha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ afee fɛ̃i. Etsiɔ jwɛi dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛfiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots become hard and woody if I leave them in the ground too long before harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ wa ni amɛfeɔ tsei kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots store starch for the plant's growth. If you leave mature cassava in the soil for too long, the plant begins re-absorbing that starch to maintain its stems and leaves, leaving the tubers tough, fibrous, and low in starch.
ga: Cassava shishifãi toɔ starch kɛha tsei adalɛ. Kɛji oshi ŋmei ni eda lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Tso lɛ baabɔi nakai ŋmei lɛ ŋmɔmɔ ekoŋŋ koni ekɛtsa eshishifãi kɛ ebaa lɛ. Shi ŋmeii lɛ ni wa, ni yɔɔ fibrous ni starch faaa yɛ mli.

english: Why does soil become hard like brick after cattle walk through my wet crop field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tamɔ brikii beni tsinai etsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy animals walking on wet soil press the dirt particles tightly together, a process known as compaction. This squeezes out all air spaces, making the soil extremely hard when dry, which stops plant roots from breathing and expanding easily.
ga: Koolooi ni tsii ni nyiɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ nyɛɔ muji bibii lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ ji gbɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ compaction. Enɛ baajie kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa waa kɛji egbi. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã mlɛo.

english: Why are the leaves and young shoots on my cocoa trees turning black and dying off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: This is often caused by 'akate' (capsid bugs) biting the tender shoots and sucking the sap. Their saliva leaves dark spots that dry out the stems and kill the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ‘akate’ (capsid kooloi) ni ŋmɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni amɛnuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shĩɔ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni haa tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni efiteɔ baai lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa tree is suffering from 'akate' pest damage or just dry weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ‘akate’ tsɛŋemɔ helai efite mi-cacao tsei lɛ loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi kɛkɛ?

english: Dry weather makes leaves dry up evenly across the tree, whereas 'akate' damage leaves clear black patches, sunken spots on shoots, and dried-up dieback on specific branches.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ fɛɛ gbiɔ. yɛ be mli ni ‘Akate’ fitemɔ lɛ shĩɔ okadii diji ni yɔɔ faŋŋ. sunken point yɛ ŋwɛi ni egbiɔ ni egboɔ yɛ niji pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ

english: Can a cocoa tree recover and bear fruit again after insects have damaged its branches?
ga: Ani kookoo tso baanyɛ aya hiɛ ni ewo yibii ekoŋŋ beni kooloi bibii efite eniji lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, if you prune off the damaged dead wood and treat the tree to kill remaining pests, the tree will sprout fresh, healthy green shoots and produce pods again.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji ofolɔ tso ni egbo lɛ ni otsa tso lɛ he koni ojie tsɛŋemɔ helai ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛ mli. Tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaawo ŋmeii ekoŋŋ.

english: What happens to my crop's leaves if I spray them with an old or spoiled chemical by mistake?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe kɛji mikɛ tsofai ni egbɔ loo ni efite shwie nɔ yɛ oshara mli?

english: Spoiled or improperly stored chemicals can burn the leaves, cause them to turn yellow, or fail to kill the pests, leaving your crops weak and unprotected.
ga: Tsofai ni fiteɔ loo akɛtoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ ashã. ni haa efeɔ ŋmɔŋ loo egbeee tsɛŋemɔ helai Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafee gbɔjɔmɔ ni abuuu he.

english: Why is it important to spray my cocoa trees before they start producing flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afɔ kookoo tsei anɔ nu dani amɛje fɔfɔii ashishi lɛ?

english: Spraying early protects the young shoots from insects like capsids so the tree can store enough strength and energy to hold onto its flowers and turn them into pods.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shishijee Ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi bibii, tamɔ capsids ahe, koni tso lɛ anyɛ ato hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛmɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ni etsɔ amɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and stop growing when there is no shade on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛkpaa dalɛ be mli ni hulutsoo bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are tender and cannot take direct sun. Without shade plants like plantain, the sun dries out the leaves and roots before the tree gets established.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni hulu la nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains bɛ lɛ, hulu la baanyɛ aha baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ agbi dani tsei lɛ adara.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees keep falling off before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi dani amɛfee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off when the tree is under stress from insect attacks, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients, causing the tree to shed flower buds it cannot feed.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ yɛ haomɔ mli kɛjɛ kooloi ni baatutua lɛ, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa fɔfɔii ni anyɛɛɛ aye niyenii.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and shrink while they are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ? Ni eji nɔ bibioo kwraa lolo?

english: Small pods shrink and turn black due to fungal infections like black pod disease or from sap-sucking insects that puncture the skin and weaken the pod.
ga: Pod bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ black pod hela, loo kɛjɛɔ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu ni tsɔɔ hewolo lɛ mli ni ehaa pod lɛ gbɔjɔɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the top leaves are green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves show that the plant is short of nitrogen in the soil, so it pulls nutrients from its older leaves to feed the new top growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, egbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni ekɛha ŋmeii heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do cassava leaves curl up and turn pale during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a sign of mosaic virus spread by tiny whiteflies. The virus distorts the leaves, making it harder for the crop to produce large tubers under the soil.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji mosaic hela ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi. Virus lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa waa kɛhaa tso lɛ akɛ ebaawo bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do some crop seeds brought from outside Ghana grow faster than our local seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi ni akɛbaa kɛjɛɔ Ghana kponɔgbɛ lɛ daa oya fe wɔmaŋ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Foreign or improved seed varieties are often scientifically bred in research labs to grow faster, resist certain pests, or mature early compared to traditional local seeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akɛ maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui loo dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɔɔ jeŋ nilee nɔ yɛ niiamlitaomɔhei koni amɛdara oya. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kooloi bibii komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ loo edaa oya kɛ akɛto blema maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ahe.

english: Why do extension officers encourage us to try new imported crop varieties instead of sticking to our traditional seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ woɔ wɔ hewalɛ koni wɔka tsei srɔtoi heei ni akɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ wɔkwɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni wɔɔkpɛtɛ wɔshishijee seshi lɛ he lɛ

english: New crop varieties brought from agricultural research programs are designed to produce higher yields, resist common diseases, and help farmers get better harvests.
ga: Afee tsei srɔtoi heei ni ajie kɛjɛ okwaayeli he niiamlitaomɔ nitsumɔi amli lɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi ni amɛnáa yibii kpakpai

english: Can I save the seeds from these modern high-yielding crops to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo nɛɛ dumɔwui lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Most modern research-bred seeds lose their high yield strength and disease resistance after the first harvest, so it is best to buy fresh certified seeds each planting season.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui ni atao mli lɛ ateŋ babaoo laajeɔ amɛ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ helai lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do improved seeds brought by agricultural projects cost more than the seeds I save from my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni asaa amɛhe ni okwaayeli nitsumɔi kɛbaa lɛ jara wa fe dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Improved seeds undergo years of careful scientific research, testing, and quality control to ensure high yields, which makes them more expensive to produce than regular farm seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsɔɔ jeŋ nilee mli niiamlitaomɔ, kaa kɛ bɔ ni amɛhi ha lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ afii babaoo. Bɔni afee ni akwɛ koni yibiiwoo aba babaoo Enɛ haa amɛfeemɔ jara wa fe blema ŋmɔ mli dumɔwui.

english: Can crops developed in cooler countries actually grow well in our warm weather in Ghana?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ maji ni mli ejɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ yɛ wɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ mli?

english: Yes, many crop varieties bred overseas are selected for their ability to adapt to warm tropical climates and sunshine like we have in Ghana.
ga: Hɛɛ, ahalaa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akwɛɔ yɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ yɛ nyɛmɔ ni amɛyɔɔ ni amɛkɛ amɛhe woɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli tamɔ nɔ ni wɔyɔɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my improved crop varieties fail to grow properly when the weather becomes too dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso ni mifee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ada jogbaŋŋ beni shihilɛi lɛ mli egbi tsɔ lɛ?

english: Many improved crop varieties require steady moisture and good rainfall to support their fast growth, making them sensitive to unexpected dry spells.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi babaoo ni atsake amɛ lɛ biɔ ni hulutsoo be fɛɛ be kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kpakpa aba koni eye ebua amɛdalɛ oya. Enɛ haa amɛnuɔ he waa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ ba.

english: Do changes in rainfall patterns affect foreign crop varieties more than our local crops?
ga: Ani tsakemɔi ni baa nugbɔshiimɔ mli lɛ saa maŋsɛɛ tsei ahe fe wɔ maŋ tsei lɛ?

english: Local crops have naturally adapted to local weather shifts over many years, whereas some foreign varieties need specific weather patterns to perform at their best.
ga: Kuu lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii etsake amɛhe amɛwo akutso lɛ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi amli yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli. Yɛ be mli ni srɔtoi komɛi ni yɔɔ srɔto lɛ biɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi pɔtɛɛ komɛi koni amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: How do agricultural researchers know if a new crop variety developed overseas will work on my farm?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni okwaayeli he niiamlitaolɔi ale kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni afee yɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ baatsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Before foreign varieties are given to farmers, researchers test them in local trial fields under Ghanaian soil and weather conditions to make sure they perform well.
ga: Dani akɛ maŋsɛɛ tsofai srɔtoi baaha okwaafoi Nibii amlitaolɔi lɛ baaka tsofai srɔtoi nɛɛ amɛkwɛ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli kaa ŋmɔji amli yɛ Ghana shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ shishi koni amɛkwɛ akɛ amɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some new crop varieties produce plenty of flowers but fail to yield fruits on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei heei komɛi woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi amɛwooo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops brought from other regions sometimes react strongly to local temperatures or light levels, which can affect how their flowers convert into actual fruits.
ga: Bei komɛi lɛ, tsei ni jɛ kpokpai krokomɛi anɔ lɛ baatsu nii waa yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ mli latsaa loo la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Enɛ baanyɛ aná bɔ ni fɔfɔi lɛ tsɔɔ aduawai diɛŋtsɛ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do new crop varieties often need different fertilizers compared to our old local crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii heei biɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi kɛ akɛto wɔ maŋbii ŋmɔshi nibii momo lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: High-yielding crop varieties grow faster and produce much larger harvests, which means they consume more specific nutrients from the soil to stay healthy.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛkɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This yellowing is a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. When nitrogen is low, the plant moves what little it has from the older bottom leaves to the new leaves at the top.
ga: Nɛkɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tso lɛ dalɛ Kɛ́ nitrogen lɛ faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves roll inwards during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a natural defense trick crops use to protect themselves from heat. By curling their leaves, plants reduce the surface area exposed to the sun and trap moisture to keep from drying out.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu ŋaa ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Kɛ́ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi, ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ koni ekagbi.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains or banana trees next to my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains loo banana tsei yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Mi kookoo tso bibioo lɛ

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to direct heat and burn easily in strong sunlight. Plantains grow fast and provide temporary shade and moisture to protect the young cocoa plants until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ, ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ehaa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines off the ground instead of letting them spread on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ sweet potato wain tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mahã amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting the vines with tall wooden stakes helps the leaves catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight allows the leaves to make food, which travels down to grow bigger and healthier yam tubers under the ground.
ga: Wein tsei lɛ ni akɛ tsei kakadaji woɔ nɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ yibii lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. Enɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi koni eha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ adara ni amɛná hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over so easily when the fruit stems start growing heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ je shishi amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees do not have deep, woody taproots to hold them in the ground. Because their roots are shallow, the weight of a heavy fruit bunch combined with strong wind can easily uproot the plant unless you support it with a wooden prop.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifã ni mli kwɔ ni tamɔ tso ni baaha amɛfi shikpɔŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Yibii akui ni tsii ni tsii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa fata he lɛ baanyɛ ajie tsei kɛjɛ amɛshishifãi amli oya. Ja okɛ tso fiɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants full of holes with sawdust-like dirt inside the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu ni muji tamɔ ŋmãa yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm. The caterpillar hides inside the central funnel of the maize plant, chewing the young leaves and leaving behind frass, which looks like wet sawdust.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ. Okɛ baai bibii lɛ atsu nii ni oshi ŋmeii bibii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my green cocoa pods turning black and rotting right on the tree during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, cool, and damp conditions. Pruning excess branches lets sunlight and air flow through the farm to keep the pods dry.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni yɔɔ duŋ, ni mli ejɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Afoɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants twisting, curling up, and showing yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. The disease stops the leaves from feeding the plant properly, leading to small roots.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ woɔ amɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ. Hela nɛɛ haaa baai lɛ aha tso lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ daraaa.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too high or when the soil gets too dry. Extreme heat stresses the plant, causing it to drop its flowers to save water and energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots start turning dark grey and rotting just two days after digging them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbo yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ ni mikɛfo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Unlike yams, cassava roots do not have a protective outer bark to store them long-term. Once dug out of the soil, exposure to air causes natural chemical changes that make the root spoil rapidly within 48 hours.
ga: Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ sweet potato lɛ, cassava shishifãi bɛ kponɔgbɛ fã ko ni buɔ mɔ he kɛha be kakadaŋŋ ni akɛtoɔ. Kɛji atsa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa tsakemɔi baa. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo oya yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 mli.

english: Yellow leaves on growing maize usually mean the plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a main plant food in the soil. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps bring back the green color and ensures good cob development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji tso lɛ mli niyenii titri ko, yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the farm after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize takes away a lot of nutrients from the soil. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground, naturally feeding the soil so it is fertile for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ No hewɔ lɛ, eyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do seeds bought from the agro-dealer perform better than seeds saved from my previous maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ahe kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds bought from dealers are specifically bred for high yields, uniform growth, and resistance to local diseases. Saved seeds lose their strength over generations, resulting in weaker plants and smaller yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ mɛi ni jaa lɛ adɛŋ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. shweremɔ ni yɔɔ ekomefeemɔ kɛ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahewalɛ Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Why are caterpillars eating deep inside the funnel of my maize plants during the dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yeɔ mi-ŋmei tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that loves to feed on the tender central leaves of young maize. Checking your field early and applying organic neem oil spray or recommended treatments early saves the center bud so the crop can grow.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni sumɔɔ ni eye ŋmãa bibii lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ. Kwɛmɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mra. Ni okɛ organic neem mu ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsuɔ he nii lɛ atsu nii mra. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tso lɛ ahi shi koni eha tso lɛ ada.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground when heavy rains flood the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits on the field for too long, the roots suffocate and rot. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaagboi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why must I put tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants make food for their underground tubers through their leaves using sunlight. Staking lifts the leafy vines off the damp ground into the sun, which keeps them healthy, catches more sunlight, and grows bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ ebaai ni hulu la tsuɔ nii lɛ feɔ niyenii ehaa eshikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking woɔ wain tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa wain tso lɛ mli waa. Na hulu la babaoo ni oha yitso lɛ agbo

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by intense heat or unpredictable watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist by watering regularly and mulching around the plant stems helps flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ hao tsei lɛ. Ehe miihia ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ nɔ. Tso shishifã ni yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my pepper plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket. It stops the hot sun from drying out the soil, keeps roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akakwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do experienced cocoa farmers plant plantains alongside young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ duɔ dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have wide leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the vital shade and moisture young cocoa trees need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why will planting my crops too close together result in a poor harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mitsei lɛ ni miduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ ŋmaa ni ehiii baa lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded together, they compete with one another for soil food, water, and sunshine. Giving each plant proper space ensures every single crop gets enough nutrients to produce full, healthy fruit.
ga: Kɛ tsei ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛyeɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ehaa enáa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo yibii ni eyi obɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize crops turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking Nitrogen, which acts like food for the plant to grow green and leafy. When the soil runs out of nutrients, adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer like Urea helps restore the green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛha tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná baai Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ni yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔji lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha amɛdaramɔ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. Excess rainfall fills up all the air spaces in heavy soil, effectively suffocating the roots and allowing harmful soil fungi to attack and decay the tubers before harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ he fɛɛ he ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ lɛ mli obɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbɔjɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni oha shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atutua ni amɛfite ŋmeii lɛ dani akpa.

english: Cocoa flowers often drop without forming pods due to extreme heat stress, lack of soil moisture, or attacks from insect pests like mirids (capsids). It can also happen if tiny midges are not present in the farm soil to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii yɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli baa lɛ hewɔ. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ mirids (capsids) ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ adesai bibii komɛi bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow much slower when weeds are growing close to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo kwraa kɛ́ jwɛi bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thief plants that steal food, water, and sunlight away from your crops. When weeds share the same spot, your crops get far less nourishment than they need, causing them to remain small and weak.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ tsei ni juɔ, ni amɛjuɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Beni jwɛi lɛ yɔɔ he kome lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaná niyenii fioo fe bɔ ni he hiaa amɛ. Enɛ haa jwɛi bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over so easily during light winds before the bunches mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli wa waa mli lɛ? Dani tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ kwraa?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots holding up a heavy stem. Tiny underground worms called nematodes or stem borer grubs often eat away the root structure, weakening the plant's hold on the soil so that even light winds can tip them over.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni hiɛɔ tso ni tsii lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ. Ehaa tsei lɛ ahe ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he lɛ baa shi. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa blɛoo lɛ po baanyɛ aha amɛku amɛsɛɛ.

english: Why do I get very small corn cobs when I plant many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmãa bibii waa nɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo lɛ? Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crowded roots fight one another for limited water and soil nutrients. Because no individual plant receives enough food, every plant produces smaller, underdeveloped cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shishifãi ni mli wa lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni fa fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso aŋkroaŋkro ko bɛ ni naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. No hewɔ lɛ tso fɛɛ tso woɔ ŋmeii bibii ni edako jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into tight knots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmeii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on young foliage, or by viruses spread by these insects that distort how the leaves expand as they grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Enɛ fiteɔ bɔ ni baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: How does putting animal manure into my soil help my crops survive long dry spells?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli?

english: Manure acts like a sponge in the soil. It binds soil particles together so the land can absorb and hold onto rainwater for a much longer time, allowing crop roots to drink even when dry weather begins.
ga: Manure tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ekɛ sũ mli nibii bibii lɛ feɔ ekome bɔni afee ni sũ lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ ni ehi mli be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ je shishi po.

english: Why is it better for me to water my vegetable garden early in the morning rather than at night?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miwoɔ mi-aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu babaoo leebi fe gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning lets the roots absorb moisture before the hot afternoon sun arrives. Watering at night leaves foliage wet for hours, creating a damp environment where fungal diseases thrive.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛjieɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ afɔ amɛ nu gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɛlɛtswai babaoo. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do my yam vines stretch so long and produce very thin leaves when planted under thick tree shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ daa kakadaŋŋ ni ewoɔ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa kɛ́ adu yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa shishi lɛ?

english: Yam plants use sunlight to make food for growing large tubers. When shaded heavily, the vine uses all its energy stretching high to reach light instead of using that strength to build thick foliage and large tubers under the ground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni amɛkɛwoɔ bulbs agboi. Kɛji akɛ ekɛ shading miiwo la mli waa lɛ Wein tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛgbalaa elɛɛmɔ mli koni eshɛ la lɛ he. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ jamɛ a he wami ɔ kɛ woɔ tsohi nɛ a mi wa kɛ bulb nguahi ngɛ zugba a sisi.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and stay small even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efeɔ bibii kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to make food and grow green. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure gives the maize the food it needs to turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsei he hiaa koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔŋ Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I clear my land without burning the weeds and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni mikɛshãaa jwɛi kɛ baai lɛ?

english: Burning land destroys beneficial soil organisms and burns away good organic nutrients. Leaving cleared weeds to decay naturally on the farm feeds the soil and traps moisture so crops withstand hot dry spells better.
ga: Hei ni ashã lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ni eshãa nibii kpakpai ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ jwɛi ni ajie lɛ lɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ adamɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa ni mli egbi lɛ amli.

english: How far apart should I plant my cassava cuttings in the soil?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ mi-cassava ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings about 1 meter apart gives each plant enough space underground to spread out its roots and grow big, heavy tubers without competing with neighboring plants for water and soil nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei niji ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mita kome lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ekɛgbɛɔ eshishifãi lɛ eshwaa ni ekɛ ŋmei ŋmeii wuji ni tsii baa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ abɔi akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do I need to make big earth mounds before planting my yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ama sũ agbo ko dani adu ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Mounds loosen the hard soil, making it easy for yam roots to expand deep underground into large tubers while keeping excess water away so the tubers do not rot in heavy rain.
ga: Gɔji lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ sweet potato shishifãi lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ toɔ koni ŋmeii lɛ akafite yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become hard and woody if I leave them in the soil too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots are meant to store food for the plant. Once mature, the plant uses up the soft starches and forms tough fibers, so harvesting at the right maturity time keeps tubers soft and good for eating.
ga: Akɛ cassava shishifãi toɔ niyenii kɛha tso lɛ. Kɛji tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ, ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akpa yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ afee bɔdɔɔ ni esa akɛ aye.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting while still hanging on the trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in dark, damp environments. Pruning excess shade branches allows sunlight and air flow to dry out the farm and stop the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni edɔ waa lɛ kɛbaa. Niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo fe nine ni afoɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa koni eha ŋmɔ lɛ mli agbi ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: What makes the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the juices out of young leaves. Spraying plants with neem leaf water or recommended bio-pesticides controls these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ neem baa mli nu loo tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni ajieɔ yi lɛ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaakudɔ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before they turn into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, dry winds, or irregular watering. Giving tomato plants consistent moisture at their roots helps flowers stay on and develop into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaaa lɛ ni bɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ hao tsei lɛ. Kɛ́ oha o-tomato tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ mli fũu daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize help my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts naturally pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil. This feeds the maize planted beside them and keeps your soil rich without buying extra chemical fertilizers.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni aha ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ niyenii. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Why do small insects destroy my harvested maize grains inside the storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miifite mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikpa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Grain weevils attack corn that still contains hidden moisture. Thoroughly drying your maize under the sun until the kernels are hard before storing them in airtight hermetic bags prevents insects from surviving.
ga: Grain weevils lɛ tutuaa ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lolo lɛ. Akɛ hulu shwieɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ baawa dani akɛwoɔ vacuum kotokui amli koni ŋmeii akahi shi.

english: How do I know which rice variety is best suited for my land in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmãa henɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha mishikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ?

english: Rice varieties are suited for different land types: lowland or valley swamp areas require varieties like Jasmine 85 or AGRA Rice that thrive in standing water, while upland varieties prefer well-drained soils without flooding.
ga: Omɔ henɔi lɛ hi kɛha shikpɔji srɔtoi: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ loo hei ni ŋmeii yɔɔ yɛ jɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ biɔ omɔ henɔi tamɔ Jasmine Rice 85 loo AGRA omɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni mli ejɔ mli. Yɛ be mli ni gɔŋ nɔ tsei srɔtoi lɛ sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nu afua bɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops yield much better when I plant right at the beginning of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai babaoo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Planting at the onset of the rains gives seeds maximum warm soil moisture to establish strong, deep roots quickly before mid-season dry spells or heavy weed pressure occur.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni afee shishifãi ni mli wa, ni mli kwɔ oya dani be teŋgbɛ nugbɔshiimɔi loo jwɛi ni naa wa aba.

english: Why are my rice plant leaves turning yellow even when there is enough water in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Ani nu lɛ fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yellow leaves usually signal a lack of essential nutrients, particularly nitrogen, which plants use to make their leaves green and healthy; adding nitrogen fertilizer or organic manure corrects this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ bɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa Nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why is it harmful if I scatter my seeds too closely together instead of spacing them out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara kɛji migbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni magbala amɛteŋ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and air, leading to tall, weak plants that produce very small grains or fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ haa tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ dumɔwui loo aduawai bibii waa lɛ baa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak and grow so slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛdaraa blɛoo waa lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for light, water, and soil nutrients, effectively starving your plants and slowing down their development.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ tso lɛ ni ehaa edalɛ baa shi.

english: Why should I purchase certified seeds instead of planting seeds I saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred and tested to give high germination rates, resist local diseases, and produce uniform, heavy yields, whereas saved seeds lose vigor and yield potential over time.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni aka amɛ akwɛ koni ana kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ. local disease resistance ni ekɛ yibiiwoo ni yaa nɔ daa ni tsii baa Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant the same crop on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and soil diseases to build up, whereas rotating with legumes like cowpeas restores nitrogen and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa ekoŋŋ ni ehaa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ kpaa.

english: Why do insect pests seem to multiply and cause more damage during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fa babaoo ni amɛfiteɔ nii babaoo yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Dry conditions stress plants, making them weaker and easier targets for pests, while hot weather speeds up insect breeding cycles without heavy rains to wash the bugs off the leaves.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ haa tsei haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ewaaa akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ atutua amɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa kooloi lɛ fɔɔ oya ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni ekɛbaafɔ kooloi lɛ ahe yɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does rice need water standing on the farm during certain growing stages?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu he hiaa ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ bei komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Standing water suppresses competing weeds naturally and provides continuous moisture that the rice plant requires during flowering to develop full, heavy grains.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ anaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ ni he hiaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛwo dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ ni tsii.

english: How can I tell when my rice field is matured and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Rice is ready to harvest when most of the grain heads turn from green to a golden yellow color and the grains feel hard and firm when squeezed between your fingers.
ga: Omɔ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa beni ŋmaa yitsei lɛ ateŋ babaoo tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ mli lɛ. Ni dumɔwui lɛ baanu he akɛ amɛhe wa ni amɛhe wa kɛji akɛ okɛ oniji mimɔ mli.

english: Why are snails coming onto my farm at night and eating my crop leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baa miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbɛkɛ ni amɛyeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ?

english: Snails are nocturnal creatures that look for cool, damp places during the day and come out at night to feed on tender leaves, stems, and fruits, leaving slimy trails and large holes in your crops.
ga: Snails ji gbɛkɛ koolooi ni taoɔ hei ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ yɛ gbi mli. Amɛjeɔ kpo gbɛkɛ koni amɛbaye baai, tsei ashishifãi, kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ. Eshiɔ gbɛi ni shwieɔ shi kɛ bulɛi wuji yɛ onibii amli.

english: How can I protect my farm from pests that seem to eat almost any plant or food they find?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ni tamɔ nɔ ni amɛyeɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ tso loo niyenii fɛɛ ni amɛnaa lɛ ahe?

english: Pests that eat many types of food are opportunistic. You can control them by clearing weeds where they hide, keeping the farm clean of decomposing waste, and using simple traps or barriers around your crop beds.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ niyenii srɔtoi babaoo lɛ ji mɛi ni taoɔ hegbɛi. Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni oootsi yɛ he ni amɛtee lɛ nɔ. Ha ŋmɔ lɛ mli atse ni jwɛi ni fiteɔ akafee nɔ ko. Ni okɛ tsɔnei loo gbɛtsii nii ni yɔɔ mlɛo atsu nii yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Can I feed leftover crop leaves and vegetable waste to snails if I want to raise them alongside my crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ maha ŋmeii baai kɛ aduawai amli nibii ni eshwɛ? Ni kɛji akɛ miisumɔ ni makwɛ amɛ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe hu?

english: Yes, snails feed easily on crop residues like pawpaw leaves, cabbage scraps, and fruit peelings, making snail rearing a great way to recycle farm waste into additional income.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ tamɔ pawpaw baai, kaabeji ni eshwɛ, kɛ aduawai ahe tsɔi oya. Enɛ haa ŋmeii akwɛmɔ feɔ gbɛ kpakpa ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ ŋmɔ mli jwɛi tsuɔ nii ekoŋŋ koni aná shika kroko.

english: Is it good to bury raw animal waste or meat scraps directly under my crop soil to fertilize my plants?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ mafu koolooi ni egboi loo loo ni eshwɛ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ koni mikɛwo mitsei lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii?

english: Burying raw animal waste directly in crop soil is risky because it attracts flies, maggots, and scavengers, and can generate harmful heat and bacteria that burn crop roots. It is best to compost animal waste thoroughly before applying it to crops.
ga: Koolooi ashwiei ni afeee lɛ ŋmɔŋ ni aaafu yɛ shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ egbalaa ŋmeii, ŋmeii, kɛ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ dɔlɛ kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni shãa tsei shishifãi lɛ aba. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofee ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ dani okɛtsu nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ.

english: Can crushed snail shells be helpful to my farm soil?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni atswa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yes, ground snail shells are rich in calcium, which helps lower soil acidity and supplies essential nutrients that strengthen plant cell walls, helping prevent fruit rotting in crops like tomatoes.
ga: Hɛɛ, calcium babaoo yɛ ŋshɔŋlooi ni atswa lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ acid baa shi, ni ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa ni wajeɔ tsei amli wala yibii lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ aduawai ni fiteɔ yɛ tsei tamɔ tomatoi amli lɛ naa.

english: Can I turn decayed crop remains from my last harvest into natural fertilizer for my next crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ matsɔ nibii ni eshwɛ ni miifite kɛjɛ minaagbee ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ mafee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, decomposing old crop leaves and stems creates rich organic compost that improves soil water retention and gradually releases nutrients back into the soil for your new crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso baai kɛ amɛshishifãi ni efite lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo. Enɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni fiofio lɛ, ehaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli kɛhaa otsei heei lɛ.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings wither and die when the sun gets too strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have tender leaves and short roots that cannot absorb water fast enough under strong sunlight, so providing shade with palm fronds or temporary nurse crops keeps them moist until they grow stronger.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tsei loo tsei ni kwɛɔ ŋmeii anɔ lɛ ha ŋmeii lɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi amɛhe baawa.

english: How does covering the soil around my crops with dry leaves help my plants stay healthy?
ga: Mulching around Te mafee tɛŋŋ madu miŋmɔshi nibii kɛ baai ni egbi koni eye ebua ni miŋmɔji lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Covering soil with dry leaves, called mulching, prevents moisture from evaporating, keeps root temperatures cool, stops weeds from growing, and eventually breaks down to feed the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho. Ha shishifã lɛ mli latsaa lɛ afee fɛ̃i. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaafite koni ekɛ niyenii aha shikpɔŋ lɛ

english: Why are small holes appearing in the young leaves of my maize plants early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ani ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ anɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Small holes in young leaves are usually caused by early insect pests like stem borers or armyworms feeding inside the plant funnel, which requires early monitoring to prevent severe yield loss.
ga: Buji bibii ni yɔɔ baai bibii amli lɛ jɛɔ mra be mli kooloi ni yeɔ awui, tamɔ stem borers loo cutworms ni yeɔ tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ. Esa akɛ akwɛ enɛ mli mra. Bɔni afee ni atsĩ nibii ni afee lɛ ni elaaje waa lɛ naa

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and drop off during long dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants naturally shed their leaves during dry weather to conserve water and survive, but severe leaf loss can also indicate nutrient deficiencies or sap-sucking pests like mealybugs.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi. Shi baa ni fiteɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mealybugs lɛ bɛ mli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the top leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential food for plants. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the younger growing leaves on top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tso lɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛya baai ni miida lolo yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and wrinkling together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the sap underneath the leaves, or by a virus spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme stress, such as very high temperatures, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients needed to hold onto the blossom.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa kpe, tamɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo niyenii ni he hiaa koni akɛhiɛ fɔfɔii lɛ ni bɛ

english: Why does my cassava produce huge leaves and stems above ground but leaves me with very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai wuji kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi ehaa mi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava puts all its energy into leaves instead of tubers when the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or when it gets too much shade, leaving no extra energy to grow big roots.
ga: Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai lɛ amli yɛ ŋmeii lɛ najiaŋ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo be mli ni enine shɛɔ hulutsoo nɔ tsɔ No hewɔ lɛ, hewalɛ ko bɛ ni eshwɛ ni baaha shishifãi wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my yam vines produce much bigger tubers when I stake them with wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ naa bulbs wuji babaoo kɛ́ mikɛ tsei tswa amɛ lɛ?

english: Staking gets the yam leaves off the ground and opens them up to sunlight. Sunlight helps leaves manufacture food, which is then sent down to build a bigger tuber.
ga: Staking baajie ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha hulu la lɛ aba amɛnɔ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛmaje shi koni ekɛfee yitso ni da fe no.

english: Why do young cocoa trees wither and die if I cut down all the big shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mifo cacao tsei wuji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under full sun. Large shade trees protect young cocoa from direct sun and help keep moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei wuji ni haa hulu kpɛɔ lɛ buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi

english: Why should I cut away the extra shoots coming out from the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni jɛɔ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Too many young shoots (suckers) compete with the main plantain tree for water and soil nutrients, which leads to smaller bunches of plantain.
ga: Tsobii bibii babaoo (tsoots) kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa plantains lɛ náa ŋmeii bibii

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than the crops I actually planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive harsh conditions, and their seeds can lie hidden in the soil for years waiting to sprout as soon as land is cleared and rained on.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Ni amɛdumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afii babaoo, ni amɛmiimɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nugbɔ nɛ.

english: Why does rainwater sit on top of my field for days instead of sinking into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji anɔ gbii babaoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Water pooling happens when your soil is heavy clay or heavily compacted from farm work, which closes the tiny spaces soil needs to let water drain through.
ga: Nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ ji shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo ejɛ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ mli ebɔle ehe. ni tsiɔ he bibioo ko naa Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ aha nu atsɔ mli.

english: Why do my seeds rot in the soil if I plant immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: The very first rain often heats up dry soil without moistening it deeply, creating a warm, damp environment that rots seeds before steady rains arrive to nourish them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ haaa. Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa koni eha dumɔwui lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: Officer, why do people advice that I should leave my farm land to rest for a few years before planting crops on it again?
ga: Amralofoi Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ ashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii fioo komɛi dani adu ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaving land to rest, or fallowing, allows the soil to naturally rebuild its nutrients, regain organic matter, and break continuous pest and disease cycles that build up when you farm the same soil every season.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ ni ejɔɔ ehe loo egbee shi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ nibii lɛ emaa shi ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. nine shɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ ekoŋŋ ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yaa nɔ ni baa kɛji otsuɔ okwaayeli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ mli.

english: Sir, if a piece of farmland is left untouched for many years, why do wild bushes grow back so quickly while my food crops need so much work to grow?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, kɛji akɛ ashi shikpɔŋ bibioo ko ni mɔ ko mɔ ko etaaa nɔ afii babaoo lɛ, Mɛni hewɔ mi koo mli jwɛi lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa oya yɛ be mli ni esa akɛ mi niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsu nii waa koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Wild plants and weeds are naturally adapted to the local environment and compete aggressively for sunlight and soil nutrients, whereas cultivated food crops are bred for crop yield and require human care to survive against wild vegetation.
ga: Koo mli tsei kɛ jwɛi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli. ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fɔɔ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii. Ni adesai akwɛmɔ he miihia amɛ koni amɛhi shi kɛjɛ koo mli tsei amli.

english: Officer, my cocoa trees have been on the land for over ten years, but now they produce very few pods. Why do old cocoa trees stop producing well?
ga: Official Mi kookoo tsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii nyɔŋma nɛ. Shi amrɔ nɛɛ pods fioo pɛ yɔɔ. Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei ni egbɔ lɛ kpaɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age, the soil loses essential nutrients, and the trees spend more of their energy maintaining their heavy branches rather than producing new pods. Regular pruning, shade management, and soil fertilization are needed to keep old trees productive.
ga: Kɛji kookoo tso lɛ da lɛ, niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ baafite shikpɔŋ lɛ. Ni tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo baatsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ niji ni mli wa lɛ anɔ fe bɔ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛfee ŋmeii heei. Ehe miihia ni afolɔ tso lɛ mli. Shade nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa koni tsei momo lɛ aya nɔ awo yibii.

english: Sir, what happens to my cassava roots if I leave them in the ground for too long without harvesting them?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni baaba mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni mikpaaa?

english: If cassava is left unharvested in the ground past its maturity period, the tubers become tough, woody, and lose their starch content as the plant consumes its own stored energy to stay alive.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmãa ni akpaaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ mli kɛyashi be mli ni etsɔ ŋmãa lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa, tso ni ŋmãa ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baaje mli be mli ni tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ehi wala mli lɛ.

english: Officer, why do my crops grow so poorly when I plant them close to large shade trees on the edge of my farm?
ga: Ofisa Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ? Akɛni midu yɛ tso agbo ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ masɛi hewɔ lɛ?

english: Large trees have extensive root systems and dense leaf canopies that take up most of the available soil nutrients, groundwater, and sunlight, leaving nearby smaller crops stunted and deprived of resources.
