ga: Tsei wuji yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ babaoo. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ egbɔjɔ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ.

english: Sir, why is it necessary to clear weeds around my young crops regularly instead of just leaving them alone?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Mi tsei bibii lɛ yɛ daa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from young crops. Clearing them ensures your crops get all the essential nourishment they need to build strong stems and roots.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la ni he hia, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛná tsei kɛ shishifãi ni wa.

english: Extension officer, I worked very hard clearing and weeding my farm, but my maize leaves are still turning pale yellow. What makes maize behave this way?
ga: Nɔyaa he nitsulɔ Mitsuɔ nii waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ mli. Shi mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lolo. Mɛni haa ŋmãa feɔ enii nɛkɛ?

english: Yellowing maize leaves are usually a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Hard physical labor alone cannot make plants thrive if the soil lacks the necessary nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitsumɔ ni wa pɛ nyɛŋ aha tsei akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Officer, can I keep planting cassava on the exact same piece of land every single year without damaging the harvest?
ga: Official Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi ni mifiteee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Cassava draws high amounts of nutrients from the ground. Planting it repeatedly on the same plot exhausts the soil, leading to smaller tubers and poor yields unless you rotate crops or add fertilizer.
ga: Cassava gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni kɛ́ adu lɛ shii abɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa yitsei bibii kɛ yibiiwoo ni ehiii baa. Ja otsake ŋmɔshi nibii loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli.

english: Sir, what kinds of plants or trees can I put along my farm boundary so that neighbors do not cross over into my land?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛɛ tsei loo tsei manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ husui lɛ ahe? Koni akutsoŋbii akafo kɛba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Farmers often use long-lasting boundary plants like teak, vetiver grass, or jatropha because they remain visible for decades, survive harsh weather, and clearly mark land limits without competing heavily with food crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, okwaafoi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ teak, vetiver loo jatropha tsuɔ nii ejaakɛ amɛhiɔ shi ni anaa afii nyɔŋmai abɔ. Hiɛ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa amli ni okadi shikpɔŋ lɛ husui lɛ faŋŋ ni okɛ niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ akaŋ akaŋ waa.

english: Extension officer, why do some farmers plant cover crops on land they are not using for the season?
ga: Nɔyaa he nitsulɔ Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ be mli lɛ?

english: Cover crops shield the topsoil from harsh sunlight and heavy rains, stop invasive weeds from taking over the land, and naturally add nitrogen back into the soil for future crops.
ga: Tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. Ekpaa jwɛi ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ koni amɛkaye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ekɛ nitrogen kuɔ sɛɛ ekɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Why are the leaves on my corn plants turning yellow before they even grow full ears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani amɛdara kwraa po lɛ?

english: Leaves turn yellow when the crop is missing essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or when the soil has too much water sitting around the roots. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore the green color and supports healthy ear growth.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo kɛji nu babaoo bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni ebaaha toi lɛ ada jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the blossoms on my pepper plants curling up and falling off without making any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛjieee pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers often drop when temperatures get too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when tiny pests like thrips attack the blooms. Keeping soil moist and using neem oil sprays can help keep flowers on the plant.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips tutuaa fɔfɔii. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni okɛ neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ akafite.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl up tightly during the bright afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes can be a defense mechanism to conserve water during high heat, but it can also be caused by insect pests carrying viruses. Providing light shade or mulch helps keep roots cool and reduces water loss.
ga: Baai ni akɛwoɔ tomato mli lɛ baanyɛ afee gbɛ ni buɔ mɔ he koni akɛbu nu he yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Shi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni hiɛ muawai hu baanyɛ ekɛba. Shading loo mulching yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa nu ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do young cocoa trees die if I clear away all the big trees on my land before planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei ni eda ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ dani midu lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that easily burn under full, direct sunlight. They need shade from taller plants or trees during their first few years to protect them from heat and help them retain moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei loo tsei kakadaji adɛŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni eye ebua ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: How do groundnuts manage to form their pods underneath the ground after flowering on top?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni amɛfɔ yɛ ŋwɛi sɛɛ?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated above ground, the plant grows a long stem called a peg that bends downward and pushes into the dirt. The peanut pod then develops and matures safely underground away from animals and sun.
ga: Beni ajie ŋmeii fɔfɔi lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ, Tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs ni shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ ni amɛdara shweshweeshwe yɛ he ko ni kooloi kɛ hulu la bɛ he.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over so easily whenever a heavy storm comes through?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and heavy stems filled with water. Supporting the fruit-bearing stems with strong wooden poles or bamboo forks prevents the weight of the fruit and wind from pulling the roots out.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ tso ni mli tse ni nu eyi mli obɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa loo ŋmeii ni akɛfee ŋmeii fiɔ aduawai lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi aduawai lɛ agbɔjɔmɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ naa koni ekagbala shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛ mli.

english: Why can swamp rice grow in flooded water while my corn plants rot and die in the same water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋshɔŋ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nu afua nu mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mi-abele tsei lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nu kome mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have hollow tubes inside their stems that allow oxygen to travel from the leaves down into flooded roots. Most crops like corn lack this system, so their roots drown and rot without air in waterlogged soil.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ tsɔnei ni mli ewo muji yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ aya amɛshishifãi lɛ amli kɛya shishifãi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ ateŋ babaoo bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to cut tall sticks to support my yam vines instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei niji ni kɛlɛ lɛ? koni akɛfi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ asɛɛ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch maximum sunlight, which provides energy to grow large tubers underground. Keeping vines off the damp soil also prevents leaves from catching fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. ni ji hewalɛ ni haa bulbs wuji kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Wain tso lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii helai baa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the soil if I leave them in flat, heavy ground during rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots require well-drained soil to breathe. In flat, heavy soils during rain, water accumulates around roots, causing root rot. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets excess water drain away.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he hiaa cassava shishifãi koni amɛmu. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni tsii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ nɔ. Nu buaa ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haa amɛgboɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: How does planting cowpeas on my farm help my corn crop grow better in the next planting season?
ga: Te tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ amli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with good soil bacteria to capture nitrogen gas from the air and turn it into plant food in the ground. When cowpeas are harvested, that extra nitrogen stays in the soil to feed the next corn crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai kpakpai tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Be ni esa akɛ akpa tsina ŋmãa Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees scorching and falling off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Without shade plants like plantains or shade trees above them, the sun dries out the leaves quickly and causes them to burn and drop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ dumɔwui bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu la baaha baai lɛ agbi oya. ni ehaa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why should I cut off extra small shoots coming out from the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Extra ni jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ plantain wulu lɛ shishi.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water and plant food from the main plantain stem. Removing the extra ones allows all the nutrients to go into the main stem so it can produce a bigger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ plantain tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie nɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ boteɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni afee dumɔwui wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize is usually a sign that the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is what gives the plant its dark green color and helps it grow strong leaves and ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji nɔ ni haa tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa kɛ ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does planting groundnuts together with my corn help the corn grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni edaa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts belong to a plant family that pulls nitrogen from the air and puts it into the soil. The maize plant can then use this natural soil food to grow stronger without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts fata tsei aweku ko ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Abɛi baanyɛ ekɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ niyenii nɛɛ atsu nii ni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when heavy rains flood my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni eha ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains leave standing water around flat ground, the roots get waterlogged and suffocate, which causes them to rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu yɛ shikpɔŋ kplanaa lɛ nɔ fɛɛ. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu. ni haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ

english: Yam vines produce food for the underground tubers through their leaves. Lifting the vines up on stakes helps the leaves catch maximum sunlight and keeps them away from damp ground diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛ niyenii haa amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Wein tsei lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni aaanyɛ. ni etsĩ helai anaa koni ekaba shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ

english: Why are there ragged holes and dark dirt inside the center leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji ni mli edɔ kɛ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the center of young corn plants and eats the tender leaves. Spotting this early helps you treat the crop before the center of the plant is destroyed.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ni eyeɔ baai bibii lɛ. Enɛ ni oookadi mra Enɛ baaha onyɛ ohere ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala dani tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ akpata.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up and turn small and twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ bibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is often caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the sap from young leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. Removing infected leaves early helps stop it from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Baanyɛ aye abua ni akpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my maize right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long dry spell before the continuous rains begin. If seeds sprout during that first rain, the young seedlings will wither and die when the dry spell follows.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ yaa nɔ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ba.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly when I delay clearing weeds from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo nɛkɛ beni mikɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and quickly steal the water, light, and soil nutrients that your crops need. Clearing weeds early ensures your plants get all the nourishment required for fast growth.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa otsei lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees producing fewer pods now compared to twenty years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei momo lɛ miiwo ŋmɔtɔ fioo fe afii nyɔŋmai enyɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 15 to 20 years, their root systems become less efficient at pulling nutrients from the soil, and old wood produces fewer flower cushions. Pruning overgrown branches, replenishing soil nutrients, or gradually replanting with improved seedling varieties can help restore your farm's yields.
ga: Beni cacao tsei lɛ yeɔ afii 15 kɛyashi 20 lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni tsei ni egbɔ lɛ haa fɔfɔi akushɛi fioo pɛ baa. Niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ Okɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he loo okɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ adu ekoŋŋ fiofio. Ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni aku sɛɛ afee oŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii ni anáa lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my farmland seem to lose its power to grow good crops after farming it for many years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai yɛ afii babaoo ni mikɛtsu nii yɛ okwaayeli mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crops remove essential nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium from the ground every harvest season. If you farm the same soil continuously without adding compost, manure, or fertilizers, the soil gets exhausted and can no longer support strong plant growth.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii ni he hia tamɔ naitrɔjin, fɔsfɔs, kɛ potasiam. off the ground every harvest season Kɛji oya nɔ otsu shikpɔŋ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ he nii ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafite ni enyɛŋ eye ebua tsei ni daraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ dɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the big trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and shallow root systems that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or leaving scattered forest trees creates a cool canopy that protects young cocoa until their roots grow strong enough to handle full light.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ dumɔwui bibii loo tsei ni ashiɔ yɛ koo lɛ mli ni egbɛ eshwã lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ la babaoo.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers without forming pods during prolonged dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Flowering requires a lot of water and energy. When water is scarce during a drought, the tree enters survival mode and drops its flowers to preserve moisture for its main stem and leaves until the rains return.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ biɔ nu kɛ hewalɛ babaoo. Kɛji nu faaa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ baaya shihilɛ mli ni amɛbaajie fɔfɔii koni amɛkɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he kɛha tso lɛ shishi kɛ baai titrii lɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why should I plant cassava or maize between my young tree crops instead of growing trees alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe tsei lɛ pɛ?

english: Tree crops take several years to mature and yield income. Planting fast-growing food crops like maize or cassava alongside young trees provides immediate food and quick cash flow for your household while your main tree crop slowly develops.
ga: Tsei heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛdaraa ni amɛwoɔ yibii. Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni aduɔ Kɛfata tsei bibii ahe Ebaaha oshia lɛ niyenii kɛ shika ni baa oya. Beni otsei titrii ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ daraa fiofio lɛ

english: Why do I need to cut off healthy-looking branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ aniji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the middle of the tree to allow sunlight and fresh air to flow through the canopy. This prevents excess humidity that causes diseases and directs the plant's food supply into growing larger cocoa pods rather than unnecessary leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli lɛ, egbeleɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ tsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni kɛ hela baa lɛ naa, ni ekwɛɔ tso lɛ niyenii nɔ kɛtsɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi wuji ni ekwɛɔ yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ najiaŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Black pod is caused by a microscopic fungal parasite that thrives in wet, damp weather. High humidity and splashing raindrops spread fungal spores from the soil onto lower pods, making wet rainy seasons the peak time for pod rot.
ga: Fungal parasites bibii ni yaa hiɛ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. Fɛ̃i ni mli wa kɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ gbɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa shishigbɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ amli. Enɛ haa nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ feɔ be ni ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ waa.

english: Why do new hybrid cocoa varieties start bearing fruit much faster than traditional cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei heei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi mra kwraa fe blema kookoo tsei lɛ?

english: Hybrid cocoa varieties are bred by scientists to grow fast, develop strong stem systems early, and flower earlier in their lifespan, allowing them to start bearing pods in about 2 to 3 years instead of waiting 5 years like older varieties.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔi fɔɔ cocoa hybrids koni amɛdara oya. Feemɔ stem gbɛjianɔtoo ni mli wa mra. ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi mra fe bɔ ni ehiɔ shi lɛ Enɛ haa amɛjeɔ ŋmeii afeemɔ shishi yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaamɛ afii 5 tamɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni etsɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it wasteful to apply fertilizer to my crops right before a heavy downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji fitemɔ akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo miŋmɔshi nibii amli dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away topsoil and fertilizer before crop roots have time to absorb the nutrients. Fertilizer works best when applied to moist soil during light rain or just after heavy rains have passed so it sinks gently down to the root zone.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo loo beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eho sɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagbee shi fiofio kɛyashɛ shishifã lɛ he

english: Why do my crops flower early in some years and late in other years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ fɔɔ mra yɛ afii komɛi amli ni sɛɛ mli yɛ afii krokomɛi amli lɛ?

english: Crops do not follow a calendar date; they respond to environmental triggers like the onset of first rains and changes in soil temperature. When rains come early, the shift in moisture signals to the plant that it is safe to begin flowering.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nyiɛɛɛɛ kalanda gbi lɛ sɛɛ. Amɛtsuɔ shihilɛ mli nibii ni tsirɛɔ amɛ tamɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli latsaa tsakemɔi ahe nii. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ oya lɛ Humidity tsɔɔ tso lɛ akɛ eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ebaafɔ fɔfɔi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning pale yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen. Nitrogen gives plants their deep green color and helps them grow big; adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will restore their health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Nitrogen haa tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does planting beans or groundnuts make my soil better for the next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like beans and groundnuts have special root nodules that pull nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with bushy leaves but produces very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai bibii shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava receives too much nitrogen fertilizer or excessive water, it puts all its energy into growing foliage above ground instead of storing starch in the underground roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmei loo nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Ebaaŋɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shweremɔ mli lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa trees lose their leaves and wilt during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ baa shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees drop leaves to save water when the hot, dry winds dry out the air. Planting shade trees nearby helps protect them from intense sun and soil evaporation.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he beni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ lɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lasu ni hoɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller harvests when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak stems and smaller yields per plant.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo ni baa shi yɛ tso kome mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and growing twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking sap from young leaves, or by viruses transmitted by these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato seedlings fall over and die at the soil line after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato dumɔwui gboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: This is caused by 'damping-off,' a fungal disease that thrives in soggy soil and attacks the delicate stem base of young seedlings.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji 'Damp', ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ ni etutuaa tsei bibii ashishi

english: Why are there ragged holes and dark dirt inside the center funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji ni mli edɔ kɛ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the leaf funnel to eat tender tissue, leaving behind droppings.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii amli koni amɛye ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ni amɛshiɔ ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off without setting any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho ni tomato ko bɛ he lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop when plants experience heat stress, irregular watering, or poor pollination, which forces the plant to discard flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo pollination ni ehiii Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛshwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do I need to support my yam vines off the ground with wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei akwɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking spreads out yam leaves so they can catch maximum sunlight to build large tubers, while keeping vines off damp soil prevents leaf spot diseases.
ga: Staking gbɛɔ sweet potato baai lɛ eshwaa koni eha amɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛfee bulbs agboi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, wein tsei ni oootsi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ he lɛ baatsi baa he hela naa.

english: Why do some cocoa trees produce ripe pods almost every month while others only produce during the main crop season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei komɛi woɔ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ daa nyɔŋ nɔ lɛ? yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi woɔ yibii yɛ be titri ni amɛdaraa lɛ mli pɛ.

english: Cocoa trees produce flowers and pods continuously if they consistently receive proper nutrients, moisture, and maintenance, whereas neglected trees only have enough energy to fruit during the peak rainy season.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baaya nɔ awo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii kɛji amɛná niyenii kpakpa, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kwɛmɔ ni sa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni aku hiɛ ashwie amɛnɔ lɛ pɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛwoɔ yibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: How often am I supposed to harvest ripe pods from my cocoa trees?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ makpa cacao tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Ripe pods should ideally be harvested every two to three weeks to prevent over-ripening, which stops pods from rotting on the tree and encourages the plant to keep growing fresh pods.
ga: Yɛ shishitoo mla naa lɛ, esa akɛ akpa Ripe pods lɛ daa otsii enyɔ loo etɛ koni pods lɛ akagbɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ agbo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ koni eya nɔ ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei.

english: How does applying fertilizer actually help my cocoa trees make more pods?
ga: Te ebaafee tɛŋŋ ni kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mi-kookoo tso lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo akwɛ̃?

english: Fertilizer feeds the soil with vital nutrients like potassium and phosphorus that cocoa trees need to form strong roots, blossom flowers, and develop healthy pods.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium kɛ phosphorus. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa cacao tso lɛ koni shishifãi ni wa aba, ewo fɔfɔi, ni ená ŋmeii ni wa.

english: What will happen to my cocoa tree if I apply fertilizer at the wrong time of the year?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛ wo amɛmli yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni esaaa mli?

english: Applying fertilizer during heavy downpours can wash the nutrients away before the roots soak them up, while applying it during severe drought can stress the tree if there isn't enough water to absorb it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ ejie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛtsu nii yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ aná haomɔ kɛji akɛ ebɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaaŋɔ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa tree lacks the nutrients needed to bear fruit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cacao tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii?

english: When a cocoa tree lacks nutrients, its leaves may turn yellow, flowers may drop off early without forming pods, and mature pods may remain small or unevenly shaped.
ga: Kɛ́ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ kookoo tso lɛ mli lɛ, ebaai lɛ baanyɛ afee ŋmɔŋ. Fɔfɔi baanyɛ agbee shi oya ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ. ni pods ni eda lɛ baanyɛ afee bibii loo amɛhe bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli.

english: Why do weeds in my cocoa farm reduce the amount of cocoa I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa kookoo ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with cocoa trees for water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients in the soil, leaving the cocoa trees too weak to produce a full yield.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ kookoo tsei yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ. Enɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo amɛyibii fɛɛ.

english: Why is it necessary to trim extra branches off my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata mi-cacao tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary branches so sunlight and air can flow through the canopy, which keeps the tree healthy and directs energy into pod growth rather than leaf growth.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni etsɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo kɛyaa pod lɛ dalɛ nɔ fe baai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to clear old cocoa pod husks from under the trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkɛ kookoo ŋmeii momoi ato lɛ? Je kpo kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi?

english: Old, rotting husks left on the farm ground act as breeding spots for black pod disease and pests, which can easily spread back onto healthy growing pods.
ga: Tso ni egbɔ ni egbo ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ he ni black pod hela kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɔɔ yɛ. ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ekoŋŋ kɛbatsɔ ŋmeii ni miida ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli lɛ mlɛo

english: Why do many small cocoa flowers dry up and fall off before turning into full pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔi bibii lɛ Fɔfɔi babaoo gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop extra flowers if they don't have enough water or nutrients to support full pod growth, or if the tree is stressed by heat and disease.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baajie fɔfɔii kɛjɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛbɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ akwɛ̃ kwraa. aloo kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ kɛ helai miigba tso lɛ naa.

english: Why do ripe cocoa pods turn black and rot if I leave them on the tree for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Overripe pods attract fungal diseases like black pod, which feed on the sweet husks and slowly destroy the cocoa beans inside while spreading to nearby healthy pods.
ga: Pods ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ gbalaa fungal helai tamɔ pods diji, ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ lɛ ni amɛyaa hiɛ fiofio. Efiteɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ be mli ni egbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ hu amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants need shade from plantains or other trees to survive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa ni ená hulutsoo kɛjɛ plantains loo tsei krokomɛi adɛŋ koni ehi shi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight and can easily dry out or burn. Planting plantains alongside young cocoa provides shade, retains moisture in the soil, and protects the delicate seedlings until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. ni ebaanyɛ egbi loo eshã oya Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ baaha hulutsoo aba. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obu dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in high humidity and excessive moisture. Rain spreads the fungal spores from the soil and infected pods to healthy ones, causing them to turn dark and rot quickly.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ kɛ hulutsoo be ni fe nine. Nugbɔ gbɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai eshwaa shikpɔŋ kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛwoɔ duŋ ni amɛfiteɔ oya.

english: Why is it important to prune or cut off extra branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afo loo ajie niji krokomɛi kɛjɛ kookoo tso ni eda lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy to allow sunlight and fresh air to reach all parts of the plant. This reduces moisture trapped among leaves, lowers the risk of fungal diseases, and helps the tree focus its energy on producing healthy flowers and pods.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ he lɛ, egbeleɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋmɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ aba shi. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa fɔfɔi kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ afeemɔ nɔ.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every time I plant maize on the exact same land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ feɔ bibioo be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Repeatedly planting the same crop depletes specific nutrients from the soil every season. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or beans restores essential soil nutrients, especially nitrogen, keeping the soil fertile for future crops.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite daa be. Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. titri lɛ nitrogen Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa shi kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my crops grow tall with green leaves but fail to produce big fruits or seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai eŋɔli shi ewooo aduawai loo dumɔwui wuji lɛ?

english: This usually happens when the soil has too much nitrogen and not enough phosphorus or potassium. Nitrogen promotes leafy green growth, while phosphorus and potassium are needed for strong root development, flowering, and fruit formation.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ sũ lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ fa babaoo ni phosphorus loo potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Nitrogen haa baa eŋɔli lɛ daa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium he miihia koni shishifãi ni mli wa aba, fɔfɔi, kɛ aduawai afeemɔ.

english: What causes holes in my young maize leaves and destroys the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji miiba mi-baby corn lɛ mli ni efite teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, caterpillars that feed on the soft interior leaves and growing point of maize plants. Identifying them early and applying approved biopesticides or recommended treatments can save your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei amli baai bibii kɛ hei ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni oooyɔse amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ atsu nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ohere oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala.

english: Why do my cassava roots start to rot underground if left in the soil too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots mature after a specific timeframe depending on the variety. Leaving mature cassava in overly wet or waterlogged soil causes soil bacteria and fungi to attack the roots, leading to underground rot and spoilage.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ be ko sɛɛ. Edamɔ henɔ lɛ nɔ Ashiɔ ŋmei ni eda yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ fe nine lɛ nɔ Enɛ baaha helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ atutua shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my crop plants curl up and droop during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and drooping is a natural defense mechanism plants use to conserve water during high heat. By reducing the surface area exposed to the sun, the plant slows down water loss through its leaves until temperatures cool down.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu nu he yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛtsɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ ni abaaba shi lɛ nɔ. Tsei baaha nu ni amɛlaaje kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ lɛ asɛɛ afo kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why do some flowers on my tomato and pepper plants drop off without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi komɛi ni yɔɔ mi tomato kɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Flower drop occurs when plants experience extreme heat, drought stress, or poor pollination. If insects do not visit the flowers or if temperatures are too high, the plant drops its unpollinated flowers to save energy.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ shɛ latsaa ni naa wa he. hɔmɔ haomɔ loo pollination ni ehiii Kɛji kooloi bibii eyasaraaa fɔfɔi lɛ loo hulutsoo be lɛ fa tsɔ Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni pollin bɛ mli lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do weeds on my farm reduce my crop yield even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiba miŋmɔshi nibii amli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for light, root space, and essential soil nutrients, not just water. Even with plenty of rain, weeds steal the fertilizers and natural nutrients your crops need to grow strong and produce good yield.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná la, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jeee nu pɛ Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ Jwɛi hu juɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: If I clear weeds from my farm, why should I leave them on the field instead of burning them?
ga: Kɛji mijie jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mashã lɛ?

english: Leaving cleared weeds on the field allows them to decay naturally. As they rot, they turn into rich organic fertilizer that feeds your soil every year, keeping it fertile without the high cost of chemical fertilizers.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi jwɛi ni ajie lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛgboi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Beni amɛfiteɔ lɛ, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli ni haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ afi fɛɛ afi. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ni ekɛ tsofai ni jara wa tsuuu nii.

english: Can rotten grass and plant leaves really feed my soil like store-bought fertilizer?
ga: Ani jwɛi kɛ tsei ahe baai ni miifite lɛ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, rotting plant matter breaks down into vital nutrients that crops need. When weeds and leaves decay in the ground, they continuously enrich the soil so your crops get steady food throughout the growing season.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei amli nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ mli gbalaa kɛfeɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ. Kɛ́ jwɛi kɛ baai gboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Amɛbaahã shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be. Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do some farmers put dry weeds around the base of their crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi fɔ̃ɔ amɛtsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Placing dead weeds around crop roots acts as a protective cover called mulch. As those weeds rot, they feed the soil with nutrients while also holding in ground moisture so your crops survive hot, dry periods better.
ga: Jwɛi ni egboi ni akɛwoɔ Tse lɛ shishifãi ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi nɛɛ miifite. Amɛbaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Will leaving cut weeds to rot on my field hurt my young maize plants?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni afo lɛ ni mashi koni amɛgbo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ awui?

english: No, as long as the weeds are completely cut and dead, leaving them to decompose actually helps your young maize. The decaying plant material improves the soil quality around the roots and helps the soil retain water.
ga: Dabi, shii abɔ ni afolɔ jwɛi lɛ ni egbo kwraa lɛ. Kɛ́ oha amɛgboi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua obi lɛ ŋmãa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Tsei ahe nibii ni egbo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ feɔ fɛo, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli.

english: Is it better to sweep my farm soil completely bare or keep it covered with cut weeds?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaatsi ŋmɔ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ mli loo akɛ jwɛi ni afo lɛ aha nɔ?

english: It is much better to keep the soil covered with cut weeds. Bare soil dries out fast and gets washed away by heavy rain, whereas cut weeds rot into the soil and build up your land's fertility every year.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ okɛ jwɛi ni afo lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ gbiɔ oya, ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, jwɛi ni afo lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ afi fɛɛ afi.

english: How long does it take for cut weeds to turn into useful food for my crops?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani jwɛi ni afo lɛ bafeɔ niyenii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Depending on rain and heat, cut weeds start breaking down within a few weeks. As moisture speeds up the rotting process, nutrients are slowly released into the soil right when your growing crops need them.
ga: Jwɛi ni afo lɛ baabɔi fitemɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Edamɔ nugbɔ kɛ latsaa nɔ Be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ haa nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ yaa oya. Ajieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fiofio. Amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni otsei ni miida lɛ he miihia

english: How do decaying plant materials on top of the soil keep my crops from drying out?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsei ahe nibii ni fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akagbi?

english: Decaying plant material forms a cool blanket over the soil that blocks direct sunlight. This stops soil moisture from evaporating quickly, keeping the ground wet longer for your crop roots.
ga: Tsei ahe nibii ni egbo lɛ feɔ nɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Enɛ baaha nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ akafo oya. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛha otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: What happens to the soil structure when weeds break down on the farm year after year?
ga: Mɛni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ jwɛi fite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi?

english: When weeds decay year after year, they build up soft, spongy dark organic matter. This improves the soil texture, making it easier for crop roots to spread out, hold water, and absorb nutrients.
ga: Beni jwɛi lɛ fiteɔ daa afi lɛ Amɛbua nibii ni yɔɔ diŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni tamɔ sponji lɛ anaa. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛha tsei shishifãi akɛ amɛ gbɛɔ amɛshwãa, amɛhiɛɔ nu mli, ni amɛmɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: How does leaving crop leftovers on the land help my harvest next season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mishi miŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua mikpamɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Crop leftovers from the previous harvest rot down over time and return essential plant food back into the earth. This annual breakdown of organic matter restores nutrients, helping the next crop yield well.
ga: Nibii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli ni ekɛ tsei niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ amligbalamɔ ni afeɔ daa afi nɛɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni enáa yibii kpakpai.

english: Why does land that always gets covered with decomposing weeds stay productive every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni jwɛi ni fiteɔ ehà nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ woɔ yibii lolo afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Land stays productive because decomposing weeds continually recycle nutrients back into the dirt. Each year that organic material decays, it renews the soil's strength so it can support healthy crop growth again.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ yaa nɔ ewoɔ yibii ejaakɛ jwɛi ni fiteɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ekɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Daa afi lɛ, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ koni eye ebua tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛdara lɛ shikome ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it a good idea for me to plant plantains if it rains unexpectedly during a dry month like December?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ madu plantains kɛji nugbɔ nɛ trukaa yɛ nyɔŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ tamɔ December mli?

english: Unexpected rain during dry periods provides rare soil moisture that allows hardy suckers like plantain to establish root systems early before the harsh dry weather returns.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni akpaaa gbɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni faaa ni haa tsei ni wa tamɔ plantains lɛ jeɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ shishi mra. Dani kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi waa lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba

english: If the rainy weather comes at an unusual time of the year, should I change when I plant my crops?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli bei ni jeee nɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ mli lɛ Ani esa akɛ matsake dumɔ be lɛ?

english: Yes, adjusting your planting time to match actual rain patterns ensures your young crops get the moisture they need to germinate and survive their early growth stage.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ otsake be ni okɛduɔ nii lɛ kɛya nugbɔ ni nɛɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha otsei bibii lɛ aná nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛmra be mli dalɛ be lɛ mli.

english: When is the best time of the year for me to plant new cocoa seedlings on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The best time to plant cocoa is at the beginning of the major rainy season so that the young plants can grow strong roots before the dry harmattan season arrives.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu kookoo ji nugbɔ be ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shishijee. Enɛ ji koni tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ aná shishifãi ni mli wa dani harmattan be ni mli egbi lɛ aba.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to plant plantain before planting cocoa on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu plantain dani adu cocoa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain grows fast and produces large broad leaves that provide vital temporary shade to protect tender young cocoa seedlings from hot direct sunlight.
ga: Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni mli kwɔ ni haa be kukuoo mli hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: How does planting plantains together with cocoa help the cocoa trees survive their early stage?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ plantains ni akɛ kookoo duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shishijee fãi lɛ amli?

english: Plantains block harsh sunlight, cool the air temperature around the young cocoa, and reduce soil evaporation, keeping the ground moist for cocoa roots.
ga: Dumɔwui tsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ mli ajɔ Kookoo bɔɔlu lɛ mli. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ aba shi Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha kookoo shishifãi.

english: Will harvesting my plantains eventually damage the young cocoa trees growing under them?
ga: Ani yɛ naagbee lɛ, mi-plantain ni mikpaa lɛ baafite cacao tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ eshishi lɛ?

english: If cut down carefully away from the seedlings, plantain trunks can be left on the soil to decay, which actually adds useful nutrients and moisture back to your cocoa trees.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afo dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ No sɛɛ lɛ, ashiɔ plantain tsei lɛ koni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni no diɛŋtsɛ kɛ niyenii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa cacao tso lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: What kind of weather conditions make plantain suckers grow best on a fresh farm?
ga: Mɛɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi haa plantain tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ sũ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Plantain suckers thrive best when there is warm weather combined with steady soil moisture, which helps them shoot up new leaves quickly.
ga: Dumɔwui daa jogbaŋŋ kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa lɛ fata he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ baai heei oya.

english: How can I tell if my farm's soil has enough water to support delicate new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha mi-kokoo dumɔwui heei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ?

english: You can dig down a few inches and squeeze a fistful of soil; if it forms a ball without crumbling easily, it holds enough moisture for planting young cocoa.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli inchii fioo komɛi ni okɛmimɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nine. Kɛji akɛ efee bɔɔlu ni efooo mlɛo lɛ, nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha kookoo bibii akwɛ̃ lɛ baahi jɛmɛ.

english: Can I earn money from selling plantains while I wait for my cocoa trees to start bearing fruit?
ga: Ani manyɛ maná shika kɛtsɔ plantains ni mihɔ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni cacao tsei lɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi lɛ?

english: Yes, plantains produce food and quick income within 12 to 15 months, helping support your household while your cocoa matures over several years.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains haa niyenii kɛ shika baa oya yɛ nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 15 mli, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekwɛɔ oshia lɛ nɔ be mli ni o-cocoa lɛ daa yɛ afii babaoo mli lɛ.

english: Why is cocoa recommended as a long-term crop to plant on my land alongside food crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ akɛ kookoo atsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ?

english: Cocoa is a reliable commercial cash crop that can generate steady income for several decades once established, giving your farm long-term financial stability.
ga: Cocoa ji jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ. ni enyɛ ekɛ shika ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ eba afii nyɔŋmai abɔ kɛjɛ be mli ni ato shishi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, oŋmɔ lɛ baafee nɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ yɛ shika gbɛfaŋ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is an important food in the soil, or that too much water around the roots is suffocating the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. aloo nu yɛ he fɛɛ he Shishifãi babaoo tsɔ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How do beans help improve the quality of the soil on my farm?
ga: Te ŋmeii baanyɛ aye abua ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Beans have special roots that take food from the air and store it in the dirt as nitrogen, which naturally fertilizes the soil for other crops planted after them.
ga: Beans yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni heɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nitrogen gbɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa tsei krokomɛi. ni adu yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ

english: Is it a good idea to plant my maize and beans together in the same field?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ aaadu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting maize and beans together works well because the tall maize gives space for light while the beans cover the ground to shade out weeds and feed nitrogen into the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa ni kɛlɛ lɛ haa gbɛ kɛhaa la yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha jwɛi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛ nitrogen awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same plot of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize in the same spot every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that attack maize to multiply in the ground.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable plants wilt in the afternoon heat even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: Hot afternoon sun causes water to evaporate from vegetable leaves faster than the roots can drink it up, so the plant temporarily droops to conserve moisture.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa nu ni jɛɔ aduawai ahe baai amli lɛ shwieɔ shi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko.

english: Why do the blossoms on my pepper and tomato plants drop off without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper kɛ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when temperatures get too high, when the plants do not get steady water, or when there are no beneficial insects around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ náaa nu daa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ bɛ amɛhe ni amɛbaawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my maize leaves and caterpillars hiding in the center funnel?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that crawls into the soft center of the maize plant to eat the fresh, growing foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ mli koni eye baai ni miida ehee lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: How do weeds hurt my vegetable farm if I do not clear them early?
ga: Te jwɛi baaye mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji mijieee amɛ mra?

english: Weeds grow faster than young vegetables and steal the sunlight, water, and soil food that your crop needs to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe aduawai bibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara waa ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer to my maize plants after planting?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ awo ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ adumɔ sɛɛ?

english: Maize usually needs fertilizer twice: a small amount around planting time to build strong roots, and a second portion when the stalks reach knee height to help form big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa he hiaa ni akɛ ŋmãa awo mli shii enyɔ: fioo ko yɛ dumɔ be mli koni etswa shishifãi ni wa; kɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ beni tso lɛ shɛɔ tsitsi nɔ lɛ koni eye ebua ni afee ŋmei agbo.

english: Why did half of the maize seeds I saved from my last harvest fail to sprout when I planted them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mijie kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ fã ekwɛɛɛ beni midu lɛ?

english: Stored seeds can lose their ability to sprout if they are damaged by heat, dampness, or insect pests while being kept in storage over the dry season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baanyɛ afite nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛji dɔlɛ, hulutsoo loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fite amɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ.

english: Why do my crops need different types of fertilizer when they are young compared to when they start fruiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi beni amɛdarako lɛ kɛ akɛto be mli ni amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Just like growing children need specific foods to build body strength before they can mature, young plants need nitrogen to grow strong stems and leaves. Once they start flowering and fruiting, their needs change to nutrients like potassium and phosphorus to produce heavy, quality harvests.
ga: Taakɛ gbekɛbii ni miida lɛ ji lɛ, niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi he miihia amɛ koni amɛná gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛ dani amɛshɛ dalɛ he. Nitrogen hu he miihia tsei bibii koni amɛkwɛ̃ amɛshishifãi kɛ baai ni wa. Kɛ amɛbɔi fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ Amɛhiamɔ nii tsakeɔ kɛyaa niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ potassium kɛ phosphorus nɔ. Koni aná nibii ni tsii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops stay small and weak even though I water them every morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa ni amɛhe waaa nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mishwieɔ amɛ nu daa leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: Water alone is like a human drinking only water without eating food. Plants need essential nutrients from the soil or fertilizers to build strong leaves and stems; without proper plant food, watering alone will not make them grow big.
ga: Nu pɛ tamɔ adesai pɛ nuɔ nu ni amɛyeee niyenii. Tsei hia niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai kɛ tsei ni wa. Kɛji tso niyenii ni sa bɛ Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ pɛ haaa amɛdara.

english: Can I spray liquid fertilizer directly onto my plant leaves instead of putting it into the ground?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ afɔ tsei ahe tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Yes, leaves can drink in nutrients through tiny openings on their surface, which works like quick medicine when a plant is weak. However, main feeding should still go into the soil through the roots where the plant gets most of its long-term food.
ga: Hɛɛ, baai baanyɛ anu niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ, ni amɛtsuɔ nii oya tamɔ tsofa kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ niyenii titri ni akɛhaa lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lolo kɛtsɔ shishifãi ni tso lɛ naa niyenii babaoo yɛ nɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my tomato plants turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tso shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: When a plant does not get enough food from the soil, it sacrifices its older bottom leaves to feed the younger top leaves. Yellow lower leaves are a clear sign that your crop is hungry and needs nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ekɛ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ baashã afɔle koni eye ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ. Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye onibii lɛ ni ehe miihia ni akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when the plant feels stressed by intense heat, improper watering, or lack of nutrients. The plant drops its flowers to save its strength, similar to how a person drops a heavy load when feeling exhausted.
ga: Fɔfɔi baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. nu ni esaaa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛhiɛ hewalɛ mli. Etamɔ bɔ ni gbɔmɛi shwieɔ nibii ni tsii amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ amɛhe ejɔ amɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like sticks during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ tsei tsei yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a plant's natural trick to protect itself from drying out. By rolling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun to conserve water inside its body.
ga: Baai ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli ŋaa ni ekɛbuɔ ehe he koni ekagbi. kɛtsɔ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ Tsei haa hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe lɛ baa shi koni ekɛbu nu ni yɔɔ amɛgbɔmɔtsei lɛ amli lɛ he.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to trim off the extra side branches on my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ mifo tsei niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Extra branches steal food and water away from the main fruit-bearing stems. Trimming them directs all the plant's food energy into producing larger, healthier fruit instead of growing useless leaves.
ga: Niji ni fata he lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso titri ni hiɛ aduawai lɛ he. Kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ mli niyenii hewalɛ fɛɛ jeɔ kpo koni ewo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaakwɛ̃ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ

english: What is the benefit of growing tomatoes inside a greenhouse structure instead of open land?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ tomato ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ he?

english: A greenhouse acts like a protective house for your crops. It shields plants from harsh rains that wash away soil food, protects them from hungry pests, and allows you to give the plants the exact water and food they need each day.
ga: Greenhouse tsuɔ nii tamɔ shĩa, ni ebuɔ onibii ahe. Ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni hoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Buu tsei ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ ahe. Ni eyeɔ ebua bo ni ohaa otsei lɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ daa gbi.

english: Why should I add animal manure to my farm soil if I am already buying chemical fertilizers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ afata shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he lɛ? Be ni miheɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ momo?

english: Chemical fertilizer feeds the crop immediately, but animal manure improves the soil itself by holding water longer and making the land soft for roots to spread. Using manure is like giving your soil a long-lasting health boost.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo kɛtsɔ nu ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo bɔni afee ni shishifãi anyɛ akwɛ̃ Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii lɛ tamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings wilt and die during hot afternoons even after watering them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli beni mikɛ nu efɔ amɛnɔ leebi po lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have small, tender roots that cannot suck up water fast enough to replace what the hot afternoon sun bakes out of their leaves. Providing temporary shade using palm fronds protects them until their roots grow deeper.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo shwane mli la ni tsoɔ waa ni jɛɔ ebaa lɛ mli lɛ he nyɔmɔ. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo ni akɛ tsei ahe tsei tsuɔ nii lɛ baabu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field without any bigger plants around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni cacao tsei wuji komɛi bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a protective canopy that guards the young cocoa trees from heat stress and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he waa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he haomɔ he lɛ baa. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves usually turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow strong green leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizers like Urea or well-rotted manure helps restore their green color and vigor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔji kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops every year even though I work it the same way?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Ni mi hu mitsuɔ nii nakai nɔŋŋ?

english: Soil loses its natural nutrients over time when crops take them out season after season without replacement. Resting the land or adding organic compost feeds the soil and restores its fertility for future harvests.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ laajeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa yɛ be kɛ bei amli ni nɔ ko bɛ ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha ejɔɔ ehe loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli afata he lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ni eha ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmaakpamɔi.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo lɛ?

english: Excess water fills up air spaces in the soil, preventing the roots from breathing and causing waterlogging. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps surplus water drain away so the tubers stay healthy.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu, ni ehaa nu shwieɔ shi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to manufacture food for growing large underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground toward the light and keeps them from rotting or getting shaded by weeds.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛyaa la lɛ he. ni etsĩɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite loo jwɛi akawo amɛhe shade.

english: Why shouldn't I allow all the small shoots to grow around one plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ? Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni miida yɛ dumɔwu kome he.

english: Allowing too many shoots to grow causes them to compete for water and nutrients, resulting in small plantain bunches. Pruning excess suckers leaves more energy for the main plant to yield a larger stem of plantain.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji plantains bibii bibii. Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi agbo.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into the leaves and center of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ baai lɛ amli kɛ mi-ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: That damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar pest that feeds on the soft growing center of corn plants. Applying approved pest treatments early in the morning or late evening stops them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni yeɔ ŋmei tsei bibii ni miida lɛ atsui lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ ni tamɔ nɛkɛ baa. Kɛ gbɛ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and twisting together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap, or by a plant virus. Spraying with neem oil or appropriate pest controls helps keep these insects from damaging new leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amli Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofai krokomɛi ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ helai nɛɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akafite tsei ahe tsei ahe tsei heei.

english: Why are flowers falling off my tomato plants without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients can stress tomato plants, causing them to drop their flowers. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps the plant retain its blossoms until fruit forms.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni akɛhaaa yɛ be fɛɛ mli Loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ ni shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ muji wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food and light they need to grow quickly.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ehaa tsei lɛ niyenii kɛ la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and die when I clear all the big shade trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie cacao tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct heat and sunlight. Keeping taller shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains beside them creates a natural shelter that keeps the air humid and protects the tender leaf tissues from sun burns.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli shihilɛhe ko ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants showing small holes and looking chewed up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni ekwɛɔ akɛ eshɛre?

english: Small holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by pests like the fall armyworm feeding on the growing center of the plant. Inspecting the leaves early allows you to remove caterpillars by hand or apply the right treatment before they ruin the grain yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii ni egbee shi ni amɛye tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni edaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii baai amli lɛ baa. Baai lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ onine jieɔ ŋmeii lɛ loo okɛ tsofai ni sa tsuɔ nii dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmaa yibiiwoo lɛ.

english: Will I harvest more cassava tubers if I plant my stem cuttings very close to each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa cassava shishifãi babaoo kɛji midu ŋmeii lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa?

english: Planting cassava too close together forces the plants to compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and resources to grow thick, healthy tubers underground.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni mli wa ni mli wa.

english: Why is it good practice for me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my field after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize draws a lot of nitrogen nutrient out of the ground. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and naturally pump it back into the soil, refreshing your land for the next crop season.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii ni ji nitrogen lɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛsu mli amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee ehee kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know when my yam tubers are fully mature and ready to be dug out of the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ edara kwraa ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yam tubers are mature when the green vines and leaves stop growing, turn yellow, and begin to dry up naturally. This shift shows that the plant has finished transferring its nutrients down into the tuber.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he kɛji wain tso lɛ kɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ kpa dalɛ. etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔi ŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa Tsakemɔ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ bulb lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and rotting before they can ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani tomato lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often made worse by uneven watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the root system absorb calcium continuously.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Ni bei pii lɛ, enɛ haa hela lɛ he okadii lɛ mli woɔ wu yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛjieɔ calcium.

english: Why do seeds saved from last season's hybrid maize harvest produce smaller yields than new certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ nyɔŋ ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred from two distinct parent lines to deliver maximum strength and yield. Seeds saved from that harvest lose those specific high-yield traits in the next generation.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔi akui srɔtoi enyɔ amli koni anyɛ ana hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ amɛ su ni haa amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable garden early in the morning or late in the evening?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning allows plants to soak up moisture before heat rises, while allowing excess water on leaves to dry up. Evening watering leaves foliage wet all night, which attracts fungal diseases.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛjieɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani latsaa lɛ yaa hiɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ agbi. Gbi gbɛkɛ nu haa baai lɛ mli fũuɔ gbɛkɛ muu lɛ fɛɛ, ni no gbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves droop during the hot afternoon sun even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: On hot days, plants lose water through leaves faster than roots can draw it from the ground. The plant temporarily wilts to close leaf pores and save internal water, usually bouncing back once the sun sets.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbo koni ekɛŋa eshishifãi lɛ be kukuoo ko ni ekɛbu nu ni yɔɔ emli lɛ he. Bei pii lɛ, efoɔ ehe kɛji hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil needs animal manure instead of just chemical fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii moŋ fe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ kɛkɛ?

english: If your soil feels hard, dry, and fails to hold water after rain, it lacks organic material. Animal manure improves the physical structure of the soil so it holds water better, while chemical fertilizers only provide direct plant food.
ga: Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ ewa lɛ, egbi ni ehiɛɛɛ nu mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ faaa. Koolooi ashishifãi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ fɛo koni nu lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei niyenii tɛ̃ɛ pɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?
