english: Young cocoa trees need protection from direct, harsh sunlight because their root systems are not strong enough to absorb enough water during intense heat. Leaving canopy trees or planting fast-growing food crops like plantains provides the shade and cool microclimate young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ ahe waaa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni akɛwoɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai amli loo adu niyenii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ aná hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for green leaf growth. Applying well-decomposed animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer early in the crop's growth restores healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni efite jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsu nii mra yɛ tsei lɛ adalɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the soil if I leave them buried during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Excess water in flooded soil starves the underground roots of oxygen, causing mature cassava roots to drown and decay. Harvesting cassava before the heaviest rains begin protects the crop from rotting.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ ahe hɔmɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi ni edara kwraa lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboiɔ. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmãa dani nugbɔ ni naa wa fe fɛɛ lɛ anɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa lɛ akafite.

english: Why should I space out my seeds instead of planting as many as possible close together in one spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbala dumɔwui lɛ amli moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he kome bɔ ni manyɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak stems and small harvests. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to feed and grow full-sized yields.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe waaa, ni akpaa nii fioo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are small caterpillars chewing deep holes into the central leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a pest that targets the tender central leaves (whort) of young maize. Checking your field early and putting neem leaf extract or recommended treatments directly into the plant funnels stops them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmei bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo (worts) lɛ anɔ. Kwɛmɔ hei ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mra ni akɛ neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ awo dumɔ nii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Abaakpa enɛɛmɛi dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite.

english: Why is it bad practice for me to plant maize on the exact same plot of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ gbonyo akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously depletes specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil nitrogen and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Ehaa nitrogen lɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture fluctuates rapidly between dry and wet conditions. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and mulching helps flowers stay on the plant and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi kɛ nɔ ni mli edɔ teŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do older farmers cover the dirt around their vegetable stems with dry grass during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni edara lɛ kɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛ aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry leaves or grass (mulching) acts like a shield against direct sunlight. It keeps the soil cool, prevents moisture from evaporating quickly, and suppresses weeds.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seeds immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ aduawai dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long dry stretch before main rains begin, which dries out newly sprouted seeds. Waiting until rains are regular ensures the soil stays wet enough for young seedlings to establish themselves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔi wuji lɛ jeɔ shishi. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ omɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔwui bibii. koni enyɛ edamɔ shi

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and becoming tiny and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ bibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Curled, distorted leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites that transmit viral diseases. Spraying plants early with soap-water solutions or organic insect sprays keeps these insects away and protects the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Ni akɛ nu ni akɛ saamɔ fee loo organic insect spray ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akabote tso lɛ he ni ebu tso lɛ he.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and dry up when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense heat. Without shade trees or plantains nearby to block the harsh sunlight, the leaves lose water too quickly, turn yellow, and burn.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ bɛ Koni ekɛtsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya tsɔ. Tsɔmɔmɔ ŋmɔŋ ni oshã

english: Can I plant beans together with my maize on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize is very helpful. Beans capture natural nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps the maize grow strong without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Beans lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa ni akɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsuuu nii.

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes the plants to grow tall and weak with small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko.

english: Why do some of the seeds I plant fail to sprout out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds usually fail to germinate if they are planted too deep, if the soil is too dry or completely flooded, or if soil insects eat the seeds before they can sprout.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo nu lɛ mli eyi tsɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ye dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: How do I know if my soil lacks nutrients before I plant my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu?

english: If your previous harvest was very low, or if weeds on the land look weak and pale yellow, your soil is likely tired and low in nutrients required for healthy crop growth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okpamɔ ni okpa tsutsu lɛ faaa kwraa Aloo kɛji jwɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etɔ ni niyenii ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ faaa.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow so much faster than my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally tough and very fast at stealing water, light, and nutrients from the soil. You must clear them early so they do not starve your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni juɔ nu, la kɛ niyenii mli nibii oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Esa akɛ ojie amɛ mra. Bɔni afee ni hɔmɔ akaye oŋmɔshinii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and showing yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curling and yellowing leaves on cassava are signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny white insects called whiteflies. Using disease-free stem cuttings for planting stops this problem.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ yucca nɔ lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni kooloi bibii yɛŋ ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei niji ni hela bɛ mli lɛ tsu nii beni aduɔ lɛ, ebaakpa naagba nɛɛ.

english: What causes my plantain leaves to get large dark spots and dry up early?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi plantain baai lɛ amli tsɔji diji wuji ni amɛgbiɔ oya lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal disease called Black Sigatoka, which spreads fast in wet weather. Cutting off damaged leaves and keeping the farm clear helps keep the plant healthy.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Black Sigatoka, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Baai ni efite lɛ ni afolɔ mli ni aha ŋmɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops wilt in the afternoon even when the soil was wet in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: In the hot afternoon sun, crop leaves lose moisture faster than the roots can suck it up from the ground. The plant wilts temporarily to protect itself from losing too much water.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Tso lɛ baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe koni nu babaoo akafite.

english: Why is it necessary for me to prune or cut off extra branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ loo maŋɔ niji krokomɛi kɛjɛ mi-kokoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unproductive or dead branches, allowing sunlight and air to move through the tree. This prevents fungal pod diseases and helps the tree put its energy into producing pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni wooo yibii loo ni egboi lɛ. Ha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ tsiɔ fungal pod hela naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ pods.

english: Yellowing leaves usually indicate that your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient that crops need steadily throughout their growth to produce strong stems and green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ amɛdalɛ be fɛɛ mli koni amɛma ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ beni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need stakes to lift their leaves toward sunlight, which allows the plant to make energy and produce larger tubers under the ground.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ko ni kwɔɔ ni ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ shishitoo mla ni ji ebaa ni ewoɔ nɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛ bulbs wuji baa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How can I set up my farm so I can harvest and sell produce regularly throughout the year instead of waiting many months for one harvest?
ga: Mato miŋmɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni manyɛ makpa nibii ni miwo lɛ ni mahɔ̃ɔ daa yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ nyɔji babaoo kɛha nikpamɔ kome lɛ?

english: Intercropping short-term crops like vegetables or plantains alongside long-term crops like cocoa or cassava allows you to harvest and generate income continuously while your main crops mature.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ be kukuoo tamɔ aduawai loo plantains ni aduɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli nibii tamɔ kookoo loo ŋmei. Enɛ haa oyaa nɔ okpaa nii ni onáa shika yɛ be mli ni oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops if I leave them growing in the same field?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baaye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui kɛji miha amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, which steals food away from your plants and slows down their overall growth.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli, ni amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli. ni eha dalɛ fɛɛ aba shi

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither when I plant them in an open field without shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn under direct, harsh sunlight, so they need shade trees or plantains nearby to provide shelter and keep the soil moist during their early stages.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ ni haa amɛnáa he ko ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shishijee bei amli.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoot suckers growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Leaving too many suckers causes them to fight the main plant for water and nutrients, whereas leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main stem grows faster and produces bigger bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni ashiɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 1-2 pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ ada oya ni efee ŋmeii wuji.

english: What causes the flowers on my tomato plants to drop off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni haa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai?

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants experience extreme heat stress, dry soil, or lack calcium, which prevents the plant from successfully setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo calcium ni bɛ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ awo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my soil is losing its fertility after planting crops on it for several seasons?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiɛ edɔ waa beni mikɛ tsei ewo mli bei babaoo lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Signs of poor soil fertility include slow crop growth, pale yellow leaves, thin plant stems, and noticeably smaller harvests compared to previous seasons.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii lɛ he ji tsei ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo. Baai ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse, tsei bibii kɛ ŋmaa ni baa shi kwraa kɛ akɛto nyɛsɛɛ be lɛ he.

english: Why do my crops grow much slower during the dry harmattan period even when I water them manually?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo kwraa yɛ harmatta ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji mi diɛŋtsɛ mikɛ nu wo mli po.

english: The dry harmattan air rapidly pulls moisture out of plant leaves and soil, forcing plants to conserve water rather than focus their energy on active growth.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi ni ji harmattan lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ oya. Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛbu nu he yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baaha amɛdalɛ ni tsuɔ nii waa lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know that my cassava tubers are mature enough to harvest without uprooting the entire plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa ni mijieee tso muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack as the underground tubers swell.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei lɛ mli fũuɔ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my maize crops are comfortable and spaced properly in the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmãa lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ ehe ebɔ he jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Healthy maize plants that are spaced well will spread their leaves wide without touching or smothering each other, ensuring every stalk gets full sunlight, water, and soil nutrients.
ga: Abɛi tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ baagbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã babaoo ni amɛtaaa amɛhe loo amɛtsiŋ amɛhe. Ha tso lɛ yitso fɛɛ tso lɛ aná hulu la ni yeɔ emuu, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my yam vines too close together on the mounds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ sweet potato wain tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: When yam vines are overcrowded, their leaves shade each other from the sun, which stops the plant from making enough energy to grow large tubers underground.
ga: Beni sweet potato wain tso lɛ mli eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛbaai lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ hulutsoo. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a crop's natural way of protecting itself to reduce water loss in high heat, but if they remain curled in the evening, it means the crop is dry and urgently needs water.
ga: Baai ni abɔleɔ he lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe he koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ aba shi. Shi kɛji akɛ ebɔle ehe lolo yɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbi ni nu he miihia lɛ oya.

english: How do I know if my wilted tomato plants are just hot or suffering from a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-tomato tsei ni egbo lɛ yɛ la mli kɛkɛ loo hela emɔ amɛ?

english: Plants wilting from heat will bounce back and look strong again in the cool morning, whereas plants affected by disease remain droopy and weak even during cool hours.
ga: Tsei ni egboi yɛ latsaa lɛ mli lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba kɛ hewalɛ yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ baakã he agbi ni amɛgbɔjɔ yɛ fɛ̃i bei amli po.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the stems before any fruits appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from extreme sun heat or lack of soil moisture, saving their energy to survive rather than growing fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ babaoo loo nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni akɛhiɔ shi lɛ baa shi moŋ fe ni aaakwɛ aduawai.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing on lower leaves shows that the soil lacks nitrogen; the plant is forced to steal nutrients from its older bottom leaves to keep its new top leaves growing.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Anyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my cassava plants grow tall and thin instead of bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi yucca tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal light, water, and plant food from the soil, forcing the cassava to stretch upward unnaturally to compete for light rather than expanding its roots.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ la, nu, kɛ tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ nyɛɔ yucca lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ehe shwieɔ shi yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ koni ekɛ la akaŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshishifãi lɛ eshwa.

english: Why do my garden egg seedlings stop growing when the soil becomes hard and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni egbi lɛ?

english: Roots need soft, moist soil to spread out and feed; when ground hardens, roots get trapped, stopping the top of the plant from growing.
ga: Shishifãi taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ, ni mli efɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛye niyenii. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ fee ais lɛ, shishifãi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ he, ni no haaa tso lɛ yiteŋ ada.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants droop and burn when there are no plantain trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiho ni amɛmiishã be mli ni dumɔwui ko bɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily under full sun; planting plantains alongside them creates vital shade and keeps the surrounding air moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa baa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does this new hybrid maize seed behave differently from the seeds I saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa heei ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred to grow uniformly, stand straight, and produce uniform ears, whereas saved seeds carry mixed traits that cause plants to grow at uneven heights and yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛdara pɛpɛɛpɛ, amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ, ni amɛná toi po. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ yɛ sui ni efutu ni haa tsei daa yɛ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee.

english: Why do some farmers grow tomatoes inside a covered plastic house instead of directly on open land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ tomato yɛ plastic tsũi ni akɛha he lɛ amli moŋ fe ni amɛduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Growing tomatoes inside a covered structure or greenhouse protects the delicate plants from severe heavy rains, harsh sunlight, and pest attacks. It helps control temperature and moisture so your crops grow faster and healthy throughout the year.
ga: Tomato ni oookwɛ yɛ tsũ ko ni akɛ nɔ ko eha nɔ loo ŋmɔ mli lɛ buɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, hulu la ni naa wa, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ koni onibii lɛ aya hiɛ oya ni amɛná hewalɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why is it better for me to start my tomato seeds in small trays before transferring them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabɔi tomato dumɔwui yɛ tsɛnsii bibii amli lɛ? Ebaafee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi dani maya shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato seeds are very small and fragile. Starting them in nursery trays gives them a safe environment with protected soil and careful watering, allowing them to form strong roots before facing the tough conditions of the open farm.
ga: Tomato dumɔwui lɛ daraaa kwraa ni amɛhe waaa. Tsei ni ajeɔ shishi yɛ dumɔwui atoohei amli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni shikpɔŋ ni abuɔ he kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɔɔ mli lɛ baa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni mli wa dani amɛkɛ shihilɛi ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni agbele mli lɛ amli lɛ kpeɔ.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my crop seeds in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ madu aduawai dumɔwui yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Seeds need warm soil and steady moisture to sprout. Sowing at the start of the rainy season ensures the soil stays wet enough for seeds to wake up and grow without drying out or getting washed away by flooding.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni mli efɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ adu nii mra yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ loo nu afua lɛ shwieee amɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young tomato plants curling inward during the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in the heat of the day is a plant's natural defense mechanism. The leaves curl to reduce their exposure to strong sun and hold onto water, helping the plant avoid drying out until the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi mli dɔlɛ mli lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ aba shi ni amɛhiɛ nu mli. Enɛ haaa tsei lɛ agbi kɛyashi gbɛkɛ mli fɛ̃i baa.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow plenty of big green leaves but fail to produce any flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi enyɛɛɛ ewo fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen fertilizer, they put all their energy into making leafy stems instead of fruits. To encourage flowers and fruit, the plant needs balanced plant food containing higher levels of phosphorus and potassium.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ feɔ baai ŋmeii yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Bɔni afee ni ekanya fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai Tsei biɔ tso niyenii ni sa ni phosphorus kɛ potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli.

english: Why do my young seedlings suddenly collapse and die right at soil level soon after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by a soil sickness called 'damping-off,' which happens when seedling soil is kept too wet and dark. Giving seedlings proper airflow and avoiding overwatering protects their thin stems from rotting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘Damping’ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa, ni baa beni dumɔwui lɛ ashikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni eyɛ duŋ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa ni tsɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe. koni ekafite

english: What causes black, sunken spots at the bottom of my growing green tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii diji loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tomato eŋɔli ni miida lɛ shishi lɛ baa?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium, often due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant feed calcium to the developing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekɛ calcium aha aduawai ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do I need to tie my tomato plants to wooden stakes as they grow taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fĩɔ tsei ahe kɛji amɛdara lɛ?

english: Tomato stems are naturally weak and will bend under the weight of heavy fruit. Tying them to wooden stakes keeps the leaves and fruit off the wet soil, preventing rot, disease, and damage from ground insects.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni amɛbaakoto yɛ aduawai ni tsii lɛ ashishi. Kɛ́ akɛfi tso ko he lɛ, ebaaha baai kɛ aduawai lɛ akajɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmeii, helai kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa.

english: How can I tell if I am giving my crops too much water or not enough water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mikɛ nu babaoo miiha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ loo mihaaa mihe?

english: If your plants are not getting enough water, their leaves will wilt and dry up from the bottom. If they get too much water, the leaves will turn yellow and look limp because the roots are drowning in wet soil.
ga: Kɛji otsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Baai lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagbi kɛjɛ shishi. Kɛji onine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ ebote shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ mli.

english: Is it better to pick my tomatoes when they turn fully red or when they are just starting to show color?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oookpa tomato beni efee tɔrɔmɔɔ kwraa loo eje shishi ebɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛkɛ?

english: It is often best to harvest tomatoes when they just start showing a pink or light orange color. They will finish ripening safely in your shed, protecting them from birds, insects, and sun damage on the farm.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookpa tomato kɛji eje shishi etsɔ pinki loo ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse. Amɛbaashwere shweshweeshwe yɛ otsu lɛ mli. Buu amɛhe kɛjɛ okpoi, kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmɔ mli hulu ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahe.

english: I noticed small webbing bags and cocoons on my crop leaves; will these turn into pests that ruin my farm?
ga: Miyɔse kotoku bibioo ko ni akpɛ. Kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ Ani enɛɛmɛi baatsɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, those cocoons usually contain caterpillars or larvae that will hatch and eat crop leaves and stems. Clearing them by hand or using appropriate controls early prevents a much bigger pest outbreak later.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni baafo ni amɛye ŋmɔshi nibii ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ yɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ amli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsɔ onine nɔ ojie amɛ kɛjɛ mli loo okɛ nibii ni sa ni akɛkudɔɔ amɛ lɛ atsu nii mra. Ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji babaoo ni baa sɛɛ mli lɛ anaa.

english: Why do insects seem to attack my crops more heavily during the rainy season than in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli fe hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Rainy weather creates high humidity and soft, green leaf growth, which insects prefer for feeding and laying eggs. Damp conditions help pest populations multiply much faster.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be haa hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ eŋɔli lɛ daalɛ baa. ni kooloi sumɔɔ ni amɛye ni amɛwo amɛwui Shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ babaoo oya.

english: Why does it take several years for a young cocoa tree to start producing pods after I plant it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ cacao tsei bibii afii babaoo dani amɛjeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need time to establish strong root systems and sturdy trunks before they can carry heavy pods. This initial growth phase prepares the tree to produce fruits reliably for decades.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ he miihia be koni amɛma shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli wa dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo ŋmeii ni tsii. Nɛkɛ shishijee dalɛ gbɛ nɛɛ saa tso lɛ he koni ewo yibii yɛ gbɛ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni baa lɛ amli.

english: If I leave my mature crops in the field longer before harvesting, will I get a bigger yield?
ga: Kɛ mishi ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ fe dani akpa lɛ, Ani mawo yibii babaoo?

english: Leaving crops past their harvest time usually lowers quality because pods can rot, dry out, or attract hungry pests. Harvesting right at maturity gives you the best yield and market value.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ haa nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa shi ejaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ agbo, amɛgbi loo amɛgbala ŋmɔshi nibii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ. Nikpamɔ yɛ be mli ni edara lɛ haa yibiiwoo ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛ jarayeli jara.

english: Why do so many flowers fall off my cocoa trees without ever growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo miiho kɛmiijɛ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Trees produce many more flowers than they can support and naturally shed excess ones. If too many fall, it usually means the tree needs more nutrients, water, or better shade management.
ga: Tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni fɔfɔi lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ nɔ. Ni fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛji ogbee shi tsɔ lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ, nu, loo hulutsoo he gbɛjianɔtoo.

english: Why does COCOBOD recommend cutting down diseased cocoa trees instead of just spraying them with medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ COCOBOD woɔ ŋaa akɛ afolɔ kookoo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ moŋ fe ni akɛ tsofa baawo amɛmli kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Certain diseases, like the Swollen Shoot virus, live inside the plant's system where chemical sprays cannot reach. Cutting down the infected tree stops the disease from spreading to healthy trees nearby.
ga: Helai komɛi, tamɔ Swollen Shoot virus lɛ hiɔ tsei amli he ni tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni aaafo lɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: How do researchers know that a new farming method or seed variety will actually work on my farm?
ga: Te niiamlitaolɔi feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛleɔ kɛji okwaayeli gbɛ hee loo dumɔwui srɔtoi baatsu nii diɛŋtsɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Agricultural researchers test seeds and practices across different local soils and weather conditions for years to ensure they increase yields and resist local pests before sharing them with farmers.
ga: Okwaayeli he niiamlitaolɔi kaa dumɔwui kɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ maŋ lɛ mli shikpɔji kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi srɔtoi amli lɛ amɛkwɛɔ. yɛ afii babaoo mli koni akwɛ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ yaa hiɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ dani akɛ amɛ aha okwaafoi lɛ.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot right on the tree before harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani akpaa?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in dark, overly wet conditions. Pruning excess tree branches allows sunlight and air flow to keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ tsɔ lɛ. Tso lɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops start turning yellow and dropping when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves drop as a defense mechanism to save water during extreme heat and dry spells. Providing shade plants and keeping soil mulched helps protect crops from heat stress.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni buɔ mɔ he koni akɛto nu he yɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Tsei ni akɛwoɔ hulutsoo mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ amɛhe lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he.

english: Why is it necessary to clear weeds around the base of my crops regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mitsei lɛ ashishi daa lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and fertilizers directly from your crops' roots. Keeping the base of your crops clear ensures all available nourishment goes straight to building healthy plants.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ oha otso lɛ shishitoo lɛ mli tse lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ yaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ afeemɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: If the first rain falls this week, should I start planting my yams right away?
ga: Otsi nɛɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ. Ani esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: No, you should wait for the rains to settle properly. Planting yams immediately after the first early rain can cause the seed yams to rot in the hot, damp soil before the wet season fully begins.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ omɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi klɛŋklɛŋ. Kɛ́ adu sweet potato amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ nɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi kwraa.

english: What does it mean when experienced farmers say the rain must 'settle' before I start planting?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ kɛɛ akɛ esa akɛ nugbɔ ‘anɛ’ dani adumɔ aje shishi lɛ tsɔɔ?

english: It means waiting until the rainy season is regular and fully established so the soil stays consistently wet, rather than planting after just one or two temporary early showers.
ga: Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ amɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be ni baa daa lɛ mli, ni asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kwraa koni ehiɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Mohu ɔ, du ngɛ leebi nugbɔ kake loo enyɔ se.

english: How do I know if the ground is ready and cool enough for my yam seeds so they do not spoil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo ni edɔ bɔ ni sa kɛha mi sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, egbooo loo egbooo?

english: Check that rain has fallen consistently over several days and the soil below the surface remains damp and cool; if the earth underneath is dry and hot, it is too early to plant.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni nugbɔ anɛ be fɛɛ be gbii babaoo. ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi ni edɔ lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ eshɛko mra lolo akɛ abaadu.

english: Why did my yam seeds rot in the soil last season before they could even sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli dani amɛkwɛ̃ po lɛ?

english: Yam seeds rot when planted in warm ground before proper rains start, because early light rains create humid heat trapped in dry soil that spoils the tuber.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo leebi lɛ haa hulutsoo ni mli edɔ ni emɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ baa, ni no fiteɔ tsɔnei ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ.

english: What will happen to my crop yield if I rush to plant my crops before the right time?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ oyaiyeli du tso lɛ dani be ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ shɛ?

english: Rushing to plant before the weather is ready leads to seed failure, rotten roots, and empty mounds, leaving you with little to no harvest at the end of the season.
ga: Oya ni oooyadu nii dani kɔɔyɔŋ lɛlɛ lɛ afee klalo lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akafee nɔ ko, shishifãi lɛ baafite ni shikpɔŋ ni nɔ ko bɛ nɔ lɛ aba. Enɛ haa eshwɛ fioo ni obaanyɛ okpa nii yɛ be lɛ naagbee.

english: How can I avoid wasting expensive seed yams when starting my new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mihe kɛjɛ sweet potato dumɔwui ni jara wa lɛ ahe beni mijeɔ ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ?

english: You can avoid wasting seed yams by carefully observing local weather patterns, preparing your mounds early, and holding off on planting until rainfall is steady.
ga: Obaanyɛ okpa sweet potato dumɔwui ni ofiteɔ lɛ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ni oookwɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Saamɔ gɔŋ lɛ mra. ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ dumɔ he kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baanyɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: What causes yam tubers to decay under the ground instead of growing strong vines and leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ wain tsei kɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: Tubers decay underground when moisture is insufficient to trigger healthy root growth or when trapped heat in prematurely planted ground encourages fungal rot.
ga: Tubers lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ni baaha shishifãi lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ. aloo kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni mli edɔ oya yɛ he ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Can I keep planting yams on the exact same piece of land for many years in a row?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu sweet potato yɛ he kome afii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ?

english: Growing yams on the same land continuously over long periods wears out the soil nutrients and increases pests, so resting the soil or rotating crops is necessary to maintain good yields.
ga: Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu sweet potato yɛ he kome be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaafite shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ, ni ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo aya hiɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hejɔɔmɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ he miihia koni ŋmɔshi nibii ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important for me to plan my land preparation before the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mato shikpɔŋ he saamɔ he gbɛjianɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi lɛ?

english: Planning ahead allows you to clear your land and build mounds on time, so you can plant immediately when the rains settle rather than rushing or missing the proper planting window.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoo kɛtsɔ hiɛ tsɔɔ akɛ obaanyɛ ojie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oma gɔŋ lɛ yɛ be naa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, obaanyɛ odu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofee oya loo ooofo samflɛ ni sa ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ mli.

english: As someone who just acquired land to farm, what is the most important rule about planting yams?
ga: Ákɛ mɔ ko ni he shikpɔŋ kɛkɛ koni ekɛtsu nii lɛ Mɛni ji mlai ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ?

english: The most important rule is patience with the weather; planting only after steady rains begin prevents your seed tubers from rotting in hot earth.
ga: Mla ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ ji tsuishitoo kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ sɛɛ pɛ koni dumɔwui ayitsei lɛ akafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is essential food for their growth. Applying NPK fertilizer or compost around the base will help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ, ni akɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he yɛ he fɛɛ he Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling and looking wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Curled or wrinkled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the plant. Spraying your pepper plants with neem oil solution or mild soapy water helps get rid of these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe loo ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Pepper tsei ni akɛ neem mu loo samla ni mli ejɔ baashwie nɔ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Black pods are caused by a fungal disease that thrives in excessive moisture and heavy shade. Pruning overhead branches to let in sunlight and quickly removing infected pods will prevent the disease from spreading.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be ni fa fe nine kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ koni hulu lɛ abote mli, ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture needed for young cocoa to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa koni kookoo bibii lɛ ahi shi.

english: Is it good for me to plant beans in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize is beneficial. Beans capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil to help maize grow, while maize stalks provide strong supports for climbing beans.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he. Beans mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eye ebua ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛfiɔ ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ ni ehaa amɛhe waa.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my crops regularly instead of leaving them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe daa moŋ fe ni mashi amɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. Removing them regularly ensures your crops receive full nutrition to grow big and produce good yields.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaadu nii yɛ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ daa lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Keeping the soil consistently moist and providing light shade during extreme heat helps the plant hold its flowers to form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi kɛ eyibii amli.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my cassava stem cuttings?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmeii ni afo lɛ?

english: Cassava is best planted right at the beginning of the major rainy season. This allows the stem cuttings to absorb water and build deep root systems before any dry weather sets in.
ga: Akɛ cassava duɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa lɛ shishijee mli. Enɛ haa tsei niji lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ nu ni amɛtswaa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ dani kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ baa.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot in the soil before I can dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mifo amɛmli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot underground when water collects around them in heavy, soggy soil. Creating higher planting mounds allows excess rain to drain away and keeps the tubers dry and healthy.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu shwie shikpɔŋ ni efɔ ni tsii lɛ nɔ. Gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ ni aduɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni ehaa yitso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my watermelon plants spread so many vines before flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon tso lɛ yɛ wain tsei babaoo ni gbɛɔ eshwaa dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Watermelon plants need to grow long vines and green leaves first to gather energy from the sun. Once the plant has stored enough energy, it will naturally start producing flowers that turn into fruits.
ga: Ehe miihia ni watermelon tsei akwɛ̃ wain tsei kakadaji kɛ baai eŋɔli dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛbua hewalɛ naa kɛjɛ hulu la mli. Kɛ tsei kɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa eto Ebaabɔi fɔfɔi ni jɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ feemɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when there is too much rain in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive rain washes away nitrogen from the soil and chokes the plant roots by removing air, which causes the plant leaves to turn yellow because it cannot feed properly.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ hoɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ejieɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ejaakɛ enyɛɛɛ eye niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are armyworms attacking my maize plants early in the morning and late in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ leebi kɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Armyworms hide inside the plant leaves or soil during the hottest parts of the day to avoid heat, coming out to feed on tender leaves during cooler hours like dawn and dusk.
ga: Asraafoi amli ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei ahe baai loo shikpɔŋ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli koni amɛkafee hulutsoo lɛ. Amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye baai bibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli tamɔ leebi maŋkpa kɛ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds instead of saving seeds from my last cassava or maize harvest to plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe ni makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ naagbee ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu?

english: Seeds saved from previous harvests lose their strength and disease resistance over time, whereas certified seeds are specially bred to fight off pests and give you a bigger yield.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baafite hewalɛ kɛ helai ahe hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Yɛ be mli ni akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛkɛwu amɛshi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni amɛwo yibii babaoo lɛ.

english: Why does applying fertilizer too close to the stem of my plants burn them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ he tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shãa lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers contain strong salts. When placed right against the stem, they suck water out of the plant tissues instead of feeding them, causing the plant to dry up and burn.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli ŋmei babaoo yɛ mli. Kɛ akɛwo tso lɛ shishi lɛ Ekɛ nu shwieɔ tso lɛ fãji amli moŋ fe ni eeebote mli. Ehaa tsei lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛshãa.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl up and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛkpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by a virus spread by tiny whiteflies, or by extreme heat stress where the plant curls its leaves to prevent itself from losing water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni nu akafite lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and tall without producing big cobs or tubers when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeee ŋmeii wuji loo ŋmeii wuji kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are overcrowded, they fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients, putting all their energy into stretching upwards for light rather than growing thick stems and food.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔi tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkpãa ehe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eshɛ la he. Mohu ɔ, e wa nɛ e peeɔ tsohi nɛ a mi wa kɛ niye ní.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops right after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ dara oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Wild weeds are naturally adapted to the local soil and weather, allowing them to absorb water and nutrients much faster than domestic crops.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe shia tsei.

english: Why do flower buds drop off my pepper plants before forming fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when stressed by severe heat, lack of water, or poor pollination, saving their energy to survive instead of making fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo pollination ni ehiii lɛ hao amɛ. Enɛ baaha hewalɛ aba shi kɛha wala yɛ yibiiwoo najiaŋ.

english: Why do my harvested grains get damaged by weevils even when I store them in clean bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fiteɔ dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛtoɔ kotokui ni mli tse amli moŋ?

english: Weevils or their invisible eggs often come with the grain directly from the field, so they hatch and multiply inside the bags unless the grain is properly dried or kept in airtight containers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni anaaa lɛ baa kɛ dumɔwui ni jɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛfɔɔ ni amɛfɔɔ bii yɛ kotokui amli. Ja agbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ loo akɛto nɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need partial shade from nurse crops like plantains or shade trees to protect their soft leaves and keep the soil moist while their root systems develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be ko kɛjɛ nurse tsei tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu baai bibii ahe ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, will I get a bigger harvest from my land?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting too close makes crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks and tiny cobs, which actually lowers your total harvest compared to using recommended spacing.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. Enɛ haa nɔ ni ojieɔ lɛ fɛɛ baa shi kɛ akɛto gbɛ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on instead of growing along the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground allows their leaves to catch maximum sunlight for food production while keeping the foliage safe from dirt-borne fungal diseases and excessive heat from the soil, leading to larger tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa etso lɛ naa hulu la babaoo kɛha niyenii feemɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ebaa lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni muji kɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ he. kɛ yitso ni da fe tsutsu lɛ baa

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and turning pale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaves, or transmitting a plant virus. This damages the leaf tissue and stops the plant from growing healthy fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo egbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ eshwaa tsei amli Enɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji ni ehaaa tso lɛ aná yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛtsɔko aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant suffers from environmental stress, such as sudden hot spells, dry soil, or irregular watering, which prevents successful pollination.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na shihilɛ mli haomɔi, tamɔ dɔlɛ trukaa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. ni tsiɔ pollination ni yeɔ omanye lɛ naa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow in a V-shape starting from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli, ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ eshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves that start at the tip and move down the middle vein indicate a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen is the primary nutrient maize needs to build green, healthy leaves.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ashishigbɛ ni amɛyaa kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni abele baakwɛ̃ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli wa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit bunches. When heavy rain softens the soil, the shallow roots lose their grip, causing the tree to blow over unless it is supported with a wooden prop.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni ewoɔ aduawai babaoo. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔ lɛ, shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei gbeeɔ amɛnɔ ja tso ko yɛ ni fiɔ amɛsɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground if heavy rain stays on the farm for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When soil stays waterlogged, oxygen cannot reach the roots, causing root cells to die and allowing fungal decay to set in, which turns the firm tubers into soft, watery rot.
ga: Beni nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ Oxygen nyɛŋ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shishifã mli wala yibii lɛ gboiɔ ni ehaa ŋmei lɛ fiteɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni ewa lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ nu.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge leafy branches but very small tubers underneath the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ niji kɛ baai wuji shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil pushes the cassava plant to spend all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in the roots below.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsirɛɔ yucca tso lɛ koni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ atsu nii ni ekɛbaa kɛ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ starch ato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli lɛ

english: Why do my harvested cowpea pods have tiny dark holes with damaged seeds inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea ŋmeii ni mikpaa lɛ yɛ ŋmeii diji bibii lɛ? Ni dumɔwui ni efite yɛ mli.

english: Tiny holes in cowpea pods are caused by pod-boring caterpillars or insect pests that lay eggs on the plant, allowing the larvae to burrow into the pods and feed on the growing seeds.
ga: Buji bibii ni yɔɔ tsina ŋmeii amli lɛ jɛɔ pod borers loo kooloi ni yeɔ amɛwui yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ amli. Ha ŋmeii lɛ abote ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛye dumɔwui ni miida lɛ.

english: Why does all the fertilizer I apply to my cassava seem to wash away whenever heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni mikɛwoɔ mi-cassava lɛ nɔ lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away loose fertilizer on sloped or bare land. Adding organic compost helps hold the soil together so nutrients stay in place for crop roots to feed on.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Organic compost ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome koni ehiɛ niyenii ni haa tsei shishifãi lɛ yeɔ.

english: Why is my sandy farm land drying up so quickly even after I water my vegetables heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ he ni miduɔ ŋã yɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji mikɛ nu babaoo wo nɔ po lɛ?

english: Sandy soil has large gaps that let water drain straight down like a sieve. Mixing in organic manure or dry grass helps trap water in the soil so your plants can drink it over time.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni haa nu lɛ hoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa shi tamɔ ŋã. Kɛ́ okɛ organic fertilizer loo hay futu mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni otsei lɛ anu yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do I need to cut off yellow and diseased leaves from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ baai ni efee ŋmɔŋ kɛ hela kɛjɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Dead or diseased leaves waste plant energy and spread sickness to healthy leaves. Cutting them off lets the crop focus its food and strength on growing big, healthy fruit.
ga: Baai ni egboi loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela eshwaa baa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ. Kpojiemɔ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa niyenii kɛ hewalɛ nɔ koni ewo yibii wuji ni mli wa.

english: If I leave my cocoa farm unkept for a few years, will the old trees fruit properly again if I just clear the weeds?
ga: Kɛji mishi kookoo ŋmɔ ko ni mikɛtsuuu nii afii fioo komɛi Ani tso momo lɛ baawo yibii ekoŋŋ kɛji mijie jwɛi lɛ?

english: Weeding helps, but long-neglected cocoa trees often carry hidden diseases and overgrown dead wood. They require proper pruning, pest treatment, and care before they can yield good pods again.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua. Shi bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei ni aku hiɛ ashwie nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ hiɛɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ kɛ tsei ni egboi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine. Ehe miihia ni afolɔ amɛ. pest control Ni esa akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ dani enyɛ ekɛ pods kpakpai aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my pepper plants not producing well even though I keep spending money on fertilizer every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ wooo yibii jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mifiteɔ shika yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe daa afi moŋ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously exhausts specific nutrients and builds up soil pests. Rotating peppers with leguminous crops like cowpeas restores soil balance so your inputs are not wasted.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be, ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Peppers ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ cowpeas tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ekome ekoŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ akafite.

english: Why do I have to spread out my harvested maize to dry before I put it in sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbi mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ dani mikɛwo kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grains contain natural moisture that creates mold and rot inside sealed sacks. Sun-drying removes moisture so your grain stays safe during storage.
ga: Nibii ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ ni haa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ kotokui ni atsĩ naa lɛ amli. Hulu ni egbiɔ lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ koni eha oŋmaa lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know my cocoa beans are fully dry and ready to be packed for sale?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kookoo lɛ egbi kwraa ni esa akɛ awo mli?

english: Fully dry cocoa beans turn a rich brown color and crackle crisply when squeezed in your hand. This crispness shows that internal moisture is gone so they will not spoil.
ga: Kookoo yibii ni egbi kwraa lɛ tsɔɔ blɔfo ni etswaa kɛji akɛ akɛ nine mimɔ mli. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ elaaje, no hewɔ lɛ, egboŋ.

english: Why should I pick out and throw away rotten tomatoes from the good ones right after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tomato ni efite kɛjɛ tomato kpakpa mli ni mashɛ mafɔ kɛji akpa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Rotten fruit carries fungi and bacteria that quickly spread to healthy fruit stored next to them. Removing spoiled produce saves the rest of your harvest from going bad.
ga: Yibii ni egboi lɛ ji nɔ ni hiɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛyaa yibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ emasɛi lɛ anɔ. Nibii ni efite lɛ ni oooshɛrɛ lɛ baaye abua ni onibii ni eshwɛ lɛ akafite.

english: What makes my stored yams rot in the barn even when I stack them neatly?
ga: Mɛni ha ŋmeii ni mikɛto ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fite eyɛ mli akɛ mito amɛhe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Yams rot if they are stored with unhealed cuts or in areas without air movement. You must let bruised yams dry out in the sun first and ensure your storage barn has cool, flowing air.
ga: Sweet potatoes baafite kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ. Obaasumɔ ni oha ŋmeii ni ekpɔtɔ lɛ agbi yɛ hulu lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ. Ni kwɛmɔ ni otsu lɛ mli aná kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ.

english: Why did the seeds I saved from last year's harvest fail to grow into strong crops this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ edaaa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds can lose their vigor over time or carry over diseases from the previous season. Buying fresh, certified seeds ensures high germination rates and strong plants.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli loo amɛkɛ helai ni jɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ aba. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ baaha tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting if I leave them in the ground during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need well-drained soil. When water logs the ground during heavy rains, it starves the roots of oxygen, allowing fungal decay and rot to set in quickly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nu ho shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ Hɔmɔ yeɔ shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ fiteɔ ni efiteɔ oya.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers without producing peppers during hot, dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shi ni ekɛ pepper baaa yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air cause heat stress in pepper plants, forcing them to shed their flowers to conserve moisture and protect themselves from drying out.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ dɔlɛ haomɔ baa pepper tsei amli. Nyɛ amɛnɔ ni amɛshwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni ŋmɔtɔ akahi shi ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why do my yam vines turn yellow and dry up around October or November?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ yɛ October loo November aaafee lɛ?

english: Dying vines signal natural maturity for yams. As the rainy season ends, the plant stops growing above ground and shifts all its remaining energy down into the underground tuber.
ga: Wein tsei ni miigboi lɛ tsɔɔ bɔ ni sweet potato lɛ daa ha yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Tso lɛ kpaɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ dalɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ yaa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow from the tips downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ eshishigbɛ kɛmiiba shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting at the tip and moving down the center usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for strong green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishi kɛyaa teŋgbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow big green leaves but produce very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes cowpeas to focus all their energy on growing foliage and stems rather than developing flowers and seed pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa cowpea kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ tsei ni miida lɛ ahe nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui ŋmɔji

english: Why does planting maize in the exact same field every year result in smaller harvests each time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ woɔ yibii fioo be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Maize heavily consumes specific nutrients from the soil. Continuous planting without rotation drains those nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the field.
ga: Abɛi kɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Dumɔ ni yaa nɔ ni atsakeee lɛ baaha nakai niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ ajɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce hundreds of flowers, but only a few grow into full cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ohai abɔ lɛ? Shi tsei fioo komɛi pɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ kookoo tsei ni eyi obɔ.

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed flowers that are not pollinated by tiny insects like midges, or when the tree lacks enough water and nutrients to feed every potential pod.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. Aloo be mli ni tso lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ ahi shi lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop dark, sunken spots on the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ hiɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni eshishigbɛ shwieɔ shi dani ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit, usually brought on by irregular watering.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why do my groundnut plants produce empty shells with no seeds inside when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli ni dumɔwui bɛ mli kɛ́ mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut pods happen when the soil lacks calcium during pod development, or when the soil becomes too dry for the seeds to swell properly inside the shell.
ga: Peanut pods ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium yɛ pods lɛ shweremɔ be mli. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ ashwere jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋshɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain leaves curl up and turn brown even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by underground pests like nematodes damaging the root system, or fungal diseases like Black Sigatoka attacking the leaves and preventing proper water absorption.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ nematodes ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. loo ŋmeii helai tamɔ Black Sigatoka ni tutuaa baai lɛ ni ehaaa nu lɛ ashɛ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I buy government-certified seeds instead of just using seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni nɔyeli lɛ eŋmɛ gbɛ lɛ moŋ fe ni mikɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli kɛkɛ baatsu nii?

english: Certified seeds are tested and treated under national programs to ensure they resist common diseases and produce strong yields, whereas saved seeds can carry hidden infections that weaken your crop and spread to neighboring farms.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ akwɛɔ ni atsaa amɛ yɛ maŋ gbɛjianɔtoo ko shishi koni ana akɛ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why is it dangerous for me to bring unapproved crop seeds from outside the country to plant on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu dumɔwui ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ ni jɛ mimaŋ lɛ kponɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Unapproved foreign seeds can introduce new pests or crop diseases that local crops have no defense against, which can quickly spread and ruin harvests across the entire region.
ga: Maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui ni bɛ he odaseyeli lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai heei loo tsei ahe helai aba. ni tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nyɛŋ abu amɛhe kɛjɛ he ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ fɛɛ.

english: Why are some commercial crop seeds coated in colorful powder before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ powda ni yɔɔ srɔtoi woɔ jarayeli dumɔwui komɛi ahe dani aduɔ lɛ?

english: That coating is a protective treatment that shields the seed from soil insects and fungal infections during early growth, giving the young crop a healthy start.
ga: Nɔ ni tamɔ nɛkɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ji tsofa ko ni buɔ dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ sũ mli kooloi bibii kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa mra lɛ. Ehaa dumɔwui lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why does a crop disease on my neighbor's farm affect my crops even if I take good care of my own field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso hela ko ni yɔɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe eyɛ mli akɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikwɛɔ miŋmɔji anɔ jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Crop diseases and pests travel easily through the wind, water, and soil across farm boundaries, which is why plant protection works best when everyone in the community follows the same control measures.
ga: Tsei ahe helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ husui lɛ amli oya. Enɛ hewɔ ni tsei ahebuu tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni yɔɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛ gbɛjianɔtoo kome ni akɛbuɔ tsei ahe lɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it better for all farmers in our community to plant our crops at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ okwaafoi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ wɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ baadu wɔŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting together creates a uniform growth cycle that prevents pests from continuously multiplying by jumping from older crops to younger ones throughout the year.
ga: Hefatalɔi ni aduɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ daa koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni amɛkafɔ be fɛɛ be kɛtsɔ tsei ni edara lɛ anɔ ni amɛjoɔ kɛyaa tsei bibii amli yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can crops be given preventive treatments to stop them from getting sick before a disease even starts?
ga: Ani tsei baanyɛ ana tsofai ni tsiɔ hela naa koni ekpa hela dani eje shishi?

english: Yes, applying approved preventive sprays and using disease-resistant plant varieties builds up the crop's natural defenses so it can fight off infections before they cause damage.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛbuɔ mɔ he ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ tsei srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ helai anaa lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni ama tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu nibii lɛ anɔ koni enyɛ ekɛ helai awuu dani ekɛ nɔ ko aba.

english: Why do agricultural officers stop farmers from moving certain plants or plant parts from one region to another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ guɔ okwaafoi ni amɛkajie tsei komɛi loo tsei lɛ fãi komɛi kɛjɛ kpokpaa kome nɔ kɛya kpokpaa kroko nɔ lɛ?

english: Restricting plant movement prevents localized crop viruses and pests from being transported into clean areas where they could destroy whole new farming communities.
ga: Kɛ́ atsĩ tsei ahe gbɛfaa naa lɛ, ebaatsi maŋ lɛ mli helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni akaya hei ni he tse. Enɛ baanyɛ akpata okwaayeli akutsei heei muu fɛɛ ahiɛ.

english: What should I do if I notice a strange, unknown leaf disease destroying my crops?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mina baa hela ko ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ni aleee ni miifite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: You should report it immediately to an agricultural extension officer so national experts can identify the threat early and prevent a widespread outbreak across the country.
ga: Esa akɛ obɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ lɛ amaniɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni maŋ lɛ mli nilelɔi lɛ anyɛ ana gbeyeishemɔi mra. ni atsĩ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa maŋ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ anaa

english: Why do I need to inspect my farm regularly even when the crops look green and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ po lɛ?

english: Early signs of pest attacks and plant diseases are often hidden under leaves or near the roots, and catching them early makes it easier to control the outbreak before it damages the entire crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai ebatutua amɛ lɛ teɔ shi yɛ baai lɛ ashishi loo yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. kɛ amɛmɔmɔ mra Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaaye helai ni baa lɛ anɔ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I buy cheap, unlabelled crop chemicals from unverified sellers at the local market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miheɔ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni jara waaa ni aŋmalako nɔ ko nɔ ko kɛjɛɔ jarayelɔi ni akwɛɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ adɛŋ yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ?

english: Unverified chemicals may contain illegal or incorrect ingredients that can burn your crops, poison the soil, or leave unsafe residues in the food you grow for the market.
ga: Tsofai ni akwɛɛɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni mla eŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ loo nibii ni esaaa ni baanyɛ ashã onibii. Poison yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo shimɔ nibii ni bɛ shweshweeshwe yɛ niyenii ni oduɔ koni okɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know which maize variety is best for my farm when some mature fast and others take long?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmãa henɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ? Akɛni kooloi srɔtoi komɛi daa oya ni ekrokomɛi hu heɔ be babaoo hewɔ lɛ.

english: Early-maturing maize varieties are best if your area gets short rainy seasons, while late-maturing varieties give higher yields if you have long, reliable rains and good soil.
ga: Abele henɔi ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ sɛɛ lɛ baawo yibii babaoo kɛji oyɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa.

english: How can I tell Pona seed yams apart from other yam varieties when buying seed at the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ Pona dumɔwui yams lɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ahe kɛ́ mihe dumɔwui yɛ jara nɔ?

english: Pona seed yams usually have a smooth skin, lighter color, and a rounded tip, unlike rougher varieties like Water Yam which have hairier, darker skins.
ga: Pona seed yams lɛ fɔɔ hewolo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, su ni mli tse, kɛ naagbee ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni esoro no kwraa yɛ henɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ nu mli yams, ni hiɛ yitsɔi babaoo kɛ hewolo ni tsuɔ waa lɛ ahe.

english: Can I plant lowland swamp rice on upland dry land if rain falls regularly?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛɔ daa lɛ, ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmãa ni ji ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ egbi nɔ?

english: No, lowland rice varieties require flooded or continuously wet soil to grow properly, and planting them on dry upland soil will cause stunted growth and poor yields.
ga: Dabi, ŋmãa henɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ loo nɔ ni mli efɔ be fɛɛ be koni enyɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Ni ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ baaha ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ebaaha yibiiwoo lɛ hu aba shi.

english: Cassava drops its leaves to save water during dry weather; once the rains return, the plant will quickly sprout fresh new leaves.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi koni akɛbu nu he yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei oya.

english: Why do groundnut plants push their flower stems down into the dirt after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ tsiɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ahe ŋmeii lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts form their pods underground, so after flowering, the plant naturally bends its stem down to bury the fertilized flower where the nut can safely grow.
