ga: Peanuts feɔ pods yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ tso lɛ wo fɔfɔi sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsɔ eshishifã lɛ nɔ efo shi kɛya shi koni ekɛfu fɔfɔi ni awo mli fɔ lɛ yɛ he ni ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe lɛ.

english: How do I choose the right plantain sucker to plant on my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain sucker ni sa kɛha dumɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Look for maiden suckers with narrow, spear-like leaves and a thick base, as they grow faster and produce stronger bunches than suckers that already have broad leaves.
ga: Taomɔ tsei bibii ni baai lɛ mli tse ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ kɛ shishigbɛ ni mli tse. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛdaraa oya ni amɛfeɔ kui ni mli wa fe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ momo lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and looking wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites feeding on the leaves, or by a virus spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. loo kɛjɛ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without growing into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high temperatures, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients, which prevents the fruit from setting.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be ni mli wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. ni haa aduawai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔɔ lɛ

english: Why are small green pods on my cocoa tree turning black and shriveling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection triggered by high moisture and shade, which rots the pods before they can mature.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo kɛbaa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ dani amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I clear all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect their tender leaves from direct hot sunlight and to keep the surrounding soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛbu amɛbaai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. kɛ koni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ

english: How does using organic fertilizer or animal manure actually help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Organic fertilizer feeds the soil naturally by adding rich organic matter. This improves the soil's structure, allowing it to hold more water and nutrients so your crops grow stronger roots and yield better harvests over time.
ga: Organic ŋmɔshi nibii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ ahiɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo mli. Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná shishifãi ni mli wa ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Maize leaves usually turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen or when the plants aren't getting enough water. Adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the plant make food properly and return to a healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛhoo nii jogbaŋŋ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell with my own eyes if the fertilizer I applied is working on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male mi diɛŋtsɛ mihe akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You will notice clear physical changes in your crops within a few weeks, such as darker green leaves, thicker stems, faster height growth, and less wilting during hot afternoons compared to untreated plants.
ga: Obaana gbɔmɔtsoŋ tsakemɔi ni kadiɔ mɔ yɛ onibii amli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli, tamɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni mli tse, ni amɛdaraa oya. ni egbɔjɔ fioo yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. kɛ akɛto tsei ni atsako amɛhe lɛ ahe

english: Why does my crop soil dry out so fast during hot days, and how can I keep it moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sũ ni mikɛwoɔ tsɛnsi mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nu yɛ mihe?

english: Bare soil loses moisture quickly to the hot sun. Spreading dry grass, leaves, or crop leftover material around the base of your plants (mulching) acts like a blanket that shades the soil and keeps water from evaporating.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shɛ enɔ. Jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo niyenii ni eshwɛ ni agbɛɔ ashwaa tso lɛ shishigbɛ (mulching) lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Should I plant my seed crops immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui tsei amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is safer to wait until the rains become regular. Planting after a single early rain can cause your seeds to sprout, only to dry up and die if a weeks-long dry spell follows.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ bɔ ni sa. Tso kome ni ooodu yɛ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha odumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃. Shi ebaagbi ni egbo kɛji hɔmɔ ni heɔ otsii babaoo ba.

english: Why do crops fed with organic manure seem to survive dry weather better than those without it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni tsei ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli haa amɛ lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli haaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Organic manure acts like a sponge in the soil, trapping rainwater and keeping the root zone damp for much longer, which keeps crops hydrated even when rain stops for a while.
ga: Organic fertilizer tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Emɔɔ nugbɔ nu ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ naa nu kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa be ko po.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce very small tubers when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are packed tightly, their roots compete fiercely with each other for space, sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to develop large tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná he ko, hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ bulbs agboi baa.

english: Why are the blossoms falling off my pepper plants without forming any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeee pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Blossom drop happens when crops experience heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and rich in organic nutrients helps flowers turn into full fruits.
ga: Blossom drop baa kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛdaraa kwraa ni amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and choke my crops whenever I clear new farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni efiteɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ be fɛɛ be ni majie he hee ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ?

english: Clearing land exposes weed seeds buried in the soil to sunlight and air, causing them to germinate rapidly. Weeds naturally grow fast to take nutrients before your crops can establish themselves.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa jwɛi dumɔwui ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ. Ehaa jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya Jwɛi lɛ daa oya yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni eŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ ama shi.

english: Why is it good for my soil if I plant groundnuts or beans on my plot before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani midu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to a plant family that grabs nitrogen from the air and puts it naturally into the ground, enriching the soil so the next crop, like maize, has free fertilizer to grow big.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji tsei aweku ko ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ sɛɛnamɔ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa, yɛ ŋmãa ni aheee nɔ ko koni etsɔ agbo.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither and die when I clear all the big trees off my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboi ni amɛgboi beni mijie cacao tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to direct heat and strong sunlight. Leaving shade trees or planting plantains alongside cocoa creates a cool canopy that protects the young seedlings from drying out while keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo adu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ baa ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why should I cut off the extra shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie plantain tso lɛ tso lɛ

english: The extra shoots, called suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for nutrients, water, and sunlight. Pruning them down leaves only the strongest shoot, allowing the main plant to produce larger and heavier bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ, tsei lɛ ahe tsei ni wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashi. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ woɔ niji wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my cassava cuttings fail to grow when I plant them with the buds pointing downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tsei lɛ akwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ shi lɛ?

english: Cassava stems have tiny growing points along the nodes that naturally direct shoots upward and roots downward. Planting them upside down forces the plant to waste its energy trying to reorient its stems, which often kills the shoot before it breaks through the soil.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ yɛ hei bibii ni amɛdaraa yɛ amɛhe ni ŋmeii lɛ yaa ŋwɛi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni shishifãi lɛ baa shi yɛ lɛ. Tso lɛ ni edaa kɛyaa shishi lɛ haa efiteɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni etsɔɔ eshishifã lɛ gbɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ haa tso lɛ gboɔ dani eboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to build wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matswa tso kɛha sweet potato wain tso lɛ ni ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need to spread their leaves upward toward the sun to make food. Staking keeps the leaves off the warm, moist soil, which prevents leaves from rotting and helps the plant put more energy into growing big underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulu lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛfee niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akabote shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Enɛ haaa baai lɛ agbo, ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize crop turning yellow and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishi baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of a maize stalk are a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen gives crops their green color and growth energy, so adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer will help the plant recover.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen haa tsei lɛ amɛhe su eŋɔli kɛ fuel kɛha amɛdalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do other farmers tell me that planting groundnuts makes the soil better for my next corn crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi miikɛɛ mi akɛ ŋmei dumɔ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha mi ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that can capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the groundnut crop is harvested, these root nodules break down and leave rich natural nitrogen in the soil for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmei tso ko ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii lɛ, akpaa amɛ. Nɛkɛ shishifãi nɛɛ fãa ni amɛshiɔ nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms drop off the plant without forming any tomatoes during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni efeee tomato ko kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, tomato pollen becomes sticky or inactive, preventing flower fertilization. The plant drops the unpollinated flowers to save energy until temperatures cool down enough for successful fruiting.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Tomato pollen lɛ shwieɔ shi loo etsuuu nii. Etsiɔ fɔfɔi lɛ afɔmɔ naa Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni fɔmɔ bɛ mli lɛ shi koni ekɛto hewalɛ he kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ bɔ ni sa ni aduawai lɛ baawo.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and becoming small and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ bibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips sucking the plant sap and spreading plant viruses. Treating the farm early with natural sprays like neem oil helps keep these insects away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ tso mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kwɛmɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ mra. Kɛ́ akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai tamɔ neem fɔ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ahe.

english: Why does my maize crop rot when rainwater stays pooled on my field for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need oxygen from spaces in the soil to breathe and stay healthy. Waterlogged soil fills all those air spaces, effectively drowning the root system and causing soil bacteria to rot the submerged roots.
ga: Tsei shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hei lɛ amli koni amɛmu ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ ayi. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi ni ebote nu shishi lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply chemical fertilizer on my crops when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer chemicals need soil moisture to dissolve into a form plant roots can safely drink. Applying dry fertilizer directly to dry soil creates a high salt concentration that burns and destroys the root tissues.
ga: Tsofai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu koni etsɔ nɔ ko ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ anu shweshweeshwe. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ŋmei ni fa babaoo ni shãa shishifãi lɛ ni efiteɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young corn plants turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your corn lacks nitrogen in the soil or is getting too much water. Adding manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer will help the leaves turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do some of my corn stalks produce small cobs with missing kernels?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ nɔ ni bɛ dumɔwui?

english: Missing kernels happen mainly due to poor pollination, which occurs when weather is too dry when the corn flowers, or when plants are crowded too close together.
ga: Dumɔwui ni laajeɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo jɛɔ pollination ni ehiii lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shihilɛi lɛ mli egbi tsɔ beni ŋmãa fɔfɔii loo kɛ́ tsei ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ.

english: How does planting beans together with my corn help the corn grow better?
ga: Te ŋmãa ni mikɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Beans pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots, which acts as a natural food source for your corn.
ga: Beans gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe kɛha o-corn lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and fall off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells to protect itself and save water in its roots. Once the rains return, the plant naturally sprouts fresh green leaves.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ebu ehe ni ekɛ nu ahi eshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when the weather gets too hot or when the soil gets too dry, as a way to save energy until conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Bɔni afee ni akɛ hewalɛ ato kɛyashi kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt during the hottest part of the afternoon even when the soil is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In intense heat, tomatoes lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it up. They usually recover in the evening as the sun goes down.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ Tomatoi shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Bei pii lɛ, amɛhe jɔɔ amɛ gbɛkɛ beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes in the middle of my young corn leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-babi corn baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are fall armyworms, a common pest that feeds on the soft center of corn plants. Spraying early in the morning or late evening when they feed helps control them.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji fall asraafoi. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe hei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa shwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ beni ayeɔ niyenii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni eyeɔ amɛnɔ.

english: Why are my yam tubers rotting inside the soil before I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mikɛ amɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot underground when water collects in the mound without draining, allowing fungi to grow and attack the soft skin of the yam.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ gɔŋ lɛ mli ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ daa ni etutuaa ŋmei lɛ hewolo ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops yield heavily in the first year of clearing land but give less in the second year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi ni mikɛkpa ŋmɔ lɛ mli shi ewooo fioo yɛ afi ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Newly cleared forest land has years of built-up plant food, but crops consume most of it during the first harvest, leaving the soil drained unless you replenish it.
ga: Kooi amli hei heei ni ajie tsei lɛ ebua tsei anaa yɛ afii babaoo ni eho lɛ amli. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ heɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ fa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nikpamɔ be lɛ mli. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa Ja okɛfata he ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my plantain take much longer to produce fruit when planted in hard, rocky ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are soft and need loose soil to spread out and drink water. Hard ground blocks root growth, slowing down the plant's development.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni ehe miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛnu nu. Shikpɔŋ ni wa tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ adalɛ naa. Ehaa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi

english: Why are my coconut trees turning yellow and dying one after another in my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmei tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi komekomei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Coconut trees often suffer from serious diseases like Lethal Yellowing, which is spread by tiny insects carrying microscopic germs. Once a tree is infected, it quickly loses leaves and fruit, so identifying infected trees early helps stop the disease from wiping out nearby healthy farms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni naa wa tamɔ yellow leaf disease, ni kooloi bibii ni hiɛ helai bibii ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ yeɔ ŋmei tsei anɔ. Kɛji tso lɛ he hela lɛ Ebaafite baai kɛ aduawai oya. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni ana tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni helai akafite ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are sick from a disease or just suffering from dry weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela miimɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ loo shihilɛi ni mli egbi kɛkɛ miipiŋ amɛ?

english: Drought usually causes whole fields of plants to wilt evenly during hot days, while a disease often shows specific signs like yellow spots, rotting stems, or plants dying randomly in patches even when there is moisture in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ haa ŋmɔji muu fɛɛ shwieɔ shi pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ hela lɛ jieɔ okadii pɔtɛɛ komɛi tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ kpo. Aloo tsei gboiɔ trukaa yɛ hei srɔtoi. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po.

english: If a plant disease breaks out on my farm, can it spread to my neighbor's field?
ga: Kɛji tso hela ko ba miŋmɔ lɛ mli Ani ebaagbɛ eshwa ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ amli?

english: Yes, plant diseases can easily travel between farms through wind, insects, rain splash, or contaminated farming tools. Removing and burning infected plants quickly helps protect neighboring farms from catching the disease.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai baanyɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, kooloi bibii, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, loo okwaayeli nibii ni mli ewo muji lɛ anɔ aya ŋmɔji ateŋ mlɛo. Tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ oya ni ashãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hela he.

english: What is a crop hybrid, and why should I plant it instead of seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ekome? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui ni jɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ?

english: A crop hybrid is created by breeding two strong plant varieties together to combine their best traits. Hybrid seeds usually grow faster, produce much higher yields, and resist diseases better than seeds saved from old harvests.
ga: Akɛ tsei enyɔ ni wa ni akɛ amɛ sui ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ feɔ ekome lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee hybrid. Hybrid dumɔwui lɛ daa oya. Yibiiwoo lɛ fa babaoo fe nakai. ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe fe dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ blema ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ.

english: Do hybrid crop trees start bearing fruit faster than our traditional local varieties?
ga: Ani tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi mra fe wɔmaŋ tsei lɛ?

english: Yes, improved hybrid varieties are specifically bred to mature faster. For example, hybrid coconut trees can start producing fruit in half the time it takes traditional tall coconut trees to bear fruit.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɔse ŋmeii sɔrɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛshwere oya. Ákɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, ŋmei tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ baanyɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi yɛ be ni heɔ koni ŋmei tso kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ blema lɛ awo yibii lɛ fã mli.

english: If I plant a disease-resistant crop variety, does it mean my farm will never get sick?
ga: Kɛji midu tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ hela mɔŋ miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Resistant crop varieties can fight off specific diseases very well, but they are not completely immune to all bad weather, poor soil, or new pests. Good farm management is still needed to keep resistant crops healthy.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ baanyɛ awuu ashi helai komɛi jogbaŋŋ waa. Shi enyɛŋ edamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa, shikpɔŋ ni ehiii, loo kooloi heei ni fiteɔ nii lɛ anaa. completely Okwaafoi akwɛmɔ kpakpa hu he miihia koni akɛkwɛ tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ hela lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does it take researchers so many years to develop a new crop seed for us to plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ niiamlitaolɔi afii babaoo dani amɛfeɔ dumɔwui heei ni wɔbaanyɛ wɔdu lɛ?

english: Developing a new seed requires breeding multiple generations of plants, testing them for disease resistance, and observing how they perform across different seasons to ensure they are safe and reliable for farmers before release.
ga: Dumɔwui heei ni abaafee lɛ biɔ ni afɔ tsei ayinɔi babaoo. Helai ahe kaa kɛ bɔ ni tsei tsuɔ nii amɛhaa yɛ bei srɔtoi amli lɛ akwɛmɔ Enɛ ji koni ana akɛ tsei lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ amɛnɔ aha okwaafoi dani ajie amɛ.

english: Why do agricultural scientists come to study crops directly in our villages instead of staying in their research centers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nilelɔi baa koni amɛbakase ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nii yɛ wɔ akrowai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe amɛ niiamlitaomɔ hei lɛ?

english: Soils, weather, and pest behaviors vary across different locations. Scientists visit villages to observe how diseases behave in real farm environments and to ensure their solutions actually work under practical farming conditions.
ga: Shikpɔŋ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ asui yɛ srɔtoi yɛ he fɛɛ he. Jeŋ nilelɔi yaa akrowai amli Koni amɛkwɛ helai asui yɛ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛ diɛŋtsɛ mli ni amɛkwɛ akɛ amɛ tsabaai lɛ tsuɔ nii diɛŋtsɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii amli.

english: Why do some crop varieties perform very well in a neighboring village but fail when I plant them on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ akrowai ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli shi amɛyeee omanye kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Even nearby villages can have different soil types, underground water levels, and local insect populations. A crop variety that thrives in sandy soil might struggle in clay soil just a few miles away.
ga: Ekolɛ akrowai ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ po yɛ sũ. shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ mli ŋwɛi ŋta kɛ kooloi ayibɔ ni yɔɔ hei srɔtoi Tsei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ yɛ ŋã shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ abɔ mɔdɛŋ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ ni kɛ jɛmɛ jɛkɛmɔ ji kilomitai fioo ko pɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: How does reporting my weekly farm problems to an agricultural extension officer help my crop yields?
ga: Te mi otsi fɛɛ otsi ŋmɔ mli saji ni mikɛbaabɔ Okwaayeli He Nitsumɔhe lɛ he amaniɛ lɛ baaye abua ni miŋmɔshi nibii ni miwoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Extension officers connect farmers with scientific advice. Reporting issues early allows officers to help you identify diseases before they spread and share practical solutions discovered through research.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ tsaa okwaafoi kɛ jeŋ nilee ŋaawoo. Naagbai ahe amaniɛbɔɔ mra Yelikɛbuamɔ nitsulɔi yeɔ ebua bo ni oyɔseɔ helai dani egbɛɔ eshwaa ni amɛjaa tsabaai ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii ni ana kɛtsɔ niiamlitaomɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: How long does it usually take after planting cassava before I can harvest it for food?
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei sɛɛ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani abaanyɛ akpa lɛ akɛye niyenii?

english: Cassava is a root crop that generally takes between 9 to 12 months to mature and be ready for harvesting, although some improved local varieties can be harvested around 6 to 8 months.
ga: Cassava ji tuber ŋmɔshi nibii ni bei pii lɛ eheɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani edaa ni efeɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ abaanyɛ akpa maŋ lɛ mli ŋmeii srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ekomɛi yɛ aaafee nyɔji 6 kɛyashi 8 mli moŋ.

english: When is the best time during the year for me to start planting my food crops in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli ni manyɛ mabɔi niyenii dumɔ yɛ Ghana?

english: The best time to plant is usually at the start of the major rainy season—around March to April in Southern Ghana and May to June in Northern Ghana—so seeds get enough water to sprout and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee. Aaafee March kɛyashi April yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ. kɛ May kɛyashi June yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛdara waa.

english: Which food crops can give me quick harvests in a few months compared to crops that produce continuously over several years?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii oya yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli? Kɛ akɛto tsei ni yaa nɔ amɛwoɔ yibii afii babaoo lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Short-term crops like maize, tomatoes, and beans mature within 3 to 4 months, whereas semi-perennial crops like plantain and cassava take longer to establish but provide food continuously over 1 to 3 years.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ ŋmãa, tomato kɛ ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ afii fã tamɔ plantains kɛ cassava lɛ shwereɔ. Eheɔ be babaoo dani etswaa shi abaanyɛ aha lɛ niyenii be fɛɛ be afii 1 kɛyashi 3.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for growth, or that heavy rains have waterlogged the soil and prevented the roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Aloo nugbɔ nɛɔ waa, ni no haa nu ewoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: What causes tiny holes in the leaves of my crops, and how does it hurt my harvest?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ Ni te eyeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Holes in leaves are caused by insect pests feeding on your crops; when leaves are damaged, the plant cannot properly absorb sunlight to produce food, leading to weaker growth and smaller harvests.
ga: Buji ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ oŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli. Kɛji baai lɛ fite lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ hulu la lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ baa shi, ni kpamɔ lɛ hu baa shi fioo.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes next to my yam plants as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso ko ama sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam plants produce long, soft vines that need to climb upward to catch as much sunlight as possible; staking exposes the leaves to sunlight, which helps the plant grow larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei woɔ wain tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni esa akɛ akwɔ nɔ koni hulu la ashɛ nɔ babaoo bɔ ni aaanyɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la he, ni no yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: What happens to my food crops if I plant them too close together on my land?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi niyenii tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe tsɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting crops too close together causes them to compete for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, resulting in thin, weak plants with small or low-quality harvests.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ he, ni no haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ loo nɔ ni ehiii kwraa baa.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly when big trees are casting shade over them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo be mli ni tsei wuji haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Most staple food crops like maize and cassava need direct, bright sunlight to photosynthesize and produce food; shaded plants grow slowly and yield very little.
ga: Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa Amɛmiitao hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee fotosintɛsis ni amɛfee niyenii. Tsei ni yɔɔ shia lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why does my soil produce smaller food harvests if I keep planting maize on the exact same spot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ kpaŋ niyenii fioo kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the topsoil; rotating your crops with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts helps restore nutrients like nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ pɛ mli. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How do weeds growing around my crops reduce my final harvest?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Te fee tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ha minaagbee ŋmaa lɛ ba shi?

english: Weeds steal vital soil nutrients, fertilizer, water, and space away from your crops, which starves the main plants and significantly lowers the amount of food you harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, ŋmɔshi nibii, nu kɛ he ko kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ, ni ehaa niyenii ni okpaa lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Why do some of my nursery seedlings grow very tall and thin while others stay short and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mi-nsɛri lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu yɛ kukuji ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Seedlings stretch tall and thin when they are planted too closely together or lack enough sunlight. Giving nursery bags enough space and direct sunlight helps seedlings develop thick, sturdy stems that survive transplanting.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baakpã kɛya shɔŋŋ ni ebaafee mlɛo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Kɛ́ aha dumɔwui lɛ aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa ni abaanyɛ adu amɛ.

english: Does planting larger nursery seedlings give me a bigger crop harvest than planting smaller ones?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ agbo mli lɛ baaha maná yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui bibii ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Not necessarily. While larger seedlings look stronger, smaller healthy seedlings often adapt faster after transplanting because their roots suffer less disturbance. Good root health matters more than the initial height of the seedling.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Eyɛ mli akɛ dumɔwui wuji lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa moŋ, shi dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛtsake amɛhe oya kɛji akɛ amɛdu amɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ gbaaa amɛnaa tsɔ. Shishifãi lɛ ahewalɛ kpakpa he hiaa fe bɔ ni dumɔwu lɛ shishijee lɛlɛ ji lɛ.

english: What happens to my maize yield if I plant seeds closer together to fit more on my farm?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmãa yibiiwoo lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ miŋmɔ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: If you plant maize too close together, the crops fight each other for soil nutrients, sunlight, and water. This competition leads to thin stalks and smaller cobs, resulting in a lower overall harvest than properly spaced plants.
ga: Kɛji odu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, hulu la kɛ nu. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, ŋmaa lɛ fɛɛ baafee nɔ ni baa shi fe tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my corn plants turning yellow during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen out of the soil, so applying fertilizer at the right stage helps the plant keep its green color and feed its growing cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli, ni ebaaha ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Should I apply fertilizer right when I put the seed in the soil or wait until the plant emerges?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo mamɛ ni tsei lɛ akwɛ̃?

english: It is best to wait until the seed sprouts and develops small roots, or place the fertilizer slightly away from the seed. Placing strong fertilizer directly against a seed can burn it before it sprouts.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛná shishifãi bibii. Aloo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo he ko ni kɛ dumɔwui lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ fioo. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni mli wa wo dumɔwui lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã amɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or lacks consistent water and soil nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil damp and shaded during extreme heat helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop their leaves during the dry season, and are they dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shwieɔ baai yɛ fɛ̃i be mli ni egboɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava plants naturally drop leaves in dry weather to reduce water loss and protect themselves. The plant is not dying; once the rains return, it will grow fresh leaves and continue expanding its tubers.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni nu egbi lɛ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu amɛhe. Tso lɛ gbooo. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ, baai heei kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ bulbs.

english: Why do some of my seeds take much longer to come up out of the soil than others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi heɔ be babaoo fe ekrokomɛi dani amɛjeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds take longer to sprout if they are buried too deep, if the soil is too dry, or if the soil surface is hard and packed down. Planting seeds at the recommended depth and keeping the topsoil moist speeds up sprouting.
ga: Dumɔwui baahe be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ wa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni atsɔɔ akɛ eshɛɔ lɛ, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baaha ekwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants need shade trees, but older cocoa trees need more open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa tso ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ? Shi kookoo tsei ni edara lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ hei ni gbɛ yɔɔ faŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa leaves are tender and easily scorch under direct sun, so shade trees protect them while roots grow. As cocoa trees mature, they become tough enough to handle direct sunlight, which fuels higher pod production.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. No hewɔ lɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ buɔ ehe be mli ni eshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ. Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Ebaafee nɔ ni wa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ekanya podfeemɔ ni fa babaoo.

english: How do weeds actually slow down the growth of my young crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aha midumɔwui lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo?

english: Weeds steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight directly from your crops. Removing weeds early gives your young plants exclusive access to the food and light they need to establish strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa otsei bibii lɛ naa niyenii kɛ la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do my cassava yields get smaller every year when I plant on the same soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops feed on nutrients in the soil just like humans need food. When you plant cassava on the same land continuously, it eats up all the specific nutrients without giving the soil time to recover, causing future harvests to shrink.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tamɔ bɔ ni niyenii he hiaa adesai lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Beni oduɔ ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa. Ebaaye niyenii mli nibii krɛdɛɛi lɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛ be haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ ehe awo mli ekoŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nibii ni afeɔ wɔsɛɛ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do weeds make my maize crops turn yellow even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi-ŋma lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds are aggressive eaters that steal food, water, and sunlight from your maize. If you do not clear the weeds first, they will swallow most of the fertilizer before your maize roots can reach it.
ga: Jwɛi ji niyelɔi ni yɔɔ basabasa ni juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ o-corn lɛ mli. Kɛji ojieee jwɛi lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, Amɛmiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ babaoo dani ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I cut down all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikookoo tsei bibii lɛ shã ni amɛgboi beni mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct sunlight. Big trees act as natural umbrellas that protect the delicate leaves from harsh sun and keep the soil cool and moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei ni eda lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni buɔ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that provide quick shade for young cocoa trees, protecting them from heat stress while creating a moist microclimate for their roots.
ga: Plantain lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔ oya. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he yɛ be mli ni ehaa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo ko ni mli edɔ baa shishifãi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up during the dry afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling up leaves is a defense mechanism pepper plants use to trap moisture inside and stop the sun from drying them out completely during the hottest parts of the day.
ga: Leaf curling ji gbɛ ko ni pepper tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛmɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ ni amɛtsi enaa koni ekagbi kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing fruits when there is heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains can wash away pollen or make it too wet for insects to pollinate the blossoms. Without pollination, the plant drops the unused flowers to save energy.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie pollen lɛ loo eha efee ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ ni kooloi bibii nyɛŋ afee pollen lɛ. Kɛji pollination bɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni akɛtsuuu nii koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do I get very small yams if I plant many seed yams close together on one mound?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmeii bibii waa nɔ kɛji midu ŋmeii babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ gɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their underground roots fight each other for limited space, water, and soil nutrients, preventing the yam tubers from expanding fully.
ga: Kɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná he ko ni faaa, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Tsi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã kwraa.

english: Why should I prune away extra leaves and branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ baai kɛ niji ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Removing unnecessary branches allows sunlight and fresh air to reach the inner trunk, preventing diseases while directing the tree's energy into making cocoa pods instead of extra leaves.
ga: Niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ mligbɛ. Etsiɔ helai anaa yɛ be mli ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over by themselves just when the fruits are growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ aduawai miikwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Underground pests like nematodes and root rot diseases weaken the roots, leaving the plant without a firm grip in the soil to support the heavy weight of the growing plantain bunch.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ nematodes kɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkɛfi plantains akui ni miida lɛ ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting within two days after I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni akpa lɛ?

english: Once detached from the stem, cassava roots rapidly undergo chemical reactions and lose water through their skin, making them vulnerable to quick decay if left exposed to heat and air.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ajie kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, Cassava shishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ tsofafeemɔ mli oya ni amɛlaajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ hewolo lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛfiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: If fire accidentally burns my cocoa farm, will the burnt trees grow back or do I need to clear everything and replant?
ga: Kɛji mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ shã yɛ oshara mli Ani tsei ni ashã lɛ baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ? Aloo esa akɛ majie nɔ fɛɛ nɔ kɛjɛ mli ni madu ekoŋŋ?

english: If only the leaves and small outer branches are scorched, cocoa trees can shoot fresh leaves when the rains start. However, if the main trunk and roots were deeply burnt, the tree is dead and must be cleared so you can plant fresh seedlings.
ga: Kɛji akɛ baai kɛ tsei niji bibii pɛ Charred exterior Cacao tsei lɛ baanyɛ ajie baai heei kɛji nugbɔ nɛ. Shi, kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifãi titrii lɛ shã waa lɛ, Tsei lɛ hu gboiɔ ni esa akɛ ajie amɛ koni onyɛ odu dumɔwui heei.

english: Does burning weeds and dry bushes before planting make the soil richer for my crops?
ga: Ani jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni egbi ni mashãa dani aduɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Fire gives a very quick boost of ash to the soil, but it actually harms your farm in the long run. Burning destroys the good organic matter, kills tiny organisms that build healthy soil, and leaves the ground dry and easy for rain to wash away.
ga: La kɛ sũ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya, shi ebaanyɛ eye oŋmɔ lɛ awui diɛŋtsɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Shãa fiteɔ nibii kpakpai ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. gbeɔ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni tswaa sũ ni wa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ gbi ni efeɔ mlɛo kɛha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ.

english: How can I build a firebelt around my cocoa farm to prevent bushfires from spreading into my crops during the dry season?
ga: Miiya ni matswa la line kɛbɔle he. Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsu mi-cocoa lɛ he nii koni koo mli la akagbɛ ashwã miŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: You can clear a wide strip of land around your farm border by removing all dry grass and wood, or plant a thick row of moisture-rich plants like plantains along the edge. This creates a barrier that bushfires cannot easily cross.
ga: Obaanyɛ ojie hei wuji. Abaanyɛ afee enɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ husu lɛ he kɛtsɔ jwɛi kɛ tsei fɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ. Aloo dumɔ tsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ dumɔwui yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa gbɛtsii nii ko baa ni koo mli la nyɛŋ afo mli mlɛo.

english: How do the cocoa seedlings from government support initiatives like Planting for Food and Jobs differ from seeds I harvest myself?
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui ni jɛ nɔyeli lɛ mli lɛ fi nifeemɔi tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ kɛha niyenii kɛ nitsumɔi asɛɛ. Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esoro lɛ yɛ dumɔwui ni mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpaa lɛ he?

english: Government-provided hybrid seedlings are specifically bred by scientists to produce pods much faster—usually within 2 to 3 years instead of 5—and they are stronger against common crop diseases than seeds taken directly from your own farm.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔi edu dumɔwui ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he ni nɔyeli lɛ kɛhaa lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmeii oya kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, amɛhiɔ shi afii 2 kɛyashi 3 yɛ afii 5 najiaŋ, ni amɛhe wa kɛha tsei ahe helai ni afɔɔ namɔ fe dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ bo diɛŋtsɛ oŋmɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my new hybrid cocoa seedlings need shade trees when older cocoa farms seem to grow in open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-hybrid cocoa dumɔwu hee lɛ he hiaa tso ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ? Beni kokoo ŋmɔ momo lɛ Etamɔ nɔ ni eekwɛ̃ yɛ kpo nɔ.

english: Young hybrid seedlings are delicate and can easily dry out or suffer heat stress under direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade like plantains protects their young leaves and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa roots grow deep enough.
ga: Hybrid dumɔwui lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbi oya loo amɛna dɔlɛ he haomɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains lɛ baaye abua ni ebu baai bibii ahe ni eye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers keep falling off the tree instead of turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by lack of water, insect attacks, or poor soil nutrients. Ensuring your trees have adequate shade, water during dry periods, and protection from pests helps flowers develop into full pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji nu ni bɛ, kooloi ni tutuaa amɛ, loo sũ mli niyenii ni ehiii lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei akwɛmɔ koni amɛná hulutsoo Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Ni etsĩɔ kooloi ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ baai ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cut off the small shoots growing on the sides of my cocoa tree trunks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? No kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ he.

english: Those side shoots, called chupons, steal food and water away from the main stem without producing pods. Cutting them off forces the tree to send all its energy to flowering and growing larger cocoa pods.
ga: Nɛkɛ sɛɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ, ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons lɛ, juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ he ni amɛfeee ŋmeii. Kɛ́ afo amɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ akudɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛya fɔfɔi kɛ kookoo ŋmɔji wuji ni amɛdaraa lɛ anɔ.

english: Can I plant cassava inside my young cocoa farm to harvest food while waiting for the cocoa to grow?
ga: Ma nyɛ ma du sino ngɛ kookoo ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli. Ani manyɛ mikɛ minɔ lɛ akpa niyenii yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: It is better to plant plantains or maize instead of cassava near young cocoa. Cassava roots spread wide and consume a lot of water and nutrients, which can starve young cocoa seedlings and slow down their growth.
ga: Esa akɛ adu plantain loo ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ahe yɛ ŋmãa najiaŋ. Cassava shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa he fɛɛ he ni eyeɔ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo. Enɛ baanyɛ aha kookoo tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni amɛha amɛdalɛ aba shi.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees turn yellow and drop off during the Harmattan period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan beaŋ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed leaves during severe dry weather to conserve water and prevent the tree from dying. Providing good shade trees helps reduce heat stress so the cocoa holds onto its leaves longer.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛtsi tso lɛ naa koni ekagbo. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo be kpakpa ha lɛ, ehaa dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa shi bɔni afee ni kookoo lɛ ahi baai lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is it better to space my crops measured distances apart instead of planting as many as fit on the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ majara miŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu babaoo bɔ ni ebaanyɛ eshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, air, and ground nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to grow strong and produce a bigger harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ eda ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field without any shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate strong, direct sunlight when they are small. Planting food crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides immediate shade and keeps the surrounding air cool and moist, helping the seedlings survive until they grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ kɛ́ amɛji bibii. Niyenii nibii tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo baa amrɔ nɔŋŋ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle he lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashi amɛ daraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛ na hulu la fɛɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing on lower leaves is a clear sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need for healthy green growth. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen deep out of reach of young roots, so applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure restores their green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni eshiɔ shishifãi bibii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Does it matter which direction the buds on a cassava stem cutting point when I push it into the ground?
ga: Kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmei tso lɛ tsi shikpɔŋ lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ eyaa? Ani esa akɛ asusu he ni ŋmeii lɛ yaa lɛ he yɛ he ni ŋmei tsei lɛ kpeɔ yɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, cassava stem cuttings must always be planted with the raised node buds pointing upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down forces the new shoots to grow downward first before curving up, which weakens the plant and leads to poor tuber yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ adu yucca tsei lɛ be fɛɛ be ni ŋmeii ni awó nɔ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu ŋwɛi ŋwɛi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii heei akwɛ̃ shi dani amɛkoto. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaaa tuber yibii kpakpai aba.

english: Why are my young coconut trees dropping their small nuts before they can grow and mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei tso bibioo lɛ shwieɔ shi dani edaa ni edaa lɛ?

english: Early fruit drop in coconut trees usually happens due to prolonged dry spells, poor nutrient levels in the soil, or attacks from sap-sucking insects like coreid bugs. Providing steady moisture and applying proper fertilizer keeps the tree healthy enough to hold its fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei tsei ni amɛyibii lɛ fiteɔ oya lɛ baa yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ hewɔ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni baa shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ spindles lɛ tutuamɔi, nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkpa aduawai.

english: What is making ragged holes in the center leaves of my corn plants and leaving dark dust inside?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miifee bu yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ ni amɛshiɔ sũ ni tsuɔ yɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a destructive caterpillar that hides inside the central whorl of maize plants. Catching them early and applying recommended neem extracts or approved insecticides directly into the center funnel stops them from destroying the growing tip.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni fiteɔ nii ni ekɛ ehe ewoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋtayaa mli lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ neem mli nu loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ awo ŋwɛi gbɛ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and soft right before they start to ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit. It usually happens when watering is inconsistent during hot dry weather, making it hard for the plant's roots to draw up calcium from the soil smoothly.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ tso yibii ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu lɛ efɔɔɔ shi be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ jieɔ calcium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm make the soil better for next season's maize crop?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts belong to the legume family, which can capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in root nodules underground. When the legume crop finishes, that captured nitrogen stays in the soil and feeds the next maize crop naturally.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛto shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli. Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa lɛ agbe naa lɛ Nitrogen ni aŋɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why does covering the soil around my pepper plants with dry grass help them grow better during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass is called mulching. It creates a protective blanket that shields the soil from direct sun, preventing soil water from evaporating quickly and keeping root zones cool and moist.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Efeɔ tsɔne ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ehaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya. kɛ shishifã lɛ he ni aaaha afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ

english: Why do seeds saved from my last maize harvest yield much smaller cobs than the original seed packet I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli lɛ wo ŋmãa bibii kwraa fe shishijee dumɔwui akui ni mihe lɛ?

english: Commercially packed seeds are often specially bred hybrids designed for high performance in their first generation. Saving seeds from those harvested crops causes them to lose their vigor in the second generation, resulting in smaller cobs and uneven growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ jarayeli mli lɛ ji dumɔwui ni afee amɛ koni amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni jɛ nakai ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ ni abaabu he lɛ baaha amɛhe awa yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii kɛ dalɛ ni ejaaa baa.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow, snap near the stem base, and cause the whole plant to collapse before fruiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Akumɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni eha tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbee shi dani ewo yibii po?

english: This leaf breakdown and trunk collapse is typically caused by Panama disease (Fusarium wilt) or microscopic root worms (nematodes). These pests block the movement of water and nutrients inside the stalk, so removing affected plants quickly prevents the disease from spreading to surrounding suckers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Panama hela (Fusarium wilt) loo shishifãi bibii ni anaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ mli shwiemɔ kɛ tso lɛ shishi shwiemɔ baa. (Nematodes) Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ tsiɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ gbɛfaa naa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and burning during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees to protect them from heat stress until their stems and leaves mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei. Enɛ ji koni akɛtsi dɔlɛ he haomɔ naa kɛyashi be mli ni ŋmeii kɛ baai lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient that plants use to make chlorophyll and build strong green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ chlorophyll ni amɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni eŋɔli.

english: Why does covering the soil around my vegetables with dry grass help them stay green during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) blocks hot sunlight, keeps the root area cool, and prevents moisture in the soil from evaporating quickly into the air.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni etsĩ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli

english: Why do I need to plant my cassava stem cuttings pointing upward instead of upside down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmei niji ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi moŋ fe ni amɛtsɔɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava stem buds point upward toward the sky; planting them upside down forces new shoots to turn around underground before growing up, which wastes the plant's energy and reduces root yield.
ga: Kasava tsei ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi ni aduɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ haa tsei heei shwieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛdaraa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni ehaa shishifãi ni baa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with small cobs when I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Akɛni midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ hewɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crowded plants compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak stems and small cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dense plants lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe waaa kɛ dumɔwui bibii.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb up wooden stakes to give me big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛná ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the plant. Staking lifts the leaves into the air so the plant can make maximum energy and send it down to swell the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha tso lɛ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ afee hewalɛ ni fa fe fɛɛ ni etsu kɛya shi koni eha ŋmeii lɛ atsɔ.

english: Why do groundnut plants push their flower stems down into the ground after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ tsiɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ahe ŋmeii lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts grow their pods underground. After the yellow flowers are pollinated above ground, the stems bend down and push into the soil so the peanut pods can safely grow under the earth.
ga: Peanuts kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ pods amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Beni fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ebɔle shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ, Tso lɛ shishifã lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ ehe woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni ŋmei ŋmɔŋ lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Extreme heat, lack of water, or dry winds stress tomato plants, causing them to drop their blossoms to save energy rather than trying to support growing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni okwɛ aduawai

english: Why should I cut off some of the extra small shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Ajie nɔ ni fa fe nine ni miida yɛ Mi plantain tso titri lɛ he lɛ

english: Extra sucker shoots compete with the main plantain stem for food and water. Removing extra suckers ensures the main plant receives enough energy to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi kɛ plantain tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii krokomɛi lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and becoming small and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ bibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Curled and wrinkled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding on leaf juices and spreading plant diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ amli nu kɛ tsei ahelai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build green leaves. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their green color and healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas in my farm make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts have beneficial bacteria on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop is harvested, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil to feed the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei yɛ bacteria ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, shady conditions. Pruning excess branches and clearing weeds allows sunlight and air to dry the pods, preventing the fungus from growing.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo yɔɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekakwɛ̃

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upward and staying small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Tomato leaf curl is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Protecting young plants with neem oil spray or insect mesh keeps the whiteflies away and prevents leaf curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Kɛ́ akɛ neem mu ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo kooloi bibii ahe ŋmeii buɔ tsei bibii ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa whiteflies baa, ni ehaa baai lɛ hu shwieɔ shi.

english: Why are small brown insects eating holes through my harvested maize inside my storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ miiye ŋmãa ni mikpa yɛ mi-nitoohe kotokui lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are maize weevils that attack stored grain if the corn was not dried fully before storage. Drying maize thoroughly under the sun and storing it in airtight bags (PICS bags) starves the insects of oxygen and protects the grain.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmãa mli ŋmeii ni tutuaa ŋmãa ni ato lɛ kɛji ŋmãa lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛto. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu shishi ni akɛto kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli (PICS kotokui) amli lɛ, ehaa kooloi lɛ náa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmãa lɛ he.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to produce enough energy to grow big tubers underground. Staking also lifts leaves away from damp ground diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulutsoo be lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees fall over so easily when heavy rains and winds come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni eda lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that cannot hold heavy bunches in soft, wet soil. Supporting the main stem with strong, forked bamboo poles (propping) keeps the tree standing until harvest.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ahiɛ panicles agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso titri lɛ ni akɛ ŋmei tso ni mli wa ebɔ he lɛ fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni edamɔ shi kɛyashiɔ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli.

english: Why are the blossoms falling off my pepper plants without forming any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo pepper yibii ko lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the root zone moist and cool with regular watering and mulch helps the flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ahã shishifã lɛ he lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How do I know that my cassava tubers are ready to harvest since they grow under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off naturally, and the ground around the base of the main stem begins to crack open as the tubers swell underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni tuber lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my vegetable plants with dry grass during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni bɔle aduawai ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves is called mulching. It acts like a protective blanket that keeps moisture from evaporating in the heat, keeps roots cool, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when there are no big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni tsei wuji komɛi bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct hot sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains or leaving canopy trees provides the shelter and moisture they need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo ŋwɛi tsei ni ashiɔ lɛ haa amɛnáa he ko ni amɛhiɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden sticks next to my yam plants for the vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso ko masɛi koni wain tsei lɛ akakwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases and allowing the leaves to catch maximum sunlight.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛnáa hulu la babaoo

english: Why should I cut off some of the small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Ajie midumɔwu titri lɛ shishi.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water, plant food, and sunlight from the main plantain tree. Removing most of them leaves only one or two strong suckers, ensuring the main tree produces a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tsoi ni fa fe nine, loo suckers, juɔ nu, tso niyenii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie emli babaoo lɛ, ebaashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha tso titri lɛ aná ŋmeii wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in the middle of the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is essential for healthy plant growth. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or planting nitrogen-fixing crops like cowpeas can restore the green color and boost crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ ni hi Kɛ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli loo adu nibii ni haa nitrogen hiɔ shi tamɔ cowpea lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ ahiɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same piece of land season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts helps rebuild soil fertility and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai aba. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why is it harmful to place fertilizer directly touching the stem of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo ŋmɔshi nibii ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer directly touching the stem acts like chemical salt that can burn the tender plant tissue and damage roots. Placing fertilizer in a ring a few inches away from the stem allows the roots to safely draw in the nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli ni baa tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli ni baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ mli fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ni efite shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wo ŋwɛi ŋta ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbala niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when we get heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water settles around them for too long, suffocating the roots. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe. Koni yitso lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Tomato flowers fall off when plants get too stressed by extreme heat or drought, preventing pollination. Regular watering at the root level keeps the plant cool and helps flowers turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo loo hɔmɔ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ ha tso lɛ hao waa. inhibits pollination Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ he daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni etsɔɔ tomato.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tightly and turning hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe waa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is typically caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites that suck the plant's sap and spread viruses. Using an approved insecticidal spray or neem oil early helps control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ baa. Akpɛlɛ nɔ mra akɛ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ atsu nii. Ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds hurt my crop yield even if my crops are much taller than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miifite miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? Shi kɛlɛ, miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ kwraa fe jwɛi lɛ.

english: Weeds have fast-growing underground roots that steal water and fertilizer from the soil before your crop's roots can reach them, reducing overall yield even if the crop looks bigger above ground.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni daa oya. Enɛ juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shɛɔ he. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni tsei lɛ dara fe shikpɔŋ lɛ moŋ.

english: How do I know if the soil on my farm is good enough for planting crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: Good agricultural soil is usually dark, crumbles easily in your hands, holds some moisture without staying swampy, and is rich in organic matter like rotted leaves.
