ga: Bei pii lɛ, okwaayeli shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli ewo duŋ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni nubu bɛ mli. ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ eyi mli obɔ

english: How do I choose which crop to plant based on the type of soil I have?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tsei ni mikɛbaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miyɔɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Sandy soil that drains water quickly is great for crops like cassava and groundnuts, loamy soil rich in organic matter suits cocoa and vegetables, while heavy clay soil holds water well for crops like rice.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ ni nu hoɔ oya lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ hi kɛha kookoo kɛ aduawai. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni shikpɔŋ sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ hiɛɔ nu jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Can giving my crops too much water actually harm their growth?
ga: Ani nu ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aye amɛdalɛ awui?

english: Yes, excessive water drowns plant roots by filling up air spaces in the soil, which leads to root rot, yellow leaves, and stunted growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu babaoo baaha tsei shishifãi lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni eeewo mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni amɛdaraaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens to my crops when there is not enough rainfall during the farming season?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ yɛ okwaayeli be lɛ mli?

english: Without enough water, plants wilt, drop their flowers early to survive, and cannot absorb nutrients from the soil, leading to a much smaller harvest.
ga: Kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Tso lɛ baagbo. Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya koni amɛhi shi. ni enyɛɛɛ ejie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: Will watering my crops more frequently make them produce flowers faster?
ga: Ani nu ni afɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ shii abɔ lɛ baaha amɛfɔ̃ oya?

english: Not necessarily; while plants need adequate water to produce flowers, overwatering can actually force the plant to focus only on growing leaves instead of flowering.
ga: nɔ ni he ehiaaa; Nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni fa bɔ ni sa he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo fɔfɔi. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ fe nine lɛ baanyɛ anyɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama baai ni miida lɛ pɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeewo fɔfɔi.

english: Why do my crops produce flowers only at certain times of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ afi lɛ mli bei komɛi pɛ amli lɛ?

english: Crops produce flowers based on natural environmental signals like changes in daylight hours, temperature, and seasonal rainfall patterns that tell the plant it is time to reproduce.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi yɛ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛ mli okadii tamɔ tsakemɔi ni baa yɛ hulutsoo be mli, dɔlɛ, kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be mli ni tsɔɔ tsei akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛfɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the flowers on my crops falling off before they turn into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers drop prematurely when the crop experiences stress, such as extreme heat, lack of water, poor soil nutrients, or a lack of insects like bees to pollinate them.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔi, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ afee pollination lɛ ni bɛ.

english: Why does water sink away so quickly on some parts of my farmland but stay stagnant on others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu shwieɔ shi oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ hei komɛi shi eshwieee shi yɛ hei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Water drains quickly where the soil has loose, sandy particles, while water collects on top where the soil has high clay content that packs tightly and blocks water flow.
ga: Nu lɛ hoɔ oya yɛ hei ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋã bibii ni etsilɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ. Beni nu buaa ehe naa yɛ he ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ sũ babaoo yɔɔ lɛ, ehaa nu lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsĩɔ nu lɛ naa.

english: What should I do to help my crops recover after a major drought or setback?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni maye mabua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ hɔmɔ loo sɛɛkuu wulu ko sɛɛ?

english: Inspect for damage, clear dead plant material, apply mulch around the base to keep moisture in, and add gentle organic manure or fertilizer to restore soil nutrients.
ga: Kwɛmɔ kɛji nɔ ko efite Tsɔɔmɔ tso nibii ni egboi lɛ. Mulch abɔle shishigbɛ lɛ he koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo afata he koni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I effectively manage a farm as large as 12 acres without getting overwhelmed?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ ŋmɔ agbo ko ni dalɛ ji acre 12 lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli?

english: Divide your land into smaller, manageable blocks, practice crop rotation, prioritize high-value sections first, and consider labor-sharing groups or modern tools for clearing and weeding.
ga: Jaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli awo kui bibii amli. ni abaanyɛ akwɛ nɔ lɛ Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ Ha hei ni jara wa waa lɛ afee nɔ ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Ni susumɔ nitsumɔ mlijaa kui loo ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛjieɔ jwɛi kɛ jwɛi lɛ ahe okwɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I clear all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei wuji kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight and extreme heat. Leaving some canopy trees or planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains protects the delicate young leaves from scorching and helps keep the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ loo adu tsei ni haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni daa oya tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaabu baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Pale yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is a major food source crops need to build healthy green leaves. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure to the soil helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii mli hewalɛ jɛɛhe titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata sũ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep falling off without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets too hot, when the plant lacks water, or if there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Keeping the soil consistently moist and avoiding excessive strong fertilizers during flowering helps the blossoms stay on and turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji nu bɛ tsei amli loo kɛji nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa fe nine he yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ tomato.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground before I get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛnáa hegbɛ ni akpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when water sits around them for too long in heavy, soaked soil. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away so the roots can breathe and grow healthily.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu ebɔle amɛhe. Etsɛɔ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni mli edɔ nɔ Ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do my harvested yams start growing green shoots in the barn when I want to store them to sell later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shweremɔ lɛ? Be ni miisumɔ ni mikɛto koni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ sɛɛ mli lɛ

english: Yams naturally break their rest period after a few months because they are programmed to start growing a new plant. Storing them in a cool, well-ventilated barn away from direct light and gently rubbing off early shoots helps prolong their storage life.
ga: Sweet potatoes baafo amɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be lɛ mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Ejaakɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ko yɛ ni akɛjeɔ tsei heei akwɛmɔ shishi. Akɛtoɔ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli. Kɛ́ okɛto he ko ni la shɛɛɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni okɛ shishijee ŋmeii lɛ shwie nɔ blɛoo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas together with my maize help my farm grow better?
ga: Te cowpea ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that can pull nitrogen out of the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots. This natural soil food feeds the nearby maize plants while the trailing leaves of the cowpea cover the ground to stop weeds from growing.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii nɛɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsina ŋmeii ni egbee shi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni jwɛi akakwɛ̃.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and twisting into tight cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni etsɔ kɔɔpoi ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips feeding on the undersides of the leaves, or from a virus spread by these insects. Controlling these pests early with neem oil or appropriate organic sprays protects the new leaves from damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Kudɔmɔ kooloi nɛɛ mra Kɛtsɔ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ, ebaabu baai heei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ fitemɔ he.

english: Why does planting my seeds too close together make the crops tall and thin with poor yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ shwiili ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops must compete with each other for light, soil food, and water. They stretch upward as high as possible to catch sunlight, spending all their energy growing tall instead of growing thick stems and big fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛmɔ hulu la lɛ. Amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛaatsu nii koni amɛdara. Mohu ɔ, e daa kɛ tsohi nɛ a mi wa kɛ yiblii nguahi.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt and droop during the hot afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli be mli ni mifeee nakai lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: In the hot sun, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up from the ground. Wilting is the plant's way of shrinking its leaf area to conserve water, and the leaves usually bounce back in the cooler evening.
ga: Yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Withering ji gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛfoɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛbu nu he. Ni baai lɛ fɔɔ shweremɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why is it a bad idea to put fertilizer on my farm right before a heavy downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ ji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes away applied fertilizer from the surface soil into drains and streams before the plant roots have time to drink it in. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after rain, rather than right before a major storm.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa nu tsɔji kɛ faai amli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛnuɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Mohu ɔ, mo ngɔ mɛ kɛ wo mi loko ahumi ngua ko maa ba.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to sprout if I plant them right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ afi lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The very first rain often just warms up the dry topsoil without soaking deep enough. If a long dry spell follows immediately, the seeds get trapped in hot, moist soil and rot before they can grow strong roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ dɔɔ ni ekɛ nu lɛ efɔɔɔ mli bɔ ni sa. Kɛji hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ba amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani shishifãi lɛ baaje shishi.

english: Why should I consider planting short-duration crop varieties when the rainy season keeps getting shorter?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ he yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ miiba kuku kɛmiiya kuku lɛ?

english: Short-duration crops mature much faster, meaning they can finish growing and yield fruit within a shorter rain period before the dry season suddenly starts.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya kwraa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei baanyɛ adara ni amɛwo yibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo mli dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi trukaa.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl up tightly during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a defense trick crops use to reduce the leaf area exposed to direct sunlight, helping the plant hold onto internal moisture until the air cools down.
ga: Baai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ji ŋaa ni buɔ mɔ he ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛba he ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ emli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do my bean plants drop their flowers when there is a long break in the rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When crops experience heat and dry conditions, they drop their flowers to save energy and water, knowing they do not have enough water to nourish full pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shɛ latsaa kɛ hulutsoo be he lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu akafite. Nilee akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ bɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my pepper plants turning yellow during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni pepper tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: In dry conditions, roots cannot pull nutrients from the soil, so the plant steals nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the young, growing leaves at the top.
ga: Yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ amli lɛ, shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ajie niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ juɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: How does covering the soil around my yam mounds with dry grass help my farm survive heat?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi shwie mi sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔ lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Covering soil with dry grass creates a protective blanket that shields the ground from direct sunlight, keeping the soil cool and trapping moisture underground longer.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad to water my vegetable garden in the middle of a scorching afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mawo mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Watering in high afternoon heat causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before roots can drink it, and cold water on hot leaves can shock the plant.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ anu. Ni nu ni mli ejɔ ni yɔɔ baai ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ he afee gbeyei.

english: Why do my cassava plants stop growing taller when the sun is intense and rain stops for weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ beni hulu lɛ mli wa ni nugbɔ lɛ kpaa gbee otsii babaoo lɛ?

english: Crops need water to carry nutrients from the soil up into their stems. Without water, the crop goes into a dormant resting state to conserve energy until rain returns.
ga: Tsei hia nu koni amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ nu bɛ lɛ, tsei boteɔ shihilɛ ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli mli koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are the edges of my plantain leaves turning brown and papery during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ ashishigbɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efeɔ tamɔ wolo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Strong sun and dry winds draw moisture out of leaves faster than roots can draw water from dry soil, causing the leaf tips to dry out and burn.
ga: Hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Ehaa baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa.

english: Why do my crops look greener and healthier after rain than when I water them by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ fe be mli ni mikɛ minine shwieɔ amɛnɔ nu lɛ?

english: Rainwater washes dust off the leaves so they can breathe better, and it naturally contains dissolved nutrients like nitrogen that boost plant greenness instantly.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ sũ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ koni amɛmu jogbaŋŋ. Ni niyenii mli nibii ni shwieɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ mli tamɔ nitrogen yɛ, ni baaha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow while the top leaves remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize crop lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient responsible for healthy leaf growth. The plant moves nitrogen from older lower leaves to feed newer upper growth, so adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps the whole plant stay green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa baai lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ Tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi dalɛ hee lɛ niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso muu lɛ fɛɛ ni ehi shi eŋɔli.

english: Why do older farmers advise me to plant plantains on the same field as my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa ko wo ŋaa akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni aduɔ kookoo dumɔwui heei lɛ yɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that dry out easily under intense sunlight. Plantains grow fast and provide tall, broad leaves that create protective shade, keeping the soil moist and protecting young cocoa plants during their early development.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ amɛshweremɔ shishijee mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the ground when we get too much continuous rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni wɔnáa nugbɔ babaoo ni yaa nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves the ground waterlogged for extended periods, air cannot reach the roots, which causes them to suffocate and rot underground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa amɛmuɔ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the central leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the funnel of young corn plants where new leaves grow. Applying recommended control methods early prevents them from destroying the plant's growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni baai heei jɛɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra Ebaatsi he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ fitemɔ naa.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants dropping off without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often fall off due to extreme heat or irregular watering during the flowering stage. High temperatures disrupt pollination, and drought stress causes the plant to shed flowers to save energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ fɔfɔii lɛ amli lɛ hewɔ. Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ tsiɔ pollination naa. Ni hɔmɔ he haomɔ haa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts naturally take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. Planting them restores vital soil nutrients that hungry crops like maize took away during the previous season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nibii nɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni aku sɛɛ aha shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ tee yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do I need to put tall sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tso kakadaŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce food that grows large tubers underground. Staking lifts the foliage off the damp ground into the sun, which improves sunlight exposure and prevents leaf diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii, ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la mli. Enɛ haa hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ehaa foli helai baaa.

english: What will happen to my pepper harvest if I plant the seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-pepper ni mikpaa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Planting pepper seeds too closely causes the plants to compete for light, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin, weak plants and smaller pepper fruits. Proper spacing lets air flow freely and reduces fungal infections.
ga: Kɛ́ adu pepper dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ pepper aduawai bibii baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does letting weeds grow around my crops reduce the final amount of food I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ oŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ haa naagbee niyenii ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi.

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and fertilizer. When weeds take up these resources, your crops grow more slowly and produce fewer, smaller fruits or roots.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii beni amɛyeɔ nibii nɛɛ. Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ blɛoo ni amɛbaawo shishifãi fioo ni amɛbaafee bibii.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my vegetables with dried grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Aduawai ni jwɛi loo baai ni egbi yɔɔ mli

english: Covering soil with organic mulch protects it from drying out under hot sunshine, retains moisture near root systems, suppresses weed growth, and eventually breaks down into rich organic matter.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ akagbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kwɛmɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi he ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni yɛ naagbee lɛ efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni woɔ yibii

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die when exposed to full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are tender and easily damaged by intense heat and dry winds. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains provides shelter and retains soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand direct sun.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi fiteɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa mɔ náa he ko ni ehiɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. When nitrogen is low, the plant moves what little nutrients it has from its older lower leaves to feed the growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii fioo ko pɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off due to heat stress or irregular watering. Extremely hot daytime temperatures or dry spells prevent successful pollination, causing the plant to shed its flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hewɔ. Gbi mli latsaa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi tsiɔ pollination naa. ha tsei afɔlɔ

english: Why does planting groundnuts alongside my maize make the maize stalks grow stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ midu ŋmeii yɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa lɛ mli tsei lɛ waa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that naturally pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. This enriches the surrounding soil, giving nearby maize plants extra nitrogen fertilizer to grow healthy and strong.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen gas mli kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ nii babaoo. Ha ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ nitrogen ŋmãa kroko koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Lifting yam vines on tall stakes allows the leaves to catch more sunlight for food production while keeping them off the wet ground, which prevents leaf spot fungal diseases and encourages bigger tuber growth.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ niyenii feemɔ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha ekɛ ehe akabɔ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ ahe. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ anaa, ni ehaa tsei wuji lɛ daraa.

english: Why do the roots of my crops rot after heavy rain leaves standing water on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu lɛ ehi miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like human lungs. Waterlogged soil fills up all air spaces, suffocating the roots and allowing rot-causing organisms to attack the dying plant roots.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu, tamɔ bɔ ni gbɔmɔ fɛ̃i feɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ eyi kɔɔyɔɔ hei lɛ amli obɔ. ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ tutuaa tso lɛ shishifãi ni miigboi lɛ.

english: Why am I finding small holes and sawdust-like material inside the stems of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu bibioo ko lɛ? kɛ nibii ni tamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the leaf whorl and stem to feed. Early detection and applying appropriate targeted treatments early in the morning or late evening protect the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwieɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii amli koni amɛtao niyenii. Nibii ni anaa mra Ni akɛ tsofa ni sa ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ baatsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to look thin and stunted even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer faster than your crops can absorb them. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients you apply.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe bɔ ni otsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why should I cut away the extra small shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ ahe krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: Too many shoots (suckers) compete with the main tree for food and water from the soil. Removing all but one or two strong suckers directs energy into growing a bigger stem and heavier bunches of plantains.
ga: Suckers (shoots) babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ajieɔ ŋmeii fɛɛ ja ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ tsei wuji kɛ plantains ni mli eyi obɔ.

english: How do I know that my cassava stems under the soil are ready to harvest without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is typically mature when the leaves start turning yellow and naturally fall off the stem, leaving bare stalks, and cracks begin to appear on the soil surface around the base of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei shɛɔ dalɛ he beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Eshi tsei ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko Ni ŋmeii bɔi baa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide essential shade and soil moisture, protecting the young cocoa plants until they grow strong enough to endure direct heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ebuɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Which way should I plant my cassava stem cuttings in the ground?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ madu ŋmei ni afo lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava stem cuttings must be planted with the node buds pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting them upside down makes it difficult for shoots to sprout and reduces the number of tubers the plant produces.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu kɛtee shishi lɛ, ebaaha ewa aha ŋmeii lɛ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃. ni eha ŋmeii ni tsei baanyɛ ajie lɛ ayibɔ aba shi

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ ŋmei yɛ ŋmei masɛi?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them with maize enriches the soil with free nutrients, helping your maize grow healthier while giving you an extra crop to harvest.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni akɛ abele duɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni aheee nɔ ko. Ye obua o-abele lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa anáa ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi hu ni akɛkpaa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season can be a false start followed by a long dry spell. If you plant too early, the hot sun will dry out the soil and kill the delicate newly germinated seeds before the heavy, reliable rains begin.
ga: Nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afee amale shishijee. Nɔ ni nyiɛ enɛ sɛɛ ji nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ ni efiteɔ dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, dark conditions. Trimming excess tree branches lets sunlight and air flow through the farm, drying out moisture so the fungus cannot grow.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni duŋ yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Tsei aniji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ akakwɛ̃.

english: Why are small worms eating the inside leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ?

english: These are fall armyworms, a destructive pest that hides in the central leaf whorl of young maize. Catching them early and applying approved pesticides or localized wood ash prevents them from destroying the plant's main growing point.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji fall armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa bibii ashishifãi ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo tso mli sũ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ tsu nii lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite hei titri ni tso lɛ daa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my main crops grow small and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miifee mitso titri lɛ bibioo ni ebɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds aggressively steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crops. When weeds take over, your crops are starved of essential food, which prevents them from growing tall and producing a high yield.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli lɛ waa. Kɛ jwɛi lɛ ye nɔ lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa. Enɛ haaa amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a sign that the soil is running low on nitrogen, which maize needs for green leaf growth. Adding animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer restores this vital food to the crop.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji bɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmãa akwɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ niyenii ni he hiaa nɛɛ aku sɛɛ aba ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Why should I leave fallen cocoa leaves and husks to rot on the farm floor?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ashɛrɛ kookoo baai kɛ ŋmãa ni egbee shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ashwie?

english: Leaving organic matter to rot creates natural mulch that breaks down into rich food for the soil. It retains soil moisture during dry periods and prevents weeds from popping up.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ gbɛ ni amɛfite lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ feɔ niyenii ni fa babaoo kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ, ni ehaaa jwɛi akaje kpo.

english: Why do I need to prune extra water branches off my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ nu niji krokomɛi ni jɛ cacao tso ni eda lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, called chupons, waste the tree's food and energy on useless leaf growth instead of pods. Trimming them directs all the nutrients into producing bigger, healthier cocoa pods.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons lɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ kɛtsɔ baai ni he ehiaaa ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ najiaŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ jeɔ kpo koni ekɛ kookoo tsei wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow instead of green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to grow green and strong. Adding manure or fertilizer early helps the leaves turn deep green and produce big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehe wa. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii baafata he mra Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛwo ŋmɔji wuji.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the tall trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei kakadaji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn under full sunlight. Leaving some large trees or planting fast-growing plantains provides shade and keeps the soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei wuji ni oooshi loo plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava produce big bushy leaves but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai wuji lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or foliage food, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing tall stems and leaves instead of storing food in the ground. Managing soil nutrients helps energy go into swelling the tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen loo foliar nutrients babaoo lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei kɛ baai ni kɛlɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ mli Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ haa hewalɛ haa bulbs lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants before any tomatoes form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ tomato tsei anɔ dani tomato baa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets extremely hot, when the soil dries out too much, or when tiny pests attack the stems. Keeping the soil evenly watered and checking for pests helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tutua tsei lɛ, kɛ́ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu daa ni okwɛ kɛji kooloi yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why do I need to put stakes up for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei awo mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ koni ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to catch direct sunlight to feed the tuber growing under the ground. Raising the vines on wooden stakes spreads the leaves out to catch light and keeps them off the hot, dirty soil.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni eye ebua ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Wein tsei ni aduɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ gbɛɔ amɛbaa lɛ mli koni la abote mli ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ akafee hulutsoo kɛ muji.

english: Why should I cut down extra shoots growing at the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Every new shoot or sucker steals water and plant food from the main plant. Leaving only one or two healthy suckers allows the main plant to produce a big, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso hee fɛɛ tso hee loo tso lɛ shishi lɛ juɔ nu kɛ tso lɛ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo tso wuji babaoo ni tsii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and stopping growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or aphids feeding under the leaves. Spraying early with appropriate pest remedies stops the insects and allows clean, flat leaves to grow back.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra ni sa Ehaa kooloi lɛ kpaa ni ehaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni he tse lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops wilt even when I water them in the middle of a hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ miiho eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Watering under hot midday sun causes water to evaporate rapidly before roots can drink it, and hot wet soil can stress the roots. Watering early in the morning or late in the evening gives roots time to absorb water safely.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ shishi lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya dani shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Ni shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ. Nu ni afɔɔ amɛ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛnuɔ nu lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does lowland rice grow better when there is shallow standing water in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kplanaa nɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants can grow with their roots submerged, but most wild weeds cannot survive underwater. Keeping shallow water in the field smothers competing weeds naturally while giving rice the constant moisture it loves.
ga: Omɔ tsei baanyɛ ada kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ebote nu mli. Shi koo mli jwɛi babaoo nyɛɛɛ ahi shi yɛ nu shishi. Nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni abaakwɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ baaye abua ni ejie jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ kɛjɛ adebɔɔ naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa ni esumɔɔ lɛ mli nu be fɛɛ be.

english: Why does maize grow better on a piece of land where I previously planted groundnuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu ŋmãa nɔ tsutsu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans take nitrogen gas from the air and leave it in the soil through their roots. When you harvest groundnuts, that trapped food stays in the soil and feeds the next crop like maize.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛjieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji okpa ŋmei Niyenii ni ekã lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ, tamɔ ŋmei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning dark and rotting right on the tree before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miifee duŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, locally known as 'Anonom'. It is a fungal infection that attacks cocoa pods, turning them black and completely destroying the beans inside if left untreated.
ga: Black pod hela, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ “anonom” lɛ kɛbaa. Eji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni tutuaa kookoo tsei. Ha kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ afee ediŋŋ. ni efiteɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛji akɛ atsaaa amɛ.

english: What is this 'Anonom' disease that other farmers keep talking about in our community?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘Anonom’ hela ni okwaafoi krokomɛi wieɔ he yɛ wɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Anonom' is the local name for Black Pod disease. It is a severe fungal sickness that infects cocoa trees, causing the pods to rot, turn black, and fail to mature.
ga: Anonom’ ji maŋ lɛ mli gbɛi ni akɛtsɛɔ black pod hela lɛ. Eji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni naa wa ni yeɔ kookoo tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji pods lɛ ni fiteɔ. etsɔ ediŋŋ ni edaaa kwraa

english: Why do extension officers always advise me to spray my cocoa trees even before I see sick pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ mikɛ tsofa afɔ cacao tsei lɛ anɔ dani mana ŋmeii ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ po lɛ?

english: Spraying acts as a preventive shield. The fungus that causes Black Pod disease ('Anonom') is invisible and spreads fast during wet weather, so spraying early keeps the fungus from attacking healthy pods.
ga: Spray lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he. Anaaa tsɛŋemɔ hela ni kɛ black pod hela (‘anonom’) baa lɛ, ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ mra Enɛ baatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni ekatutua ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: What does spraying chemicals on my cocoa trees actually do to protect the pods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ buɔ cacao ŋmeii lɛ ahe diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Approved fungicide sprays kill the fungal spores of 'Anonom' on contact and create a protective coating over the pods so new disease spores cannot penetrate and rot the cocoa.
ga: Tsofa ni gbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ gbeɔ 'anonom' tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛji akɛ eshɛ he. ni efeɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he yɛ tsɔne lɛ nɔ Enɛ ji koni helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai heei akabote mli ni amɛha kookoo lɛ mli agbo.

english: How often do I need to spray my cocoa farm to keep 'Anonom' disease away?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ awo kookoo ŋmɔji amli tsofa koni akɛtsi ‘Anonom’ hela lɛ naa?

english: To protect against 'Anonom', cocoa farms should be sprayed regularly throughout the rainy season, usually every 3 to 4 weeks, to maintain a continuous defense as new pods grow.
ga: Bɔni afee ni akatsi ‘Anonom’ naa lɛ, esa akɛ afɔse kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ tsofa daa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ, bei pii lɛ daa otsii 3 kɛyashi 4, koni akɛbu he ni yaa nɔ be mli ni ŋmeii heei baa lɛ.

english: Why does Black Pod disease seem to trouble my cocoa farm every single year around the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ black pod hela lɛ kɛ naagbai baa mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: The fungus responsible for 'Anonom' loves moisture and cool, humid air. Raindrops splash the fungal spores from the soil and old plant material onto healthy pods year after year.
ga: Fuji ni kɛ ‘Anonom’ baa lɛ sumɔɔ hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ tsei momo amli lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ afi fɛɛ afi.

english: I noticed a small dark spot on one of my cocoa pods that spread until it covered the whole pod. How does that happen?
ga: Miyɔse he ko diŋ bibioo ko. Yɛ mi kookoo ŋmɔji ni gbɛ eshwa ni eha ŋmɔ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ Te fee tɛŋŋ ni eba lɛ?

english: That is the typical behavior of 'Anonom' (Black Pod disease). Once the fungus lands on a pod, it multiplies quickly, completely circling the pod's outer shell until the entire pod rots.
ga: No ji subaŋ ni sa kɛha ‘Anonom’ (pod diŋ hela) beni ŋmei lɛ shwieɔ pods lɛ anɔ lɛ. Ebaalɛɛ oya. Ebaabɔle ŋmei lɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ he kɛyashi ŋmei muu lɛ fɛɛ baagbo.

english: Can 'Anonom' disease attack tiny young cocoa pods, or does it only affect full-grown pods?
ga: Ani ‘Anonom’ hela lɛ baanyɛ atutua kookoo tsei bibii? Aloo yibii ni edara pɛ baaba?

english: Black Pod disease attacks pods at all stages of growth—from small young pods (cherelles) to fully mature pods. Protecting all pods with spraying is necessary to prevent yield loss.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ tutuaa pods lɛ yɛ amɛdalɛ fãi fɛɛ amli. Kɛjɛ gbekɛbii bibii (cherelles) kɛyashi ŋmeii ni eda kwraa lɛ anɔ. Ehe miihia ni abu pods fɛɛ ahe kɛtsɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ koni yibiiwoo lɛ akafite.

english: What will happen to my cocoa harvest if I decide not to spray for Black Pod disease this season?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cocoa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mikpɛ miyiŋ akɛ mikɛ black pod hela lɛ shwieŋ nɔ yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Anonom' is very destructive. If you do not spray to protect your crop, the disease can spread across your farm and ruin up to most of your cocoa pods, leading to a massive loss in yield and income.
ga: Anonom’ lɛ yeɔ mɔ awui waa kɛji okɛ tsofa shwieee nɔ koni okɛbu onibii ahe. Hela lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ ni efite kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ babaoo. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa kɛ shika ni anáa lɛ fiteɔ babaoo.

english: What should I do with cocoa pods on my farm that already have 'Anonom' spots on them?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ cocoa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni yɔɔ ‘anonom’ ŋmeii momo lɛ?

english: You should pick off the infected pods immediately and bury or destroy them away from your farm. Leaving black pods on the tree allows the 'Anonom' fungus to spread to healthy pods nearby.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ofu loo okpãtã amɛhiɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ oŋmɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii diji yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ‘Anonom’ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: How do I know the best time to plant my maize when the rainy season starts in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Wait until the major rains have fully settled—usually after two or three heavy downpours that thoroughly soak the soil—so your seeds do not sprout and then dry up during an early dry spell.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔshiimɔi wuji lɛ aba shi kwraa—bei pii lɛ, yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo nu lɛ sɛɛ—koni odumɔwui lɛ akakwɛ̃ ni amɛkagbi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under the scorching sun. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and giving the young cocoa the shade it needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa kookoo bibii lɛ náa hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak if I plant seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Plants are like people sharing a single plate of food; if they are packed too tightly, they fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, leaving all of them weak.
ga: Tsei tamɔ gbɔmɛi ni yeɔ niyenii kome. Kɛji eyi obɔ lɛ, ebaatswa akaŋ kɛha nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, amɛ fɛɛ amɛgbɔjɔ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans on the same land where I just harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmãa yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of nutrients from the ground, but crops like groundnuts and beans take natural food from the air and put it back into the soil, restoring its strength for the next season.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, shi ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ŋɔɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ

english: Why is it important to clear weeds when my crops are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops are delicate and cannot outgrow tough weeds. Clearing weeds early ensures your crop gets all the water, sunlight, and soil food instead of losing them to wild plants.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye jwɛi ni mli wa lɛ anɔ kunim. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafite amɛ amɛha koo mli tsei

english: Why should I spread dried grass or cocoa husks on the soil around my vegetable crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ashwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dried plant materials acts like a blanket that traps moisture in the ground, keeps the soil cool under hot weather, and stops heavy rain from washing your good topsoil away.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ tsei ni egbi woɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket, ni emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi. ni etsĩ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to put wooden poles in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need sunlight to produce energy that grows large tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines high up into the light and keeps the leaves off wet soil where diseases spread easily.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛná hewalɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa la lɛ mli, ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ, he ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Curling yellow leaves are usually a sign of cassava mosaic disease, spread by tiny white insects. It prevents the leaves from capturing sunlight properly, which stops the cassava roots from growing big.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Akɛni kooloi bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ amɛshwãa hewɔ lɛ, amɛtsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ akadara.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from very hot, dry weather or a lack of water. Keeping the soil moist and well-fed helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji shihilɛi ni mli edɔ, ni egbi loo nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni ehi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔii ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: What is the best time of day for me to water my vegetable garden?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ aduawai abɔɔ mli nu?

english: Water your garden early in the morning or late in the evening when the sun is low. Watering during the hot afternoon causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before the plant roots can drink it.
ga: Okɛ nu awo obɔŋ lɛ mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and looking wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like mites, thrips, or aphids feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early prevents damage to your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ mites, thrips, loo aphids ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ni amɛnuɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni akafite okpamɔ lɛ.

english: Why are there holes in my young maize leaves with small green droppings inside the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This is a key sign of a Fall Armyworm attack. The caterpillars hide deep inside the central leaf whorl to feed on tender growing leaves, which can severely damage the plant if not treated early.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi titri ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm tutuamɔ eba. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe teeɔ baai lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ koni amɛye baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ afite tso lɛ waa kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ mra.

english: Why do insects attack my cowpea crop heavily as soon as the flowers open?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-cowpea tsei lɛ waa beni amɛwo fɔfɔi sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers produce sweet nectar that attracts pests like flower thrips and pod borers. Inspecting the field when flowering begins and managing these pests protects the flowers so they can turn into healthy pods.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔii lɛ woɔ nu ni gbalaa kooloi tamɔ fɔfɔi thrips kɛ pod borers. Kɛ́ okwɛ he ni fɔfɔi lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ, ni okwɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellowing starting from the bottom leaves indicates a nitrogen deficiency. Nitrogen moves to young growth first, so the older lower leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks enough nutrients from the soil.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. Nitrogen lɛ yaa tsei bibii ni miida lɛ anɔ klɛŋklɛŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and dry at the edges during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate roots and thin leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight and strong Harmattan winds. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects young cocoa until it is strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe waɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits in heavy soil, it starves roots of oxygen and promotes fungus growth, causing root rot. Planting on ridges helps drain surplus water.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ aya hiɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture fluctuates drastically. Keeping the moisture steady with regular watering and mulching helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ waa. Kɛ́ ahiɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be mli kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when strong winds blow before the fruit is ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ dani eyibii lɛ kwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can become weak if attacked by nematodes or stem borers. As the fruit heavy-bunch grows, the top becomes top-heavy, so propping the stem with strong wooden poles prevents wind damage.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfee nɔ ni yɔɔ oshara kɛji akɛ nematodes loo stem borers tutua amɛ. Kɛ aduawai lɛ je kpo yɛ kuu agbo mli lɛ Yiteŋ lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii yɛ yiteŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa fĩ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ akafite tso lɛ.

english: Why do my stored yam tubers start sprouting in the barn even when I want to save them for later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji miisumɔ ni mikɛto kɛha sɛɛ mli po.

english: Yam tubers naturally break dormancy after a few months of rest, especially when temperatures rise inside the barn. Keeping your yam barn shaded, cool, and well-ventilated delays sprouting and keeps tubers fresh longer.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ wɔɔhe yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni amɛkɛjɔɔ amɛhe lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ ato he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hu boteɔ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ blɛoo ni eye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains get full of small insects and powder after just two months in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli eyi kɛ kooloi bibii kɛ sũ lɛ? Yɛ nyɔji enyɔ pɛ ni akɛto lɛ sɛɛ

english: This destruction is caused by grain weevils that lay eggs inside dry maize. If the grain was not dried completely before storage or if the storage space was not cleaned and sealed, weevils multiply rapidly.
ga: Dumɔwui amli ŋmeii ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni egbi mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ hiɛkpatamɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛto loo kɛji akɛ atsumɔko he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ ni atsĩii naa. Moo lɛ baagbɛ eshwa oya.

english: Is it good for me to plant plantains on the same land where I am growing young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ kookoo tsei bibii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, it is very good. Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct heat from the hot sun. Plantains grow quickly and provide wide leaves that shade the young cocoa plants while also giving you food and income while you wait for the cocoa to mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehi waa. Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I clear all the tall trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei kakadaji fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are delicate and burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. They need temporary shade from crops like plantain or cassava during their first two years to keep the soil moist and the surrounding air cool.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi lɛ oya. Amɛbiɔ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains loo cassava mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli. Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How much distance should I leave between plantain stems when planting them alongside young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo plantain tsei lɛ ahe gbɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe?

english: You should space your plantains about 3 meters apart. This provides enough filtered sunlight and air movement for the cocoa trees underneath without overcrowding them or blocking out light completely.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ plantains lɛ ato he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 3, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ hulu la lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa tsɔɔ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. ni ehaaa kookoo tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ loo etsĩii kane lɛ fɛɛ naa.

english: Can I plant onions in the middle of my cocoa and plantain farm, or will the shade stop them from growing?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu sabala yɛ mi-kookoo kɛ plantain ŋmɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ? Aloo ani shade baanyɛ akpa dalɛ?

english: You can grow onions alongside young cocoa and plantains, but onions need plenty of direct sunlight to form big bulbs. They grow best in open areas of the farm before the plantain and cocoa foliage grows thick enough to cast heavy shade.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu sabolai yɛ kookoo bibii kɛ plantains ahe. Shi ehe miihia ni sabolai lɛ aná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee bulbs agboi. Amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli hei ni yɔɔ faŋŋ lɛ dani dumɔwui kɛ kookoo baai lɛ shwereɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛhaa hulutsoo.

english: If I plant vegetables like onions near my plantain trees, won't the plantains steal all the water and fertilizer?
ga: Kɛji midu aduawai tamɔ ŋmei yɛ plantain lɛ masɛi. Ani plantains lɛ ejuŋ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow, wide roots that take up a lot of nutrients. To prevent competition, plant your vegetables a few feet away from the base of the plantain trees and give extra compost or fertilizer directly to the vegetable beds.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo. koni akaŋshii akafee Dumɔ aduawai 2-3 feet kɛjɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashishi ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he tɛ̃ɛ yɛ aduawai lɛ ashishi.

english: Will mixing vegetables with cocoa and plantain trees cause pests to spread from one crop to the other?
ga: Ani kɛ́ akɛ aduawai futu kookoo kɛ plantains mli lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai agbɛ ashwã tso kome nɔ kɛya ekroko nɔ?

english: Usually, no. Most insects and diseases that attack vegetables do not attack cocoa or plantains. In fact, planting different types of crops together can confuse pests and make it harder for them to destroy your entire field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ebɛ Koolooi kɛ helai babaoo ni tutuaa aduawai lɛ tutuaaa kookoo loo plantains. Kɛ amɛfee ekome lɛ, amɛbaanyɛ amɛfutu kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ, ni eha ewa aha amɛ akɛ amɛbaafite he ni oyɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Since cocoa trees take a few years to produce, what crops can I plant to make quick money in the meantime?
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kookoo tsei heɔ afii fioo komɛi dani amɛwoɔ yibii. Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu koni maná shika oya yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: You can plant fast-growing food crops like plantains, cassava, and vegetables like onions or peppers in the spaces between young cocoa trees. These allow you to harvest food and earn income within a few months while waiting for the cocoa to bear fruit.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu niyenii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains, cassava, kɛ aduawai tamɔ sabolai loo ŋmɔtɔ. kɛtee he ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ Enɛɛmɛi haa onyɛɔ okpaa niyenii ni onáa shika yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli be mli ni omɛɛɔ kookoo lɛ ni ewo yibii lɛ.

english: Does planting plantains and vegetables on my cocoa farm help reduce the amount of weeding I have to do?
ga: Ani dumɔwui kɛ aduawai ni miduɔ yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ baa shi?

english: Yes. Covering the soil with food crops and plantain leaves blocks sunlight from reaching the ground, which prevents weeds from growing as quickly and saves you time and labor.
ga: Hɛɛ. Niyenii tsei kɛ plantain baai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baatsi hulu la naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa oya, ni ebaaha okɛ obei kɛ ohewalɛ akafite.

english: When is the best time for me to plant plantains on my farm to ensure they grow well?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni makwɛ akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: The best time to plant plantains is at the beginning of the major rainy season. This allows the roots to establish strongly while the soil is naturally wet before the dry season begins.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ waa yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ewo nu yɛ adebɔɔ naa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: What kind of soil do onions need if I want to get a good harvest on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɛkɛ sabala he hiaa kɛji miisumɔ ni maná ŋmaa kpakpa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Onions grow best in loose, rich, well-drained soil that does not hold excess water. Creating raised beds helps keep the soil loose and prevents the onion bulbs from rotting in wet conditions.
ga: Sabolai kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse, ni baa nii, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nu babaoo nyɛɛɛ ahi mli lɛ nɔ. Saji ni awó nɔ ni afee lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ afite yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to grow green leaves and make energy. When fertilizer is scarce or expensive, adding animal manure or compost can restore that rich green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli ni amɛfee hewalɛ. Be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii anamɔ wa loo ejara wa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee diŋŋ.

english: Can my crops still grow well if I am unable to buy chemical fertilizer this season?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lolo kɛji minyɛɛɛ mahe tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Yes, crops can still produce good yields without chemical fertilizers if you feed the soil using organic manure, compost, or by growing nitrogen-fixing crops like cowpeas and peanuts, which naturally enrich the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei baanyɛ awo yibii kpakpai lolo kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuuu nii. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo tsei ni haa nitrogen hiɔ shi tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts, ni kɛ adebɔɔ mli sɛɛnamɔ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves get scorched and turn brown during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are very sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains or shade trees beside them keeps the soil moist and creates a canopy that protects the cocoa leaves from burning.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Shade tsei tamɔ dumɔwui loo shade tsei ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔ ni tsiɔ kookoo baai anaa koni ekashã.

english: Why are the leaves on my plantain trees curling and drooping during the hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves curl and fold downwards during high heat to prevent water from evaporating too quickly from their broad leaves. It is the plant's natural way of saving water during dry conditions.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfoɔ amɛhe yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni nu akajɛ baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli oya tsɔ. Eji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off before producing any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani pepper yibii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or irregular watering. Covering the soil with mulch keeps the roots cool and helps the plant hold onto its flowers until they turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ latsaa mli haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Mulching haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why is my cassava producing huge stems and many green leaves, but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ tso agbo kɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: When cassava gets too much water or excess nitrogen, it puts all its energy into growing tall stems and thick leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei nine shɛ nu babaoo loo nitrogen babaoo nɔ Enɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baawo ŋmei lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli ni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I plant many seeds close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ebɛ hewalɛ beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the young plants end up fighting each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, causing all of them to grow tall, weak, and produce small yields.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei bibii lɛ baawu amɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni kɛlɛ, ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi baa.

english: Why do my tomato plants get sickly and produce less if I plant tomatoes in the same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ hela mɔ amɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Diseases and pests that target tomatoes stay hidden in the soil after harvest. Planting tomatoes in the same spot repeatedly allows those diseases to build up, so rotating tomatoes with crops like maize or cassava cleans the soil naturally.
ga: Akɛ helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ tomato nɔ lɛ teeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Tomato ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ lɛ Ebaanyɛ ekɛ hela aba No hewɔ lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake tomato. Ebaaye ebua ni etsumɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into the very center of my green maize stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-abele tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars, known as Fall Armyworms, hide deep inside the tender center whorl of the maize plant where the freshest leaves are. Checking your farm early and using neem leaf extract or recommended sprays can stop them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ni ale amɛ akɛ Fall Armyworms lɛ teɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ ateŋ ŋtayaai amli shɔŋŋ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mli kwɛmɔ mra Ni kɛ neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekpa ŋmɔ lɛ dani efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting or sprouting prematurely when I keep them inside my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ loo ekwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛto mitsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are alive and need cool air to stay dormant. Storing them in a warm, closed room traps heat and moisture, which causes the yams to rot or tricks them into thinking it is time to sprout again.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni amɛmiitao kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ koni amɛwɔ. Kɛ́ okɛto tsu ko ni atsĩ naa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaamɔ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i. Enɛ haa sweet potato lɛ fiteɔ loo elakaa lɛ ni esusuɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni ekɛ heei baakwɛ̃.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow root systems that burn under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains beside them creates a canopy that shields the young cocoa from heat and retains moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ lateral plantains lɛ adumɔ. Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually means your soil lacks nitrogen, an essential food for maize. The plant steals nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new top growth, so adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will fix this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmãa Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋmãa heei ni yaa hiɛ lɛ niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why is it helpful for me to plant beans or groundnuts in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When planted with maize, they naturally feed the soil and boost maize growth while giving you an extra crop to harvest.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ adu ŋmãa Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛhaa ŋmãa dalɛ yaa hiɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni obaakpa.

english: Which way should the buds point when I am pushing cassava stem cuttings into the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ nɔ atsɔɔ kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei nine lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: The small leaf nodes or buds along the stem cutting must point upward toward the sky. If you plant the stem upside down, the green shoots struggle to reach the surface, resulting in weak growth and small cassava tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ baai bibii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ he lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu tso lɛ shishi lɛ, Green shoots lɛ baaná naagba ni ekɛshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmei shishifãi bibii baa.

english: Why do I need to clear tall bushes and set up wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni mikɛ tsei ama shi koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to capture as much sunlight as possible to produce energy for heavy tuber growth. Lifting the vines off the ground on tall stakes keeps the leaves healthy, exposes them to sunshine, and yields bigger yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato baai lɛ amɔmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ adalɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso kakadaŋŋ wo wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ yibii ni mli wa, hulu la ni baashɛ enɔ, kɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji lɛ aba.

english: Why am I finding small holes in my young maize leaves with sawdust-like dirt in the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu bibioo ko lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii ni yɔɔ muji tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides deep inside the leaf funnel and eats the growing shoots. Spraying recommended botanical or chemical treatments early in the morning or late evening helps protect your crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground when heavy rains flood my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi ŋmɔji lɛ amli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air inside the soil to breathe. When water sits on the field for too long, oxygen cannot reach the roots, causing them to drown and rot; planting your cassava on high ridges or mounds prevents waterlogging.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni haa efoɔ nu mli ni egboɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why do my maize seeds rot in the ground when I plant right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ afi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by intense heat and hot dry soil, which bakes the seeds before they can establish roots. It is safer to wait until the rains become steady and consistent before sowing your seeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli egbi waa nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gbiɔ dani amɛ nyɛɔ amɛ kwɛ̃ɔ shishifãi. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa, ni ehi shi daa dani odu dumɔwui.
