english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their yellow flowers without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures get extremely high or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet. Giving your plants consistent moisture and mulching the soil keeps them cool enough to set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ mli fũu be fɛɛ be ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa edɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the bottoms of my pepper fruits turning soft and black before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper lɛ shishi feɔ blɛoo ni eyɛ ediŋŋ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit due to irregular watering. Watering your peppers on a regular schedule helps the roots draw up the calcium needed for strong fruit walls.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ, ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-peppers lɛ nɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛheɔ calcium ni he hiaa amɛ kɛha aduawai gbogboi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: If I clear unused land that has been sitting idle for years, why do my young maize leaves turn yellow?
ga: Kɛji mijie shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuuu nii ni akɛtsuuu nii afii babaoo lɛ. Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Unused land covered in wild grass often lacks quick-release nitrogen in the soil. When cleared, the soil microbes breaking down old grass temporarily use up the available nitrogen, leaving young maize plants yellow until organic manure or fertilizer is added.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuuu nii ni koo mli jwɛi ehà nɔ lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni ajieɔ lɛ oya kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji ajie Shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii bibii ni gbeɔ jwɛi momo lɛ kɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ be kukuoo mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Shi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ kɛyashi obaakɛ humus loo ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ afata he.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crops whenever I open up a new piece of farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be fɛɛ be ni magbele ŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ?

english: Weed seeds can lie dormant in idle soil for years. Clearing the vegetation brings those hidden seeds to the surface where direct sunlight and rainfall cause them to germinate much faster than your planted crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ awɔ. yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ afii babaoo Aduawai ni ooofɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛkwɛ̃ oya kwraa fe dumɔwui ni oduɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge green leafy bushes above ground but small tubers under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ yɛ jwɛi agboi ni baai eŋɔli yɔɔ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or green material relative to other nutrients, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing leaves instead of storing energy underground in large root tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen loo nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli babaoo kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Cassava tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa ebaai ni miida lɛ amli. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ he wami ɔ ngɛ zugba sisi ngɛ sisifãhi agbohi a mi.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with tiny corn ears if I plant several seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tso lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni eyɛ ŋmãa toi bibii kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too closely causes the young plants to compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition makes the stalks grow thin and weak instead of strong and fruit-bearing.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei bibii lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee hewalɛ ni ewo yibii

english: Why do the vines on my yam plants need tall sticks to climb on instead of just trailing along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wain tso ni yɔɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ niji kakadaji ni esa akɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves up in the air to catch sunlight for food production. Keeping the leaves off the damp ground also protects the plant from diseases and helps it build larger tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛná hulu la lɛ bɔni afee ni amɛná niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ helai ahe. ni eye ebua ni afee yitso ni da hu

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings scorch and die when I plant them in an open field without plantains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni plantains bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive direct tropical sunlight and strong winds. Fast-growing plants like plantains provide necessary shade and cool humidity to protect cocoa seedlings during their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa koni akɛbu kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why does planting cowpeas on my land make the next season's cereal crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil. When the cowpea plant dies, it leaves that free plant food behind for heavy-feeding crops like maize or millet.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji cowpea tso lɛ gbo Eshiɔ tso niyenii kɛha niyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: Why do the flowers fall off my pepper plants without turning into actual peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee pepper diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience stress, such as extended hot spells without water, sudden heavy rains, or a lack of essential soil nutrients needed to support fruit development.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni nu bɛ mli. nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa loo niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha aduawai lɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli

english: Why do the lower leaves of my tomato plants turn dark and rot during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall splashes fungal spores from the bare soil onto the lower leaves of tomato plants. Placing dry grass mulch around the base prevents soil from splashing up and protects the leaves from disease.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Mulch ni egbi ni ebɔle shishi lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ akashwie shi ni ebu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ helai ahe.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops every year if I plant maize on the exact same spot without resting it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year while allowing specific soil pests to build up. Resting the land or changing crops gives the soil time to recover.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi komɛi buaa amɛhe naa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hejɔɔmɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa be ni ekɛsaa ehe.

english: Why do my harvested vegetables turn soft and spoil so quickly after I pick them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai ni mikpa lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya beni mikpa amɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When produce contains too much moisture, it creates an easy environment for rot and bacteria. Vegetables with lower internal water content stay firm and fresh much longer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo Ehaa shihilɛ ko ni fiteɔ oya kɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ baa. Aduawai ni nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ faaa lɛ baahi shi shiŋŋ ni efee ehee be babaoo.

english: Do I need a refrigerator to keep my harvested crops fresh for a long time?
ga: Ani friji he miihia mi koni mikpamɔ lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ?

english: No, you do not always need a fridge. If your produce has low moisture, placing it in a dry, cool room at regular house temperature will keep it fresh for weeks without softening.
ga: Dabi, jeee be fɛɛ be friji he hiaa bo. Kɛji akɛ o-fruits kɛ vegetables lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ faaa Kɛ́ okɛwo tsu ko ni mli ejɔ ni mli egbi mli yɛ shia lɛ mli fɛ̃i ni sa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛhi shi otsii babaoo ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ.

english: What is the best place in my house to store my harvested vegetables so they last?
ga: Mɛni ji he ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ mishia ni abaanyɛ akɛ aduawai ni akpa lɛ ato koni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Store them in a dedicated dry room where there is plenty of space and shade. Keeping them away from excessive heat and direct moisture prevents them from decaying fast.
ga: Okɛto tsu ko ni egbi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni he ko kɛ hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ tee he ko ni hulutsoo ni fa fe nine kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ bɛ lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite oya.

english: How long can I expect my produce to stay fresh if I keep it in my kitchen at room temperature?
ga: Be enyiɛ manyɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ minibii lɛ baahi shi ehee? Kɛji akɛ mikɛto shĩa mli latsaa mli

english: Certain crops with controlled water content, especially those grown under cover, can stay completely fresh on a kitchen counter or room for up to three weeks without spoiling.
ga: Tsei komɛi ni nu falɛ ni akudɔɔ yɔɔ mli Titri lɛ tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Ebaanyɛ ehi shi ehee pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ loo yɛ tsu lɛ mli kɛyashi otsii etɛ ni efiteee.

english: How can I prevent my stored crops from losing their firm texture and becoming watery?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛto lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee nɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni nu yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Keep them in a cool, well-ventilated indoor space instead of placing them in humid areas or cold refrigerators, which can alter their texture and cause them to soften.
ga: Okɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli yɛ shia mli. Moŋ lɛ, okɛwo he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ loo friji ni mli ejɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ atsake bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ ni eha efee blɛoo.

english: Why do crops harvested from a greenhouse stay fresh longer than crops grown in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ fe tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Greenhouse crops grow under controlled watering, so they do not absorb extra moisture. Less moisture inside the crop means it resists rot and stays fresh far longer after harvest.
ga: Greenhouse tsei lɛ daa yɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni akudɔ lɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieee shi. Fɛ̃i ni faaa yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ eteɔ shi ewoɔ fitemɔ ni ehiɔ shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Should I treat and store my open-field crops differently from crops grown under cover?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni agbele naa lɛ atsu nii ni mikɛto yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ?

english: Yes, crops grown outside in open fields absorb unpredictable rain and weather heat, making them spoil faster, so they require different handling than indoor or greenhouse produce.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni adu yɛ kpo nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ gbalaa nugbɔ kɛ dɔlɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛgboiɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛbiɔ ni akwɛ amɛ nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe nibii ni akɛwoɔ shĩa mli loo nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my outdoor crops seem to decay faster when I leave them at room temperature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mi-kpo nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ mishi amɛ yɛ shĩa mli latsaa mli lɛ?

english: Outdoor crops are exposed to rain and humidity, giving them higher internal water levels that make them go soft quickly when left out.
ga: Nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo be baa ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ kpo nɔ lɛ anɔ. ni haa nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ oya kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it true that greenhouse vegetables can be stored without electricity or cold storage?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ abaanyɛ akɛ aduawai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ato ni sarawa hewalɛ loo he ko ni fɛ̃i bɛ mli?

english: Yes, because greenhouse vegetables have balanced internal moisture, they do not require electric cold storage or fridges to stay fresh for extended periods.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ greenhouse lɛ yɛ mligbɛ fɛ̃i ni sa. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsu ni mli ejɔ loo friji ni akɛ srawa hewalɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ atsu nii koni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How does water content inside a crop affect its shelf life after harvest?
ga: Te nu ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ saa bɔ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: High water content makes harvested crops break down and go soft quickly, while low water content keeps the crop structured, firm, and long-lasting.
ga: Nu ni fa babaoo lɛ haa tsei ni akpa lɛ shwieɔ shi oya ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni faaa lɛ baaha tso lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ, ni ehi shi shiŋŋ, ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants roll up tightly like tubes during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up during hot afternoons to protect themselves from losing too much water. It is the plant's natural defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to the hot sun when moisture is low.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ he. Eji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ekɛbaa hulu la ni shɛɔ enɔ lɛ shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ faaa.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with plenty of green leaves, but the tubers under the soil turn out very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or is planted in very rich soil without enough potassium, it spends all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in the roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ aha ŋmei nitrogen ŋmei babaoo loo adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Ekɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛkwɛ baai kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ

english: Why are the small flowers on my cocoa trees falling off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ cacao ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often drop if the tree is stressed by too much direct sunlight, lack of moisture, or during dry Harmattan winds. It can also happen if there are not enough tiny midges (pollinating insects) around to fertilize the blossoms.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee shi kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shɛ tso lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Fɛ̃i ni bɛ loo yɛ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ mli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ aŋkroaŋkroi bibii (pollinators) ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ aná fɔ lɛ bɛ.

english: Why does my plantain tree produce so many suckers around its base, and should I leave all of them to grow together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ ŋmeii babaoo ebɔle shishi lɛ he lɛ, ni ani esa akɛ maha amɛ fɛɛ amɛdara yɛ he kome?

english: Plantain plants produce suckers to multiply, but leaving all of them creates heavy competition for food and water. You should remove most of them and keep only one or two so the main plant can produce a big, heavy bunch.
ga: Plantain tsei woɔ ŋmeii kɛha shweremɔ. Shi amɛ fɛɛ ni ashiɔ lɛ kɛ akaŋshii ni naa wa baa niyenii kɛ nu he. Esa akɛ ojie emli babaoo ni okɛ tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi bɔni afee ni tso titri lɛ anyɛ awo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my ripening tomatoes turning black and soft before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni egbɔ lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the tomato plant cannot absorb enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering where the soil gets very dry and then suddenly very wet.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni eeeha egbi waa ni efee ŋmɔtɔ waa trukaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sun exposure to make food for the tubers underneath. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, giving them maximum sunlight while preventing fungal diseases caused by wet soil.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ mɔ nɔ babaoo yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ hu he.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips, aphids, or mites sucking sap from under the leaves, or by a virus carried by whiteflies that disrupts normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ anɔ. ni tsiɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ naa.

english: Why do people say planting cowpea or beans makes the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni adu lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with friendly soil bacteria to capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant leaves and roots decay in the farm, this stored nitrogen feeds the next crop naturally.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni ji naanyobɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Beni tsei ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi fiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli Nitrogen ni ato nɛɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow starting from the leaf tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts at the tip of older leaves and moves down the center is a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency. The plant is moving its limited nitrogen up to support new leaves at the top, leaving the bottom leaves to starve.
ga: Yellowing ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ anaagbɛ ni eyaa shi kɛyaa teŋgbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni ale waa ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Tso lɛ miitsi e-nitrogen fioo lɛ kɛmiiya ŋwɛi koni ekɛfi baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ asɛɛ. Ha shishigbɛ baai lɛ aye hɔmɔ.

english: Why do my small watermelons turn yellow and rot off when they are just the size of an egg?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ watermelon lɛ ji bibii nɛkɛ? Minɔ lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbo eyɛ mli akɛ Eyɛ ŋmɔŋ dalɛ mli moŋ?

english: Young watermelons usually turn yellow and die because they were not properly pollinated by bees, or because the young fruit sat directly on overly wet soil, allowing fungal organisms to enter and rot the fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, watermelon bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ ejaakɛ ŋmeii lɛ ekɛ amɛhe wooo mli jogbaŋŋ. aloo akɛni aduawai bibii lɛ kpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ tsɔ lɛ hewɔ Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ boteɔ mli ni ehaa aduawai lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my farm helps my maize grow better afterwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmei lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the plants die, that nitrogen stays in the soil as natural fertilizer, feeding nitrogen-hungry crops like maize in the next planting season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. ni ekɛ niyenii aha tsei ni he hiaa nitrogen, tamɔ ŋmãa, yɛ ŋmãa be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my vegetables turn yellow and die when water stays pooled on my farmland for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nu hi he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like human beings do. Standing water fills up all the small air pockets in the soil, suffocating the roots so they can no longer take up food or water, which makes the plant turn yellow and drown.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ yiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi aahu akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii loo nu dɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nu mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die if I do not plant plantains or shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛji miduuu amɛ loo mikɛ hulutsoo haaa tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves and delicate roots that dry out and burn quickly under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving the cocoa trees the cool shade and moisture they need to survive their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo tso lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall sticks to climb on instead of just spreading across the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ moŋ fe ni eeegbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines climb high so their leaves can trap as much sunlight as possible to make food for the plant. Lifting the leaves off the ground also keeps them dry and safe from rot, allowing the plant to build bigger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ amɔmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha tso lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa amɛgbiɔ ni amɛkafiteɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants roll up tightly during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural defense to protect themselves from losing too much moisture. By shrinking the leaf area exposed to the sun and heat, the plant saves its water until the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni fiteɔ lɛ he. Tsei buɔ nu he kɛyashiɔ gbɛkɛ mli fɛ̃i kɛtsɔ amɛbaai ni hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ baa amɛnɔ lɛ ni amɛbaa shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop most of their leaves during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fiteɔ yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves in dry weather to save water. Without leaves, the plant loses very little moisture into the air and goes into a resting state, storing its energy safely inside the underground tubers until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli koni ekɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ tso lɛ baai bɛ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ fioo pɛ yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni eboteɔ hejɔɔmɔ shihilɛ mli. Ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is low on nitrogen. When nitrogen is scarce, the maize plant takes whatever nitrogen it has left from its older lower leaves and sends it up to keep the young top leaves growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji nitrogen faaa lɛ, Abɛi jieɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli ni ekɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ aya nɔ ada.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without growing any fruits when the weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii ko beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat makes tomato pollen sticky and inactive, preventing the flowers from getting fertilized. When a flower is not fertilized, the plant stops sending food to it, causing the flower to dry up and drop off.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato pollen lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsuuu nii. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ fɔ. Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔi ko ehiɛɛɛ fɔ Tsei lɛ baakpa niyenii ni amɛkɛmajeɔ amɛ lɛ. Fɔfɔi lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: Why do my green cocoa pods turn black and rot during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Black pod is caused by a tiny fungal organism that loves cold, damp, and shady conditions. During heavy rains, the fungus multiplies fast and spreads from pod to pod through splashing water droplets.
ga: Fungi bibii kɛ pods diji baa. Esumɔɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ, fɛ̃i kɛ shade yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli. Fuji lɛ fɔɔ oya ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ pod mli kɛyaa pod mli kɛtsɔɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and twisting like tiny cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids. As they feed on the sap under the leaves, they damage the tissues and can spread viruses that cause the leaves to deform and stop growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. be mli ni amɛyeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ Amɛfiteɔ fãji ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai ni fiteɔ baai lɛ amɛshwã ni amɛkpaa dalɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many flowers, but very few of them actually turn into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi fɔfɔi fioo komɛi pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects like midges to move pollen from one flower to another. If there are not enough of these beneficial insects on your farm, most flowers will simply fall off without growing into pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi he miihia kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii, koni amɛjie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛya ekroko nɔ. Kɛji akɛ oŋmɔ lɛ bɛ nɛkɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ babaoo lɛ, Fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: How do small insects on my farm help my cocoa trees give me a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Tiny insects act as natural pollinators for cocoa. As they crawl inside the flowers to feed, they transfer pollen, which fertilizes the flower and allows it to grow into a healthy cocoa pod.
ga: Kplukai bibii tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa kookoo mli ŋmeii baa. be mli ni amɛkpãa fɔfɔi amli koni amɛyatao niyenii Amɛbaaŋɔ pollen. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi ni ehaa amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ kookoo tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Are all insects on my cocoa farm bad pests that I need to kill?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ ji kooloi fɔji ni esa akɛ majie kɛjɛ mli?

english: No, many insects are helpful. While some pests damage crops, tiny midges and beneficial ants help pollinate cocoa flowers or fight off diseases. Killing all insects reduces the natural helpers your cocoa needs to produce fruit.
ga: Dabi, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ kooloi babaoo ahe. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii moŋ, Shi ŋmei bibioo ko Kɛ ŋmei ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛwoɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii loo amɛwuɔ amɛshiɔ helai. Kɛ́ ogbe kooloi bibii lɛ fɛɛ lɛ, ebaa adebɔɔ mli nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa o-cocoa lɛ koni ewo yibii lɛ shi.

english: Can spraying heavy chemical insecticides on my cocoa farm reduce my crop yield?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni tsii ni mikɛshwieɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayibii aba shi?

english: Yes, indiscriminate chemical spraying can kill off the friendly insects that pollinate your cocoa flowers. Without these pollinators, fewer flowers get fertilized, resulting in fewer pods on your trees.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ ni ajieee mɔ ko mɔ ko kpo lɛ baanyɛ agbe kooloi bibii ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo ni haa o-cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ. Kɛji nɛkɛ kooloi ni haa fɔfɔii nɛɛ bɛ lɛ, fɔfɔii fioo pɛ baafee. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ baa.

english: Why should I keep shade trees on my cocoa farm instead of cutting them all down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ mli moŋ fe ni mafo tsei lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Shade trees protect young cocoa from harsh sun and help maintain moisture in the air and soil. They also provide a natural home for beneficial insects that pollinate your cocoa flowers.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Ehaa adebɔɔ mli shia hu kɛhaa kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛhaa o-cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ.

english: Why do cocoa trees seem to produce more pods when there are rotting leaves and moist logs around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ be mli ni baai ni egboi kɛ tsei ni mli efɔ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Decomposing plant matter and damp logs create the ideal damp breeding ground for tiny pollinating midges. More midges on the farm lead to better flower pollination and higher cocoa yield.
ga: Tsei ni eshwɛ ni fiteɔ kɛ tsei ni mli efɔ lɛ feɔ he ni efɔ yɛ ni sa kɛha ŋmeii bibii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Dwarf babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ kɛ pollination ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ cocoa yibii babaoo baa.

english: How does keeping my cocoa farm humid help the crops grow better pods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mihaa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cocoa flowers and their insect pollinators both thrive in warm, moist conditions. High humidity keeps flowers fresh for longer and allows pollinating insects to remain active and healthy.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi kɛ amɛ pollinators lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa pollinators lɛ koni amɛya nɔ amɛtsu nii ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why does cocoa seem to depend on other forest plants to survive and produce well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo damɔ koo mli tsei krokomɛi anɔ koni ehi shi ni ewo yibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Cocoa originally evolved as a forest plant under bigger trees. Surrounding vegetation protects cocoa from extreme heat and creates the natural ecosystem needed for pollinating insects to live and thrive.
ga: Shishijee lɛ, kookoo bafee koo mli tso ko ni yɔɔ tsei wuji ashishi. Tsei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. ni efee adebɔɔ mli nibii ni he hiaa koni kooloi ni feɔ pollin lɛ ahi shi ni amɛshwere.

english: Why do cocoa flowers grow directly on the thick trunk and big branches rather than on the small leaf stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ tsei ni mli tse kɛ tsei niji wuji anɔ fe baai bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce flowers on the main trunk and old branches under the leaf canopy where it is shady and cool. This position makes it easier for tiny crawling and flying insects to reach and pollinate the flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ tso wulu lɛ nɔ kɛ tsei niji momo ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ anɔ, he ni amɛyɔɔ hulutsoo ni amɛhe jɔɔ lɛ. Nɛkɛ shihilɛ nɛɛ haa kooloi bibii nyɛɔ amɛfoɔ ni amɛfoɔ. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ aaaná ni aná fɔfɔii amli pollination

english: Why does hot, dry weather cause my cocoa flowers to dry up without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ haa mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni efeee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Dry weather lowers humidity, causing delicate cocoa flowers to wither quickly. It also reduces the population of tiny pollinating insects, leaving flowers unpollinated before they drop off.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa hulutsoo baa shi. Enɛ haa kookoo fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ shwieɔ oya. Ehaa kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ayibɔ hu baa shi, ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieee fɔfɔi lɛ dani amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: Can I plant cassava together with my maize on the same farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, you can plant them together because maize grows fast and is harvested early, while cassava grows slowly and takes up space only after the maize is harvested. This helps you get two crops from one piece of land.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu amɛ yɛ he kome ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya ni ekpaa mra. Shi ŋmãa lɛ, daa blɛoo ni eŋɔ he ko beni akpa ŋmãa pɛ kɛkɛ. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. Adding animal manure, compost, or urea fertilizer will help the leaves turn dark green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi a-ŋmei, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I leave old crop leaves on my field instead of burning them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mashã amɛ?

english: Burning crop leaves destroys valuable plant nutrients and dries out the land. Leaving old leaves on the soil acts like a blanket that keeps the ground moist, cool, and turns into natural fertilizer as it rots.
ga: Tso baai ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ mli niyenii ni jara wa lɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gĩɔ. releasing old leaves Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ tsɔne ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ, ni ebafeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji egbo.

english: How do I know if my land is suitable for planting cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmei ŋmɔ?

english: Cassava likes loose, sandy, or loamy soil where water drains away easily. If your land stays waterlogged like clay after rain, the cassava roots will rot under the ground instead of growing big.
ga: Cassava sumɔɔ ŋã loo ŋã he ni nu hoɔ oya yɛ lɛ. Kɛji nu eyi oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ agbo lɛ, amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: What causes the leaves of my pepper plants to curl up into small knots?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi bibii bibii?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck the juice out of young leaves and spread plant viruses. Spraying neem leaf extract or insecticidal soap can protect the plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai bibii amli ni egbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tsei amli Neem baa mli nu loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ baanyɛ abu tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off before any tomatoes grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani tomato lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or too much fertilizer. Regular watering during hot weather helps the plant hold onto its flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ hao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ, nu ni bɛ, loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu daa yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli koni ewo yibii.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are mature enough to dig up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa?

english: Most cassava is ready between 9 and 12 months after planting when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to crack open from the growing roots.
ga: Cassava tsei babaoo efee klalo akɛ amɛbaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ kɛjɛ shishifãi ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize plants fall over easily when a strong wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Maize falls over when its roots are not deep enough or when stem borer insects weaken the stalks. Heap extra soil around the base of the stems when weeding to give the plants stronger footing.
ga: Abɛi baagbee shi kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni sa. aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii wo tso lɛ shishi ni eha tso lɛ gbɔjɔ Okɛ sũ krokomɛi abɔle tso lɛ shishi beni okɛ jwɛi shwieɔ shi lɛ koni eha tso lɛ aná shishitoo ni mli wa.

english: Why should I not save seeds from hybrid maize to plant next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ hybrid corn mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially created to yield well only for their first planting. If you save seeds from that harvest to plant again, the second generation will produce uneven plants and very small cobs.
ga: Afee dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ pɛ mli. Kɛji ohere dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔɔ lɛ mli ni odu amɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ, Yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ woɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmeii bibii waa yɔɔ mli.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen. Maize needs plenty of nitrogen to stay green, so when nutrients run out, the plant pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ fite lɛ Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my vegetable crops with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, traps moisture in the ground during hot weather, keeps crop roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing and stealing plant nutrients.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkaju tsei amli niyenii.

english: Why do my crops grow faster during the rainy season compared to when I water them by hand in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛ akɛto nu ni akɛ niji shwieɔ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ he?

english: Rainwater carries natural nitrogen dissolved from the air and distributes moisture deeply and evenly across the whole field, which helps plant roots absorb food much better than manual watering.
ga: Nugbɔ nu kɛ nitrogen ni ji adebɔɔ mli nibii ni egbɛ eshwa lɛ baa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ejaraa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ fe kɛ́ akɛ niji shwie nɔ nu.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when planted in direct sun without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sun. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains nearby creates a shady canopy that protects young cocoa plants until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Nurse tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Ehaa hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden poles to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to lift their leaves high toward the sun. Supporting them with poles helps leaves catch maximum sunlight, which provides the energy needed to form large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu lɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei fiɔ esɛɛ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ náa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Enɛ ji hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi tsɔnei wuji.

english: Too many suckers compete with the main plantain tree for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Leaving only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main tree gets enough energy to bear large plantain bunches.
ga: Tsobii babaoo tsɔ kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaaye plantain dumɔwui wuji.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when water supply is irregular. Without steady moisture and moderate heat, the flower fails to set fruit and drops from the stem.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni tamɔ ekome kɛ dɔlɛ ni sa bɛ. Fɔfɔi hu nyɛŋ awo yibii ni amɛgbee shi kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and looking wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Curling leaves are usually a sign of tiny pests like thrips or mites sucking sap from the leaves, or a virus spread by insects. Treating the crop early stops pests from stunting the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii, tamɔ thrips loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nuɔ baa nu lɛ he okadi. loo helai ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa Tsei akwɛmɔ kɛjɛ amɛgbekɛbiiashi Ebaaye ebua ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akatsi tso lɛ dalɛ naa.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots spoil within two days after digging them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ fite yɛ gbii enyɔ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni atsa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots lack a protective outer skin once removed from the ground, causing rapid internal discoloration and breakdown within 48 to 72 hours when exposed to air.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ bɛ kponɔgbɛ hewolo ni buɔ amɛhe kɛji ajie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa emli su lɛ tsakeɔ oya ni efiteɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 kɛyashi 72 mli kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: How does sorting my harvested produce by size and quality help me get higher prices at the market?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mikpamɔ lɛ mli ni mijaraa yɛ elɛɛmɔ kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ naa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ni minine shɛɔ jara ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ yɛ jara nɔ?

english: Traders and consumers pay premium prices for uniform, undamaged produce. Sorting separates damaged crops to prevent rot from spreading and allows you to market top-quality goods for top value.
ga: Jarayelɔi kɛ jarayelɔi woɔ nyɔmɔ ni nɔ kwɔ kɛha nibii ni amɛfeɔ daa, ni efiteee lɛ. Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite lɛ amli koni ŋmeii akagbɛ ashwã. ni ehaa onyɛɔ okɛ nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ yaa jara nɔ yɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ fe fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow instead of bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is starving for nutrients like nitrogen, or the ground is flooded with too much water. Adding the right fertilizer or improving drainage helps the leaves turn green so the plant can make food and grow big corn ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai, tamɔ nitrogen, loo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ loo nu ni hoɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ afee niyenii ni ekwɛ ŋmãa toi wuji.

english: If I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year, why does my harvest keep getting smaller?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ miiba shi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season without giving it time to recover. It also lets pests and diseases that love maize build up in the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves curl up and droop during the afternoon heat even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli beni mikɛ nu ewo amɛnɔ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: In the hot afternoon sun, leaves lose moisture into the air faster than the roots can pull water from the soil. The plant curls its leaves to shield itself from the heat and save water, usually recovering once the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni amɛbu nu he. Bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛji hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Why do my corn seeds fail to come up when I bury them deep down in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔɔ beni mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds carry only a small burst of stored energy. If planted too deep, the young shoot exhausts all its energy trying to push through the heavy soil before it ever reaches the sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ni ato. Kɛji akɛ adu mli tsɔ lɛ, tsei bibii lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ dani amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds and put long sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni majie niji kakadaji koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves in full sunlight to make food for the tubers underground. Tall weeds block this light and steal water and soil nutrients from the plant.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo ni amɛkɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ niyenii. Jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ tsiɔ kane nɛɛ naa ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa tsei lɛ yeɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when we get heavy rains for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains flood the ground, water fills all the air pockets, essentially drowning the roots and causing rot to set in.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu lɛ baayi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ fɛɛ amli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni ekɛ fitemɔ baa.

english: Can I plant peppers and tomatoes together in the same bed, or will they hurt each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tomato yɛ saatso kome nɔ loo amɛbaaye amɛhe awui?

english: It is better to separate them because pepper and tomato belong to the same plant family. Planting them together makes it very easy for shared pests and diseases to quickly wipe out both crops.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ amɛhe ejaakɛ pepper kɛ tomato jɛ weku kome mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei enyɔ lɛ fee ekome lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ yeɔ tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ oya.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their blossoms before any pods start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed blossoms when they are stressed by drought, lack of soil nutrients, or when tiny insects attack the flowers before they can be properly pollinated.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ hao amɛ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii Tutuaa fɔfɔi dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut away the small shoots growing around the main trunk of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishifã titri lɛ ajie.

english: Too many extra shoots fight with the main plantain tree for soil food and water. Removing extra shoots leaves only one or two strong stems, which results in much larger plantain bunches.
ga: Tsoi ni shwereɔ fe nine lɛ kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ baawu koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ daraa kwraa.

english: Why are my green tomato fruits falling off the plant before they get a chance to ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ená hegbɛ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their fruit early when there are sudden changes in water supply, severe hot spells, or a lack of key minerals like calcium in the soil.
ga: Tomato baashwie eyibii lɛ oya kɛji nu lɛ jɛɛhe lɛ tsake trukaa, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa, loo nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Cassava plants naturally drop their leaves during dry spells to conserve water and protect themselves from drought. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves and continue growing normally.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hɔmɔ be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hɔmɔ he. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eda bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling upwards during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a defense mechanism plants use to reduce water loss and protect themselves from intense sun and heat. If the plants bounce back when temperatures cool in the evening, it is normal heat stress.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛha nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛji tso lɛ ku esɛɛ beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ Abuɔ lɛ akɛ eji hulutsoo be mli haomɔ ni yaa nɔ daa.

english: Extreme heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer can stress pepper plants, causing them to drop their blossoms before fruits can form.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni akɛhaaa yɛ be fɛɛ mli Loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baanyɛ aha pepper tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo.

english: Why do my cowpea plants spread out over the ground instead of growing straight up like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ miigbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Many traditional cowpea varieties are naturally crawling or vining plants. This growth habit allows them to shade the ground, prevent weed growth, and hold moisture in the soil while fixing nitrogen.
ga: Kusum cowpeas babaoo ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni shwereɔ loo wain tsei. Nɛkɛ dalɛ su nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni esaa nitrogen lɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize crops turning pale yellow starting from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting at the tip and moving down the central vein indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea will help the plant regain its dark green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ ni amɛyaa shishi kɛyaa teŋgbɛ, ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmei ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni eku esɛɛ eba eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow small and bent instead of big and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee agbo ni eja lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, loose, deep soil to expand freely. If the soil is hard, stony, or compacted, the growing tuber cannot push through easily, resulting in stunted or crooked yams.
ga: Sweet potato hia shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, tɛi yɔɔ nɔ, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, bulb lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ mli mlɛo. Enɛ haa sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ bibii loo efiteɔ.

english: Why do plantain suckers grow so slowly when planted in dry or rocky soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ daraa blɛoo nɛkɛ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo tɛi amli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and need heavy amounts of organic matter and constant water to thrive. Hard or dry soil starves the roots of moisture and food, delaying plant development.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni ehe hiaa nibii babaoo ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ nu daa koni amɛkwɛ̃. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo egbi lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei lɛ adalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants burn and die when there are no big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate full, direct sunlight. Shade trees or companion crops like plantains act as natural shields, protecting the tender young leaves from sunburn and drying out.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fɛɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei ni fata he tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii. Ebuɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔlɔ he.

english: Why do armyworms attack and destroy my maize leaves so quickly during the early growth stage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi-abɛi lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ oya yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Armyworms target young maize because the central tender leaves inside the funnel are soft, sweet, and easy to eat, allowing caterpillars to feed heavily and multiply fast.
ga: Asraafoi akuu lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ kwɛɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ anɔ ejaakɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe ŋɔɔ, ni amɛyeɔ oya, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ nii babaoo ni amɛfɔɔ oya.

english: Why is it important for me to remove weeds around my crops when they are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ majie jwɛi ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops have small, weak root systems that cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for water, light, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early ensures the main crop gets all the nutrients it needs to build a strong stem and roots.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha nu, la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso ni hereɔ lɛ lɛ naa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛfee shishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni wa.

english: Can I start a cocoa farm if I already work a regular monthly job?
ga: Ani manyɛ mabɔi kookoo ŋmɔ kɛji mitsuɔ nii daa nyɔɔŋ nɔ momo?

english: Yes, many people successfully combine regular jobs with farming. Cocoa requires intensive work mainly during specific periods like planting, weeding, and harvesting, allowing you to manage the farm during weekends or by hiring local help while maintaining your regular job.
ga: Hɛɛ, mɛi pii kɛ be-fɛɛ nitsumɔ kɛ okwaayeli efee ekome yɛ omanyeyeli mli. Kookoo biɔ nitsumɔ ni wa babaoo yɛ be pɔtɛɛ ko mli, tamɔ dumɔ, jwɛi shwiemɔ, kɛ nikpamɔ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ otsii lɛ anaagbee loo oŋɔɔ maŋbii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nitsumɔ yɛ be mli ni otsuɔ nii be fɛɛ be lolo lɛ.

english: How do I know if my land is suitable for growing cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Cocoa trees thrive in deep, well-drained fertile soil with rich organic matter and good rainfall. If your land stays moist without getting waterlogged during heavy rains and has rich topsoil, it is usually good for cocoa.
ga: Cocoa tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛfata nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo kɛ nugbɔ kpakpa ni nɛɔ lɛ he. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi ni nu ehiɛɛɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli, ni eyɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ hi kɛha kookoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and burning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiitso lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. When left uncovered, sunlight burns the leaves, causing them to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ashi lɛ, hulu la lɛ baaha baai lɛ ashã. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do flowers fall off my cocoa trees without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers due to stress from dry weather, poor soil nutrients, or insect pests. Keeping the soil moist and providing proper cocoa fertilizer helps the flowers stay on the tree and turn into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ amli baa lɛ hewɔ. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How many years after planting should I expect my cocoa trees to start producing pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ sɛɛ beni adu cacao tso lɛ esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ ebaaje shishi ewo ŋmeii?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa seed varieties can start producing pods within 2 to 3 years of planting, whereas older traditional varieties take about 4 to 5 years under proper care.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aje ŋmeii feemɔ shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ, yɛ be mli ni kusum mli ŋmeii srɔtoi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 4 kɛyashi 5 kɛji akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Which food crops can I safely plant together with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ mikɛ cacao tsei bibii akwɛ shweshweeshwe?

english: You can plant plantains, cocoyams, and maize together with young cocoa. Plantains provide essential shade, while other food crops give you food and income while waiting for the cocoa to mature.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ plantain, kookoo, kɛ ŋmãa afata kookoo bibii ahe. Plantains haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa. be mli ni niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi Haa bo niyenii kɛ shika be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do extension officers recommend keeping some big trees on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ tsei wuji ahi mi-cocoe ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Big shade trees protect cocoa from excessive sun and wind, cool the farm down, and bring up nutrients from deep in the soil, helping cocoa trees live longer and remain healthy.
ga: Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fe nine lɛ he. ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo tso lɛ ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting right on the branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Black pods are usually caused by a fungal infection called Black Pod disease, which spreads rapidly in heavy humidity and excess shade. Removing infected pods and reducing heavy farm shade helps prevent it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ kɛ hulutsoo be ni fe nine mli lɛ. Pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmɔ mli hulutsoo ni tsii ni baa shi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why do I need to prune or cut branches off my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo loo majie niji kɛjɛ kookoo tso ni eda lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches, allowing air and sunlight to move freely through the farm. This reduces disease outbreaks and encourages the tree to produce more flowers and pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli oya. Enɛ haa helai ni baa lɛ baa shi, ni ewoɔ tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: How does the dry season affect my cocoa trees, and what can I do to help them survive?
ga: Te hulutsoo be lɛ saa mi cacao tsei lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ? Ni mɛni mafee koni maye mabua mi-cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi?

english: During severe dry seasons, cocoa trees lose leaves to conserve water. You can protect them by spreading dry leaves or mulch around their roots to hold moisture in the soil and keeping shade trees overhead.
ga: yɛ hɔmɔ be ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ baa lɛ fiteɔ koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Obaanyɛ obu amɛhe kɛtsɔ baai ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaabɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ. shishifãi lɛ koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ahi sũ lɛ mli ni eha hulutsoo aba yiteŋ

english: Yellowing lower leaves in maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. The plant automatically moves available nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to support new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛ ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee aba.

english: Why do my bean plants produce plenty of lush leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ woɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas produce mostly leaves when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Excess nitrogen encourages top growth while delaying or preventing flower and pod development.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ fɔɔ baa kɛji nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shweremɔ yaa hiɛ waa yɛ be mli ni ehaa fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo etsĩɔ amɛnaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when I clear all the big shade trees away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni edara lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct sun and heat. Shading them with larger trees or planting plantains alongside them shields their fragile leaves from harsh sunlight and keeps the surrounding soil moist.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei wuji ni akɛwoɔ hulutsoo mli loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ Ebaabu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without forming fruits during hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry soil stress tomato plants, causing them to drop their flowers before pollination can take place. The plant sheds flowers to conserve moisture and protect itself.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ haoɔ tomato tsei. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani pollination baa. Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni amɛbu amɛhe.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very thin with small cobs when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ Dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving them with weak stems and small cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why should I remove the extra small suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal nutrients and water away from the parent plantain tree. Pruning excess suckers allows the main plant to direct its energy into producing a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tsobii loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ dumɔwu lɛ he. Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ tsei agboi ni tsii.

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that spreads rapidly in wet, cold, and humid conditions. High humidity trapped under dense leaf growth allows fungal spores to easily infect the pods.
ga: Black pods ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ, fɛ̃i, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ baai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ shishi lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ fungal spores lɛ baatswa pods lɛ hela.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or thrips. As they feed on the sap of young leaves, they distort leaf growth and can spread plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Beni amɛyeɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ Amɛfiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ amɛshwã tsei amli.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when the farm gets flooded?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nu afua lɛ?

english: Cassava roots require well-drained soil to breathe. In waterlogged soil, the roots suffocate from lack of oxygen, which allows damp-loving fungi to invade and rot the tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he hiaa cassava shishifãi koni amɛmu. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni sumɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ boteɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines onto wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsɔseɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha eda yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam vines need to reach sunlight to create energy for growing large tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground, protecting them from soil diseases and maximizing sun exposure.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni ekɛfee hewalɛ kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Buu amɛhe kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ ahe ni oha hulu la lɛ aya nɔ babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops curling up and dropping off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling or drooping is usually a sign that pests or fungal diseases are attacking your plant and draining its nutrients. Applying the right crop medicine helps destroy the pests so the leaves can recover and return to their healthy position.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi loo ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko miitutua tso lɛ ni eefite niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso tsofa ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekpata tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ hiɛ bɔni afee ni baai lɛ anyɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba shihilɛ kpakpa mli.

english: Why can't my crops heal themselves from a disease without spraying medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛŋ atsa amɛhe kɛjɛ helai amli kɛji akɛ awooo amɛ tsofa?

english: Crops do not have strong immune systems like humans to fight off heavy pest attacks or fungus on their own. Once a disease takes hold, the plant needs external chemical medicine to kill the organisms causing the sickness.
ga: Tsei bɛ gbɔmɔtso mli nii ni gbeɔ helai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ tamɔ adesai ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛwu amɛshi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ gbeyei. Beni hela lɛ ba Tsei lɛ he miihia tsofai ni jɛɔ kponɔgbɛ koni amɛkɛgbe nibii ni kɛ hela baa lɛ.

english: What should I do when a crop disease spreads very fast and covers my whole farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ́ tso hela ko gbɛ eshwa oya ni eha miŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: When a disease reaches a severe stage and overflows across your farm, you must immediately report it to an extension officer to get the specific chemical spray needed to stop total crop loss.
ga: Beni hela lɛ shɛɔ he ni eshɛɔ he ni eyeɔ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Esa akɛ obɔ hela lɛ he amaniɛ otsɔɔ o-extension official lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni onine ashɛ tsofai pɔtɛɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni he hiaa koni akɛkpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ fɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does the officer tell me to spray my farm two times instead of just once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai lɛ kɛɛ ŋmɔ lɛ akɛ amɛwo mli shii enyɔ moŋ fe shikome pɛ lɛ?

english: The first spray usually kills the adult pests or active fungus, while the second round targets newly hatched eggs or remaining spores to ensure the disease is completely eliminated.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ gbeɔ kooloi loo ŋmeii ni eda lɛ fɛɛ. yɛ be mli ni fã ni ji enyɔ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii ni afɔ ehee loo ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ anɔ koni ekwɛ akɛ ajie hela lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How soon after spraying crop medicine should I expect my crop leaves to look healthy again?
ga: Te esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ mitso lɛ baai lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ beni akɛ tsofa ni akɛ tsofa ewo mli lɛ eshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ tɛŋŋ?

english: Depending on the type of crop and disease, you will usually notice leaves lifting up and regaining their normal shape and green color within a few days to a week after treatment.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, obaana akɛ baai lɛ woɔ amɛhe nɔ ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa amɛhe ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli yɛ gbii fioo komɛi kɛyashi otsi kome mli yɛ tsofafeemɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ damɔ tso lɛ henɔ kɛ hela lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I just buy any farm medicine at the market to spray on my sickly crop leaves?
ga: Ani manyɛ mahe ŋmɔ mli tsofa yɛ jara nɔ koni mikɛshwie mitsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ?

english: No, different crop sicknesses require different remedies. Using the wrong medicine can fail to cure the disease or even burn your crop leaves.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii ahe helai srɔtoi biɔ tsamɔi srɔtoi. Ekolɛ tsofa ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nyɛŋ atsa hela lɛ loo ebaaha tso baai lɛ ashã po.

english: How can I tell if my crop leaves are dying from hot sun or from a pest attack?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbeɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miigboi?

english: Sun heat usually affects all plants evenly across the field, but pest attacks or diseases cause specific leaves to spot, curl, or droop unevenly before spreading to other plants.
ga: Hulu la lɛ fɔɔ tsei fɛɛ anɔ hewalɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Gbɛjegbɛ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ Shi tsɛŋemɔ hela loo hela ko ni baa lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛkpãa, loo amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ dani amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa tsei krokomɛi anɔ.

english: Will spraying liquid medicine directly onto my crop leaves harm or burn them?
ga: Ani nu lɛ ni mikɛshwieɔ mitsei lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaye amɛ awui loo ebaashã amɛ?

english: If you measure and mix the medicine correctly as advised by an expert, the spray will heal the leaves rather than damage them.
ga: Kɛji osusu otsofa lɛ he ni okɛfutu mli jogbaŋŋ taakɛ ohe nilelɔ lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ekwɛ baai lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni eeefite amɛ.

english: Should I spray my crops as soon as I see the first sick leaves, or wait until the sickness increases?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mina klɛŋklɛŋ hela baai lɛ pɛ loo mamɛ ni hela lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: It is always best to treat the farm at the very first sign of sickness. Waiting until the disease overflows makes it harder and more expensive to cure.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be akɛ abaatsa ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ hela he okadi klɛŋklɛŋ nɔ. Kɛ́ mɔ ko mɛ kɛyashi hela lɛ baaye enɔ lɛ, ehaa tsamɔ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni eheɔ shika babaoo.

english: Who can help me identify the exact medicine my crops need when pests attack?
ga: Ani mɔ ko baanyɛ aye abua mi ni mana tsofa pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa mitsei lɛ kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai batutua mi?

english: You should consult your local agricultural extension officer, who can examine the sickness on your crops and prescribe the correct spray and dosage.
ga: Esa akɛ oyabi okwaayeli he nitsumɔ he nitsulɔ ni yɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ ana hela yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii amli ni etsɔɔ bo tsofa ni sa kɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow before the crop is ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to stay green and healthy, or that excessive water in the field is drowning the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. Aloo nu babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows specific pests and diseases to build up in that field.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. ni eha kooloi kɛ helai komɛi abua amɛhe naa yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do groundnut plants make the soil richer for other crops I plant later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ fee fɛo kɛha tsei krokomɛi ni midu sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to a plant family that traps natural nitrogen food from the air into the soil through their roots, leaving free soil food for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts fata tsei aweku ko ni kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen nibii ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa niyenii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I not plant my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a hot dry stretch; if seeds sprout during this dry period, the young seedlings will dry up and die before the real rains begin.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni mli egbi nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ hɔmɔ be nɛɛ mli Tsei bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi dani nugbɔ lɛ anɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller heads and lower yields when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa bulbs bibii ni yibiiwoo faaa kɛji midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving no single plant with enough food to grow strong.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haaa tso ko kwraa aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha eda waa.

english: Why do weeds in my field cause my crops to stay small and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ miifee bibioo ni ebɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than main crops and steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients that your crops need to grow big and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers instead of turning them into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi yɛ aduawai najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or small insects attacking the blossoms before fruit can form.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi bibii hao amɛ. ni baa ni amɛtutuaa fɔfɔi lɛ dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo

english: Why do my cassava roots become soft and watery instead of firm when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ nu moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee nɔ ni wa kɛ́ mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots absorb too much water if harvested immediately after heavy rains or if left standing in waterlogged soil, which leads to rotting.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu babaoo tsɔ kɛji akɛ akpa amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ loo ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ, ni no haa amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why does my harvested corn get destroyed by small insects when I store it in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii bibii fiteɔ mi-abele ni akpaa lɛ kɛ́ akɛto ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Insects like weevils thrive in moist grain; if corn is not properly dried before storage or kept in airtight bags, insect eggs hatch and destroy the grains.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ dumɔwui ni mli efɔ mli. Kɛji akɛ agbiko ŋmãa jogbaŋŋ dani akɛto loo akɛwo vacuum bag mli lɛ, ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ ni amɛfiteɔ dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot quickly when I stack them together in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ato amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Direct sunlight and trapped heat wound the skin of the yam, allowing fungi and bacteria to enter easily and cause rapid rotting.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni baa lɛ baafite sweet potato lɛ hewolo. Enɛ haa ewaaa akɛ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ baabote mli ni amɛkɛ fitemɔ baa oya.

english: Why do market traders prefer buying beans imported from other places like Nigeria instead of buying from local farms like mine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayeli jarayelɔi sumɔɔ ni amɛhe ŋmeii ni akɛba maŋsɛɛ kɛjɛ he ko tamɔ Nigeria moŋ fe ni amɛbaahe kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔji tamɔ mi nɔ lɛ?

english: Traders prefer beans that cook quickly, have a uniform size, and are free from insect damage. If local harvests vary in quality or take longer to prepare, traders look to foreign suppliers to get the exact standard their customers demand.
ga: Jarayelɔi sumɔɔ ŋmeii ni hoɔ oya. Na dalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa Ni kooloi ni baafite lɛ bɛ. Kɛji akɛ maŋ lɛ mli nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yɛ srɔto loo eheɔ be babaoo dani asaa he lɛ, Jarayelɔi lɛ baakwɛ majimaji ateŋ nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ koni amɛshɛ shishitoo mlai ni amɛ jarayelɔi lɛ biɔ lɛ ahe.

english: How do bean plants help improve the soil for my other crops?
