ga: Bean tsei haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi. Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná minɔ lɛ?

english: Beans are legumes that gather nitrogen gas from the air and store it in tiny bumps on their roots. When the plant leaves and roots decay after harvest, this trapped nitrogen naturally fertilizes the soil for the next crop.
ga: Beans ji ŋmeii ni buaa nitrogen gas naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shishifãi bibii amli. Beni tsei ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi fiteɔ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Nɛkɛ nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ nɛɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my bean plants falling off before any pods form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-bean tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani ŋmeii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Bean flowers often drop off when the plants experience extreme heat stress, poor watering, or attacks from small insect pests like thrips. Keeping the soil moist and protecting the flowers ensures they develop into pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. nu ni ehiii loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ thrips ni baatutua amɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe ni abuɔ lɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ aya hiɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my stored beans get small holes in them after sitting in bags for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kɔfi ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Beni eta kotoku lɛ mli otsii fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ

english: Small insects called bean weevils lay eggs on the seeds. When the eggs hatch into larvae, they feed on the inside of the bean and chew small exit holes, which can destroy your harvest if the beans are not properly dried and stored in sealed containers.
ga: Kooloo bibioo ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ bean moth lɛ fɔɔ ewui yɛ dumɔwui anɔ. Kɛji ŋmeii lɛ fɔ ni amɛbatsɔ ŋmeii Eyeɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni ekɛ ŋmeii bibii ni jeɔ kpo lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Enɛ baanyɛ afite onibii lɛ kɛji akɛ agbiko ŋmeii lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtooo tsɛnsi ko ni atsĩ naa mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my bean plants turn yellow and curl up during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing and curling leaves are often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that multiply during dry weather, sucking the nutrients directly out of the plant leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies lɛ kɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ. Ni baafɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be mli. Kɛtsɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni jɛɔ tso baai amli lɛ ni enuɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ

english: How do I know when my bean crop is fully ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-bean tsei lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Beans are ready for dry harvest when the pods turn brown and dry, and the seeds inside rattle when you shake the pod. Harvesting too early leads to mold, while waiting too long causes pods to burst open and lose seeds on the ground.
ga: Beans lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ ni egbi beni ŋmeii lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi lɛ. Ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hosoɔ kɛ́ otsi pod lɛ. Nikpamɔ mra tsɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, mɛmɔ be kakadaŋŋ haa ŋmeii lɛ fãa ni dumɔwui lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I just plant the dry beans I buy from the local eating market, or do I need special seeds?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii ni egbi ni miheɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ? Aloo dumɔwui krɛdɛɛi he miihia mi?

english: While eating beans will sprout, certified planting seeds are specifically tested and treated to resist common field diseases, give higher yields, and grow evenly, making your harvest far more valuable to traders.
ga: Beni ayeɔ ŋmeii lɛ, amɛbaakwɛ̃. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ akwɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni atsaa amɛ koni ana kɛji amɛnyɛŋ amɛye ŋmɔ mli helai ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ anɔ. Yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ ni edaa pɛpɛɛpɛ Enɛ haa okpamɔ lɛ he hiaa waa kɛhaa jarayelɔi.

english: What happens if I plant my bean seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planting beans too close together forces them to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stalks, fewer pods, and poor airflow that encourages fungal diseases.
ga: Beans ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei bibii, ŋmeii fioo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii ni woɔ ŋmeii hela he hewalɛ.

english: Is it beneficial for me to plant my beans together with my maize crop on the same farm?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa baafata ŋmãa he yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, intercropping beans with maize works well because the beans add nitrogen to feed the maize soil, while tall maize stalks can provide physical support for climbing bean varieties to hold their pods off the damp ground.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ kɛ nitrogen fataa ŋmãa shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmãa tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ŋmãa srɔtoi ni kwɔɔ lɛ yɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ koni ekɛtsi ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested beans turn dark and lose their clean color before I take them to market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kɔfi yibii ni mikpa lɛ mli edɔ ni amɛsu ni he tse lɛ sɛɛ foɔ dani akɛwoɔ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans lose their bright color when exposed to direct heat, sunlight, or high humidity after being harvested. Drying them under gentle shade and storing them in cool, dry places preserves their fresh look so buyers pay a higher price.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii, hulu la, loo hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, amɛhe su ni kpɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Kɛ́ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni akɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehiɛ ahi ehe nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, mɔ ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ jara ni nɔ kwɔ fe no.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in high moisture and heavy shade. Clearing weed growth and removing infected pods early stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ waa kɛ shade mli kɛbaa. Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ akpa.

english: Why do older cocoa trees in my village get swollen stems and stop bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei ni edara ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ ashishifãi efuu ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: This is caused by Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, which is carried from tree to tree by tiny insects called mealybugs. Removing infected trees is the main way to protect the rest of the farm.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, ni koolooi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ mealybugs lɛ jieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ. Tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ titri ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ ŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Why is it better for me to harvest my cocoa pods early in the morning instead of late afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ leebi moŋ fe shwane mli?

english: Harvesting in the cool morning keeps the harvested pods and beans from overheating under the strong sun, preserving their moisture quality before you begin fermentation.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ, ebaabu ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ ahe koni amɛkadɔ fe nine yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mlihilɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ dani ajeɔ ŋmɔtɔ shishi lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell when a cocoa pod is fully ripe and ready to pick?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ajie amɛ?

english: Ripe cocoa pods change color completely; green pods turn bright yellow, and reddish pods turn orange. Pick them as soon as they change color so they do not overripe or attract pests.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su kwraa. Pods eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. ni ŋmeii tsuru lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii Tsɔɔmɔ amɛ kɛji amɛtsake amɛhe su pɛ. Enɛ baaha ekahoo fe nine loo egbala kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ.

english: How do I keep my dry cocoa beans cool and safe from spoiling while waiting for buyers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-kokoo ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekafite be mli ni mimɛɔ mɛi ni baahe lɛ?

english: Store your thoroughly dried beans off the ground on wooden pallets in breathable jute sacks, keeping them in a cool, well-ventilated dry room away from direct moisture.
ga: Okɛ ŋmeii ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ato shikpɔŋ yɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ jute kotokui ni haa mumɔ tsɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ. Kɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni egbi, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli. He ni hulutsoo tɛ̃ɛ yɔɔ he.

english: Why do my cocoa beans mold when I store them in plastic bags after drying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii kɛ́ mikɛwo plastic kotoku mli beni migbi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plastic bags trap residual heat and moisture inside, creating warm damp conditions that cause mold to grow rapidly. Jute bags allow air to flow and keep the beans dry.
ga: Plastic kotokui mɔ̃ɔ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ mli. ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa oya. Jute kotokui haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli ni egbiɔ kɔfi yibii lɛ.

english: How many years do I need to wait after planting before my new cocoa trees start giving fruit?
ga: Kɛ́ mɔ ko du lɛ, afii enyiɛ esa akɛ emɛ dani kookoo tso hee ko aje yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually start producing pods within 2 to 3 years with good weeding and care, while older varieties can take 4 to 5 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfee tsofai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji ajie jwɛi kpakpai kɛ amɛhekwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 4 kɛyashi 5.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings drooping and turning brown during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa roots are shallow and suffer quickly in heat and drought. Planting shade crops like plantains near young cocoa keeps the soil moist and protects leaves from harsh sunlight.
ga: Cocoa shishifãi bibii lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa, amɛdaraa oya yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ tsei ahe tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he.

english: Why do many of the small flowers on my cocoa trees drop off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii bibii Tsei babaoo ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers but drop most of them because the tree can only support a limited number of full-sized pods at a time.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo gbeeɔ shi ejaakɛ cacao tso lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ ŋmeii ni fa fioo pɛ nɔ yɛ be kome mli.

english: How does keeping shade trees on my farm help my cocoa survive long dry periods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa mikoo lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli?

english: Shade trees act as natural umbrellas that cool the air temperature around cocoa plants and reduce water evaporation from both the soil and cocoa leaves.
ga: Shade tsei tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shade ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli dɔlɛ yaa hiɛ. Kookoo tso lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni ehaa nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ kookoo baai fɛɛ amli lɛ baa shi.

english: How can I make a young fruit tree produce good fruit if I don't know where the seed came from?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ aha tsei bibii awo yibii kpakpai? Be mli ni oleee he ni dumɔwui lɛ jɛɔ lɛ?

english: You can use grafting, which means cutting a branch from a tree known to produce good, sweet fruit and joining it to your young seedling so it grows improved fruit.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ grafting atsu nii. Enɛ tsɔɔ tsei ni ale akɛ amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai ni ŋɔɔ lɛ aniji ni afolɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛtsa odumɔwui lɛ anɔ koni aduawai lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why would someone cut a branch from an old, sweet orange tree and attach it to a young seedling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi komɛi shwieɔ akutu tsei momoi aniji lɛ? Ni okɛkpɛtɛ tso bibioo ko he?

english: This practice is called grafting. It transfers the good fruiting qualities and fast growth of the mature parent tree directly to the young seedling.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ grafting. Ekɛ yibiiwoo kpakpa kɛ dalɛ oya ni yɔɔ tso nyɛ ni eda lɛ mli lɛ yaa tso bibioo lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: What should I do if my tree is growing tall but producing poor quality fruit?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ mitso lɛ kɛlɛ shi ewoɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: An agricultural extension officer can help you graft branches from healthy, high-yielding trees onto your existing tree to change the quality of fruit it bears.
ga: Okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aye abua bo ni okɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ nine awo otso ni oyɔɔ momo lɛ nɔ koni ekɛtsake yibii ni onine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ mlihilɛ.

english: Can agricultural extension officers come directly to my farm to assist me with plant grafting?
ga: Ani okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aba miŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ koni eye ebua mi yɛ mihe nibii ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ mli?

english: Yes, extension officers can visit your farm to help perform technical tasks like grafting and teach you how to select the best branches for your crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ayasara oŋmɔ lɛ koni amɛye amɛbua bo yɛ ŋaa nitsumɔi tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ bo bɔ ni ooofee ohala ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How do I choose the right branch from a tree to graft onto another plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tso nine ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ yɛ tso kroko nɔ?

english: You should select a strong, disease-free branch cut directly from a mature tree that is already known for bearing plenty of good quality fruit.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala tsei niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni hela bɛ mli ni afolɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni eda ni ale akɛ amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai babaoo lɛ amli.

english: Why do grafted trees start bearing fruit much faster than trees grown straight from seed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni akɛwo mli lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi mra kwraa fe tsei ni jɛ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: A grafted branch comes from a mature parent tree that is already ready to reproduce, allowing the new plant to skip the long years it takes for a seedling to mature.
ga: Akɛ niji fɔ̃ɔ tso nyɛ ni eda ni efee klalo akɛ ebaafɔ bii lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei heei hoɔ afii babaoo dani dumɔwui lɛ daa.

english: Is it possible to improve a tree on my farm even if I planted it years ago?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ aha tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ kɛji midu amɛ afii babaoo ni eho nɛ po?

english: Yes, through top-working or grafting, you can cut back older branches and join cuttings from superior fruit-bearing trees to improve your existing tree's yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ ojie tsei niji momoi ni okɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni afolɔ afata he koni eha tsei ni yɔɔ momo lɛ ayibii aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: What happens if I plant a fruit tree from a seed whose origin I do not know?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni mileee he ni ejɛ lɛ wo aduawai tso ko?

english: The tree might produce poor or unpredictable fruit, but you can correct this early by grafting a proven high-yielding branch onto it.
ga: Tsei baanyɛ awo yibii ni ehiii loo ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba. Shi obaanyɛ osaa enɛ mra. Kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni ana akɛ amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some trees grown from seeds produce sour fruit even when the original fruit was sweet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui amli lɛ woɔ yibii ni mli edɔ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛjɛɔ dumɔwui amli amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ? Akɛ shishijee aduawai lɛ ŋɔɔ?

english: Seeds carry mixed traits from nature and do not always grow exact copies of the mother plant, which is why farmers graft branches from known sweet trees instead.
ga: Dumɔwui ji adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni akɛfee ekome ni jeee be fɛɛ be amɛkwɛɔ tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ henɔi. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni bei pii lɛ okwaafoi kɛ tsei ni ale akɛ amɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ aniji shwieɔ shi moŋ lɛ.

english: How does attaching a branch from another tree help my young crop survive and yield better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei krokomɛi ahe niji ni mikɛfataa he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai?

english: The root system of your planted seedling provides strong support and soil absorption, while the attached branch brings the proven high-yielding fruit qualities of a successful tree.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu lɛ ashishifãi lɛ haa yelikɛbuamɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu jogbaŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni tsei niji ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ he lɛ haa tsei ni yeɔ omanye lɛ ayibii ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni ana he odase lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, a key nutrient they need to grow strong. This often happens when heavy rains wash nutrients deep into the ground where the young roots cannot reach them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha gbɔmɔtso lɛ dalɛ kpakpa Enɛ fɔɔ baa beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are mature and ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving foliage only at the top of the stem. You can also carefully dig around one plant to verify that the roots have grown thick and firm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ yiteŋgbɛ pɛ eshwɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ ohe awo mli hu. Kwɛmɔ tso ko mli jogbaŋŋ koni ona kɛji eshishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why are my green cocoa pods turning black and rotting right on the branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, shaded conditions. Pruning excess tree branches allows sunlight and air to reach the pods, which helps keep them dry and prevents the fungus from spreading.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Tso lɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ aniji lɛ akagbi ni eha ŋmei lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden stakes in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ awo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to capture sunlight, which allows the leaves to make food that feeds the growing tuber underground. Staking also keeps leaves off damp soil, protecting the plant from fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛnyɛ amɛná hulu la lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Buu tsei ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa tsei ahe lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my maize seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell that can scorch young seedlings before they establish roots. It is safer to wait until the rainy season fully sets in so the soil stays consistently moist.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui bibii dani amɛshishifãi lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baashɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why are the blossoms on my pepper plants dropping off without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ pepper ko baaa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or excessive fertilizer. Ensuring the plants receive steady water and light shade during the hottest parts of the day helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ nu ha tsei lɛ daa ni aha amɛ hulutsoo yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes the leaves on my tomato plants to curl up and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves and spread viruses. Controlling weeds around your farm and using safe insect sprays help protect young tomato plants from these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ Oŋmɔ lɛ kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmeii anɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ baaye abua ni abu tomato tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ahe.

english: Why do extension officers advise me not to plant maize on the exact same plot of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ etsɔɔɔ akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously in the same soil drains the same specific nutrients every season and allows maize pests to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas restores natural nitrogen to the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ebaajie niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kpo daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa mli ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during heavy rain and strong winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that spread near the surface rather than growing deep into the earth, making heavy stems easy to push over. Mounding dirt tightly around the base and removing extra suckers gives the main tree better balance.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛbɛŋkɛɔ nu lɛ hiɛ. moŋ lɛ, edaa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Ehaa tsɔne ni tsii lɛ gbeeɔ shi mlɛo. Okɛ muji lɛ ato shishigbɛ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ ni ojie tsɔnei ni akɛmuɔ nii lɛ koni eye ebua ni tso titri lɛ afee ekome jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and thicker than my planted crops after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants that are naturally adapted to local soils, allowing them to absorb water and nutrients much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early gives your young crops a fair chance to get the sunlight and food they need.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo jɛmɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha odumɔwui lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: Why do my young rice plants die almost as soon as I transplant them into the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eshwɛ fioo ni midumɔwu lɛ baagbo beni mikɛwo ŋmɔ mli pɛ kɛkɛ ni mikɛwo ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Transplanting causes shock to the plant roots. If the field dries out suddenly or water is too deep right after transplanting, the root system cannot absorb nutrients and the seedling fails and dies.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ haa tso shishifãi lɛ shooɔ. Kɛji akɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ gĩ trukaa loo nu lɛ mli kwɔ tsɔ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. ni dumɔwui lɛ baagboi.

english: Is it better for me to sow rice seeds directly in the ground or raise them in a nursery first?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmãa dumɔwui awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo aaadu yɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Direct sowing saves labor but leaves seeds vulnerable to heavy rains or dry spells. Raising seedlings in a nursery produces stronger plants, but they require wet soil and careful timing when moved to the main field.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa nitsumɔ baa shi shi ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo nugbɔshiimɔ bei lɛ nyɛɔ etswaa dumɔwui lɛ waa. Dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ. Shi ebiɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ kɛ be ni sa jogbaŋŋ beni aduɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops rot and fail when my land gets flooded with excess rainwater?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfiteɔ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ eyi mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ lɛ?

english: Too much standing water smothers plant roots by cutting off their air supply. Without air, roots rot and cannot feed the plant, causing it to die even though water is abundant.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ fiteɔ tsei shishifãi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa egboɔ kɛ́ nu babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ po.

english: How can I level my rice field so water doesn't flood one side and dry out the other?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsake bɔ ni ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ mli koni nu akaho yɛ fã kome nɔ ni fã kroko lɛ hu agbi?

english: Leveling the land with a hoe or tractor prevents deep water spots that drown plants and dry high spots that starve them, ensuring water spreads evenly across all seedlings.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akɛ ŋmei loo trakta shwieɔ shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ nu mli hei ni mli kwɔ ni haa tsei shwieɔ shi lɛ anaa, kɛ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ ni egbi ni hɔmɔ gbeɔ tsei lɛ. Enɛ haa nu lɛ mlijaa yɛ dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ amli pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: How can I protect my transplanted crops when the rains stop unexpectedly after planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa beni midu nii sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When rain stops after transplanting, soil moisture drops quickly. Mulching around plants with dry grass or using simple bucket irrigation helps keep soil moist until the rains resume.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ baa shi oya. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baagi mli nu ni yɔɔ mlɛo shwie tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are my old planting methods no longer giving me good results during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii tsutsu lɛ wooo yibii kpakpai dɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rain patterns and soil conditions change over time. Old methods like direct seed broadcasting suffer when heavy rains wash seeds away, making modern planting in beds or rows more reliable.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ tsakeɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Gbɛi ni etsɛ tamɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ kɛ naagbai kpeɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie dumɔwui lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ saatsoi loo ŋwɛi ŋtayaai amli lɛ feɔ nɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to transplant my seedlings to stop them from dying?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu dumɔwui koni amɛkagboi?

english: Transplanting in the late afternoon or on cloudy days protects weak seedlings from the harsh mid-day sun, giving them the cooler night hours to recover and settle into the wet soil.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shwane mli loo yɛ atatu gbi nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu dumɔwui ni egbɔjɔ lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa enáa gbɛkɛ ni mli ejɔ koni ekɛ ehe awo mli ni ehi shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How old should my rice seedlings be before I move them out of the nursery bed?
ga: Esa akɛ mi-ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ aye afii enyiɛ dani mafo amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmãa saatso lɛ nɔ?

english: Moving seedlings when they are around 15 to 21 days old gives them the best chance of survival. If they stay too long in the nursery, their roots grow too big and break easily during transplanting.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he kroko beni amɛye aaafee gbii 15 kɛyashi 21 lɛ baaha amɛná hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛhi shi. Kɛ amɛhi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ Eshishifãi lɛ feɔ agboi tsɔ ni amɛkuɔ oya yɛ be mli ni aduɔ amɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my seeds rot in the ground before they even sprout when I plant early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ?

english: If seeds are planted in heavy, waterlogged soil before the soil warms up and drains properly, excess moisture suffocates the seed and causes fungi to rot it before it can sprout.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ dani shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ dani enyɛɔ ekwɛ̃ɔ.

english: How should I prepare my mud field so transplanted seedlings root quickly without failing?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ masaa ŋmɔ ni afee lɛ klon lɛ mli koni dumɔwui ni adu lɛ anyɛ atswa shishifãi oya ni nɔ ko akafee nɔ ko?

english: Puddling the soil—churning wet soil into soft mud—helps hold moisture, makes it easy for young roots to penetrate deep into the ground, and keeps weeds down.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii—ni agbalaa shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ awoɔ muji ni mli edɔ mli lɛ—yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi bibii ni amɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ oya. ni ojie jwɛi lɛ

english: How do I know if the first few rains mean the main rainy season has truly started for planting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔi fioo lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ eje shishi diɛŋtsɛ?

english: A single early rain can be a false start. It is best to wait until the soil stays moist for several days in a row so your seeds do not sprout and then dry up when the rain takes a break.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ afee amale shishijee. Ehi akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni odumɔwui lɛ akakwɛ̃ ni amɛkagbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa.

english: Can I still plant fast-growing crops if heavy rains fall late in October?
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ October naagbee gbɛ lɛ, ani manyɛ madu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lolo?

english: You can plant short-duration crops like vegetables or early-maturing beans, but you must be careful because the dry Harmattan season usually follows soon after and can cut off water before crops fully mature.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu be kukuoo mli nibii tamɔ aduawai loo ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya. Shi esa akɛ okwɛ ohe jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ, harmattan be ni egbi lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ. ni ebaanyɛ efo nu mli dani tsei lɛ adara kwraa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow when it rains almost every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Too much rain washes essential nutrients like nitrogen deep into the ground where roots cannot reach, and waterlogged soil prevents roots from breathing properly.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Ni sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the blossoms fall off my pepper plants when heavy rain hits them continuously?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni naa wa miinɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Heavy raindrops physically knock fragile flowers off the plant and wash away pollen, which stops the flowers from turning into fruits.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tswaa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ ni efoɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: What happens to my cassava roots if rainwater sits on my farm for many days without drying?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu hi miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni egbiko gbii babaoo?

english: Standing water starves the roots of air and encourages fungal rot, causing cassava tubers to soften, turn bad, and rot under the ground.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni ewo ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo, amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my young plantain suckers easily fall over after several days of heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Continuous rain makes the topsoil soft and mud-like, causing shallow roots to lose their grip on the ground when the plant gets heavy with water.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ fee blɛoo ni efee tamɔ sũ. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ wo muji shishi.

english: Why do dark spots and rot spread so quickly on my vegetable leaves during rainy periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji kɛ ŋmeii gbɛɔ eshwaa mi-vegetable baa lɛ nɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Fungal diseases love cool, wet conditions, and rainwater drops splash disease spores from leaf to leaf and from the soil onto the plant.
ga: Fungal helai sumɔɔ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli. Ni nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛjɛɔ baa nɔ kɛyaa baa nɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛyaa tso nɔ.

english: Is it good to harvest my cocoa pods right after a heavy downfall of rain?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaakpa kookoo ŋmeii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ?

english: It is better to wait until the weather clears because harvesting in wet weather spreads black pod disease spores across fresh cuts on the cocoa tree.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi kɔɔyɔŋ lɛ mli baatse ejaakɛ ŋmaakpamɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ mli lɛ baaha hela ni ji black pod hela lɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ agbɛ ashwã niji heei ni yɔɔ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ amli.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my crops when I see dark rain clouds coming?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli beni atatui diji miiba lɛ?

english: No, applying fertilizer right before a heavy downpour washes the expensive nutrients away into nearby streams before your crops can soak them up.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli nibii ni jara wa lɛ aya faai ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops whenever wet weather lasts for a week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be fɛɛ be ni hulutsoo be lɛ baaye otsi kome lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants with strong root systems that can consume water and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops during wet spells.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji maŋ tso ko ni yɔɔ shishifãi ni mli wa ni baanyɛ aŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for strong growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizers like urea or well-rotted poultry manure helps restore green leaves so the plant can produce large cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ ni mli wa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloi aŋmɔŋ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ awo ŋmeii wuji.

english: What is making holes in my young corn leaves and hiding inside the central funnel?
ga: Mɛni miiha bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ miitee amɛhe yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the plant's growing center to feed on tender leaves, so checking fields early and applying registered control methods early protects your yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ he lɛ koni amɛye baai bibii. No hewɔ lɛ, kwɛmɔ he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mra. kɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ nii ni aŋmala awo wolo nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why should I leave proper space between my cassava plants instead of planting them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ ni sa yɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing ensures each cassava plant has enough room to grow large, healthy roots underneath.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmei tso fɛɛ ŋmei tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni shishifãi wuji ni mli wa baakwɛ̃ yɛ shishi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their leaves during the dry Harmattan period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ baai babaoo fiteɔ yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed leaves during dry periods to reduce water loss from dry winds. Planting permanent shade trees on your farm and mulching around the roots helps hold soil moisture so trees survive the Harmattan.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni nu ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ daa ni ooodu yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni okɛ sũ awo he ni ebɔle he lɛ. Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni tso lɛ ahi shi yɛ harmattan mli.

english: How can I tell when my cassava roots are fully mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually mature when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, the soil base around the stem begins to crack, and testing a single tuber shows it is firm and full of starch, usually 9 to 12 months after planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ eda kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ bɔi fãmɔ. Ni yitso kome he kaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyi kɛ ashikishaŋ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of specific soil minerals like calcium and boron. Consistent watering at the roots and feeding the soil helps flowers set fruit properly.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo sũ mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ calcium kɛ boron ni bɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli daa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni akɛyeɔ niyenii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I work dried animal manure into my soil before planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Dried animal manure feeds the soil with essential plant nutrients, improves soil texture, and helps the ground hold water longer during dry weather, providing steady nutrition to your crops.
ga: Nuŋtsɔ ni egbi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ni eye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Ehaa oŋmɔshi nii lɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and becoming small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips or whiteflies that transmit plant viruses. Controlling these small insects early prevents leaf distortion and keeps plants growing normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. small insect control Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Ebaatsi baa lɛ sɛɛkuu naa ni eye ebua tsei ni amɛdara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why is it harmful to plant pepper on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmɔtɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously lets pest populations and soil-borne diseases build up in that field while depleting specific soil nutrients. Rotating with crops like cowpeas breaks pest cycles and restores soil nitrogen.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ baaha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ayibɔ aya hiɛ yɛ jɛmɛ yɛ be mli ni ehaa sũ mli niyenii komɛi baa shi. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ tsina ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ ni ehaa nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings wither and die when I water them during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Watering under hot afternoon sun heats up the soil water around fragile roots and causes water drops on leaves to scorch them like tiny magnifying glasses. It is always safest to water seedlings early in the morning or late in the afternoon.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ baaha nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ. Shishifãi ni waaa lɛ mli dɔɔ. ni eha nu ni hoɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ shã tamɔ glase bibii ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo. Ehi jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be akɛ oooha dumɔwui lɛ nu leebi loo shwane.

english: Why is it better for me to spray my crops or water them early in the morning around 7 AM instead of at noon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mafɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ loo mawo amɛ nu leebi aaafee ŋmɛji kpawo moŋ fe shwane?

english: In the early morning, temperatures are cool and the air is calm. This gives leaves time to absorb moisture and treatments properly before the strong afternoon heat causes water to evaporate or burns the leaves.
ga: Leebi lɛ, hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛbaaŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛtsu he nii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ ji dani shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi loo eshãa baai lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow much stronger when I remove weeds while they are still small rather than waiting for them to grow tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli wa waa kɛ́ mijie jwɛi lɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ moŋ fe ni mamɛ ni amɛdara lɛ?

english: Small weeds are easy to clear and haven't had time to steal much food or water from the soil. Waiting until weeds are large allows them to rob your crops of essential nutrients and sunlight.
ga: Jwɛi bibii lɛ agbemɔ waaa ni amɛbɛ be babaoo ni amɛkɛbaaju niyenii loo nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ omɛ ni jwɛi lɛ dara lɛ, ehaa amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ hulu la yɛ onibii amli.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants curl up tightly like tubes during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe tamɔ paipii yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is the plant's natural defense against heat. By curling up, the leaf reduces the surface area exposed to the sun and traps moisture, preventing the plant from drying out.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Curling haa baai lɛ anɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi, ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Tsĩ tsei anaa koni amɛkagbi

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers during hot dry spells before producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ dani ewoɔ pepper lɛ?

english: When pepper plants suffer from heat or water stress, they drop their flowers to save energy and stay alive rather than spending energy on growing fruits.
ga: Mɛɛ be hulutsoo loo nu he haomɔ haa pepper tso ko naa amanehulu? Ebaashɛ fɔfɔii ashwie shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite ni ehi wala mli moŋ fe ni ekɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛdu aduawai.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees next to my young cocoa trees on a new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu kookoo dumɔwui bibii yɛ ŋmɔ hee mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide crucial shade and keep the air moist, protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to come up when I bury them deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔɔ beni mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: A seed has only a small amount of stored energy. If planted too deep, it runs out of food before the sprout can reach the surface to catch sunlight, causing it to die underground.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ni ato. Kɛji adu mli tsɔ Niyenii lɛ baaho dani dumɔwui lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la. ha egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize turning yellow while the top leaves remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baa lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves mean the soil is low in nitrogen. The plant naturally steals nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new top leaves so it can keep growing.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baa heei koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Why do my yam plants produce massive leafy vines but only tiny tubers underneath the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ woɔ wain tsei ni baai wuji yɔɔ mli shi ŋmeii bibii pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil causes yams to put all their energy into growing stems and leaves above ground instead of sending nutrients down to build large underground tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛba shi koni ekɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants twisted with light green and yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Twisted yellow leaves are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. The disease stops the plant from making food, resulting in very small cassava roots.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Hela nɛɛ haaa tsei afee niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ daraaa kwraa.

english: Why do the bottoms of my ripening tomatoes turn dark, flat, and rotten while still on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ, efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni egboɔ be mli ni eyɔɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Dark rotten bottoms, called blossom-end rot, happen when tomato plants cannot draw enough calcium from the soil, which is usually caused by irregular watering patterns.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ su ni tsuɔ waa lɛ akɛ blossom end ŋmɔtɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense direct sunlight and heat. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa acts like a protective canopy, keeping the soil moist and shielding the fragile leaves until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ, ebaatsu nii akɛ hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ebuɔ baai ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa ni enáa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Will I get more cocoa pods if I pack as many cocoa trees into my land as possible?
ga: Ani maná kookoo ŋmeii babaoo kɛji mikɛ kookoo tsei babaoo wo mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔ ni manyɛ?

english: Planting trees too closely causes them to fight for sunlight, ground water, and soil food, which results in thin trees and fewer pods. Giving each tree proper spacing allows air to flow and branches to spread, leading to a much higher harvest.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni ŋmeii hu faaa. Kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko to he ko ni sa lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli ni eniji lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji kpamɔ ni fa babaoo kwraa.

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the tree before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in dark, humid conditions. Pruning excess leaves and clearing weeds around the base allows sunlight and wind to dry the farm, preventing the fungus from ruining the pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ojie jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ. Konii lɛ haa hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Etsiɔ ŋmeii anaa koni ekafite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut off the extra shoots growing out from the base of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ cacao tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Those extra shoots, called chupons, steal food and water from the main trunk without producing good fruit. Removing them focuses all the tree's energy into developing strong main branches and producing healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine nɛɛ, ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons lɛ, juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ mli ni ekɛ yibii kpakpa ko baaa. Kɛ́ ajieɔ lɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa niji titrii ni he wa lɛ anɔ ni eeefee kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: My cocoa tree produced plenty of small flowers, so why are most of them falling off without turning into pods?
ga: Mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo, no hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop extra flowers, but severe flower loss happens when the tree lacks water, missing soil nutrients, or when tiny insects that pollinate the flowers are missing. Keeping soil rich and watered helps more flowers become pods.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, cacao tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi krɛdɛɛi. Shi fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ waa lɛ baa kɛji nu bɛ tso lɛ mli. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii Pollinators lɛ laaje. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse ni nu yɔɔ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is lacking the food my cocoa trees need to grow strong?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni cacao tsei lɛ akwɛ̃?

english: When cocoa leaves turn yellow, growth slows down, or pods stay tiny, the soil is missing key nutrients. Adding organic manure or proper cocoa fertilizer feeds the soil so the tree can produce big, healthy pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, amɛdaraa blɛoo loo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa loo kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Can I plant cassava inside my mature cocoa farm to get extra food to sell?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ ko ni eda mli koni maná niyenii krokomɛi ni mikɛbaahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Planting heavy feeding food crops like cassava inside a mature cocoa farm damages the crop. Cassava roots steal water and nutrients from the soil, and its tall leaves block light, which reduces cocoa production.
ga: Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmei, ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji ni eda lɛ amli lɛ baafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Cassava shishifãi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ebaai ni kɛlɛ lɛ tsiɔ la lɛ naa Enɛ baaha kookoo ni afeɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do cocoa pods change color from green or red to bright yellow when they are ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru nɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse nɔ kɛ́ amɛfee klalo lɛ?

english: Color change is the plant's natural sign that the seeds inside are fully grown and rich in sugar. Harvesting when pods turn fully yellow or orange ensures the beans will ferment properly and yield good quality cocoa.
ga: Su tsakemɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli okadi ko ni tsɔɔ tso lɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ edara ni sugar eyi mli obɔ. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni ŋmeii lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ kwraa lɛ, ehaa kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa kookoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ baai babaoo fite yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is a protective habit cocoa trees use to save water when the weather gets dry and hot. Placing dried leaves or grass around the base of the trees helps trap soil moisture so the trees lose fewer leaves.
ga: Baai ni egbee shi lɛ ji su ko ni abuɔ cacao tsei lɛ ahe koni nu akafite kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ. Baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛaabɔle Tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo

english: What causes the leaves on my cocoa trees to get dry holes and look burned?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ bu ni egbi ni etamɔ nɔ ni eshã?

english: Dry holes and burned leaf edges are usually caused by sap-sucking insects like mirids (capsids). These pests attack young shoots and leaves, but maintaining proper farm shade and spraying recommended organic or chemical treatments keeps them under control.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mirids (capsids) lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni egbi kɛ baai lɛ ashãa lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ tutuaa tsei bibii kɛ baai. Shi hulutsoo be ni sa ni oookwɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsofai ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛbaatsu nii lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni amɛhi shi yɛ kudɔmɔ shishi.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have thin leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under direct sunlight. They need fast-growing shade crops like plantains planted alongside them to act as living umbrellas until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya, tamɔ tsei bibii ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni etsu nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka kɛyashi cacao tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen or too wet around the roots. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer or compost helps the leaves stay green and produce larger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: How do I know which direction to push my cassava stems into the soil when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni esa akɛ matsi ŋmei tso lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava stem cuttings should always be planted with the small buds pointing upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down forces the shoots to curve around, making the plant weak and reducing root growth.
ga: Esa akɛ adu fɔfɔii bibii ni afolɔ yɛ cassava mli lɛ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, ŋwɛi ni oootsɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ Dumɔ ni okɛ ohiɛ tsɔɔ shi lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ abɔle. Ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant before they can grow into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara ni amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers usually drop off when the weather gets extremely hot or when the plant experiences sudden drought. Keeping the soil consistently moist during flowering helps the blossoms turn into tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na hɔmɔ trukaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfɔ̃ yɛ tomato nɔ.

english: Is it helpful or harmful if I plant beans in the same field as my maize?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ baaba loo ebaaye mi awui kɛji midu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: It is very helpful because beans capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which naturally feeds the maize crop and keeps the land fertile.
ga: Amɛhe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa ejaakɛ ŋmeii mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmãa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves in full sunlight to feed the tubers growing underground. Staking holds the leaves high above weeds and off wet soil, preventing rot and fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ aha amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he koni eye ebua bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ jwɛi lɛ anɔ ni ejɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ naa.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my maize seeds immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara kɛha mi akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by several hot, dry days. Seeds that sprout after the first rain can easily dry up and die before the main, steady rains actually begin.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, gbii babaoo ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ agbi oya ni amɛgboi dani nugbɔ lɛ aya nɔ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily once they start growing big bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ amɛje shishi amɛfee ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that struggle to support heavy fruit during strong winds. Cutting off extra shoots around the main stem and piling soil around the base gives the plant stronger support.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtere tsɔne lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni ebɔle he lɛ Jiemɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ ni okɛ sũ lɛ ato he. Shishitoo lɛ baaha tso lɛ aye abua lɛ waa.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking juices from the undersides of leaves. Removing infected plants or spraying neem oil helps protect the rest of the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ loo akɛ neem fɔ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do people cover the ground around vegetable plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi kɛ jwɛi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛ aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, stops the hot sun from drying out the soil, keeps roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: Why do my groundnuts form their pods under the soil instead of growing on branches like tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts lɛ miifee pods yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ yɛ niji tamɔ tomato nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants flower above ground, but once pollinated, the flower stalks lengthen and push into the soil where the groundnut pods can safely mature away from sun heat and surface pests.
ga: Peanut tsei fɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛ́ afee pollination lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bean pods lɛ baanyɛ adara shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do other farmers say planting groundnuts makes the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha mi ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which naturally captures nitrogen gas from the air and stores it in the soil through their roots, acting as a natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, emɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How do I know the exact right time to dig up my groundnuts so they do not rot in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii? Koni ŋmeii lɛ akafite yɛ sũ lɛ mli?

english: Groundnuts are ready to harvest when the leaves turn yellowish, and when you open a few sample pods, the inside shell wall shows dark vein patterns rather than being plain white.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa kɛji baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Ni kɛ́ ogbele sample pods komɛi lɛ, ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli gbogboi lɛ jieɔ line ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ kpo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee eyɛŋ kwraa.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is healthy enough to support crops this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Healthy farm soil is usually dark in color, crumbles easily in your hand, holds moisture well without staying waterlogged, and has living organisms like earthworms present.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kpakpai amli lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni nu bɛ mli Ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow even though it rains regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant lacks vital nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil is waterlogged and drowning the plant roots, preventing them from taking up nutrients.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu eyi sũ lɛ mli obɔ ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ mii miiho nu. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii mli hewalɛ

english: Why do my crop leaves curl up or droop during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants curl or droop their leaves during peak afternoon heat to reduce their surface exposure to the sun and save water from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Tsei lɛ baabɔle amɛhe loo amɛbaagbee shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ koni hulu la ni shɛɔ amɛhe lɛ aba shi ni nu lɛ akatsɔ oya tsɔ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants adapted to survive harsh conditions, allowing their seeds to sprout rapidly and consume available soil nutrients and water before crops get established.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Enɛ haa amɛdumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛyeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu ni yɔɔ momo lɛ mli dani tsei lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: I only have a small plot of land; how can I get the highest harvest possible from it?
ga: Shikpɔŋ bibioo ko pɛ miyɔɔ. Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ mli?

english: You can maximize a small plot by practicing intercropping—growing two complementary crops like corn and beans together—and planting in precise rows to give every plant adequate light and soil nutrients.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha he bibioo ko aya hiɛ babaoo kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni ooofee lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛhe, tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ nɔ. ni adu yɛ sɛɛkuu mli bɔni afee ni tso fɛɛ tso aná la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: What happens if I plant my crop seeds very close together to fit more into my field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa koni ekɛ mihe lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: Planting seeds too close forces plants to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak, thin stalks that produce tiny or no yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo loo amɛwoɔ yibii ko kwraa.

english: Why shouldn't I just save and plant the maize seeds I harvested last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikpa nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ toɔ ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds from high-yield commercial varieties lose their vigor and yield potential in the second generation, leading to unequal plant growth, smaller cobs, and weaker pest resistance.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahereɔ kɛjɛɔ jarayeli nibii ni woɔ yibii babaoo amli lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo nyɛmɔ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Cob lɛ ji bibioo fe no. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my old cocoa trees stop producing as many pods as they used to?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso momo lɛ ekpa ŋmeii babaoo ni ewoɔ tamɔ tsutsu lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees grow older—usually past 25 to 30 years—their natural productivity drops significantly, and their roots become less effective at taking up nutrients from the soil.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ eda Yɛ wala be fɛɛ mli (bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni fe afii 25 kɛyashi 30) lɛ, kookoo tso lɛ yibiiwoo ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ baa shi waa. Ni cacao tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it good practice to cut down old cocoa trees when I want to replant my farm?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tsei momoi beni miisumɔ ni madu amɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yes, cutting down old or non-producing cocoa trees clears space and nutrients for healthy new seedlings, allowing you to restart a strong, productive harvest cycle.
ga: Hɛɛ, cacao tsei ni egbɔ loo ni wooo yibii lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa gbɛ kɛ niyenii haa dumɔwui heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Eye ebua bo ni obɔi ŋmaakpamɔ be ni mli wa ni woɔ yibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does the extension officer advise cutting down healthy-looking cocoa trees next to diseased ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ afolɔ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Tso ni hela emɔ lɛ?

english: Diseases like cocoa swollen shoot spread invisibly through roots and mealybugs. Cutting surrounding trees creates a buffer zone that stops the disease from wiping out the rest of your farm.
ga: Helai tamɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ gbɛ ni anaaa nɔ kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi kɛ mealybugs nɔ. tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Ehaa buffer zone ni tsiɔ helai anaa koni ekafite oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and burn when there are no big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight. Without shade trees to filter the sun, the tender leaves scorch and cannot make food properly.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he waa. Kɛji tsei bɛ ni baatsi hulu la lɛ naa lɛ Baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhoo nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do shade trees help my cocoa farm during the long dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli?

english: Shade trees act as a natural blanket, keeping the soil cool, reducing moisture evaporation from the ground, and protecting cocoa trees from harsh dry winds.
ga: Shade tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi. ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni mli egbi lɛ he.

english: Why do I need to trim or prune extra branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ loo mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata he kɛjɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches, letting air and sunlight inside the canopy. This prevents damp conditions that cause black pod disease and helps the tree focus its energy on growing pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ahi ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli. Koni akafee ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ maa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: What happens to my cocoa trees if I plant them too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When planted too close, cocoa trees fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, causing them to grow thin and tall with very few pods while allowing diseases to spread easily between branches.
ga: Kɛ adu Cocoa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛkwɛɔ ni ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa helai gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei niji ateŋ mlɛo.

english: Why do cocoa trees drop many of their young flowers during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall increases humidity, which encourages fungal diseases like black pod that destroy delicate flower cushion buds before they can develop into pods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaha hulutsoo be lɛ aya hiɛ. Enɛ woɔ ŋmeii helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji ni fiteɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava on the same plot right after clearing old cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie ŋmei tsei momo lɛ?

english: While cassava grows well on cleared land, it competes aggressively for soil nutrients and light, so it must be spaced far away from young cocoa seedlings to avoid stunting their growth.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni gbɛ yɔɔ moŋ, Shi amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ la mli lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ cacao tsei bibii ahe koni ekɛtsi edalɛ naa.

english: Why do cocoa trees start flowering after a short dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi yɛ be kukuoo ko ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Mild dry stress signals to the cocoa tree that weather conditions are changing, triggering it to burst into flower so pods can form once rainy weather returns.
ga: Haomɔ ni mli egbi fioo lɛ tsɔɔ kookoo tso lɛ akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ miitsake. Wo cacao tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ bɔni afee ni pods lɛ afee kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow and stop growing when there is no rain for two weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛko otsii enyɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow during dry spells because water carries vital nutrients from the soil up into the plant. Without enough water, the plant starves and slows down its growth to conserve energy.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli ejaakɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Tsei lɛ hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni amɛhaa amɛdalɛ baa shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: How can I tell if my crops are getting too much water or not enough water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu babaoo loo amɛnáaa nu bɔ ni sa?

english: When crops lack water, their leaves wilt, curl, or dry up. When they receive too much water, the leaves turn pale yellow and the roots rot underground because waterlogged soil prevents them from breathing.
ga: Kɛ nu bɛ tsei lɛ Baai lɛ baagbi, amɛbaakpã, loo amɛbaagbi kɛji amɛná nu babaoo. Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa amɛmuɔ.

english: Why do I need to walk through and check my crop field early every morning instead of visiting once a week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔ mli ni makwɛ ŋmɔji lɛ amli daa leebi maŋkpa lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooyasara shikome yɛ otsi mli lɛ?

english: Pests and crop diseases spread very quickly in warm weather. Inspecting your field daily helps you catch early warning signs, such as chewed leaves or fungal spots, before they destroy your entire farm.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ daa gbi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii mra, tamɔ baai ni ashɛre loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Dani ebaafite oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with big green leaves but produce only tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi eyɛ yitso bibioo Shikpɔŋ shishi pɛ

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, the plant uses all its strength to build big leaves above ground instead of storing food in the roots to make large tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tso lɛ kɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛfeɔ bulbs agboi.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress caused by extreme heat, irregular watering, or lack of insect pollination, saving their remaining energy to survive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli baa lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ni bɛ Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ baa shi kɛha wala.

english: Why do my young vegetable crops bend and lean towards one side as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ amɛhe shi kɛyaa he kome beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Crops naturally stretch and lean toward the direct sunlight because they need light energy to manufacture their own food through their leaves.
ga: Tsei lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná la hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛbaai lɛ afee niyenii.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow weak and thin when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crowded crops fight each other for light, soil nutrients, and moisture, resulting in weak, skinny plants with small cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dense plants lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ŋmɔtɔ bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests when I plant maize in the exact same field every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and soil diseases to build up in that field over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai babaoo buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do leaf-eating caterpillars appear on my cabbage plants right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-cabbage tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The moisture and warm temperatures following early rains create ideal conditions for moths to lay eggs on tender young leaves, which quickly hatch into hungry caterpillars.
ga: Fɛ̃i kɛ latsaa ni mli edɔ yɛ leebi nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ ha shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ba kɛha ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛwui awo baai bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anɔ. ni baatsɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ oya.

english: How do weeds hurt my tomato plants even if I give the tomatoes enough water?
ga: Te jwɛi yeɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal sunlight, soil nutrients, and root space away from your tomato plants, reducing the size and quality of your tomatoes.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ oya kɛjɛɔ tomato tso lɛ mli Ehaa tomato lɛ dalɛ kɛ ekpakpafeemɔ baa shi.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants lack nitrogen, which is a key food they need from the soil, or that the soil is too waterlogged, suffocating the roots. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and wrinkle during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl up to protect themselves from losing too much water in extreme heat, or because small insects like thrips and aphids are sucking the sap from underneath the leaves. Regular watering and spraying neem oil can protect the plants.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite babaoo yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Aloo akɛni kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips kɛ aphids miimu nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ wo tso lɛ nɔ daa ni akɛshwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ebu tso lɛ he.

english: Why do you advise me to plant my crops in straight lines instead of scattering the seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okɛɔ akɛ madu tsei yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines with proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without competing with its neighbours. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much easier for you.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ ni gbɛ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ yeee akaŋ. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo.
