english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy that feeds the growing tuber under the ground. Staking lifts the vines off the damp soil, preventing leaf rot diseases and ensuring the plant gets maximum light to build bigger yams.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni haa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aba. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsi baa ni fiteɔ lɛ naa ni oha tsei lɛ la babaoo koni amɛwo sweet potato agbo.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense daylight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to your young cocoa provides a protective cover, keeping the air humid and shielding the tender leaves until the cocoa roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei ahe lɛ, ebaaha abu he. Kwɛmɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ ni obu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ baaná shishifãi ni mli kwɔ.

english: Can I plant cowpeas and maize in the same field, or will they spoil each other?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ loo amɛbaafite?

english: Planting cowpeas and maize together is actually very good for your farm. Cowpeas gather nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps the maize grow stronger while ground cover prevents weeds.
ga: Tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni ooodu yɛ ekomefeemɔ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔ lɛ. Cowpeas buaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ buɔ he kɛjɛɔ jwɛi ahe.

english: How does putting dried poultry manure into my soil help my cassava yield better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kooloi ashishifã ni egbi ni akɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmei shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Poultry manure adds rich nutrients like nitrogen and organic matter to the soil. It improves the soil's ability to hold moisture and stay soft, allowing cassava roots to expand easily into large tubers.
ga: Kooloi ashishifãi kɛ niyenii kpakpai tamɔ nitrogen kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ehiɔ shi blɛoo. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why shouldn't I just save and plant maize seeds from my last harvest for the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni jɛ naagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni miduɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds from hybrid maize varieties lose their strength in the next generation, producing uneven plants and smaller cobs. Fresh certified seeds give you strong, disease-resistant plants that yield much more grain.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmãa srɔtoi ni akɛfee ŋmãa mli lɛ baafite hewalɛ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ ekome kɛ ŋmei bibioo ko. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ baaha tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba. Te shi owo helai ni okɛ dumɔwui babaoo awo.

english: How can I tell that my groundnuts under the soil are fully ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ he kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Groundnuts are ready when the plant's leaves turn yellow and begin to drop. You can pull up one test plant; if the inside of the pods has dark brown markings and the seeds fill out the shell completely, it is time to harvest.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii efee klalo kɛ́ tso lɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbɔi shwiemɔ. Obaanyɛ ogbala kaa nitsumɔhe kome kɛya ŋwɛi. Kɛji pod lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ eyi lɛ, be eshɛɛ ni abaakpa.

english: Why do my dried maize grains turn into white powder after sitting in the barn for a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei ni egbi lɛ batsɔ powda yɛŋ beni mita ŋmɔ lɛ mli nyɔji fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Small insects called grain weevils burrow inside dry maize kernels and eat them from the inside out, leaving behind dusty powder. Thoroughly drying the maize and storing it in airtight bags or sealed containers prevents these pests from damaging your harvest.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ seed moths lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ nii kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ, ni amɛshiɔ sũ amɛshwieɔ amɛsɛɛ. Kɛ́ ogbi o-corn lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛto kotokui loo tsɛnsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow mainly because the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the essential food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer gives the crop the boost it needs.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ titri ejaakɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ahiamɔ nii aya hiɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and stopping the fruits from growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi yibii lɛ anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck the sap from under the leaves. Spraying the plants with neem oil or soapy water helps clear the insects so the leaves can expand and feed the growing fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo nu ni mli edɔ shwie tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe kooloi bibii koni baai lɛ anyɛ alɛɛ mli ni eye ebua aduawai ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my growing tomatoes turn black and rotten while still on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni miida lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ be mli ni eyɔɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This black spot is caused by irregular watering, which stops the plant from absorbing calcium from the soil. Watering your tomatoes evenly and regularly, rather than letting the soil dry out completely between waterings, prevents this rot.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Okɛ nu awo tomato mli daa ni ekɛ nu awo mli pɛpɛɛpɛ Moŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi kwraa yɛ nu ni ooowo lɛ teŋ. Ebaaye ebua ni akafite.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground during the wet season before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long in heavy soil, suffocating the roots and causing soil germs to attack. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa amɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many flowers, but most of them fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo gbeeɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ pods?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when the tree suffers from heat stress, lack of soil moisture, or insect attacks. Keeping light shade trees nearby and protecting the farm from sucking insects helps flowers stay on the branches and develop into pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kooloi tutuamɔ Ehaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ ahe, ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ tsei aniji anɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak with small yields when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ mli tseee ni ebɛ hewalɛ shi ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too tightly, they fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room and food to grow thick stems and produce big yields.
ga: Beni tsei eyi obɔ lɛ Tsei wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ tsei ni mli tse ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during heavy rains even when the wind is soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ miitswa blɛoo po lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall easily when tiny microscopic worms called nematodes destroy the underground root system, leaving the tree with no anchor. Using clean planting material and adding organic compost creates strong roots that hold the plant firm.
ga: Ewaaa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ fite shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Feemɔ tso lɛ ni ŋwɛi ŋta bɛ he Kɛ okɛ dumɔ nibii ni he tse tsu nii ni okɛ organic compost fata he lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi ni wa ni haa tso lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ lɛ aba.

english: Why do my harvested yams start growing sprouts and becoming soft while stored in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo kɛji akɛ akɛto mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally start sprouting when exposed to heat and light because they think it is time to grow a new crop. Storing yams in a cool, dark, and well-ventilated barn slows down sprouting and keeps them firm for market.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ baaje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo kɛ la he ejaakɛ amɛsusuɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛdu tso hee. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ sweet potato ato he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni yɔɔ duŋ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli. Enɛ baaha amɛshweremɔ aya hiɛ fioo ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ jara nɔ.

english: Why is it risky to plant my seeds after the very first rain instead of waiting for the main rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ moŋ fe ni ooomɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ?

english: The very first rain is often followed by a long dry stretch, which bakes the soil and kills newly sprouted seeds. Waiting until the rains fall consistently ensures the young roots stay moist and keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ashã ni egbe dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ. Kɛ́ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaya nɔ anɛ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi bibii lɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans on my land make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aaadu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special plants that pull natural fertilizer directly from the air and trap it in their roots. When the crop is harvested and the roots rot, that natural food stays in the soil to nourish your next crop.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛŋmɛɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni shishifãi lɛ egbo Nakai adebɔɔ mli niyenii lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my fruit pods turn soft and fall off the tree after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi aduawai lɛ ahe tsɔi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When heavy rain or high moisture sits on developing fruits for too long, it creates a perfect environment for fungal diseases. The moisture weakens the outer skin of the fruit, causing it to rot, soften, and drop off before harvest.
ga: Beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa loo eyɛ hulutsoo be babaoo tsɔ. Ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai baa. Fɛ̃i haa tso yibii lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni ehaa egboɔ, efeɔ blɛoo ni egbeeɔ shi dani akpaa.

english: How can I stop wet soil from rotting my low-hanging fruits?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ akafite aduawai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: You can stake plants to lift low branches off the ground, prune lower leaves to keep fruits away from damp dirt, and place dry grass mulch around the base to stop muddy water from splashing onto the crop.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tso lɛ awo he ko ni ewo niji ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ofolɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ koni aduawai lɛ akashɛ muji ni mli efɔ he. ni ekɛ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛfee tsɔne lɛ bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ he koni nu ni mli ewo muji akashwie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my vegetables get watery spots when the air feels damp and warm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ náa nu he hei be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ?

english: High humidity prevents water from evaporating quickly off plant surfaces. When water droplets stay on leaves and fruits in warm weather, bacteria and fungi easily enter the crop tissues and cause soft rot spots.
ga: Nu ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haaa nu akajɛ tso lɛ nɔ oya. Beni nu shwieɔ shi yɛ baai kɛ aduawai anɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Muawai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai boteɔ tso lɛ mli oya ni ekɛ hei ni fiteɔ baa.

english: Why is it important for wind and air to blow freely through my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atswa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Good air movement quickly dries wet leaves and fruits after rain, which stops fungal diseases from spreading. It also supplies fresh air for plant growth and keeps the crop canopy cool.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ baaha baai ni efɔ kɛ aduawai agbi oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ kpaa. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hu haa tsei lɛ adalɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Does wind shaking my young crops harm them or make them stronger?
ga: Ani kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni tswaa midumɔwui lɛ miiye mi awui loo eeha amɛhe wa?

english: Gentle wind that moves plants slightly is actually good because it signals the stem to grow thicker and stronger to support heavy fruits later. However, very strong winds require windbreak trees to prevent breaking branches.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli jɔ ni tswaa tsei lɛ fioo lɛ ŋɔɔ waa diɛŋtsɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehe wa koni ewo yibii ni tsii yɛ sɛɛ mli. Shi kɛlɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa waa lɛ biɔ ni atsi tsei ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ he koni tsei aniji akakumɔ.

english: Why do some farmers put electric fans or air vents inside seed nurseries?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ tsɔne ni akɛtswaa la loo tsɔnei ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli lɛ woɔ amɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: In enclosed nursery sheds or greenhouses, fans keep the air moving so dampness does not build up on tender seedlings. The gentle movement also strengthens stems and lowers the heat inside.
ga: Yɛ ŋmɔ mli loo ŋmɔ ni agbe naa lɛ mli Fan lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya nɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ akabua ehe naa yɛ dumɔwui ni mli tse lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akɛ enyiɛ mlɛo lɛ, ehaa tsɔne lɛ mli dɔlɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why do some of my fruit trees shed their own inner branches naturally?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ ekomɛi aniji shwieɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ?

english: Trees shed inner branches that do not receive sunlight because those branches consume more energy than they produce. This natural self-pruning allows the tree to save nutrients for outer branches that bear fruit.
ga: Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛmli niji ni hulu la shɛɛɛ amɛnɔ lɛ ejaakɛ nakai niji lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii fe nɔ ni amɛfeɔ lɛ. Adebɔɔ mli tsei ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha kponɔgbɛ niji ni woɔ yibii lɛ.

english: How does trimming excess leaves from my trees help produce better fruits?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua lɛ ni ewo yibii kpakpai?

english: Pruning extra leaves lets sunlight and fresh air reach the inner parts of the tree. It directs the plant's food and water straight into growing bigger, healthier fruits instead of useless foliage.
ga: Baai ni afoɔ lɛ krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ mli. Ekudɔɔ tso lɛ niyenii kɛ nu lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ewo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ fe baai ni he ehiaaa.

english: Why do fruits hidden deep inside dense branches stay small or fail to ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ni akɛtee niji ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ shɔŋŋ lɛ ji bibii loo amɛshɛko lɛ?

english: Fruits need sunlight and good air flow to develop color, sugar, and size. Dense leaves shade the fruit, trap moisture, and attract pests that damage the crop.
ga: Yibii he miihia hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni tsɔɔ mli koni ená su, su ni tsuɔ kɛ dalɛ. Baai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa aduawai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni egbalaa kooloi ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: What causes unripe fruits to fall off my trees long before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa aduawai ni eshɛko lɛ shwieɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ dani kpamɔ be baashɛ?

english: Unripe fruit drop is usually caused by water stress, poor nutrient levels in the soil, insect damage, or fungal rot caused by excess humidity trapped inside the tree canopy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu he haomɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ aduawai ni eshɛko shi lɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii, kooloi ni fiteɔ nii, loo ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize plants need to build food and grow strong. It can also happen when heavy rains wash nutrients deep into the ground where roots cannot reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa ŋmãa tsei koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa tree flowers dropping off without producing any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ ko lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when they are not pollinated by beneficial insects like midges, or when the tree suffers from heat stress. Keeping shade trees on your farm maintains cool humidity that protects flowers and attracts pollinators.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ midge lɛ eshɛɛɛ amɛhe, loo kɛ́ tso lɛ naa dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Kɛ́ okwɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo ni buɔ fɔfɔi ahe ni egbalaa ŋmeii ni baa fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil for too long because of poor drainage. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: What causes small holes and ragged edges on my young maize leaves right in the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Ni ŋmeii ni ekpɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This chewing damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the leafy funnel of the plant. Applying recommended biological controls or safe remedies directly into the leaf funnel early stops them from killing the plant.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei ahe baai amli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii nɛɛ baa. Kɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akudɔ loo tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe awo baa lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ akagbe tso lɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas alongside my maize help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cowpea plants trap natural nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, acting as a natural food source for the nearby maize. Their leaves also cover the soil, keeping it moist and stopping weeds from taking over.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe kɛha ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ. Baai lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo. Enɛ haa efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during strong wind even when they look full of green leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni baai eyi mli obɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall over when tiny pests called nematodes or banana weevils eat away the underground roots, destroying the plant's anchor. Using clean planting suckers and adding organic manure strengthens the root system.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji kooloi bibii ni ale amɛ akɛ nematodes loo banana moths lɛ yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi. efiteɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi Kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ mli nu ni he tse tsu nii ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomato fruits turning black and rotten while still hanging on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ be mli ni amɛkã wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit when watering is irregular. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant transport calcium from the ground into the fruit smoothly.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ amli kɛ́ afɔɔ amɛ nu be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛjieɔ calcium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa aduawai lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants twisting and curling upward into small tight cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ baai lɛ anɔ ni abɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Curled leaves are usually a sign that tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids are feeding on the leaves, or transmitting a plant virus. Controlling these insects early protects the plant's ability to produce peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids miiye baai lɛ loo amɛmiihiɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baaye abua ni abu tso lɛ nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛbaafee chili ŋmɔtɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do some of my seed yams fail to sprout in the ground while others grow very fast?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi kwɛɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu daraa oya waa lɛ?

english: Yams enter a natural resting phase called dormancy after harvest. If seed yams are planted before this resting phase finishes, or if the soil is too dry and hot, they will wait or rot instead of sprouting.
ga: Sweet potatoes boteɔ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ adu sweet potato dumɔwui dani nɛkɛ wɔɔhe be nɛɛ ba naagbee, loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni edɔ Ebaamɛ loo ebaagbo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ̃.

english: Seeds should only be planted after the soil receives two or three steady rains that soak deep into the ground. Planting after just one light shower tricks the seeds into sprouting, but the heat will dry them out before the next rain comes.
ga: Esa akɛ adu dumɔwui beni shikpɔŋ lɛ ená nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni yaa nɔ ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ fioo ko sɛɛ shikome pɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baabɔi kwɛ̃mɔ. Shi latsaa lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi dani nugbɔ lɛ anɛ.

english: How do I know that my maize crop is fully ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ eshɛ kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the leaves turn completely brown and dry, and the kernels become hard with a tiny black mark visible at their base where they attach to the cob.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kwraa ni amɛgbi lɛ. ni dumɔwui lɛ wa ni amɛyɛ okadi bibii diji. Ejeɔ kpo yɛ shishigbɛ he ni akɛ cob lɛ fĩɔ lɛ.

english: How can I protect my harvested beans from insects without using expensive chemicals?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-beans ni mikpa lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ahe ni mikɛ tsofai ni jara wa tsuuu nii?

english: You can mix dry, clean wood ash or dried powdered neem leaves with your fully dried beans and store them in airtight containers. This prevents insects like weevils from breathing and laying eggs in the seeds.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tso sũ ni he tse ni egbi loo neem baa ni egbi afutu ŋmeii ni egbi kwraa ni okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli. Enɛ ji koni akamu ni amɛkawo ŋmeii yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper plants keep dropping their flowers instead of turning them into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they suffer from stress, usually caused by extremely hot weather, improper watering, or a lack of insects like bees to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie fɔfɔi kɛji amɛhao. Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. nu ni esaaa loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni baawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ ni bɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow before it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the soil lacks nutrients like nitrogen or the plant is experiencing drought. However, if it happens right before harvest, it is normal as the plant directs its food energy into growing the tubers below ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo tso lɛ miiye hɔmɔ. Shi, kɛji akɛ enɛ ba dani kpamɔ lɛ, Enɛ ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa ejaakɛ tsei kɛ niyenii hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my plantain leaves dry up and droop during the harmattan dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The harsh harmattan wind sucks moisture out of large plantain leaves very quickly. The plant purposefully droops its leaves to reduce its surface area exposed to the dry air and conserve water.
ga: Harmatta kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ plantain baai agboi lɛ amli oya. Tsei tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛha he ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu nu he.

english: Why should I wait instead of planting my maize immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ moŋ fe ni madu ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell. If you plant too early, the hot soil dries out, killing the young seedlings before the main rainy season fully establishes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ baagbi. Kpatamɔ tsei bibii lɛ ahiɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aje shishi.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow small and twisted instead of big and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni egbɛ eshwa moŋ fe ni eeefee agbo ni eja lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, deep, and soft soil to expand properly. If the soil is hard, shallow, or compacted, the growing tuber struggles to push through and becomes bent, small, or deformed.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni egbɛ eshwa jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, ekɔɔɔ he eko, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, bulb ni miida lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni etsɔ mli ni ebɔle ehe. bibioo loo ehiii

english: Why do experienced farmers plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same farm with maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ duɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni amɛduɔ ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to the legume family, which naturally grabs nitrogen from the air and puts it into the soil, acting as a natural food supply that helps the maize grow bigger.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli. Nɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why does letting weeds grow around my crops reduce the final yield I get at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ oŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ haa naagbee yibiiwoo ni minine shɛɔ nɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ baa shi?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm; they aggressively steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crops, leaving the crops weak and unable to produce high yields.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why shouldn't I save grains from my market crop to use as seeds for the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmaa ni jɛ jara nɔ lɛ toɔ koni mikɛtsu nii akɛ dumɔwui kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from market harvests lose their vigor and disease resistance over time, leading to lower yields, whereas fresh certified seeds are specially produced to resist pests and produce a heavy harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ jara nɔ nibii ni akpaa lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ kɛ helai ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi. Yɛ be mli ni afeɔ dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient in the soil. It can also happen when heavy rains wash away soil nutrients or when weeds compete with the maize for food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ loo kɛ́ jwɛi kɛ ŋmãa miitswa akaŋ koni amɛye niyenii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize in the same spot every season continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the dirt. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ajɛ sũ lɛ mli aba be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why shouldn't I spread fertilizer right before a heavy downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shi dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes the fertilizer away off the top of the field before the soil can absorb it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the ground is damp, but not during heavy rains, so crop roots can take up the nutrients.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔji amli ŋmɔshi nibii dani shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ana niyenii mli hewalɛ

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Most cassava varieties are ready between 8 to 12 months after planting. You will know it is ready when the lower leaves dry up and fall off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to crack as the tubers swell underground.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo efee klalo kɛha dumɔ yɛ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Obaale akɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Is it really necessary to support my yam vines with tall wooden stakes?
ga: Ani ehe miihia diɛŋtsɛ ni akɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ ni akɛfee sweet potato wain tsei lɛ atsu nii?

english: Yes, staking lifts the yam leaves off the hot ground and helps them catch maximum sunlight. Yam plants that receive good sunlight produce much larger and heavier tubers than plants left trailing on the ground.
ga: Hɛɛ, staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni hulu tsoɔ yɛ lɛ, ni ehaa amɛnáa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Sweet potato tsei ni hulu la kpakpa shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ baawo bulbs ni dara kwraa ni etsii fe tsei ni ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: How many suckers should I allow to grow around my main plantain tree?
ga: Esa akɛ maŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii enyiɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ ehe? Midumɔwu titri lɛ

english: You should keep only two or three healthy suckers of different heights alongside the main tree. Allowing too many suckers to grow steals food and water from the main plant, resulting in small, lightweight plantain bunches.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛlɛ srɔtoi lɛ ato tso titri lɛ masɛi. Ha ŋmeii babaoo aju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Enɛ haa plantain tsei bibii ni tsiimɔ waaa lɛ baa.

english: Why are my green cocoa pods turning black and rotting on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in wet, damp conditions. Clearing weeds, pruning excess cocoa branches, and letting sunshine reach the pods keeps them dry and prevents the rot.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. weeding Kookoo niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ ni ahaa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe Ehaa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaaa amɛfite.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences high heat stress or a lack of water. When it gets too hot or dry, the plant drops its flowers to save energy and moisture to keep itself alive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa loo nu ni bɛ. Kɛji edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ tsɔ Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he koni amɛhi shi.

english: What is making small holes in my young maize leaves with dirt like sawdust inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-baby corn baai lɛ miifee bu bibii? Ni muji tamɔ ŋmei yɛ ŋmei ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the growing center shoot of the maize. Applying approved treatments directly into the central shoot early in the morning or evening helps kill the pest before it ruins the yield.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii ni miida lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ wo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ dani efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and twisting tightly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe waa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips sucking sap from the leaves. Spraying the plants early with insecticidal soap or recommended crop protection products stops the pests from destroying the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Akɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi loo nibii ni akɛbuɔ tsei ahe ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛbaatsu nii lɛ ashwie tsei anɔ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akafite baai lɛ.

english: Officer, why should I plant plantains on the same land with my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ mi kookoo dumɔwui heei lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct heat from the hot sun. Plantain trees grow very fast and have large leaves that create shade and hold moisture, acting as natural umbrellas to protect the tender cocoa trees while they get established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo baa ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni buɔ kokoo tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe be mli ni aduɔ amɛ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up to catch as much sunlight as possible to produce food for the tuber growing under the soil. Lifting the leaves off the bare ground also prevents wet soil diseases from rotting the plant.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ haaa tso lɛ afite.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize farm turning yellowish instead of healthy green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ fɛfɛo najiaŋ lɛ?

english: When maize leaves start turning yellow from the center out, it is usually a sign that the soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for green leaf growth. Applying a nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure will restore their green color.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baa lɛ je shishi etsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ miiho. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloi aŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha eŋɔli lɛ su lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do you officers advise me to plant groundnuts or beans on my plot after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily and leaves the soil weak. Legumes like groundnuts and beans have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and feed it back into the soil, naturally restoring soil fertility for your next crop.
ga: Abele haa kooloi babaoo niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it wrong for me to spread fertilizer on my crop field when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ejaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baashwie miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ be mli ni mikɛfeee nakai lɛ? He ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Crop roots cannot eat solid fertilizer; they can only drink it when it dissolves in water. Putting fertilizer on dry ground keeps it sitting on top where hot weather can evaporate it, or it can burn the plant roots when rain finally drops.
ga: Tso shishifãi nyɛŋ aye ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛnu kɛji akɛ etsɔ nu mli pɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hiɔ ŋwɛi he ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ mli lɛ. Aloo ebaanyɛ eha tsei shishifãi ashã kɛ́ naagbee lɛ nugbɔ nɛ.

english: What is causing small worms to chew inside the funnel leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Mikɛ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ a-cone baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Those worms are Fall Armyworms, which hatch from eggs laid by small moths. They hide deep inside the central whorl of the maize plant to eat soft leaves; spraying safe recommended control agents or neem water early in the morning reaches them best.
ga: Kplukai lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ni fɔɔ lɛ amli. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ he ŋaa akɛ akɛbaatsu nii loo neem nu lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe fɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers sudden water stress or extreme heat. If the soil goes from very wet to very dry, the plant drops its flowers to save water for its own survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu he haomɔ loo hulutsoo ni naa wa trukaa lɛ na tso lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ waa mli kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto nu kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛshihilɛ.

english: What will happen if I plant my cassava cuttings very close to each other to save space?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he koni mikɛha he ko akafee nɔ ko?

english: If cassava plants are too close, their roots will fight underground for water and soil nutrients, while their leaves block sunlight from each other. This results in tall, thin bushes with tiny tubers instead of large, heavy roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni ebaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe Enɛ haa anáa jwɛi kakadaŋŋ agbo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shishifãi wuji ni tsii yɔɔ mli lɛ najiaŋ.

english: How do I know that my cassava tubers are ready for harvesting so they do not spoil in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa? No hewɔ lɛ, egbooo yɛ sũ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting when the lower main leaves turn yellow and drop off. Leaving them in the ground too long—especially during heavy rainy seasons—makes the tubers woody, watery, and prone to underground rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni baai titrii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Ni aaashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ afee tsei, nu ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow stunted and weak even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and are aggressive; they steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. Removing weeds early leaves all the soil nutrients and water available strictly for your crops to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ basabasa. Amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaadu nii yɛ mli lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ahi shikpɔŋ kɛ nu lɛ mli koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Maize plants move available nitrogen to top new growth when soil runs low, so applying nitrogen fertilizer early helps keep the plant green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa dalɛ hee mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ faaa. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli mra. Ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or beans makes my soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei dumɔ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have special root nodules that grab nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, leaving natural plant food behind for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes expensive fertilizer away from your plants into gutters and streams before the crop's roots can soak it in.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli kɛyaa nubui kɛ faai amli dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves but produce tiny tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi e-tuber lɛ ji bibioo lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much shade or excessive nitrogen, it spends all its energy producing leaves and stems instead of sending food down to build thick storage roots.
ga: Kɛji ŋmei ná hulutsoo babaoo loo nitrogen babaoo Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye ní kɛ yaa si konɛ e pee sisi nɛ mi wa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when weather gets extremely hot or when soil moisture swings from very dry to very wet, causing stress that prevents the flower from setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ waa nɔ. Enɛ kɛ haomɔ ni haa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo yibii baa.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout when I plant them in dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds need water to swell, break open their outer shell, and start growing. Without soil moisture, seeds remain dormant or wither and die.
ga: Nu he miihia dumɔwui koni amɛfu. Gbalamɔ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ. ni ebɔi shweremɔ Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baakã he ahi shi. loo egbi ni egbo

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in dark, humid environments. Pruning cocoa branches to let sunlight in helps keep pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni duŋ yɔɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kookoo tsei ni afoɔ koni hulu la babaoo abote mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: What is eating holes in my young maize leaves and leaving green dirt in the center shoot?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni ayeɔ yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli ni ashiɔ muji eŋɔli yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ?

english: That damage comes from the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing center of the plant to feed on tender young leaves.
ga: Nɔ ni fiteɔ nii lɛ jɛɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ dalɛ he lɛ mli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why does my harvested maize get moldy and spoil while sitting in my store room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ni efiteɔ beni mita nitoohe lɛ?

english: Maize spoils in storage if it is not dried completely before storing. Moisture encourages fungus and insects to grow inside the stored grain.
ga: Abɛi fiteɔ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kɛji egbiko kwraa dani akɛtoɔ. Fɛ̃i woɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ amli.

english: Why does spraying weed killer sometimes slow down the growth of my main crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ adalɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: If weed killer touches crop leaves or is applied during extreme heat, the plant has to spend energy breaking down the chemical instead of growing.
ga: Kɛji tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ kɛ tso lɛ baai kpe loo akɛwo mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Esa akɛ tsei lɛ afite hewalɛ ni amɛkɛgbala tsofai amli moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ̃.

english: How do I know if my rice field has too much water?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ nu babaoo yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔ mli?

english: When rice fields hold too much deep water for too long, the plants turn yellow, root growth slows down, and stems can weaken. Keeping water at a controlled, shallow depth helps rice breathe and absorb nutrients properly.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa ŋmɔji hiɛ nu ni mli kwɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Tso lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Shishifãi lɛ adalɛ baafee mlɛo. ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ baanyɛ afee gbɔjɔmɔ Kɛ́ akɛ nu lɛ to he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni emuɔ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I drain excess water from my farm after heavy rainfall?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ majie nu ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ?

english: Digging shallow drainage channels around and through your field creates pathways for extra rainwater to flow away safely without washing away your topsoil or drowning crop roots.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni oootsi Oŋmɔji lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ mli lɛ feɔ gbɛ ni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baanyɛ ajo foi shweshweeshwe. ni ekɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ efɔɔɔ loo ekɛ tso shishifãi lɛ shwieee nu mli

english: What causes crop leaves to turn yellow when the soil stays very wet?
ga: Mɛni haa tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa lolo lɛ?

english: Excess water fills all the tiny air pockets in the soil, preventing roots from taking in oxygen and vital nutrients like nitrogen, which causes the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ amli, ni no haaa shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, ni no haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do grain buyers in the market prefer certain crop varieties over others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ ŋmaa yɛ jara nɔ lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmaa henɔi komɛi fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Market buyers and consumers look for specific qualities like grain size, cooking taste, aroma, and color, which makes high-quality improved varieties sell faster and at better prices.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jarayelihe lɛ kɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ sui pɔtɛɛ komɛi tamɔ dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ, niyenii ni ahoɔ lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ, amɛhenumɔ kɛ amɛhe su, ni haa ŋmeii srɔtoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni atsake amɛ lɛ hɔ̃ɔ oya kɛ jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I choose the best seed variety to plant on my farm in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala dumɔwui srɔtoi ni hi fe fɛɛ ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ Ghana?

english: You should select seed varieties based on your local rainfall patterns, soil type, and market demand, choosing certified seeds that resist common local pests and drought.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala dumɔwui henɔi ni damɔ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ henɔ, kɛ jarayeli taomɔ. Amɛhalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ hɔmɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to walk through my field regularly as my crops grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔji amli daa yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miikwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Regular field visits help you spot early signs of plant stress, pest attacks, or disease early so you can treat them before your entire harvest is ruined.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛ nɔ saramɔi ni afeɔ daa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni ona okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ miihao mra. Abaanyɛ ana tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai mra. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ otsa dani onibii fɛɛ akpata.

english: What makes a field of crops look healthy and productive during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: A healthy crop field shows rich green leaves, uniform plant height across the farm, sturdy stems, and no visible damage from leaf-eating insects or disease.
ga: He ni aduɔ nii yɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baajie tsei fɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kpo. Tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa ni nɔ ko bɛ ni anaa ni jɛɔ kooloi loo helai ni yeɔ baai lɛ amli baa.

english: How does proper spacing between plants affect how well my crops grow?
ga: Te gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ saa tsei lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Planting with correct spacing ensures each crop gets enough sunlight, airflow, and soil nutrients, preventing overcrowded plants from starving each other and growing thin.
ga: Dumɔ ni akɛ gbɛ ni sa shwieɔ shi lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Etsiɔ tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ anaa koni hɔmɔ akaye amɛ ni amɛfee shwiili.

english: Why do crops grow much better in some areas like Agogo compared to other regions?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei komɛi tamɔ Agogo kɛ akɛto kpokpai krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Certain areas have rich, fertile soil, good water retention, and reliable weather conditions that naturally support healthy crop growth better than drier or rockier regions.
ga: Hei komɛi yɛ sũ ni baa nii, ni baa nii ni hiɛɔ nu jogbaŋŋ. kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ Ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ fe hei ni egbi loo tɛi yɔɔ.

english: Can I visit other farm projects in my region to learn better planting methods?
ga: Manyɛ mayasara ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔi krokomɛi. Yɛ mikpokpaa lɛ nɔ koni makase bɔ ni afeɔ adara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, visiting demonstration farms and successful neighbor projects allows you to see effective crop management techniques in real life and adapt them to your own farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ŋmɔji kɛ akutsoŋ nitsumɔi ni yeɔ omanye lɛ saramɔ haa onaa ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ he ŋaai ni mɔɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛ mli diɛŋtsɛ. ni okɛto bo diɛŋtsɛ oŋmɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb up stakes to spread their leaves fully in the sunlight. When leaves get maximum sunlight, they make more food for the plant, resulting in much larger tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tso ko nɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ aje kpo yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Be ni baai lɛ ná hulu la babaoo lɛ Ebaafee niyenii babaoo eha tsei lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ dara kwraa.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up into tight tubes during the hottest hours of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tsɔnei ni mli wa yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants curl their leaves to save water when the weather gets very hot and dry. By rolling up, less leaf surface is exposed to heat and wind, preventing the crop from drying out.
ga: Abele tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu nu he kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa. kɛji akɛ abɔle ehe Ba lɛ hiɛ lɛ, hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baafee nɔ ni bɛ mlɛo. Tsi ŋmɔshi nibii anaa koni amɛkagbi

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without growing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather temperatures become too high or when soil moisture changes suddenly. High heat dries out the pollen inside the flower, preventing it from forming a fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsake trukaa lɛ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ agbi. tsiɔ yibiiwoo naa

english: Why do my cassava roots become woody and dry when left in the ground during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ tsei ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During dry periods, the cassava plant stays alive by eating the starch stored in its underground roots. As it uses up that stored food, the roots lose water and turn tough and fibrous.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, Cassava tsei hiɔ shi kɛtsɔ ŋmei ni ato yɛ amɛshikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛyeɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ekɛ niyenii ni ato lɛ fɛɛ tsu nii lɛ Shishifãi lɛ laajeɔ nu ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Wrinkled or curled leaves usually mean tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies are sucking sap from the underside of young leaves, or transmitting a plant virus that distorts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni egbɔjɔ loo ebɔle ehe lɛ tsɔɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies. Nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ mli nu ni anuɔ. loo egbɛɔ tsei ahe helai ni fiteɔ amɛdalɛ lɛ eshwaa.

english: Why are there ragged holes and sawdust-like dirt inside the center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji ni mli ewo muji kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei yɔɔ mi-ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides inside the center whorl of the maize plant during the day, eating the young leaves and leaving behind droppings.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ekɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Ye baai bibii lɛ ni oshi ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my groundnut roots have small round bumps on them when I pull them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut shishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ? Be ni mikɛbaawo ŋwɛi?

english: Those bumps are called root nodules, and they are beneficial. Helpful bacteria inside them pull nitrogen out of the air and feed it to the crop, naturally fertilizing your soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akɛ root nodules ni amɛhe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ. Muawai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why should I avoid spreading my granular fertilizer right before a very heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ granular fertilizer ni mikɛshwãa dani ahum ni naa wa waa aba lɛ he?

english: Heavy rainwater sweeps across the topsoil and washes your fertilizer off the field before root systems can absorb it, wasting your money and leaving crops unfed.
ga: Nugbɔ nu ni naa wa baatsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebaafɔ o-fertilizer lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Efiteɔ oshika ni ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have broad leaves that catch wind like a sail, but their roots grow very shallow in the topsoil. Without heavy support sticks or deep soil, the weight of the fruit bunch easily pulls the plant down.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ tamɔ ŋshɔ hiɛ tsɔnei. Shi eshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ nɔ ko bɛ ni fiɔ sɛɛ loo shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ Tso yibii akutsei lɛ amli tsiimɔ baanyɛ agbala tso lɛ shi mlɛo.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when I clear all the big trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out soil moisture. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or leaving larger forest trees keeps the soil cool and helps the cocoa survive its early years.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gĩɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni ashiɔ yɛ kooi wuji amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines naturally climb so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight. Raising the vines on stakes keeps leaves off the wet ground to prevent diseases and helps the plant create larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Wein tsei ni aaakwɛ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni helai akabote mli, ni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete against each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. Giving plants proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to grow strong and produce good yield.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ haa tsei lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient maize needs to build green leaves. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will restore green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni eha baai eŋɔli aba. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the land where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of nutrients from the soil, but legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. Planting them refreshes the soil naturally for future crops.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Tsei nɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why is it bad to put chemical fertilizer on my crops when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baawo miŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so plant roots can safely drink it in. When applied to dry soil, fertilizer remains concentrated and can burn or destroy the plant's roots.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu amɛ shweshweeshwe. Kɛji akɛ oowo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakã he ahi shi ni ebaanyɛ eshã loo efite tso lɛ shishifãi.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. Excess rain causes waterlogging, which drowns the root system and allows fungi and bacteria in the mud to turn the roots soft and rotten.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ kɛ nu shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli. ni eha ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ muji lɛ mli lɛ aha shishifãi lɛ afee blɛoo ni amɛgboi.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ewo pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they suffer from stress, such as intense heat, uneven watering, or dry soil. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps the flowers stay attached and turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa, loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛfee.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves with tiny caterpillars hidden inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Akɛtee tsɔne lɛ mli?

english: These holes are caused by Fall Armyworms, a pest that feeds on young maize leaves and growing tips. Spraying safe treatments like neem leaf extract or recommended pesticides early in the morning destroys them before they ruin the harvest.
ga: Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. Tsofa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe tamɔ neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baafite enɛɛmɛi dani amɛbaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my ripening tomatoes split open on the sides right before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ afãi dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when they receive a sudden heavy downpour or heavy watering after a dry spell. The inside of the fruit absorbs water quickly and swells faster than the outer skin can stretch. Regular, steady watering stops this splitting.
ga: Tomatoi tswaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa trukaa loo nu babaoo shwie amɛnɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni efuɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Nu ni akɛhaa daa, ni afeɔ daa lɛ baakpa mligbalamɔ nɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are delicate and lose water rapidly through their soft leaves in direct sunlight. They require partial shade from nurse crops like plantains or shade trees to retain leaf moisture and protect their roots while getting established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛtsɔɔ baai bibii lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be ko kɛjɛ nurse tsei tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ amli fɛ̃i lɛ hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe beni amɛmaa shi lɛ.

english: Why should I plant plantains in my farm before putting in my new cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu kookoo tsei heei?

english: Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that create shade, acting as natural umbrellas that protect sensitive young cocoa seedlings from strong sunlight and heavy winds while keeping the soil moist.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Excess water and cold, humid conditions cause a fungal infection known as Black Pod disease. Moisture builds up on pods that do not get enough sunlight or airflow, allowing the fungus to spread rapidly.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine kɛ shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod disease baa. Fɛ̃i buaa ehe naa yɛ ŋmeii ni hulu la loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ shɛɛɛ amɛhe lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Why do sap-sucking insects like capsids attack my cocoa trees mostly when new shoots appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ capsids lɛ tutuaa mi-cocoa tsei lɛ babaoo kɛ́ ŋmeii heei je kpo lɛ?

english: Capsids prefer feeding on fresh growth because young shoots, leaves, and soft pods contain soft tissue and high nutrient sap that is easy for them to pierce and consume.
ga: Capsids sumɔɔ ni amɛye nibii ni eda ehee ejaakɛ ŋmeii bibii, baai, kɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ fãji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ nu ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa ni enyɛɔ eboteɔ mli ni eyeɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen, a key nutrient in the soil responsible for making leaves green and helping plants turn sunlight into food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hia yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛ tsakeɔ hulu la amɛfeɔ niyenii.

english: Why do my crops yield far less food when I let weeds grow among them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa niyenii fioo kwraa beni mihaa jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛteŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, soil nutrients, and water away from your crops, competing directly with them and leaving fewer resources for your crops to produce pods or fruits.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la ni he hiaa waa. niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ kɛjɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ kɛ jwɛi lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ ni eshiɔ nibii fioo komɛi ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii loo aduawai.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves but give me very small roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ kɛlɛ waa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eshishifãi lɛ daraaa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to potassium and phosphorus, plants spend all their energy growing stems and leaves above ground instead of storing nutrients in their underground tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛtoɔ potassium kɛ fɔsfɔs he lɛ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ tsei kɛ baai ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baato shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: Why is it bad for my crop yield if I plant seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehiii kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, their roots tangle and fight for limited nutrients in the soil while their leaves block each other from sunlight, leading to weak, stunted plants.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii fioo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwu lɛ baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛgbɔjɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why is it better to plant my seeds right at the beginning of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Planting at the start of the rains ensures seeds get consistent water to germinate and allows their roots to grow deep into the soil before hot, dry spells arrive.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ náa nu babaoo be fɛɛ be koni amɛkwɛ̃. ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ dani hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do flowers drop off my pepper plants before turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shiɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ mli dani amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress, such as extreme heat, poor watering, or a lack of insects like bees to pollinate the blooms.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni ehiii, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ pollen.

english: Why do grain buyers offer me a lower price when my harvested maize has chaff and dirt mixed in it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ ŋmaa lɛ kɛ jara ni baa shi haa mi lɛ? Akɛni miŋmaa ni mikpaa lɛ yɛ ŋmei kɛ muji ni efutu mli hewɔ lɛ

english: Buyers must spend extra time and money cleaning and sorting dirty grain before processing or milling. Clean grain prevents machine damage and stays fresh longer, which is why market buyers pay higher prices for clean produce.
ga: Esa akɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ afite be kɛ shika kroko ni amɛkɛtsumɔ ŋmaa ni mli ewo muji lɛ mli ni amɛhala mli dani amɛtsu he nii loo amɛshwie nɔ. Dumɔwui ni he tse lɛ tsiɔ tsɔne ni fiteɔ lɛ naa ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ hewɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ woɔ jara ni nɔ kwɔ kɛhaa nibii ni he tse lɛ.

english: Why does my harvested corn get moldy and rot inside my storage barn even after I cover it well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli ewo muji ni efite yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ miha nɔ jogbaŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Grains trap internal moisture after harvest. If you store corn before drying it completely in the sun, heat builds up inside the pile and creates damp conditions where mold and insects quickly destroy the grain.
ga: Dumɔwui mɔ̃ɔ nu yɛ mli yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji okɛ ŋmãa lɛ shwie shi dani ogbi lɛ yɛ hulu lɛ mli lɛ, Dɔlɛ buaa ehe naa yɛ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Fungi kɛ kooloi bibii lɛ baafite ŋmãa ŋmaa lɛ oya.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants turn yellow and curl up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves curl and turn yellow when plants suffer from water stress or tiny dry-season pests like green mites. The plant sheds leaves to save water and protect its roots until rains return.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nu mli haomɔ loo hulutsoo be mli tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ na tso lɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crop seedlings after I plant my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mitso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with deep roots naturally built to grab soil water and nutrients very quickly. They steal light and food from young crop seedlings, which grow at a slower, controlled pace.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni abɔ amɛ koni amɛgbala sũ mli nu kɛ niyenii oya. Amɛjuɔ la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui bibii amli, ni amɛdaraa blɛoo ni akudɔɔ amɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants fall off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme sun heat or irregular watering. Heat stress prevents the flowers from properly pollinating, causing the plant to shed them to conserve energy.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ loo akɛ nu haa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Heat haomɔ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei ajie lɛ kpo koni amɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous harvest yield smaller crops than new certified seeds from the agrodealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni okwaayeli mlijalɔ ko ema he odase lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their original vigor and genetic strength over seasons, making them weaker against local pests and weather. Certified seeds are specially produced to guarantee strong growth and uniform yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ laajeɔ amɛ shishijee hewalɛ kɛ amɛfɔmɔ su mli hewalɛ yɛ be lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛ oya. Afeɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni ekɛha amɛdara waa ni amɛwo yibii ni yaa nɔ daa.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning light yellow instead of dark green while growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize mean the crop lacks essential soil nutrients, particularly nitrogen. Without enough nitrogen, plants cannot produce chlorophyll, which turns leaves green and powers healthy growth.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa. titri lɛ nitrogen Kɛji nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee klorofil. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni ebaaha amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings scorch and die when I clear away all the large trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ shã ni amɛgboi beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft, sensitive leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight. Tall shade trees act as natural canopy umbrellas, lowering temperatures and keeping soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why do my stored yams rot from the inside within a few weeks of harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ emli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni akpaa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams rot when cut or bruised during digging, as open wounds allow rot-causing bacteria to enter. Storing them on warm, unventilated ground speeds up this internal decay.
ga: Sweet potatoes baafite kɛji afo loo atswa yɛ be mli ni atsaa lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, pilamɔi ni agbele lɛ haa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ boteɔ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛmli fitemɔ aya hiɛ oya.

english: Why shouldn't I mix different varieties of beans together in the same bag when selling to buyers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi futuɔ kotoku kome mli kɛ́ mikɛmiihɔɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ?

english: Different bean varieties cook at different rates and taste different. When mixed together, food processors and consumers cannot cook them evenly, making mixed bags less desirable and less valuable at market.
ga: Bean henɔ fɛɛ henɔ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ, ni esoro bɔ ni eyɔɔ ŋɔɔ ha. Kɛ akɛfutu mli lɛ Jeee niyenii he nitsulɔi kɛ mɛi ni yeɔ lɛ fɛɛ ji mɛi ni abɔ amɛ ekome. Enɛ haaa mɛi asumɔɔɔ baagi ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ, ni amɛjara hu waaa yɛ jara nɔ.

english: Why do my crops wilt and dry up so quickly when there are no big trees around my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho ni amɛmiigbi oya be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Big trees act as natural shields that block scorching sunlight, hold moisture in the soil, and lower the temperature around your crops so they do not lose water too fast.
ga: Tsei ni eda lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gãimlibii ni tsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa. Ha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oha hulutsoo ni yɔɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ aba shi koni nu akafite oya tsɔ.

english: Why does my farmland feel much hotter and drier today than it used to years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni egbi fe bɔ ni eji yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ?

english: When large trees and forest canopy are cleared or destroyed, the land loses its natural shade, allowing direct sunlight to bake the soil and raise ground temperatures significantly.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsei wuji kɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fite loo amɛfite Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite ebɔɔ su hulutsoo lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔlɛ yaa hiɛ waa.

english: Why do my young crops need protection from full, direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni abu mi dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Young plants have tender leaves and small root systems that cannot pull up water fast enough to replace what intense sunlight burns off, causing them to dry out and die.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii. ni nyɛɛɛ agbala nu oya bɔ ni sa koni ekɛwo hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he nyɔmɔ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: What simple thing can I do on my farm to keep the soil cool during the dry season?
ga: Mafee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: You can leave or plant specific shade trees and cover the ground with fallen leaves to shield the topsoil from direct heat and preserve soil moisture.
ga: Obaanyɛ oshi loo odu tsei ni ajɔɔ nɔ aha hulutsoo ni okɛ baai ni egbee shi lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why is it important for me to plant trees alongside my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsei yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Planting trees provides protective shade, improves soil fertility as leaves fall and decay, and creates a cool environment that helps your crops survive harsh heat.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ koni ekɛ hulutsoo kɛ hebuu aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ yaa hiɛ kɛji baai lɛ gbee shi ni amɛgboi. ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli.

english: Can I leave any wild tree standing on my farm to provide shade for my crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi koo mli tsei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: No, not every tree is suitable. Some trees steal too much water and soil nutrients from your crops, while ideal shade trees enrich the soil and let in filtered sunlight.
ga: Dabi, jeee tso fɛɛ tso sa. Tsei komɛi juɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛhaa hulu la ni mli tse lɛ boteɔ mli.

english: How do I know if a tree on my farm is competing with my crops for food?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miitswa akaŋ koni amɛye niyenii?

english: If crops growing directly around a tree look stunted, yellow, or thin compared to the rest of your farm, that tree likely has shallow roots stealing water and plant food.
