ga: Kɛji tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Tso lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ. Eyɛ ŋmɔŋ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ akɛto fãi krokomɛi ahe. yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli Ekolɛ tso lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli.

english: How does having a thick tree canopy overhead help protect my farm's soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni mli tse ni yɔɔ miyitso nɔ lɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: A canopy breaks the force of heavy rainfall so topsoil does not wash away, blocks drying sun rays, and constantly adds natural leaf fertilizer to the ground.
ga: Kpoji lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baa shi. No hewɔ lɛ, nu shwieee sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ hulu la ni egbi lɛ naa. ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli baai amli lɛ afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he daa

english: Why are my crops struggling to grow on land that was recently swept by bushfire?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni koo mli la shã nɔ nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Bushfires burn off the protective shade trees and natural organic matter that feed the earth, leaving exposed soil that hardens and lacks vital nutrients.
ga: Koo mli la shãa tsei ni haa hulutsoo kɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ ni miiba lɛ mli wa, ni niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ mli.

english: How do bushfires during the dry season affect my farm's future yield?
ga: Te koo mli la ni tsoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ saa ŋmɔ ko mli nibii ni ebaaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Bushfires destroy shade canopy and kill beneficial soil organisms, leaving your land exposed to direct sun heat and reducing crop yields for several seasons.
ga: Koo mli la fiteɔ hulutsoo ni efiteɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ wala ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Ha oshikpɔŋ lɛ aná dɔlɛ kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ mli. ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ ba shi yɛ bei babaoo mli.

english: Why do my crops wither and droop in the afternoon heat even when I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: Extreme environmental heat causes plants to lose moisture through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the soil. Watering early in the morning or late in the evening, combined with covering the soil with dry grass (mulching), keeps the root area cool and conserves water.
ga: Shihilɛ mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ ni akɛ mulching (mulching) fataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ ahe jɔɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants fall off without turning into fruit when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai kɛ́ edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: High temperatures cause heat stress in crop plants. When it gets too hot, the plant drops its blossoms to conserve energy and water, which prevents fruit from forming until the heat reduces.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ haomɔ baa ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu akafite. Enɛ baatsi aduawai anaa kɛyashi la ni tsoɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: How can I protect my delicate young vegetable seedlings from dying under the heavy sun?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-vegetable dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkagboi yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi?

english: Young seedlings have weak, shallow roots and thin leaves that easily burn in hot weather. Constructing simple nursery shade sheds using palm fronds or shade cloth lowers the surrounding temperature and protects them until they are strong enough for full sun.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma loo mama ni akɛwoɔ hulutsoo mli lɛ ma tsũ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha hulutsoo ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ aba shi, ni ebaabu he kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baawa bɔ ni sa kɛha hulu la ni naa wa.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upwards during the sunniest hours of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a crop's natural defense against heat. The plant rolls its leaves inward to reduce the surface area exposed to direct sunlight and trap air, helping it reduce water loss during intense heat.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛyaa mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mɔɔ lɛ lɛ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu ni laajeɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: What happens to my maize crop if I plant too many seeds close together in hot weather?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, hot air gets trapped between them and creates a harsh environment. The crowded plants also fight for limited soil water and nutrients, leading to thin stems and poor yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ boteɔ nakai tsei lɛ ateŋ. ni ekɛ shihilɛ ni mli wa baa Tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ hu wuɔ koni amɛná shikpɔŋ nɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is wind and air movement between my crop rows so important when temperatures are high?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni nyiɛɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ he hiaa yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa lɛ?

english: Airflow acts as a natural cooling system for your farm. Proper row spacing allows breezes to blow through, which carries away trapped heat around the leaves and reduces high humidity that causes fungal diseases.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni haa oŋmɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ dɔlɛ ni ebɔle baai lɛ ahe lɛ. ni eha hulutsoo ni fa ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa lɛ aba shi

english: Do bigger, older crops tolerate hot weather better than young plants?
ga: Ani tsei ni edara ni dara lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ amɛhaa fe tsei bibii?

english: Yes, mature plants have deeper roots that can reach moisture stored far below the ground and tougher leaves that handle heat better. Young crops have small roots near the hot surface soil, making them far more vulnerable to heat damage.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei ni eda lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni baanyɛ aná nu babaoo ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Ni baai ni wa lɛ baanyɛ atsu dɔlɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ. Tso bibioo lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii. ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ dɔlɛ baanyɛ afite amɛ.

english: How does hot ground soil affect how my crop roots grow underground?
ga: Te shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ saa bɔ ni mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When direct heat bakes the topsoil, it becomes too hot for sensitive feeder roots to survive, causing root growth to stop. Covering the ground around the crops with mulch shields the soil from direct heat, keeping roots cool and active.
ga: Kɛ́ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã lɛ. Ebaadɔ tsɔ bɔ ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ahi shi. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ Mulching around Mulch ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ baaye abua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛtsuɔ nii.

english: Why are my seeds taking so long to germinate during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Crop seeds need a cool, moist environment to sprout. Excessive environmental heat dries out the seedbed quickly and overheats the seeds, causing them to go dormant or die before they can break through the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ejɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Shihilɛ mli dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ agbiɔ oya ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ mli dɔɔ fe nine. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ yaa wɔɔhe loo amɛgboiɔ dani amɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: If I am expanding my crop farm to grow a much larger quantity, how does heat management change?
ga: Kɛji akɛ mikɛ mihe miiwo mi tsei aŋmɔ lɛ mli koni eha amɛfalɛ aya hiɛ. Te bɔ ni akwɛɔ dɔlɛ nɔ ahaa lɛ baatsake aha tɛŋŋ?

english: When you plant crops on a much larger scale, heat gets trapped across a wider area and water disappears faster. You must carefully manage field orientation, row spacing for air movement, and shade or irrigation planning to prevent widespread heat stress.
ga: Kɛji okwɛ tsei ni da waa lɛ Dɔlɛ mɔ̃ɔ he ko ni da ni nu lɛ laajeɔ oya. Esa akɛ okwɛ ŋmɔ mli gbɛtsɔɔmɔ nɔ. Gbɛ ni ato kɛha kɔɔyɔɔ ni nyiɛɔ kɛ gbɛjianɔtoo kpakpa kɛha hulutsoo loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi. Bɔni afee ni atsĩ dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ naa

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key food they need to grow strong. It can also happen if the soil is too waterlogged and drowning the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ shwie nu mli.

english: Is it better to put fertilizer on my farm right before it rains or after it rains?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli dani nugbɔ anɛ loo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer on moist soil right after rain or before a light rain, so the water dissolves the nutrients and helps the roots soak them up without washing the fertilizer away in a heavy downpour.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ enɛ loo dani nugbɔ enɛ fioo. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni nu lɛ atsɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ nɔ, ni eye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛŋɔ amɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efɔɔɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa.

english: Why do people tell me to cover the soil around my crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the ground cool, traps moisture so you water less, stops weeds from growing, and turns into rich organic food for the soil as it rots.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Eŋmɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli koni okɛ nu akawo mli fioo Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni ebafeɔ niyenii ni jara wa kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ be mli ni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Mi plantain tso titri lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Too many small shoots, or suckers, steal food, light, and water from the main mother stem. Leaving only one or two strong shoots ensures the main stem produces a large, heavy bunch of plantain.
ga: Ayɛ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii bibii. Nɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ niyenii, kane, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ nyɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha plantains akuu agbo ko ni tsii aba.

english: Why do I need to push tall wooden sticks into the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi tso lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi nɛkɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Staking holds yam vines up off the hot ground so their leaves get maximum sunlight to make food, which allows the tuber under the ground to grow long and heavy.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ wo he ko ni mli edɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yibii lɛ aná hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhoo nii yɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ shwiili.

english: Most cassava is ready between 9 to 12 months after planting when the bottom leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the main stem starts to crack.
ga: Cassava babaoo efee klalo akɛ abaadu aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso wulu lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping their flowers before they turn into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed their flowers when they are stressed by dry winds like the Harmattan, lack of shade, or lack of water. It is the tree's natural way of saving its strength to survive.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi tamɔ harmattan, hulutsoo ni bɛ, loo nu ni bɛ. Enɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehiɛɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛhiɔ shi lɛ mli.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the juice out of young leaves, or by a virus they pass to the plant, which stops the pepper plant from growing well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. ni tsiɔ pepper tsei anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ

english: What causes small holes and sawdust-like dirt inside the top leaves of my maize?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ amli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar feeding inside the soft growing center of the plant. Treating the central leaves early with approved bio-pesticides or neem water helps save your harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni naa niyenii yɛ tso lɛ mli hei ni bibii lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ. Nibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ ahe tsofafeemɔ mra Kɛ bio-insecticide loo neem nu ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ baahere onibii lɛ ayiwala.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning brown and crisp during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle full, direct sunlight because their roots are not deep enough to take up enough water. They need shade crops like plantains planted next to them to shield their leaves from intense heat and keep the surrounding soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni sa koni amɛná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni ebu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he ni eha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ

english: What will happen to my maize harvest if I put four or five seeds in a single hole?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa ejwɛ loo enumɔ wo bu kome mli?

english: Planting too many seeds together causes the growing plants to steal food, water, and sunlight from each other. This results in thin, weak stalks and small or empty corn cobs instead of full, healthy ears.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa tsei ni miida lɛ juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaná toi ni yeɔ emuu ni mli wa lɛ

english: Why are small ragged holes appearing on the leaves inside the funnels of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bu bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Ragged holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on tender leaves inside the whorl. If left untreated, these pests eat the growing tip and drastically cut down crop yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fall armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baa bibii yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ baa. Kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Maize takes away heavy amounts of nitrogen from the soil, leaving it tired. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen from the air and return it to the ground, naturally feeding the soil for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ha etɔ lɛ Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ. Taakɛ eji lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does putting dry grass on top of the soil around my vegetable roots keep them green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ jwɛi woɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mishishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, stops the hot sun from evaporating soil water, keeps the root area cool, and slowly rots down into rich plant food.
ga: Ale jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ akafee nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ tsei niyenii babaoo.

english: Does it matter which direction I point a cassava stem when I stick it into the ground?
ga: Kɛ́ odu ŋmei tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ani ebaatsɔɔ he ko?

english: Yes, cassava stems must be planted with the small growth buds pointing upwards toward the sky. If planted upside down, the shoots struggle to reach sunlight, leading to late sprout emergence and smaller tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, efɔɔɔ kaa akɛ ŋmeii lɛ baaná hulu la. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ sɛɛ ni bulbs bibii baa.

english: Why do I need to clear tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tso kakadaŋŋ ko mli koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the air to catch maximum sunlight. When leaves capture plenty of sunlight, the plant creates more energy to grow large tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa Tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why shouldn't I apply dry fertilizer onto completely dry ground when there is no rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi woɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kwraa nɔ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve so that roots can drink it in safely. Applying fertilizer to hot, dry soil concentrates the chemicals and burns the plant roots, which can yellow or kill the crop.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu lɛ shweshweeshwe. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha tsofai lɛ afee ekome ni ebaashã tsei lɛ ashishifãi. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsei afee ŋmɔŋ loo efite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are my weed-infested crops turning pale and stunted even when it rains every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei ni jwɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa gbi lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that drink up nitrogen and mineral nutrients faster than crops. Even with adequate rain, your crops stay hungry because weeds are stealing their food.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ nitrogen kɛ mineral niyenii oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po Hɔmɔ miiye oŋmɔshi nibii po ejaakɛ jwɛi miiju amɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my green tomatoes rotting and turning black before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ fãi lɛ miifite ni amɛmiitsɔ ediŋŋ dani amɛshwere lɛ?

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes, called blossom end rot, happen when the plant cannot pull calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering where the soil flips between very dry and soaked.
ga: Atsɛɔ hei diji ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa teŋ.

english: Why do some types of cassava take two years to mature while others take only one year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii henɔi komɛi heɔ afii enyɔ dani amɛdaraa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu heɔ afi kome pɛ lɛ?

english: Different cassava stem varieties have different genetic traits. Improved fast-growing varieties mature within 9 to 12 months, whereas traditional or local varieties grow at a slower rate and require 18 to 24 months to build up full starch in their roots.
ga: Cassava henɔi srɔtoi yɛ fɔmɔ sui srɔtoi. Henɔi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni daa oya lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli, yɛ be mli ni blema loo maŋ lɛ mli henɔi lɛ daaa blɛoo. Ni eheɔ nyɔji 18 kɛyashi 24 dani ŋmeii lɛ eyiɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Is it better for my farm business to plant one-year cassava or two-year cassava?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha miŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ lɛ akɛ makwɛ ŋmei ni yeɔ afi kome loo ŋmei ni yeɔ afii enyɔ?

english: One-year cassava allows you to harvest quickly and sell faster for quick money, but two-year cassava allows you to leave the crop safely stored in the soil until you find a buyer or face a food shortage.
ga: Cassava ni eye afi kome lɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa lɛ oya ni ohɔ̃ɔ oya koni oná shika oya. Shi ŋmei ni eye afii 2 lɛ haa onyɛɔ oshiɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ona mɔ ni baahe loo okɛ niyenii ni faaa kpeɔ.

english: Why does my harvested cassava spoil so much faster than my harvested yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya fe mi-sweet potato ni mikpa lɛ?

english: Yams enter a natural sleeping period after harvest and have a thick skin that protects them, whereas cassava roots start breaking down internally within 2 to 3 days of being cut from the main stem because they have thin skins and high moisture.
ga: Sweet potatoes yaa adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ ni eyɛ hewolo ni mli tse ni buɔ ehe. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ baabɔi gbee yɛ emli yɛ gbii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli beni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ sɛɛ. Ejaakɛ eyɛ ŋmei ni mli tseee kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo.

english: What happens to cassava tubers if I transport them long distances right after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni baa ŋmãa shishifãi anɔ kɛji akɛ akɛtee he ko ni jɛkɛ yɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cassava tubers lose moisture rapidly and bruise easily during transport. If left exposed to air and heat during transport, blue-black streaks will form inside the tubers, causing them to rot within a few days.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya, ni kɛ́ akɛ amɛ tee lɛ, amɛfiteɔ oya. Kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ dɔlɛ mli yɛ gbɛfaa mli lɛ, bluu-diŋŋ ni baafee line yɛ yitso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli.

english: Why do some of my cassava plants produce thin, woody roots instead of big, thick tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ ekomɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni tamɔ tsei yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni mli tse lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Thin or woody cassava roots happen when the soil is too hard for the roots to expand, when the plant lacks nutrients like potassium, or when the cassava is harvested too early before it has time to swell.
ga: Kasava shishifãi ni mli tse loo tsei baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. Be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii tamɔ potassium loo be mli ni akpaa ŋmei mra tsɔ dani enáa be ni ekɛfutuɔ.

english: What will happen to my cassava crop if I leave it in the ground past its maturity time?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni eho lɛ nɔ?

english: Leaving cassava in the soil past its natural maturity period can cause the tubers to turn fibrous and woody, lose their starch content, or rot if heavy rains arrive.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ mli kɛho bɔ ni edaa lɛ he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmeii kɛ tsei. Starch babaoo ni baafite loo fitemɔ kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa ba

english: Why do my cassava plants drop their leaves during the dry season, and will this kill the crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baa shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ? Ni ani ebaagbe ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves during the dry season is a natural defense behavior. The plant drops its leaves to conserve water and survive the heat; once the rains return, it will grow fresh leaves and continue maturing.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli su ko ni buɔ mɔ he. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni amɛhi shi yɛ dɔlɛ mli. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ, baai heei kɛ dalɛ ni yaa nɔ lɛ baaba.

english: How does rainy weather affect how fast my root crops grow underground?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ saa bɔ ni mishishifãi lɛ daa oya yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ he?

english: Good moisture encourages the plant to make plenty of leaves, which produce food that gets sent down to swell the tubers, but excessive water can cause waterlogging and rot the tubers in the ground.
ga: Fɛ̃i kpakpa yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ baai babaoo. ni haa niyenii ni atsuɔ kɛyaa shi koni eha ŋmeii lɛ alɛɛ mli Shi nu babaoo baanyɛ aha nu abɔle ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ahe ni amɛfite.

english: Can I plant cassava on the exact same land right after harvesting my yam crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Both cassava and yam take large amounts of nutrients from the soil, especially potassium. Planting them right after each other will exhaust your soil unless you rotate with beans or apply fertilizer.
ga: Kasava kɛ sweet potato fɛɛ heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. titri lɛ potassium Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee shoo. Ja oodu ŋmeii loo oowo amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do cassava plants grow so well in poor soils where other crops struggle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii ni tsei krokomɛi bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava has deep, strong root systems that can search for water far below the surface, and it can survive with fewer soil nutrients compared to heavy feeders like maize or yam.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa. ni baanyɛ ana nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ akɛto tsei ni yeɔ niyenii babaoo tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for green leaves and strong growth. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer early in the season helps restore the green color and improves grain production.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai eŋɔli kɛ dalɛ ni mli wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ wo mli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni eha ŋmaa lɛ aná babaoo.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting under the ground when there is heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ŋmeii shishifãi jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when too much water stays around them because the roots cannot get air in waterlogged soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo ebɔle amɛhe ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Why should I plant plantain trees on the same land as my newly planted cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni adu kookoo dumɔwui heei lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow very quickly and provide broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa plants the shade and moisture they need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋtayaai. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their yellow flowers without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures are too high or when the plant experiences water stress during flowering. Watering consistently at the root zone and applying grass mulch around the base keeps the soil cool and damp, helping flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe daa kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. Ye obua ni fɔfɔi lɛ afee aduawai

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my crops and make my crops stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ ni ehaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibioo lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants that absorb water, sunlight, and fertilizer much faster than farm crops. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks after your crops sprout ensures your crops get all the food and light they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛheɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli beni otsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná niyenii kɛ la fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Why are there small ragged holes and powdery dirt inside the central funnel of my maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii ni ekpɔtɔ kɛ muji ni tamɔ powda yɛ mi-abele baai lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by caterpillars like the fall armyworm feeding on soft young leaves. Checking your farm early and spraying neem leaf extracts or recommended organic treatments directly into the leaf funnel kills the pests before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii tamɔ cutworms ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mli kwɛmɔ mra Ni neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofa fɛɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ni oooshwie tso lɛ tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baagbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food that feeds the underground tuber. Lifting the vines on stakes exposes more leaves to sunlight and keeps them away from hot, wet soil where fungal diseases spread.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛhaa amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Wein tso lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ haa hulu la babaoo shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔɔɔ ni ehaaa edɔ, he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous maize harvest grow weaker crops than certified seeds bought from agro-dealers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ ha tso ko ni baanyɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni ahe kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Certified hybrid seeds are specifically bred for high vigor, pest resistance, and high yield in their first generation. Saved seeds lose these strong traits in the next generation, resulting in uneven plant sizes and smaller cobs.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni ehi shi shiŋŋ. Nɔ ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei lɛ adalɛi lɛ jeee ekome ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hu faaa.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce small, few fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for soil nutrients and water, while their branches block sunlight. Spacing pepper plants properly allows every plant to get enough food, air, and light to produce abundant, large peppers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni amɛniji lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii tsei lɛ to amɛhe jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni fa babaoo.

english: Why is it risky to plant seeds right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long dry stretch before regular rains start. Seeds that sprout after the first rain will dry up and die if the soil dries out completely, so it is safer to wait until rains become steady.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ jeɔ shishi. Dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. No hewɔ lɛ, eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and drying up during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. They need temporary shade trees like plantains or cassava planted alongside them to block direct sun and retain soil moisture until the cocoa trees mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he, ni akɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi sũ lɛ mli kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl upwards and look wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ekpɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny pests like aphids, thrips, or mites sucking the plant juices, or by a virus transmitted by these insects. Applying neem oil or appropriate organic insecticides helps manage these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni akwɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ.

english: Why are my corn leaves turning yellow from the tips down to the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛyitseiaŋ kɛmiiya amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting from the tips of older corn leaves is a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizers like urea or well-decomposed animal manure will restore healthy green foliage.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa baai ni egbɔ lɛ ashishi lɛ ji okadi ni ale jogbaŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make my soil better for future crops?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas have beneficial bacteria in their root nodules that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for the next crop planted in that field.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ bacteria ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni aduɔ yɛ nakai ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves with small droppings inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the central whorl of the maize plant. Early detection and applying targeted biological or chemical sprays into the leaf funnels can stop the damage.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni anaa mra Ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpa nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting and turning soft under the ground before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava root rot happens when water logs in the soil for too long, depriving the roots of air and allowing fungi to grow. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ jieɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over when the crop starts bearing heavy fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ je shishi amɛwo yibii ni tsii lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that cannot support heavy fruit bunches during strong winds. Supporting the main stem with sturdy wooden Y-stakes or bamboo props prevents the trees from snapping or uprooting.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛŋ akwɛ aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ anɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni tamɔ Y loo ŋmei ni wa fĩ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakumɔ loo eshishijee.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines to grow on tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsɔseɔ sweet potato wain tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ tsei kakadaji anɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high on poles to expose maximum leaf area to sunlight, which generates the energy needed to grow large underground tubers while keeping leaves off wet soil to prevent fungal rot.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ tso ko nɔ koni hulu la ni amɛbaai lɛ ahe lɛ aná babaoo. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akaje shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ koni ŋmeii akafite.

english: Tomato flower drop happens when plants experience heat stress, extreme dry soil, or excessive humidity. Regular, consistent watering at the roots and mulching the soil helps stabilize the plant so flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa, loo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli daa, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni eha tso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni ewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii.

english: Why do my rice leaves turn pale and stunted when the soil dries out for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Rice plants require consistent soil moisture to absorb essential nutrients from the soil. When soil dries up, root nutrient uptake slows down significantly, causing leaves to turn pale and growth to stall.
ga: Omɔ tsei taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛnyɛ amɛŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ amli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ baa shi kwraa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛdaraaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: How far apart should I space my cocoa seedlings when planting them in the field?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo kookoo dumɔwui lɛ amli kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ saatso lɛ nɔ?

english: Spacing cocoa seedlings properly (usually 3 meters by 3 meters) gives each tree enough room to spread its roots, access soil nutrients, and get enough airflow, which prevents fungal diseases from spreading.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ (bei pii lɛ mitai 3 x mitai 3) haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃. Nibii ni haa mɔ he waa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni anáa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa ni tsɔɔ mli Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why is it important for me to register my farm with the local cocoa officers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ miŋmɔ lɛ awo maŋ lɛ mli kookoo he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ wolo nɔ lɛ?

english: Registering your farm allows agricultural extension services to map your land size so you can receive government support like free or subsidized hybrid seeds, fertilizers, and pest control sprayings.
ga: Oŋmɔ lɛ ni oooŋmala wolo nɔ lɛ haa Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ feɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ he mfoniri. Koni akɛ nɔyeli yelikɛbuamɔ tamɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ aha bo ni shika loo yelikɛbuamɔ ko bɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees planted around them to block strong sun and keep moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ tsei bibii loo hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ amɛhe lɛ. Koni abu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Can I plant cassava together with my newly planted cocoa seedlings?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cassava kɛ cocoa dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ?

english: It is better to avoid planting cassava near young cocoa because cassava takes away too many nutrients and water from the soil, which can stunt your young cocoa tree's growth.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmei dumɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei jieɔ niyenii kɛ nu babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: How long will it take for my new cocoa trees to start giving me pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani mi-cacao tso hee lɛ baaje ŋmɔtɔ shishi?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually start producing their first pods within 2 to 3 years after planting if they are properly weeded, shaded, and fed with nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ cocoa hybrids lɛ jeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ afeemɔ shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ, kɛji akɛ ajie jwɛi jogbaŋŋ, aha amɛ hulutsoo ni aha amɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut off extra branches from my cocoa tree when it is growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji krokomɛi kɛjɛ cacao tso ko nɔ be mli ni cacao tso lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead wood and extra branches called suckers so the tree directs its energy into producing heavy pods instead of wasting resources on excess leaves.
ga: Tso ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei ni egboi kɛ tsei niji ni fa fe nine ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei kɛ hewalɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni tsii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite nibii yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: What causes the green cocoa pods on my tree to turn black during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: Pods turn black due to Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet conditions when excess water sits on the tree and air cannot circulate well through dense leaves.
ga: Pods lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ black pod hela lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli beni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ kpɛtɛɔ tsei ahe ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ tsei ahe tsei lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: How do I know if my cocoa farm needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If your trees show slow growth, pale yellow leaves, or dropped flowers, the soil has run out of essential food like nitrogen and potassium and needs organic manure or specialized cocoa fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ miida blɛoo lɛ Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo fɔfɔi ni egbee shi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛ ko awo mli

english: Why do the small flowers on my cocoa trees keep falling off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when the tree experiences stress from dry weather, lack of water, or a low population of beneficial insects (midges) that naturally pollinate the flowers.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ (teŋgbɛ nibii) ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ ayibɔ ni faaa lɛ mli.

english: Why does letting grass grow around my cocoa trees reduce my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ahaa jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ ebɔleɔ he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mikokoo tsei lɛ ha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ba shi.

english: Weeds actively steal fertilizer, soil nutrients, and water away from your cocoa roots, while also creating a hiding place for insects that bite and damage your cocoa pods.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ nu ni jɛɔ o-cocoa shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ kɛ miishɛɛ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kooloi ni shwieɔ o-cocoa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ naa he ko ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe.

english: Why does my plantain stem seem to die after I cut off the mature fruit bunch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi beni mifo aduawai akui ni edara lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A plantain stem (pseudostem) only produces fruit once in its entire life. Once it bears a bunch, its growth cycle is finished, and that specific stem naturally dies off so new shoots can take over.
ga: Plantain tsei (pseudostem) baawo yibii shikome pɛ yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli. Kɛ eje kpo yɛ kui amli lɛ Edalɛ be lɛ baa naagbee. Ni nakai tso pɔtɛɛ lɛ gboɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni eha ŋmeii heei abaye enajiaŋ.

english: Should I cut down the plantain trunk right after harvesting the fruit bunch?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo plantain tsei lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni akpa aduawai akui lɛ?

english: Yes, you should cut the trunk down after harvest. Leaving the old trunk standing wastes nutrients and blocks sunlight from the young shoots growing at the base.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛji okpa. Kɛ́ ashi tsei lɛ ahe tsei momo lɛ, efiteɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ, ni etsĩɔ hulu la ni jɛɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛshishi lɛ amli lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my plantain leaves dry up and turn brown after the plant forms fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ egbi ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni tso lɛ ewo yibii sɛɛ lɛ?

english: As the plantain fruit matures, the plant shifts almost all its energy and water into filling the fruit bunch, causing the older outer leaves to naturally age and dry up.
ga: Beni plantains lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Tsei lɛ tsakeɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ amɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu lɛ fɛɛ koni amɛkɛwo amɛ aduawai akui lɛ amli ekoŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kponɔgbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ daa ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Can I replant an old plantain stem that has already produced fruit?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu plantain momo ni ewo yibii momo lɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: No, an old stem that has already fruited cannot grow or bear fruit again. To grow new plantains, you must dig up and plant the young shoots (suckers) growing around the bottom of the old stem.
ga: Dabi, tso momo ni woɔ yibii lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ loo ewo yibii dɔŋŋ. Kɛji oosumɔ ni odu dumɔwui heei Ehe miihia ni otsa ni odu ŋmeii bibii (dumɔwui) ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso momo lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: How do I choose the best plantain shoot to plant on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantains ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaadu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Look for 'sword suckers'—these are young shoots with broad bases and narrow, spear-like leaves. They have strong energy reserves and grow into healthier, more productive plants than shoots with wide leaves.
ga: Taomɔ ‘klante ŋmeii’, ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni shishigbɛ lɛ mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni mli tse ni tamɔ akpɔlɔi. Amɛyɛ hewalɛ ni mli wa ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo fe tsei ni baai lɛ mli kwɔlɔ lɛ.

english: How long does a newly planted plantain shoot take to produce fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani plantain tsei ni adu ehee lɛ woɔ yibii?

english: Under good soil and rain conditions, a newly planted shoot usually takes about 11 to 15 months to grow, flower, and produce a mature bunch ready for harvest.
ga: Yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa kɛ nugbɔ shihilɛ shishi lɛ, tsei ni adu ehee lɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji 11 kɛyashi 15 dani amɛdaraa, amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni eda ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: What should I do with the chopped plantain trunks after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee plantain tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You can chop the harvested trunk into smaller pieces and spread them on the soil around your remaining plants. As the trunk rots, it releases moisture and nutrients back into the soil and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofolɔ tsei ni akpa lɛ amli bibii bibii. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛshwã shikpɔŋ ni eshwɛ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛji tso lɛ tso lɛ miifite lɛ Ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Why do so many small shoots keep growing at the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei bibii lɛ babaoo miida yɛ mi plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Plantain plants grow from an underground stem that continuously produces shoots called suckers to multiply and ensure the plant survives for the next generation.
ga: Dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni yaa nɔ amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛkwɛ koni tso lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi yinɔi ni baaba lɛ amli.

english: How many young shoots should I leave growing around one plantain stem?
ga: Esa akɛ mashi tsei bibii enyiɛ mabɔle dumɔwu kome he?

english: It is best to keep only 2 to 3 strong shoots of different ages around the main stem. Leaving too many shoots causes them to fight for nutrients, resulting in smaller fruit bunches.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ tsei 2 kɛyashi 3 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eye afii srɔtoi lɛ abɔle tso lɛ yitso lɛ he. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Do I need to clear all the weeds around my farm before planting new plantain shoots?
ga: Ehe miihia ni mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ. Okwaafoi lɛ fɛɛ dani adu dumɔwui heei?

english: Yes, clearing weeds gives young shoots full access to sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, helping them root quickly and grow strong without competition.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi oya ni amɛdaraa waa ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Why is it important for me to clear all weeds and loosen the soil before planting my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mafolɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Clearing weeds and loosening the soil allows the young roots to easily dig deep into the earth. It prevents wild weeds from stealing water and plant food away from your young crops, giving them a strong foundation to grow upright and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛfoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ amli. Enɛ haa amɛnáa shishitoo ni ma shi shiŋŋ koni amɛdara ja ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do I get very poor harvests when I plant maize on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ yibiiwoo nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets specific pests build up in the earth. Rotating your maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts puts natural food back into the soil and breaks the cycle of crop diseases.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ekpa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe helai ni yaa nɔ lɛ

english: Why are some of my maize plants growing tall and strong while others right next to them stay small and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ekomɛi daraa ni amɛhe wa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ daraaa lɛ? bibioo ni bɛ hewalɛ

english: Plants in the same field can grow differently because of uneven soil fertility, seeds planted at different depths, or crowding. Giving every seed equal space, consistent watering, and even fertilizer application helps all your crops grow uniformly.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ada yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ hewɔ. Aduɔ dumɔwui yɛ hei srɔtoi ni mli kwɔ. loo eyɛ density Hamɔ dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa Nu ni oooha lɛ daa Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii po awo mli lɛ baaye abua ni onibii lɛ akwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: How can I prevent my cassava and maize plants from falling over when strong winds blow?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ atsĩ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tsei anaa koni amɛkagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa?

english: Crops fall over when their roots are too shallow or their stems lack strength. Mounding soil around the base of the stem (earthing-up) and applying fertilizers rich in potassium strengthens the roots and stems so the plants can stand firm against heavy weather.
ga: Tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ loo tso lɛ shishifã lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni aaabɔle shishitoo lɛ he (ni akɛwoɔ tsɛnsi mli) ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni potassium eyi mli obɔ awo mli lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifã lɛ mli awa. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ adamɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings wither and die easily right after I transplant them into the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu amɛ yɛ saatso wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young seedlings experience shock when moved from a shaded nursery directly into the hot sun. To help them survive this hardship, transplant them late in the afternoon, water them immediately, and provide temporary shade for a few days until they adjust.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ ahe feɔ amɛ yaa kɛji ajie amɛ kɛjɛ he ko ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ yɔɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛje jaramɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ mli. Akɛ amɛ awo mli yɛ shwane mli, awo amɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni aha amɛ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo gbii fioo komɛi kɛyashi amɛbaatsake amɛhe.

english: Why should I raise pepper seeds in a nursery bed first instead of planting them directly into the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu pepper dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani madu yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper seeds are very tiny and vulnerable to harsh rains, hot sun, and insect attacks. A nursery bed acts as a safe shelter where you can closely protect and nourish the young plants until they are strong enough to withstand field conditions.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui lɛ daraaa kwraa, ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ nyɛɔ etswaa amɛ. hulu la ni mli edɔ kɛ kooloi bibii baanyɛ atutua Nursery beds tsuɔ nii akɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni obaanyɛ obu tsei bibii lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ ni okwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anaa.

english: Why do pests and insects seem to attack my crops more heavily during a dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni kooloi bibii kɛ kooloi bibii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops suffer from water shortage, their natural strength declines, making them weak and easy targets for hungry insects. Covering the soil with mulch keeps moisture in the ground, helping the crops resist pests during dry periods.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu he naagbai kpe Amɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ baa shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfeɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai yɛ hɔmɔ be mli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn turning yellow and drying up before the corn is ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves mean the crop is starving for nitrogen. When nutrients run low in the soil, the plant is forced to consume food from its older leaves to support new growth, showing that the farm needs compost or nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli. Kɛji niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa lɛ, abaanyɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni eye baai momoi koni eye ebua dalɛ hee. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How can I tell if the seed or fertilizer I am buying in the market is genuine and not fake?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ ji anɔkwale ni jeee amale?

english: Fake farm inputs often lack official seal tags, have misspelled brand names, or are sold unpackaged at unusually cheap prices. Always buy inputs from licensed agro-dealers and check for government certification labels on the bags to avoid being cheated.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔ mli saji ni ji amale lɛ bɛ stamp tag. Gbɛi ni aŋmalaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo ahɔ̃ɔ ni awooo mli yɛ jara ni waaa kwraa nɔ Hemɔ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ adɛŋ. Ni be fɛɛ be lɛ, kwɛmɔ nɔyeli lɛ he odaseyeli wolo ni yɔɔ kotoku lɛ nɔ lɛ koni akashishiu bo.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my cocoa pods so I do not pick them too early?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ? koni akabua naa oya tsɔ

english: Cocoa pods change color clearly when mature, turning from green or red to a bright yellow or orange. Harvesting only fully colored pods ensures the beans inside have finished developing properly and will ferment successfully.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su jogbaŋŋ beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Tsakemɔ kɛjɛ eŋɔli loo etsuru kɛya ŋmɔŋ loo akutu ni mli tse. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sui fɛɛ pɛ lɛ, ehaa kɔfi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛshwereɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are armyworms eating the inner leaves of my young maize crop so fast?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii miiye mi-baby corn lɛ mli baai lɛ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Fall armyworms prefer to lay eggs inside the leafy funnel of young maize plants. Warm, dry weather speeds up their hatching, and the tiny caterpillars eat the soft inner leaves before the plant has a chance to grow strong.
ga: Fall cutworms sumɔɔ ni amɛwo amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ amli. Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ baaha amɛfɔ oya. kɛ ŋmeii bibii Amɛyeɔ mligbɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ dani tso lɛ naa hegbɛ ni edaa waa.

english: What causes the black pods on my cocoa trees whenever heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ baa be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa?

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that spreads rapidly through water droplets splashing on the trees. The high humidity and wet leaves during the rainy season give the fungus the perfect environment to grow and rot the pods.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ nu ni shwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ baai ni efɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii ni amɛdaraa ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies. They suck the vital juices from the leaves and often spread viruses that distort the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Amɛmuɔ nu ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ baai amli ni bei pii lɛ amɛgbɛɔ helai ni fiteɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ amɛshwãa.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains next to my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantains yɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide living shade umbrellas, keeping the young cocoa cool and moist while it gets established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be mli ni ekɛ ehe woɔ mli lɛ.

english: How does planting groundnuts help make my soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that work with good bacteria in the soil to pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the groundnuts are harvested, that extra nitrogen stays behind to feed the next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ bacteria kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ sɛɛ koni ekɛha ŋmeii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I avoid planting my oil palm seedlings too close to one another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ ahe?

english: Oil palms need large amounts of sunlight, water, and soil space. Planting them too close forces them to fight each other for resources, resulting in tall, weak trees that produce small and few fruit bunches.
ga: Mu tso biɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ babaoo. Kɛ́ adu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ nibii ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ ahe. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ baawo yibii bibii.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow when my field stays flooded with water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nu eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air from the soil to stay healthy. When excess water fills all the air spaces in the ground, the roots choke and can no longer absorb nitrogen, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nu ni fa fe nine eyi kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛjie nitrogen dɔŋŋ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Why does my land yield less maize if I grow it on the exact same plot every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo kɛji midu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize continuously pulls the exact same nutrients from the soil every season. Planting it repeatedly without a break strips the soil of those nutrients and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the field.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Nibii ni aduɔ shii abɔ ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ni ekɛ helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ baa ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves, but produce small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes cassava put all its energy into growing green stems and leaves above ground, instead of sending food energy down to expand the tubers in the soil.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei mli babaoo lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ yeɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmei kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu niyenii hewalɛ kɛba shi koni ekɛgbala ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting just a few days after I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ bɔi fitemɔ beni mikɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ tsu nii lɛ?

english: Once cassava is harvested, oxygen enters the cut roots and triggers a natural breakdown process within two to three days, unlike crops like yam which have a protective skin that allows longer storage.
ga: Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei Oxygen boteɔ shishifãi ni afo lɛ amli ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli fitemɔ nifeemɔ ko jeɔ shishi yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli. Enɛ tamɔɔɔ tsei tamɔ sweet potatoes, ni yɔɔ hewolo ni buɔ amɛhe ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants turn yellow and burn under direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sun because their roots are shallow and lose water faster than they can absorb it. Shade trees or plantains act as living umbrellas, keeping the cocoa cool and retaining soil moisture until the trees mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛlaajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ nu lɛ. Tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ kɛyashiɔ tso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does spreading dry grass around my crops keep the soil damp for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ji No hewɔ lɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, creates a protective barrier over the soil. This shield blocks direct sunlight from evaporating moisture, keeping the root zone cool and hydrated during dry spells.
ga: Ale jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ tsɔne nɛɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa. Ha shishifã lɛ he lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape pattern?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for leafy growth. The plant takes nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the new top leaves, causing the bottom ones to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Tsei kɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant groundnuts on the same field after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen from the soil, leaving it weak. Groundnuts and other legumes have special roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally restoring soil fertility for the next crop season.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ Amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot inside the ground when the rains become too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: When heavy rain fills the soil with excess water, air cannot reach the plant roots. Starved of oxygen in waterlogged soil, cassava roots become weak and easily rot due to fungal and bacterial infections.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ahewɔ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off without producing any tomatoes during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air put stress on tomato plants. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy and water for survival rather than spending energy to make fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he koni amɛhi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛfee nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my main crops after a good rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to local soils. Their seeds can sit in the soil for years and are built to absorb water and nutrients faster than cultivated seeds, giving them a head start.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji tso ko ni yɔɔ koo mli ni wa ni ekɛ ehe ewo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli. Amɛdumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ ahi sũ lɛ mli afii babaoo. Ni abɔ amɛ koni amɛhe nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ. ni haa amɛnáa sɛɛnamɔ

english: Why do I see ragged holes in my maize leaves with tiny brown dirt in the middle of the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ kɛ muji bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ? yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm damage. The caterpillars hide inside the funnel (whorl) of young maize plants to eat the soft inner leaves, leaving behind sawdust-like droppings called frass.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm lɛ efite nii. Kplukai lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ a-funnels (rings) lɛ amli koni amɛye amɛmli baai bibii lɛ. Eshiɔ ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ frass lɛ yɛ esɛɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same patch of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that crop needs and allows pests and diseases that feed on that crop to build up in the soil. Changing crops starves out those pests and restores balanced nutrients.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ tsei lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ lɛ baaha nakai kooloi lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni ebaaha niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know the right day to plant my seeds when the rainy season keeps changing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ madu nii kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ tsake?

english: It is best to plant only after the ground receives a deep, continuous rainfall that soaks the top soil layer (about 3 straight days of steady rain). Planting after a light splash can cause seeds to sprout and then wither when dry days follow.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu nii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ ená nugbɔ ni mli kwɔ ni yaa nɔ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ edɔ pɛ. (Nugbɔ nɛ be fɛɛ be aaafee gbii 3 ni nyiɛ sɛɛ.) Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ la mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbo kɛji nugbɔ gbi lɛ bashɛ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crops with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Akɛ jwɛi loo baai ŋmɔɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, acts like a protective blanket. It keeps the soil cool under the strong sun, prevents water from evaporating quickly so roots stay wet longer, and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu shwieɔ oya Shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Why is it bad to apply my fertilizer right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa aba lɛ?

english: Heavy rain acts like a flood that washes your fertilizer away off the top of the field before the plant roots can absorb it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist or right after a light rain so the nutrients soak down to the roots.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nu afua, ni ekɛ o-fertilizer lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ yiteŋ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ momo loo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ koni niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ abote shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why are my young maize leaves turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize crop is lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green leaves. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the leaves turn green so the plant can grow big corn cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo loo ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ akwɛ ŋmei ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop to the ground without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni tomato ko kwraa kwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat stress, drought, or from receiving too much leaf-growing fertilizer instead of fruit-growing nutrients. Regular watering and partial afternoon shade help keep the flowers on the plant.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli fe nine mli lɛ mli moŋ fe niyenii ni jɛɔ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa kɛ shwane mli hulutsoo be ko yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and scorching?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiitso lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have very tender leaves that burn easily in full, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantain beside them provides temporary shade until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand the heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii waa ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Nurse tsei ni yɔɔ ekãa ni daa oya lɛ ni aaadu yɛ Emasɛi lɛ baaha hulutsoo be kukuoo ko aba kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ hulutsoo lɛ naa.

english: What causes these little ragged holes in my maize leaves with dirt like sawdust inside the plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni haa mi ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ buji bibii ni egbɛ eshwã kɛ muji tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The sawdust-like dirt is the caterpillar's waste, which it leaves behind as it hides and feeds deep inside the growing center of the maize plant.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Muji ni tamɔ ŋmei ji ŋmeii lɛ ashwiemɔ. ni eshiɔ yɛ esɛɛ beni ekɛ ehe teeɔ ni eyeɔ kɛyaa ŋmãa tso lɛ dalɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids hidden under the leaves. As they suck the plant's juices, they cause the developing leaves to grow unevenly and curl up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. be mli ni ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei amli lɛ Ehaa baai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ daraa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni amɛkpokpoɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slowly even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo yɛ nugbɔ babaoo ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow very fast and aggressively steal food, space, and light away from your main crops. Even with good rain, the crops suffer because the weeds are drinking up the soil nutrients first.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ niyenii, he ko, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ, shi Dumɔwui hu naa amanehulu ejaakɛ jwɛi yeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why should I cut off the extra small shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ Mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishitoo lɛ jie

english: Allowing too many shoots to grow causes them to compete with the main plantain tree for nutrients. Removing extra suckers and leaving only one or two allows the main tree to put all its energy into producing a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo akwɛ̃ lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ abɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kpakpai. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi eko loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are ready to harvest without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare upper stem, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack open from the growing tubers underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. Ashi ŋwɛi tso lɛ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ mli. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ kɛjɛ bulb ni miida yɛ eshishi lɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when the sun gets very bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They require shade from companion plants like plantains to shelter them from scorching heat and retain soil moisture while their roots develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni fata amɛhe, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli beni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen. Maize plants need nitrogen to grow, and when there is not enough in the ground, the plant moves what little it has from the older leaves to feed the new top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃. ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ faaa Tso lɛ jieɔ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momo lɛ amli kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off before they turn into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant is stressed by severe heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. Without enough moisture or energy, the plant drops its blossoms to save itself.
