ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni esaaa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ loo hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baafɔ fɔfɔi ni ekɛtsa ehe.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground during heavy rainy periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays waterlogged for too long without proper drainage. Excessive standing water suffocates the roots and encourages fungal diseases that decay the tuber.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni kɛ tuber rot baa lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every year even though I use the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ miiba shi daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops pull essential nutrients out of the earth every time they grow. If you plant on the same soil repeatedly without adding organic manure, compost, or fertilizer, the soil becomes empty of food and cannot produce strong plants.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be ni amɛbaakwɛ̃. Kɛji odu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shii abɔ Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni enyɛŋ ewo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger than my actual crops after I clear my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe mitsei diɛŋtsɛ lɛ beni mijie miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie hidden in the soil for years and are naturally adapted to germinate immediately after light and rain hit the ground. They grow aggressively to steal water and sunlight before planted crops get established.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe teeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afii babaoo. ni atsake lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekwɛ̃ kɛji la kɛ nugbɔ ba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ. Amɛdaraa waa koni amɛju nu kɛ hulu la dani adu ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why should I rotate my farmland by planting beans after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake mi-acreage lɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ beni mikpa ŋmeii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of soil nitrogen, while leguminous crops like beans put nitrogen back into the dirt through their roots. Alternating these crops keeps the soil fertile and breaks the cycle of pests.
ga: Abɛi kɛ nitrogen babaoo tsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nibii nɛɛ ni akɛtsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to leave wide spaces between our plants instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei anɔ lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔshi he ko ni da yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni wɔbaadu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their leaves fight for sunlight and their roots fight for water and nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to feed and grow thick, healthy cobs or fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Shishifãi lɛ baatswa akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ niyenii. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ nii ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii loo aduawai ni mli wa, ni mli wa.

english: What causes small green caterpillars to hide inside my young maize stems and eat the leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ mi-abele bibii lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, hatched from eggs laid on maize leaves by flying moths. They feed on the soft, growing parts of the stem and leaves, which can destroy the stalk if not treated early.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni fɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛwoɔ ŋmeii baa anɔ lɛ amli. Amɛyeɔ tsei ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ ahe nibii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ afite tso lɛ yitso lɛ kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ mra.

english: How do I know if the ground is ready for seed planting at the beginning of the rainy season?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔwui adumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Soil is ready for planting after two or three continuous, deep rainfalls that soak into the earth. Planting after just one light shower is risky because the dry soil underneath will absorb the seed's moisture and stop it from sprouting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔ ni aaadu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Shikome pɛ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ baaŋɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli nu lɛ ni ebaatsi enaa koni ekakwɛ̃.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, a key food they need to grow strong. It can also happen when too much water stays around the roots after heavy rain, preventing the plant from taking up food from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu babaoo eshwɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under the harsh sun. Plantains grow very fast and have broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving the young cocoa shade and cooler soil to help it survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha lɛ hulutsoo kɛjɛ kookoo ni mli tse kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ mli koni eye ebua lɛ ni ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava plants shed their leaves during the dry season, and will the crop die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ? Ni ani ŋmɔshi nii lɛ baagbo?

english: Cassava drops its leaves on purpose to save water during dry weather so it does not dry out and die. The tubers underground remain alive and safe, and the plant will grow fresh leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi koni akɛbu nu he yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, egbiɛɛ ni egbooo. Tubers lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni amɛyɛ shweshweeshwe. Ni tsei lɛ baakwɛ baai heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ pɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and soft before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efee blɛoo dani eshɛ po lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit or irregular watering. When the plant goes through dry spells followed by sudden heavy watering, it cannot move calcium smoothly into the growing tomatoes.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ. Beni tsei tsɔ hɔmɔ be mli ni nu ni akɛhaa amɛ trukaa, ni mli wa nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ. Enyɛŋ ekɛ calcium lɛ aya tomato ni miida lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant many maize seeds together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa babaoo yɛ he kome yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants must fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. This competition causes all of them to grow thin and weak, resulting in small ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Esa akɛ tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extremely hot temperatures, lack of soil moisture, or a shortage of plant nutrients. Keeping the soil evenly moist and cool can help the flowers stay on and produce peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ hulutsoo be mli. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo niyenii ni jɛɔ tsei amli lɛ ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli ejɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply my chemical fertilizer right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainwater washes fertilizer off the top of the soil and carries it away into streams or deep underground before your crops have time to drink it. It is best to fertilize when the soil is moist but heavy rain is not falling.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛshwieɔ faai loo shikpɔŋ shishi dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛnuɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enɛɛɛ.

english: Why do I need to provide tall sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi niji ni kwɔlɔ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch as much sunlight as possible. Staking lifts the foliage off the ground, preventing leaf diseases and helping the plant produce larger underground tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: If I get a great harvest from hybrid maize seeds this year, why shouldn't I save seeds from that harvest to plant next season?
ga: Kɛji minine shɛ yibii kpakpai anɔ kɛjɛ hybrid corn mli afi nɛɛ. Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred from two different parent plants to produce high yields only in the first generation. If you plant seeds saved from that crop, the next generation will lose its strength, growing unevenly and producing much smaller yields.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔi tsei srɔtoi enyɔ amli koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ pɛ mli. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ Yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baafite hewalɛ. shweremɔ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee ni yibiiwoo lɛ faaa kwraa

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas in my field make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to the legume family, which has the natural ability to take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When you harvest them, they leave behind enriched soil that feeds the next crop you plant.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛyɛ adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛgbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji okpa amɛ Ebaashi shikpɔŋ ni baa nii koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I clear all the big trees off my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight because their foliage is soft and delicate. Large trees provide shade that lowers temperatures, retains soil moisture, and protects young cocoa leaves from scorching during their early growth stage.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo. Tsei wuji haa hulutsoo ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo baa shi. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni obu kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee mli.

english: Why do my harvested cassava tubers start to spoil and turn dark within just two days of digging them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ lɛ bɔi fitemɔ ni amɛfee duŋ yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ mli beni mifo amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots stop receiving water and nutrients once detached from the living plant. This triggers a rapid natural reaction called post-harvest physiological deterioration, where internal tissues break down quickly if not processed or preserved.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ kpaɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni amɛyeɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni hiɛ ka lɛ amli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni yaa nɔ oya ni atsɛɔ lɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ baa. Mli fãji lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii loo akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow even though there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? He ni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate that the maize plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is an essential nutrient responsible for leaf greenness and growth, and heavy rains can sometimes wash it away deeper into the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baa lɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛ dalɛ. Ni bei komɛi lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ atswa baai kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: Why does my yam plant grow thick green leaves above ground but produces very small tubers under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli tse yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or green organic matter relative to other nutrients, the yam plant directs all its energy toward leafy vine growth instead of transferring starches downward to swell the underground tuber.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ fa babaoo kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Sweet potato tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa wain tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni eeekɛ starch aya koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into fruits during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: High temperatures stress tomato plants and dry out the pollen inside the flowers, preventing pollination. When a flower fails to get pollinated, the plant naturally drops it to save water and energy.
ga: He ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ waa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ egbiɔ. Tsi pollination naa Beni anyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ pollination lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my plantain trees yield small fruit bunches when I allow many shoots to grow around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii bibii lɛ? Akɛni miŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ tso wulu lɛ he hewɔ lɛ.

english: Multiple side shoots, or suckers, compete directly with the main plantain tree for nutrients, water, and sunlight. Pruning extra suckers ensures the main tree receives full nourishment to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tsoi lɛ, loo tsei ni yɔɔ afã lɛ, kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ fɛɛ koni ekɛwo tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my dried maize grains develop tiny holes and turn into brown powder after a few weeks in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni ebafeɔ powda ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi ni akɛtoɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Maize weevils lay eggs inside stored grains. When the eggs hatch, the larvae eat the nutritious inside of the grain and bore tiny holes to emerge as adult beetles, leaving behind dust and hollowed seeds.
ga: Abele ŋmeii woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmaa ni ato lɛ mli. Beni ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ lɛ ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛfoɔ buji bibii amli. Koni ebatsɔ ladybug onukpa Eshiɔ sũ kɛ dumɔwui ni mli ewo muji.

english: Why do my citrus trees shed a lot of small green oranges before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso lɛ miijie akutu bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Babaoo dani eda?

english: Citrus trees naturally shed excess immature fruit when they experience water shortages, poor nutrient supply, or insect damage. Dropping fruit helps the tree reduce stress and keep the remaining fruits healthy.
ga: Citrus tsei lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji amɛkɛ nu ni faaa kpe. Niyenii loo kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ efiteee Yibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa nɔnyɛɛ baa shi ni ehaa yibii ni eshwɛ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does planting cowpea or beans in my field help the maize crop I plant next season grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpea and beans have special bacteria in their root nodules that capture nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into a natural soil fertilizer that benefits future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni yeɔ ebuaa ni emɔɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up tightly and stop growing during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is a self-defense mechanism to reduce surface area and minimize water loss during dry conditions, but it can also be caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding under the leaves.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he koni akɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni nu ni fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ shi. Shi kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai ashishi lɛ hu baanyɛ aha eba.

english: Why do some maize seeds have special names like 'Obaatampa' while others are just called local seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui komɛi yɛ gbɛi krɛdɛɛi tamɔ ‘Obaatampa’ yɛ be mli ni atsɛɔ ekrokomɛi akɛ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Special names are given to 'improved varieties' developed by agricultural researchers. These varieties are carefully bred to give higher yields, resist diseases, or contain higher nutritional value compared to traditional local seeds.
ga: Akɛ gbɛi krɛdɛɛ ko haa ‘Improved varieties’ ni okwaayeli he niiamlitaolɔi fee lɛ Akwɛ nɛkɛ srɔtoi nɛɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛná yibii babaoo, helai ni nyɛɔ amɛhe amɛyeɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ babaoo kɛ akɛto blema maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ahe.

english: What does it mean when you tell me a crop variety was 'developed by scientists'?
ga: Beni okɛɛ mi tso nɔ̃ Mɛni ‘jeŋ nilelɔi fee’ lɛ tsɔɔ?

english: It means plant breeders spent years testing and combining different plant strains to select the best traits—such as fast growth, strong stalks, and drought resistance—into a single seed variety for farmers.
ga: Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei anɔ lɛ yeɔ afii babaoo amɛkaa tsei srɔtoi lɛ amɛkwɛɔ ni amɛkɛfeɔ ekome. Kɛji akɛ ahala sui ni hi fe fɛɛ tamɔ tso ni dalɛ yaa oya kɛ hɔmɔ ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ hɔmɔ akɛ dumɔwui komekomei kɛha okwaafoi

english: Are improved maize varieties like Obaatampa healthy and safe for my family to eat?
ga: Ani ŋmãa ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ tamɔ Obaatampa lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha miweku lɛ ni amɛye?

english: Yes, they are completely safe and often healthier. For example, Obaatampa was specifically bred by researchers to contain higher levels of essential proteins (Quality Protein Maize) to improve family nutrition.
ga: Hɛɛ, amɛyɛ shweshweeshwe kwraa, ni bei pii lɛ, amɛyɛ hewalɛ. Akɛ nɔkwɛmɔ nɔ lɛ, niiamlitaolɔi efɔ Obatampa pɔtɛɛ koni protein ni he hiaa babaoo ahi mli. (abɛi mli protein ni hi jogbaŋŋ) koni akɛha weku lɛ niyenii aya hiɛ

english: Where do certified maize seeds sold in agrovate shops come from?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ agrovate shwapoi amli lɛ jɛɔ?

english: Certified seeds originate from agricultural research centers (like the Crops Research Institute in Kumasi) where plant breeders produce foundation seeds, which are then multiplied under strict quality checks by seed producers.
ga: Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ jɛɔ okwaayeli he niiamlitaomɔ hei (tamɔ Crops Research Institute ni yɔɔ Kumasi) he ni mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ shishijee dumɔwui lɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, mɛi ni feɔ dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɔ bɔ ni amɛhi jogbaŋŋ ha lɛ nɔ amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa.

english: Will buying improved maize seeds give me a bigger harvest than using seeds saved from my last crop?
ga: Ani ŋmãa dumɔwui ni atsake lɛ ni miheɔ lɛ baaha maná yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mikɛbaatsu nii kɛjɛ minaagbee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yes, improved seeds are bred specifically for high yield potential. Seeds saved from previous harvests gradually lose their vigor, productivity, and resistance to pests over time.
ga: Hɛɛ, afɔɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio. Efiteɔ hewalɛ, yibiiwoo, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ.

english: Can I save seeds from my harvested Obaatampa maize to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ Obatampa ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ ato koni madu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: You can plant saved seeds from open-pollinated varieties like Obaatampa for a season or two, but buying fresh certified seed ensures you get the highest yield and full disease protection intended by the breeders.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni agbele naa tamɔ Obaatampa lɛ amli kɛha be kome loo enyɔ. Shi dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ni ooohe lɛ haa onáa yibii babaoo kɛ helai ahebuu ni yeɔ emuu ni dumɔwui akwɛlɔi biɔ lɛ.

english: Why do some maize varieties mature in three months while others take four months or longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi shwereɔ yɛ nyɔji etɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni srɔtoi komɛi heɔ nyɔji ejwɛ loo nɔ ni fe nakai lɛ?

english: Breeders create different varieties to match different rainfall patterns. Short-duration varieties mature quickly for areas with short rainy seasons, while long-duration varieties maximize yield where rains last longer.
ga: Mɛi ni kwɛɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ feɔ kooloi srɔtoi koni amɛkɛ nugbɔshiimɔi srɔtoi lɛ akpã gbee. Henɔi ni hiɔ shi be kuku lɛ daa oya yɛ hei ni nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo yɔɔ lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii srɔtoi ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do pests attack my local maize crop while an improved variety field nearby stays healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai miitutuaa mimaŋ ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔji ni asaa amɛhe ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ kã he amɛyɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Researchers specifically breed improved varieties with natural resistance mechanisms against common field pests and diseases, allowing the crop to defend itself better without heavy chemical use.
ga: Nibii amlitaolɔi fɔɔ kooloi srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli gbɛjianɔtoi ni teɔ shi woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ. Ehaa tsei buɔ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ ni tsofai ni tsii he ehiaaa amɛ.

english: How do I know which maize variety is best suited for the soil and weather in my district?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmãa henɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha mishikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ?

english: Scientists test new varieties across different ecological zones in Ghana before releasing them. Extension officers use these research results to recommend the exact variety that thrives in your region's rainfall and soil type.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔi kaa kooloi heei amɛkwɛɔ yɛ bɔɔ nii sɔrɔtoi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ amli dani amɛjieɔ amɛ kpo Extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛ nibii ni amɛna nɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛtsɔɔ kooloi srɔtoi pɔtɛɛ ni shwereɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my maize crop roll up its leaves when it doesn't rain for two weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi beni nugbɔ enɛko otsii enyɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a crop's natural survival mechanism to reduce water evaporation during dry spells. Certain improved drought-tolerant varieties are bred to withstand this water stress longer without damaging the crop yield.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛha nu ni hoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ aba shi. Afɔ tsei srɔtoi komɛi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ nu mli haomɔ naa be babaoo ni amɛfiteee ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when there is too much direct sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and shallow roots that cannot store enough water under hot, direct sunlight. They need temporary shade from crops like plantains to protect them from high heat and keep the soil moist while they build strength.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ahiɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains mli koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛtswaa hewalɛ amɛmaa shi lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and turning small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaves or spreading a virus. Controlling these insects early with neem oil spray helps protect new foliage from twisting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu loo helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ buɔ baai heei ahe koni amɛkatsɔ amɛhe.

english: Yellowing lower leaves indicate that your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient needed for green leaf growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or well-decomposed manure helps restore green leaves and improves grain development.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmeii ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai eŋɔli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ ni eha dumɔwui lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why should I avoid planting maize on the exact same plot of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ŋmãa dumɔ he afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot drains specific soil nutrients and lets maize pests build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpea or groundnut refills nitrogen in the soil naturally and stops pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, abaajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi. ni oha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Ebaaha nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ebaakpa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: What causes my cassava roots to rot in the ground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani manyɛ makpa amɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much standing water, which prevents air from reaching the roots and encourages fungal diseases. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps water drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo tsɔ. Enɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela he hewalɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do I need to support my yam vines with tall stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tsei kakadaji fiɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ asɛɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mahã amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking yam vines lifts leaves up into the sunlight so the plant can make more food to grow bigger tubers underneath. It also keeps leaves off damp soil, reducing fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Staking sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ afee niyenii babaoo ni ekɛ bulbs wuji akwɛ̃ yɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ he. Ha fungal baa helai aba shi

english: Tomato plants shed their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat, long dry spells, or a lack of nutrients like phosphorus. Consistent watering during flowering and balanced soil nutrients encourage blossoms to stay and set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji latsaa ni naa wa hao amɛ. be kakadaŋŋ ni egbiɔ loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa yɛ fɔfɔii ashishijee mli kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Why does my plantain mat produce small, weak bunches when I leave many shoots growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ beni mishiɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ tso lɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Having too many shoots (suckers) forces them to compete with the main plant for food, light, and water. Pruning away excess suckers so only 2 or 3 shoots remain allows the main stem to focus energy on growing large bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ amɛná ŋmeii (ŋmeii) babaoo lɛ, no haa amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ yɛ niyenii, la, kɛ nu he. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ tsei 2 loo 3 pɛ bɔni afee ni tso titri lɛ ajwɛŋmɔ ahi tsei wuji ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating holes inside the middle leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a pest that hides deep inside the whorl (funnel) of young corn plants to feed on tender leaves. Checking young plants early and applying biopesticides or ash into the funnel stops them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Tsei bibii lɛ akwɛmɔ mra kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo sũ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ Kpa amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why should I wait for steady rain instead of planting my seeds right after the very first rain shower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain shower is often followed by hot dry spells that dry out topsoil, causing newly germinated seeds to wither and die. Waiting for continuous, established rains ensures the soil stays wet enough for seedlings to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ gĩɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛgboiɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ mɛmɔ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize start curling up during the dry afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ yɛ shwane ni nu egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural survival mechanism that maize uses to reduce water loss. By rolling its leaves inward, the plant exposes less leaf surface to the hot sun and wind, helping it retain moisture until the soil cools down.
ga: Leaf curling ji adebɔɔ mli wala ni ŋmãa kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛba nu ni fiteɔ lɛ shi. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni aaatsɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ baajie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ hulu la fioo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do my vegetables turn yellow and dry out when the afternoon sun gets extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When sunlight and heat become too intense, crops lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can take it up from the soil. This extreme heat damages the leaf tissue, causing the plant to turn yellow and wilt as a reaction to heat stress.
ga: Kɛ hulu la kɛ latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa nɛɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ akɛ nɔ ni jɛɔ hulutsoo mli haomɔ mli baa.

english: Why do crops grown inside small, low-roof shade structures sometimes overheat and wither?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ tsũi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shishi lɛ amli lɛ mli dɔɔ fe nine ni amɛgboɔ lɛ?

english: Structures with low roofs trap hot air near the plants because there is not enough height or space for the hot air to rise and move out. Without proper height and airflow, heat builds up inside like an oven, causing heat stress to the crops.
ga: Tsuji ni amɛyiteŋ baa shi lɛ mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ yɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋwɛi ŋsɔɔdo loo he ko bɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ baanyɛ aya ŋwɛi ni efã kɛya he kroko. Kɛji akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni sa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ bɛ lɛ, Dɔlɛ buaa ehe naa yɛ mli tamɔ flɔnɔɔ. Ekɛ dɔlɛ haomɔ baa ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ.

english: Why do plants inside tall, protected structures develop larger leaves than crops exposed to open field winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ tsũi ni kwɔlɔ ni abuɔ he lɛ amli lɛ woɔ baai wuji fe tsei ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa amɛ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Strong winds force open-field crops to grow smaller, tougher leaves to prevent damage and excessive water loss. Inside tall, sheltered structures, plants are protected from harsh wind and can safely expand larger leaves to capture maximum sunlight.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa nyɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ anɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ afee bibii ni amɛhe wa. Enɛ haaa nɔ ko afite kɛ nu ni hoɔ fe nine. Tsu lɛ mli lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe. Abuɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ baai wuji shweshweeshwe koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow very tall and thin instead of producing fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: When plants do not receive enough direct sunlight or are planted too close together, they stretch upward searching for light. The plant spends all its energy growing high instead of using that energy to produce flowers and fruit.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tso lɛ shwieɔ ehe kɛyaa ŋwɛi ni etaoɔ la. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ jamɛ a he wami ɔ tsuɔ ní kɛ woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yiblii.

english: Why do my pepper flowers drop off before turning into fruits during warm periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when air temperatures rise too high or when soil moisture is low. The plant intentionally drops flowers to save energy and water so it can survive until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ mli latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ faaa. Tsei tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he koni amɛhi shi kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall sticks to climb up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tsei kakadaji koni enyɛ ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to reach higher sunlight above ground level. Climbing tall stakes keeps the leaves exposed to sun and off the damp soil, which improves airflow, reduces leaf diseases, and helps the plant send more energy down to grow large tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa hulu la ni nɔ kwɔ fe shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni akwɔɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ naa hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe helai baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛkudɔɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shi koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji.

english: Why do my cassava plants lose their leaves during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai miifite yɛ harmattan be ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry weather to stop water from escaping through leaf pores. This dormant state allows the cassava root to stay alive underground until the rains return and new leaves sprout.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ koni nu akatsɔ baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli. Shihilɛ ni yɔɔ dioo nɛɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ni baai heei jeɔ kpo.

english: Why do my cabbages produce loose leaves instead of forming solid heads when planted close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he lɛ?

english: Cabbages require adequate root space, nutrients, and sunlight to form firm heads. When crowded together, their roots compete for food and their leaves shade each other out, preventing the inner leaves from tightening into a head.
ga: Cabbage he miihia shishifãi ahe gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa, niyenii mli hewalɛ, kɛ hulu la koni ekɛfee yitsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ amɛbua amɛhe naa babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ niyenii he akaŋ ni amɛbaai lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ ji koni mligbɛ baai lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ aahu akɛ amɛtsɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need plantain trees planted right beside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa ni adu dumɔwu yɛ emasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that easily burn under full, direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad shade leaves that protect young cocoa plants from harsh sun and keep the surrounding air humid during their early growth stage.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ shishijee be mli ni edara lɛ

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting from the bottom leaves usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to make green leaf material and grow strong. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted manure restores nutrient levels.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee baai eŋɔli nibii ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Nitrogen babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same plot drains the soil of specific nutrients and allows pests to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with leguminous crops like beans or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ daa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa niyenii pɔtɛɛi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Enɛ baaha nitrogen lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How do I know which end of a cassava stem cutting should face up when I am planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male fã ni esa akɛ mafo mi yucca niji lɛ anɔ kɛ́ midu nii?

english: Look closely at the tiny buds or nodes where leaves used to grow; those buds should point upwards toward the sky. Planting cassava stems upside down forces the shoots to grow downwards first, which weakens the plant and reduces tuber yield.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii lɛ. Ebɛŋkɛ he ni tsutsu lɛ baai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Esa akɛ nakai ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu cassava ni atsɔ hiɛ awo shishi lɛ, ebaaha ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ akwɛ̃ shi klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha ŋmeii ni baa lɛ aba shi.

english: Why is it important for me to clear tall trees and plant plantains alongside my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo tsei kakadaji ni madu dumɔwui yɛ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight and need shade to survive their first two years. Plantains grow fast and provide big leaves that act as temporary sunshades while keeping the soil around the cocoa moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Ni ehe miihia ni ená hulutsoo koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ mlɛo. kookoo ni mli efɔ

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need sunlight to make food for growing tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground to catch maximum sunlight and prevents leaf diseases caused by direct soil contact.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la koni amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ niyenii. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ená hulu la babaoo ni ekɛtsiɔ baai ahe helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akɛkpeɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli baa lɛ naa.

english: What is causing small ragged holes and sawdust-like dirt inside the top funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Muji ni etse ni tamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ mi ŋmã tsei bibii lɛ anɔ ŋmei lɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the growing tip of maize. Spraying approved pesticides or applying neem extract directly into the central funnel early in the morning kills the pest before it destroys the shoot.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ niyenii yɛ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ loo okɛ neem mli nu lɛ wo tsɔne ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi lɛ dani ebaanyɛ efite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava roots turning soft and rotting inside the soil before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays waterlogged for too long, allowing fungal infections to develop underground. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the root zone.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop and look dead during hot afternoons even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gboɔ ni etamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: In intense heat, plant leaves lose water into the air faster than roots can draw it from the soil. Drooping is a temporary self-defense mechanism to reduce sun exposure, and plants recover once temperatures drop in the evening.
ga: Yɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ Tso baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Hiŋmɛii ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ mɔ he yɛ be kukuoo mli koni hulu la ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Ni tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when plants experience stress from high heat, dry spells, or lack of soil nutrients like calcium. Keeping soil consistently moist and applying balanced fertilizer prevents flowers from falling off prematurely.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa, tamɔ calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli lɛ, ebaatsi fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi oya lɛ naa.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my crop seeds right on the day I plant them?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo midumɔwui lɛ amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ dumɔ gbi lɛ nɔ?

english: No, seeds already contain stored energy to sprout and do not need external fertilizer immediately. Applying chemical fertilizer too early can burn young roots; it is best to wait about two weeks after sprouting when roots can absorb nutrients safely.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui eto hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ momo. Ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛɔ kponɔgbɛ awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsu nii oya lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi bibii lɛ ashã. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ aaafee otsii enyɔ beni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to strong sunlight and heat. Plantains grow quickly and produce wide leaves that act like natural umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa trees from intense sun and keeping the soil moist during their first couple of years.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plants are hungry for nitrogen, an important food crop plants need to grow strong and green. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea near the stems will help them regain their dark green color and grow big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa Esa akɛ tsei lɛ adara ni amɛhe wa ni amɛfee ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ená eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ kɛ etsitsi agbo lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Does it matter which direction I face cassava stem cuttings when planting them in the soil?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmei ni afo lɛ akpee beni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, cassava stems have tiny buds along the stick that must point upward toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the shoots have to bend awkwardly to reach the surface, which weakens the plant and reduces the amount of cassava roots you can harvest.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei tsei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi bibii ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu ŋwɛi Esa akɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ abɔle ehe yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ gbeyei nɔ koni eshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmei shishifãi ni obaanyɛ okpa lɛ baa shi.

english: What causes the bottom parts of my green tomatoes to turn black and rotten before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani ekwɛ̃ɔ?

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot, and it happens when the tomato plant cannot draw enough calcium from the ground, often caused by irregular watering. Water your plants regularly and evenly so calcium can flow properly into the developing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa kɛji akɛ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Okɛ nu awo tsei lɛ amli daa kɛ daa koni calcium ni sa lɛ aya aduawai ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Covering your soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, blocks the hot sun from drying out the earth quickly. It keeps the roots cool, stops weeds from growing, and slowly rots to feed the soil with rich organic nutrients.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsĩ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ akagbi oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛfiteɔ fiofio koni ekɛ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo aha shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants shed all their flowers without growing any fruits during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the afternoon sun gets too hot or when the soil becomes too dry. The heat stresses the plant, so it sheds flowers to save water and energy just to survive until cooler conditions return.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ shwane hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Dɔlɛ haa tsei haoɔ Amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi kɛkɛ kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it good practice to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are special plants that pull natural fertilizer from the air and deposit it straight into the soil through their roots. When you grow them alongside maize, they naturally feed the soil so your maize crop grows better without needing as much store-bought fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ odu lɛ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, o-abele lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ awo mli.

english: Why do I need to spend time putting long wooden sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafite be babaoo kɛma tsei kakadaji anɔ lɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need to climb tall sticks so their leaves can spread out widely in the direct sunlight. The more sunlight the upper leaves gather, the more energy the plant creates to grow big, heavy yam tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei niji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã babaoo yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Babaoo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ anɔ lɛ naa lɛ, babaoo ni tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together so I can get more crops on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close forces the maize plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition makes the stalks thin and weak, resulting in tiny cobs instead of the big, full cobs you get when plants have enough room to feed.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ebafeɔ ŋmei bibioo ko. Yɛ ŋmei agbo ni eyi obɔ najiaŋ lɛ, beni tso lɛ ná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ nii.

english: How do I know if my farm soil is healthy enough to start planting when the rainy season starts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Healthy soil should crumble easily in your hands, feel slightly moist, and look dark brown or black. Adding animal manure or decomposed compost before planting improves soil texture and ensures seeds have the early nutrients they need to sprout quickly.
ga: Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ akumɔ oya yɛ oniji amli. Enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo ni etamɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni efite fata he dani adu lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ni eha dumɔwui lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ mra koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize crops turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to grow green and strong, or that water is logging the roots and starving them of air.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehe wa. Aloo nu boteɔ mli ni efiteɔ shishifãi lɛ ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground if I leave them buried during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy; when heavy rains soak the ground without proper drainage, excess water drowns the roots and allows fungi to attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ shishi ni eha ŋmeii atutua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfite.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping many of their blossoms before any pods actually form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ miiho baai babaoo dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop extra flowers if they do not get enough nutrients or soil moisture, or if small pests like mirids attack the delicate flower stems.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baajie fɔfɔi kɛjɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛnáaa niyenii mli hewalɛ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ pollen lɛ tutua fɔfɔi lɛ ahe tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and soft before they get a chance to ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit while it grows, which often happens when watering is irregular during dry spells.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli beni edaa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu lɛ efɔɔɔ shi be fɛɛ be yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my mature plantain plants keep falling over even when there is no strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni eda lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko bɛ po lɛ?

english: Tiny underground pests called nematodes or banana stem weevils eat away at the roots and base of the plant, weakening its support until the heavy plant topples over.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi bibii ni ale amɛ akɛ nematodes loo banana ŋmeii, amɛyeɔ tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ eshishi. Enɛ haa sɛɛfimɔ lɛ baa shi kɛyashiɔ tso ni tsii lɛ gbeeɔ shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into tight shapes and stopping new growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ hee lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant juices, which twists the leaves and stunts the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii, tamɔ aphids loo thrips, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ shishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ nu lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ tsɔɔ baai lɛ amli ni ehaa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why should I wait a few weeks after my maize sprouts before giving it its main dose of fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ otsii fioo komɛi beni ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ dani maha ŋmãa titri lɛ?

english: Very young maize roots are too small to absorb heavy doses of fertilizer right away, so applying it when the crop reaches knee-height feeds the plants right when they start growing rapidly.
ga: Abɛi shishifãi ni darako kwraa lɛ daraaa tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo amrɔ nɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛwo mli beni tsei lɛ eshɛ amɛkuɛ he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ niyenii kɛji amɛbɔi dalɛ oya pɛ.

english: Why do my stored yam setts take a long time to shoot sprouts after I plant them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers go through a natural rest period called dormancy after harvest, requiring time and warm soil conditions before chemical signals inside trigger new shoots to sprout.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Akɛ be kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii dani tsofai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii heei kwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas alongside my main crops make the soil better for future seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ masɛi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with good soil bacteria to pull nitrogen directly from the air and fix it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for surrounding plants.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai kpakpai tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛsaa lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa tsei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ.

english: Why does plowing the soil before planting help my crops grow faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛtsuɔ nii dani miduɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya lɛ?

english: Plowing loosens hard, compacted dirt, allowing young crop roots to easily push deep into the earth, breathe air, and absorb water and nutrients much faster than in unplowed soil.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoo haa muji ni wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, amɛmuɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, ni amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe shikpɔŋ ni atsuuu nii yɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds sprout so much faster than my crops right after I clear and plow my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mijie sũ lɛ ni mitsu he nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds can lie sleeping deep under the ground for years; plowing brings them up to the surface where heat and sunlight wake them up to sprout instantly before your crop seeds can catch up.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ afii babaoo. Gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ kɛ amɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la lɛ teɔ amɛ shi yɛ dani odumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe.

english: If I plant my cassava closer together, will I get a bigger harvest from my farm?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe Ani maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, because plants need space to share sunlight, water, and soil food. Planting too closely forces crops to fight each other, resulting in tall, skinny plants with tiny cassava tubers instead of thick, heavy ones.
ga: Dabi, tsei he miihia he ko ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛja hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe awuu. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe tseee ni amɛyɛ cassava shishifãi bibii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsii

english: Maize needs nitrogen food to grow. When the soil runs out of food, the plant pulls remaining nitrogen from its old bottom leaves to feed the new top growth, causing the bottom leaves to yellow and dry up.
ga: Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii Tso lɛ gbalaa nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up tight like tubes during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe tamɔ paipii yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves is the plant's natural defense against heat. By curling up, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun to stop itself from losing precious water.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Kɛtsɔ curling nɔ lɛ, tsei haa he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi koni amɛkpa nu ni jara wa ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why does my field produce smaller harvests if I grow maize on the exact same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛji midu ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Each crop type feeds heavily on specific soil nutrients. Planting the same crop repeatedly drains those exact nutrients completely and allows pests that feed on that specific crop to build up in the soil.
ga: Tso henɔ fɛɛ tso yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Ebaajie nakai niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ lɛ kwraa. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ nakai tso lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do extension officers advise planting cowpeas or beans on land after harvesting corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu cowpeas loo beans yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special plants that pull nitrogen food from the air and fix it back into the ground, naturally enriching the soil for the next crop without needing extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa niyenii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping all their flowers without producing any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni ewooo pepper yibii ko lɛ?

english: When plants face extreme dry heat or excessive nitrogen fertilizer, they get stressed and drop their flowers to save energy to stay alive, rather than spending energy making fruit.
ga: Kɛji tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe wo latsaa mli, hulutsoo be ni mli egbi waa loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli. Amɛhaoɔ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi wala mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛfee aduawai

english: Why do caterpillars like armyworms attack young corn leaves more than old ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tamɔ armyworms lɛ tutuaa ŋmãa baai bibii fe baa momo lɛ?

english: Young corn leaves are soft, tender, and full of water, making them easy and tasty for young pests to chew through, unlike tough, fibrous leaves on mature plants.
ga: Abɛi bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni nu eyi mli obɔ. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛyeɔ ni amɛ ŋɔɔ. Ejeee tamɔ baai ni wa, ni yɔɔ fiber ni yɔɔ tsei ni eda lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot so fast if I pack them into transport trucks immediately after digging them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mikɛwo lɔle lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mifo mli lɛ?

english: Freshly dug yams have thin skins and fresh scratches from harvesting tools. Letting them dry in the shade for a few days cures and hardens the skin, creating a protective barrier against decay organisms during transit.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni atsa ehee lɛ Kpãa bibioo ko baafee nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni eyɛ ŋmeii heei ni jɛ ŋmaakpamɔ nibii amli Kɛ́ oha egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ, ebaatsa hewolo lɛ ni eha ewa. Efeɔ gbɛtsii nii ko ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ.

english: If the rains do not come on time, how can I keep my young crops from dying in the dry soil?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ yɛ be naa Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsei bibii akagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ?

english: You can protect young crops during dry spells by mulching—covering the soil around the plants with dry grass, leaves, or straw. Mulch acts like a blanket that traps moisture in the ground and prevents the sun from drying out the roots.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu tsei bibii ahe yɛ hɔmɔ be mli kɛtsɔ sũ ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ—ni okɛ sũ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ awo mli. Kɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo jwɛi du. Mulch tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ sũ mli, ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ naa ni ehaa hulu la lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ agbi.

english: Is it better to wait for the heavy rains before planting my maize, or can I plant right after the first light rain?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ waa dani odu ŋmãa loo ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is safer to wait until the rains are steady. Planting after just one light rain can trick seeds into sprouting, but if the sun comes back for weeks without rain, the young sprouts will dry up and die in the soil.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baa shi. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Be kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃. Shi kɛ́ hulu tso otsii babaoo ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ hu? Tsei bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if my crops are suffering from too much water or not enough water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu babaoo loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ miipiŋ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: When crops do not get enough water, their leaves roll up, turn dull, and wilt during the day. When crops get too much water, their leaves turn pale yellow, feel soft, and the roots start to rot because they cannot breathe in soggy soil.
ga: Kɛji tsei lɛ naaa nu bɔ ni sa lɛ, amɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nu babaoo lɛ Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛnuɔ he akɛ amɛhe ejɔ, ni shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Does clearing and digging the soil deeply before planting really help my crops produce more food?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni mifoɔ ni mifoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani miduɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii babaoo?

english: Yes, breaking up hard soil allows plant roots to grow deep and wide easily. Deep roots help the crop search for underground water and nutrients, making the plant stronger against strong winds and dry weather.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ ni wa ni akumɔ mli lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ tsei shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛmli kwɔ. Shishifãi ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enaa shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ niyenii. Ehaa tsei nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi.

english: Why do my crops grow well on land where clear weeded grass was left to rot, compared to land where I burned the grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni jwɛi ni mli tse efite lɛ nɔ lɛ? Kɛ akɛto he ni mishã jwɛi lɛ yɛ lɛ he?

english: Leaving cleared grass to rot naturally turns it into organic manure, which feeds the soil and keeps it moist. Burning grass destroys beneficial soil life and washes away key nutrients when it rains.
ga: Jwɛi ni he tse ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni efiteɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ haa efeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa sũ lɛ náa hewalɛ ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Jwɛi ni ashã lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ wala ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ, ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛji nugbɔ nɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops wilt and drop during the hottest part of the afternoon even when the soil is damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: During intense midday heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the ground. Wilting is the plant's defense mechanism to shrink its leaf area and save water until the sun cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Withering ji tso ko gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe koni ekɛbaa baai lɛ amli ni ekɛto nu he kɛyashi hulu lɛ baajɔ.

english: Why do pests and caterpillars seem to attack my crops right after a short rain followed by strong heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ ŋmeii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ fioo lɛ? ni dɔlɛ ni naa wa nyiɛɔ sɛɛ

english: Warm, humid weather after light rain creates ideal conditions for insect eggs to hatch quickly. The heat also stresses the plants, making them weaker and easier for pests to feed on.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa baa kɛha kooloi bibii lɛ afɔfɔi oya. Dɔlɛ hu haa tsei haoɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai yeɔ amɛ mlɛo.

english: What causes seed maize to rot in the ground without sprouting into a plant?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛkwɛɛɛ, kɛ ekrokomɛi?

english: Seeds rot when the soil is overly waterlogged and cold, or if buried too deeply where air cannot reach them. Seeds need a balance of moisture, warmth, and air to wake up and grow.
ga: Dumɔwui fiteɔ kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni edɔ tsɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ afu lɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he. Dumɔwui taoɔ fɛ̃i, dɔlɛ, kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa koni amɛte shi ni amɛdara.

english: Why do experienced farmers in my village advise planting cassava alongside groundnuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ wo ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ ŋmei masɛi lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. This acts as natural fertilizer for neighboring plants like cassava, improving soil health without extra cost.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmei, ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ yaa hiɛ ni awooo he nyɔmɔ kroko.

english: Which food crops can I plant that will survive best if the dry season lasts longer than usual in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu ni baahi shi jogbaŋŋ fe be ni nu hɔmɔ baa yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Crops like cowpeas, millet, sorghum, and sweet potatoes have deep roots and tough leaves designed to survive long dry spells, making them reliable food options when rainfall is short.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ tsina ŋmãa, ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni ŋmãa yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni wa ni afee koni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ niyenii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ fioo.

english: Why do I have to keep my crop seedlings in a nursery bed before moving them to the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ dumɔwui awo ŋmɔ mli dani mikɛwo ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young seedlings are extremely delicate and sensitive to harsh sunlight and heavy rain. Keeping them in a nursery allows you to protect them, water them properly, and ensure only the healthiest plants survive before transplanting them to the main field.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa waa ni amɛnuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he waa. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ to gbekɛbii akwɛmɔhe lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ obuɔ amɛhe. Ha amɛ nu jogbaŋŋ. kɛ nɔmimaa akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ ahi shi dani akɛ amɛ awo saatso wulu lɛ mli.

english: How do I know when my young crop seedlings are ready to be moved from the nursery to the main field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaashi ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Seedlings are usually ready when they develop three to four strong true leaves, have a sturdy stem, and have spent the recommended time (usually two to three months) growing strong enough to withstand direct field conditions.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ feɔ klalo kɛji amɛyɛ anɔkwa baai 3-4 ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni wa. ni okɛ be ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ atsu nii (bei pii lɛ nyɔji 2-3) koni etsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni enyɛ edamɔ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi ni yɔɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ anaa.

english: Why do some crops take three months in the nursery while others can be planted directly into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi yeɔ nyɔji etɛ yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni abaanyɛ adu tsei komɛi awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Some crops have very small, delicate seeds that need extra care and protection to sprout successfully, whereas hardier seeds like maize or beans are strong enough to germinate directly in open farm soil.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ekomɛi yɛ dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa. Ehe miihia ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni abu amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni wa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli.

english: Why do extension officers advise picking out weaker seedlings instead of planting every seed that sprouts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ ahala dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ moŋ fe ni abaadu dumɔwui fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Removing weak or diseased seedlings ensures that you only spend time, water, and fertilizer on strong plants that will give you a good harvest, while also preventing the spread of diseases across your field.
ga: Dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooojie lɛ haa onáa be, nu, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baaha oná ŋmaa kpakpa lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oŋmɔji lɛ fɛɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: Why is it important to clear and prepare my land before transplanting my crops?
ga: Mɛni he je nɛ e he hia nɛ a dla zugba a nɔ nɛ a dla lɛ loko a du ní ɔ?

english: Clearing removes weeds and pests that compete with your young crops for food, water, and sunlight. Proper land preparation softens the soil, making it easier for new root systems to spread quickly.
ga: Kɛ́ otsi ohe lɛ, ebaajie jwɛi kɛ kooloi ni kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni asaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ shishifãi heei baagbɛ amɛshwã oya.

english: Why can't I just plant my seeds as close together as possible to get a higher harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ madu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe bɔ ni manyɛ koni maná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Giving each plant proper spacing ensures it grows bigger, stays healthy, and yields more high-quality produce.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ adara. amɛná hewalɛ kpakpa ni amɛfee nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ babaoo

english: Why should I shade my newly transplanted seedlings for the first few weeks on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ shade yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Direct sunlight can dry out and burn vulnerable young plants before their roots fully connect with the field soil. Temporary shade acts as a protective shield while the plant settles into its new environment.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ agbi ni eshã dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ dani shishifãi lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ abɔ he kwraa. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ mɔ he yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ tsakeɔ ehe kɛyaa shihilɛ hee ni eyɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How does the start of the rainy season affect the best time to move my crops to the main field?
ga: Te nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee saa be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii kɛya ŋmɔji wuji amli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Transplanting at the beginning of the rainy season gives young plants consistent natural water to establish strong roots, helping them survive through drier spells later in the season.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei bibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei bibii lɛ aná adebɔɔ mli nu ni yaa nɔ daa koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa. Eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: How do I tell if my young crops are not getting enough nutrients from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midumɔwui lɛ enine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Look at the leaf color and growth speed. If the leaves start turning yellow, look pale, or the stems remain unusually thin and stunted, it usually means the plant is missing vital nutrients like nitrogen or phosphorus.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ahe su kɛ bɔ ni amɛdaraa oya. Kɛji baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔŋ, efee tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo eshishifãi lɛ ahi shi ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen loo phosphorus.

english: Why do my young crop shoots sometimes wilt even after I have given them water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, mi-ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ miha amɛ nu po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Wilting can happen if water is applied during the hot midday sun, causing heat shock, or if excessive watering has rotted the roots, preventing them from drinking water properly.
ga: Wilting baanyɛ aba kɛji akɛ ashwie nu nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. ni kɛ hulutsoo baa Aloo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Enɛ haaa anyɛ anu nu jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if pests are starting to attack my maize crop before the whole field gets destroyed?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ miibɔi mi-ŋma lɛ tutuamɔ dani akpata jɛmɛ fɛɛ hiɛ?

english: Early signs of pest attack include small holes or ragged edges on young leaves, yellowish spots, and fine powder or dark droppings in the center leaves (whorl) of the maize plant.
ga: Nɔ ni fata mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ebatutua amɛ lɛ ahe ji buji bibii loo ŋmeii ni etse amɛhe yɛ baai bibii lɛ anɔ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, kɛ powda bibii loo ŋmeii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ateŋ baai (rings) lɛ amli.

english: If fall armyworms attack my maize farm, will my whole crop fail if I do not spray immediately?
ga: Kɛji cutworms tutua mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ Ani mi ŋmãa fɛɛ baafite kɛji mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwieee nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Yes, armyworms eat the growing points of young maize plants. If you do not act quickly, they can destroy leaf tissues, weaken the plants, and reduce your harvest to almost nothing.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, cutworms yeɔ hei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ. Kɛji ofeee oya Amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite baa lɛ mli fãji. ha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni okɛ nɔ ni ojieɔ lɛ aba shi kɛyashɛ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko.

english: Why do insect pests keep coming back to my maize farm every season even after I clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mijie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ moŋ?

english: Pests often survive between seasons inside old plant stalks left on the field, in surrounding weeds, or in the soil itself. If the field is not fully cleared and soil treated, the pests quickly move onto new crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hiɔ tsei momo ni ashi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli yɛ be lɛ mli. yɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mli kɛji ajieee jɛmɛ kwraa ni asaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yaa oya kɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii heei amli.

english: Can pests from my neighbor's farm move over and destroy my maize crop?
ga: Ani tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛ akutsoŋnyo ko ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ mli ni amɛfite mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Yes, many crop pests can fly, crawl, or be carried by the wind from untreated neighboring farms to yours, which is why managing pests requires attention across adjacent fields.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo baanyɛ afã, atsɔ, loo atswa amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli kɛba oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ hewɔ ni esa akɛ akwɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ nɔ yɛ shikpɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it important for all farmers in our community to control pests on our farms at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni okwaafoi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ wɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ akudɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ wɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: When farmers treat their crops together, pests have no safe fields to hide in. If only one person treats their farm, pests simply fly to nearby fields and return once the chemical effect wears off.
