ga: Kɛ okwaafoi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fee ekome lɛ Pests hu bɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni amɛbaahi. Kɛji mɔ kome pɛ ji mɔ ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ No lɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ fãa kɛyaa ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa kɛji tsofai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ efo mli pɛ.

english: Why does my maize yield keep decreasing every time I plant on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi be fɛɛ be ni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting maize on the same soil repeatedly without adding manure or fertilizer drains specific nutrients. It also allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil over time.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ, niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi baafite. Ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai hu bua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How many times can I harvest maize from the same field before the soil gets exhausted?
ga: Shii enyiɛ manyɛ makpa ŋmãa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ kome mli dani shikpɔŋ lɛ agbe naa?

english: Without adding fertilizers, compost, or rotating with crops like beans or groundnuts, soil typically becomes exhausted after two to three continuous planting seasons.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsakeɔ tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi yɛ bei enyɔ loo etɛ ni akɛduɔ nii daa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, or that water is sitting around the roots for too long after heavy rains, preventing the plant from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo nu ko ebɔle he. Shishifãi lɛ kɛlɛ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Enɛ haaa tsei lɛ anine shɛɛɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some of my maize plants produce small ears with missing grains on the cob?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ yɛ toi bibii ni dumɔwui bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Missing grains are usually caused by bad weather during flowering, poor soil nutrients, or pest damage to the silks, which prevents proper pollination of the cob.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmaa ni elaaje lɛ baa. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii Aloo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ miifite lɛ? Enɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ afee nɔ ni sa.

english: What should I do with old corn stalks after harvest so pests do not attack my next crop?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee ŋmãa tsei momoi beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ? Koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akatutua miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: You should plow the old stalks into the soil, burn them, or use them to make compost. Leaving dry stalks standing in the field gives stem borers and other pests a place to live until the next season.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ tso momo lɛ atsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shã loo okɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni egbi yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha stem borers kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai krokomɛi aba. He ko yɛ ni abaahi kɛyashi be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Is borehole water from underground safe to pour directly on my vegetable crops, or can it harm them?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafɔ nu ni jɛɔ nubu mli lɛ mashwie mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ? Aloo ebaanyɛ eye aduawai awui?

english: Underground water can sometimes contain high levels of dissolved salts or minerals like calcium and iron (hard water). Over time, these minerals can build up in the soil, making it harder for crops to absorb water and causing leaves to burn or turn yellow.
ga: Bei komɛi lɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ baanyɛ ahi ŋmeii ni egbɛ eshwa loo minerals tamɔ calcium kɛ iron (nu ni wa) babaoo yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ. Nɛkɛ tɛi nɛɛ baanyɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei akɛ amɛaaŋɔ nu. ni ehaa baai lɛ shãa loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my crops seem to grow much faster after rainfall compared to when I water them with well water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya waa beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Kɛ akɛto nu ni akɛnuɔ nubu mli lɛ he.

english: Rainwater naturally absorbs nitrogen from the air as it falls, giving crops a free nutrient boost. Well water often contains heavy minerals and lacks this extra atmospheric nitrogen, so rain triggers faster growth.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni egbeeɔ shi lɛ. Ehaa tsei naa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni aheee nɔ ko Bei pii lɛ, nubu mli nu lɛ mli nibii ni tsii yɔɔ mli, ni titri lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen bɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, nugbɔ woɔ dalɛ oya he hewalɛ.

english: Where can I take water from my farm to test if it is safe for growing crops?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ maná nu kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni aka lɛ akwɛ koni ana nɔmimaa akɛ ehi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ?

english: You can take a clean bottle of your farm water to a local agriculture extension office or a regional water research laboratory, where they test the salt and mineral levels to tell you if it is good for irrigation.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli nu ni mli tse lɛ aya okwaafoi akuu lɛ mli okwaayeli mlilɛɛmɔ nitsumɔhe loo kpokpaa nɔ nu he niiamlitaomɔhe lɛ. Enɛ kaa ŋmei kɛ mineral ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli koni ekɛtsɔɔ bo kɛji amɛhi kɛha nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi.

english: How can I tell if rainwater sitting on my farm field is going to destroy my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nugbɔ nu ni buaa ehe naa yɛ miŋmɔji amli lɛ baafite miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If flooded rainwater stays pooled around your crops for more than two days, it cuts off air to the roots. Roots need air to breathe; without it, they turn brown, rot, and cause the crop leaves to wilt and fall off.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe fe gbii enyɔ. Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia shishifãi koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ ebɛ lɛ, amɛfeɔ blɔfo ni amɛgboɔ ni amɛhaa tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Can using hard mineral water from my underground well turn my farm soil hard and compact?
ga: Ani nu ni mli wa ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee nɔ ni wa ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Yes, repeatedly using hard water high in calcium and salts can leave mineral deposits on the soil surface, forming a hard crust that prevents crop roots from spreading easily and absorbing rainwater.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni wa ni calcium kɛ ŋoo babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii shii abɔ. Ebaanyɛ eshi minerals yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Efeɔ ŋmei ni wa ni tsiɔ tsei shishifãi anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã oya ni amɛkaŋɔ nugbɔ nu.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants curl up like straws during hot dry afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ jwɛi yɛ shwane ni edɔ ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during extreme heat as a survival trick to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, helping the plant hold onto its internal moisture until the weather cools down.
ga: Abɛi baai shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ be mli akɛ wala yiwalaheremɔ gbɛ koni akɛba he ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ emli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves when moisture is scarce to conserve water stored inside its stem and roots, entering a resting state until the rainy season begins again.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi kɛ́ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ ahiɛ nu ni ebua ehe naa yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ bɛ. ni eboteɔ hejɔɔmɔ shihilɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ boteɔ mli ekoŋŋ

english: How do I know if my crop leaves are turning yellow from too much water or too little water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ nu babaoo loo nu fioo mli?

english: Leaves turning yellow from too much water will feel soft, limp, and soggy because the roots are drowning, while leaves turning yellow from drought will feel dry, crispy, and brittle.
ga: Baai ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ nu babaoo mli lɛ baanu he akɛ amɛhe ejɔ, amɛhe efee shoo, ni amɛhe ejɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ miiho. Baai ni tsakeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ hɔmɔ mli lɛ baa nu he akɛ egbi, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni egbɔjɔ.

english: If rainwater collects in an open earth pond on my farm, can I safely store it to water my tomato plants later?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ sũ nubu ko ni agbele naa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Ani manyɛ makɛto shweshweeshwe koni mikɛwo mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ nu sɛɛ mli?

english: Yes, but open pond water can carry fungal spores washed off nearby topsoil. It is safest to pour the pond water gently around the crop roots rather than spraying it onto the leaves where fungi can spread.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi nu ni yɔɔ nubu ni agbele naa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ ŋmeii ni efo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Gbɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ ji ni okɛ nubu lɛ mli nu lɛ afɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe blɛoo, moŋ fe ni oooshwie baai lɛ anɔ he ni ŋmei lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ.

english: Will heavy rainfall right after I sow maize seeds cause the seeds to rot under the ground?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa beni adu ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: If heavy rain washes mud over your seeds and buries them too deeply in waterlogged soil, the seeds cannot get oxygen to germinate and will rot before they can sprout above the ground.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shwiemɔ muji ni yɔɔ odumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ ni ofu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Dumɔwui nyɛŋ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni amɛkɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛbaagboi dani amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green. The plant steals nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the young top leaves so it can keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli. Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Why do my tomato leaves roll up tightly during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants curl their leaves inward during hot hours to trap moisture and reduce water loss caused by direct sun heat. It is a natural defense mechanism to keep the plant from drying out.
ga: Tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛha nu ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ aba shi. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛtsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkagbi.

english: Excess rainy weather and high humidity create a humid environment where fungal diseases thrive. Without enough sunlight and airflow through the farm to dry the foliage, fungi quickly spread across the pods.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ fe nine kɛ hulutsoo be ni fa babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ baa. Kɛji hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni baaha baai lɛ agbi lɛ, Ŋmei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmeii lɛ amli oya.

english: Why do my pepper flowers keep falling off without turning into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant experiences stress from extreme heat or lack of water. When temperatures get too high, the plant sheds its flowers to save energy and water for its own survival instead of making fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ mli lɛ mli. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of leaves but produce very small roots under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen or is grown in extremely rich soil, it puts all its energy into growing leaves and branches above ground instead of storing starch in the tubers below.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii waa nɔ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ baai kɛ tsei niji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baato bulb ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize plants fall over so easily when a light wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko tswa lɛ?

english: Maize plants fall over if they are planted too close together or lack strong support roots. Planting seeds too close together forces stems to grow thin and weak as they stretch upward for sunlight.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo amɛbɛ shishifãi ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ afee mlɛo ni amɛgbɔjɔ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee lɛ.

english: Why does my yam vine dry up and turn yellow before I dig up the tuber?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ mli egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ dani mikɛ ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally dry up when the underground tuber has finished growing and storing food. This natural dieback is the plant's signal showing that the yam is fully mature and ready for harvest.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji agbe ŋmeii lɛ adumɔ kɛ amɛkpamɔ naa pɛ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli gbele nɛɛ ji tso lɛ okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ sweet potato lɛ eda ni esa kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my plantain suckers dry out right after I transplant them to a new field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ wo saatso hee nɔ lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ midumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: When you dig up a plantain sucker, its roots are damaged and cannot absorb enough water for all its large leaves. Cutting off the older leaves before planting stops water loss until new roots can grow.
ga: Kɛ́ otsa plantain tsei lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ejie nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha baai wuji lɛ fɛɛ. Kɛ́ afo baai momoi lɛ amli dani adu lɛ, ehaa nu ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ kpaa kɛyashiɔ shishifãi heei baakwɛ̃ɔ.

english: If I save seeds from my harvested hybrid maize to plant next season, why do I get a much smaller yield?
ga: Kɛji akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ to koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ, Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ nɔ fioo kwraa lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred from two unique parent plants to give high yields for one generation only. The seeds saved from that harvest lose those special combined traits, resulting in smaller and irregular yields.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔɔ tsei enyɔ ni yɔɔ srɔtoi lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo kɛha yinɔ kome pɛ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ sui ni haa amɛfeɔ ekome lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ faaa ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee.

english: Why do weeds sprout and grow so much faster than my crops right after the first rains arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ba amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie dormant in the dirt waiting for water and are naturally tougher than farm crops. They are adapted to absorb nutrients rapidly and outcompete planted crops before your crops can build strong root systems.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui kã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛmiimɛ nu. Ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ewa fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛhe niyenii mli hewalɛ oya ni amɛye tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ kunim dani otsei lɛ afee shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Why do my crops rot and die in large patches when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hei srɔtoi kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too densely, their leaves touch and trap moisture while blocking fresh air. This damp, crowded environment makes fungal diseases spread rapidly from plant to plant, suffocating and killing them in clusters.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei babaoo tsɔ lɛ, baai lɛ taa ni amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛtsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa naa. Shihilɛ ni mli efɔ ni mɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ. Okɛ mumɔ atsu nii ni ogbe amɛ yɛ kui amli.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings weak and die off all at the same time in my nursery bed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables dumɔwui bibii lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛ fɛɛ amɛmiigboi yɛ mi-nsɛri saatso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by a fungal condition called damping-off. When seeds are overcrowded and overwatered, wet soil fungus attacks the tender stems at ground level, causing entire groups of seedlings to collapse together.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fungal shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ damping off, be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii tutuaa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. ni haa dumɔwui akuu muu lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ekomefeemɔ mli

english: Why are my maize plants thin and falling over when I sow many seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Seeds sown too close together compete intensely for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Instead of growing thick, sturdy stems, they stretch upward too quickly to reach light, making them weak and easy to fall over.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nu lɛ mli waa Moŋ lɛ, ekwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa ni amɛhe wa. Mohu ɔ, e ngmɛɛ e he oya tsɔ nɛ e nyɛ we nɛ e ya su la a he. Ehaa egbɔjɔɔ ni egbeeɔ shi oya.

english: Why do my corn leaves curl up into tight tubes when the sun is very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural survival response to heat stress. By rolling its leaves into tubes, the maize plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun to hold onto its water until temperatures cool down.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yibiiwoo hetoo kɛha dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni aaatsɔ mli awo tsɔne mli lɛ nɔ. Abɛi haa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi koni ehiɛ nu mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do my bean leaves fold together and close up at night?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛŋmɛɔ amɛhe gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes naturally fold their leaves at night to reduce water evaporation and protect delicate young tissue from cold night air and dew. It is a normal plant behavior and not a sign of sickness.
ga: Legumes lɛ fɔ̃ɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ gbɛkɛ koni nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aba shi, ni ebu amɛfãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ kɛ gbɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ he. Enɛ ji tso lɛ subaŋ ni sa, ni ejeee hela he okadi.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants droop and look dead during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni egboi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves temporarily droop during peak sun hours to minimize water loss through heat. As long as the plant gets cooler temperatures in the evening, the leaves will bounce back upright.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni nu ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ mli baa lɛ aba shi. Shii abɔ ni tsei lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ, Baai lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants suddenly wilt even when the ground around them has plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho trukaa eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli egbi moŋ? Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa baahi jɛmɛ.

english: When soil stays flooded, roots cannot get oxygen and begin to drown and rot. Damaged roots stop absorbing water, which makes the plant wilt as if it were drying out, even in wet soil.
ga: Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Shishifãi nyɛŋ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. ni ebɔi nu mli shwiemɔ kɛ fitemɔ. Shishifãi ni efite lɛ kpaɔ nu ŋmɔmɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eegbi. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ po nɔ

english: Why do strong winds during rainstorms cause whole stands of plantain trees to snap at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni tswaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ haa plantains lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi shikome lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have heavy bunches and shallow roots, making them top-heavy. When heavy storm winds hit, the sudden pressure snaps their fibrous stems or pulls their roots out of soft, saturated soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ niji ni tsii kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. kɛ muji babaoo baa Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko tswa Trukaa nɔnyɛɛ baafo amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli loo ebaagbala amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni eyi obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves turn yellow and drop off starting from the bottom of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛjɛɔ amɛshishi amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Older leaves near the bottom of the plant get less light and are closest to soil moisture and splashed diseases. The plant naturally shed these stressed lower leaves to send energy up to newer leaves and fruit.
ga: Baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ naa la fioo. kɛ nɔ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ splash hela fe fɛɛ. Tsei shwieɔ nɛkɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni haoɔ nɛɛ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ awo baai kɛ aduawai heei amli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop all their leaves suddenly after a short dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ be kukuoo mli ni amɛgbi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during severe drought as a defense mechanism to save water in their main trunk and branches, helping the tree survive until the next rain comes.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ nu ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ eniji wuji lɛ ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ baa.

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during dry weather to conserve water and protect its root system. As long as the stems remain green and healthy, the plant will sprout fresh leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Yucca lɛ shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu eshishifãi lɛ ahe. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ yitso lɛ baahi shi akɛ eŋɔli ni ehe wa lɛ Tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ pɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava on the same piece of land every single year without leaving the soil to rest?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi ni mishiŋ shikpɔŋ ko yɛ sɛɛ?

english: Planting cassava repeatedly on the same land drains the soil of essential nutrients over time, resulting in smaller tubers and poorer yields. Resting the land or rotating with legumes helps restore soil health.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii kɛ yibiiwoo baa shi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akɛjɔɔ he loo ni akɛ ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Which way should I point cassava stem cuttings when planting them in the ground?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu shikpɔŋ lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ atsɔ nɔ atsɔɔ ŋmei niji lɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings should always be planted with the raised leaf buds pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting them upside down slows down growth and causes weak stem development.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni baai lɛ ashishifãi ni awó nɔ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ebaaha ekwɛ̃ ni ebaagbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo lɛ?

english: Too much standing water in the soil deprives the underground cassava tubers of oxygen. Waterlogged soil causes the tubers to suffocate, turn soft, and rot before harvest.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa bulb lɛ shwieɔ shi, efeɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ dani akpaa.

english: How do I know when my plantains are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni dumɔwui lɛ eshɛ ni abaakpa?

english: Plantains are ready for harvest when the individual fruits look full and rounded rather than sharp and angled, and the dried flowers at the tips of the fruits easily fall off.
ga: Plantains lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔɔ beni aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko tamɔ nɔ ni eyi obɔ ni eyɛ kokroo lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Ni fɔfɔi ni egbi ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ anaagbee lɛ shwieɔ shi oya.

english: Plantains have shallow roots that stay close to the top of the soil. As the fruit bunch grows heavy, the plant becomes top-heavy, so supporting the stem with a wooden pole prevents it from falling.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛ́ aduawai akuu lɛ batsɔ tsii Tso lɛ baafee tsii waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tsei fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekagbee shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my plantain plant turning brown and dying from the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ midumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigboi yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Browning leaves can be a sign of drought stress, nutrient shortage, or fungal leaf diseases. Removing affected lower leaves stops diseases from spreading to healthy new leaves.
ga: Baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ baanyɛ afee hɔmɔ he haomɔ he okadi. niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa loo baa hela ni ŋmei kɛbaa Kɛ́ ajie baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ena hela lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa baa heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Should I allow all the young plantain shoots growing around the main mother plant to stay?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashi plantain bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mihe lɛ? Ani nyɛ tso titri lɛ yɛ lolo?

english: Leaving too many shoots creates competition for light, water, and soil nutrients. Keeping only two or three strong shoots per plant gives you larger and healthier bunches of fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tsei bibii babaoo ni ajie amɛ kpo lɛ, ebaatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso kome mli ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha oná yibii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Will my cassava grow well if I plant it under big, shady trees?
ga: Ani ŋmei baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko ni yɔɔ hulutsoo shishi?

english: Cassava needs plenty of direct sunlight to manufacture energy for stem and tuber growth. Heavy shade causes the plant to grow tall and thin with very small roots underground.
ga: Cassava he miihia hulu la babaoo tɛ̃ɛ koni ená hewalɛ kɛha eshishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ adalɛ. Shade ni mli wa lɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛshishifãi bibii waa yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings wilt during the middle of the day even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: On hot afternoons, young crops lose moisture through their leaves faster than their tiny roots can drink water from the soil. They usually recover in the cooler evening once the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, tsei bibii lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe shishifãi bibii lɛ. koni enyɛ enu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ Bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if a crop disease has spread to the cocoa trees on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tso hela ko egbɛ eshwa kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ?

english: Look closely at your trees for signs like yellowing or deformed leaves, swollen branches, or pods turning dark brown and black before they are ripe. Catching these signs early helps you protect the rest of your farm before the disease spreads.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tso lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛha okadii tamɔ baai ni efee ŋmɔŋ loo efite, niji ni efuu, loo ŋmeii ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ediŋŋ dani amɛkwɛ̃. Okadii nɛɛ ni ooomɔ mli mra Ebaaha onyɛ obu oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he dani hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: If a plant disease enters my community near harvest time, should I harvest my cocoa right away?
ga: Kɛji tso hela ko bote mi akutso lɛ mli ni ebɛŋkɛ kpamɔ be lɛ Ani esa akɛ makpa kookoo amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: You should harvest all fully ripe pods immediately to save your yield, but do not pick green, unripe pods. Removing ripe pods quickly prevents diseases like black pod from jumping from infected pods to healthy ones.
ga: Esa akɛ okpa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite. Shi kaahala ŋmeii ni ekwɛko. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ oya lɛ, no tsiɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ anaa koni amɛkajɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛya ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why are some of my cocoa pods turning black and rotting right while hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite beni amɛkpɛtɛ tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: This is commonly caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet, cold, and dark conditions. Clearing weeds and pruning excess leaves lets sunlight and air in, which helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ, ni mli ejɔ, kɛ duŋ mli. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi kɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do crop diseases seem to spread much faster on farms located deep inside the forest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Forest environments have high humidity, constant moisture, and heavy shade, which create perfect conditions for fungi and bacteria to grow and spread rapidly from tree to tree.
ga: Shihilɛ ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔ waa. hulutsoo be fɛɛ be ni eyɛ hulutsoo ni mli wa Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ adara ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya kɛjɛ tso kome nɔ kɛya tso kroko nɔ.

english: How can I know the exact right time to harvest my cocoa pods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods are ready for harvest when their skin turns completely yellow or orange, depending on the variety. Harvesting when fully ripe ensures the highest bean quality and stops pods from rotting on the stem.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni ŋmeii lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ kwraa. Edamɔ tso lɛ henɔ lɛ nɔ Nikpamɔ kɛji ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ haa ŋmeii ni hi fe fɛɛ baa. ni otsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ

english: How often am I supposed to harvest ripe pods from my cocoa farm during the main season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ makpa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ kɛjɛ kookoo ŋmɔ mli yɛ be titri lɛ mli?

english: It is best to harvest every two to three weeks during the peak season. Regular harvesting keeps ripe pods from over-ripening and stops diseases from building up on older pods.
ga: Esa akɛ akpa amɛ daa otsii 2-3 yɛ be mli ni mɛi fa babaoo lɛ. Nibii ni akpaa daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ fe nine, ni ehaaa helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmeii ni egbɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Does the tool or method I use to cut cocoa pods off the tree affect future harvests?
ga: Ani dɛŋdade loo gbɛ ni mitsɔɔ nɔ mifoɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ saa miwɔsɛɛ kpamɔ lɛ he?

english: Yes, always use a sharp harvest hook or cutlass to make a clean cut on the pod stem. If you tear or damage the flower cushion on the tree trunk where the pod grows, that spot will struggle to produce new flowers and pods in the future.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛ nikpamɔ ŋmei loo kakla ni naa wa baatsu nii. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, ŋmɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛji ogbala loo okpãtã fɔfɔi akushin ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi he ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ hiɛ Nakai be lɛ mli lɛ naagbai baaba yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii heei ni ajieɔ lɛ mli wɔsɛɛ.

english: Does heavy shade from big forest trees help or hurt my cocoa crop?
ga: Ani hulutsoo ni mli wa ni jɛɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa loo eyeɔ mi kokoo tso lɛ awui?

english: Young cocoa trees need heavy shade to survive heat, but mature cocoa trees need a balance of gentle shade and direct sunlight. Too much shade traps moisture, which causes pod diseases to spread easily.
ga: Kokoo tsei ni edara lɛ taoɔ hɔɔŋ ni mli wa koni amɛnyɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ dɔlɛ mli. Shi kookoo tso ni eda lɛ he miihia ni ená hulutsoo blɛoo kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ shade babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa helai ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Can my cocoa farm still give a good harvest if it gets attacked by a disease earlier in the season?
ga: Ani mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii kpakpai lolo kɛji hela lɛ ba mra yɛ be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, cocoa trees are resilient. If you quickly remove all infected pods, prune affected branches, and apply the correct protective sprays recommended by extension officers, your trees can recover and yield well.
ga: Hɛɛ, cacao tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ shi. Kɛji ojie ŋmeii fɛɛ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, Kpãa niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ni okɛ tsofa ni buɔ mɔ he ni sa lɛ atsu nii taakɛ mɛi ni kwɛɔ helatsamɔhe lɛ nɔ lɛ ŋaawoi lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ. Otsei lɛ baanyɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: What basic steps should I take to protect my cocoa farm's yield when disease outbreaks threaten my family's income?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛi titrii esa akɛ matsɔ nɔ mabu nibii ni jɛɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe beni hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa mɛi lɛ woɔ miweku lɛ shika he gbeyei lɛ?

english: Keep your farm clean by weeding regularly, prune dense leaves to let in sunlight, safely burn or bury diseased pods away from healthy trees, and seek advice from an extension officer on safe treatment options.
ga: Ha oŋmɔ lɛ mli atse kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ooojie daa lɛ nɔ. Kpãa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ amli koni hulu la lɛ abote mli. Shãa loo fuɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe yɛ he ko ni kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ. Ni obi ŋaawoo kɛjɛ mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ helatsamɔhe lɛ adɛŋ yɛ helatsamɔ gbɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ ahe.

english: Why do I need to trim or prune branches off my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo loo mafolɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ?

english: Pruning removes excess branches so the tree directs its nutrients into growing large, healthy cocoa pods rather than wasting energy on extra leaf growth.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ heɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii agboi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine ni miida lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Will cutting back cocoa tree branches help me get more pods at harvest?
ga: Ani cacao tsei ni afoɔ lɛ baaye abua mi ni maná ŋmeii babaoo kɛ́ akpa?

english: Yes, proper pruning opens up the tree canopy to sunlight and air, which encourages healthy flower growth and improves pod development.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni afolɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɔ eshɛɔ tso lɛ he. ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa pod lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do people recommend pruning cocoa trees in November?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ afo cacao tsei yɛ November mli lɛ?

english: November provides gentle sunshine that helps the fresh cuts on the tree stumps dry out quickly without causing severe heat shock to the plant.
ga: November haa hulu la ni tsoɔ blɛoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ niji heei ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni ekɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa baaa tso lɛ nɔ.

english: What happens if I prune my cocoa trees in February during the severe heat?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mifo mi-kokoo tso lɛ yɛ February mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: The intense sun in February causes cut stalks and leaves to wither and dry out very fast within a week, which makes clearing them easier but requires careful handling so the tree isn't scorched.
ga: February hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ baai ni afo lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya waa, yɛ otsi kome mli. Enɛ haa shwiemɔ feɔ mlɛo. Shi esa akɛ akwɛ jogbaŋŋ koni akashã tso lɛ.

english: Is it good to prune my cocoa trees when the rainy season starts?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaafolɔ kookoo tsei yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: No, pruning during heavy rains is risky because excessive moisture keeps fresh tree cuts wet, which can cause the pruned area to rot or become infected with disease.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni afoɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ yɛ oshara. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔtɔ babaoo baaha tsei ni afo ehee lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha he ni afo lɛ lɛ agbo loo hela aba.

english: How does dry weather help a tree cut heal after pruning?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni afolɔ lɛ ni amɛtsaa beni afolɔ amɛhe lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Sunlight and dry air rapidly dry out the liquid on a fresh cut, creating a natural seal on the stump that protects the tree from fungal infections.
ga: Hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi baaha nu lɛ agbi oya yɛ ŋmeii heei ni afo lɛ anɔ. Ehaa adebɔɔ mli tsɔne ko baa tso lɛ shishi ni buɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Should I wait for the rain to fall before I clear out extra branches on my farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ dani majie tsei niji krokomɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: It is better to prune before continuous rains start, as dry conditions allow cuts to dry safely, whereas rainy weather delays healing and leads to rotting cuts.
ga: Esa akɛ akpɛ tsei lɛ dani nugbɔ anɛ be fɛɛ be. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shihilɛ ni mli egbi lɛ haa pilamɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ shweshweeshwe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ haa pilamɔ lɛ tsaa oya, ni ehaa pilamɔ lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on cut cocoa branches turn brown and shrink so fast in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ hulu la shɛ kookoo tsei ahe lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi oya waa lɛ?

english: Once a branch is cut, it no longer gets water from the root system, so intense sun heat drains the remaining moisture from the leaves and stalks within a few days.
ga: Beni afoɔ tso lɛ nine lɛ Enáŋ nu kɛjɛŋ eshishifãi lɛ amli dɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ jieɔ nu ni eshwɛ yɛ baai kɛ tsei lɛ amli lɛ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli.

english: What should I do with the withered leaves and cut stalks after pruning in the dry season?
ga: Kɛ́ mifo tsei lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ baai lɛ egbo ni afo tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ?

english: Once the cut branches dry out and wither in the sun, you can easily gather them and spread them as mulch around the base of your trees to protect the soil.
ga: Beni tsei niji ni afo lɛ egbi ni amɛgbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ. Obaanyɛ obua nakai tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anaa ni okɛ sũ awo he ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Tso shishitoo koni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he mlɛo

english: How can I tell if a fresh cut on my cocoa branch is healing safely?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ pilamɔ hee ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo nine lɛ nɔ lɛ etsa shweshweeshwe?

english: A cut is healing safely when the surface dries up firmly in the sun without showing signs of wet decay, dark mold, or softness.
ga: Pilamɔi lɛ tsaa shweshweeshwe kɛ́ nɔ ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ mli egbi kwraa yɛ hulu la mli ni ejieee ŋmɔtɔ ni efite lɛ he okadi kpo. fungus ni tsuɔ loo blɛoofeemɔ

english: How do I know if my crops are sick with a disease instead of just needing water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela miipiŋ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ moŋ fe ni nu kɛkɛ he baahia amɛ?

english: Water-stressed plants usually wilt during the hot afternoon and recover at night, whereas diseased plants show symptoms like yellow spots, leaf rot, strange growths, or powdery coatings that do not disappear after watering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni nu bɛ amɛhe lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, ni amɛhe feɔ shoo gbɛkɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ baajie okadii tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ, baai ni egboi, kɛ dalɛi ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ kpo. Aloo nɔ ko yɛ ni tamɔ powder ni sɛɛ efooo kɛji awo nɔ nu.

english: How does plant medicine actually work to cure a disease in my crops?
ga: Te tsei ahe tsofai tsuɔ nii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ koni amɛkɛtsa helai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Plant medicines work by either killing the germs and fungi on the outside of the leaves or absorbing through the plant's skin to travel inside, stopping the disease from spreading and letting the plant heal.
ga: Tsoi ahe tsofai tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔ muawai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baa lɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ gbemɔ nɔ loo kɛtsɔ tso lɛ hewolo mli ni amɛboteɔ mli koni amɛya mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni ehaa tso lɛ tsaa.

english: Why do crop diseases spread so quickly from my neighbor's farm to mine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai gbɛ eshwa oya kɛjɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛba minɔ lɛ?

english: Diseases travel on wind currents, splash across fields during heavy rain, or stick to insects and farm tools that move between infected fields and healthy plants.
ga: Helai kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ fãa gbɛ. Egbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli. aloo ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni nyiɛɔ ŋmɔji ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ateŋ lɛ ahe.

english: How can I tell if a expensive plant treatment is worth buying for my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ tsofai ni akɛtsaa tsei ni jara wa lɛ sa akɛ mahe kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: A treatment is worth buying if the extra yield you harvest—or the crop loss you prevent—sells for more money at the market than what you spent on the chemical and its application.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ohé tsofafeemɔ ko kɛji akɛ yibiiwoo ni fa ni okpaa—loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni otsiɔ naa lɛ—jara fe nɔ ni ofite yɛ tsofa lɛ kɛ nitsumɔ lɛ he lɛ.

english: Why are some crop medicines sprayed on the leaves while others are poured into the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ tsei ahe tsofai komɛi shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni afɔseɔ ekomɛi awoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf sprays work quickly to kill pests and diseases visible on the surface, while soil treatments are absorbed by roots so the whole plant can drink in protection and nutrients from the bottom up.
ga: Nɔ ni akɛshwieɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii oya ni ejieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jeɔ kpo yɛ nɔ lɛ. Taakɛ eji yɛ helatsamɔ mli lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tso muu lɛ fɛɛ anu nu ni ekɛbu he ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aha kɛjɛ shishi kɛya ŋwɛi.

english: Why do crop leaves turn yellow when there is too much rainfall on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ?

english: Excess rain fills up all the air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots so they cannot breathe or absorb nitrogen, which causes the leaves to lose their green color.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi aahu akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu loo amɛŋɔ nitrogen. Enɛ haa baai lɛ ahe su eŋɔli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why do my crops stay small and weak even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daraaa ni ebɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Water helps plants grow, but plants also need food from the soil like nitrogen and potassium; if the soil nutrients are exhausted, the crops remain small despite getting enough water.
ga: Nu yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa. Shi tsei hu taoɔ niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen kɛ potassium. Kɛji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fite lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baakã he ahi shi bibioo kɛji amɛná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa po.

english: How do my crops know when it is time to start flowering and producing food?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ leɔ be ni esa akɛ amɛje fɔfɔii afeemɔ shishi ni amɛwo niyenii?

english: Plants react to subtle changes in their environment such as the length of daylight, air temperature, rainfall patterns, and their own age, which trigger internal signals to begin flowering.
ga: Tsei tsuɔ tsakemɔi bibii ni baa amɛshihilɛhe lɛ ahe nii, tamɔ bɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ha. kɔɔyɔɔ mli latsaa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, kɛ afii diɛŋtsɛ Enɛ haa mligbɛ okadii lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔii ashishi.

english: What makes a harvested crop rich in healthy nutrients so that people who eat it gain strength?
ga: Mɛni haa tsei ni akpaa lɛ feɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa babaoo koni mɛi ni yeɔ lɛ aná hewalɛ?

english: Crops gather nutrients directly from healthy soil rich in organic matter and minerals; when a plant receives balanced soil food and sunlight, it stores those vital vitamins and minerals in the food we eat.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ buaa niyenii mli hewalɛ naa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ shika tsuru babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ tsei ná shikpɔŋ kɛ hulu la ni sa lɛ, Tsei kɛ nakai vitamini kɛ mineral ni he hiaa lɛ toɔ niyenii ni wɔyeɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I alternate planting different crops on my land instead of planting maize every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni maduɔ ŋmãa daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every season drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up, whereas rotating different crops restores soil balance and starves out pests.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo baa amɛhe shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ekome ekoŋŋ ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai yeɔ hɔmɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the crop matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ eda lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for strong growth. It can also happen when plants are crowded or flooded with too much standing water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ ni mli wa Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe loo nu eyi mli obɔ fe nine.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and twist together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Twisted or curled leaves are typically caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites, or a plant virus spread by these insects, especially during hot and dry weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni etsɔ loo ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo tsei amli helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Titri lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be baa lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves wilt and drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have small roots that cannot reach deep water. During hot, dry weather, they drop their leaves to conserve moisture and avoid dying unless protected by shade trees.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii. ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Amɛbaashwie amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni amɛkagboi. ja tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ ebu he

english: Why do my cassava roots turn out watery and soft instead of big and firm at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji nu ni amɛhe yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee agbo ni ewa kɛji akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots become watery if planted in heavy soils that retain too much water, or if harvested too early before the plant stores enough starch inside the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi baanyɛ ahiɛ nu mli kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛji akɛ akpa mra tsɔ dani tsei lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa eto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli

english: Why is my plantain stalk falling over on its own even when there is no strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shwieɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ waaa moŋ lɛ?

english: Stalks fall over when microscopic worms in the soil (nematodes) or stem borer pests eat away the root system, destroying the plant's anchor in the ground.
ga: Tsoi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. (Nematodes) loo kooloi ni boteɔ tso lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ. Efiteɔ tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my green cocoa pods turn black and dry up while still hanging on the trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ he lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet, overly shaded environments with poor airflow between the cocoa trees.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulu enyɔ shi fe nine. kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii ni hoɔ yɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ

english: Why do my yam vines develop dark black spots that spread and kill the leaves early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni egbeɔ baai lɛ?

english: Dark spots on yam leaves are caused by a fungal disease called anthracnose, which spreads quickly during rainy conditions and weakens the vine before the underground yam fully grows.
ga: Hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ baa. ni baagbɛ eshwa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli ni ebaaha wain tso lɛ agbɔjɔ dani shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei lɛ agbɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants flower heavily but drop most flowers without producing pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi waa shi fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flower drop in beans and cowpeas is usually triggered by high heat and dry spells during flowering, or by insect pests like thrips attacking the flower buds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, latsaa ni naa wa kɛ hulutsoo be mli fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii amli lɛ jeɔ shishi. aloo kɛtsɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ thrips ni tutuaa fɔfɔii ashishifãi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and sunken before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efoɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This problem, called blossom-end rot, is caused by a shortage of calcium inside the fruit, which happens when water supply to the plant is irregular or uneven.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ ejaaa loo ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee.

english: Why do some of my grain heads stay completely empty without developing seeds at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ ekomɛi efee efolo ni dumɔwui ejeee kpo kɛ́ akpa lɛ?

english: Empty grain heads happen when the crop experiences extreme heat, severe drought, or pest attacks right during the flowering period when grains are supposed to form.
ga: Dumɔwui ayitsei ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. hɔmɔ ni naa wa Aloo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko baa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli beni esa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ afee lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate that your maize lacks nitrogen, a crucial nutrient for leaf growth, or that the soil is waterlogged. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizers like Urea or well-rotted animal manure helps plants regain their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛ su ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do farmers cover the soil around their crops with dried grass and dead leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛ jwɛi kɛ baai ni egboi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This practice is called mulching. Dry grass and leaves protect the soil from direct heat, hold moisture in the ground during hot days, and prevent weeds from growing and competing with your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ oŋmɔshi nibii akaŋ akaŋ.

english: When is the safest time for me to put fertilizer on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the ground is moist, either early in the morning or after a good rain. Applying fertilizer to dry soil during bright sunlight can scorch and damage your plant roots.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Eji leebi loo yɛ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite tsei shishifãi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when exposed to full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and stems that easily burn under strong sun. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or cassava next to them acts like a canopy, providing the shade and humidity needed for young cocoa to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaafee tamɔ tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe. Ha hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa koni kookoo bibii lɛ ahi shi.

english: How do I choose the best cassava stems to cut for planting my new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mafo koni mikɛdu yɛ ŋmɔ hee mli?

english: Select mature, healthy stems from plants that are 8 to 12 months old and free from diseases. Cuttings taken from the middle portion of the stem with closely spaced buds sprout strongest and produce better yields.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni edara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 ni hela bɛ mli lɛ amli. Niji ni ajie kɛjɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ baakwɛ̃ waa ni amɛbaawo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden stakes next to my growing yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso ko ni miida lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam plants are vines that need to lift their leaves off the ground to catch sunlight efficiently. Staking keeps the leaves away from wet soil, which prevents diseases and fungal rot, helping the plant grow larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la jogbaŋŋ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akaje shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai kɛ ŋmeii akafite. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: How does allowing weeds to grow on my farm harm my main crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni miŋmɛɔ gbɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ awui?

english: Weeds act as silent thieves—they consume the water, sunlight, and soil food meant for your crops. Removing weeds early gives your crops full access to nutrients so they can grow bigger and produce a better harvest.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi ni efee dioo—amɛyeɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaadu onibii lɛ mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa otsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni amɛdara ni amɛkpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is causing small, round holes in my tomato leaves and fruits?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ baa? Yɛ mi tomato lɛ baai kɛ aduawai anɔ

english: Holes in leaves and fruits are typically caused by insect pests like caterpillars or fruit borers feeding on the plant. Picking them off by hand or spraying natural controls like neem leaf extract helps stop the destruction.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii loo aduawai amli ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu baa baai kɛ aduawai amli. Okɛ oniji ajie amɛ loo okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ko ni akɛyeɔ nɔ tamɔ neem baa mli nu lɛ afɔ amɛnɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni akpa hiɛkpatamɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I avoid planting maize on the exact same patch of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ he yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop year after year drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases to multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or beans replenishes nitrogen in the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai shwereɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: How do I know if the ground has received enough rain for me to safely plant my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ená nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu dumɔwui shweshweeshwe?

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first rain of the season, as the deep soil underneath may still be dry. Wait until you have had two or three good rains so the soil is soaked deep enough to keep seeds moist until they sprout.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ekolɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi lolo. Mɛɛ kɛyashi obaaná nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa fioo bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ waa bɔ ni sa ni eha dumɔwui lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ kɛyashi amɛbaakwɛ̃.

english: Is using organic fertilizer really better for my young cocoa trees than chemical inputs?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛhaa mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ hi fe tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii?

english: Organic fertilizers improve long-term soil health and naturally nourish young plants without harsh chemical burn, allowing young cocoa seedlings to develop strong root systems safely.
ga: Organic fertilizers haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ yaa hiɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaa tsei bibii lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni tsofai ni mli wa shãaa amɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo dumɔwui ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni mli wa shweshweeshwe.

english: How can I tell if my newly planted cocoa seedlings are actually thriving after I feed them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cocoa dumɔwui heei ni midu lɛ miiya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ beni mikɛ amɛ eha amɛ niyenii sɛɛ?

english: Thriving cocoa seedlings show vibrant green foliage, quick leaf development, and steady stem growth, indicating that the plant roots are actively taking in soil nutrients.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui ni miiya hiɛ lɛ baaná baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ. baai lɛ daa oya ni tso lɛ shishifã lɛ yaa nɔ edaa Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso shishifãi lɛ miitao niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ miishɛɛ.

english: Can natural or homemade organic sprays still cause side effects on my crops?
ga: Ani adebɔɔ mli loo shia tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nibii anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ naagbai aba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Yes, even natural mixtures can damage plant tissues or soil chemistry if applied in wrong concentrations or prepared incorrectly, which is why proper dosage is always necessary.
ga: Hɛɛ, adebɔɔ mli nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ po baanyɛ afite tso mli fãji loo sũ mli tsofai kɛji akɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo akɛsaaa he jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni shika ni sa he hiaa be fɛɛ be lɛ.

english: Why does Cocobod ban or place strict warnings on using certain chemicals on cocoa farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Cocobod guɔ loo ebɔɔ kɔkɔ waa yɛ tsofai komɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji amli lɛ he lɛ?

english: Cocobod enforces regulations to protect crop health, prevent chemical residues in exported cocoa beans, and ensure farms meet international safety standards.
ga: Cocobod kɛ mlai tsuɔ nii koni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe hewalɛnamɔ he. Tsi tsofai ni eshwɛ yɛ kookoo yibii ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ amli lɛ naa. kɛ nɔmimaa akɛ ŋmɔji lɛ kɛ majimaji ateŋ shweshweeshwefeemɔ he mlai lɛ kpãa gbee

english: How do I check if a new fertilizer or spray is approved for use on cocoa in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana kɛji akɛ akpɛlɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofa hee ko ni akɛshwieɔ kookoo nɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ nɔ?

english: You can verify approved products by asking your local agricultural extension officer or checking Cocobod's list of certified agrochemicals before buying or applying anything to your farm.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ nibii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ni yɔɔ oakutso lɛ mli lɛ ni ooobi lɛ nɔ. Aloo kwɛmɔ Cocobod agrochemicals ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ahe wolo lɛ dani ohe loo okɛ nɔ ko awo oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do experts tell me to prepare or process organic mixtures first before applying them to my trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nilelɔi miikɛɛ mi akɛ masaa loo matsu nibii ni akɛ tsofai tsuuu nii yɛ mli lɛ ahe nii dani mikɛwo mitsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Raw or unfermented mixtures can carry harmful pathogens or be too concentrated; proper preparation breaks down ingredients into safe, plant-usable nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ loo ni afeee lɛ ŋmɔlɔ baanyɛ aŋɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ tsɔ. Hesaamɔ ni sa gbalaa nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ amli kɛfeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha tsei.

english: Why do some fertilizers help young cocoa trees grow fast while others burn or kill them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi yeɔ ebuaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi shãa cacao tsei lɛ loo amɛgbeɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Young trees have delicate, shallow roots; balanced inputs release nutrients gently, while overly harsh or incorrect mixtures overwhelm the roots and cause chemical burn.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni ja lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii blɛoo Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nɔ ni mli wa tsɔ loo nɔ ni ejaaa ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aye nɔ ni ekɛ tsofai shãa.

english: What happens if I mix two different crop remedies together without asking an extension officer first?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ futu ni mibiii mɔ ni kwɛɔ nɔ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Mixing unapproved substances can cause chemical reactions that destroy the effectiveness of the treatment, ruin crop leaves, or create compounds that harm the plant.
ga: Nibii ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofai ni fiteɔ tsofa lɛ nitsumɔ lɛ aba, ni efite tsei ahe baai, loo ekɛ tsofai ni yeɔ tsei awui aba.

english: Why do young cocoa trees require more careful attention than mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ fe cacao tsei ni eda lɛ?

english: Seedlings are tender and easily stressed by full sunlight, harsh sprays, and poor soil conditions, requiring gentle nutrients and shade until their root systems mature.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli oya. nu mli afua ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii Amɛbiɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni mli jɔ kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baadara.

english: Who should I consult before trying a new plant food mixture that another farmer recommended to me?
ga: Namɔ esa akɛ mabi lɛ dani maka niyenii hee ko ni akɛ tsei fee ni okwaafonyo kroko etsɔɔ mi lɛ makwɛ?

english: You should always talk to your local agricultural extension officer, as they can confirm if the mixture is safe, legal, and effective for your specific crop and soil type.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ okwaayeli nɔ lɛ awie be fɛɛ be. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaanyɛ amɛma nɔ mi akɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe, mla eŋmɛ gbɛ, ni amɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ ni oyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in an open field under direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate strong direct heat because their leaves dry out quickly. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees planted around them to protect them from the sun while their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ amɛhe. Enɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ he yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: Why do I need to trim off the small shoots growing straight out of the main stem of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ mli lɛ

english: These side shoots, often called water suckers, waste the tree's food and water without producing any pods. Cutting them off allows the tree to send all its food straight to producing healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, atsɛɔ nɛkɛ sɛɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu. Efiteɔ tso lɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa baaa. Kɛtsɔ efomɔ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ baatsɔɔ eniyenii lɛ fɛɛ gbɛ koni ekɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba.

english: Why does the newer hybrid cocoa produce pods in three years while my older trees took five years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo heei ni akɛfee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ afii etɛ mli lɛ? yɛ be mli ni mi-kookoo tso ni eda lɛ he afii enumɔ.

english: Hybrid cocoa varieties are specially bred to grow faster, stay shorter, and resist local diseases better, allowing them to flower and yield fruit much earlier than traditional tree varieties.
ga: Afee kookoo henɔi ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛdara oya, amɛhi shi be kukuoo, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye maŋ lɛ mli helai anɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ yibii oya fe tsei srɔtoi fɛɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava together in the same space with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmei yɛ he kome ni miduɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava has thick, aggressive roots and wide foliage that compete heavily for nutrients and sunlight, which can choke young cocoa seedlings. It is better to plant plantains or vegetables instead.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli tse, ni wa kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ hulu la he akaŋ waa. Enɛ baanyɛ aha kookoo dumɔwui lɛ agbɔjɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu plantains loo aduawai moŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many of their flowers before they can grow into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miifɔlɔ babaoo dani amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can support. A drop in flowers is normal, but excessive loss happens when the tree lacks water, nutrients, or natural insect pollinators in the farm.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa. Shi nibii ni laajeɔ fe nine lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ nu, niyenii mli hewalɛ loo adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees turn yellow and start curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow curling leaves usually mean the soil is missing essential food like nitrogen, or small sap-sucking pests called mirids (capsids) are damaging the young leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu ni atsɛɔ amɛ mirids (capsids) lɛ miifite baai bibii lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot on the tree before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛshwere lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in cool, wet weather. Keeping the farm weeded and pruning dense branches lets sunlight in to dry out moisture and prevent rot.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ waa mli. Ehe miihia ni aha ŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi afee jwɛi ni afo mli waa koni hulu la lɛ aha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi ni ekɛtsi ŋmɔtɔ naa.

english: How can I tell that a cocoa pod is completely ripe and ready to be picked?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ajie amɛ?

english: A ripe cocoa pod changes color completely, turning bright yellow or deep orange depending on the variety. Harvesting when fully ripe ensures the seeds inside have enough sugar for rich chocolate flavor.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su kwraa. Etsakeɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli kwɔ. Edamɔ henɔi lɛ anɔ Amɛkpamɔ beni amɛshwere kwraa lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ amli sugar ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha tsokolate ni ŋɔɔ waa.

english: Why do cocoa beans change from white or purple to brown during fermentation?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eyɛŋ loo purple kɛyaa brown nɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ lɛ?

english: Fermentation heats up the beans under banana leaves, killing the seed inside and starting a chemical process that destroys bitterness and turns the beans brown, creating the signature rich taste.
ga: Fɛ̃i baaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ banana baai lɛ ashishi lɛ mli adɔ. efiteɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ebɔi tsofafeemɔ nitsumɔ ko ni fiteɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Ehaa ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto, ni naa wa baa.

english: Why must I dry my harvested cocoa beans on raised bamboo mats instead of directly on the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ migbiɔ mi-kokoo yibii ni mikpa lɛ yɛ ŋmeii anɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Raised mats allow fresh air to flow both above and below the beans for quick, uniform drying, while keeping dirt, animals, and mold away from the beans so they maintain premium international quality.
ga: Mat ni awo nɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ kɔfi yibii lɛ anɔ kɛ amɛshishi koni amɛgbi oya, ni amɛgbi po. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaaa muji, kooloi, kɛ ŋmeii akabote kɔfi yibii lɛ amli. Koni akɛkwɛ majimaji ateŋ nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ nɔ

english: Maize leaves turn yellow mainly because the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the plant's essential food for green leaf growth. It can also happen when there is too much water sitting around the roots or when weeds are stealing nutrients from your crop.
ga: Nɔ titri ni haa ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ji akɛ, nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei baanyɛ akwɛ koni amɛná baai eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu babaoo ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe loo kɛ́ jwɛi ju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and die suddenly even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tso lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by a soil-borne disease like bacterial wilt or root rot. The disease blocks the plant's internal water transport channels, preventing water from moving up from the roots to the leaves, which causes the plant to droop and die even in wet soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa tamɔ bacteria wilt loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Hela nɛɛ tsiɔ gbɛi ni nu tsɔɔ nɔ kɛyaa tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekajɛ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛya baai lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa tsei gboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ po nɔ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants without turning into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off pepper plants when the weather becomes extremely hot and dry, or if the soil lacks nutrients like phosphorus. Extreme heat stresses the plant, causing it to drop its flowers to survive rather than spending energy growing fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ pepper tsei anɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa. Aloo kɛji akɛ niyenii tamɔ fɔsfɔs bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛhi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii kɛdu aduawai

english: Why should I plant plantain trees alongside my newly planted young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are delicate and easily scorched by direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow very quickly and have large leaves that create living shade, protecting young cocoa plants from heat and keeping moisture in the soil during their first couple of years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden stakes in the ground for my yam plants to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ awo shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs sunlight to produce energy for expanding big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to light, improving air flow, and reducing the risk of leaf fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛkwɛ̃ bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ha baai lɛ afee la. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ni oha tsofa ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ aba shi

english: How do I know when my cassava is ready to harvest, and why do the roots rot if left too long?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa? Ni mɛni hewɔ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ amɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest between 9 to 12 months after planting when lower leaves start drying and falling off. If mature tubers are left in flooded or heavy rainy soil for too long, lack of air in the soaked ground causes the starch-filled roots to decay.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi Kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmeii ni eda lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, Kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi ni starch eyi mli obɔ lɛ fiteɔ.

english: What causes small holes in my maize leaves and saw-dust-like material inside the middle of the plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ nibii ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ anɔ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest in Ghana that hides and feeds inside the growing central funnel of maize plants. Treating the crop early with recommended control measures stops them before they destroy the yield.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei, ni ji ŋmei ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni kɛ ehe teeɔ ni eyeɔ nii yɛ ŋmei tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe nitsumɔ mra Kɛtsɔ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ ekpaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani efiteɔ yibiiwoo lɛ.

english: Why does planting maize on the exact same piece of land every single year lead to lower harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season without giving the land time to recover. It also allows specific pests and soil diseases that feed on maize to multiply and build up in that field.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe. Ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi kɛ helai komɛi ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ hu feɔ babaoo ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Is it better for me to apply fertilizer right before a heavy rainstorm or after the rain stops?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli dani nugbɔ anɛ waa loo beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa sɛɛ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist or right before light rain. Heavy downpours will wash the fertilizer away from your plants' roots into nearby gutters and streams before the crop can absorb it.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo loo dani nugbɔ fioo ko baanɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi amli kɛyaa nubui kɛ faai ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli dani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow smaller and produce lower yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than cultivated crops and aggressively steal vital groundwater, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients from the soil. Clearing weeds early ensures your main crops get all the food and light required for a strong yield.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. ni ekɛ ekãa juɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ aná niyenii kɛ la fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa.

english: Why are my crops producing very small fruits this season even though I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii waa yɛ be nɛɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Fruit size depends heavily on seed quality, soil nutrients, and crop spacing. If you use saved seeds from bad harvests or plant too close together, the crops fight for food and light, resulting in small fruits regardless of watering.
ga: Yibii lɛ dalɛ damɔ bɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ hi ha lɛ nɔ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ sɛɛ ni kã tsei ateŋ lɛ fa waa Kɛji akɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ gbonyo mli loo ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baawu kɛha niyenii kɛ la. Enɛ haa aduawai bibii baa ni ekɔɔɔ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ he.

english: What can I do on my farm to help my crops produce bigger and heavier fruits?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji ni tsii?

english: To increase fruit size, use certified seeds, apply fertilizers rich in potassium during the flowering and fruiting stages, prune excess branches, and ensure proper spacing so each plant receives full sunlight.
ga: Bɔni afee ni aduawai lɛ aya hiɛ Kɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ atsu nii. Okɛ potassium ni fa babaoo awo mli yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo be mli. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ. ni okɛ amɛ abɔ he bɔ ni sa bɔni afee ni tso fɛɛ tso aná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Does the source where I get my seeds or planting materials affect how large my harvested fruits will grow?
ga: Ani he ni mináa midumɔwui loo nibii ni miduɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ lɛ saa miyibii ni mikpa ni baakwɛ̃ lɛ dalɛ he?

english: Yes, seed genetics set the maximum limit for fruit size. Certified seeds bought from approved agro-dealers are bred for high yields and uniform fruit size, whereas uncertified seeds from market produce often yield small or irregular fruits.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui amli wala yibii kɛ husu ni nɔ kwɔ haa aduawai lɛ adalɛ. Akwɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni ahe kɛjɛ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔi ni akpɛlɛ amɛnɔ lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo kɛ aduawai lɛ adalɛi ni yaa nɔ daa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni bɛ he odaseyeli ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ woɔ yibii bibii loo amɛwoɔ yibii ni ejaaa.

english: Will adding more fertilizer make my fruits grow big if the original seeds came from poor parent crops?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha miyibii lɛ adara kɛji akɛ shishijee dumɔwui lɛ jɛ fɔlɔ tso ni ehiii mli?

english: Fertilizer helps plants reach their full natural potential, but it cannot override bad genetics. If the seed naturally produces small fruits, excess fertilizer will mostly grow larger leaves rather than bigger fruits.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛshɛɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔi fɛɛ he. Shi anyɛɛɛ aye fɔmɔ su ni ehiii lɛ nɔ kunim. Kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ woɔ yibii bibii yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ekolɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ baaha baai lɛ adara fe aduawai lɛ agbo.

english: How can I calculate or estimate my total harvest before I start picking the crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nii lɛ fɛɛ he akɔntaa loo mabu he akɔntaa dani mije miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akpamɔ shishi?

english: You can estimate yield by choosing ten random plants across your farm, counting the average number of good fruits on them, multiplying that by your total plant count, and converting the total number into expected crates or weight.
ga: Obaanyɛ osusu yibiiwoo he kɛtsɔ tsei 10 ni ohalaa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kanemɔ aduawai kpakpai ayibɔ ni aja mli lɛ. Okɛ enɛ ato tsei ni oyɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ ayibɔ he. ni otsake shika fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ owo adeka loo shwiili ni akpaa gbɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it important for a farmer to calculate expected yields before harvest day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni okwaafoi abu ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛkpaa gbɛ akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ he akɔntaa dani amɛkpa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ?
