english: Calculating expected yields helps you prepare the right number of crates, arrange transport in advance, and negotiate fair prices with buyers instead of accepting low offers at the farm gate.
ga: Nibii ni akpaa gbɛ akɛ abaaná lɛ he akɔntaabuu haa onyɛɔ osaa adekai ayibɔ ni sa. Too gbɛfaa he gbɛjianɔ kɛtsɔ hiɛ. ni okɛ mɔ ni heɔ lɛ agba jara ni sa he sane. Mohu ɔ, kplɛɛ sika nɛ a kɛ haa mo ngɛ ngmɔ ɔ agbo ɔ nya ɔ nɔ mohu.

english: Why do buyers force farmers to overfill harvest crates until the fruits spill over?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ nyɛɔ okwaafoi anɔ koni amɛwo ŋmaakpamɔ adekai amli babaoo kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛyiɔ aduawai babaoo lɛ?

english: Buyers overfill crates to get extra weight without paying for it, which reduces your profits. Using standardized crates with agreed weight limits protects you from giving away produce for free.
ga: Mɔ ni heɔ nii lɛ wo adeka lɛ mli fe nine koni enyɛ ekɛ muji ni fata he lɛ awo mli ni ewooo he nyɔmɔ. Enɛ baaha sɛɛnamɔ ni onáa lɛ aba shi. Kɛ okɛ adekai ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni akɛ husu ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ eshɛɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaabu ohe kɛjɛ nibii ni okɛhaa yaka lɛ he.

english: How do small container measures like caps or tins translate into standard market crates?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsɔnei bibii ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe tamɔ tsɔnei ni akɛwoɔ mli loo tsɛnsii tsɔɔ jarayeli adekai ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ lɛ amli?

english: Small containers hold specific average quantities; knowing how many caps fill a single standard crate allows you to calculate your actual yield and negotiate fair prices based on volume.
ga: Nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɛnsi bibioo mli lɛ hiɛɔ shika fioo ko pɛ. Kɛ́ ole ŋmɛlɛtswai enyiɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɛlɛtswaa kome mli lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ obuɔ yibiiwoo diɛŋtsɛ he akɔntaa ni okɛ jara ni sa ni damɔ bɔ ni amɛyi fa ha lɛ nɔ lɛ susuɔ he.

english: Why do my crops yield smaller fruits when I plant many seeds close together in a small area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii beni midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ he bibioo ko lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, their roots compete for limited soil nutrients and water while their leaves block sunlight from one another, causing the crops to produce smaller, underdeveloped fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli kɛ nu ni faaa lɛ he akaŋ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ bibii ni amɛyaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does removing excess flowers or small fruits from a crop help the remaining fruits grow larger?
ga: Fɔfɔi loo aduawai bibii ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ Te tso lɛ ni ashiɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa aduawai ni eshwɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa tɛŋŋ?

english: Removing excess flowers or smaller fruits—a process called thinning—forces the plant to direct all its water and nutrients into the remaining fruits, making them significantly larger and heavier.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine loo aduawai ni dalɛ faaa lɛ ni ajieɔ - nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ thinning - nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ enu kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ majeɔ aduawai ni eshwɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni da ni etsiiɔ kwraa.

english: Why are my young cocoa pods turning black and falling off the tree before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is often caused by Black Pod disease or natural pod thinning. Black Pod is a fungal disease that spreads rapidly in wet and shady conditions, so keeping weeds down and opening up tree shade helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji black pod hela loo bɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli ni agbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many flowers, but the flowers just dry up without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔi lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeee ŋmeii?

english: Dry weather, extreme heat, or pest attacks like mirids can cause flowers to drop off. Ensuring your farm has enough shade trees and protecting the farm from sucking insects helps flowers turn into healthy pods.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ atatu baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ agbo. Kɛ́ okwɛ koni oŋmɔ lɛ aná tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa, ni obu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What causes small dark patches and blisters on my young cocoa stems and pods?
ga: Mɛni kɛ okadii diji bibii kɛ ŋmeii baa? Yɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ kɛ mi-pods lɛ anɔ

english: These dark spots are usually caused by tiny insects called mirids or 'akate'. They bite and suck sap from young branches and pods, which can dry out shoots and ruin young pods if not treated with approved pest sprays.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ mirids loo ‘akate’ lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ ni amɛnuɔ tsei niji bibii kɛ ŋmeii amli nu lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni efite ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsuuu he nii.

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or shade trees creates an umbrella that protects young cocoa from heat and preserves soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ tsei bibii loo shade tsei ni aduɔ. Ehaa hulutsoo baa ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he, ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi.

english: Why should I measure exact distances between my crops instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu gbɛ pɔtɛɛ ni kã miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ he? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots and leaves fight for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper spacing ensures every crop grows strong and yields well.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tse lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni sa yɛ tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ, ebaaha tsei fɛɛ adara waa ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: What does it mean when the leaves on my maize crops turn yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛ́ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your crop lacks key nutrients like nitrogen in the soil. Adding proper fertilizer or organic manure feeds the plant so it can regain its rich green color and grow bigger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo tso lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ená ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni da.

english: Is it safe to cut off extra branches from my cocoa trees, or will it hurt my harvest?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata mi-cacao tso lɛ he lɛ? Aloo ebaafite nibii ni mifeɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning extra branches actually helps your farm produce more cocoa. It lets sunlight and fresh air reach the stem, reduces fungal diseases, and allows the tree to focus its strength on growing healthy pods.
ga: Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔ lɛ ni ewoɔ kookoo babaoo. Enɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ shishi, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ maa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni wa ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: How do weeds growing around my cassava plants reduce my yield?
ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle mi lɛ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni mi-cassava tso lɛ aha mi yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi?

english: Weeds steal the water, food, and sunlight that your cassava needs to build large roots. Clearing weeds early in the season leaves all the soil nourishment for your crops.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa ŋmei koni shishifãi wuji akwɛ̃ lɛ. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii ni haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baatsu nii.

english: Why do the roots of my crops rot when rainwater stays on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei shishifãi fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu ta ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Crop roots need oxygen in the soil to breathe. Standing water blocks air from reaching the roots, causing them to drown and rot, which is why digging simple drainage paths helps drain excess water away.
ga: Tse shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni haa efoɔ nu mli ni egboɔ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni nu ni hoɔ gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsa lɛ Enɛ baaye abua ni ajie nu ni fa fe nine lɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my cocoa pods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Fully ripe cocoa pods change color cleanly—green pods turn bright yellow, and red pods turn deep orange-yellow. Harvesting at full maturity ensures the beans inside yield the highest weight and quality.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su kwraa. Pods eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. ni ŋmeii tsuji lɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Nikpamɔ beni edara kwraa lɛ haa kɔfi yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tsiimɔ kɛ amɛhe feɔ fɛo fe fɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight burns their tender leaves and dries out the topsoil. Planting plantains or shade trees nearby acts like a natural shield, giving young cocoa the moisture and cool environment it needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi. Tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi.

english: Why do I need to cut off extra shoots growing from the trunk of my mature cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifoɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ cacao tso ni eda lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: These extra shoots, called water shoots, suck nutrients and energy away from the main tree without producing pods. Removing them allows the tree to send all its food to developing cocoa pods.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi nɛɛ akɛ nu ŋmeii. Ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ shwieɔ tso titri lɛ nɔ ni efeee ŋmeii. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ eniyenii fɛɛ majeɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I wait until after the rains start before applying fertilizer to my maize field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ akpa dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Fertilizer requires soil moisture to dissolve so plant roots can absorb it. Applying it in dry soil can burn the roots or waste the fertilizer since the plant cannot take up dry chemical nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ okɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ loo eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei nyɛŋ aná tsofai ni mli egbi ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce very small tubers when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava is planted too close, the plants compete with each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Spacing them properly gives each root enough soil volume to grow big tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ baaha shishifã fɛɛ shishifã aná shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha bulb agbo ko akwɛ̃.

english: Is it beneficial for me to plant cowpeas or beans on the same land where I grow maize?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ baaba he akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmã yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, leguminous crops like beans pull nitrogen from the air and naturally feed it into the soil, which acts as a free natural fertilizer for your maize while preventing weed growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa o-corn lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, humid shade. Trimming dense branches lets air flow through the farm, keeping pods dry and reducing fungus attack.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni shade yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do armyworms destroy the center of my maize plants so fast during warm weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii fiteɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ oya yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Armyworms hatch quickly in warm temperatures and feed directly on the tender leaves inside the maize crop's funnel. Inspecting the leaves early allows you to catch and treat them before they damage the growing point of the plant.
ga: Roundworms lɛ fɔɔ oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. ni ayeɔ yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Baai lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ omɔɔ baai lɛ ni otsaa amɛ dani amɛfiteɔ he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt in the afternoon heat even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: Hot midday sun makes leaves evaporate water faster than roots can draw it from the soil. Watering deeply early in the morning or in the evening ensures water penetrates down to the roots where it stays cool.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane teŋ lɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli waa leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ hei ni jɛmɛ ejɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I save seeds from my hybrid maize harvest to plant for the next farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid corn kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ toɔ kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli dumɔ?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops lose their high yield strength and disease defense in the second generation, resulting in weak growth and smaller yields compared to purchasing fresh certified seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛ yibii babaoo kɛ helai ahebuu yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shweremɔ baa shi ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahemɔ he.

english: Why must I dry my harvested cocoa beans on raised bamboo mats instead of directly on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ migbiɔ mi-kookoo ni mikpa lɛ yɛ ŋmeii anɔ moŋ fe ni mikɛbaa shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Raised mats allow air to circulate above and below the beans for even drying while protecting them from mud, ground moisture, and animal contamination that ruin bean quality.
ga: Mat ni awo nɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ anɔ kɛ amɛshishi koni amɛgbi po. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ kɔfe yibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ muji he. shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi amli muji ni fiteɔ ŋshɔŋlooi lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my mango trees suddenly developing severe black spots and dying so fast?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei lɛ feɔ diji waa ni amɛgboiɔ oya nɛkɛ?

english: This is likely a fast-acting fungal disease locally known as 'biris' or 'mango COVID'. It spreads rapidly between trees and can severely damage a farm quickly if not caught early.
ga: Enɛ baanyɛ afee fungal hela ni tsuɔ nii oya ni ale yɛ maŋ lɛ mli akɛ 'biris' loo 'mango Covid'. Egbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ateŋ oya. Ni ebaanyɛ efite ŋmɔji waa oya kɛji akɛ amɔmɔɔɔ amɛ oya.

english: What does it mean when other farmers talk about 'mango AIDS' or 'mango COVID' in our area?
ga: Beni okwaafoi krokomɛi wieɔ Mɛni ji 'Mango AIDS' loo 'Mango Covid' shishi yɛ wɔ akutso lɛ mli?

english: These are local names for an aggressive fungal disease called 'biris' that recently emerged in Ghana. Farmers call it that because it spreads quickly from tree to tree and severely weakens the plant.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji maŋ lɛ mli gbɛi ni akɛtsɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbeɔ mɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘biris’ ni eba Ghana nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ. Okwaafoi tsɛɔ lɛ nakai ejaakɛ egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ, ni ehaa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ waa.

english: Why are new crop diseases appearing on mango farms in Ghana that we haven't seen before?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso hela hee ko miiba yɛ mango tso yibii abɔɔi amli yɛ Ghana ni wɔnako eko dã lɛ?

english: Changing weather patterns, changing humidity, and the movement of infected plant materials allow new fungal strains to emerge and thrive in areas where they were not common in the past.
ga: kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni tsakeɔ hulutsoo kɛ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ agbɛfaa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii henɔi heei jeɔ kpo ni amɛdaraa yɛ hei ni afɔɔɔ namɔ tsutsu lɛ.

english: How quickly does a fungal treatment start working after I spray it on my crop?
ga: Te tsofa ni akɛtsaa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ jeɔ shishi etsuɔ ​​nii oya beni mikɛshwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Fungal treatments begin working almost immediately upon contact. They act within seconds to form a shield on the plant surface or stop the fungus from penetrating deeper.
ga: Tsofa ni gbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ jeɔ shishi etsuɔ ​​nii aaafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji mɔ ko kɛ ehe wo mli. Amɛtsuɔ nii yɛ sɛkɛndii fioo komɛi amli koni amɛfee nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he yɛ tso lɛ hiɛ loo amɛtsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni ekabote mli shɔŋŋ.

english: How does a fungal spray actually protect my crops from getting destroyed?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ abu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni amɛkafite?

english: When applied, the spray creates a protective chemical barrier on the leaves and stems. This barrier stops fungal spores from growing and triggers the plant's own internal defense mechanisms.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsofa ko tsiɔ baai kɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Nɛkɛ gbɛtsii nii nɛɛ haaa fungal spores lɛ adalɛ ni ekanyaa tso lɛ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Is one spray of fungal treatment enough to keep my crop protected forever?
ga: Ani tsofa kome ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni baabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛya naanɔ?

english: No, while the treatment acts fast to protect the plant, new growth, rain, and intense sunlight can reduce its effectiveness over time, requiring periodic reapplication during disease outbreaks.
ga: Dabi, yɛ be mli ni atsuɔ tsofafeemɔ lɛ he nii oya koni akɛbu tso lɛ he. Nɔ hee ni yaa hiɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ, kɛ hulu la ni naa wa baanyɛ aha bɔ ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ ehaa lɛ aba shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Esa akɛ akɛtsu nii ekoŋŋ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Yɛ be mli ni hela lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ

english: How can I tell if a disease on my farm is caused by a fungus rather than poor soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela ko ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ jɛ ŋmei mli moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni ehiii?

english: Fungal diseases usually spread rapidly across nearby plants, causing dark spots, rotting, or sudden wilting, whereas soil problems usually affect plants more slowly and evenly across a specific plot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela mli baa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ fɛɛ oya. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, loo ŋmɔtɔ baa trukaa. yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ he naagbai fɔɔ tsei anɔ hewalɛ blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ ko nɔ.

english: Why does a disease like 'biris' spread across an entire farm so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ helai tamɔ ‘Biris’ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔji amli oya nɛkɛ?

english: Fungal diseases produce thousands of microscopic spores that travel easily through wind, rain splashes, farm tools, and insects, allowing them to infect healthy trees rapidly like an outbreak.
ga: Fungal hela lɛ haa ŋmeii bibii akpei abɔ ni baanyɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, okwaayeli nibii kɛ kooloi bibii amli oya lɛ baa. Enɛ haa amɛyeɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ hela oya tamɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: What should I do immediately if I suspect a fast-spreading disease has hit my mango farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji misusu akɛ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya eba mi-mango tso yibii abɔɔ lɛ mli?

english: You should apply an approved fungal treatment immediately to protect unaffected trees, prune off heavily diseased branches, and avoid moving unwashed tools between infected and healthy trees.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni ebu tsei ni enaaa hela lɛ ahe. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ waa lɛ. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ nibii ni afɔɔɔ he lɛ ni oootsi kɛya tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ateŋ lɛ he.

english: Can my pruning tools spread fungal diseases from one tree to another?
ga: Ani mitsɔne ni mikɛtsuɔ nii kɛfoɔ tsei lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ashwã tso kome nɔ kɛya ekroko nɔ?

english: Yes, cut surfaces on plants easily absorb fungal spores from contaminated cut tools. Sanitizing your cutlass or shears between trees helps stop the spread of fast-moving diseases.
ga: Hɛɛ, hei ni afo yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmeii ni jɛ tsei ahe nibii ni mli ewo muji lɛ amli lɛ mlɛo. Kɛ́ akɛ tsɔnei loo tsɔnei ni akɛgbeɔ helai ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ baaye abua ni akpa hela ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya nɛɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: How can I tell if the crop seeds I buy in the market are genuine and registered?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ ji anɔkwale ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ?

english: Genuine seeds come in sealed bags or containers with official certification tags from approved seed regulatory bodies. Checking for these official tags ensures the seed has been tested to sprout well and produce healthy crops.
ga: Dumɔwui diɛŋtsɛ baa yɛ kotokui ni atsĩ naa mli loo tsɛnsii ni maŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ eji nɔ ni jɛ dumɔwui ahe gbɛjianɔtoo ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aŋmala ashwie shi nɛɛ ni akwɛɔ mli lɛ haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ aka dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Which government agency in Ghana is responsible for checking and registering good crop seeds?
ga: Mɛɛ nɔyeli nitsumɔhe ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ ji mɔ ni kwɛɔ tsei dumɔwui kpakpai anɔ ni eŋmalaa amɛgbɛi awoɔ wolo nɔ?

english: The Plant Protection and Regulatory Services Directorate (PPRSD) under the Ministry of Food and Agriculture is responsible for registering seed companies and inspecting seeds to ensure they are safe and high quality for farmers.
ga: Nitsumɔhe nine ni kwɛɔ tsei anɔ kɛ amɛhe gbɛjianɔtoo nɔ (PPRSD) ni yɔɔ Niyenii kɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ shishi lɛ ji mɔ ni kwɛɔ dumɔwui nitsumɔhei lɛ anɔ ni amɛkwɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli koni amɛkwɛ akɛ amɛyɛ shweshweeshwe ni amɛhi jogbaŋŋ kɛha okwaafoi.

english: What details should I check on a seed container before buying it for planting?
ga: Mɛɛ saji fitsofitso esa akɛ makwɛ yɛ dumɔwui atsɛnsi mli dani mahe koni mikɛdu?

english: Look for the registered company name, the official seed certification label, the crop variety, the germination rate, batch number, and the expiry date printed on the packaging.
ga: Taomɔ nitsumɔhe lɛ gbɛi ni aŋmala awo wolo nɔ lɛ. Akala dumɔwui ahe odaseyeli wolo lɛ, tso henɔi, bɔ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ, kuu yibɔ kɛ gbi ni esɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some seeds I buy from open market sellers fail to sprout even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miheɔ kɛjɛɔ jarayelɔi adɛŋ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po?

english: Unregistered or loose market seeds are often poorly stored, old, or mixed with bad grains. Certified seeds are tested for high germination rates so that almost every seed planted will sprout under good rainfall.
ga: dumɔwui ni aŋmalako amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ loo ni etse Bei pii lɛ, akɛ amɛ etooo jogbaŋŋ, amɛdara, loo akɛ dumɔwui gbohii efutu mli. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ mli koni ana kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, nɔ ni miihe ashɛ dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu ni adu lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kpakpa shishi.

english: If I plant seeds saved from my previous harvest, will they perform as well as registered seeds from a shop?
ga: Kɛji midu dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ Ani nakai dumɔwui lɛ baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ tamɔ dumɔwui ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ kɛjɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds often lose their vigor and disease resistance over time, leading to lower yields. Registered seeds are specially bred and processed to give higher yields, uniform crop growth, and better protection against diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ helai ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni atsuɔ he nii koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. tsei lɛ adalɛ ni yɔɔ ekomefeemɔ mli ni amɛtsi helai anaa jogbaŋŋ

english: Will buying registered crop seeds ensure that my crops grow and mature at the same time?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ ni miheɔ lɛ baaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛshwere yɛ be kome too mli?

english: Yes, registered seeds come from pure, high-quality parent plants, which means the crops will germinate together, grow uniformly, and be ready for harvest at the same time.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ jɛ nyɛ tsei ni he tse, ni hi jogbaŋŋ amli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ he kome. ni yaa hiɛ be fɛɛ be ni efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ yɛ be kome too mli

english: How does using certified crop seeds help prevent crop diseases on my farm?
ga: Te dumɔwui ni awo he hewalɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe helai anaa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Certified seeds undergo strict health checks to make sure they are free from seed-borne diseases and pests before being packaged, preventing you from introducing infections into your soil.
ga: Dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yaa hewalɛnamɔ mli kwɛmɔ mli waa koni ana akɛ helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni jɛɔ dumɔwui amli baa lɛ bɛ mli dani akɛwoɔ kotoku mli. Enɛ baatsi bo gbɛ ni okɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ akabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why are certified crop seeds packaged in sealed bags while local seeds are sold loose in cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ woɔ kotokui ni atsĩ naa mli yɛ be mli ni ahɔ̃ɔ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ kɔɔpoi amli lɛ?

english: Sealed packaging protects high-quality seeds from moisture, insects, and air damage, and guarantees that no one has tampered with or swapped the certified seeds inside.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ buɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ, kooloi bibii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ ahe. ni eha nɔmimaa akɛ mɔ ko mɔ ko tsakeŋ loo etsakeŋ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ mli.

english: How do I verify if a new seed seller coming to my village is selling approved crop seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji dumɔwui heei ni baa mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ hɔ̃ɔ dumɔwui ni akpɛlɛ nɔ?

english: You can ask the seller to show their official registration credentials or consult your local agricultural extension officer to confirm if the company and their seeds are recognized by the state seed authority.
ga: Obaanyɛ obi nihɔɔlɔ lɛ ni ekɛ woloŋmaa he saji aha loo obi okpokpaa lɛ nɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ lɛ koni ema nɔ mi kɛji amɛ nitsumɔhe lɛ kɛ dumɔwui lɛ ji nɔ ni omaŋ lɛ dumɔwui ahe nitsumɔhe lɛ kpɛlɛɔ nɔ.

english: What should I do if a seed dealer sells me a package that does not have any registration label on it?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mɔ ko ni kɛ dumɔwui baa lɛ hɔ̃ɔ mi paketii ni aŋmalaaa nɔ ko awoɔ mli lɛ?

english: Do not buy or plant unlabelled seeds, as planting unverified seeds risks complete crop failure. Report unlabelled seed products to your local agricultural office so they can protect other farmers in the area.
ga: Kaahe loo kadu dumɔwui ni aŋmalako nɔ ko nɔ ko. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni akwɛɛɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Bɔɔ dumɔwui ni aŋmalako nɔ ko lɛ he amaniɛ kɛya okwaayeli nitsumɔhe ni yɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ. Koni enyɛ ebu okwaafoi krokomɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahe

english: Why shouldn't I plant four or five maize seeds together in the same hole to get more cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa ejwɛ loo enumɔ yɛ bu kome mli koni maná ŋmãa babaoo?

english: Planting too many seeds in one hole causes the young maize plants to crowd each other out and fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks and very small or empty cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ baaha ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ afee ekome ni amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings drying up and dying during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under full sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them acts as a living umbrella, protecting the seedlings from heat stress until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ baatsu nii akɛ shade ni hiɛ ka. Buu dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the central leaves inside the heart of my young corn stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye baai ni yɔɔ mi-bibii ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest, which burrows into the growing center of the maize plant. Checking your farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract into the leaf funnel destroys the pests before they ruin the whole crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm, ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ dalɛ mli lɛ mli. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baakpata kooloi lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛbaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into tiny shapes and stopping the fruits from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe bibii bibii lɛ? ni ekpaa yibii lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or mites that spread viruses to the plant. Controlling these insects early with soap sprays or insecticidal treatments protects the crop from getting diseased.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni gbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ nɔ Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Samla loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ helai ahe.

english: Why do my tomato plant leaves get dark spots and rot when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ diji ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Excess rain splashes soil onto leaves and creates moisture that spreads fungal diseases like blight. Staking tomato plants off the ground and removing lower leaves keeps them dry and prevents the disease from destroying your harvest.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni gbɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ late blight lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kɛ́ okɛ o-tomato tsei lɛ wo shikpɔŋ ni ojie shishigbɛ baai lɛ, ebaaha tomato lɛ agbi ni helai akafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why does allowing tall weeds to grow around my crops make my final harvest smaller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi kakadaji akwɛ̃ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ha minaagbee nikpamɔ lɛ nɔ ba shi.

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal the fertilizer, soil moisture, and sunlight meant for your plants. Clearing weeds early in the crop's life ensures your plants get full nutrition to produce heavy yields.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ kɛha otsei lɛ Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ náa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why am I advised to trim off the extra low branches growing out of my tomato stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Trimming those lower side shoots, called suckers, forces the tomato plant to direct its food and water into growing larger, healthier fruits rather than useless foliage.
ga: Atsɛɔ shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ akɛ ŋmeii. Ebaaha tomato tso lɛ ato niyenii kɛ nu he gbɛjianɔ koni efee aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ fe baai ni he ehiaaa.

english: Should I spread fertilizer on my farm right before a heavy rain comes?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ashwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ ni naa wa aba?

english: No, heavy rain will wash away loose fertilizer before the roots can absorb it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already damp after a light rain, and lightly cover it with soil so it stays near the root zone.
ga: Dabi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etse ehe lɛ dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. ni okɛ sũ fioo aha nɔ bɔni afee ni ebɛŋkɛ shishifã lɛ he

english: What happens if I leave my mature cassava tubers in the ground for too long before harvesting?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi ŋmei shishifãi ni eda yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani mikpa?

english: Leaving mature cassava roots underground for too long causes them to become tough, woody, and lose their starch quality, and wet soil can cause the roots to rot.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmei shishifãi ni eda lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee shiŋŋ, amɛfee tamɔ tsei, ni amɛbaafee nɔ ni bɛ sɛɛnamɔ. Ni shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: How can I stop small insects from eating my stored dry corn and turning it into powder?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa? Te aaafee tɛŋŋ aye ŋmãa ni egbi ni ato ni atsake lɛ afee powda?

english: Storage weevils attack maize if it is stored wet or in open sacks. Properly drying your corn until it is hard and storing it in sealed hermetic storage bags suffocates insects and keeps your harvest safe for months.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ amli ŋmeii baatutua ŋmãa kɛji akɛ akɛto kotokui ni agbele mli loo akɛto ŋmãa mli. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ebaawa ni okɛto kotoku ko ni akɛtoɔ nii amli ni atsĩ naa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ ni eye ebua ni okpamɔ lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo.

english: How long does maize take from the day I plant the seeds until it is ready for harvesting?
ga: Be enyiɛ ŋmãa heɔ kɛjɛɔ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni esa akɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Most common maize varieties in Ghana take between 90 to 120 days (about 3 to 4 months) to fully mature, depending on whether you plant an early-maturing or late-maturing seed variety.
ga: Abele henɔ ni afɔɔ naa waa yɛ Ghana lɛ heɔ aaafee gbii 90 kɛyashi 120 (aaafee nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4) dani eshɛɔ shweremɔ he. Edamɔ dumɔwui ni shwereɔ mra loo dumɔwui ni shwereɔ sɛɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my corn plants grow tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When corn plants are crowded, they compete with one another for light, water, and soil nutrients. This forces them to stretch tall looking for sunlight instead of growing thick stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ amɛteŋ. Enɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛgbala amɛhe kɛya shɔŋŋ koni amɛtao hulu la yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my growing maize plants turning yellow while the top leaves remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a sign that the plant lacks nitrogen fertilizer. When nitrogen in the soil is low, the corn plant pulls stored nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the young, growing top leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa lɛ, Abele tsei gbalaa nitrogen ni ato kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my corn leaves roll up tightly into tubes during the dry, hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ shwane ni edɔ ni edɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a natural survival trick corn plants use to save moisture. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the leaf surface exposed to direct sunlight, slowing down water loss.
ga: Baa ni atsiɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ ŋaa ni abɛi tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛbu nu mli. Tsei baa hulu la ni baa amɛnɔ lɛ shi kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ lɛ nɔ. ni eha nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo

english: If I plant cowpeas together with my maize on the same land, will the cowpeas steal food from my maize?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa fata he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Ani tsina ŋmeii baaju niyenii kɛjɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli?

english: No, cowpeas actually help feed the maize. Cowpea roots work with natural soil microbes to capture nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil, providing free food for your corn.
ga: Dabi, tsina ŋmeii yeɔ ebuaa diɛŋtsɛ kɛhaa ŋmãa niyenii. Cowpea shishifãi kɛ adebɔɔ mli sũ mli nibii bibii tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto sũ lɛ mli. akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha o-corn

english: Why does planting maize on the exact same farm patch every year lead to smaller harvests each time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ haa yibiiwoo fioo baa be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on specific soil nutrients every season. Repeating the crop on the same spot without resting the land or adding manure exhausts those key nutrients, leaving the soil depleted.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo daa be mli. Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akɛ sũ lɛ ejɔɔɔ he loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ, ebaaha nakai niyenii mli nibii titrii lɛ afite. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ.

english: Why do some of my corn cobs have missing kernels or empty spaces when I peel the husk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bɛ mli beni mifoɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Empty spaces mean pollination failed, often due to heat or drought when the plant was flowering. Every silk thread must receive pollen from the top tassel to form a single full grain of corn.
ga: He ni nɔ ko bɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ pollination lɛ eshɛɛɛ he. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ loo hɔmɔ ni baa yɛ tso lɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Esa akɛ siliki kpãa fɛɛ kpãa aná pollen kɛjɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaa lɛ mli koni efee ŋmãa ŋmãa ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do fall armyworms attack the deep inside center of my young maize plants instead of the outside leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall worms lɛ tutuaa mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ yɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: The inner central funnel contains the softest, most nutritious young leaves. Pests hide deep inside this moist funnel to stay protected from heat, direct sun, and natural predators like birds.
ga: Baai bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni niyenii yɔɔ mli fe fɛɛ lɛ yɔɔ mligbɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ mli. Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ nɛkɛ gbɛjegbɛi ni mli ewo nu nɛɛ amli shɔŋŋ. Koni abu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ, kɛ adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi tamɔ okpoi ahe.

english: Why is it critical for me to clear weeds from my corn farm within the first month after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ ni mikɛdu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The first month is when young maize roots are small and weak. If weeds are left to grow during this early period, they quickly steal most of the water and fertilizer before the crop can reach them.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ ji be mli ni ŋmeii bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa. Kɛji akɛ aŋmɛ jwɛi gbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shishijee be nɛɛ mli lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo oya dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe.

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil or grow mold quickly if I store it immediately after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya loo ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛji mikpa lɛ beni mikpa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly picked maize still holds a lot of moisture inside the seeds. Storing wet grain traps heat and moisture, creating an environment where destructive mold and fungi quickly multiply.
ga: Abɛi ni ajie ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lolo. Dumɔwui ni efɔ lɛ ni akɛtoɔ lɛ baamɔmɔ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ko baa ni fungal kɛ fungal helai baanyɛ aya hiɛ oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and dropping off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade from bigger plants like plantains or shade trees to protect them from direct heat and conserve soil moisture during the Harmattan dry season.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei adɛŋ. Koni abu kookoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ he. kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their blossoms without growing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɛɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni miduko tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop blossoms when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture swings quickly from very dry to very wet, which stresses the plant and prevents fruit formation.
ga: Tomato baafɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ehaaa ewo yibii.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves and small green droppings inside the central plant leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Yɛ baa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli?

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on your crop. They hide in the central leaf whorl during the hot day and chew through the fresh green leaves, which slows plant growth if untreated.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ miiye oŋmɔshi nibii. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai lɛ ateŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni efoɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni kpɛɔ lɛ amli Enɛ baaha tso lɛ dalɛ aya hiɛ fioo kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my young maize leaves turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs to build green leaves and grow strong stalks. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted poultry manure helps restore the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas in my field help my next crop of maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas work with beneficial soil microbes to capture nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil, naturally fertilizing the ground for the crops that follow.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas kɛ sũ mli nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛto sũ lɛ mli. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha tsei ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ.

english: How do I know which direction to push cassava stick cuttings into the ground when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male he ni esa akɛ matsi ŋmei niji lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ midu?

english: Look at the small leaf buds along the cassava stem; these buds should point upwards toward the sky so that new shoots can easily grow upward while roots push down into the soil.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. along the cassava stem Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii heei lɛ anyɛ adara oya be mli ni shishifãi lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden stakes in the ground for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi lɛ? Yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground allows the leaves to catch maximum sunlight and protects them from rot and soil diseases, which gives the plant more energy to grow large tubers underground.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yibii lɛ náa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fitemɔ kɛ helai baaa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛwoɔ bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Too many suckers steal water and soil nutrients from the main plantain stem. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main stem gets enough energy to produce a large, heavy fruit bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo juɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ plantain tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo aduawai akui wuji ni tsii.

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, prevents water from evaporating quickly, and stops weeds from taking over around your pepper plants.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaaa jwɛi akaha o-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my maize seeds rot in the ground when I plant them immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ afi lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The very first rain often heats up dry soil without soaking it deeply, creating a hot, wet environment that rots seeds before steady rain pattern begins to support steady germination.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ekɛwooo mli. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa ni haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ dani nugbɔ yaa nɔ nɛɔ koni eye ebua amɛkwɛ̃mɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ.

english: How long does a complete crop cycle take from the nursery stage to the final harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ emuu lɛ heɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ mli kɛyashiɔ naagbee ŋmaakpamɔ be lɛ mli?

english: A full crop life cycle can take up to one year, starting from seed preparation in the nursery, transplanting to the field, and continuing all the way through to the final harvest.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ wala be fɛɛ baanyɛ ahé afi. Jeɔ shishi kɛ dumɔwui ahe saamɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. fãa kɛyaa ŋmɔji amli ni eyaa nɔ aahu kɛyashiɔ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: How many months after planting will my crops be mature enough to reach the ground for harvest?
ga: Nyɔji enyiɛ mli miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baatsɔ agbo bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: It typically takes about four months for the crops to reach maturity and grow tall enough to be ready for harvesting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ aaafee nyɔji ejwɛ dani tso lɛ daa ni edaa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to track the life cycle of my plants from start to finish?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ makwɛ tso ko wala shihilɛ sɛɛ kɛjɛ shishijee kɛyashi naagbee lɛ?

english: Knowing the life cycle helps you plan your farm labor and expenses properly, as you will know exactly when to care for seedlings, when to harvest, and when the crop season ends.
ga: Shihilɛ mli nibii ni yaa nɔ lɛ ni ooole lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni otoɔ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ kɛ shika he gbɛjianɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ. Ejaakɛ obaale be pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ okwɛ dumɔwui lɛ. Be ni esa akɛ akpa kɛ be ni dumɔ be lɛ baa naagbee

english: Is it possible for me to collect produce from my farm every week, or must I wait to harvest all at once?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ mafo nibii ni jɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa otsi? Aloo esa akɛ mamɛ dani makpa fɛɛ shikome?

english: Depending on the crop, once the plant reaches full maturity, you can do weekly harvests to get continuous yield over a period of time.
ga: Beni tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Obaanyɛ okpa nii daa otsi koni onine ashɛ kpamɔ ni yaa nɔ yɛ be ko mli. Edamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Should I cut down my crop during harvest or leave it on the field to dry?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɛ kpamɔ be mli loo mashi ni egbi yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: You can either cut down the mature stalks during harvest or allow them to dry naturally on the field depending on whether you want fresh produce or dry grains.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofolɔ tsei ni eda lɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli loo oha amɛgbi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Edamɔ kɛji oosumɔ nibii heei loo ŋmaa ni egbi lɛ nɔ.

english: What naturally happens to my crops on the farm if I do not cut them down when they mature?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii ni midu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ kɛji mifooo amɛ beni amɛdara lɛ?

english: When crops complete their growth cycle after a few months and are not harvested fresh, they will naturally begin to dry out on the field.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii gbeɔ edalɛ be lɛ naa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ ni akpaaa lɛ ehee. Tsei lɛ baaje shishi amɛgbi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔji amli.

english: How do I know when the harvest season for my crop is completely finished?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni miŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ eba naagbee?

english: The harvest season finishes when the plant completes its full life cycle—often around one year from the nursery stage—and no longer produces fresh yields.
ga: Nikpamɔ be lɛ baa naagbee beni tso lɛ egbe ewala be lɛ naa—bei pii lɛ, aaafee afi kɛjɛ be mli ni ekwɛɔ lɛ lɛ—ni ewooo yibii heei dɔŋŋ.

english: Why does this improved farming method require so much of my time throughout the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli gbɛ ni etee hiɛ nɛɛ biɔ be babaoo yɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Managing a crop across a full one-year cycle—including nursery care, field transplanting, regular maintenance, and weekly harvesting—requires continuous effort and time investment.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ yɛ afi kome muu fɛɛ mli Nɔ ni fata enɛ he ji ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ he kroko, kɛ amɛkwɛmɔ daa. kɛ otsi mli ŋmaakpamɔ Ebiɔ ni akɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ kɛ be awo mli daa.

english: What is the purpose of starting my seeds in a nursery before moving them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ashishijee he yɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe lɛ dani ajie amɛ kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: A nursery allows delicate seeds to sprout safely under protected conditions before being transplanted into the main field, ensuring stronger plant growth.
ga: Dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe lɛ haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ shweshweeshwe yɛ shihilɛi ni abuɔ he lɛ amli. dani oya shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ adara waa.

english: Can I start harvesting parts of my crops while the rest of the farm is still growing?
ga: Ani manyɛ mabɔi miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi akpamɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ miida lolo lɛ?

english: Yes, once your plants reach initial maturity around four months, you can begin regular weekly picking while the main plants remain in the field.
ga: Hɛɛ, beni otso lɛ eda kwraa yɛ aaafee nyɔji ejwɛ mli lɛ. Obaanyɛ oje ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ shishi daa otsi be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ.

english: Why does my farm produce less maize every year if I keep planting it on the exact same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi kɛji midu yɛ he kome pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on nutrients in the topsoil. Planting it continuously in the same place drains those specific nutrients. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas helps naturally rebuild soil fertility for future seasons.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ oya nɔ odu amɛ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ atsɔ mli. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ bei.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in an open field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to strong, direct sunlight and dry heat. Plantain trees or shade trees provide a canopy that shelters young cocoa leaves from burning and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ latsaa ni mli egbi lɛ he waa. Dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when heavy rain leaves water standing on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa ni nu hiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. Waterlogged soil cuts off oxygen to the roots, which causes soil organisms to attack the tubers, leading to rotting.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa bɔɔ nii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa yitso lɛ. kɛ fitemɔ baa

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they suffer from stress caused by extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or missing soil nutrients. Keeping soil moist and mulched helps protect flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ haomɔ ni shwane mli latsaa lɛ kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves indicate a lack of nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. The plant starves and moves available nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to nourish new growth at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Tso lɛ baaye hɔmɔ ni ebaajie nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ, baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛya ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Weeds produce tough seeds that lie hidden in the soil, ready to sprout immediately after the first rain. Crop seeds take longer to wake up and root, so clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing light and water.
ga: Jwɛi woɔ dumɔwui ni wa ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni efee klalo akɛ ebaakwɛ̃ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ Dumɔwui heɔ be babaoo dani amɛteɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi. No hewɔ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju kane kɛ nu.

english: Why do my tomato plant leaves curl up and look weak during the afternoon sun, even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji mikɛ nu wo nɔ leebi po.

english: Under intense hot sun, tomato leaves lose moisture to the air faster than roots can drink it from the soil. Curling leaves reduces the surface area exposed to the sun to conserve internal water.
ga: Yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ laajeɔ nu ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Baai ni abɔle amɛhe lɛ haa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi koni nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akafite.

english: Why should I remove the extra shoots growing at the base of my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Multiple shoots (suckers) around a single plantain stem steal food and water from the main tree. Removing extra shoots ensures all nutrients go to one strong stem that yields a large bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei babaoo (tsei) ni bɔleɔ plantain tso kome he lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ yaa tso kome ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni feɔ ŋmeii babaoo lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops turn brown and burn when I pour fertilizer right against their main stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Concentrated fertilizer acts like harsh salt on fresh roots. Placing it directly against the stem pulls moisture out of the plant roots instead of feeding them. Fertilizer should always be applied a short distance away from the stem.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋoo ni naa wa yɛ shishifãi heei anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ niyenii. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ fioo.

english: How does growing groundnuts or beans make my land better for the next crop I plant?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni madu lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans have tiny beneficial organisms living on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil. When the legume crop harvested, this trapped food stays behind in the soil for future crops.
ga: Peanuts kɛ nuts yɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni hiɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii Niyenii ni awo mli nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and fall over when I plant seeds very close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close forces the crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. They stretch upward too quickly to reach light, making their stems weak, tall, and thin.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛheɔ oya tsɔ ni amɛshɛɛɛ la lɛ he. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ekwɛɔ ni eyɛ mlɛo.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow in the shape of a V?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow starting at the tip and moving down the middle, it means the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps keep the leaves green so the ears can grow full.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛnaa kɛba shi kɛtee teŋgbɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛaawo mli lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli bɔni afee ni toi lɛ anyɛ adara kɛyashɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ he.

english: Why does my land dry out so fast and turn hard like a rock after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ oya ni ewaa tamɔ tɛsaa beni nugbɔ enɛɔ lɛ?

english: Soil low in organic matter loses its ability to soak up water and hold moisture. Mixing dried plant material, compost, or animal manure into the soil helps keep it soft and holds water longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ faaa yɛ nɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli dɔŋŋ. Tso mli nibii ni egbi, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfutuɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni efee blɛoo ni ehiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small even when the leaves and stem look very big and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara waa ni amɛhe wa moŋ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, cassava puts all its energy into growing tall stems and lush green leaves instead of sending energy underground to swell the tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu hewalɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ shishi koni eha yitso lɛ adara lɛ

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when afternoon temperatures get too hot or when soil moisture changes too drastically between wet and dry. Providing light shade and steady watering prevents this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ teŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo be ni mli tse ha kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why are my yam vines drying up and dying off toward the end of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: When yam vines turn yellow and dry up naturally late in the season, it means the plant has finished its lifecycle and transferred all its energy into the tuber underground, signaling it is ready for harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe ewala shihilɛ naa ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ etee shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ amli. Etsɔɔ akɛ eshɛ kɛha nikpamɔ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into tight tubes during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛfeɔ tsɔnei ni mli wa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Curling leaves are a defense action pepper plants use to reduce surface area and stop water from evaporating too quickly in hot sun. If they uncurl when the sun goes down, the plant is simply protecting itself.
ga: Curling leaves ji pepper tso ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi ni akɛtsi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛji amɛjie amɛhe beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miibu ehe.

english: Why do worms keep hiding inside the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which prefer eating the soft, young inner leaves. They hide deep inside the funnel of the plant where it is cooler and safe from birds and heat.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛye baai bibii amli nibii. Akɛ amɛ tee tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni amɛhe jɔ ni okpoi kɛ dɔlɛ bɛ amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn into powder and get tiny holes after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ feɔ powder ni eyɛ bu bibii lɛ? Yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli?

english: Weevil insects lay hidden eggs inside dried grains. When they hatch, the young insects eat the inside of the grain until only powder remains, leaving tiny holes as they crawl out.
ga: Kpɔŋɔ lɛ woɔ wɔji ni akɛtee ŋmãa ni egbi mli. Kɛ́ efo lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ yeɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli aahu kɛyashiɔ powda pɛ eshwɛɔ. Buu bibioo ko pɛ eshwɛ. Beni amɛkpãa kɛjeɔ kpo lɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and scorching during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot withstand harsh, direct sunlight and heat. Without temporary shade crops like plantain or cassava planted nearby to block the intense sun and trap moisture, the heat burns the young cocoa leaves and causes them to dry out.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛji akɛ ebɛ lɛ, abaanyɛ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ koni ekɛtsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Dɔlɛ lɛ baashã kookoo baai bibii lɛ ni amɛgbi.

english: Why do my young maize leaves suddenly have small holes and sawdust-like dirt inside the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni muji tamɔ ŋmei yɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest in Ghana. The caterpillar hides inside the young maize central stem (the whorl) to feed on tender leaves, which weakens or kills the plant if left untreated.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii amli (rings) koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ loo egbo kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and shrinking into small shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips, which transmit a virus to the plant. These insects feed on the leaf sap, causing the plant to grow unnaturally and curl its leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. ni kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ yaa tsei amli Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ baa mli nu. Enɛ haa tso lɛ daa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ, ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are fully grown and ready for harvest under the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava plants show visible signs above ground when tubers mature, usually around 9 to 12 months. The lower leaves will dry up and fall off, and the soil around the base of the main stem will crack as the growing roots expand underneath.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ baajie okadii ni anaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ daraa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ eye aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 lɛ, shishigbɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ mli fãa beni shishifãi lɛ daa yɛ eshishi lɛ.

english: Yam plants use their vines and leaves to capture sunlight to produce food for root growth. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot, wet ground, preventing leaf diseases and allowing maximum sunlight exposure so the plant can grow larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛ wain tsei kɛ baai lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛmɔɔ hulu la koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha shishifãi lɛ adalɛ. Staking baaha baai akabote hei ni mli edɔ ni edɔ. Tsi folier helai anaa ni oha hulu la babaoo bɔ ni ooonyɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ bulbs wuji.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress or irregular watering. When the plant does not get steady moisture in hot weather, it sacrifices its flowers to survive rather than using energy to set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Ekɛ fɔfɔi baashã afɔle koni ehi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii koni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ

english: Why does my maize grow much faster and darker green when I apply poultry manure to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa oya ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ waa kɛ mikɛ kooloi aŋmãa fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Poultry manure contains high amounts of nitrogen and organic material, which act as vital plant food. Nitrogen encourages leafy green growth and strong stem development, while organic matter helps the soil hold onto water.
ga: Nitrogen kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɛ kooloi aŋmɔ mli. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ tso niyenii ni he hiaa Nitrogen haa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ daa kɛ tso lɛ yibii ni wa. yɛ be mli ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli.

english: Why do farmers plant cowpeas or beans together in the same field with maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally adds essential nutrients to the ground, feeding the neighboring maize crop and keeping the soil healthy.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ha ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ niyenii. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi

english: Why should I cut off some of the small shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishigbɛ ni ajie lɛ

english: When too many young shoots (suckers) grow around a main plantain tree, they compete with the mother plant for water, sunlight, and nutrients. Removing extra suckers ensures all food goes into producing one large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Beni ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) babaoo ni miida yɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ he lɛ fa babaoo. Amɛkɛ tso nyɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ yɛ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ koni ana akɛ niyenii lɛ fɛɛ baaha ŋmeii agboi ni tsii aba.

english: Why can valley swamp rice grow in standing water while my maize crop dies if water sits around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-valley peat lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi mli yɛ be mli ni mi-corn lɛ gboɔ kɛji nu yɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have hollow air passages inside their stems that send oxygen from the air down to their roots underwater. Maize plants do not have this system, so standing water drowns their roots by blocking the oxygen they need to breathe.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsui ni mli ewo muji yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa nu shishi shishifãi lɛ amli. Abɛi tsei bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛmu lɛ ni etsĩɔ amɛnaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as temporary natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa plants the shade and moisture they need to survive their first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli be kukuoo mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize turning yellow before the stalks fully grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil or the roots are sitting in flooded soil. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or improving drainage helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo shishifãi lɛ yɛ sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he loo oha nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and showing yellow spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is usually caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava cuttings is the best way to keep the crop healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whitefly lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Yucca tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I build my yam mounds in low areas where water settles after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ matswaa ŋmeii akuu yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni nu buaa ehe naa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, well-drained soil to expand and grow big. If water stays around the mounds for too long, the seed yams rot in the ground before they can sprout and produce tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛdara. Kɛji nu hi gɔŋ lɛ he be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ baagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛbaakwɛ̃ ni amɛwo ŋmeii.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep dropping off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress or erratic watering. Consistent watering at the root level and providing light shade during very hot weather helps the plant hold its flowers so fruits can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ koni ewo yibii.

english: Why do my pepper plants wither and stop growing during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gbo ni ekpa shweremɔ yɛ harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The dry Harmattan wind sucks moisture out of plant leaves very quickly. Covering the soil around the pepper roots with dry grass (mulching) and watering regularly helps keep the root zone cool and moist during dry spells.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli lɛ oya. Shikpɔŋ ni bɔle pepper shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulching) kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ be mli ni nu bɛ lɛ.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close, the crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This results in tall, thin, weak stalks with small or missing corn cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛlɛ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa, ni ŋmãa bibii yɔɔ mli loo amɛbɛ.

english: Why does my sweet potato crop grow plenty of green vines but tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ woɔ wain tsei babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli shi ŋmeii bibii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Giving sweet potatoes too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to put all its energy into growing big leaves above ground instead of developing thick tubers below ground.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen wo sweet potato mli fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ afite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛwoɔ ebaai wuji lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ tuber nɛ mi wa ngɛ zugba a sisi.

english: How can I tell when my groundnuts are ready to be harvested from under the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-peanuts lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Groundnuts are ready when the leaves start turning yellow and dry. You can pull up one test plant; if the insides of the pods have dark veins and the nuts fill the shells tightly, it is time to harvest.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ baai lɛ je shishi amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi. Obaanyɛ ogbala kaa nitsumɔhe kome kɛya ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ fãji ni tsuɔ ni ŋmɔtɔi lɛ ebɔle amɛhe jogbaŋŋ lɛ, no lɛ be eshɛɛ ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Why does covering the soil around my vegetables with dry grass make them grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) acts like a blanket. It prevents sunshine from drying out the soil, stops weeds from growing, and rots over time to feed the soil with rich organic matter.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ (mulching) lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Kpaa jwɛi lɛ adalɛ kɛ fitemɔ yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ koni ekɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo aha shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why is it better to put fertilizer right next to my maize plants instead of scattering it across the whole farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli lɛ hi fe ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: When you apply fertilizer directly near the base of each plant (a method called targeted application or side-dressing), the plant roots can easily reach and absorb all the food. Scattering fertilizer across the entire field wastes money because weeds will consume it and rain will wash it away before your maize gets it.
ga: Kɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso fɛɛ tso shishigbɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, (Gbɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ spot fertilizing loo side fertilizing.) Tso lɛ shishifãi baanyɛ ashɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ he mlɛo ni amɛŋɔ. Shika ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ heɔ shika ejaakɛ jwɛi yeɔ lɛ ni nugbɔ hoɔ lɛ dani ŋmãa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Can I mix fertilizer with water and pour it on my maize crops as a liquid solution?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu afutu ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛshwie ŋmãa tsei anɔ akɛ nu mli tsofa?

english: Yes, dissolving fertilizer in water allows crops to absorb nutrients very quickly through their roots or leaves. However, you must follow the correct proportions so the liquid is not too strong, otherwise it can burn and damage the plant leaves.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ nu mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi loo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ onyiɛ bɔ ni sa lɛ sɛɛ bɔni afee ni nu lɛ akafee nɔ ni mli ewo muji tsɔ. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã ni efite tso lɛ baai.

english: Should I give all the fertilizer to my crops at once, or is it better to apply it little by little?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ fɛɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii shikome loo ehi akɛ makɛwo mli fioo fioo?

english: It is much better to apply fertilizer in smaller amounts at different stages of growth, which is called split application. Giving fertilizer little by little ensures the crop gets fed as it grows, rather than losing nutrients to heavy rains early in the season.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo komɛi awo mli. yɛ dalɛ mli fãi srɔtoi amli Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fãi ni akɛwoɔ fɔmɔ kotoku mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli fioo fioo lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná niyenii be mli ni edaa lɛ. Mohu ɔ, nugbɔ nɛ nɛɔ wawɛɛ ngɛ be ɔ sisije ɔ he je ɔ, níhi nɛ haa nɔ he wami ɔ puɛɔ.

english: How close to the stalk of my crop should I place solid fertilizer so I do not destroy it?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa awo tso lɛ he tɛŋŋ koni mikafite lɛ?

english: Place the fertilizer about two to three finger-lengths (around 5 centimeters) away from the stalk and cover it lightly with soil. Putting chemical fertilizer directly against the stem or roots will cause chemical burn and kill the plant.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo 2-3 inches (aafee sɛntimitai 5) kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi ni okɛ sũ aha nɔ fioo. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ tso lɛ shishifãi loo shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha tsofai lɛ ashã ni efite tso lɛ.

english: My maize plants look weak and tired in the field, what kind of fertilizer or care can I give them to bring them back to life?
ga: Mi-abele lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni etɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kwɛmɔ esa akɛ maha amɛ koni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba wala mli ekoŋŋ?

english: When maize leaves look yellow or weak, the plant is usually lacking nitrogen. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea near the roots and clearing surrounding weeds will give the crop a boost of energy to grow strong and green again.
ga: Beni ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo amɛhe waaa Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo tamɔ urea ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ajieɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ babaoo ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni efee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Can I use the same type and amount of fertilizer for both my maize and my potato crop?
