ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ henɔ kome kɛ bɔ ni fa ha lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ?

english: While both crops need nutrients, maize requires high nitrogen to grow tall green leaves, whereas potatoes need higher amounts of potassium and phosphorus to expand their tubers underground. Using targeted fertilizers for each crop gives you the best yield.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei henɔi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ biɔ niyenii kpakpai moŋ, shi nitrogen babaoo he miihia Abɛi koni enyɛ ekwɛ baai ni kɛlɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii biɔ potassium kɛ phosphorus babaoo koni amɛ ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha tso fɛɛ tso lɛ, ebaaha yibiiwoo ni hi fe fɛɛ aba.

english: At what stage in its growth does a maize plant need fertilizer the most?
ga: Mɛɛ dalɛ mli ŋmãa tsei he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii fe fɛɛ?

english: Maize needs fertilizer most when it is about knee-high (roughly 3 to 4 weeks after planting) and again just before it tassels, as these are the critical stages when the plant expands rapidly and forms its grain.
ga: Abele he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii fe fɛɛ beni eshɛɔ tsitsi nɔ (aaafee otsii 3 kɛyashi 4 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ) kɛ agbɛnɛ hu dani enáa ŋmɔshi nibii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, enɛɛmɛi ji gbɛi ni he hiaa ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ he nii beni tso lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya ni ewoɔ dumɔwui lɛ.

english: How and when should I apply fertilizer to my potato plants to get big tubers?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi-potato tsei lɛ anɔ koni maná ŋmeii wuji, ni mɛɛ be?

english: Apply fertilizer in the soil mounds or trenches beside the seed potatoes at planting time, and add a second small portion when you mound up soil around the stems. Potatoes need phosphorus and potassium early on to help form and swell the tubers underground.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo gɔŋ loo nubu ni bɛŋkɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ mli yɛ dumɔ be mli. Ni okɛ fã bibioo ni ji enyɔ afata he beni okɛ sũ toɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ. Atomɔ he miihia fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium mra. Koni eye ebua ni ama shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are my potato plants growing very thick green leaves on top, but only producing very small potatoes underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-potato tso lɛ hiɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli tse waa yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, e woɔ ngma bibii wawɛɛ pɛ ngɛ sisi.

english: This happens when potato plants receive too much nitrogen fertilizer. Excess nitrogen causes the plant to spend all its energy growing big leaves above ground instead of transferring energy down to grow the potatoes underground.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ babaoo nɔ. Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ hewalɛ nɔ ekɛdu ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: What happens to the soil and crops if I apply too much fertilizer at one time?
ga: Mɛni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo mli yɛ be kome mli?

english: Applying too much fertilizer at once creates too much salt in the soil, which burns the crop roots, dries out the plant, and can turn the soil overly acidic over time. It is safer and more effective to feed crops in small, regular amounts.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei babaoo aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ shãa tsei shishifãi, egbiɔ tsei, ni ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee acidic tsɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Niyenii ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii daa, daa lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow and looking weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants are starving for nitrogen or the roots are drowning in too much water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea and ensuring proper field drainage helps the leaves turn dark green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli loo shishifãi lɛ ebote nu mli tsɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he ni okɛ nu shwie oŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop all their flowers without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ fɛɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ ko lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often drop when the tree is stressed by too much direct heat, lack of shade, insect attacks, or poor soil nutrients. Maintaining good shade trees and protecting the farm from insects helps flowers stay on and turn into cocoa pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni fa fe nine, hulutsoo ni bɛ, kooloi ni baatutua lɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni abu ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi bibii ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii.

english: Why is my cassava crop growing very tall with many leaves, but the roots inside the ground stay tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ daraaa lolo?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or grows in overly rich soil, it spends all its energy producing leaves and stems above ground instead of sending food down to expand the tubers underground.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ loo ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmei tsɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ baai kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baatsu nii koni ekɛdu shikpɔŋ shishi tsei.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily whenever heavy rains and strong winds come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots near the surface and carry very heavy bunches at the top, making them top-heavy. Supporting the main stem with strong wooden poles or bamboo forks prevents wind from knocking them down.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ, ni eyɛ fɔfɔi ni tsii waa yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. make it top heavy Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni wa loo ŋmei ni akɛfee ŋtayaa fiɔ tso titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and soft before they even turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato shishigbɛ ni ji eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani efeɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ po lɛ?

english: This black rot at the bottom of the tomato is caused by a lack of calcium inside the fruit, which often happens when soil moisture goes from completely dry to soaking wet. Keeping soil watering regular and steady prevents this issue.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake kɛjɛ nɔ ni egbi kwraa kɛtee nɔ ni mli ewo nu mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni oooha lɛ daa kɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and shrinking into tight wrinkles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the juices from under the leaves. Spraying proper insect control and clearing surrounding weeds protects new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kplukai ni akɛshwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ahe nitsumɔ baaye abua ni ebaatsi baai heei adalɛ naa.

english: Why do I need to spend time lifting my yam vines onto wooden tall stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ be ni mikɛwo sweet potato wain tso ko nɔ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food that feeds the big tuber underground. Lifting the vines on stakes keeps leaves off the damp soil to prevent rot and helps them catch maximum sunlight to grow bigger tubers.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ niyenii. Wein tso lɛ ni ooowo nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ akajɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ nɔ koni ekafite. ni ehaa wain tso lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛ bulbs wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Why do experienced farmers say planting cowpeas or beans makes my soil richer for the next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛɔ akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nii babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans have small lumps on their roots containing friendly bacteria that trap nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the soil, leaving natural plant food behind for the next crop like maize.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji naanyobɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ Enɛ baamɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why is it bad for me to spray water directly on my crop leaves during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ tsei ahe tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ ehiii kɛha mi lɛ?

english: Watering during the hottest part of the day causes most of the water to evaporate instantly before reaching the roots, and wet leaves under scorching sun can easily get burned or develop fungal leaf spots.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ la amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ni baai ni efɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ baanyɛ ashã loo amɛná baai ni ji fungal spots lɛ oya.

english: Why does swamp rice grow fine in standing water while my cassava and maize rot and die in water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋshɔ mli ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni yɔɔ dioo mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mi-cassava kɛ ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ ni egboɔ yɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have tiny internal air tubes inside their stems that carry oxygen from the air down to their roots underwater, allowing them to breathe in flooded ground where other plants suffocate.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi bibii. Yɛ tso lɛ mli, ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa enyɛɔ emuɔ yɛ hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ, ni tsei krokomɛi nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: How much water do my young oil palm seedlings actually need every week during the dry season?
ga: Nu enyiɛ he hiaa mi-oil palm tso lɛ daa otsi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Young oil palms need about 10 to 15 liters of water twice a week during dry periods so their roots can establish deeply without drying out and dying.
ga: Mu tsei bibii lɛ biɔ nu aaafee lita 10 kɛyashi 15 shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Enɛ haa eshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛgbiee ni amɛgbooo.

english: Why should I cover the soil around the base of my crops with dried leaves or straw after watering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ nɔ beni mikɛ nu ewo mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil—known as mulching—acts like a protective blanket that traps moisture in the ground, stops weeds from growing, and keeps the plant roots cool during hot days.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni ŋmɛɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli

english: How can I tell when my oil palm nut bunches are fully ripe and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-oil palm tsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Oil palm nuts are ready to harvest when bright reddish-orange fruits start dropping naturally to the ground around the base of the tree.
ga: Mu tsei ahe tsei lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji tso yibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni kpɛɔ lɛ je shishi amɛgbee shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow when the soil stays waterlogged for too many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When soil remains soaked with water, the roots drown because they cannot breathe oxygen, which prevents the plant from taking up nutrients and causes the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagbo ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: What important farm activities should I write down in a notebook to help me manage my crops better?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔi ni he hiaa esa akɛ maŋma awo miwolo lɛ mli koni eye ebua mi ni makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Writing down planting dates, fertilizer applications, rainfall patterns, and harvest amounts helps you track crop performance and make smarter decisions for future seasons.
ga: Gbii ni aduɔ nii, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ ŋmaa lɛ falɛ ni aŋmalaa Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okwɛɔ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuɔ nii amɛhaa lɛ nɔ ni okpɛɔ oyiŋ jogbaŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ bei lɛ.

english: How can I prepare my crop farm so it stays safe and healthy when I travel away for a few weeks?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa miŋmɔ lɛ koni ehi shi shweshweeshwe ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ beni mibɛ jɛmɛ otsii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Before traveling, clear competing weeds, apply heavy mulch to preserve soil moisture, and leave clear, simple instructions for a trusted worker or family member to supervise the field.
ga: Dani obaafã gbɛ Jiemɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ. Kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ atsu nii. koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛ ŋaawoo ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yɔɔ faŋŋ aha nitsulɔi loo weku mli bii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛkwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves droop and curl up during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants curl their leaves in extreme heat to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, which conserves water loss until the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Cassava tsei kɛ la ni mli wa shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ yaa nɔ aahu kɛyashiɔ gbɛkɛ mli fɛ̃i baa.

english: How does planting my crops in straight, measured rows help them yield more food than planting randomly?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mitsei lɛ ni miduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja ni asusu nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii babaoo fe bɔ ni miduɔ amɛ trukaa lɛ?

english: Row planting ensures every crop gets equal access to sunlight, air flow, and soil nutrients without fighting neighboring plants, while also making weeding much easier.
ga: Row dumɔ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la. kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ awuu yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very thin and pale if I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, they compete aggressively with each other for light and soil food, causing them to stretch tall and thin instead of developing strong stems and large ears.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ niyenii ni waaa kɛ shikpɔŋ he akaŋ waa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmeii ni wa kɛ toi wuji.

english: What causes my crop leaves to turn pale green or yellow even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni haa mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ?

english: Pale yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food needed to make green leaves, which can be restored by adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa koni akɛfee baai eŋɔli Abaanyɛ aku sɛɛ afee enɛ kɛtsɔ kooloi aŋmei ni egbo loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I cut down all the large trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ shã ni amɛgboi beni mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle intense, direct sunlight. Large trees provide essential shade and retain soil moisture, protecting young seedlings from drying out and dying during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni eda lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Buu tsei bibii ahe koni amɛkagbi ni amɛgboi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen. The maize plant automatically moves the limited nitrogen it has from its older lower leaves up to its newer top leaves to keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ jieɔ nitrogen fioo ko kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei amli koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Waterlogged soil prevents oxygen from reaching the roots, causing the plants to suffocate. This damp environment also allows rot-causing fungi in the soil to multiply quickly and attack the tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni ji oxygen lɛ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi Nɛkɛ shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ nɛɛ hu haa ŋmeii ni haa sũ lɛ fiteɔ lɛ feɔ babaoo oya ni amɛtutuaa ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do the blossoms on my tomato plants drop off without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or lack of pollination. The plant discards the blossoms to conserve energy until growing conditions improve.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni naa wa waa he. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo pollination ni fa bɔ ni sa Tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and twisting tightly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe waa lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding on the undersides of the leaves, or by a virus carried by these insects that distorts normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ hiɛɔ ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ nɔ

english: Why do I need to stake my yam plants with wooden poles instead of letting the vines crawl on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei awo mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha wain tsei lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Staking lifts yam leaves high into the sunlight and away from hot soil and pests. Better sunlight access allows the plant to produce more food, leading to larger and healthier tubers underground.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la mli ni ekɛ ehe jɛkɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe. Hulu la ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tsei woɔ niyenii babaoo. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce very small bunches when I leave all the shoots growing around the base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa beni mishwieɔ ŋmeii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Excess shoots, or suckers, compete with the main plant for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Pruning away extra suckers leaves more energy for the main stem to grow large, heavy bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ mli ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ babaoo koni efee agbo ni etsii.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my plot make my next maize crop grow stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni mikɛduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha mi ŋmei tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ waa lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the ground after harvest, they enrich the soil with natural nitrogen that feeds the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Amɛbaahã shikpɔŋ lɛ aná adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ni baaya nɔ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up like thin tubes during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi?

english: Leaf rolling is a defense mechanism. By rolling its leaves, the maize plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun, helping it conserve internal water during the hottest parts of the day.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he. Baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ baa shi yɛ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ toɔ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why should I avoid applying granular fertilizer right before a heavy downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahe dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away loose fertilizer from the topsoil into gutters and streams before the roots can absorb it, wasting your investment and potentially damaging nearby plants.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etse ehe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa nubui kɛ faai amli dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Enɛ haa shika ni okɛwo mli lɛ fiteɔ, ni ebaanyɛ efite tsei ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant lacks nitrogen, which is a key nutrient it needs to grow big and green. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen-based fertilizer like urea around the stems can give your plants the food they need to recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni etsɔ agbo ni efee ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it good practice for me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas in the same farm as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil, giving nearby plants like maize extra food to grow better without needing as much expensive chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ naa niyenii krɛdɛɛ ko ni baaha amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why do the small flowers on my cocoa trees fall off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ cacao ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when the trees face extreme heat, prolonged dry spells, or damage from tiny sap-sucking insects like capsids. Providing shade trees in your cocoa farm helps keep the soil moist and protects the delicate flowers so they can form healthy pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ shɛ la ni naa wa waa he. Nuu be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. loo nɔ ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ capsids lɛ fiteɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ shade wo o-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebuɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe koni amɛwo ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds from around my young cassava plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Kasava tsei bibii?

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, water, and soil nutrients that your cassava plants need to build strong tuberous roots. Keeping the farm clean during the first three months allows the young cassava to grow quickly and shade out new weeds on its own.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa o-cassava tsei lɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa. Kɛ́ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tse yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhaa jwɛi heei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees bend and fall over easily when strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya ni egbeeɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and become heavy when carrying a full bunch of fruit. Planting clean, disease-free suckers deeply into rich soil and supporting fruiting trees with sturdy wooden props prevents them from tipping over.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛhe wa kɛji amɛwo yibii babaoo. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni he tse ni hela bɛ mli lɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ eyi obɔ lɛ nɔ, ni akɛ tsei ni wa fiɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Yam vines need to climb so their leaves can spread out and catch direct sunlight, which fuels the growth of the tubers underground. Elevating the vines off the damp ground also prevents leaves from catching fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. ni ji tsofa ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ daraa Wain tso lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii helai shɛɛɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up and stopping the fruits from growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi aduawai lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies, or by stress from extreme heat and irregular watering. Controlling whiteflies with organic sprays and keeping soil moisture steady helps prevent leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly loo kɛjɛɔ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa mli baa lɛ mli. Ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmeii anɔ lɛ akudɔɔ ŋmeii yɛji kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ afite.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers instead of producing green peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo pepper eŋɔli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when the soil gets too dry, temperatures become extremely high, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer in the soil. Watering regularly at the roots and using balanced plant food helps the plant keep its flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa loo be mli ni nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli daa kɛ tso niyenii ni ja ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell when my cassava roots are fully mature and ready to dig up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ edara kwraa ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 and 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off. You can also carefully dig around the base of one stem to check if the roots are thick and firm before harvesting the whole field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsa tso kome shishi hu koni okwɛ kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli edɔ ni amɛhi shi shiŋŋ dani okpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do small insects appear and ruin my harvested maize after a few weeks in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii jeɔ kpo ni amɛfiteɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi ni mikɛto lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: These insects are grain weevils, which hatch from tiny eggs hidden inside the maize kernels from the field. Thoroughly drying your maize in the sun until the grains are hard and storing them in sealed, airtight bags prevents weevils from surviving and eating your harvest.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji ŋmãa ŋmeii ni fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii bibii amli. Akɛtee ŋmãa mli kɛjɛ ŋmɔji amli ŋmãa ni oooha ŋmãa lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa ni okɛto kotokui ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli lɛ amli lɛ baatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkajo foi ni amɛye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves get burned or turn black after I spray them with pest medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa loo amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ eshwie amɛnɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When chemicals are mixed too strong or applied during the hottest part of the day, the solution burns the sensitive outer skin of the leaf. Mixing the exact recommended amount of water dilutes the chemical so it kills pests without damaging the plant.
ga: Kɛ tsofa ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo akɛtsu nii yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ, tsofa ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ baashã baai lɛ asɛɛ hewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Nu ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛfutu mli lɛ baaha tsofa lɛ afee mlɛo. No hewɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ egbe tsɛŋemɔ helai ni efiteee tso lɛ.

english: Why is it better for me to spray my farm early in the morning instead of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa afɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ leebi moŋ fe shwane?

english: In the hot afternoon sun, liquid chemicals evaporate into the air before the crop can absorb them, and intense heat combined with chemicals can scorch the leaves. Cool morning weather allows plants to absorb liquid treatments safely.
ga: Yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Tsofai ni ji nu lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Ni dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni akɛ tsofai fata he lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ ashã. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ leebi lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsuɔ nii shweshweeshwe.

english: How does chemical sprayed from above reach insects hiding underneath my crop leaves?
ga: Te tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛi lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ eshɛɔ kooloi bibii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ahe?

english: When liquid medicine is turned into a very fine mist, the tiny droplets float and swirl around in the breeze, coating both the tops and the undersides of leaves where insects like to hide.
ga: Beni tsofa ni ji nu lɛ tsɔɔ afua ni mli tse waa lɛ, nu bibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ehaa baa lɛ yiteŋ kɛ shishi fɛɛ he ni kooloi sumɔɔ ni amɛtee amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when weeds grow tall around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni jwɛi kakadaŋŋ abɔle he lɛ?

english: Weeds compete with maize for nutrients, water, and sunlight. When weeds surround maize, they steal the nitrogen in the soil that the maize needs to stay green, turning the leaves yellow and slowing crop growth.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ ŋmãa yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la. Kɛ jwɛi bɔle ŋmãa lɛ he lɛ Ejuɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa ŋmãa lɛ koni ehi shi eŋɔli lɛ. Baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eha tso lɛ ada blɛoo.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of leaves but produce very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: If the soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of sending energy down to develop big root tubers.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe lɛ, Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu hewalɛ kɛba shi koni ekɛfee bulbs ni shishifãi wuji yɔɔ mli lɛ

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when they are under extreme heat or water stress. The plant sheds its blossoms to conserve energy and survive rather than spending nutrients to develop new fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi kɛji amɛyɔɔ latsaa ni naa wa loo nu he haomɔ shishi. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ níhi nɛ haa nɔ he wami ɔ tsuɔ ní konɛ a ná yiblii ehehi.

english: Why do pests multiply so much faster on my farm during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo yaa hiɛ oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Warm temperatures speed up the life cycle of many farm insects, causing their eggs to hatch faster. At the same time, dry heat weakens crop defenses, making plants easier targets for pests to destroy.
ga: He ni mli edɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔ mli kooloi babaoo ashihilɛ yaa oya. Enɛ haa amɛ wuji lɛ fɔɔ oya. yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, la ni mli egbi lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ahebuu baa shi. Enɛ haa tsei feɔ nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ akpata amɛhiɛ oya.

english: Why do insect pests keep coming back to my farm even after I have sprayed chemical medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yaa nɔ amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai shwieɔ nɔ moŋ

english: Chemicals might kill adult bugs but miss eggs hidden in the soil or leaves. Furthermore, if you use the same chemical repeatedly, the surviving pests build up resistance, making the medicine less effective over time.
ga: Tsofai baanyɛ agbe kooloi bibii ni eda. Shi ŋmeii ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ loo baai amli lɛ baaje kpo. Kɛfata he lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tsofai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii shii abɔ lɛ, Surviving pests lɛ maa hewalɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ tsofai lɛ. Enɛ haa tsofa lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do some weeds on my farm die quickly after spraying while other types stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gboiɔ oya kɛji akɛ afɔ amɛ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni jwɛi krokomɛi yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ eŋɔli lɛ?

english: Different weed species have different leaf textures and internal chemistry. Some chemical weed killers only target broad-leaf plants, leaving narrow-leaf grasses unharmed, or vice versa.
ga: Jwɛi srɔtoi yɛ baai srɔtoi kɛ mligbɛ tsofai. Tsofai komɛi ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ tsɔɔ tsei ni baai babaoo pɛ yɔɔ mli. ni efiteee jwɛi ni baai bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ loo nɔ ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are suffering from a disease or just thirsty for rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela emɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ loo nugbɔ he kumai miiye amɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Drought stress causes leaves across the entire tree to wilt evenly and dry up from the edges. Plant diseases usually cause distinct dark spots, swollen stems, or pods rotting in specific patches on the tree.
ga: Hɔmɔ he haomɔ haa baai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi pɛpɛɛpɛ. jogbaŋŋ ni egbi kɛjɛ eshishigbɛ Bei pii lɛ, tsei ahe helai haa tso lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, eshishifãi lɛ efuu, loo eshishifãi ni egbo lɛ he ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa tso lɛ nɔ.

english: What does it mean when agricultural officers say a maize seed is a 'hybrid'?
ga: Kɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi kɛɛ akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ji ‘hybrid’ lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ?

english: A hybrid crop is created by intentionally crossing two different parent plants with strong, desirable traits—such as high yield and drought resistance—so the resulting seed gets the best qualities of both parents to produce a superior harvest.
ga: Afeɔ Hybrid ŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsɔ fɔlɔi tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ ni yɔɔ sui ni wa ni asumɔɔ, tamɔ yibiiwoo ni fa kɛ hɔmɔ ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ amɛtsui shi lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ baaná fɔlɔi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ahe su ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha yibiiwoo ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Hybrid seeds give their best yield only in the first generation. If you save and replant those seeds, the new plants will lose their balance of good traits, resulting in uneven growth, smaller cobs, and a much lower harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ haa yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Kɛji obua nakai dumɔwui lɛ anaa ni odu lɛ Tso hee lɛ baafite sui kpakpai ni eyɔɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee. Cob lɛ ji bibioo fe no. ni kpamɔ lɛ hu faaa kwraa

english: Why does my traditional local maize give a lower yield compared to the improved seeds sold at the agro-shop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mimaŋ ŋmãa lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni asaa amɛhe ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ okwaayeli shwapoi amli lɛ he lɛ?

english: Local seeds saved year after year gradually lose their vigor and strength. Improved seeds are specifically bred by crop scientists to resist local pests, tolerate dry spells, and produce bigger cobs.
ga: Kuu lɛ mli dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ baa shi fiofio. Dumɔwui ni asaa amɛhe lɛ ji nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nilelɔi fɔɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Ekɛ majik ni egbi lɛ teɔ shi ewoɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii wuji baa

english: Why do some of my white corn cobs have yellow kernels mixed in them when planted near my neighbor's yellow corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ hiɛ dumɔwui ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ mikutsoŋnyo ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Corn relies on the wind to carry pollen between plants. If white corn and yellow corn flower at the same time nearby, their pollen mixes in the air, causing individual kernels on the same cob to take on different colors.
ga: Abɛi kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ koni ekɛ pollen awo tsei ateŋ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa yɛŋ kɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ fɔ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ Amɛ pollen lɛ futuɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko ni yɔɔ ŋmei kome mli lɛ náa su sɔrɔto.

english: If I plant two different varieties of cassava next to each other in the same field, will their tubers mix together?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmei henɔi enyɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ. Ani abaafutu ŋmeii lɛ ekome?

english: Planting two cassava varieties side by side will not change the roots or stems you harvest that season. However, if their flowers exchange pollen, any seeds produced from those flowers will contain a genetic mix of both parents.
ga: Kasava henɔi enyɔ ni ooodu yɛ he kome lɛ tsakeŋ shishifãi loo ŋmeii ni okpaa yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ tsake amɛhe amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ, dumɔwui fɛɛ ni jɛɔ nakai fɔfɔi lɛ amli baa lɛ baaná fɔlɔi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ a-fɔmɔ nii ni efutu.

english: How do crop scientists create new seed varieties that can survive long dry seasons in Ghana?
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe nilelɔi feɔ tsei ahe dumɔwui heei Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni mɔ ko ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ mli?

english: Scientists take a crop variety that naturally handles drought well and cross-pollinate it with another variety that yields a lot of food. Over several generations, they select the offspring that keep both the drought strength and the high yield.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔi kɛ tsei sɔrɔtoi ni baanyɛ atsu hɔmɔ he nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ eba. ni akɛ cross-pollinated kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni woɔ yibii babaoo Seshibii ni ahala ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ amɛtsui shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli.

english: Why do some cocoa trees on my farm yield big pods while trees right next to them yield small, sick pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi woɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ be mli ni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji lɛ? Ekɛ pods bibii baa ni hela mɔ bo?

english: Cocoa trees grown from unselected seeds carry different natural traits, just like human children differ from one another. Trees with small or sick pods came from weaker parent stock, whereas high-yielding trees come from selected, resistant parent varieties.
ga: Cocoa tsei ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni ahalaaa mli lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli sui srɔtoi. Tamɔ obii ni ji adesai srɔtoi lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ Tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii loo helatsɛmɛi lɛ jɛɔ fɔlɔ tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ amli. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ jɛɔ fɔlɔi srɔtoi ni ahala ni nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ amɛhe lɛ amli.

english: If I want my tomatoes to be sweeter and last longer before spoiling, can I cross different tomato plants myself?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ miisumɔ ni mi-tomato lɛ afee nɔ ni ŋɔɔ ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ dani egbo hu? Ani mi diɛŋtsɛ manyɛ mafo tomato tsei srɔtoi amli?

english: You can select seeds from your best tomato plants over time, but controlled crossbreeding for specific traits like long shelf-life requires carefully moving pollen by hand and covering flowers so unwanted pollen doesn't mix in.
ga: Obaanyɛ ohala dumɔwui kɛjɛ tomato tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ amli yɛ be ni sa mli. Shi crossbreeding ni akudɔɔ kɛha sui pɔtɛɛ komɛi tamɔ shihilɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ Esa akɛ okɛ oniji atsu nii blɛoo. Tsi pollen lɛ he kɛbɔle ni okɛha fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni pollen ni ataooo lɛ akafutu mli.

english: What is grafting, and how does it help my mango trees bear fruit faster?
ga: Mɛni ji grafting? Ni te aaafee tɛŋŋ aye abua mango tso lɛ ni ewo yibii oya?

english: Grafting involves attaching a branch from a mature, high-yielding mango tree onto a strong young rootstock. Because the attached branch comes from an already mature tree, it skips the long juvenile stage and starts bearing quality fruit much sooner.
ga: Nɔ ni fata tso ni akɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ he ji ni akɛ niji ni jɛ mango tso ni eda ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ mli lɛ akpɛtɛ tso bibioo ko ni yɔɔ hewalɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei niji ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ he lɛ jɛɔ tsei ni eda lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, efoɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli ni ebɔi yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ womɔ mra kwraa.

english: Why do improved crop varieties seem to need more fertilizer and care than my wild local crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ biɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ kwɛmɔ babaoo fe mimaŋ koo mli tsei lɛ?

english: Improved crop varieties are bred to produce maximum yield, which means they require more food and care to reach their full potential—much like a hard-working farm animal that needs extra feed to do heavy work.
ga: Akwɛ tsei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii kɛ kwɛmɔ babaoo he miihia amɛ koni amɛshɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ he. Nakai eji yɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni tsuɔ nii waa ni niyenii kroko he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsu nii waa lɛ hu ahe.

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn under direct sunlight. Plantains or shade trees planted beside them act like natural umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and protecting the cocoa leaves until the trees are strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obu kookoo baai lɛ ahe kɛyashi tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are my young maize plants turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize plants are hungry for nitrogen in the soil or their roots are suffocate in waterlogged earth after heavy rain, preventing them from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ he miihia nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo shishifãi lɛ miihoso yɛ sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. ni haaa anyɛ aye niyenii

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn watery and rot underground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in clay heavy soil without proper drainage, or when soil pests create tiny holes that allow wet rot diseases to enter.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu shwie shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Aloo kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fee buji bibii. ni haa gangrene ni mli efɔ lɛ boteɔ mli

english: Why are the planting months that worked 15 years ago failing to give me good yields today?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu afii 15 ni eho nɛ lɛ wooo yibii kpakpai ŋmɛnɛ lɛ?

english: Weather patterns have shifted over time, causing rains to start later and end abruptly. Listening to updated advice from extension officers helps you match your planting dates with the actual rainfall patterns of today.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi tsakeɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Enɛ haa nugbɔ lɛ nɛɔ fioo ni esɛɛ foɔ trukaa. Ŋaawoo hee ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsulɔi adɛŋ lɛ toiboo baanyɛ aye abua bo ni okɛ gbii ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ ato ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ he.

english: Will planting cowpeas between my maize rows steal food away from the maize?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ teŋ lɛ baaju niyenii kɛjɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli?

english: No, cowpeas actually feed the soil by trapping nitrogen from the air through their roots, which helps nourish the maize while covering the ground to stop weeds from growing.
ga: Dabi, tsina ŋmeii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii diɛŋtsɛ kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni amɛmɔɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni ekɛ ŋmãa woɔ mli koni jwɛi akakwɛ̃.

english: What is eating small ragged holes in the middle whorl of my maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the deep funnel of the leaf shoot to eat tender new growth before the corn cob forms.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli koni amɛye ŋmeii heei ni eda dani ŋmeii lɛ baa lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Extreme heat during the day or sudden dry spells cause tomato plants to drop flowers to save water and energy when they feel too stressed to grow fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he beni amɛnuɔ he akɛ amɛmiifee basaa tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants crinkling up into small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni efee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on young leaves, or by a plant virus these insects carry from farm to farm.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow back much faster than my crops right after I clear my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni mijie he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Clearing the top soil exposes old weed seeds buried underneath to sunlight and rain, giving them a fast start before your crops can grow big enough to shade them out.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha jwɛi dumɔwui momoi ahi hulu kɛ nugbɔ shishi. Ehaa jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi oya dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛhaa amɛhe.

english: Why did my maize leaves wither and turn dry after I put fertilizer right next to the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ beni awo amɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa tso titri lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Concentrated fertilizer acts like strong salt and pulls water out of the plant roots if placed too close, burning the stem instead of slowly feeding the plant.
ga: Fertilizer ni mli ewo muji lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmei ni mli ewo muji. ni egbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli kɛji akɛ akɛwo he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ. Enɛ baashã tso lɛ shishifã lɛ moŋ fe ni eeeha tso lɛ niyenii blɛoo.

english: Why do my groundnut plants produce flowers above the ground, but the pods end up growing underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani pods lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Groundnut plants flower above ground, but once pollinated, the stems (called pegs) grow downward and push into the soil, where the pods safely develop and mature away from sunlight.
ga: Peanut tsei fɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ (ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs) lɛ wo mli lɛ, amɛdaraa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Pods lɛ baanyɛ adara shweshweeshwe ni amɛdara yɛ he ko ni hulu la shɛɛɛ he.

english: Why are some of the groundnut shells empty with no nuts inside when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ amli efee efolo ni ŋmeii bɛ mli beni mikpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut pods, often called 'pops', occur when the soil lacks calcium or water during the period when the pods are filling up, preventing the seeds from developing inside.
ga: Peanut ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ nɔ ko, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ 'pops' lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium loo nu yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ eyi lɛ. Enɛ haaa dumɔwui akwɛ̃ yɛ mli.

english: Is it better for my yield if I plant my crops very close together or leave wide spaces between them?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe loo mashi gbɛ yɛ amɛteŋ?

english: Giving crops proper spacing ensures that each plant receives enough sunlight, air, water, and soil nutrients without having to fight neighboring plants for survival.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ awuu koni ehi shi

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow instead of healthy green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen in the soil or that water is sitting around the roots, preventing the plant from making green food (chlorophyll).
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ehaa tsei nyɛɛɛ afee niyenii ni ji ŋmɔŋ (chlorophyll).

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant suffers from extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of essential soil nutrients needed to support fruit growth.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa hewɔ. Nu ni ashwieɔ shi daa loo niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha aduawai adalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: What causes holes in the leaves of my cowpea plants before they start producing pods?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bulɛ baa mi-cowpea baai lɛ amli dani amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Insects like beetles and caterpillars chew on young leaves to feed, which reduces the plant's ability to capture sunlight and produce a full crop of pods.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ŋmɔɔ baai bibii kɛha niyenii. Enɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛmɔɔ hulu la ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: How do I know the exact right time to pull up my groundnuts so they do not rot in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ magbala mi-peanuts lɛ koni amɛkafite yɛ sũ lɛ mli?

english: Groundnuts are ready to harvest when the leaves begin turning yellow and brown, and the inside lining of a opened test pod turns dark brown or black.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa kɛji baai lɛ je shishi amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ. ni kaa pod ni agbele lɛ mligbɛ tsɔne lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested grains develop mold even after I put them in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛwoɔ baagi mli moŋ?

english: Grains develop mold if they are bagged before being thoroughly sun-dried, as trapped moisture inside the bag creates an ideal environment for fungi to grow.
ga: Nibii ni ŋmaa baanyɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ kɛji akɛ awo kotoku mli dani agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔtɔ baanyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why does a mechanical sheller crush my groundnut seeds instead of cleanly removing the outer pod?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ ŋmeii lɛ miitswa mi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeejie kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ ni he tse nɔ lɛ?

english: A sheller crushes nuts if the gap setting on the machine is too tight for the seed variety or if the groundnuts are over-dried and brittle during processing.
ga: Mɛi ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ baakumɔ ŋmeii kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni ato yɛ tsɔne lɛ nɔ lɛ mli wa tsɔ kɛha ŋmeii srɔtoi lɛ. Aloo kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ egbi tsɔ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ be mli ni atsuɔ he nii lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots start turning dark and spoiling just two days after I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ lɛ bɔi duŋ ni amɛgboi yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni mifo amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots spoil quickly after harvest because exposure to air triggers a natural breakdown process once the root is separated from the living plant.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ oya kɛji akpa amɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli fitemɔ nifeemɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ mli egbala kɛjɛ tsei ni hiɛ ka lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them under direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and tender root systems that dry out quickly under harsh sun. They require temporary shade crops, like plantains, to shield them and keep the soil moist while their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛbu shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: Why should I start my pepper seeds in a small nursery bed before moving them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu pepper dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli dani mikɛwo shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper seeds produce very fragile sprouts that need close monitoring, steady watering, and protection from harsh weather and pests. Starting them in a nursery ensures only strong, healthy plants are transplanted into the main farm.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui woɔ dumɔwui ni waaa kwraa ni biɔ kwɛmɔ ni bɛŋkɛ kpaakpa. Nu daa ni obu he kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe. Tsei ni ajeɔ shishi yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ baaha tsei ni he wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ ajie kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings fall over and die right after sprouting in wet soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui bibii lɛ gboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Excess water traps moisture around the stem base, creating favorable conditions for fungal diseases like damping-off. Young stems rot easily when the soil stays constantly waterlogged.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi baa kɛha ŋmɔtɔ helai tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Tsoi bibii lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do I need to tie wooden sticks to my tomato plants while they are growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei akpɛtɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe beni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato stems are soft and tend to bend or snap under the weight of their own leaves and fruit. Staking keeps the plant upright, keeping fruit off the wet ground where insects and rot can destroy it.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛfɔɔ shwiemɔ loo amɛkumɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛbaai kɛ amɛyibii lɛ ashishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ. Kɛtsɔ aduawai lɛ ni atsĩɔ naa koni amɛkahi shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. he ni kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni fiteɔ nii baanyɛ akpata lɛ hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on once they sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ kɛji ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yam plants store energy in underground tubers by capturing sunlight through their leaves. Stakes lift the vines high so leaves get maximum sunlight and airflow, resulting in larger yams.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ hewalɛ toɔ amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛnaa kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Piles woɔ wain tsei lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni baai lɛ aná hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ babaoo. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, sweet potato lɛ baatsɔ agbo.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce very thin tubers when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse waa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers need space underground to expand and access soil nutrients. When crowded, the plants compete for light, water, and food, causing them to yield thin, low-quality roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ shishi he ko koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ehiii lɛ baa.

english: Why do weeds make my young maize plants grow thin and yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi-baby corn tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young maize crops and steal essential plant food, water, and sunlight. Without enough nutrients, young maize leaves turn light yellow and stems remain weak.
ga: Jwɛi daa oya fe abele bibii ni amɛjuɔ tsei niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hia. Kɛji niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ, ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my young maize crop turn pale yellow early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Pale yellow leaves on young maize indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is essential for leafy growth, and applying the right fertilizer early helps the crop stay green and vigorous.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia kɛha baa lɛ adalɛ. kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why should I mound up soft soil around my young yam and cassava plants instead of leaving the ground flat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabua sũ ni mli jɔ mabɔle he lɛ? Sweet potatoes kɛ cassava tsei Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mounding creates loose, well-drained soil that makes it easy for young roots to push downward and expand into big tubers without compacting.
ga: Mounding haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shi oya ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa kɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni amɛhiɛɛɛ amɛhe.

english: Why is it necessary to trim off lower branches on my young cocoa trees as they grow higher?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli beni tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Pruning removes weak, low branches so the tree directs its energy toward developing a sturdy main stem and a high canopy, which leads to better pod production later on.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ niji ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛná tso titri ni mli wa kɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni kɛlɛ. Enɛ haa anáa pod ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense full sun. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa plants need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to stay green and grow strong. Adding fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How do I know when my cassava is ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to swell and crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi shwiemɔ ni egbɛ eshwa.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off before turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop when temperatures get too high or when the soil dries out completely. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the roots helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha ebɔle he lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Is it good to burn the cleared bushes on my land before planting?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ mashã tsei bibii ni ajie yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani madu?

english: Burning destroys valuable nutrients in the soil and kills good organisms that keep the earth healthy. Clearing land without burning allows the plant waste to rot and turn into free natural food for your crops.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ni efiteɔ nibii kpakpai ni haa shibɔlemɔ ŋulami lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ashãaa lɛ haa tsei lɛ amli jwɛi lɛ fiteɔ ni ebafeɔ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko, ni ji adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop during the hot afternoon even if I watered them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ moŋ?

english: In intense heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up from the soil. They temporarily wilt to save water, but usually recover by evening as the temperature cools down.
ga: Yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiisumɔ ni amɛto nu he gbɛjianɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Shi bei pii lɛ, ehiɛɔ shi gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ waa lɛ.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and dry up on the branch?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet conditions and heavy shade. Pruning extra branches to let air and sunlight through your farm helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ amli koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ amli tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than the crops I actually planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya diɛŋtsɛ fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally suited to quickly grab sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing them early stops them from stealing the food your young crops need to grow.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe esa akɛ amɛŋɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkaju niyenii ni he hiaa otsei bibii lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: What will happen if I plant my crop seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots fight for the same water and soil food, and their leaves block light from one another. This results in thin, weak plants with small yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ faaa.

english: Should I apply chemical fertilizer immediately when I put seed into the ground?
ga: Kɛ́ miidu dumɔwui miwo shikpɔŋ lɛ, ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Applying strong chemical fertilizer directly on seeds or fresh shoots can burn and kill them. It is best to wait a few weeks until the plant forms strong roots that can safely absorb the nutrients.
ga: Kɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii amli lɛ tsu nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ dumɔwui heei loo ŋmeii anɔ Enɛ baanyɛ aha amɛshã ni amɛgboi. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ otsii fioo komɛi kɛyashi tso lɛ baaná shishifãi ni wa ni baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii kpakpai awo mli shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do some maize seed varieties take longer to grow and mature than others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi heɔ be babaoo dani amɛdaraa fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Different maize varieties are bred for different weather conditions. Short-duration seeds mature quickly to cope with brief rainy seasons, while long-duration varieties grow slower because they spend more time building strong stalks and larger ears.
ga: Akwɛ ŋmãa henɔi srɔtoi yɛ bɔ ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi srɔtoi yɔɔ ha lɛ naa. Dumɔwui ni hiɔ shi be kuku lɛ daa oya koni amɛnyɛ amɛkpee nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ naa. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei srɔtoi ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ daraa blɛoo ejaakɛ amɛheɔ be dani amɛnáa ŋmeii ni wa kɛ toii wuji.

english: Why are my maize seeds taking so long to sprout after I plant them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize seeds delay sprouting if the soil lacks sufficient moisture, if they were planted too deep, or if the specific seed variety has a naturally slower germination rate.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui lɛ baaha amɛkwɛ̃mɔ aya hiɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. ni adu lɛ mli kwɔ tsɔ loo kɛji dumɔwu pɔtɛɛ ko kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo fe bɔ ni eji yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ.

english: How do I choose between fast-growing maize seeds and regular maize seeds for my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmãa dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni daa kɛhaa miŋmɔ lɛ ateŋ?

english: If your area has short or unpredictable rains, fast-growing seeds are best so you can harvest before the dry season starts. If you have reliable, long rains, regular varieties can yield more grains over a longer period.
ga: Kɛji akɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ naa nugbɔ ni naa wa loo ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba. Dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ hi fe fɛɛ bɔni afee ni onyɛ okpa amɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi. Kɛji oyɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ Regular henɔi lɛ baanyɛ awo dumɔwui babaoo yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Can I save unused seeds from this planting season to plant next year?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni akɛtsuuu nii kɛjɛ nɛkɛ shweremɔ be nɛɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu afi ni baa lɛ?

english: Stored seeds lose their vigor and germination power over time, especially in humid conditions. Most improved seed varieties perform best when planted fresh during the season they are bought.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ kɛ amɛkwɛ̃mɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Titri lɛ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ Dumɔwui srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ateŋ babaoo tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ ehee yɛ be mli ni ahe amɛ lɛ.

english: Is it safe to spray my crops with farm chemicals that have been sitting unopened in storage for a long time?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai ni agbeleee ni akɛto be kakadaŋŋ lɛ baafɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Chemicals can degrade, settle, or become overly harsh over time. Using old or expired chemicals can damage your crops or prove completely ineffective against pests.
ga: Tsofai baanyɛ afite, afee oya, loo afee nɔ ni mli wa tsɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Tsofai ni etsɛ loo ni efite ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii loo abu he kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe kwraa.

english: What causes my crop leaves to burn or turn yellow after spraying them with agrochemicals?
ga: Mɛni haa mi tso lɛ baai lɛ shãa loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ beni akɛ agrochemicals eshwie nɔ sɛɛ?

english: Leaves burn if the chemical mixture is too concentrated, if you spray during hot midday sunshine, or if the chemical is applied at the wrong stage of the plant's growth.
ga: Baai lɛ shãa kɛji tsofa ni akɛfutu lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. aloo kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofai tsu nii yɛ be ni ejaaa mli yɛ tsei lɛ adalɛ mli

english: Why shouldn't I keep re-applying the same crop protection chemical every time I see pests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni buɔ tsei ahe lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii ekoŋŋ be fɛɛ be ni mana tsɛŋemɔ hela ko?

english: Continuous use of the same chemical can build pest resistance, render the chemical useless over time, and leave toxic residues in the soil that stunt crop growth.
ga: Tsofai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ baanyɛ aha tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ anyɛ atsu nii. Enɛ haa tsofai lɛ feɔ nɔ ni he ehiaaa yɛ be ni sa mli. ni eshiɔ nibii ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni eshwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni haaa ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃.

english: What happens to my crops if I apply chemicals or fertilizers at the wrong growth stage?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofai loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii yɛ be ni esaaa akɛ amɛdaraa lɛ mli?

english: Applying chemicals too early can kill tender seedlings, while applying them too late wastes money because the crop has already passed the point where the inputs can help it.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli oya lɛ baanyɛ agbe dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛtsu nii sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ofite shika ejaakɛ tso lɛ eho he ni nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow fast at the beginning but suddenly slow down before producing fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ daa oya yɛ shishijee mli shi no sɛɛ lɛ egbɔjɔ dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Crops need different nutrients at different stages. They use nitrogen for early leaf growth, but require extra phosphorus and potassium when transitioning to flowering and fruiting; without these, growth stalls.
ga: Tsei biɔ niyenii srɔtoi yɛ fãi srɔtoi amli. Akɛ nitrogen tsuɔ nii kɛhaa baai lɛ adalɛ mra. Shi ehe miihia ni ekɛ phosphorus kɛ potassium afata he yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo be lɛ mli. Kɛji nibii nɛɛ bɛ Stall of dalɛ

english: How does sudden dry weather affect how quickly my crops mature?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ oya lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Lack of water causes plants to stress, which can either delay their development or force them to mature prematurely, resulting in small and poorly formed crops.
ga: Nu ni bɛ lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ehiɛyaa lɛ aya hiɛ fioo loo enyɛ ehiɛyaa nɔ oya. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ su kpakpa baa.

english: How does a greenhouse actually work to help my vegetable crops grow?
ga: Te greenhouse tsuɔ nii ehaa tɛŋŋ koni eye ebua mi aduawai lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: A greenhouse traps sunlight to protect plants from heavy rains and pests, but it must be properly ventilated so that it does not trap too much heat and damage your crops.
ga: Greenhouses mɔɔ hulu la koni ebu tsei ahe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe. Shi esa akɛ aha kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa abote mli bɔni afee ni ekahiɛ dɔlɛ babaoo mli ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: What is the difference between a plastic greenhouse and a net house for growing vegetables?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ plastic ŋmɔ kɛ trellis ŋmɔ teŋ?

english: A plastic greenhouse traps heat and keeps out rainwater, while a shade-net house allows cool breeze to pass through, keeping the air much cooler for crops in hot areas.
ga: Plastic tsũi ni haa jeŋ dɔɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ dɔlɛ ni ehaaa nugbɔ nɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsũi ni yɔɔ ŋshɔŋlooi lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ waa kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hei ni latsaa yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Can I successfully build and use a standard plastic greenhouse in hot areas like Northern Ghana?
ga: Ani manyɛ matswa plastic tsũ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ he ko ni hulu tsoɔ tamɔ Ghana Kooyigbɛ lɛ yɛ omanyeyeli mli ni mikɛtsu nii?

english: Standard plastic greenhouses can turn into hot ovens in regions like Northern Ghana; it is better to use net structures or top vents so hot air can escape and keep plants cool.
ga: Abaanyɛ atsake plastic ŋmɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ afee flɔnɔɔ ni mli edɔ. Yɛ hei tamɔ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛ trellis loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ baatsu nii koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ ajɛ mli ni eha tsei lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: If my greenhouse gets too hot in the afternoon, can I change the roof or walls to cool it down?
ga: Kɛji mi-greenhouse lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ yɛ shwane mli Ani manyɛ matsake ŋwɛitsu loo gbogboi lɛ koni greenhouse lɛ mli adɔ?

english: Yes, you can modify a hot plastic greenhouse by replacing sections of the plastic walls or roof with insect mesh netting to allow cool air to flow through.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ otsake plastic tsũ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ plastic gbogboi loo tsũ lɛ yiteŋ fãi komɛi ni okɛ kooloi ŋmɔji baatsake koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ atsɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops wilt and drop their flowers during very hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho ni fɔfɔii lɛ miiho yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, plants shut down their growth to save water, which causes delicate flowers to fall off before they can turn into fruits.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ Tsei lɛ tsiɔ amɛdalɛ naa koni amɛbu nu he. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why are my vegetables turning yellow even when I water them inside my farm structure?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa miŋmɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ moŋ?

english: If the air inside your structure gets too hot, the soil becomes too warm and plant roots struggle to drink water and absorb nutrients properly.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ otsu lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Ni tsei shishifãi lɛ baaná naagba yɛ nu ni amɛnuɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ he.

english: Do my crop plants need direct afternoon sun all day to yield well?
ga: Ani hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ he miihia miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ shwane muu lɛ fɛɛ mli koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai?

english: Crops need light to make food, but strong afternoon sunlight combined with extreme heat can scorch the leaves and reduce your total yield.
ga: La he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛfee niyenii. Shi shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa fata he lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai lɛ ni eha yibiiwoo lɛ fɛɛ aba shi.

english: Is it safe for me to spray pesticides inside an enclosed crop structure?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni agbe naa lɛ mli?

english: Spraying in enclosed spaces requires great care because chemical vapors get trapped in the heat, which can harm your health or burn your crop leaves if applied heavily.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ hei ni afo he lɛ biɔ hiɛdɔɔ waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsofai ni mli edɔ lɛ baakã hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aye ohewalɛ nɔ awui loo eshã tso lɛ baai kɛji akɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ hewalɛ mli.

english: How can I avoid burning my crop leaves when I spray them with chemicals?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mihe kɛjɛ shãa ni mikɛ tsofai shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ ahe?

english: You should spray lightly during cool morning or evening hours and avoid spraying too close to the leaves, especially when air temperatures are high.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ nɔ fioo yɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ nɔ. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni bɛŋkɛɔ baai lɛ ahe tsɔ lɛ he. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa.

english: Why do fungal diseases spread fast inside covered crop gardens during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shia mli abɔɔi amli yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Warm, trapped air creates high humidity inside covered gardens, which creates an ideal environment for plant diseases and fungi to grow quickly.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni amɔmɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo babaoo baa abɔɔ ni aha nɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsei ahe helai kɛ ŋmeii ni baa lɛ oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow starting from the tip down the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛnajiaŋ kɛyashi amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing along the main vein of maize leaves usually means the soil is low in nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main food plant leaves use to stay dark green and make energy for building big ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ fãji titrii lɛ ahe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei ahe baai kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ni amɛfee hewalɛ ni amɛkɛmaa ŋmãa toi wuji.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young oil palm trees developing bright orange spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Orange spots on lower oil palm leaves show that the palm lacks potassium, a key nutrient it needs to build strong leaves and produce heavy palm fruit bunches.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ mu tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ potassium bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni akɛfee baai ni wa ni akɛwo ŋmei yibii babaoo.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomato fruits turning soft and black before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi feɔ blɛoo ni eyɛ ediŋŋ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is known as blossom-end rot. It occurs when the plant cannot draw enough calcium from the soil, which usually happens if watering is uneven or the soil dries out completely between rains.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ateŋ.

english: Why do my yam vines keep trying to climb up wooden stakes instead of growing across the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekwɔ tso ko nɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally search for height so their leaves can catch full sunlight. Using stakes keeps leaves off the damp soil to prevent disease and gives the plant enough sun energy to grow larger underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ naa amɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei tsu nii lɛ, ehaaa baai lɛ ajɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ koni helai akabote mli, ni ehaa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my groundnut plants push their flower stems down into the soil after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ tsiɔ efɔfɔi lɛ awoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni ewo fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants practice subterranean fruiting. Once the flowers are pollinated above ground, the stem pegs extend downward into moist soil to protect the developing nut pods from drying heat and surface pests.
ga: Peanut tsei feɔ yibiiwoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔii lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ stem pins lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni abu ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ ahe kɛjɛ latsaa ni mli egbi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cowpea plants drop all their flowers without producing any bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa baaa lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers drop off mainly when tiny insects called flower thrips attack the blossoms, or when extreme heat puts stress on the plant during the early morning flowering period.
