ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ gbeeɔ shi babaoo kɛji kooloi bibii ba amɛnɔ. Ale amɛ akɛ fɔfɔi thrips, ni amɛtutuaa fɔfɔi. aloo be mli ni latsaa ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ yɛ leebi maŋkpa fɔfɔi be lɛ mli.

english: Why does my cassava crop take so many months before the roots underground start swelling into tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ heɔ nyɔji babaoo dani shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cassava spends its first few months building tall stems and wide leaves. Once it has enough green leaves above ground to catch sunlight, it begins storing extra energy down in its taproots to form heavy tubers.
ga: Yucca heɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ dani enáa ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ. Beni baai eŋɔli ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni hulu la baanyɛ ashɛ nɔ lɛ. Ebaaje shishi ekɛ hewalɛ kroko ato eshishifã lɛ mli koni ekɛfee bulb ni tsii.

english: Why do the leaves on my plantain suckers wilt and fold downwards during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfoɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Plantain stems are made mostly of water rather than hard wood. In high heat and dry weather, leaves lose water faster than the roots can drink, causing the leaves to fold down to protect the stem from scorching.
ga: Nu ji nɔ ni akɛfeɔ plantain tsei lɛ babaoo fe tso ni wa. Yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa ni egbi lɛ, nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Okɛ baai lɛ abɔ shi koni tso lɛ akashã.

english: Why are small green cocoa pods on my tree trunks turning black and dry instead of growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ tso lɛ shishitso lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ agbo lɛ.

english: Small cocoa pods turn black either due to Black Pod disease caused by high moisture and fungus, or through natural pod thinning where the tree drops excess pods it cannot feed.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ ŋmeii diji hela ni hulutsoo ni fa babaoo kɛ ŋmeii kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ. aloo kɛjɛ adebɔɔ mli pod thinning ni tso lɛ shwieɔ pod ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aye niyenii lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why does my maize crop grow thin and weak when I delay clearing weeds around the young plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ mli tsɔ ni egbɔjɔ waa beni mikɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ?

english: Young maize has soft, shallow roots. Tall weeds quickly steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients before the maize roots can spread out, starving the maize plants early in their growth.
ga: Abɛi bibii yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya dani ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmãa tsei yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee mli.

english: Why do my young maize leaves turn yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient they need to grow strong. It can also happen when heavy rains wash nutrients deep into the ground where roots cannot reach them, or when water stagnates in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ kpakpa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. aloo be mli ni nu ekã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: How do I know it is safe to plant my seeds after the long dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ midumɔwui ni mikɛduɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe?

english: It is safest to plant after you receive at least two or three steady, deep rains that thoroughly soak the soil. Planting after the very first light shower is risky because a sudden dry stretch right after can dry out and kill your germinating seeds.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ akɛ aaadu yɛ kɛ hoo lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ oshara. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ mɔ ko shwie shi trukaa yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my cassava sticks very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded together, their leaves shade each other from the sunlight, and their roots fight for the same soil water and nutrients. Giving them proper spacing allows each plant to make full use of the sun and soil to grow larger tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ efee ekome yɛ kui amli lɛ, baai lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ hulu la. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hu he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nyɛɔ ekɛ hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛwo bulbs wuji.

english: Yam plants produce larger tubers underground when their leaves catch maximum sunlight above ground. Staking lifts the vines off the earth, spreading the leaves out to capture sunlight while preventing wet-soil diseases from damaging the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ amɛbaai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ. Gbalamɔ baai lɛ amli koni hulu la lɛ aba nɔ yɛ be mli ni otsiɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu naa koni amɛkafite baai lɛ.

english: Why are the pods on my cocoa tree turning dark black and drying up before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet, shady conditions. You can reduce it by pruning unnecessary cocoa branches to let sunlight and air dry out the trees, and by picking off infected pods so the fungus does not spread.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Obaanyɛ oba enɛ shi kɛtsɔ kookoo niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni ooofo mli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi aba tso lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ koni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes tiny holes in my cabbage leaves and how does it harm my crop?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ cabbage baai anɔ Ni te eyeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii awui ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Those holes are caused by small caterpillars and insects feeding on the leaves. When insects destroy the leaves, the cabbage cannot produce enough food for itself, which stops the tight head from forming properly.
ga: Buji nɛɛ ji nɔ ni ŋmeii bibii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ baai lɛ feɔ. Kɛji kooloi bibii kpata baai lɛ ahiɛ lɛ, Kaabaji nyɛŋ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa eha ehe. Enɛ haaa bulbs ni mli wa lɛ afee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience severe heat or water stress. If the air gets extremely hot or the soil dries out completely while flowering, the plant drops its flowers to conserve energy and survive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu he haomɔ he. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and die during heavy rainy weather when there is plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli ni nu babaoo yɔɔ lɛ?

english: When heavy rain keeps the soil constantly waterlogged, the plant's roots drown because they cannot get oxygen from the air in the soil. Damaged roots can no longer absorb water or food, causing the plant above ground to wilt.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ waa lɛ, nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. Tsei shishifãi shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛná kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Shishifãi ni efite lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ nu loo niyenii dɔŋŋ. Ehaa tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster on my farm than my planted crops after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni adu yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants natively adapted to your local soil, so they wake up and consume water and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing light and food from your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni kɛ amɛhe ewo he ni oyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛteɔ shi ni amɛyeɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Ni oootsi ohe mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: How do I tell if my cassava is ready for harvesting underground without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ efee klalo akɛ akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni akuuu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli?

english: Cassava is usually ready around 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell it is maturing when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the main stem starts cracking open from expanding tubers beneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha dumɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baai lɛ edara kwraa kɛ́ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in a open field without bigger trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?
